Absolutely love Annie! She is the best. I thought I would fail the course but she was so good at teaching the material. Definitely the best accounting professor out there. There are enough extra credit opportunities and if you pay attention you can 100% do well.

I definitely wasn't always a fan of Annie, but really loved her as the class continued. She is an amazing professor who actually cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Go to office hours if you're struggling. She is so helpful and kind. Highly recommend taking a course with her.
Annie will help you get to where you need to be and keeps it real. She stayed with us for over four hours the day before the final to help us study, which is rare.
she is a good professor but she is a bit too much. she believes that this class is the only class student have and gives a lot of work.

Annie was honestly great. I really really really struggled with accounting so it required me to put in work but not an overwhelming amount at all. Great preparation for exams and her notes r so helpful. 2 interim exams, 1 2 part group proj, hw, quizzes, participation, and the final. I think if I took another professor I would not have done as well.

If you are going to take this course, don't. Or at least do not take it online. The group project was terrible and impossible to coordinate and Annie had no sympathy. She also would not respond to emails in a timely manner. The only reason I got a decent grade is because I bought a Chegg subscription specifically for the class.

She is honestly amazing!!! I would take any course she teaches. Although she said her tests are harder than some, she prepares you really well for them and helps for the final. Her homeworks have unlimited tries, and her quizzes are not graded (unless your class lacks participation). She gives extra credit opportunities during class exercises.

11/10 Professor. Made accounting easy to understand. Pay attention in class and you will get an A. Super helpful, forgiving grader, gives a lot of extra credit, makes you want to attend class. I would take any class taught by her. Best teacher/professor i have ever had anywhere. TAKE HER. We STAN Annie!

Annie is a caring professor and she is good at what she does. Accounting isn't the easiest topic, but she makes it a little more enjoyable with her lectures and her willingness to help students out in difficult situations. The homework is helpful and guaranteed 100%; reading the textbook and paying attention are important, but is very worth it.

Annie made me love accounting. Her lectures are amazing and she explains everything so clearly. The exams are really fair and if you pay attention in class and study you'll succeed. The homeworks are really helpful and unlimited check your answers too. She gives a lot fo extra credit and she loves if you participate. I recommend 100%.
Great professor. Exams are manageable and she is a forgiving grader. Annie cares a lot about her students and wants them to learn. As long as you pay attention in class, you will do very well.

The class is very structured, and her tests are easy and straightforward so long as you study. There is one group project that takes time but she allows you to spread out the work to be manageable. 

Her teaching methods aren't may favorite; she uses skeleton notes and entertains way too many questions. Found myself to be very disorganized w/ notes
She is great, just get ready to study for the exams

Annie was a great professor, her class was very organized and she made sure her students understood what they were learning. Make sure to participate even if you're wrong and you'll most likely do well in the class.

Super great professor. Very intelligent and is both good at teaching material and a caring person. Has a great balance between difficult enough that you learn, but not too difficult that the class is overly stressful. One of my few 10/10 professors.

No laptops allowed, but she keeps class casual and lectures with fill in the blank slides will hold your attention. Do the homework and practice problems on canvas to prepare for exams. Would take again.

a tough, but great teacher. a little bit of a rocky start, but she went out of her way to make sure most if not all her students obtained a solid foundation of accounting. read the textbook, do the homeworks, participate in class even if youre wrong. shes super organized, overall great! best 1201 accounting teacher at NEU.

Annie was my favorite professor I had this semester. The class does have a lot of tests, basically 1 per week, but she gives ample notes and class time to ace every one of them if you put in the work. She does truly care about her students and loves teaching, which is not always the professional standard. Overall great teacher and would recommend.
Annie was the best no contest. Shes direct, cares and made accounting my favorite class of the semester. Shes entertaining and youll pass easily if you follow her advice.

reviews.comment: Annie is extremely caring and wonderful at teaching accounting. If you participate or engage with the material during class, it becomes so much easier to do well in her class. reviews.comment: Annie was a pretty decent prof. I think she said she was new to Northeastern, so I'd give her the benefit of the doubt. Lectures were very good, but Accounting is always tough
Really great professor, definitely one of my hardest classes and she makes you work for an A. Very organized, answers emails super fast, and will help you out if you're struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good teacher, definitely makes you work. Probably the most work i've put into a first-year class. Prepared us greatly for the final with her chapter quizzes/ cumulative exams.

Annie is an amazing professor! Although her class is difficult, she is very flexible with her time in order to provide help to ensure you get the grade you deserve. I have learned a lot from her. reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Although the class is super challenging, Annie was an amazing professor and was really good at teaching the subject with analogys and all. She was also super supportive outside the classroom and treats her students as equals. To me, having a teacher thats good at teaching the content is more important then my grade in the class. Would recommend:)

Annie is always available for help in and out of class. She is extremely understanding and will work with you until you understand the topics that are taught. The class is challenging (but manageable) - and because of this you will be prepared for the final. I would 100% recommend taking her class. She is a great teacher and even better person!

Annie is AMAZING!!!! Study the packets and ask questions in class and you'll be fine. Her quizzes are tough, but she drops the lowest two and gives you a bonus. Exams are fair. She makes class fun considering the subject and will always help if you ask.

Annie really cares about her students and wants to see everyone succeed. She keeps class engaging , will make you laugh and is very approachable for asking questions. The content is challenging though.

Annie has a kind heart, but reminds me of a high school teacher. She clearly does not understand that learning can take place WITHOUT the use of excessive testing. reviews.comment: Great professor!

COM1511. Although I felt nervous to take the class, Professor Allen created a warm and welcoming environment on day one. He truly cares about your growth and is judgment-free. Pushes you to become the best version of yourself. A super kind and caring man.
Really understanding, and allowed me to flourish in ways that I didn't think I could at the beginning of the semester.

reviews.comment: A must-take at Northeastern! Greg is such an amazing professor with a lot of experience and creates such a welcoming environment. You'll definitely learn a lot in this class and have lots of fun!!

Greg is by far one of my favorite professors I've EVER had during my three years at Northeastern. He is so funny and caring, and this was the one class that never felt like a chore. Every single class we would come in, have fun, laugh with our classmates, and just genuinely have a wild amount of fun. Just take his class- I swear it will be great.

The best professor I've ever had IN MY LIFE! He is so caring so funny and really wants to see you succeed in and out of his class. Love him would take all of his classes if i could. TAKE ANY OF HIS CLASSES YOU WILL HAVE THE BEST TIME AND LEARN SO MUCH!!!!

For COMM 1511: Greg is genuinely a great guy and I recommend the class for anyone, not just theater people. He truly cares about each of his students and makes the class enjoyable and a safe space to present, even if you aren't great at public speaking.
Amazing person, easy class, and I learnt a lot. I did COMM 1511 with him.

!! For COMM1511, which is not listed for some reason. !!

Amazing and super chill prof, class really felt like a community by the end of semester. 

Beware, attendance is mandatory, with the extent of this policy unclear until well into the semester. Go to the classes! (then again, you will look forward to and enjoy the classes.)

super chill guy! i took this class as an easy A but really enjoyed it and am sad it's over. it can get tiring at times if u hv a 1hr40 section but overall a super chill and stress free professor. super funny and personable as well, and gives a lot of feedback and encouragement.
Greg is one of the best professors I've ever had.  He is incredibly kind, interested in his students, and very good at creating an inviting environment in the classroom.

I only withdrew from this class because I was moving up to a different one. Greg is super kind and his class is really chill. As long as you're ready to step out of your comfort zone and put yourself out there you'll be totally fine! There's minimal homework and the whole thing is super chill, 10/10.

Dr. Apfeld is probably the sweetest professor ever. He's always posting cute animal memes, which make the class feel much less stressful, and he's always available and willing to help you during his office hours. Exams, including the final, are all online, which is absolutely sweet because it means you can be in bed taking an 8 am exam.

Prof Apfeld is one of the best professors I've ever had. I loved the lectures and he was very deliberate to mention how the field interacts with societal bias. Expectations were clear, I learned a lot, and I thoroughly enjoyed the class as a whole. Couldn't ask for anything more from a professor
DONT TAKE G TAKE JAVIER

Great teacher for genetics. lectures in person and on zoom which is great because I find it easier to pay attention on Zoom. All the tests are online open-book but need studying to do well. He is very passionate about his content and seems to love teaching. does tophat questions for attendance credit in class, but gives 75% credit even if wrong.

He is the nicest professor ever and extremely leniant with late assignments and absences. He really cares about the subject and preparing his students for the real world. I would definitely reccomend taking him if you want to learn useful skills in a low stakes environment.

Javier was a wonderful professor and truly passionate about his students learning in class & out (service learning). Classes are small group discussions based on a variety of aging papers. There are no exams and he is flexible with assignment deadlines. I would definitely recommend taking this course!

Dr. Apfeld is an extremely caring and kind professor, and is very understanding about personal issues and willing to be flexible with deadlines. The class itself is a lot of reading, but very discussion based and helpful in learning how to approach reading research papers. He is very passionate about this topic and cares about his students.
Dr. Apfeld is so kind, flexible, and passionate about the content.

Dr.Apfeld isn't the best lecturer, but it's easy to succeed if you review lectures, teach yourself, and complete all homework and review materials. Tests are online, open book, and not hard with a good understanding of the material. He drops the lowest of 3 exams (each 25%) and the final is cumulative (35%). He's kind and wants students to succeed.

He is not so great at lecture/oral presentation skill, but he is a GREAT teacher, he cares about you and gives you good grade and a lots of extra credits, he is always there if u want to reach out outside of class. I had to admit that he so far the only prof who actually cared about their student and their grades after high school.

For starters, he is an amazing guy who is very caring. I had a lot of family stuff going on during the semester and he was supportive and would excuse me when I missed class. Apfeld was a good guy, however, I never understood his lectures because he would mumble. His exams were hard, but open note. He was a caring guy, but I never got much out of his class and therefore wouldn't take him again.

reviews.comment: Such a sweet guy but unfortunately a bad lecturer. I tried to follow his train of thoughts until I realized he gets lost in his own logic, and I stopped paying attention. Uses Tophat for in-class questions, quizzes, and exams. Not hard to get an A, but you won't learn anything unless you study all the materials yourself.

Professor Apfeld is very kind and actually quite funny at times. His fatal flaw is that he tends to mumble his way through lectures and it is quite impossible to stay engaged in class. With that said, all of the tests are online and open note so it is easy to get a good grade.

Good guy, and not the hardest class, but a few things: do the hw at the end of lectures and be prepared to pull out ones from past lectures for his quizzes, lecturing skills are mid so printing out the slides and jotting ideas down for review afterward might help more than full blown notes, and tests do have problems that require a lotta practice.

There's tophat questions every class. You can look at the lectures ahead of time on canvas and find the answers on quizlet. None of the tophat questions are on the exams. Exam 1 and 3 are easy, 2 and the final were not as easy. The tophat questions are required. He just reads off slides and can't answer questions.

reviews.comment: I love Professor Apfeld so much!! He really cares about his students and takes your feedback on the class into serious consideration. He makes the classroom a safe and inclusive place--overall a very kind man and great professor

Personality wise professor apfeld is so understanding and actually cares about your mental health Quizzes and Tophat questions were easy Exams were somewhat confusing but fair- please do the practice exams Hes open to any questions in office hours but doesnt really answer them well during lectures Mediocre lecturer, reads off slides a lot

Dr. Apfeld doesn't really go too in depth with the material, and usually reads off of powerpoint slides. Not too helpful when in need of some clarification for some material. Generally a nice man, but does not make things clear enough for his students.

Professor Apfeld is a PowerPoint reader. He gives HW from the textbook and doesnt know how to answer them. His test questions are weirdly worded. He loves to talk about worms, but they get extremely annoying. His office hours are useless, get ready to self teach yourself. Only good thing about the class was that the man is nice and the cat memes.
Just a ppt reader, boring.
Loves talking about his c. elegans. Sweet, funny guy but unfortunately a terrible professor. Class was based on tophats, three exams, and a final :/
good!

I didn't realize how amazing Gillen was for 1501 until I had a different professor for 1502. He is honestly amazing, he cares, grades fairly, and is always available for help. actually the sweetest guy ever- if you have cornerstone with him, you've lucked out. i learned a good amount between taking cornerstone 1 & 2 with him and he's super kind + down to earth; he does go a little slower than other cornerstone teachers but i still got a lot out of his course.

I cannot brag about how lucky I got with my cornerstone professor. I LOVEEE Professor Gillen. He truly cares about you and your education and is always offering extra resources and help whenever something is difficult. He gives amazing feedback and is super chill. I learned a lot from Gillen and would definitely recommend to take his class.

Just put a little effort and do your hw, and you'll pass with an A, along with learning so much new things. Very keen of animals as well.

Where do I begin with Professor Gillen? He is the GREATEST teacher I have ever had, including pre-university. Give the boy a chance, even if you don't need the credit!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I genuinely learned so much and Professor Gillen is wonderful at explaining everything. He is super caring and it is enjoyable coming to class everyday. He plays music sometimes while we work, and sometimes does breathing exercises which is super nice. Highly recommend taking cornerstone with him!
Classes are very engaging and give adequate time to complete every assignment. Very caring and will take the time to answer any questions students have.

BEST prof ever. Such a sweet understanding guy that makes students excited to get into engineering. Very reasonable workload, never a stressful class (except when projects r due lol). This was easily my favorite class this semester. Gillen is an amazing teacher and his class has no crazy expectations. Gillen is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He is very kind and understanding. Would def recommend him to anyone taking this course.
THE GOAT! Take this class you will not be disappointed. So caring and easy to reach outside of class.

GILLEN IS MY GOAT!

Would take his classes again!

Great professor. Puts in the work to make the lectures super engaging and is honestly a great guy. He makes. a lot of sense. Would recommend.

He is good teacher that does really care about his students. He is extremely easy, especially when compared to other cornerstone teachers. You may not learn all the material quite as well as you would in other class just because of how easy the work is, but in the end it doesn't really matter.

Professor Gillen was great. He knows the material and can answer questions; if he is ever unsure, he is completely honest. Lectures are interactive and engaging. Good professor. The class is pretty easy if you just pay attention and do your work.

Professor Larson is great! She's exactly what a professor should be. You need to participate in her class, but she is an entertaining lecturer and cares about her students and helping them learn the content. The midterm and final are written answer but you get a cheat sheet.

The best professor I've had in the business program. She cares about students and wants you to do well. The grade is primarily based on a couple of tests (you are allowed a sheet of notes) and a large final paper. Good feedback, enjoyable class, and I learned a lot.

By far the best professor to take Fundamentals of Software Engineering with. Much more reasonable in-class expectations than other professors during my semester, and super accessible for help outside of and during class. Highly recommend.

HE IS AMAZING

GOAT. Take if u can

Super fun teacher even when the material felt slow, has engaging lectures and works with students to meet them where they're at. Would take a class with him again.

Nik is the best professor I've had so far! He's hilarious and genuinely cares about his students. There's a lot of reading each week, but you can get by with just skimming. TAKE THIS CLASS! Nik Beimler is an amazing teacher who gets to know his students and wants them to succeed. He is available outside of class if you don't understand something and is very helpful. His lectures can be a bit long and content heavy but he will take time to make things clear if you don't understand the content. Amazing teacher!!
One of the most amazing professors. Such a nice and caring person, too. He offers so many extra credit opportunities and genuinely wants you to do well.
Great professor and an even better person
I would not recommend taking this course. The professor often responds to emails late, and there are many tests with numerous essay questions. Grading also feels quite strict.

The class itself isn't that bad but her lectures are ridiculously dense and repetitive. reviews.comment: Do yourself a big favor if you love yourself. Don't take her. Very disorganized person in general, she doesn't know how to use technology, and despite the fact she knows her subject, she doesn't communicate effectively. She doesn't now how to communicate at all.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Professor Berent's slides are extremely confusing, misrepresentative of the exam questions, and does not explain the information well even in office hours. Get ready to spend hours studying.

She is not as bad as everyone is saying imo, it is just a difficult class. She is a good teacher however and I think attending class and going to office hours will benefit you. Attendance is mandatory. Final is optional. I got an A by attending lecture, rewatching lecture recordings, and practice mcq. The final replaced my lowest grade.

very nice person but not a good prof. if you miss one lecture you'll be left wondering what is going on. i had to miss a few due to athletic events and it became confusing quickly after. also don't know how to post the canvas hw right half the time so you'll end up missing deadlines you didn't even know exsisted.

This course is not as difficult as everybody says it is. Tests are all multiple choice, and the cumulative final is optional. Professor Berent is super nice, but you HAVE to show up to class to do good otherwise you'll be lost; can't learn from slides alone.
I dropped this class three weeks before finals bro, one of our tests the class mean is 60 something... please do yourself a favor dont fxxking take this class

Take this class if youre super interested in learning sentence structure, if youre not, then don't take it. Class material is not interesting. Heavy course material, I genuinely don't see a point of taking this class lol if it's not mandatory.

She's one of the sweetest prof i've ever had. lecture is a bit heavy, you really have to lock in and focus during class. homework are super easy. tests are all multiple choice. materials are quite abstract, not much of psychology related content. highly recommend to go to her office hour if taking this class just so she can recognize you.

This was the most tedious class as it is so lecture heavy and the tests were ridiculous. Nice person but very poor professor. Unorganized and repetitive.
LOVE THIS CLASS TAKE IT

reviews.comment: I wouldn't call this class an easy psych elective, but if you go to class, pay attention, and take notes you will really be fine! Only con is her slides can be quite disorganized.

The theories and concepts presented in the class often lack logical coherence. The grading of exams seems to be subjective. While she is a pleasant person, as an educator she is not supportive or helpful. Additionally, the practice tests look nothing like the actual exams, diminishing their usefulness as preparatory tools.

Do not take this class unless you have an interest in linguistics. Not a psych class, and sounds more interesting than it is. Go to one of her office hours at the beginning of the semester because it's nice for her to know you in such a big class. Classes can be really boring and feel long, so it's hard to pay attention. Don't buy the textbook.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She was genuinely one of the most unhelpful professors I have had at Northeastern. She is honestly sometimes just rude and even will just choose to not answer students' questions in class. Her study guides/practice tests are not helpful and she gave us our last exam on the last day of classes for the semester (not a final).

Don't understand the low rating, she's one of my favorite profs I've had at Northeastern. People are just complaining because the class is heavy on linguistics I guess? Just pay attention in class - the lectures are interesting, and if you stay present (for the admittedly long class block), you'll do well on the exams.

She knows a lot about the subject but I honestly really flopped in this class and I was trying...she's not a good lecturer. Don't take this class unless you have a genuine interest and maybe even background in linguistics- an interest in psych isn't enough

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you have an interest in linguistics or have taken a linguistics class in the past. She knows a lot about language but I struggled to learn

she's not horrible but she's not good. she moves so slowly and wastes time at the start of class doing a review of last class and repeats herself too much. her lectures are boring and not engaging. the course content could be so interesting but she presents it in the most boring way possible. she greatly exaggerates the difficulty of the tests
Interesting topic and very cool to be taught by a professor with experience in the field

Although this class can be hard, looking back it's been my favorite class at Northeastern. The topic is truly fascinating and you can tell Dr. Berent is passionate about the subject. She's an expert in the field, and though she doesn't talk about it, her own research is fascinating if you look it up! She's so kind and cares about her students.

I loved her class! She was definitely passionate about the material and wanted us all to succeed. Although the class can be slow at times, if you pay attention to the lectures and study, you will do fine on the tests.

The class was very easy, but also painfully slow. It made learning the information easy though - everything was very simple as she seems to think we are all dumb. The material was very interesting and the professor was clearly passionate and wanted everyone to understand the material.

Dr. Berent offers a very interesting course. Linguistics is a challenging subject and she did a great job of conveying the information in a more simplistic way. You must attend lectures! I would not recommend taking this course if you are not interested in the areas of linguistics or psychology. She is VERY open to receiving questions and feedback.

She is very intelligent, if you like to think and are creative this class if for you. She is difficult- but the class is very interesting and her class made me a stronger student. If you spend time with the material and put in effort you should be good- if you like to do minimal studying do not take this class. I think she was great.

the worst professor I've ever come across. She doesn't care about students and everyone saying she was good, I don't know if they were actually in her class. She doesn't care about you at all and she also has no idea how to teach. You won't learn a thing, don't waste your money.

reviews.comment: Trust me don't take her

I don't think this course should be a psychology course, it should be called "history of language". It is not related closely with Psychology! Also, the professor is awful, even the TA is better than her!!

This class covers complex topics and she does an excellent job making them more accessible. Paying attention and asking questions is crucial to understanding the material as her initial delivery of the information isn't always the best. She's done a lot of really interesting research in the field that was fascinating to learn about.

Challenging, interesting class. English is not her first language, but she most DEFINITELY is a fluent English speaker, and an intelligent one at that. Attendance is essential to understanding the material. She is clearly passionate about linguistics, and wants to help students understand the subject. Power points are clear cut and simple.
It is ironic that she teaches a language class without the ability to convey her materials clearly in a universal language. Power points are super messed up.....
Loved her

English skills are absolutely not good enough to each a class in English, let alone about complex ideas in the english language. Dr. Berent could improve her lecture skills, as she sped talks in her lectures. She often "taught to" the exams and as such, was unable to foster real learning. The course content drastically varied, and the grading was too test-oriented. Suggestion: a legit written component, instead of unhelpful BB homework, such as writing a paper.

She's really not as bad as people think. If you show up to class and pay attention you'll be fine. Her powerpoints are very descriptive, but you won't understand what's going on in them without actually going to class and listening. If you want to be lazy and not go to class, don't take this class. If you don't go, you'll be lost. Tests are easy.

Though the teacher wasn't really helpful...if you did assignments and studied the powerpoints, it's really not that bad at all. I did not find the class all that difficult, but I did most of the learning on my own
AWFUL AWFUL AWFUL!! Pointless class. You cannot understand her and when you ask for clarification she just repeats the same thing and keeps going. DO NOT TAKE IT!it will only hurt you

God awful teacher. Can't speak English, the book is very unhelpful, powerpoints are very vague and she doesn't explain concepts well.  You can't even look up concepts because the book is not really a textbook. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
No Comments
totally incomprehensible.  the material really shouldn't be this hard to understand, but she makes it impossible.  read the powerpoints online and hope for the best.

WORST CLASS AND TEACHER OF MY LIFE! do not take! she cannot speak english and is impossible to understand! the material is interesting however difficult to understand without clear explination, wich she does not give! she is not open is others opinions  favors those who fluently speak a second language. only class i have ever had to take pass fail!
The most lovely lady you will ever meet!! Truly lives up to her name because she absolutely lit up the room with every lecture

THE BEST PROFESSOR. Went into this class not sure if I'd like it but I LOVED IT. She is so kind, so passionate and makes the class enjoyable for everyone. She is so kind and will answer any question you have. Also love how passionate she is about dogs. Also love our group work at the end of class (ungraded) it really reinforces the concepts :)

She is very passionate about the topic and great at answering questions. All quizzes and tests are remote. Class prepares you well for them and is interesting. Sometimes the class does not feel necessary to go to but it is enjoyable. Readings are easy and helpful.

Such a great professor who clearly has a passion for psychology. She uses a lot of her past experiences as an animal trainer to explain concepts in class to make it easier to understand. While attendance isn't mandatory, her lectures are extremely insightful and entertaining.

You can tell she is super knowledgable about what she's talking about. Lectures are heavy but interesting, she shows a lot of videos to get tangible examples of what's happening. Tests were online and take home, and overall I did well on them. Just look over your notes and stay engaged. She always ends on the dot, and has lots of group projects.

I really like Prof Bright as a person, but I found her class to be a bit boring at times. There were 6 quizzes for the class, excluding the midterm and final. All were MC and if you pay attention in class, there should be no problem. No extra credit opportunities, but she drops the lowest grade and averages the rest, which I found very nice.

I didn't find the class material interesting but it was very manageable. Terri really loves the material. There were group projects (ungraded) at the end of every class to help you understand the material.

Dr. Bright is a great prof who cares a lot about the subject. The entire grade for this class is based on quizzes and the final. However, as long as you show up and understand the material, it's straightforward (she also drops the lowest quiz grade). Dr. Bright is AMAZING. She cares so much about the topic of ABA and behavior in general. Her lectures are always interesting and she cares if her students understand the topics. She is not very accessible outside of class because she has another job, but always emails back right away and even gives her cell number. Take a class with her if you can!

Dr. Bright is a great teacher. There is assigned reading that is reasonable in length, and no graded homework. The quizzes are straightforward and if you pay attention and read you'll do fine. Great lecturer, always ends class a bit early. The textbook is very clear and useful.
Dr. Bright has been my favorite professor so far at Northeastern. Super straight forward about everything and inspirational in the work she does.

Loved Terri; one of my favorite professors so far at NEU. Didn't run out the room right when class ended - waited to help students with questions or concerns. She always called on a student if their hand was up. WONDERFUL faculty member and mentor. Her work with dogs is inspirational. Excellent professor! 80% quizzes & 20% final  straight forward.

Very passionate about her subject. She is not a bad professor, but sometimes has test questions that are very ambiguous and can have many answers. Prof. Wilson's exams (especially the final) are fair, however she is very picky with grading and even if you get the correct answer if you don't have the work that she wants, you don't get credit. do not take her. you will hate your life. she does not care about her students one bit, but once something happens to her she will drop everything to take care of her business. switch or drop before you have the worst semester of your life

Professor Wilson writes and talks as fast as she can during the lectures, and she doesn't care if her students understand. Dr. Wilson is the best professor I have ever had. I feared calc II prior to taking Dr. Wilson, but her expressions of concepts and her examples for every unit are incredibly clear. Calc II has been my favorite course so far because of Dr. Wilson, would take the course 1 million times over again.

She tends to move quickly in lecture, but it is a very fast pace class in nature. It is sometimes hard to get individual help, as she tends to only explain things one way and has very busy office hours which can sometimes turn into another lecture. Very average.

She will give you plenty of resources to study and is readily available to help students that are confused. Keeping up in class can be difficult as she writes and talks very fast. Overall she's a good teacher but if you have trouble initially grasping concepts make sure to utilize the past recorded lectures and other resources or you'll fall behind

Honestly, while I wasn't fan of professor Wilson at the start of the semester she is actually a pretty decent teacher. The class is work heavy, homework each week and a quiz, but if you work hard and, most importantly, stay on top of the content, you'll do fine! She's also very patient and it was a nice classroom environment

Professor Wilson is someone who keeps up to schedule and updates her students throughout the semester. Examples are up in advanced to keep up with the lectures and the quizzes and exams are pretty straightforward. The only issue is if you're someone who needs to reach out to your professors, that may be the only drawback, otherwise she's great.

Her teaching style is writing the theories on the board then showing different examples. I found it helpful to come prepared with questions on the homework/reviews. She's not very accommodating with quiz remakes and your final grade is largely made up of quizzes/ exams. Attendance isn't mandatory and she has her past lessons posted on youtube.

Professor Wilson is good at math but not a great teacher. However she gives extra points on quizzes if you go up and do homework problems on the board which ended up being the reason I got an A in the class. If you struggle with math, don't take her. If you tend to teach yourself anyway, Professor Wilson is a good professor for that.

Professor Wilson knows what she is doing, but sometimes is difficult to understand. However, if you take notes during class and do the weekly homeworks which are not that long, then her tests and quizzes are easy. The questions are exactly the same concepts in the homeworks, just switched a bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wilson is a decent calc professor. Lectures are fast, but she always lets you ask questions. Come to class w hw done so you can get extra credit on quizzes by doing a problem on the board. Very fair - drops lowest two quizzes (weekly quizzes) and hw can be turned in late for full credit. If you need to contact her, she never answers emails on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I was kinda surprised by the negative reviews here. I think prof Wilson is such a good teacher. I wish I had her for Calc 1. She is a tough grader but offers extra credit, and I am never surprised by what is on a quiz or test. She is very routine about lectures and answers questions very well without being condescending. I love her teaching style!

Attendance is not mandatory but if you answer questions on the board you can get extra credit on the quizzes that happen each week. Hard to reach outside of class besides office hours. Can be overwhelming and doesn't speak in a way that is easy to understand.

Prof. Wilson likes to give weekly quizzes and nightly homework. Pros: extra credit and hw grade is for completion. Cons: she regurgitates the textbook, can't explain topics well, tests are 80% of your grade, and if you want to meet with her to go over examples, better be lucky enough with your schedule to attend office hours. She is not flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Wilson gives quizzes every week, usually not that challenging, but the class is mostly graded on the midterms and final. Gives opportunity to get extra credit on quizzes and drops the two lowest quiz grades. Homework is assigned every class, but she gives the whole semester to turn it in full credit. DON'T BUY THE BOOKS. Overall good teacher.

Wilson is a really good teacher, which isn't something I can say about all my professors at Northeastern. She is excellent at explaining things and shows plenty of practice exams to study from. Know that the quizzes make up a chunk of your grade, and you have to stay up with the homework for those. 10/10

I'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews on Dr. Wilson. I had her for Math Fundamentals of Games and she was honestly the best. Her style of teaching makes it a lot easier to grasp topics in linear algebra, as well as put them into practice. She responds very quickly to emails and always values her students' opinions on deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have taken her class multiple times and you will get a good grade if you pay attention. She reviews all the homework and is very accessible. It's not a class where if you don't listen you can get an A but in all honesty just like paying attention and doing the bare minimum will get you an A.
Easy class, good professor who is clear and has reasonable but simple expectations. Good class, if not a bore.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson is a good math teacher. She teaches clearly and effectively and answers all students' questions as they come. She can be quiet at times, but that isn't too much of a problem. There is a quiz every week and the final is 40% of the final grade. Overall, good teacher, good class -- nothing amazing and nothing horrible.

Either she's improved a lot or the other reviews aren't as accurate. I found Dr. Wilson's lectures to be well organized and she is very approachable and friendly during office hours. Homework packets were given out each week which was very convenient and very reflective of tests. Overall, one of the best math professors I've had at northeastern
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her explanations are not very clear and keeps beating around the bush, which exhibit her lack of proper knowledge of the subject she's teachings. All she does is write on the board from the notes that she carries. Very rarely answers question of students properly. Students generally depend on learning from the text book. Very confusing lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved math until meeting Dr. Wilson. She reads directly from the textbook and can't teach or explain anything if she isn't directly reading from the book. The final is 40% of your grade and is way harder than any of the HW and classwork. I don't know anyone who got above a B in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: All class every class, she she lectures and barely stops writing on the board. When a student asks a question that deviates the slightest amount from her notes she's unable to answer the question. The lectures are boring, dry, and don't engage the students. Would have switched out but this was the only class that fit in my schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: While Wilson is a nice person, she is incredibly poor as a professor. Her lectures are super unorganized and she doesn't seem to know the material well evident by her answering questions with "I'm not sure," or "that's just the way it is." Quizzes and tests are based off of practices ones so memorizing those can help, but not to learn material.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Has refreshingly high expectations of students, solid professor, moves very fast in lectures so make sure you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you like dealing with unnecessary pain and suffering, then by all means take MATH 1260 with Prof. Wilson. She is super unhelpful, dry in personality, and sets you up for failure. Her lectures are all over the place, and the online class notes that she provides do a way better job of teaching than she does. STAY AWAY! I REPEAT, STAY AWAY!
The tests are exactly the study guides she gives out. Study and memorize it and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You ever read one of those books where a bunch of kids get stranded in the woods and have to fend for themselves, slowly becoming savages until they've lost all humanity? That's MATH 1342. You will be offered no guidance, leave every lecture feeling more confused than the last, slowly losing all hope and humanity until you eventually just give in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She cares so much about the success of each student. Classes could feel slow but overall she is so sweet and takes the time to make sure every student has their needs met. Lots of assignments that I think were repetitive but were not super hard.

She cares about each student and genuinely wants them to learn and develop. Just make quizlets for the tests and pick a good group at the beginning. The group assignments get really. really. annoying and redundant so beware. Still, I would take this class shes so sweet. Madoff HW was really annoying too
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Banalieva is one of the best professors I've had. Somewhat of a tough grader for presentations/debates; gives a lot of partial credit on exams and you learn SO much. One midterm and one final (non-cumulative.) You get what you put in so don't half ahh your way thru bc it'll show. There's also like no hw. Def take her class if you can!

Super sweet lady and is clearly passionate in intb. VERY group-project heavy but not bad if you get a good group-you pick your groups day1 and are with them til the end. Participation matters A LOT. There's only like 2 tests and they're pretty easy. Also she assigns every assignment at the beginning of the semester so get ahead of things!

One strength about Professor Banalieva is the way she taught classes. She encouraged class discussions on reading materials or to challenge and expand classmates' arguments. This created an inclusive learning environment. If you have to take INTB1203, take her, she's is probably the best INTB1203 professor here.
Grading is a bit weird she grades some things easy and other things harshly. Exams were pretty easy, a lot of your grade is dependent on your group. Overall decent class shes nice.

This was a very hard class and she is a very tough grader but she is very kind and wants to help you. The exams weren't that bad, as long as you studied what was on the rubric. One group project whole semester, and you get to choose your partners. She is a stickler to formatting and will take off points if you forget page numbers.

Phenomenal professor who genuinely cares and wants to see you put in effort to get a good result. Participation matters and she respects if you put in effort in that way. Choose a good group... will be essential for how easy/difficult this class is (besides exams). She is very qualified and passionate about her work. Strongly recommend. Loved it.
loves her job and is knowledgeable, i would say pick ur groups wisely because group projects are worth over 40% and be ready to put in the effort

She gets confused by technology a lot, which is annoying. She is very harsh with her participation grading. She's not the worst professor ever, but it's just very boring, she isn't very helpful, and she gives a ton of group projects with unclear instructions.

Basically all group projects, so choose your group wisely. Students pick the format of the exams. The questions are based off of her lectures not the textbook, so go to class. While I loved her as a Professor the amount of work felt like she thought we were only taking her course. If it says to start something early on the syllabus start it early!

Incredible professor -  my favorite class I've taken so far. It does involve a lot of work, specifically group projects,  but as long as you take it seriously you will do well. Don't bother reading the textbook and make sure to participate!!! Also, the test are basically just about lectures so make sure to go.

Pick your groups wisely because there will be a lot of group activities and projects. Follow the syllabus and you will be fine. Two exams for the whole semester where the class decides on the format and questions to the exams. 4 online "quizzes" but they're just 2 multiple choice questions each. Very fair professor with a lot of hands on activities

She is a decent teacher and knows what she is talking about. There are 2 tests but some test content is not discussed in class. Your grade is also highly dependent on group projects so choose members wisely because you'll also be working with them for the whole semester. I would say this is a B+/A- class if you actually try.

She was a great professor and really nice. Interesting class but be prepared for lots of group work. She does grade tough on certain assignments but at the end slightly curves grades. A- is very attainable if you put in the work you can pull away with an A. Overall would highly recommend Professor Banalieva.

It was honestly a very fun class. I learnt so much. I have almost completed 2 sems and INTB has been my fav. It was a bit of work but fun work, interactive work, where we learnt. We had class structured debates and presentations. So so fun. I would love to take the class again. She really did not like me, regardless I loved the class.

not too hard but it's a waste of time if you're trying to learn something usefull. The study guides and exams contain a lot of material that is not covered during the lectures. She will harm your participation grade if she doesn't agree with your opinons, and spends a lot of time doing discussions about content with little to no value.

Great professor with engaging lessons and class activities that make you think. A lot of the grades rely on group projects so make sure you choose members wisely. She clearly lays out the requirements and grading rubrics for assignments and gives good feedback so they are relatively straightforward and even enjoyable.
Lot of work but its fun
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: She did an awesome job delivering the class materials to students. Very engaging lectures! If you want to do well in this class, make sure you participate in class discussions. She introduced so many perspectives for students to debate and discuss. I heard great things abt other INTB professors but prof. Banalieva is definitely a solid choice

She can be unreasonable. She took my midterm away when I hadn't finished for asking a question (after she answered it). She is not nice if you don't agree with her opinions. Exams are straightforward, it's easy to do well if you go over the study guides. Participation grade is worth a lot , and grading is subjective since it's not a small class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. B has really good in person lectures that require participation. She grades tough, so be prepared to answer every question during presentations. Read the book, it helps. DIscussion boards used when we went online, so my grade improved. 2 Tests & no final, but lots of projects! Overall, a good class! She wants you to succeed and really cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: THE most enjoyable class I took last semester. A lot of class discussion and many people offering their opinions. Not a difficult class content wise, but there are many projects and papers. Make sure you choose a smart group, because your grade will be heavily dependent on their work. Participation matters but still possible to get full points.
The tests are really easy if you look at the study guide she provides. Class discussion was probably the best among all my classes as everyone gets involved.

Amazing professor, in fact my favorite professor I took last semester. We have 2 tests, no final, 1 group debate( very interesting topics ), and 1 group project. Professor Banalieva allows her class to be an interactive lecture and is more than open to others opinions. SHE IS A MUST TAKE FOR THIS COURSE!

Participation is important in  her class, and she can be a VERY tough grader on papers and presentation. However,Professor Banalieva is definitely a passionate and caring teacher, and she definitely knows the material. The slides and her lectures are very engaging, which makes the class fun. Exams are not too bad. I would recommend.

Professor Banalieva's class is not an easy A by any means, however, if you want a challenging class where you will learn a lot take this class. Her grading for writing is difficult and her exams are very fair. She wants you to learn and do well in her class. Her lectures are very enthusiatic and informative. There are also two large group projects.

Professor Banalieva was really great. If you put in the work, go to class, participate, and are actively willing to do well, you will succeed. There are a few big projects and papers, but expectations are very clearly laid out in the syllabus from Day 1. She genuinely cares about students. If you want to learn a lot, definitely take this class!

She's a very tough grader and refuses to give people A's even when she admits that their work is outstanding. Avoid taking her at all costs if you want to do well because she gives people low grades for participation (worth 150 points) even if they've shown up to class everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst professor in my entire college experience. Avoid if you can

Sweetest person I've ever met. Loved her; absolutely hated her class. There were 3 separate group projects for the one class and they were graded so harshly.  Only two exams, no cumulative final.  The exams are not in synch with the review guide she provides.  The workload was crazy, I felt like I had to choose between this class and my others.
Dont take her if you dont want to suffer!!!!
Worst experience of my life!! Avoid her

Banalieva's class was probably the worst experience of my life. She thinks that INTB is your only course and assigns an insane amount of work. She seems so sweet, but in reality she'll take off points on your assignments for no specified  reason. Also she rounds down, if you have a 94.9 she rounds down to an A-. Pretty sure an A is impossible.

She is a hard grader and deduct huge points(30 out of 100) for not handing in unrelevant things like peer evaluation. Also make unrealistic and vague requirements for papers. Loads of work and need to be avoided!!!

Banalieva is a very good instructor, she was enthusiastic about the topic's she taught, and her class discussion not only made class interesting, but I really learnt a lot. I have to admit that this course was challenging, and that at times you do have to fight hard for a good grade, but I did learn a lot at the end of the day. Definitely recommend
Alot of reading, most of it optional but sometimes gives pop quizzes that aren't very hard. Pretty interesting class but she expects alot of participation.
i wish i can write something nice about her, why she still

The prof is a nice person, very respectful. But the class is tough. Too many reading, writings, projects. I feel like I am majoring in IB in this semester, doing IB things everyday. Her lectures are interesting, but participation is mandatory. Grading in writing is also harsh... Avoid her if you're not ready for tons of readings and writings.

Great class if you are motivated and willing to put effort. In addition, we learn to think analytically and gain first experience in collaborating with other. Not a class for those who are seeking an easy way out.

There is a lot of work, and you spend a lot of time outside of class, but she is very fair.  I learned a great deal from this professor, and really enjoyed the class. Participation is a must, and reading is a must.  If you are looking to coast, this isn't the class, but it is a beneficial class!  She is an excellent professor.
Interesting class and nice teacher. She is passionate about the subject and wants student to succeed. Quite a lot of reading, fair tests and project. Do not hesitate to take her!
Very nice and professional. Has a passion for the subject. Would recommend.
She is amazing! Fun, caring and resourceful teacher that makes everything easy. However, she does have a HUGE preference for foreigners.

Banalieva is amazing! I thoroughly enjoyed her class; she's knowledgeable, engaging, and helpful. The class is a fair amount of work, but the projects and debates are enjoyable. Participate and read the class pack.
Good teacher overall. Does have a significant amount preference towards foreigners, ESPECIALLY Frech students. If you are French, she will love you.
Amazing teacher. Very nice, professional, and willing to help. Encourages questions, and is not afraid to explain her point of view unlike some professors who get angry for questioning them.

Highly recommend this teacher for anyone wanting to take international business. She is extremely nice, always available to meet with you, and clear on telling you what she expects in work. Have 2 Tests the entire semester, 2 news article write ups, and a major IB project. Must show up to class, participate. Do this and ur guaranteed a good grade.

The best professor ever. She will always help and encourage you. You will learn a lot from her, not just about International Business, but also about life. Attend every class, it is an enjoyable class. Don't be afraid to participate, just say what is in your mind. She will not embarrass you even if you have a stupid comment. Take her for INBU203!

Very knowledable, helpful, and sweet professor. She really knows her stuff. When we went over the syllabus on the first day of class, I was overwhelmed. This class is a lot of work but I learned A LOT. This has been one of my favorite classes because you learn a lot and it's a fun class. TAKE HER!
A LOT of work but fun teacher

Majority of grade is based off of participation, attendance, and in class excercises that are guaranteed 100's. I did not like this because I never went to class. However, if you aren't intelligent and would like to be graded more on coming to class, definately the one to take. Final project and hw counts for almost nothing.

Extremely straightforward professor who makes her expectations really clear.  Showing up to class guarantees you at least a B on exams ... EVERY SINGLE QUESTION on her tests has been discussed in-class.

random inclass exercises, only three written homework assignments, exams are 160 points 4pts per question, know slides for exams, CLASS PARTICIPATION IS IMPORTANT so if you're not into joining in on discussions (which is pretty much the whole class) then maybe you should stay away from this class.

If you don't know anything about international business policies and organizations then you better be ready to study extremely hard! Participation is a MUSTT and she's a really hard grader.  If you don't understand something it's really hard to catch up.  There are a lot of random graded exercises, and the exams are all multiple choice, 4 pts each.

Good professor, very clear about what she wants. Tests are multiple choice, very easy if you stay on top of the readings. Has very little tolerance for students that come to class unprepared (ie not doing the homework / reading). Very engaging during lectures and tries to make the class interesting. Good overall.

I feel bad leaving this review bc Prof Blake is such a nice guy, but this class was odd. While the material was cool, I felt like class time was not used effectively. He spoke really fast and class felt like I was watching it through somebody else's eyes. The amount of homework was also wild, even as someone who enjoys writing. Fair grader tho.

Just a pleasant and caring person who clearly has a passion for what he teaches. Most of the class time was spent watching movies, which is fun. If you like writing, this class is thoughtful, interesting, and a great elective overall. But be warned, there is a hell of a lot of writing. A great professor that I'd recommend to film and writing lovers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is incredibly demanding. I took his Film 101 class this semester, and it was packed with work. We had daily discussion board posts of at least 350 words, weekly screen notes for films, and six quizzes, each accompanied by an essay. On top of that, both the midterm and final included not only exams but also large papers to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you come to class and try and participate you will succeed in his class. He makes the class environment very welcoming and if you get sick or anything he is the most understanding of your situation. He wants the best for his students and obviously loves what he is teaching. One of the best professors I have had at Northeastern.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really like professor Blake. He is a really good person!

He's gives excellent feedback on papers and open responses. His Film 101 lectures are pact full of all the information you'll need for quizzes/midterms. All necessary knowledge is within his lecture notes. His grading rubric allows you to achieve an A relatively easy as long as you complete all the assignments with reasonably good effort.

This was one of my favorite classes by far, Professor Blake is enthusiastic and knowledgable about film, he teaches because he wants to share his passion. Speeding up the movies can make the workload lighter. He is an easy grader, if you put in visible effort you get an A. Engage with the content and the work is easy, only takes 1-2 hours a week.

Professor Blake is a great teacher and knowledgeable about almost every film. There is a significant issue with the criteria of this class. This class requires you to watch over 30 movies in which you will write specific screening notes. I absolutely love movies but honestly, this class has temporarily ruined movies for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
*MSCR 2895 REVIEW*
Professor Blake is extremely passionate and knowledgeable.  As someone who took this credit purely out of interest, he made the class far more than what it was on the surface.  There's a lot of reading and writing assignments are pretty detailed, but he is a fair grader and is transparent about what he's looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Blake is a nice guy. Even though this class is honestly a lot of work because you have to keep up with the readings and watch all the films, he makes it interesting. He goes a fast in lecture but he posts everything online so you don't really need to go to class. The quizzes and exams are online which is nice and there are only 2 papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got turned off of the class quickly due to how much work was required outside of class time. I spent more time working on this class more than my actual required classes for my major. It just felt a bit unnecessary. To his credit, the tests and quizzes were online, so it was fairly easy to get good grades on them, though they are timed.

Nathan is caring, passionate, knowledgable and attentive! This class is asynchronous this semester which can be hard at times but he is devoted to making it as easy to manage as possible. The course is still well thought out and grading is clear and easy to understand. He really cares about students thoughts on films and gives insightful feedback.

Really thoughtful and kind professor. Genuinely super passionate about what he teaches and it is sad that not many people participate in class over zoom as much as they should. Great guy, it's a difficult class in terms of concepts but he makes it accessible.

Nathan outlines exactly what he wants, with very clear percentages. He tells you exactly what you need to do to get an A, and if you are engaged in class he will bump you up to the next letter grade if you're on the cusp.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Courseload is heavy but tolerable. He is very nice, saved my grade. Replies fast and very helpful and caring. He'll help you learn a lot about film.
Such a nice guy. Honestly my grade saver.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading for the midterm and quizzes, but the class is well balanced with a great selection of films. Professor Blake is very nice and caring who cares about his students and is always accessible outside of class. The class is mostly lectures which can get boring.

Professor Blake is incredibly intelligent and kind to students. I love our conversations in class and he makes some abstract film theories very accessible, which everyone appreciates. I'd love to take another one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Nathan is a great professor. He's very patient and he treats everyone's work seriously. He gives a lot of feedback in details. He replies email very fast. Overall, if you really want to learn about film, he is a great choice. Workload is kind of heavy so it depends on your choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot from this course, but I don't recommend co-op student to take this course because there are just so many readings, lecture recordings and movie clips each week. And you won't get a good grade if you skip any of these. Not an easy A- class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Gave good feedback. Great in-class discussions. No 2 classes were the same. Students helped each other w/possible sources for their individual research projects. Classroom felt like a community. Didn't always understand students' perspectives. Banned computers by saying that he would look things up on his computer,  but never did.

Prof. O'Connell was a good professor, but stacked cornerstone is a tough class and extremely time consuming. Tons of homework and be prepared to spend at least 15 hrs/week on your group projects on top of the hw. He has good lectures and if you reach out to him he is usually very helpful. sometimes grading criteria can be a bit vague, but not bad.

He'd grade things two weeks after we submit, making us repeat mistakes through our projects. His deadlines: unreasonable/impossible. I know this is a hard class but the workload was absurd. I'd get no sleep during the week and sometimes wouldn't have time to eat. His instructions: extremely vague with harsh grading. He's on some kind of power trip.

First day: "You will have at least 2 hrs of HW for every hr of class." You have ~6.5 hrs of class a week. That's not counting the 15+ hrs per week on group projects. And the 150+ page report due DURING finals week. Nice and passionate professor, always available, HARD class. This class is disproportionately harder than other cornerstone sections.
I am unsure as to why there are so many negative ratings. Professor O'Connell is very nice, and his class is engaging. It can be a lot of work, so make sure to stay on top of things.

Avoid this class unless you have nothing else going on. Mandatory volunteering plus 3+ assignments most nights, each taking 1–2 hours with tedious steps. Grading is harsh, the late policy is unforgiving, and getting a response outside class is nearly impossible. If you can get out of stacked cornerstone DO IT AT ALL COSTS
He chill and shi

Stacked cornerstone is a weed out class. I often had 40+ hrs of hw a week, group projects were very intense and grading was harsh. He's a very nice guy but has very high expectations in an INTENSE class. You will be LIVING in fyelic if you don't have a foundation of coding before this course. This class will erase your social life. Good luck.

O'Connell is a passionate, good professor. He is open to helping students at a moments notice almost 24/7 through teams, and is focused on leaving students with a solid understanding of the course curriculum, which is very important given the nature of the course. Put in some effort, don't expect to have your hand held and you will do great.

O'Connell's great. Available, gives good feedback, answers questions promptly. However, stacked cornerstone is so miserable that I wouldn't recommend anybody take it. The flipped classroom method means half the lectures are useless. The group project is frustrating. Do not take 1501+1502 if you have other difficult classes running concurrently.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His directions for group projects often is contradictory. The rubrics were different than the guide and it ended with us at one point getting a 65 on part of a project. With weekly assignments, I felt more self taught when it came to graphics and coding as the learning style was reversed and he would just show a presentation. He is online for help.

The overall class isn't that difficult, but taking stacked cornerstone is so much work, like 30+ hours a week. O'Connell is a pretty decent professor and responded to my questions and messages within a couple hours. I felt that the lectures did not connect with the homework. I would not recommend stacking cornerstone unless absolutely necessary.

classes were completely a waste of time, as we were assigned to learn the same thing online before class.

he definitely is a fan of what he teaches, and that much is apparent, whether you agree with his teaching methods or not

The instructor did a good job explaining new software/coding languages. While there's some criticism about the difficulty of the course, you are in class to learn, and O'Connell provides an amazing environment to learn in.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is willing to work through things with students when they need help and is very accessible during the projects. He is fair in that if you communicate to him, he is understanding, and if you do not communicate with him, he will not be as lenient.

Professor O'Connell is always available for help, whether in person or on Teams. His assignments are challenging, but he is fair with grading. If you communicate well with him, he is understanding with work/deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He does not deserve the bad ratings! Really nice professor, answers every question, and is more than willing to help you. Also, he responds on teams almost instantly. Compared to the other stacked cornerstone class, he was a much more relaxed professor, and even gave us a lot of extensions on assignments. PRO TIP: GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS!!

Of course its a hard class, it is your first engineering class. Go to lectures. Do the in class portions, in the class. He teaches and grades strict because that is what engineering is like in the real world.

O'Connell is super accessible outside of class. Anytime you're struggling with homework or anything at all just message him on Teams and he will respond right away. Not a good Professor

Super chill and nice guy, had him for full cornerstone so he definitely worked us pretty hard but it was nothing I couldn't handle.

I do not recommend taking a class taught by him online. His slides and method of teaching is very choppy and does not make sense most of the time. Course should be taught online

O'Connell consistently gives more work and grades harder than other Cornerstone professors. However, he is also a better teacher and all around great guy. If you're willing to work for the grade, you will learn a lot from him.

Prof Zullo overall is a good teacher and he knows the information well and is good at explaining it. The no laptop policy during lecture, Ipad is fine as long as it is flat. reviews.comment:
Will he teach you tax? Yes. Does that mean he should be a professor? No.

Very good professor who values getting work in on time. If you can't adhere to schedule and submit assignments when you are asked to, don't take his class. If you are ready to learn, his class is for you.

Just a bad guy overall. He's there to make fun of students and give them a hard time with grades. Northeastern please address this issue!

Professor Zullo gets a bad rep because he has high expectations, but if you show up to class and put in the effort to understand the course concepts then you will definitely meet them. honestly a really good prof. if you pay attention and actually try to learn, you will do so and do well in his class. couldn't recommend more

Prof Zullo is hands down one of the best professors ever. He is funny and kind and cares deeply about every one of his students. Super nice guy. As long as you show-up to class and participate it's not too bad. Homework assignments aren't bad at all (just a few connect problems each week). Professor Zullo is so kind and funny which makes the class great. He does take forever to grade assignments but other then that, I recommend this class!

Prof Zullo is a great teacher who cares about his students. Glad I didn't listen to the other reviews and took his class. Wasn't as bad as I expected honestly. If you're one of those students that just slacks off and complains when you perform badly, well you should've expected that. Put in the work, and youre gold.

He is a tough grader and has the driest lectures where he talks at you for an hour and expects the entire class to participate, then the class average on each test is a B- and he refuses to curve or adjust any grades, honestly any other professor would be better. he's an accountant who obviously doesn't understand the impact of low grades
DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS

Super surprised at how much I liked Zullo! He gets that tax is tough and he makes sure to go over concepts thoroughly and invites questions. I didn't think he was a tough grader, I'd say average. I'm so glad I didn't listen to the negative reviews on here. I absolutely LOVED Prof. Zullo! He made some hilarious dad jokes throughout his zoom lectures, and made sure that everyone participated. I made the mistake of reading the harsh reviews on here before taking the course & was so worried but they couldnt have been more wrong. Took this over the summer and it was the biggest regret of my academic career. Zullo would rush through a chapter a day, skipping through slides for the sake of saying that we "covered the material." EXAMS ARE SO HARD. He said certain things would be on the exam but the opposite were. Even if you completely understand a topic the exams will make you feel dumb. This professor does not even curve the exams for some reason. Please professor if you are reading this take it into consideration.

RUNAWAY!! TESTS ARE SO HARD AND UNCLEAR. BIGGEST MISTAKE was taking a class with him! Take with someone else, he's so hard and his midterm and finals are unnecessarily difficult. Worst. Take another prof, you'll thank me later!

worst professor EVER!!! he didnt reply to my emails, and when I went to his office hours he was rude and unwilling to help!

reviews.comment: Ron is a terrific guy. Always makes class enjoyable. Grading can be a bit tough but the material is relatively easy and the pacing is extremely manageable
Zullo is a good teacher and makes managerial easy. Pay attention in class and you will do fine on tests. Case studies are a bit more difficult but aren't graded harshly.

Professor Zullo is my favorite professor I've ever had. You definitely have to put a lot of work into this class to do well, but he makes lectures interesting and enjoyable and he's a great guy. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

Prof.Zullo is a great teacher but a hard grader! His classes are not easy but because he teaches the material so well,   I recommend him highly!

Prof. Zullo is an amazing teacher. He made the class enjoyable for me. His class isn't easy, but if you do the work you'll be fine. Zullo is very fair with his grading and reasonable with his expectations. He will push you, but at the end of the day you will learn something.

Good class but not easy. You have to study for every class, material is not easy. Read slides before class, do all your homework and study for tests, I would say its an easy C+ B- if you are willing to study you should get a B

Professor Zullo is awesome. Although this class is difficult, he truly does everything he can to make his students succeed. He does plenty of examples in class and always asks for questions. He is very fair and will tell you exactly what concepts are covered on tests and exams. He is often available for extra help and makes the class very engaging.

Professor Zullo is really great!  He does take attendance so you should show up, but it's honestly fine to miss a few days, he doesn't care that much.  The quizzes and midterms are fair, not hard but you do have to study to do well.  The online homework isn't too bad.  He is a really funny guy and is always willing to help out!

I absolutely love Professor Zullo! He's a great teacher and also has a great sense of humor.
