Definitely one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. Awesome!
Very unhelpful professor. Would not recommend him to anyone
Great professor and just an overall cool guy.  Classes arent that boring for accounting.  Not super easy but not hard by any means.  He is really helpful especially during office hours.

One of my favorite professors so far at northeastern. the class is not super easy, but Zullo definitely cares about his students and wants them to do well. If you read and pay attention in class youll do fine. He also loves when you ask questions and go to office hours. I would recommend him!

Professor Lancaster is a great professor. He explains concepts clearly and makes the material easy to follow. His lectures are organized, and you can tell he really knows the subject well. He is also very approachable and willing to help if you have questions.

Professor Lancaster is a great professor! He explains concepts clearly and makes the material easy to follow. His lectures are well-organized, and it's clear that he has a deep understanding of the subject. He's also very approachable and willing to help if you have questions. The workload is fair and definitely manageable.

Wow, Professor Lancaster is truly one of the best teachers I've had during my time at Northeastern. His passion for his work evidently shines through in every lesson he teaches. One of the highlights of his class was the guest lecturers he brought in — industry professionals from all aspects of the entertainment industry. Incredible!

Professor Lancaster took 5 points off of our groups final grade after one of our group members submitted an assignment incorrectly. He only allows assignments to be submitted by email and your grade is based on your group project and attendance. He makes public emails about other groups projects being sloppy or not what he wants.
Bill is very passionate about his classes. Very accommodating and the class is not too difficult. 4 quizzes, attendance, and one paper. If you are sentient you will receive an A.

A class that truly prepares you for the real world industry— very involved and has you create a great final product for the portfolio. Content was highly informative and well curated to the audience and his care for student success shines. Highly recommend!

Very enlightening class— the guests are incredible and Bill has great real world connections that prove invaluable to your learning. Tough grader and highly specific on what he wants, but that's representative of entertainment as a whole so very prepatory. Learned so much from his class and was one of my favorites of the entire semester.

The guest lectures are a standout, they're always incredibly engaging and highly relevant to the course material. It's clear that a lot of thought goes into making the lectures both informative and applicable. I learned so much and felt connected to real-world examples. Highly recommend taking his class!

Prof. Lancaster is a great professor! He brings in guest lecturers who are always happy to chat with students and share what their careers are like. There are multiple group projects in this class but each one was unique and an awesome opportunity to be creative and make projects that are really interesting. Overall a great class. Highly recommend!

Idk why people are glazing this professor so hard. I'm not even done with the course yet but I'm so livid right now I had to come on here and do a rating. Oh brother, this guy stinks! Actually worst prof I've ever had. He has a NO LATE WORK policy. Gives no extensions. Terrible about attendance. This class is not worth it!

Professor Lancaster's class was by far the most relevant class I took as a COMM/MSCR major. The quizzes are challenging and you have to memorize little details from class materials. Prof. Lancaster is one of the kindest and most knowledgeable teachers I've had during my time at Northeastern. With tons of industry experience and personal anecdotes, he embeds plenty of real world examples in the concepts behind the business of entertainment. He genuinely cares about your individual creativity and fosters such a fun environment.

I highly recommend Professor Lancaster's class. He's a passionate and hilarious teacher who is excited to share his vast knowledge of the entertainment industry with his students. This class is great for any student interested in the film/TV industry, regardless of their course of study. As an MSCR major, I found the course to be very rewarding.

Professor Lancaster is good! This class consisted of writing a screen play in groups (worth 55%), participation (20%), and quizzes (25%). The quizzes are difficult as they come from past student work, 1+ hour videos, and readings. Additionally, the feedback provided can be confusing, but is helpful. I took this course to fulfill the EI requirement.

Professor Lancaster is a great teacher. He brings his life passion to this lecture-based class, and curates an incredible experience for those passionate about the media industry. He cares about his students professional endeavors + brings in many guest speakers! The class centers on a large group project, take it seriously and don't wait till end.

Bill wants the best for his students and really wants them to grow an interest and appreciation for the industry. He is very kind and will always be open to talking with you. The class is certainly challenging as tests cover small details and the course is centered around a large, involved group project; however, in the end it is very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Lancaster was great! I'm not majoring in communication or entertainment but his lectures and the interviews we watched in class were inspirational and actually interesting. Attendance is mandatory and the 4 quizzes and one essay essentially make up your entire grade but the class itself was great.

Prof Lancaster curated a welcoming class environment. I learned a lot about the entertainment industry from both him and my peers. However, his deadlines sneak up with little warning beforehand. His quizzes are created from vague facts from the readings. Be prepared to read the readings and spend a lot more time than necessary on a comm elective.

Great final project, engages with students, encourages discussions. Only issue for me was his quizzes asked what I thought were insignificant memory questions. Very understanding when I had a few deaths and needed an extension. Very kind, funny man. Shares his professional experience, asks about your pro experience.

I took Professor Lancaster's class and learned a lot about the in's and out's of the entertainment business. He also goes out of his way on bringing professional experience to class, would definitely take one of his classes again!

Prof Lancaster is an amazing professor His lectures are very interesting with lots of discussion. He always wants to know your opinion and likes class participation. There are no textbook or exam. Readings are easy. Projects are creative and fairly straightforward. I'd definitely take his class again. It was fun and I learned a lot about producing.

Bill Lancaster has a ton of practical experience as a producer in film and television. That kind of knowledge is invaluable in a professor, especially if you want to go into the industry. Bill will introduce you to some really cool players in the industry as guest lecturers or video. His lectures are succint and relevant. Great course projects.

Very fun projects in this class, the final one being a very satisfying culmination of what you'll learn. Bill is great to talk with inside and outside the classroom. He likes to offer extra credit opportunities in the form of helping him out with video shoots, like interviews and panels, which are great ways to get some hands-on production skills.

Bill is a great guy and teacher. Class is always fun and engaging thanks to him. Bill provides a unique perspective from his own professional experience as a producer/filmmaker. He also brings in several notable speakers to further enrich the learning experience. If you engage with the material and lectures, you will both learn and succeed.
Nice guy but doesnt seem like theres a lot of care or effort in his course. If you wanna talk about Netflix and his career and follow some odd rules for occasional assignments, go sign up.

Great guy with a great personality. He makes a lot of jokes in class. Majority of the grade for this course was from quizzes and a final paper. The quizzes sometimes were a bit difficult because they asked very specific questions about guest lectures and articles. The class itself is extremely discussion based. Highly recommend a class with him.

Bill is a really funny, friendly, and engaging guy. He has a lot of experience in media/film and can translate that. Always talks about interesting topics in class. Brings in a lot of guest speakers/professionals. Majority of grade comes from a few quizzes and a group business project.

Bill is a great professor! I would recommend him to anyone interested in film or production. He is an actual producer so he has a lot of real world knowledge. The majority of your grade is based on the project at the end of the semester, and there is also a paper due at the end of the semester too. Not terribly hard but would definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bill is unlike any professor Ive ever had. Theres some reading, a few papers and usually a group project, but hes funny, caring and makes all his lectures interesting and engaging. If you like television, film and production dont miss out on any of his classes!
Professor Lancaster is awesome! You HAVE to take his class if you are interested in film/the entertainment industry. A true asset to NU.

Lancaster is the man. He knows so much about the film industry and it is awesome to have a real producer as your professor. He offered extra credit to us and he is really reasonable about the coursework. There are a few papers in this class, so make sure not to procrastinate before they are due.

Professor Lancaster is an incredible teacher. He is an expert in the producing field and he is so excited to share his knowledge/craft with all of his students! Not only is he intelligent, he is funny and keeps the class both engaging and hands-on. I loved how he brought in guest speakers to the course, it added so much to my experience in class.

Bill Lancaster was the best professor I've ever had at Northeastern. He not only does an amazing job teaching, but he also puts in so much heart and really gets to know his students. He's had an amazing career in the entertainment industry and shares his own examples with us. He's truly inspiring.

Bill is the most passionate instructor I've encountered at Northeastern. A beacon of light with a boatload of experience in media and comms professionally and academically. The engaging and timely material selected for his courses reflect the wide array of his expertise; cultivates a holistic learning experience. Encourages creative collaboration.

Professor Lancaster is one of my favorite professors in the Comm Department as well as Northeastern. He has so much experience in the producing industry and gives you the opportunity to learn what YOU want when taking this class. Great feedback and great opportunity to gain hands on experience. He's also hilarious -- very understanding.

Cares greatly about the success of his students, and is more than willing to give feedback and answer questions. Class is very interesting and engaging. Very knowledgeable about the entertainment industry, and a great resource for someone looking to pursue this career path.

Course teaches students the skills producers use everyday in the TV/film industry. Bill connects students to professionals in the industry, encourages students to create their own content, and does everything he can to support the projects of his future media makers.

Bill is a really interesting guy with a lot of experience in the entertainment field. His grading is solely based on participation; if you talk enough in class and he knows who you are you get an A; if you don't, you'll get an automatic B at best regardless of your grades on other assignments.

Quizzes are really hard because he picks random questions to ask during the quiz. Lectures are fine and brings in people, but there is no feedback throughout the semester. Never really seemed prepared for class and lectures were boring. Never got grades back the whole semester either. Pick a different class

Professor Lancaster is an amazing professor... He's an industry veteran with plenty of connections, and he really cares about his students and what he does. If you put in the work he will help you with anything, and he's been an incredible help to myself and other students starting out in the entertainment industry. You won't regret class with him!

Lancaster has great connections in every part of the entertainment industry, and he's not afraid of asking them to come in and be a guest lecturer (they're cynical if informative on their fields). However, he's not decisive on assignments (we were supposed to have five papers, but only did two), and the final project was unclear all around.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Bill Lancaster's class was easy if you participated and he liked you. If you are shy and do not contribute, beware. The lectures did not have much structure and he talked about himself a lot.

Bill Lancaster is the example of an exceptional teacher.  Never frustrated by any questions concerning topic, doesn't mind repeating, loves what he does and is vested in his students.  If you take him, you'll not be disappointed.

Mr. Lancaster is an AMAZING teacher! I highly recommend taking his class.  Mr. Lancaster has restored my faith in academia and teachers that care. His lessons are well planned out, has exercises, he also inspires you with websites of what designers are creating. if this is your first design class this is this is the one you want to take

Best teacher I've ever had. If you show him you care, he will do everything to help you in and out of the classroom. He takes a genuine interest in his students future's. Amazing teacher. No homework, except you have 4 responses due at the end of the semester, and a project due. Easy class and very interesting! 100% take it!!

Lancaster has definitely been the best and most influential professor I’ve had at Northeastern!  His lectures are fantastic and he has so much experience! I especially enjoyed bus. of entertainment not only because of the VIP speakers, but also since it was so interesting to get their perspectives from the industry. Take all of his classes!

I never really write on this website but I had to write about Lancaster. Hands down the best professor I've ever had. As long as you show up to class (and you'll want to because it's really interesting) and participate, the class is a must take. Any class with Lancaster is a must take. He's a legend and knows his stuff.

You will leave Mr. Lancaster's class with a thorough understanding of the entertainment industry and how businesses manage productions from start to finish. If you're lucky, he will take you under his wing as a production assistant. Ask him about his time producing reality TV- he has many stories to share.
Lancaster really enjoys teaching and  Makes sure the students understands the topic and has all of us engage by putting us in groups he is a great teacher and I would recommend him to all Students

With decades of experience in TV and film producing, Bill brings industry knowledge and a realist perspective to the table.  He's invaluable because he's lived it; from producing for the Montel show to grant writing for documentaries.  He'll just as easily talk about his successes and blunders & this makes him empathetic to students eager to learn.

One of the best most dynamic, passionate and real professors I have ever had. Not only a great professor he is talented and experienced in the industry he is teaching. This is a rare combo! I took two of his classes at once and he kept every class entertaining! He exceeded my expectations. Don't leave Northeastern without taking one of his classes!
Great teacher.  Taught us a lot and feel like I learned from his stories from experience working in the industry.  Great guy, definitely a great class to take!

Prof Lancaster is without a doubt one of the best professors I have had throughout my college career. If your goal is too eventually work in the entertainment industry on the creative/production side, he is the perfect teacher to have. He has the experience and the knowledge to answer any questions you may have and the class is alo of fun as well.

If you want to learn about the industry from a true professional who has expert experience in the field this is the course to take. The assignments are interesting and your final project is an accomplishment you could bring up in an interview!

Professor Lancaster is a tremendous asset to the Communications Dept as well as to the entire University. His classes give information applicable to jobs in our field, something many courses in Comm lack. This professor will go out of his way to help students learn and grow into media professionals. I would recommend this course to all students.

I'm not a communications major, but took broadcasting management & programing and really liked it. If I had another elective left, I'd deff take another Lancaster class. Also no textbook to buy-epic win!

Lancaster is a great professor definitely one of my favorites at Northeastern. His lectures are really clear and he's always willing to clarify the things you might not understand in office hours. The degree of difficulty of the work is very reasonable and he makes the material really interesting and engaging. Take this class!

Broadcasting with Lancaster was a pretty solid class. His lectures were not bad because he usually had TV clips mixed in and he gets to point without rambling like most comm profs.  The class is about TV so its pretty easy to pay attention, so its worth it to participate. He's a nice guy, take him if you can.

Lancaster is awesome! His class supplemented by videos and speakers so its different almost everyday. It's really easy to take notes because he puts everything in lists. The final project is one of the most interesting in Northeastern: Pitch a television show. It's a cool class, take it!

For those interested in gaining professional insight into the inner workings of the entertainment industry, Lancaster is your guy.  Given his extensive career in TV & documentary filmmaking, Bill teaches real-life, practical tools of the trade.  A true producer at heart and one hell of a guy.  Best for those interested in/or going into TV/Film Ind.

Professor Lancaster is great; I recommend him to my friends. The only way to fail his class is by not going or not doing the assignments.He has a great deal of experience in the industry. He brings in industry professionals as speakers,  which is invaluable. He is the kind of professor that truly wants to see his students succeed, which is rare.
Professor Lancaster is a fair teacher, very nice and clear. make assignments and class interesting. Goes over everything and makes the most out of it. Recommend to take his class with him- very kind!

William "Bill"  Lancaster has by far one of the most enlightening professors at Northeastern University. His work speaks for itself, and he always makes it a point to educate he students with a very hands on approach. I have had him for 3 classes in my 4.5 years, and he is one of the best the University has to offer. He knows his craft!

Bill is by far the best prof I have had at NU. His lectures and assignments are clear and informative about the media field. He is extremely knowledgable of various aspects of TV and production and has worked everywhere in TV.I have taken 2 of his classes and I am truly disappointed that I can't take any more classes with him.Don't miss out!

Prof Lancaster is by far the most enthusiastic and passionate professor I have encountered.He cherishes his students, is always supportive and gladly shares his experience and knowledge in an energetic, engaging and fantastic way.He's always understanding of students' needs and encourages inspiring, lively debates. A genuinely extraordinary person.

This is the first class i've taken with Lancaster, and i am proud to say its been the best class i've ever taken at Northeastern University. He is down to earth, smart, enjoyable to listen to, very interesting and has been around the block, so to speak. His passion is producing and is extremely helpful. I highly recommend his classes!!!

Prof. Lancaster brings years of experience to the table and you would be a fool not to take advantage of that. He enhances the classroom experience by bringing in industry professionals who share their stories. The projects give you an accurate idea of what its like to work in the entertainment industry. Put the work in and you will be rewarded.

I have learned more in Professor Lancaster's comm. classes than any other. His immense experience in the field and the renowned speakers he brings in, really give you a great perspective of the media "industry." His classes are lecture based but leave room for informational, entertaining anecdotes and class discussions. He will help your career.

Really nice guy! Does not know alot about teaching but has alot of real world expierence. Very easy to do well in his classes. Quizes can be tricky-- does not read most papers. Can learn alot from him if you choose to.

Incredibly nice guy, but has no idea how to plan a syllabus, plan a class, or teach a class really. He makes you scratch your head at why you're actually paying for the service he provides. Easy class, but a waste of time

Prof. Lancaster was a decent professor with years of experience in the field. I wasn't wildly interested in the material, but Lancaster was very knowledgeable and reasonable. Quizzes and assignments were pretty easy, but often assigned last minute.

Lancaster is a very likeable guy.  However he is a terrible professor who can't seem to plan ahead. His assignments are easy and the quizes are only hard because he asks random questions. If your looking for an easy class to bs through this is great. But if your looking to learn something new try another professor.

Lancaster is a fool who doesn't plan ahead and can't write a syllabus let alone follow one. He has no plan for any of his classes, will randomly give out quizes, and assigns a bunch of work at the end of the semester when he realizes he has nothing to grade you on. Unless your interested in getting into tv of film production dont take this class.
Such a nice guy. He is funny, listens to what anyone has to say during class, and has interesting discussions. If you have a chance to take one of his classes, do it!
Easy quizzes as long as you pay attention to him, attendance not  mandatory, interesting class, easy going, easy grader, take him if you want a good grade

I loved this teacher.  If you are a comm major, you should take a class with him.  However, if you take more than two classes with him, you notice he teaches a lot of the same material, I even noticed he repeted assignments, which I didn't respect.  That aside, he's totally fun and funny and worth taking a couple times.

TAKE any class you can with this guy. He's funny and really interesting. He's one of the few CMN professors who has some sweet real word experience. His classes are always enjoyable and you wont be falling asleep...easy grader too!
He is just a super-duper guy.  Take this class.  No no, seriously...DO IT.

Hes a great guy and if you take more than one of his courses you will see a pattern, a pattern of they are all the same class.  Great class but try to only take one of them unless you are into not learning much new stuff.  Great discussions if you get good people in it with you too.

Most overrated professor ever...everyone said how great he was.  He was so boring and the class was so unstructured.  He likes to show clips of himself on TV.  I think he's a bad teacher and the class wasn't fun...but not too much work overall.  He's lazy, so not too hard of a grader.  Quizes are hard though b/c they ask wicked random questions.

Awesome awesome teacher who knows such a great amount of stuff about the industry.  He's hilarious and brings in so much real life stuff into the class that his stories never get boring.  He doesn't lecture so it's more about an interactive class so it's awesome.  His classes are great so i advise you take as many as possible!
Lancaster is awesome...I'm taking as many classes with him as possible. He makes the class fun and interesting!!!
Great class great professor. Do the readings and its a done deal

Lancaster is a cool guy. I would highly recommend taking his classes!!!! I know I had fun. He keeps it intersting. There were some sections I thought i would hate but I still ended up enjoying them. Get involved in class discussions and do not skip on the day of quizzes cuz' there are no makeups! Have Fun!!!

Lancaster is a blast! He's extremely personable, funny, and really gets to know you. class is pretty easy overall, just a few projects that require some work, but the quizes were pretty hard. Do the readings. Can't get over how much experience he brings to the class and his funny stories.

I got the feeling that he hadnt put much time into planning the Intro class.Really funny guy! the class seemed like a bit of a joke (although with manditory attendence), but maybe that was because it was the 101 class. he has the knowledge and experience that might be good for higher level classes.
bill is awesome!!! i'm taking as many classes with him as possible..he's very understanding and willing to work with you on anything. he's got a really good sense of humor as well.

really nice guy but isn't really all that challenging...has some great stories to tell because he has worked in the field but wouldn't recommend him if you are really interested in really getting a grasp on communication studies at the intro level....also make sure you understand the way he grades!

Awesome guy, hilarous teacher, and very knowledgable. This guy has it all, he has great connections and you learn from his stories in class. Unless you really mess up you'll get at least a B in his class. I enjoyed the class and love him as a teacher.

He was really knowledgeable about the subject and was really fun to talk to. he was one of the cooler teachers i have ever had. just remember to figure out his grading system early in the semester, it will help your grades on papers - i still have not figured it out though.
very good prof
Great lecturer that has great connections. He helped me get an internship before I went on co-op to get more experience for a better co-op position.

He's one of the coolest teachers I've ever had. His class is so laid back yet I feel like I've learned so much. As long as you keep up with the assignments and have fun stories to tell in class, you'll get an A. He's funny and has great stories! He tells dirty jokes!!

Awsome guy one of the best teachers I have had at NU. Relaxed and funny. Has great stories to tell and always wants to hear your stories. Quizez are easy, he goes through the book and tells you what to study and what you should know.
very interesting and an easy grader

Great Req. Class, If you're interested in production, Lancaster has real world experiance, so try to get in his class. He's a great guy, very funny. Just take notes on his lectures, as that's what's on the quizes.
great guy, easy to work with. just keep up on the work and youll be fine.

By far the best teacher I have had at Northeastern thus far.  He is a bit of a hard grader, definitely not that bad, but makes up for it in his sense of humor, personality, and knowledge of the field.
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Santelices is a very kind and understanding professor. Lectures could get long and boring sometimes, but she was very passionate about what she teaches. Quizzes and exams were pretty fair and assignments were fairly easy. If you sit in the front she will call on you a lot but overall a great professor and would take again.

Very supportive teacher but lectures are hard to follow. Exam questions are hard because info is often barely covered in class and wording is off. She is lenient about late work and you can negotiate grades usually/retake a quiz

Professor Santelices is a nice woman, but the class was boring. She just reads off the slides. There is a ton of work and readings, and it doesn't follow the syllabus in terms of dates, which makes it hard to follow along. The mid-term was difficult. Very approachable professor, though, and wants her students to thrive.
An angel on earth. Not a single complaint. Great slides, even better lectures, and a genuinely kind person. I'd take her again.
It's an okay class. I personally don't like lecture-heavy classes. Professor is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: so so boring but not too hard

Prof Santelices is amazing! She makes her lectures engaging and always ties them to personal stories and research. When she assigns papers, she lets you send drafts beforehand for feedback and is very accessible in and out of class. She is kind, accommodating, and overall incredible. She will change the due dates to what works better for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Claudia was an AMAZING professor. I took her biology class and had absolutely 0 complaints. If you pay attention in class, do the notes, and just put in effort, you will do just fine. The quizzes and tests always align with what she teaches in class, which is always appreciated as a student.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher! Clearly explains the material, with interesting personal stories. Workload is quite manageable and requires little work outside of class.

Claudia was very sweet! You could tell she cared about her students and wanted them to succeed. Her lectures were very interesting and her grading and tests were very forgiving. Her unique perspective as an anthropologist with interests in public health shaped the scope of the class in an interesting way too!

Claudia is the best! She's so easy going and wants all of her students to do very well in her class. She's always willing to work with students about anything, so don't be afraid to ask for assignment extensions or extra help with something. DON'T buy the book!! You don't need it, she'll assign readings but then she goes over everything in class.

Claudia is a fantastic professor. She is clearly passionate and experienced in her subject and her stories tie into her lectures well. FLEXIBLE: if whole class agrees will move due dates. BREAKDOWN: 4x 1 page reflections, 4x (usually take home) quizzes, midterm, final, one long paper. manageable workload/INTERESTING lectures. PAY ATTENTION IN CLASS

Amazing professor. She is caring, approachable, and gives inspiring lectures that are based on her own experiences. She wants her students to succeed in class and will help you achieve an A if you put in the work.

Professor Santelices is so kind and is willing to work with students who need quiz retakes, missed class, and allows the class to pick midterm and quiz dates.  She gives great feedback and uses her own research as examples so lectures are engaging. I loved her class and didn't need to spend much time outside to get a good grade.

Really liked the class and most quizzes and reflection papers were take home. As long as you try, she will give you a good grade. There were 4 quizzes (3 take home), 4 reflection papers (3 take home), a midterm and a final. She is very kind and sweet, she has come a long way from her previous reviews because the class and canvas were organized.

The class is super easy and she is a very easy grader. Everyone in the class got 100 for every reflection paper and take-home quizzes. the Lecture slides are boring and mostly common sense, so you do not need to study hard to get a 100 on her exams. Check canvas! She changes deadlines and posts assignments without mentioning them in class.

Class material is pretty dry but prof did pretty well making it engaging with her own stories/examples. Very kind person who wants you to succeed. Assignments are chill and based off the material on slides

Prof. Santelices was so understandable and very kind when it came to class! She is easy to talk to, and for me personally, finding a professor I can converse with in Spanish is nice. She has been one of the many public health class professors I really enjoyed having. Amazing person, but the lecture is boring. Quizzes and reflection paper are easy.

One of the best professors I've had. I took Anthropology of Latin America as a Spanish minor and totally changed my worldview. She shares her personal experiences in Chile as well as fieldwork, and shares profound, often unheard perspectives on the "third world" countries, capitalism, indigenous resistance, etc. I was captivated every lecture.

I found her lectures super interesting and she wasn't a super harsh grader. You need to study the material on the slides really well. The tests weren't hard but definitely harder than what we learned in class... She's not super great at communicating and will definitely forget your name even after meeting her multiple times; not very genuine.

Prof Santelices is a caring and enlightening professor. Amazing stories and experience in Anthropology. A bit iffy with technology and expect all assignments to be pushed back and delayed in grading. However, she really makes an effort to know everyones name and hear everyone out. IMO amazing professor, love coming to lecture. PARTICIPATE!

The class was an actual waste of money, as in the fact that many classes were cancelled and recorded for online. The most helpful part of the class is the slides, and I did actually come away from the class with helpful info. But was it worth the money spent on the class, no. Look for another class or even better, another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved her! She was one of the most caring professors at Northeastern! Through her personal stories, it is clear she is a professional and teaches for her love of learning. Her class was very lecture-heavy, but her material was always accessible, and students learned a lot. Grades depend mostly on exams, quizzes, and projects, not attendance.
Very kind, understanding woman. Barely knows how to use technology. I barely went to class and did well - if you stay on top of your coursework and STUDY THE CLASS SLIDES you'll do well.

Claudia is a really genuine, caring professor who has amazing life stories and lectures that brought me to tears on several occasions. It hurts to admit that she is all over the place with technology and deadlines, if she had a little more structure I'm sure she could be amazing.

Obviously cares a lot about the subject and has interesting stories, but lectures were hard to follow. Assigns way too much pointless reading. Assignments and exams were confusing, complicated, long, and frustrating. Not good with technology. Attendance was not taken but missing lectures does not help for later on. Class was all over the place.

Kind, passionate, good lectures. Everything else not so good. Horrible with technology. Extremely busy outside of class and didn't seem to have time to actually be a good professor. Her assignments can be confusing, especially the tests. Cancels class often, which is not a good thing. Could be good if she actually had time to focus on the class.

Dr. Santelices made lectures more interesting by adding her own experience of working in the field. You could really tell she was passionate about public health and how she has contributes and how we as students can further contribute. Assignments were based off of videos. As long as you pay attention to lectures and review, you'll pass. :)

One of the best professors I've had. Learned a lot in this class and it's clear that she cares a lot about her students. The class involves a lot of role plays to try out different counseling techniques, but even as an introvert they were totally fine. Not a lot of hw and not hard to get an A.

Cali is a considerate and kind professor. You can tell she is very invested and knowledgable about her work and comes to class every day ready to teach. She assigns a reasonable workload, and there is no busy work. The hands-on aspect of the counseling class was a great way for students to get practice experience with this kind of work as well.

Cali is very passionate about her work and is very knowledgeable about the different types of counseling offered. I really enjoyed her class and I have learned a lot and gained a lot of knowledge about helping people in different backgrounds. She's very caring and has a very lenient late policy and is very lenient in grading.

Professor Staton teaches pretty well, but her lectures are much easier compared to the questions she gives us for weekly workshops and exams. She also rushes through lectures and rushed through the material at the end, making me feel pretty unprepared for exam 3 and the final. It was nice having test corrections but could only help so much.

Orgo is hard, but Prof Staton gives you the resources to succeed. She expects you to dedicate a lot of time to her class (polling Qs, achieve HW, weekly psets), but you need to spend time on orgo daily to do well. Generous grading policies (test corrections, extra credit, 90% is an A). Thorough lectures; however,  end of semester was rushed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She explained Organic Chem REALLY well, I honestly thought this was my most fun class simply because I understood chemistry for the first time. Tests are really difficult, but you get 50% back. Just make sure to complete every homework; I forgot to do a few, and it would have helped my grade a lot. Overall, a good teacher just has a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The final was actually the worst one ive ever taken. She taught new information right up until the last class which showed up on the final.  The workshops were not as helpful as I wished since this exam barley included exam 1/2 material. Homework is alright but I wish she went over the exam 3 and after exam 3 material more and give more examples.

Staton was good, homework was manageable and lectures were easy to follow. My biggest issue was her exams, they were difficult, but we has test corrections. The days leading up to final, the work was unbearable. She gave too many lenghtly homework assignments and having exam 3 just 2 weeks before the final, making it extremely difficult to study.

Prof. Staton is your best bet for orgo 1 especially if you are preparing to take the MCAT. Her teaching style is amazing and even though her tests are harder than other orgo 1 profs, there is a 50% test correction policy. Be ready to study! Orgo is one of those subjects where you have to put in the hours for a good grade anyways. Highly recommend!

Tests are insanely hard and a lot of work load. She barely gives any time to actually practice the material because in three days there is so much new material. Good teacher, she cares about the students but it is impossible to keep up with all the work especially at the end of the sem when everything is so cramped up.

The exams are impossible to pass even if you study so hard. The practice problems she gives are no where near as hard as her exam problems. Majority of her exam is not multiple choice and it is so much drawing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are so impossible, and she falls behind on grading so you won't even be sure what to study for the next exam or the final. Heard from others that she has yet to give back exam 3 scores until after the final. Practice tests are nothing like the real ones. She is sometimes condescending as well.

Staton is one of the better orgo profs but it is a hard class, there is so much homework and the tests are actually impossible but we do get up to 50% back in test corrections. shes very nice and organizes slides very well but she expects a lot of outside time dedicated to this class

Carla is a wonderful person! She is always accessible outside of class and very helpful. At the start of the semester, she was very good at explaining things in detail, but as we got into reaction mechanisms, the explanations were rushed and honestly pretty bad. I felt like I was drowning in the material by the end and it was very stressful.

Really engaging lecturer and cool grading policies (50% corrections on exams). However, her tests are just insanely difficult. The practice exams are not similar at all to the real thing, making it hard to study. She has very little leniency for personal circumstances but is always willing to meet with you. Would've taken Orgo 2 with her if I could
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is super hard and content heavy but Prof Staton gives you everything you need to pass. Having test corrections was a godsend and you really can improve your score a lot if you put in the time.

I loved taking Organic II with Professor Staton. The class is difficult, but with 50% test corrections back on the three midterm exams it's more than fair. She is readily accessible outside of class and genuinely seems to care about her students and the course itself. I definitely recommend for Orgo II.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great prof for Orgo. She knows what shes talking about and can explain things super well. Lectures and canvas are organized very well. Her tests are SO difficult. Corrections for midterms make it easier to get a good grade and tons of padding w. extra credit, homework, and participation.

Take this class if you're worried about getting doing bad in orgo 2, but not if you're aiming for/think you can achieve an A/high B. She's a very nice professor and she does genuinely care about her students. Her tests are just too hard (even with 50% test corrections), so her grading criteria makes it so no one fails but no one does great either.

She is an amazing prof and I genuinely learned so much in her class. Her exams are very tough and she prioritizes her students understanding concepts but if you do the weekly practice and homework she gives you will be able to succeed. She is the best professor I have had so far.

She taught in a way that was easy to understand. She provided many resources to help like test corrections.She falls behind grading and it's really frustrating to have to wait. It would be nice if she communicated when things were taking her longer, she would promise us grades back by a date and then give them back 12 days later.

Prof Staton is great at teaching, however grading takes too long(we still don't have our third exams or workshops back after the final). The final was hard and workshops don't resemble tests so our averages were low. It's her first time teaching it, her lectures had a lot of depth. I just wish there was practice that resembled test like questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Staton's teaching style for Organic Chemistry I really clicked with me personally. Her tests are difficult, but in the non-Honors section, you are offered test corrections where you can get 50% of your points back. I also found the test corrections really helpful for incentive to review content that you previously got wrong.

If you want to truly understand orgo 1, I'd take Staton's class. She's not the best at grading assignments promptly, (just the took the final and assignments from week 4 are ungraded), but her quality of teaching is great. Exams are HARD which can feel really unrewarding and discouraging especially after studying so hard but, her class is do-able.

Lowkey the goat idk her test corrections come in clutch and the content/practice she gives lowkey reflects some of the exam material. Her exams are extremely hard, but with test corrections its not that difficult to end with an A/B. Just study a lot and really try to learn the conceptual stuff. She's really sweet.

Honestly, a very kind and sweet professor, but those exams were ridiculously long and complex. Despite corrections, I felt like I was in an honors class. Since exams determine most of your grade, just go for another professor; it's not worth the headache. She is not generous at all with partial points; it might as well be multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved her class so much; she made organic fun and enjoyable. She offered test corrections over the summer, which were very helpful. Her office hours are amazing! She cares about her students and wants everyone to understand the content.

She is very nice and approachable. Orgo is an incredibly hard class but she makes it easier to digest with her lectures, which are easy to follow and very detailed. Her tests are very hard, harder than other orgo profs from what I've heard, but she gives you the resources you need to succeed and her test corrections are very forgiving.

I took Summer II Orgo 1 w/ Prof. Staton and loved her! Yes, the course goes fast but that's just the nature of orgo. She did a great job at giving clear lectures and providing time outside of class for students to get extra help. Test corrections were offered for most tests and extra credit opportunities were made. She clearly cares for students!

Took orgo 1 in the summer (6 week course) with carla. she's a great teacher but had to go quick bc of how short the class is. I was able to succeed in her course by her quiz and test corrections and really studying her problem sets (semi similar to her quizzes and tests). orgo isn't easy, you have to really understand it conceptially to do well

Prof Staton gives you everything you need to succeed in orgo 1. Her exams are pretty difficult, but she offers corrections; lectures are clear and easy to follow; and she is great at answering questions. While she isn't perfect, she is very 
respectful and open to feedback, and she actually takes it. Prepared me well for orgo 2 and the MCAT!

Professor Staton is one of my favorite professors. She is super approachable and cares about her students. She is always looking for feedback and is willing to adapt her teaching based on it. She explains everything well and finds fun analogies and stories to help students remember content. Definitely recommend her for Orgo 1.

Prof. Staton is a great teacher. ORGO is a tough class, but she is a great lecturer and gives you a lot of opportunities to learn and get help. Her exams are hard, but she gives test corrections, which always helped my grade. I definitely recommend taking her for ORGO I!

Dr. Staton's exams are the most difficult--by far--out of any in the entire Organic Chemistry department at Northeastern, but she is very fair with grading (her "Follow-through policy") and gives test corrections, so you have many chances to bring up your grade.

SO GOOD- those complaining need to remember this class is hard but she gives you every possible opportunity to get a good grade. Bonus points, lower grade scale, easy HW points, test corrections, you name it. Talks fast, but still manageable and gives so. much. practice. Really works your critical thinking skills in a good way.
Amazing orgo professor. Although she goes fast, she provides the resources necessary to do well in the class, and she has test corrections to ensure that you can correct your mistakes

Though I didn't do as well I would've liked, she is very knowledgable and overall a wonderful professor. Coming from having an awful gen chem prof, she made me love and actually enjoy orgo, no matter how difficult it was. Orgo in general is a hard class, so be ready to do a lot of work outside of the class. Take her! Best prof I've had yet.

I really do not understand all of the negative reviews. She is the best professor I've had. As someone who hated gen chem, this class made me love chemistry. It truly is not that bad if you lock in and go to office hours. Many people on here complain about exams but I honestly found them not bad, especially with test corrections. Take her!!!!

She was super nice and a good lecturers, but everything relied on the lectures. The exams were rough and I honestly thought I failed the final but the test corrections were great help. She wanted students to succeed, but you definitely had to put in the work. I  thought she was a great lecturer and would take again. Also her fits were fire

She is the WORST professor EVER. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS unless you want to be in an eternal stress. She allows for test corrections which it's the only good thing but she gives tooo much content for so little time. She expects you to know everything. Do not take her.
Lectures and notes were tough to follow unless you dedicate your life to this class. Very unaccommodating and does not seem to care for the students.

Lectures and notes are extremely difficult to follow. If you aren't ready to dedicate your life to this class then I suggest finding a different professor. Attending office hours is basically mandatory if you want to stay caught up. Overall I found her to be very unaccommodating and inflexible

Very caring & nice but def the most difficult prof to take for Orgo 1. However, she does do test corrections + partial credit & the grading scale is "lowered" (a 90 is an A, for reference). Wish she had given us more practice material bc the textbook questions didn't reflect what was on the exams. Office Hours were only helpful for gen questions.

Is obviously very knowledgeable about the class and cares about students, but the lecture notes are very unhelpful regarding review. Office hours are PACKED and are the only time homework problems are ever reviewed, so it becomes very easy to get behind or stuck if you cannot make it to office hours.

Her class is very difficult simply due to the fact that the exams are much more advanced than the class itself. The only good thing is that she gives test corrections, which boost your test grade. so far the exam averages after the corrections have been in the low to mid 70s, so that means that the raw scores have to be somewhere in the 50s-60s

the 1 star reviews have got to be rage bait... staton is the goat of the chemistry department. if you study and put in the effort, you will do just fine. she gives a ton of partial credit and so much opportunity for remediation. this isn't a class you can cram last minute, you have to learn the material in order to do well.

The negative reviews are uncalled for and just plain rude. Professor Staton is easily one of the best professors at NEU. She is an incredibly smart woman and cares a lot about her students. This class is difficult, but remember she is teaching a very difficult subject. If you're planning on taking Orgo 1 or 2, take it with Staton, she is great.
amazing person overall for those who are rating her a 1 she is hard but this is college man
full time studying on your own basically
If you like taking exams take this course the exams are challenging and a good way to prep for the dat or mcat but the teaching style is not helpful at all!

She is very nice but I spend a lot of time outside class teaching myself the material. I wish she covered more of what's actually on the exams. Her TAs aren't helpful and seem bored and unmotivated especially in the Zoom recordings.

She's a great teacher but can be condescending. She expects us to fully learn the easy material she lectures on and gives us barely a minute to two to try problems in class. However, the problems don't reflect the exam, which is frustrating. For Exam 2, there was no ranking, yet the problem set had tons of those questions.

She's very easy to understand during lectures and when going over her slides but the exams are really difficult and don't match what we go over in class. It's great to be challenged but it would help if that difficulty was also part of the lessons. The test corrections are helpful but I'd prefer to understand the material the first time around.
Whoever is giving her a 5 is crazy. i literally took 40 pages of notes and still failed the unit 3 exam, and know many many many people that studied sooo much and did horrible..
FYI I'm pretty sure all the bad reviews are by the same person. Likely someone upset they didn't do well on the third exam. Take that into consideration, because Staton is an amazing professor.

I have no idea what the other reviews are talking about. She's understanding, kind, and wants us all to succeed. Her lectures are comprehensive, and although her tests are challenging, she provides us with the foundation necessary to help us understand the material. I did AWFUL on her third test, yet I still got an A as her grading is forgiving.

Staton is the best. Her tests are hard, but she sets you up to succeed. If you get a 50% on a test, you can get back up to a 75%. Her grading system is so forgiving. A 90 is considered an A. Organic chemistry is hard. Not understanding this course isn't Staton's fault, it's just the complexity of the material. TAKE HER.

I love Prof Staton, she's so kind and thorough with her lectures, and even more so in her office hours. Her tests definitely aren't easy, but she does test corrections which have saved me. Downsides are that she doesn't post enough practice problems and recorded lectures, but overall I managed fine in her class. Attendance is done through PollEV

I was terrified to take orgo 1, but Prof Staton eased my worries. She's so kind and thorough with her lectures, and even more so during her office hours. Her tests definitely aren't easy, but I found that her exams were pretty similar to the problem sets. Attendance is taken by polling, which do make up a small chunk of your grade.

STAY AWAY from this professor. As someone who is usually a straight-A student this class has made me reconsider my entire academic path, major, and career. I ended up guessing on the entire exam because the content felt completely disconnected from the lectures. The lectures may seem easy but they don't adequately prepare you for the exam.STAY AWAY

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE IF IT'S TAUGHT BY HER. SHE SEEMS LIKE A GREEN FLAG AT FIRST BUT IS ACTUALLY A MASSIVE RED FLAG. I HAVE NO IDEA WHERE ALL MY HARD-EARNED KNOWLEDGE IS GOING. HER TEACHING STYLE IS WAY TOO SIMPLE IN CLASS AND THEN THE EXAMS ARE RIDICULOUSLY COMPLEX. NOTHING LINES UP. IT'S FRUSTRATING AND COMPLETELY MISLEADING.

Also, it is very hard to study because you don't have references to see how hard the exams would actually be compared to what is shown in class. She also doesn't even record her lectures, which is a HUGE disadvantage to people taking her course.

I've studied so much for this course, but the professor only reviews the easiest topics in class—almost like elementary school. It gives a false sense of understanding. The exams are completely different and expect advanced thinking we were never taught. She's one of the worst professors I've had—condescending, unhelpful, and misleading.

She doesn't give any review at all for her midterms, and for her final, she doesn't even give a final review of the exam at all. Also, do not even bother using ChatGPT or AI to help cause her problems are so complex that you would still fail and get the questions wrong even after using all "outside sources".

When it comes to office hours, she gives much easier problems than what's on the exams, her lectures are fine and she is great lecturer overall, she needs to understand that we are not 4th yrs ready to take the MCAT and that we are 1st years just recovering from Gen Chem at best. Also, she teaches the course in a much complex way overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Beware: She seems nice, but her materials are way too easy compared to how insanely hard her exams are. You'll think you're ready, but nothing she gives actually prepares you—you'll be completely blindsided. She's also petty and arrogant about regrades.

BEWARE!!! THIS WOMAN IS THE MOST TOUGH GRADER OUT OF ALL THE ORGO SECTIONS. YOU WILL STUDY FOR HOURS ON END TO RECEIVE A C+ AT BEST. You may think that you would know what ur doing inside and out, and her questions will still stump you. Trust me; take Danahy instead. PLEASE SAVE YOURSELF. When it comes to her exams, they are significantly harder!!!

Took this class her first semester of teaching. She is a kind person but her tests are significantly harder than the other orgo sections. Try to memorize every small detail on slides. The practice problems given are way easier than the exams, beware. Very strict grading on tests.

She is very kind but can be condescending at times. Her exams are very tough, but you get test corrections, which help boost your grades on them by a lot. Since the exams are open ended, if you do not study all of the information down to the specifics, it is hard to do well, especially on exam 3.

By far the best professor I have ever had at NU. She is clear with expectations, extremely fair, and does not waver in her stance. It is a tough subject and you have to put a lot of work into this class but once you understand how she grades her exams it is within reach to get an A. I absolutely encourage you to take Dr. Staton for OChem.

Professor Staton is the best professor I have EVER. HAD. She is so amazing at her job, spends all her free time and helps students in office hours or scheduling one-on-one sessions. She teaches a very difficult course but does it beautifully. She is helpful, and responsive, always open to help, very approachable, and wonderful.
She is an awesome lecturer. She is caring and can explain hard topics very easily. She allows for test corrections and overall wants you to do well, She is enthusiastic and very smart.

The lectures were extremely informative and helped me learn the material. Tests are difficult and focus on the small details, but they don't focus on just one thing. Wouldn't take if you just need the credits, because there are easier professors, but she is really good if you need to take orgo.

Lecture-heavy but easy to follow if you pay attention. Office hours are very helpful. She does not provide enough practice material/homework, and her exams are very hard but she grades fairly. She is kind, passionate, and receptive to feedback, so I'm sure her class will improve, especially as a newer professor.
The most subjective and discouraging professor I have ever had. Led me to change my major and consider transferring

She honestly is one of my favorite professors! She acknowledges how difficult the orgo material is and she teaches it in a way that is really simple and easy to understand. She also is very generous with test corrections and grade curves. My one complaint is that her slides are hard to follow if you fall behind in class. But, overall super caring!

She's really sweet and goes over a lot of material in class, office hours are such a huge help! A lot of her material is covered in class and she is very accommodating. I would recommend her over other professors, she genuinely wants you to learn the content so the tests are a little hard but offer test corrects to help with mistakes&MCAT questions

The test material is solely from what she says in class. She also refuses to record her lectures. Her handwritten notes are impossible to follow. Minimal study material. Other teachers allow test notes, but she doesn't. She will take points off correct answers if you don't use exact language. You need to use the textbook, or you won't do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AMAZING. Best professor I've had at Northeastern by far. She is so kind and puts in so much effort to make herself available outside of class. Makes complicated topics easy to understand. Her exams are difficult, but certainly doable. Offers test corrections. She is clearly extremely passionate about orgo and makes me excited about it too.

She is a great lecturer. She asks a lot of questions during class and practices a lot of active learning techniques which helps a lot. She is young so she understands what the students are going through and she is  a great professor. Her tests are hard but she is a fair grader and wants her students to learn as much as possible.

Rewarding course that blends consulting frameworks with real-world application. Clear, practical approach to talent management and engaging teaching style makes concepts easy to grasp. Strengthened my interest in consulting/business ops. Could benefit from more data analysis and individual reflection assignment but a valuable experience overall.

Professor Odom gave great lectures, and the syllabus was very clear from the beginning. He listens to students and adjusts the syllabus and lesson planning based on our wants. The simulation was a great group project, and if you work together and pay attention throughout, you will do well in the class.

Professor Odom's class was one of the more memorable classes I've taken at Northeastern. What stood out most was the real world perspective brought from his experience currently running his own firm. His focus on AI education and strategic adoption of AI in the consulting world was inspiring, realistic, and should be taught more at Northeastern.

Professor Odom is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. Never have I felt more engaged in a class than in his Global Talent Management section this spring! His enthusiasm for what he does and his ability to meaningfully connect course content to real-world experience made the class so fruitful and enriching for me. Take his class!
Hope you get a good group

Professor is a very accomplished management consultant who designed his class to prepare students for the consulting world. You are treated like a consultant and learn how to give executive presentations, work effectively in teams, problem-solve, and other valuable skills. You are required to learn and to use AI. There is no Essay or Exam.

Curtis Odom is a fantastic professor with deep industry knowledge in HR & Talent Development. He has been an executive leader and currently runs his own practice. He is so knowledgeable, he has CEO's reaching out to him to perform independent audits for their own firm. If you want to level up your business capabilities, please take this class!

Professor Odom has deep industry experience and expertise, and his lectures were highly engaging and applicable to real-world situations. He encouraged students to think and problem-solve like consultants during the semester-long simulation. He cares for his students' learning and preparedness for the real world. Overall, a great class.

One of the best professors. Engaging and organized classes with clear expectations. He truly cares about students learning practical skills for the real world. The course pushed structured, professional thinking. He welcomes feedback and creates a collaborative environment. I learned a lot and highly recommend him

The professor did a great job creating an inclusive environment with fun assignments and group projects. The class was primarily based on a group simulation project. Try to get close to your groupmates, as your enjoyment of the class will probably depend heavily on that. He is very understanding and helpful if you ask him questions. He was great

Professor Odom comes to every class well-prepared and enthusiastic. His course covers all the key aspects of how a business operates. The simulation used is particularly effective, even for those who aren't usually fans of them, as it trains you to think from a consultant's perspective.

Professor Odom was the best professor I've had at Northeastern. He is an amazing lecturer, so funny, and clearly outlines expectations. He truly wants the course to be as engaging and enjoyable as it can be for students, and he encourages feedback. He prepares his students to enter the workforce professionally and I can't recommend him enough.

The curriculum lacked clarity, especially around the paid online simulation. We were expected to “figure it out” without foundational instruction, and questions about how it worked were not clearly answered. Lectures felt disconnected from Canvas and the Sim. The 5 weeks of intense group work were challenging, and overall the course felt disjointed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Odom is awesome!! Super knowledgeable in consulting and shares a lot of his personal experience. He's really down to earth and treats his students as equals. Class is very discussion and activity heavy. Few things make up your grade like the simulation and a couple presentations, so try to do good in that. 10/10 recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Odom's class. Throughout the semester, the professor uniquely integrated AI, and students learned how to write clearer prompts. To be transparent, the simulation is a significant portion of your grade, so I would try to get comfortable with it and ask questions earlier on.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have a bad group in this class you will have a very difficult semester. The amount of work you put in does not reflect your grade. Unless this class is require I would not recommend.

I really enjoyed Professor Odom's class this semester and would say he is one of my favorite professors in DMSB! He recently restructured the course to include AI and is extremely receptive to feedback. The group airline simulation project is a lot of work, and it rewards detailed analysis and group decision-making. I recommend Prof. Odom

Professor Odom is genuinely one of the best DMSB professors! He really embraced the use of AI during class, gave really engaging lectures, and he is very passionate about what he teaches. The group simulation is a fair amount of work but so worthwhile, and he was always checking in on our progress throughout the semester. 100% recommend taking!

Professor Curtis cares, knows what he is talking about, and is passionate. He has experience and has been in the industry which provides stories, lessons and advice throughout the course. Heavily weighted on an airplane simulation & presentations that if not done well, can impact grade severely with minimal individual grades to make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Odom is easily one of my favorite professors I have had at Northeastern. He has completely restructured this course to remove exams and papers. It is heavy group project based and he has very clear grading criteria and a clear syllabus. He integrates AI into the course well and really wants student input into making the course better.

Professor Odom is awesome. The course is well-run, with a clear focus on preparing you for your professional life. There is an emphasis on AI as well. The course requires thought and organization more than it is difficult, so stay on top of things. There aren't any exams; it is all presentations and the airline simulation. Highly recommend.

Professor Odom is an amazing professor! His teaching style is structured very well and there are many opportunities to ask questions and learn from his real world experiences. He is very pro AI usage and always willing to meet with students outside the classroom setting to talk about consulting or give career advice. Everyone should take his class!

Professor Odom is great. You can really tell he has practical consulting knowledge through his own hands on work in consulting and previous work experiences. The course is not necessarily hard but there are many weekly timelines/deadlines. Be ready to organize yourself and work ith a team to successfully address simulation and presentations.

Enjoyable class. Professor Odom is upbeat, interesting, and treats students like adults. Forward on AI.

Class curates an authentic experience by putting students into groups to work through a realistic simulation. Students are graded on their team's simulation performance and several client presentations, rather than papers/tests.

I mean he really is a good Professor. Yeah it's a lot of work, but if you come to him for help, he'll work with you. He is also very receptive to feedback. Would take again, I would just recommend taking the class during a lighter semester

Professor Odom's humor and personality made the class enjoyable, and I always looked forward to it. He treats students like adults and values feedback. He can be inflexible on grades and seeing alternative perspectives on assignments, but he is consistent with his expectations. It was a fun, challenging class and a good way to end my last semester.

Although he can be pretty hard to reason with at times, he's genuinely a good professor. He has a lot of experience and he is a good person to ask about anything regarding post-grad plans. If you don't communicate or reach out to him, you most likely won't do good. Just talk to him regularly and you will be fine, don't worry.

This professor and this class are by far one of my favorite classes at Northeastern. This class is tough, and it isn't going to be easy, but it's gratifying if you attend class and pay attention. I recommend this class to everyone that I know, and I wish that this professor would teach more classes because I would take a class with him again.

EXTREMELY harsh grader - avoid if you care about GPA. Going forward this class has a lot of proposed changes that will make it even harder. He treats you like an adult, but is really inflexible with grades and deadlines. His class had a lot of potential to be more enjoyable, he's a fun lecturer. Wish my grade reflected the time and effort I put in.

Typically felt like meaningless busy work. Would NOT recommend.The whole semester you are working with the same group, and he offers no peer evaluations so if you get a bad group, you're screwed.I was hoping to get some real consulting experience in this course, but instead, I left with nothing but a lower GPA to show for it. RUN.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
One of the least understanding professors. Very tough grader and doesn't ever give partial credit on any of the assignments. 
Don't listen to the comments saying he provides ACTUAL consulting experience since this semester he switched to the simulation which has nothing to do with real consulting. 
Overall it was a useless class that tanked my GPA

Professor Odom creates a collaborative and dynamic work environment that enables students to absorb the material long-term. He will challenge you as a professional while providing support and autonomy throughout the semester (Make sure to take detailed notes and try not to miss class lectures, the info will be important for your deliverables).

Professor Odom makes his lectures very interesting and gives students a lot of autonomy throughout the semester. The course is extremely back heavy so it is important to keep up to date with assignments and manage your time properly. Tip: make sure to take notes during class (especially things Professor says 2x) and make sure to include in papers.

Prof. Odom is an engaging lecturer that prioritizes how useful the class is for students. We had "reading days" to work on our group project or written assignments, which were helpful in balancing this class with other responsibilities. Working with real clients is also a great experience! Grading is tough at first, but gets better.

Professor Odom was always available outside of class to meet and provide any support needed for the client project. He is very passionate about the class and has a lot of previous knowledge from his experiences. I felt like I learned a lot because of his teaching style and his deep experience in the field. His lectures are worth coming to class.

Amazing Professor! Professor Odom is a great lecturer and makes each class not only educational but also very fun to listen to and participate in. There are a few papers in this course, but he gives plenty of time to prepare, I would advise starting each paper a week in advance though so you're not rushing at the end.
Would not recommend this class. Gives no instructions when you meet him one on one to ask what he expects on the paper says just follow rubric. All the other comments about him are completely true
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I met in NEU. His feedback to your papers totally useless (use same comments to students have the same grade). It's great that you can engage with real-world clients. However, it has nothing to do with the professor. Without the knowledge you learned from the course, you can still perform well in client project. No curve.
Opportunity to work directly with organizations as consultants!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't get why people claim he's a bad professor. The class offers a lot to apply to real world, the podcasts really get you thinking about how you choose your career, both as a consultant and otherwise. I feel like if you really pay attention to what he says and the things assigned, you learn a lot more and find this class is absolutely great.

Curtis is a disrespectful professor that acts like he cares about his students but won't even take the time to meet and discuss grading issues. Very unclear with his grading and is unreasonable when you challenge his feedback. Overall, one of my worst class experiences, and I regret taking this class. This class makes me not want to do consulting.

He really cares about the course and is able to bring relevant real world experience to his lectures. The grade is heavily weighted in a few large assignments (a paper and the final exam being worth 60% of the grade). He is in interesting and engaging lecturer, but the grading criteria isn't always clear. Pretty easy B but definitely not an easy A.

Professor Odom is a smart, professional professor who also runs/works for a consulting firm in Boston. For that reason, I highly recommend taking Consulting in Orgs with him. You get real experience with real clients and he is super helpful throughout the entire semester. Its not an easy class, but its one of the best ive taken here
Talked a lot how amazing his course is but grading is so confusingly unreasonable. Not an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AMAZING - super nice guy who knows how to teach. He also has some amazing work experience that he shares, infused with Ted talks, which makes the classes overall interesting. No need to read the textbook - tests are an in class paper on a case study which is kindly graded. Super inspirational too!

One of my favorite classes and professors at NU and even better guy. Decent work load, but topics are interesting. He will change it up if the class is feeling stressed. 5 stars all the way. You have to take him at some point, very interesting, gets to use his real life experience in lecture

He gives difficult 5-question quizzes every Wednesday and uses a ranking system for grading which makes it difficult to achieve an A. He is very unresponsive to emails and does not provide enough support when students are failing quizzes and asking for additional resources.

What a tough professor,  the lectures were very entertaining with tons of new content in each lecture. He really pushed us but at least I learned a lot, most than in any other class. Awesome class and professor.
He cares about his students alot. Course is very hard but he cares abt students
Very difficult class but it's all curved.  He's a great professor who cares about his students a lot.

Prof Cortes is awesome. The class was tough (lots of tests, tons of practice problems, and a really fast pace) but honestly, I've learned more here than in any other class at Northeastern. He's strict but fair, super funny, and really knows his stuff. Easily the hardest class I've taken, but also the best.

The professor is extremely rude and disorganized. He would constantly go off the planned schedule and seemed chaotic. Would NEVER recommend him to any student who actually wants to learn. His rude demeanor turns students away from being excited about the class material. I've never disliked a professor this much.
so many quizzes and he drops two but its lockdown browser and camera on. the content was so hard to understand. i recommend taking this in person rather than online cause it is extremely math heavy
very unorganized and quiz is way too hard and pointless
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Risk management was very hard.

Absolutely loved Felipe Cortes. He hates memorization and will go through the intuition of every process and problem with you. Quizzes are hard but the class is graded on a heavy curve (Top 50% get at least an A-). Honestly a gem in the otherwise meh group of finance professors at Northeastern. I thought he was pretty funny too.

By far the best professor I had. I am glad I took his class before graduating. In just one class, he rekindled my passion for Finance. He is very technical but always wants students to focus on intuition first and then on the math part. Awesome class!

Best profesor ever. Very caring about his students and wants everyone to do well. If you show up to class, do the worksheets before exams, you will get an A. Codesso is the goat. One of the Best profesor I ever had.

He forgot to post assignments halfway through the semester. Didn't really learn much at all during his class, and I never felt challenged or inspired by anything we discussed. Lots of 'code' in our projects was just his that he told us to copy. Easy A if you want to waste 4 credits.

Mauricio is really a detriment to both the accounting and data analytics programs at the school. I feel like if anything, my data skills suffered as a result of atrophying over a semester with him, and I wish had the opportunity to have literally anyone else teach me coding and databasing.

Mauricio is an awful professor and a detriment to Northeastern's accounting/data analytics dept as a whole. Codesso is the goat. Take him if you can
