DJ is such a caring and passionate professor. You can tell he loves to teach! Learned very useful clinical skills and was always willing to help during lab. The two exams were a little difficult so make sure to review the lectures. The practical exam was not too bad either!

DJ is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so caring and makes every lecture enjoyable with his enthusiasm and kindness. DJ is so awesome!  Great professor with a passion for all things EMS. He responds quickly and is strict, but not in an unreasonable way. If you utilize all of the tools he gives you, it is basically impossible to not succeed. 10/10 DJ is the best.

reviews.comment: Dr. Metzger was an amazing professor. He would always take out the time to answer any questions, and was never rude. He really cares about his students, giving extensions if you email or ask in person. Just showing up for class isn't enough though. As long as you aren't on your phone you will be fine. He's a really easy grader too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Doctor Metzger was one of the best English professors I have ever had through my academic career! As long as you come to class, immerse yourself in the writing process, and show enthusiasm for the course, this is an easy class to achieve an A in. Dr. Metzger is extremely passionate about writing and shows care for his students.

Professor Metzger is a wonderful professor. He always makes sure the classroom environment is inclusive and welcoming to all. He is very clear with his grading. His Canvas page is very organized. There are no surprises with this course.

Professor Metzger always ensured that the class was fun and engaging. He cares for the students and will take the time and effort to help everyone out. The class is relatively easy if you do the work on time. This has been one of my favorite classes that I have taken.
Dr. Metzger is an amazing professor. Class is easy, just do your work on time and participate in class.

Dr. Metzger clearly cares about his students and the class was not too hard. He gave us clear rubrics about the essays we were writing about, and helped us tremendously while working on them. He's easy to access out of class, and responds to emails quickly. I would recommend taking his class 10/10. Great professor, and great person.

Sometimes, the lectures get analytical or philosophical, but otherwise, the class is easy and based on papers that if you think about your topic, are interesting. Dr. Metzger is personable and cares about each student individually.

Quite literally my favorite professor at Northeastern. His class was fun and engaging. His grading criteria is clear from the beginning. It's an easy class but he makes it so interesting. 100% recommend taking his class given the opportunity.

Dr. Metzger is amazing!! He tailors the course in a way that the writing and research could be helpful to you outside of the course itself (co-op, resume, etc.). He is very kind and helpful. If you tend to procrastinate, this course is great because he splits the projects up well and you get tons of feedback from him and the rest of your peers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I recommend taking professor Metzger for writing! He's a fair grader when it comes to your writing and will give you the opportunity to improve your writing before you turn it in for your final grade and improve on yourself as a writer. He does this by meeting with you one on one to work on your drafts and also does peer reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It's clear that Dr. Metzger truly cares about his students and their success in this course (and life). I truly looked forward to coming to class every day because of the relaxed and collaborative environment Metzger facilitated. Assignments were very do-able as long as you followed along with draft deadlines. Highly recommend for AWD!
This professor is very kind and great at giving feedback. I highly recommend taking this professor for AWD if you can.
He tries his best to accommodate students. He also tries his best to create a good learning environment.
Professor Metzger is very fun and very skilled in engaging students in the course material. For this course, it wasn't very difficult as long as you stay on top of work and come to class every day.
Very helpful with feedback and draft revising and super nice!! The work in this class was very interesting and engaging and I was never bored during class. Highly recommend!

I love this man. He cares so much, and really means what he is saying. He is very inspired, and because of it, you want to try as hard as you can in order to preserve his perception of academia - in all of its glory. I have never had a professor so caring and genuine. If he could teach all of my college courses I would be in heaven. Loved it all.
One of the best professors. Understanding and gives good feedback.
He is a really down to earth professor who cares how his students do.

Professor Dan is one of the best professors I've ever had at NEU! He cares about every student, and if you work hard, you will get a good grade. Although sometimes the assignments are heavy, this will definitely make you really learn something. His classes are interesting most of the time and the syllabus is clear. I 100% recommend his class!

Dr. Metzger was one of my favorite professors. I hate english, and this course was honestly very enjoyable and made me feel very confident in my writing abilities. Writing projects are structured so you won't need to get them done last minute and gives class time to work on them. Highly recommend for Advanced Writing in the Sciences (ENGW3307).

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever met in university. As a math major student, Prof.Metzger help me a lot with his patience and kind. He is the best choice!

Dr. Metzger was an amazing first year writing professor. I was expecting this to be my least favorite class, but it honestly might've been my favorite. Super chill, very understanding of any situation if you explain it to him, but you also learn a lot from what he says, the material he gives, and the feedback you get. Take him if you can!

Dr. Metzger is hands down one of the best english professors.  He is very passionate about writing and clearly has done a lot in his field of writing. He know how to structure his classes and use time well. First Year writing was a class i thought would be horrible but Dr Metzger made it one of my favorite classes.

He is the nicest and most caring professor I have ever had. He is the best. I would 1000% recommend him. He is an easy grader and has clear criteria. He is very understanding with extensions. Take this class with him plz!!

Prof Metzger is probably my favorite professor. He's understanding and caring to his students and wants the best for us. He has a good balance between strict and relaxed, but very fair. 

His online resources and schedule are always super up to date and super clear. The in-class discussions and his unique teaching style and ideology are amazing.
He is a great Professor and assigns relevant assignments that he provides great feedback for after grading.  Accessible and understanding when you email him in advance.

reviews.comment: the best professor in Northeastern
One of My favorite professors
Great feedback and informative class. He is clearly dedicated to helping his students succeed. I learned lessons in this class that I will remember throughout life because of how applicable they are.

Dr. Metzger is an excellent prof. Although he may give slightly more work than other profs who teach this class he does a great job outlining his material and making sure assigned projects are topical, interesting, and relevant to your future studies. Get to know him and participate in discussions and you will find the course well worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had a fantastic time in Dr. Metzger's first-year writing course. He was kind, compassionate, and always eager to see his students. I found his lectures engaging and each of the writing projects to be straightforward yet interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Metzger was one of my favorite professors. He is understanding of personal situations and cares alot about his students. His lectures are interesting and encourages class participation. He made me enjoy writing even though I typically hate it. I recommend taking his class; as long as you put in the effort, you will do well.

He's really nice and understanding. Gives great feedback and is very approachable outside of class to take doubts and queries. grades assignments fairly. would definitely take him again for my advanced writing class.

The class is very lecture heavy which can be boring at times but you learn a lot in the class and he gives great feedback on writing projects. You will do well in the class as long as you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tests felt very different from lectures. There were lectures where he raised his voice, which made the class uncomfortable, and several classmates I spoke to felt similarly. After exams, he would comment on low averages and say things like “I'm surprised not a single person studied,” which was insane.
Great professor, but he had to teach so much material that it made the class very difficult. He is very passionate and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: This class is hard. There is nothing wrong with the professor himself, the curriculum is what is stacked against you. Dransfield is a good teacher that seems to get a bad rep from these reviews. He is always willing to answer questions, explain things further, and is a very generous grader. He gives you everything you need to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield did everything he could to make it possible to get a good grade in this notoriously difficult class. He  is a very intelligent guy and great lecturer, he records the lectures daily, gives partial credit on multiple choice questions, and was great with curves. If you need to take chem1151, Dransfield is EASILY the best choice

Dr. Dransfield is extremely knowledgeable in his field (Got his phd in atmospheric thermochemistry from harvard) and his incredible talents are almost wasted on first year chemistry. He is a great lecturer and will debate chemistry or quantum mechanics with you all day if you want. Highly recommended for motivated students who want to learn.

This professors class was good but he talked really fast which made it hard for me to learn. He's very passionate about chem but when you don't know what's happening, he has a tendancy to make you feel silly.

My biggest advice is to study and practice problems ALL THE TIME. He did an amazing job all semester. I received a bad grade because I did not adapt to the class's difficulty quickly enough. He gives you a ton of resources and support to do well. He's a stickler for participation, so come to class with a good understanding of the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Any bad ratings from here are really outdated, because Dransfield was the GOAT. He's both energetic in lectures and easy to approach afterwards and is willing to help out anyone who shows up to office hours. Grades were curved a lot too, to the point where the average grade in the class was like a low A-.

Bad ratings for this professor are cope. This guy is the first professor at the school that I've noticed genuinely cares about his students academically and emotionally.He is disgustingly educated and a great teacher.He emphasizes LEARNING.Try your best, do what he advises you to do, and you will get an A. I didn't get an A cos I didn't listen.

I don't get all the bad ratings. Prof. Dransfield was a great professor, he explained concepts very well. The content was challenging and tests were very difficult, but he gave partial credit on multiple choice, curves were generous, and offered extra credit opportunities. If you put in the work and attend his office hours, an A is very attainable.
i always hoped the T broke down so i had a reason to miss the class and avoid hearing him yell throughout the whole lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic professor, his lectures are super helpful. Participate in class, he's more likely to help your grade if he knows you. People that don't like him just don't pay attention, I got a 64 and 71 on 2 of the 4 exams and still ended up with an A- so I hope that helps! He scales too and provides a bunch of different resources for practice.
not helpful at all. very test heavy and wouldn't let me take a day off for recitation WHICH IS A ZERO CREDIT COURSE because i had the flu.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is great at teaching and if you put the work in you can do well in this class -- even if you hate/suck at chemistry. Although, at times he can be a little belittling and rude but he also knows what kind of student he is talking to. Sometimes you will hate his class, but in the end he was a great teacher for a fast paced and difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: awesome guy. he is very enthusiastic which makes the class better. lots of content, but as long as you really try to apply yourself + understand content you'll be okay (exams curved + extra credit). he's also super understanding and helpful, but can come off as blunt or sarcastic (he means well).

Prof Dransfield is honestly one of the best professors I've had. At first he might be intimidating but if you ever go to one of his office hours you'll see he's always ready to help and knows how to explain concepts clearly. He's the best lecturer but note taking can be hard so just make sure you do that after each class. Work hard you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy and a super engaging lecturer. Raise your hand as much as you can, and don't take it personally if he says you're wrong. Lots of scare tactics at the beginning, but if you keep up with his material, it is very doable. The negative comments are understandable but blown a little out of proportion

Absolutely never take this professor. He is possibly the rudest man I have every met in my life. I do so much and nothing works. I went to office hours and he just told me I was dumb and needed help. WHAT DO U THINK IM THERE FOR SIR. I literally cried after and slightly in front of him and got no apology

I found Dransfield's class to be quite engaging, even from the perspective of a student who doesn't like chemistry. He was funny, caring, and made class fun. I would take him if you have the choice for chem professors.
Maybe the worst professor you will ever have, especially as a first year. He will berate you for asking simple questions, shame you for having a life outside of class and makes an
Single handedly the worst professor I ever had or

Professor Dransfield is a very engaging lecturer who is clearly passionate about what he does. Not sure why there are so many comments about him being condescending he might chuckle a bit if you say something silly but don't take him so personally. Gen chem here is two semesters fit into one so its a lot of work but the curve is generous.
He is clearly passionate about what he does but he's very demeaning and makes you feel terrible when you ask questions. Hard tests too.

Professor Dransfield works hard for students to understand the material, not to memorize. Exams were very difficult, but he does prepare you well for them. I strongly recommend attending all lectures and his office hours. He is more than happy to go over difficult concepts.

CHEM 1161 is notoriously tough. His exams are challenging, but if you apply yourself it is possible to do well. I'd recommend him as a prof to anyone who asked. He's a great guy. Don't be scared by any low ratings. If you show effort and grit, he'll help you get to the finish line. Best prof I've ever had hands down

He made me hate learning. 10% of your grade is attendance taken off a chemistry problem on the info you just learned. If you get it wrong you only get .5 attendance for the day. It's a hard class. He thinks it's fun to create the most difficult test possible. I could write a paper on how bad he was. If you have the option pick another professor!!

This guy cares and wants you to succeed. That being said, he needs to cram a lot of material into a very short time. It will be tough, but Dransfield knows what he's doing. His PhD is from Harvard in Atmospheric thermochemistry and he also does interesting research. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He loves his scare tactics. Be prepared for him to tell you you should drop the class; honestly, don't listen. With how he curves, it will be easy to get a b- or above if you do all the homework and attend recitation. He can seem harsh, but he cares about what he teaches. His tests are just incredibly hard and hard to prepare for. But he's good

Dransfield didn't make the class difficult, curriculum crams a lot of info into a semester, so we moved fast. Funny, explained topics very well, and ensured frequent office hours, especially closer to exams (I recommend these). Find the textbook online for free. You don't need it to do well if you took AP. Records lectures, so you can review notes.

Funny and engaging lectures, probably the best part of the class. He answers questions, but often runs behind in his plan for the lecture. However, he likes to put ambiguous questions on the multiple-choice section and makes you guess between two answer choices. This is especially annoying since the final exam is entirely multiple-choice questions.

Great lecturer and he cares about what he does, but he can be VERY condescending. Asking questions is a coin toss between getting an actual answer and being made to feel stupid for even asking it. Test averages are usually terrible but he heavily curves
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dransfield didn't make the class difficult, curriculum crams a lot of info into a semester, so we moved fast. Funny, explained topics very well, and ensured frequent office hours, especially closer to exams. Find the textbook online for free because you don't need it to do well if you took AP chem. Records lectures, so you can review notes.

I think Dransfield does a great job making chem interesting. I really liked chem and I attribute that almost entirely to Dransfield himself. That being said, he has a tendency to come off as condescending to students that ask questions that may seem obvious. If you show interest, he is willing to put in time outside of class to ensure you succeed.

If you didn't take AP Chem in hs, prepare to struggle. If you're honors/not ChemE, I would recommend avoiding taking his class for the honors credit. Interesting class, but dented my GPA. He moves fast, covers topics even outside the curriculum, and hw/recitation problems were much (purposefully) easier than the midterms/final. Be cautious.

Professor Dransfield was overall a great professor. I didn't take AP Chem so I was a little nervous. It is great that he curves the exams A LOT (about 10-20%) and the final as well. I had a B for most of the class but after recitation was added and the final, I ended with an A-. I would recommend him. It is not easy but he is ALWAYS eager to help.

While he is a good lecturer and clearly cares about what he teaches, it's impossible to ask questions or get clarification. If you don't already know the concepts don't even ask him. He'll make you feel like the most unintelligent person on the planet when answering them. I kid you not he laughed at me when I asked him a question in class.

Professor Dransfield is so passionate about his field and such a passionate & high energy lecturer. However, the first-year engineering chem class is difficult (he says this the first day). If you're fine with being challenged, Dransfield is a fantastic professor. His research is in climate science, something you will learn a lot about in his class
It's Gen Chem...what can u expect

Dr. Dransfield moves at a very quick pace, and it's really difficult to keep up at times. It's a lot of material for one semester, and he does his best with what he's given. Tests are hard, but he's always available outside of class and is really helpful one on one. Grading is also extremely fair. Showing up to class/recitation is 20% of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is amazing and he aims to challenge the best students in his class, so his exams are a bit tricky, so if you like chemistry and are good at it, go to his class, you'll find him fascinating. If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask him. He loves to answer questions both in and out of class. "Thinking is more important than memorizing."

Chem1151 was honestly the hardest class I've ever taken, but the only reason I still liked it was because of Dr. Dransfield. The content is really fast, there were four exams counting the final, and overall the class was just hard. But Dransfield was always caring, had awesome engaging lectures, and was available outside of the classroom.

Professor Dransfield is very passionate about chemistry and it reflects everyday in class. I took AP chem and decided to retake this course to get an easy A before orgo, but I was mistaken. I did receive an A but this course was very very hard. Overall I thought his lectures were very engaging and his class was my favorite this semester.

Unless you are in love with chemistry and took AP Chem, PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He teaches at such a high level and if you don't already know the concepts you will not understand. If you already took AP chem, you will enjoy his teaching pace. BUT I DID NOT UNDERSTAND A SINGLE LECTURE. Be prepared to put in a lot of effort.

Dransfield is a great guy. He's a little intimidating and blunt, but is super helpful when approached one-on-one. Tests are a little difficult, but definitely manageable. There are lengthy homework assignments each week, but they can really only raise your grade. If you can put in the time to study, you'll do well in the class.

To be honest, if you see yourself as less self-disciplined and "searching for a comfortable" person, just don't take his lecture will be much easier for you. Professor Dransfield's class requires 100% attention in class and 5-6 hours of after-school work to do well. Chemistry is hard, and getting good grades depends on self-studying.

Teaches super fast and teaches harder than the other chemistry classes. Teaches some unnecessary things and got into Orgo topics. 3 midterms and one resurrection final. Homework and participation points to get your grade up. Exams are fairly hard. You can do well in the class if you spend hours a week in the class.

Professor Dransfield is one of the most arrogant people I have come across. Instead of helping a student understand when they have question, he will automatically make you feel lesser without actually explaining anything. He can be unprofessionally aggressive when dealing with students and does not to seem to care about understanding the material.

He's arrogant, passive agressive and intimidating, which makes you not want to ask questions. Not comprehensive and there are no make ups. Even though the midterms are off class hours and online, they are very hard. At least he curves them. His lectures are heavy and he goes in a very fast pace. DO NOT take his class. avoid him at all costs.

This is the worst professor I have had in my life. He is extremely rude and is not understanding. He goes through the material as we were all familiar with it, making it intimidating when we would like to ask questions. For the midterms, they are extremely hard although he curves it at the end. Also, he has no respect for his students at all.

Take this class if you enjoy chemistry and would like a challenge. Do not take this class if you are looking for an easy A. If you take this class carefully balance out your schedule with easier classes if you can. Professor Dransfield can be intimidating and talks highly of his class, but have confidence in yourself that you are able to do well!

He is so passionate about chemistry. You're graded on participation (in-class poll everywhere), three midterm exams, a final (can replace midterm scores), weekly homework, and recitation attendance. He knows he's a hard teacher and offers plenty of extra credit and outside support. You have to engage with and stay on top of the content to do well.

Professor Dransfield works extremely hard to get through all of the material because it is so much stuff. You definitely have to have some discipline and put in hours of work outside of class. I definitely recommend a study group! There are 3 midterms but he has a resurrection final! He has office hours and so do the TAs which are extremely helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield's class is the hardest college class I've taken so far. Not having a strong chemistry background, I struggled greatly. He went so fast that I could not keep up at times. His tests are extremely difficult and I barely passed all of them. To pass this class, you must dedicate a few hours a day studying for it.

Professor Dransfield is a great professor but the class goes very fast and is pretty difficult. You should definitely devote time outside of class to studying and making sure you know the material. The tests are hard but extra credit and the weekly homework assignments help your grade. Having a background in chemistry will help you immensely.

Professor Dransfield is an efficient lecturer, he is able to convey his points easily, but he speaks too fast and the class is very difficult. His tests are also very difficult and backtracking is disabled. The only way to be adequately prepared for this class is to have taken AP Chem (I did not, and I struggled, but my friends who did did fine).
He pulls the high school teacher "I'll wait" phrase when students don't know answers to his questions within literally 10 seconds of him asking it.

for the exams and the final you had to answer the question before moving on to the next one. Also, once you submitted answers to questions, you couldn't go back and revisit. Prof thought this would prevent cheating but all it did was waste time and leave you with literally seconds left before the end of the exam.
YOU MUST GO TO CLASS IF YOU WANT TO PASS. This professor is amazing, but it will be difficult to do well if you don't study regularly and show up to all classes.

Professor Dransfield is a great guy and professor, but the course is rough. It moves at a very fast pace that he worsens by adding in unnecessary material. The exams are MUCH harder than any examples he gives. He does offer many opportunities for extra credit, which is much needed. Overall, you will learn a lot in this class but it is hard.

The lectures are so fast and very dense. You can fall behind in notes and in the class very easily. He is very enthusiastic about chemistry, so I had high hopes in the beginning. If you have a good background in chemistry, go for the challenge. But if you are not confident in chemistry, do not take. He is also extremely passive aggressive.
Sometimes when students asked questions, prof Dransfield would literally laugh in their face. He's so pretentious and passive aggressive and his exams were so unbelievably hard.

The lectures went EXTREMELY fast and we were given new material for the final TWO DAYS before the final test. The lectures contained WAY too much information and I walked out extremely confused after every class. Be prepared to do most of the learning on your own outside of class and spend 30+ hours studying for each exam to barely scrape by.

professor dransfield goes extremely fast in every lecture, theres lots of homework and often he comes off a bit pretentious in class. but if youre confused he truly wants you to understand. He really wants you to succeed in his class. keep up with lectures and do practice problems from the textbook!

He the best lecturer I have had so far in college. He is engaging, interesting, and provides helpful ways to help you understand the content. It's a lot of content, but that isn't his fault, and he does everything he can to help you. He is very accessible at office hours, answers questions very well, and will work with you until you understand.

Professor Dransfield is a dedicated professor who loves chemistry and is thorough. However, CHEM1151 is basically 2 semesters of chem in one (fast). Also, while homeworks and quizzes may be straightforward, his exams are EXTREMELY HARD. One of the hardest courses I have ever taken and I only got through with excessive studying. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield is so enthusiastic about chemistry, and it's shown throughout the lectures. He goes through units fast so study every unit thoroughly. DO NOT DO LAST MINUTE STUDYING. THE TESTS ARE DIFFICULT SO BE PREPARED. TIPS: Do well on the quizzes and HW to boost your grade. Also find a study group! Resurrection Final is the move!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield is a great professor. He is passionate and occasionally funny, and he really wants you to learn. He is put in a tough position teaching a stacked class, but he manages to get through all of the material and more. I took an honors section of the class and I don't recommend it. The tests are way harder than other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture is like drinking through a firehose. I had him for honors gen chem, and he will teach the honors section additional topics, so we go insnaely fast.. Very nice teacher, cares about people who works hard, but I think there was too much information.

Professor Dransfield is passionate about Chemistry but goes very quickly. He always says we are behind but added a new chapter to the final that is not even in the curriculum (I would've rather spent the extra 2 days on review). He is not an empathetic professor at all. Prepare to put in lots of work outside of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Dransfield is a good professor, but the amount of material he goes through is insane. Started off not liking him too much, but by the end of the class his dedication to his students really shone through. He tries to make the class as bearable as possible, but he can only do so much. Midterms are tough but bearable. Resurrection final is clutch
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher, class is tough but he makes it as easy as possible. This is my third year of chemistry, so it wasn't too hard for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Had him for an Honors section of Gen Chem for Engineers. Very enthusiastic about all the topics, but he goes through lectures VERY quickly. Homeworks are reasonable. Exams are extremely time-sensitive and fairly difficult, though he curves final grades to compensate. Also, definitely ask him questions about kinetics or global warming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He may talk fast and cover more material in a semester than seems possible, but he's a phenomenal teacher. Midterm averages are low, but mostly because people intentionally bomb them knowing they can make up for the bad grade with the resurrection final. He's a tough professor, but I learned more in this class than any other at Northeastern so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice and funny guy who has a lot of knowledge about the subject, but this class is a CHALLENGE. I study at least 25 hours before each exam and barely scoot by with a B/B- on each. Be prepared to be overwhelmed in lecture, take hours to do homework, & study your butt off. Definitely harder than other chem sections for this course. Learned a lot tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He taught so fast it was impossible to keep up. We where like 5 chapters ahead of the other section. It got to a point where he wouldnt even accept some questions because he wanted to go faster.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class average was generally around a 75 with a curve. He talks like you're watching his lecture on 2x, so get ready to write. He's super lecture heavy, with weekly HW that's about 25 Q's. I studied for 12-15 hrs per test and averaged mid-high 80s, but I'm not naturally great at chem. Wouldn't take him again, but he's a cool dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: First off- This course is VERY difficult. If you aren't already pretty comfortable with high school chemistry, prepare to be confused 90% of the time. Be aware, the professor is not very understanding.

This professor made chemistry very difficult for me to learn and to deal with emotionally. Many tears were shed because of conversations with him. I personally was not receptive to his harsh delivery at times, and I would have preferred a more understanding and compassionate professor. I will say that the homework assignments are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: THIS CLASS IS HARD! If you're taking this class prepare to have the ride of your life. There's a lot of material and the course goes by veerryy fast. Start studying on day one and I recommend watching Organic Chemistry Tutor after every lecture to make sure you understand everything from that video. He's rly nice but pls take this class seriously.

He's an incredible person, but his class is way harder than any of the other profs. Tests are incredibly difficult and not like practice problems. Lectures are great, he's very passionate about chem, and really cares about his students. A good amount of homework, but nothing crazy. Lots of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield was a good professor but his classes and tests were considerably harder than the other chemistry professors. His classes were very fast-paced but he was always in a good mood, ready to teach. Attending classes was definitely a must to do well in the course. There were lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dransfield, though new to Northeastern, is by far one of the best professors. His class is not easy, and it won't be easy. However, he is the most caring and passionate man I've met and won't let you fail as long as you put in the effort and the work. Try hard and. you will succeed in his class. Go to his office hours if you need help!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Milbauer is one of the sweetest souls I've met at Northeastern. The class discussions are very relaxed, and all opinions are welcome and appreciated. She gives slideshow review decks for the midterm and final, so doing well is very easy. There are group projects, but you get to choose what you present on.
LOVED IT! Not too hard.

She was so understanding of everything that has happened to anyone ever. Her class lectures could drag on a bit but her assignments were interesting as was the content most of the time. She would help relate what was being taught to the real world and encouraged students to share real life experiences to enhance the class.

Professor Milbauer was so sweet and caring. Her exams are very straightforward. She sends out a powerpoint of all the topics on the exam as a study guide which is extremely helpful. As long as you read the assigned chapters of the textbook, you will do good. I would take her class again!!
Such a sweet and caring professor! I would definitely take the class again.

She is the sweetest!! the class is super chill and easy, so as long as you show up (bc its apart of the grade) and participate in discussion every so often you'll be fine. Lectures can be boring but she tries her best to get everyone engaged and is extremely understanding with extra credit, deadlines ,etc.

She is so so sweet, and one of the best professors to form connections with outside of the classroom. She is so passionate about everything she talks about and creates such a welcoming environment. Highly recommend going to office hours just to get to know her.

Amazing professor who cares about each of her students. The class is not hard to get an A in, and she has clear study guides before the midterm and the final. Reading checks are just quick one question quizzes.

Prof. Milbauer is extremely thoughtful and considerate. Her class was very enlightening and wasn't difficult. She is pretty lenient and super understanding if you need an extension. The assignments are pretty spread out and she gives you plenty of notice before they're due which was very nice. Overall a great class and professor!
Great professor who cares about her students and tried to make class interesting. Would recommend taking.
She is full of energy and super relatable. You will love her if you take her!

She is so full of energy and brings that energy to each class. She is a lecture based professor but she makes sure that you understand what you need to know as well as what you dont. Her homework and assignments are very light. If you participate and pay attention in class, you will do great! I highly recommend her.
Queen. Love her, she is super sweet and understanding. Easy class too
Best professor ever. She is so nice and such a fun person to be around.

super nice prof who genuinely cares about all her students. she really tries to understand student's pov and doesn't want to create any extra stress. class itself is very easy. ur never gonna take notes cuz the lectures themselves aren't very engaging, but before the midterm/final she gives a review guide with basically everything u need to know

She is very sweet. Super passionate about topics in course, which helped me understand the course. She wants everyone to succeed and will not hesitate to explain something you're confused on. Very discussion/lecture heavy and there are group projects. Overall super awesome and I love her.

She is an amazing person and a great teacher too. Her lectures are very informative and she knows what shes talking about. She is hilarious too and the class overall has a very comfortable and chill vibe. The midterm and final arent weighed too heavy, and they are straightforward. If you pay attention in class and review the slides, you'll be fine.

Literally one of (if not the) best professors at Northeastern. She is so caring and really does want to ensure that you're doing okay in and outside of class. The exams and assignments are not challenging at all if you show up to class and have a basic understanding of the concepts. She is such a lovely human if you can take classes with her, do it
She is very passionate about what she is teaching and it is very clear. Love her.
If you can take this class with her. It was great there wasn't too much homework and she's a really nice grader
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at my time at NU! She is so accommodating and you can tell she has a lot of passion for the subject, which makes the class so much more exciting. There is a lot of reading but the reading prepares you very well for the quizzes. Class was definitely manageable, take it with Prof Milbauer if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amazing & kind professor who genuinely cares about her students. Takes attendance every class but will excuse you as long as you explain your absence. Group projects are work but easy, so are the exams. If you show up and try you will do well.

Very easy class and super nice professor. It wasn't my favorite subject material but her class was easy and enjoyable due to that. She is a very caring professor and grades pretty easily. The tests are also pretty easy.

Dr. Milbauer was the best professor I've had at Northeastern so far. She is caring and always willing to help you. Effort and participation matters a lot. Her class is really hard especially in the summer, but she knows it is hard and has a lot of measures to help you do well even if you're struggling. If you put in the work, it works out. Love her

I have never loved a professor more. She makes boring subjects interesting. She is so passionate and enthusiastic. There are a few group projects that require a decent amount of work but they aren't difficult and she provides amazing feedback. Final and midterm are very easy if you pay attention in class. Easy class but I learned so much!

The most supportive lenient professor ever. We had two presentations and a midterm and a final and then a bunch of mini easy assignments. Learned sooooo many things that were honestly so valuable for anyone especially health science majors. Take her!!

Her lectures were extremely clear and she would often use videos/media to further emphasize her points. Overall, I believe I came away from her lectures with a great understanding of all the class topics. Her exams were fairly easy and were all based on class material. In class discussions are plentiful and really helpful to further learn material.

Super sweet, kind, caring woman. This professor is one who really tries to make her class easy for you and is focused on comprehension of the material rather than flying through all of it. Most assignments are discussion posts and we had two tests and two projects. Kind of chaotic and a bit unorganized at times. She relies really heavily on her TA.

Prof Milbauer is super passionate about public health, it's very inspiring and gets you super interested in the field. Took it over the summer, so didn't get all of the usual curricula, but there was a small group project with one partner and a presentation. She is super understanding if you run into issues. Take notes! They'll help a lot for exams

A very kind professor who is there if you need help. If issues come up she is more than willing to accommodate and help you. There are a few big assignments that a decent amount of time needs to be put into, a few hours, but overall they are easy. She can be a little disorganized, but this has a small impact because of how go with the flow she is.
Super knowledgable, very understanding, makes a boring topic interesting. Highly recommend!
Hands down one of the best professors at NEU. Genuine, caring, and invested are the key characteristics of both her personal attitude and teaching philosophy.

Professor Milbauer is the most understanding and caring professor I have had at Northeastern! She is funny, inspirational, and clearly cares and supports her students. She really appreciates student input and when students participate in discussion. 10/10 recommend taking her class. Also the textbook is on Zlibrary :)

Professor Milbauer is my favorite professor I've taken so far in my first year of college. She is very understanding, caring, and funny. Her lectures are engaging and interesting, and you learn so much without it feeling overwhelming.This class requires a lot of reading, so make sure to check the syllabus for the assigned readings! Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have taken at Northeastern so far. Very understanding when it comes to deadlines. Very interesting lectures too.
Very good professor, passionate about material, real world experience in the opioid epidemic. Interesting personal anecdotes. Fair grader. Will be doing some reading but they are all interesting.
Shes very passionate about the material and grades fairly!

Just need to do two presentations, and maybe reading quizzes. But overall is easy. She is so nice and awesome. It is already the second time to take her class. We all love her and she is nice on grading as well.

I love Dessy, she's so sweet and genuinely just wants us to learn. Exams are weighted heavy BUT they're all open note and lowest gets dropped. Micro is so interesting and while her lectures can be long the content is fun and she tries to make what could be a difficult class super manageable. 100% recommend.

Dessy is the best professor I've ever had. She is so kind, all exams are open note and easy as long as your notes are detailed. Attendance is based on pollev participation so you can afford about 5 absences a semester without hurting your grade. She is super nice and understanding, 10000% take her class if you get the chance.

Basically AP Biology. Her class is easy but I really did not like her. She seems nice at first, but she consistently oversteps boundaries (like touching me to try to wake me up outside of class and grabbing my purse and trying go through it because she thought I had my phone visible?). She allows unlimited cheat sheets, though. Just annoying.
Dessy is amazing, she is very kind and understanding. Her lectures can be pretty long but she does a lot of participation activities to keep you engaged.

She's a great professor who really cares about her students. She gives a lot of HW at first but then chills out. Pretty easy class, but her grading was kind of harsh towards the middle of the semester so I was worried. She was very lenient with the final paper and presentation in the end though so it more than balanced out. I learned a lot.

I had her for bio project lab and she is a nice person and understanding, but she grades so harshly for no reason. She would take points off for no reason especially for our presentations and paper like it made no sense. Her feedback would never be consistent and she was so nitpicky.
Her exams are straightforward as they are open notes. Loved her class even though lectures were boring

So kind and made sure the class wasn't a hassle. you have to write about a paragraph a week and/or some discussion questions which are very easy but she is still forgiving if you are late. Also the best and gives really helpful advice!!
Love her. She is so caring and has amazing lectures. her tests are open notes. If you show up and study you will be fine.

I loved this class! she loves teaching and if you do your work and go to class you should be easy to pass. her tests are all open note as well. this is great if you are not good at tests and at the end of every one she gives EC points of just answering a open minded question. she drops lowest grades as well.

Prof Dessy is the best is the best professor and truly cares about her students well-being, work ethic, and overall success in her class. This class is challenging, but with going to office hours, organizing your notes, and rewatching lectures you will do great! Attendance is mandatory and heavily contributes to your grade :) Good luck!

Dessy was definitely the best professor I had this year. You can tell she is very passionate for what she is teaching and I was always was very interested in class. She explains concepts very well and the lecture slides are very organized. Some of the test questions were a bit nit-picky, so make sure you put everything on your cheat sheets.

I wasn't a fan of her teaching. She had a super condescending attitude and would rude comments in class sometimes. She was constantly changing the rules about notes allowed on tests after saying they would be unlimited at the beginning of the semester. Some people enjoyed her class, but I was not one of those people.

Dessy deeply cares about her students and wants them to pass. Exams heavy however she allows you to take notes during the exam. If you write the detailed lecture notes, passing will be easy. She is really passionate about her teaching. Attendance is mandatory and you are graded on it with your teammates.

She's one of the rare profs. that cares about their students. Not only does she want to teach (which she does wonderfully) she wants to know about you. Open note exams, very accessible; drops lowest quiz, homework, and exam. Homework and quizzes help a lot with the content. Absolutely lovely :)

Best teacher ever. Open note exams. very knowledgeable in microbiology. So nice and caring towards hwr student. offers extra credit. offers an exam drop at the end on the semester. If you have the chance to definitely take her.

Dessy had such a big class for Microbiology, but she still wanted to get to know each of us personally. Participation in her class matters; you are going to get graded on your individual participation and your participation in your group. Tests are open notes and open internet. If you have the chance to take a class with Dessy, I recommend!
Long but interesting lectures. Exams are open-note. Two online quizzes per week. Participation is mandatory. Love this class and would recommend!
Professor that really cares for her class and everyone understanding the material. It is a lot of assignments, but they are all very helpful for understanding the material.

Professor is one of the few good professors at Northeastern. Her class is very heavy complex but it is not difficult. She drops the exam and it's four exams once you are happy with your grade. You do not have to take the final if you are passing. She does assign quizzes online before every lecture and homework once a week but it's easy. Very easy A

Extremely cool and knowledgable. Make sure to be a bit familiar with the chapter and lecture slides before the lecture so it's easier to follow along. I also highly recommend reading the textbook along with the lecture slides because you'll understand the concepts a lot better if you read the textbook.
Funny awesome dude. Super underrated and hope he continues to teach investments, as all the other investments professors suck. If you test well this class will be light.
pls drop this class immediately. Very strict professor. mental torture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: A very lecture-heavy course, but she expects that everyone learns most of the information out of class. She is also a very specific grader and very particular about following her guidelines exactly. She is really strict about attendance and participation. There are two overall exams that are online, one in class and one take-home.

She is an okay teacher (despite what other reviews said), and I I thought she was nice. Although I will say she almost never gives As on stuff (always something silly like 3.8 out of 4) and her lectures are not engaging, but overall the class is fine. Two tests, lots of hw, some group projects, but mostly easy.

I don't understand all the bad ratings. She gave one take-home exam with a clear grading format, lots of individual work, and no final. The only thing was that she gave us one in-person proctored exam, but she gave us a study guide and lots of materials with open notes. Not bad at all, and she is very nice and accommodating, 2 exams worth 10% each

The content of this class is not of personal interest which might have influenced my rating, but the lectures are confusing with weirdly organized slides and she has an irrelevant assignment every class for each table group. The worst part she rarely gives full score on any of the assignments, including participation so forget an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not listen to any of these reviews. This class is minimal work and prof is so sweet. It is extremely hard to do bad in this class. Both tests are online. The only thing that may affect your grade are the HW analysis but it is just really hard to get an A. With that being said I have not received lower than a B on one. TAKE THIS CLASS I PROMISE.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: the worst class ever actualyl pointless and has NOTHING TO DO WITH MY MAJOR. so much work for no reason i couldnt care less about computers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst. How is this her primary job? She's reading stuff of her slides. I just hope she retires and spares future students the torture.
Good professor
There are likely better options out there.
dry lectures & grades aren't rounded up.
What a bore! She really needs to reevaluate her career choices. Currently the worst professor I had and probably the worst professor I'll ever have.

Lots of small writing assignments, and you need to make sure to specifically follow her writing format. (Bullet points only, no big paragraphs). Lectures were overall not super interesting, and there was a lot of groupwork throughout the class. The 3 tests are all online, and I think that she grades lighter on you if she likes you, so participate
I'm convinced that all her positive reviews are written by her. Such a terrible professor whose lectures are a snooze fest. I've got a good grade, but didn't learn anything at all. What a joke.

such a sweetheart in the class. can be a mix of lectures and group work in the class (i hated the group work). 3 tests which are all online and 1 final project and assignments were sometimes difficult to understand since she wanted specific requirements (no paragraphs, but bullet points instead). only annoying thing is she kept us overtime.
She is super sweet and definitely appreciated if you make any sort of effort to participate, certainly recommend her!
Decent class, but she definitely favored some groups over others when grading group projects

She is such a sweetheart! Despite the reviews, her grading really isn't that tough if you make sure your responses are thorough and you follow her format. DO NOT write case studies or discussions in paragraph form. Also make sure to participate, because that grade really matters to her. Overall, the course was easy if you follow instructions.

Although professor soule can be a very tough grader, the class is not super difficult. So long as you do the assignments on time and put effort into it, as well as attend class and participate, it should be an easy A-. She is a very kind professor and cares about what she teaches. Just put in the effort and you'll be fine.
dry lecturer, but the class is okay. there is a lot of HW that are reading assignments and quizzes on it. Tests are not too hard if you study the case analysis well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nice person, but an extremely dry lecturer and does not teach well. She barely explains concepts in class, and spends the entire time explaining complex concepts we were rarely tested on. You are expected to read the textbook and know everything before classes, which makes you question what you're paying for.

Don't expect an A, because she does not give any. You will not learn anything helpful in this class. Almost all of the topics are outdated, and only the surface is scratched for each subject. Attendance is mandatory, but either way, no one is paying attention. B+ is very easy to get as long as you put minimal effort into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice professor but unclear guidelines on written material make it impossible to improve after she gives you 80s on every case study which is worth most of your grade. Even if you talk to her in person she is still vague with how she wants you to complete the assignments. If you want an A in this course don't take her.

Dry lectures which feel outdated, have few examples, and just dull material, and still expect participation in every class. Papers every week and 2-3 small quizzes every week. Begins the class by saying A is basically not attainable, and she stayed true to her words; no one got an A. Very demotivating thing to start with. Never curves.
DO NOT TAKE HER! Her lectures are not engaging and her grading is very unclear. You will never get an A in this class because she does not give them. Stay away from this class if you can.
sometime take attendance. She covered lots of material without digging further, literally learn nothing from her class. lots of quizzes and boring classes.

Very lecture heavy in class but she likes to include some group discussions a few times a week. She wants you to read a chapter of the book every few days, but you can get by withtout reading. There are case studies as assignments every week, which are not difficult just very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: WARNING:DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!A lot of case studies and she grades harshly, providing little feedback. No one ever gets 5/5, highest always 4.4/5 when they're worth ~25% of your grade. 2 tests that were also very difficult w/ questions unclear/broad. You need at least a 94 to get an A so not only does she grade hard, you also need to work harder.

very average professor. my biggest gripe was how slow she was with grading and a bit unclear on her criteria. when she did provide feedback though, it was decent. she tried her best to make class engaging, even though it usually didn't work. they're revamping this course though so hopefully it's better whenever you take it.

Grade based on Individual + group case studies, chapter quizzes, 2 exams + Capstone assignment. Exams are kind of confusing, they follow the case study format and aren't multiple choice. You'll do well if you follow the case study format. Lectures are kind of confusing but she is super sweet and will help if you ask her. Quizzes aren't difficult.
This class is hard, and this professor makes it harder. Don't ever take it. I prepared so much before every class, but still confusing what the professor is talking.

Professor Soule is a nice lady, but a horrid grader.The material is given from the text and is supported using case studies. She doesn't offer individual corrections so that one may learn,rather she posts broad guidelines. The exam I took was the broadest, most unclear exam ever.Little to zero instructions were given. No one knew what was expected.

a lot of quizzes but its easy, a ton of individual and group case studies that she grades really hard on and doesn't provide individual feedback so you have no clue what you did wrong, very condescending, doesn't respond to emails, tests are stupid hard. i learned nothing. thank god this isnt my concentration.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Soule was very kind and always available to answer questions. She valued student feedback and worked very hard to make this boring material engaging and encourage conversations about the material. If you used vocabulary and frameworks she presented in class you can get an A on every assignment.

Prof Soule is kind and enjoys what she teaches. Unfortunately she does not know how to teach undergraduate students business statistics. She rarely does examples in class, you have to figure everything out by yourself, is unclear, and if you arent an expert with excel youre in major trouble. She made the class more difficult than it needed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Handed a lot of case studies, seldom get feedback.

He's kind of condescending towards students in class and just constantly talks about other students for some reason. He rambles a lot about unimportant stuff. I'm not a fan of his teaching style. He does not post notes online in the big 2026. The only reason this is not a 1 is that the practice tests actually help a lot with the tests in the class.
He is fun to rage bait

He is very enthusiastic about math. He explains content very well and also gives visual explanations of concepts. His exams are very similar to the practice problems he gives, so it's easy to get a good grade. Attendance is mandatory but his lectures are very good and helpful.

I can definitely understand the bad reviews he gets, but for me personally he was a great professor. It was funny asf when he yells at people when they're on their phones during class or when he gets passionate about the material, but otherwise his grading structure of 4 tests + the final was really good as someone who's strong with tests.

Professor Lang is definitely enthusiastic about math but I feel that most would say his teaching style was not effective. He doesn't come across as approachable and often complains about students in class. He spends way to much time on proofs and things you don't need to know, but if you understand the practice exams you'll be fine.

He shouts at us like we're misbehaving children, and very frequently complains about students in general mid-lecture. He yells at us for answering, not answering, or asking questions. He will scoff if someone enters late or leaves on time (if he goes over time). He shouts about anything and everything, like he's trying to teach through a hurricane.

Professor Lang really cares about math, and is very enthusiastic in his pedagogy. However, this tends to come across as him being quite loud and dry, drilling in basic concepts for an excessive amount of time.

I would not recommend this professor at all for MATH 1215. I did not learn anything from his lectures, and he overcomplicated everything, I had to get a tutor who was my saving grace this semester. He answers questions very condescendingly in class. The only good thing is that the quiz reviews typically match the quiz format.

Prof. Lang is a pretty good teacher and is ready to teach. Attendance is mandatory. If you're a bad test taker, I wouldn't recommend this class, because 88% of your grade is composed of the finals and tests, the rest being attendance. He teaches super quick, so missing just one lecture will leave you behind.

He has a loud voice and yells a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the best teacher of all time but he has his charm. He's always dripped out with his suit and tie and also loves proofs (that you do not need to know, but proofs are important, so go to class and watch him ramble). Get ready for mental math because no calculator is allowed. Pay attention when he does examples and you'll do fine.

Professor Lang is crazy to the point where you'll either really excel or fail with him as a professor. His boisterous personality makes it extremely challenging for classes to be productive. Asking him to explain an idea will always either end in further confusion, or him berating the person who asked, or both.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lang is not a chill dude beware he likes to yell a lot he is VERY PASSIONATE abt his calculus. He complained all semester that no one showed up but thats because his lectures are super fast paced and he spends way too much time going over proofs of equation rules in calc then examples very confusing. But he wasn't too bad I did good go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lang is the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures are just him screaming at a projector about unrelated content, and then berating anybody who asks questions about what we're actually tested on. You have  to teach yourself the entire course. The final was incredibly hard and over stuff we barely touched on. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this course if you are looking for a considerate professor. Lang will belittle anyone who asks questions and is completely condescending in emails. This is an easy course, with practice tests modeling actual midterms. He just isn't kind!

David Lang is the worst professor I have ever had. He is condescending and rude, berating students for asking questions. His policies/grade weighting make it difficult to do well in his class. I highly recommend you find another professor if you are not extremely gifted in math and can follow along with convoluted explanations of complex topics.
Will race through lectures, but his tests are very similar to the practice ones he posts. Might get upset about a dumb question, but is very willing to help at office office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His tests are pretty fair. He will yell at you if you ask him a ‘stupid' question. Someone literally asked him what the test was on and he yelled at them for not listening during class. Also, trigger warning, he randomly emphasizes words throughout his sentences (low key keeps me awake). Other than that, he scares me a little.
The best teacher I ever met.
He's the best teacher who taught calculus, he's extremely knowledgeable and care about his stundets.

Professor Lang is overly passionate about math to the point where he refuses to slow down and explain concepts to people who are struggling. In fact he has no issues yelling at and berating you for simply asking for clarification on often time confusing topics. Save yourself ghe headache and never take any of his classes.

Professor Lang is very passionate about the content that he teaches, and because of that, he tends to overcomplicate the course material, leaving many students confused. He moves at a very fast pace. If you ask questions, he will berate you. If you understand the examples he covers in the lecture, you will do well on the exams. There are no tricks.

Professor Lang is great. His quizzes are just like what he goes over in class. He moves pretty quickly and what he covers in class isn't exactly like what's in the textbook or on the exam. He's hilarious without meaning to be.

Overall a great professor, you may need to spend more time after class on this course. The only issue is that the concepts taught in class were not so sufficient for the final exam and it made me feel a bit worried.

Prof Lang's lecturing style is clear and fast-paced. He tends to scream with excitement and loves to talk about how important math is. I think if he just lectured and gave homework the course would be great. Sadly, the tests were insanely difficult and graded harshly. He won't be everybody's favorite prof, but you will probably learn a lot!

Prof. Lang's lectures are unhelpful and he will yell or talk down to you if you ask questions. I spent his lectures frantically copying down his notes, not absorbing the information. His communication style is ineffective and if you dare to ask a question, he will not reframe the idea but will reiterate what he said. Worst professor I've had.

Prof. Lang was very passionate about his studies in math theory and this was evident in his lectures. While I hated taking Math Reasoning, as a professor, Lang had multiple office hours and was always eager to explain math to anyone. I wouldn't take him again because he's very intense but that isn't necessarily a bad thing for everybody.

Prof. Lang is amazing. Although he sometimes gets a little too passionate about his work, he always explains everything clearly and gives plenty of examples to help him understand the material. Tests are always straight to the point and if you do the homework and review problems, you will do amazing. Great professor overall.

Lectures are very fast and you're given very little time to actually understand what he is saying. He is very passionate about math but it isn't easy to keep up with his pace. Also, the screen he uses for lectures tends to be blurry more times than not.
L professor
don't take it if you don't have to, he makes class difficult because he gets to passionate and doesn't really answer questions well.

Everything you need to know you will learn in lectures so go to class. In class examples are similar to his test questions so just know how to do the in class examples. Grade is based off of 6 tests and a final that's worth 40% of your grade so if you don't test well good luck. He likes to teach and you can tell and is willing to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Lang is extremely passionate about his job. He will not dumb down any concepts for you, and will rather tend to berate you for not understanding. He gets extremely passionate and loud during online lectures, which makes it difficult to focus on the content being taught.

Lang is an awesome teacher. Had him for calc two, the class was 4 tests and a final. Its kind of scary since each test is 15% of your grade and the final is worth 40. But honestly, his practice exams are just like the real test, and the examples he does in class are also extremely useful and similar. Crazy enthusiastic and loves math.

Professor Lang is very passionate about math and wants to share it with his students. His lectures are fast paced an in-depth, but he gives the opportunity to ask questions. He gives plenty of optional hw. His test review sheets are almost identical to exams. He is a fair professor - did horrible on my first exam, but Lang did everything to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lang is the best professor I have had at Northeastern so far. He prepares students very well for midterms and provides separate canvas PDF homework problems that are very helpful. I would highly recommend Lang to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The zoom classes didn't work for me. He is very rude.

Having previously taken a similar formal logic class, I found this class to be fairly easy. This was partially thanks to Lang's clarity and thoroughness when explaining different concepts. My primary complaint regarding the structure of this class is that your entire grade comes from only four exams, with the final accounting for 40% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A real one
Read the textbook, easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor with ok lectures. No graded homework, grade comes only from midterms and final. If you want a prof that is going to guide you every step of the way and hold your hand, find a different prof. If you want a prof that will help you as needed, and not have constant homework deadlines, lang is the man. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Highly recommend him for diff eq/linear algebra.

Professor Lang has high energy for the class and its amazing. He lays out a clear class agenda with grading consisting of weekly quizzes and the 3 main exams. He spends class time going over problems that will likely be on quizzes/tests, so you will never get tested on an unfamiliar problem. The class is fairly easy and he is lenient with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Lang is absolutely insane (about math). Bottom line is, he loves math. His class is very easy, but is teaching is meh. He still uses one of those camera feeds to display his paper from his desk onto the board and he will not attempt technology; he swears by it. "Technology is messy, but math, math is clean. Straight forward. Perfect" -Lang2k19

Great professor who is really passionate about what he teaches and tries to get his students on the same level, although he can be a bit intimidating, as he has a loud voice and more energy than you'd expect for a math professor. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll probably be worse off for skipping. Overall not a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This guy lives and breaths math. I don't know if you'll find a professor more into his material than Professor Lang. He's got a bit of a mad scientist vibe to him, can definitely be kind of zany. Very good at explaining clearly and making sure everyone is on the same page, but almost always loses track of time. Definitely recommend him for Diff. Eq

He preaches as he teaches. Really helpful outside of class, will give extra problems for you to do if you need some extra help. Quizzes every week like other calculus classes but the questions are related to the homework. Prof Lang keeps it straight forward, but don't expect the tests to be easy though! GREAT PROFESSOR!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Lang is a good choice for anyone that is looking to take Calc 2. Although he moves quick, he clearly explains all the concepts with plenty of examples that follow (similar to what is seen on quizzes/exams). It's important to attend lecture and although he assigns problems to do in the textbook, I found the problems on handouts to be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the more interesting calc 2 teachers. You can tell he wants everyone to succeed and provides all the means to do so. He can get a little lost in his own explanations and derivations, but there's always a joke in there.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Lang prepares you well for assessments and wants you to do well. He's eccentric, but once you get past it, he's a good professor. Explains things thoroughly. The final comes out of nowhere, but it's doable.

David Lang was by far the best maths teacher I have had. After struggling in maths through high school, I grew a disliking towards maths. However, after the first few weeks with Prof. Lang, I have significantly improved and regained my liking for math. He is very clear and precise with the work and quiz/test schedule.

On the first day of class, I have to admit, I was a little intimidated. But David is a great professor. He knows really his stuff. If you pay attention in class and do a little bit of homework, it shouldn't be very difficult to get an A. He's also a nice guy, and will occasionally crack a calculus joke here an there. He loves math.

I had him for clac 1 and he was a good very clear professor. He goes fast in the lectures so if you have no calc experience the class will probably be hard but if you have some then it will be easy. The quiz's are really easy and he gives one every week and he drops the lowest two. If you have a question in class he'll answer it.

Great professor. Loves math but is not a people person (although he is willing and available to help). He talks really quickly and the class is fast-paced. You should have a background in calc and be decent in basic algebra. Would definitely take again for a math course.

He never collects homework, which is a huge benefit, but it is fairly necessary to really understand what's going on.  He can be hard to take seriously because of his ill-fitting suits and very thick accent.  A solid background in calculus is also really important.
Good
Great teacher, way too excited about math.
He is an awesome professor.

I would recommend some experience in calculus before taking this class. He adores calculus and really knows his stuff, but he does not dumb it down (he regularly made me feel stupid for not understanding "BASIC ALGEBRA!" as he put it). Despite this, however, his review sheet made quizzes easy. You may find his ill-fitting suits  distracting...
Excellent guy. Knows his stuff. Just make sure you take notes and do the homework.

He likes calculus more than he likes people, but he's very enthusiastic and clear about every topic. Always available for office hours to help out and answer questions. Moves through topics pretty quickly, but the quizzes are not bad at all as long as you do the hw problems.

Great professor for Differential Equations. Very clear, very knowledgeable. I've never seen anyone so passionate about math.  Hands out review sheets before each quiz.  I never felt under prepared for the tests.  Highly recommend.
I got an A with lots of learning. She was always friendly. Would recommend if you want to learn something.

Prof. Yang is a dedicated instructor with well-structured courses and lenient grading (I got 2 As). Her assignments promote real learning, and she encourages AI use for skill development. She is responsive, offers research opportunities, and provides valuable academic guidance, though lecture presentations could be more summary & interactive.

Nit-picky grading. SPSS is challenging software to use, minimal class time is dedicated to it, and projects require its use. I agree with a previous review that she is kind, but her classroom practices are not. Two tips: she doesn't care much about prose quality and adds additional extra credit during the term.

While Professor Yang is knowledgeable in her field, I found her teaching approach hard to follow. The workload was excessive, and course material was not always digestible. Many students, myself included, were accused of academic dishonesty over (correct) midterm answers. This experience left me feeling discouraged in the learning process.

Loved the class. Lecture on Tuesday, quiz on Friday (only content from Tues). Also labs/tutorials on graphing on Friday that basically help you finish lab assignment. Alternates between lab assignment (visualization tied to question(s)) or a reading + discussion post. She gives a lot of opportunity for extra credit. Drops lowest quiz score. Loved
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class
