reviews.comment: Very by-the-book, but still kind. Many opportunities for extra credit; like so many. Class content isn't difficult, there's just a lot of content. Could be more understanding/flexible, but also does what she can without going out of order if that makes sense. Sufficient amount of assignments to be graded from.

Very kind and understanding. Class was at 8AM, but the content was delivered well. She really wants you to do well. She's kinddd of intimidating but it's because she's so organized and objective. I honestly loved her and the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and don't take this class if you can help it. Professor can't convey the material well and doesn't properly answer questions. She's nice when you approach her, but her classroom practices are not.

I tried to give the benefit of the doubt, but the instructors lectures are confusing to follow. She never answers questions, she is unforgiving as far as late assignments and life events go. She seems kind, but her practices as a professor make you forget that. People have lives outside of school and she is not willing to work around it.

Took this class for INSH 6500 for the criminal justice graduate program. I would not recommend this class. It is incredibly R heavy, the midterm is timed with an R portion to it and long complicated theory questions. Homework is very time consuming and intense.

Unclear grading scheme and feedback. Pre-recorded lectures were tedious and hard to follow. If you didn't understand something in the in-class lecture, you were left behind. Prof often refused to answer questions.
Class avg. was ~70 for the midterm and ~60 for the final, fortunately, she offered a lot of extra credit to bring the grade up.

Unorganized and long lectures. Confusing instructions with errors. Incoherent lab notes. Assignments were challenging and took hours. Professor is unwilling to cooperate with the students. Please do not take this class, I literally did not learn a single thing.
Not much HW, the instructions are not clear, professor herself doesn't know what she is teaching. The class is super boring. Midterm was hard. The lecture was not clear. Horrible class

Dr. Dan was a good professor, only thing that annoyed me was mandatory attendance, although he did allow up to 6 free absences. Tests are tough but manageable if studied a bit in advance for. Very available with office hours and his TAs are great. Would recommend, but make sure you spend a good amount of time outside of class as well studying

He shows you the "why" rather than HOW to solve the problems. I basically taught myself how to do the problems, and I got a tutor. He gives you free points for attending class and recitations, and homework is graded on completion. Homework and Aktiv don't help with the exams, but they're good for basic practice. Practice exams were unhelpful too.

Overall he was a really nice guy, but the tests were pretty difficult and largely concept based. It is important to learn why things work the way they do and how overall as well as the math. Doable class!

Dr. Dan was an amazing professor. Some of his exams were a bit difficult, but if you study well you should be fine. Sometimes the Aktiv problems were a bit funky, but helpful if you really study the material.
Lectures are misleading and not helpful for actual exams, which are so difficult and not like any of the practice he gives you. Is nice but not a good professor, I'd avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I genuinely think he's a really nice guy who cares about his students and is very passionate. However, in class, you focus more on why something is the way it is rather than actually using or applying the formulas, etc for a test. So homework is basically you teaching yourself chemistry. The tests are pretty different from class problems
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Practice problems are so different from test
Never curves even when tests are hard
No empathy for students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really awesome professor. Never took chemistry before, but he helped me understand everything. Even when I bombed a test, I still felt proud of what I learned, and I eventually improved. Gives lots of extra credit on exams, has good policies, and tries to help you succeed. Just a really great professor to have, especially for such a hard course.

Very caring and fair professor. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and cares about their wellbeing. Easy to get help outside of class. Tests are a bit difficult and require critical thinking but he gives 3 extra points on every test. Lots of homework but ample time to complete it. Only critique: study guides often didn't match actual tests.
He was such an amazing chem professor. He made the concepts seem so simple and was so nice. The homework wasn't too bad, just a little tedious.
loved him! just do the homework and go to office hours if needed

Very kind and accessible and a great, great professor (like the best I've had thus far). Material was tough but if you come to lecture and go to office hours he's great at explaining things. Also gives extra credit and practice problems on Aktiv are super helpful on exams, and he'll replace your lowest midterm score so a good grade is very feasible

Super kind and caring, and great at teaching (like the best I've had yet). The material is hard but going to lectures and office hours made it seem very simple. Very feasible to succeed in the course if you put effort in, he also gives extra credit which is nice and will replace your lowest midterm exam grade.

If you're taking CHEM1161, take it with Dan Matthew. I would recommend the chem ramp up (it was extra credit but it was actually helpful). An A is totally achievable by completing all the homework (unlimited tries) and studying using the practice exams and aktiv problems. Of course, try your best to stay proactive the class can move fast at times.

The actual goat. I had zero chemistry knowledge coming in and finished with an A, and that's all thanks to Dr. Dan's teaching! Take notes on the homework, study the practice exams, and focus on what you're struggling with. Also the ramp up is helpful if you have no idea (like me) what to expect coming into a chem course. Thank you!!!

I would absolutely recommend Prof Matthew for gen chem!! If you attend class regularly and do the homework assignments you'll be set up for success in his class. He's a good lecturer and easy to follow, he takes notes during class that you follow along on. Attendance is mandatory, but he allows a couple of absences. He's also super nice :)

By far the best Chem professor I have ever had! He cares about how the students are learning more than grading, and his lectures really made me understand the concepts so much more clearly. Plus, he gives many opportunities for extra credit. Recitation can feel like more of a chore but you get a bump up in your grade if you go to all of them.

BEST PROFESSOR SO FAR! I was so worried about taking a good chem professor because the class can be difficult, but what you put in is what you get out. Biggest advice is follow along lectures, and you will be perfectly set. I went to almost all office hours and he bonded with all the students, taking hours out of his week and day to help. love him!

DAN MATTHEW AKA THE BEST PROF EVER!!!! He is an amazing professor. He really knows how to teach. He gives 4 midterm exams and a cumulative final exam. If you score higher on the final than one of your midterms he will replace your lowest midterm grade with the final exam grade. He gives tons of practice and is willing to meet with you anytime!

I LOVE DR.DAN! He is one of the best professors I've had here at Northeastern. His lectures are straightforward and the activ practice questions he gives really help for his exams. He really helped me enjoy chemistry and solidify concepts that I forgot in high school. If you understand the material well, the exams should be straightforward.

Dr. Dan is the best! If you're taking chemistry, definitely try to take it with him. He takes notes with the class, so the lecture stays at a good pace. He's willing to reexplain anything if a student is confused. He's so easy to reach outside of class and his office hours are very useful.

I love this man. So amazing at seeing what works and does not work for students and changing his teaching style around that. There were so many resources for the exams. He is so kind and very approachable at office hours. You will always get 100 on the hw because you get unlimited tries.
Good professor and makes the most out of lectures. Notes are really helpful, and going to his office hours are too.

Cool dude. Genuinely cares about his students understanding the course content. This slows down his lectures heavily, but he helped me actually learn some things I had memorized and forgotten in high school. Though while the material was often familiar and low-level, his tests reached into dimensions class time couldn't dream of.

Take him for Gen Chem! He can be reached outside of class and really cares about his students. Also, instead of having slides for his lecture, he writes out his notes along with his class, so it goes at a natural pace. He structures his class with the textbook (not essential), but you do have to purchase Aktiv (practice problems). Overall, great!

Challenging for those uncomfortable with chemistry. He did not curve any exams but he gave extra points at the end of them. If you make a good-faith attempt, but come up with a D by the end of the semester, he will boost your grade so you will pass. He is a safe bet, but the other professor did curve exams which would've been extremely useful.

Dan is one of few professors I've had who genuinely cares about students. If anything were to happen, whether its falling behind, simply sleeping in, or an emergency, he's gracious and understanding. Chemistry is not easy but he taught it well. Homework and class work is easy to get 100s on despite the tests being difficult, so avg grade is boosted

Dr. Dan cares a lot about his students and wants you to succeed. He provides a lot of study/review resources for exams. I liked his teaching style too-- he walks you through the notes/example problems on his iPad. Highly recommend!
Dr. Dan was an amazing teacher. He did a great job at explaining the material in a simple way. He also gave us tests from the previous semesters to help us prepare for exams, which was super helpful.

Overall the class was pretty good. I like his lecture style (he writes his notes in notability) and he cares a lot about his students. The one thing I did not like was how he stated he purposely wanted the tests to be harder. Better than other professors for gen chem.

Dr. Dan is a fantastic professor. You can tell he really cares about his students by how he always stops to answer questions. His tests are very reasonable and have questions that appear in the homework.

If you want to have a (fairly) easy time in gen chem take it with Dr. Dan. I withdrew from chem class my 1st semester and thought just I wasn't cut out to understand the material. That all changed with Dr. Dan. He's a great lecturer and cares a lot about his students. He's very personable and hosted in-person review sessions before every exam.

I liked his teaching style (actively writes out notes during lecture) and his tests were fair. He is generous with partial credit. An etextbook and 2 online accounts are required to be purchased for this class.

dr dan is a tougher prof than people say - he even prefaced this semester by saying he knew on rate my prof he was known to be easy, but he's not anymore. this class isn't impossible, lectures are good (though a bit rushed), he's amazing with extra credit on tough exams. my biggest piece of advice? stay on top of lectures and USE THE TEXTBOOK.
I was not a fan of the way he lectures. His notes were not conducive to review after class. he also mentioned that his goal is to make his exams harder than past semesters.

Great professor, despite his tests being a bit challenging. Writes his notes with the class, making it easy to understand and visualize. His practice tests were not like the actual exams in terms of difficulty, but if you understand the material you should be fine if you study outside of class. Great guy, super nice and approachable.

Dr. Dan was fantastic! Such a caring individual who puts in the effort for you if you are willing to do the same. Exams were slightly difficult, but as long as you prepare with the resources he provides, you should succeed.

great, intelligent professor with riveting lectures on fascinating content. very engaging and allows abstract concepts to make sense. 
class moves very fast DO NOT fall behind, exams do not match up to practice tests or problems in terms of difficulty. exams are tricky and challenging. hard to earn a good grade. deep concept knowledge guaranteed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Dan during spring 2023 and he was one of the best professors I've had here! His lectures were so helpful. He usually takes notes while teaching in front of the class and makes them accessible for everyone at any time. Notes are clear and everything on the tests will be stuff that has been in the lectures. He's genuinely a great guy too!

He started off the year strong and was a great prof. He made chemistry understandable. However, his exams are way harder than they need to be. He said he purposely made them harder than past exams. He often would recognize that they were harder then they needed to be b
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dan's pretty easy. 3 exams before the final and attendance is mandatory but he takes attendance by giving out a code at the beginning of class so if you have friends in the class it is helpful. The exams are pretty easy but get harder as the semester goes on just because of the material. He posts all his notes online so it should be fine.

Awesome guy, made me love Chemistry after I hated it in hs. Honestly a very nice dude that goes over all the content clearly in his lectures and his tests are all very fair. If you show up to class and do HW then you will be fine, he also gives out a lot of extra practice problems that prepare you well for the tests.

I dreaded chemistry coming into college but Dan has made my chem experience amazing. His lectures are clear, not overwhelming or over complicated. Would 100% take him if you think chem is not your best subject because he makes the material understandable. VERY generous when grading exams. Exams are difficult and long but manageable.

Wonderful professor. Reminder, always go to his lectures, unless you want to miss a TON of materials. Class pace was incredibly fast but his lecture and explanation were super detailed. Exams are VERY DIFFICULT but very fair. Get ready to study a lot for this course, and if you do you will learn a lot and in good shape.

Prof. Matthew is an amazing lecturer. Instead of slideshows, he opens up pages in notability & writes notes with you which is a much more effective way of learning/teaching chemistry. His tests are also fair, simply practice & make sure you fully understand important concepts (conceptual questions are asked). There is also always a bonus question!

Dan is super approachable, and knowledgeable about chemistry. His office hours and extra help sessions were helpful, and he posted lots of practice problems. It wasn't all good though, he would say his class was too easy in past semesters and purposely made exam questions more difficult or trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although I really enjoyed his lectures, his exams tended to be extremely difficult. He does give practice exams before every exam, and when I would take those, I would get high 90s. Then when it came to the actual exam, the questions would be different formats and would ask you to do things that were never taught in class.

Dan is great at explaining. Only thing I would say is that they can word some test problems weirdly, and it just throws me off. I don't understand why they can't just clearly state open response questions. Other than that, great professor, there were 3-4 exams + 1 final. Go to class, do your homework, and study a lot, and I think you'll do well.

Professor Matthew is a great professor. He explains concepts very clearly and cares a lot about his students and the subject. Tests were not too difficult as long as you studied, and the weekly homework assignments had unlimited attempts, so they were good practice.

DAN SLAYS but it was a difficult course due to the material. As long as you stay on top of the homework and do the practice exams you will do good.Dan is really caring and his office hours help a lot.
As long as you put the work in you can get a decent grade.

Expectations are very clear. Most of the class finished with an A- or an A. Lectures are easy to follow and he makes the concepts easy to understand. Go to the class the week of Thanksgiving for extra credit!!

Dr. Dan is amazing! He is very clear about grading. There were 3 midterms and the final exam. Participation is mandatory and he gives weekly homework assignments. He explains everything so clearly and always answers questions.

Dan is such a great teacher. He makes concept very simple to understand. His office hours are very helpful.   Exams are fair and he post a lot of practice exams/questions (+ easyy bonus points on every exam). Attendance is mandatory every day which is meh. Other than that, no other complaint, loved the class and the teacher.
I love Dan!!! Everyone loves him. He makes the information so understandable and you can tell he really cares. He is very accessible outside of class.

Professor Matthew made general chemistry a breeze! I hadn't even thought about chemistry since sophomore year of high school and he made everything engaging and easy to understand. He posted practice exams that were almost identical to his tests. Class averages were consistently above 80%. Every test has a bonus question for extra credit.

Overall, the class is not too hard, he teaches well, the only complaint is sometimes it is frustrating that class is mandatory especially if you have taken a course like physics already and know some of the material.

explains everything in a way that's easy to understand and will take the time to make sure you understand topics. assigns weekly homework but it can normally be completed in about an hour. tests are very fair and he gives you points whenever he's able to on non-multiple choice problems
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Probably the best instructor I've ever had - take Dan if you can! He is very clear and lectures while he projects his own notes which is super clear. Fair grading, accessible, and great explanations. I took chem in high school but this class has left me with a totally higher level of understanding.
You can just tell he really care about his students and how they do. He is very reasonable with grading and genuinely teaches well. I would take more of his classes for sure
Took Chem1161 from him in Spring 2022, very easygoing and is a very fair grader. Super accessible outside of class and does his best to make sure all of his students learn the course material

I loved professor Matthews' class. I had such a hard time with chemistry in high school, but he made me enjoy it. There's weekly homework assignments (they're fairly long), 3 midterms, and a final (score will replace your lowest midterm grade), as well as attendance in lecture and recitation that goes into your grades. Work hard and you'll succeed!

Professor Matthews is the best professor I have had so far at Northeastern. He gives amazing lectures and makes sure students thoroughly understand content, and is always available outside of class for help. He also only tests on what he lectures, so there are no surprises on his exams. For new chemistry students I couldn't recommend him more!

Amazing professor! I hated chem back in high school but he made the class enjoyable and he taught concepts extremely well. He is always willing to help and there are many different tasks that make up your grade, so it's not just based on exams. Take the class, you won't regret him as a professor.

Take this class! Dr. matthew makes all the material very interesting and does a great job explaining it, he also uses his ipad to write lecture notes during class which makes it easy to keep up. Clear grading and gives a good amount of partial credit. Weekly homework assignments and exams make up most of the grade.

Really good teacher! He explains concepts very well and is always willing to help and answer questions. Also a really nice guy. He gives fun bonus questions on tests like, "What's your favorite place to go in Boston?" and they're usually worth a lot of points. Chem is hard and you do need to study, but he makes it a lot easier and more fun.

Wonderful professor, his lectures are very clear and easy to follow. If you struggled with chemistry take him, as he takes the time to explain theoretical concepts. I would definitely take a course with him again.

Dr. Dan was a really good professor for gen chem. He took the time to explain the concepts in class through his interesting teaching style which is writing on his iPad and we copy down notes. His tests were very true to what we learned in class so you wouldn't expect any surprises on the test if you study all the material from class.
Great for chemistry - teaches well and is understanding

Wonderful professor, goes every extra mile to help with student understanding and is great at explaining theoretical concepts in understandable ways. Also just a super cool dude, really patient and makes a hard class (chem 1 and 2 accelerated) understandable for students. Would definitely take a course with him again.

Dan is a really knowledgable professor. He's clear, direct, and caring for his students. I really enjoyed learning with him, and I think that other student's did as well.  Homework was genuinely helpful.  Unlimited attempts and no point penalty for wrong answers. He encourages guesses in lectures because that's how you learn.  Highly recommend!

Best professor I've had at neu so far. Love the way he teaches lectures; he basically writes the lectures on his iPad as he is teaching you, making them very easy to follow and visualize what he is talking about. He explains concepts simply and clearly, and is very accessible for office hours. 10/10 would take again

Dr. Dan is the best professor I've had at Northeastern. I took gen chem 1 and 2 with another professor before and withdrew from the class because I was struggling and unsupported but I have done well in this class. Dr. Dan is an amazing teacher, his lectures are easy to follow, and he cares deeply about his students' success. A rare find, amazing.

The class isn't too difficult, but can be a little boring. No textbooks but gives one reading per class and gives pop quizzes based on the readings. We had two midterm exams, one group presentation, and one final assingment.

If you're looking for an easy A, go for it. but be aware this class is extremely BORING, pray that the window is open so times go quicker. She's an easy grader but the lectures are very boring. there are readings for each class and be aware as she randomly gives pop quizzes on the readings. Other then that it's a ok class.

Professor Otis was amazing (IDK why some of these reviews are rude). She led interesting group discussions, and was a fair grader. Yes, she gives pop quizzes and there is one/two readings for each class, but it is nothing crazy. If you do the readings, participate, and show up, you will do well. She is also kind, and wants to know her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment:
too Woke!!
There is no uniformity to the pop quizzes and there are so many readings. Each class has at least a 10-15 page reading associated with it. The class has many interesting discussions but they often deviate from the course itself.
quizzes are out of 2 points and often have a huge impact on your grade and she does not drop the bad ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof was very passionate about (interesting) course material and class discussions, but often classes just repeated the (plentiful) reading; not productive. Syllabus and assignments were a bit all over the place, and prof was hard to reach outside of class. Frequent pop quizzes, but final exams weren't difficult. Critical thinking= must.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor!

I don't think she is qualified to teach global lit. She may be good at Shakespeare but she does not know enough about global cultures to teach this class (she asked me how i speak English so well - I'm from an ex-British colony ) She is not a very caring professor in my experience and does not try to help. Unsupportive environment.
Appreciate the effort put into the syllabus and the structure. I do think she makes things unnecessarily hard though
wouldn't really recommend. Enjoy the guest lectures but the regular classes themselves are not exciting. a lot to read as well which can be tiring.

He explains things so well, and his exams were exact copies of what he discusses in class. He tends to go for the full lecture time, but personally I almost never got bored. I would 100% recommend this class!
Very fair. What he said he would test is exactly what he tested. Never tried to trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy to pass class, but impossible to reach professor, assignments aren't graded for like years, if you like getting extra help from your professors, don't expect it here. You'll probably pass but won't understand everything you're doing. If you want an easy A, this class is for you, but if you actually want to understand the content, it's not.

Teacher was very nice and taught the class well. Exams weren't hard if you understood the homework, nothing tricky. Would sometimes have a hard time reaching him outside of class, but other than that the class was easy
Professor Eidson is very caring and an amazing professor. His lectures are good, tests are online and open-book. Homeworks are easy to do. This was a very chill class. 100% recommend!

Professor Eidson is super funny and easy to follow in class (he made stats fun!). Grade is based on 4 tests, 4 electronic data sets, 4 graded homeworks, and a final. The grading was super fair, and the lectures prepared me  for everything. Textbook is optional, but I was disappointed at how difficult he is to reach outside of class.

grades with exams and papers but are extremely easy, writings can be practically stories and informal just connecting the topic to your personal life. exams are also online and his study guide goes over everything covered honestly copy and paste the study guide into a doc and fill it out as the units go easy A.

Really nice guy and super easy class. 4 tests which are open-note and an open-note final as well. Extra credit was also offered on the final. However, he's very hard to reach and never responded to my emails, and took forever to grade exams and papers. All that aside, interesting class for an easy A.

The best prof at NEU! This is my 2nd class with him and I'd just like to say - if you can take any of his classes, do it! His teaching style really helped me navigate the process of writing research papers. Feedback is super specific, improving my 2nd drafts. No exams. Grp project was an experiment you come up with and was such a fun experience.

Professor Eidson is one of the best professors I've had so far. Cognition class was overall easy, textbook is not required, only assignments are 8 writing assignments (short) total and exams were open note. Agree with the other comment about class being like a podcast and sometimes I find it hard to pay attention. Could be just me though

TBH Prof. Eidson is one of the nicest guys. The issue with him is that he is impossible to contact. Never responded to multiple emails I sent through the semester. Quizzes exactly like the HW. Lecture isn't necessary because he reads right off the slides. Many examples in slides and an easy A if you submit everything. Easy class would recommend.

Love Dr. E! He's such a great guy. No readings!! Almost no outside work other than a few one-page writing assignments and studying for the exams. Exams were all open note. I thought cognition would be hard, but it was super chill and interesting. (His name is Robert on the official registration for anyone confused.)

Cognition with Dr. E was a very interesting course! Lectures were very informative, and required little outside learning. Textbook is not required, but I found it helpful. Also tests are open note! There aren't many assignments, just two writing assignments per unit and only 5/8 are required. Overall, I'd recommend that anyone takes Cognition!

Dr. Eidson is a really good professor. His lectures are clear and easy to digest while also being informative. The work is super manageable. Cognition is a good class if you want to learn a lot but not do a ton of outside work.

Really entertaining classes; he always tries to keep his students engaged. Homework assignments were manageable and actually contribute to your overall grade. Exams were a little difficult, but if you take good notes in class, you will be fine. No need to teach yourself via textbook. He's a great professor and I wish more were like him!

I genuinely can not recommend Professor Eidson enough: he is easily the best professor I've had. He's caring, kind and more than willing to help students at all times. His lectures are interesting and convey a lot of information in a thoughtful way. He also offers many ways to boost your grade, but does not overload you with work. 100% recommend!

Dr Eidson is amazing. He is kind, calm, and very approachable, gives great feedback and makes class discussions really interesting and funny. In 4612 you watch a bunch of movies and analyse them (amazing for a film buff, good fun for others) can't rage about Dr E enough, a really great prof (plus fair grader) HIGHLY RECCOMEND

Prof Eidson was a fantastic professor; one of the best I've had at NEU. He's caring and approachable and really wants all of his students to succeed in his class while also giving us skills we can use in research beyond his class.

If you like podcasts, you'll like this professor. Prof. Eidson seems to have adopted the speaking mannerisms of someone delivering a podcast. The downside is that he often overexplains simple concepts, which draws out the class.

prof Eidson is an alright professor, he makes the material easy and honestly does care about his students, he's just the slowest grader I've ever had. he even has TA that grades quizzes for him, but we get those grades back like a month after we've actually taken the quiz. That's the only frustrating thing about him , otherwise he'd get 5*.

One homework packet due before each test. Tests are exactly like the homework. You have to do Data Sets on SPSS and Excel which are a pain, but he grades them easily. Nice teacher. Lectures have plenty of examples.
He's an interesting professor but class never starts on time and he takes forever to grades exams.

Talks in circles. A lecture that could take 20 minutes takes 2 hrs bc he drags everything out. Promises that assignments/grades/study guides would be posted by a certain day and then didn't post until 3+ days later. His exams are mostly multiple choice with one open response at the end. Very nit picky and takes of points off for irrelevant stuff.

Dr. Eidson was a great professor for Developmental Psych this semester. Only 4 exams, 6 writing assignments, and no final which was super nice. He is always willing to help you and is very accommodating, just be sure to let him know if you have to miss class for any reason and he'll be understanding.

He's a really nice guy who just wants his students to succeed. He was the most accommodating professor I've had in terms of open office hours or scheduling things around my schedule. He made sure we really understood statistics rather than just memorizing the computations, which I appreciated.

This Professor really knows his stuff. I thought this class would be difficult but his teachings are interesting. Class style is mostly lecture but you can learn a lot. He is fair and respects his students on an individual basis. I would highly recommend him to anyone needing to take Cognition for their PSYC major or minor.

Dr. Eidson is a young professor who cares about his students. He is intelligent, but not uptight. He tries hard to make class interesting and gives detailed feedback on lab report drafts. I didn't like how he always returned them a few days to a week later than he said he would though- he should either make realistic claims or not make them at all.
He is the perfect teacher

I love him he is my GOAT. if u have to take supply chain take it with him he's so chill and doesn't really gaf about attendance he is understanding and so kind. Once I literally had to present and my info was all wrong and he told me to fix it and I still ended up getting an A for it. He's literally the best please take his class

the exams are only “open note” if you cheat. i didn't so i found the exams to be difficult. if you show up to office hours, participate, and show that you care about the class, you will do well (he rounded my 92.3 up.) boring lectures but they end early. very nice guy with great connections & experience, probably the easiest schm prof. no final

Professor Forbes is awesome!!! 10000% take this course with him. He is very understanding and knows that majority of people in his class are required to take this course so he tries to simplify all concepts! His tests are relatively easy if you keep up with the material. Also he's extremely well experienced in the field--great person to learn from!

The sweetest and most approachable person ever! If you're considering a career in SC, he has a lot of experience and connections. He also understands that this class is a required course for all bus majors so, he tries to explain concepts in a comprehensible way. Very assessable outside of class. Lectures are boring but he ends early most days.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Forbes is the best. He is literally the nicest man I have ever met. I wish all my professors were like him. Test are online but non-lockdown. He is passionate about the supply chain but realizes that not everyone in the class is an SCHM major, so he teaches very logically. Best Guy.
easy tests, has an "is it used in the industry" mindset so he will not teach anything he didn't use in his work the past 30 years. Nice guy, flexible grader
He's awesome, don't skip out on taking Professor Forbes! All of the tests are simple and open book and no final exam. The final project is simple and he makes it very fun!

Professor Forbes is very caring and wants his students to succeed. He has a lot of real-life knowledge that makes his class more interesting. Three tests that are all multiple choice and based on the textbook. He usually goes over the exam questions during class before, which is beneficial. It's hard to fail this class, very easy!!
Professor is great with a lot of experience. Focuses more on assignments and projects gives final grades based on that.

Great Professor! Lectures can be a little dry but it's not a big deal. Homework is fairly simple and the three tests we have aren't overly difficult. There are two group projects which help with the real-life application of SCHM. Overall, great guy who likes what he does and cares for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: (Took for STRT) Professor Moore had engaging lectures and valuable insight into the course materials. She cares about each of her students. Take Elizabeth's class!

Even though the professor is caring and responsive, the exams are extremely hard and detail-specific, and many questions/ terms are not included in the study guide. Short on time ( too many questions within a short amount of time). To get an A on exams, you have to study by yourself and read each line of the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: RUN if you want get A

I love Elizabeth and will take her for any class I can. She deeply cares about her students and is super approachable willing to help you out however way she can. She has offered me great advice and guidance not just in INTB1205 but also INTB4983. Truly pillar in her industry and amazing mentor and role model.

I had her at 8am which made it hard to enjoy, but she's a good lecturer who cares about students. The material isn't hard, but the test format makes exams difficult. Participation is graded harshly, and the group project is a big part of the class.

I LOVED Elizabeths 1205 class this semester, her tests were multiple choice, which I struggle with, however, there were SO many other ways to raise your grade. You can tell she really cares and wants you to do well so she'll give extra credit assignments. The 2 things worth the most are a group project and participation, but she's a fair grader!

Professor Moore is the BEST. She loves what she teaches and makes you love it too. Although her class is not easy, it's so worth it for the amount of learning you will take away. She posts all slides on Canvas, so there is plenty of study material. By far my favorite Professor, if you have the chance, take her class! Can't recommend it enough!

Really cares about the students and wants you to succeed. Knows the material well and makes the lectures interesting and entertaining. Long exams and semester long group project (2 presentations + one optional paper). Accessible outside of class, rubric a little confusing sometimes. Participation does matter.

Overall, she is a good professor and does her lectures well. I will say she tends to like certain students more than others in a very obvious manner. Her tests aren't bad, if you go to class, pay attention, study a bit before exams, you should be fine. The group project has aspects that are unclear since she has a lot of rubrics that she releases.
Great lectures, wants you to do well

exams were really hard and tedious. nevertheless, I genuinely enjoyed this class' lectures, homework and group assignments. Professor Moore also genuinely cared about each student and is entertaining to converse and listen to speak. I highly recommend taking her for International business
Elizabeth is open to accommodating if you need help, if you need a test deferred for a 10% reduction, and is flexible; she has helped me out a lot.

she knows a lot and class is interesting. attendance not mandatory but if you miss class you will be lost. a normal amount of homework, participation matters and get ready to present and work in groups. overall would take again, not an easy A tho.
Great Professor, loved learning from her! Extremely knowledgeable and approachable

I feel quite bad giving this score considering Professor Moore is genuinely so kind and cares (would take any in person class with her) but DO NOT take her online class. Was disorganized, her test questions were literally no where in the textbook or slides (likely just mentioned in lectures), and was generally just impossible.

She is very enthusiastic and you can tell she likes what she teaches. Her grading was fair and all of the classes were mostly lectures, she does go very fast but it was manageable. I didn't do so good on her tests but she gave us ways to boost our grade up so my final grade wasn't terrible. No final too which was so nice.

Dr. Moore is SUPER passionate about INTB which is great- very engaging. She is extremely harsh on grading (blames it on Business Department cracking down). You can participate 10 times in class and still get a B+ on participation. Exams will break your balls but can make some up through presentations and hw. Good luck that's all I have to say.
Professor Moore was the best. Very professional, efficient, knowledgable, caring, and smart. She works to make the class enjoyable and not stressful.

I loved Elizabeth so much, one of my favorite professors here! I had class 4 hrs a week from and she would give us a break and often let us leave early. Her lectures were engaging and I learned so much! Her tests were around 60-70 questions long, mcq and short answers. You should study for her tests but if you review her slides you'll do great.

Elizabeth is an extremely knowledgeable professor who makes every effort to connect with her students. She is caring, thoughtful, intentional, and well-traveled, and wants every student to truly comprehend what she's teaching. Her passion for teaching and research is tangible - I would take any class she teaches a million times over.
Impossible to get an A. Extremely tough grading.

I took Prof Moore in both this class and 2501 at the same time and she was great! I took this class once a week for 2-3 hour blocks ending around 7pm and even with that I looked forward to attending her class. She relies heavily on participation but the assignments are pretty manageable and interesting. Highly recommend!

Please take a class with Dr. Moore - I've had the chance to have her twice in my three years at Northeastern - never have I looked forward to getting to class more than when she teaches. Come prepared, be respectful, be engaging, do your homework and you'll be just fine!

loved this professor and the class! only hw was the online debate (200-word post twice a week), and as long as you do them on time, she'll give an A. 3 online exams were pretty manageable. group project is a lot of work, so just hope you have a good group. cares about peer reviews, which is nice. would definitely take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An amazing professor, I looked forward to this class weekly! It was challenging at times, especially the tests, but I genuinely feel like I left this class a better student and learner.
This was my favorite class I have ever taken. Lectures are extremely interesting/engaging and the debates are fun! Would definitely take again if I could.

Dr. Moore is such a great professor. Although this was not the easiest class I have taken, I feel like I got a lot out of it. Her tests are hard (there are 3 throughout the semester and the last one is sort of optional). Group project is a huge part of the class and there are 2 parts of it. informative lectures, doesagreatjobkeepingtheclassengaged.
Suffering class
Exam too difficult, hard to get a good score
Excellent professor, very caring!
Class was purely on memorization with little teaching
Awful.

Cream of the crop. She is engaging. She is caring. She is clear. She is informative. I have learned so much. Her tests are somewhat difficult but serve its purpose -- if you truly are grappling with the ideas and nature of what she is saying they shouldn't be too bad. Also shes super understanding in case you have any issues.

Professor Moore is absolutely amazing! She is not only knowledgeable about the subject matter but is also very passionate about it. Her lectures and supplementary materials were very eye-opening and I learned a lot. Group projects are common and participation matters, but this is all to help you become a better global manager. Definitely recommend!

Professor Moore is genuinely one of my best professors, not only because of who caring and generous she is, but also because of how she challenges you in class. She made my love for international business grow fonder while giving the class exams and assignments that were well thought out, not feeling like busy work. She's amazing and reachable!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Moore is wonderful; I liked her from day one. Her tests are hard and practically impossible to get an A on. BUT, she's seriously a fabulous teacher who pushes you and has your best interest at heart. Very sweet, approachable, cares for her students. Very experienced too. I would highly recommend and can't wait to take another class with her!

Wonderful teacher! Had her my first semester for freshman year and she is one of the most engaging and interesting professors. Speak up during lectures and actually participate in class because there are a lot of discussions and opportunities to participate, and if you do it will make the class that much more rewarding.

Best professor ever!! I seriously cannot say enough about Elizabeth. Let me say that this was NOT an easy class by any means, the material is tricky and you definitely have to work hard, but her lectures are very interesting and the work/grading is fair! Not intimidating at all, awesome instructor for my first semester of college!

She is probably the best professor I had so far in the program. Her lectures are amazing and clear. There is a lot of work but it is actually interesting. I really like this course and the professor. If you had the option to have her as a professor, would recommend to def pick her class.
Elizabeth is truly an amazing person. She's extremely smart, personable, and cares for the materials and the students in her class. If you get the chance, try to take a class with her !!!

Moore is hands down the best professor for any class you need to take. She is interested in her work and brings that passion to class. The lectures are super interesting, but there are a lot of group projects, and you'll stay in the same group for the whole semester. She's really accommodating and works with you through any issues.
The best teacher for any INTB class, no doubt about it.
Without a doubt, the best teacher for INTB1203.

best teacher i have ever had. very interesting lectures and makes class so much more enjoyable with great content and engaging debate activities. 3 non-cumulative tests and a big project but no final. best teacher at northeastern!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Liz is fantastic! She truly cares about students and making sure everyone learns. I really hate statistics but I am so glad I had it with her because she could make even the most boring subject fun, exciting, and understandable! She is always available to answer questions or meet with student outside class. Would take anything she teaches again!

Liz is the coolest teacher you'll ever take. By far favorite teacher of the semester, she's nice and her class is interesting. You learn a lot without feeling pressured and she is very understanding about the amount of course work given. Wish I could be in her class next semester.

Grace Ferris is a really great orgo 2 professor! The class is definitley hard but she makes it manageable. You are only really graded on HW  and 4 exams. She isn't know for having a true curve but did have small extra credit questions on 2 of her exams. She is really accesible outside of class with tons of office hrs slots and review sessions!

Orgo 2 with Ferris was definitely not easy, but for me it was doable. All the tests are open-response, and she did add extra credit on 2 of the 4 exams, and they were worth about 4 points, which was a decent amount. She also gives you the opportunity to redo an exam for a better grade. Good lecturer, but you need to put the work in to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ferris is exactly what you want from an Orgo Professor.  She walks around the room to help her students through problems, takes extra credit, and will go lengths to help you succeed in this class.  1 star reviews are from people who expect easy tests and grade inflation.

Professor Ferris is great, take her especially if you care about understanding the actual material (like if you need to take the MCAT). She has lots of practice problems and practice tests that are graded on completion to pad your grade a little. No extra credit, curving, or bumping grades. Cumulative final, hw due daily but it's low stakes.
Chuddd.......

Orgo 1 and 2 are very difficult classes and she covers a lot of subjects super quickly in order to fit them in. If you pay attention in class and do the homework carefully you'll understand the material. She tests very fairly and will explicitly tell you what will be on exams, also her office hours are super helpful.

She is an amazing professor. She really wants the best for every student. Yes her class is hard but orgo is hard in general. You need to put the work in, in order to do well in orgo in general. She is super nice and wants every student to succeed. Please take her and enjoy her class.

All the negative reviews are just from people who did bad in her class. Organic Chemistry is a hard class and is known as a weed out class for a reason. Her practice exams are very similar to the exams and there is a decent amount of practice. Her tests are pretty hard but fair for the content of organic chemistry. She cares and is accessible.
Retaking this class with a different professor and its going so much better AVOID
She's really good at explaining the material in a digestible way. Even though OChem is a hard class, if you put in the work for her class it really pays off.
Ferris provides way too many materials rather than focusing on a single textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are really good and make a lot of sense. Very accessible outside of class with office hours and TA's hosting recitation sessions. Biggest recommendation is finding worksheets online from other teachers and practicing those cause the aktiv PS are not at all like the tests. Orgo is bad no matter who u take it with.

Exams are impossible difficulty our averages for them were very low. Everyone who says we didn't dedicate enough be for real we have other classes that are also difficult I studied for week and half earlier and still did bad.Most of the class  ended with Cs. Other Ochem profs classes had retakes, extra credit, curves and ended with better grades.

Grace Ferris is one of the few Orgo professors who actually wants you to learn the material and do well. Is Orgo hard? Yes, it's a weed out class. But she provides extensive resources to understand the material and truly understand the class.

Very difficult class because she just expects so much compared to the other professors but if you are able to keep up you will leave her course set up so well for further classes. She's very funny/personable and I don't think she deserves the hate she's got on here recently but I will say she isn't super understanding when the class gets hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ferris was amazing. She made organic chemistry easier than gen chem. Her lecture slides make it so easy to follow and understand the material. All you need to do is read her slides and do the exam exactly how she does in her examples and you'll get an A.

If you wish to have no life,24/7crash outs,live in Snell,no final exam practice,75%of your grade based on 4 exams that look like nothing like the lectures that you sit in everyday, NO EXTRA CREDIT, HW ARE EZ BUT TESTS 20x HARDER, STUDY GUIDES ARE FIGURE IT OUT YOURSELF, “ORGO IS MEANT TO BE HARD” SO SHE CAN SCREW U EVEN FURTHER W NO REMORSE OR HELP
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very over-hatted professor. Orgo is supposed to be very hard and other professors are easier and offer extra credit, but this shouldn't warrant bad reviews for Grace. She is an incredible lecturer and cares how the student absorb the material. If you go to class and study hard, it is very rewarding.

Professor Ferris is really nice and clearly feels passionate about ORGO. That being said, her grading criteria makes it crucial for you to spend a significant amount of time studying for you to do well. It is possible to get an A in the class it's just really really hard. However, this does make sure you really understand the material.

She explains tough concepts well and is always available for help. She's the sweetest and genuinely wants us to succeed. However, textbook/Aktiv problems are not like how she writes them, but that is the primary resource we have for practice. My biggest piece of advice is to study EVERY day. You cannot get by with only studying the week of an exam.

This class is difficult, but its orgo. While it would be nice if she were to allow a test retake, give extra credit, or add fluff to the grade -she really knows how to teach this class. She knows what she is talking about and wants students to understand all the concepts. Her office hours are so helpful and she gives to many resources for studying.

If you want a good grade, don't take her. If you want to actually learn the material then take her. Orgo is generally a tough class and it's unfair that she doesn't give extra credit or test retakes, however if you actually put in the effort and understand how to study then you can do decent in exams but it's really hard to get an A in this class.

Worst class I have ever taken in my life. Such a sweet woman but that's all she is. The homework assigned is so time consuming and irrelevant to the assigned lectures. The midterms are insanely hard and the practice tests she provides are almost nothing like the actual exams. The final was agonizing. Select a better section if you can.

She is such a sweet person, but save yourself. Not generous at all when it comes to exams, they are very difficult and she gives no EC, corrections, or curves. Class averages were usually in the 60-70 range with no curve.
Literally never again. So unhelpful shows no care if you do bad and wtf was the final.
She gives us practice exams which is a benefit but gave us no clarity or guidance on whats on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor and has very clear and engaging lectures. Homework is helpful to solidify topics but is time consuming. The only negative is her exams are VERY difficult and you really have to dedicate a lot of time.

Grace is tough; this is true. If you're looking for an easy class to coast by, do not take her. If you truly want to understand the concepts and feel confident in your abilities, then she is the best possible. Her lectures are clear, and she gives many examples and practice problems. Put in the work, and her class will be rewarding.

I loved Professor Grace! She's a breath of fresh air. Orgo is tough, but she makes it manageable. Go to office hours and stay on top of the work, and the class is very doable. Her tests are fair, but you need to show up and put in effort. I truly gained a mentor. Don't wait until the last week to study! All-nighters will not work for orgo! TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It starts out great. Then it just gets worse. She's so kind and truly does seem to care about the success of her students, but her tests and grading are impossible. The homework progressively gets harder and harder until it will take HOURS. The tests are completely incomparable to all in class work and homework. Lectures are great, but don't help.

Grace is a very kind person who is clearly passionate about organic chemistry. Her lectures style, practice exams, and Aktiv in-class questions made it seem like exams would be a breeze. Until you find out everything that you thought would be on the exam isn't on it at all and you realize you wasted hours studying to basically fail.
Her lectures are fine, but her exams and homework are awful.
do not take her.
Literally everyone is lying I study for 20 hours like a part time job and still fail.

Grace is an amazing teacher and is one of the best lecturers in chemistry. Her practice exams are exactly like her actual exams. I personally am doing well and learning so much. Compared to other orgo teachers at this school she is amazing. If you are someone who actually wants to put in work you will do well in this class. Disregard cruel reviews.

Everyone who is on here being disrespectful needs a reality check. Just because you cant study doesn't mean the professor is bad. Orgo 1 is meant to be hard. There are chances to improve grade with attendance, homework and practice tests. There are also many outside of class opportunities to get help. If you don't have the time to study dont take.

ok yes she is a good prof when it comes to explaining but her exams are just too hard and unrealistic unless you're just cracked. When I asked her for some advice and comfort, all she said was to review study guide and rest. REST??? I am always at snell and still can't do well. There's so much covered on the exam and not enough time.
You will cry a lot and your gpa will go down. Test grading is insane. No curve. No extra credit.

Lectures are pretty engaging; her way of explaining things was pretty intuitive for me. Pleasant and understanding if you have an issue during office hours. The material is really difficult, but she has it set up in a pretty digestible way. Just be ready to spend a lot of time outside of class on review and practice.

POV im at snell for DAYS on end, stomach grumbling, tired asf, nothing in front of me except my hope and dreams and my ipad obvi. Study sessions are 10+ hours. You take the exam feeling alright, tears in your eyes though. Then it gets graded and you failed. Ya i know this will probs happen to u (sorry) so dont take her class, unless u r cracked..

This professor has given me nothing in life. When I think of life, I immediately think about my life before this class and how much better it was. Mind you this professor went from a 4.1 to a 2.7. I want to change my major because of her. I think my life expectancy just insanely dropped because of this lady because THIS CLASS TOOOK YEARS OFF LIFE.

Beware. If you even want a chance of getting anything above a B- do not take this prof. She grades extremely harshly and does not ever consider another opinion, especially during regrading. She makes up her own "rubric" or criteria for what she wants because of her superiority complex. You will not touch an A in her class, and lots of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I got well above average in class 100% in the other categories, and still don't have an A. Other teachers at least curve!!no test corrections, no ability to move up a grade. Study for about an entire week before exams still dont do as well as id like. Doesnt regrades even when I wrote the same thing as the answer key, at least give me one point.

This teacher has a very unfair curriculum with no curve, extra credit, and abhorrent grading. She genuinely grades so hard and expects us to read her mind on tests. Other teachers offer curves and extra credit, I know people in other sections of Orgo 1 that have 100. How is that fair? It's not. I studied 30 hours and did not do as well as I wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This review is for Organic Chemistry 1. The grade breakdown is that almost the entire grade is dependent on the exam grades (3 Exams, 1 Final), with around 10% from other work. If you are struggling with the content, she offers NO opportunity to improve your grade (make-up exams, notecards), which can make it hard to pass the class. Never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grace Ferris is a great person and I appreciate her humor. However, I spend 2 weeks studying for her exams and still don't do that well. Her lecture slides and homework problems are so much easier than the exams. Every single other Orgo teacher gives some sort of grade redemption except for her so keep that in mind when you're picking classes.

2311:  Studied for more than a week and still  did bad every exam. Other ochem professor offers something to help curves, notecards, exam corrections but she gives absolutely nothing. She just reads slides and shows ridiculously easy examples nothing like the exams. Homework is long and brutal, the textbook is useless, and office hours don't help.
Chopped cheddar cheese
changed my major in the middle of lecture. i think that speaks for itself.
I literally purposely stopped in front of the T while walking to class in hopes i wouldnt make it
just run far away

I have shown up to every lecture, I went to office hours, took extra notes from the lectures, and I would still NEVER take this class with her. She reads off the lectures, which you can do at home. The homework is always 40+ questions, and the practice exams never reflect the actual. RUN. I would rather retake Physics 2 than Orgo with HER.

Great professor. I definitely would recommend taking her for Ogro 1 and 2. She wants you to succeed. Orgo is hard to begin with so do not blame the professor blame yourself if you are not putting in enough work. Do the homework, do some practice problems and you will be fine.

I would rather walk through the fiery pits of hell than walk into her lecture. She's a nice professor, sure, but probably the worst professor in ALL of my eons. I never see my home, my family, my life because I'm consumed by orgo. If you can LITERALLY take any other professor, do it. Because if not. ALL of the life in your eyes will become drained.

Please NEVER take her. I never see my home anymore and i am constantly at snell because of this lady. This makes my life 10 times harder and she does not do corrections or retakes so actually makes me want to give up. If you like crying and being miserable take her, but if you like life, don't.

Teaches by literally reading off a lecture for an hour and 40 minutes and expects all students to fully understand everything. Tests are nothing compared to what we do in class and my class averaged 67 and 70 for the first exams. SHE DOES NOT CURVE, GIVE RETAKES, OR ANY EXTRA CREDIT ANYONE WHO SAYS SHE DOES IT LYING. God awful teacher don't take

Grace Ferris is an angel that actually made gen chem as well as orgo concepts make sense, it is not an easy class but she explains the material clearly and in depth. I got a C- in gen chem but am doing well in orgo thanks to her. GO TO CLASS. If you miss even one you will have a VERY hard time. If you work hard you will definitely succeed.

One of the best science professors I have ever had. Lectures were easy to follow along, and she explained concepts and reactions incredibly well. Not much homework, but exams were somewhat difficult. Spend a few minutes each day outside of class rewriting reactions and going over her slides before exams, and an A is very doable. Exam redo is nice.

I loved having Grace as a professor so much! She really cares about her students, and teaches in a way where you really get to understand the material. Her class may be slightly harder to get an A in compared to other ORGO profs, but if you really want to learn the material, taking her class is the way to go. 100% recommend her, best ORGO prof imo
One of the best science professors I've had. She truly explains material well, and her lectures are easy to follow. Exams are not easy, but if you devote time to studying, an A is very achievable.
great teacher but wouldnt round up my grade 0.2% to bring me to the next letter grade.

I absolutely adore this woman. It's obvious that she actually cares about her students and genuinely wants them to do well. I really liked her lectures, her slides were very organized, and she explained things really well. I went to her office hours every week just to absorb knowledge because she was so welcoming and inviting and such good vibes.

Grace is such a great teacher! Super nice and breaks down concepts very well especially if you go to her office hours. Took me after the first exam to get used to her style of exams, but there are no surprises everything covered in lectures is what she tests you on. At the end of the semester you can also retake an exam which helped me a lot
She is a great professor, and honestly should teach every chem class. However, her exams are very specific and challenging. She does provide good buffers tho.

I LOVED Grace. She was a great lecturer and made the material easier to understand. Her PowerPoints and annotations were very helpful. While her tests were hard, she did cover all the material in class but sometimes focused on smaller parts that weren't emphasized in class. Very funny and made the class enjoyable. Would definitely take her again!

Homework/lecture is super easy. Tests are not. Tests are sometimes worded strangely and have topics barely touched upon in class. But, her exam redo policy is very generous and can only help your grade, so A's and B's are very attainable.

Professor Ferris was a really great professor for organic chemistry. Her tests were tough but if you prepare and work hard throughout the semester you can do well. She makes an effort to get to know all her students and even has an exam redo policy where you can retake one exam at the end of the semester

Dr. Fontenot is a great professor from my experience! No final exam. The two midterms fairly reflect the material (you can use a cheat sheet too). Lectures are engaging. Attendance isnt required but random days he'll take attendance for extra credit. Early homework submission gets you extra credit. Group project is heavy so choose ur group wisely!
Easy class until the final project

Class is free until the group project. Hws usually took 20 min and the slides for a 1 hr lecture could be read and understood in 10-15 min. Does not answer questions and ghosted someone on slack asking abt the final project

Take the online section. The course content is extremely relevant, but he comes off unapproachable which reflects in the lack of participation in class. Its a bit frustrating with the side comments, ends class 30 minute early, & often breezes through the lectures. Head TA's are helpful, but the quality with other TA's is often a miss.

The homework for this class is fairly time consuming and does not really help with the exams. The exams are difficult but doable with studying and your allowed 1/2 sheet of notes. 0 late submissions and the professor is fairly rude and does not appreciate questions. The final project is given very late and is time consuming so be prepared for it.
Good lectures, final project is a lot and kind of crammed, homework and project submissions were often posted last minute, but was a nice guy and seemed to care about his students.

The professor is actually pretty nice and cares that we learn, he gets snappy with people but it's usually for a valid reason. The TAs I dealt with were really condescending and not helpful at all and I was always scared to ask for help, and they usually post the submissions for HW and Projects really late. The project was fun and not too hard.

The class wasn't bad. I didn't pay attention in class and did fine. The slides and homework have all the information you need to perform well on the midterms. The final project is a lot and is heavily dependent on how good your groupmates are. Fontenot can be sassy, but if I were teaching a class full of freshmen, I would be too.

I ended up doing well in the class, but it was a frustrating experience overall. Lectures often felt unclear, and it was hard to understand what would be important for exams. When I tried to ask questions, I didn't always feel like I got helpful clarification, which made it difficult to know how to prepare effectively.

Really disappointing class. The professor often seems impatient and unhelpful, making students uncomfortable speaking up. Lectures are confusing and lack structure, so most learning is done independently. Grading is unclear, feedback is minimal, and communication is poor. Overall, a frustrating and stressful experience.

Not a good experience. The professor feels unapproachable and often dismissive, which makes asking questions uncomfortable. Lectures are unclear and poorly structured, so most material has to be learned on your own. Grading lacks transparency, and communication is minimal. Overall, a stressful and frustrating class.

Poor experience overall. The professor is often dismissive and unhelpful, which makes the class uncomfortable. Questions aren't encouraged, lectures lack clarity, and expectations are unclear. Most learning happens outside class. Communication is weak, and grading feels inconsistent. I would avoid this course if possible.

Very disappointing experience. The professor comes across as unapproachable and dismissive, which makes students hesitant to engage. Lectures are confusing and lack structure, so most concepts have to be learned independently. Grading criteria are unclear, and communication is minimal. Overall,stressful and not worth taking if you have alternatives

Extremely frustrating class. The professor is often rude and dismissive, making students feel uncomfortable asking questions. Teaching is unclear and disorganized, so most learning is self-taught. Grading lacks transparency and communication is poor. Overall, a stressful and negative experience I would not recommend.

One of the most frustrating classes I've taken. The professor is often dismissive and condescending, creating an uncomfortable environment. Questions are met with unhelpful responses, which discourages participation. Lectures are disorganized, grading is unclear, and communication is poor. Overall, a stressful and disappointing experience.
Probably one of the worst professors in the university he has no shame or manners on how to behave with students strict for no good reason doesn't know what he's teaching or doing either

Lectures "require" attendance with only a 0.3 point addition to Exam 2, in which attendance is taken far too inconsistently. Lectures are unprepared and rushed. Assignments are never created timely, come out with mistakes, and submissions release late on the deadline. Professor and TAs are condescending and the class is treated as if it is a joke.

This guy decided to create a new assignment a week before the group project was due stating that It would help with the group project. When most groups had already gotten past that part of the project which was the easiest part. Also very condescending according to others, I never paid attention much to see this happen tho.
He was asked to leave his previous job at SMU for being racist btw
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the most realistic response for this class.His exams are pretty difficult I failed both despite studying a lot. For the second exam he lied about what would be on it, and he's genuinely the sassiest professor I've met. He rushes lectures ESPECIALLY the final project. The ONLY reason I passed was extra credit, and he only gives during class.
The lectures were not that great, and he often had a condescending attitude. The final project is difficult and rushed, with limited support.

Very divisive for a few reasons: he's a very knowledgable professor who (I think) cares for students. However, his general demeanor in class, while amusing at times, can be questionable and discouraging for students. Also, gives extra credit but grades harshly, and the final project is quickly paced and not well supported by class lectures.
Avoid this professor. He is very condescending and does not understand that students have other obligations and cannot always make his class their highest priority.

Dr. Fontenot is far and away my favorite professor at Northeastern. Aside from great teaching skills, he's a great human. Always available to connect outside of class and cares deeply about his students. Also, if you have the chance to apply to the dialogue he runs, 10/10 recommend. Great professor and great mentor, if you can handle a little sass.

Took this course when he taught it Spring 2025. He made sure that EVERYONE got something out of the class, whether it was through lectures or group projects. He made sure that everything came together nicely so no lecture was ever useless. Fontenot taught us important industry concepts like RAG and AWS.

Definetely one of my fav professors at Northeastern! Lectures are super engaging and as long as you pay attention in class you should be fine on homeworks and tests. Don't understand the bad rep he gets tbh the guy's hillarious
Fontenot is obnoxious and dislikeable.

Taking his class Fall of 2025 and wish I listened to the negative comments here :( only responds to questions with sass and pomp. I'm a girl, and a lot of us actually made it a point to only attend office hours as a group to get away from "Creepy ReMark"... heard a ton of things about people needing to go to the dean to get him to settle down

Hiis lectures are literally useless, spends more time reminiscing about his time in industry than the material

Final project was impossible with his rushed semester schedule

I'd avoid this professor like the plague if you don't need this class to graduate

Don't take this class if you want to learn anything, especially for resumes/co-op interview

His lectures were really clear and did a great job setting up for success on homework. You get extra credit just for showing up to class, and there are tons of ta office hours to help with the final project.

Fontenot is a great lecturer and his classes are enjoyable. You learn a lot but he's slow at grading and responding outside of class. This semester, he introduced the concept of 'Practicals' which were like mini projects so in total we had 4 HWs (if you submit early you get 2 bonus points), 2 practicals, 1 final project, and 1 exam. Fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hate to give him a low rating because I genuinely enjoyed his class and what we learned. But the grading is so slow. Stuff we submitted in  February still hasn't been graded and we have no idea how well we're doing throughout the class. Also very rude in class, makes students feel uncomfortable by calling them out and drawing attention to them.

Fonte is awesome. Genuinely very caring, hard working, knowledgable. If you put in effort in his class it will pay dividends. Prof is dedicated to creating new engaging assignments that go beyond the book and teach you real skills.

Project is, as he puts it, "trial by fire." I wish the last phase of the project had been released way sooner - it's very time consuming and you need to teach yourself how to do a lot of it. My low rating is due to his attitude - can be rude and very quick to anger. Almost made my entire class retake an exam due to one student's behavior.

I took this professor for a summer section of OOD. He didn't know what we learned in Fundies II and what we were supposed to learn in OOD other than Java. He spent more time making snarky comments and setting up his PowerPoints than actually teaching. The homeworks were often unrelated to or far beyond the scope of the material covered in class.
Easily the best professor at NU and if you're up in these posts complaining about him you should look inward

Funny reading all these reviews given that no one I spoke to who took his class had anything positive to say about it

The worst if you're trying to learn actual content and grow as a developer

Ditto that if you're looking for an easy A or a project you'd be proud to talk about for an interview or something

Creepy and disrespects women/minorities
Love this guy. A lot of the bad reviews are people who never come to class and then are surprised when they do poorly on projects and exams. Just come to class and you won't regret it
By far my favorite professor I've taken here. Funny and gives lots of extra credit.

Reviews are polarizing for the right reasons. 

If you want to learn, you will learn more with Fontenot than the alternatives

If you don't care, you should take someone else and leave the seat open for someone who does

Prof. Fontenot was a character to say the least; couldn't keep control of his classes and resorted to snarky comments and passive aggressiveness to get his points across. Inflexible outside of class, and spent more time mingling than teaching. Lectures left much to be desired, and projects had little in common with lecture material. Glad to be done

People think he's rude, but its just a matter of tone. If you have 1 on 1 conversation with him or go to his office hours, you'll realise its just a consequence of only talking to him in a large class setting. Lost of extra credit, and he's very knowledgable on the subject and on professional advice.

Fontenot's lectures are filled with tangents, and key concepts are rushed, especially for the final project, which relies on barely taught material. Grading is extremely lenient, with low engagement. Expect random discussions and unprofessional behavior, including singling out students in discouraging ways. If you value structure/respect, beware
professor is p unorganized. but the class is easy so its a free A. Regardless if I did not have previous knowledge coming into this class i wouldve done a lot worse.

Group project was very infuriating but Dr. Fontenot was amazing overall and doesn't deserve any low ratings. If you need one to one support, he's very helpful during his office hours. He gives tons of extra credit so just do his homework early and do well on the exams (very easy btw) and you'll be fine. Not a bad class overall

Classes are heavy, sometimes takes attendance as extra credit. If choose cs3200, make sure to find reliable team members, start the final project earlier! First hw for ds4300 is difficult: write the logic for binary search tree in python and run it. If you meet problems just go to his office and ask him. Final project need you go to every classes!

Dr. Fontenot is a fantastic professor. Teaches content well and is very accessible outside of class. His TAs are helpful too. He gives soooo much extra credit and is a lenient grader. Databases is an easy A. Personality-wise, he is funny and witty, but sometimes his sarcasm is kinda condescending (although usually warranted). Highly recommend

My fav course this fall since I actually looked forward to coming and hearing his funny observations about us. Every few lectures he'll ask us to write names on paper for extra credit. hw keeps getting posted too close to the deadline so that's a bit stressful.
