Definitely form groupchats early on to bounce questions off each other

The class content is very learnable, but he expects you to self-teach during the 2nd half of the semester. 6 easy HWs, 2 exams, 1 big final project. Final project uses Python. He is pretty disorganized, which affects the quality of the class. Most of the HWs were posted very late. The TAs are, truthfully, unapproachable and snarky.

Professor Fontenot clearly cares about his students and wants to prepare us for the real world. However, while the material is good and the class has a reasonable difficulties, the TAs and in some ways the Professor are rude and condescending. When questions are asked, TAs will just respond with snarky remarks, trying to assert their power.

I dont have anything to say about his humor like others. His class is hard, 2 exams, VERY lengthy project, and the TA's are literally no help and will only reply in sarcastic comments or make u feel like shit for asking questions online. Its not clear what the exams cover and the slides are only 60% of prep. Overall pretty restrictive teacher.

His class is extremely easy, teaches like he assumes everyone is learning for the first time. Extra credit just for showing up to class (amazing). Has a lot of office hours. +10 essentially to all exams (2). Very sarcastic but only to those who truly do not care about his class at all. Pay attention, just show up to class, easy A, nice guy

A lot of criticism is unfair. The final project scope is a little broad given what the class covers, but it forces you to learn. Decent lecturer and in-class problems are helpful for homeworks and exams. Also many extra credit opportunities. He can be sarcastic, but calling him rude is a stretch.

I've never taken CS classes before college, and I've often felt intimidated, but not in this class. He creates such an entertaining atmosphere (if you can take a joke...which based off the reviews people can't). He explains concepts clearly, and doesn't make assumptions on what people already know. He will call out students who obvi don't gaf

Too much hate. He isn't rude, he is sarcastic and dry that is his sense of humor. If he ever believes someone is hurt, he talks to them after class. If you can't take a joke don't take his class. He explains concepts clearly and isn't afraid to go over simpler concepts to make sure everyone understands them. He is available via slack. fav cs class!

Maybe I'm insensitive, but anytime he snaps back at students or makes comments that sometimes people take the wrong way, he is very obviously joking. I don't understand these bad reviews. I get that he is a pretty tough grader, so I honestly think most reviews reflect that and not how he is as a person. He wants us to do well and is always helpful.

Fontenot gives you extra credit for showing up to class. Show up and do the world and you'll be fine. He is extremely sarcastic, but he's a nice guy who cares about your success. He adds extra office hours to make sure that he is always available to students, and responds to slack messages quickly.

He is amazing! Very caring and takes time before and after class to help students debug issues with their homework, as well as holds many office hours. Gives a lot of extra credit and it should be simple to get an A in if you do well on the tests. Homework is sometimes long but are definitely doable in the time span. One big group project.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His teaching skills are bad, I'd rather go study on my own than go to his class... He doesn't have clear guidance for projects and when you're trying to reach out on Slack his efficiency's terrible.

I get that students either love or hate Fontenot, and to me, his jokes are pretty mean and doesn't really care about his students. He barely answers questions from students on forums and rarely posts solutions to his answers. I can't remember a single thing from the lecture. One good thing is that he has a bunch of extra credit opportunities.

I can see why Dr. Fontenot is a little polarizing on this page. Some students find his snapbacks funny and laugh it off with him but some students perceive them as condescending. 

The course material itself is great and the end-of-semester project is a great combo of real-world tools that are key for anybody who wants to do literally anything inCS

Mark Fontenot is genuinely the worst teacher at Khoury. He is rude and constantly belittles his students. He insults them on slack and in class, and his teaching skills are incredibly subpar. He reads off of powerpoints and doesn't cover material remotely related to the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Super understanding! love him

Whilst this class was very time intensive, as long as you attended lectures and reviewed materials from labs, everything was very doable. Additionally, I found Fontenot's lectures very engaging and easy to follow.

OOD was challenging, but it was definitely doable.  The projects took a lot of time to complete and were related to lectures.  Some of these other ratings sound like upset students who didn't want to actually do the work.  If you want to have a challenging but doable experience, take this prof.

Professor Fontenot was honestly a pretty good teacher. He is clearly very knowledgable about java and computer science in general. I liked his assignments and projects, and the tas in the class were always available to help people. Despite this, I generally just do not like the guy. He ignored my emails and messages, and just was not respectful.

No doubt about his knowledge of Java but I think he couldn't convey it to the students. The overwhelming amount of things due(which he later realized about) meant that we had something to submit every day which was OK at first. Then it turns out that I am basically not learning much in lecture that I would use for the PA/HW.

I learned more about OOD outside of this class than I did during his lectures or doing his PAs. He covers the basics, but his demeanor in class is so unfriendly that his sense of humor just doesn't make up for it. He yells at students during class for not paying attention, which is really disruptive for the students that are actually trying to.

Professor Fontenot is very understanding and caring. He can come off as snarky or irritable, but he's genuinely a nice guy who is knowledgeable and funny. Assignments are difficult, but interesting. His lecturing and slides often contained little info & felt under-prepared. Learning how to do the assignments taught me more than the lectures did.

Mr Mark fontentot is very knowledgeable about the things he teaches but seemingly does so begrudgingly. He is good at teaching students new concepts but only a small portion of the concepts he covers are helpful in completing the assessments. These factors in tandem with the course's difficulty led me to drop the class.

Compared to all of the other CS classes I have taken thus far at Northeastern, OOD with Fontenot was by far the best. Despite the fact that this course was condensed over Summer I, I felt like I learned the most. Fontenot clearly cared about his students and was there for us every step of the way.

I took Fontenot's CS3200, then CS3500 over the summer. Long story short, everyone complaining should understand that they took a 4 credit course over the summer.. and I personally learned SO MUCH from Fontenot and feel much more real-life equipped now than before. He brought the theoretical concepts we learned in Fundies 2 to more applicable things

classes were prety much useless. He came in 10 min late, read slides, and ended class 30 min early. Too much material that should've been covered in class wasn't covered at all or crammed into labs that dind't explain things clearly. But the PAs were not too long and did cover a lot of content (15 h on average).
I would be a husk of a human without my acquired knowledge of SOLID principles.

he came into OOD without understanding what cs students have learned in fundies 1 & 2. He expects students to pull all nighters every week. Taking this class is like taking 8 credits. The projects aren't spread out in a reasonable manner. He expects you to have knowledge of algo. The written exams expect you to have full knowledge of code.

Mark Fontenot demonstrates expertise in the subject but has an off-putting attitude, making learning difficult. He offers minimal guidance on projects and provides delayed feedback on assignments. Communication is sparse and undermines student confidence. Taking the course with another professor would be a wiser choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark Fontenot's demeanor is a huge disadvantage. Despite his expertise, he's unresponsive, scoffs at questions, and brushes off concerns. Steer clear if you can and save yourself the frustration caused by his discouraging attitude. Wish I never had to suffer through his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is actually a good teacher, but not very good with people. Everyone focuses too much on his personality and overlooks his impressive teaching ability. You can tell from his course materials and website that he puts a lot of effort into them and is very passionate about what he teaches. I believe he's underrated

Avoid Mark Fontenot at all costs. He's rude, unhelpful, and fails to create a productive learning environment. Asks for feedback but retaliates when given. Lectures are useless and assignments unclear. Took CS3200 for learning, left with pure disappointment.

Mark Fontenot is, by far, the worst professor I've had. His lectures are a mess, and he's extremely rude to students who ask questions. Don't expect any help from him. Unbearable arrogance and a complete lack of empathy make for a terrible learning experience. Avoid CS3500 with him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark Fontenot is a frustrating professor to deal with. Despite CS3500 being an easy class, he's really condescending while answering questions, making whole learning process extremely difficult. His rudeness destroys class morale. Do yourself a favor and pick another prof if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mark Fontenot is the WORST CS3200 professor ever. He's always delaying assignments, changing grading rubrics without telling us, and breaking promises. It feels like he's purposely making our lives difficult. The class is a nightmare because of him. Avoid at all costs!
Great professor, although flexible, a bit messy when it comes to assignment structure and sticking to dates which can cause a bit of stress.

Dr. Fontenot is a really personable guy and I loved getting to know him this semester. The course material is important but he makes it really easy to learn it with his lecturing style. He also teaches you a lot of practical knowledge and breaks it down into small chunks so you never feel overwhelmed. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

If you can take this course with another professor, consider your other options. Dr. Fontenot is very knowledgable, but is difficult to work with. He is dismissive and passive-aggressive, as well as incredibly resistant to feedback. His attitude creates a negative learning environment that in turn makes the class a negative experience.

I took a course with him last semester and unfortunately, I cannot recommend this professor. While they are undoubtedly knowledgeable in their field, their lecture style was a hindrance to my learning experience.

The professor had a tendency to go off on tangents.
I would never take his class again.

He was not a very helpful professor. He barely answered any questions, especially towards the end of the semester, so we were left with very little direction on our final project (which was not very well explained and haphazardly put together anyway). We never even received grades for half of our things by the end lol.

Highly recommend taking professor Fontenot for Database Design. I learned a lot of practical knowledge in his class, and he cares a great deal about his students. If you take the time to really learn the material, an A is more than attainable.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Study guide solutions are wrong. When a majority of the class failed a quiz, he gave an extra credit assignment as a grade booster, BUT THEN NEVER UPDATED THE GRADEBOOK. He told us one quiz would be on two chapters and then added questions from another chapter. How he is still employed at Northeastern is beyond me.

SCHM 3310 is honestly the most boring class I've taken. The professor is unclear, doesn't follow the syllabus and makes you present just to grill you and say you're wrong. Tests are weirdly written and teaching isn't helpful at all. Would not recommend. Save yourself unless you want to suffer with a boring class for a whole semester.

Professor Huq is a great supply chain professor! You will need to put the work in to do well but it is worth it. He is extremely passionate about the material and has lots of stories to share about his time in his career. I will say, he doesn't update the syllabus so be sure to double check with him if something seems off.

Took 3310. He would constantly give us the wrong information (especially when it came to the algorithm/work problems) and then when we were completing them wrong, would try to gaslight us. He truly believes he's never wrong. Also used outdated textbook slides for his lectures, never replied to emails, and had extremely unclear grading criteria. ugh
This professor is not clear about expectations.

I took Professor Huq's morning SCHM 3310 course. A lot of his information was out of date and just flat out not right. Professor Huq also always thought he was right and could never be wrong. The tests were really weirdly written for no reason, and difficult to understand what he was actually asking. You need to participate a lot if you want an A.

I took SCHM3310 with professor Huq and the class was very enjoyable especially if your interested in transportation. The professor is very knowledgable on the topic and makes the class an engaging discussion based class. Participation is very important to your success. Group projects have a large affect on your grade so you do them well.
run! DO NOT take his class

The class content was really boring but he cared about it. Very knowledgeable in the subject. If you didn't participate he didn't like you. If you disagreed with him, he did not respect that. The simulation assignments take a long time but aren't too hard once you get the hang of it. He curves grades which is really nice. Nice guy, ok professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class online, and it was A LOT of work. Definitely not unmanageable, but probably the most time-consuming async class I have taken at Northeastern. Exams are difficult and heavily weighted (60%). The professor was easy to meet with - hosted office hours twice a week for two hours each and was willing to meet outside of those times as well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible. His solution sheet for his practice exam will have tiny tiny differences in the question itself making the answer completely different and you have to figure it out, he will not tell you. His due dates are incredibly inconsistent, he will not provide clear guidelines or rubrics, then grade very harshly. The final module also takes 6 hours

Prof. Huq was great! His lectures are interesting, and I enjoy his teaching style. If you read the textbook chapters and participate, the class is engaging, and you will do well on tests. His office hours are helpful. The simulations are time-consuming but enjoyable and a nice break from regular work. I would 100% recommend you take him!
I love Dr. Huq. He's like a father to me.
excited to teach and enjoys supply chain. If you put in any respectable level of effort in participating he will like you

HORRIBLE. I got the highest score for 3 out of the 4 exams but still get an A- because he gave me a 7/10 for my participation grade even when i went to all of his classes. Don't take him if you don't want to ruin your gpa.
Avoid if you can. Not good at all.

He is hilarious and entertaining and clearly actually passionate about the subject. The simulation modules will kill you once you get to module 6 it takes like 5 hours on your first try at least

As long as you put in the bare minimum participation wise he will lowkey love you and you'll probably do well.

Avoid at all costs!! His Canvas page is extremely hard to follow with two or three different due dates for the same assignments. My group never knew when anything was due and he would be very vague in his emails when we asked for clarification. He doesn't grade anything until the end of the semester, so all his feedback is useless.

I have never had a worse professor in life, avoid at all costs. He does not seem to care about students actually doing well in the class and he doesn't know how to teach an asynchronous course effectively. None of his content is original. He doesn't provide consistent due dates. Terrible teacher NOT a professor.

professor huq is a great person and a great professor! he is very engaging and cares about schm a lot. the drawbacks of this class are the group presentations and projects. there is no clear rubric for presentations, and the simulation is ridiculously long (it took my grp around 7 hrs!!) his grading seemed to be relative to the rest of the class

Professor Huq was not a bad professor but he also wasn't good. The class was pretty hard and I didn't think that the material was all that interesting which made it harder. The class was pretty straightforward and if you study for the tests and quizzes you'll do well. The simulation module was super long though so be prepared for that.

Dr. Huq is very knowledgeable, I learned so much in this class. The quizzes (10%) are multiple-choice and pretty difficult (I did fine with the curve). The midterm & final (25% each) also curved. They were easier than the quizzes because they were more problem-based. There is a graded simulation with unlimited attempts. Good to know stats before.

He is a harsh grader who lets you go to his office hours but doesn't explain. He says this is the answer and assumes the students know why. Exams are challenging, and everyone dislikes his teaching style because he reads off the slides. I participated and never missed a class, but still got lower than a 7/10 for participation. Avoid him SCHM2301

This is my second class I have taken with this Professor, honestly it was even better than the first! Our project was to an actual client which made the class so fun especially getting a free zoo membership. His lectures are always so engaging and it really feels like a group discussion. He is very understanding just make sure to do the readings!

Paul was by far one of my favorite professors. He takes his time to get to know each student and has a great sense of humor to keep the class light. You will learn a lot of you lean into the experience. I would 10/10 recommend.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Loves the subject, but somehow doesn't realize that he's teaching an introductory level course. Material is scattered and hard to follow. Don't bother emailing him, he doesn't care. Has tests that make up majority of your grade despite having no way to practice the problems or see any previous tests beforehand.

Honestly, run. I was forced to take this class because I need it to graduate soon and it was the only asynchronous section available. For an ONLINE & asynchronous section, he makes it too much work. 1/2 the work you do is practically useless.

P.s. most of the reviews below seem fake. Good luck, and i hope you take this as a warning.

Professor Fombelle is a knowledgeable instructor who knows how to lecture very effectively. He ties his lecture slides into real-world examples and all slides are made by him. He cares about attendance and will call you out for showing up late, but he means very well and cares for all of his students (especially those who show up ready to learn).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is the reason I switched my major to marketing, class is never boring, he is honestly a very fair grader, values creativity for projects and just overall effort. Make sure you pick a good group for the projects as its the key to success. I would take this again in a heartbeat make sure to read theres easy pop quizzes when he feels likeit
He definitely expects participation and is very respected in his field. He has lots of real world advice he uses during his lectures which I love.

Paul's lectures were very interesting to say the least. His tone and jokes are pretty entertaining which got me engaged. He can seem arrogant or judgmental to some, but I enjoyed watching lectures and thought his approach was unique and funny. Class comes with a lot of material to remember though, so make sure you're studying for those tests.
If you're taking this class because you think it's asynchronous and easy, then avoid it. Takes a good amount of time and effort, but relatively easy. TA grades most of the work.

Most of the bad reviews are from when he taught the class online a few years ago, ignore them. Paul is a great professor, engages with the class, and there are many times everyone is laughing in his class. It takes work to get an A but it is manageable and I definitely learned a lot. One of the best professors Ive had. Wish he gave makeup tests tho
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Has a passion for what he's teaching, which really comes through in his lectures, and a good sense of humor. Read textbook and engage in class, and you will do well. Tests were all mcq so as long as you read they're easy. Not much graded homework other than group project. Fombelle made 2201 my favorite class of the semester, would take him again!

TA grades almost every assignment; material was clear and easy to understand but his exams were strangely difficult in comparison to what was in the textbook (coming from someone who read the entire thing -- you need to in order to do decent). He's a good guy and clearly passionate about what he's teaching, which makes lectures easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: His lectures were very interesting and you can tell he likes what he's teaching. He does have a bit of an ego but he is funny. Attendance is very mandatory and you really have to take notes on the textbook to do well on tests. He didn't allow any laptops/ipads in class but it was honestly fine. Workload was very manageable too.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Frankly I would take a class by this professor on watching paint dry, and I'm confident I would come away with, if not new insights, an enthusiasm for the topic previously assumed impossible    
Attendance is very mandatory but honestly talk to him about it, he genuinely wants to see you succeed.
Not much homework other then group projects.

Prof. Paul is funny but a little self-centered. He really encouraged participation, but as someone who is introverted, I never felt comfortable answering questions because of his fast pace and sometimes abrasive attitude. The tests/assignments aren't that hard as long as you put in effort. Good lectures. Would take again if I really had to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Fombelle does not deserve the low ratings that he gets on here! I was originally so worried to take his class due to the Rate My Professor-- but they were very wrong. He is one of my favorite professors and I am going to take another class with him. He is hilarious and genuinely cares.  Seriously, take his class. He is the best.

Tests were terrible - asked really oddly specific questions from book. I did so well on everything else in the class but because tests were brutal and weighted so heavily, I didn't get as good of a grade as I would have liked. Passionate about the material but also a bit arrogant. Part of simulation grade is on performance compared to classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Paul is such a nice guy, but the asynch marketing class was weirdly semi hard. It's not hard to do well, but don't take this class thinking you'll get an easy A because it's intro level. TA grades HW and there are only 3 pretty heft/hard tests. Watch lectures, REALLY read the textbook, try your best on the simulation, and ur all good.
Take literally any other marketing professor and you will be 10x happier

Don't take this guy. Seriously. Any other marketing professor will infinitely more helpful. He grades everything extremely strictly, which for an intro to marketing course is a bit ridiculous. If you want to have a decent GPA stay away.

I took his MKTG2201 asynchronous so I cannot speak on the in-person quality but I definitely recommend. Assignments were creative and fun to do and exams were easy as long as you studied. This was a required course, but he made marketing interesting and a class that I thoroughly enjoyed. Easy A as long as you do your work!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Professor Fombelle this year and I loved him. He's a fun and comedic, yet serious, guy and is super caring. While there is a lot of reading, it's pretty much just the textbook. Participation is mandatory but you learn so much in each session it's really worth going to class. Be respectful and he will have respect for you in return.

I took the asynchronous version of Intro to Marketing with Fombelle. Please do not make the same mistake I did. Lectures rarely align with chapter, tests are insanely hard, homework is a waste of time. He makes this subject unnecessarily hard and has completely averted me from marketing. Also decided to assign double the weekly work on a test week
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Entertaining enough that I can listen to lectures without falling asleep

Paul is a really nice prof. I took his course twice, both MKTG2201 and MKTG4502. He is very kind and friendly, and especially fun. The course is kind of hard but I definitely learned a lot and enjoy taking this course.

One of the most unlikeable people you will ever encounter. Brags about how his "success", shows pictures of his boat and cars, etc. I was sick and he got mad at me and threatened my grade because I had to miss class. It creeps me out how different he is outside of class than his nice guy act. 

Have to admit he does give good lectures though.

Professor Fombelle is the best professor at Northeastern. He cares about his students. Getting an A in this class is difficult, but you will learn more in it than with any other professor. He has high expectations for his students, but matches that with high expectations of his own teaching ability. Take this course, you won't regret it.

Mr. Fombelle was the harshest, strictest, most critical professor ever. He assigns exorbitant amounts of homework, grades harshly, and is extremely unaccommodating. Most online professors have open-note exams: not him. He forces students to record audio AND video during exams. I started out excited to learn about marketing, left despising it.

Prof is knowledgeable & experienced, lectures do a good job of summarizing what matters from the book, & if you want to see him outside of class he's pretty accessible. Unfortunately, his attitude is like a high school teacher's in that he takes strict attendance every class, mocks students for minor issues, and grades much harder than is necessary
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The general trend of his class is 1) he will mention he has tenure at least once every class 2) he is so afraid of people cheating on his tests he will literally create so many incoherent questions that don't make sense "to trip up cheaters" that messes up everyone 3) not go over all the questions you get wrong on tests so you can't learn from them
modern day embodiment of a business major - this isnt a compliment
not worth your time
do not take this class with him for the love of god - most people i know dont do well on the tests and that impacts your grade SEVERELY
assign tons of homework and let students figure things out by themselves

He tries to be a good professor and has good experience within the field, but he doesnt actually care about his students like he claims. He is sarcastic and harsh and unhelpful when it comes to actually helping you despite his caring claims.
One of my favorite profs. Super caring and funny. He makes you work for an A but keeps class engaging, especially if you participate. :)

paUL was a great marketing professor. He can come off as intimidating, but he really cares about his students. He makes you put in the work in so don't skip classes and pay attention (he will call you out on it). Overall, I learned a lot and had a funny professor and classmates (1:35PM). Hopefully this will appear on one of his presentation slides
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Amazing professor you won't regret taking his class. He's very understanding and wants to help you succeed as long as you come to class and read the textbook.

Professor Fombelle is one of the most inspiring people youd ever get to meet. 11/10 recommend taking this class: be prepared for your life to be changed. He is so passionate and excellent at what he does and it shows in every class youll take with him. Leaving this class, theres NO WAY you wont want to take a concentration in marketing.
Most enjoyable class I've taken at Northeastern. Fun lectures. Tests can be a bit tough but won't be too much of a problem if you read the textbook.

Warning: This class will change you forever. You will become very intolerable of any bad service / marketing, become an expert complainer to service providers, and always judging how much companies couldve done better. You can never turn it off. And hes not sorry about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Younger prof but on tenure. Really loves the class and has good experience in it. Definitely need to be engaged in class to get a good grade, but its easy enough. Big consulting project for the Zoo, but its pretty interesting. If you are interested in Marketing in any form of service, highly recommend. Connor's trip at the end of the semester!

Paul Is a great professor. He gives a lot of homework, but the homework makes sense. The syllabus looks intimidating but the work is really manageable. He is also very helpful and will be willing to meet with you outside of class. He makes real world connections to the material and class feels more coproduced as oppose to be lectured at
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Hands down the best professor at Northeastern, no competition. Paul makes every class engaging, content interesting, students laugh - and loves every minute of it. This is the first class at Northeastern I actually never skipped - my attendance record would show that's pretty incredible. Take one of his classes even if you don't have too.

He will likely show this at the start of your sem with him, and frankly, I hope he does. This is my only prof review. Even though I def wasn't his best student, Paul was the best Prof I could've ever had. Challenged me for the better, for that I can't be more thankful. Bring your A game every day, and he will ensure you grow in more ways than one.
Great professor and a very enjoyable class. I highly recommend taking his class, I definitely would again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best teacher ever. He can be tough and sarcastic but he is a great resource to have on campus. He truly care about his students that show that they want to be in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The worst class I ever had. The professor does not care about individual student. Exams are hard even if you read the whole book. If you like to raise your hand in front of 40 students, take his class, or don't. He even would not remember you. And BTW, he will take a screenshot of these commends on rate my professor and discuss in class. Have fun:)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I loved Paul so much. I found that students either loved him or hated him. Get on his good side (participate and talk in class) and he will love you too. Easy B, hard A class. Be prepared to do work, although it isn't at all overwhelming. I would recommend Paul to anyone. (dont skip class- he takes attendance)

Good dude. Pretty Funny. Dont show up late, hell be annoying about it same with leaving to go to the bathroom. Other than that really great class, not too much homework just reading the chapters before class and he'll ask you what was covered. Tests are reasonable.

Paul is a cool guy. He will give a few pop quizzes to make sure you are reading. He likes class participation since he gets bored without it. He will get distracted if you get up out of your seat or are surfing the web o your labtop/phone so don't do that. He takes attendance so definitely show up. Tests are easy if you know how to study.

Paul is a great professor. He makes every class relatable by providing a lot of examples  and enjoyable by showing videos and pictures to help teach course content. He is very engaged with the class and acts pretty much like one of the bros. To do well you must read the textbook and show up to class on time-he knows when you don't! Easy B, hard A.
Amazing Professor. He is the most hilarious professor in NU.

I made a rate my professor account solely because of the bad rating Fombelle just got. He is the best professor ever, and every kid I know absolutely loved him. Build your entire schedule around getting into his class. Extremely nice and helpful, and makes the class fun.

Bad? I'm not saying he's a bad teacher. I'm sure he's very good in doing his work but he's very rude and impolite!!! He doesn't respect his students at all. I was so scared when I was in class with him because he was always making jokes about students and treating everyone very badly. Someone liked him; the majority of us don't!

Professor Fombelle is a really funny and charismatic teacher. He is an extremely hard grader, and you would most likely get a letter grade higher taking marketing with another professor. Participation was worth a lot and it was hard to earn. Also, he grades the group projects extremely hard. He is a great professor but a very tough grader

Take him! Tests are do-able as long as you pay attention in class and read beforehand. Participation is very important, as is reading the chapters before class because sometimes he'll throw a pop quiz in there.  He keeps the class interesting, has a great sense of humor, and you learn in an enjoyable environment.
The in-class participation is really ridiculous. The presentation  is hard to get higher than B+.
One of the best professors Ive had at Northeastern. Classes are fun, you never get bored. Read the chapters and you will be fine. Exams are fair and not too hard.

Not a good upper level professor. Pop quizes and his participation requirements are ridiculous, and patronizing to say the least. His tests are also horrible- just memorization of unimportant tables/flow charts from the book. Learned very little in this class. He's also incredibly pompous.

Honestly I believe Fombelle was a great intro teacher but does not understand how to teach an upper level course. Other than the fact that he is pompous and arrogant, he treats his students as if they are freshmen. The reading pop quizzes and a paper stating every time you participate is busy work and not appropriate for junior/senior level course
Lectures are engaging and fun. Never a boring day. Definitely take him if you have the opportunity, one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern

Professor paUL is a gem of Northeastern.  He is totally worth rearranging your schedule for-- do whatever it takes to get him.  Make sure you express your love for Best Buy/hatred for nature/sports in the first class and you'll be golden.

Best Professor. My concentration was Finance, I am now double majoring in Marketing and Finance, only because of him. He is one of those teachers that inspire you with their teaching. Absolutely love his sense of humor and wit! If you get an opportunity to take his class don't miss it!! -- but be willing to work.
Prof. Paul is the BOMB. Tests are straightforward and clear.  His lectures are engaging and he is very relate able.  I can't wait to take another class with him.

actually runs a dynamic, interesting class which most cba professors do not. lots of funny videos/jokes, keeps mood light. tests are totally reasonable, reviews everything beforehand. no homework whatsoever besides the simulation. has a lot of interesting experience and stories - really knows his stuff. 100% recommend

Good Professor. Just read the textbook before class and participate. His exams were very straight forward. He also has you play a fun marketing simulation game. Also, he likes to be impressed by the work you do so be creative.
Not a good teacher.
One of my favorite professors ever. he's a cool guy and you get work done while having fun in class. if you read the book you'll do fine. definitely recommend getting him

One of the best professors I've had! He's young and relatable and communicates the concepts in a way that was easy to understand. His tests are not difficult as long as you take notes during the powerpoints he presents in class. He's big on participation so as long as you show up to class and participate in the discussions, you'll be fine.

He was a GREAT professor and made class really interesting. We did a really fun simulation that took up at least one class a week. Tests were easy as long as you wrote down the answers in the review sessions and knew the vocab from the book. Must participate at least once in awhile.

I had no interest in marketing prior to taking this class, but may consider changing my major after having Paul as a teacher. By far the best professor I have had to date. He is the equivalent to a friend in college that happens to teach the class, but has had an immense amount of experience in the marketing world.   Change your schedule to get him

Genuinely my favorite professor i ever took. Shes so kind and caring, and loves a class discussion and for the first time throughout my university experience i never felt shy to speak because english isnt my first language.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very approachable and gives helpful feedback on assignments that helps you improve throughout the course. The class feels designed to support learning rather than overwhelm students. There is a decent amount of work, but it's manageable and useful. Overall, a very kind and supportive professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice and easy prof, a few papers throughout the semester, (long) but interesting lectures. Easily available after class for support and general conversations, highly approachable.
Please take her for Advance Writing 3304, you will not regret it. Easily one of the nicest teachers here @ NEU! As long as you partiicpate in class, and stay on top of deliverables youll do well.

She is the best professor I've had for a class I would've expected to be too hard to take. She makes writing fun and optional class interactive. She allows drafts and peer edits and provides her own feedback which ensures understanding and an A.

I loved having Professor Olivier for First Year Writing. She was always ready to talk about something unrelated with her student and even turn it into a fun assignment. Most of the assignments didn't have clear guidelines, but this was because she wanted her students to be creative. Fun and easy class, she's awesome.

One of the few professors at Northeastern who actually cares about you and would work with you to get the best grade possible. She would never reject a meeting outside of class and would always be open to discussing ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not only is she a great teacher, but a great person. From day one you know what to expect, there are peer reviews and revision opportunities. She is not only devoted to helping you in the class but in life. The class is designed to help you write in the professional world, and she is truly like a mentor. She is so caring and fair. Best professor.

Professor Olivier is amazing! She makes it very clear what her expectations are for each assignment and is available to meet if you need help on your drafts. She's super understanding if you're experiencing any difficulties completing the assignment and is willing to give extensions. Definitely take her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Started the first day saying, "I've never given below a B+ in this class" BY FAR the easiest AWD class offered at NEU. Dont let "Pre-Law" scare you, the amount of work is nothing compared to the essays and projects in other Advanced Writing courses. Plus shes just a good person who you will enjoy being around.

Hands down the best Professor I've had at NEU. She's kind, caring, understanding, efficient and overall a good teacher. Sure she may go off topic in some ways, but the tangents always connect back to the core topic at hand. Take her as a teacher if possible - do yourself a favor.

By far the best professor at NU. Does anything she can to help you succeed both inside and outside the classroom. Makes everyone feel comfortable speaking and participating and sharing work. Very enthusiastic and smart. Take her!!!

She is by far one of the best professors I have had in my academic career. She helped my with recommendations and building my resume. Her class had 4 "papers" all of which were easy if you put in the time and effort. She is brilliant and a teacher at Bentley Univ. too. Get to know her and she can give you advice on anything! Cheers!

A nice lady who goes off topic very often in class and is pretty unhelpful. She does not help you during the process of writing the paper and provides very generic feedback. She also does not make her expectations very clear. AND I am not even joking, when I say that she thought it was necessary to teach us about spell-check on word!!!
Very chill class with all assignments and exams online. Attendance was also not mandatory! Would recommend if you need to get your biostats credit out of the way.

Challenging class with heavy R coding and basic statistics. Weekly assignments, a midterm, and a final made it intense, but Dr. Ferdows is amazing—clear, supportive, and always available. The TAs and both professors offered constant help, which made the workload manageable and the learning experience rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is taught by two professors who alternated by the day. Loved Smith, found Ferdows confusing. Often felt like she was seeing the slides for the first time herself and would be stumbling over explanations. Class itself is easy though, all R code examples are posted online. Copy paste + edit them for the weekly assignments. Exams take home

I loved this professor, and he may have been one of my favorites at Northeastern so far! His class is based on attendance and is completley lecture focused, which can get boring at times, but also has clear information in the lectures that relates exactly to the tests. Funny guy who cares about his students, definitely would take him again.

he was great and a super nice guy. he brings us snacks almost every class which motivated me to show up. there are 3 finals, his tests are. usually like 10-15 multiple choice and probs like 5-7 short answer. he is clear with what he wants.

one of the best professors i have ever had. he was passionate and truly wanted to help his students. lectures were kinda boring but he often brought treats. his tests were also easy if you studied his slides. he cold calls sometimes and he doesn't release your average till the end of the semester but it's super chill. TAKE HIM!!

I had Prof. Hartman his first semester teaching here, he is very smart and very accomodating hes a such nice, genuine guy and I really learned a lot for him, brings snacks and always a good mood to class. Exams are pretty each but 3 are worth like 80% pretty typical for a accounting class though, take him!

INTB 1203 was a pretty easy class. Lectures were pretty entertaining. I would say there are few things graded, which makes it pretty bad if you do horribly on one thing, and it can be unclear what will be on the quizzes, but other than that, she was great.
noooooooo just bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are long yet unhelpful. Grading criteria is unreasonable and does not match other professors whatsoever, but most likely she won't grade your work for months. Do yourself a favor, either take a different professor for the class or just take it online. Take this class with her if you want to learn nothing, waste your time and tank your GPA!

Her class is not difficult. However there is a very limited amount of things to grade, so doing bad in something will hurt your grade. Grading is a bit unclear and can be rough, specially group project heavy. Also it is unclear what will be on the mcq tests. Yet her classes are entertaining and fun to be in which makes mandatory attendance not bad.
Lectures are hard to understand, which didn't support my learning. TRACE extra credit was given, but midterms were difficult.
She does not explain this course well at all. She is not an easy to explain teacher.
Your grade will be fine because she gives a lot of homeworks out. She is good, a little boring, but it's just another college class. She's the safest choice for sure.

Tests are online (except the final). Lectures are so hard to pay attention to - monotone, boring, and doesn't ask for participation. This makes absorbing the content significantly harder than it should be. She is sweet and cares about her students and course material. Take her for an easy A, but not if you plan on taking other finance courses.

Great finance prof. She knows the material well and gives great lectures with a ton of practice. Attendance is part of your grade, but participation is not. Two midterms were online and were just like the practice and homework. Final is cumulative and in person. Overall great class with a prof who knows what she's talking about.
Take her for finance. She knows what she is talking about. Definitely go to class and try to keep up to make the final easier (it's a cumulative in-person final) but the other exams are online.

Online exams except final. offers curve and TRACE credit. I found her to be really concise, her powerpoints cover everything that makes reviewing a breeze. Office hours and availability was great and she offered a lot of help. can sometimes rush over some steps but just talk to her she will go over it. Overall extremely patient and kind.

All of the exams are online. There is a cheat sheet allowed on the final. Lectures can be boring but she is definitely the best finance prof I have heard for this course. She is so nice and actually wants people to do well. Offers extra credit for TRACE and will scale exams if need be.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Gu was an overall okay professor, she's super knowledgable but her lectures are so boring and it's difficult to pay attention. But her exams are all online which is a huge plus.

Knowledgeable professor but struggles to convey information often. GO TO CLASS. Professor can often get confusing with material because of backtracking and forgetting to explain things. Teaches material but often tests have content that was barely covered or only somewhat related to reviews. HWs are also not relevant to tests or the class.

Professor Gu is one of the best professors I have ever had at Northeastern University. I am a senior taking her course, and finance or financial accounting lecture heavy classes at Northeastern can be generally dull. However, this is the first finance class where I (a non-finance major) felt like I learned.

Its clear she knows the material perfectly, but her lectures are incredibly dull and confusing. There are only 4 grades in the class (Hw, 2 exams and final). You have to teach yourself EVERYTHING and its pretty challenging and time consuming. By the end of the semester there were only 6 students attending the class. Don't recommend taking.

Gu knows finance like the back of her hand but it is often hard to understand and follow what she discusses. She teaches super quickly and has admitted that she teaches us stuff that she learned during her masters at Yale. Exams are all online, but students still score in the 70s. The final grade is curved. Connect HWs weekly and take 10 hours.
not responsive
Professor Gu is not an easy A, but if you do the homework and use the practice problems as review for exams you are gonna get an A.

-Confusing to understand -Sometimes would assume we understood more than we did in an intro class and had to backtrack making it even more confusing -based on a very few things -I learned by making a group with friends and struggling through the hw - would spend hours doing the hw to try to understand then she would put odd cases on the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gu is a very nice and kind teacher. There are only three assignments during this semester, and they are pretty easy. Grade is based on three tests which weighted heavily. As long as you review her PPT and HW, you will be fine for the exams. Exams are pretty easy, no surprise, all questions are based on HW.
I did extremely well at the beginning, but did not do as well on the final, which was weighted 35%!! I would not take. She's hard to understand and I had to teach myself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is extremely difficult to understand, and does not teach with any type of organization which does not match my learning style. Sometimes she assumes students know things that we do not. I had to teach myself how to do most things in this class.
She was a very easy A and also learned a lot! I loved her class and shes super helpful take it with her!!

Nice young lady, listen carefully and pay fully attention in class then you will do good, the tests are exactly the same style as the homeworks, do her homeworks and ask questions you will get an easy A in her class
She was rather hard to understand so it made it difficult to learn. I relied heavily on the book for tests.

She is a very nice professor, always willing to help. Even her lectures sometimes are awful but go to her office hours. She give a lot partial credit for exams, so easy to pass. Take her and go to class, I ended up with an easy A
Nice person. Terrible teacher. Relies on the students way too much. Sometimes it is difficult to understand her.
Nice professor who is always trying to help you understand the material. I barely read the books but still learn and understand well in her class
Gu is a nice young professor and always willing to help.  She treats the job seriously. Her class is helpful and kinda interesting.  Take her class, it's not hard to pass.
She barely knows english and can't comprehend the questions students ask. If you attend class sit close to the front if you hope to hear anything she says.

I wouldn't recommend unless required for your major. There is no one who loves to hear the sound of his own voice more than him, and he made me want to drop out every class. All of the grading was done by TAs who took weeks to grade, were extremely unfair and unthorough, and gave unhelpful comments.
Don't take if you're a STEM major. You'll learn nothing and still have to complete tons of busy work. Attendance is the only reason to go to class.

Like others have said, if you don't have to take him... don't. The course is very easy, but he complicates it, and the assignments and everything are graded by the TAs (So it's the luck of the draw for how your grade turns out). Furthermore, the ONLY reason to go to lecture, is if he MAYBE gives an attendance code, which he baits us half the time.
Your parents pay $10,000 for an attendance code.
Would take again only if I need more material for my experimental noise album. Holy pretentious yapperoni and cheese.
This professor will use great opportunities to push his christian values on you. Held us captive via the attendance code until we got a prayer service bestowed on us by the Fellowship club.

Gutierrez is the most pretentious professors I've ever had. Majority of students take 1001 as a requirement, but Gutierrez expects everyone to be passionate about music. He uses a condescending tone and acts as though he is smarter than everyone else. The workload is heavy considering the course level. It's not super hard but very time consuming.

This class required me to do more homework than all of my other classes combined. The TAs take weeks to get back and a few more weeks to grade assignments. But an A- or above is very attainable, even if you put in the bare minimum effort. Find a better NU-path class. Take this only if you have to.
There is very little work for this class, and the professor is very engaging. I wish the class were smaller, but the content is interesting.

85% of the class takes this course to fulfill a NU-path, and I genuinely had more homework and projects for this class than my STEM requirements. Attendance is MANDATORY even though it is a massive lecture hall, and don't even get me started about the TAs.

I genuinely cannot stand this professor with all of my being. You know those people who become professors just to hear themselves talk? That's him. He thinks he's the next coming of christ and that he's the smartest person to ever exist. PAINFUL
The class is very interesting, easy and taught well, pretty much an easy A but the way its set up sucks. no contact with the teacher.

Professor doesn't grade assignments himself so your entire grade rests upon his TA's which are horrible and don't give constructive feedback and are unreachable. Insane given the amount of projects we have and don't receive feedback at all.
Free A for the MUSC1001 class. Midterm was open note, 17 MCQ. Doesnt mind you being on your laptop in class, and only takes attendance 1/3 of the time. Pretty much just show up and you will get an A

It is our third week, and we're already getting grades that we don't have feedback on. I got a 72% from a module assignment, and the TA is unresponsive. Most of us are not interested in or in love with music; we are mainly STEM majors trying to have ONE easy course and this professor is just being unnecessarily complicated, giving a heavy workload.
I have him right now and I already hate it. He is just one of those bad professors

Professor Gutierrez acknowledges that this is just a required course to fulfill NEU Path. However, the workload is the equivalent of high-level music major classes. The class itself isn't hard; it's just immensely time-consuming, which doesn't help if you're in a hard major like STEM. The grade breakdown is insane, with multiple projects.

I took this class asynchronously, but it was very work-intensive. There were many group discussions, and the projects were pretty time-consuming.  There is also no communication with prof, you can only contact the TA's which I thought was weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The material is easy and it would be more straightforward if all the articles weren't so pretentious and pseudo-sophisticated. The course flow is so confusing. Module 2 is due before module 1, module 4 (big project) is due before module 3. I don't know if it's purposeful or a mistake but it's so confusing to follow.

I took him summer 2, I didn't interact with him much but most of the assignments are easily although they get progressively more annoying as the semester goes on, but they are never terrible. He isn't too tough with grading either.

the class was okay i took it summer 2, definitely not just an easy a class but not difficult or anything, but this guy wrongly accused me of using ai and wouldn't believe any evidence i showed, not even edit history in the doc i wrote it in. him and the ta basically called me a liar and told me to learn to write better

Professor Gutierrez is hit or miss. He is a very nice guy but as a professor is extremely arrogant and speaks in a condescending tone with fancy language to make himself sound smarter. He is an easy grader though

I don't recommend Dr. Gutierrez. Everything is done by a TA, so there's zero personal connection. The rubrics aren't clear for grading. He'll ignore any emails for extensions. The TA also ignores any requests for help. MUSC 1001 is ok except for tedious projects. The grading is slow and feedback isn't given or its just bad. The TA polices diction.

Overall, easy A course. Weekly quizzes were not timed w/ 3 attempts. Assignments and discussion posts were fairly simple. There are 3 major assignments submitted through VoiceThread which is kinda of hard to navigate if you've never used it before. Everything graded by TA (so very opinion-based) with no feedback. Email responses from Prof are quick

There were many participation-based grades and weekly quizzes, all of which were simple but a lot of modules. There were a few major assignments- also not too bad, but he ended up putting some of these grades in the week final grades were due and doesn't add comments for why you got the grade you did. Working with VoiceThread is also a nightmare.

Says things like "superfluous" and "capricious" and "trepidation" just because he knows how to use those words, not because they actually add any sort of depth or specificity to his lectures... rolled my eyes a few times. How about making academia more accessible and inclusive by ensuring your lectures are something everybody can understand?

Do not take this class if you want to get an easy A or fulfill NUPath. The TA's grade the assignments and do not give any feedback, even if they take off a significant amount of points. Dr. Gutierrez is passionate but his lectures are long-winded and he will take attendance only when he feels like it. Choose a different class to fulfill electives.

This class would probably be a little more work than you'd expect, but definitely doable, and the online midterm and final are both very easy. I don't really get the hate this professor gets for "being pretentious" (?) He just seems like a good guy trying to give a good lecture. Nothing seemed pretentious to me.

Engaging lecturer who is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He teaches with a great depth of knowledge while still being entertaining. You can get a lot out of this class as long as you come in with an open mind

The pretentious professor made the class unbearable. The assignments, although they were very simple, were graded very harshly and with no feedback. He never submitted grades for multiple assignments and when this was brought to his attention, he reacted very defensively and put the blame back onto the student. Don't waste your time and money.

Prof. G is great! There are weekly async quizzes on the readings and class notes, but they're all very short and super easy. The class material is really interesting and it's clear that he's really invested in what he teaches. The course is good for anyone, regardless of prior music experience. He's really enthusiastic and it makes class very fun.

He is clearly passionate about music and knows the topics very well. However, he is very pretentious in his lectures and has an inflated ego. Content is easy, but if you aren't a music minor/major, can be a little harder. Also, not super clear in grading criteria. Easy content but annoying teacher.

Such an incredible professor and the content was always so engaging and interesting. Prof G is very smart + this class is so much fun! Projects are fun to complete and the exams are very doable. I highly recommend taking this class, you will not be disappointed and if you show up and pay attention, you will get an A.
Had a quiz, discussion, and assignment due every week. Quizzes, midterm, and final were all online and open book. Grading rubrics were provided, but not always clear.

Professor Gutierrez's class is organized by unchecked readings (he assigns an interesting and diverse curation of articles), weekly discussion posts, weekly open-note, untimed mini-quizzes, a few large projects, a midterm, and a non-cumulative final. He's thoughtful, passionate about class materials, and an engaging, qualified professor.
Really engaging class. The lectures are pretty interesting. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches.
Professor Gutierrez is the best!!!!! His lectures are so interesting, and he is so knowledgeable and involved. Great man. great class.

The type of professor that uses big words to sound smart, but in reality is saying a bunch of nothing. Useless class that overanalyzes the minutia of things most people don't care about or will ever study again after this.

Overindulgent explanations on topics that are less than riveting. Tries WAY too hard to sound smarter than he is. Won't stop mentioning he lectures at Harvard. Just a lot for a 1000 level course imo...

I absolutely loved this class. Definitely take it with him if you are able to. Lectures were extremely interesting and he was clearly knowledgeable about every subject he taught. I would want to talk to him about music after class just to hear more about it. I am in love with this man.

Took him for 3550. Professor Guilfoil was a great instructor and very knowledgeable about the Journalism Industry and the First Amendment. The course material and readings were interesting, and I learned a lot. He doesn't receive a 5 because the lectures and homework can get repetitive, and there was minimal discussion. Otherwise, great prof!

I enjoyed Prof Guilfoil's PR Principles class, he's clearly very knowledgeable, experienced, and approachable. He includes a lot of anecdotes from his own career, and I left his class with a very detailed picture of what the PR industry looks like.
Great lecturer ! and pretty easy grader

Took him for PR Principles. He's really nice and knows what he's talking about. You do have to buy his book for the class, and each week you write a reflection on the chapters. There's also a group project, which is actually cool and a good learning experience. Overall, he's a great professor, but he's not the best at replying to emails.

Pretty nice guy, not a whole lot of work except the final project. Although I wasn't the biggest fan of how he taught and explained some things, he gave a somewhat decent basis to an interesting topic. Helped prepare expectations for journalism.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: John Guilfoil is an amazing lecturer, he knows how to captivate an audience. His grading guidelines are clear, and it's hard to receive less than an A in the class. His lectures often end early and are just chill discussions. The course is probably the most costly one I've taken, with a $190 price tag on his book and the Globe subscription.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Guilfoil was the most amazing lecturer I've ever had. He challenged our class with difficult conversations and loved to make us uncomfortable but in a good way. He canceled class very often, but understandably considering that teaching is not his primary job. I highly suggest that everyone takes Understanding Today's news with him.
such a fun class! super chill

He's a nice guy, has a lot of real world experience. That being said he was very unavailable, cancelled class very frequently (with the rate of tuition and the frequency of cancelling this was upsetting), he also did not grade anything till the very end and barely answered emails.

Professor Guilfoil was great. I had him for two months before online class due to COVID-19 but was still great during online classes. He did pop quizzes based on news of the Boston Globe posted that morning. Classes were fun and laid back, he encouraged discussions and touched on really interesting topics. Weekly reflection papers (1 page).
Knowledgeable and great at his job. Took class as an elective and it was my favorite class all semester. Best prof I've had

Took him for Interpreting the Day's News at Northeastern.   Great professor, really knows a lot about reporting and the whole journalism industry. Lectures were really laid-back and he encouraged discussion, not just him talking at the students. Not a harsh grader. Lets you pick your own topics for papers--really interesting.   WOULD RECOMMEND!
Really great professor. Enjoys his job. Very knowledgeable.

Took Dr. Heefner for Capstone (HIST 4701). She always made herself available when people had questions. Very lenient on requirements for class assignments as long as you put in some preparation and become familiar with your topic. A great professor and a valuable resource for History majors. Definitely take a history class with her if you can!

[HIST 1215] Take a class with her! Despite being a department chair, Professor Heefner still made herself incredibly available to us. Classes went by fast because they were engaging. Her class is reading heavy and she requires you to purchase all of the books you read, but it's worth it for the amount of knowledge you come out of the class with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class to take. Prof. Heefner is a solid professor - interesting lectures and engaging in conversation. There is lots of reading, but the reading gives context to discussions and expands on the lectures. For this COVID semester, she emphasized participation and attendance pretty hard, but it wasn't ever boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor who was very encouraging and helpful with my paper! Made me love history even more.

This is the second course I've taken with Professor Heefner. She is a phenomenal teacher. You'll have to do a lot of work (SO MUCH READING) but it'll be worth it and you'll learn a ton. Professor Heefner is also one of the kindest, caring, and understanding professors I've met. If you're ever struggling she's there to help out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: TONS of reading, but interesting course! Professor Heefner was easily accessible outside of class and was always willing to meet to talk about my paper which was really helpful. This was one of my first history courses at NEU and I'm very happy with my experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Heefner is one of the best professors I've ever had. She's engaged, funny, down to earth, and knowledgeable. You have to read a lot for her class, but she goes out of her way to pick interesting materials and create a good atmosphere for discussion. Genuinely wants to help students learn; if you put in a lot, so will she.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is super engaging and I learned a ton. I think this class should be mandatory for Econ majors. That being said it wasn't an easy class. You have to show up since there's a quiz every day, but he gives out tons of extra credit and the readings are short. He's also super literal so take everything he says exactly as he says it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor porter is understanding, he is also a very great teacher who forces you to do the work. I enjoyed this course because he truly is passionate and hilarious. He keeps his students engaged and he grades fairly. What you put in is what you get out

Super easy class. Flipped classroom (you learn everything at home and then he quizzes you every single day in class.) Bad at teaching when it's something that's not from the textbook.  Reinterpreted the capm formula to his liking, quizzes you on extremely trivial topics. You feel like you are trying to avoid his trick questions rather than learn.

Not a bad guy, but not a good prof. Don't recommend taking this course unless you are SURE that you want to go into this industry, bc otherwise, with the way it's structured, it feels worthless and a waste of resources. You will get cold-called, and you will develop a tolerance for potentially being humiliated in class.

If you complete the readings, you're in good shape. It definitely takes time to get used to, but he is very funny. He is also very caring, always responds to emails, and is ready to understand circumstances.

Super engaging professor who makes sure concepts are understood before moving on. As an econ major without much prior finance knowledge his course was super useful for my co-op search.

Pretty straightforward daily quizzes with material straight from the readings, and clearly tells us what to expect on midterms and finals

Tough class. Got a B- but I've never learned more in one class. Genuinely cared that you learned. 10/10 best class I've ever taken at NEU. You have to go to class and you have to do questions all the time but that pushes you to learn.

Words cannot describe how terrible I find this guy. He is a complete drama queen who cares more about theatrics and jokes than actually teaching. He doesn't know how to teach the content and will keep on goin even when half the students have no idea what's going on. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Porter is legitimately so easy, I'll never understand the bad reviews. The daily quizzes are basically always taken directly from the previous night's reading and even then you can ask him to explain the material at the beginning of class. The way he teaches is a little slow, but definitely ensures everyone understands the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He will make fun of you specially if you are shy, english is not your first language and/or are a women. He gets along better with guys, but everyone hates him. NOT DRC FRIENDLY. AROUND 3 QUIZZES EVERYDAY. He does not know how to teach and his classes are just him reading the book on the board and asking people if they have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a super easy class, but I made his class engaging regularly, knowledgable. I took class with him and he would go out of his way to make sure we learnt. Great Guy.

Took macro theory then money and banking with this prof. You can't coast through his classes and you really have to work for an A. He quizzes often (if not everyday) and assigns reading - do them or you'll be humiliated when he cold calls. All of the other reviews are pretty accurate, you might have trauma from his class but you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The GOAT. Don't listen to these salty-ass kids complain about their grade since they barely want to do 15 minutes of reading. An over accomplished professor throughout his career. Gives amazing feedback, really make to tie all concepts to the 'real world'. If you want to excel in finance, this is your guy. We need more professors like Mr. Porter.

Genuinely the most embarrassing human being I have ever met. The first day he screamed at our class to call “Thor - God of Thunder”. reviews.comment: PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD DO NOT TAKE. FDOC said "im not here to teach you" bruh. he cold calls, HARASSES you, multiple quizzes daily, so much textbook reading he assigns the day before class, said he'd throw a book at my head as hard as he could if i didn't answer a question right. basically just schizophrenic rambling all class. PLEASE AVOID!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This professor was horrible. He wanted us to take daily quizzes about things he hadn't taught us yet. Also, he started each class with weird music.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Enjoys roasting the class, talking over everybody, and daily quizzes, I would take a different teacher if you can!
Really awful professor, quizzed every day and based on self-reading. Grades are only dependent on exams, if you don't score high on your daily quiz then you will end up with low grades as well.

If you have at least half a braincell, go to class, and do about 20 minutes of reading before going to class, you will do great. Emphasizes examples in lectures, practically tells you every single question that will be on the midterm and final. Really cares about his students learning the material. Easiest 100+ in my life

I greatly enjoy Prof. Porters classes. I understand the criticisms of him having quizes every day, and that they are a majority of the grade you receive, but he almost always tells you exactly what he's going to ask on the quiz before class and if you do the reading and pay attention to canvas you will be 100% fine.

He quizzes before teaching you. I was about to take his class again because he is super exciting and teaches really interesting material but he's to unpredictable, the quizzes are worth too much. I'm protecting my peace. Also he never has real office hours. I got an A on the final and B+ on the midterm quizzes are your grade. PERIODT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In my experience Professor Porter is the best professor in the Econ/Finance department at this school. He is extremely engaging, explains complex concepts in simple terms well, and always provides real world context. Whether you are a strong or weak student, he treats every person with the same level of importance, patience. Highly recommend.
Takes quizzes every class... i am not getting a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: P/P taught intermacro at BU this semester as well. He puts a closer focus on the business aspect of macroeconomics, which could be troublesome for theoretical economics majors (me). Class is very easy, take good notes and you will be fine. The class average for the mid-term was 91% with a lot of extra credit opportunities. I ended with 100.3%.

Understand where bad reviews come from, but my favorite prof @ NEU. Only homework is reading a few sections & taking notes before classes. Has a quiz once a class on reading, but always open note and several extra credit. Teaching style is very applied learning (don't take if not your pref): answers questions by walking student through example.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He will cold call and it is awkward because he gets mad at you if you don't know. He can be brutal to you if you don't know the material, however, if you are prepared and read and make sure you understand the material you will do well. He is good at explaining things if you ask him to go over things.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor created a very unwelcoming environment. Students attempt to speak/ask questions, but Porter would immediately shut them down or respond in a rude manner.
