reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Im absolutely appalled by this man. Have to report him to the dean and dropped with a W because I felt unsafe in the class. Weirdly one day started to pick on me made fun of my handwriting, my quiz answers infront of the class, then cussed at me and told me I wasn't trying hard enough. Never posted the readings and was pissed if we didn't do them.

Absolutely avoid this man at all costs. I had him my first year and I never had a class as bad as his. He's a d*ck. You ask him a question and he gives you a passive aggressive response. Never taught anything well but gave pop quizzes. I still have PTSD from this guy. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Porter is known at Northeastern for being one of the worst economics professors. He's infamous for his unique combination of harsh grading and obfuscating teaching style. If you take one of his classes, expect frequent quizzes on topics and models on which you will be ill-prepared. Porter's mantra is quiz now, teach later. Avoid if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He has a weird/mean sense of humor which nobody in my class was particularly fond of. Class consists of reviewing old material, a daily quiz, then going over the quiz material (for the first time after you failed the daily quiz instead of before taking it). He does reach out when you miss class/feel down though so I like him.

You get an easy quiz everyday. Non conventional teaching style and overall a nice guy. He likes to joke around so some people can perceive that as hostile, but he's just trying to have fun. He is very 'real world' . By the end of the class, we were barely learning anything though, so I wish he taught more in Intro to Macro.

He gets a bad rep because he quizzes every day, but they are easy and he gives you an idea of what's on them. He is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable, explains concepts very well, and makes class interesting. You have to take a lot of reading notes, but if you do them you can easily get an A. He cares abt students and helps u succeed. Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Porter gets a bad rep, but he isn't that bad. He just has a non-traditional teaching style. Just engage with the readings and if you demonstrate that you are putting in effort, he will help you understand stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have right now. He creates a hostile work environment where we are all afraid to ask questions because he is rude/condescending. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I dont understand Gerald's negative reviews. He's really not as disrespectful as they make him out to be. The class is hard, but the pace (around a week per chapter) is very chill, with plenty of time to earn something you don't understand. Really nice guy. Only problem I had was that pop quizzes are 1/3 of the entire grade and they are NOT easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst economics professors at Northeastern. Rude and disrespectful. He doesn't teach you anything, he just makes you read the textbook and then quizzes you on the content you self-taught. He does ask if there was anything in the reading that confused you but there is never enough time as he needs to do the quiz. Don't choose him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: An extremely disrespectful and rude professor. In fact, I don't understand why he's even allowed to be a professor. Even if students struggled in class, they'd be deterred to get help from him since he'd simply make condescending comments at them.
Horrible professor and person. Instead of helping you if you are struggling, he will accuse you of cheating. Avoid.
Worst professor ever. Do not take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easy class if you pay attention. Pop quizzes are just word for word repeat of him/textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Couple of notes for Prof. Porter: -Read the textebook before classes for pop quizzes; RTFQ!!! -Daily quizzes in class(approximately 40-45 quizzes throughout the Fall semester) -Mid(30%) was easy, Final(40%) was like a nightmare -Lots of extra credit opportunities -If your Canvas's overall percentage before Final >98% ----> Waive Final Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: AWFUL PROFESSOR! He is not prepared to teach Principles of Management! We did accounting and formulas all course!!! He has no structure of the lesson. He even didn't have a table of contents s of the course! We never knew what are we going to study! When I asked him for a Syllabus he said "take really great notes during the class". Worstteacherever

Bruh people who are bashing him clearly didn't show up to classes or did not take any notes. The class was quite easy if you did both of the above. He takes as much time as needed to go over topics that are giving the class a tough time, and those "daily quizzes" are either straight from the book, partner quizzes, or he told you topics last class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES. He is condescending towards students and is unable to teach effectively. Please do not take his classes - I'm writing this review to hopefully help out future students and to deter them from this awful experience. Side note: I'm sure he would be fine in other contexts (funny, even!), but he does not belong in academia.

Never met a worse Econ professor. I dreaded going to class every time, even though I had to due to the frequent pop quizzes. He's unhelpful during office hours, though he is always there; the only way you'll learn is by reading the textbook. He also has this weird bit where he likes to pretend (maybe he's serious) he's obsessed with Taylor Swift.

reviews.comment: Prof. Von Strunck is a really funny guy who definitely wants his students to learn. However, all of the work he assigns is quizzes and assignments through an outdated textbook that are not relevant to the content on the lectures at all. Still a fun class.

He basically just read off of the slides, which seemed a bit old (ex. graphs from 2015). If you keep up with the homework you should do fine, but try to actually do the readings as well. I felt the tests had very random questions on them that no one would know the answer to, since it was never gone over in class.

Prof. von Strunck was funny and an entertaining lecturer, but the lectures themselves were pretty useless in the grand scheme of things. The tests came directly from the info from the textbook -even the smallest details you may skim over- so reading the book is extremely important to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor von Strunck is an amazing Professor. Very intelligent guy who really makes you understand psychology stuff very well. Takes time to explain to students when they have questions. He asks a lot of questions during lectures and keeps the class engaged.

Great guy but terrible lectures. All the homework is based on the textbook and all tests are generated through homework questions. Fun and entertaining class, however don't rely on his lectures because they can be incorrect. He doesn't ever know how to answer students questions based on the lectures either. He'll make you laugh though.
Amazing professor. Made class fun and enjoyable. Really engaging and well in explaining difficult topics.
Just finished my final exam with Dr. Von Strunck. Great experience, and such a funny guy. Also probably best dressed professor.
Do not take unless you want to memorize a textbook in order to do well. Exams have NOTHING to do with lecture.
loved him. taking another class with him next semester.

One of the best professors I have taken at NU. Very knowledgeable, caring, and knows how to engage students. This is my third class with Dr Von Strunk, and I can only recommend him. If you want to learn, take his classes.

Had him freshman year loved him so I retook him this year for 3406. Tests are not hard at all, the rest of the grade is based on you showing up to class and completing some online activites to completion. Funny guy too always likes a good laugh and will challenge you when you are confident in your claims to push you to give a real explanation.
Prof. Von struck is awesome. Had fisrt exam yesterday and scored well. Lots of homework but counts to your final grade. It also helps on the exams. Funny guy. Knows his stuff, and super smart.

Amazing professor! Funniest guy I've ever been in class with. Makes lectures very fun and intresting. Gives good examples so you understand the material better. Lots of homework, but it's part of your grade and will help you on the exam.

Highly recommend him!
Terrible. Don't take him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I started writing down all of my issues but ran out of words pretty quick. In short, Prof Von Strunck made many mistakes (directly contradicting the textbook) which he refused to correct or admit to, was very difficult to reach out to for help, and generally made class very unenjoyable. I have never hated psychology more.

I absolutely loved taking this course with Dr. von Strunck. A very insightful Professor with much knowledge and plenty of examples during class so you can understand and learn the different concepts of psychology. Funny guy as well with a very sarcastic humor. 5 exams determine your final grade, and the final is not a cumulative one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great professor. made concepts easy to understand. so enthusiastic and funny. thanks for a great semester!

Try getting any other professor for psych but him!! I walked into class expecting it to be enjoyable, but it wasn't. His slides had mistakes in it, and when corrected, he wouldn't admit he was wrong. Very ignorant to social justice issues as well. Grade based off 5 hard exams that are textbook-based. Rude teacher who didn't want to see us succeed.

I think he is very overrated. There is no incentive of going to class because the textbook company makes the exams. The entire grade is based on 5 exams, 20% each. I attended maybe 5 lectures in total. You have to know everything on the chapters to do well in the exam. He is funny but that wasnt enough for me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Truly an amazing professor. Dr von struck is funny and hilarious. Though lectures can be long he makes them very interesting, he knows his stuff and his knowledge is scary at times as he can always relate the info to every day life. Take his classes if you truly want to learn!
do not take any of his classes. very unhelpful and not a good teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Von Strunck is a very funny and good lecturer. He provides many examples that help to better understand the concepts. Your entire grade is solely based off of 5 exams which can be very frustrating. If you read the textbook and do the practice exams you should be fine, but beware that the exams can be very tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So far i realty like his development class. He knows his stuff and is super funny. He explains the material in a way you can relate and understand. Thumbs up!
amazing professor. looking forward to taking another class with him starting tomorrow.

Very thoughtful person and educator. He would like all of his students to attend so that they can engage with the material, but he is understanding of life unfolding and barring attendance. Be sure to communicate with him if you are not able to be the best student you can be, he is there to hear it. Will miss learning from Dr. Von Strunck.

There was no point in showing up to class. He just lectured on small ideas from the textbook. The tests were made from specific details about the textbook. You had to read the textbook and do the practice Hw that's not even graded repeatedly to do well on the tests. Mcgraw Hill made the tests not him. Might as well had been an online course.

This was an absolutely great experience. Professor von Strunck was so enthusiastic about the subject and I learned a lot from him. He is funny, caring, and has a great personality. Great knowledge and you will do great if you read the book and pay attention in class.

truly an amazing professor. very funny, caring and helps students outside of class as well. his lectures are funny and you need to attend and study to do well on the exams. i would definitly recommend dr. van strunk again.

Dr. Von Strunck was fine, generally just inoffensive as a professor. He's funny, which can make his otherwise pretty dry lectures tolerable. Entire grade was based on 5 tests, all of which come directly from the textbook company. Read the chapters and do the practice problems and it's impossible to get anything below a 90.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: only graded on five exams and there's no hw besides reading. you do have to read the entire textbook to do well. tests are the same as practice questions.Professor von struck is a little witty old man and he is super sweet but he refuse to give out lecture slides. please von struck they would've been so helpful for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really bad teacher overall. Final grade determined by 4 midterms and 1 final, so very test heavy class. He doesn't curve and doesn't round. Seems like his slides are very old and sometimes have wrong info, so studying for the test was fully based on textbook since his lectures are so unhelpful. For a psych class, it was unreasonably hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It seems like he cares about his students, but that is not reflected in the grading. I went to him one day and he told me that tests are not representative of someone's knowledge but still refused to change the grading. The averages were terrible and there was no curve. He also doesn't post his presentation notes and blocks them while in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good professor for a beginner psychology class. His lectures are engaging and he is always open to questions and further discussion of certain topics. He is a very caring professor and really wants his students to do well. As long as you study with the resources he provides the tests should be pretty simple, 10/10 recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a solid professor and had enjoyable lectures. His tests were tough though and averages were often in the high 70s low 80s. For a class that is only graded on exams that is pretty scary. If you study the textbook you should be good though but even with that I still did not do great on the exams.

Not a fan of this man as a professor. He seems really nice, but he just cannot teach to save his life. In order to do well in this class you have to read the textbook and even then the tests are pretty hard. Don't take this class if you are bad at test taking.

Unhelpful. He puts up slides and reads them. Half the time he goes too fast and stands in the way of the board. He doesn't post the slides afterward. Everything is based on the textbook-generated exams and if you meet with him you can tell he has never even seen the questions before. Exams are 100% of your grade so you just have to teach yourself.

Dr. von Strunck is an amazing psych professor. This class is all about putting in the work. Exams are difficult. You have to memorize everything in the textbook and be able to apply the knowledge on the exams. Heavy on memorizing but exams aren't too bad. Exams make up the whole final grade. 5 exams each 20%. Very engaging and classes are fun.

Von Struncks's developmental psych class is the hardest/most involved psych classes I've taken. You have to do the readings to do well in this class, and they are pretty long. But it's so worth it, because it ended out being my favorite psych class ever as well! Von Strunck is the best. He's super funny and caring.

He was the worst professor I've ever had! First of all, he doesn't lecture at all. Divided us into 8 different groups and make us teach in class while he sits at the back listening to the presentations. Quizzed/tested us on content that he did not teach but insisted that he taught them. Anyone in that class can agree that he did not teach at all.

Attendance was "mandatory" but not graded, yet he targeted people who chose to not attend class by reporting us at risk to fail & emailing counselors (regardless of grade). Taught 1 lecture himself, the rest were student presentations (again, required but not graded). Tests are made from infinite (not graded) connect questions/assignments.
He's very nice and truly tries his best to make psych interesting. Tests are not too bad, just be sure to review the textbook beforehand. He tells the best jokes also!

Truly passionate about psych, tried to engage with students. Homework is time consuming but easy, lectures and practice tests are exactly like exams, and exams take max 30 mins. Posts everything online, accessible after class, but very strict about grades (no curving or leniency). As long as you do the practice tests, you will do great in the class

The most amazing professor!!! Super smart and it shows, he really knows what he is talking about! Also super funny and engaging, makes you want to come to class. The online learning structure is great and the practice quizzes are just like the exam. Loved it so much I am taking another class from him in the fall!

Professor Von Strunck loves psychology and you can notice this through his lectures. He truly loves what he is teaching and it makes the class even more engaging. The final grade is based on 5 exams and homework. As long as you pay attention, and practice before exams, you should be good!

I had Dr. von Strunck for both Abnormal and Developmental Psychology, and his teaching style is pretty much the same across both courses. He's very passionate about psychology and encourages thoughtful discussions in class. Lectures are very important to exam material, but the homework/practice quizzes are equally (or arguably more) important!

Highly recommend reading the textbook. Lectures are directly based off of the textbook; however, in class he breezes through the slides and skips important information and explanations. Exams are just like the practice quizzes. Sometimes there are a few questions that seem random, but they are definitely fair.

He is an awesome professor. He knows what he’s talking about and really wants his students to do well. Exams were online and were very straight forward if you studied by taking the practice quizzes. Always had funny stories to say and was very enthusiastic about learning!

Amazing professor. Cares so much about the well-being of all his students. Lectures were great as well but not mandatory. Showed up every day with a smile on his face. Intriguing lectures. Only grades were 5 tests which were identical to the practice quizzes. Totally recommend. Awesome guy.

Dr. von Strunck really does care about what he teaches and that makes his lectures enjoyable. The syllabus is what we stuck to the entire semester and it's important to keep track of. In Foundations, exams are 100% of our grade - however the required textbook has practice quizzes and they're basically the same as the test. Would take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely love him he's so sweet and really wants you to learn. I remember reading somewhere that people found him tough so I was skeptical but I got to know him and he's super friendly and easy to reach out to. He replies quickly to emails and puts your mental health first, he really does care about you as a person not just as a student.

This class was mostly lecture, but the prof is prepared and knows his stuff.   He posts slides after each class which helps with studying for tests.   Most of the grade is based on tests and quizzes but the prof give a study guide before each test.  You have to attend class to be ready for tests.

Grade is mostly based on tests but he is up front about that.  If you go to class and use the study guides he provides before exams you will be prepared.  The class was a good overview of a field I've been curious about for a while.  Interesting lecturer especially the polling and real world data uses
I took this class as an elective and am glad I did!  Dr Hunt is organized and gives good power point lectures (and he posts the slides).  I would take another one of his classes..
Lectures are sooooo boring and you are forced to come to class because he will literally ask the most specific questions ever such as "what did I say in this about blah blah blah"
He makes exams worth 75% of your grade and his exams are soooo specific. Don't take this class if you think it'll be easy
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All you need to do is attend class, take notes, and ask questions if you are confused. Prof Hunt is a very straightforward lecturer but he cares about his students and the topics he teaches

Course is lecture-oriented and test-heavy, but this is all covered in the syllabus.   Attendance is a component of the grade but is not mandatory per se (you just lose points for unexcused absences, which some students are okay with).   Class meetings were interesting and instructor is well-prepared and knowledgeable.   A good experience overall!

Taken all three classes he offers. Straightforward and teaches right from the textbook, but that can make the mandatory attendance feel a little redundant if you read. Unfortunately cursed with an extremely flat tone but you learn to pick up on his passion. Exams are largely predictable but have one or two random questions on minor sidenotes.

Such a cutie and so nice. People are too mean to him. I dedicated 30% of my brain to listening to him in this class and the rest to studying and it was great! As long as you go to the lectures you'll be fine. The exams are full of questions about something he mentioned in passing that you didn't even write down because it sounded too specific.

Teaching style is mostly lecture (big class).    Lectures are clear and he posts his slides after each class.  Grade is based on three exams but I hear he generally offers an extra credit paper toward the end of the semester.  Attendance is important if you want to do well on exams since he uses examples in class that go beyond the textbook.

reviews.comment: Grade is based on two exams and nine homework assignments.    Professor Hunt is very knowledgeable and seems to care about his students.

Extremely boring and monotone lectures, cant teach. No assignments, graded only by 3-4 exams that are really hard, so if u dont do well on those good luck with ur grade. Attendance is mandatory and part of ur grade. if ur taking this cause u think this is gonna be a easy grade DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. be prepared to teach urself
if you hate yourself and you love listening to white noise take his class.

Hunt honestly seems like a super sweet guy but he has the MOST boring lectures. reviews.comment: I was scared to have him at first but he's honestly not a bad professor at all. It's easy to pass this class and the topics we discuss are genuinely interesting! The exams in my opinion are pretty straightforward but I will say attending this class will help you a lot.

reviews.comment: Very easy just 3 exams, but he does not record his lectures and slides are a bit dry. You have take notes in class to know whats going on.

reviews.comment:
He does not record his lectures and his slides are a bit dry. So you have to go everyday and take notes to know whats going on.He does give great extra credit with a paper that can be up to 10 points and if you have a great and strong attendence he will give you points.

DO NOT TAKE IF YOU ARE NOT A TEST TAKER OR CANT GO TO CLASS 95% OF THE TIME!!

Good professor, been teaching a long time. Will help if you reach out. Graded by only 3 exams and an extra-credit paper. reviews.comment: Completely lecture based with no homework only graded on 3 exams and one extra credit paper (SOCL1101)

Prof. Hunt, although sometimes a little monotone, is clearly passionate about the subject. His lectures are very organized and easy to follow. If you need to take an intro to sociology class, he's a great option.

Beware that this class is text heavy and you have to read in order to do good. As someone who did not pick up the textbook, I did okay based of his lectures because he is clear and sums up the textbook pretty well. There are 9HW assignments and 2 tests (mid-terms & final). Overall this is a good class, I do recommend it especially if soc major

Professor clearly knew the subject, but lectures weren't very engaging; often taught directly from the textbook. Chapters are long, but textbook is very easy to read. 9 HW assignments, he drops the lowest. Exams are MC and pretty straightforward.

For social psychology, there is no homework. The grade is based solely on three tests which is a little intimidating but it's an easy course if you look over the study guides he provides. You learn a lot in the class and it really makes you think/curious. I declared a minor in sociology because of it. Hunt is a good professor and would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hunt’s lectures are very dry. Class time is poorly spent, as discussions were unhelpful. The class is very unstructured and disorganized. His lecture slides are not available to us on Blackboard. Most proximally, the class is too test-oriented, the final grade is only based on three MCQ exams. I don’t recommend taking this class with him.

Great class.  Prof. Hunt is very organized and presents the material clearly.  I liked the class format: good mix of lecture and discussion (but you have to do the readings to get anything out of the discussion days).  I only went to office hours once but found the prof helpful.  I'd definitely recommend this class.

Hunt gives good powerpoint lectures- he knows how to sum things up and present them in an organized manner. However once he switches to class discussions class feels disruptive, and doing so unhelpful for learning. He should just stick to lecturing with powerpoints. Too much assigned reading by the way.
Prof. Hunt is a good, fair teacher. Some find him on the boring side but I felt that his explainations for certain concepts was refreshing.

I find him to be a nice guy.  He can be a bit on the dry side, but he makes an effort to get to know your name, grades fairly, and is excellent at explaining things.  Very good professor, in my opinion.

Really knows what he's talking about and wants everyone to pass. Literally just does quizzes based on content clearly covered the previous lecture. Exams are very similar to example exams provided on canvas. Attend every lecture, pay close attention and take notes and you're golden.

Hashemi is probably the professor that will have the longest lasting impact on me and how I work. The class (ME 4550) is very fast pace in the first few weeks but definitely chills out the 2nd month onward. He might be strict and have some aggressive grading policies but he recognizes effort and makes sure you learn and retain the material

Consistently makes mistake on in class example problems, only noticing them when pointed out by students. Does not teach the material well contradicting the book often. Incredibly boring lectures. Constantly upset when a student asks a "undergraduate question" in a graduate class (not understanding some students have been out of school for a while)

harsh prof, super hard class, do not reccomend

reviews.comment: Homeworks are hours of incredibly difficult busy work. Spends the whole lecture deriving equations without any suggestion on how to use them.

spend every single minute of class time solving random examples without explaining the reason behind. keep emphasizing how easy the course would be if you follow his method while making a lot of mistakes when solving example problems.
Real good teacher, usually not hard to understand and always willing to do another example.
Very smart and conscientious. The best professor among whom I have ever met!

Hashemi knows the material well, however he teaches in a very oldschool fashion where he always demands "respect," forces you to use outdated homework software and punishes you heavily for simple mistakes that propagate easily in a class with a lot of small calculations. Avoid at all costs

reviews.comment: I changed my section after the first day of class! he maybe smart, doesn't know how to talk to people, very rude! Needs to learn how to respect students! Do not take him.

The best Professor you can have a course with if you really want to challenge yourself, go out of your comfort zone, and learn something that will be beneficial for you later in job or academia. Very nice personality, super intelligent (MIT man), while very serious in the class. You need to really read, work, and show some level of intelligence.
incredibly harsh grader, consistently gives 0's even if you have the correct answer and he doesnt like your work.

Professor Hashemi knows what he is talking about but is not very good at teaching. He expects the class to know the subject already and skips teaching new topics and goes right into doing example problems. He will use his own complicated manner to solve a problem and when a student points out an easier method he cant understand it.

Had Prof. Hashemi for three different classes - an entry level FEA class, sernior level Mech Design, and a grad level mechanics of materials class. One of the most demanding professors I've had (currently a grad student and haven't had any classes nearly as hard as his). Can come off rough, but will put the effort to help you learn IF YOU DO.

Online lectures were all out of order. He put materials that were not covered in any lectures in the exam. Arrogant inside and outside of classroom. Assumes you understand and remember everything from undergrad and would refuse to answer some of your questions. Might as well talk to a wall before you go to his office. Your'e on your own

I would akin his lectures to an electric eel. The swiftness of his voice combined with the intensity of his electric personality combine to form a create of unmatched beauty and perfection. He talks very quickly but always answers questions and finds time to entertain his class with jokes so brilliant that, many times, even I could not comprehend.
Hard teacher, but he knows what hes talking about. Expects a lot of work from his students but will reward you if you show you put in a real effort.

Hashemi is the man. Although he has an accent, he is very easy to understand. His teaching methods are clear and concise, and he makes great analogies to learn the material. He can tell when the class is losing interest and will tell jokes to keep everyone entertained. He was hilarious and a great teacher. I learned a lot in his classes!

He is hard to understand, and he tries to be funny, but fails to make sense.  He yells at the class constantly wasting a lot of time.  You cannot bring food or drinks to class.  Unless you suck up to him, you will have to basically teach yourself.

Overall a good professor. Lectures are interesting and he goes on several humerous tangents about his personal life. Teaches at 100 mph, but very clear and concise. His tests are very difficult, but if you go see him he usually provides you with some valuable insight.  Likes to see students who make an effort and care about the class

He's easy enough to follow at first and understanding him then makes it easier towards the end of the semester. Kinda harsh when it comes to answering questions. Tests were tricky but he made sure we knew what to expect.
Alot of work to do, starts off easy, then gets harder.  Exams are really difficult compared to class work.  He likes blueberry muffins.

She is hands down one of the best professors at Northeastern. Cares a lot about her students. Grade is mostly based on the client consulting project, which is time-consuming but extremely worth it at the end for personal skills. Participation and attendance matters a lot, so show up and raise your hand, you will be fine! 100% take this class!

Prof. MacNiel is really nice and cares about her students a lot. She facilitates a very welcoming environment for students, and has interesting lectures on managing change. Most of the work is group project stuff. Not really HW outside of class, just reading. If you show up and participate once in a while you'll do fine.

Class is majority group projects (whole semester project), good professional opportunity unless you get stuck with a rough group. Teacher is phenomenal, very caring, wants you to learn, consistent class discussions. Grades based off rubric. Participation matters, but its easy to participate. Valuable class content, generally engaging/not boring.

This is absolutely the Organizational Behavior professor you should take! I honestly had fun in this class, and felt like it was so applicable to the things I encountered on co-op. Professor MacNeil is a very fair grader, and is always willing to accommodate students. She leads by example and is so kind. Highly recommend!

The class was fun with the group projects and there were no exams but her attendance policy is really difficult as she does not excuse you out of class even if you are sick beyond the two wellness days you can take which is really not practical if you end up falling sick or have any sort of emergency. 
She is very strict with participation as well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of work for a business minor class. There is a ~300 word reflection after every class. 25% of the grade is also a group project which involves interviewing personnel from an organization and presenting the findings. Professor Macneil is caring and will always try to do different activities in class.

Definitely take ORGB with professor MacNeil! It's such a fun class and she really cares about her students. As long as you show up to lectures, participate, and do your assigned work, you should get a good grade. The textbook readings aren't necessary.
just dont take

one can not maintain good Gpa under him, if u want to increase gpa I would not suggest his class. Exams are too heavy, you need to memorize 20+ pseudo codes, and in assignments also, you will not get full marks always. He is a strict professor and would not listen to what you have to say, if he sets his mind to something.

Amazing lectures. If you do the work, you'll learn a lot.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Very clear and helpful.
No matter how much other students berate him, one can't deny that he is a great instructor for algo. He knows what he's teaching and his lecture delivery style is also clear.

reviews.comment: Great professor. He's always there to help his students!

reviews.comment: People are just fearmongering in his reviews page. He isn't a bad professor. Students just have to pay extra attention to his lectures, and that's it. Exams are very predictable and he offers ample supports to students who approach him for help.

reviews.comment: Prof. Iraklis isnt as bad as other people show him to be. They all are rating him low cuz they couldn't maintain their sanity and grades in this class.

reviews.comment: Disorganized rubric and poorly structured exams that expect answers in one rigid format. Even correct solutions get zero if they differ (e.g., using a stack instead of a queue). Little concern for students. Take this course only if you can memorize and reproduce CLRS exactly as expected.

I got baited into memorizing 30+ pseudocode for the final.
which i guess is alright to know 
but it didnt feel good when i didnt get to apply my 30+ pseudocode of knowledge on the 5 questions which are on the final
it feels like he said gullible is written on the ceiling and i looked up

The grading practices are excessively punitive, communication is effectively nonexistent, and the lack of transparency has caused extreme and unnecessary stress. This experience has significantly impacted my mental well-being and delayed my academic progress, and it should be formally reviewed.

If you want to sharpen algorithms, this course delivers. Lectures are structured and well paced—until the end, when it suddenly accelerates. But if you're aiming for a smooth learning curve or you're protecting your GPA, think twice: grading feels bureaucratic, partial credit is hard to defend, and the pressure can make learning feel punishing.
Run, worst professor of all time, would ask you to follow EXACTLY how the slides or the book implement the algorithm, or you lose a lot of points even if you are correct.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Algorithms is a very hard class to take in general. Materials are heavy - it's just not a fun topic. But Prof. Herc really tries his hardest to make it work in the short time frame and the knowledge people already have (1st Sem. Grads all the way to PhD).

Poor learning structure. Exams are questions directly from the textbook but the textbook is dense. His lectures help a little with the exams and homework but they are more so supplements. Also, not enough questions on exams, if you miss just one, you fail.

I am pretty sure the good reviews are fake reviews. He is a bad lecturer and barely explains anything. He insists on following the book and visiting office hours and TA's but the book is dense af and the office hours are just a repetition of the class. Given how abysmal he is at teaching it feels almost criminal how harshly he grades. AVOID!!
Worst professor ever seen in my life. I failed by 0.21% and gives direct 0 even if your approach is in correct direction. RUN!!!!

Won't Recommend. 
The grading criteria for assignments and exams is non-sensical. Each exam has 4 questions, so if you commit a mistake in one, you risk falling by a letter grade. Highly theoretical, will not help in passing interviews. Nothing to learn here, stay away. Take some other worthwhile course, and LeetCode if you wanna pass interviews.

Do not even think of taking this class, professor is very rude and does not care about students. Run away from this course and professor. I failed by 0.1%, the professor didn't consider my case, didn't reply to any emails or messages. Grades ruthlessly.  If you mess up even one of the exam, be prepared to retake the course. RUN!!!!!!!!!!

I really enjoyed being in class with this professor. His course work was very flexible and fair, his lectures were very engaging and informative. His class was the perfect length. Overall I feel this was one of the most effective educators I've had in my program this far. I would absolutely take his class again if I could.
run, don't take with him
not a good lecturer

Worst grader I have ever seen. If you do not do things by his book you will loose marks, irrespective of if your answer is right, if it is not the way he has taught the topic you will be loosing your grade. I will not recommend taking this course under him in any circumstance. He refuses to give the answers for the assignments.

agree with other comments. he is a nice guy but an awful lecturer. his slides are just copying textbooks and it is hard to understand what he talks at class. i attended all the classes and felt it was such a waste of time. he is also very tough grader and he makes everything more confusing. this is the worst course I ever took.

Lectures are informative and engaging. Course is very well organized with assignments every week, and grades released timely. 

However, not an easy A, you will need to study and may need to attend OH often. 5-8 hours a week outside of class is expected. 

Grading appears harsh sometimes, but all assignments(and exams) have some bonus points.

The professor grades based on concept clarity. If you understand and justify the concepts well, it greatly benefits you. He is clear on fundamentals and pays attention to details that matter. His challenging assignments prepare you for exams and promote growth. The subject is easy if you're strong on the basics. TAs are responsible and helpful.

This was the worst I've had. Useless lectures with empty slides. Condescending on Piazza and impossible to understand due to his accent.  Grading was insanely harsh. Lost 10 points on a 15-point problem for a small mistake! Even with the right answer, a missing step meant you were wrong.  He also refused to give us homework solutions.
Grading criteria are unclear, and TAs require excessive explanation of basic concepts with no partial credit. very frustrating and inconsistent.

This course was pretty difficult. I took it as an undergrad as part of the PlusOne program. Prof Herc is super nice and willing to help you out. The lectures are informative, but reading the textbook is essential for doing well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cares about his students, is a nice guy, and will answer any question, but is an awful lecturer. You can tell he is really trying to explain the concepts, but he just makes things more confusing and hard to understand. I spent the whole semester working with a tutor and he was able to explain the concepts WAY better.

While Prof. Khan has her favorites, it really is not that bad. She likes the students that do what is expected of them. If you are not doing your work or showing up to class on time, then yeah she is not going to be as lenient with you. I promise you her class is not much work, just be a good student and you will be just fine.

Professor Iffat Khan's assignments are generally easy and manageable, and the exams are not too difficult if you keep up. She does use cold calling in class and she can come across as biased at times and she is very strict about deadlines even being a few minutes late on submissions isn't accepted, which can be frustrating.

I love Prof Khan, she is a great professor! She obviously wants the best for her students and is accessible outside class/responds to emails quickly. Not many things contribute to the grade, so it was my fault I got a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her class really isn't that difficult but it is confusing. Her quizzes and lectures are all over the place. She even said herself that she doesn't make her own quizzes and tests so when it comes time for the actual exams it can get confusing because that stuff wasn't too focused on in class. Overall a chill class but show up on time and participate

Professor Khan is an extremely unorganized professor. She teaches from a textbook, but quizzes/tests do not relate to the teachings in class. She sends weekly announcements recycled from years ago, and left a syllabus from 2020 on Canvas, which created confusion. I would avoid taking ANY class with her, as her teaching style was horrendous.

Very caring and nice professor who genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. Exam questions weren't too hard as long as you went to lecture and did reading. Sometimes will cold call during lectures but not often.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took her in the fall. SIT IN THE FRONT. She will like you more. Nice but not great at teaching, tests are weird but not that hard. Easy grader but usually will give like 95s. Cold calls people but the questions aren't hard.

She honestly doesn't teach you anything. I feel like my dad can teach me better, and he doesn't have a background in marketing. She gives mom vibes and will say beautiful work, but the content doesn't matter as much as how you present yourself to her. She will cold call you if you don't participate.

She requires students to sit in the front and not be late even for a minute, otherwise, she will question you in front of everyone when you enter the door. By the way, she is a bit discriminatory towards students who don't have American looks.
never take her class she has so much attitude and never look or reply to any of your e-mail.
Heavy emphasis on participation and puts students on the spot. Didn't understand half the content she attempted explaining. Take this class with anyone else.
She is amazing. I love her so much. she is great. no joke fr.

Khan is sweet and cares about students. Her lectures follow the textbook and she typically recites slides for the entire class. She cold calls but the questions are never too complex if you're paying attention. I feel that for our project she focused more on confidence and effort rather than small details and content. She never gives above a 95.

Nice person, but not meant to be a professor. You are graded by very little, it's easy for your grade to suffer if you do badly on one exam. She is an easy grader but it is extremely rare for her to give you a 100, she will take one point off for no reason. Lots of favoritism, teaches word-for-word text book, cold calls, boring lectures

Doesn't normally seem too sure of what it is she's going over. Nice, but very disorganized. Professor also doesn't make her own tests, making the exams confusing to do well on even if you know the concepts because they're so random.
Don't take this prof's class. Pretends to be kind but do not respect the students and will cut you off multiple times no matter how polite you are.

At first, her class might seem scary, but she is a very sweet and nice professor. If you show up on time and participate, you will have no difficulty. She is a very easy grader and wants everyone to pass with good grades, as she will say many times. As long as you are respectful and come to class, you will be just fine. Do not let her scare you.

Huge on participation, attendance, and getting to class on time. Will make it clear if she does not like you. Cold calls, will cut you off. Will claim reading textbook is necessary, not a soul in my class did and we all did fine. Incredibly easy grader, easy A. Exams multiple choice. Guidelines say to not claim favoritism, but ask anyone- she does.

Strange. Very clearly targets certain students that she does not like, specifically men. I was not one of them but it was obvious everyone could tell. Incredibly easy grader, pretty awful teacher. Can be scary when she singles you out or cold calls you but all the assignments that she grades are crazy lenient- the lowest was an 84%. Take for credit

Professor Khan might be the worst professor in all aspects. Barely teaches class, reads off a script as if students will fully comprehend what she's saying. Everything she says comes straight from the textbook and its definitions. I can confidently say that I learned nothing in her class. Highly recommend to stay away from any of her classes.

I see where all the other ratings are coming from, she does give a lot of stories and examples of companies (amazon, tesla, Microsoft) or her friends and family which are unrelated but it made the class fun with applicable knowledge for me. She may not be the best teacher but she is a great person and really understanding. I would recommend.
I participated in this class like no other. Literally made it my life's mission and she just gave me a trash grade. AVOID.
Tests were so easy but her lectures were really bad and she only cares about participation and attendance

Zero knowledge of course content. Lectures are essentially just repeating the text book. Makes it almost impossible to receive an A by refusing to give grades higher than 94 on any assignment. She is a nice person but not fit to be a professor of marketing

Dr Kahn is certainly the worst teacher I have ever had. We missed multiple chapters of the text book and classes consisted of her going on extensive rants that are completely unrelated to any course content. I left each class with a migraine headache after the professor had spoke continuously the whole class while not moving past the first slide.

Professor Khan is horrendous. Her classes consist of her rambling about Amazon and Elon Musk. Since she hasn't taught anything the entire semester, the exams are a complete gamble. My grade dropped 2 letter grades after the final. She needs to retire because clearly she is not fit to be a professor at this level. I feel bad for you future students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please take another professor if possible. The class itself is easy -- that isn't the problem. It's the fact that she is the most inconsistent grader of all time and doesn't give any individualized feedback on your work. If you question her, she just gives a roundabout answer that doesn't explain what you did wrong.

I would not suggest taking her. Nice person but not a great teacher. She reads off the textbook and isn't super clear about requirements for the projects. 45% of your grade will be based on 3 exams that have very few questions (the final had 10) and she grades projects/papers unnecessarily harshly. Don't feel like I learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher.  Only reason she is not getting a 1 because it is very easy to get an A- in this class.  Almost impossible to get an A.  3 tests worth 45% of grade, but tests vary from 10-20 questions so each question is worth about 1 percent of your grade.  The other 65% she gives students B+/A-, nothing higher and nothing lower.  Stay away

i dont suggest her. little work but quizzes are graded so heavily it's insane. lectures are unprepared and useless. syllabus is worthless and due dates are often unclear. she is really nice, but also rude sometimes and undependable. quizzes are fine if you read the textbook. grade is dependent on a few days of actual work throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Khan is a very kind and fair professor. A few things: participate in every class and raise your hand at least 2 times per class. Secondly, sit in the front rows of the class, it does help. Attendance is also a big emphasis. Unexcused absences will immediately dimmish your reputation in her eyes. Participate and you will get a good grade.

professor khan is genuinely sweet and wants the best for her students but she is a bad professor. Classes seemed unprepared, she tells the same stories over and over. She tries to change the due dates to make it easier for students but this makes everything more confusing If you can avoid her do it but it's not a difficult class to pass on your own
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized course. I didn't feel like I was learning anything most of the time during her lengthy lectures. While being a heavy lecture course, there are very few assignments given (no homework)making it very difficult to boost your grade. Strays off-topic all the time while also talking in circles. I would avoid taking her to save your GPA.

You have to attend class or else you won't know what's on the exam. The syllabus is pretty unhelpful and unorganized. She'll ask a question and then go around the whole class for a response, but shell judge your answer and cut you off.

does not give feedback or tell you anything that's going on during class. shes super nice but extremely disorganized and you won't know your final grade until the day grades are due. the syllabus is super off and you have to be in class otherwise you won't know what's due or what to study

Although this professor is very caring she calls on students randomly and will cut off your answer, she also does not give time to think and then will judge the answer (this judgement cut down on how much students openly participated). You are also graded on very little in this class: a case study paper, 2 quizzes, and a large group project
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most disorganized and disrespectful professor ever. She was often late to class, the syllabus was never accurate, and she never had a clear plan for class. Actively extremely rude to certain students and simply not good at explaining the course content.

She seems to be caring for her students but she oftentimes confuses me and makes me feel like this class is highly disorganized. Tests are kind of hard and you have to read textbooks. Participation is impossible because she cuts people off and does not wait for people to answer questions. I learned nothing from this class.

Professor Khan is a super caring person and always puts her students first in the classroom. She will always ask what the students prefer before assigning due dates and requirements for tests and projects. Though it is an easy course, she is very unclear with due dates and she can be forgetful at times. Overall great professor though

Professor Khan is a very nice person. She cares about her students but at times can be disorganized. The class has 3 group presentations and a midterm and final exam. The exams were super easy, just regurgitating definitions from textbook. Class discussions include textbook references. No reading and only homework is weekly discussion posts.

Prof Khan was like aight. Her class was so easy, all you have to do is show up and participate. make sure she knows who you are by the end of the semester. Tests are regurgitations of textbook definitions. However she takes random small points off just bc. Heavy group projects with presentations too
She is a wonderful professor, 100% take the class with her. Make sure she knows who you are (your name).

Prof Khan is nice, but the class is so disorganized. There was no syllabus and random unwritten expectations. My class was often confused about what we were learning because there were no modules or assigned readings or really a plan. She also cold calls and often interrupts students when she disagrees with them.

Prof Khan is a sweet person but she doesn't teach this course that well. Her lectures are often unorganized and unrelated to what we're learning. She tends to drag out her stories/examples which can make lectures boring and confusing. The exams/content are overall easy making it easy to get an A in her class but you won't learn much valuable info.

Pick any other prof. Both her class and her Canvas are disorganized to the point that you never know what's due. She cold calls people to ask their opinion on a topic, then shoots them down when she disagrees. Majority of class time is wasted on group projects that loosely correlate to content. Only used the textbook for the vocab midterm & final.

Prof Khan is a knowledgable professor. However, she is very disorganized and goes off on tangents. You can't really take notes in class cause the lectures aren't organized. The canvas page isn't organized either. She is reasonable with her tests though which are just defining 10 vocab words. You're also graded on 3 group presentations.

Professor Khan is amazing! I am currently in her International Business course and every class is so fun and unique. She clearly is passionate about her job and enjoys what she does. Can be a little disorganized with the syllabus sometimes, but nothing that clarification in class won't solve.

The absolute worst professor. She is constantly cold calling and then disrespecting your answers, she literally yelled at us every day, had such unclear expectations but somehow expected us to read her mind, and overall so disorganized. If you have to take international business, literally take it with any other teacher.

Great & funny professor. She is all over the place & unsure of her own due dates but will give extra time if needed. Weekly discussions were very easy, a midterm & final, & 2 group projects. The midterm & final were very easy & included memorizing textbook definitions. Would recommend just be ready to be called on to participate in discussions.

Although she generally nice, she has a tendency to call people out and tell them straight up that their points in class discussion are incorrect. Extremely disorganized. Didnt know my name and I attended every single class. Gave me a D in class participation and attendance even tho I participated in most classes. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: What a wonderful Professor! Although some students found her class boring, she has a vibrant personality that makes class interesting. Class is discussion based with two big group projects. Exams are vocab words and Dr. Khan wants everyone to do well. She was kind, understanding, enjoys what she teaches, and believed in every student!

Khan is a very nice teacher, very easy online midterm/finals. No pop quizzes, textbook optional, highly encourages in-class participation. Sometimes, the class can feel a little long. A little disorganized, but very understanding if there's miscommunications. Theres two group presentations, two group write-ups. Overall easy class!

Dr. Khan is one of the sweetest professors. She really cares about students' needs. Her class is very light on work. No need to read the textbook, just pay attention in class. Group projects and an easy midterm and final are majority of the grade. This class is a stress free one and you should try to get into Dr. Khan's section if possible!

Dr. Khan is a literal legend. Super nice and energetic. She has great stories to tell the class which relate to international business which then truly enhances the course. She may sound mean sometimes but it is simply because English is not her first language. Overall, an amazing professor and a perfect class to start my time at Northeastern.

So disorganized its ridiculous. Doesn't put due dates, tells us not to look at the syllabus because information is incorrect (doesn't bother to fix this). She shares some interesting stories during her letures but honestly I got nothing from the course.

Good person but very disorganized and confusing when lecturing. Never has proper due dates and often forgets student Qs, assignment dates, or her own announcements. Discussion Qs every week, couple of group projects, and 1 midterm and 1 final both just answering 1 question. Interesting course, easy because she makes it, but try for another prof

She is a really nice person but is all over the place. You can get through the course without reading the book if you understand the course concepts easily. The class has 2 projects that are worth almost half of your grade and participation is worth 30%. It was her first time teaching this class and I think it is going to get harder in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Baris was incredibly kind and available to the students, but lectures were a little unhelpful. He would give “in class assignments”, but they were never done in class. You'll survive the class as long as you study and have friends with other professors to compare notes and get info on the tests and quizzes since he doesn't make them lol

Overall, he is okay, the lectures are boring, and it can be very difficult to understand and hear him. The homework assignments take a while but aren't that difficult. He seems like a chill and nice guy, just not the best at teaching. Attendance not mandatory but most of the time you need to go to class to solve the ICA unless a friend can send it.

He's kind and really wants his students to learn. He even brought demonstrations to class. You can always ask questions since he is frequently in office, but his explanations can be confusing. Lectures drone on with equation derivations. LOTS of hw and also difficult, especially if you've never taken physics. I learned most in ILS.
lectures are unhelpful and make everything more confusing, but hes nice and chill.

I LEARNED A LOT but he was a so so professor. He wasn't bad, but wasn't particularly interesting. He was nice, but his lectures kind of droned on. He thoroughly showed the derivations of equations, taking up the whole board, but these weren't valuable, and actively made the content more confusing. By the end, no one showed up to his class.

super chill guy, but his class can get quite boring. especially in a big lecture hall, it's difficult to hear him. goes too fast sometimes and doesn't really give you time to do the examples yourself (important if you prefer that). his explanations aren't the clearest, but the course isn't too difficult.

Overall pretty good guy, not the best at teaching the material but not bad at all. He derives everything which is cool but can be boring and also not help sometimes. The homework can take a while Aswell.

Great lecturer, put all the equations we needed for the quizzes on the board, he also brought demonstration objects to every ILS which were cool to see. He was also really helpful when doing the group problems and provided guidance.

Baris allowed for late submissions on homework with no penalties and would extend deadlines if everyone needed it. He even moved our second exam to be take-home since he wanted the class time to properly cover the material before the final

Honestly a very good professor. He genuinely wants to see his students succeed, and he usually allows formula sheets. He derives equations so that we can understand the concepts but that can be a bit confusing, so don't be too worried about lecture. Make sure you mostly know how to tackle the homework (which is harder than the exam/quiz questions).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I could not have had a better re-introduction to physics than through Dr Altunkaynak (or Baris as he likes to be called). Physics is physics, so studying and preparation is going to be needed regardless of the professor; however, Baris does the most to make sure you are prepared and honestly just wants to see you succeed.

She's very nice and passionate. The lectures are dense, but bio psych is a dense subject so it's not really her fault. It's easy to zone out, but if you pay attention and study it's not that hard. Plus she gave LOTS of extra credit. If you easily get sidetracked while taking notes on your computer don't be surprised when you do badly on the tests.

There is a ton of content in this class. Her lectures start with repeating the last 20 slides from last class and she pauses to check her lecture notes after every slide. It is very difficult to stay engaged in lectures. Attendance mandatory but lectures are recorded. Exams are manageable if you study.

shes sweet yes, but i think she fails to recognize she is TEACHING, not explaining concepts to people just as educated as her. terms are not broken down, you get LOTS of info thrown at you without a lot of reinforcement. claude will become your best friend. take that how you wish.

Ingemi is a great professor, even if her lectures can be a bit dry at times. Tests are open note and not too bad, and she will go over everything in-depth at office hours. Easy points from discussion boards and extra credit at the end of the semester. Very manageable class if you pay attention, and lectures are recorded in case you don't.

Dr. Ingemi is super nice and very knowledgeable. I would recommend her for any course neuroscience/biology related. Her lectures are SUPER dense but she records them. She does Poll Everywhere in class so you have to attend lectures. Her tests are online but she makes them really tricky. There's a lot of content in this class but she's great

Very nice woman, but her teaching style does not work for me (and probably many others). Lectures are dense, and she talks extremely slowly to the point where it's impossible to stay engaged. Very hard to take notes and slides were unhelpful. However, the exams are all online, so everyone does very well.

Professor Ingemi is a great professor. Class is pretty easy to do well in, exams are online and there are lots of extra credit opportunities. She obviously cares a lot about her students and is very open to accommodations when needed. Makes jokes in lectures and is generally very chill. Attendance is based on pollev and she drops 2 classes worth.
The materials is super overwhelming. You will learn A LOT in this class.
I love her. She genuinely loves what she is teaching. Although exams tend to have trickier questions, as long as you pay attention in class, you will do well. I 100% recommend taking her.

Dr. Ingemi is a great professor who's really passionate about the course material. While a lot of the content is dense, she does a great job at explaining important concepts and is always open to answering questions. Also, quizzes and exams were both take home, but very application based and therefore required a lot of thinking and problem solving.

Dr. Ingemi is very friendly, understanding, and willing to help! The lectures are dense and have a lot of content but as long as you are present in class and take good notes they aren't too difficult. Personally, I found the content really interesting. There are poll questions that count as attendance (not graded on accuracy). Exams are online.

Prof is passionate about the subject matter and that helps make the class more engaging, but lectures are 1.5 hours of dense content. Its extremely bio heavy for a psych class. You have to pay attention to everything she says otherwise you spend a lot of time reviewing recorded lectures after of class. Overall good teacher and fair grader though

Professor Ingemi really cares about her students and is passionate about the material she teaches. The lectures can be very dense at times but if youre interested in the subject material it is a really engaging class. The class is almost completely lecture, and the grade is almost entirely tests (however they are pretty fair).Overall great teacher

Super nice and helpful. Encourages asking questions! She changed the testing style to be all open-ended when I took the class. While this made me nervous, it changed how she taught the class and made me feel like I could actually apply the skills I learned in professional settings. Lectures are dense however so you should always attend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ingemi was helpful and accessible. As an underclassman, the content felt like a bit much. Her lectures were packed full of detailed information so I suggest attending lectures and taking notes. Grades consisted heavily of exams, but also discussion posts and in-class participation.

This class is the most lecture heavy class EVER. The lectures are 1 1/2 hours and just filled with facts that you are expected to memorize. There isn't too much outside work but this means that a large chunk of your final grade is exams. The exams and quizzes are unnecessarily hard and she throws in so many trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taking Prof. Ingemi's Biopsych class was an absolute dream. I was scared at first because of the lecture-heavy teaching style, but her slides and study guides included everything we had to know. She never turns down a question someone has in class. She seems so passionate about neuroscience and wants us all to succeed. 100% would take her again

Prof. Ingemi is a very nice lady who is very willing to help. She explains concepts well in slides and is very knowledgeable about neurobiology. The slides are pretty dense and specific, and tests can be tough because you really have to apply what you know. Also, tests are worth 80% of the grade. However, she definitely wants students to succeed.

Prof. Ingemi was definitely one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. Her lectures were clear, but interesting. She does tegrity recordings in case you miss class (but would recommend going b/c of Tophat questions). She posts study guides for exams and is super approachable in office hours.

Dr. Ingemi was super knowledgable and (I thought) likable, but the class is 100 minutes of straight lecture. No activities, or any chance to apply what she says. The online quizzes are harder than they should be, and tests are worth 80% of the grade but she was very nice & approachable. Posts all lectures on tegrity
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Reads off the lecture slides. Blackboard quizzes are harder than they should be. Final isn't cumulative which is nice.

Judge Ireland is a great professor & brings so much knowledge and experience to the classroom. He is a very engaging lecturer and brings students to various courts within the Boston area for an immersive learning experience. While Judge Ireland doesn't take attendance for lectures, he doesn't post any slides, so going to class is very beneficial.
Super immersive, took us to court for the second half of the semester and I learned a ton. The guest lecturers were very engaging, and he was extremely knowledgeable.
The best professor. The sweetest man who truly cares that you learn all about the subject. You will leave knowing so much about criminal justice and get real experience going to court.
Easy grading, very insightful trips but lectures can be a bit of a drag. Definitely worth it

lots of reading and papers but its the type of work that really connects what you're learning in the classroom to the real world. Judge Ireland is an amazing teacher who cares about his students. The field trips he takes you on are amazing and I realllllly recommend going to all of them!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Judge Ireland is the best.  He's super interesting and a great resource for pre-law.

I loved this class! The lectures may get a bit boring since he reviews a lot of statutes in class (necessary evil) but the field trips and guest speakers he brings in are super insightful and he knows ALOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Not the most interesting speaker but learned A LOT in his class. Tests were very straightforward. The main highlight of this class was the field trips to the municipal, juvenile, superior, and supreme courts, and the county jail. he was the former chief justice of the Mass. supreme court so he knows a LOT of things
Lots of readings but they prepare you well for the class. Field trips were helpful and he is an easy grader if you are willing to make sure you get all the assignments completed on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: As a CJ major,  You try as hard as you can to respect him b/c he's the former chief justice of the juvenile court of Suffolk county. His teaching is confusing. His syllabus doesn't tell you what anything is worth. We didn't even get a rubric for the final paper. The only thing I appreciated in this class was the field trips (good experience).

Hands down, the greatest professor and class ive taken @ NU (coming from a senior). The guy is a justice on the MA supreme court and was a Juvenile Justice for years. You take a field trip to secure Juvie facilities and court. Awesome experiences. But dont take this class unless you're willing to WORK - its not easy, but you can do well if you work

You can go to class and not do the readings, or do the readings and not go to class.  His lectures are completely pointless because he literally dictates statues to you the whole time!  Worst class I've ever taken.  20 page paper for undergrad too.  Talks too fast to take adequate notes and never repeats himself unless you ask. Gives pop quizzes.

Hany can be absolutely brutal. If you don't attend class or don't do well on quizzes, he'll keep an eye on you. For the physics topics, look them up on YouTube because he can't explain them well. He teaches every other topic pretty okay, and you can succeed in the class as long as you stay on top of the homework. He offers many practice tests.

reviews.comment:

Dr. Livanis is very personable with his students and cares a lot for them. He will put your mental and physical health before any grade. Also a great guy to sit down and have a conversation with! Recommend 100%

Professor Livanis is a really interesting guy who gives great lectures, but his class isn't super structured. If you're type A, be prepared to let go, and trust that you know the material well enough to write the papers and take the exams.

Professor Matthews is the best professor I've had at Northeastern. Honestly she's the best, nothing bad to say about her. Just show up to class, review the lectures, readdddd the textbook please readddddd the textbook again read the textbook, once more read the textbook!!!! and please do the homework and practice problems and you'll be just fine.
.... don't do it, class has gotten so much harder (to the point where it feels unfair). No multiple choice anymore, all free response - no test corrections either.

I am not great at orgo but matthews pushed me to think about these topic from a new perspective. The white board practice days are so helpful and test content is similar to things done in class. Test all multiple choice, some homework. Compelling and respected professor.

She is amazing! She has no bs kinda thing and she grades very fairly.

Best orgo professor. I love Jude. Her lectures are awesome compared to other orgo professors and her tests actually reflect what was taught in class. She is knowledgable and understanding. If you put in the time, you will get a good grade. I would def take her class again if I have the chance.
She is one of the best professors in my experience. She makes orgo so easy. If you just pay attention and do her homework there is nothing to worry about.

PROF MATHEWS IS AWESOME! She genuinely wants her students to do well and is very approachable and is always willing to answer questions about the material. Professor Matthews explains everything very easily, and is ready to answer your questions. She is very approachable and nice, which makes questions so much easier. She also tries very hard to relate the material to the real world, so you get to understand why what you're learning is relevant.

She is really kind and nice professor, just Orgo is though.

Professor Mathews was awesome. She delivered the information clearly and made it clear what to study for the test. She makes herself available for extra help and does not try to "trick" you on exams. Organic Chem requires studying and understanding the mechanisms. Basically if you STUDY and ATTEND  OFFICE HOURS, an A+ should come easy.

Stopped giving us bonus pts and started to deduct pts on exams  if we don't write our name on every page of the exam front and back. Completely unnecessary.

One of the good teachers out there. She listens to each student and also goes out of her way to help explain difficult concepts such as NMR. Make sure to attend class and esp. review sessions.

Helpful when asked, too.

You think you're better off taking this professor's class because you think she'll be easy? Don't make the same mistake many people made. You're better off taking other professors. A great professor, very reaching out to all the students. Reviewing the materials every day is crucial as cramming a day before the exam wont gurantee you an A. After all...no matter how easy and reaching out the professor is, the course taught is Organic Chemistry.

A genuinely nice professor. Her tests can be difficult... It is organic chemistry. She is still new here and I believe working on her teaching style. Thank you Dr. Sosnik!

Professor Sosnik is very passive-aggressive and does not respond well to criticism. If you rely on practice questions to study like I do, I would avoid Professor Sosnik at all costs but if you do take him you might be able to scrape by with a B+. Extremely specific questions!

I just want to warn students Sosnik is an erratic professor with tests that dont align with class material. reviews.comment: Prof. Sosnik is a good choice for inquiries. I felt that as long as you show up, participate in presentations, and make a decent effort you could definitely get an A.
