If you pay attention and complete the handouts, you'll do great. The handouts are extremely extremely helpful. Fully understanding them WILL help you ace all exams. He just moved to America this semester and takes the bus to campus daily. He really deserves no hate. He's kind, respectful, and a great professor if you get to know him.

Had the privilege of being in Solomon's accounting class as a freshman. I will say he is a very sweet man, but his lectures make no sense. He reads off slides. He gives exam prep questions but the exams are entirely different. Sometimes difficult to understand through accent. Make sure to do good on your randomly assigned group project.
Lectures are very informative, class work and assignments are not hard. McGrawhill needed. Classwork and quizzes are easy, midterms and finals are fair if you studied.
An amazing teacher, she is so kind and understanding. Just put in the effort.

Dr. Otero was great. The textbook is free and online. It is not used for the class, but it is beneficial for self-study. Her tests go more in depth then the lectures, so be well-versed with the material. There is extra credit, she cares about you & your success, and she is approachable. She made class enjoyable and is personable. I recommend her.

I do not recommend taking this course, it was not worth the struggle. The lectures were boring and based on disorganized slides, and the exams were super difficult and based on small slide details. She also left some harsh comments on a few assignments. I just don't recommend taking this elective when there are other enjoyable classes out there.

higk shes great. i went to office hours often and i was originally supposed to get a B+ but ended up with an A- (AYYYY). you don't really need to use the textbooks. if u download the slides, all of her notes are in the speaker notes section. biggest tip is DO THE ASSIGNED PRACTICE QUESTIONS on time. its relatively similar to her exam questions

Grade is heavily based on midterms which she doesn't curve or offer corrections anymore and the questions are worded so confusingly. The tests go way more into detail than lecture and you have to study so much to get a good grade. That being said she is passionate about the subject and very positive and funny.

She was a good professor that explained the slideshows pretty well. However, some test questions were not even remotely related to the slideshows' content, hence averages in the 60's and 70's on all three tests. However, she offers many extra credit opportunities, so if you spend at least a week studying, and do the extra credit, you will do fine.

She lectures a lot and can be difficult to keep focused. You are expected to memorize an unrealistic amount of small details from all of the slides. A lot of your grade relies on her exams and the wording on the questions makes the entire exam feel like a riddle. Choose another elective unless you want an unnecessary amount of work.

Decent course. Her notes are clear, but if you want to do well on her tests, READ THE TEXTBOOK. It clarifies everything, and teaches you much more effectively and thoroughly. 3 exams and a final, all MCQ. She teaches simple concepts. All of the questions on her tests are application-based, not concept-based. Take note of these and you'll do fine.

Professor Otero is great! She's super friendly and funny, and I never felt nervous going up to her after class with questions. Lectures can be a bit monotonous, which is generally unavoidable in Biology. Attendance is via a daily poll, but you can get 100% with 80% attendance. Exams have some hard questions, but study and you'll be fine!

Dr. Otero is a great professor! I highly recommend you have some biology background before you take her class, but overall, she's great. She uses Poll Everywhere in every class, so make sure you show up for that. Exams are all multiple choice and offer many extra credit opportunities.

So much content over such a variety of topics; expected to remember every detail from the lectures. Way too much memorization and impossible to do well on the two exams, which are a huge part of the gradeI
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MUCH easier than AP biology as the tests are all multiple choice, lectures can be boring and wordy, but no homework so everything is based on the 3 midterms and final, the tests are like not super hard but not easy, just don't procrastinate studying, 90% of test material was taught in class but she does have some random questions thrown in

I don't get why so many people gave her bad reviews on here. Lectures can be boring, but overall the content wasn't too much. Lecture slides can be a little messy, but she usually supplements with details in class and will tell you when to remember something she said that wasn't on the slides. Tests are pretty easy and all multiple choice.

Deceptively easy class until you get to the tests. Very kind professor who gives a lot of examples and tries to connect with the class, but you will be surprised at the amount of content on tests that was barely covered or not covered in class. Go more in depth then you think you will need to and learn to think critically and you will be fine.
Chill class just don't submit work late. She's also super accessible outside of class to help with the final project. Quizzes and final test are easy - just read the slides

Super easy, lectures were boring. All of her tests are free-response and direct copies of the slides she presents in class. Her class difficulty is similar to a high-school level AP Environmental Studies class and there was no final - just a project. If you're looking for an easy A or GPA booster, this is the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Terrible class... however, if you're deciding between her and Potts-Santone probably take Otero. Avoid this class if you can, but if you must take it: memorize every slide in the presentation and before the exam, practice with the textbook problems she provides (you'll get an A). Test corrections (class averages in the 60s ->70s) and final curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Otero honestly gets a bad rep. Yes, her lectures can get boring, but they're recorded and attendance isn't required. Her exams are all memorization so study just about everything and don't cram. Look at the slides and do the practice questions she provides because they're very similar to the exam. Also lots of opportunities for extra credit!
She truly is nice and her class is fun but her tests are so hard, you really need to study a lot and it is the bulk of our grade...

Do NOT do NOT take Dr Otero. Her lecture slides are very disorganized and do not contain things that are on the exam. Her exams are very very difficult and very long, around 60-70 questions. The only thing good about the class are the online take home quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ana Otero is one of the worst professors I've had at Northeastern. Her content is very disorganized and the questions that she gives on exams are so niche that you can't even take an educated guess on them. Her lectures are a little useless because she does not know how to teach the content well enough for us. beware taking otero.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is one of the worst professors in my opinion that Northeastern has to offer. She does not lecture well at all. She is extremely disorganized and does not know how to teach. She gives only 2 midterms with a final. They are about 60-70 questions long. She does give a lot of extra credit. Content is so boring and she does not know how to teach.

Ana Otero is one of worst professors I have ever had. Her powerpoints are very disorganized and there is so much specific information that you have to know for her tests. Me and my friend studied so much to only get 60s - 70s on Otero's exams. Luckily she gives corrections but honestly her tests are pretty unforgiving and challenging. Beware!!
Honestly dont even know how to study for the final.... she lacks study materials.. be prepared to teach yourself

Textbook work is not required but very helpful for doing well on exams. Exams are content heavy and sometimes focus on trace details but her review Q's are sometimes on the exam so definitely do the outside work. Not much required homework so grade is based mostly on exams; 1111 is a tough class and 1113 is a snooze but she is a very nice woman.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's hilarious + explains concepts very well with good slides. Records lectures, 2 exams 1 final. If you have questions during an exam just ask her for help. She wants you to do well even if she seems passive aggressive! I relied on funny acronyms, bio rap songs, and quizzing my friends to study. This is not a class you can last minute cram in!
exams never felt like they were on the material, but outside assignments and lots of extra credit help

READ THE TEXTBOOK- exams are much more in-depth than the lecture slides go. Had to spend a lot of time outside of lecture learning the material bc slides are super basic. She's nice though and lots of extra credit as well as test corrections.

i think otero is a good and engaging professor! there are many extra credit opportunities. activities can drag out but they're ungraded so dw about it. 

tips: the slides are very basic; to pass the exams you need to read the textbook and do all the practice problems she provides. exams are more difficult than what is discussed in class. 3.5/5!

Would read the slides in class and sometimes do a class activity. Attendance was checked by doing a poll everyday. Her slides were kind of basic but the exam was on detailed content. Definitely read the textbook and study in advance to exams. Thankfully she gave test corrections and have lots of extra credit opportunities.

This class was for sure interesting... Her lectures were essentially devoid of content except for our second unit, at least in my opinion. She seems to only teach the basics, but then gives us exams with questions that are far beyond the scope of what she teaches in class. She doesn't really say you need to read the textbook, but you def need to!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take this class with a different prof like McElligott or Grabiner. Do not take Otero.

She is extremely unapproachable and her tests are impossible unless you've already taken bio or have time to teach yourself every concept. She offers test corrections but only for the most commonly missed questions. She does not curve or round grades. She is very cold during office hours and does not care how you do.

She is a very good teacher. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and test corrections on both midterms worth 40% of our grade. However, her tests are relatively hard and you might have to self teach yourself a lot to understand the questions fully. I took her for Bio 1 and will be taking for Bio 2.

Love Professor Otero! She's super sweet and she genuinely cares about students. In order for me to understand the material I had to do a lot of self-learning with the textbook because her lectures are super basic, but the exams are super difficult and in-depth. Average is usually in 60s. She gives corrections though. 2 midterms, 40%. 1 final, 25%.

She comes off as nice and funny, but the lectures and slides were very unhelpful. I only went to class because we were graded on attendance. The tests are incredibly hard and do not reflect the slides. Tests: 40% of grade and finals 25%. If you want to succeed in this class, read the textbook chapters and do the practice questions from the textbook
Tests are really hard and not a reflection of what we go over in class

It is impossibly difficult for an introductory course unless you have extensive practice with Biology. the people who did well took AP bio. She will joke around in class but is super judgemental during office hours and doesn't make study guides. There are test corrections but only for the most commonly missed questions.

Ana is extremely passive aggressive and unhelpful during office hours which makes her extremely unapproachable. Her tests have no correlation to lectures or anything she posts, so if you have her be prepared to essentially teach yourself every topic.

If you can take any professor other than Ana, do it. Her tests are impossible, she is extremely unapproachable, and doesn't care how you do. Says the textbook isn't required but it is. Lectures do not match test content. Do. Not. Take. Bio. With. Her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Otero is an awesome prof, easily accessible outside of class. If you attend class, do the optional assignments, do the textbook reading and generally pay attention you will pass the class. There are corrections on both the quizzes (the average will be in the 60s) and a curve on the final.

*PERSONAL TIPS* If you DOWNLOAD her slides off Canvas, you have access to the speaker notes with ADDITIONAL detail that you can read to actually understand. People say that the class is textbook dependent, but it's more important to know how to interpret the exam questions that she asks. I reccommend taking ONLINE AP BIOLOGY practice quizzes.

Honestly, the attendance is not mandatory, but you can go if you want to. I most definitely recommend getting the textbook and using it as a guide to get through the class. The exams are hard and not anything like the classwork, or take home quizzes. Good luck!

Prof Otero is a very very nice person, but her lectures are a little confusing. The only way to be succesful in the class is to go to lecture, and read the entirety of the textbook. READ THE TEXTBOOK she says you don't have to, and no one does, and then the average on the exams are 60s. If you read the textbook, and go to lecture, you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The exams are crazy bc we have extra problems in the exam, the other professor only tested anround 30 questions. Everyone receives about a 60s in her class while exam counts more than 60% of our grades.

This class is impossible to do well in. There are only two exams plus the final, which all cover way too much content for anyone to succeed. The class average was always in the 60s. She is nice during lectures but when going to office hours she is usually extremely unhelpful/unapproachable. Exams are heavily based on textbook and oddly specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ana's video lectures didn't go into much detail, so topics were mostly self-taught from the textbook. The assignments were pretty easy, but extremely subjective. There is no partial credit or thorough explanation of a grade. Her grading system is a bit strange (everything is 20%). Exams are very specific and based on the textbook and Ana's videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Otero is a better option for Bio 2 than Potts-Santone, but the lectures are quite dull and there's tons of material to learn for each exam because they're basically all term-focused. The tests are pretty unforgiving but she gives exam corrections for partial points. Bio 2 is just ecology so if you have AP credit take only Bio 1 instead.
Amazing professor!

She a very lovely professor, but her tests are impossible, and often, her lectures don't teach anything. You must read the textbook to prepare for tests since her lectures only cover 30% of the test. One hint for her tests is she typically will make a majority of the test about the most recent topics (including the finals exams topics).

Otero was such a fun and caring prof. She genuinely cares about her class and listens to feedback. She would give breaks during class, and tell jokes/funny stories. She allows test corrections on certain problems and extra credit opportunities. Textbook is not required, nor used, unless for some practice problems to study with. Take her for BIO2!

Prof Otero is a good professor, I learned a lot in the lectures but it helps more if you do the homework readings. But her exams are terrible, despite studying and understanding the concept I would still get really low scores. And I still have no idea how or why but she does give exam corrections only for specific problems on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely kind and knows the material! Very helpful, but exams can be difficult/unclear based on learning in class. Overall great prof!

Prof. Otero is spunky and fun! She tries to make lectures enjoyable by incorporating jokes and encouraging peer conversation. However, her tests are rather difficult, and I recommend doing the assigned readings and studying. If you put in the effort and do all the assignments, it's definitely possible to get an A.

Ana Otero is a kind professor who listens and answers questions. Her classes are tough and require time and effort. She offers extra videos and readings, which are helpful but not required. If you're short on time, consider a different class.

Prof Otero is a nice lady and sometimes funny, but her whole whole class is based off of reading the textbook. I'm not paying thousands of dollars to read a text book we need to ALSO PAY $80 for. I also never took AP bio and her lectures aren't very good so I was even more confused in the end. If you haven't taken bio, don't take Otero.
She is a great teacher and is passionate about her students and the subject taught. She is very understanding and also is super accessible outside of class. Class is super easy

Very bad teacher when it comes to teaching material. I had taken bio in the past and somehow I felt more confused in the class. Lectures are not clear and does not go over all the material on exams. However, she is a very nice person, funny in class, and gives lots of extra credit opportunity. She is very accessible outside of class.

You have to get the textbook (~$80, digital per semester) and it's associated software for homework. Attendance taken every lecture through polleverywhere (5% of grade). Do the pre-class work, even though her lectures are quite elementary her tests use more textbook knowledge. Three midterms all have corrections!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shes a sweetheart. Class was very easy and she cares about her students. Accessible outside of class and works to make sure everyone understands and gets good grades.

Dr. Otero was a great professor. Took the inquiries section of Climate Change and she made sure that the material given was interesting. She provided a lot of help with the research project. Her exams are fairly easy to pass if you use the study guides she gives. Attendance matters tho and it can be easy to not want to go to a class like inquiries.

Her tests are pretty difficult and are entirely mutiple choice so there is no way to show your knowledge. I am pretty sure she does not write her own tests and gets them off of the internet so in my opinion they are not geared towards the class. I did not like this class at all and this was my lowest grade due to her harsh tests.

Great professor! It's nice to have a professor actually interested and experienced in what they do, and it shows from the way she teaches. Class based off exams, homework, participation, and a few extra credit opportunities. Slides and study guide need some work, but she's great overall. Also, there's opportunities for test corrections! Lifesaver

By far my favorite professor/class at Northeastern. There are 4 take home assignments, 3 quizzes, and 3-4 assignments that work towards your final research poster presentation. There is a lot of in-class group work, but it's nothing high stakes. One of the funniest professors I have ever had, very accessible, understanding, and knowledgeable.

Otero is a good professor. Tests are super easy and based directly off the notes posted online. Can sometimes cold call, so make sure to read course materials. A very easy class as long as you attend class and study the notes.
Prof otero is really sweet and really cares about her students. Her exams were a bit challenging but her office hours are a big help. there are other assignments that make up for the overall grade.
Her class is so boring, struggled to stay awake. Work is easy overall but she's just not engaging. Quizzes are also all open response and she expects u to remember random words for them.

Second time taking this professor and I'm so glad I did. Just go to class and do the work and you will get a good grade. Quizzes are really easy and professor is very understanding and kind. She loves students who go to office hours and communicate as much as possible. Already planning on taking a 3rd course of hers next semester!
incredibly rude.
Terrible teaching style. Inconsiderate. Wouldn't wanna take any class with him again.
No thanks.
Too tough. Not considerate. Assignment and exam structure was awful

Conceptualizes difficult concepts in an easy to digest manner. Somewhat lecture heavy, but all notes are posted online. Transition to online semester due to pandemic was great. I would highly recommend taking systems with Professor Whitney.
All conceptual, very few problems ever solved

Professor P cares about teaching, and has engaging lectures. The class was definitely challenging, don't take it if you aren't ready to dedicate time to fully paying attention and participating. 1 group project given the start of the semester, and 1 at the end which was fun. Tests 2 and 3 were written poorly, but generous with curve for Test 3.

This professor is great if you get on his good side, you will actually learn in this class if you go to lectures, he cares if you show that you put work in. aside from that the test a middle difficulty and the project at the end is fun.

Prof. Power is excellent IF you like supply chain and want to explore it as a career option. However, the class is very hard for those just taking it to fill a requirement. A's are nearly impossible, even if you're top of your class. He's an awesome guy with an interesting class--just be ready to receive a lower grade in exchange for learning.

Getting an A is literally impossible - exams are so difficult. The lectures are very interesting, and I learned a lot in his class. The group project is very much dependent on your team, for me it was fun but if people slack of it will be hell. Chapter readings are long, but he goes through them in class. Get ready to study a lot.

This is a hard class. Tests can be very difficult but if the class does poorly on an exam he usually curves the test. The SIM at the end of the semester is fun but does take a lot of work. P.S. don't expect to get an A in the class he is a tough grader.
Never again. Take anyone else.

I understand the mixed reviews of prof power because he is a pretty harsh grader but i think schm ended up being my favorite class this semester. He's very knowledgeable in his work and the group project simulation was actually so fun. I think if you want to learn take him but if u want an easy a dont.

I was initially hesitant because of the rating, but I ended up having a very positive experience in this class. The lectures were engaging and helped clarify the material in a way that made the exams feel manageable. The course included three tests and a final project, and the project was enjoyable while still reinforcing what we learned.

He knows the material he's teaching and is very passionate about the subject, but he is so hard to impress and his exams are very difficult. He frequently yelled at students over small things, which often made the whole class uncomfortable and scared. Get ready to feel like you're walking on eggshells every class.

Overall he's definetly passionate about supply chain but the class is overall hard. Kids average like 60s-80s on the test, and they don't usually cover most of what was on his slides and he doesn't usually curve. Class consinsts of mcgraw hws, 3 tests (non-cumulative), 2 group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Do not take Power. There are so many better professors out there. His tests were useless, and getting a good grade was super hard. Did not prepare for tests at all and usually gave new content in tests.

first let me say that his lectures were useless. nothing he put on the tests was anything i studied for using HIS homework. the homework is useless, it's just for a 5% grade. not only are his classes useless, he also screamed at my group inside of a closed-door office, essentially telling us we were all stupid and pointless. run while you can.

Professor Power definitely knows his stuff and cares about students. He doesn't like lateness or distractions like phones. Really interesting class you will definitely learn a lot, if you want a class for an easy A with no work don't take this, you have to study for exams. Exams are difficult. Overall a good professor and class, would take again.

Funny guy with decent lecturing ability. Draws a lot on real-world experience and does his best to make 8 AM lectures manageable. Doesn't let shit slide, so if you plan on missing lectures and not reading the textbook, you will not get above a B+. Also very project-heavy, so pray you get assigned a good team for the many projects.
The exams are really hard and classes are lecture heavy but he is a super sweet guy and appreciates any sort of participation effort!
He's a great professor. Very passionate and enthusiastic. Tests are hard, and the simulation takes a lot of time, but I learned a lot in this course. Highly recommend.

Prof Power is a fantastic professor! He gets a bad rating because he isn't easy, but don't let that persuade you from taking the class. I know so many people who took this class with another prof and regretted it because they didn't learn anything. If you truly want to benefit and learn supply chain, take prof Powers class.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!! He tries to seem like he cares about us but in reality he is a terrible teacher and the averages on all our exams were in the 60s or 70s. Took my phone out in class once to silence it and he screamed at me in front of the entire class. It's impossible to get an A in participation from him. Legit take anyone else.

I actually loved this class and the way Power teaches. He is a super nice dude, but he WILL get onto you for cheating or using your phone bc he wants you to learn. Some assignments are tough but nothing crazy. Homework is easy. 2nd group project was super time consuming (8+ hrs), but I became really great friends with my group during the process.

Not sure why Powers gets so much hate — he's a great guy who wants students to succeed. The class is tough, with bi-weekly case studies and three exams (first is easier, last two are harder), but he curves generously. He's clear about expectations, gives solid feedback, and you'll learn a lot. Just show up and do the work, and you'll do great!

I love this professor. The class is incredibly difficult (for me) but he made me enjoy the classes. He's very clearly qualified and very knowledgable. Even though I am struggling with the subject matter, I do not dread class because he talks about the information in such a way that I like learning about it. Tests are very hard though.
don't take this class even as a last resort. avoid it at all costs
RUN! DONT EVEN THINK ABOUT IT.

Power is a great professor and I learned a lot in this class, however, it is extremely difficult to get an A or A- in this class. It was by far my most time-consuming class and I had to spend a LOT of time outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Power's class is challenging, but if you put in the work, you'll do well. The exams are tough, but he curves them. I found unstuck ai really helpful for test prep, along with the textbook and attending lectures.

He is very smart, knowledgeable, and knows the material in and out. No final, grading was hard, classes were kind of boring. He did have us do a paper individually that other professors either didn't do at all or did as group projects which was unlucky.

just stay away. Multiple Choice test results account for much of your grade and are way more difficult than you think, because its hard to study for it (calculations are easy tho). group projects are easy if your group members are good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nice person but highly recommend not taking this class. Expected great effort for an intro class. Got an A after extreme dedication: studies 4-5+ hr for each exam, weeks of work for final group proj and essay, 100% attendance, participated every class. executive briefs graded harshly, no extra credit. Class was a great source of stress for me.

Professor Power is the worst teacher I've had. His test questions are vague, and he's too lazy to clarify anything. The virtual supply chain lab is a confusing mess, and even he doesn't understand it. Worst of all, you'll write 6-8 pages for it to be worth just 5%. Avoid him unless you're stuck majoring in SCHM—and good luck if you are.

He's a good professor, but the class isn't very interesting, and doesn't really matter unless your concentration is schm.  Gave two projects at the end of the semester, and one of them isn't run very well.  Tests are 45% of the grade.
Do not take a course with this professor.  I asked him a simple question about rounding on an exam and he gave me the wrong answer. 0/10 doesn't know his own exam and people cry in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You're pretty much expected to learn the course material on your own, then class lectures are just review of that - but if you skip you will not pass. Not a super tough grader, but doesn't give out A's easily (for group projects and homework) - tests are pretty difficult but sometimes curved - also he posts everyones individual test grades online..

Lots of mixed reviews in here and I get it. If you are good at testing, this class will be a breeze. I think I studied maybe 2-3 hours for the tests and wound up with good grades. He's knowledgeable, entertaining, and if you put in the work on your presentation you'll do well. HOWEVER- his curves do NOT make up for the averages on his tests/sim.

I absolutely LOVE Professor Power!!! He and his class was a pleasure. He is very intelligent, witty, funny, caring, and is more than willing to help when needed. I would recommend Professor Power to anyone taking classes. I wish I could take all of my classes with him. Thank you for a great experience

Very fair professor. If you are respectful (he will call you out for using your phone or dozing off), turn hw's in on time, and participate, he will have a good impression of you. Very test heavy (hard but often curved), ~3 hw's/week. I really enjoyed his lectures, they were interesting and I liked hearing his stories about working for UPS.

DO NOT take this professor's class. His class is ten times harder than any other of the supply chain professors. I had to go home because I needed to take care of my sick grandpa and he would not give me any extra credit to make up for attendance points he literally yelled at me over zoom and made me cry, while my other professor understood.

His tests are very difficult but if you study it is possible to get an A. Prepare well and manage your time and expectations. You cannot breeze by in this class, you must work for your grade. He is nice, a good lecturer, and doesn't waste time. His outside assignments are HARD and TIME CONSUMING. He does give 100%'s, just not for everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is like walking on 15 Legos sets, its awful. He gives so much work compared to the other supply chain professors, and his test are the hardest things ever. No extra credit, and is a tough grader. Lectures are okay at most, and I wished he assisted more with the simulation. Good luck if you have him, you'll need it.

Insanely hard professor. Unless you are majoring in supply chain, this class is useless and boring, and you will not get an A. Out of my entire class, there was probably 2 or 3 kids that might have gotten an A. He refuses to give out 100s for anything. Very exam focused, and they are long with lots of ambiguous answers.

Group projects in asynch classes have to me the most painful thing ever. I got lucky with one of mine but the other was impossible. Prof Power is not understanding these things and I was frustrated when he did not assist me. Overall, you need to be ready to do a lot of work for an online class but I recommend Prof Power!

Knowledgeable about the industry. Straightforward guy. You can be anybody but as long as you participate you'll be fine. Unluckily for me, I liked him and his class but I was experiencing a tremendous amount of anxiety and his class just made me compartmentalize and try to be a perfectionist. Supply chain is all about metrics. I withdrew.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I was the only freshman in his 8am T/F class. He liked me but that's cause I wasn't afraid to participate. Even still, I don't know how someone can get an A in his class. The tests are hard, and some of the questions are ambiguous and outrageous.

He's very knowledgeable & has the industry experience, but I don't know if teaching is his forte.
Just Run!!!!!!!!!!! Please listen!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! For your own good!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

I love prof power. It's a hard class in general but he made it interesting with his real life experience. The exams are easy as long as you study the textbook well. He is relatively strict with following the guidelines he sets but he is understanding if there is an honest issue. He acknowledges when you put in effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guy's not a very good teacher to have, especially for supply chain. He is a very strict grader and despite coming first in the class in multiple group projects, my participation grade was amongst the lowest in the class. He also won't excuse any missed classes no matter how sick you are. I would recommend taking somebody else.

Powers was amazing. He has a lot of experience so his classes are pretty engaging. He is strict about his guidelines but they are very upfront so as long as you follow them you can do well. There are 3 tests, I suggest you study from the textbook. Spend time checking and re checking before you submit it. For the executive briefs, look online!

He is really mean to students and would humiliate you in front of the whole class. He said he is open to questions but would make you really uncomfortable when you actually ask questions. He gave a lot of work and rushed through all of the grades. In conclusion, I HATE him.
Don't understand how anyone likes this guy?
THE GRADMASTER OF ALL JERKS.
This Professor is very mean to students. He does not respond to your email when you need help and he looks forward me to drop out of this class

He humiliates students during class for the smallest of things, and doesn't seem to care much about teaching. Makes you work A LOT and won't give you any leniency for inconveniences. DO YOUR BEST TO AVOID HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It was so bad I want to give him a zero. But I can't. So I give him a 1.

Prof. Power gets too much hate on here. He's a pretty good professor with tons of real world relevant experience to supply chain. The tests are really not that bad if you study sufficiently. The game at the end is also very fun and one of the group projects I actually enjoyed. He is very strict with attendance, and takes it the second class starts.

Exams were much more difficult than the material we covered in the lectures, the project was very hard, and he is an extremely tough grader. Power is rude and will show no empathy no matter what your situation is.

I wouldn't recommend him at all. In the first class, I thought he was going to be the best professor of the semester but instead he was the worst. The class may seem easy but his tests are not. He doesn't like giving A's, he usually gives only B's. VERY tough grader. He will never give you 0.01 points to have a better grade, so don't even ask.

Professor Power will make you work, but you will learn a ton. Expect every class to always be a mix of 70% his lectures and 30% two group presentations. The course includes a simulation game which is an excellent way to apply the info you learn throughout the year. An A is attainable if you do all your work, but beware he will make no exceptions.
Professor Power gives clear and understandable lectures but the tests and projects are a lot harder than the class material. He is a tough grader and will call you out in front of the class.

Professor Power's real world experience makes the lectures more interesting and easier to understand. Besides the tests and one project, everything is graded on completion. He is always open to answering questions from students during lectures, so take advantage of this. As long as you give him respect, he is understanding and will help you out.

not a nice guy. Yelled at someone for using the bathroom too much, gives absolutely no leniency for anything for any reason. Assigned a group project that takes 8-10hrs. only gave 8 days to work on it, had to be worked as a group. The project opened online the first fay of thanksgiving break, so we only had 3 weekdays to do 10hrs of group work
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is extremely easy for tests, but the bulk of your grade is subjective from participation and presentations. His grading scale is only between 84 and 88. If you do a bad job you get an 84.... if you spend 10 hours on something and it is spectacular you get an 88. This makes it extremely easy to get a B+ / A-, but difficult to get an A.

Power was a great professor, one of the best I've had at NU. He made Supply Chain really interesting and showed that he cared about the topic, but also cared about making sure we understood the material. He was also great about giving real world examples for just about everything. 3 Tests, non cumulative, final project simulation instead of final.

If you want to learn about supply chain, take this class. If you want an A, don't. Power knows everything about supply chain and you can learn a ton from him, but the course is super fast paced and his exams are next to impossible. His questions are confusing and sometimes aren't related to in class material at all. Only take if you're a SCHM conc.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Power is a super nice guy and is very accessible outside of class. However, he makes his tests so hard (and will tell you that on day 1) that you cannot learn Supply Chain past memorizing and forgetting it for the tests. It is a shame because the subject was interesting. There are WAY easier profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Most difficult intro class taken so far! He tells you at the very beginning that class is not easy. Strict grader and tough on class policies. Heavy use of powerpoint so lectures can be boring. On the plus side he does have a lot of experience in the industry so he does make it relatable. Tests are super difficult so READ ahead of time! Good Luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DO NOT be late to his class. He takes attendance at the very beginning of class (and I mean 8am, not 8:01) and he notes who comes in late, who is not paying attention, etc. He covers all topics for the course very completely, but it is best to come to class having already read the material. He is demanding of your attention, but his class is fun
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Read the textbook, pay attention/participate in class, you'll survive. He has a ton of relevant industry experience. The other reviews are pretty soft,  he is a tougher grader but if you read the textbook and the highlighted learn smarts you can easily get above a 90. The overall grade also if very distributed through different assignments.

Take his class if you are good at multiple choices. Almost no students would get overall hw and presentation scores lower than 87 points. The  biggest issue is the three tests. Extremely hard tests. A hint here: If you have to take his class, after he graded your tests, try to argue with him about questions you got wrong, he make mistake sometimes

I enjoyed Professor Powers class for the most part. He knows what he's talking about & gives good examples. There is hw due every class but its very helpful in learning how to apply the material. Tests are fair & you'll do well if you listen in class & read the textbook. Only complaint is he seemed unnecessarily hard in grading final presentation
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not bad. Lectures done well and he has a lot of experience in the field. He is very clear about what he wants for assignments and is very strict about getting that. Exams are a little tricky - but he does let you dispute questionable answers. Again, strict, but gets his point across well.
Worst professor I've ever had. Huge workload for an introductory class. Tests are very hard. Hard to take notes he whizzes through powerpoints and doesn't allow laptops. AVOID
He's actually a really nice guy. He was really understanding and helpful towards me.
avoid at all costs.... test heavy class and hard OVERALL.  AVOOD HIM GUYS!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: No practice for tests forever

He is clear about what he teaches. Super interested in his subject. His tests are fair game and not easy to ace if you dont study. Lots of his homework answers can be found online. Participation is important so make sure he knows your name

A bloated, inconsiderate, do-things-strictly-by-his-own-arbitrary-book kind of guy. Has the most inane and draconian attendance rules; if you're late to class even by a minute, you're counted absent all day. He refuses to except late work. He lacks total sympathy, even scoffed when I told him my grandfather was dying. A bureaucratic oaf.

Professor Power is the most rude and disrespectful professor I've ever had the displeasure of "learning" from at Northeastern. He acts like he could care less about how you perform in his class and is not willing to help at all when asked. If you want to save your GPA, don't take this guy.

In-class participation and coming to class is 20% of your grade. His tests are 50 multiple choice questions (averages: 80-84) Not an easy A, you must work for it. Make sure to be as creative as possible whenever you have a presentation. He expects a lot from you. Overall he is a very nice guy but I don't really think he is that good of a professor.

No negotiations, no slack, very strict when it comes to participation and tardiness. Penalized me for missing classes that I didn't miss. Lectures are well-explained and tests are fair, but policies are unforgiving.

Professor power has little to no interest in helping anyone in class. He just zooms through material, tells you only to study his slideshows, then the exams are on book material and anything else he decides. Avoid at all costs.

The worst professor I have ever had at Northeaster. Extremely hard exams and he doesn't make you feel comfortable to participate in class. I regretted taking the transportation class with him. Avoid if you can!

I loved this class. It is VERY hard to get an A in but I felt that I learned a lot. The tests are hard and sometimes the questions misleading. While there are assignments almost every class he makes it fun and class isn't boring.

This professor is extremely disrespectful to students. The tests he writes are grammatically incorrect which makes it difficult to understand the questions that are being asked. He gives little to no feedback for means of improvement. His grading is arbitrary and he provides no basis upon where he makes up his numbers. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
Goes through power points too fast for you to write things down. Tests are very hard and confusing. Direspectful to students. Doesnt provide good feedback. DONT TAKE HIM.
Lectures make material seem super easy, but the tests will get you

Great person, really cares about his students. If you're rude he doesn't tolerate it. He works hard for every student he has and wants to see effort from us. Makes class SOO enjoyable. So much knowledge for the field, and has great connections. Always willing to help students.

The thing people don't like about this prof is that he's very blunt. You can take that to mean a good thing or a bad thing. At the beginning of each year, he lays out everything he's going to do in his syllabus. Make sure you follow that syllabus, and you'll be fine. As long as you're a hard worker, you'll enjoy it. If not, then don't.
He's class is interesting but he is definitely a tough grader. Try take a nap play your phone in class and see what will happen.

Bans computers in the class. Goes through power points too fast for you to write things down. Includes extra material in the powerpoint that he tests on but doesn't leave on the screen long enough for you to write it down. Most of the syllabus is clear, but for the parts that aren't he doesn't see the need for elaboration. No real feedback on cases

Mr Power is crazy when it comes to his guest speakers and attendance. Unfortuantely it seems like he has so many personal issues that he's angry at the students all the time. Extremely uptight and terrorizing that you worry about class more than about learning.

Great man, if you put in effort, he will take notice. AS simple as that. The course material is kept interesting, and participating only helps you. He isn't out to get you and he doesn't play favorites. If this is your major, take this class with him.

I had Power for SC&OM. Studied 10 hours a week (reading the chapter + homework), participated in class, went to office hours.His class itself is interesting, seems simple during the lecture but his tests are SUPER ambigious, very hard to get above a 70%. He won't help you out and will not negotiate grades even when he made a mistake. dont take him!

he knows a great deal and can teach you a lot.  put some effort in and you will probably get a B+...im getting a B a did very little studying.  attendance is a must for him...always be there and never leave early...never use your phone either.  he's funny, too, so class isn't bad.  use the ppt slides for all your projects - they're always available

Supply Chain Management is not hard topic yet somehow he makes it really tough. You get stuff from point A to point B, everything else is extra. If you want to work really hard for a bad grade and take a class from a "professor" who can be nasty and disrespectful then this is the class for you.
He's a good professor, very clear with his ideas. But if you just don't pay attention, he becomes downright nasty. Just pull your phone out and see what happens...
He is a good teacher, but the way his supply chain class is graded, getting an A is very difficult.

One thing to know about this class is that getting an A is no as easy as often thought. That apart, prof. Power is a really good professor with a great sense of humor and is always willing to help. Don't ever use your cellphone or sleep in class (even if it's 8am) or he will become your worst nightmare. All in all a great professor.

He's a true goofball, a real nice guy and a great professor. He is really passionate about the subject and makes the class seem actually quite entertaining. However, don't you EVER sleep, space out or use your cellphone in class. He will crush you down and penalize you quite severely. Course load is fair but meaningful.

Very enthusiastic, difficult grader. Make sure you participate during every class (big part of grade-25%). Do well on the quizzes and final business plan w/presentation (40%). There are definitely easier professors for the subject but he is very comprehensive and helpful.
He is super hard professor! if you wanna an A, never take his class. I got my first B in my life when I had with him. So upset!

Enthusiasm. This is the key. Power is a nice guy, and he's worked hard all his life. Takes the same approach to teaching, and expects you to do the same. Like I said, show enthusiasm and read the chapters, or even just the slides if ur lazy/smart, and you'll get an A and learn a lot. DONT USE UR CELL PHONE!
LOVE POWER! he's amazing! easy grader, easy to follow, great stories, doesn't waste class time and we got out early a lot!
Amazing teacher! Hilarious jokes. and people who say he's mean are just the jerks he's called out

Really helpful guy.  Unlike the rest of the class I really enjoyed the TJX project that takes up most of the class and he really wants to help you with this.  Writing a 35 page business plan might suck but just one semester later I've referred to it 10+ times for help in other classes in terms of formatting and projects.  Funny stories, no final.
Fun class but IMPOSSIBLE to get an A. I am a straight A student and I busted my butt in this class and only got a B+. If you want an A, don't take this professor!

All of these negative comments are true.  Calls anyone out, not understandable of your situation and makes no sense grading.  We had 3 tests; the first one was too easy, second one everyone failed (he had to drop it) and the third one made no sense and got curved.  If you enjoy random stories about FedEx, tough grading and being insulted take this.
Power is a great teacher.  He's very clear, and I learned a lot.  As long as you prepare for the quizzes and work hard on your project, you'll do fine.

Disagree with the previous ratings. If you go to class, pay attention (dont sleep), and give an honest effort he will show you nothing but respect. The material isn't exciting, but Power is a great professor and his lectures are always clear and easy to pay attention to. Only complaint I have is that the test questions are ridiculously specific.

So awful. Do not take this class. Especially if it's for an MIS elective - the guy is a joke, he constantly yells at students like they're children, and knows nothing about current SCM. Should be an easy A, yet was everyone's hardest class. Don't take 201 with this guy!!!

In-class lectures vaguely overlapped with the text book, leaving us VERY unprepared for exams. He could also stand to be nicer to his students, rather than alienating and embarrassing people in front of their peers. Who does that? Not even a middle-school bully struggling with adolescence issues is as mean as Professor Power sometimes was in class.
Really good guy. Quizzes are pretty ridiculously hard but don't count that much. Presentations are most of the grade. Tough grader.

Professor Power is a good guy. In intro. to business you take about 10 quizzes and attendance is mandatory. We also did a group project that made up 50% of our grade. He is completely fair, he is extremely helpful, and if you don't do any work that's the only way you will do poorly. Otherwise, you attend class, study, and ask for help. you'll be fi

Just finished up the semester with this professor...have to say was by far my favorite. Awesome guy, always available to help you out and great at explaining things. We had a lot of work compared to my friends but I learned a ton more than all of them and I really became much more interested in business after this class.

You will have 3 exams that make up most of your grade. His lectures cover a lot of material, but youd fail if you took rigorous notes at each class. You have to go through each studyguide per chapter and answer each T/F,MC,etc. Do that and you will do fine on the exams and in the class. NEVER fall asleep in class. EVER. Don't go if you feel sleepy.

Overall nice guy, hard grader and unclear on what should be put on powerpoints. His comments made me frustrated because he gave you the same grade no matter how hard you worked to improve. Make sure you go to class, do your homework and study for his random and hard quizes.

Very entertaining, but tough to reach by email, not crystal clear about requirements on powerpoints, and is not objective when it comes to grading.  He was very skeptical of our idea for the business project, and our consultant had no idea where some of the comments were coming from on our evaluations, or why we continuously got C's on everything.

He has an extremely short fuse.  He victimizes the students on his bad side and embarrasses them inappropriately in front of the whole class.  He is a control freak and a tough grader.  NOT A NICE PERSON.  That being said, he is very smart, experienced, and knows his stuff.  This is one of those classes that wish you could skip every time.
He gave everyone the same grade on every singe presentation (B).  He's very charasmatic and talks about the same UPS stories all the time

Power is a really nice guy. He loves business and wants you to love it too. He tends to be more strict than the other intro to business teachers, but I also learned way more than my friends in the other classes. The only real work is the business plan and presentations. Go to class and pay attention and you will love him too.
He's such a difficult man to work with. He seemingly just dislikes everyone equally.

Talks loud and clear. He knows his stuff and is experienced. However, he seems to have split personalities and if you cross him the wrong way, he will b*tch you out badly. I've seen him do it to many students and its very rude. He's real strict on coming on time and attendance. Do NOT sleep in his class. You will have to work hard in his class.
horible professor. lets his emotions get the best of him. class is useless tought my self everything from the textbook.

Professor Power is a good local guy, who is demanding of good work, but isn't going to kill you with homework or boring lectures, if you just listen to what he says and always attend class you'll be fine
Dont piss him off..haha, aside from that...he's great.. sure kept me awake in class
emotional and intense
Power is a good teacher.  Ethics is a boring subject, but he keeps you interested.  The debates were fun.

I'm taking an International Bus class with him and he doesn't know what he talks about. He's always talking about his SCM job he used to work for. He skips a ton of slides because he doesn't know how to teach them!! He'll show videos. You need to do a presentation. Particpating in class is key. Also know current news. He's an avg teacher.
Bad teacher, this is the first time that a professor miss more class than I do. If you want to learn something, you should avoid this techer.

ok hes an easy teacher, but your not going to get your moneys worth.  he has cancelled 5 classes and usually ends class an hour to an hour and a half early. i pay for my education so i get pissed when teachers do that.  im tqlking to the dean tommorow.
No Comments
Very funny guy, very nice guy, very personal with students. Excellent, experienced, and knowledgable teacher. Very enjoyable.
Lovely teacher!!!!!!!!!!
Awesome teacher.  Tells you exactly whats going to be on the tests.  Lots of work, def. worth it!

In class there is 2 presentations, 1 solo, 1 group, no final test or paper just a group project. Very smart guy with lots of knowledge. Pay attention in class and you will get at least a B. Participation is a must.
Global Supply Chain Management, Do the work (which is easy), pay attention, and show effort. You'll get a good grade and make a great reference with this professor! UPS Tour ~ hahaa

If you are into business you will learn a lot from him, as he is very knowledgeable.  As long as you always attend class, particapte often, and study you should do well. Always lets you know exactly what he expects from you. Overall a great guy.
Professor Power is very controlling. He is always in charge. Make sure you go to class and stay awake. Study and give your input and you will do fine.
Great Teacher, very helpful, outlines and specifies all material that is needed, no gimmicks, go to class, study a little, and you should do great.
No Comments

If you like any aspect of business, you will be tuned-in to the class the entire time.  You will have to do work, that will take time, but you will learn. Go to class, do work, and participate, and you will be happy. This guy is great.
Great teacher
fun this teacher

Genuinely she was one of the worst professors ever. She enjoyed making her class difficult and expected a lot of memorization that wasn't really relevant to the course. Spent pretty much the entire testing time talking out loud about nonsense and got mad if she heard people cracking their knuckles during the test.

I took Human Parasitology with her and the class was awesome, one of my favorites I've taken so far. You have to show up and really pay attention with her because the material is dense, and her tests are both oddly specific and tricky. You have to REALLY READ EVERYTHING-- there are trick questions on the tests sometimes! Take notes make flashcards

definitely avoid at all costs
GOAL IS TO FAIL STUDENTS
NEVER WANTS TO HELP OUTSIDE OF CLASS...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to do good in this class you can't skip lectures. This is difficult because this class is so so so boring especially at 8am. The tests are way too hard and actually made me not enjoy one of my favorite subjects. If the professor likes you you won.

I love biology, but her class truly made me question and slowly chipped away at my love for the subject. She goes extremely quickly in class, and you'll likely have to teach yourselves a lot. She records her lectures, which are convenient for studying, because anything she says could show up on the exam. Exams are SPECIFIC, so expect to study!

She can be super intense, especially on test days. Her class truly is difficult, but she will do her best to help if you go to class and show interest/effort. She was very caring and understanding with me, but important not to get on her bad side... GO TO LECTURE!! Impossible to do well if you don't

RUN. Take ANY other professor for Bio 1 or 2. Potts makes this course unnecessarily hard—harder than upper-level classes. Expects unrealistic memorization. I excelled in other rigorous courses but couldn't do well here despite intense studying and a tutor. Exam questions are purposely confusing. She offers poll extra credit but it barely helps.

Her class is manageable if it's the only difficult class you have. It's not a heavy work load besides periodic quizzes but the material/slides are messy and poorly organized for students to learn properly. She moves quickly and unclear while expecting you to memorize previous lecture details. The class is hard but she makes it harder.

Her class is hard + exams are memorization heavy, but so are most bio classes. She gives a HUGEEE amount of extra credit which boosted my grade so much. She is super passionate and knowledgeable, and I really liked her enthusiasm + flexibility. People enjoy hating on her as a way of coping about their grades, but i think her class is very doable.

if you can't memorize she isn't the prof for you. tests are SUPER specific, like she will add content she talked about one like for like 30 seconds. sometimes she can be super sweet and at others times super cold. clearly very passionate about what she does, but also expects everyone to come to class with that same mindset.

Tests are memorization-heavy and VERY specific. You can only do well if you memorize ALL the slides word for word. Lectures are recorded and she gives a lot of extra credit opportunities if you attend in-person. Lectures are a little boring and not engaging. If you're good at memorizing, her class might be ok, if not, not the best class to take.
dont take.

Honestly I think some people are a bit dramatic about Potts-Santone. I think a lot of the animosity people have towards her is just because the class is really hard. She is a lovely human and cares about you succeeding, and you get extra points for going to class. It is entirely memorization but so are most bio classes so I think it was reasonable.

Sometimes puts extra credit hints in the syllabus so make sure to read it. Also gives out extra credit to people who come to class when not many people show up. Is a fine professor, just don't get on her bad side and don't crack your knuckles during tests or she WILL crash out

Her lectures were not very interesting, and she doesn't take attendance however if you choose to skip you will most likely fail the tests. If you don't go to class, it's very important to watch the recording of the lecture to catch up as the tests are based majorly off the content discussed in class. She offers lots of extra credit opportunities.
Way too much content to know and exams are pretty detailed. Offered corrections for 2/3 exams. Offered extra credit points in class here and there. Would avoid.

read off of the slides during lecture and didn't explain the information at all. reading the textbook 1000 times is more helpful than going to her lectures/office hours. 3 exams and one final but only offers corrections for the first two exams. the material seems easy but her exams are difficult for no reason. i don't recommend taking potts-santone
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor that I have ever had. I had read the reviews before taking her and assumed they were from students who did not try and expected a good grade, but that is not the case. It seems like she purposefully makes this class as hard as she can. Doing well on any test is a miracle. Avoid at all costs.

She has an attitude that made me not want to attend class. Her voice is irritating and all she does is word dump off of slides that are terribly put together. I feel like she made this course a lot harder than it needed to be. She isn't understanding and has yelled at people during exams(loudly) for having tech issues or cracking knuckles.

She does give a lot of information that you need to know for the exam, but she made that aware the first day. Just make sure to be going over your notes on a regular basis and you'll do fine on the exams. She allows for corrections on every exam and gives extra credit opportunities. Don't let these reviews scare you, I really enjoyed her class.

I took this class 2 years ago and am still scarred. Exams require you to know the content in extreme, unnecessary detail. The slides are very disorganized. The professor was unhelpful when I went for office hours.

She seems super sweet as a person-- I just could not learn from her. Daunting, wordy lectures that are impossible to understand. Only offered 8am so it was just bound to be bad. Tests are super heavy (+ stuff you never learned) but she will actually help answer questions mid-test. If you put in the effort, you will do well--it's just annoying.

I had her my freshman year and tried to avoid her at all costs. Fast forward and I also have her my senior year. Nothing's changed. She makes exams SUPER detail heavy and sometimes I have to wonder when she even mentioned certain things in lecture. I've taken all the upper stem classes and this class requires me to put in more work than those.
Take this class if you want to decipher the most disorganized, not descriptive, and JANK powerpoints. She is a lovely woman (such a sweetheart!) but her powerpoints suck.

I don't think I have ever met a more caring professor. I got extremely sick this semester, and Mary worked with me and helped me. She pushed back exams to when I could take them and was always available for Zoom office hours, even if it wasn't the normal time. People usually don't like her cause her tests are hard, but it's not if you study right.

The most material dense course I took my first semester at NU. Lots of memorization but she makes the material interesting sometimes which makes that a bit easier. She's serious about teaching, which is respectable, and she expects that to be reciprocated. I learned a lot, but it was not easy learning. She could've organized the material better.

Lecture-heavy but posts recordings so you can go back over it. She provides a study guide and if you just follow along with the study guide and review overall you will be fine. Exam questions were multiple-choice. Offers exam corrections for points back and small extra credit opportunities along the way. Sometimes a little rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Confusing and disorganized lectures. The instructor reads off of a script. An unrealistic amount of memorization is expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've ever had in all my years of being a student. Does not explain things in a clear way, but rather just spits out information we are expected to immediately absorb and understand. I don't feel as though I've been taught to understand concepts. She is throwing random facts and details at us and hoping they stick.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture-heavy with crazy slides (not pleasing to the eyes) as well as a script that she reads off of. This course does require a lot of memorization and requires a lot of time to study (expected to know every detail of a topic) and her office hours don't help too much. Avoid her, but if you can't, take notes of everything NOT on the slides!

Mary is extremely rude and demeaning to students. The icing on the cake was when she screamed "whoever cracks their knuckles next is getting thrown out of the room and receiving a zero" while we were taking our final exam in the dead silent lecture hall. Every question asked is returned with a sarcastic and humiliating response.Also awful teacher!!

Every lecture is a 60-minute info dump where the ONLY reason you don't fall asleep is because of how grating her voice is. It doesn't appear at first, but just wait until her rude and condescending side comes out. I couldn't be happier to be done with this professor and this class. I hope you have good memorization skills!

Not as bad as everyone says. She gives a ton of extra credit and automatically rounds your grade. Let me make up an exam when I had the flu as well. It is pretty memorization/lecture heavy but she records everything. Definitely not an easy A, however.

Ms. Potts-Santone reads from a script and expects you to memorizes every word of that script. Personally, I have nothing against her I am sure she is nice and whatever. However, her style of teaching is meant to take over your life. I was a top performer in this class and hated every second of it. Be prepared to spend all of your free time on this.

This class is just straight memorization. If you can memorize every vocab word spoken during lecture that's kind of the only way to do well in the class. She does offer exam corrections. Can be very condescending when a student asks a question. Class was basically an info dump, and very boring.

Potts-Santone's class is designed to be a weed-out class, and while I had to withdraw for personal reasons, it just wasn't a class I'd ever take. Classes are exam-based, with minute details on the exams. She was caring for sure outside of class, and actually does look out for her students. Buckle up, because the semester will be rough.

Every little detail matters to MSPS. Understanding concepts isn't good enough. She has designed this course as a weed-out, and it nearly worked for me. Stick with it, find a study buddy, and buckle up for a tough semester.

Prof. Potts-Santone has an unfair reputation, IMO. She is very knowledgeable and offers many opportunities to correct exams. You have to put in a considerable amount of effort to do well, but I'm walking away with what I think is a solid foundation in biology. Don't be intimidated: study hard, go to office hours and you'll see results.

reviews.comment: Never take this professor. Avoid at all costs if you want to pass. Her voice is excruciatingly painful to listen to. The hour lecture is unbearable and time feels so slow.

reviews.comment: Never experienced a professor who cares less about her students. Avoid at all costs.

I would not take class with this professor again. She does not seem to care about the success of her students. The test are extremely specific and volume of lecture material does not match the level of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was the actual worst, i have never written a review on here before but had to after I took this class. AVOID if you can, you will be tested on the most minute details that have no meaning to your life or sometimes even the course. Save your mental health by not taking this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite an intelligent woman who should be working in research. If you go to her office hours, this is the best way to seek assistance for her course. She is very hardcore and very thorough. Her lectures are not the most intriguing and you will be tested on minuscule details. (course completed in 2020)
Terrible teacher and voice.

Good professor with thorough lectures and many opportunities to earn extra credit. She is a nice professor and wants students to succeed, although her exams are highly specific and contain material she would mention briefly in class.

She is not as bad as people say she is. Just go to class, take good notes, and you will be fine. She records every lecture, allowed us to correct our exams for some credit back, and offered many extra credit points.

Incredibly tedious for an introductory course. Memorize every single bullet point. Says she wont test on numbers and then proceeds to ask for specific statistics -- misleading for the exams. Revels in the needless difficulty of her exams, then blames the students for being "poor test takers" and "not careful enough". Avoid if you can.

Worst professor I've taken in my entire academic career. Avoid at all costs. Incredibly rude to students in class & during office hours. I genuinely do not think she should be a professor. Not sure if she's unhappy with her profession, but it seems to take it out on her students. Will test on 1 sentence she said off-hand; Memorize entire lecture.

I took Mary Sue's class freshman year and am still amazed I passed. She is clearly incredibly knowledgeable but is often rude to students who have questions. Even when I went into her office hours for help, she was dismissive and I left more confused than when I went in. Avoid taking her class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Potts-Santone is not as bad as some of the reviews on here say, her tests may be specific but if you pay attention in class and write down everything she says (and rewatch the lectures if necessary), you will be fine. The class consists of the final, 3 exams, and 4 quizzes, but she does give ample opportunities for extra credit.

Potts may be difficult, but she lets you know that exams are detail oriented and difficult. I would recommend taking notes directly on her slides, and writing down the important details she says. Her exams are on the content and what she says in lecture. To study, I rewatched the lectures on 2x speed and did active recall with friends. Good luck

The difficulty of her classes comes from the exams, which have very specific questions about the application of the material, however during her lectures she doesn't cover this type of application and doesn't prepare you for her own exams. Lecture slides are disorganized, prepare to self-teach
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Put in the hours and you'll most likely do fine. She gave lots of extra credit. Pay attention in the lectures and write down what she says, not what is on the slides. When you study, just review both. Do lots of active recall when studying, don't just read over your notes. Don't waste time with the textbook.

Despite lower ratings on this website, I enjoyed Professor Potts-Santone's lectures and class overall. Because exams are lecture-heavy, I suggest that you attend lectures on a regular basis and take good notes. She also gave multiple opportunities to earn extra credit and improve your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While her class covered a lot of material in a very short amount of time, I feel that she was very clear about what you needed to know to do well. I definitely put more time into studying for her exams than I expected, but her study guides were very helpful. The content on the exams was the content she emphasized during class. Don't skip lecture!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you can try to avoid her, the exams are super specific. You have to take notes on literally everything that she says.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her tests are insanely specific and her lectures go by so quick that it is hard to catch up. If you have Potts Santone, get ready for a crazy semester. Study more than you think you should. Each tests gets worse and the professor seems to not care.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Potts-Santone is an effective teacher and gives you opportunities to improve your grade. She does go through material very fast, so if you miss anything in class you should rewatch the lectures. It helps to have taken biology in high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor's exams are very specific to what we learned in class, but I think some of the reviews on here are exaggerating. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Surprised about these reviews on Prof. Potts-Santone. She makes exams very doable (given you listen in class) and even gave multiple opportunities for extra credit. People are dramatic, do not listen to the reviews on here.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you can avoid taking Potts-Santone, I would advise you to do so. Grade is essentially based on a few tests. When going to office hours, she was short with me and often unfriendly. Not sure why she chose to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Listen I know everyone dislikes her because she's really difficult but it IS possible to do well in the course, you just have to spend a lot of time studying. She is a personality most people dislike, but I get her teaching style. Rewatch lectures on 2x or download fast panopto to watch even faster. You don't need to go to class but WATCH lectures.
