He does try to adjust grades to not screw people.

Not great in beginning - verbose, confusing lectures and couldn't explain. Second half was 10x better, topics better explained and lectures more structured. Incredibly forgiving/generous when it came to grading, and offered extra credit/remedial assignments where possible. Algorithms is a *very* tough class, but for his first time, he did well.

It was his first year teaching, and some lectures may have been better taught. However, he really improved towards the end and was genuinely a very understanding professor. Algorithms is widely regarded as a challenging course, which unfairly caused some students to direct their frustrations toward him. Homework heavy but it prepares you for exams.

Its his first semester teaching, so it was kind of unorganized in the beginning. But he improved a lot towards the end. Most of the negative reviews are from September-October, so i wouldnt take them into consideration. Class is hard tho(algos is just a hard class in general)

He is a great person, very kind and caring. But his lectures might not be the best. Honestly, i found them useless so I had to self teach myself most of the material. He gives lots of extra credit (drops 3 quizzes, drops 1 homework, late days, 18 points curve, tons of extra points on final and midterm) If you put time in this class, you ll succeed

Don't get me wrong he's a hard teacher esp at the beginning of the year, but kept putting in effort to get better based on the student's reviews/thoughts. Listened to feedback. Even tho midterm was hard, he took that into account for final and bonus points. Homework and quizzes are consistent with the schedule as well so nothing was surprising yk.

I know we were all stressed about the midterm, but honestly Algo is just a hard class. Akshar is not bad and definitely cares about his students. He's very flexible too. Was willing to look over my final to get me a couple extra points.

This was Akshar's first time teaching full-sem algo and he was stuck with all in-person sections (4), so I'm gonna give credit where credit is due. Algo in general is a pain, and the sem got off on a rocky start (why there are so many negative rmps), but prof adjusted things & made it easier. Also if you go to his OH and annoy him, it's pretty fun.

A lot of his course materials are buns (errors in HW problems, some slides not engaging) and he was done dirty by having to teach all of his sections back-to-back. He has, however, reflected on his mistakes on many occasions and accomodated the class accordingly. Right now he's ok at best but the earlier reviews were too harsh.

I am changing my review as Professor Varma is a very fair professor. Although his lectures were hard to understand at times, he does try to improve, which is the most important part. He graded exams and assignments very generously. He cares that every student has learned something in his class and doesn't want the grade to negatively affect that.

Course overall was great. Self-study should be the main method and lectures/OH should be considered additional support. Exams allow reference sheet but are not useful during exams. Psets are straightforward but time consuming. Quizzes are manageable since it's best of 8. Participation grade is easy to get. Overall, manageable if done right.

as I said George Foster and Colin Wong are the teaching assistants to go. don't go to Akshar Varma, you wouldn't understand him. I heard from peers that Ezgi Bas is also another good teaching assistant, but she's graduating from Northeastern University, so she's gone. don't be those people that leave right away after a quiz, you are LOSERS!!!

i would say try to learn the material using chatGPT, meaning after each lecture spend two to three hours understanding the material on the lectures. every week go to office hours (George Foster and Colin Wong are the best TAs to go to) and refresh your memory on what you learnt. that's the only way to succeed and get a 94+ in this class.

i would chatGPT the lectures and study it hard. learnt the material as well as i could. that's the only way to survive in this class. he sadly didn't curve and scale the final, or else I could've gotten an A- or A, but that's what he is. i'm surprised that people did a lot better on the final than the midterm, usually it's the other way around
shoutout akshar

Lectures were kind of boring but that's all bro did wrong. HWs + TAs are really useful. Prof. scales exams (if needed) + opportunity for lots of extra credit on exams. I am not a fan of his teaching style, I don't think his approach to teaching the class is fantastic, but I will say that self-studying and doing LC problems can help.

these kids ts pmo fr fr they are so cooked lmfao

I'm leaving this note because I don't think the other comments here are properly indicative of the class. The grading on exams is more than fair, and almost everyone consistently gets 95-100 on homeworks. His midterm had 20 points of extra credit (before curve), and the final had 30 points of extra credit. If you study you can get an easy A.

I also took this course with OOD and very math-heavy classes in parallel so the workload is manageable imo. Go to office hours if you can't self-study or find a group to study with

reviews.comment:
I took this summer of 2025, it was not a good class. Basically ruined my summer. The lectures teach you very minimal material. I would not know how to solve any problems. He never shows and teaches us example problems and quiz problems, so basically it's a guess game. 

Find a tutor on Knack who took the class, that's my suggestion.

This teacher has no idea what he's doing. He gets mad when people don't ask questions, but gets even angrier when you ask one. The lectures are mostly him reading directly off the slides, and the material he covers doesn't really prepare you for the quizzes or homework, so you're left to teach yourself everything.
Very good professor! Highly recommended
I'm literally going to be teaching myself the algo curriculum, he just reads paragraphs off his slides. Waste of time going to his lectures, you'd benefit more by studying on your own.

He literally can't teach. That's it. 

Also had people who had him in the past & they said they always went to the other prof's lectures instead. He's the only option this semester so!...
Get ready to teach yourself the entire curriculum because what he attempts to teach in class will be entirely different than what is given in homeworks and written assessments.

Prof Varma seems like a very smart person, and even could be a good teacher--if his curriculum wasn't so garbage. What we learn in class seems entirely disconnected from the homework, with little in the way of actual, practical examples. Most of the class will be learning on your own and consulting other sources where prev sections did not have to
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is difficult to follow along with and presentations are unclear.

Professor comes to class entirely unprepared and seems like he is trying to figure out the lecture notes alongside us. Sometimes, his notes are even wrong and he has to change them. He posts recitation worksheets

Not too bad, maybe just inexperienced. Is often late to post materials (didn't open the canvas page until a week into the semester), and lectures generally skim through topics. However, what does end up being covered in the lectures is taught pretty nicely. You will probably need the textbook or online sources as supplements

Professor often comes unprepared and not ready to teach class. Recitations feel like a goose chase, where he is constantly confused on how to solve the problems he wrote. Struggles to confidently answer questions. I have years of experience in algorithms... yet somehow leave confused on topics I am knowledgeable in.

I understand this is his first year teaching. However, he is very unresponsive to campus wire posts asking for more information. He also does not go in depth in his lectures on the topics in any sort of way. Solved examples are few and far between. I may be overreacting as this is the first few weeks, but few resources seem to be provided to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty good class. Weekly quizzes and 3 tests, but the lowest score of each is dropped. There is also a group project that is simple. The final is worth 40%, but you are well prepared for it. If you do the practice problems, you should do well. TAs did the grading. He really cares about making sure you know the concepts behind the math problems.

I had him for 1153 ILS and he was very helpful when you needed help figuring out a problem. wrote helpful diagrams and equations on the board. the TA got grading done by the next week. quizzes were easier than 1151 HW and went over basic examples of the concepts you learned & are standardized across all ILS sections and lecturers.

tests + final were fine except for midterm 2 which he curved. good lecturer and made hard concepts like triple integrals easy. hard to prepare for tests tho, there were suggested textbook problems but they were different and harder to what we learned. grading quizzes took a long time and the grader often made mistakes. didn't respond to emails

He's a good professor. Never responds to emails but was always at office hours when I went. He doesn't grade anything, the graders do so sometimes it can take a while to get stuff back but it's usually within a week or two. If you pay attention to the lecture or just do the homework problems you should be fine for the quizzes and exams.

I took Prof Webber for ILS and he was the BEST at explaining things. I felt like I really understood the concepts compared to explanations from my actual professor, and he'd consider every question I'd ask and explain why/why not something applies. I didn't actually take a class with him but I'm sure he's the same in his actual classes.

He does well to make his lessons understanding/concise and lectures not boring. Quizzes and tests are moderate, not hard if you study. Homework load is light. Doesn't take attendance but might have been because my class was an 8am. Not the most personable guy but still nice and willing to help.

Prof. Webber is not personable and outside of class he is not enthusiastic nor forthcoming. His lectures are OK, manageable but ChatGPT teaches me better. Attendance is not mandatory but there is a quiz every Monday that you need a code to access. Would not take him if you do not have a Physics background or if you're bad at math.
He was a good teacher. His lectures move fast, so it is sometimes hard to keep up, but he offers a ton of help hours and time in class to answer questions.
Cool guy, knows his stuff. only way you don't pass is by not trying
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Webber is great. His lectures were very engaging and he went at a very good speed for the average student. The class is very test heavy, final grade consists of two midterms, the final and weekly quizes. Everything was graded fairly and reflected the material we learned in lecture. Final exam was VERY similar to given practice finals.

Calc 3 is definitely a hard class, but I would honestly say that Webber was a pretty good teacher. I found his lessons to be pretty clear and slides were always posted on canvas. It usually took a while for quizzes to be graded (didn't get them back until after we took the next one a week later, idk if that was the TA though).

Professor Webber is a solid teacher who knows his stuff. His grading felt inconsistent and he would take off a lot of points on the weekly quizzes for very small mistakes which was consistently frustrating. Outside of teaching he was kind of a jerk, just super rude and passive aggressive all the time which was offputting. Class wise he was fine tho

like others are saying, great in class, doesn't respond to emails outside of class. imo grading was a little weird, with HW, quizzes, 4 exams, and a semester long project and somehow the final was still worth 40%, but none of the content is too difficult and he's a good lecturer, and makes things easy to understand
Great teacher inside class, explains really well. Outside of class, non responsive and doesn't check emails.

Professor Webber is a great professor who clearly explains concepts and always answers questions. Outside of class, he's a little hard to reach, but if you show up and pay attention, you'll be prepared for exams and quizzes.

I was so scared to take calc, I failed in highschool. Matthew made it so easy for me to learn. He always went slow and in depth, explaining the core explanations of why some stuff in calc works. The best teacher + teaching style. I felt well prepared for quizzes and exams.
The absolute best calc prof at neu

Professor Weber is a very good lecturer, he explains concepts well, so if you take good notes and pay attention you'll be well prepared for quizzes and exams. However, his teaching style is pretty one-sided, there's minimal class participation and he doesn't respond to emails that much.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Webber was a nice guy however he is not organized at all and that made it hard during the course. There is an online textbook that I relied on heavily because of the homework. The study guide for the final saved me. He would put questions on exams that he had no taught us so beware. He also does not answer emails.

Im not that good at math but I did extremely well in this class. I took precalc in highschool and did horribly in it, and still that was enough for me to ace this class with minimal effort. Seriously, i am not that good at math. Hes a very good math professor, and definitely better than all the other options for this class. Would 100% recommend.

i had matthew webber for physics ILS and he did a better job than my lecture professor in actually explaining the material. he is passionate about physics and is helpful with explaining difficult concepts

Lectures are monotonous and there's no sense of community in the classroom.. doesn't even ask people to share their names on the first day. Knows his stuff well, but I didn't align with his teaching style. Weekly quizzes. Helpful in office hours if you come in with specific questions and lenient if you need to take a quiz another day.

Takes the time to explain basic topics which is nice so you don't lose some of your basic math skills. Lectures can be long but they tell you everything you need to know. Accessible during office hours and will redo/explain problems and topics to help you understand them. Would also sometimes do practice problems before a quiz to help review.

His examples were also super helpful in terms of understanding concepts and homework. He's also good at deriving all formula step by step, so not sure why he got rated so low. He might seem to take a long time on explaining basic probability, since a lot people already learnt this, but as new materials come up, his teaching pace is good.

Great guy, awesome at answering questions. Yeah, the exam questions were a bit harder than the quiz ones. Responded very fast, structured reviews around what we asked for, and was sensitive to the rate the class was going. A pleasure to learn from would take it again. 

Wish there was practice exams and quizzes, but is what it is.
Professor Webber is a decent professor. His lectures do a nice job summarizing the content from class that week, which is really helpful with the homework.

Not the most interesting lecturer and usually takes twice the time he needs to in explanations. Tests and quizzes are quite easy if you're good at math, but final is difficult and very different from the other problems. I didn't bother showing up to class except quiz days and I still did well so take that how you will.

He's a good teacher and explains things well. However, he is a bit behind in grading. It is the end of the semester and he hasn't graded any parts of the group project or given feedback especially when it's worth 15% of our grade. There is a lot of homework and quizzes but they do help in understanding the material for the final.
No study material at all. Take Sadaka's section plzzzzzzz. Make your life much easierrrrrr
Nothing is accessible except his PPT. NO STUDY MATERIAL AT ALL. AVOID AS BEST AS YOU CAN!!!!!

I have taken calculus before but he makes calculus very easy to understand for first-timers and actually explains how to do the math with sample problems and worksheets. There is one group project (like all other calc sections) and multiple tests & quizzes throughout the semester. The final exam has a heavy weight.

He is a very chill guy. The quizzes and tests align perfectly with the material taught during lectures. The homework, on the other hand, is often more complex than what's taught in class and on the quizzes/tests. He's a very fair grader, and he explains concepts extremely well (no fluff). He is also quick to answer emails and is accommodating.

I took math3081 (stats) with him, I barely went to lecture but attended the quiz every week. You honestly don't need to go to lecture, just study for the quiz every week. And the midterms and final. He's also very nice but a bad teacher.

He was a nice guy and clearly very smart, but was not great at explaining the concepts in an easier way. Also took way too long with grading the weekly quizzes and was very harsh. Homework is not mandatory but if you want to try to understand what's going on and do somewhat well, you have to do it.

Loved him as a professor all year until the end and I already submitted a good TRACE eval for him. He filled the exam with time-waster problems (think 4+ triple-integrals), put the heaviest weighted q's on the last page, told us to fully evaluate them at the beginning, then laughed and said we didn't fully need to with 5 minutes left. No curve.

The routine on zoom is we watch his long pre-lectures, do a group activity in which we awkwardly do on our own and then take quizzes every week. Just read through the book or research if you're struggling cause you're not gonna learn anything much from him.

Sometimes he can be very slow at responding to emails or giving feedback on quizzes, or it can be hard to understand his explanations. Most of the time he is a reasonable grader and a pleasant guy. My advice is to do the homework!

Prof. Webber gave us weekly quizzes that he would not grade until one of the big tests of the semester (of which there were two midterms and one final). This was incredibly frustrating, since I had no idea how well I was understanding the material. He's a good guy, but grading my midterm from two months ago right before the final was the worst.

He is a nice guy who makes an effort to help students outside of "class." He likes visuals and the graphical applications of math. The homework probs/lecture probs were not extremely similar to the quizzes, but you should still do those probs and it will give a good foundation for the quizzes. He is a reasonable grader.

His lectures aren't super entertaining. He explains the main topics and gives examples, but the explanations are not in depth enough and I often had to read the textbook to teach myself some of the content.
I had Matt Webber for both 1151 and 1153. His lectures aren't very good because he glosses over stuff, but he's a lenient grader in ILS. Do the homework and read the textbook and you'll do fine
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Matt tries his best, and always lets you out early which is nice, except that theres so much material you miss out on that if he just took a little more time to explain, it would make so much sense. You never know how youre doing in this class. HW isnt collected and quizzes dont get graded for weeks, so you never know if you actually understand

Professor Webber is a type of professor that covers the bare minimum for each topic. In order to do well in the class, comes down to self studying because he doesn't talk for very long in each class and just scratches the surface of all topics.

I really liked him for Physics 1. I'm not an engineering major but had to take this class in the summer, and he was super helpful and the amount of material squeezed into a summer semester didn't seem overwhelming.

Class is just weekly homework + one group project which is pretty simple. Not a ton of work for a 4000-level course, spent 1-2hrs on the hw on average. Group project is a couple hours per person, just get a good group. She gives rubrics for project submissions, follow them to a T. No attendance, extra credit opportunities, anyone could get an A.

The ratings here are way too harsh. Yes, the class can be disorganized and lectures aren't the most engaging, but the class is an extremely easy A even without going to class. None of the content is super difficult either, and she allows you to use AI as well.
The written exams are the worse part of the course because it's memorization.70% of your grade is exams!
Teacher is chill, take them
Not the worst class, but definitely frustrating. Lectures often felt disorganized and assignments required a lot of guesswork.

reviews.comment: Very difficult to understand explanations. I spent more time searching online for tutorials than learning in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: THIS WAS ONE OF THE WORST CLASSES I'VE TAKEN. Instructions were vague and expectations constantly changed.

reviews.comment: Bad experience. Lectures were confusing and moved way too fast. I felt like I had to teach myself everything.
DONT TAKE PROF YANG!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super boring lectures, easy course, take for a free A

Lectures were bland. Easy take-home quizzes weekly. Assignments were manageable. Big final group project on any topic you choose. Appreciated that she used a form to match students with similar styles and allowed you to pair with people you know.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture content was a little boring but she found ways to make it interesting and interactive. She gave a lot of examples and content needed to complete the homework successfully.

Weekly at home quizzes that are extremely easy. The final is a group project that is not too much work. There is a few homework assignments, but they are all fairly simple. Easy for a 4000 level class, lectures are boring and optional and she posts the filled out notebook at the end of the week. Definetly take for easy A.

She's super sweet, and I think is genuinely interested in the material. It's been pretty easy so far despite being a 4000 level class. The workload is also pretty manageable. There is a group project, but she makes an effort to pair you with people with similar work styles to you if you don't have someone to work with.

The class itself is fairly easy. The lectures are kinda boring as Prof. Yang reads off the slides most of the time. Going into the first lectures, I expected the class to be very interesting based on the material. Grades based on hw, weekly online quizzes and group project.

She's not bad. Attendance isn't mandatory as class is available on zoom and notes are posted. Homework can be a lot, but she responds promtly to emails. Lecture itself wasn't very interesting but she was helpful during office hours and understanding when an extension is required.

Horrendous. Does not care about you or your education. Assignments, although very easy, are unclear and often blatantly missing instruction. Her lectures are horrible, as she silently copies code from her notes zoomed too far in to follow. If you want an easy A without having to go to lecture, take this course before she gets fired.

Not that bad but the written exams were kinda weird because they tested you on facts some of the concepts. I learned enough about using sklearn and gradient descents. The class is pretty free if you stay on top of the conceptual stuff. Coding exams were probably easiest. Wouldn't recommend though

DS 4200: Lectures are pretty boring and useless. When she codes she just copies down what she has in her notes, it doesn't seem like she really understands the material she's teaching. She can be helpful if you ask and the homeworks and projects are not difficult.

The course policy was generally lax, you could do the homeworks and coding exams pretty easily since they were open notes and the coding demonstrations were usually consistent. The written exams are the worse part of the course because it's memorization. It's either a hit or miss and 60% of the grade is exams, projects were cut out of the content.
Free A+, 25 mcq tests, open book, grades very nicely on the semester-long project.

Professor Xu was a great professor! So caring and wanted all of us to succeed. There are weekly take-home quizzes based on the reading and a case study, which was manageable. Also, two midterms with a cheat sheet allowed. We had a final group project where we designed an app, which was pretty cool. I definitely learned new things, such as Python!
cool, exams were super easy, 25 mcq open book.

All 3 exams are 25 multiple choice, open book. Group project is semester long, and graded very nice. Lectures are very boring, and you have Mcgraw Hill assignments every week, and attendance is mandatory. If you were to take Supply chain, make sure to take it with this professor, free A.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures but I don't blame them given that the class is very common sense. Overall what a sweetheart of a professor, absolutely amazing. I will say that most of your grade depends on one midterm (40%) and final exam (35%). With that the practice exams given are essentially copy paste so if you do those you'll guarantee at least a 85%.
Great professor. Lectures include practice problems that are similar to the homework. Graded on weekly assignments, a midterm, and a final. Pay attention in lecture, it helps.

Professor Xiaolin is very knowledgeable about all the topics taught in this class she didn't have to read from a slide deck or repeat/recite a text book back to us, she is also very engaging in class, and would directly ask students for their thoughts on a problem set which made the class exciting /thought provoking.

Professor Shi is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. Her interest and knowledge on this subject is so clear and she cares about her students' learning. She genuinely wanted us to do well and always took the time and effort to explain concepts and help me. I learnt quite a bit.

She was very understanding of deadlines and prioritized quality over submission. She is a very fair grader and clearly outlines expectations and materials and knowledge needed to succeed during the course. How much effort you put into this course is what you will get out of it.

She is a great professor. She really explains all the concepts clearly and will go over as many times as needed if students are struggling or have questions. Lectures can get boring sometimes because she doesn't use any slides and instead uses an Ipad to explain everything which does seem to drag on sometimes.
She was the best. Im registering for next semester classes and im already looking for her again. TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: lectures are difficult to follow. she goes through examples without really explaining why/what she's doing, makes the lectures difficult to sit through. 3 exams worth 75% of the grade, the average of which generally hovers around ~70%, i don't think she's the worst prof in the world but idk why she has a 4.7.
One of the best economics professors out there. Beyond caring and understanding, and is always willing to put in the extra effort to make the class a great experience.

Super helpful professor and very knowledgeable about her work. She wants you to succeed, evident by the in class prep and recordings being available for each class. She expects you to put in effort and participate but you learn a lot. If you pay attention during class and do the problems you'll be set. She is very helpful if you have questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very helpful outside class especially during office hours. She provides enough materials such as practice problems for each topic and practice exams that are relevant to the exam so you can be well prepared. She makes it hard to not do well and wants success for her students. Also she's got a good sense of humor.

Taken over 3 classes with her, highly recommend her for econ classes. She's a good teacher, encourages participation, but will not penalize you if you don't talk at all (me) as long as you show up to class. The way she teaches makes it easy for students to understand, which means you have less to study for exams since you already know it.

BEST PROFESSOR!!
would recommend.

Great professor!   
would recommend.
THIS IS THE BEST PROFESSOR IN THE WORLD!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her lectures r insanely hard to follow

Professor Xiaolin is very knowledgeable in economics and statistics, and she provided many resources to help you succeed. All modules were posted on canvas; professor outlined what we would cover each week; example questions, study materials, and many other resources were all posted online.
She is such a kind and fun professor; the classroom environment is amazing and she seems so happy to teach. Such an awesome professor.

Professor Shi is very thoughtful and supportive of her students. She posts all course materials on Canvas, including plenty of practice problems and exam study guides. She also records every lecture on Zoom in addition to teaching in person, making it easy to catch up if you miss a class. Highly recommended!

Professor Shi is a wonderful professor; she is interested in student success, appreciative of critical thinking, engaged with her students, and flexible to student needs/concerns. Extremely funny as well. Highly recommend! btw, no final exam, just a group research paper, which you can get a lot of help/guidance from her.

Very friendly and helpful professor. Grading consists of exams, homework assignments, participation, and a big final paper. It is an easy course but don't slack, she can tell and will be less kind. Most classes are lecture-based. She is not the best lecturer but makes up for it by being available for individual review with every student.

Prof. Shi is an absolute angel. She wants you to succeed and is willing to go out of her way to make sure you get there. She is the most helpful professor I've ever had during office hours; take advantage of that. Her classes are lecture heavy, but she uses a good amount of repetition to make everything stick. Pay attention = good grade.
Amazing professor! Makes a tough subject extremely engaging. Tests are fair, lectures are recorded, and she wants to see you succeed. She really knows what she's doing, and I learned a lot.
Professor Shi has a strong academic background and extremely responsible attitude. I have learnt a lot from her. She is the best! God bless this woman!

I learned A LOT from Prof Xiaolin, such as having faith in what you love, treating everyone equally, and being sincere with people as if never been hurt before. She is always cheerful and optimistic, passionate about teaching, and full of respect, love, and sympathy toward students. I feel highly honored to have met such a role model in my life.

Professor Shi is very good; she often interacts with the students in class, memorizes the names of the students by heart, and sometimes has a roll call interaction; such a learning atmosphere is enjoyable. She also posts all the notes and in-class practice with annotations on Canvas. I think Professor Shi is excellent!

Professor Xiaolin is sweet and always open to answering students questions. However, she is terrible at teaching, has an un-engaging lecture based class which is not structured very well, and you end up learning nothing. Another $7k down the drain for a useless class where I have to memorize all the problems for the exam, and then forget everything

Professor Shi is so nice and really cares about her students. She is a good professor but often goes on tangents that become difficult to follow. If you keep up with the material and make sure you pay attention you'll have a great time in her class.

Prof. Shi is very easy to talk to. She's willing to help you anytime with anything you ask. She's super organized, you can literally find everything in Canva files. But she could improve on teaching us how to run regression on STATA.

Professor Shi has the sweetest soul! She is uper understanding, caring, respectful, and such a good person. We also learned a lot, and the course was challenging but well-organized. Zoom is always an option, so no one would miss content if they couldn't attend class. Plus, every lecture was recorded and easy to access shortly after each class.

Professor Shi attaches great importance to attendance, and each lesson is very careful, and uploads study materials and class notes in a very timely manner after the lesson, an there are consolidation exercises in each lesson, which is very helpful to my study.

Professor Shi is the funniest professor I've had! The course will be super difficult to understand in the first weeks and you will want to cry and get angry at her, but give her time! Eventually, you'll totally understand it and succeed and realize it wasn't even that hard to start with.

I loved taking this class with Xiaolin! She can be a bit scattered in class sometimes, but she's always willing to go back and clarify questions. She's very accessible if you need help and her tests are fair. I found it helpful to go into class after skimming some of the course content beforehand, which stopped me from getting lost !

Participation and attendance matter. About 8 easy homework assignments graded on completion. 3 hard exams, but she is very clear about what is on the exam and provides great practice problems and wants to give students as many points as possible. Super caring and good lectures. Scales final grade.

WOW! Best online experience I have ever had with a professor here at Northeastern. She is very organized, and everything is accessible via Canvas modules. She also has Zoom recordings posted immediately after class. Very tech-savvy, and it is much appreciated.
The BEST Professor I have ever had at Northeastern! Very good at explaining difficult concepts. Always made herself available for her students outside of class time.

First of all, Xiaolin has the sweetest soul! The course was extremely entertaining and pragmatical. She forced us to think outside of the box and encouraged dedication and attention to details. If you wanna take econ2316, highly recommend prof. Shi!
She is amazing at accommodating students. If you were sick, missed a class, etc. would make zoom so accessible. She was also very accessible outside of office hours.
Phenomenal organization and online canvas page. EVERYTHING she talks about is uploaded and zoom classroom has past recordings which help out a TON if you miss a class.

Although the course was one of the most intellectually challenging of them all, Xiaolin clearly communicated the material and guided me through it masterfully. btw, she has the sweetest soul ever! Highly recommend!!

Xiaolin knew what she was talking about and was straight to the point in teaching what we needed to know. She was effective, especially at helping us model which was the main draw of the course. Would definitely take her again.

Professor Shi told us on the first day this was one of her favorite courses to teach and I can see why. For such a complicated subject, she explains everything so easily and makes it understandable. She spent the first week going over statistics and it helped so much. Overall, the best professor I have ever had at Northeastern.

Sweetest professor ever, but gives the most unstructured, convoluted lectures I've ever seen. She just constantly starts to teach something and then interrupts herself to explain something that's irrelevant and may or may not ever return to the original topic. Incredibly difficult to follow. Would be better if she just used some slides.
I think her name should be Xiaolin if anyone could correct it. An approachable professor who clearly explains the content and rubric of exams and homework.

Grades came out today so I decided to do a review. I am honestly not the smartest person ever but still got an A. If you show up, partipate, and do the work you will get a good grade. This might be one of the nicest prof's i have ever had fr. She just wants her students to do well and will go the extra mile to do so. Take her if you can.

Was scared because she had no reviews but she is beyond great. The content can be confusing at times but thats also because its a confusing topic. She did a really good job of simplifying everything. Homework was also just graded for completion which was nice. Take her if you get the chance, she is one of the best econ professor's at the school.

Amazing professor. Tests were the examples from class and zoom lectures were available if you missed class. This professor is super tech savvy so the canvas page has EVERYTHING you need (so no textbook!). She has textbook slides though so if you like that it is there. You will do well if you try and leave with so much knowledge. 10/10 recommend.

I you want to understand something as important as financial accounting, don't take this professor. She can't speak English properly, as her thick accent makes it sound as she is saying something completely different to what she means. Lectures are boring and slow, and course materials are not properly ordered.

If you are going to take accounting with anyone, take it with Professor Xiao, she gives you everything you need to get an A. I thought at the beginning of the year I would fail, but after I realized all I had to do was use her resources and GO TO CLASS, my grade went up. It is A LOT of work, and a hard class, but it is the best with her. 
:)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Xiao is an incredible lecturer. She uses class time super effectively and is very good at explaining concepts and giving examples to students. If you come to class regularly and pay a lot of attention, you will learn a lot and the tests will not be as difficult as they seem.

She is a wonderful professor and I don't think her accent is hard to understand like many people say. I really enjoyed it even if was very lecture-based. There are 4 quizzes, most were curved and so were the midterm and final. If you just study and pay attention in class, you'll do perfectly fine.

Prof. Xiao is a great professor who is very caring. Her accent is thick but she is still easily understandable. People complain about the accent but I think they are just making excuses for why they did bad in the class. Very straightforward class, not complicated. She also curves quizzes and tests on a situational basis. Literally ended with a 101
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures can be slow at times but overall bearable. I think she does a good job making concepts clear and digestible. Tests are pretty fair, but the final can be tough given the amount of memorization required. Definitely spend a good amount of time preparing for it.

If you want complete clarity when learning a class such as accounting, avoid. Unfortunately this class is lecture heavy and she doesn't have the necessary English-speaking level to teach this class. It's hard to understand what she says sometimes, making students feel lost or confused. This made the topics and ideas harder to grasp.

Professor Xiao has a very straightforward course, but I did not find her lectures very helpful. I had to read the textbook from cover to cover to understand the topic. She is a very nice person and will help you if you ask any questions.

Absolutely would not recommend. Extremely impersonal, switched class to zoom only after registration, doesn't even turn on camera and difficult to understand. Lectures are very confusing. I dont even know what she looks like as the TA does literally everything. Exams every other week in person, no notes but the textbook and exams are very helpful.

this is my second time taking this class and im barely passing. just do yourself a favor and never take this professor. never even saw their face once the whole semester. extremely impersonal class experience, you're just a box on zoom. supposed to be calc 1 but doesn't even teach calc. u need to already know/have taken calc to even do decent

Nice enough person and clearly understands the material, however she simply should not be teaching it. Goes through material extremely fast, finishes units a week before the exam and starts the next unit before we even review for the test on the old material. She is also difficult to understand, especially online. Prac exam v similar to actual exam
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is very efficient and straightforward in lecture. It is clear what she will test you on. She is very traditional: Chalk board lecture, no Zoom classes, and tests are on paper. You should go to class to better understand the material, and she holds office hours before every exam. Do tons of practice problems in order to do well
test heavy - six tests determined grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wu's class requires you to have some basic knowledge of differential calculus, otherwise you will have a hard time fully understanding what she is talking about in class. You'll take an exam every two weeks on what you have learned during those two weeks. There is nothing difficult about this course as long as you review it carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She never talks about the concepts of math, so if you're genuinely interested in exploring this topic do not take her. If you don't already have a calc background, this class is going to be really hard for you. Tests are every other week and aren't bad if you do well on the practice exam.

Dr. Wu is a caring, friendly professor, but sometimes she is hard to understand. This makes it hard to get clarification on in class questions. If you have never taken calculus before, make sure you get ahead before this class starts. There is a test every other week, so there basically is no downtime in the class.
Sometimes hard to understand and very detached, Don't take her if you have trouble with any the concepts you will learn

Dr. Wu is my favorite professor. She goes through material very efficiently -can take time to get used to speed. She welcomes questions and checks if anyone is confused. The homework is not mandatory but helpful before weekly quizzes. The quizzes are also helpful to study for exams. Don't buy the textbook - only need it for hw and can find online

Professor Wu is effective and answers questions well. She posts lecture materials and practice exams on Canvas for you to look at outside of class. Homework is not mandatory but it is good practice for exams. This class is not very difficult but is definitely easier if you have prior knowledge of calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Wu gives clear lectures and sends class materials before class so that it is easy to keep up with. Also, she did a lot of examples that are similar to the tests. If you do the sample test and take notes in class, you will absolutely get a great grade.

Professor Wu provides a lot of practice problems and I found it so helpful. While she runs through material somewhat quickly, she posts handouts online of the classwork. She is also very understanding of her students.

I don't consider myself to be good at Math but Dr. Wu really wants her students to do well. She explains concepts clearly and does lots of examples in class that are similar to homework, quiz and test questions. She is willing to help you in any way she can. If you understand the material and do your homework, you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu was a really good professor. There were a lot of example problems, and would offer help whenever needed. I would definitely recommend her for math, as she made it a lot easier for me to understand!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is very sweet and really wants to make sure you understand the material. At times, you can't always understand exactly what she is referring to but she makes sure to write everything down on the board and take questions after every problem. There's 5 tests, but she'll drop your lowest grade at the end. Great choice for a calc teacher!
She's dedicated and eager to re-explain problems that you don't understand. Attend class, take good notes, practice given materials and you will get good grade

Wu really tries her best to make sure everyone is prepared for tests. If you put in the work and pay attention in class, you'll do well. The only trouble I had was that she has a strong accent and it was difficult for me to understand her at times.

She's not a bad professor by any means. But I was definitely one of the people who her teaching style didn't really work for. She does a lot of examples of various scenarios but it doesn't always get the idea across the best. If I hadn't already taken this class before I would have struggled. She's also very rigid about her policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wu really wants her students to succeed. I am not a math person, but she made calculus understandable and interesting for me. The test questions are based on the problems she explains during lecture, so it is very important to attend class. The textbook can be helpful if you need another perspective of what she discusses during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is an amazing professor. She teaches things the more traditional Asian way, where you go through a TON of examples in class of every type of problem you need to know. Each problem is explained very thoroughly and she writes everything out. As long as you make sure you understand and do the practice tests, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is a great calc 2 teacher who clearly understands the material very well. Her tests are just like the practice exam and if you do the homework and prepare you will do well.

Professor Wu is a very caring professor and is very accessible outside of class. The exams are extremely straightforward and the practice exams are super helpful. Would choose her again even if it means waking up at 7:30 every day!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is a really caring and respected professor. She is straight forward. She makes sure to teaches all that's gonna show up on the test. Textbook has no use basically. As long as you take note and do the practice test, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best Math teacher I have ever got in Northeaster. Practice quiz and exam make life much easier as long as you do it.

Took this class during the summer having never taken math reasoning or probability + stats (highly recommend taking those 2 beforehand), concepts were quite hard. That being said, Dr. Wu really does her best to make sure everybody is prepared before tests, absolutely a huge help inside + outside of class. Put time + effort in, you'll get results.

Very nice professor. Although you may not understand her accent at first, it gets better later on. She goes through everything you need to know and gives lots of practice so don't even worry about getting a bad grade.

Dr. Wu is a great Calc 1 professor. She goes over everything you need to know. Pay attention to the problems she does in class because she will sometimes use the same ones on exams. She always lets you ask as many questions as you want and makes sure everyone understands before moving on. If you took IB SL math you will get an A easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: In Calc 1 you have a test or quiz once a week. You need to go to lectures because all the problems that she does in class are the same types she uses on the tests. The textbook is not very useful. She does drop one test and one quiz grade but is a pretty harsh grader. I went to her mid-semester and after she was more lenient on grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Wu is nice and straight to the point. She wants students to do well in the course and will help if you seek it out. She goes over the material very quickly and there is a quiz or exam every week. Go to class regularly-she takes attendance and she wants you to do the problems the way she presents them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She can be hard to understand in the beginning but you get use to it. She really wants people to ask questions. She teaches you the subject at a super fast pace so if you are not good at calculus you won't pass, take a pre-calc class first.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's sometimes hard to understand her accent but she gives amazing lectures. If you go to class, you'll understand the topic. She'll either give a quiz or exam every week, so you need to keep up with your work. She assigns homework every lecture, but she doesn't check them so you don't have to do them if you just don't care. Put in some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: In the beginning, Wu seemed very nice and helpful. She's at times very hard to understand and she moves on with material very quickly. She isn't very welcoming to questions. I went to her office hours a couple times & have personally experienced & witnessed her being rude to students when they do not understand material. Quizzes and tests weekly!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wu started the semester as the best professor I've ever had- clear, concise, and always asked whether she was going to fast and if everyone understood. However, towards the middle of the semester, she became less clear in her explanations and went too fast, in my opinion. She's a very sweet, smart woman, and an overall great professor, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing Prof if you are bad at math. Her lecture is very systematic and logical, which really help you to understand.  She writes everything on the board.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wu was the first teacher who really helped me understand calculus. I loved her lectures, especially because she wrote everything on the board. If you don't understand, she is always willing to change the examples to help you grasp the concepts.
I loved Wu!! She was clear and wonderful and I found her extremely helpful. For those who aren't math brained, I still think you would do well. She really just wants to see her students succeed.
You will love it if you take notes and pay attention in class. Just make sure to listen, its hard to understand sometimes but as long as you write down notes you will get an easy A.

Shu-Shih is a great teacher. Her accent takes a bit to get used to but she writes everything, and I mean everything down, even if she does it rather quickly. If you don't understand anything, she'll help. She wants us to learn and do well.

A littel difficult to understand in the beginning due to her accent, but you get used to it really quickly and she writes everything clearly on the board. As long as you go and take down the notes, you'll be fine.

amazing teacher. if you go to class and pay attentiondo homeworkgo to office hours you will do really well. she has an accent but its not hard to understand. i was horrible at math in high school but got an A in this class with some effort. great great greaaaaat teacher!!

She does have an accent, which I can understand may be difficult for some students to understand. However I personally found that - combined with the notes on the board - she teaches the course with clarity and swiftness unusual to receive in a math course. It was my favorite class of the semester, actually. She just really knows the material.
very nice good teacher helpful at times but all she said is you need to improve and when you where that get your act together
She is a very intelligent professor and knows her stuff. Hard to understand but you get used to her accent. She writes everything she says on the board anyway.

Accent is kind of thick but you get used to it. Wants you to do well in the class, and is really helpful during her office hours, I highly recommend going to them. Gives review sheets for quizzes and tests which are extremely helpful in preparing for them.
Great Proffessor, accent pretty thick, Always willing to help i her office hour but come prepared with thoughtful questions. She wants to see you work hard and do your best.

Her accent is very thick, but she writes everything she says on the board, so you understand the point she is trying to teach you. If you don't understand something, her office hours are very helpful. She also gives practice quizzes and exams prior to the actual quizzes and exams, which show you exactly what to expect.

It is fortunate for me to have taken Dr. Wu's Calculus. I feared math before, but have gained much confidence in math with her teaching. Her class is serious. Don't expect many jokes in class. But working hard will certainly get delightful reward.

I'm grateful to have taken calculus before having a class with Dr. Wu, otherwise there is no way I would've passed. Her method of explaining otherwise simple concepts is obscure and convoluted. Furthermore, her class is extremely boring. The practice quizzes she posts on blackboard are helpful, though.
She's super nice and she really does want everyone to do well in the class!

She really cares about her students and explains the material very very patiently if you don't understand and ask a question. Her accent is not hard to understand like some people stated here. Definitely study the practice quizzes and tests! I'd recommend her classes.
Great math teacher. She wants the students to do well.
she is a great professor. I wish i can take another class with her.

Dr. Wu is absolutely amazing.  Her lectures, though not very clear, are very thorough.  She gives weekly quizzes which make up the greatest part of the grade, but if you do the practice quizzes she gives, and attend class regularly, you'll be fine.
Very bad accent . Chinese way of teaching and explaining.Don't take a class with her if you don't like math and you have to take it.
She is awesome. If you listen - you are gonna get a good grade. Take notes of the examples on the board cuz quizes are very similar to them and to the practice quizes.
Prof. Wu taught in an intelligent way, made sure everyone understood the material, and was willing to help.  She is the best math teacher I've ever had.

Great Professor! Hard to understand but she's adorable and really tries to help you if you try in her class. The material was a joke but I already had two years of calculus before this class. It's super easy, easy A++ and Wu is highly entertaining. Practice tests are very very similar to the Exams- DO NOT BUY A BOOK, Homework was not necessary.

Her exam/quiz reviews were very helpful for learning the materials, though they were NOT the same as the exams/quizzes. A previous comment stated "the practice quiz is same as the test", which may mislead others.In fact, her exams were challenges.

I took this class because everyone here says shes awesome! You're in for a very bad joke. She has a VERY thick accent that you just can't understand her. True, she is nice, and also that the practice quiz is same as the test. But you still can't get what she is saying. She's a robot who doesn't make a convo, just comes in and starts writing on boar
Su Wu is an amazing teacher! She is so nice and the practice tests are exactly like the real thing!

She is by far one of the best professors that ive ever had in my life. the review sheets help out alot on tests and if you go to her office hours thats extra brownie points for you. she yelled at me alot for not getting stuff although i had a 98 average in her class. dont ask stupid questions and just go to class cause she knows when you dont go.

Math has always been a difficult area, but Prof. Wu goes above and beyond to make sure the students understand the material. If you aren't willing to do the work however, don't plan on getting a good grade.

Professor Wu rocks my mathematical world! She really squares my roots and and dots my imaginary i's. Her accent is contagious. I find myself speaking like her on a regular basis. By day, she is a wonderful math professor, but by night, she saves the world, one pawabowa at a time. Thank you, Dr. Wu. You have changed my mathematical life forever!

Awesome.  She has an accent but if you pay attention to her you get used to it.  she gives a lot of examples and is always helpful. if you go to class pay attention and study the quiz reviews your garunteed an A.  The quiz reviews are almost exactly like the quizzes same with the midterm and final, respect here and shell respect her shell respect y
Prof. Wu is a good math teacher. She gave a lot of examples and explained them thoroughly. She was very enthusiastic and eager to help. I love Prof Wu.
one of the best professors.

Her heavy accent was the most difficult aspect of class. A kid actually got a refund for the class when his dad (a lawyer) complained about it. The kid was just dumb though, and I was equally as dumb b/c I didn't do well but I liked her alot.

Prof. Wu is a great teacher. She explains material well and is willing to help. If you attend the class and pay attention, it is easy to get a good grade. I never did math well before, but I am doing very well in this course.
Prof Wu is the best math teacher i've ever met. I used to hate math. Now i like math because of Wu.
wu is a great math professor. she is patient with us.
dont get on her bad side

Professor Wu is a wonderful person and an excellent mathematics professor. She is always willing to help her students and really cares about their grades. The class project is kind of awful, but as long as you follow the directions, you should be fine.

She is the best teacher I have ever had.  She is extremely nice person. She loves teaching!  She helps a lot! Her explanation is easy to understand. If you don't miss her class, you can get an A easily.
Great teacher.  She explains everything so it is easy to comprehend.  Tests and quizes are very similar to the reviews.  Easy A is you go to class and pay attention.

She is the best teacher ive had yet.  Her accent is difficult to understand at times but to compensate she teaches very slowly and writes everything on the board very clearly.  Grade is based on 6-7 quizes and she drops the lowest grade.  The quiz review mirrors the actual quiz.  I love Wu.
Pretty easy class. Quizzes are based on the Quiz reviews. Just study for the midterm and final. Don't even have to do the homework. Shes a pretty nice woman though hard to understand sometimes.

She was a great professor.  She is always willing to help you understand the material in class.  Her accent was sometimes challenging to work around in class but ask her questions if you don't understand something.
She gives a lot of examples, which is very nice.  Doing the homework can help with your understanding of the course content.  Very helpfull if you're having problems.
She is an alright teacher. Sometimes it's a bit hard to understand her because of her accent but she always makes sure to help anyone who is confused.
A very sweet lady. Wants you to know the information and constantly asks students to come to her for help. She's not that hard to understand like some ppl complain about. I recommend her class.

She was a pretty easy teacher. Be careful with the class project... Tests weren't too hard. She's willing to give extra help as long as you're willing to put in the time. Despite her accent, a great teacher.
OH I loved her! Depsite the thick accent, she means well. The reviews for quizzes and exams made the class easier. The final project was ridiculously easy!
shes a good professor.  her accent is a little tricky to get used to, but after that, she's sweet.  She gave reviews for every quiz and major test and made sure we knew the material.
Her accent is impossible and she only helps the kids who already know calc, if you are a troubled math student stay away from her!

Her accent is overwhelming. Its very very hard to understand what she is saying.  She does use a ton of examples, but goes way to fast and you can get lost very easily.  The only way to do well in this class is to teach the material to yourself.
shes an awesome teacher. and u just wanna pinch her cheeks shes so cute!! and shes so so nice.

Great teacher...teaches with a million examples which is great. The only people who don't like her are the ones who do bad in the class and blame it on her thick accent, which I didn't find very hard to understand at all. Definitely take her class.
This is the best math teacher I have ever had. Her accent is strong but she more than makes up for it. Her review sheets are a major plus, I wish all math teachers were like her.
Despite her somewhat difficult to understand accent, she was a decent  teacher.  The review sheets were quite helpful, and she wanted people to do well.
Hated this class, she is too hard to understand and only heps the kids that are doing well in the class
Aw, shes soo cute! Def wants everyone to understand the material. Quiz Reviews, etc. are excellent and very helpful! Dont drop this class...it's great!

Very good class.  Review sheets are almost identical to the quizzes and midterm if you do that you should do great.  She wants all of her students to understand the work.  one of the best teachers i have ever had

Best math teacher I have had thus far in this school. Her strong accent takes a little to get used too, but once you get used to it, the class becomes better. She goes out of her way to teach the stuff.
Awesome professor and person, I loved his class even as a non-math person

Peter was a good professor and cares abt his students. Attendance wasn't taken everyday but it was a surprise so people should j go to class. Only 2 tests (midterm and final). At times he could get a bit confusing but the material he gives helps with the course. Overall very good!! Hes also rlly sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Xu is the first instructor who genuinely made me understand and enjoy math. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would recommend you show up to class; he regularly gives hints for exams and answers for projects. Fun lecturer if you pay attention. Light workload. Easily one of the best professors I've had.

Peter Xu was nothing short of phenomenal. He makes an effort to understand everyone's background regarding statistics and constantly makes time to help you outside of class if you need assistance. I had zero stats history and yes at times not going to sugar coat it I was confused but because of the kind of professor he is I could figure it out.

Really good at explaining concepts, likes it when you ask clarifying questions, reasonable grader, nice person, thick Chinese accent but didn't actually get in the way of any understanding for me at least.
Good prof. Also, this prob is in Business school, not the Math dept.

Peter is a caring professor with a lot of knowledge of stats. He can be frazzled when teaching and doesn't follow a specific slideshow or textbook. However, he is very available outside of class and always willing to help. I would recommend taking him for stats. There are two individual projects, weekly homeworks, a midterm, and a final.
The first time I want to write a review for a professor, the best teacher in neu!

Homework due every week except the week a project is due. Two projects. He has a thick chinese accent so it's hard to understand sometimes. Syllabus said attendance was worth 10%, it ended up being worth 20% and that brought me down a lot because I didn't even realize attendance was mandatory.

There's 2 projects and homework due every week (but not th week there's a project). I would've had an A but I never showed up and didn't realize participation (attendance) mattered. Syllabus said it was worth 10% of our grade. He actually made it worth 20% and that brought me down a lot. If I attended class more I wouldve gotten an A.
He lowkey doesn't speak very good english but he's honestly a fun lecturer if you're paying attention and the work is fairly straightforward.

I took 1501 and 1502. Sweet lady but doesn't seem to know what she's talking about. If you ask her any questions that are not in her slideshow she will not know the answer. She often says "she is learning with you" or "she doesn't know all the answers but will look them up and get back to you". She does not get back to you. Not a helpful professor.

1 time she tried to teach us how to write a Matlab script to convert Fahrenheit to Celsius and COULDN'T DO IT and she had to leave the room bc she was "flustered". bad lecturer and you're better off learning the softwares yourself. class and HW is simpler than other 1501/2 profs and her inability to teach will leave you behind your peers

Round 2: STILL A BRICK. Somehow knows Matlab a little better, i'll give here that. If you don't know Solidworks before, you will learn nothing. She nice, but NOT QUALIFIED TO TEACH. Actively brought down my eng. experience, especially for interviews. Enjoy the second half of your yeaman journey. SHE'S LEAVING NORTHEASTERN! REJOICE! (Forcibilly???)

She is not knowledgable in Python, Matlab, Auto Cad, Solidworks (All the things she is supposed to be teaching us). She does not grade any of her own assignments because she does not know the softwares and is really unhelpful.

I am shocked that Northeastern hired Dr. Yeaman. She is the most clueless professor I've ever had. We even caught her answering a student's question with AI. Class is a waste of time, unless you want to make friends, but in terms of learning, there was almost none done in class. Very nice teacher, but nothing going on up there.

Terrible teacher. Completely Clueless. She know none of the course content and has no critical thinking skills. Literally useless. Do Not Take Her Class. She will literally bog down your engineering level. The final project was incredibly stupid and because of that will definitely impact co-op interviews. Should be fired. How did she get a degree??

真的很差了。DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS
1. She knows nothing
2. She never prepares for class (especially AutoCAD and Python; she always did something wrong and could not find her errors).
3. BAD Communication (essay-style instruction for each homework, has to be read very carefully, otherwise F is waiting for YOU)
4. The left brain attacks the right brain

Unfortunately, she does not know what she is teaching. Although she is a great person and cares for her students, I had to learn all the course material myself because she cannot teach. 

Great person, horrible teacher.
The professor is very sweet and approachable, but she's not very skilled at teaching and the class can be confusing. You will have to spend time outside of class to learn the materials yourself.

Don't believe the haters. Prof. Yeaman is awesome. She is super caring and works hard to teach us everyday. When she doesn't know something she admits it and then figures it out and updates us quickly. It's rare to find a teacher this caring and humble.

Yeaman is a sweet and kind soul, but barely knows what's going on herself. You can tell she cares for her students, but is just often time confused on the concepts as she is teaching them. Grading is pretty clear, and she does allow you to see what your grade is throughout the semester.

Professor Yeaman is very kind and sweet, but she knows nothing. Assignment take weeks to be graded, lectures are completely useless, and she's lost the entire time. If you genuinely want to learn, DON'T TAKE HER CLASS. If you just want an easy grade and have a basic understanding of the concepts, take it.
Does not have any knowledge of the material. Always lost.

You can tell Mrs. Yeaman is genuinely a kind soul, but she doesn't know what she is doing. Answering questions only leads to more confusion and she has stated that she is "learning with us". Grading is light so nobody is failing, but nobody has learned from class. Classes at Northeastern are expensive, and I didn't get anything out of this one.

Professor Yeaman is extremely kind but unfortunately she seems to not know any of the course material. Hopefully this is just a result of it being her first time teaching the course, but as it stands she is unable to make it through a lesson without confusing herself and the class.

doesn't really know what she is doing; class can get confusing if you don't know the material already. however, but she's super nice and the class is chill. grading is not too hard and assignments are easy; workload is not bad at all. tests are take home but can be confusing.

The pace is extremely slow, and yet she fails to understand the concepts of what she is teaching. Its as if she's learning with us and is seeing the slides for the first time while presenting. If you don't understand the basics of coding and CAD going in, she won't help you. You can watch a 10 min video to learn the same thing as an hour class

professor canavan is an angel, she is the sweetest professor at this university and if you have the chance to have a class with her definitely take it. she gives barely any homework outside of class and builds such a safe environment in the class. i cannot recommend her enough!!

AMAZING! If you are lucky to take Professor Canavan you will have so much fun in her class. She really cares about her students and her classes are super fun and engaging. You will have homework due the night before each class and quizes can be a bit hard but not worth that much of the overall grade. Overall amazing professor and made learning fun!

So amazing! Made class super fun and engaging, and was very easy to come to with any problems. Would learn content for homework day before which could be hard, but next classes would always go over it, so not leaving you out to dry. Cannot recommend her enough, such a sweet, fun human and a great professor

This is the sweetest professor you will ever have. She was so understanding! If you think you were graded unfairly, she will hear you out and change it. If you talk a lot in the beginning, she will love you all year.

Yanet Canavan truly is a gem at northeastern. You dont find many professors that are actually enthusiastic about what they do, but Yanet runs into class everyday excited to watch you grow and learn. It's a really refreshing and friendly environment. Solely speaks in Spanish, which could be hard, but it helps us learn and retain. TAKE. HER. CLASS!!!

Monica is so kind and understanding, I'm genuinely really glad that I got to take her class for Spanish after not taking it for a couple of years. There are lots of assignments, but they all helped me in the long run. Highly recommend taking her class especially if you're nervous about getting back into Spanish!

Professor Canavan was the sweetest professor I have had. She always tried to make class interesting and fun. Some projects felt a little extra and unnecessary but all in all a great class. Tests are not hard and she gives the option of dropping one.
She is really a good professor in teaching language, and she is full of enthusiasm. Plus she will give high grade if you really make effort on it.

she was ok. I wish we would have sat an actually gone through the material more thoroughly because we would learn something and move on so quickly that most of us just pretended we knew what was going on. She talks alot so my listening got a lot better. The textbook will be your lifeline.

Sweetest teacher ever!! She wants students to do well in her class and will give you extensions, help you with your homework. She has a great technique to help you learn and the program for the classroom is well laid out so you learn a great deal.

Highest class in Spanish, obviously it's supposed to be hard, but she's a generous grader. I would say she's more fitted for the lower level course because you are not going to learn a lot from her. Of course, she is a lovely, approachable person. But was her class worth my every single penny? Probably not. She's not horrible, just not fantastic.
One of the nicest teachers I've had. Very passionate about spanish, wants you to understand everything. Tests are easy, she's a fair grader. Recommend if you're looking for an easy grade.
She is the nicest woman on earth. so enthusiastic and passionate about spanish. very very easy class that is also very very enjoyable and engaging. i highly recommend any class with her.
Easy. Cool teacher. She is helpful and makes the classroom an easy going, fun environment

Great teacher! If you want to actually learn Spanish take this class! Yes there is a lot of homework but it helps you learn.  She also plans fun activities in class and gives fair tests.  If you participate and show interest she will see it.  Overall, amazing class and gifted teacher!

Just go to class and put in effort. The work is not hard but there is a good amount of work. But it doesn't matter how you do on the homework as long as you try you will get an A. She also is helpful. THe tests are not bad and their is one project.

Soooo much homework!!!  If you are a science/ engineer/math major... beware!  There is a TON of workbook homework, on top of that she assigns text book homework, then the worksheets she makes, and then there is an online homework site too... expect 5+ assignments per night...sucks for a bio major like me, but her tests are the practice tests

Monica is amazing. I was dreading taking spanish then i had my first class. If you dont get the homework on the supersite done on time she will extend the time for you or change your grade at the end. she really only cares if you complete the work. The class is amazing its incredibly interactive, but talking isnt required. Highly recommended prof!!

Canavan is awesome. She's so enthusiastic about her teaching and makes the class fun and interactive. If you did well in 101 or have a previous knowledge of some spanish it's an easy A..and even if you're struggling she'll make sure that you understand everything.

She gives an INSANE amount of homework. Homework will be posted on the Supersite but she won't tell you that she has assigned anything so it's easy to fall behind. Goes off on tangents in the middle of class. Doesn't know anything about being politically correct (atleast nothing about being PC the American way). Mocks people all the time.

Monica is great and she is very nice.  Will go the extra mile in class or out of class to help you.  Very excited about Spanish and teaching it.  102 is a little tougher but she makes it very easy to understand and do very well.  Always be sure to do the HW and online assignments and you will surely get an A.
Super awesome guy, take the class. One presentation, research project is a lot of reading but its worth it. Super interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: very enthusiastic and energetic lectures which are more recaps of the readings followed by class discussions. was expecting him to be a difficult grader but all you have to do is be engaged with the material and opinionated about the content, which isn't that hard given that there are multiple relevant contemporary case studies discussed each week.

Ethics of Food was actually really fun! We got to cook during one class. His lectures are discussion heavy and there is a good amount of reading assigned. He can be out of pocket, but it's not that bad. Good amount of group work too.

Only professor that I've looked forward to going to lectures to. Super funny and makes the material interesting to learn. You have to talk occasionally in his class, but I found myself engaging beyond just to get a participation grade. Would take again.

About 3-4 assignments as week, each having over 10 pages of reading and analyzing. Discussion boards, Perusall, random books, but uses it to fuel a discussion every class so you have to read it. Grades tough despite the class being required for NuPath. No technology in class, and the first philosophy class that you struggle to maintain an A in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I took Prof. Yelle for his Philosophy and Literature class but it wasn't available here.

Professor Yelle is very cool, funny and open. There is definitely a lot of reading and a good amount of writing, given it is a mix of philosophy and literature course, but it's super interesting and he gives great guidelines. Be ready to contribute in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Yelle is a G. He has very particular ideas about how assignments should be completed, but if you're willing to talk to him, he tends to be more forgiving in his grading. The discussions felt unfortunately prefabricated- he has a predetermined outcome for each conversation, regardless of whether students agree with the readings being discussed.
Really funny and interesting lectures, but a tough grader at times. Forgiving of late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures were always enjoyable, and Prof Yelle always made an effort to ensure discussions were inclusive. The topics we went over were interesting.
