He's not as tough a grader as other people here make him out to be, but be prepared to spend a good amount of time on the final paper.

If you are serious about philosophy, don't take his class. He has a strong tendency to avoid tough questions. He grades erratically and too harshly. Essays can only repeat his ideas rather than yours. And must be extremely straightforward, otherwise he will "not detailed enough" and give low marks for any rhetorical questions, irony, and intimation

Professor Yelle was one of the best professors I had. He was always welcoming and inclusive and completely unbiased. His classes were always engaging and funny and I made some amazing friends because of it. I don't know how anyone could leave a bad review, his classes are awesome. He's a harsh grader but college grades barely matter anyways.

Food Ethics with Ben was a MISTAKE. He was not an expert on the topic. Thankfully class discussions were typical, but he would still cut off meaningful thoughts to return to his poor slides. And assignment sheets were sloppy and not representative of how he graded.

If Ben graded his own materials like he graded student papers, he would fail BAD.
Nice teaching but tough grading

Prof Yelle is extremely likable and makes philosophy interesting with seminar-style lectures and no tests/quizzes. He's funny and cares about engaging his students. He is critical about the final project but not overly hard, I'd absolutely recommend taking him!

Has a genuine passion for making his class meaningful. No tests/quizzes. Almost all of your grade is comprised of writing assignments which he grades very harshly. You could follow all instructions and requirements for writing an essay and he will give you an 80 (coming from a decent writer). Generous with extensions
Really engaging class but tough grading for the final project

He is the most fair teacher I've ever had. You will walk away with exactly what you put into the class. He is a very tough grader, but if he sees you're trying he will cut you slack. Aside from that everything is 10/10. Great lectures. Very personable. Understanding with students. Just be ready to work and trust that you will be rewarded if you do.

I had for PHIL2143 (philosophy for children) not PHIL1185, Yelle was a great, energetic professor who fully engaged his students. You're not allowed to have your laptop out/open in class, which actually really helps focus, and I would love to take his class again.

Professor Yelle is one of the coolest professors out there! His classes are super interesting and engaging. He can be a tough grader on reading question assignments, but he gives good feedback. I loved his class and I encourage everyone to take PHIL 1101 with him.

His lectures are super engaging as he encourages everyone to play devil's advocate and analyze the reasoning behind their beliefs. He got me really interested in philosophy, a subject I was unsure of prior to taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ben made the classes enjoyable. However, he is an extremely tough and inconsistent grader and the feedback he gave was not helpful. If you want to succeed, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. Make him know you are interested in the class, regardless of if you are or are not. If you participate in class, you will succeed. If not, good luck mate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the toughest graders. You could go to office hours and spend a ton of hours on a single paper just to receive a B. The lectures themselves only require you to listen and sometimes contribute to the conversation. DO NOT take if you're expecting an A, unless you are an exceptional writer, because you won't get an A on your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: you don't have to put much time outside of class. the class had weekly discussion board posts, reading assignments, 2 papers, and one final paper. VERY TOUGH GRADER on papers. i do not recommend if you are a weak writer. however, he does give thorough and specific feedback to help you improve on future papers.
Good.

This class was excellent, and I would ABSOLUTELY take another class with him. I'll be going to office hours next semester just to talk to him even though I don't have his class. Be prepared to write, but I would definitely consider it manageable if you're a decent or strong writer.

More than anything, Benny is entertaining and endlessly fun. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Made lectures interesting. He is a tough grader but gives a lot of feedback so that you can improve on the next paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A good guy and a great lecturer, however he grades papers extremely unfairly, as if the people who are taking his class are doing so for a PHD in philosophy rather than NU Path credit. He also is insistent that you spend the money on the two books, despite his lectures come directly from them - turned out to be a waste of money in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are amazing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T LIKE WRITING ESSAYS. VERY VERY TOUGH GRADER. but an amazing professor. Would not take his class again because personally, i do not understand his grading.

Professor Yelle is overall a great professor, however his grading on essays was ridiculously hard and he gave almost no feedback. Any feedback that was given was very passive and borderline rude. The essay grading alone makes me not want to take another of his classes, but if you enjoy discussion based classes you will like this professor.

simply a king. very passionate about the subject matter and leads great discussions, I learned a lot about philosophy despite putting in not a lot of effort. you don't realllly have to do all the readings, maybe just skim to know important broad concepts but he leads the discussions. he is a pretty tough grader on papers, be very very thorough

Professor Yelle is very knowledgable about philosophy, and I enjoyed the lectures we had in class. He is quite a tough grader on papers, but if you go in to office hours for help with your arguments he is happy to help you out. I also recommend going to office hours after he grades your paper so you can get very specific advice on how to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Yelle is very knowledgable and class discussions are engaging. Readings are assigned, but not necessarily required because the material is gone over in class. A little bit of a tough grader on papers, but not a heavy workload. Professor Yelle changed my way of thinking, and inspired me to minor in Phil! Definitely take this class!!!

Professor Yelle is one of the best professors I've had. He's able to spark interesting conversation in a 30 person class of mostly first years. Lots of readings that make you learn and grow - this class turned me vegan. Grading isn't bad and I get by with skipping class a lot and not doing all readings. Take this class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Yelle is clearly passionate about this topic and class was absolutely very interesting. My review of him would've been a lot different if he didn't think of himself and his class as the main focal point in his students lives. most ppl are just taking this class for an elective, and he is an extremely harsh grader to a ridiculous point.

Professor Yelle is really good at explaining philosophical topics effectively and has introduced me to a lot of interesting technological concepts. However, he rarely gave feedback which made his grading style confusing at times (we also did not get any feedback for our final paper aside from a grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: extremely tough grader and comments on papers feel like insults
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Yelle is a fantastic professor. His lectures and discussions are incredibly engaging, making the class fun to be in. Regarding homework, there are some small assignments and readings are very important to do, but the workload is manageable. Writing is a big part of the grade also, but he is available for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: tough grader, difficult for international students to get a high grade if you don't spend enough time in reading and taking reading notes, especially for whose major is not in liberal arts,

Unlike other subjects, it takes a solid understanding of philosophy and morals to be a good teacher and prof Yelle is extremely qualified. His lectures hosted some of the most thought-provoking conversations I've ever heard & I feel I'm better off for taking his course. As long as you read the passages and take notes, you'll be fine. Amazing class.

His Technology & Human Values class is very interesting and he really captivates the classroom with his lectures. There are a few quizzes, he tells you when they'll be but you'll need to take notes every day if you want to do well on them. There are only 3 essays throughout the semester, but he is a very tough grader, go to office hours to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Excellent in class conversation. He is truly an amazing devils advocate which forces you to think through your ideas far more deeply
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Usually would hate the idea of any class with pop quizzes, but besides the fact that they're usually easy to see coming, you'll want to be at every class anyway and as long as you briefly look over the readings they're pretty easy. Professor Yelle is really an amazing, young professor who cares about his students and also makes you think.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Stand up guy. *Slow clap*. His lectures are super engaging and he delivers the content in a way that really makes you think. The setup is pretty much based on lectures and discussions and most of your grade is made up of papers (which I like). I would recommend meeting with him for each paper assignment because he gives excellent feedback!

Entertaining professor and gets really into his lectures. Pop quizzes are super easy. Nice guy who always helps out at his office hours. He's really picky with his essays though, will take off points for minor things.
He's a good guy but he is pretty inconsistent with his grading.

Most amazing teacher I ever had! Had class at 8 am but it was a pleasure to come, he makes everything very interesting, and the classes are just discussions around ethical concepts. All exams are take home, and as he gives great feedback it pushes us to give our best. Plus he gives extra credit if you wanna give a presentation. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! I took Intro to Philosophy with him and his lectures really made me think. The readings are always interesting and he always pushes you to be the best writer/thinker you can be! I would definitely take his class again.

I absolutely loved this class! He was amazing. He is very passionate about this subject and you can tell. He is NOT boring at all. No exams, just papers and a few pop quizzes. If you do the readings though they are really easy. Honestly best professor I have ever had. We talked after almost every class and I wish he could be my best friend lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super chill and caring. Gives credit just for writing your name on tests, I studied 3 hours for each of the 3 tests, and was heavily overstudied for them. You'll learn a bunch. Homework are the only hard thing just take your time and start them a week in advance

He was awesome! Cares a lot about his students and has very fair and clear grading criteria. He makes sure that there are opportunities to consult TAs or himself so that you know what's going on. Took the effort to learn almost everyone's name in our lecture, which is impressive for a DS prof. Def would take again.

Professer Yu is very caring towards his students and about the course content, and he wants to make sure you understand the content. Lectures aren't always engaging and attendance isn't mandatory, but there are opportunities to talk to TAs or the professor if questions come up. Homeworks are hard but he offers regular and late deadlines.

This teacher genuinely doesn't care to give every student an A. He simply just wants every student to get a solid grasp on what it takes to be a data scientist. Labs are easy and make up 20%, homework's are long but manageable, only 3. Theres a final project (26%) at the end that's very time consuming but everyone gets an A. quizzes are final 24%.

The HW in this class is HEAVY, but that's the same for every professor in the section. Deahan is very nice and understanding, extremely knowledgeable, and really wants his students to understand the material and succeed. I would absolutely take him again, he was fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Suuuuper caring guy. Attendance not mandatory, but he'll reach out to you if you haven't attended class to check in if things are okay. Lectures weren't the most engaging but he means the best for all students. Quizzes and homeworks were mostly straightforward with some challenging applications, but for the most part, professor yu is your guy.
Very caring professor who wants his students to do well. If you do all your work and put effort into the group project you should do well.

Really Nice Professor, genuinely has one of warmest vibes. The HW can be a lot, and some quiz things are a bit questionable, but overall, it's super easy to get an A in this class if you just put a little work in, and you know basic Python.

I appreciated how he learned students names who participated in class and went to office hours. Though attendance was not mandatory I recommend going! Very helpful and nice professor and a pretty easy class if you turn everything in.

Great guy bad teacher. Doesn't explain concepts fully and I found the homeworks to be significantly more difficult than the problems we did in class. The exams are on paper but simple with some coding and multiple choice and the final is a project. Overall and easy A class but didn't learn a lot.

Happy guy, poor teacher. Doesn't explain concepts well and has a quick pace. Labs are useless, don't aid learning at all. Quizzes are weirdly difficult and often extend past material covered in class. Homeworks, labs, and team project assignments are all easy. No opportunities for extra credit except for on the team project. Would not recommend.
He's just a happy guy, enjoyable class. Weirdly paced at times but pretty easy.

This professor was a nice guy, but his lectures were SLOW. There would be about 20 minutes of valuable information in each 1 hour and 40 min lecture. However, the class was insanely easy and he gave a ton of bonus points, so it was an easy A. I'm pretty sure this was his first time teaching, so maybe he will change things in the future.

10/10 Professor. I didn't expect my any ds professor to care but he have us alot of extra credit. Your final will be a project. Attendance is optional but u should def go. I took this during summer one so it was packed but it was doable. I do have some background coding knowledge but It was easy to understand his lectures.

Great Professor. Gives extra credit and is very caring. He gives surveys each class(for extra credit) and listens to them and adjust based on that. The labs and hw are the hardest part. Overall it's a hard class but he does everything in his power to teach and help u understand. Also plenty of gas ta's to help. Good prof.

This professor gives an amazing amount of extra credit, and this class is NOT exam-heavy. If you farm all of his extra credit, you are pretty much going to get a good grade in his class. Makes it clear he wants us to succeed. He literally employs 8 TAs so that we can reach out when we need help. Most classes only have 3 TAs max, but not this one.

Overall he was a decent professor. He often teaches material quickly, and does not always explain everything well. You can tell he cares about his students and wants them to succeed since gives numerous chances to earn extra credit points. He is reachable and encouraged students to talk to him with any questions about course material.

Prof Yu has been very accomodating with our needs, he actually changes teaching style and deadlines on the fly to respond to our feelings in his daily survey. Makes it clear that he wants us to succeed. Sometimes teaches too fast but will always be available outside of classtime to help out. He waives late penalties on submission, very considerate.

Prof. Yelin is very interesting. You can tell he is very passionate about languages and teaching, but his grading is often convoluted. He can also be passive-aggressive at times, correcting things that aren't mistakes. If you don't need to take this class, don't take it. If you need to, be prepared. Attendance matters, and it will be a small class.
professor gives lots of homework, however you do learn a lot. grading can be sometimes unclear

He is very passive aggressive in class and in grading. Definitely do not take if you have no prior knowledge of Portuguese or Spanish. I would avoid at all costs if possible. Multiple homework assignments before each class and quizzes/projects almost every week.

I would avoid taking this professor at all costs. I found him to be extremely passive-aggressive and not flexible. Grading felt nitpicky. Points were taken off for everything, including things that had nothing to do with language, such as margins or tiny technicalities. The class was unnecessarily stressful and not a supportive learning experience.

Profe is a good teacher and I learned a lot this semester. There is A LOT of homework, but it doesn't take super long and allows for more speaking time in class. Take this course if you want to learn Portuguese, not if you want a fun, chill elective. It is definitely helpful to have a basic understanding of Spanish before entering this class.

Prof. Yelin is very passionate about the Port language. The class had different methods of conveying information, and you will learn a lot about Brazil (and Portugal) and parts of its culture. The assignments were interesting, I enjoyed the films and short videos. I would focus on grammar review in class- it gets confusing with all the tenses.

He was fine. He is not even close to a native speaker. He gives A LOT of homework and grades pretty strict especially on unit tests. Everything new we learned was online and for homework so class didn't add much. He mixes different dialects of Portuguese, which is confusing because they have partially different words and conjugations/grammar.

Profe Yelin was the best! I had him for PORT 1101 and he was super easygoing and did his best to answer everyones questions and accomodate everyone. A lot of times language teachers can be really intimidating but he was great.

Profe Boris is such a great professor. He really cares about students learning a new language and therefore requires a decent amount of work. Work is very manageable if you are organized and do not let assignments stack up. Also, be ready to participate in class and do not miss classes because it will affect your grade badly.

As long as you participate and do all your work on time, you will be totally fine (I did not, which is why I got a B+). He encourages coming to office hours and talking in class, and if you do so, there is a high chance that he will be more forgiving with the rest of your grades. Homework can take a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Profe made class fun with his jokes here and there. Learning Portuguese was made simple with all the help we had by working with groups and having a small class size. You will get called on randomly, and make sure you are prepared with homework and the textbook.
He made basic Spanish impossible.

Profe is great. I've taken two classes with him and he obviously is very passionate about the material he teaches. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and so he will hold any conversation in Spanish so his students can practice. It is extremely helpful.
Literally loved Professor Yelin. Very good teacher and he makes class entertaining. Participation is VERY important. If you want a class that will teach you spanish skills take this one.

Profe Yelin is awesome! He structures the class as mostly group work and discussion- which really forces you to be engaged and learn. He's very accessible outside of class and responds to emails super quick. You just need to come in being ready to put in work. Overall he really cares about his students.

He is super generous with partial credit on exams. He provides a study guide that is very accurate. It is easy to do well if you put in genuine effort when studying. He is very kind an approachable, the HW is not very demanding. His lectures can be tangential, but he is very open to questions.

Pr. Chai is very kind and he's very approachable. His lectures are incredibly boring though. It was hard to stay awake. Exams are easy, half the questions are from homework and his study guides are good representation of whats on the exams. Show up, spend a couple days going over slides before exams and you'll be fine.

Clearly a good teacher, but a tough class at times due to organizational issues. It was his first time teaching capstone so he might get better. Nothings been graded for the past two months so i'm very uncertain about my final grade. Not a lot of feedback. He had us do peer review of each others work but didn't give us the peer review notes.

Professor Chai is one of the nicest teachers I've had and really tries his best to make his class doable for everyone. Potential test questions are posted before the test and he picks a few of them to ask on the actual test so studying guarantees a good grade. He also has very interesting anecdotes about random phenomena in class.

The study guide was very helpful for the Quiz, not as helpful for the midterm. The level of difficulty when comparing the quiz and midterm is exponentially different. Other students were stating he gets his test questions out of the textbook and the free response out of the study guide so keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Chai mid-semester changed the weight of an assignment he said was worth full points as long as our name was on the paper to something that needed to be right to get all the points for that assignment. I believe this is very unprofessional, he must respect his students work and follow through with what he promised before the assignment was due.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Chai is great!! Please take him for Microbiology. He is very knowledgable about his field. Also, the class is very doable if you keep up with his lectures, which are great! His quizzes are literally from the power point slides and he is a very fair grader! Strongly recommend him!!

Dr. Cheng is definitely not someone I would take the class with again. It was such a waste of time and money. I took the Fundamentals of Cloud Computing (CS 6620). Not actually related to cloud computing. Mostly virtualization with no hands-on. The professor has no experience at all. No Public Cloud hands-on. Even AWS or GCP or Azure. Never again.

I took CS5010 on San Jose campus, fall 2022. His lecture pace is friendly for beginners to Java. Tom's style is distinctly different from my past professors. He don't use PPT, but code through all concepts he wish to illustrate and explains those with great clarity. His exam is heavy. It distingushish average from the best. I enjoyed his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lecture is well-organized and includes essential practical tips for actual work coding.

Professor Tom Cheng does live coding in his lecture which is helpful, but on certain occasions he will jump around his codes too much which will leave you confused. The assignment given are horrendous and very hard to comprehend. The class is challenging because of the assignments! Get ready to camp on Google to get solutions
I feel he could have used more slides.
Super understanding and just a good person! Also really knowledgeable.

POLS1155: This class is very straightforward. He does a mix of lecture/discussion. Best parts of the class are the off-topic discussions. The lectures can sometimes be long and boring however. Assignments are relatively easy. He's very flexible/understanding.
He was a super understanding and fair professor. If you are to take an online course for political science take his. I've never had such an organized professor, nevermind being online. Great guy.

Professor Agatstein cares so much about his students, explains things clearly, gives relevant examples, is very understanding about giving extensions + grades kindly. He would have a class every couple of weeks dedicated to letting us access his knowledge + ask him about things going on in the world from an IR perspective. Best professor I've had.

Professor Agatstein is an intelligent, organized, and kind professor. Overall, if you are looking for a good, chill class with a Professor who knows his stuff, take his class!! He is excellent at considering each student's needs while being fair to the entire class. His specialty in humanitarian crises is fascinating.

He's super chill. The class was weekly essays, and the same went for the final project. He's a really fair grader and was super understanding. Definitely a great online course, and managed everything well.

Great professor! The classes are discussion-based, and he always makes sure to explain the material thoroughly. Provides study guides for exams and posts all lecture presentations, which is super helpful!

I have never rated a professor before, but I have to, for Dr. Agatstein was amazing. I loved his discussions, as they were always interesting and relevant. He doesn't force you to reply. All assignments are argumentative essays, which I love. He responds quickly and gives great constructive feedback. Great class to take for NU Path or for credit.
Difficult course but not that difficult if you put in the work. Prof. Jin is the goat
Very friendly and takes great care in making sure students understand the material.
I got cooked in both midterms but he is still the goat

If you attend lectures regularly and ask for help on homework questions, you will do well in Professor Jin's class. He is friendly and always willing to answer questions on Piazza or in person. Tests can be challenging, but final letter grades may be curved to compensate for that. Participation can also boost your grade. Overall, great professor!
The esteemed gentleman in question endeavours to take meticulous care that the entirety of one's comprehension be satisfactorily addressed.

This class in my opinion was amazing... Professor Jin is by far one of the best professors I've had - his passion with respect to theory makes learning enjoyable. I would recommend that if you do not enjoy proofs as much, potentially stay away from this class but overall Professor Jin makes it manageable and bearable. 10/10 if I could

Tests are fair and the grading was very fair in my experience. Lectures are dry but Prof Jin was a nice guy and would take all the time you need to understand things. I think this was his second semester teaching and from what I heard previously he really has gotten his stuff together and is great now. A lot of time on HW though. Would take again!

Dr. Y truly cares about her students. She opened her first lecture with jokes and immediately created a welcoming environment. You can tell she enjoys teaching and is willing to go into depth on any question you may have. She cares about your grade and that you understand her lectures, which can be heavy content. She will help you learn a lot!

If you like biology you'll enjoy her class. Exams aren't difficult (one dropped), and the poster project sounds scary, but it's actually easy and fun. She's very light-hearted and cares about her students. Main flaw is that the lectures are unorganized and not detailed. You need to be able to study and rely on yourself to learn exam material.

I love Dr. Y. Classes are definitely lecture-heavy, but she records them. And sometimes lecture won't be interesting, but lock in & you'll do fine on every exam. She has lots of resources and will always help you. + She clearly loves teaching.
4 exams, one of which is dropped; take-home quizzes (2 tries); sometimes extra credit + test corrections!

Dr Y is a sweetie! Her class is interesting and the poster project is a semester long effort and not bad at all. Her tests are a bit tricky, but not that heavily weighted. Her lectures are crucial for details on exams, so review daily because content builds up. Make sure you follow rubrics to get full credit on classwork grades and it's an easy A.

This class was interesting and Professor Y was very funny, but her teaching style was often hard to follow. There were a few exams and open note quizzes, but they weighed very lightly in terms of your grade. There were slideshows shown in class, but they weren't very helpful so make sure your attendance is good.

I thought Professor Yesilatay was really nice and caring of her students, but her lectures were often confusing. You have to attend class to know what will actually be on tests because the lecture slides are not helpful. There were few assignments, but they were all pretty lengthy. She is very understanding and lenient though!

Dr Y was an engaging lecturer and explained material clearly. Lecture heavy, so attending class was necessary since slides were not comprehensive and most content on quizzes/exams was only taught in class. Grade was determined by many small assignments. She gave detailed rubrics and lots of feedback. Exams were not weighted heavily and fairly easy.

I took A&P 2 with Professor Yesilaltay and I don't regret it at all. She's super caring and wants her students to succeed. There are 4 exams (lowest one gets dropped) and a final. She also allows for test corrections which gets added to your test grade. There's a lot of content but that's to be expected.

I had Dr.Yesilaltay for both A&P 1 and 2, she is amazing! It is a lecture heavy course but lectures are recorded so you can always go back and rewatch. There is test corrections after each exam and your lowest exam grade gets dropped. She is very enthusiastic about teaching and was an overall great professor! I would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she's awesome!! makes great analogies and answers questions well, and she's honest when she doesn't know an answer. lecture-heavy but she is funny and gives breaks so i've never found a lecture boring.

She is a very nice lady and cares a lot about what she is talking about. However the way she explains things is not straightforward at all and her lectures are very hard to follow. Luckily her exams are pretty easy, as long as you get the big concepts you'll be fine. Lectures are not recorded and slides are not helpful.

By far the best professor I have this semester! Definitely recommend if you want a professor who will bring enthusiasm and inspiration to both yours and her own work. Very intelligent individual. Love this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She makes stuff really detailed and deep more than what we are learning in class during the test. She also walks around so much during the test. I personally wouldn't take her class again since she not really teaching us anything, she just copy and pasting things from the text book that's not really related to A&P and not really teaching us things

Organized, learned a lot, fair exams, exam corrections, and she is really nice and answers all questions. We had online quizzes with multiple attempts and a page of notes for our exams. The lab is the hard part. Great professor and I got an A!

She rambles and goes off topic a lot during lectures but you can tell she's really passionate about her job. Slides are not helpful at all to study with so make sure to attend lectures to catch key points here and there she'll test you on. Amazing lady and so caring as a person. She tries and really wants her students to do well
Very charismatic personality, truly wants her students to succeed! Also very understanding, did well with explaining more difficult concepts whenever prompted.

take-home quizzes every week, poll ev for attendance, and exams that are completely fair/not too difficult, it is manageable to pass this daunting class. she is super sweet and answers emails so fast. if anything the lab was the hardest part and i mean its HARD, so time consuming for a 1 credit course but the lecture is more than fine honestly.

Dr. Y is the sweetest person ever. It is very feasible to get an A in this class. The tests only make up a small part of your grade and there are no curveballs. A lot of the grade is based on a poster project which she does not grade harshly. The lectures can feel long and monotonous, but that's really the only negative thing I can think of.

she is such a sweetheart and i absolutely loved this class. she truly cares about her students and i've maintained a relationship with her afterwards. if you can, take this class, especially if you're new to northeastern.

LOVE HER OMG. she has a funny personality and was very good at answering questions. she had 3 EC assignments and all exams were open note (hand written) and final was online. she also does corrections so not hard to pass her class.

Prof Ayce genuinely cares about her students and goes above and beyond to support their success. She's kind, and approachable, and provides helpful resources like exam corrections and others to help you. Her engaging teaching style makes class enjoyable. Having her for Anatomy 2 was amazing, and she made the challenging material fun!!!

I absolutely loved Dr. Y. She is so so kind and her course was interesting. She allowed us to write a paper for the final instead of a final exam, and she is very reasonable with grades. All exams had corrections as well. She really cares about your education and well-being, and I would take any class she offers just to have her again as my prof.

Dr. Yesilaltay really cares about her students and wants them to do well. If you go to class and do the assignments, you cannot get a bad grade. You can tell she really knows what she is talking about. She is very sweet, funny, and approachable. There was sometimes busy work but it did help boost your grade. She also offered test corrections.

The lectures are a bit hard to follow. She often goes on tangents that are unrelated and the slides are not very helpful in explaining the content. The test questions are often more detailed and difficult then the lecture slides or what is covered in class.  She does give extra credit which I really appreciated.

Literally nothing bad to say about her, impossible to get lower than an A in her class and would make up extra credit if you needed it. So funny and cared about all her students, her class was so easy and even if you failed the exams, they were barely worth anything, she also gave corrections. Wish I could take her forever.

Dr. Y is super nice and always there to help. If you have any questions she has no problem helping you and making sure you're all caught up. Super accommodating. I would take all my classes with her if I could.

Dr. Y is the best professor out there she is so kind and caring. She responds to emails quickly and is always willing to help. Her lectures are engaging and she genuinely cares about all of her students. She wants to see everyone succeed and engage with each other in class.

I LOVE DR Y!!!! She is both passionate about what she teaches and helping her students succeed. Some homework is time consuming and a bit difficult, but she is kind with grading and often moved due dates back to give us more time. Dr Y is also very fun. I was never bored in her class. Take her if you can!

My favorite professor at Northeastern! She made the content engaging, and I feel like I truly learned something from her class. She is very accessible outside of class and genuinely cares about her students. There is a poster project and a lot of reading, but everything is manageable and easy. Exams are done online and at home. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Y knows how to make class engaging. She is constantly coming up with little rhymes or songs to help you remember concepts. She is also the most caring professor I've ever had. She recognized me from her BIOL1000 session the semester prior and emailed me to check in on how I was doing. Genuinely the sweetest.

Prof Y was amazing! I took her cholesterol section of this class, she gives great lectures, gets to know everyone, barely any out-of-class work, and an easy grader. Loved her class, was never confused and found the material interesting. Highly recommend :)

Dr. Y is great! She's so caring about her students. The class has many articles and you can easily fall begin if you don't take notes. There are 2 exams and the final one. She gives opportunities for corrections for the exams. There are also quizzes taken only for completion grades. There's also a big project poster about an article of your choice.

Prof. Y is a great teacher and is extremely passionate about biology. She will take as much time as she needs to explain a topic if someone is confused. 2 exams and a final. Some long homework assignments here and there but its all very doable. She offers points back on exams, and for the quizzes, we got 2 attempts and discussed answers in class.
walking dub

Professor Y was all I could have hoped for in a biology teacher. She had weekly "figure facts" that were really straight forward from research papers we read in class, was extremely time consuming though. All tests and quizzes were online, quizzes had multiple attempts and there were test corrections. She was extremely caring and knew everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at Northeastern. Her lectures are always involving and interesting but doesn't pressure those who don't want to participate. All quizzes and tests are online, and she offers the ability to correct your mistakes to earn some of your points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Y was a joy of a professor. She really emphasized engagement within the class and tried to make everything as stress-free as possible. She wanted her students to enjoy lectures by making them interactive and was always accessible in case you had questions on anything. Exams and quizzes are all online and she provides corrections.

Professor Yesilaltay has been my favorite professor at Northeastern so far. She is so caring and understanding and just genuinely wants you to learn the material. Grades aren't really stressed, but trying to understand the material is. I was not even interested in cholesterol before taking her inquiries but I thoroughly enjoyed the class.

Prof Y is the nicest and actually teaches you. She is the best professor I have had at NEU. She cares about you and understands when something is difficult. She encourages asking questions and explains things well. The class is very project bases with two major exams. Most things have the opportunity to do corrections that can help your grade!

One of the best professors I've ever had. She's so sweet and really does want everyone to succeed, and lets you do corrections on all quizzes/exams to earn points back. Great at explaining concepts and super helpful if you have questions, I would highly recommend her class

Professor Yesilaltay is the type of professor who truly cares about you and wants you to succeed. I loved being in her class as she made lectures interesting. There were some online quizzes which were open note, and she did offer corrections on them. There were a couple midterm exams which she also allowed corrections for. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Yesilaltay is the most caring, helpful professor. She will help you if you need something, and make sure you get concepts, and her lectures are fun, collaborative, and not just the professor speaking to the students. There isn't a ton of reading, and if you pay attention and stay engaged during class you'll do good.

Dr Yesilaltay is an extremely knowledgeable and all around great professor. If you are taking inquiries, you want this teacher. She is understanding with grades, keeps lectures engaging and interesting, and cares about both what she teaches and her students. HW load is a bit lighter than other classes, if you pay attention its a pretty easy A.

Dr. Yesilaltay is an incredible professor who deeply cares about her students. The cholesterol class can be a little intimidating, but you learn so much more than that in a fun and inviting setting. I'd definitely take Bio Inquiries with her if you get the chance!
Nah don't take him for this class

from the moment you walk into class everything is about him. given his rich background and expertise, he can't teach even if his life depended on it. there is so much ego in the classroom and there is no other way to describe how futile this class was. definitely do NOT recommend the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is so much ego in the classroom.  It drips with his importance.

Naeem is incredibly well-versed in VC, and gives great lectures from an insider's perspective into the startup ecosystem in the Bay. Guest speakers were few but good. Take this class with a willingness to participate and soak up everything you learn. Be prepared for cold calls. Group project represents over 50% of class grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor I've ever had. He's certainly a bit of a hardass but he's got the track record to back it up. Goes above and beyond but can be difficult to please. Keeps you on your toes and your head on a swivel. Be accepting to learn. Overall 10/10 and I wish I could take every business class with him. This man is a wealth of knowledge.

I would highly recommend taking any class by Naeem! I absolutely loved his entrepreneurship class, and his lectures were engaging and interesting. His class is geared to prepare you for the entrepreneurship process, and it is very well structured. Naeem is an awesome professor who cares a lot about his students - take his class (buy his books)
Naeem may have cold caller, but was an amazing professor in the long run. He ingrained the entrepreneurial mindset into our heads.

I loved this course and Naeem! He is extremely passionate about entrepreneurship which made the course so much more enjoyable. It was a heavy course load and content heavy but it was so worth it. I learned so much from this course because of it. The group projects were fun and helped you learn the material.
An amazing guy would recommend that he actually cares a lot about students. I love him.

Great professor, one of my favorites at Northeastern. He taught Organizational Communication and actually made me interested in the topic. be ready to get called on because the class is very interactive and you have to do each reading to follow along w the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zaremba is my favorite professor I've had at Northeastern. He makes organizational communication, something that doesn't sound very interesting, fun to learn. Though he does cold call in his lectures, they're very engaging and funny. If you pay attention in class and follow the agenda, you will do well on the tests and in the course.

Took his Sports Media and Communication class for my senior year. I think it is safe to say this class was one of my favorites during my four years at Northeastern. At first, I was bummed out that it wasn't a class I could sleep through and had to participate in, but quickly realized just how much fun the class was. Take it. You will not regret it!
Took for Organizational Communication. Very tough grader. I found him to be condescending at times. Didn't do as well as I thought. Would not take another course with him again. Hurt my GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Zaremba is one of the best teachers i've had at NEU. I would look forward to his class everyday, it was super interactive with a lot of discussion (if you want to participate that is). The guy is hilarious and knows what he is talking about, tons of enthusiasm. He is super helpful and specific on what is going to be on each of his tests.

you have to be there participate an do the work, but he is clear about his expectations- he sends out an agenda for the next class before you have it so that you know exactly what you need to do. He really knows his stuff- as long as you are engaged and do your work you will do well and enjoy this class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Zaremba is a great teacher. He knows everything about the subject matter(after all, he wrote the book) and does everything he can to be sure that we understand it. The class isn't exactly difficult, but you do need to keep up with your work.
Greatest teacher I've ever had.  Be ready to work hard and throw yourself into the class, but you will get so much out of it! His class was an amazing experience.
The best teacher I've ever had. So helpful and great guy.
He is the man.  Only class I could ever pay attention in, and that says a lot considering it was org comm.  Always willing to help out.  If you can take one of his classes, do it.
One of my favorite Professors
One of the best professors I've ever had.  He literally wrote the book on Organizational Communications and Crisis Communications.  You are cheating yourself if you take at least one of his classes.

Zaremba is by far one of the best profs I've had in the 3 years I've been here. He isn't easy (some big projects, writing-intensive exams) but he makes things managable if you go to class, he explains everything very well and correlates with the book perfectly since he wrote it. I hope I can take another class with him before I graduate!

Fabulous professor, one of the best at Northeastern.  Wrote the book, so if you don't know it it's rather hard to argue your way through the material in terms of being right.  For a subject matter that I didn't even know was something people studied, he did an amazing job with clarifying the material in all accounts. TAKE HIM.
If Steve Buscemi taught an Organizational Communications class at Northeastern...

Zaremba has to be one of the best professors at NU. Any opportunity you have to take a course with him you should. You learn so much and he is so interesting to listen to. You will a lot but you won't mind it.
Zaremba was one of my favorite teachers. He made everything very clear and understandable. Its a hard class but his teaching style made it a ton better. I actually look forward to class.

I had him for org com and advanced and he has been one of my top 2 fav teachers. The class isnt super easy, but he teaches the materail so well that you walk away understanding. Theteests are essay and elabotrate but as long as you show up and do your work youll do fine.
Great Class, Great teacher, he wrote the book so he knows his stuff
I had him for Principles of Org. Comm. and he knows his stuff!  (he wrote the textbook!)  Very hard tests, but if you go to class and keep up with the reading, it makes them more managable.

Zaremba is an excellent professor. I took org comm and advanced org comm with him and learned a tremendous amount in both classes. His a tough teacher which is one of the things that make him so effective and good.

i have taken 3 classes with prof Z, and he is tough... but in a good way! he makes u think, and really learn what he is trying to teach you. he is by far my favorite prof so far, because he has taught me so much.
Graduating in May.  Business student.  Took one COM class... had Zaremba.  Ranks in the best 3 profs I have had at NU.
The man wrote the book.  He is very clear and good at what he does.  But yes, skim the material becuase you will be called on
can't be just another face in the crowd with this guy.  but he teaches right from the book and the material is simple.
if you read, and participate in class, you'll do fine. but trust me, you need to at least skim because he includes everyone in class discussions.

The GOAT. Attendance isn't mandatory and everything was online/ take home. This class IS a guaranteed A. Lectrues were a bit fast-paced, but he was happy to answer any questions that students had. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!!!

First time teaching so he was def learning how to teach the class. I enjoyed his lectures as he was passionate about the course, but a lot of people found it boring. Class was very easy with the take home tests.
His classes were lecture dense and not very engaging. However, everything in this course is take home, so it's not a hard class as long as you complete all the assignments online.

He's knowledgeable in his field, but his lectures can sometimes be repetitive and also fast-paced. Everything in the course was take-home (including midterm and final) so it's basically a guarenteed A in his class. As long as you complete all assignments, quizzes, and tests, you'll do good.
40% final 30% midterm but both are take home. No attendance required, which is sad bc only 10 people would show up. A bit backloaded but a fun class, good content and good professor. Fair grader.
Nan zhou is the goat. Easiest A.
more profs should be like nan

Everything in this class is take home, including both the midterm and final, so it is a pretty light class in terms of work. Prof. Zhou gives interesting lectures as well, so if you are interested in the material, going to class is nice. Attendance is not mandatory as well, so if you don't like the material, you dont have to show up

super easy class. all of the assignments are online and open note, no textbook required, and attendance isn't mandatory. econ is generally super boring imo but he does a pretty good job using engaging examples. def recommend if you need an easy econ credit
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: really easy A. all of the quizzes and tests are online (midterm/final). he is a nice guy and great teacher, he uses a lot of interesting examples to explain the concepts. however, because attendence wasnt mandtory no-one would show up to his lectures 3 weeks in.
Nan is so chill. Sometimes the take home quizzes and assignments were a bit tricky but nothing that couldn't be figured out. Cool dude and really is so lax. Would recommend
Easy A dont sleep on him

Such an easy A, don't ever go to class... take home midterm and final. All the homework's and quizzes are also online. The TA literally says it's impossible to get less than 80 on the assignments/midterm/final as long as you complete it, as well as impossible to get less than 50% on any problem even if you are completely wrong. Such an easy A.

reviews.comment: Easy A, take home midterm AND final, it's so free
Absolute Goat
Absolute gem of a Professor. Attendance isn't mandatory, all assignments including the Midterm and Final are administered online. Easy A for every freshman taking this course with him.
take it. surface level lectures and speech pattern that will put you to sleep. But trust me, take it.

She is awesome! Tough grader but if you work hard you'll see results. She gave some pop quizzes but grades improved the more we took. Grading based on attendance, homework, midterm, final, and a few interesting papers and performances. Would definitely recommend for ASL1101.

Laurie is a super sweet professor, she wants to see her students succeed. Even though she's deaf she is still so funny and easy to understand. I would 100% take it again and anyone who is looking to fill in their schedule with a fun class, I would recommend taking ASL with laurie.

Professor Achin genuinely cares about her students, is very helpful and passionate about teaching students ASL. There are outside-of-class assignments (events) to be aware of, that deadline will sneak up on you. Very interactive class with lots of practice and daily (but helpful) HW assignments. Excited to take ASL 2 with Professor Achin!

Very, very unclear in how the points are distributed. I spent 6 hours on an assignment that she stressed as very important, only for it to be 15 points. Then I blew through another assignment in 10 minutes that was worth 95 points. This doesn't really matter though because it's very easy to get full marks. Fun to learn and an interactive class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Very good prof highly recommend. The quizzes are very hard and if you do bad on them do not worry. Lab reports are easy and the labs are very helpful for learning. He has a lot of knowledge and wants you to participate so definitely participate.
Poor teaching
Wants you to do well...
Often provides interesting insights about circuits and their in real world.
Genuine goat. He has so much to teach you, if you actually engage the class, and he genuinely wants you to succeed. Best prof ive had so far.

Challenging but covers a niche subject rarely offered at colleges. Half the course focused on linear regulators, then jumped to various topics in the last month; combined with the project made things hard to follow, but talking with the prof helped clarify topics and HWs. Very lecture heavy too. Critique: late to post grades/solutions
Explained concepts poorly, poor presentations, was not approachable.

He's awesome. He would start out the class sharing his weekend stories, and they were always hilarious. He's super chill and caring; he takes grading seriously and will give you great feedback, so make sure to put effort into your assignments. Also, you don't know what grade you have until the end of the semester, which is a bit scary.

Prof. Block is great!! He has a great personality and really cares about his students. He gives plenty of time for writing assignments which makes them very manageable. He also helps his students to learn new ways to think about writing which was great!! Definitely take his class!!

Mr. Block is the perfect First Year Writing teacher; His assignments are very manageable and provide good learning to anyone looking to improve their writing. He respects your time and doesn't assign tough or unreasonable assignments. He constantly takes student feedback and actually constructs the rubrics to meet the needs of the students.

Dr. Block gave me a fantastic advanced writing experience. Dr. Block made the class incredibly fun and engaging. He clearly cares a lot about his students and loves teaching. There are only 3 major assignments during the semester and he gives you ample time to do each. If you need to take this class, I'd highly recommend Dr. Block

I love him. I'm not the best in English classes but I loved his class. He truly cares and asks you about your day every day. I feel like I learned a lot from his class. He gives you a score rather than a grade for your assignments, which I feel like made it easier to get an A. I'm really glad I had him as my first semester in college.
Great Prof, will take his higher level class!
Not friendly to everyone

Super easy class, and he is a very chill professor. It is really easy to get an A as long as you do all parts of each project (assignment itself, peer review, and personal reflection) -- there are four projects throughout the semester. He grades with rubrics and leaves thoughtful feedback about each assignment -- doesn't use Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is clear that he cares about his students. He takes time at the beginning of class to ask the students how they are doing. He doesn't use Canvas, so if you want to find out your projected grade you just have to ask. Super nice, very funny, and great feedback.

Super easy class, doesn't expect too much from his students (just do the work). Super easy to get an A (don't think he gives anything below a B). You will have 4 writing projects that are mostly topics of your choosing. Even if you hate/are bad at writing you could get perfect scores on all projects
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory. There are only 3-4 papers and peer reviews with each offering a unique writing style or thought process. Professor Block himself is relatable and keeps his lectures interesting despite the material. Unfortunately, he has extremely poor handwriting which makes notetaking a little difficult.
Block is very good at making a fun and interactive class environment. He gave us donuts in our last class together too.

He is very caring about his students and makes class interesting. He always starts class with a daily story and tries to really create a class "community" by inviting others to share their stories. I really felt connected to my classmates by the end. Can be tough grader but as long as you put effort into the assignment/follow feedback, you're fine.

Really loved taking his class. I never thought I'd say this about advanced writing in biz, but I wish the class was longer. He gave really great feedback on each writing assignment and is easy to reach via email or office hours for anything. If you try your best and make revisions often based on his feedback and the peer reviews, you'll do well.
Block tries to make this class and his assignments interesting. The class is based off of 4 main projects/papers and they're all interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Block was a great professor! Essays were actually fun to write (we got to choose our own topic within a theme). Besides writing our own essays, we also had to write many peer reviews. Very fun class! To get a good grade you really had to listen to the feedback from the professor and peer reviewers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Aaron is one of the best professors ever. He spends time at the beginning of class to take about your day which is nice. He cares about his students. Not too much work. You don't find out your grade until the end which is interesting. Super nice guy and funny. Take him if you can.

I really enjoyed Aaron's class. Started off every day with stories and he shared some of his own about weird weekends he had and stuff. Super casual class with not a lot of work, so make sure you do well on every assignment. He does use the full class time, though, but his lectures aren't at all boring and he's really funny.

He's really funny and honestly doesn't give that much work. Sometimes we spend half the class just talking. It's super interesting though, and he's not a tough grader, just make sure you fulfil the requirements and show effort. He loves it when people participate. Always takes attendance. If you want to take an easy and chill class, take his.

It really sucks because he genuinely cares a lot and wants everyone to succeed. But his lectures are all over the place, he'll make mistakes not only when doing example problems but on the exams itself, in which case he'll just omit the entire question usually. Diff eq is brutally difficult course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do the homework, he is very nice and there to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He is actually so sweet, I've taken him twice, those who rate him low honestly it might just be not their learning style. He is very organized and if you show up to class you will get SO much info on what tests or quizzes are on. He uses a lot of direct homework problems for quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: occasionally makes mistakes. exams are tough.

It's somewhat annoying that he doesn't use slides and writes everything on the whiteboard by hand, but he is ultra passionate about what he teaches and loves to answer questions if you're confused. I'm not going to lie and say he's the best professor in the math department, but he's better than the bottom half of math dept. professors.

Can def see how he's disliked. Very hit or miss in terms of lectures. Some are good, others are very disorganized. He'll spend most of the class on an example, make a couple mistakes and then decide to not ever go over that topic again. However, he is so easy to approach out side of class and is willing to help and set up up as many meeting as u ne

He's nice and cares about his students. His lectures could use some more organization; his quizzes can be poorly written; sometimes he takes a while to reply to emails; but he's very approachable and always willing to set up meetings if you can't make his office hours. Just show up with an effort to learn and you'll be good

Do not take this professor. You will not do well and he is completely inaccessible outside of the classroom. You spend hours and hours studying and his lectures are beyond useless. He also puts no review material or notes on Canvas so basically ChatGPT will be your professor. Just don't do it.

He runs himself in circles and often makes mistakes. He is very hard grader and uses very hard examples in class while learning the material. Would not recommended at all. He is a genuine guy just not a good teacher.
Would often make mistakes in class until someone points it out. The instructor is down to earth and takes a long time to respond to emails.
poor feedback, but funny instructor. There are likely better professors out there.

His classes are pretty useless they have zero structure to them whatsoever. Instead, answers questions regarding the homework problems. If there aren't questions, he will wait until there are questions and he will often make mistakes when doing examples. In addition, he doesn't post practice quizzes/tests and responds to emails many days after.
Instructor can be occasionally awkward and skips steps during lecture. The test material is insufficient compared to the difficulty of the exam.

It's disheartening to see a professor who genuinely cares about students fall short. He's easily one of the kindest professors I've had, but the cons outweigh the pros. He often comes in unprepared, skips steps in explanations, and gives difficult quizzes graded on just one or two questions. His test prep is poor, and the study guides are lacking.

Good professor. Weekly quizzes are based on homework, so doing the homework and showing up to class sets you up for an A. He's nice, learns names, and will give you points back if you think you were graded unfairly. Class isn't easy, but putting in the work is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Enthusiastic! He must have had little patience before, but made obvious effort to change. Kind & clearly wants to create positive experience for students. Always very patient with questions makes sure to be most helpful for everyone. 
Homeworks only had answers, no worked out solutions so hard to correct your mistakes without going to office hours.

this is the worst professor i've ever had in my entire life. he makes absolutely no sense. i hate the fact that I'm paying for this class. if northeastern wants to be a good school it should get decent professors. no one I have talked to has had anything good to say abt this guy
he is a very bad professor. take anyone but him. i have to go to other professors class or teach myself because he makes absolutely no sense.

Spends 30 or 40 minutes diving into a random problem that does not look like the homework or the test. Fragments the big picture so much that everything feels disconnected from each other.  Basically self taught in exam week.

This is a very bad professor. He spends an abnormal amount of time reviewing a single proof and never gives any examples. He also makes a lot of mistakes. You basically have to teach yourself the whole course.

Its been a week with this guy and I already am super confused. He is all over the place and spends 40 minutes asking if people have questions but he doesn't solve any problems. The homework is super hard because he doesn't do any example problems. Would not recommend.

he is a great guy but i did not like his teaching style at all. the homework is optional but if you do not do it you will fail the course. quizzes are pretty much taken from the textbook. exams are difficult. i would not recommend

This professor is terrible. Don't choose this professor. His emails are basically never answered, and the test and midterm exam will often be wrong, have to chase him after class to get the points back on the line, don't choose, otherwise the course is doomed. And he won't post any answers to any practice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hoffmann really cares about the students and the course. He'll make sure that you understand the content before moving on and stop for any questions to make sure that you understand the course. The course in general does move pretty quickly and the homeworks (although not mandatory) are really good for understanding the material.

Super awesome guy, makes funny jokes in class, cool references, keeps a very difficult class fun. that being said, he does NOT teach to the test. . The optional homework shouldn't be optional,  If your looking for a good grade, dont take his class, but if you want a solid understanding of calc 3, and dont care about your grade, hes a super fun prof

He's a caring professor but terrible at teaching. He spends class time just explaining the mathematical reasoning behind topics, confusing me, rather than giving us relevant examples. I don't feel as though he properly prepares us for the quizzes (which can be difficult). However, he is at least lenient with the grading and gives partial credit.

it's sad bc he's a good guy but a terrible professor. just should not be teaching calc 3 or any calc because i have yet to see him solve a problem in class without making a mistake, but he expects us to solve more difficult problems on quizzes. do NOT take him , at least for a summer class you will regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework is optional - definitely do ALL homework if you want to do well on quizzes. The weekly quizzes are very hard, but prepare you well for exams. Very nice professor, although disorganized.
A kind and enthusiastic teacher but don't know how to teach

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! He gives textbook problems for homework that do not prepare you for the difficulty of the quizzes. He had mistakes on the mid term review and the actual mid term exam itself (of which he showed up 5 min late). During class he makes mistakes constantly throughout the lecture and expect students to catch them.

Do not take a class with professor Hoffman. He spends large portions of the class answering useless questions and his explanations are often very unclear. He makes mistakes on the board at least 5 times per class and relies on students to point them out. He doesn't give quiz reviews and makes assessments much harder than the assigned homework.

The teacher is a horrendous with poor knowledge of teaching material, making mistakes and expecting a "heartfelt apology" to make students forgive him. He struggles to make calculus 3 feasible, especially during an accelerated summer semester. Quizzes and exams lack homework-related questions, making it difficult for students to learn the material.

I found Professor Hoffman's lectures to be well organized and cover everything, and he was good at answering questions. They had the perfect amount of deeper explanations of how things work in diff eq. for an otherwise mostly computational type math class. It seemed like really he wanted his students to understand the how and why of the topics.
he doesnt teach anything and expects the students to learn everything on their own. half the material on quizzes isn't covered in class careful

Really nice guy and he makes sure that you understand the material before continuing. He's friendly and will listen to anyone willing to talk to him. Quizzes every Thursday, lowest 2 are dropped. Study or they may spring up on you

I had Dr. Hoffman for diff eq. I don't really agree with the other posts saying he was a poor teacher or didn't care about students. He was always available outside of class, made an effort in class to help students understand the material, and overall was very friendly and had good lectures. I would recommend.
Not good. Let the class be hijacked by the same students asking useless questions every class. Went over some material WAY to slowly causing him to go over other material WAY to quickly.

Dr. Hoffman is an instructor that clearly cares about his students. He will stop at nothing to make sure that his student's understand the material if any questions are asked. That being said, often times this will lead to the pacing of the class grinding to a halt at times, leaving the material covered to be very surface level. Use the textbook!

He does seem like a nice person but MY GOD. No one is forcing you to be a professor. I had him for diff eq and the class is more or less entirely out of the textbook. There wasn't much info for quizzes and tests online so lecture attendance was mandatory. Also had no practice material for the second test. Mostly just felt like he didn't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was such a confusing professor. I struggled so much in class because his way of teaching is so confusing. My roommate has him for diff eq while I have Lupi, and I am definitely learning more. Aaron is not very clear, and while he is accessible outside of class, his explanations are very confusing. He does care about his students.

not the best teacher but the class is not too hard so if you attend lectures and do the hw, it should be fine. he's super sweet and cares a lot about his students and their comprehension, which I think is rare in a professor. very lecture heavy so if that is not your type of learning, don't take him.

Not a good professor. Repeats the most basic things twenty times without going over the complicated content anymore than one example. I did well in the class since I'm somewhat familiar with the topic, but if you are not take someone else.

Worst professor I've ever had. He is such a sweet guy, and it is clear he cares about his students. However, he cannot teach AT ALL. If anyone would ask questions his answer would confuse us more. We learned different things than other professors taught, and he went into depth on things we didn't need to. TAKE ANY OTHER PROFESSOR!!!

I will first start this off by saying I have taken Calc 3 two separate times, failing the first time with Garcia. This time I took it with Hoffman. He seriously cares about the input of everyone of his students and slows down the class for people to ask questions. He is a saint when it comes to giving relevant examples. I urge you to take Hoffman!

I had Professor Hoffman for an online semester. He doesn't use class time effectively and doesn't explain concepts super well. If you really don't care about the class and just want to get through, he won't be very tough on you, but if you want to fully understand the material, be prepared to teach yourself. Super nice guy, but a poor teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I had Professor Hoffman this semester online. He's really caring and supportive. Sometimes his lectures are not that organized and he might make mistakes, but he always tries to answer every single question and explain the concepts again if needed. He will always try to talk to you and figure out if something's not working for you in class.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Yes, he is sometimes a little disorganized, but he cares so deeply about the concepts and his students. Was really willing to work with me when I was in a tough spot. Also, I personally LOVE that he goes very deep into derivations and theory, his classes are not about rote memorization, thank god.

Hoffman is horrible at communication and organization. He often apologizes for making mistakes or not grading quizzes, but never does anything to make up for that. His philosophy seems to be that if you mess up, its your fault, never his. If you already understand the content, youll be fine, but if its your first time learning it, good luck.

He really cares about actually teaching not just getting though the class. Acknowledges the importance of getting a good grade so he often curves assessments and is constantly reaching out to provide extra help.

Hoffman was in love with teaching but spent far too much time on derivations and the theory. We spent the whole lecture deriving something and he would rush through one practice problem at the very end of class. I'm taking it with a different prof this semester and it's so much better. Friends who didn't drop have to retake it anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hoffman is very kind and willing to address questions in class and at office hrs. However, it was very hard to know what was expected of us on quizzes/tests because what he lectured in class didn't always match the textbook. This means a good deal of tutoring and txtbk reading was required. But he seemed passionate and I liked the class (Diff'l)

Hoffman doesn't ever seem to have a lesson plan. It's like he makes up examples on the fly and makes constant mistakes. He does care and he does seem to try in the moment, but doesn't teach well because of a seeming lack of preparation. If you go to him after class he is very helpful but he isn't good in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr Hoffman is a self-centered, arrogant, and ambitious instructor. He was over energetic to an extent that his lectures seemed very disorganized. He was not as familiar with the curriculum as other instructors. He was difficult to approach in person.

She was the second professor in this class, which should have just been one professor. She would rush through slide shows and often talk herself into circles when trying to explain a concept. Attendance does count as extra credit but the lectures are not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was our joint professor for PHTH 2210. She was unable to answer questions and  often speed through an entire lesson in 45 minutes when class is double that. She is also hard to reach outside of class.

the prof was really good at finding topics to allow students to understand the entire scope of using ds in healthcare. there are weekly assignments that can be completed in class and a final group project. though a bit difficult, I would really recommend this class as the prof is really flexible and understanding of students' time.

Interesting class section, I learned a lot in regard to health science data programming. There is a large semester-long group project and you get to choose the topic, which makes the project more interesting. Dr. Sathyanarayana was helpful and willing to assist with programming challenges and parts of the project.

Professor Sathyanarayana understood the challenges of being a beginner in coding and brought lots of practical applications to the teachings in DS 2000. I often found that our assignments had more than enough time, and class periods were used to meet with TAs or ask her any questions. So knowledgeable and positive, truly wants her students to learn

Assignments given in class didn't align with the corequisite course (DS2000); I had to seek help from TAs for almost every hw. Final project was very tedious, but she gave good feedback during early stages and was a relatively fair grader. She's willing to assist students outside of class, but overall it was too difficult for an entry level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: By far the best class I have taken! Professor Aarti shows so much care for her students. Her grading is very fair and the projects are incredibly useful for both resume and learning through supplemental resources. She is open to new ideas and has helped me get to a level of programming in the data science realm that I never knew I would achieve!

I wish this course had aligned more with the content from DS2000. I did however find it empowering to create my own research report as part of the final project, which was worth 70% of the overall course grade. Small assignments such as the programming challenges matter, so go to office hours and stay on top of them throughout the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the second class I took with Professor Daniels, and I enjoyed it just as much as I did the first one. He is very well-educated in his field and a great professor. His class is paper-based (6 throughout the semester), so if you enjoy writing, take him! The topics covered are interesting, and he is a great lecturer.
