Even on essays, she wants you to make mistakes and have typos.. if its too put together its an issue for her. I'd reccommend this class it'll be a light english class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Crain's very kind & genuinely wants you to succeed. She creates a safe space & encourages all her students to recite. No quizzes/exams, just 2 big essays and a presentation + short reading/homework after every class (
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wants all her students to succeed. Easy grader if you follow her instructions and attend class (strict on attendance).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very kind professor, cares about her students. Easy class and assignments, if you just do all the work you will get an A and also learn!!! overall recommend :)

Marks is genuinely the most understanding and caring person. Had a rough semester this year dealing with family issues and he accommodated me when I couldn't show up to class which was a lot of days. Class is very low stress and he emphasized this a lot. Just show up to class and do the work, and an A is guaranteed. Please take this man's class.

Super kind and supportive prof and easiest A ever, but sooo many completion grade assignments (at least 1 per week, usually 2 that were like paragraph responses). Attendance is mandatory but class was pretty interesting and he shows a lot of engaging videos and has lots of discussions. Lots of group work but in a chill way
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Best professor i've had at Northeastern for SURE. A must take. He cares and you learn things that you actually will use.
Good guy. He's super understanding. Class isn't super hard. A 2.0 in difficulty sounds about right.

Prof Adam was great. He kept class as entertaining as he could and would let us out early. All the quizzes were at home online and there was no final exam. Workload was light. He does take attendance but very understanding.

If you're taking PSYC1101, take it with Dr. Adams. Even with an 8am, I made it to almost every class. Attendance is basically a free 30% of your grade and exams are easy if you attend class. He is engaging and a great person. Homeworks are time consuming but easy and can be done without much thought.

Really great prof. Funny, engaging & cares about his students. Easy class to do well in even if you are not confident in math because he's so helpful and your grade is a result of attendance + homework + quizzes + exams. Couldn't recommend him enough.

Professor Adams was very good and helpful. Attendance is mandatory but for most classes you end up leaving early anyways. He cares about his students and understands that Statistics is a somewhat boring class and he tries to make it fun. He sounds scary when you read the syllabus, but he is super nice in person and just has a few expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you're taking considering taking Dr. Adams, you totally should! Although attendance is mandatory, it is literally impossible not to get an A in this class since it is worth 30% of your grade. I enjoyed going to his class at 8am since he is very engaging and knows the subject well. I promise, he is super approachable and an overall great prof!

Genuinely a great professor. News flash: lectures are not supposed to be for your entertainment. They are supposed to be informational and might be boring sometimes, but Dr. Adams does his best to include fun demonstrations and stories to help students understand the topics better. Exams were not hard. Loved this class as my 8am.

Why is attendance mandatory if we're going word for word of the slides? Like genuinely the entire class could be an email.... Also, he is not funny so idk why ppl are saying that. Idk tbh I'd take a different prof

Prof. Adams is a great teacher! He does cold call on people very often so be ready for that, but other than that, lectures feel pretty light and has weekly McGraw Hill reading assignments that could take some time.

Attendance is very mandatory but prof adams is a really funny guy so they were enjoyable. Exams were easy and based solely on his lectures so you have to pay attention in class, and there is no final. Only thing is there was a lot of Mcgraw Hill homework that took hours and wasn't even tested, but, it was graded on a completion scale and worth 20%
TAKE HIS CLASS!!! Adam's is the best.

Lecture time was not used efficiently, lots of rants. He also loves to cold call so you can even zone out during those rants. The McGraw assignments are long and annoying. His “humor” is also very elementary but if you're into middle school banter you'll love him.

Social psychology with Dr. Adams was hands down the best class I have taken at Northeastern. He is super understanding about late assignments as long as they are not regular and you show effort in class. He is clearly very passionate about his area of study and it comes across in lectures!
He's super flexible and open to correcting things. Also memorized everyone's names on the first day, never forgot one.

Best professor I've had at Northeastern, and I had this class in my 6th semester at this school. I've never had better attendance, despite this one being at 9:15 AM, because I wanted to go to class. He truly wants you to learn, and if you participate, engage, and show you want to learn the material, you'll do well. I would pick him again every time

There wasn't a lecture where Prof. Adam's didn't make the entire class laugh. He always kept things lighthearted and spoke to the class with engaging and often hilarious anecdotes and examples. There were quite a few exams but all multiple choice and very similar to homework questions. He sets up homework in a very helpful way. Definitely take him!

If you can't handle his mildly inappropriate jokes that he makes because we are all ADULTS... go back to middle school. His sense of humour and ability to connect to us makes this class so much easier to understand and way more bearable. Attendance is HUGE, and so is something called SPSS.
His lectures were a bit squirrely, but he was super chill and nice. I did good
Really fun lectures, gives interesting demonstrations, keeps lectures interesting, exams are cumulative but simple. Fun guy. Accommodating. Take him :p
easy class

Professor Adams was a very good teacher. He made lectures very entertaining and interactive. Attendance is worth 30% of the course which can significantly help your grade if you attend class. He is also very accommodating when it comes to making time outside office hours to meet if you have class and for time to makeup work if you miss exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Adams is pretty mean. Whenever his students are having difficulties due to his sloppy teaching style, he'll outwardly call them out and moan his frustrations when he's the one who can't teach effectively. His lectures are awfuland all over the place usually not including things that are on the hw. Dont listen to the other reviews. Dont take him.

Dr. Adams is a great professor! The class is graded more heavy on attendance, but his lectures are super interactive and engaging so I always look forward to his class before all my others. He is very knowledgable and passionate about psychology and you will learn a lot from him! We love Dr. Adams :) 
(Also hello Ms. Adams your son is amazing!!)

If you don't take Dr. Adams, you're missing out. One of the funniest, most real, understanding, and passionate professors (his enthusiasm is contagious). Lectures are always captivating- his in-class demonstrations are hilarious and help us retain information. Exams are cumulative, encouraging us to TRULY learn and remember the content. Take him!

Dr Adams was a great teacher, very funny, his lectures are very engaging. He makes the class fun. I took it at 9:15 and managed to not miss a single class since I would look forward to his lectures before the rest of my classes. His passion for the topics makes them easy to digest, and the interactiveness of his lectures helps absorb the material.

Dr. Adams is a great professor. Attendance is mandatory, but every lecture is captivating and worthwhile, so it is easy to want to show up to class. He was very helpful and understanding, I would definitely take a class with him again!

Dr. Adams is amazing. Great teacher and a great person. He is the best professor I've had at Northeastern so far. The lectures are engaging even when there is a lot of information to cover. He is always happy to answer questions. His tests are fair and based on the slides and the quizzes. There are no surprises.

Professor Adams is great he really understands how boring statistics is and wants his students to be engaged. He also really cares about student feedback and keeps trying to improve his class the longer he is here at Northeastern. The only thing I wish he did was round up grades or include extra credit. Attendance is also mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall a great prof. I went to every lecture and felt like most, if not all of them were worth my time. Statistics are boring, and he acknowledges that and does his best to make it engaging. Offered some extra credit opportunities, and made himself available to help every student in and out of class. Very kind and funny, would highly recommend :)

Despite his efforts, he contradicts himself by constantly forgetting to provide quizzes throughout the semester and then dropping a large quiz at the end to test us on everything. His jokes are, at times, inappropriate for a classroom setting. A lot of content is confusing. Half of the class failed the second quiz, so he had to provide a retake.
He is a super funny professor, and he makes it very easy to succeed in his class. If you're taking Intro Psych, definitely take his section!

Dr.Adams teaches with enthusiasm, and although attendance is mandatory, his sense of humor makes the class worth attending. Attendance is also 30% of your grade, and the homework is very similar to the questions on the exams given. He does cold call so be aware.

He is really great and engaging in class. It is clear he loves to teach and that he loves psychology which makes the course engaging. He is very patient and does not give a lot of work which is why it is important you take notes in class to stay up to date. His classes are funny and you feel welcome to participate.

Professor Adams manages to make every lecture engaging and  we laugh at least once a lecture. Attendance is 30%, important but a HUGE grade boost. Only 4 mcq exams throughout the semester but all of them are cumulative so this can sometimes pose as a challenge to study for but there is no final. Very easy A and a great understanding professor!

He is amazing, he cares about if you learn the information and there is tons of resources he provides if you dont. Very few quizes/tests that are not hard if you study for. The only thing graded a bit harsh is the SPSS assignments, but he only takes of minimal points to give feedback.
Such an entertaining time, attendance is required but the actual class makes it worth it.
Dr. Adams is awesome. He's super down to earth and is really passionate about psych. He's funny and is an engaging lecturer. I look forward to his class!

I have never written anything on Rate My Professor, but Prof Adams is amazing. I've never taken a psyc course before but, so far, he has made everything so easy to understand and very engaging. Highly, highly recommend. It is an earlier class for me, but I still manage to wake up because I know the class will be so interesting.

This was Professor Adams's first semester at Northeastern, so he was a bit disorganized as he was trying to get settled into the new environment. However, he is a very nice guy who cares deeply for his students' success, if you meet up with him during office hours he is more than willing to go above and beyond for you if you ask!

He's a nice guy and is very knowledgeable about math. However, the course was poorly managed. Lectures were not very helpful for homework purposes. I'll admit that stats is not easy to learn (at least for me), but if the class is disorganized and the lectures are rushed through, it is hard to absorb all this. It was just an OK sort of experience.

He can't clearly communicate to students and lecture slides are confusing. Homework's helpful, but you kinda have to reteach yourself everything since he speeds through lectures and doesn't emphasize important info. Also dropped a huge exam on us after realizing he forgot to test us basically the whole semester and just overcomplicated the course.
John Adams is a great professor and allows stats to be digestible and enjoyable

Lectures are VERY topical you need to figure out 80% of the project work outside class. I agree with another review here, the class needs to be reworked to better fit current industry standards. Spent too much time on good documentation practices instead of working on a technically challenging project that would actually be impressive on resumes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want a real software job, build real projects. This course makes you play pretend as a developer on a toy project that a single AI prompt can finish. The professor is obsessive about requirements that don't reflect actual industry standards. More docs than code and a waste of AI credits.

The class itself is very heavily project based, and one midterm. Bhutta is a good prof, but his lectures are a bit monotonous at times. A lot of things in the class require more practice on your own time, and the projects do take a while, so don't make the same mistake I did about procrastination. Overall, good prof but the course itself is hard.

It's like a speed run of OOD but in a more complicated language. Each homework assignment given feels like a whole project, and they're usually assigned with 6 hours of lectures to watch, 5+ readings, and two practice activities. It is difficult to balance with other responsibilities.

It's an insane amount of work if you have responsibilities outside of this class. It's nonsensical as to why so much work is assigned each week. I find myself constantly trying to finish the assignments rather than learning and absorbing the material. I'd try to avoid this class if you aren't good at time management.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a ton of work and not a lot of leniency. I understand that the Professor expects 20+ hours of time commitment per week for quality learning, but the EXTREMELY harsh grading criteria and little to no exceptions given make it very difficult for students with obligations outside of the class. If you have another class or worse, a job, then GL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had the pleasure of taking your CS3520 during Summer 2024. Throughout the course, I consistently attended TA office hours to deepen my understanding and improve my programming skills, and I greatly appreciated the support and guidance from the course staff. Course was both challenging and rewarding, significantly enhancing my proficiency in C++.

I took CS 4530 in spring 2024. Taking this class helped me develop strong programming, design, and development skills. Because of the final project I completed in this class I felt ready for graduate-level work and improved my proficiency in coding.

I truly enjoyed the C++ course, where I earned an A, and I'm currently in Software engineering class, where I expect to achieve the same. These courses have strengthened my programming and problem-solving skills, and I deeply appreciate the insights I've gained from his teaching.

It was a great semester. I genuinely learnt so much from this class, and it was one of my favorite CS classes. I have grown so much as a person having learnt the skills that I did in this class. I appreciated all of the lectures very much, so thank you Professor Bhutta for giving us such a wholistic view of software engineering.

Thank you so much for an amazing semester. It's been a blast learning with Professor Adeel and I can't believe how much I've learned in such a small period of time. This class has been so rewarding and I enjoyed a lot.

This professor and his entire team of TAs are so unhelpful. It's a summer class, so things move pretty quickly, so the support of TAs and the professor is critical. However, these TAs would answer every one of my questions with "I can't tell you that" or "You're going to have to figure that out yourself" which I found bizarre.
This professor gives a LOT of work.

At first I could not tell if I liked the guy or not, but eventually realized he was a good lecturer, very professional, and treated the students like adults. The class was very fair. Not really anything to complain about.

Excellent course. Lecture were insightful and rewarding. It was a great learning experience. Projects were not too difficult but I would recommend giving yourself time to work on them. Professor was very kind.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS, it's a waste of money time and effort. He makes rude jokes and makes the lecture very boring. You also don't really learn much from the lectures, I basically had to watch tutorials to self-teach myself.

Programming in C++ was a hard class with a lot of assignments. Despite this, the class was not horrible because the professor was a good lecturer and a great person. Attendance is taken once a week, but if you are sick or have any issue (even the smallest one), just email him and he will mark you excused. He is kind, understanding, and helpful.

Everything that you need to know for tests was done in lectures, no work outside of class except a weekly homework with group (if that), felt like I actually learned a lot in this class great prof would highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: good professor. really cares about what he's teaching, and wants his students to learn and understand. strict in class, makes up for it with bad dad jokes. class is mostly determined by midterms and final. covers a lot of content, from residential to commercial while including legal. test questions are also incredibly specific. review all slides

Adonis is an amazing professor. He cares about his students and genuinely wants them to do well. He can be strict sometimes, but it's because he cares. There were 2 20 question midterms and a 10 question final, non cumulative. Very interesting content and he definitely has been one of my favorite professors. Take this class if you can get a seat.

A great professor!! Super passionate about the class & really wants you to learn. The class is difficult, but if you put in the work it will be rewarding. Homework, case deliverables, & finance in practices are all groups assignments so make sure to get a good group at the beginning. There is midterm & final of 20 mc question & get a ref sheet.

One of the best profs at Northeastern. Cares about his students and subject matter a lot. Class isn't easy but nothing too bad and he makes expectations clear plus is very willing to help. He is also a very clear lecturer and goes to great lengths to make sure that everyone is on the same page.

Prof. Antoniades is a bit of a hardo in that he expects a lot out of his students, but if you put in the work you will be well rewarded. He's a great teacher and a super nice guy. All work is group work so make sure you know someone in your class/meet people early. Once you get used to his style this course is not too difficult and youll learn lots

Adonis is a very good teacher. He will challenge you, but the class is very rewarding if you put in the work. He emphasizes group work so taking this class with a friend would be smart. Tests are multiple choice on paper. Homework is also on paper. Overall, best professor I've had at Northeastern.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: All you have to do is show up to class. He does talk a lot, and it's very easy to get lost in what he's saying, but he did have interesting things to say, and he's clearly very passionate/experienced with the subject. Lots of field trips around the city, which were cool.
Basic intro to arch class, lots of fun field trips, some boring guest speakers, only graded on attendance
Attendance is mandatory but all he does it talk, super easy
fun and relaxed professor, very passionate about architecture!

Dan Adams is one of the most inspirational teachers Ive ever had. His lectures are interesting and his perspectives are really helpful in critiques. Hes also funny and laid back. I absolutely recommend taking his classes even if you dont plan on majoring in architecture.
Very inspirational and knowledgeable teacher in design tactics, highly recommend him for that course.  Get him to show you his projects in his firm, it is very interesting!
Wish he still taught the fundamentals studio.  Dan was amazing!
I had a great freshmen year studio experience with him. Wrote me a stunning recommendation letter for co-op. Very thankful for him.
Very good.

Talks like a machine gun but he's an interesting person. Make sure you don't put mulches in your design because he hates mulches. Very knowledgable and goes beyond the syllabus. The down side is that the class often finishes late, which is quite frustrating sometimes. Overall he's a great professor who has a good sense of humor.

He's very knowledgable, probably one of the best architecture professors in Northeastern University. But you will need to put in a lot of good and hard work to impress him. He also talks a lot so you'll always need to stay behind after class for at least an hour.

He's a good teacher who knows what he's talking about but he talks so much that you are sometimes forced to stay over an hour after class before he critiques you.  You'll learn the most from him but you're also assigned the most work.
Great professor, lots of fun, and very interesting. Assigns a lot of work and is quite tough with the grading but is very informative.

This studio teacher is such a jerk. The amount of work he assigns is nearly impossible to complete in the allotted time. He'll look at your work for 2 seconds, laugh in your face, and tell you that your work is hard to look at.

ling2350 was the hardest class i took last year. very tedious work which was cool in the end, but so time consuming. very niche in depth papers ~biweekly but u get very detailed feedback and peer editing time etc. hes very nice but so so boring i fell asleep. so knowledgable id recommend taking one of his classes at least onc
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Intro to Ling can be tedious--it is a hard subject to teach and a lot of other people are taking the class for credit and aren't very interested. For all other Ling classes, I have only good things to say about the course content and Dr. Cooper--caring, well-respected, accessible, provides thoughtful answers to questions, opportunity for extra cred

Prof. Cooper was great! He's very knowledgeable in linguistics and wants to share his love for the subject with his students. Our class (through the Explore Program) covered intro topics not in much detail but it was still interesting to learn about and I looked forward to our classes. Assignments are reasonable and fun to complete - I recommend!

Prof Cooper is the best intro linguistics prof one could ask for! Hes flexible, willing to help with homework, and overall a very reasonable, down-to-earth guy. The lectures are engaging and fun, and all quizzes/final are open book/note. Be prepared to dedicate a substantial amount of time to hw tho as there is a decent amount. Highly recommend!

Dr. Cooper is a nice guy, but he is extremely boring. His canvas is super clear but the material is tedious. He puts everything on canvas after class and all the assignments including the final, were take home.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was a fine professor but I was always incredibly bored in his class which made me want to skip lectures (rough cause he takes attendance for credit). His slides are very detailed, he puts absolutely everything on blackboard, and he gives meticulous feeback on homework assignments. If you show up to class you'll have no problem getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is a great professor. His lectures are always very detailed and well planned and his assignments have clear criteria and generous grading. I do have to say though that he tends to go very slowly, and he recaps the previous class every day, meaning class can sometimes get boring, especially in the beginning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is a really good professor. He is not a harsh grader and is super accessible outside of class (go to his office hours and you'll be sure to get answers to your questions!). My only complaint is that I found lectures could be a little boring, but that could just be due to me not loving the subject matter.

It's been a while since I took a class with him, but I needed to leave a review because Cooper is the GOAT. He is super knowledgeable, his lectures are always well thought-out and run smoothly, he's a really fair grader, accessible outside of class, and he's funny. People need to appreciate this prof more because he's the best in the department.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is a wonderful professor! He makes his material accessible and interesting, I always looked forward to class with him. He will pay attention to student feedback; helped make the class environment feel unified and provided a platform for everyone to participate.  Class with him was fun, insightful, and productive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper has the clearest lectures out of any professor I have ever had. You always know what you are learning, and each topic is clearly defined and discussed. he begins every lecture with a concise summary of the last class, and then he tells you what is on the agenda for the day. Not an exciting speaker, but he is still a good lecturer.

There are homework assignments about every week and a half.  In general they are pretty easy but kind of long.  There is a lot of extra credit so getting an A is fairly easy.  There was only 1 midterm and then the final so not too many tests.

He's relatively monotone when speaking but his powerpoints are great and he explains things really well. He's also very accessible and will quickly respond to a question sent through email with a clear and thorough explanation. The material can be difficult but the way the class is structured enables you to do well

Pretty disorganized prof. Rarely gives feedback for work which makes it difficult to understand how to do better. Not really helpful in communication. Waits until the last moment to post important info about projects. When she does post, its very short and lacks detail, unlike other profs. Doesn't seem like she really knows how to be a prof.

horrible professor. not only does she not actually teach anything (no lectures/ppts/videos/etc.), she is rude and dismissive over email. not once have i gotten a real and useful email response from her. i have never had a professor this bad at neu. if there's another prof available for digital marketing, take the other professor
rude and unhelpful

The class objectively is not that hard if you put typical effort in, but the prof is pretty unorganized and never provides clear criteria for grading. You will never be able to estimate what grade you will receive on a project.

Usually, if a professor has a low rating but is an online class I will still take it because how bad can it be? It's bad. For exams he gets rid of the modules 2 hours before the exam starts. He makes you take it on zoom and lockdown which takes 30 minutes to set up. Releases hws 2 days before there due.

As he did in the positive rating below, Nick makes spelling mistakes among the other irritating things he does to ruin simple material to get on your nerves. You may think I'm joking, but absolutely no one in the class found this course useful. I'm probably going to raise a complaint against this guy.

Honestly, I think Dedeke is over-hated. He puts in effort to make lectures less boring, even though the content itself is pretty dry. I didn't do great on the exams, but I still got an A thanks to the curve and tons of extra credit. Overall, if you have a group with at least 3 responsible guy and do the practice exams, dw you'll be fine.
Worst professor to take

The kind of professor who makes you want to join Squid games instead. Every lecture made me question what I'm doing at Northeastern. He must have some leverage on the admin, because it's hard to fathom how he is still employed.

One word - RUN!
Two words - RUN AWAY!
Three words - RUN AWAY QUICKLY!

oh no. just no. i scrolled through pinterest in class and participated like once a week and did fine but omg his lectures are so incredibly useless. he read directly off the slides and talked about nothing of substance. i dont understand why this is a required class for business ive never hated anything more.

SUPER boring lectures and just reads off slides. Tough grader and quizzes are hard due to content heaviness. Sit in the front and participate, will be more lenient with you. In general, not recommended, a boring subject, a boring teacher, and a tough grader. DQ at 7 AM was annoying, and readings often had nothing to do with lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly I don't get the hate? Some people say he's hard to understand-- I didn't encounter this problem. DQs due by 7am for most classes (like 5 question quiz based on reading, not hard). Random groups given in beginning of semester you have to complete occasional HWs with. Tests are hard because its content heavy MCQ + boring lectures & subject

Here's how you do well in this class: Sit in the front and participate. You will hear Dr. Nick clearly, he will learn your name, and he will give you opportunities to answer questions. You MUST pay attention. If you want to sit in the back and half-listen, don't expect to do well. Lectures are boring but it's up to you to make something of it.

Honestly, when I saw the reviews before the class, I thought they were an exaggeration, and I walked in with an open mind. But after taking the course, I can say the concerns were accurate. The exams are extremely brutal compared to what is covered in class, and the lectures are often unclear and difficult to follow. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

This class is a joke. I'm convinced that Nick himself has given the higher ratings because I'm convinced no one in my class even remotely liked this course. Terrible exams where students lose points for trick questions. He isn't clear when he speaks, and just makes it very difficult to learn anything. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you make an effort to participate, this class is a lot easier because he cares a lot about knowing people's name and group discussions. Good extra credit opportunities that helped bump my grades up, but lots of group assignments. Tests were hard but it's a lot of memorization of the slides and following his practice exam that he gives.

Despite it being an online class, deliverables are due every Wednesday and Saturday night, and assignments are locked to the Monday or Thursday before, respectively, only giving 3 days for every assignment, no matter the length. This becomes a huge issue in group projects in an asynchronous setting where your groupmates are unresponsive. Beware.

take someone else if you can. his class is very confusing and disorganized. studying for tests is torture. the midterm review videos and practice test had different answers (even though they were the same questions?). the group projects could be hell if you have a bad group. never responds to emails. don't expect him to help you at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is pretty tough with a large volume of work. He gives a lot of DQs, but they are easy and you do them at home. He has 2 big exams, but posts a detailed study guide and review slides. He is very passionate about the class and overall very sweet. He gave us 4 different extra credit opportunities. I recommend taking his afternoon sessions.

Guy always does his best, and his best is pretty good. I don't understand why his rating is so low, yeah his class is hard, but this is Northeastern, suck it up. He gives great out of classroom opportunities to meet high level business professionals (amazon, IBM, etc.) for extra credit.

Nick is a mumbler and a rambler, so not a great combo. Its so hard to understand him, and he just goes on and on about useless jargin. I really wish his slides were less packed, they are full with info that wont be relevant or on any exams. There is little to none real study material for the class, which makes studying and doing well on exams hard

He's not horrible but proceed with caution. He's very knowledgable and passionate about MIS. It's also clear he cares about his students. However, his canvas page is a mess, he makes diagnostic quizzes due at 7am, and his exams are brutal (gives a curve). If you take him, go in with your guns blazing, and he will respect the effort.

Absolutely do not recommend taking this class with this professor. Unclear rubrics for assignments with differing templates, lots of group projects which are hit or miss, and very harsh grading. Did not learn a lot either and the most disorganized class I've ever taken. This class stressed me out a lot and will stress you out too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dedeke is very nice and you can tell he's passionate about the topics and he often tells stories to try to enhance students' education. However lectures are super boring. Instructions for assignments are often confusing and vague and there are a number of group assignments throughout the semester that take much longer than they probably need to
Very difficult grader, barely curves, nobody gets an A in his class. Boring lectures he justs reads off slides and grades every single assignment difficult.

He didn't know the material he was teaching. Asked what topics we wanted to review, ignored them, read off endless slides, then said questions were "already covered." Put incorrect answer on a practice quiz, reused question with different correct answer on test, refused to give the point back. Said curve made up for HIS errors. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

His lectures are EXTREMELY boring and useless. He grades everything out of 3 and is super tough with the grading. His Canvas page is a mess and all the instructions for the group projects are poorly made. All his tests are in class, on paper, and the questions don't make sense. I don't know how he got hired by Northeastern. DO NOT TAKE DEDEKE!

While the lectures themselves weren't too bad, a lot of group projects were assigned and made up a good chunk of credit. They were also graded harshly, so you were out of luck if you had bad teammates. Professor Dedeke's exams were also very difficult, with multiple choice answers being very similar to each other.

Hands down the WORST professor I've ever had. Assignments/quizzes are not testing you for knowledge, but for nitpicky wording of questions. As a ESL student, I felt like I was reading for trick questions rather than the content. Also, theres a bunch of games you play as assignments. Absolutely useless assignments, I learned nothing in this class.

This guy gives homework quizzes that are due at 7 am, so sometimes I'd forget to do them and it affected my grade tremendously. Then he gives tests and each question is like "Which of the following is ____" and the answer choices are so similar that you don't even know what to answer. The tests are not a fair representation of what you know.

This professor has to be one of the most horrible professors I've ever encountered in my life. On the first day of class he introduced himself and he makes it seem like he's this very intelligent and caring man, but he just doesn't know how to teach. It's a disgrace that Northeastern even hired this guy. I didn't learn ANYTHING this semester.

LISTEN TO THE OTHER REVIEWS. Assignments are poorly written and riddled with typos. Exam and DQ questions are not well thought through, and even contradictory to class lectures. And don't bother asking for clarification, he will just tell you that he "went over it in class" in the most poorly written email you have ever read.
Horribly picky grader, will take points off for random things that were not specified in the instructions, and will never admit to being wrong if you meet with him.

Very tough professor. I took the online accelerated course for the summer and it was really difficulty because of his grading system. Group work is hell if you do not have a good group. Consistently takes off points off hw for minor things. good luck

At all costs do not take dedeke! He is one of the worst professors in d'amore-mckim. He never sets clear expectations but grades extremely tough. Never admits he's wrong, when frequently there is errors in exams and hw. Also its impossible for each person to get the same grade for group projects because of his grading method.

Nice, but is a very tough grader. His classes are very boring. He did some extra credit, but it does not really matter that much because he is a tough grader. Tests are very hard, and most assignments are group ones. His class was not the worst, but I would not recommend it.

Dedeke is one of the most passionate teachers I have had so far at Northeastern, his lectures were very engaging and interesting. Sure the class was hard but that's life, just read the textbook when you're confused. I must admit I got lucky since I got a great group, but he gave us a ton of extra credit opportunities anyways and a generous curve.
A very tough grader, but offers a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Heavy on group work.

Horrible. Incredibly unclear and disorganized. He puts the wrong answers on tests and quizzes frequently and is rude when you correct him. Spelling and grammar errors everywhere in his slides, tests, and course material. He may have a PhD but he is in no way capable of teaching a class at this level. Very rude to some people so get on his good side

So so so unnecessarily hard for an online class-- I was spending up to 18 hours a week on homework and notes and recorded lectures. Nice guy but compared to other classes this is like training to be a navy seal.

Extremely confusing and disorganized professor. Posts assignments and rubrics a day before they're due. Does not explain himself well, constantly speaks in circles. Exams depend on memorization of content and often contain topics that were never discussed. Group projects were assigned often, but they aren't too hard. Attendance is mandatory.

Professor Dedeke is nice and respectful to his students; however, he is a TOUGH GRADER. Every assignment is counted towards your grade, including DQs (case studies and you answer questions) and group projects. PARTICIPATION matters a lot, and I talk to every class by answering and asking good questions but I still get a 9/10.

Be ready to take notes. Very lecture intensive, read up to 300 slides per exam, 2 exams in total. His tests are very easy, providing the perfect review slide and practice exam to get 95+. He curves the class if everyone performs poorly, he doesn't deserve all these negative comments. Many group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Passionate professor but the material is sometimes a decade out of date. Not understanding of student issues, poor communicator, and failed to learn several students names weeks into the course. Only lecture material which are not relevant to the exams. Materials riddled with grammar errors & all assignments group based - so you need a good group.

Terrible professor, showed up late constantly, and didn't understand the subject material. Clearly passionate about the subject but poor at teaching. He doesn't teach well and constantly has test answers that are wrong and incorrect, meaning students have to correct him. Avoid this class at all costs it's the only class he teaches and it's bad.
Doesn't deserve the hate he gets - he gives good lectures and helpful materials. Class is hard but fair for the most part. Grading is very meticulous and every point counts.

I can see why he is rated so low but he really isnt that bad. Keep up with weekly synopsis videos and DQ quizes. He splits the grading up into a bunch of different categories which is much better than having 80% of your grade based off tests like in most classes.
Dedeke is a nice person but a horrible teacher. The slides are very confusing and the tests are very hard. He was not able to provide an explanation as to why the answer on the test was correct.

Teaches from powerpoint slides which are not well organized and doesn't explain concepts that well. Exams are similar to the homework. Many group assignments and if you and you're group don't know what you're doing you're screwed. He is nice and a funny guy

prof dedeke is super understanding. his lectures are quite long, but he gives us breaks in between. his exams are very similar to the study guide, but he changes a few words so it trips you up. the rest of the class is group project-based - if you don't have a good group, you're done for. he is very dedicated; he writes his own materials for class.

Very kind and funny professor, truly cares about his students. Gives a break in the middle of class each day and you will usually get out a few minutes early. One thing though is that all of the assignments amount to 100 points total, so every point counts in this class. Can be a harsh grader. Definitely have to work for a good grade.

He cares about his students, that's very clear. Terrible teacher. It's hard to understand him, his exam questions are often very difficult to interpret because they are in borderline broken english. The course is VERY outdated, and although he tries to teach excel through the course, it is so abundantly clear he doesn't know how to use it.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR! He was unclear in his expectations and would change them after students asked questions. He was extremely rude and changed grades after students corrected him for mistakes. Though his instructions would say to give "at least two examples," he was upset that people only gave two examples rather than more, which he expected.
worst.

Class is entirely lecture. Don't recommend taking this class at 8am. The professor has a funny personality and occasionally tells anecdotes. I found the course intellectually challenging but not extremely difficult nor easy either. One big thing to note is that he has quizzes at least once a week that are due at 7am so be sure to not miss those!

Lectures are not engaging, which caused me to zone off a lot. I studied last minute for both of the big exams, which I probably could have avoided. The study guides are very helpful- some of the questions on the test are exact repeats or are very similar. He is also a tough grader so make sure to go above and beyond on the group projects!

Terribly disorganized. He constantly changes lecture slides and homeworks, even with the deadline in a few days. My group was backstabbed by starting early on a project when he changed the assignment's raw data two days before it was due. When we asked him about the points lost, he basically said "be glad I didn't give you a zero".
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor to teach this class. you cannot hear this professor at all ... mumbles (i.e. you can't tell when he calls on you) ... slides are disorganized ... on the test, the choices he shows you for a question are different from the choices i got on a test ... can't explain why an answers wrong like idk how i'm supposed to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 26% of the grade are short quizzes that take around 20 minutes to read and do, each worth 2% of the grade. Participation is very important (10%) and you must actively participate to get a high grade. Tests and projects are easy if you know your computers but if not it can be difficult. Overall not a bad teacher for a remote class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dedeke is a really kind professor, and cares a lot about his students. He goes out of his way to talk to every single person in the class, even while virtual. Overall if you pay attention in class it is not that hard, but hw and tests are specific to exactly what he says, and you cant google the answers. I enjoyed the class!

Lots of short 2% tests throughout the course that are really time-consuming and annoying. The tests are pretty difficult and participation is important. I think my main issue with Dedeke was that he's not clear about what he wants. Seems like he doesn't understand what he tries to teach. The class itself is not that hard but he makes it difficult.

Don't understand all the hate he gets on here. He's a super nice guy who is very passionate about what he teaches. Although his lectures and slides were a bit disorganized they were always understandable. Tests are pretty easy as long as you do the study guide, which is similar. Only annoying thing is many short take home tests for 2% of grade each

Professor Dedeke is genuinely a good and enthusiastic person but his teaching method is terrible. His midterm tests are tricky, if you want to score high on them you must memorize the study guide and sample test. I think it is unfair and ineffective. Also, the DQ quizes are tricky in wording and one mistake is worth a lot.

Gives Excel assignments, but doesn't know how to do a Vlookup. Goes over test answers and cant explain why one answer is right and one answer is wrong. Material is outdated. Textbook is free, but you are tested on his slides which are not organized at all.

Nice guy, and relatively easy workload. Tests are just repeats of the study guides, but he changes the words and answers around almost to try to trick students. Also he seems to be unaware of the world around him. Needs a time keeper in class to tell him how much time is left. Will mark you absent if you are not in the room when he's taking role

This class is about modern technology (think hard drives, cloud computing). The problem is 2 things 1) he is teaching it as if it were a decade ago and 2) the guy is clueless and ambiguous. Sole reason why I wouldn't major is MIS. This has been the worst professor I've had at Northeastern. Easy to get a B, impossible to get an A.

Terrible teacher! Unable to understand what's going on during the lecture through all his random mumbling and rants. Disrespectful towards students when they bring up info from the slides that contradict test answers. Half his powerpoint slides used during class are blank. Tests are similar to the study guide but meant to confuse you! DO NOT TAKE!!

Dedeke is a great person and is excited about how we can use MIS to impress coworkers and co-op interviewees. It is a subject hard to understand, but he made it doable. He encourages participation in the classroom and his exams are multiple choice.

Prof Dedeke's class was a joke. Very short, easy take-home "diagnostic quizzes" account for a quarter of your grade, and the tests are very similar to the practice test he provides for studying. If you're serious about learning MIS, avoid Dedeke, but otherwise it's an easy class

Worst teacher I have ever had. I didn't hear more than 5 words every lecture from all the mumbling on random things that were irrelevant to the class. terrible professor and extremely unfair grader, he doesn't even explain any of the assignments EVER BRO!!!!

Dedeke is definitely a Computer Science professor trying to teach business students. He assumes you know things that there is no reason for you to know. SAVE this class for later in college. It may be business core, but you learning nothing. Case analyses are HARD, he is not clear with what he wants. No final, no textbook.
Professor Dedeke doesn't provide any clarification on any topics. When you ask a question in class related to the material, 910 the answer is 'I don't know'
no! please no! do not take his class, thats too awful

He goes about as if he knows what he is talking about and when a student asks a question, he struggles to answer sometimes even answering  I don't know. Unclear as to what he wants and is unwilling to take the time to clarify. When you push for clarification he disregards you and talks down to you. Quite a rude and frustrating teacher

He's really good! I will reccomand him. His class is super funny and he is a easygrader! You can easily get an A just attending his classes. He loves getting e-mail so if you don't understand anything just send him an e-mail and you will recive a better partecipation grade. His class was helpful and he is a very good professor!
This guy is the worst professor I've had so far in my college career
Worst instructor ever. Unclear what he wants all the time. AVOID!!!
bad prof. He said I am gonna receive an average grade, but gave me a C in the end. He seems to be helpful, but not truly.

Honestly, he was a very nice person and really enjoys what he's teaching, but he's unclear about what he wants, and grades harshly if you didn't do an assignment exactly how he wanted.  Nice guy, but his grading is ridiculous.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. I did not learn anything in the class and the work was useless and tedious. He is an unfair grader and does not want to help his students i.e. he NEVER answers ANY question with a straight answer. Do not take this course whatever you do.

Professor Dedeke is one of the worst professors I have had the misfortune of having. He has ridiculously high expectations for case studies that are on fairly simple concepts. He asks you to make the process extremely complicated by forcing you to segment your answers into strange tables that make it hard to explain your thougts correctly.
Extremely boring... grades very harsh and his lectures are straight from his powerpoints... he even gave points off on a yes or no OPINION question (Do you think...yes or no)

Honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. Rambles all class and the information he goes over and cases we have little to do with what you are tested on. Grades really harshly and all cases are really repetitive.

He's hard to follow in lectures. When you ask him to clarify something he never really gives you an answer, he sort of babbles for a little bit and then moves on. You never know what he's looking for on homework or the tests, he wants to to say exactly what he was looking for. No final if missed 2 or less classes. Avoid him if possible!

He was a decent teacher. I didn't mind his lectures, but the his grading on the cases was pretty tough and they were pretty hard. His tests were okay, and he does curve. Participation was a big deal. I ended up getting an A, but it was really hard to do; I ended up writing a final case that was over 20 pages long to get it.

It's not only his teaching that's bad but the course is awful and useless. The work that he assigns is in such detail that makes it unfair and the final assignment is the worst thing ever. I did well in the class but still hate it. His tests are easy but his classes are boringggggg. Don't take him. He's awful

As a person, Dedeke is the man is obviously really nice and understanding. But as a teacher, his grading policies are a little weird and tough to understand. That's what made it hard for me to love this class.

This is one confusing class. I am usually an A/A- student, and found I could only get a B+. He is not the worst teacher, but it is very difficult to know what to study for the tests and what to put into the cases. He refuses to discuss grades or argue with students, even if it is he who has made the error. Attendance mandatory. No final.
Great prof. If you got to classes and participate this class is a very easy A.

Attendance and participation count for ALOT of your grade. 6 out of 8 hmwk assignments are mandatory. there are two tests. If you have PERFECT attendance, the final is optional. Test are extremely hard but his curves are ridiculous. class is long and dull but his dry jokes are meant to keep you attentive. pay attention and you'll do fine.

Overall, I had a great experience with Professor  Dr Akaiso His teaching was clear, engaging, and very helpful in understanding the fundamentals of project management. I appreciate his dedication and support throughout the course. Highly recommend!

Professor Darlington's insightful lectures and engaging teaching style have greatly enhanced my understanding and appreciation of the subject matter. The guidance on projects and the real-world applications provided in your classes have been invaluable in preparing me for my career.

Professor Akaiso is very responsive and is ready to answer your queries in no time. He is very helpful and supportive. I took more than one course with him (I guess 4) and I was really happy with his teaching style. I truly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Awesome learning experience of all business analytics courses.
Awesome teach, never fails to make the class engaging. Can be tough at times but always leaves room for improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVED Professor Akbari. He's a great guy, great sense of humor, and he's very chill. He wants his students to do well and is very easy to talk to. Definitely recommend taking him for advanced writing.

Extremely verbose guy to the point that assignments are difficult to parse through to figure out what he actually wants from you. Only 4 assignments for the whole semester, 2 of which are kind of useless. Very slow grader with relatively inconsistent feedback, but easy A if you follow the rubric and scattered instructions in his lengthy documents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid teacher & good guy, class is very politically polarizing which is annoying. Show up to class and you'll do fine.

I enjoyed Akbari. He's passionate and enjoys talking about currents events. He loves to laugh at his own jokes (which usually aren't funny), but overall I really don't have much to complain about. If you're a strong writer this class will be very easy, but he will also try to push you to get better. The four major essays determine the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely good feedback on your writing. You only get feedback once a paper is submitted. Professor is extremely kind and caring, always available to chat.

Tom is a great professor who really cares about his students. The class was not easy, but he explained our goals for each unit well and allowed us to structure our work how we saw fit. This is the only English class I can say I enjoyed. Thank you, Tom!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hate writing in general, but he's the reason why I still show up to class and want to do my best. He's an overall good person and professor. Ask for feedback and you'll get it, it's a small class anyways. He remembers the littlest things you say, so he remembers you and it makes me feel I am cared for. Nice grader as long as you put some effort.
He is the BEST! His assignments are hard yet interesting and he is very inspiring and caring, but you need to work hard to get a good grade.

Just the absolute best. I've never had a professor that's so engaging, funny, down to earth, and smart all at the same time. You'd be hard pressed to find another professor who teaches a mandatory class (First-Year Writing) with the same enthusiasm. Please participate though, he really values everyone's input, and deserves all your attention.

"How did Tom Akbari treat his students during COVID-19?" Absolutely hands down the best professor I've seen across multiple universities. Helped students move with his own personal van when everyone was kicked off-campus housing, sent emails immediately asking about personal situations and whether they needed help or aid.
