reviews.comment: This professor was intimidated by actual writing in the sciences. He had no clue about basic scientific literature, and clearly needs to become more updated in the field. I would avoid taking at all costs, this class will make you a worse writer
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I LOVE Tom! He is such a good professor and hilarious. I love when he makes a "dad" jokes and is the only one laughing. Seriously though, he is a pretty chill guy and is super nice. Take him!

I'm having a genuinely great time in his class. He gives a lot of reading and there's only a few papers, but if the class didn't get to all of the reading or isn't satisfied with drafts, he's good about giving more time. Cares more about the craft than running with the syllabus. Plus he's really nice, an I personally like his lame jokes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Don't be afraid if you get 5 hours of homework in one weekend. Deadlines for papers are reasonable for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: take him he's cool

Relies heavily on peer reviews and doesn't give his own feedback on rough drafts before final papers are due. Only grades final papers (only feedback you get is after final grade) & grades as if he told you what you had done wrong & you didn't fix it. Feedback & instruction is lengthy, sometimes hard to understand.  10/10 would suggest dif prof.
he clearly failed at being a writer and now thinks his adjunct professor elective classes are doctoral symposiums on literature.

Thinks everything he says is the funniest thing in the world. Also tries to sound like the smartest person ever. Feedback on papers is hard to understand, given you don't know many of the words he uses. Overall,  class is decent, lots of discussion, no busy work.

Akbari definitely gives good feedback on papers, and they're pretty easy. However, many of the classes we spent entirely peer editing ordiscussing our paper ideas with the class, which was useless. Take advanced writing in the disciplines online andsave yourslef the time.

On the first day of class, Akbari spent the allotted 100 min going the syllabus. He comes to class prepared only to talk about a few topics and refuses to lecture; he relies on the class for discussion, but when we try to bring up slightly more intelligent topics he just stares and continues talking about his shallow topics of choice. Bad prof.

Mediocre Professor. Doesn't really teach anything to help your writing get beyond high school level, but he could be worse. His lectures are useless, but when he gives individual attention to a paper, he sometimes genuinely surprises me with his stellar advice. The best part is that he thinks he's hilarious, doesn't notice silence after his jokes.

I took Advanced Writing in Literature with Tom Akbari. His lectures are repetitive, he refuses to clarify anything, and is very close-minded despite his lip service to open-mindedness. Absolutely do not take a class with him.

He has the worst grading policies, essays are 1000 words long minus the semi final essay which was 2500 words. 5 essays in all. no final but very boring in class. Take this class online if you can. English 302 aka Advanced Writing for the Disciplines
He is a great guy who seems to want to help you learn the material. Sometimes he isnt the greatest for advice but still a great prof.
Funny in class, cares about students, expects a lot from them in class and on writing projects. Really good.

akbari is one of those teachers who seems nice enough, but does not know how to give you any feedback/help on any of the work you've done. he does not follow a comprehensible way of grading papers, so you end up getting docked for random things. overall, he's an alright person, but not a great teacher. look for someone else if you absolutely can.

He is the worst lecturer I have come across in Northeastern University. His subject is so abstract, he tried to teach everything but nothing at all. I took his subject last year and let me tell you, it was a roller coaster. No concrete instructions, exam patterns, probably the only professor who has used Whatsapp. Take other course instructors!!

The Professor doesn't have knowledge on the subject and so does the field. 

The projects he is choosing are so low level and teaches full of mathematics and makes class sleepy at times also and doesn't have knowledge or skills on python.

If you ask for any doubts he will just say I'll get back to you.

1. Zero knowledge about data science.

2. Teaches core concepts by learning  from youtube and medium articles(He can share those to students instead)

3. Not even familiar with DSEM basic concepts, but teaches you full mathematics, doesn't even know  python libraries that are used for data science.
Professor is friendly and keeps the class interesting and interactive

ORGB is the closest thing you'll get to a "waste of time"

and on top of that you are graded based off of .......... I don't even know, truly. Prof. zeynep does not follow the grading criteria. 

It feels like she assigns you a grade, and then writes comments to make the grade make sense. 

Try to get another section if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: ORGB alone is a pointless class, and with prof. zeynep I received a low grade for no reason. ORGB is basic and very easy to understand so prof feels the need to grade harshly on tests + short papers (usually about our co-op experience...so much talking about our co-op). The class is super repetitive and basic, avoid and take a diff section.

Would not recommend her for ORGB 3201. She grades off her own criteria which isn't explained in the assignments, and grades way harder than she should for this BS of a class. Boring lectures, just discuss the same old BS about work environment blah blah blah. Would recommend a different prof if possible.

GREAT PROFESSOR!!! She practices what she preaches in lectures, and you can tell how passionate/knowledgeable she is about the subject every class. There are a couple short essays and two exams, all of which feel very doable and fair as long as you pay attention in class. TLDR, super accessible, interesting, and human professor. would take again.

She is a good professor! Very caring, listens to students suggestions and lectures are not that heavy. There are no exams, but some group projects. She is always encouraging us to engage and network with different people in our class, which is nice. There are a few homeworks, nothing crazy.

She is knowledgeable, caring, accessible, and understanding. Attendance is not mandatory but is included in the class participation grade. And a lot of the project work is done in class with your group. So you should attend anyway.

If you have the opportunity to take MGMT 3435 with her, you definitely should! The content may be confusing at times, but she is genuinely very caring, accessible, and understanding. She always accounts for student feedback and creates a relaxed environment. I never felt stressed about her class this semester.

Where do I begin. Oh boy. She will either hate you or like you. No in between. Prefers girls or guys and will let you know. One of the most direct professors I have ever had the unfortunate liberty of having. I have so much time on my hands that I would write a FOUL review. But here are my final words. 

Avoid at all costs. A big NO.
Listen well and take good notes.

The class content seems needlessly convoluted and academic, but that might just be the nature of ORGB. Aksehirli keeps class engaging but expects very thorough knowledge of said content (especially theories). Solid professor who actually listens to student feedback, would recommend if you can look past the very heavy use of textbook content.
Very tough tests but I loved him as a professor.
Drakula was a very lecture heavy professor, we had no in class activities to engage ourselves and his exams were extremely difficult. If you don't read the textbook, you wont pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Foundations with Dr. Akula was not good. His exams are difficult even after paying attention and studying for hours/days to the point where only 4 people in a 114 person class got an A on the exam. He also regularly made a majority of the class uncomfortable by making unnecessary, out of line comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: -I would not take a class with him again. Even if you study everything covered in lecture in detail, you will at best get a B on exams. -Speaks without a filter and says some very questionable things during lecture -Overall, would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His "Good morning friends" really makes the class for me. I wouldn't suggest asking him a question and expecting him to answer it but overall he is very accomodating to students and grades fairly.  His lectures are a bit dull and he repeats himself a lot but overall its a good class.

can be boring to sit through, do have to do quick presentation then term paper and present that..one midterm...didn't use my book and still got an A in class, not as bad as some people make him sound..loves to smile starts class with "yes, friends"
Exams were based on the class notes; book & articles were not used. Term paper & presentation required.

I am not a conspiracy theorist, but I do believe with all my heart that Aisulu is an angel. When I am not looking in her direction, I swear I see wings sprouting out behind her back, and dare I say, the glimmer of a halo on her head. Aisulu cares deeply about her students and real learning. She has a beautiful respect for the field of linguistics.

She was a great professor. She was very lecture driven but she is always willing to make sure that you understand. She will incorporate practice problems into her lectures so you have a better idea of what she is teaching us. Her homework is pretty easy if you review the lecture slides. She is very lenient and is always to help accommodate you.

The professor is extremely nice, she wants to make sure you actually learn the material. There is only 1 test. The homework is graded fairly with great feedback and she does not really mind latework. The lectures in class are long and can be boring but you will understand everything from her with no studying. I 100% recommend taking her class.

Very negative experience regarding the course and the handling of intellectual property. Students should be extremely cautious about protecting their original work with Michal Aibin. Avoid at any cost.

Beyond the severe ethical red flags, the instructor's professional standard is alarmingly subpar.

The teaching quality is honestly very poor. He often seems confused and doesn't explain things clearly, which makes me doubt if he even understands the material. It feels like he is just doing the bare minimum to get by, without caring about the students at all.
Very negative experience regarding the course and handling of intellectual property. Students should be extremely cautious about protecting their original work with Michal Aibin. Avoid at any cost.
Lots of positive feedback and ideas how to do projects - helps learn how to do research.

The best Capstone Prof by far. Lots of knowledge, industry connections and applied, hands-on approach. We build disaster management tools for wildfires and got internships after in the industry. Strongly recommend!

Nicest professor at northeastern. She truly cares about her work, her contribution to science, her students, her place within the university, and as the editor of the Northeastern Journal of Linguistics. Amazing human. Amazing professor.

She's the NICEST lady! Super caring and understanding - I had to join her class online during the summer, and she was really accommodating. She gives great feedback and is really passionate about what she teaches. The class was super engaging and you learn a lot, yet the workload is manageable - take her class!

Aisulu Raspayeva is a WONDERFUL professor who genuinely cares about her students. She wants you to be as passionate about linguistics as she is. The workload in manageable and contributes to the content of the class. I recommend taking something with her if you have the opportunity.

She's a very accommodating professor who's generally open to whatever you need, as long as you can explain your reasoning. The assignments are flexible, you can miss class or arrive late if you communicate with her. She's extremely understanding and creates a comfortable classroom atmosphere where you can work at your own pace, listen to music.

Very sweet professor, is usually okay with anything you do as long as you have a good enough reason. Assignments are flexible and you can skip class or come in late of you just tell her why. Very understanding and good class environment - you can have music on while you work, go at your own pace, etc.

I did great in her class but she is the kind to tell you what is wrong with your artwork in front of everyone. I was doing a presentation and made me stop because of something I said was "wrong" and proceeded to tell the entire class why what I said was wrong, basically called me stupid and that I didn't know what I was talking about while laughing
very kind, easy class, can draw or paint anything if you have a clear enough profession of your work or enough reasoning, very process oriented.
Pretty rude, talked down to me because I couldn't draw certain styles. Very unclear of what we are doing in class that day and grading scale is wack.

She clearly has favorites. After missing two weeks for personal reasons, she developed a weird vendetta against me, even making remarks about me in class. Though I put A LOT effort into my work (mind u this is an 8am 2 credit course) and followed her guidelines, she graded unfairly. For my final, I met all requirements but still ended up with a B.

Judgemental + pretentious. Will grade you on how much SHE likes it/match her style, not if you did it right. Her suggestions are basically mandatory fixes if you want a good grade. Clear favoritism. She often singles people out for not having art knowledge or doing the project wrong (will make people come look at your work and explain why its bad)

Good at at teaching art but she likes to give her thoughts on things when she thinks you are wrong. Graded by very few things, but very picky if you are late. I think her grading was unfair at times. But she was an easy class for me.

She was a fun person, depending who you were. She is picky on art style at times and said she didn't like the way I drew a project on my style. She could tell I wasn't a good at the type of art she gave.

She always singled people out. When I participated in her class at the beginning, she pointed out my apparent difference. And she always treated me differently, and when everyone introduced themselves, she gave positive feedback. When it was my turn, she ignored me. She only ignored me.

i was sick and could not come in for the midterm, emailed and nothing back. midterms are by appointment and i came in and she gave me a 0 for it, later on a guy in my class said he just overslept and she just gave him an A.

not good at all types of art? don't even think of getting an A in this class. she singled out people in the class and would laugh it off when no one laughed with her. also drew all over on and on back side of my art piece in sharpie of what she didn't like about my work.

she has her fav in students and has double standards. she is very passive aggressive when it came to people artwork. i had her as a 8am and she would shame students that would come late (by 5 mins) and say that there was no excuse of being late when she got there at 6am. gave me a C on a project because she didn't like my style i drew something.
She's trying to make me the minority, I feel isolated by her words.
An incident where she commented on physical differences between students left me feeling marginalized and uncomfortable. Her approach lacked sensitivity, which significantly affected my ability.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A specific interaction in class involved comments that emphasized personal differences in a way that felt isolating and inappropriate.

The professor's teaching style made it challenging for me to engage with the material. While she is knowledgeable, her approach to addressing students at times felt dismissive and uncomfortable. An interaction during class left me feeling singled out due to unnecessary comments about differences.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a student currently in Professor Ainslie's Color and Comp course, I've found that her passion for her work and creativity enhance your learning experience tenfold. She approaches issues with empathy and kindness. Communication and effort are key in this course; you cannot half-ass your work, but it is absolutely worth it in the end!!

If you are not someone who has fundamental art skills don't go with this professor. She is dismissive in communication and is very vague in terms of how she grades your assignments. She never gives clear feedback or instructions on the projects in class.

Grades are based on projects and attendance. There are 3-4 projects during the semester, most of which have a quick turnaround time. you will have it put in a LOT of time and effort outside of class; even then, you are not guaranteed an A. she does not grade by effort, she grades it based on what she thinks of your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't have the best experience with Sophia in this class. You will have to put a lot of time aside to do the projects she assigned. Sophia was a very harsh grader, even if you did do the work or you participated in class, there was always going to be something she had to say.

You'll need to spend a lot of time doing the project every week, get ready for it. She is a hard grader even you put a lot of effort into work, you may still not an A. She can have so many to say about your work, so don't be afraid.

The only 8 AM class I actually enjoy and attend every single class. Very friendly, encouraging, good teacher, but somewhat harsh grading if you're used to easy As. Has some trouble with lectures assuming previous knowledge, but does answer questions and is willing to talk about it further with individual students if asked to. Overall, great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Sophia is phenomenal! Always very encouraging and full of ideas. I didn't come into the class an artist, but she made sure I left with a passion for art. Her enthusiasm is contagious

She either gives very vague feedback or she tells you exactly what to do, but then still gives you a low grade even if you follow the feedback perfectly.  A very kind and understanding woman, who wants to help.  She seems to be very proficient at art itself, but maybe not at teaching art. She says "push the work" as the main feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Sophia is funny, upbeat, and really nice, so she's willing to help you if you ask. She's also a really tough grader, and though you can always revise your work, expect to spend a lot of time on your projects.
Hard class, lots of work, but pays off. Best teacher I've had at Northeastern. Sweet, funny, and willing to help.

Sophia is the best teacher I have ever had.She accepts everyones technique and style and is excited to explore it.She is extremely down to earth and understands that students have other work and gives a fair workload. She gives a lot of personal attention and will rearrange her schedule even to meet with you and she wants to see individual progress

nice person, but just ok professor. she was a bit harsh with her grading, and she was also a bit hard to please.  projects were sort of hit or miss, either she liked what you did or she didn't.  if you take her 2d class, make sure tone is a key element of your pieces, she definitely focuses on that the most, and subtlety in tone works against you.

Sophia is a lovely lady who is passionate about art and teaching. Color 1 is an easy class, which actually allowed me to produce some of my best work.  She doesn't respond to emails too quickly but she is more than willing to talk to you for a significant amount of time before or after class. She has an awesome British accent.

Great teacher, passionate about art and active in her field. Defintly my favorite teacher of the semester! critiques are honest, which is helpful, and advice given is quite useful for those who would like to improve.
Great prof, passionate about art, good critiques. Fair grader, but you've got to work a lot! I highly recommend her.
Ainslie is very knowledgeable and helpful. Critique can be harsh sometimes, but you really learn a lot. It's really hard to get an A on pieces, but not impossible.

Though art is subjective, yes, this teacher always didn't like my work--even the class came to notice that she just picked on me. I was very upset due to the large amount of bias that she took out on me as an individual. She gives you the chance to re-do your work--but she'd just give me the same grade after I did the extra work. DO YOUR HOMEWORK
What a great professor! Even though class was at 8AM it was so interesting that I didn't mind. I learned a lot and my drawing definitely improved. Ainslie is fun and supportive!
great teacher! enthusiastic, passionate, interesting.
No Comments
They probably don?t have this class anymore. But she was an awesome teacher when I had her 3 years ago; she gave us a lot of freedom to explore and gave us great feedback on our work.

Really good class. I love to draw, so it was easy for me. She is a really good teacher, helps in any way she can - listen to her advice - it does help. MOST DEFINITLY do the hw - increases the grade. Be ready to spend a few hours on it. the homeworks are simple yet effective in getting you to draw. i highly recommend this class :)
Excellent class. I loved it. She is a mirracle worker to get me to be able to draw

friendly,  creative woman is helpful in teaching you the basics. she likes extremes- in areas like shading as well as in concept. she doesnt mind if you take a different approach to an assignment. just be able to justify it. must attend all classes.
her class was very simple and shes a nice teacher.  just make sure that if you do sumthing not her way, to do it well.
Inconsistent in her grading. If you have her, make sure you concentrate on tone with extreme darks and lights. I'm not a good drawer but I pulled off an A in the class because of tone.

she is an incredibly organized and thoughtful to students. clear communicated expectations on exams and assignments. thorough feedback. lectures and informative

Professor's lectures are very monotone but she's a good teacher. Assigns lots of readings and its up to you to do them but you can get by class without doing them. Professor Kitagawa's class was one of the most interesting and rewarding experiences I have had at Northeastern. Even in the online setting, she has been super helpful. She is also the best lecturer that I have ever had. Would definitely recommend taking a class with her.

Amato is a great professor and the fact that the class is hard is not a him thing so much as that rl is a tough subject. I thought it was a great class, but if you blew off lecture and the readings, would probably be next to impossible to do well.  Personally, I felt like I learned a lot taking his class and thought he was a good lecturer.

Berkeley lectures much more effective than going to class, he just points and reads the slides. Said the best review for the exam was the HWs, but didn't grade HW until exam week. Study guides were just HW problems + irrelevant theory problems. Project guidelines poorly explained, feedback vague. If there's another prof teaching, take them instead.

Really just truly awful in CS 4100. By far the worst course I've taken at Northeastern, fundamentally random grading, dismissive and apathetic professor. Save yourself the 8 grand and watch a youtube video on AB Pruning. 

Chris, if you don't want to teach, then don't. There's other places that will pay you to play with robots.

He doesn't care about his students' time or wellbeing. Honestly I never write reviews on this website, but I just had to warn people. I would try to start with some redeeming qualities but as I type this out it is hard for me to find any. He is not an engaging lecturer. You would be much better off skipping class and watching the Berkeley lectures. Beast of a prof.

would take again

She is nice but she got mad at me once during office hours because I didnt understand a question, like???? Oh and be prepared to take a very important exam the Monday after thanksgiving break very early in the morning. Your end of semester results will be delayed as well.

Prof. Shesh has amazing teaching skills. He can explain the concepts very well by using real-world examples.
