Prof Pritchett is SO SWEET, caring and clear about what you need to do to succeed. She is very helpful outside of class as well so if youre confused just go to office hours. Just put in the effort for accounting and you'll be fine.

Professor Pritchett is a really good professor who is clearly passionate about accounting. Accounting really just wasn't for me though, so I don't blame the professor for anything because it's a hard subject to make fun. She is a very nice woman who is willing to go out of her way to explain a concept that you might not understand.

Great person, but not the best prof. Isn't the best at explaining things but tries a lot and cares for every student. Quizzes are online/open book & get 3 attempts for a better grade but were worth barely anything. HW had unlimited attempts. 1 group project & only in person tests were midterm & final. Definitely take her if you want an easy A.
Very knowledgable about accounting and is generally very caring about her students, but uses time very ineffectively in her lectures and is pretty textbook heavy.

By far one of the most caring professors I've had at Northeastern. She really makes it a point to encourage her students to speak up if something does not make sense. Her tests are easy, and lectures are not necessarily stressful. Participation is graded so just show up to class and ask questions.

While she demonstrated some enthusiasm for the course she was almost never effective in her teaching or use of class time. This combines with some difficulty with English to ensure that the mandatory lectures were almost entirely a waste of time. Formula sheets are allowed for the tests and the class is not particularly difficult.

Certainly knowledgeable but struggles to explain information in an understandable way. The same goes for his feedback. Critical to get off to a good start in his class as this will change the way he views your work. Also, he values the final product more than your iterations, which was annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgable and he would push you hard. If you really want to learn a lot and you don't mind working hard, you should take him. He gives extremely good feedback and as long as you take his feedback to improve your work, you would do fine. He takes attendance very seriously so print your work before class and come to class on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lack of clarity with everything. Constantly moves deadlines from the syllabus, not returning work in time for revisions for final draft deadlines, etc. My whole 3.5 hour class involved <20 minutes of lecture and the rest of the time was silent, awkward solo-work as he moved around giving feedback. Very little group critique, zero class engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally thought he was a great professor. He taught throw lecture slides that you would fill in as you went through the material. He emphasized patterns that have helped me through Orgo 2. He wasn't there to be your friend, but he was so helpful at office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Aparece is by far one of the best teachers I've had in my life. His lectures helped me learn a lot, and he repeated certain key words and color coded his notes to really reinforce our learning. He teaches Orgo like a puzzle, which made it enjoyable to learn. Office hours were practice sessions for exams, and I highly recommend going to them.

Very inspirational and caring Professor. Orgo 2 is already hard enough but he makes it interesting and accommodates all the students. Very accessible outside of class and the tests are not hard if you just study and do everything he tells you to do outside of class. Lots of office hours.

Super accessible outside of class. 3-6 office hours/ week where he practically gives away test answers. People worry that his tests are open response, DONT! He is super liberal w/ partial credit, if you answer everything youll get a good grade. Hes consistent and fair, not tryna trick you. Truly cares for his students & wants them to love orgo

Prof Aparece was thorough and very passionate about Orgo Chem. He works hard to try and explain concepts to students and assist them in understanding them. He truly made the stress and difficulties of orgo chem slightly easier. His exams were definitely hard, but his office hours cleared any confusion.

Aparece is by far the best professor I've had in the science department. He is so knowledgable, funny, and personable. He has a lot of office hours throughout the week where you can meet other students in the class and do practice problems. His tests are open response, which requires you to truly understand the content. Would definitely recommend.

I took chemistry before professor Aparece but he really helped me understand the topics I was confused about. He held office hours in chem central and made himself super accessible. I would definitely take him again.
I actually enjoyed Organic chemistry by the end of his class. Never thought that would happen
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pick another professor if you can. The homework is very difficult and doesn't help you on the tests. His lectures don't even help at all, they are all so boring and don't even help you learn. The material on the test is so much more confusing than his PowerPoints. He is very aggressive. When you ask him a question, he gets mad if you don't know it.

Professor Aparece is a great chemistry instructor and is always accessible for office hours. If you show up to class, follow along with the slides, and go to office hours to do work if you're confused, it's not hard to get an A. His tests always align with lecture and he lays out the covered content very well.

Although I barely got an A in orgo 1, I felt like I didn't really KNOW the material. In Orgo 2, Professor Aparece helped me really understand the concepts in organic chemistry, allowing me to solve the problems rather than just memorize reactions. Using the Office hours was crucial and doing practice problems is key Frq tests are hard but not bad

Aparece is a great professor. He's so nice and it's easy to reach him with questions outside of class. The material is tough and his exams are all open-ended, but he gives you as much partial credit as possible. I struggled with orgo, but it's nice to have a professor who wants you to succeed. If you have to take orgo, take his class.

Aparece was one of the best professors I've had. He explains things in a very clear way and he always prepares for his lectures. His exams are free-response, which I think is helpful because he gives partial credit. He emphasizes understanding and not just memorizing but getting an A is not hard if you pay attention. Holds lots of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: What a great guy. Aparace made me actually like organic chemistry. His classes are fun, interesting, and comprehensive. To get a good grade in the class, really try to put in the work at the beginning so you understand the mechanisms/patterns. He gives you all the study materials necessary to get an A. Use them!!!!

Dr. Aparece was a great teacher for General Chemistry at Northeastern. Although his 100 minute lectures can drag on, his tests are very fairmostly multiple choice and a couple short answers. Not only that but he's pretty funny, tries to relate to students, and gives free points by PollEv. If I could have him again next semester I definitely would.

An amazing professor who really cares about his students. I took orgo 2 in the summer, and he continuously adjusted the syllabus to our tight schedule. Graded our exams by hand & gave us partial credit and error carried forward. If you do the practice exams, old exams and practice questions you're well on your way to a good grade.

This professor gave very helpful lectures that prepared me well for the exams. Also, although he never gives multiple choice questions on his exams, he gives a lot of partial credit & is a generous grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mark is nice and a good lecturer. His exams are a little challenging but if you do the textbook and worksheet problems you should be good. His exams are free response while the other profs give all multiple choice.

Professor Aparece was extremely enthusiastic, applied what he taught us to concepts in Biochemistry and really cared about our learning. Though we are mostly graded on a few exams, he is generous with partial credit. The textbook isn't necessary if you attend the lectures. I couldn't recommend him more.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Aparece was great. I had him for orgo 2 and he did a really good job at making lectures understandable and relevant. He gives his students all the tools they need to succeed and was very willing to work with students outside of class and offer additional help and practice problems. Also just a great dude. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Orgo 2 is a very tough class for most people, perhaps even notoriously difficult, and I knew that going into the class but Mark helped me get through it. He put in a great amount of time with extensive office hours, and he's very conscious that the material is not easy. He's super kind, and if you put in the time the way he does, you will be happy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Overall really good teacher. Sometimes his explanations didnt make sense and I needed to teach myself a concept myself. What makes him so good though is that he is a strict, but fair grader. Put forth effort, show up every day, genuinely seek knowledge, and he will reward you. I learned a lot about myself and how to fight on in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very boring lecturer who is very unclear during class. Often makes simple concepts much more difficult to understand. It is wise to not go to lectures and just show up for discussion sessions with the TA, which is actually helpful. Definitely would not recommend this professor to anyone.
calc is a hard class. professor appel makes it much easier. put in the work and pay attention to her lecture and do every homework problem and the tests will be a breeze for you.
Do the work and homework and the tests will be a breeze. Paying attention in class is essential and you will get an A in the class. Very good math 118 teacher. Recommend class
Very confusing lectures; often not relevent to the course and out of syllabus. Can be a little condescending sometimes but if you ask specific questions, he will help.

Took Calc 1 with him at USC. I was surprised I got an A because I found his material very confusing because he focused on proofs and theory.  He's one of those teachers that thinks hard math is simple for everyone. However, he is helpful and willing to work with you. Language barrier was sometimes an issue with both him and the TA.

Actually teaches CALC I at University of Southern California now. I've taken Calculus before, but this was infinitely harder. Hates calculators, loves proofs. Italian accent can be an issue if you've never heard one before. Overall, I hated this class immensely. If stuck with  Andrea, just follow along with the text book in class.

Average Instructor. Has an Italian accent and uses strange terms sometimes but is overall understandable. Attendance is pretty important for the weekly quizzes, but he only uses 6 of 10 of them for your grade. He likes it when students really participate. HW is online and incredible easy. This class has a low demand for studying outside of class.
Cool Teacher. She knows a lot. Gave some hard assignments and assigned several readings but proved helpful with my writing and analytical skills.

Horrible teacher. She comes to class fifteen minutes late all the time and is never prepared. She reads essays aloud in class and will only give you comments on your paper then, making people sit there for an entire hour and a half of class time just listening to her drone on.
Horrible teacher poor communication never thought a class could be so bad

Really nice teacher teaching an incredibly easy class. You'll watch a lot of movies and if you suggest any movie and have a reason for suggesting it, chances are she'll let the class watch it. Extremely approachable, by far my favorite first semester professor.

Interesting professor.  Classes can be boring to sit through and sometimes she tries creating ideas just so there is more to talk about.  But she will help you improve your essays, and shes a fairly easy grader.  More essays than most professors, but easier as well.  Attendance is mandatory though, but overall, good professor.

She was unclear...her assignments are unclear and she changes it constantly, but she is a pushover...ask her to watch a movie to relate to the essay and thats all you will do in class...will make classes a whole lot easier...she grades easily...but is a stickler for grammar (if you go to the writing center she will give you an extension for sho)
she knew her stuff-very intelligent. and helpful.

I really enjoyed Prof. Nabil's class, so much that I enrolled in another course he teaches. His teaching style combines lectures with hands-on practice, which makes the material very easy to understand. He is also understanding and fair with grading.

Professor Atallah is one of the best instructors I've ever had. He has a rare ability to turn complex topics into clear, engaging stories that actually make sense, rather than material you're forced to memorize. His class never felt overwhelming, because the teaching was thoughtful, structured, and genuinely focused on student learning.
Very good professor

Nabil's class was not just smart, it was current, and bioinformatics was accessible, human and relevant. I felt intellectually alive, safe to ask questions and show up as my full self.  More of this in STEM, please.

As a software developer, Dr Nabil didn't just teach tools but thinking patterns. I learned how to design for high-stakes production environments, and how to integrate automation from the very beginning. I moved beyond simply writing functional code and I began thinking in terms of architecture, systems, and clean, elegant engineering practices.

I'm beyond grateful to Professor Nabil Atallah. Every piece of advice he gave me stayed with me, and during a highly competitive job interview, his exact words guided my answers. I got the job at a top bioinformatics company, and HR told me it was because of how I answered. I couldn't have done it without his mentorship! Best Professor ever!

He is a thoughtful and exceptional professor, clearly passionate about Bioinformatics and made the course material very interesting. He consistently goes the extra mile to help students understand complex material and creates a supportive learning environment. If I get the chance, I'm definitely signing up for more of his classes!

Hi I usually don't write comments, but I have to make an exception. Dr. Nabil Atallah class is sharp, engaging, and makes Bioinformatics easy and exciting. Tbh I never thought I'd enjoy it this much. I hope to take another course with him.

I am taking currently his course on Computational Methods in Bioinformatics (BINF6310). Professor Nabil Atallah brings passion and expertise to his teaching. The class is enjoyable and fun, making challenging subjects more approachable and interesting. I highly recommend.

Nabil is one of the best professors I have had the pleasure of learning under. He is knowledgable, understanding, and more than happy to help when asked. I had him for both 6310 and 6420 (I'm not sure if he's still teaching them) but there is a reason I took 2 classes with him he makes concepts feel easier to grasp without it feeling overwhelming.
An outstanding professor! Incredibly knowledgeable and always eager to support and guide students.

Absolutely incredible teaching! The way Dr Atallah break down complex topics into easily understandable pieces is truly impressive. Great passion for the subject shines through, and it's clear how much you care about your students' success. Every lesson feels engaging and informative.

Most of the homework are discussion posts and discovery-related homework. He does NOT teach these components during the lecture. You will spend time learning how to code to do homework.

The lecture material is undergrad biology that could be taught in

He is kind and wants the students to succeed. He is disorganized and did not provide a syllabus so we did not know when assignments were due. This was made even worse when assignments were posted online without due dates. He would often go off topic in lecture making it hard to pay attention. Group projects are hard but we taught ourselves a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy and helpful
hands down best professor

He is kind to his students and enthusiastic about teaching. Classes do not feel rigid and are usually quite engaging. There was an irregular upload of assignments in the course but I'd chalk this purely up to inexperience as he is a new professor and I'm sure the course will only get better with future iterations.

Polly is a very insightful instructor and provides very detailed feedback to your work. Lots of reading but she is always willing to help. However, her grading is extremely hard. Getting an A is very difficult unless you are very good at analytical writing and follow her rubrics exactly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Gives a good chunk of reading from textbooks that are referenced heavily in class but pretty irrelevant if you have any background knowledge. Group projects for days too, and she doesn't want to be told who's the one guy not doing anything. Assessments are self-reflections, so if you already understand material, good luck showing progress.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Had Polly for many ed courses. Although her class entails lots of reading, she may be the best professor in the ed dept. All you really need to do to get an A is show up to class, and offer opinions on the regular class discussions. She is incredibly supportive, and will continue to help even when you finish taking her class.
Polly is a great teacher. Although the class has a lot of required reading, it was interesting and I didn't mind doing the work. Come to class prepared and ready to participate; easy A.

talk about having your cake and eating it too. this serbian professional  enlightened me to all aspects of education and what it takes to be an independent teacher (like not dependent at all). I give this class a V for Viciously Vigorous
great teacher, great experience. too many repetitive books

Very interesting class and professor, thought provoking.  Assigns A LOT of reading material and not much else, which becomes the basis of class discussion.  Very much a participation based class and it is essential to do the readings.

Great professor, very interesting. She really cares about her subject, and really wants to help students become as passionate about teaching as she is. EDUC1111 requires a good amount of reading, but the class discussions that are a huge part of the class are very interesting and a great way to learn to widen your perspectives. Highly recommend her
why is the final paper 10 pages? ridiculous. she is alright. alot of unnecessary and repetitive work. BLAHHHHH

The ratings on here do not do justice to Polly Attwood as a Professor. The class is a lot of work, but it is worthwhile and you truly leave it with an understand of the subject. She is supportive, passionate, and generally there to help you succeed. Very genuine and fair.

Be ready to read and overanalyze everything. If you put in the work and actually do the critical readings, you'll be fine. Polly knows a lot about kids and teaching and is very passionate about it in class. She is also passionate about her personal beliefs, though, so try not to oppose them too often...

One of the worst professors I have had at northeastern. Gives enough work to accumulate at least three courses. Seems to think her class takes priority over any other class. Readings are redundant and mostly unnecessary. Very strong on her beliefs so dont dare to disagree because you wont get anywhere.
She gives a lot of work but she's really not as bad as these reviews say. Occasionally confusing but she always makes herself available for any help you need

I had to laugh while I was reading the other comments. While they are aggressive, they're definitely true. Polly made me second guess majoring in Education at Northeastern until I read about her days at Lesley (as mentioned in one of the other reviews). She would be better suited teaching at a disciplinary high school lol

Polly loves to teach n no one can argue against that. unfortunately, she has a "benefit of the doubt" view on the world; the same one among politicians that has created more and more horrible poverty and racial tension in this country. b/c of this u have to have about 10 sources to back up every statement u make. she is helpful but get out if u can

Really nice woman with a sort of hippy-sh spin on education. Very supportive and helpful. The class itself is really repetitive, but she does her best to draw on her own and your personal experiences as well as various media to make it interesting. Easy A.

Very little clarity in what he wants, need to ask multiple times and still do not get a clear answer. READ THE SYLLABUS, he will not warn you when things are due. Also, the lectures are pointless, he goes off on tangents of his own life and never quite gets into the material. I honestly cannot tell you what I learned in this course.
Prof was good. I found him interesting because of his accent. He is knowledgable about International Business.
Not helpful and will not even respond

Class is very boring, the professor is absorbed in "cultural" awareness - but I personally find the topics in the course promote more stereotypes than remove. The prof. also is not suitable to teach part time, adult students - treats all students like young undergrads or first year grad students.
can't "decenter" from his cultural background
Very experienced and knowledgable professor in the field. He uses the book and his personal accounts to teach the class. Answers any questions asked and is a very friendly person!

He turns every class discussion into an irrelevant story about himself.  He also makes the students teach the class, having each class session consist of a presentation of a reading or book.  Certain groups have to do case studies, others have to do 5 page articles, and others have to do 300 page books.
Very experienced in international business.  Very interesting to listen to in a 2 hour class.

I said my idea for my project and he jus said it was a bad idea.I stayed after class to ask y but he got defensive and did not clearly explain why it was bad, he jus said if u think its a good idea then do it. some1 asked to ellaborate on the details and he jus told us to read the syllabus

Though seemingly well versed in the subject Dr. Charles was completely disengaged with the class. Not a single email reply, carelessly sparse feedback, apparent random assignment of grades outside of the rubric (even though I personally scored high). Very unfortunate that NEU has allowed this from a teacher in the ED.d program.

Course and subject matter was very interesting. Dr. C was not active in discussion boards, however, she graded according to the rubric. I had no issues with her or the coursework. I do wish she was more engaging as this was a six week course on a subject matter I was very interested in. Overall a good experience and material was useful in my work.

No feedback on assignments, discussions, or grades until last week of class, despite repeated attempts to engage via e-mail. Grades were not calculated according to the standards in the rubric. And she repeatedly submitted incorrect grades, so watch out! Make sure to challenge it if your grades seem unusually low; it's probably her mistake again.
Best. Professor. Ever. Literally nothing bad to say about him. Funny, makes classes interesting and is the nicest person ever
Best professor I have had to this day. Amazing guy who really cares about his students. Stay in contact with him!
THE BEST TEACHER EVER!!!!! George is the man If you never have him as a professor then you are missing out
An amazing professor. Hands down my favorite.

He's a great instructor, tries to be funny which is entertaining. Breaks the class up into different parts making a two hour class fly by. Def suggest choosing him if possible. Great guy, book is easy reading.

It was always difficult to understand what was going on. He would rush, stutter, and make mistakes often which made it difficult to follow along with the lecture. He was willing to clear any confusion but it wasn't always helpful. The question s on his tests and quizzes are difficult to understand. The textbook helps explain the core concepts.

Mr. Gomez's teaching style is not effective at all. At times he questions himself, and it's pretty difficult to understand him, and if the class asks too many questions, he ends up getting frustrated and tells everyone to go to his office hours if they have more questions. He does give opportunities to increase grade but its minimal.

His teaching style was really effective and the way he words his questions were confusing as times. He is willing to help out but once again the way he explains things is difficult. He is a strict grader.
I feel like his teaching style isn't really affective
He's very strict and his class is confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez just needs to get settled as a new lecturer, then I think he'll be great. Class was rough sometimes because participation was awful, and during lectures he would sometimes second guess himself which could be confusing. However, grading was fine and he reached out frequently over email with updates on assignment rubrics and stuff.
Uses AI for course content by the way.

I had Professor Arrowood during the Summer of 2023, and I can say without a doubt that he is an effective Org B teacher, and I did enjoy his class. 

The class was extremely simple to understand under professor Arrowood, and if you simply showed up to class and listened, it was easy to score above a B. All you had to do was show up and listen.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Rick Arrowood is a joke! He made my class purchase an "Organizational Behavior Support Materials and Cases" which was $40, made us upload a screen shot of Canvas showing that we purchased the materials. He NEVER USED THEM IN ANY OF THE CLASSES!!!! Waste of my money and time, plus he would constantly cancel class. Unprofessional, should be fired.
Joke of a professor, though not a bad person himself.
I'm still baffled that's he extensively used AI for his course.
Uses AI instead of own knowledge and time to prepare their lectures.  Yet doesnt want you utilizing tools. I guess its great for teaching the greedy and hypocritical side of business instead

Worst instructor I've had. Grades were based on flattery, not work quality. He bragged about himself, put students on the spot to entertain himself, ignored deadlines, and said the syllabus was irrelevant. Class was always cut short and often canceled. Sloppy, AI-generated lecture slides and notes were the least of his many shortcomings. Fire him.
Using too much AI.

Rick might be the worst ever. He spends all the class time on an egotistical rant or creating useless activities and then gives extremely difficult quizzes on lecture notes that he has never discussed. Attending class is a waste of time, though attendance is mandatory, and he never wastes an opportunity to put you down personally and embarassingly.
Very fun professor, super memorable!

Arrowood is a fine professor and this class was not particularly challenging, the content was even interesting. His teaching style was objectively bad. He mostly attempted to actively recall course material aloud in a way that was very difficult to follow. Double standards. Extremely arrogant and disrespectful towards his students. Authoritarian.

(Boston College) Professor Arrowood is charismatic and he tries to make his classes funny and engaging but ends up embarrassing students and himself a lot of the time. He is very unserious during class only for his assignments to be unexpectedly more complicated than they ever should be. Disorganized. Would not take again.

Truly dedicated to his craft great atmosphere & students encouraged to joke & contribute Teaching style not for everyone Went on tangents w/ lectures & interrupted students to embarrass/correct them in front of class Little criteria given - fun at times but expected to know what he wants &  answer how he likes Fun class but introverts be warned!
Amazing gave my group a straight A on the project

Very disorganized and confusing professor. You have to pay for a case study that he wrote which has tons of mistakes and is poorly written. And then he's ironically tough when grading. Asked for feedback on a quiz multiple times and never got it. Discussions are fun but he interrupts frequently and can be disrespectful. Charismatic guy, though.

My second class with Rick and if I could take him again I absolutely would. He truly wants students to learn things through experience rather than from a textbook so the class was very entertaining. Consisted of lighthearted and interesting discussions on EVERYTHING and fun activities. Provided that you match his enthusiasm, you will get an A.

My favourite professor at northeastern. He is the only option to take for ORGB in my opinion. Provided that you go into this course with an open mind about what you normally expect from a class then you will enjoy it. To do well you must participate but all classes are very casual discussions which I loved

One of the most enjoyable classes that I've had at Northeastern so far despite it being a 3 hour long class once a week. 

Professor is nice, funny and fair. Takes a very different approach to classes which involved constant discussion which was a very effective way to learn for me. If you have no trouble participating then this class is for you.

We rarely went over the necessary and applicable materials for this class, and if we did, Arrowwood would only do half of it and ask us to look at it on our own time. Most of the classes were discussions about a topic he chose that was somewhat related to the class. one time he graded my essay with a grammarly screenshot

I think her lectures are good. Going to class vs. not going definitely makes a huge difference. She has notes, but they're a little disorganized/hard-to-follow. Overall, she's a good teacher! TAs a generally helpful. Most of your grade is based on quizzes + final exam.

This class was probably my favorite of all the classes I've ever taken! Though the class was lecture-heavy, it sets you up very well for the exams and weekly homework assignments. Prof. Hamlin and the TA's are easily accessible if you have any questions as well. If you regularly go to class and recitation, then the course is very straightforward.

Lowkey the tests were just super hard imo LOL, I did well on every homework but pretty bad on midterms + final, maybe just me. Ariel as a person is great, she's very accessible outside of class but if tests are hard for you (like me) it may not be the best so go to class because her lectures are very in depth.

Professor Hamlin cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The class is lecture only which is fine, some lectures are better than others. The first exam was relatively difficult, second was extremely easy and just like her guide. The weekly problem sets become increasingly annoying and are worth 40% of your ENTIRE grade, so put in effort.

Incredible engaging and clear lectures, is very knowledgable of the content, and makes you learn it so easy. A bit ackward and cringey. Attendance is not mandatory but I would highly recommend going to class, subject is very interesting too. One of the best professors I've had.
Super nice professor and also very chill. Homework can be time-consuming but will prepare you for the exam. Probably the nicest professor in all of Khoury.

I went to the other professor because i didnt like her she tries to be funny and im just bored of her lectures so i never paid attention. even tho i did the practice exam, i didnt do good on the exams but for some reason i ended with a B+ lolll so ig it chill.

Professor was very warm and welcoming and its hard not to like her. Be prepared to type homework, including tedious mathematical operations, but you get used to it. She teaches really well, grading is fair, and you can really tell she cares about her students. Easy 5!

Very well-explained lectures; knows how to make students understand a completely new topic. Transitions from content is very smooth and easygoing; if you attend all lectures and ask questions, she will make this complicated class way easier. *Be sure to go over formatting for hw since the first day cause you might get deducted some points.
Very good professor, knows a lot about the content and makes the lectures simple to follow and understand.

Tough Professor who wasn't able to provide a lot of support within the classroom. Also notes are horrible, so try to attend the TA Office Hours to understand what happened in class but beware, there are no zooms to check the lecture again so be careful as this professor's notes were bad and there was no zoom to look back at.
Nice professor, easy to follow and understand during classes. Notes aren't great; stay focused during classes.

Great! Will talk about her cats at any given opportunity. HW can get a little heavy, but its not too much work, and the tests are easy. However, do not miss class, there is no textbook and her notes aren't great.
The class is not hard, and you can easily skip classes based on the topic of the class. It's not hard to get an A as long as you go to class and pay attention

Good teacher tbh. Made content that wasn't super straightforward rather easy. I just wish she didn't try to be funny or get the class to participate because no one gives her energy back and it was really hard to watch.

Had very good energy during class. Grading was extremely lenient and fair. Lectures were very clear and easy to follow, she used class time efficiently. Questions on homeworks, quizzes, and the final did not contain material not taught and were very doable if you paid attention in class.

Instructor grading is pretty lenient and they curve the exams if needed. Instructor makes a lot of mistakes during lecture which can hinder your learning experience, but they do correct themselves. Professor would be unprepared and unorganized at times with their notes which can get pretty difficult in understanding material in a timely manner.

Prof. Hamlin is smart, and while the class is lecture heavy, I like her lecture style. She's great at answering questions during lecture, makes herself available outside of class, and is incredibly kind. It's absurd to expect an instructor teaching abstract math to never make a mistake in lecture; she's a great teacher sensitive to students' needs

Often gets confused by her own notes, messes up in lectures, and gets corrected by students. I honestly think she is confused on the topics herself, making it impossible to learn. Homework often includes problems we spoke about in class for 2 minutes. I think if she went over questions that paralleled the homework I would learn much better.
AWESOME

Professor Hamlin is by FAR the best option for CS1800. Attend her lectures even if you aren't placed into her section. The class itself kinda sucks but she does the best job out of any professor of explaining the material in lecture. She's really nice and a bit awkward but that's just part of her charm.

One of the best professors I've had! Professor Guha is very kind and approachable which was huge for me as a freshman in my first semester. He's very knowledgable and is always willing to help. Also a great lecturer. Coursework wasn't so bad but did require a decent amount of work
Arjun is a good guy who cares a lot about what he's teaching and the students' success. His lectures can be somewhat shaky at times. He's very fair and considerate and wants his students to succeed.

Professor Guha was great at dealing with issues in this class. I had an issue with a lab partner and he resolved it quickly. Though the homework and exams were graded pretty toughly, that was due to the rubric of this class more so than Guha himself. Though his lectures left something to be desired, he was definitely the best option for fundies1.

Arjun is a god. He gives paper practice exam problems all the time in class (often they are harder than the exam itself so don't stress too much if one is particularly hard to understand) and he loves to answer questions. Hilariously sassy too.

Professor Arjun has possibly become my favorite professor at Northeastern, so far. He's very engaging in his lectures; he's funny, attentive,  and caring. If someone has a question, he does his best to answer it in a way they understand, and he actually gives enough time for people to ask questions, unlike some other professors. Highly recommend.
The Best professor in CS 2500 for 23 Fall!

Stopped going to Patterson's lectures to go here and learned so much. Loves how he literally gives practice questions during lectures and gives students time to work w/ each other on the code he wrote. Very interactive space and he's very engaging to listen to.
Very caring professor, the explanations of each concept is clear and understandable.

Arjun was one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern so far. His lectures were funny and I always went to them, even though attendance wasn't required. His lectures can seem unrelated to the homework at times, but you will appreciate them at the end of the course. Will often explicitly write code during office hours --  extremely helpful!

His lectures were good, but if you didn't review the material beforehand it could be very difficult. But yes, it's also a weeder intro CS class, so don't expect it to be easy. He was amazing considering the difficulty of the class. Still, many students didn't come to class and used the recorded lectures (that were great) made by Prof. Derbinsky.
Such a good teacher, class also had recorded video lectures which were helpful. However, even if you learn a lot you can still end with a less than amazing grade.

Arjun is awesome. He is so knowledgeable (granted you are willing to go beyond the topics covered in class) and will help you solve any issues. He has a very good humor that gets you engaged into the lecture. Also, He responds to email in minutes. Would take him again in any class.
Loved taking fundies 1 with Arjun. I feel that regardless of your level of comp sci knowledge before the class, you can come out confident about the material.
Great guy. Has a great sense of humor and cared about his student's success. His live coding style was helpful. He is responsive to feedback and a fair grader.
Online class with her was a light workload and she is very generous with grading! Responds quickly to emails and is willing to meet with you if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If Cheryl is your co-op advisor, you are in good hands. I had a rough application cycle, and even when I thought my chances were gone she helped me find more opportunities and connected me with a professor so that I could secure a (paid!) work-study co-op. She's very supportive, and I wouldn't have wound up in this great situation without her.
Lectures could be a bit slow but the class was run well overall. Fair grader and always willing to help.

The professor is very fair, great at teaching, and assigns weekly homework with coding reviews conducted by TAs. He is caring, understanding, and professional. He answers all questions, but midterm questions are not directly from slides; they are based on lecture content. I would highly recommend taking his class.
Very good teacher, my concepts are clear because of him
Thoroughly Enjoyed his Class!
Literally the kindest ever

She is so sweet and caring and it is clear she genuinely cares about her students. She never made the class stressful and made any rules/guidelines clear from the start of class. She made me enjoy writing again! Her TA is also very nice and chill.
Best Professor in the world!

Professor Emily was great. Highly recommend this class because since there is a service aspect you have way less homework than other first year writing course. Professor Emily is super sweet and super understanding if something happens. Her TA is useless so no need to pay any attention to her.

The sweetest professor ever! She is super caring and wants the best for all of her students. The class itself is chill and is a very collaborative and welcoming environment. I honestly looked forward to class every week because Emily is very passionate and optimistic. Overall, this is a great class to take 10/10!!

BEST PROFESSOR EVER. If you plan on taking any writing class, please take Emily. She is super kind and respectful to her students. She dedicates so much time to the course, which creates a sense of community within our class. Emily is very open-minded, optimistic, and understanding so assignments are not only easy, but are stress relieving.

Great professor, accepts late work and is super understanding if you can't attend class or something, just email her. Class is often discussion heavy but you don't have to participate if you don't want. Honestly a really great semester. She doesn't have an intense rubric for most assignments but if you ask she'll give specifics

Thought this class would be a pain, but I really enjoyed it! Professor Avery-Miller is super laid back, her writing assignments are fun and thought provoking. Really got to know people in my class and looked forward to it every week, if you need ENGW1111 take it with her, highly recommend!

Emily is super sweet and an easy and helpful grader, but kind of exhausts group work. I feel like I barely wrote in this class, it was a lot of creative assignments. Feels like a high school class. She isn't a super engaging lecturer but overall her class was easy and the assignments were totally manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Extremely easy 3rd year writing class. No lectures, just occasional readings that you don't get tested on. Just remember to do your discussion board posts on time and put marginal effort into the 4 main assignments - and you will get an easy A. She is also extremely nice and caring. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a great professor. Cares about her students, and her class is not too tough if you do what is asked of you.

Dr. Avalon is extremely approachable and passionate about helping to support the next generation of healthcare leaders. She serves almost like a mentor as well as a professor. I encourage all of her students to make a connection with her and rally engage in the classroom discussions. She offers so much more than just the syllabus. great person.

There is weekly discussion boards, readings and articles to read. There will be a midterm paper which is easy. The final paper was a little difficult because Ive never done a grant proposal writing. Be sure to ask and questions or things that may seem unclear. The professor will provide good feedback and clarity. Great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Avalon is a great teacher and very understanding. If an assignment is unclear she will communicate with you by email or phone. I love her she wants to see all her students succeed and is available outside of her class. This class is based on choosing an internship so there will be writing assignments based on that and discussion boards .
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher.  Mrs.  Avci  made the class fun in and out of class with interesting  readings and class discussions.  She is also very clear with what she expects and grades based on effort.  Overall a very understanding and nice instructor.
Very easy to work with and understand. Just show up to class, do the assignment, turn it on time and you're good.
Very sweet. Shes young, so she understands her students. Knows what shes teaching well. Very easy to talk to. Definitely recommend

He is wonderful, and I am excited to be taking a third class with him. He is engaging, and the classes are based on group collaboration with an emphasis on practicing speaking skills. The tests can be challenging, but he is always available to help if you are confused. Such a sweet and passionate professor.

He's amazing!! I took Elementary French II and am thrilled to be taking another class with him. He's incredibly passionate and genuinely cares about his students. My French improved so much, and he's always patient and understanding. He speaks mostly French, which really helps, and he's always willing to support students in and out of class.

Such a chill and nice guy. His lectures were interesting, a lot of collaborative work, and fair grader. There was a decent amount of homework due but it was never hard. I definitely reccomend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took FRNH 1101 but they didn't have an option for that so ignore the course number but please don't take this class unless you speak French. He's a sweet person however all his lectures are 100% in French so I didn't know what was going on most of the time. Take it if you speak French to some degree or you will be lost.

I enjoyed having Professor Hancock this semester. He is a great professor and cares about his students. My level of french increase through his teaching. He made classes fun and interesting with activities that pertained to the topic of study. Although he grades some assignments pretty hard, I would still recommend him.

For French 1101. Only took a week so disregard the rest of this rating. Just know that he teaches in French as much as possible. Take him if you are a quick learner who is very present during class time. Also, rather strict homework policies.

Prof Hancock is a new, young professor. He's been an amazing teacher and makes class interesting by having activities or presentations lined up the whole time. Super genuine and willing to help you out anytime. Very easy grader on the homework tasks too. My french has gotten a lot better with him.

The review for CHME 7601. This course was very disappointing. The professor often wrote equations on the board without any explanation, and when asked, she said they were copied from the textbook.  The exam was very difficult and didn't reflect what we were told to study. Overall, the course lacked structure and proper guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Augustes class is very challenging and work heavy. Sometimes lectures are disorganized but her tests are very fair and she isnt that harsh a grader. She also cares and wants students to succeed.
Poorly organized and hard to follow lecture. There was a semester long group project and didnt teach some of the required information for it until after the first draft was due.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Talks a lot about current events, which is a good time waster. Likes to name drop, but it just gets humorous after awhile. She's very friendly with students and really does know a lot about the industry. Teaches very well and is really nice.
I don't agree with the majority here. She was super informative, helpful, and a real sweetheart. She went out of her way to help me out in the industry. For that she gains my love and respect.

i had her last semester and she was basically the thorn of my semester. she's kind of like the mean middle school teacher everybody hated. her class is not enjoyable by any means and i didn't learn a thing i couldn't have learned by sitting down and reading the book for like an hour. she also holds grudges.

Lawrence was very boring and I didn't learn much from the class at all. Usually ended up wasting half the class with current events chat. She worked at a record label once and likes to mention that a lot. Not much teaching, lots of browsing web sites and videos.

Ava Lawrence is a horrible professor. She is incredibly boring and being in her class i a waste of time! She does not have a clue on how to teach and is incompetent. I strongly suggest switching teachers if you can!
DO NOT TAKE MUSIC INDUSTRY WITH LAWRENCE. PERIOD.

Without a doubt the worst teacher I've ever had in all my years of schooling.  How this woman got a teaching job (or any paid employment) is beyond me.  Sitting in this class made me feel guilty that my parents were actually spending their money on this.  Did you know she worked at TVT records?  She should mention that more in class.
name dropper.  not a good teacher.  "i worked at tvt records" yeah good for you.  i just hated her.

I feel bad that eva thinks she's *still* a hot shot in the business. tells lots of stories about herself, her career, very boring class. take Prof. Strasser instead, i took him for music industry 2 and it was SO much better

She's really nice and knows what she's talking about, but perhaps not the best at actually TEACHING it to others. She lets you know what's on the final a few days before so that helps and it's easy enough, as well as her projects. Perhaps not the most engaging class but still fun.
this class was a waste of my time.  i expected a lot more out of this class and this major in general...this professor was one of the reasons i dropped out.
This class was a waste of time. Take another professor.

Not good if you want to learn computer programs you don't already know how to use(ie.ms-word)Projects are vague without clear explanation of conceptsShe'll try to help you,but sometimes it's hard to get beyond the condescending attitude&name dropping every.005seconds.I think she misses the industry.
The class was straightforward and easy...she tells you directly what will be on the midterm and final but overall it is very boring.

She's a nice and helpful professor, especially with scheduling and stupid NU paperwork crap. I think she's still getting used to how to add entertaining things into class and still make them relevant. SHe'll get better I'm sure... as long as she stops saying "When I was at TVT..." everyday.

I didnt like her at all.  she constantly talks in circles, so its hard to take notes because everything is so disorganized.  the papers are easy, tests even easier.  she also likes to name drop:  "when i worked at TVT records where the ying yang twins and ja rule are signed...blah blah blah..."
Has a good attitude and a high tolerance for people not understanding every step of the projects. She is willing to explain the steps numerous times and is very helpful.
prof. lawrence is a great professor. she is always there if you need answers and will work her hardest to help find you a co-op come dec.2nd and you still have no job.
No Comments

honestly, i can't stand her as a person, as she can be extremely condescending at times (pretty much all the time actually).  but, the class is really easy and most people just surf the internet the entire time and completely ignore her...a good throwaway music industry class.
makes you wanna switch majors....

She has no idea how to do math. Taking 10% and then 30% is not the same as taking 40%, but it is to her. (idiot) However, I am biased, went into the class not liking her. Janikian is easier and better, so if you have the oppurtunity take Janikian's class.

She is a nice lady, but her lectures can become a bit boring, and sometimes it feels like what she's saying isn't important. She gives bonus points for attendance and participation which is nice. Her grading is pretty harsh. The textbook is almost completely useless. Tests are tough and fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Edwards was a great professor. Lectures are based directly off the textbook and the slides were very comprehensive. She is super nice and understanding towards students and holds review sessions in class before exams and on Zoom with office hours. Exams are hard, but you should be well prepared if you take notes in class and make a good cheat sheet

Overall, Prof. Edwards was great. The lecture slides are well done, with lots of pictures, and they closely follow the textbook readings. Homeworks are generally very helpful for understanding the content. Tests are intentionally very difficult, but the grades are curved at the end. Overall, great professor, great class.

Edwards is one of my favorite professors. I wish more professors were like her. She knows QP is difficult and she does her best to help everyone and take feedback on her lecturing. She listens and clearly cares about her students and is also definitely passionate about the course content. 10/10 would recommend her for QP.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Edwards is an amazing professor. QP is VERY difficult, and for the most part she makes it straightforward. She is willing to meet you halfway as long as you show up and put in the effort. Classes are roughly 2/3 lecture, 1/3 in class practice. The tests are difficult because she's really testing you on application, but the curve is amazing.
She's a good professor but tends to rush through lectures and spends the second half of the class on practice problems.

QP is a notoriously hard course in the BioE curriculum, but Edwards made it really interesting and not too terrible. To be honest, I never read the textbook chapters until before the exams. The lectures and example problems in class are good prep for the exams. She cares about our feedback, will implement changes suggested by students

She is a really good professor for QP. Reading the textbook is a must, but she'll meet you once you've gone that far. She tells you exactly what she's looking for you to know and allows for info sheets on tests. Overall really cares people know the material and is willing to change things around if a lot of people ask/ need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ganguly is very knowledgeable in his field. He actively tries to make his students interested the subject, and invites them to a lot of seminars and presentations. He tends to be a little busy sometimes, but his TA is more than capable of handling things when he isn't available. I highly recommend taking any course taught by Prof. Ganguly.
Learned a lot and got exposure to many new areas in time-series.

Don't take a class with him!!! He assumes you already know everything and teaches class like a review session. He doesn't interact with class, just dumps material on board. Homeworks are easy, but exams are crazy hard and pretty conceptual.
he can't teach for more than 10 students, and he always goes out of subject , but is helpful when we need him
Good prof. The only problem with him is that he used to care too much about bad students. He tried that bad students learned something, so at the end the good ones wasted their time.
No Comments
By all means, i think hes a nice guy, a good speaker, but the class is pointless.  We dont learn things that are important to our major.
Love this proffesor, his classes are great if you truely are commited to your education. He is always more than willing to assist student in and out of class. A+++++++

I had him for C++, Operating Systems and Embedded Systems 2. August is an awesome teacher if you give him a chance. In a small class like 5 or 7, he will go out his way to teach you because he is more passionate. But in a large lecture class, you're better off reading the book because he only picks on his favorites. you'll never learn that way.
No Comments

Hes a good guy and knows some stuff. BUT other then that he SUCKS! class is waste lectures are all over the place, Doesn't care about his students, does not show up to office hours, and will screw you on a test. Questions are scrambled and homework doesn't make sense. RUN AWAY!

Weak professor.  His homework assignments are okay, his tests are often confusing and subjective, and his lectures are almost completely useless.  He makes no effort to engage the students.  He lectures as if it is only a secondary or tertiary responsibility of his as a university professor.

Obviously all the students above had a class average below 60.I think he is great if you actually follow along with the book. You can't expect to sit down and relax wishing that everything will come and take a sit in your head.

I really like him as a professor. I've had him for several classes and he gives challenging work that makes me work hard, but I like the challenge.  He most definitely does NOT qualify as the "worst teacher ever" or anything like that. He knows his material.
Horrible teacher ... doesnt care about the students, never shows up to office hours, all over the place when lecturing. For the amount of money you are paying for this school we deserve much better.
FULL OF HIMSELF

By far the worse professor I have even taken. He's horrible. Confusion doesn't explain the way you feel after one of his classes. On top of that, he's full of himself. He's not clear and doesn't give a $**t if you fail or pass.
clueless
He knows his sh*t but can't teach. Definitely not professor material, stick to industry.
This teacher sucks, does not teach the material assignments have nothing to do with the class. In one word TERRIBLE
I HATE this guy!!  He SUCKS!!  By far, the WORST teacher E-V-E-R!!
He is one of the worst professors i've ever had. He teaches you nothing and cares even less. The whole program is a joke, switch majors before its too late

GOD AWEFUL... he needs to quit and have someone who knows and cares take over the CET.. Fing BS, and he is in charge... think bout how terrible everyone else is below him! ****IN BULL**** WASTE OF MONEY...
No Comments
sucks!!! worst teacher ever

Okay teacher- obviously knows his code, but you'll need to do the reading and figure out some of the material out on your own. Pretty easygoing when it comes to late assignments- he just wants you to get the work done and learn the material.
knows his stuff, very tough time explaining class material to students.  tries to be helpful...but just leads to more confuzion. i'd give him a c+
Best Teacher EVER
HORRIBLE TOO MANY ANALOGIES
I learnt a lot in this class and prof ashley is the sweetest and really knows her content!!
Kate's teaching quality is very high. The course difficulty is appropriate, and she explains details very clearly. I learned a lot from this class.

professor ashley is really nice and attentive. she provides lots of outside of class feedback and support and very easy to talk to so i do like her lectures. the material itself though is very challenging— lots of work, 4 heavy projects throughout the semester. there are 2 exams which we can bring notes in so should be easy if you actually study.

Prof. Ashley is very by the book, rubric grading, but took FOREVER to get grades back to us. The amount spent on the class as a whole outside of going to class was very minimal, but if you don't pay attention you end up having to teach yourself everything. The final project is with a real company and gives real experience. Hardest content is R code
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ashley is the best professor I have had during my time at Northeastern. I am a senior and she is so knowledgable about consumer behavior and is a caring grader. She really cares about you as a person and knows every one of her students by name. I highly recommend this class if you are interested in consumer behavior + discussion based class.

Ashley is a fantastic teacher, one of the best in the marketing department. I loved the discussion based class and the fact that Ashley was able to integrate her industry knowledge. The course material was extremely interesting and I loved working with my classmates. As other reviews mention, participation is HUGE, start talking early in semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont take this class if you are not a discussion, actively participate person. Require you to speak in every class and she will note down. All of the grades are subjective and she does not show grade on canvas.
She's a great professor! The class was very discussion based and interesting.

Ashley was a wonderful professor. This was one of her first zoom classes and she worked very hard to make the class interesting even as an 8am. I especially appreciated she broke down the participation grade in several ways so you could still succeed in the class if speaking in a Zoom class made you anxious. Cares about her students.

I think this guy might be power tripping. He smiles watching students struggle to answer obscure and unclear questions that have no relevancy to anything he has taught us (which is essentially nothing), and expects a perfect answer. Worst professor of my life.

Imagine the worst qualities of a professor - mean, rude, unprepared, cruel, unfair, and terrible at teaching. Well, that's what we have here. He will yell at you for things that are out of your control, like not having a camera, or not knowing topics he never even taught. Quite honestly the biggest waste of money, and infuriating to say the least.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HE IS THE GOAT

The worst professor I've had. Just don't take the class if it will be with him. He is extremely bossy, you don't learn anything. And btw, there's no rounding so if you get for example 89.8, he won't give you the A- which is 90%.

Do NOT take CS4520 with this professor unless you don't want to learn. You will be assigned time-consuming projects, to then be deducted points for random, and irrelevant stuff. No live coding, and lectures are very boring. 
If you take the class with him you won't learn unless you spend hours and hours on your own trying to figure things out.

lectures provide zero preparation for homework/projects which is the entire course grade. covers little to no code examples in class. left on your own to scour the internet for docs and code examples. a particular TA would CTRL+C CTRL+V our code into ChatGPT to grade, at least have the decency to actually grade. point deductions for random reasons

Very bad lecturer, he goes through the topics extremely fast, and explains very little. Doesn't provide code after lectures and has slides which are not readable at all. Very hard to learn, he just talks and doesn't even do much live coding. 
Takes a long time to answer Piazza posts.
One of the best professors I've had, breaks down technical papers so that they're clear, understandable, and interesting
Best Professor at Northeastern. Hard NOT to pay attention

I truly enjoyed Professor Asthagiri's course. He is incredibly knowledgeable  and has a way of simplyfing complex topics in a way that makes them easy to understand. Moreover, he maintains fairness in grading and is always available to help. He has become one of my favorite professors, and I hope to take another course w/ him soon.

Tough weekly exams (on Fridays. Lectures were convoluted on slideshows and not relevant to the exams. Went over very few examples in lectures and resorted to self-learning from the textbook + mini-lectures.

Prof. Asheghan did his best with the amount of material he had to teach in a short period of time. He is very approachable, enjoys interacting with students, and will go out of his way to help anyone who is struggling with concepts in the class.

The most eager professor to teach I have ever seen. The exams were somehow difficult, but we had three days for four problems and legally were allowed to use any external source. Moreover, the final score can be over 100 (Extra points) that compensates the exam difficulty. Helpful in private meetings.

Worst professor I've take at this school, although I am a second year. He blazes through notes made for him by pearson and they suck, his hand writing is chicken scratch. Also the midterms: The single worst test I have taken in my entire life, it was written like it had gone through google translate from 5 years ago a couple times. Do NOT Take.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lori is kind, her directions are straightforward, and she wants to make sure her students truly learn the content. If you complete the assignments as directed, you'll get a B+ or A-. She really makes you work for the A. Highly recommend contributing more than you think you need to and always including outside resources.

Lori's class is as difficult as you make it. Her instructions and expectations are crystal clear, so if you don't pay attention, you get what you deserve. Yes, participation matters, so all it takes is to show interest and join in discussions. She really knows the subject and went beyond to help me understand it. Inspirational! Thank you, Lori!

Even you speak more than 3 times on the class she still gives you a B- on your class participation, even you tried very hard to make your final paper perfect you may still eventually receive a very low score. Her classes are all very hard.
She is very unorganized and unclear with her instructions. She will give vague instructions and will give you a bad grade if your assignment isnt to her standards (which she doesnt tell you).

Lori is the most hardest grader ever!!!! She doesn't even know what QUITE literally mean. She might give you a C even you talked one or two times in the class. Even you prepared and spoke up more than 3 times, she might also say you are quite.
good professor

Prof. Awatef is one of the nicest professors at Northeastern. She is really helpful outside class, she is an easy grader, and she gives easy exams. Don't expect the best teaching. However, if you do the HWs and go to class you will get an A.

Prof. Awatef is a very nice person. She teaches really good. Even though she has a little problem with communication, she tries her best to teach the subject properly. If you attend classes regularly and pay attention, then you don't face any difficulty in exams. She takes a lot of examples in the class for practice. She is very caring.

This is the single worst professor Ive ever had the displeasure of having. She cannot hold the attention of the class.  When asked a question she never provides an answer that makes sense. Her examples aren't helpful. She'll spend 20 minutes on problems that only need a minute. When she is going over in class examples her explanations are all over.

Very nice person, not a good teacher. Had a lot of difficulty keeping the attention of the class. Read off of powerpoints for her lectures. IE4516 very similar to a Probs & Stats course but she rarely provided practice problems. Students will most likely get a good grade but will have a hard time learning much.
The mot genuine professor I've had, cares about his students and simply wants you to enjoy writing and improve your ability to write. Gives great feedback, if you put in the effort you'll get an A.

He's super chill and gets the work done. He made me enjoy reading and writing and has a very laid back demeanor. Class isn't hard, just do the assigned work (not bad at all). If possible I would 110% take him for first year writing.
Such a nice and helpful professor, definitely recommend. He's really funny and the assignments consist of a few projects and writing assignments.

really good teacher. Ends up having a good relationship and gets very connected to all his students. At the end of the day he just trying to make you a better writer. He doesn't use textbooks and makes the class fun and engaging. Homework wise its not bad at all, he gives like project essays every once in a while and somehow you want to do them.

The best teacher you will ever have understands how to make a class that is supposed to be easy, be easy. Shows you the most important errors you have to improve your writing. Is the funniest teacher I've ever had, fun projects, fun class videos and documentaries, overall the GOAT.

Amazing prof and such a funny and cool guy! Gives helpful writing tips, but the more you give the more you get out of it. If you do the assignments you will do well. Def take this class cuz he makes it fun and is caring towards students!

Prof. Ayala is so nice! He does not assign homework but there are some very small presentations here and there (you choose the topic). He is very flexible and understanding. Also an easy grader. Definitely recommend!!!

Professor Yildirim is a great professor in class and cares a lot about what she teaches. The grading is a bit off and can be confusing, but the material is typically fun and interesting. She is great for communicating and engaging in a fun class environment. The workload can get a bit much at times but overall great class.

So you see, the class itself is quite interesting. You may be thinking hmm I like this! That is until... you get a paper every week that is at least 9 pages. Argh. However, she tries her best and is very nice in class. The lectures are fun and all, but don't necessarily teach too much. I would recommend going tho bc it means a lot to her and is fun

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Genuinely cares about what she teaches and rewards effort.

So nice. taught super interesting material but also wanted us all to succeed. Lots of chances to get extra credit or points.

She is really nice. You don't NEED to go to class but the material is interesting and she ends early sometimes. Tests are online and open note. She is very understanding with late assignments. Cares about the topic and the students.
really chill, readings aren't too necessary to do, easy work, engaging lectures, no exams

Ayanna was amazing! Her lectures follow the required textbook but also follow very current events in our society. She facilitates great discussion in class and is very accepting and open. Professor Ayanna was amazing and understood the content to teach it. She cares about the class and is passionate about what she does. She is an easy grader and will offer you room for improvement. I do not recommend to take this course. This course is not hard to understand, but it is hard to get a high grade in the exam.

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! Go to his office hours and ask to go over tests and he will give you extra points. Very kind, funny, personable. Professor Fotovatian is okay. 2 + 2 = 5 ahh professor

Not as bad as people make it out to be. You do have to do a lot of learning on your own, but he makes sure that all the resources you need are available to do so. He can't teach. He's very uninterested in everything he talks about except personal stories. He is funny, but not forgiving in any way. Where do I start?I love this professor so much. He is always ready to help if you actually try in this class and are respectful. Class is terrible. The flipped learning setup doesn't work at all. You teach yourself everything. The professors barely explains anything in class and expects you to already know the material. The tests were harder than the quizzes, but you should do fine if you study.

He is a very good professor. The class was graded only on tests which made it more difficult but he dropped the two lowest quizzes. The in-class midterms were nowhere near as difficult of the final. I had a 97 going into the final but ended with a B because of the final even when I got 10% above the average so study A LOT for the final.

Great Professor, this was my second time taking Diff Eq's and he was so much better than my first professor. For Diff Eq's if you can't get loopi, Assad's the second best professor. Is a physics guy so if you're into that, you'll love Assad.

Assad is such a sweet guy; he is very understanding and truly wants you to succeed. 
I only took pre-calc in high school so this class was def challenging for me, but he gave us extra credit to keep our grades as high as possible before the final, which is 40% of ur grade. He drops ur lowest test grade too, which helped my grade a lot. I recommend!

Really kind and caring professor. I thought he did an amazing job explaining the concepts. His quizzes and tests were quite easy and homework was optional. Doesn't know how to work canvas at all and won't ever respond emails. Takes favorites. Super kind, teaches through examples. You honestly don't even have to go to class to succeed. Gives practice quizzes/exams that are just like the actual thing. He confuses himself a little sometimes but nothing crazy. Definitely would take him again

love the man. Calc 1 is a lot of lecture and examples w little explanation of actual concepts, but ILS lectures aren't helpful.

Very nice professor, but his lectures aren't great. He doesn't explain the topics you are learning he just does example problems on the board. So be ready to teach yourself the topics outside of class. Exams can be tricky as well.

Very nice and funny guy but your graded entirely on test scores which kinda sucks, participation isn't mandatory but he did start taking participation near the end of the semester because if you attend class he says he will bump your grade up a bit

Overall not a bad professor, he drops 1 out of 6 quizzes during the semester. He doesn't require homework but in return your whole grade is based on your quizzes/tests/final. Took Calc 1 in Fall 2024. 6 quizzes, and only the top 5 are graded. 2 midterms, 1 final worth 40% of the grade. Class was alright, very lecture-heavy, and he is NOT tech savvy, lol. Everything (syllabus, practice tests, etc) was just posted into the 'Files' tab on Canvas. Also he never has slideshows, he just writes stuff on the board. He is funny.

He seemed like a genuinely nice guy but very forgetful. I did not have him for the physics class but for physics ILS. While I got along with him well, his explanations at the beginning were a bit confusing, and he kept forgetting to grade the quizzes of students who went to the DRC for test taking. I received my quizzes back RIGHT before exams.

MATH 1241- love love love! Definitely recommend having him as a professor. Everything is super straight forward. If you go to class, pay attention, and do the practice exams, you will do well. 6 tests that are each 10%, final is 40%. Attendance isn't mandatory and neither is buying a textbook, but I would recommend doing so.

Best professor I've had so far! As long as you go to class and do the homeworks this class isn't bad at all. Lot's of the examples that he does in class are really similar to the questions on the exam and you get a cheat sheet for the exam. He's super funny and I would really recommend going to his office hours. Final was hard compared to midterms.
The Group problem is hard and he hardly ever explain it.

Physics 2 with Assad was a cakewalk over Summer 1. Super easy exams, similar in difficulty to the practice exams. Some questions on the homeworks and quizzes can be challenging, but the most challenging questions won't be on exams. Lectures are great but are very long and slow paced. Physics II Lab isn't hard, but is a time sink; some bad TAs.

Assad is a great professor. His lectures are very clear and goes through many practice problems in class. The practice quizzes and tests were exact representations of the tests and quizzes given in class. He cracks jokes throughout lecture and is very kind.

Assad is the best professor I've ever had! He makes class funny and enjoyable and explains difficult concepts really well. Outside of class I really recommend going to office hours  he is very kind and is always willing to help.
This is by far the best profession I have had at Northeastern. His study guides laid out clearly what was going to be tested on the 6 exams we had before the final.

Assad is the best. His lecture are very clear and he tells you exactly what you need to know for quizzes and exams. He does tons of practice problems that are similar to assessments. He is so sweet, I recommend going to his office hours whether you have questions or just to chat. I wish I had him for physics 2, he's truly the best!

Assad was great. He derives formulas and does primarily practice problems. He's often late to class. Has an accent, but easy to understand. He gives notes on common mistakes and drops the lowest quiz. The practice exams he posts are exactly like his actual exams. Just find the textbook online for free. Easy if you took BC and just need refreshers.

He provided the notes online and his practice quizzes closely resembled the real ones. However, your grade is entirely made of quizzes/tests -homework/participation has no impact. No extra credit was offered. He mainly wrote on the board, rarely explaining the material. He was often late to class. The average class attendance rate was about 50%.

reviews.comment: This guy does not know how to teach and at 10pm the night before final gave 2 more topics to learn

Assad was the best math professor I've ever had throughout my school life. Assad is a very caring and funny professor. I had him for Calculus for Business which is a very easy class especially if you've taken calculus before. AWFUL prof. His lectures are terrible, not clear, and all over the place. Easy A tho.

Assad is a good guy. Really funny and clearly knows the subject. He's very receptive to feedback when a student points out an error in his work. Prof. Fotovatian is a great professor. He is funny and clearly loves physics.
