reviews.comment: He always tells great jokes and keeps people engaged
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Doug made the classroom actually feel like a classroom despite the small class size. He personalized each lecture in order to make an easygoing and enjoyable atmosphere. He really made me enjoy coming to a 4:35pm class!
Doug is an amazing professor, he cares about his students and the subject matter, and he rocks. I felt cared for and seen in his class and it is a joy to be taught by him.
Funny! Very engaging and excited about the material.

Doug Bielmeier really brought his job as a mix engineer to fruition in my mind. He's very understanding of his students when they have "off-day" and doesn't hesitate to accommodate our needs to the best of his ability. He's great at answering questions in a well communicated manner and he's quite charismatic as well.
Dr. Bielmeier is the worst professor I've had at Northeastern so far.
Dr. Doug is a great teacher and his course helped me feel more comfortable in Pro Tools and learn the fundamentals of mixing and sound from a recording standpoint.
Love Dr. Dougs teaching style. Favorite at Northeastern thus far.
A really fun course if your willing to work for it. Love the way my mixes sound now.
Great teacher
Great class. Dr. Doug is great
Great course, cool teacher. I mean the guys a rock star.

I was able to learn a lot throughout the course about the history of music recording as well as numerous techniques when it comes to using microphones, and most of all, I learned how to utilize techniques in mixing such as EQ, compression, and time-based effects.

My main goal for this course was finally achieved through the completion of the final project. My goal had been to take away many basics of mixing which would in turn allow me to record performances by myself and members of my band which could then be mixed into a good-sounding final product.

I learned how to utilize techniques in mixing such as EQ, compression, and time-based effects. I was able to use all of the information gathered to work on kickstarting my endeavor into becoming a proficient mixing engineer.
Really tough and rewarding class. Dr. Doug helped me get through the tougher projects. He is a Zoom master.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was so much fun! Dr. Doug makes learning fun!

I was hoping to grow independent of reliance on a producer/engineer and to better understand the mechanisms of a DAW, and I feel that I have succeeded in taking my steps to doing as result of this course.

Dr. Doug, helped me learn the basics of mixing (such as EQ, compression, and effects) and understand how they work. I will take these skills into my own work as a singer/songwriter who wants to delve into the world of recording.
This class was so much work, but I'd take it again if I could. There was so much content and it was all from his expert incite. Can't find this on Youtube!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Doug worked hard to include everyone, and was there to help me while I was struggling.
Awesome person. Great class. He helped me release an album on Spotify of my own work. I'm glad Northeastern has him.

Seeing as the course is over, a goal that I had for the course was to get better at making sure everything feels like it's sitting in the mix rather than on top of it. I think that I have gotten significantly better at this by changing the way I EQ each track. Dr. Doug sets up the class for future producers to be successful.

Dr. Doug is perfect for students who actually want to work in the industry after graduation. In this course I wanted to learn how to go from raw audio to a finished track using volume, panning, eq, compression, and reverb/delay, and I think that I learned the basics of how to do those things fairly well.

Dr. Doug is great. One goal I had for this course was to learn more about music recording so I could apply it to my own personal, musical endeavors and continue to improve my skills. I achieved my goal over the course of the semester because I was able to take everything I learned and apply to one of my own songs for our final project.

Dr. Doug is a great teacher and his course helped me feel more comfortable in Pro Tools and learn the fundamentals of mixing and sound from a recording standpoint. When starting this class, my end goal was to be comfortable enough in protools to edit and mix my own tracks.
Not a good teacher at all.

Dr. Doug, has created a really great class, especially now in times of Covid. He also is super accessible via Zoom and Email to answer questions. Have basic computer skills for the class. A lot of students don't and they end up wasting everyone's time.
Great Teacher. Dr. Doug is one of the best at Northeastern!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not rewarding at all. Professor is not very helpful. Did not respond to emails and dismissed me when I had a question. Waste of time and money.

You can learn all of this stuff easier online and Bielmeier can be very condescending if you don't have prior experience with recording. This class is not worth your money and neither is the instruction.
Great teacher, musician, and human.

I really thought a recording class would be sort of a silly Easy A. But after studying with master recording engineer and composer Dr. Doug Bielmeier I realized how important recording is and what a specific set of skills it demands.
If you respect yourself or anything about the subject matter do not take his class. Doesn't care about students at all

Took 3301 with him. Professor Murray was the best. I truly learned so much from him. I am not one to participate in class, but it is truly necessary to succeed and get a good grade in this course. Lastly, his exams are super fair and have no multiple choice.
Best professor!!
Great Professor! Extr
bob's great. he has great speakers and interesting personal anecdotes. he still skis all the time which is insane... overall, i really enjoyed his class and my friends did too. i recommend :)
The prof is awful, I was at a high A and but my final grade was something else. He did not disclose as to what my grades are for participation and negotiation. All my efforts went to waste.
In SCHM6318, you get more than a crash course in all things supply chain, you also get the opportunity to guess how your professor wants you to write your answers!

He definitely makes an effort to make a somewhat dry subject (if you're not interested in it, that is) engaging. A decent amount of work every week, but it's necessary to stay on top of everything. Gives plenty of opportunities to ask him questions and really cares about learning.
I learned a great deal and although it is a lot of work, he is an incredibly helpful and caring professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Bob was an awesome and inspirational supply chain professor. He made a seemingly boring subject so interesting that I'm pursuing it as a concentration! We did write a lot of small case analyses which he graded fairly and quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was nervous going into SC because I heard that it was very tough, but I found Bob and I really enjoyed going to this class. He has lots of real life experience, and friends in the field that come and give guest lectures. Prepares class for the tests very well, fair grader, makes sure everyone understands the material and overall class avg was B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Bob is a great person who cares for all his students. He takes attendance and participation greatly. Learn from all the materials in class and you should end up with a pretty good grade. He brings in speakers and offered students who are interested in internships with connections.
Great class. If you are serious about learning more, I'd highly recommend. Workload is very manageable.

Bob Murray is a very down to earth, nice guy. Very much enjoyed having him as a professor- he is super intelligent, has worked in the field, is well connected and is passionate about what he teaches. I would highly recommend him and if you put in honest effort into the class, you will do well.

Methodical approach to how class operates. 1 page executive brief every week, 2 tests, and a case study presentation. He comes straight from industry holding multiple VP roles and organizes his class towards the real world. Incredibly smart and teaches you a lot. Put in a decent effort and you can get an A.

Bob is absolutely an awesome guy, both as a person and as a professor. He really is one of the good ones. He is incredibly knowledgeable about supply chain and has decades of experience in the industry, and it proves so worthwhile in class. I hope to have him as a professor once again, I've really never learned more  from a professor than from Bob.
So two faced, so fake. Shows you on side but the truth is different. Doesn't allow different opinions if they threaten hers.

presents as thoughtful but she judges you so quickly. It's interesting given her academic focus on Holocaust studies, she is so closed  minded. She tends to come across as quite authoritative, despite a softer tone in delivery. At times, her grading also feels influenced by her personal interpretations, which can make it seem less objective.
She grades based on her personal opinions.

Reading heavy, as to be expected for a theorys class. While the materials are engaging, Professor Bormann style isn't. The classes are mostly comprised of long, dry lectures. Hard to stay focused. The class being comprised of ungraded and graded parts makes grading vague. She grades on her own personal opinion. Wouldn't recommend.

Absolutely wonderful woman!! She is so sweet and so kind, yet can still discuss difficult topics analytically and with grace. You will be graded on only a few assignments, however, she gives you enough time and clear rubrics. Her class was very meaningful and I feel like I learned a lot.

Clearly cannot handle the workload of being a department chair and a POLS professor as she cannot give feedback/ grades or email back in a timely manner. You will not get anything out of her classes. I think her being the department head shows how bad the POLS curriculum is at Northeastern University.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: god awful. super annoying and boring lectures. horrible grading feedback and grades based on her own opinion
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is easy, pick 2/4 essays, groups project, final paper, and bi-weekly module posts. Personally, Prof Bormann's teaching style is not my thing. Its giving the whimsical philosophy teacher from a sitcom. Sometimes was annoying with grading/ gave vague feedback. The lectures are long but no attendance taken.

Professor Bormann is fantastic! She was frequently available for in-person or online office hours to further discuss readings, assignments, etc. She is very passionate and knowledgeable in her field and respectfully pushes students to challenge and discuss topics that might be uncomfortable.

The class is fairly simple: 2/4 essays to align best with your schedule + 1 group presentation. Professor Bormann is very kind and caring to each student. Class topics and get a bit argumentative and dark as you discuss topics of genocide (Ex: Israel vs Palestine, Turkey vs Albania) though she allows you to step out of class if you need to.

Graded on 1 group presentation, 2/4 essays, and discussions (full credit just for attending). Very easy class and you do not need to go to every class nor does the class meet every block; attendance is only taken on discussion days. She is super nice and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Natalie is an amazing professor. She gives you the option of writing two papers out of five potential options for each unit of the course. I got a concussion before spring break and she gave me nearly an extra week to submit one of my papers. She is extremely caring and empathetic to her students. Her mindfulness sessions are very nice as well.

Professor Bormann is a good professor. Her grading criteria is clear and she's not a tough grader if you follow her instructions and understand the course material. If you aren't familiar with the subjects, she is a great professor, but if you're looking for something challenging, she can sometimes go too slow. I'd recommend.

Hands down the best professor I have had, by a long shot. The class had no exams, only papers, and relied on the interactivity of the class to function fluidly. This was made easy with the amount of interactive group work that was required. As someone who has taken many pols thought classes I highly recommend hers.

Shes really nice and great to talk to. However, I felt it was a waste of time and I didnt get much out of it. I felt I didnt learn much about the topic of genocide instead just discussed it. While she is super nice, the lectures were a complete waste of time and the class was poorly set up. Its easy to get a good grade but you may fall asleep.

There were a lot of wasted class days (e.g., 3 classes on student introductions, 4 as extra office hours, etc.). The lectures and readings are repeats of one another--there is also zero primary source material. Professor Bormann is not a tough grader at all and the feedback is minimally helpful. It's an easy course but it's also a quite boring one.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. You learn a lot from her and she helps you understand the material better than anybody. Extremely accesible, will help you with any questions or concerns and makes you feel comfortable. Lots of papers and a semi tough grader, however her feedback was extremely helpful and she was always extremely fair. All in all a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Boremann is phenomenal. She is a great lecturer and clearly very knowledgeable. Not only that but she is incredibly sweet and always willing to chat and help out her students. In this class the grade consisted of 2 papers, 1 small group presentation and a final project non of which were especially difficult. Very doable and interesting class

A super knowledgable and effective scholar and lecturer. She does at times push her own perspectives almost as facts to her students in class, but that doesn't mean she's close-minded. While she may disagree with you, Professor Bormann encourages and supports her students to have their own points of view.

Here's the thing about Dr. Bormann, if she has a TA you get an easy A, if she is grading the papers herself you will have to work hard for it. Although she is EXTREMELY knowledgeable on Holocaust content, she is very stubborn to allow student points of views and ideas to succeed in papers. Being too politically correct is also her visible weakness.

Prof. Bormann is super nice, and clearly knows a lot about political science, but her Modern Political Thought class was pretty surface. Would not recommend taking if you've taken social & political phil, it's mostly the same authors. If this class is required for you though, you can't go wrong with her.

Professor Bormann is extremely knowledgeable. The thing I like the most is that she understand you take other courses and thus gives you a reasonable amount of papers for you to complete. She is nice and if you work and understand the material you definitely can get an A

Lectures are never boring, her accent and sense of humor make it interesting. Papers are fairly easy, but she can be a kind of tough grader on them. She lets you be creative with the final assignment, so if you're not a big writer there are opportunities to boost your grade.

Great professor, very enthusiastic about the subject and good sense of humor. Class wasn't hard to go to ever. She knows what she's talking about and it doesn't hurt that the class was only 4 1000 word papers
Absolutely fantastic member of the PoliSci department. Love love loved her class.

Class grade  4 papers (each 1000 - 1200 words) worth 20%each of grade and 10% attendanceparticipation. No tests, no surprises, no busy work!  One extra credit (5pt value) assignment.  Great class and professor!
Overall great teacher! Always promotes a positive and engaging learning environment. Her accent is pretty awesome.
She is so great.  She leads an amazing discussion and her accent is fun.  She is very intelligent and really encourages thinking outside of the social norm.  Love her!
Great professor, super helpful, knows what she's teaching. Also, quite funny.
She is a really good professor. She takes time to help, and is always available when you need her. Make sure you hand your work in on time and you will be fine.

She likes to pick on people and call you out in front of the entire class, but don't take anything personal. Every grade you receive will kind of feel random, but as long as you put effort in and do the homework (all mc from the textbook), you will most likely get a decent grade. She also really does not care if stuff is late.

Alma is VERY serious about deaf culture. You need to put 100% into her class or else you will not succeed. For ASL1, it can define toy be hard adjusting to a deaf professor but I think it helps with learning sign language faster. She is a very harsh grader, especially when it comes to production tests so just be aware of that.

ALMA IS THE BEST! Her ASL class is completely immersive, so you get the best learning experience. She is funny, kind, and adorable; you genuinely learn so much in one semester. The complete immersion takes a bit to get used to, but it's great. Homework is pretty easy, but be prepared to record yourself. I only have good things to say about Alma!

Alma is an incredible professor! If you had her for ASL 1 I HIGHLY recommend taking her classes again. She is very serious about deaf culture-- no talking in class, no phones, practice your signing-- but she is also quite understanding and really cares about all of her students

Alma was the best professor I have ever had! She would always take extra time to repeat something even if only one person didn't fully understand. The last day of class she went around and gave everyone hugs which made me start tearing up. I would 100% recommend taking Alma's class! ALMA IS THE BEST and you will have the best time!

Alma is a great professor! Her class is structured in a way you can fully immerse yourself in Deaf culture, and you have no other choice but to learn. It's a great learning environment, and it's a class that you must show up to. She is also very funny and wants you to learn and understand!

Alma is one of the best professors I have ever had. She has a great sense of humor and is an awesome professor. Do the work assigned and you should get an A, I recommend taking her because she really immerses you into learning the language, as she is Deaf and the whole class is taught in ASL. Don't be fooled by some of the older reviews.

Alma is great! She may come across as intimidating at first, but once you get deeper into the semester she is quite fun and caring about her students. As long as you attend class and complete all the homework, the class is relatively easy. She makes sure to adapt to students who may not catch on as quickly, and will repeat things.

Professor Bournazian is a really great ASL teacher. She is patient with beginners and always tries to make the class entertaining and fun. She is very sweet and cares a lot about her students. Attending class and doing all the assignments will have this course be a breeze. She will hold you accountable for your work and for how much you practice.

Professor Alma is the best. I read some reviews of her (on here) prior to taking her class and was a little skeptical, but she turned out to be one of the best professors I've ever had. She's very caring and genuinely wants you to learn about Deaf culture. She uses immersion which is the best technique for learning. Definitely recommend her class!

Alma is deaf so for ASL there is complete immersion but she would make sure we understood what was said. She does favor those who put effort in and are direct (as is deaf culture) and will get a translator if needed.

She was very very funny as well, and ASL was the one class that I never zoned out in as it was always engaging.
Shes amazing so sweet and funny. Yeah the class is hard but the subject itself is hard.

the deaf community as a whole are a very blunt group that is based on honesty and this can be shocking and come as harsh to hearing students. alma is a great professor who wants you to succeed and be ready for the next level. she will explain something 15 different ways until you understand and always is understanding. get out what you put in

Alma is awesome! She is adorable, really funny, and really nice. She is a great example of Deaf culture and genuinely cares about her students. It's a little tough because the entire class is in sign language and written English, but if you pay attention and go to class, you'll definitely pick up about 95% of what she says.

She is ADORABLE. I really dont agree with any of the comments.. She is very clear with all the material, I just think that ASL is hard in itself. It gets harder in higher levels, but asl 1 is WAY better with her than with anyone else. Go to class, do your work and will get an A.
Fantastic for those who care about ASL;  not so great for those who don't.  Get ready for a hard class, get ready to apply yourself, get ready to learn.

Fantastic!  She's a little bit hard, but very funny.  Always willing to answer questions and always appreciates honesty and the desire to learn.  The class isn't easy, though:  it's all in ASL.  If you're not going to try, don't take it.  You'd probably fail as well as end up on her bad side.  DO NOT TRY TO CHEAT OR TEXT UNDERNEATH THE TABLE.
Very funny, likes to tell stories but itsn't very clear. Signs fast and moves quickly. No clear order to the class or standard for the homework. Hard grader.

She is one of the worst teachers I ever had, she gives no hand outs no explanations. She is an fair grader and will make fun of  students.  Now that I am an ASL teacher and I strive to be the opposite of her.  She can be a very nasty person.
worst professor i've ever had
Very bad class. If you are interested in actually learning ASL do not take this class. Highest grade given on assignments was a B. Often explained assignments incorrectly and was not accessible

Prior to this class, I had earned and 3.93 GPA in my five years at NU.  During the class, I quickly realized I should aim for a "C." This class is HARD. Here are my tips: don't skip; study your ASL vocab; and do ALL assignments. If I had followed my own advice, I *might* have pulled an "A."  Ah well.  Alma is funny and nice but ASL is NOT easy!

Entire class is in ASL, pretty much understands you as well as you understand her...which is not so much. Sets extremely high standards for students, which are rarely met by anyone in the class. Generally nice, and funny teacher who makes class enjoyable, but very much an unfair grader. One of the toughest classes ive ever taken.
She's a very strict and fair grader but very funny and helpful.
No Comments

Alma is a great person but a tough teacher. She is deaf and rarely writes anything on the bored so be prepared to pay full attention all class long because it is entirely in ASL. This is NOT an easy class, don't take it if you plan on slacking off or you'll be adding an F to your GPA.
I really like Alma, despite her being a hard grader. She's a lot of fun, otherwise. Just as long as you don't blow the class off.
Very hard, not understanding, time comsuming, not very fair.

she was unresponsible...she didn't come to class at least 3 times and i asked her for a recommendation and she agreed to it and the day before the recommendation was due she said she wasn't going to write it..very tough grader..not very understanding or approachable

Alma is a tough but fair teacher. She expects you to work and you end up learning a lot from her. She's spunky and when you get to know her she's nice. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU WANT TO SLACK OFF.
I loved Alma!  Just take a little time to get to know her.  She really is a fun person!
No Comments

Very tough, especially at first. Funny once you get to know her, but still intimidating, especially if she thinks you are not serious. A harsh grader. Class is taught entirely in ASL, so if you don't get it at the beginning, you become lost very quickly.

11/10. Hilarious dude. Class isn't too hard. Given option to skip midterm and to stack the weight onto your final. Don't do that, as the final is a bit hard. He curves the final so no worries. Final group project is easy asf he grades lightly.

Chill and reasonable guy. Gives out random extra credit all the time. Do good on the HW assignments and study for the two exams (he lets you have a cheat sheet) and you'll be fine. Do cold call, but I actually enjoyed it. Recommend him although he does go through materials kind of fast at times.

Bogert is a great professor and clearly passionate about his work, a really easy class with him. 35% on 5-6 hw assignments 50% on a midterm and final 14% on a group pres and 1% on a reflection essay. He gives a lot of extra credit and lets you have a 1-page cheat sheet for tests. He goes thru class materials extraordinarily fast though, so attend.

Great professor, super clear and specific about what he expects and how to succeed. Attendance not mandatory but highly recommend going to every class. He cold calls heavily but it kept me on task is pretty chill. Very good materials to study/review outside of class and a good lecturer. Class is tough at times but very doable. Highly recommend
Great guy, very chill. Clear about expectations. Give out random extra credit. Very reasonable, just make sure you show up to class and do the homeworks and you'll be fine.
TRUST. He's the one

Lectures and provided class materials are pretty useful even though attendance isnt mandatory. Cold calling is a bit scary at first but it honestly helps you stay on top of stuff and is super chill (mostly to get people to follow along). Homeworks are fair and easy to complete. Overall nice prof

Professor Bogert is one of the funniest professors out there. I really enjoyed his class. You can tell he's really loves data viz! Don't understand why he has such a low rating here, but I think those students are the ones who never show up to class and clearly don't pay attention to what's going on! Highly recommend taking his class especially

Attendance is not mandatory, but I don't recommend skipping. If you go to class, pay attention, and do some light reading of materials on canvas, then you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: Idk why bogert has such a low rating, pretty sure the ppl that dislike him r fully just haters. Hes super clear about expectations from the start, the avg grades r pretty high, just PAY ATTENTION in class and youll succeed. Its not easy, but you learn a lot. Hes strict ab small things, but its js to prevent cheating. Love this prof, hes a G

Great professor, if you pay attention in class and study, the exams go very smoothly. Cares about his students' success and was very helpful. MISM2510 was really helpful in getting better at Excel and SQL (even Python), so this class was really useful for future careers in finance/business. Highly recommend taking any class with Professor Bogert.
Just pick him trust, he's chill and funny (spams the 67 joke), pay attention in class, and do the practice questions, you'd be good for the exam. He also allows cheat sheets.
Loves to punish his students, and categorizes them into "good and bad." Weird guy.

reviews.comment:
Don't feel like I learned anything but he doesn't gaf about attendance and is a lenient grader
Feels like he expects everyone in the class to already know everything
Two tests and 3 hw assignments, tests require some effort but hw graded loosely
Reading the textbooks right before test will not help(pretty sure I would have failed if he didn't curve

This course has a reputation for being tough, and I believe that depends on the student's background. Those comfortable with data and can learn software (Tableau) fast will do well, while the opposite is  also true.

Prof. and TAs want you to be successful & go out of their way to offer help.I loved this class, but understand why some find it hard.

reviews.comment: Each question on Exams & HWs are worth a lot, so it's easy to quickly lose points if you make mistakes, but it's a very easy class, so if you're attentive, it should be easy. Very lenient grader (gave everyone 100% on the project). Office Hours are very helpful. Professor was amazing! Accommodating, lovely, caring, respecting & knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly I don't know why he has such a low rating. The class is definitely hard and requires attendance (although he does post the video recordings) but he's a great professor. Provides more than enough practice to ace the exams and homework. 1 group project but easy to score in as well.

He is smart and is passionate about what he teaches, but he isn't a good teacher. He cold calls, asks hard questions on purpose, and exams are oddly specific questions that you can't answer even if you follow along in class.

Doesn't properly teach how to use Tableau,just expects you to know everything off the bat even though he made us install it for the 1st time. Super biased to his own tastes when grading assignments, if you use a color he doesnt like,he'll mark you down.Assignment criteria is terribly unclear and with the lack of actual teaching makes the class hell

I would say I was shocked by how many low rating scores he has, but I'm not after seeing how many people don't show up to his class and then expect to do well on exams. Bro literally makes it so easy for us, if you actually show up to class, he tells you past test questions (that more often than not show up on the test). Just show up, he is chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Writes his own 'textbook' readings. Explains complex technical stuff in HUMAN LANGUAGE. I love this guy. Not sure why his rating is so low, as I have had a great experience. He may lack a little bit of enthusiasm and he does cold-call, but he is a great instructor nonetheless. Just do your readings before class, dude!! They are amazingly helpful.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had so far. I had no prior coding experience and still got through it with a good grade. Yes he cold calls but that made me pay more attention in lectures which made me do well on the tests. Type of class where if you pay attention and do the work he recommends the work will pay off.

I'm shocked that Prof Bogert doesn't have a higher rating. To be fair, his assignments & exams were pretty difficult. However, if you put in the effort, the class was very fun and enjoyable. He always came prepared and is truly knowledgable about what he teaches. He also really cares about the students and just wants to see you perform your best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly not sure why he's getting so much hate. The class is difficult, but I never feel like I'm being asked to do something I'm not capable of (I had ZERO prior coding background). Bogert is a great professor, very clear during lectures. Midterm and final you get a  front+back cheat sheet. Homework is weighted heavily and difficult, but doable.

Bogert is actually the worst professor I've ever experienced. His lectures are extremely dry and boring and his exams are unecessarily specific. His grading on assignments and projects is very harsh and you have to make dashboards to the way he likes them rather than what might look good to you or others. Don't waste your money and time on him.

Just don't feel like I'm learning much compared to other professors that teach this course. I'd agree that his rating is low for many of the reasons others have stated. If you could take another professor's course definitely do. His way of teaching isn't giving at all - at least not for me and those I know who take him.

Simply expects you to know how to use Tableau, Excel, SQL, etc. already. Doesn't take into account of beginners. Lectures just go over the textbooks, nothing new being taught. When he does teaches, rarely, Tableau, Excel, SQL, etc. he teaches very quickly so you have to really focus. Assignments lack instructions. Exams are off from what he teaches

Expects you to know how to use Tableau without really teaching you. Essentially just goes over the textbook in class, again not much is actually being taught. Canvas page is unorganized and assignment guidelines are no where to be seen. Unless you are already skilled at Tableau you teach yourself basically. Would not recommend him.

He is an awesome professor! I am taking him for my second class now and he's still great. He is very good at making each homework assignment useful for our future, i.e. each deliverable is either LinkedIn-worthy or the assignment itself is some sort of competition and our participation could be worthy of a LinkedIn post.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor is extremely knowledgable about the subject and while directions for exams/assignments aren't always obvious, if you attended class and paid attention they shouldn't be a big issue. Very interesting class and a lot of practical knowledge about data visualization practices. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course lacks clarity in its guidelines for tests + tons of useless guidance in assignments, resulting in confusion. Prof barely teaches Tableau visualizations, yet expects students to do homework beyond the taught material. Also, lack of empathy and poor communication skills further hinder learning, refuse to give any study guide of the exams.

Great professor & class and you'll learn a lot. Was scared of the RMP reviews but I think it's been a good experience. Wish he had more exams that weren't weighted so heavily; It's just 2 exams & both are tough. Wish he had an outlined study guide, but just take as much from each class and reading as you can and you'll be okay.

reviews.comment: 3501 is a good class. You learn so many amazing skills. HWs are time consuming because he wants you to go above and beyond. Very doable class. Eric does a good job of trying to engage students as much as possible. I wish there were mini quizzes rather than just 2 exams that determine a lot of your grade. I would take 3501 again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bogert is a cool guy but it is really hard to follow along in lectures because he goes so fast. If you have no experience in Excel, Python, Tableau, or SQL this class may seem really overwhelming and difficult to grasp. His office hours were very limited. The class content is very valuable, but I wish there were more resources outside class.

Avoid at all costs, impossible to understand any of the material, way more advanced than what it is supposed to be. Does not take into account people with no experience in Computer Science. It will just make your semester hell

This professor teaches very fast and it is easy to get lost, plus he doesn't open the exam answers after grading so you can't see what the wrong answers were. The homework is impossible to answer if you are not a cs major. TA office hours were always fully booked and you could only book a 10 minutes spot, impossible to get answers to all questions
This man is teaching nothing in class and expect you to be an expert in the test, literally the worst professor ever
don't come unless you want an F or a D.

Harsh grader with no guidance. Expects you to know everything, and will not explain or help you on things when you're confused. His assignments are hard, and are not clear. He flys through all his lectures, which makes it hard to follow and understand what is going on.

The upsides of his Info Visualization class are that you learn valuable Tableau skills, and get useful feedback.
The downsides are that he goes way too fast when teaching Tableau and his exams questions are very specific to lectures and textbook readings. He is also reluctant to answer questions because he wants you to figure them out on your own.

I was able to do well in the class & I learned valuable Tableau skills but at the same time, the class kinda sucked. Tests weren't based on class but rather on the readings. I couldn't tell if he cared about his students bc it seems like he has really thought through his lectures but also refused to give us a study guide or anything for tests??
Lectures will put you to sleep
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class time is exclusively spent on lectures and he is a very tough grader. Is reluctant to answer questions about the case studies or tests due to potential academic dishonesty, and takes participation so seriously that he'll stand there and wait until someone who hasn't talked yet raises their hand to answer a question.

Sofia is super caring and passionate about what she teaches. She clearly cares about students. Class is very long so they do get boring but majority of the class time is used for group project work. Homework is pretty light and all group work is done in class. For an 8am 3 hour class this is ideal. she also lets us start at 8:15.
One of the best teachers I have had. great feedback, great class structure, very very very nice, and really cares about her students.
Loved this professor! She was extremely understanding and accommodating, but also pushed us when she knew we had more in us.

Couldn't say enough about how great she is. If you don't understand something, she makes sure to hammer it down so you can understand it. Full of Energy and a great teaching style. One of the better teachers at this school.

Extremely disappointed with Boyson and 4604 overall. The class lectures did not have solid structure and were not time effective. The midterm was a pretty fair exam, but the final was extremely difficult with students having no practice with questions she was asking (practice exams were useless and had no in-class examples to work off of).

Professor Boyson is easily the best professor I have had at Northeastern. She genuinely cares for her students and makes something like fixed income interesting and relevant with the news. She is a great role model for all students and I would highly recommend.

I absolutely loved Professor Boyson. Although the nature of the class was challenging, she made the class very doable. She is also a very understanding professor who wants her students to succeed and is willing to move deadlines if needed! She is an incredibly inspiring professor and I could say enough kind words about her.

One of the best professors I've ever had. She goes the extra mile to help students (both in class and career), gives interesting, engaging lectures, and makes sure to give thorough, well-explained exercises and study resources. Not a ton of work, but I learned more than in pretty much any other finance class at NU. Can't recommend highly enough.

Professor Boyson is easily the best Finance professor I have had at Northeastern. She is kind, hilarious, accessible, and extremely passionate about her work. I can't endorse another as highly. She is so knowledgable and helpful. Do not listen to other reviews on here where marketing students may have had her for Financial Management. She is a gem

One of my favorite professors at Northeastern. She really cares about the subject and is good at teaching it. Exams can be tricky but she'll tell you what is going to appear in the exam beforehand. Participation is also important.
Very hard exams

I love Professor Boyson. She is a hilarious professor, but definitely leads a very tough course. Her course was mostly based off of 2-3 tests and participation. The tests were also extremely difficult with averages ranging in the 40's-50's. BUT she really enjoys what she does, and everyone should stop by her office hours to get to know her.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I LOVE professor Boyson. I wasnt thinking of finance as a major before her class but now I am for sure going to have that concentration. She is by far the hardest professor for this class but she is AMAZING. Definitely recommend if you want to learn the material in depth but be aware that her tests are very hard.
FDB she's actually the worst teacher of all time. Makes everything so hard and asks questions on her tests that she never went over in class. Horrible teacher. Don't even think about it.

I love her! It was her first year teaching intro level, and you could tell by how hard the exams were, but she curved a lot and did so much to make sure this class was fun. I didn't always pay attention, but she always put slides and stuff online, which was super helpful for studying. This class makes you work, but she is always willing to help!

Herthe deal with her: she is extremely nice, compassionante, and cares for her student's success. Nonetheless, she expects way too much from others and does not seem to realize how insanely harsh her grading is! I have never studied as long and hard as I did with her class, and only did ok in the end. It's a shame because she could be amazing.
Really bad grader
she thinks that her class is the only one that her students are taking... too much work
very nice but much harder than investments
TOO HARD

I took investments with her and it was alright. This is why i decided to take Fixe Income with her But...it was much more difficult!!!  The maximum grade that you can get is B+... Something too low for an elective

One of the best teachers at NU. Incredibly helpful and very friendly. Her class is tough but as long as you try hard and participate she will do her best to give you a good grade. Highly recommend taking any of her courses.
TOOK HER CLASS IN THE ONLINE MSF PROGRAM. EXTREMELY NICE AND HELPFUL. WOULD TAKE HER AGAIN.
The best professor I've ever had. Love her :)
Took her in the online MBA program. Very responsive, easy to understand. Workload is heavy but, she makes it easy if you put the time in.
Excellent professor. One of the best I've had in the MBA program. She communicates very clearly, has great positive energy which helps make the class more lively, and no ego to deal with.
Shes extremely nice and cares for her students. Lenient grader, very approachable. VERY flexible! Take investments with her! Great sense of humor as well!

Awesome teacher - VERY helpful, and funny. She really likes this stuff, so she's great to talk to. Pretty easy subject as long as you pay attention. She doesn't take attendance, but if you skip class, it's easy to fall behind. Def take her!
She was awesome.  Have to pay attention and do your work, but she's fair and tries hard to get you to learn.  I've really enjoyed this class
Pay Attention and show effort and you will get a good grade...and maybe some free drinks as well
She is an amazing teacher, not a class to coast by but interesting and you will learn alot! she is always available to help you and very laid back! remembers what it was like to b a student

was excited for this class.  new teacher to the school.  fun class at times, but really confusing at other times.  not much homework.  overall, tests are exactly like the homeworks, but dont expect to coast by.

Wayyyyy too much homework for a 2 credit course. the lectures are also very long and boring. dont take unless you live and breathe sketching and drawing. please take a different class if you just need a art elective. weekly sketches are graded too harshly.

reviews.comment: Class is long, repetitive, and truly made to be boring. Do NOT take if you've had any previous art training.
Meh. I took this class because I needed an art elective and it was time consuming but not the worst. Doesn't really teach unless you seek out her direct feedback.
