reviews.comment: Gives far too much work for a 2 credit hour class. 5 weekly sketches in addition to textbook reading and reflection, as well as occasionally videos. Class is a bore, and she doesn't speak to you unless you seek her out. Grades weekly sketches very harshly. Don't take this as an elective unless you're great at drawing and willing to put the time in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Skylar Borgstrom is an awful instructor. She forces everyone to draw only her way, ignores prior experience, and grades you unfairly. Class is just two hours of mindless still lifes with zero teaching. She falsely accused me of copying photos and handed out C- and D- grades despite accurate work. This class ruined drawing for me. avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The HW for this class is 5 30-min drawings every week without exceptions for holidays. She claims that a 30 minute drawing every day isn't time consuming, but this simply isn't true. I took this class as one of my general electives because I thought it would fit well with my very busy schedule, but that was not the case.

She takes this class far too seriously and does not accept absences even if excused or wellness days. It is an introductory drawing class but she grades harshly. There was no final/final project which was nice, but the outside of class homework and writing just got so tedious and it is difficult to know whether she is happy with your work or not.

Class was less drawing-focused than expected. There were readings, weekly sketchbook assignments, weekly self-evaluations, etc. She gives good advice but only if you seek it out, otherwise she won't speak to you. It felt like I had to do the learning myself and she was just giving work. Workload exceeded what you'd want from a 2 credit class.

this class made me not like drawing anymore. assignments are repetitive & the sketchbook homework was time-consuming & did not teach me much. she prides herself on giving feedback, but most of the time her suggestions are so vague and not helpful, and when grading homework she will often give a low grade with few words instructing on how to improve

Brian is a great professor, he truly cares about students. honestly just wants your feedback of how you felt you learned and how he should improve the course. LTAs are bs and don't matter during conferences. Honestly you can do the work or not but as long as that claude map has A ranges you will get an A. Didn't hear of anyone getting below a B+

I have mixed opinions on this professor. You can honestly do all the CO problems and work on group projects and someone else can do none of that and he is well aware in documented proof and use ai for everything, and both of you will still walk out with an A. He's honestly a great guy and my favorite professor here but like come on.

Start your course outcome problems in the first week! Lejeune cares about his students a lot and he will put in much time and effort outside of class. He wants to mentor you. His office hours are a great way to work on homework with others. His lectures aren't excellent and the crossover on the homework leaves some to be desired.

One of the most caring professor I've ever had. The class is hard but it's not his fault (I mean it's grad thermo what do you expect) but he def tries his best to help you to understand the material. He's always available outside of class and super patient even if the question is trivial. Hands down good prof

Professor Brown is extremely knowledgeable. We had an opportunity to read his book in class and it was SO good. Not only does Dr. Brown ask the class intriguing questions he meets his students where they are at. He has patience, unflagging in his efforts to give his students grace in times of quiet. Dr. Brown is such an amazing professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 12 books. Endless papers. Read 150 pages/week. Tiny discussion class so you can't hide. Prof doesn't actually teach; we discuss other people's books while he sits there acting like an expert despite never offering his own viewpoint. Feels like he's learning with us but won't admit it. Conclusion: capitalism is bad. Just read Greta Thunberg at home.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: HIST2211:AMAZING best teacher ive ever had, so interesting and is SO knowledgable. important to take notes but content is interesting so its not boring at all. theres a quiz every week but he always makes it clear what the questions will be, also 2 short easy essays. LOADS of readings discussion is basically 50% of the class time so u have to read!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and gives easy tests given you take notes during class, all the questions are usually hinted on during lectures so its easy to study just that and get an A, usually just studied for the night of but he also gives plenty of opportunities to pick up your grade if you're falling behind
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This class was super interesting, but hard. There were 10 books to read, one was about 1500 pages. The quizzes were easy though because he gave us 'review' sheets with EXACTLY what he was going to ask on them. Has you write a lot of 1 page papers on some of the books, which can be annoying. But he is very concise and knows what he is talking about.

Professor Brown is a wonderful teacher! He is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches and his lectures reflect that. Definitely attend class because the quizzes are based mostly on his lectures and not as much on the reading. TA's are very helpful and knowledgeable as well. Great class!

This World History prof. is the one to take. The stuff  Prof. Brown covers is way interesting and his TA Sam is AWESOME. She is  really helpful, realy smart, and will help you any way she can. They both will. They make an awesome team and there was just so much knowledge between them - they knew everything! A great class and professor.

Great Professor- knows a ton about the subject and treats you like an adult (refreshing at this school where a lot of prof's treat you like teenagers!) Always responded to my emails within a day - I really like him.

Both Prof. Brown and the TA's are extremely knowledgeable and academic. The class wavered between average to somewhat difficult, but I can definitely say I know a lot more now then when I started the class.

This was an amazing class!  Very interesting, and the Professor really knows what he is talking about.  Definitely do not buy all 10/11 books, I got by with about 3 of them.  Take this class if you're interested in Hitler/WWII!

Probably the best professor I've ever had; he is a true professional. His knowledge of the material is great and the readings (although a lot of books) are extremely interesting and you will learn a lot from them, together with the discussions in class. If you want to learn...learn a lot about Nazism, take this class. Fantastic!

TA is extremely helpful. Professor Brown is a great lecturer and presents the information of Hitler and the Holocaust very well. His lectures made me want to attend class. It was not difficult to miss a day here and there without getting penalized for attendance. Three research papers (easy) and quizzes on the lectures. Don't buy all the books!

One of the best profs at NU. He's very passionate about the material and a genuinely nice guy. If you aren't interested in Germany/WW2 DO NOT take this class as there is a lot of reading, and attendance is strongly recommended. But if you keep up with it all, you will get more out of this class than any other... Great professor!

He was teaching a 200 level course like it is a 400 level course! Overall, 12 books to read (primary and secondary sources). You would need to submit group discussion postings, essays, and weekly quizzes (plus midterm and final).
I loved this class and I loved Professor Brown, it was always so interesting and I hope to be able to take more classes like this.
Grading is difficult! TA was grading 200 level class like 400+

Interesting class, with good lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory, since he posted his lectures online. Since Germany is his specialty, even on papers where he's asking our opinion, he's looking for students to side with his opinions. Learn what he wants to hear, and send it back at him. Still, I'd recommend the class.

not as interesting as i expected, but not a bad class. honestly, i think he just wasn't that interested in teaching it--germany is his specialty. good readings. the way he grades papers is a little arbitrary.
Awesome professor and interesting class

A very interesting class.  Lots of assingments so you get more grades.  Good teacher, clearly knows his stuff and has well prepared lectures.  A TON OF READING.  Had to buy NINE books for the course.  That was the only negative.
He is an amazing professor who cares about the success of his students. As long as you're consistent on quizzes and do all the extra credit, you should be able to get an A.

I thought this was a great introduction to a finance course, lightly covering each topic. The professor tried to engage us and is passionate about the course. There are 10 weekly quizzes (lowest 2 dropped), a final (easier than the quizzes), and extra credit. Attendence is graded on Poll Everywhere participation, and can attend any class section.

Professor Wolfe is very clearly passionate about this class clearly wants you to perform well in his class and does his best to try to make the content interesting (imo failing because it was just completely uninteresting) Most of your grade comes from weekly, fairly easy quizzes and online progress checks.

He talks to us like we're like 5 but it works when the topic is complicated. Participation is through PollEverywhere which is nice because it gives everyone an opportunity to take part in class. In the class, there are 10 quizzes and a final, two of which are dropped. If you study and understand the material the quizzes are pretty straightforward.
really passionate about what hes teaching and gives great support and feedback
Chill dude. He's the goat.

Prof Wolfe is super nice guy. His lectures are boring and I didn't really pay attention ngl, but that's finance for you. The tests are hard but as long as you study the assessments/hws A LOT you will be fine. Overall difficult class but he makes it a lot better and is always willing to help.

Super nice guy and he clearly wants everyone to succeed. Every test can be taken using excel and with a cheat sheet, but even if you don't do great on the tests, he offers lots of extra credit opportunities that go a long way.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but you're graded on participation for each unit using polleverywhere. He allows cheat sheets for both midterms and the final, and a bunch of easy points assignments and extra credit opportunities. I barely studied for this class (mostly just by making my cheat sheets) and got a solid A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice guy but the class is entirely based on Connect assignments which can be random and not reflective of what we practice in class. The midterms and final are all on Connect, and they were a lot harder than the homework we had been given or the problems we did in class.
great guy and great teacher overall
Chill guy, reasonably difficult class. I sold with my grade, but that's on me, not Professor Wolfe. Zero complaints about the guy and would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown is a great professor and definitely does things differently than most professors. She does contract grading, however, effort and participation is still expected. She is a great and engaging speaker, her classes never dragged.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Genuinely the best teacher at this school, one of the most chill, kind, and caring professors I have ever had the chance to meet. As long as you take her class seriously and put in effort you'll do well.

Nice professor, but didn't believe in the traditional "grading system". No assignments were graded and only found out my grade the day they were due on the student hub. Discussion based class and could easily make up stuff to pretend you read the readings.

Dr. Brown is by far my favorite professor I've taken a class with at Northeastern. She is incredibly knowledgeable, caring and funny! She fosters an electric and fun class environment where you actually look forward to going to class because you feel like you're friends with everyone there. Plus great insights and readings! Highly recommend

Dr. Brown is incredibly passionate about civil rights and the many problems in Western society and the class challenges thinking on several topics that plague modern civilization. She cancels class relatively often and uses student presentations or discussions to structure classes. She's not very responsive via email and her canvas can be outdated.

Prof Bruell is a really caring professor, and I enjoyed the way he structured class periods. Although it was a lecture, he encouraged class discussions, which I appreciate in a CJ course. I found the class content to be interesting, and although attendance is required, I never felt like I wanted to miss it.

Recommend anyone to take this class or any class with Bruell. Very engaging, encourages participation, and creates a comfortable space. Really interesting lectures and the homeworks are not tedious and allow a lot of freedom

Bruell is a really good teacher and lecturer. His class can be a bit boring and feel repetitive (especially if you've already done criminology in the past), but he has a talent for sparkling debates in class about various subjects. Even though participation is not graded (but attendance is, be careful), he still manages to get people engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Provides all the materials you need to thoroughly understand the material. Homework is weekly and takes some time, but not unmanageable. Midterm and final are open-book, open-note with 4.5 hours to finish (more than enough time). Be careful of the methods you use, he WILL accuse you of cheating if they aren't what you were taught in class.

Professor Bruell is a gem—engaging, organized, and deeply knowledgeable. He blends humor with sensitivity, especially on tough topics. Once, during a domestic violence unit, he bought out a student's donut fundraiser supporting survivors and shared them with the class, saying, “Actions speak louder than words."
Would do an in class assignment and day “it wasn't in depth enough” but then when more information was added, still said it wasn't enough. The length of the final was not that clear either.

He is such a great professor. I had him for CRIM 5900 online over the summer and I learned so much. The class was a lot of reading and work, but it was worth it! He is very approachable and knowledgeable. Take a class with him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bruell is one of the best professors I've ever had. He cultivates a dynamic and fun classroom environment that encourages students to participate in discussion and make comments to drive critical thinking forwards. He isn't an easy grader, but it is because he wants to see his students succeed and learn!

Professor Bruell is a great guy and a good professor.  His lectures can be a bit dull, especially if you're already familiar with the material, but nothing crazy.  He's responsive and helpful if you reach out with questions.  He's very clear in what he is looking for when it comes to assignments. Overall, I recommend this course.

This was an online summer class and the modules were organized very well. In my opinion, the grading was a bit on the tougher side, but nothing too crazy. I would definitely take another class with Professor Bruell again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Even though this grad class was online, all the modules were so organized and the discussion posts were short and to the point. Does not assign busy work and the readings are actually helpful and you learn something!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Stats-Prof Bruell has little respect for your time as a student. He makes assignments due on holidays/ breaks, and always over the weekend. The problem he is expects students to respect his weekends and holidays and won't provide any help during those times. He also cancels or pushes out a majority of appointments students make with little notice.

I really liked Professor Bruell as a professor and as a person. The only issue is he doesn't realize how intelligent he is and that we aren't at his level as grad students. I often felt he looked at topics as very easy and simple when it was far more challenging for the class to grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's nice, but he gets sidetracked and sometimes fails at refocusing the class. He does pick minute details out of vast amounts of information, so be sure you know your theories.

Excellent teacher despite being a grad student. Really cares about getting his students to understand the course material. Makes class interesting despite the dry topic. Attendance is graded based on easy short pop quizzes. One of the best.

Research Menthods can be a very tedious and boring class, but Professor Bruell made it fun and interesting! I definetly recommend him! His pop quizes were easy if you took notes and reviewed them before class & the exams weren't too bad, everything is off the powerpoints. Overall great teacher!

Professor Buell may be very young but he certainly does not run his course like a novice. He is obviously very engaged with his students, and even though the class subject is a little boring, he always tries his best to make it as interesting as possible. Even though he gives pop quizzes, they were simple. He tries very hard to make his tests fair.

He is a very smart guy and relates the material well to the students.  Very clear lecturer and there are some pop quizzes.  The research assignment is kind of a pain but not too hard.  Bruell is very fair and wants students to do well.
Very awesome professor. Really knows his stuff and keeps you interested! Wants you to do well! quizzes are a breeze and exams are not very hard either.TAKE HIM

Awesome teacher, awesome class. Has small quizzes throughout the year, but crams most of them in at the end. Has 3 tests throughout the year, so midterms and finals are only a third of the semester. Attendance isnt taken, but you need to take notes.  Book is never used, and tests are all multiple choice, t/f, and short answer
Very nice

Great professor. Uses Powerpoint lectures and a lot of discussions - always keeps the students interested. Very fair tests - just study the slides and read the articles. Pop quizzes are pretty easy, especially because he drops 2. Great class.

Good guy - although I'm not sure he grasped the idea that none of us really had an interest in criminal justice, his lectures and discussions were interesting and personal, he treated us like adults, and his tests were completely fair.  Just make sure you read the articles he assigns - he's known for a pop quiz here and there
Clear and organized during lectures, and is very concrete in his tests. It is not his goal to trick you.

He's a really good guy. I would highly recamend him. He doesn't think he is better than you and likes to see both sides of an issue. Talks to his students as peers. His classes are all powerpoint presentation, but he likes to keep the class involved with conversation. Also i never even bought the book for either of the 2 classes, hes pretty easy.
No Comments

Nice and funny teacher. very young and after getting used to things he becomes very funny. class consists of 30 minute leacture, two 3-5 page papers, and two tests. read the articles and come to class and get an A

Learned a lot from this course, but exams are HARD, and there are only 3, so doing poorly on one greatly affects your grade. The study guide lists every single concept covered, not a narrowed-down list of the most important content, which made it hard to study, given how content-heavy the course is. Don't take it if you want an easy elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good professor who is very passionate about the topic. Lectures can be a bit long, but the material is there if you pay attention. Most of the course is exam heavy, but he curves them so you should do okay. Really nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unorganized (Material for exams isn't clear on Canvas). Boring lectures (tbh I am not into environmental science, I took this class as an NU path elective, but it could've been taught more interestingly, given that so many people take it for their NU path).

Professor Helmuth was amazing! Even though I took this course for NUPath credit, I have no regrets. He is truly passionate about the topics. I will admit the lectures were a little boring, but the course load was very light. It is exam heavy, however, but he drops the lowest grade, and the exams were online and unproctored.

Prof Helmuth truly wants his students to learn & gives great examples with videos to explain concepts better during class! I wish the grading structure wasn't so test heavy with 85% being given to 3 tests and a final - Would've been nice to allocate more points to homework. Overall a fair prof that makes you work hard for a good grade in his class!

I loved taking Environmental Science with Brian! I was only in the class for my Nupath requirements, but I'm really glad I took it. Brian does a great job of making the material interesting and the amount of out of class work he assigns is super reasonable. If you need ND or AD, you should definitely take this class.

Fantastic professor. I was only in this class for NUpath credit but I learned a lot and became really invested in the material. Professor Helmuth is an entertaining lecturer and he really cares about the subject matter. Talks a lot about his real life experiences from research. Really awesome guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The course quality is top-notch, and the instruction is excellent. However, the workload is very heavy. The course entails weekly assignments, simulation labs, in-person laboratory sessions, 3 exams, and—for graduate students—an additional 4 projects. Every two weeks, students are required to spend at least 3 hours watching pre-class videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nicest professor in the world.   Inspiring lectures.  World famous researcher and scientific leader that helped guide modern era power electronics community at international level.

He's the 2012 Heat Lebron of teaching power electronics. The best professor I've had in my life. If I could give him 6 stars I would. In his life he invented and innovated with the cutting edge of the field, wining several awards and becoming IEEE Power Electronics Society President, and it shows. Go to his office hours too, he's great

Why not take power electronics with someone who is pioneer in the field,  president of IEEE Power Electronics Society,  and one of the nicest , insightful instructors in the world?  I read Princeton Review rated him one of the top 300 professors in usa.

Really excellent, knowledgeable. Top professor I've taken at the school. Material requires some reading to excel, which is seems like very few people do. Beyond that, class is not difficult relative to other grad offerings.
Lots of work. Learn a lot. Get to run experiments on solar pv and hydro. This is a course and professor worth the outrageous tuition.

By the end of the semester, I became a believer in his teaching greatness. We actually had the other Electronics instructor at NEU substitute and then everyone realized how great Brad is at teaching. Unbelievable thing: at the end of the semester he had a world famous  entrepreneur who sold his company for $1B come teach us about startups!!!
He is a ok professor. Sometimes, he talks about other course unrelated stuffs than class materials.

I do not share the enthusiasm with the other students. He is an ok professor but certainly not one of the best in ECE. He gives the initial impression of an idiot but he is extremely intelligent and sharp upon further observations. His grading is fair but you will need to put in a good amount of effort for a high grade.

Ditto to all the comments. Very clear instructor and easily approachable. No trick questions on exams. He is challenging, though.  Besides teaching the basic electronics material we got some exposure to solar energy and LEDs from his research lab.        JUST GET THIS GUY IN ANY CLASS YOU CAN, EVEN IF YOU ARE NOT INTERESTED IN THE CLASS.

Apparently, this professor can teach anything! He is better at Sustainable Energy course than the Electronic course. Take anything from him you can. This class was not easy, but I am prepared to do deep technical engineering work in the field of sustainable energy. His specialty is solar energy.

I was opposed to cloning humans until I had this professor. Get rid of the rest of the faculty and let him teach every class. I will probably switch to Electronics specialization because he gave me so much insight.

Took his class Fall '08 and he's one of the best engineering professors at NU. The way he teaches makes it so much easier to understand what is going on. Gives access to tons of past tests/problems. Genuinely concerned with how students are doing. Makes connections to real world engineering. Homework is hard but he's really fair on Midterms.
He is as good as everyone says he is. Homeworks are hard but every minute spent is helpful to learning material. By the way he gives candy out when you hand out HW.
Friendly and fun electronics. Who would of thought it possible?
Best teacher in Northeastern University

Such a great, patient, clear  and helpful instructor. I guess the girls think he is cute, but this is nothing to me(guy). Tough class, but he excites you about learning material and becoming an electrical engineer. He shows research, such as LED lights, in his class. Wish all professors taught like this. Grading is fair, though he works you hard.
Patient, funny, helpful and very organized. Cares about the students learning.
Really know his stuff, is funny, and although not easy, very reasonable. He shows respect to students and keeps attention of everyone.  Brings relavence to class material.
Great class. This is how engineering professors should teach.
Great professor! Very organized, knowledgeable, energetic, and fun.

Seems like a great professor. On his homepage he writes about how important teaching is to him and how much he cares about what he does (http://www.cdsp.neu.edu/info/faculty/lehman/teach.htm). So far it shows. The material can be hard but he tries his best.
No Comments
Great Professor, helpful.  Only difficult because of the material.
No Comments
One of the best teachers in the ECE department. Really easy going, very personal, easy to follow and understand. Take his classes if you have the opportunity.
Great teacher.  Uses good examples and relates it to real-life applications.  Easy to talk to.  Always available

Great teacher who focuses on actual student learning, doesn't give much homework, which gives you time to work on presentations. Always encourages students to be creative and push the envelope with their ideas and presentations. Cannot glaze this man and his class enough.

I learned so much about marketing in this class through actual examples. The many group projects and presentations were fun. The one issue I have is that everything is graded subjectively and if you're not the most talkative person in the room, then there is no way to get an A. However, I can look past this in light of all that I learned from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class pushed me to think outside the box further than I've ever gone before, and bring those big ideas to life in a way where I was constantly engaged and having fun with it. I highly recommend this course if you're interested in creative marketing, but be ready to challenge yourself to think differently

He said "Malaya... or whatever her name is..." when talking about Malala.

He also said to forget sustainability and the environment because marketing is more important than using recycled plastics.

Butler is a great professor if you want to be pushed to think outside the box and challenge yourself in a new way as a brand marketer. I enjoyed the semester project and his lectures. My biggest issue is his unfair grading scale that is extremely demotivating to students who spent so much time and money on this class to meet his expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For MKTG 3720: Professor Butler is a great guy who really cares about his students. The class is structured very loosely, and can be kind of abstract at times. A lot of this class can be boiled down to if you have a good group that's willing to put in work to create a good final product. However, the class is interesting and you can learn a lot.

Great Professor who cares about each student. Case every week and 2 presentations during the semester with some lectures. you don't know your grade until the end of the semester but he really emphasizes participation and being engaged in class. Great class if you want to go into marketing but, it is a lot of work. Couldn't recommend enough!
great guy, had him in spring 2025

Pretty good professor. He has this handbook that forms the basis of much of the class, and unless you follow it perfectly, he doesn't really like it. He uses a contract to base your grade so, so long as you do the work and do it the way he wants you are guarenteed the grade you asked for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend taking him for ENGW1111, as long as all the work you are contracted under is completed you will mostly receive that grade. Is super nice and caring while giving great feedback to his students. Loves to hear about your passion for certain topics.

He was super caring and really easy to talk to. If you ever have any concerns, you can talk to him right after class or send him an email and he'll respond quickly (within a day). His grading is different from high school English, but he outlines his grading system within the first week and I honestly preferred it over traditional grading.

Genuinely one of the best professors Ive had, I really hope I get him again for more advanced courses. Sometimes Id head to the classroom early to use the empty space to study, and on days when he'd arrive early as well we would talk about all sorts of funny and interesting stuff. He's awesome, please take him, pay attention and you'll learn tons.

Literally such a caring professor who just wants everyone to enjoy the class and succeed. If you show up and participate (even in little ways) you will do just fine (obviously also complete the assignments). I loved going to this class because no two classes were ever the same from different discussions to new takes on writing. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I highly recommend taking Prof. Bushnell's class! Not only is he a passionate and caring teacher, but his grading criteria is clear from day one. He is helpful and accessible outside of class, and the material discussed in class is engaging. I learned more from this writing class than any other Writing/English class I've taken.
Take Jeremy! He really cares about you and cares about your grades. It's hard to do badly in his classes. Just show up, participate and you'll be fine.

Bushnell was the most caring and sweet professor -- honestly a life saver with his grading policy. As long as you do the work assigned and participate in class you will do well. Highly recommend taking first year writing with him!

Bushnell is super nice and cares about his students. The criteria to get an A is to literally do the work. As long as you submit the papers you get an A. There was a decent amount of time to write each paper and the class never felt like a burden. Would definitely take him if you have the chance.
Professor Bushnell is an awesome. He will give you an A if you participate in class and put effort into your work. He was a real life-saver this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor was very nice and understanding. Made class somewhat enjoyable. Clear grading criteria, so pretty easy to get an A in the class. Only three big papers in the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Bushnell is a super cool guy. He's passionate about his field and he really wants students to succeed in their writing. The class is based on students attempting to get their work published and he takes a realistic approach to the publishing world. We workshop a piece written by everyone and explore other writers works. would recommend

Professor Bushnell is not worth taking for advanced writing within the disciplines. He is not knowledgeable in the business field and has you work on assignments that are not relevant in the business field. He is nice but can be a jerk. He is not clear about what he wants from students at all - take with someone else or take the class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He appears to care about his students, but if your interest do not overlap with his you will struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bushnell is a great english professor who teaches well and is also not a harsh grader. His assignments aren't boring and tedious since you get to choose your own topic to research and write about. As long as you follow the guidelines for the major assignments, you'll do well. He also gives good feedback so you can improve as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I didn't learn anything from his class, but he is incredibly clear about what he wants in your papers. It came down to a formula, and once you figure that out, it's easy to get a 100 on every one. Didn't enjoy the class, but you could choose most of your essay topics which was nice. My writing suffered, but give him what he wants & get a good grade

Seemed to know what he was doing, was clear in teaching and his standards, but was a pretty tough grader and it seemed a bit rigged at times. Didn't really take away much from the class. Not a bad teacher, just very forgettable and if you want a flat A you will need to both do the busy work and really know what he's exactly looking for on papers.

He is a nice teacher but I personally felt that he did not give the appropriate amount of feedback for the grades he would give. He tells you that you are doing good but keeps giving you a grade that does not reflect that.

Professor Bushnell is great! He is always looking to help you and if you go to his office hours he definitely will help you a ton! Participate in class a lot, keep up with the minimal readings he assigns, and hand  in the three papers on time following the rubric and you'll be fine. He is my fave english teacher ever and is super fair! Love him!

Jeremy is a great professor and super nice guy, really funny. The class itself is interesting, as well as helpful (if you're looking to get into publishing or be a writer). His assignments are pretty straight forward, not hard if you do them... The classroom vibe is really chill. I highly suggest taking Pub. Arts with Jeremy if you can!

Prof is very well informed and a consistent, straight forward teacher! Go to class, do the PollEverywheres and Quizzes, & review them before exams and study with classmates. Make friends and sit with them so you actually go to class and lock in since his lectures are a bit monotone and content heavy. Go to office hours and ask questions after class
Great teacher and lecturer. Plenty of opportunity to boost your grade with extra points for TRACE evaluation, drops the lowest quiz grade, and weighs your two best exams the highest.

Ngl this is a test-heavy class, taking up a big portion of your grade. But I personally found his lectures engaging and interesting. He does repeat stuff, but it reinforces stuff you need to know and makes the material stick. He's also super nice, so if you reach out to him with any questions, he will really help you and give you good guidance.
Even when you think you studied enough. It's never enough.

He knows his stuff, but his lectures are extremely boring and dry. He also has zero leniency in his syllabus, so if you get sick for more than three days or have a family emergency, your participation grade is tanked. Tests are difficult and he doesn't answer any clarifying questions during the test. Not the worst professor, but avoid if you can.

Bunce is overall not a bad teacher, but his lectures are so boring. He is redundant while lecturing, and I honestly learned better just watching the videos he recorded. Tests are all 50 MC questions and were not too bad. The class isn't that difficult, but I wouldn't take this class with him if your teacher being engaging is important to you.

Prof. Bunce is kind, caring and very knowledgeable who genuinely wants students to succeed. The course has 3 open response exams (lowest weighted less), 6 reflection articles (lowest dropped) and poll everywhere attendance with 2 drops. If you put in the work, you'll do well.

My complaint with Dr. Bunce was that his lectures were boring and very slow paced. All of his lectures are recorded which was really helpful. There are 3 exams, the lowest scoring of the 3 he weighs the lowest, he drops one quiz grade, and gives 1% extra credit at the end for trace. This gives you plenty of opportunities to get a good grade.
He is a great guy, and the class is easy enough if you are a behavioral neuroscience major. But im sorry, the lecture are a bunch of repeated information that makes me disengage.

A lot of materials in a semester, but exams were okay as long as u put in adequate effort. He also gave out 1% boost for your overall grade for completing the trace evaluatio,n which I think is very generous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't encourage people to take this class unless necessary. Lectures are uninformative but mandatory. I had to teach myself the content before each exam. Incredibly harsh grader and gives no extra credit. Grade is 3 exams and 6 reflections. He's a nice guy, but this class was unnecessarily hard. @BNS students: take a different BNS core.

Theres so much content to learn esp. if you havent taken and bns classes before. Bunce is super passionate but I couldnt keep up with him and there was so much to memorize. Your grade is only composed of quizzes and exams so theres not a lot you can do to raise your grade. Attendance is also mandatory. Great guy but a lot of content to learn.

Professor Bunce is very understanding and an excellent lecturer. Getting an A is attainable if you're willing to put in a lot of work. He films all his lectures on Panopto (very helpful), and all of the questions on the Test can be found in the lectures. However, you will need to rewatch every lecture before an exam to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is super passionate about what he teaches. His exams are based on lecture material and he is a very fair grader. Your effort in this class corresponds to your grade. Bunce is supportive, kind and accessible outside of class. Wants the best for his students. Material can be complicated, so go to class. Great for BNS students.

Dr. Bunce is honestly too disliked, he's great. Tries so hard to make class engaging even with dense material. Wants students to do well. You have to actually come to class to succeed, but if you pay attention and study the exams should be pretty fair. Weekly quizzes and poll everywhere help buffer grade so it's not just exams.

If you don't memorize each slide (and each midterm is about 80-90 slides each) you are cooked. All of his questions are so specific and he gives no other opportunities to raise your grade, even when half the class (I'm not joking) get below a D.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is a great professor. He explains things clearly and thoroughly and welcomes questions. Exam questions are heavily borrowed from weekly quizzes and PollEverywhere. Your grade is almost entirely based on exams, but he weights your lowest one the least. Attendance is via PollEverywhere, you can miss 3. Lectures are recorded.

Dr. Bunce is great! Exams are extremely fair; mostly all content comes from lectures, and pay attention to what he says (and not just the words on the slides). You don't really need the textbook content for the exams, maybe 1 or 2 questions (I would still skim it though). I personally enjoyed his lectures. Learned lots of useful information.

Professor Bunce is wonderful. His neuroanatomy course is moderately fast-paced, but he always reemphasizes important concepts. He is encouraging, and he provides you with everything you need to succeed (like recording all the lectures!). He is also helpful during office hours, and his tests are very fair. I hope to take another class with him soon.
He is really fun and a generous grader. He tends to go on tangents during lecture but they are usually pretty interesting. His office hours are super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce reads from a slidedeck, resulting in boring, monotonous lectures. On the bright side, his tests are an easy 50 MCQs that are pulled straight from the slides. I would take him again for the class, even if it is a little boring.

This man talks A LOT. Sometimes it does also feel like he grades based off of a set grade he decides to give you (I've lost points on tests and gone to office hours and he has said that I got the right answer but didn't answer it how he wanted me to even though he says we can answer it however). He does seem interested in what he teaches though.
He looks evil. PPT not designed for self-study-iers, class good, not boring

- lectures can sometimes be boring and material is made more complicated than necessary 
- exams are not too hard if you put in the effort and study (taken from slides and lecture)
- material is interesting and he is very clear when communicating the material 
- Good prof. and if your willing to put in some effort you will do in the class
professor bunce literally bombards students with information

He is a great professor thats passionate about what he teaches. Sometimes his explanations of pathways are a little rocky but then again they aren't easy so its not his fault. Can get caught up in tangential discussions which is good if you are curious but can be boring for some.

Bunce is probably the nicest person I have ever met. He clearly cares about all of his students and wants them to do well. Sometimes his lectures feel like a lot, and he can be monotone at times, but all lectures are recorded, so you can review anything you did not catch in class. The tests are multiple-choice, and no textbook is needed.

Nice teacher, lectures can be monotone and dry, but its valuable information condensed and made easier to understand. Lectures are recorded so it's easy to go back to if you miss class. Exam questions are pretty straight forward if you study the material. If you go to his office hours, he is very supportive and will answer any questions.

Professor Bunce is clearly a very knowledgable and passionate member of his field. His lectures can be pretty dry, but he's always excited to answer questions. I would say to make sure you are actively listening, because his tests often have material that he doesn't put in the notes. Despite that, tests were very fair, not necessarily easy though.

Professor Bunce is great! While his lectures themselves can be a little dry at times overall the course material was interesting and his exams are super fair as long as you study. He is really accessible both at office hours and via email and overall is just a really nice guy!
He is pretty good at making long, information dense lectures bearable. However, your entire grade is based on 5 multiple choice tests.

Professor Bunce really cares about his students and has a strong passion for neuroscience. Lectures can sometimes be a lot to take in, but if you visit office hours, he'll help clarify any ambiguous topics. Exams are very fair; there aren't any surprises. Overall, a great professor.

Absolutely loved Professor Bunce and his Neuroscience of Aging class. His quizzes and exams are easy as long as you show up to class and review the lecture slides beforehand. Overall a great professor, you could tell that he was really passionate about the topics we discussed in class and was very, very helpful when I went to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bunce is very knowledgeable. The lecture slides are all posted on Canvas but most of the information isn't summarized in the slides, so you have to take good notes in class. Always posts lectures on canvas. Moves pretty fast, but repeats info a lot and answers questions. Pay attention in class, study/do the readings, and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Bunce is great! He knows his stuff and is clearly into what he teaches. He is super organized and has very clear expectations- great class would take one with him again :)

Prof. Bunce is a good guy. He's passionate about neuroscience, and you can tell in his classes. His lectures can be drawn out and repetitive at times, but he gets across the information. Grading rubrics are important, and he sticks to them. Tests are very specific but doable, so be ready to study to know all the information.

Dr. Bunce is a nice man and seems to care about his students, but if I'm being honest Neuro of Aging with him gave me a headache. He goes on super long tangents in class and then expects you to know stuff he mentioned once for the tests. Overall I found him super confusing, but at least he was easier on the poster project and write ups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Had Spring 2020 so half online. OH MY GOSH the lectures are so boring. Do not be sleep deprived or you WILL fall asleep. Counter that with the fact that they are PACKED with information, and every detail will be tested in the quizzes (50 multiple choice questions). Grade is completely made up by quizzes. At least he records every class.

Prof. Bunce is well knowledgable and whatnot but I honestly find him irritating. He makes the material seem more complicated than it is which makes me anxious, and his tone makes him seem stressed out as well. He can spend the first half of class outlining what we did the class before. Tests are multiple choice and can be tricky.

I really enjoyed the content of this class but get ready to study a lot. No hw. 3 exams, 3 quizzes, if you don't do well, your grade will suffer. Definitely rewatch his lectures to study because some questions relate to very small parts mentioned once. If you memorize well, you'll do fine. I liked Jamie despite it all but I get the boring part.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man's class made me want to switch majors. In fact, my roommate DID switch majors after taking his class. He is dry in his lectures and will put you to sleep. His tests are all MC but there are few of them, so if you bomb one you're screwed for the rest of the class. I actively avoid taking him as a professor for any other class.

Professor Bunce's Biopsychology class is incredibly boring. His lectures are dry and full of information. His multiple choice tests and quizzes are specific and very challenging. The questions do not seem representative of the material covered in lecture. I would not recommend this, at it was by far the hardest PSYC class I have taken.

One of my favorite professors at Northeastern. Material can be tricky but he is a very fair grader and not hard to do well in his class as long as you study before exams. Everything you need to know for exams he posts on Blackboard. He also posts all of his lectures on Tegrity so attendance is not mandatory. He really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing and clear lectures. He is the best lecturer I've had at Northeastern. You need to attend or at least watch the lectures online. The material is not easy and a bit complex, and you have to show you understand it in the exams, but if you watch the lectures and read the papers you should be fine.

I had Bunce for Neuroscience of Aging and Biopsych and I really enjoyed his classes. As long as you pay attention during his lectures and take notes, you will do fine! He's super nice and willing to help and it's not hard to figure out what he is looking for on tests.

Boring.

reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Carey could get judgemental of students and she often targeted me in a class of 15. I enjoyed the content of the class but not her.
She's one of the nicest and most caring professors you will have.

Professor Noland seemed awesome at first and then as the semester continued I began to hate her. She is condescending, opinionated, and if you do not agree with her she embarrasses you in front of the whole class. Would not recommend this class to anyone.

I took the course prior to it being made a Writing Intensive. Carey is very opinionated, but admits when she is wrong or if you have made a good point. Relies entirely on readings posted to Blackboard and attending class is a must. If you do the readings and attend every class, you never have to study for her exams.

Carrie is awesome, you'd expect her to be a very easy grader because her lectures are always so informal and light, but she grades pretty strictly. She's very very dedicated to teaching and is very kind and funny. She can be a little disorganized and unclear, but she will no doubt be one of your favorite professors.

Noland is really witty and you can tell she knows what she's talking about.  The lectures range from interesting to not so interesting depending on what the topic is, but she at least always sounds interested while she's talking, and that helps a lot of times.  She's good about helping you when she can.

She is a nice teacher, but she's very disorganized and can never tell you exsactly what you need to do.  She's terrible about facilitating discussion, and doesn't give good feedback.  Sometimes she'll skip a whole section because she can't figure out how to word it.

Probably the best teacher I have had.  Her stories are funny, helpful, and on-topic.  She is fun but also a good teacher.  I learned a lot from her and switched concentrations because of her.  She is generally a fair grader, but does pick favorites.  Of course, her favorites are the kids who work hardest, so it makes sense.
good teacher

Awww she is great...wonderful professor...for the most part in her class you get what you deserve but she is such a great teacher that it makes you want to study hard on your own, just to keep her happy. I reccommend this class to you.
Great professor, really nice and helpful.  Fair grader.

Not helpful at all, unclear with the projects, chooses favorites and pretty much fails the people she doesn't like, no helpful comments even when I came after class and asked her specifically about the project and what I did wrong. I SWITCHED OUT of my major because of her.

i love professor noland; she's really friendly and made me feel comfortable in the class (cause usually i'm a very shy person). i don't think she's a tough grader; i think she's pretty fair; she makes the class incredibly interesting with the best stories; i highly recommend that you try to get into her class ... you won't regret it!
No Comments

I loved Careys class so much, she was really a wonderful teacher that I'm taking another class with her next semester.  She's a tough grader, but fair, and I really like her as a person. So far, my favorite professor at NU.
No Comments

Carey is an awesome professor in the sense that she makes the class exciting and fun. She's interested in hearing our stories and experiences whilel tying it into the class material. The only downside is her tests are hard and she's a hard grader. Otherwise, she's a great teacher!

Prof Noland is really hilarious and is able to keep a really casual atmosphere in class. I wasn't interested in OrgComm at all before, and I really enjoyed the class.  One downside: she doesn't give very good feedback.  Kind of nods her head and moves on to the next person.  That's discouraging.
No Comments

Course was hard but she grades very easily. You can tell that she would much rather be doing cosmetic science and not gen chem.. Very sweet person, not the strongest teacher, she mainly just reads off of the slides and if they're difficult to follow you're cooked.

Sweetest and friendliest professor but her lectures were long, fast, and difficult to keep up with. Be prepared to relearn most of the content independently before exams—which make up almost all of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a sweet person; she does the best job possible at condensing a dizzying amount of content into one class. Her lecture slides are clear and she provides plenty of online resources in Canvas. Two tests and the final make up the majority of the grade in her class, with a few comparatively small, low-stress assignments/extra credit opportunities.

The course in general was long, but she has lecture heavy slides everyday. Make sure you are VERY familiar with each days content as it goes quick and she does not slow down. Her practice exams are very different from her actual exams. Nice person.

Prof. Cassano is very nice but you will need to put in effort and work hard to pass this class. There are only two midterms and a final exam that determine your grade. She only gives five homework assignments, which are not even about the chem hw . This class covers two semesters worth of material in one semester.Slides are easy to understand.
Very lecture and test heavy, but amazing class and very caring professor!

Dr. Cassano is not only knowledgeable but extremely passionate about chemistry. She made accelerated gen chem in one semester easy with her organized chem lectures and wide access to practice problems and resources. She is so nice too!

Probably one of the best teachers I've had. Lectures and slides are so clear and in-depth. Both walk you through examples step by step. Made accelerated gen chem genuinely enjoyable and somewhat easy. She posts all her slides, resources, practice problems, and textbook (for free) and her Canvas is super organized. Wish she were at Boston campus.

He's a nice guy but hilariously poor communicator. At one point I reached out to him 3-4 separate times for feedback, both in person and online, and he just never responded. For the final exam, he had "technical difficulties" preventing the questions from being released on time. Don't take his classes if you can't handle frustration well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super interesting guy and really interesting class. He's definitely very passionate about philosophy and it shows. He's kind of intimidating especially when he follows up with a question on you during class discussions so unless you know what you're talking about don't raise your hand because you'll sound slow when you can't respond.
Awesome guy. If you're interested in philosophy, you'll love him. Not too much work either.

Class was online/async w great vids made by another professor. Prof Caouette was extremely difficult to reach outside of class(ignoring emails, not sending zoom links). Did not grade a lot of content until the end, gave grades without a rubric or explanation-in my opinion graded a little harsh for not offering us any direct advice or contact.

It is async so be ready for a lot of homework. The class is mainly weekly canvas quizzes and papers. A lot of writing, but as long as you try and follow the guidelines its not too difficult, just takes time. He is a very nice professor and much easier grader than syllabus makes him out to be since that is written by the course coordinator, not him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a good and engaging lecturer. The class is pretty easy, and there isn't much work aside from a couple of group projects and the final. Participation is a pretty decent bit of the grade, so as long as you are regularly speaking in class, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: best professor so far, super funny and engaging, speaks very confidently. philosophy content gets a bit boring sometimes but he makes it interesting. tests are moderately difficult, memorizing takes a bit of time. grading criteria is not clear, but he is lenient and reasonable with grades. wish there were versions of him for other of classes.

He's a pretty easy grader, I think the lowest anyone got on our final was a 13/15. Participation matters and it's a pretty big part of your grade. The first half of the sem was lectures and the second half was a group project and each class was ppl presenting, very chill guy, makes topics relatable, good prof.

Professor Caouette is just all around a great guy. He's really passionate about what he teaches, and he uses examples from his life to help you understand the ethical theories covered in class. I recommend sitting in the front row because it really forces you to participate, and participation is 20% of your final grade!

Professor Caouette likes to experiment with some of his classes, so your in-class experience may vary. Nevertheless, if you like philosophy he is a great teacher to have. We had a lot of readings to do, but even though these are "mandatory" nothing happens if you don't. You spend a lot of time debating with him and your peers, which is very fun.
Definitely was my favorite class last semester! His lectures were very interesting and he was super nice, participation matters a lot but I would definitely recommend this course.

Participation means a lot so try not to miss and be sure to raise your hand. Prof C is caring, funny, and down to earth. I took hom for Moral and Social Issues in Health Care and he always had cool case studies and examples. Presentations take up most of the class time after the midterm and I actually learned a lot from the class discussions.

I took this class for my moral reasoning requirement and I really enjoyed it! He is very nice and cares about his students. First half of the semester had almost no work outside of class, and the second half was weekly readings, a group presentation, and a paper. Midterm and final were exactly like he said they would be. Interesting class overall!

Caouette is such a personable and caring (not to mention downright hilarious) teacher that no matter what the class content is, you'll enjoy just being in class. A lot of your grade is just showing up and participating, so I'd suggest you do that. The grading is strict, but the assignments are easy. Just talk in class, and you'll be fine.
Awesome professor, encouraging and relates to students when participating.

He would post modules days after he was supposed to and all course material was created by a different prof--it was obvious he didn't care about the course. He didn't grade any papers until after the semester ended, so I spent the whole term not knowing where I stood grade-wise. He showed literally no interest in the course or his students at all

Regarding Research Ethics online -
The prof was inaccessible and only gave a grade for 2/11 of the papers I submitted throughout the semester despite these papers being 80% of my grade. I basically never knew my true grade until I randomly received an A days after the semester grade submission deadline. But, I got an A, so take this as you will.
He's very nice and grades fairly easy. He will automatically like you if you participate in class often, and he will also grade easier on you because he knows that you pay attention in class.

Always challenges your opinions because he wants you to grow. Heavily discussion based. Cares for his students and is understanding. Group project with partners that ends in a presentation. LOTS of reading. get on his good side and your set for the class. don't get on his bad side.

Took him for a summer session. First half of class was him lecturing, the second half was presentations. I liked both tbh. Chill guy, fair grader, and thought-provoking discussions. I would def take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Caouette's class was super interesting! The first half of the semester was focused on him lecturing on ethical theories, and the second half was class presentations on essays. The class is extremely discussion heavy, but participation really only counts in the second half of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is mostly lecture and discussion for the first half of the semester, but the second half is structured around group presentations and discussion that you definitely have to participate in. Dr. Caouette is super chill and wants everyone to pass- midterm and final exams were exactly as he told us they'd be, but final paper was poorly worded

Love this class! Professor Caouette is hilarious and very personable. Discussions are fun and very interesting. You do have to read a lot, but the readings are interesting and really make you think. Prof really cares about his students and wants us to learn.

Prof is super easy to talk to, explains everything we go over and what exams/papers will require in detail so you know exactly what to expect. Incites great discussion in class. Super enjoyable which makes the class feel easy. He makes everyone feel comfortable. Class is VERY discussion heavy.

Justin Caoutte is one of the worst professors I've ever had. He goes out of his way to be pretentious and speaks condescendingly to students, as if they should already know the answer to their question or it is not valid. He talks entirely way too much and mainly about himself during our class period. He speaks in a rude tone. good luck...

Cool prof. He really made me question my own justifications for many of the positions I held and he did it in a nice way. Super inclusive environment and many different students (with different views) spoke up and I learned as much from them as I did the prof. His teaching style is really cool and I always looked forward to going to class.

I really enjoyed Prof Caouettes class. He is extremely engaging, really nice guy, and cares about his students. If you participate in class and pay attention to material, youll do well. Definitely not an easy A, as the cut-off is 95! Cons - 1165 didnt really focus on healthcare, was more generic philosophy, and class went long almost everyday.

Took this class for my philosophy requirement and hated it. Spent the first six weeks learning useless theories & the second half of the class regurgitating other philosophers' works and discussing them, all of which felt very irrelevant to the goals of this course. Heavy emphasis on papers at the end, terrible communicator, & posted things late
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class as part of my ethics requirement and regretted it so much. The conversations often go out of topic, and you have to write so much in this class. The things he teaches are not really going to help you in the future, and there is just so much reading and writing. An A is also from a 95, which is nearly impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Caouette is a very human professor. He understands the worries you're having, he grades in a very fair and logical way, and he wants to have genuine discussions and debates with his students. I would take any of his classes again in a heartbeat. If you attend classes and think about the questions outside of class a little bit, you'll do fine.
Passionate prof. Seems like a genuinely nice guy. Took a while to grade things but otherwise I really enjoyed him. Gave me lots of things to think about overall. Id take him again if I could.

Professor C is very passionate about this course and knows the topics inside out. However, no feedback was given in the class, and most grades were posted after the faculty deadline. He canceled many of our Zoom lectures, and rarely adheres to his timeline/posting materials. Overall, he is a good professor, but a terrible communicator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Everything is impossible with this professor !!! Extremely disorganised, never on time for anything, you either have no work at all or you have 3 essays in a week. No feed backs were given, no grades until the very last minuet.

She is very nice, but the language barrier is an issue. When she's lecturing or explaining something, what she says sometimes doesn't make sense, or she'll pronounce something so that it sounds like a completely different word. The exams are impossible (on stuff we didn't learn); the class average for the final is literally a 65%.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is honestly not bad at all if you attend class and pay attention because she goes over EVERYTHING and how to do absolutely everything that can possibly on the exam. This class is very midterm and finals heavy because of how little points are in this class. I would not call this class hard if you just simply attend class and participate.
Cao Fang is a great professor, most of the assignments and tests are on the computer and she will randomly call on people from time to time for participation.

Professor Fang is easily one of the best professors ive had at Northeastern. She shows up to class every morning with so much energy and a smile on her face. She respects her students and makes the class actually fun to go to. she uses great analogys and I feel like her grading style is extremely fair. Her class is fit for real life .

My favorite class at Northeastern. Brilliant professor, Jonathan challenges you in incredible ways and gives amazing feedback for you to grow as an actor. If your class takes it seriously, you can make the most fantastic friends and build a great community. Expect to give this class more time out of your week than you think. Lots of group meet ups!

Johnathan genuinely cares for all of his students. He makes the class feel welcome for all and does a great job providing feedback. He is strict in his attendance policies, but if you go to class and participate, you should do just fine. He understands that this class isn't built for acting majors and teaches you more than you expect.

He truly cares about students and the subject.

However the pacing of the class is a bit weird with some weeks being very heavy and others with nothing. 
A lot of your grade could depend on your scene partner and their willingness to put in time outside of class.

Needs a lot of time outside of class. around 5 hours a week

one of my favorite professor's i've had. be warned if you are with him for intro to acting that even though the first half of the semester is pretty light on assignments, you are expected to put in quite a bit of time and effort into midterm/finals which might be rough for some who have tighter schedules
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I love having Jonathan as a professor! He made class fun and engaging. There were a lot of readings but if you don't do it/skim it, you'll be fine. He's a harsh grader but is still pretty understanding. If you come to him with problems, he'll understand and try to come up with solutions. Great guy and great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Carr is funny and engaging. I loved learning with him; he is flexible and emphasizes more on the material than the assignments, which is really helpful for actually being willing to learn. I would recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: His grading criteria and workload are not suitable for an intro course. He not only considers attendance but also records the number of times you speak in class. If you don't like speaking in class, you're out of luck. You even have to write an essay after completing 18 questions in the final. His course is much more difficult than it should be.
He's a great professor but an awful grader. If you just want to learn stuff, take his class. If you care about your grades, then don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Jonathan's class. You can tell how much he cares about his students and puts his all into the class. I felt it was an easy and stress-free class while enjoyable and learning a lot from it. I'm a theater person which obviously helps but I think anyone with a small appreciation for the arts will enjoy the class and do well.

Loved his class! Johnathan was is very passionate and genuinely cared about our own passion, goals, and success. While he does have his own way of doing things, if you keep an open mind about it and actively pursue improvement, you will gain so much from this class.

Professor Carr is a very arbitrarily hard grader. You must act in such a specific way that the enjoyment of acting just disappears; there is no room for creativity at all. It feels like you must be "on your game" every day, or you're bound to not succeed in this class. This class leaves little leeway to those that are introverted. Don't take.

Teaches the intro to acting class in the weirdest ways, allowing almost no room for other ways of learning how to act. It's like that one math teacher that forced you to do every step her way in middle school, and his grading is another level of nonsense. Feels like he stretches the tiny mistakes you make into taking off points. Don't take him.

Super nice, super good at actually teaching the content and you get to see a lot of cool plays in this class. Kind of weird how specific he can get with grading stuff sometimes, some of the grading can seem arbitrary. Likes things done exactly how he tells you, which in a theater class doesn't leave a lot of room for creativity of presentation.

Jonathan is a very nice and interesting professor but he's a harsh grader for an intro level class that anyone can take. If you don't write the papers exactly how he imagines It should be written he'll give you a bad grade. The final group project is also rather advanced for an intro level class. Beware if you're looking for an easy NUPATH.

Jonathan is amazing. I've worked with him on theatrical productions before, but this class was great too. He knows theatre as well as anyone and is more than effective when teaching it. He's sometimes a little less than receptive to outside opinions though. If you don't write your papers the way he would write them, your grade won't be as great.

I have taken two classes with Jonathan now and loved both of them. He was always very clear and helpful inside and outside of class. It isn't unusual for him to respond to your emails within the hour if you need his help. As far as grading, he makes it extremely clear what he expects from you but  wants you to excel at it. Great no nonsense prof.
Best class I've ever taken

Probably the friendliest and most approachable prof at NU. He really knows his stuff and wants you to improve as an actor. He tries his best to make the class fun, which I thought it really was. As far as being a tough grader: If you complete the assignments as required and put in rehearsal time (which shows in your scene) you'll do well.

I love Jonathan. Yes, you have to give him a lot for you to give you a good grade, but you want to give him all that you can. Participation for this class is everything, but you can't be in an acting class without expecting to act. There is a significant amount of rehearsal expected outside of class, but only in the second half of the semester.

Sure he grades you on participation, which can be annoying, but it helps to keep you involved in the class. Jonathan is one of the nicest and most lighthearted professors I know, if you ever don't understand something or if you want to get more involved in theatre he's ready to help.

Jonathan was an amazing professor with an obvious passion for the class and the material. He is extremely fair in his grading. He expects you to bring your best to class everyday. Minimal assignments but each is worth a large part of your grade. Text book seems useless at some times but overall the class was very enjoyable.
The class is fun and you do meet nice people, but the professor is a very strict grader and demands participation. Would not recommend that you take him.

there are quizs based on two books and some really annoying papers. Sometimes the class is really boring, you are supposed to spend more than 12 hours each week on rehearsal. Not a easy class to get A- and not too much fun. The professor doesn't care about you that much.

Unless you really like theatre, take a different elective. He demands participation and class discussions make me fall asleep. Also, he made it mandatory to go see a theatre piece he directed (which you had to pay for). Would not recommend for people looking for a fun elective

Hard Grader.. He demands participation so if you are expecting to relax in this class, forget about it. It is true that it is interesting and he makes the class fun, but it is definetly not an easy A. Loads of work and group work, won't recommend it if you dont like theater or are just willing to fill the humanities req.

Jonathan is super nice but you really need to think of something intelligent to say. If you say something stupid,then you'll feel embarrassed. Class participation is important! This class is so easy to pass if you show up and participate and study for the midterm and final. He is a really nice, understanding teacher and he is very smart!

Attendance is definitely required. Participation is definitely required. And you better read the assignments. The good news is he makes discussions interesting and you actually want to read the books he assigns. It's a good class.

I love this professor! I have taken both art of theatre and the&soc and enjoyed both immensely. I'm a pharmacy major but it was a nice change of pace from the sciences. He's really passionate about the subject, discussions are thought provoking, and every class was worth going to. Attendance mandatory. Not hard if you actually do some work. Easy A

Ridiculously hard grader. As a pharmacy major, I took this as an arts/humanities elective thinking it would be an easy A. It is far from an easy A. I had much harder classes that I didn't work nearly as hard in that I received an A for, including my core classes, but I worked my butt off for his class and I only got a B+. Ridiculous.

Prof. Carr, I believe, is well aware that 50% of his class is there simply because NU requires an art course. He does his best to make sure that students actually learn something, through the attendance policy and surprisingly difficult exams - as long as you keep up with reading (!) and go to class you will be fine.

Very nice, smart, funny. I never wanted to skip, which is fortunate, b/c attendance is mandatory. Knows so much from personal experience, and explains things clearly. For 101 great to have, whether or not you know anything about theatre. You learn about all kinds and sides of theatre and he lets you share your opinions, rather than dictating them.

He does not only rate on how often a student participates, but also on how effective their comments are. I found this very demeaning because he was very rude when someone did not fully understand something. I felt that his grading system was unjust and he is the reason I am switching out of theater as my major.

Interesting professor, makes a lot of jokes. I enjoyed the discussion based class. My only complaint would be that even he admits that his grading is tough and somewhat subjective. There are barely any graded assignments, so it's hard to tell what he is looking for. Participation is a large part of the grade so if you're shy you might have trouble.

Professor Carr is awesome. He is definitely one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. Attendance is mandatory but he makes class really interesting; it's never boring. He has a great sense of humor and he is always willing to help. I definitely recommend this class to anyone who wants to fulfill a requirement or is interested in the theatre.
He's such a nice professor and he always cares about his students. It's fun to be in his class.
He's such a nice guy, and he's so passionate about what he does. I recommend him to anyone.

He's an incredibly nice professor.  I'm not an avid fan of the theatre and took it just to fulfill a core requirement, but he got me into the whole idea of the complex world of theatre.  The reading's dry, but even he admits that.  Good class over all.
