He is mad chill. Attendence is manditory and you cant be late. Acting is a smaller class, and he cracks jokes + pokes fun at students all the time. Awsome guy. Not really a hard grader, but def not an  easy one either. Its really hard to get an A in his class, but its fun and interesting just the same.
No Comments

Great Class! Carr is an awesome prof, and I would recommend him to anyone.  His lectures actually make me want to go to class... and that's rare! Class topics are interesting and engaging, worth taking for any reason - but also satisfies Core requirements
Real Nice guy. He seems to know what he's talking about. The class is fun and easy, and as long as you show up and aren't an idoit, you'll do well. Attendence is manditory for this class.
Really great guy.  Knows his stuff, and makes class fun.  Definitely recommend taking any of his classes regardless of your major.
No Comments
Amazing professor, especially for an online class. Organized her Canvas really well and generally just made it easy to succeed in her class. She really cares about her students!

Love her so much, very in person discussion based but you will get to know everyone in the class, your whole grade is three essays plus some small projects in between, but such an easy and chill class. She does take forever to grade though. She does talk to us like we are five though.

Caitlin is an amazing person. Her teaching style allows for lots of conversation and collaboration. I learned a lot in this class, and we only wrote two papers. This class is an easy A. The only caveat is that Caitlin took a really long time to grade our papers, like over a month, which is frustrating when you're trying to calculate a final grade.

GOAT GOAT GOAT. loved her class and she is the best professor. Although the class is not very challenging you will be able to make connections with classmates and learn about essay writing. Please do yourself a favor and take the class.

Such a lovely prof. She accommodates everyone, meeting them halfway.Goes through everything thoroughly and is always willing to meet to help you gain an understanding.Great literature to read and talk through. She loves group work which makes it easier to make connections. Doesn't assign much work just three papers throughout the semester.

This was an AMAZING TEACHER. such an easy grader and explains step by step what we beed to do. is very organized and makes sure that everyone understands. She caree about all of her students and makes sure to check in every day and so offers extensions without questions on papers. easy and small assigbments.

Caitlin is a great professor! I currently have her for FYW and appreciate how she makes everyone in the class feel connected through our discussions. In addition, she always leaves helpful comments on drafts that allow you to succeed on the final project.

Although Prof. Thornbrugh is not a tough grader and Writing Boston is an easy course, some things felt dumbed down and too slow. We spent entire period discussing how to write a thesis. She also speaks to the class like were elementary students and takes long time to get papers back. That being said, she absolutely cares about students well being.

Literally one of my favorite teachers I have ever had for anything. Caitlin is so focused on mental health awareness and treats students as equals while still giving great feedback on assignments. 100% take her courses if possible, she relates topics to real life and I love her so much lol.
Prof Caitlin is great! The class is interesting and she is so friendly and understanding. Not too much work at all compared to the other English classes. 10/10 recommend!

Good professor who cares for her students, aside from times where she can be a bit sassy but I honestly dont think she realizes. She is good at teaching and tests are basicaly the same as the homeworks she gives out for each chapter (which are very helpful). She is also helpful with group projects and is flexible.

Professor Lee is great! She truly cares for her students, but, as other reviews have noted, her class is very lecture-heavy, and the exams are hard. If you pay attention and put in the work outside of class, you'll be ok, but the whole class basically revolves around 3 exams (worh 60%).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework assignments were all long, but doable. If you pay attention in class and do the hw then the tests are easy. Doesn't provide extra credit, but is available for office hours. Hard to bounce back if you do bad on one exam. Professor Lee took the time to learn all of our names and would ask us all questions about ourselves.

Professor Lee was awesome! She made sure everyone understood the concepts, provided many examples, and was always eager to answer questions. Additionally, she was really nice and caring and you could tell she cared about her students.
Prof has a lot of assignments. Harsh with late deadlines and attendance. A bit boring at times during class. Don't expect a good grade. A DS class is prob more useful than the MIS classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Carol Lee is a great professor! As someone who didn't take Stats in high school she made it really easy to understand.There are no quizzes but there is a final group project at the end of the semester which she gives you plenty of time to do. Carol Lee is such a friendly professor and she just wants the best for her students.

Professor Lee is one of the most caring and underrated professors at NEU. She never wants to overwork her students, gave us breaks during class, and even snacks after exams. She had three equally weighted exams which were not bad if you did the homework. Class can be boring at times but you won't regret taking Professor Lee for any of your courses

Carol is nice, but seems a bit under qualified, struggling to answer questions in class. Textbook reading is useless as she just recites the readings during class, which can get monotone and sleep-inducing. She was an okay teacher but didn't offer many practice problems or much feedback and didn't feel very invested in teaching our class.
Very boring. Cant hold the attention of the class. Wont learn anything from the class.
Does not show enthusiasm and lectures are boring. Assignments are long and brutal and it is horrible if you get placed with team members who do not care. Harsh grader at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Fundamentals of Info Analytics with Professor Lee/Sah 1) kind and lectures are interesting 2) Tough grader- for many of the assignments the questions are randomly assigned points (usually not that many questions so they're each worth a good amount- mess up one/two/three could get -15) important because hw is 30% (worth the most- more than final)
Horrible class, unclear assignment instructions, and arbitrary grading. Avoid this professor if you can because she will make your life more difficult.

Professor Cetin is truly one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. He is super smart, relaxed and encourages participation that really helps us learn. I came into class liking Micro Economics, but three months in and I love that stuff. Definitely recommend!

He's so great and nice! His lecture is relaxing, and he explains everything clearly. He always asks us if we follow him and give a lot of actual examples to help us understand. One more thing here, people complain about his accent a lot. I don't think it 's a problem. English is not my first langue, and I can't understand what he says.
Tamer is the GOAT of Econ. I would like nothing more than to kick back and smoke with him. Chill guy, great flow, class isn't too hard.
You can't really understand him, but all in all not a horrible guy and pretty easy course.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Teaches from PowerPoints, hard to get much out of them. Tests are easy, based off the 1-2 hw assignments (MC and a few short answers) per unit, and the recitation class right before the test. Super chill, doesn't care if you come to class, very nice guy. Super accessible by email/office hours, v understanding. From Turkey, so his English is ehh.
this guy has no idea about anything in the subject. he copies the stuff he teaches from other books. he is sooo bad, if you want to understand try to avoid him.
The guy is sooooo bad. he has no idea about the subject and he doesn't know how to teach or anything. avoid him because you will not learn anything and you will spend money for nothing.
I don't know how northeastern university hired him as a teacher. The guy has know idea about the subject and has know idea about anything in IE.
Easily the worst teacher i've ever had to deal with. nice enough guy, means well, but NOT knowledgeable in area of study. always blames the TA, is very unprofessional, and CANNOT TEACH.
No Comments

Had him for Digital Simulation.  One of the useless professors I've ever had.  I'm still not sure what I even learned from that class.  Very unclear, and not an easy class.  Nice guy, pretty awful teacher for this subject.

Definitely not an easy A, you have to put in the work to get your grade, but if you complete all assignments she guarantees you get a B. Other than that, she is very sweet and listens to her students. I can tell she really cares about our mental health and success. She's always available for extra help if you reach out.

I loved Dr. Musselman! She is more than willing to take you under her wing if you show interest. Her essays and projects are made to pull you out of your comfort zone while still being simple. Grading is confusing and vague at times so be sure to ask questions! If you follow her guidelines and listen to her feedback you will do well. Super sweet!
Great women and professor,  available if you need extra help. Gives constructive feedback in each paper to help you improve.

Great Professor. Dr. Musselman will make you appreciate writing and you will enjoy writing about 3 essays and 1 video project/graphic novel. With enough effort and re-writes, you will be able to receive a good grade.

Great professor, really keeps class interesting. A tough grader, but really helps you to improve. She was very willing to meet with you outside of class to help you. I was in her honors section of College Writing, and class was always a lot of fun. She brought in food for us several times, and overall was my favorite professor this semester.

I was in her Honors section of College Writing. She's an interesting person, but will not give you a good grade if you don'r write what she wants to hear, which is sometimes hard to determine. Her written feedback is often vague and unhelpful, but if you go to her office hours and ask a lot of questions you can sometimes get the idea.

I took the honors section of Advanced Writing in the Disciplines. She is available to help you if you need it, but I found the class and the assignments really stupid and uninteresting. If you put in effort, you will do fine, but she thinks writing is the most important subject when Pharmacy majors have more important things to worry about.

Always ready to help. Well informed and enthusiastic. Accepts other opinions -- people who say otherwise couldn't defend their position well enough or didn't have the motivation or confidence to do it anyway. I got an A and I disagreed frequently -- maybe not with subject matter, but sbout writing styles and sentence structure.
Nice lady and passionate about her work. The history of english course is difficult to grasp, but she is a very kind and fair grader.

Cecelia loves what she teaches. I enjoyed listening to her lectures. She is always there to help you if you need it. Show up, do the problem sets. She offers a lot of bonus points and second chances! Just make sure you do them and hand everything in!
this class requires a lot of work, like any writing class. the assignments are somewhat open ended and can be confusing, but she is very easy to reach for help.
very helpful when you need help.  If you want to do well, you will, and you'll improve your writing on the way.
Best writing teacher ever

Ok...this goes out to all of the science majors who really, REALLY don't want to take Middler Writing.  TAKE THIS CLASS!  The writing part is the same as any other ENG 307 class, but Professor Musselman is always willing to lend a helping hand with papers.  Her teaching is enhanced by her bubbly personality and enthusiasm for science.

Prof. Musselman is the best writing professor I've had (I am a biochemistry major).  She is very straightforward with what she looks for when grading, provides direct answers and helpful feedback when inquiries are made, well informed, and very approachable.  I highly recommend taking her middler year writing class if you are a science major.

Very opinionated and if you argue with her she'll drill you until you give up. She really gets on my nerves. Other than that be prepared to write a lot of drafts. If you follow her suggestions you'll do pretty good.
No Comments
Is very opinionated like already said, although if you ask her how to improve your paper, she'll tell you what to do, and you'll do well.

Is all about the busy work.  Get on her good side by participating in class and asking her opinion about your papers.  Paper guidelines are very unclear,  I don't think she even understood them.  The worst english teacher I have ever had.

You have to spit back her information or you'll be marked down- easy class, just a lot of editting. Just hand in all your work, and you can't get below a B because we do SO many drafts. Harder than most writing classes.
Weirdo. Very opinionated. Share her opinion or get a bad grade. Has some weird views.

Solid prof whose practice tests are so helpful to prepare for real exams. However, the TA's were horrendous this sem. They click rocks together in their free time and only one TA actively responded on Piazza. HW grades came out weeks late. Head TA was a ghost and screwed multiple people when finals came around.

Prof Wu is a great teacher, easily one of the best at NEU. However, the course was VERY disorganized. Schedule changes weren't communicated, assignment date changes came last minute, homework grading took 5 weeks on average, and grading guidelines were unfairly unclear. Sadly, his teaching quality didn't outweigh the chaos.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. The TA's this semester were really bad though, had to wait months for homework grades at times. You need a 97% for an A but every exam has extra credit, and he offers extra credit just for showing up to class. He truly cares about all his students and wants everyone to succeed.

He is clearly a great professor and loves teaching. I felt like some topics were merely just memorization of formulas or memorization of how to do certain math problems without much learning of why something was the way it was. If you actually want to do DS take this section. If you want a free A i wouldnt recommend. Basically all math little code
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the best prof ive ever had at northeastern lecture can be difficult at times but he makes it easy and his notes r so easy to understand, the exams are exactly like the practice exams and he gives extra credit just for going to class

You just gotta go to the lectures and be ready to learn the math. The three tests do weigh a lot, but if you know how to do everything on the practice exams, you are all good. Good professor, and it's clear he cares about students and whether of not you actually learned. The class is super fun, but don't pick him if you want an easy class.

Honestly I took the course with Prof Wu because of his high rating, but honestly I regret it. The other teacher for the course is basically a free A, but you don't really learn as much. In this course you do need a 97% for an A which can make it a little tough even though there is about 4% extra credit if you just go to lectures. Great prof though.

Incredible professor, truly wants you to succeed in every way. Lectures make understanding content easy because of how he relates it to tangible contexts. Extra credit all over the place, exams are carbon copies of practice tests. Genuinely one of the best math professors I've ever had. Places big emphasis on linear algebra and matrix calculus.
THE GOAT. tests are super easy and almost a 1-1 copy of review tests, attendance not required but hes super funny and makes the class fun so I recommend you go.

It is a math boot camp, and its presented well. Get ready to cover: Linear Algebra, Calculus I, III, Optimization, Probability, Matrix Calculus. Unless you learn very quickly or have prior experience, the lectures can feel a bit handwavy at times. Many things I love about this class, and some things I don't. Wu is of a different breed.
The best DS professor, the GOAT!!

Prof. Wu is by far the best DS3000 professor at northeastern. Class can be a bit of work at times but still manageable. He's also really funny. If you're taking DS3000, make sure to take it with Prof. Wu and no one else.

Arguably the best data science professor in Northeastern. He somehow compresses an extreme amount of teaching material into a very comfortable learning experience. Extra credit is given for showing up and doing in-class work. Exams are very long but rewarding. Just an extremely selfless guy who only thinks about his students. enroll at all costs

Prof. Wu is genuinely the best professor I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgeable, caring, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. His lectures are engaging, and he emphasizes true understanding over memorization. His students have an amazing track record for landing co-ops/jobs and leave with a very strong foundation in data science.

Professor Wu is probably the best professor I have ever had. He is deeply invested in his student's success. His class will leave you with a much deeper understanding of the material. If you have the opportunity to have him as a professor you should 100% take his class.

Lots of extra credit, extremely funny and an amazing lecture to go to. Lots of math, but he uses real world examples that are relatable to everyone. You will not regret going to class. There is a bit of homework, and the tests are average difficulty. Make sure to do the practice exams!

He has to be the best, most caring professor in the nation. This man is the absolute goat. He makes the class difficult, but only because wants to prepare you for future classes and job interviews. He really knows his stuff and cares so much about his students, I have never seen a professor like him before. If you can take his class, make sure to.
Professor Wu is the best, its true!
the lebron of professors

Prof. Wu my goat, he moved from the ML courses to DS3000 (linear algebra in disguise) to give ML students the linear algebra foundation they were lacking. Attendance technically isn't mandatory if you do the in class work at home but I still go to lectures because of how great they are.
my goat is overqualified

My king, my knight in shining armor Professor Wu is the best professor at Northeastern. He makes it so easy to learn, no reading the textbook just show up to class, do the exercises and you get extra credit. He not only teaches you the concepts but also the code really easily with entertaining stories. Exams and coding exams are easy if u practice.
Absolute beast - lots of work but pays dividends

Prof Wu is kind, inspirational, very knowledgeable and clearly cares about his students. Had a wonderful experience in his Machine Learning & Data Mining class. Prof Wu strikes a good balance b/w the mathematics behind common ML algorithms, how to code them in Python, and where they are used in the real world. Would rate 6 / 5 stars if I could.
His lectures/content can be intimidating but his tests are easier than expected. Memorize the practice exams! He is very friendly and explain things well.

Written exams could be harder.
But overall I learned a lot.

Honestly guys if you can take DS4400 with Wu you absolutely HAVE TO. He was by FAR the best professor ive had at neu. His lectures are upbeat, and while the content is tough and definitely mathematically tricky to understand, Wu is an incredible lecturer and makes it bearable. Lots of class time for practice, and he loves to come around to help.

If you have to take this class, remember these rules to achieve an A:
1. Go to his every class and get each class activities credit
2. If you worry grade, take extra credit assignments
3. Memorize his practice exam! The more you practice the more you write faster in the exam.
4. Don't look him in the eye, he'll ask you for knowledge he just taught.
best professor at northeastern.

I served as a TA for Prof. Wu for two semesters. He is an exceptional professor who teaches concepts from scratch and inspires his students. Creating solutions and hosting office hours deepened my ML knowledge, helping me navigate the job market and secure a Data Scientist role. He is simply the best!

Being a TA for Prof. Wu's DS4400 course helped me develop a deep understanding of fundamental machine learning concepts beyond just using packages. Teaching and explaining these ideas to students enhanced my problem-solving and communication skills, which enabled me to approach interview challenges with confidence and articulate solutions clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: absolutely goated

Professor Wu does a great job presenting ML concepts and algorithms in an accessible manner. He really just cares about helping students understand the material, and he provides a ton of opportunities to succeed. Lectures are well-paced, easy to follow, and teach you a lot!

Professor Wu is brilliant and awesome at teaching the machine learning class. He went through mathematical principles which makes the model of machine learning easy to understand. The mathematical requirement was not high and he went through it during the class.

Literally the greatest, most knowledgeable professor in DS at Northeastern. I seriously recommend taking him and really forcing yourself to truly understand the material because he goes deep into the proofs of what makes machine learning possible. Also, try to attend his office hours because he is such a fun human to talk to!

Great professor and very knowledgeable. Explains what looks like complicated topics in machine learning that involve math, in a way that you develop a deep understanding on what's going on underneath the hood. It is very rewarding when it all clicks and you understand how the given machine learning algorithm works. Highly recommend him!

Moderate difficulty, math-intensive. Prof. Wu emphasizes deep understanding of ML concepts, not just using libraries. Balances written and coding tasks; effort yields significant learning. Ideal if you care about getting a very deep understanding of machine learning; consider another professor for an easier experience. Prof Wu cares about students.

Wu's lectures were really engaging. I can tell he put a lot of effort into preparing the lectures. The material can be challenging to some students, as they are math-heavy. I personally think this is a good thing. At the end of the day, you need a strong math background to stand out in DS. Prepare your math and you can learn a lot from this class.

Very good professor! Cares more about students learning the material than scores, and you'll do well in the class as long as you put in the effort. Also listens to student's feedbacks, and creates videos for students struggling to understand concepts!

Very enthusiastic prof who is highly dedicated to making sure students get the most out of class. Lectures are well-paced, organized, and challenging enough to keep students motivated. Also goes out of his way to create additional helpful videos. Grading is fair as long as you put effort in. Overall enjoyed taking the class and highly recommend!!
AMAZING! super easy and actually interesting, very accessible.

NUMBER ONE PROFESSOR AT NORTHEASTERN. His class is super easy BUT if you want to learn things you totally can because he is quite passionate. It is definitely what you get out of it, which I enjoyed a LOT. HIGHLY recommend!

I love professor Chichirau! Such a sweet and caring guy. His class is really simple, we have weekly quizzes that you take whenever you want, with unlimited time, and can use any resources you'd like. He records all his lectures on zoom as well.

VERY easy class. Neighborhood walk and reflection takes up one class a week. The lecture takes up the other class, but lectures are not needed at all. Discussion post and walk reflection are only weekly assignments other than the big final paper which is broken up into five smaller papers. But, he is a great guy and an interesting lecturer.
He's okay. Super easy, but honestly didn't learn much. The neighborhood walks were definitely the highlight of the class. Nice guy.

The class is fun, and he conducts weekly walks around Boston. You have to try to not get a good grade on the essays, which don't even have to have proper APA citations. Since everything is based on essays and discussion posts, he doesn't take attendance and his class was practically empty by the fourth week. This is a good elective for slackers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: George. What a great guy. Makes you want to come to class every day, even for 100min lectures, and the weekly neighborhood walks are a great experience too. Consider yourself lucky if you get a class taught by George.
This class is an experience. George is quite a guy. Wow. Take this class.

I think she gives a lot assignments that are not worth it. I don't love the project. But she is super knowledgeable on the subject and has a lot of opinions. She also supports students out of the classroom with co-op if she can. She's really nice as well. I would take this class just be prepared for the work!
Terrible professor with unclear requirements and deliverables. Pretends to be kind then stabs you in the back when grading with vague critiques on your work and unexplained grades.

You miss one class and she takes 2% off your average. Doesn't matter if you're on your deathbed. She loves telling us to turn and talk about something and then immediately yelling at the class to be quiet. No late work is accepted, and you just have to accept that she took off another 2% from your average. Too shy to talk? Take another -5%.

Professor Miteness will drown you in meaningless busy work and take off points for random things. Incredibly unorganized group projects and assignments make you feel like you are in second grade, but asynchronous. Maybe she is better in person. At the end of this class, you will feel dumber.

Mitteness is passionate about what she teaches, but is an unfair grader and often marks down unreasonable points with little explanation and no rubric to follow. She has a strict, unempathetic late policy under the claims of the "real-world". Do not expect your grades to be reflective of your understanding or hard work in the class.
Class is incredibly easy, but her grading seems random and almost like she doesn't review the work submitted. You will lose points for no reason, despite any "feedback" given.

Unfair grader and was very inconsistent. Graded things with little to no feedback. She grades your participation based off how much she likes you. She assigns all busy work and rambles on and on about her life that no one actually cares about. Worst teacher ever. She makes it a point to make sure you dont succeed in her class.
She was pretty great up until inconsistant grading on the group projects and taking off points that had no business being taken off. She picks favorites watch out!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of my favourite classes at Northeastern so far. Cheryl uses a learn outside class and work in class format which worked pretty well. This class was a great combo of being pretty easy but also learning a lot.

She is the most outgoing, engaging, and kind professor I have had at Northeastern. Has a passion and deep understanding for entrepreneurship and teaching. She always incorporates in class activities and discussion. Majority of the work in the class is a group venture project.

Ms. Miteness was a good professor, I enjoyed her class and she was engaging when lecturing. You'll watch a lot of shark tank and do some group discussion during the lecture. I feel like I learned something and I felt like she did a good job giving students freedom to make and change groups that made the group work much more enjoyable.

One of the most confusing classes I've ever taken. She changes the due dates for assignments and tells you in class, but doesn't remind you until the day it's due. Insanely hard grader and not fair. Very hard to talk to and approach. I ended up dreading going to this class because of her.

Professor Mitteness is one of my favorite entrepreneurship professors. She is clear, knowledgeable and her lecture is very engaging. She's always looking to innovate. One thing I liked a lot is that she is structured and clear about what's due and when is it due.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cheryl is an adorable person and makes the class pretty interesting. We watched a lot of Shark Tank. Grading is pretty easy if you read the little book, not too hard to do well on the group project. I had a bad group and she dealt with it very well. I'd take her again for a class. Highly recommend, keeps it one hundo
TAKE HER. Who says learning has to be hard and not fun? We learn a lot and its not boring most of the time. Love Shark Tank, and her hair style.
Great Professor. You would not regret taking her class. Test are pretty challenging but not devastating.

I now work for Professor Mitteness because of the relationship i have created with her through this course. Really reasonable and will be your #1 supporter. Go to office hours! Group projects can either benefit you or really destroy you. I on the other hand chose my group ahead of time while some waited to be grouped. Really great professor..

Cheyrl is a great Professor. She's very clear about the concepts she is teaching and gives great real world examples. We spent quite a bit of class time breaking down episodes of Shark Tank. She's laid back, the class is fun, and you'll learn the topic well. Keep the textbooks, they come in handy down the road.

Cheryl is AWESOME! Fun lady, good teacher, gets "it." I generally find classes to be uninteresting and a waste of time, but Cheryl kept things interesting. She's really sweet. You could do a lot worse.
Great teacher. Always helpful. The quizes can go from wicked hard to easy pending on the week. But she keeps you interested and it very down to earth. Highly reccomend.
Prof is fun and engaging and supportive with amazing stories and such an open mind. Prof led amazing discussions on deeply moving content. Great insightful readings and great class environment.

She literally accused half the class of using AI with zero evidence. She didn't know that OSCCR was punitive and just reported or threatened to report half the class. Ridiculous. Her classes are mandatory, but absolutely useless. I got 100s on every exam by reading the textbook, I had headphones on in every class, didn't listen ot a word she said.

Exams were unfairly difficult in comparison to the content we learned. She only gave the class 43 minutes to complete 55 questions for the final exam, which is much less than the time exams usually would be. She also yelled at a student for asking about their grade in front of the whole class.

Class is VERY easy, you can probably pass WITHOUT AI. Papers are graded leniently. The only thing that'll probably get you are the exams, so make sure to study for them. Idk why people hate her, she just doesn't want people using AI.
Not a fan of reversed classroom, weird attitude in emails, suspects students using ai and made a study out of it lol.

this class was very easy the whole semester, i didnt learn much from class but with the textbook my grade was good, 3 days before finals she accuses the whole class of using AI on a paper. she wouldnt look at someones version history because "she just knows" and "took classes on AI usage" she gave them all 0, i still have to get my grade back on it

Reported the entire class for AI usage with no evidence. Snapped at a student for even asking. Wouldn't let students explain, said "she doesn't want to hear it" and she "doesn't have time to debate with everyone." Regularly accuses students of cheating with 0 evidence.

I took her class over the summer and online, but really enjoyed her class. Professor Cisewski was very accessible online when I needed feedback on assignments or needed an answer to a question. There were about four papers for this class, but all of which straight forward and applied lessons from the book to real world problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her PSYC4666 ClinicalPsySeminar. It's an amazing class that almost all classes were taught by students. If you are interested in clinical psychology, please take her class! She is a reasonable person and always caring students. Be prepared to read papers each week and write 2 pages reading reflection. No homework, just a paper needed.

She is a very caring individual and easy to access outside of class. The course has flipped model, meaning you watch lectures online and then discuss/apply knowledge during class sessions, however at the end of the semester I felt like this wasn't always the most productive. Exams can be pretty challenging as well, but it's an interesting course.

Dr. C is very caring, I took her class online but she was always very responsive to emails and enthusiastic about the material. There are papers and exams but they aren't too challenging if you stay on top of the textbook reading and her lectures. She explains things well and provides other resources for reinforcement.

The class is a flipped model, meaning you read the textbook and watch the lectures at home and mostly have discussions in class. Because of this reason, I felt like she didn't teach very much and I felt like some of the discussions weren't totally helpful. That being said, she is incredibly approachable and easy to access outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. C is a really great professor--if you have the chance to take a course from her you should certainly take advantage of it. She is textbook-heavy but also provides really insightful lectures and is extremely communicative and caring of each student.
love her

I didi find her course very interesting and she is very knowledgeable in what she teaches and I definitely learned a lot. This is not a terribly hard class but it does require constant effort with the 4 exams and 4 papers throughout the semester. My main issue is her communication issues, she usually takes 2 weeks to get back you if ever.
Class was super easy if you read the textbook you will be fine for exams. Professor is also extremely nice and topics were interesting.
She's actually the cutest human ever. I learned a lot. I'm not a psychology major but I would love to take another class with her. Lots of reading.

She is an easy A! She gave me full marks for all four essays in one semester! And her exams are not difficult, they don't require students to memorize a lot of concepts, but you do need to understand. She's a really good professor, and she's not strict. Make sure you take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Please just save yourself from trouble, don't take this class. I feel like I'm always bein notified of assignments toward the end of the semester... Even tho classes were recorded, i know instinctively that she is reading. Exams have nothing to do with lectures, but make sure you do the super long readings in case you unwisely choose this class...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took the course online and we read the entire psych book in 7 weeks. So yes, very heavy on the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: the worst teacher I have ever had at NU. Read straight from powerpoints huge waste of time and money!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: lectures were inconsistent, and class didn't go the whole time. Her exams were not based on our textbook and I feel like the class was a huge waste of my time because I learned nothing would not recommend her.
she was tough, gave lots of tests and lectures were too long. would not recommend

She was great. I took this class online but she was really engaging. She grades fairly and the tests were pretty direct from her slides, the textbook is helpful but has more info then she expects you to know. Overall great class

An absolute sweetheart. One of if not my favourite psych prof. This class may be different from her usual ones because it's an online one, but she was super flexible and made the curriculum easier because it was a stressful time. The exams and papers aren't hard but you do have to read the textbook and assigned materials. TAKE HER CLASS! love her<3

Prof. C is great, she is a lenient grader and gives extra credit opportunities. Her lectures are not mandatory, if you can make time to read the textbook and case studies on your own time you'll be fine for the exams.
She treats you like a person and makes class interesting and engaging.
love her!!!
LOVE HER!
Very nice professor and great at explaining any questions you may have
excellent teacher

She is a great teacher! Sometimes we spend too much time on one topic, but if we did, it was always beneficial. We would get into huge discussions which help you get lots of examples and the tests aren't too difficult. just make sure you follow the directions for papers and you should be fine :)

Great teacher!  Has a fun and engaging personality which helps the class go well.  Offers extra credit for those who attend class on days others do not.  Tests are fair but there are only four exams so each one is important.  Overall, a great teacher because she is passionate with the subject she teaches.

Took her for personality and she was amazing.  So sweet and knowledgeable and probably my favorite professor that I've ever had. Like the other person said, take the online quizzes for extra practice and you'll do awesome on the tests.

She's really nice and really helpful. I would definitely recommend taking her class. Make sure you read over the book and DEFINITELY do the quizzes from the book's website. But the tests mostly consist of her PowerPoints. She has a long paper on a celebrity - make sure it's long enough and that you include everything from the psychologist's theory.

She's very nice and is one of the few professors that actually knows what she's talking about. Loves what she does, and gives great examples on ALL the topics. Tests are pretty straight forward. Class is not mandatory, just go to the review session before the tests.  Gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit.

Made the content EXTREMELY easy to follow, classes were optional. If you don't feel like going to class, reading the book is fine. Class lectures were all that were necessary for the tests. So helpful and overall the nicest professor I've ever had.

Prof. Cisewski definitely knows psychology. The class is all thoroug powerpoint lectures but they are entertaining because she relates each concept with the real world. 3 exams and 1 final with extra credit opportunities. I tried not buying a textbook since quizzes are online. I got C's on my exams without reading. You actually learn in this class!

not the easiest course But this professor grades very fairly, gives partial credit& happily answers any questions(even stupid ones that some teachers are annoyed by)Overall, i think she is super helpful and surprisingly nice. the really tricky part is memorizing all the formulas but other than that just do the hw and go to class and you'll be fine

She's very clear in her lectures and notes, she tends to go a bit fast so its helpful to get the notes on blackboard before class. She's understanding and is willing to help with any problems.  Quizzes are not too hard as long as you study. Once you get used to the class its smooth sailing.

very interesting class. she explains things very well and knows exactly what she's talking about because she actually practices what she teaches outside of the classroom. oh yeah she's a total **** too, makes going to class that much better.

I took Foundations of Psych. my freshman year and got the worst grade I've gotten in all four years at NU. I studied hard and still bombed the tests. She's a Psych Professor...she wants to think she's smarter than you. The entire class is Power Point and BORING!!!! Psych can be interesting, too. I was disappointed!!!!

Fav professor this semester! She's extremely knowledgeable, always making helpful references to everyday & her work experience. Her speech is clear & easy to understand. All powerpoint lectures posted on blackboard. 5 MC tests. She makes it very clear what will be on exams. Doesn't take attendence but going to class & reading the book helps alot.
She seems annoyed when you ask a question!

This class was extremely easy. All the quizzes were based directly off of the powerpoint slides, which made it really easy. She only gave formulas for the final, but I'd say that this one a very easy class and she was a very good/interesting professor, even teaching statistics!

She provided a formula sheet for the final which was  extremely helpful. The rest of the quizes were straught from the powerpoint slides but she takes points off if your definitions aren't exactly in her words which is frustrating. She is willing to listen to student feedback and help when she can. Very understanding and nice even in Stats.

Her lectures will put you to sleep, when you raise your hand to ask a question she does see you most of the time and goes on teaching. She goes through material VERY fast and she grades your homework based on whether its correct rather than if you tried your best. Tought new info until the last day of classes, no review. Grades tests pretty tough.

A really nice lady. Flexible and understanding with her students. It was a little tough to take stats with her because unlike most profs she didn't let us use a formula sheet but I'd recommend her otherwise!  Her slides made things much easier.
No Comments

She is such a nice lady and you never have to take any notes b/c her slides sum everything up.  She can be a little repetative and boring but as long as you get the grade that you want, I dont care how boring it is.  Her tests are right from her notes. Not everyone even goes to class!!  Take her if u can!

She is a great teacher, really nice, posts lecture slides on blackboard as well as practice assignments. Offers extra credit before every exam. Answers questions, holds study sessions, very pretty woman, hardly went to class and still did really well, just read text and notes b4 exam. recommended.

Her class is wicked easy!  Most people don't show up for class but I found it helpful to go to class, however you deffinetly don't need to go to every class in order to pass.  She wants everyone in her class to pass so she does everything possible in order to help you out. Go to her study sessions!
real nice lady... notes provided for you which resemble tests.  not much work involved... attending class benefit of learning but not essential to pass. stick with her she's a fair grader!
Interesting class, and a really nice teacher. All of her lectures were online, so if you missed a class you could make it up.  Also, the tests were just like the lectures.
No Comments
super funny and kind and makes orgo a bit easier to understand. really cares about his students
Abysmal lectures. However, the tests and the final were straight from the practice problems.

Professor Chung definitely made Organic Chemistry 2 interesting and exciting with his jokes, but be ready to teach yourself the majority of the course by reading the textbook. His lectures can go by very quickly with a lot of content that needs to be reviewed on your own time. The pros are that his exams are very similar to his practice material.

If you need a sign not to take Chung's class, take this as one. He lectures every class and always deviates from the topic and makes an attempt to insert a cringe joke where one isn't needed. I always walked out feeling like I didn't learn anything and had no idea what was going on. And on top of that his exams are impossible. Waste of my money.

Professor Chung is very funny and dedicated, but his lectures were hard to follow. Lots of studying and self-teaching is needed, but the quizzes were very easy. Homework problems were difficult but graded on completion. If you are not willing to study or teach yourself things, don't take his class. However he is very nice and the class was easy.

If you actually want to learn, do not take Prof. Chung. He is a sweet man and means well, but he is a very poor lecturer. He is not good at responding to emails, and if you ask him a question, he never gives you a solid answer. Tests are 20 MCQs that are pretty straightforward, but if you have one bad one, it can really mess with your final grade.

Overall, solid class. Professor tends to go off topic, but as long as you attend class you'll understand the foundational material. Exams were similar to practice problems, and only 20 MCQ, meaning if you had a reasonable understanding of the units you did well. Attend class and go to his office hours for extra help, and you'll do good.

Prof Chung was passionate about chemistry and funny, but not the best lecturer. Some of his explanations were unclear and he would overcomplicate simple concepts. However, I liked how he emphasized understanding over memorization. Exams were easy, 20 MCQ each and very similar to practice problems. A good high school chem foundation is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, no major complaints. Dr. Chung is kind, and doesn't want to make it a stressful class. But, he often read directly from slides, arrived 10-15 min late, and went off topic A LOT. Exams closely match practice problems, so it's easy to get an A. Exams are only 20 MC, no open response unlike all the other gen chem classes which made it easier
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Learned absolutely nothing during this class. He teaches poorly and never stays on topic, but it's an easy GPA booster, wouldn't recommend for general chemistry because I literally know NOTHING.

He's very funny and passionate about chemistry and science overall, often incorporating his philosophical interpretations of the stars and human existence into his lectures. His slides are very informational and his exams are very manageable (usually all multiple choice).

Ken Chung is super smart and funny. His lectures can be a bit confusing, but he provides lots of context and gives extra help before exams. He gives out random 5 point extra credits during the semester. 
Also he has the most out of pocket jokes. 

GO TO CLASS, do his review problems, and you will pass.

The exams are straightforward. Ken's a goat.

Ken Chung is the goat. He is willing to go above and beyond for his students, hosting office hours at 8pm from home and almost everyday on exam weeks even with his busy schedule. If you listen to him in class and do his practice problems you will succeed. He is like a dad in the best way possible and a comedian at heart.

Ken chung is amazing. Not only is he funny, but it's clear that he cares about his students. He makes a ton of funny jokes and gives many extra credit opportunities if you pay attention in class. Just do the practice exams and the tests will be super clear. People who rated him bad are lazy.

He is funny but prepare to hear the same joke repeated every single class & he is kind. He allows for extra credit opportunities in class like "solve this problem for 5 points added to last exam". One of my friends literally failed the first exam and still got an A. If you're taking the class to actually learn organic chemistry II... good luck!

Ken Chung is a wild card if you take him. He's pretty unpredictable. His grading is set up in a helpful way where an 80 is an A, a 70 is a B, 60 is C and so on so forth. But, his exams are almost impossible. He doesn't give you the structures and just gives you their names. If you fail more than 2 exams, you're done. Take him cautiously.

Professor Chung is a great teacher and a great person. He always tries to be accessible outside of class for his students, and will help you as long as you are willing to put the work in and learn the material. I took both Organic Chemistry I and II with him, and really enjoyed both courses. He also curves final grades (although tests are hard).

Reading the textbook before class is very helpful. He's not gonna hand out free A's to everyone for no reason. If you do the practice problems (which are very very similar to the exam, sometimes the exact same), you'll be fine. + great curve around 20%! The low reviews on this page are from people who do no work and expect an A. Skill issue.

If you can NOT teach yourself chemistry, do not take him! He never explained anything and assumes you already know everything. I had to drop the course because I failed every exam (even though I previously passed orgo 1 with an A-). READ: I asked him what I can do to bring my grade up and he said "just pass the final exam." He was so rude!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo 2 is a hard class and no matter who you take, you NEED to put in work OUTSIDE of class. Prof Chung is enthusiastic, tries to be funny, and a good lecturer but is a little unorganized. Exams are based off practice problems. Read the textbook, be willing to learn and you'll be fine. He has a great curve and wants you to succeed, as long as u do

While he has passion for chemistry, he is a not a chemistry teacher. Your grade is completely dependent on 4 exams and the final exam with no chance for corrections or extra credit. His lectures can feel like an eternity as he tends to distract himself and ramble on unimportant things. Only take if you're confident in teaching yourself chemistry.

ur graded by 4 exams all of which are ridiculously hard/bad. He constantly is complaining about how students do not care/how traumatized he is and yet makes no effort to be a better professor/lectures were awful. TAKE 2313 WITH LITERALLY ANYONE ELSE I PROMISE YOU WILL NOT PASS BECAUSE OF HIS CLASS SET UP. u bomb one exam and its over actually
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chung has a bad rep but is genuinely the best chem professor at NU.  He is passionate, funny, and very smart.  He actually explains the material.  Your grade in the class is entirely based on midterms and the final exam but he is generous with extra credit during class.  He records his lectures but it is worth going to class.

He was funny in a weird awkward not really funny but funny way. I don't think I learned a thing tbh but if you read the textbook you'll manage. Idk if he still does this but for our class our homework was hella extra credit and he curves sometimes on his quizzes. But I've heard recently that he no longer curves lollll

Professor Chung is a very funny guy. He always makes students laugh during the lectures. The class is very lecture heavy and is good if you have taken IB Chemistry or AP Chemistry prior, if you haven't, you may struggle a bit due to the fast pacing. He is very caring and will do his best to help you when you're having a hard time with something.

Genuinely, Professor Chung is such a nice guy, prone to go on funny side quests mid lecture, but he 100% cares about his students learning. If you supplement lectures with reading the textbook, and DOING THE PRACTICE TESTS, you will get a good grade. He will definitely hit you with a nice curve at the end of the year as well.

He has an interesting teaching style which can be hard to follow, you honestly won't learn a lot in his class but he is very funny and keeps students engaged. The miderms were basically just practice problems and your grade gets boosted.

I really liked Professor Chung's class. His teaching style was a little difficult for me to get used to, but if you attend his class regularly and participate you learn a lot from him and he'll be generous with grading. He does seem to be very busy but he tries his best to make time for you if you need help outside of class.

PLEASE take Ken Chung. He is the sweetest and most relatable professor ever. At first it may seem like he does not know how to teach and a little disorganized, but if you show up to ever class and genuinely show him that you are trying to put in effort, he WILL make sure you succeed. Trust me on this one, do not give up on him.

funny but highly unorganized. Didn't have a syllabus the first day of class. Grades were just the 3 tests, but I don't think he follows them when giving letter grades. I learn things, but not sure if it was everything we were supposed to learn. Gets really into the math and derivations. People who were always in class + participated saw grade bumps

Chung may come off as a bad professor at first--his life is a little over the place. But he tries his best and in the end everything works out he is very nice with grading (good scale and takes off some questions in the final to give us more time). Give him a chance, but I would not take a class you actually really need to learn something with him.

He did not have slides and often went on tangents. Very interesting guy and funny, but I did not learn anything. His practice exams are the actual exams with maybe one or two questions changed. Good GPA boost, but if you plan on taking more chem classes with a different professor you will struggle.

Really funny guy. Class is not mandatory, but you should probably go it'll help you learn. He's super unserious and moves kinda fast. However, if you have taken chem in high school you'll be fine. Recitation is basically optional. Only a few tests and they're multiple choice 20 questions and based on the practice problems. Overall good guy and prof

Funniest guy i have ever met in my life as a student. He is passionate about what he is teaching. He is knowledgeable and always come to lecture prepared beforehand. Inspire students to continue the study of organic chemistry. Love him. It is so great to have him as my organic chemistry teacher. Definitely recommended!

I enjoyed orgo with Prof Chung. I thought his lectures tended to be confusing at times and it was hard to get in touch outside of class, but his exams were pretty straightforward as long as you read the textbook and did homework. It was easy to get a good grade since he curves at the end of the semester and his coursework was pretty chill.

Very nice professor, but explains things very quickly so it is hard to build a strong foundation. Concepts can be difficult at times too. Curves generously so you do not have to be very worried about your grade. Cares that you learn.

If you took regular chem in hs (not ap chem) and had a basic understanding of it, you will be fine. This class is incredibly hard to fail as he curves the grade drastically. He is not the best at explaining topics and the lab often goes ahead of what is taught in lecture. They made the recitation mandatory, but it is basically a waste of time.

He was funny HOWEVER this man just cannot teach. He lectures in a way that he assumes we already know the content. Grades are quite literally made up of 3 exams but he's lenient with the grading system so thats a plus. There's no way to take this class to truly learn and comprehend Chemistry its literally just to pass and move on.
Was good for gen chem, sometimes goes off topic during lectures but still makes the lectures easy to understand and follow. geniunely wants students to pass the class and curves really generously.

Took his general chemistry course during the Summer I semester. He tends to go a bit off topic throughout his lectures but other than that is a good teacher. He uses analogies and real life examples for topics which helps students make real connections. Pretty easy grader and tends to curve

Has a very unclear grading system. Whenever asked, he will beat around the bush. Says that he has "4 different grading systems" and will grade based on what system will give you the highest grade. What are these grading systems? I could not tell you. He expects you to know the concept, so if you did not take AP Chem, you may be lost. Easy class.

Lectures are long but he keeps you entertained while also explaining concepts. Explains concepts through lots of examples. Tests are hard but the quizzes beforehand are a good indicator of what you know. He wants his students to learn but seems fed up with his job. I liked him but I know a lot of people who had a lot of complaints about his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's amazing for a chem professor. The grade depends on 3 tests. There is a curve but it is applied at the end of the semester. He uses downloadable PowerPoint slides and follows them pretty well, however, there were a couple of topics that were covered that weren't on the slides. He explains concepts very thoroughly so they are easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chung is not only a great professor but a funny and caring person. He definitely cares about his students. The curves for the tests are very generous and the practice exams he gives out are super helpful in studying. You can obtain an A in this class if you use the resources he provides and by going to office hours.

If you took AP Chem you will be extremely prepared -- this course was an easier version of AP chem for me. I never showed up for class and just came to take the exams. I prepared by really studying the practice exams. He only made us take 3 exams, curved them a lot tho. Super kind teacher and funny. I ended with a 100% by doing very little work.

Would not recommend Ken Chung. Four quizzes are worth 60% of your grade and there are only four questions each on each quiz meaning if you get 1 question wrong you automatically get a C. Do not take his class if you do not test well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only graded on three exams total, though he is VERY generous with the curve for grades below an A. For this course, taking notes in lectures helps but more importantly do the practice problems in the textbook. Working through those problems was the only way I really learned, otherwise the recitation really helps if you still need more help.

Most of your grade will be based off of three tests that he will provide practice preparation for. Its recommended to do the optional textbook problems in order to ensure all your bases are covered. The class environment created by Professor Chung is exceptional and is very entertaining.

Ken was a good professor who really wants to teach the class in a funny way. However, his class pace is so fast that almost no one can follow his track. He used to finish only one difficult chapter even in a 2-hour class.

Professor Chung really cares for the student. Lectures are straight from textbook, so definitely want to do optional practice problems. He teaches with no slides (not great), so just pay attention in class w/ good notes. Even met with me and my classmates outside office hours. Lots of effort required, but he's supportive if you ask for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He had a great spirit but all he did was practice problems on the board. he began the semester telling us to make the textbook our #1 priority and to do all the practice problems. Id often leave his lectures learning nothing or leaving more confused. As long as you devote almost all your free time to doing practice problems you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized and doesn't prepare any slides. He simply does a bunch of random problems on the board in class and spends a lot of time on the easy stuff while leaving the complex concepts for you to understand on your own. The class is graded on three very difficult exams and one final. He also gave one of the midterms a week before our final.

Ken Chung's teaching style only works for a select few students, as he doesn't provide lecture notes or powerpoint slides, but rather writes random problems on the whiteboard. The grades are based on 3 midterms and a final, with problems that are too difficult or time-consuming.  Everyone failed the tests, only form of studying is the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chung has a teaching style that does not work for most people. The class was weighted only on 4 tests and some quizzes. The only prep for these tests were questions from the textbook. I spent hours doing those practice problems, but there was simply too much info and not enough help/clarification to make this class manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chung is decent. His lectures are simply him writing on the whiteboard showing examples. In order to understand what happens during his class, you have to read the textbook and do the textbook questions he posts. He does not require HW, but the only way to succeed in his class is to do the textbook and use his lectures as supplements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were him scribbling reactions onto the whiteboard, and there were no presentations online for us to look back on. We were never taught anything conceptual, just thrown problems and expected to understand what was going on. Did not prepare me for orgo 2 whatsoever.

The classes basically consist of him ranting at the board (no slides). If you stop paying attention for 5 minutes, you will be lost and it'll be hard to catch back up. The whole grade consists of 3 midterm exams and a final, with 4 quizzes included in the grade if it increases it. The exam questions come from the textbook though which is good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My review is not the result of "not wanting to work hard", I spent over 10hrs a week (outside of class) reading the text/doing problems. Didn't help. Exams are all MC, no room for error/partial credit. Students are told on day 1 they should be learning from the text not the lectures. I gave it my best effort, still never passed an exam. Worst prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chung is a really good professor. Although he doesn't use slides, which would be nice for organizational purposes, I think that the way he teaches is effective. As long as you pay attention/take notes in class, do the practice problems assigned, and ask him questions you have, you'll be fine. 3 tests 1 final. 4 quizzes are only added if boost grade
I thought Kenny boi was so good at teaching he really taught me to expand me mind and he made my eyes open to the world. Truly an inspiration
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Chung does not have any structure to his presentations. He just draws on a whiteboard and kind of goes on tangents. He does not use slide presentations or anything which is kind of confusing b/c we sometimes dont know what exactly we are studying. He is a funny guy but doesnt make up for his teaching!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Chung was funny in class and showed that he was on our side when grading tests. It would've been helpful to have something else in our grade as it only depended on 3 exam grades (all curved). Doing practice problems on the side helps enforce what is being taught.

He seems to be a nice guy and can be funny but it seems like he goes on tangents. You are graded on 3 exams and there's no finals so if you're a bad test taker like me, don't take his class. He has no office hours and provides minimal feedback. They say if you do the practice problems, you'll be fine but that's not always true
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ken is a funny guy, but cannot teach. He expects you to come in knowing a lot of material. The majority of class is him doing problem examples and racing through content. 3 tests (no final), curved but hard. Even though it is not required, get and read the textbook, it will help for studying the material that is on the test but not covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There were only 2 midterms and an optional final exam, so this class is really graded by few things. The tests are very doable as long as you pay attention in lectures and take good notes. Chung has an amazing personality and keeps you entertained during lectures. Although he goes on tangents often, he explains complicated concepts very well.

Lectures provide the basic information but it is up to the student to read and do all of the practice problems if you want to do well. He often makes mistakes in his answer keys so compare your test with friends to make sure that you were graded correctly and consistently. He will not catch these mistakes himself. Also he gives minimal feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wonderful at explaining complicated concepts. Dr Chung made Organic chem fun and understandable. There is no office hours, however. The best way to succeed is attend lectures and do the hmk.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He usually teaches by doing one or two practice problems as a class, and then the rest is on you to teach yourself using the textbook problems he gives you. If you keep up with your work outside of class then you'll be able to understand the information enough to do well on his tests, which are the only thing he grades you on.
A lot of self-studying is definitely necessary, but he tries and is very funny. Tests are much easier than other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Overall, Ken is an alright professor. He teaches the material mainly through example problems so you'll have to do a bit of self studying. I definitely enjoyed class as he often likes to crack jokes. The exams really aren't too difficult as long as you keep up with his constant example problems, and they're curved really nicely.

Ken Chung was an amazing professor. He taught in a way that was understandable to people who hadn't ever taken Orgo. He also was always able to make us laugh. By far one of my favorite professors ever.

I had Ken for general chem for health science majors and loved it. Thought it was pretty easy considering the majority of topics were covered in my high school chem class. He teaches mostly through example problems, so if that's not your style there's many khan academy videos I found helpful. If you go to class, you don't really need the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I had Ken Chung for orgo and loved him. He knows the material is hard and knows how to break it down so that you can understand it. His practice tests are very helpful for the exams and he reviews a lot. Grade is only made up of 3 exams, but he curves them nicely. He is HILARIOUS and I enjoyed his lectures

Chung is not a great professor. He has a really specific style that may be good for some but I found I difficult. Rather than teaching in a manner that explains the content, he teaches how to solve problems. Youre graded on 3 toUgh 20Q multiple choice exams. He scales a lot but that doesnt mean you know the material which you need for orgo 2
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Grade was determined by three tests. He curves. I may be biased because I like chemistry but the class wasnt terribly hard. Even though he doesn't take attendance go to lectures they are very helpful. The textbook is good for clarifying concepts. Dont buy the new edition, just get the cheaper 8th edition.

ken Chung is so nice & funny. sometimes he gets off topic, as most of his teaching is done through examples. his tests are kind of hard but he scales the grades. he helps the class out tho & always answers questions or reviews a lot if a lot of people are confused. sometimes he may assume you know things so ask questions or ask for help. great guy

He is a wonderful goofy person but as a professor he could use improvements. You take 3 tests and thats it. His lectures tend to be useless and he goes off on story telling often. I would not say the material is hard but because of the lack of helpful lecturing I find that a few days before the test everyone teaches themselves the material.

My main man ken chung. He is ridiculous but you have to embrace it. I hadn't taken chemistry since sophomore year of hs (not AP) and the class was easy. He knows you're only there for the credit, so he scales a lot. Definitely do not worry about your grade, just show up for the performance.
If you come to Chung's classes, pay attention, and do the homework you'll do well. He's an enjoyable and funny professor.

Ken is a good guy and can be funny. He likes to compare the concepts with real world examples, BUT, that is where the good ends and the bad begins. This is supposed to be an ENTRY LEVEL CHEM course. He does not teach entry level Chemistry, he assumes that you know basic and not-so basic chemistry. Well what if you took Chemistry 10 years ago. Poor.

Pretty easy as long as you do the homework. Homework isn't collected or graded, but all the tests have very similar questions. Lectures a bit helpful, but if you still remember high school chemistry it's basically the same thing anyway.

If you were good at high school chem and remember it, then this class should be a breeze. You don't even have to go to class, just do the practice problems and you'll be fine.  If chem was never really your thing, then Ken isn't that great. He teaches concepts well, but he goes off on tangents often and speeds through actual chem problems in class.
chung was a good professor, his lectures can get off topic and you wont do well on his exams if you just study off the lectures. do homework and go to recitation and you will do well

Very good prof. To get a good grade in his class you need :  1. Have taken IB or AP (then it's super easy) If you haven't taken APIB , then :  2. Read the book  3. DO THE HOMEWORK!!! - all the questions on tests are from the homework  In other words, he isn't a hard teacher, pretty good at lectures . If you do the HW , you will get an A .

LOVE Professor Chung! His lectures are extremely easy to understand since he draws everything out on the board. Doesn't make you memorize anything and says he'll even tell you unit conversions or any equations while taking the test. My interest in Chemistry has increased immensely after taking his class.

Ken Chung is a legond! If you actually study you can get an A, his powerpoint and test questiones are copied right from the book. If you don't go to class read the book, if you do go to class all you need to do is a few practice problems that he tells you to.

Doesn't explain anything.  Going to class only confuses you more.  Taught myself everything with the practice problems in the textbook.  It was brutal and it was an intro class.  Get a different teacher if you can!
doesn't explain anything. you will fail.
LOVE THIS MAN! Such an easy class.  Just read the book and do the homework, and you'll get an A.

Wicked easy class. Lectures are so good, take down all notes. Its so easy to follow. I didnt read a single page of the text book, fell asleep in class (but still got all his notes) and got an A in the class. His lectures show step by step how to solve problems. Great guy, with funny jokes.

I had Ken Chung for CHM 101 and CHM 104. 101 was a complete joke, and if you put in a little effort you got an A. Chem 104 was a lot harder and you actually had to go to class. He isn't that great of a teacher as he jumps all over the place, but if you do the problems in the book, you will do fine

Ken Chung is a good guy and really wants his students to do well, but I really struggled in his class.  Going to class never really helped me because he tends to go on tangents.  I think he means well but is slightly overrated.

He is very silly, nice, and helpful but is horrible at teaching. Just kind of goofs around during class time and a lot of the material in class doesn't really show up in the exams. The homework is somewhat helpful.

Professor Chung is great. His class is always interesting, though he may get sidetracked sometimes it's nothing too distracting and he usually always get side tracked by something really interesting. He's also kinda funny sometimes. Chung's class is always a good time.

Took this class in the summer. It was a lot of material crammed into a short amount of time but chung made it pretty easy to understand. His tests were not very hard. If you study the book you will get an A.
cool

Great prof, I had him in the summer so it was really laid back and relaxed. He's a funny guy who clearly explains topics and writes everything on the board. He doesn't grade to hard and doesn't proof read his tests so you'll usually end up getting a few gimmes on every test. Do your work and its an easy A.
The man.  Good teacher, really smart.  Tests are very challenging, have to study hard to do well.  Based off both the notes and the book. he is the man though.

Kenny Chung is a great guy, but the material is difficult to understand if a)u arent listening and b)if u just dont get it. Hes helpful for the most part. A lot of the stuff he goes over in class isn't on the test, so make sure you know how to do the practice problems in the text book. The text book/answer key book will become your best friend.

Chung is the man. Organic chemistry is hard and he definitely understands that. Towards the end of the semester he tends to be more difficult becuase he wants to get through the material. But, he's funny! If you go to class, and use the book, the class is fair.

He definately knew his material, and was avaiable for questions.  Not a signle thing that we went over in class was on the exams.  The tests were among the most difficult of my life.  hes funny, but not very nice out of class.
Chung is a great guy. You'll laugh every day of class, I promise. If you know some basic chemistry, he makes it easy go get the harder stuff. Be amazed at his chalk-board skills.
Not a bad teacher, but he tends to rush through things if nobody asks questions.  He has a funny personality though.  The course is very helpful for exam reviews.

Chung is such an awesome teacher; the best I have had so far.  The material is hard but he is so funny, and it is a releif to have a teacher so passionate.  He is such a funny guy, and I like going to class.  He tells the greatest stories and is one of the few professors that you can tell actually wants to be there.
Very funny and does the best he can to give everyone a good grade.

Started off as best teacher but became the worst towards the last 1/4 of the semester. In the beginning he was great, put things in a way you could relate to.  At the end it seemed like he stopped caring.  The material also gets much harder.  In class open-book quiz answers are all from solutions manual ;)

He actually makes it easy to understand organic chemistry....well not easy, but manageable.  He makes jokes throughout the class and lets you know what examples are going to be on the tests so there are no surprises

One of the top 3 professor's i've had at Northeastern. Very clear, very helpful. Teaches Organic in a way everyone can understand. Great guy who tries to be funny and you can't help but laugh at the attempt :)

He kept things interesting by telling lots of antedotes and was always willing to help. He also made sure that the grades of the class were in the A/B range for all of those who showed that they worked for it.

Most enjoyable teacher I've ever had.Only teaches what you need to know and keeps class interesting,which is not something common at NU.I've never laughed so much in any class,let alone chemistry!Wish I could take every subject with this guy.Do suggested problems and you're guaranteed an A or B.
i love this professor.  He's the best.  He's clear and very helpful and fair
He is awesome. He wants you to do well and learn the information. Makes time available for the students. Highly recommend him, especially for organic chemistry!
No Comments

Chung is the best. He's so engaging and knowledgeable in ALL fields (he now teaches organic and taught math at Harvard). REALLY smart guy. Talk to him after class. He'll get to know you and be more likely to sway your way. Give him a chance! I had a great experience!
CHM1106 too. As long as you show improvement he'll pass you. Show up to office hours, email him. Very reasonable teacher. May not be the best, but definately not the worst.

She was a great professor, her accent is a little bit hard to understand at first but she will do whatever she can do to help you out. Also for her music elective class as long as you show up and pay attention you are almost assured at least a B. I suggest taking her class for sure

Prof. Ciucci is honestly a great professor. She can seem very intimidating at first, but once you get to know her and she gets to know the class, she's hilarious. Yes, her tests can be challenging, especially if you don't pay attention, but she really wants her students to succeed. She offers a lot of help and looks favorably on those who as for it
