she is one of the sweetest professors at northeastern! i love her so much. she is a good lecturer, her homework is doable & helpful but the tests are hard. go to office hours & she will help you study! tests seemed fast/hard but overall great class! highly recommend this prof!

Professor Paparounas is great! She's super nice and understanding, and always has available time for extra help. She's very good at explaining the practice problems during class. Her tests are just a little difficult at times so make sure to study BOTH the concepts and the problems!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I made a RMP account to give Mrs Paparounas a 5 star rating. She's super kind, funny, and truly genuinely wants to see her students succeed. She will help you out in any way possible to make sure you understand. The course material is pretty tough and paying attention in class is a must, but she explains things well and does plenty of examples.

Professor Paparounas was definitely one of my favorite professors I've ever had. Her class is very high pace so it is important to attend and pay attention. Her study guides are very helpful for the tests because some of the exact study guide questions are on the test. She made going to class a lot of fun and I would definitely recommend her.
Professor Paparounas is very funny and light-hearted. However, lectures are very confusing and hard to follow. Be prepared to do a lot of studying on your own time if you want to do well.

Overall good, light-hearted professor. Class size is small so it is easy to ask questions. 3 non-cumulative quizzes, one individual project, easy homework assignments, one final exam. She is flexible with her students and gives the option of online quizzes. One downside is she teaches excel and SPSS software quite quickly, but it's manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. P was a great online professor, one of my first courses and couldn't have been better. She really cares about her students and actually tailors her lectures and hints at homework problems you tell her you struggle with. Great prof, would definitely take again.

Fantastic professor who made physics genuinely engaging. He connects the material to students' interests and is clearly invested in everyone's success. He'll have a lasting impact on the students he teaches.

I thought this class would be super hard, but you honestly don't even need that much Physics 1. He gives a lot of extra credit and teaches really well. If you actually put in effort, you're basically guaranteed an A. Also he is a very sweet and kind person, I would definitely retake this course if I had the opportunity to!

Professor Alberto is the most amazing professor ever! He is so caring and considerate, reach out to him outside of classes if you have any issues. An A it is 92-100, 88-92 is A-, etc. Opportunities for Extra Credit in for all criterias. Gives take home quizzes, which has extra credit problems. For Final he gives extra 5 points for Trace.

Take physics with Alberto! He cares about your success and is passionate about his research, which is very inspiring. His office hours were great for further understanding. He records lectures, provides take-home quizzes, and gives ample extra credit. Overall, a great experience taking his class.

Such a kind professor who really just wants you to succeed. He's super responsive to emails, very flexible, and gives you everything you need to succeed in the class. As long as you put in effort, you'll get an A!

One of the best professors I've had. He's so sweet, easily accessible outside of class, and so genuine. Gives so much extra credit it's truly hard to pass with lower than an A. Double sided cheat sheets allowed for the midterm(25%) and final(30%), take home quizzes that are open everything, and in class problems you have 24h to do.

Alberto is my favorite professor I've had at Northeastern!! His passion for physics and his students is so evident. He is always available outside of class and his office hours are really helpful. He gives ample extra credit. Take physics with Alberto!

(CS2100) Live by the pawtograded, die by the pawtograder. You get three chances on each quiz, and if you keep your lab average and homework average up, it's an easy A/B. Especially if you've coded before, in that case the class is brain dead easy and you'll never have to even show up.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a king. Always responds fast to emails, clearly cares about student and is so helpful. Just king.

Derbinsky goated. Engaging, funny lectures. Knows how to explain complex topics like functional programming to CS beginners. Made lots of time for office hours and seemed to genuinely care about everybody's success. Quick to grade and explain feedback. Best introduction to CS I could have asked for.

Derbinsky is awesome!! I took Fundies I as a non-CS major with very little prior programming knowledge, and while the course is definitely challenging, he made it such a positive experience I could succeed in. He is an engaging lecturer, very knowledgeable, and so genuinely caring for his students (def go to office hrs!) Would highly recommend him!
Derbinsky was one of the most impactful professors I've had at Northeastern. He is very understanding and knows how to break difficult topics into more simple concepts.

Professor Derbinsky is awesome at teaching programming to beginners. He provides many informative videos to help students get started with programming. He definitely took care of his Fundies 1 students. Course was definitely time-consuming, but Derbinsky does not give you a hard time.
the absolute GOAT.

AMAZING. Probably the best professor I've ever had. His lectures are super clear and engaging; I found the time flying by and I was never bored. He's hilarious and makes learning CS fun. Also super accessible - he's always happy to talk to students after class and help with code. If you have the opportunity, TAKE HIS CLASS!
I just wanted to document this experience. I worked as a researcher with Prof. Derbinsky. My experience is that Prof. Derbinsky is a rude person from my personal interaction.

Great Professor. Class is run really well. Stays on top of Piazza comments like a hawk.
10 / 10 - would take again.
Prof. Derbinsky is funny, engaging, and really good at teaching students how to code, even if they have no prior coding knowledge/expierence.
Derbinsky is great, he goes over topics very thoroughly and is very funny. His lectures are fun to attend and he clarifies any doubt a student has. He is also very approachable after classes.
Literally the goat
Really good lecturer made it interesting. Probably wasn't difficult enough, especially for people with prior cs experience.
Cool professor

Quite literally the best professor I have ever had in my life. His lectures are actually fun and engaging. The outside of class material is super helpful. Explains lessons fluently and eloquently. Fundies can be challenging, but if you have Derbinsky it is 100% better for you and your grade. He should be your first priority in course selection.

Derb is great, If you have an opportunity to take any of his lectures I would highly recommend him. He takes the time to answer any questions asked in lecture to best fit how he feels the student would understand it, and makes sure to make himself available after lecture if more detail is needed. If you can, take his sections!

Derbinsky's an amazing lecturer, makes it engaging and is a charasmatic CS nerd in the best way (as a non-CS major). Made the content easy to understand. Homework can be tough and GO TO OFFICE HOURS w the TAs, but I thought it was fine overall. Posts supplemental online lectures that take 1/2 the time so u dont have to show up in person, but I did.

Prof Derbinsky is the nicest and best teacher I have ever had! He truly cares about his students and will take the time to re-explain and help with any topic. His class was super interesting, easy to understand, and extremely useful. He did such an awesome job of engaging everyone and even met with us outside of class to help with projects!
Lectures are easy to follow and he is a nice funny guy. Just get ready to play the lottery on getting a coding partner.
Great, clear lectures. Professor Derbinsky makes complex topic digestible.

In my first sem online and he was by far the best in terms of replying to emails instantly, tons of help from the TA's also. He made online classes so much more bearable with pair programming and other opportunities to connect with people so we don't feel alone.
Awesome professor, lectures are clear and interesting and really helpful outside of class too. Highly, highly recommend!!

Prof. Derbinsky is super approachable and encouraging! Overall he's one of the best professors I've had. Doesn't talk down to students at all, even in an intro course where it's easy for some profs to do, and very understanding. Even when course material got more complicated, his explanations were really helpful. 20/10 would recommend!

Need no introduction, one of the BEST profs at NEU. Nice guy, fun classes, always there for u. I won't say the class is difficult but there're some assignments that you need to spend time with, but the prof and TAs are always there for u.

Professor Derbinsky is an amazing professor! He's one that isn't condescending or makes you feel bad if you don't understand a concept. He will help you and be really supportive if you reach out to him! Super friendly on piazza and all around nice guy. His lectures are really helpful and he will answer any questions you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good professor. The curriculum is standardized for this class so the professor doesn't matter too much. However, he is a very compassionate guy and really wants people to succeed. Lectures are pretty good, but where he really shines is when you ask for help. Prompt responses to emails, and is very accessible outside of class.

This is the best professor I've had so far at Northeastern. He found a good balance between being funny and making class interesting and still getting through everything we needed to cover. Even if you didn't like his jokes, he doesn't make them often enough for it to become frustrating or distracting. Also just a nice dude and brilliant.
Great professor, makes lectures fun to learn.
What a guy, great lecturer and professor, would take his class again for sure.
Best professor Ive had, he makes the class fun and a lot more enjoyable. Hes very interactive with students and knows how to make everyone happy while in class.

Very approachable, both inside & outside the class. Attend his classes, he simplifies everything & teaches all you need to learn in the course with clarity. Get ready to work though, you won't get an easy A here. I detested DBMS before taking up his class & now I will be graduating with a specialization in DB, need I say anything else?
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The 1-star reviews do have a point, the class is a lot of memorizing jargon. None of the class work is all that difficult tho, most is just applying the aforementioned jargon. The exams are open note too. The lectures are hard to sit through because it just keeps going and going and going. Prof. Dias himself is a good dude, energetic and passionate

If you are a very technical person, then this class might be good, but it's not for everyone. 

He makes it very difficult to understand the concepts if you don't have prior understanding. Repeats lectures every week. Started off the semester by warning us that "we will probably fail." Thinks its ok to grade work like 3.4859 USING AI TO GRADE!
hes actually the chillest mf so funny and is such a lil caring man

Martin a G. the guy offers inspirational lectures I mean are we da??? If you fail this class u stupi alls you gotta do is raise yo hand ery now and then he even clap back wit a lil giggle its ma favorite class. We eve get a wacky wednesday last class he brought in his action figure collection,I tried on his light up batman mask. Luh this guy fr

He thinks it's okay to give a student a 89.9876 on an exam and not round. He gave one student in the class a 6.99 for participation. He is on a high horse, and you don't learn a thing, saying you'll probably fail.

I wish I read RMP earlier. The entire class is just memorizing jargon. I'm convinced that he designed the introductory MIS course to steer students away from the department. Good for him, because I'm never taking such a course again, especially when he's teaching. Avoid at all costs.

Just back to remind everyone that he designed MISM 2301. Yes, all the 10 odd sections who take this class every semester learn the same outdated jargon filled stuff because he does not care to change anything about it. He needs to go.
Honestly, he shouldnt be that bad for you, if you actually put in some work.

I hope he stops teaching. Spending a third of each class “revising” the previous class while skipping slides in the current class is ridiculous. Easy material made unnecessarily hard. Pointless jargon, outdated class materials… I could go on. Avoid this class at all costs.

I have no words. I have learned nothing from this course, and I got an A with 95% attendance. I found out today that his professor is responsible for the course being designed in this manner. Hundreds of students learn nothing in this class every semester due to him. I hope NEU changes something because this should not fly with the amount we pay.

Pros: Excel, Figma, group work doesn't trash your grade, professor Dias is lively and has (dry) humor, theme Thursdays are fun, provides feedback even for hw, literally tells you "this will be good for your notes..."
Cons: 1> hw due per week, required textbook ($$), some topics felt less necessary than others, lectures can get boring, grading
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Frustrating course. Slides have little to no text. Prof spends 20 minutes talking about the previous lecture which can easily be avoided. Then he skims through the current lecture while going off on tangents at every turn. Case studies are graded pretty randomly. Exams are weird, and require you to spew out the same jargon he said in class.  Avoid!

I got a good grade in this class, but let me make this very clear - every lecture is boring. This professor cannot talk for 5 minutes without going on tangents, and it feels intentional because there is nothing worth talking. As others have mentioned, you may do well in the class depending on your notes, but you are guaranteed to learn nothing.
Enjoyed having Professor Dias this semester. The tests were online, open-book.  Assignments and tests weren't too difficult as they were all based on how well you could take notes.

If style over substance were a professor, you've got your guy. If you think positively of him, it's likely that you got a good grade. But if you care about learning, you can't help but be disgusted because you'll learn absolutely nothing that's useful. It blows my mind that this is a mandatory class for me. Makes me pity the MIS folks.

legit one of my favorite profs ever. the class is a lot of work but he does his best to really help students do well and feel comfortable with the class. tbh if you do badly it's kinda ur own fault cuz he has so many good resources and office hours are super helpful. as long as you do the reading and put effort into work you should be just fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a weird class. The professor talks a lot, and yet when you leave the class you don't feel like you've learned anything. The class materials seem terribly outdated. It's a shame that he is the one who's in charge of this course at the university and is largely responsible for how bad this is. Busy work with no learning.

He's mostly fair, there are a lot of case studies, exams are a bit hard. He definitely cares about his students. I feel like there wasn't a lot of learning in the class, but there also is, it's a really weird class. MAKE SURE TO TAKE NOTES when he says "You might want to write this down." He is a good a person, but I didn't really like the class.

Subpar professor that teaches with enthusiasm, however is overly critical of work. Wastes 20 minutes every class engaging students and covering the previous classes material. The rest of class is spent covering slideshows that are visually incredibly difficult to understand.

I honestly don't even know what this course was about. I would participate in class but not even know what I was saying. I'm think he sometimes doesn't even know what he's saying either. He goes off on many tangents which don't help and won't ever answer a question directly. Really weird course and I'm still just as confused as I was at the start.

A submitted assignment that's complete & accurate won't get a 100; thorough case study submissions will get a 3.6 out of 4 unless they go above and beyond. Because of this and the fact that every point of the assignments count to a total of 100, I found it hard to get above a B+/A-. Still, he def cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Professor Dias's class is definitely more difficult than other MISM courses but you will learn so much from him. The class is based on weekly case studies and he gives very detailed feedback on them. Class participation is weighed very heavily, participation every class is expected. Hard but definitely worth it, Professor Dias is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Extremely professional. sometimes felt like an etiquette-esque class. Focus on the main ideas, I found that its one thing then 4 little things and that was primarily it. Exams are online slightly difficult but are just how and why you would implement certain things. Case studies are short yet you have to be clean and extremely precise and detailed.

If you take MISM2301 with Martin Dias, you will need to put a lot of effort into this class to get a good grade. He grades your participation on each class session (which was intentionally kept secret as far as I could tell) so if you don't go to class you're kind of screwed. But if you put in the effort you realize he's a dope professor.

Professor Dias was great. As long as your participate and you put in effort into the case studies, you will do fine. I personally got an A- because I did not participate in class discussions as much as I should, so I could have gotten a higher score if I did.. MISM 2301 is a hard course, but Prof. Dias is the best one there is so take it as u will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The only reason that people wouldn't get an A in mism is because they don't participate. Graded on case studies, at home quizzes, at home (REALLY HARD. but graded leniently) exams, and participation. Case studies were definitely time consuming (not hard to get a good grade if you read rubric). Sit in the front row and participate and you are fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My favorite professor! He's passionate about teaching! His class can be daunting since it requires high engagement and performance, but he is really understanding. He has an uppity personality that some people may be taken aback by, but his being himself is part of what makes his teaching great. Assessments are 100% fair. Don't be disorganized.

as far as professors go for MISM, Dias is pretty good. He's a really nice guy who cares about students and is available outside of class. The assignments are pretty tough and exams are the hardest I've taken at NU. Still, I think he is one of the better professors for information systems and an overall good choice!
Amazing professor , bad course

Passionate about the course, but grades very harshly considering he skims over concepts for the test in class that are not even explained on the slides or the textboo. Emphasizes participation, but students are less inclined to participate because of his tangents and his extra obnoxious personality. If you want an A don't take this course

I think Dias is a great professor, but I hated the course. The course is just simple concepts stretched so thin like a trojan on a gourd. I don't know why this course is a must for CSBA students who take courses from both colleges. I really hope Dias gets to teach a higher-level course. He's passionate and knowledgeable and I think he'd be great.

Prof Dias is super enthusiastic about the course. The course itself is honestly pretty hard to understand if you aren't tech inclined and he made it as easy to understand as he could. If you constantly participate, really focus on textbook readings, and are able to keep up in lectures, you'll do well. Assigns 1-2 cases a week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dias is great, if you're willing to work hard. He is very clear about his expectations and expects you to bring 100% to everything you do. If you aren't willing to work hard or learn, don't take his class. He LOVES what he does and is always willing to meet outside of class to go more in depth. He can get carried away on tangents during lectures.

Smart guy, terrible teacher. He is knowledgeable about MIS but can’t get the concepts across to students in a meaningful manner. Its obvious from his feedback that he only glances over homework and grades them based on how many buzzwords you throw around. As other students have said he is incredibly condescending

All of the reviews here are entirely correct. Made the mistake of reading these reviews and still taking the course. Don't make the same mistake. The class makes no sense, and he throws around meaningless buzz words that he rarely ever takes time to explain. Sometimes it feels like he does not even know what he's saying.

MISM just makes no sense in general. Idk why they teach it, everyone I talked to says the same. Given that this course makes no sense, this guy goes out of his way to be a tough grader. To get an A- or an A, you have to tryhard every single class and schedule a meeting in the beginning of the semester on "how to get a superior grade" :/

Its not even the confusing instruction that bothers me (use technical word salad in assignments and your solid). Professor Dias is just an obnoxious dude, something I sensed from the first day of class. Ive observed on more than one occasion him embarrassing well-intentioned students for no good reason. Hands down the worst professor Ive had.

Prof. Dias is passionate about MISM2301. He assigns 2 cases studies a week along with take home quizzes that both rack up to be a large portion of your grade. 3 exams, first one is very difficult while the last 2 are very similar, but you get used to his "style." PARTICIPATE -- it will help you stay engaged in the class because it can get boring

Unless youre 100% focused the whole class you cant pass. His grading is horrible, even if you try so hard you can never get a full grade. The class is the hardest class that I ever took, my friends took the same class but different professor, and it was much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don'. Take. Him. I'm a CS kid and his class is harder than my cs classes. Easy concepts are twisted and forced into irrelevant case studies for the exam. He rounds grades to the 20th decimal place just to increase your anxiety. The slides barely cover the textbook. Atleast 2 quizzes and case studies are due every week. He makes it hard on purpose.

Professor Dias' lectures are very hard to understand. A lot of the information within the textbook and lectures isn't applicable to the case studies. He grades case studies strictly and tests (there are 3) more leniently. It's pretty hard to get an A in this class so if you're trying to protect your 4.0, you probably shouldn't take this professor.

Literal hardo for no reason. Dias thinks that his class is the center of the universe and assigns a ton of work, however his feedback sucks and his lectures are hard to understand. He also grades participation for each individual class, something he didn't make clear at the start. Worst prof I have ever had, stay away.

Dias is definitely passionate about MIS which really shines through his lectures, not many professors are as enthusiastic as him about a base level course. On the other hand, he is very unclear when giving feedback and is a very strict grader even about simple hw assignments. He also makes tests unnecessarily difficult and quizzes 1-2 times a week.

Person below me is the teacher's pet, go figure. Dias holds a high standard for his students and none for himself He waited until the last month to grade everything and is extremely condescending and unhelpful with all of his feedback. I can confidently say I didn't learn a thing in his class and was a total waste of time. Never again.

Dias is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable, I guarantee anyone who rated him poorly wasn't really paying attention. It is difficult to get an A, but if you have any remote interest in the topic and aren't just taking it for a grade-booster, I would definitely recommend. Amazing lectures and you NEED to go to class to understand the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Extremely clear lecturer, very passionate and a great guy. The class content is not the most interesting, but he definitely explains the topics clearly (you will learn!). Difficult to get an A, but very easy to get a B/B+ w/ minimal effort. Due to the amount of work due, grading was handed back fairly late. If you're a serious student, take him!

The topics are fairly straightforward, but he makes them much more confusing. He is very disorganized but has rigid structure for what you can/cannot say and do. He goes on lots of tangents and gets distracted easily. He is very unclear about his tests. No clarity into how he grades or assesses you. Has high expectations for you but not himself.

Professor Dias is very knowledgeable and clearly knows what he is talking about when it comes to MISM. With that said, his case studies can be difficult at times, but his tests are graded more leniently and are open note. Overall a really great guy who is amazing at teaching and connecting with his students. Not an easy A though so be ready to work
The most awful professor I have met. He does not lecture in a logical way and his presentation slides are nonsense. Plus you never know what grade you will receive.

Of the harder MIS teachers. Easy grader for tests. Hard grader for case studies. Participation and preparation matters a lot to him. The textbook is useless. His lectures are boring, but if you don't actively pay attention, the slides make no sense. Its hard to apply his lectures to case studies. This class was hard for no reason compared to others
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dias is super passionate about MIS but makes the class more difficult than it should be. Lectures are often hard to follow, exams are challenging and stressful but graded leniently, and case studies take a long time to do them right. If you're looking for an easy class, avoid Dias, but if you want to work hard he will teach you a lot!

This class was one of the biggest wastes of time and money I have ever experienced. This dude is really fired up about the class which is cool, but I learned absolutely nothing. The grading makes no sense, and he gives almost no feedback. He sets deadlines but can't keep any himself. Overall just a really bad class with a really mediocre prof.

One of the more difficult professors I've had. Definitely a smart man, and he's engaging. However, his grading is not straightforward and very ambiguous. Its very easy to get a B or B+ with adequate participation, but getting an A is very very hard (94+). Participation is HUGE and his slides are incomprehensible if you don't follow along in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Only take him if you're serious about the class. Absolutely phenomenal lecturer. Has extensive knowledge in his field, and committed to students' success. Class material needs careful work, participation is a huge deal, but everything positively compounds on each other if you work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: if you do not answer questions in class, your participation will be 4/10 even you come up every class. 10 minutes quiz before each session, 1 case study every week, 3 exams, no final.

Loved his classes! So engaging and keeps MIS material exciting (and funny too). Exams are pretty challenging but he's definitely worth it! His depth of knowledge in MIS and technology is overwhelming! Although I'm probably going to end up with a B+ in his class and I'm typically a straight A student, I don't regret taking his class.

If you don't want to participate daily in this class, do not try and get an A. If you want a B, then this class is an easy B regardless of how hungover you are. Case studies are all on course hero, its worth the $15 a month for an easy B+ or A-

Dias was one of the most life changing professors I've had in my life. So passionate about MIS, his lectures force you to listen to him and furthered my fascination in MIS. Tests are rather difficult (open book, but notes didn't personally help that much) so he makes you work for it. In office hours, he is more than willing to help you do well.

Dias is a very passionate, very great teacher. He reiterates the most important topics to assure everyone understands the foundation and is very energetic. He really cares to make sure students learn, regardless of major or even if no-one wants to be there. Participate and you'll be his best friend. He really appreciates participation.
tough grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: DiasBEST professor ever. I'm NOT naturally smart (never a 4.0 student) & didn't have prior MIS knowledge but took MIS in Summer 1 (2x faster than Fall/Spring) & got an A. If you're willing to put MANY HOURS into case studies & studying you'll succeed. Dias will prepare you for coop like no other by challenging you & make $60k tuition worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Dias is exactly what I look for in a Professor. He is knowledgeable, fair, and he treats students as his equals. The class requires effort, and is probably more difficult than the same course taught by other professors, but Professor Dias will ensure each student receives the grade they earned. He is a role model to future educators.
Makes boring material exciting and interesting, I enjoyed his class and found him to be a fair and clear grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MGSC 6204 Managing Information Resources was a require MBA course focused on IT systems. This class had very little value to me and a heavy workload for a 1.5 credit class. The only positive experience I had was with Prof Dias. He kept us engaged every class and was a joy to listen to. Great professor! Boring subject that had very little value!

Dias is a great professor. So passionate and enthusiastic that he makes a dull subject interesting. He's also one of the most articulate guys I've ever met. The course will challenge you and class participation is a big part of your grade, but his teaching style facilitates discussion so the participation is natural. If you want to learn, take Dias
he's good but he wont just give you a grade

Dias is an amazing teacher and one of the best I've had at NU. Im not a "tech" person and he was able to actually get me engaged in this dry MIS class material. You need to participate and do the HW! FYI you can google online quiz q's for answers. Definitely need to study for tests and read the grading criteria, it really helps to score higher.

He is great! One of the best professors I have had a NU. He makes the dry material of MISM interesting and engages all the students in class. You have to come to class to learn/pass the class. But if you work hard he will notice and he's willing to help anyone who asks for it.

Professor Dias is awesome- the topic is not the most interesting business class but he makes it practical in terms of being a business person. He is one of the most intelligent and insightful teachers I have had at Northeastern and is the only teacher one should consider when taking MIS.

He is very passionate about MIS. He makes a boring subject kind of exciting. He has a good sense of humor. He will always try to do something different to keep your attention. Go to office hours and participate and you will see a difference. Grading is fair. Tests and Cases are challenging but they are the same for all MIS classes.

He is the only prof. teaching the MIS class that changed the way things are done, making students think "outside the box". I personally found that i wasnt falling asleep in his class, but subject is not interesting. All exams are heavy on analysis and absolutely no memory.

DIas is very passionate about teaching and keeps classes interesting. He gives his own version of the material, which seemed good at first, but by the end caused the class to be really hard. Avoid if you don't want the hardest tests ever.

He's a mathematician and not an engineer. Mediocre lecturer, sometimes does the mathematician thing where he has to cover all his tracks and be specific with his language. You don't have to show up to lectures if you can teach yourself the content from lecture notes online. Every homework assignment and test had corresponding practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall cool guy, your grade is just 20% quizzes, 40% midterms and 40% final, but the quizzes are similar to the practice ones which is good. You can honestly skip his lectures and just teach yourself the material in the same amount of time and get easy A's on the quizzes.
Just take it with any other professor! There's no extra credit, Very hard to understand, and not accesible.
Good teacher, lectures sometimes hard to follow, but very good notes and practice quizzes/tests.
He's just a lil guy.

He's a pretty good professor for Diff Eq; he teaches the material well and the quizzes/tests are very similar to the practice problems. He also posts all of the lecture notes onto Canvas and the notes are well organized. He does occasionally trail off and the lectures can be boring but he's not a bad teacher.

I didn't have to attend to any of his lectures to get an A in the class, the notes are really good if you understand everything on notes you will get 100 in all the quizes ez. Also the slides for notes are only 3-5 pages so lock in.
I liked Dmitre. His lectures were wildly boring and he sometimes struggled with solving the example problems. However, he posted goo

I'm not sure why his rating is low because he's a great professor. He explains concepts thoroughly and focuses on understanding over memorization. He posts practice tests for every quiz/exam(a week+ ahead), and the real tests are very similar. He also tells you what's on the exam a week in advance. Highly recommend.
He posts practice problems which are very similar to his real quizzes and midterms, if you go to recitation you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this class with Dimitre. He is a nice guy; however, he is extremely difficult to follow and pay attention to. He is very wandering and unformatted. He often backtracks and goes off on tangents. By 3 minutes in, everyone is lost. As I said, reasonably nice guy, BAD teacher.

This was my favorite professor I have had for a math course since being at NEU. He is very nice and has a great understanding of the material. He goes over some notes, then does a few examples which really make sure that you know what you're doing. Go to office hours because he is always willing to help.

I took this class in summer 2, and idk if it was just the summer semester vibes, but I felt he was very forgiving in grading. Partial credit can get you pretty far. Also he allows cheat sheets on exams and there's really no trick questions on quizzes. I had a terrible Calc 2 prof so this class helped me like math again tbh.
he is SO hard to understand and hella unapproachable, buttttt he gives great detailed lecture notes and llets you have a full page of notes for every test including the final.

hes a nice guy but his accent is literally so hard to understand and his vibe is so unapproachable. the lecture notes were very detailed tho, and hes a generous test grader. the course material is not very hard andddd you get an entire page of notes for every exam

Just took this professor and he pretty much sucked. If you really care to learn the material do not take this teacher. I basically taught myself the entire course since Dimitre was hard to understand and really really boring. hw is pretty similar to the quizzes but a few of the quizzes are just super hard for no reason.

This class was one of my least favorite because of not only the course material, but the homework. Homework was very hard.
the professor always mumbles when he speaks and it is hard to understand what is going on in lecture, I could never keep track of what was going on. I will say, he does grade the exams very generously

Professor Dimitre Tzigantchev was honestly the best professor I have ever had in my life, he brings the life into the classroom. While many may have the opposite reaction to him, I think that he brings fun to what is not a very fun subject. He is consistent with class examples, pictures, homework that matches what he puts on exams. GO DIMITRE!
lots of lecturing, most people have already taken calculus so he doesn't hold your hand through it; however, there is lots of help available and most importantly he is really genuinely nice guy.

Honestly I did not feel that Professor Dimitre was bad at all. There were times where he would mix up his words or forget some but it wasn't to the point where I couldn't understand what was being taught. Your grade is dependent on only quizzes and exams, so attending the lectures is important and the practice quizzes given are insanely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tzigantchev means well, but his lectures are useless and end up being confusing. If you haven't take calc before I wouldn't recommend him, also your grade is only dependent on quizzes and exams.

Would not recommend. Would often approach him after class to ask questions and would receive vague and unhelpful answers. Doing the research myself proved to be more helpful than reaching out to him for extra help. 

Quizzes involve lots of multiple choice, which I have not seen before in a class like this.

His lectures aren't very helpful he spends time talking about why he;s doing something irrelevant to the problem he's solving. There's a lot of quizzes, if you haven't recently taking an AP calc class in high-school I wouldn't recommend him. His office hours aren't really helpful either and he doesn't check or post the answer to hw assignments.

I took AB Calculus in high school (got a 3 on the exam so I didn't get credit), and this course was a lot easier. I never went to class because I didn't find it very helpful - when I did I just did practice problems on my own. He posts practice tests that are almost exactly like the actual tests - definitely do them!!! Super easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are informative and this class is not hard if you pay attention. Unfortunately, he doesn't really explain the ideas conceptually and just teaches you how to do the math. Homework is optional and grading comes entirely from quizzes and tests.

Absolutely do not take this class if you haven't taken calculus before. He treats the class like review and is not good at answering questions. The class is mostly self-taught and he often mumbles during lectures.

I do not recommend taking this class with Dimitre if you did not take calculus in high school, my grade is solely on background knowledge. He is hard to follow and strays from the topic. I recommend using the guided notes that he provides. You are graded on 6 highest quizzes of 7, a midterm, and a final. He gave substantial bonus points at the end.

Nice guy, teaches everything by the textbook. He often does calculations in his head which can lead to confusion. Homework is not mandatory as long as you understand the topic. There are quizzes mostly every week but as long as you do the practice problems you'll be ok. Tests have formula sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DID NOT TAKE AP CALC!!!!! His lectures are very confusing and he has messy hand writing which it very hard to understand. Anyone who didn't talk AP calc is struggling. Also 40% of ur grade is ur final. He does give extra credit though which is kind.

Good guy, kinda bland but he teaches the material in class pretty well. It's all very formulaic. No practice problems, I did no homework the entire time bc it is optional. Do the practice before the quiz because they're pretty much the same thing. Quizzes every week. Tests allow formula sheets.

The professor is incredibly boring and hard to follow. He simply writes on the board without engaging with the class and when presented with a question, he struggles to give a clear answer. The only reason why I am doing ok here is because of AP Calc last year. The quizzes/ tests are graded harshly and minor mistakes cost you greatly.

This variation of calc1 should be avoided as it covers concepts way into diff eq and linear algebra. Prepare to solve systems of ODE and use lambda substitution to find eigenvectors. Dr T did not help digest this rather challenging material which became more apparent as the class shifted to more difficult topics. U can still do well if ur smart tho
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a great teacher, be prepared to study tons outside of class. Would brush through problems and start new topics without ever explaining the content or the methods used. There is a significant amount of extra material posted on canvas which made it somewhat helpful to practice with, however the entire grade was dependent on quizzes and the final.

Don't buy the textbook! everything you need is uploaded to Canvas including practice quizzes, lecture notes, and homework problems. the math in this class isn't too complicated as long as you listen and participate in class. His lectures can be difficult to follow because he goes on tangents but generally, he isn't a terrible professor.

Professor Tzigantchev means well, but his lectures are often confusing and he does not explain concepts well. He does provide practice quizzes that are very similar to the real quizzes. He also allows you to drop your worst quiz grade. If you haven't taken calc before, you will struggle in this class.

Do not take if you haven't taken calc already. I took calc before and the class was still bad. Someone else grades the tests, and they are not fair with scores. He is hard to understand at times and when asked to elaborate on a concept, he gives no explanation or overcomplicates. Practice problems uploaded are helpful, go to the recitations!!!!

Just shows no care for his students. A genuine disregard for how well his students are doing and whether or not they understand. Class moves so fast and covers topics well into calc 2 despite being a calc 1 class. No matter what you do, just take regular calc 1 for the same credit. Office hours and recitations are available and u will need them.

He is very scattered during lectures and always over complicates concepts. If you go into this class without having any prior knowledge of calculus, you will struggle a lot. The final is worth 40% of your grade and there is only 6 other exams, but the lowest grade will get dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People aren't lying here. I thought I could beat the odds.....don't take it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly feel that dimitre is given too much hate. I think he gives enough resources to do good in class like practice problems from a textbook. The test questions are almost exact to these questions and sometimes he will take questions straight from the textbook. If you took AP Calc then this class will be easy, i found it easier than AP Calc.

Has a very thick Russian accent that can be difficult to understand. There is a separate grader for the class who is not generous with partial credit AT ALL. I already took calc in high school but he tended to overcomplicate things.
If I didn't already know the content of this class from AP classes in high school I would have been completely lost otherwise.

I loved his ambition to practice lessons as much as class time goes. Please come to class every day, it's worth it. There's a separate grader for our exams and he is very evil when it comes to taking off points. Go to office hours and get them points back! ;) P.S. do the homework! It helps you with exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was an average professor-that is if you took calc before. If not, you will have to put in more work for this class. The grading was limited to 6 midterms (60%). If you get a bad grade on one, it takes a toll on your grade. Lastly, the last grade is the final (40%). Idk who graded the midterms but sometimes the points taken off are inaccurate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures can be difficult to follow, but he does a lot of examples and answers questions. There's biweekly quizzes and a final, all of which he posts a lot of practice material/past quizzes for. If you do those practice problems, you'll do well. There's also two homework assignments, which boost your grade. Funny guy.

This professor was the worst one I have had in my 2 years at Northeastern. You are graded on 6 tests and 1 final exam. With the limited things to be graded on it does not help that the grading in the class is inconsistent, you could have exactly the same work and answer as a person in the class and receive completely different grades. DON'T TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A walking disaster giving Fs everywhere. Every morning I go to his class and see his face, I have PTSD and wish to un-alive myself. Does NOT care about his students at all. He only grades exams and the final exams. He is devil reincarnated. Horrible sense of styling and his checks are made by BLOOD, SWEAT, AND TEARS of students in his class.

reviews.comment: He is literally satan reincarnated. I wanted to unalive myself every single time I stepped out of my dorm because of this class. DO NOT TAKE.

Professor T was very hard to understand in his lectures, and is not clear when answering questions regarding the material. The class is based on 6 exams and the final, and although the difficulty of them was not terrible, the lectures just confused me and I spent a ton of time outside of class before assessments teaching myself!

no quizzes, your entire grade is based off 6 exams and a final. calculators weren't allowed on exams, yet he would teach example problems that you needed calculators for. some questions on the exams weren't like what we did in class nor were they like the homework.

reviews.comment: Dimitre seems like a good guy who is pretty funny. It's a lecture heavy class and it is very difficult to understand what he is saying or what he means when he is teaching. But he gives homework which most MATH1251 professors do not give that helps to boost your grade.

Not a good professor. Goes over problems on the board that take up almost the whole class and then says they won't be on the tests. Only graded based on 6 tests that are very hard to do well on. Doesn't provide any resources or extra credit opportunities even though class grades aren't good. Easily distracted and goes over class. AVOID HIM!!!

Overall ok professor. Does go over time but if you take his class go to every lecture if you can and DON'T take the remake tests if you are not able to take the test at the original time. The remake test was way harder than the original test for no reason and only has fewer questions with more weight to the points you can get.

reviews.comment: Out of the few Calc 1 professors, he is one of the better ones. Few days before a quiz, he will send out a recitation PDF that literally look like the exam and I would recommend just reviewing that for the night, and you will be all set for his quizzes. He assigns only two homeworks which count as a quiz and is very helpful to boost your grade.

Prof is okay: make sure you, like, really know all the material before bi-weekly quiz day or you'll inevitably lose 10% on ur exam b/c quizzes are ~6-8 Qs each. Grading demonstrates the 'butterfly effect': if you make a small error w/ your numbers you lose most of ur points on that question. Also does a 'meh' job of explaining course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I felt like I learned more from my online research to study than from his class. The only reason you make a good grade is from recitation and the online example quiz, not from his teaching. If you try you won't get a bad grade, but if you haven't taken calc in HS the prof is almost impossible to understand. Go to the recitation!

The lectures were straightforward and super easy to understand. As for exams/quizzes, he gives a practice quiz on Canvas that is literally the exact format as the quiz we get, so it was easy to pass. He also was just a nice/funny person.

Lectures are pretty boring, but the quizzes and tests are pretty easy and he gives a lot to practice from so there are never any surprises. Honestly, you probably won't get much out of lecture unless you already know what you're doing, but it doesn't take much time out of class to teach yourself what you need to get a relatively easy A.

Tziagatchev's lectures are soft-spoken and difficult to follow. However, his quizzes are very fair, and he always posts a lot of online material that help prep for the quizzes. There is also endless online (youtube, etc) material for Calc 1, so it's very possible to teach yourself the content necessary for quizzes.

Lots of people find his lectures boring but I got a kick out of them cause he's unintentionally a pretty funny guy. As long as you put in the work on homework you should expect no surprises on his tests and quizzes and get a good grade.

Hard to understand accent, very messy handwriting, and can talk in circles but you can tell he's trying. He's an easy grader and gives lots of partial credit just make sure you understand the material. His explanations aren't very helpful, and many times can confuse you more. Although he's nice I would take with Prof George instead
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard class to take at 8 in the morning (or any time). Lectures are dull, and he moves very quickly over new topics and on to the next . Will answer questions, but gives long, meandering answers that may or may not give you the answer you needed. Be prepared to spend lots of time outside of class teaching yourself the parts you don't understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know why he has such a bad rep. Lectures are boring, but it's an easy A with no surprises! Only thing is that you need to have a solid background in calc to understand. His quizzes are very straightforward, exactly like his practice quizzes. He is so sweet and always willing to help even though his feedback isn't great. Love him!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst math professors I've ever had. He puts a slide up and talks about it for 30 minutes without writing anything down. The notes he does right down don't make sense and he talks himself in circles. Wouldn't reccomend.
Quizzes are straightforward, and there are no surprises. He's very nice, but his lectures are a bore. He will help you if you have a question but his answers aren't always straight forward.

Lectures are boring, but easy to follow. He's a really nice person and will help you if you ask. Quizzes are straight forward, no surprises. Does practice problems in class that are like what you see on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I went to the first week of zoom lectures him, and bailed on learning the material from him after that. His lectures were extremely difficult to follow and his notes were hard to read. I ended up teaching myself the material using youtube videos instead.

He teaches this class like its the most boring thing hes ever taught. Its very hard to stay engaged and he rarely ever checks zoom chat. He constantly goes back on his sentences and it makes it hard to follow what hes saying and he goes on very long tangents trying to answer questions and still doesnt answer them.
I enjoyed this class and the professor. Group project grading felt fair overall. Laptops aren't used in class, so be prepared to take notes by hand.
Soooo boring. Classes are like a Wikipedia (but more boring). You don't learn anything. Pointless lectures
so boring and mandatory attendance, everything was kinda guessable and easy?

Professor Youly is really nice and genuinely cares about her students. Overall, her class is very straightforward and easy, as a lot of the content is common sense. Just be aware that attendance does impact your grade and she also doesn't let you use computers.

Great professor. Super chill. 100% recommend. Homework is very manageable. Exams are easy if you focus in class. Very kind and respects all students--also remembers everyone's names and backgrounds :) Never cold calls and ensures a safe space! Also extremely understanding!

Youly is very sweet and understanding of her students' needs. The class is very lecture heavy when I've heard that other teachers make it much more interactive. The class utilizes a lot of group work that lasts throughout the semester.

Youly is a great professor and she truly cares about her students. She is always inviting people to utilize office hours and frequently offers opportunities for students to expand their learning beyond the classroom. It was a great course to get an overview of related topics, and exams are straightforward. I highly reccomend her course!

She's a great person, cares about her students and I found her lectures to be pretty interesting. Class structure is super weird - 3 essays, 7 pages all about the exact same topic. She is not a super easy grader, but I would still recommend as I did look forward to hearing her lectures every day.

Definitely an easy grader and the class is easy to pass if you pay slight attention and study a bit for the midterm and final. Her lectures are incredibly boring and she forces students to take handwritten notes but a lot of it is common sense. She does allow students to do class via zoom which is very nice.

I took her as an elective and this class was great. I learned alot tbh.  She is flexible on zoom. To be honest easy A ,study lecture slides and you will be fine for the exams . Theirs alot of discussions board but its straight forward. She is accessible through her emails and office hours. she so nice.

A really kind professor, an easy grader, and flexible with extensions or anything you have going on outside of class. I wouldn't say that I learned much in the class but I don't think there is much more to learn in IAF after foundational courses so I don't think that is her fault. I would recommend taking her if you have to take and IAF class.

She is an incredibly kind and understanding professor. I enjoyed her class a lot, even though it did get a bit dry sometimes. I really liked that she brought in many guest speakers who had amazing stories to tell. If you put in the work, it's an easy A. Many discussion boards, midterm and final, and a few papers. Overall, not a very hard class.
Would totally take her again. Papers are easy and the exams are based on the slides. Easy A if you put in the work. Shes super kind too.

This professor is super nice and invested. The class consisted in a semester-long group project. It wasn't an easy one but very rewarding when you got it right. Not super homework-intensive and lectures are interesting. She also set up very interesting talks with international speakers. Would recommend!

Took her intl conflict & negotiation class, honestly loved it!! Lectures might not be the most interesting if you aren't invested in the topic, but she's the sweetest and most caring lady! Sometimes she has funky opinions but oh well. I would 100% take another class with her! If u have to take INTL2400, make sure you take it with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Youly's INTL 1101 course online. She is so so so so nice and caring. You're going to have to read a lot, watch her lectures, and write papers. Her class can be boring at times, but also very interesting. It depends on the student's personal interest. There is a lot of critical thinking and research, but she is very willing to help anyone!

Youly is very nice and clearly cares about her students. She is more than willing to help inside and outside of class and always wants students to share their opinions. Sometimes discussions are long, boring, and off-topic. The class is a little dry at times and mainly informational but expected for an introductory class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Youly is a really nice professor! She lectures from slides and posts them online so you don't have to worry about missing things. Her assignment instructions were sometimes unclear but she is very approachable and always willing to help. She was also a pretty fair grader imo. My only complaint is she sometimes lets students go on off topic tangents

Took the honors section of this course. Straightforward professor who clearly knows what she is talking about. Lectures every class, questions on quizzes are basically straight off the powerpoint slides.

reviews.comment: Wasn't great, doesn't respond to email communications.

He is nitpicky with wording and grading, and it's hard to grasp in the first few assignments, but he cares about his students doing well. This course is best taken in-person. Reach out with questions you have, he will ensure formatting/wording he wants to see.

If u want to go to therapy to undergo the depression you endured from taking a class w this guy be my guest. Total complete as. Doesnt grade consistently. If u ever slightly make him upset he takes off points for no reason. This guy should not be teaching if he hat es his students so much
Extremely unfair grader, left a failing class average for all exams. Did not respond to any communications asking for help or clarification.

Terrible! RUN at any cost. Same as the other grader points out. Terrible at grading. Delete Canvas right after the final exam. Very strict in answers and have very limited time in quizzes and exams. Outside knowledge will be considered 0 points. The slides are not easy to understand, and there are no extra resources at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really felt like I genuinely learnt a lot in class. Encourages participation, and classes are conducted just the way they are supposed to. Agreed, the grading is tough, don't believe all the negative comments, make sure that if you take this class, to balance this with scoring subjects!!

His grading criteria are very difficult to understand. He reduces marks for not writing enough and not writing too much if you don't write your full name for the assignment submission. You must write the answer exactly as he wants it, or else he will give you a zero!
I got my points taken away because I said "A is equal to B" and he said I should instead say "A is same as B". Now you see why everybody complains about his grading.

I've had him for two courses: BIOT5120 and BIOT6214. Avoid him at all costs. He's a terrible grader and nitpicks the smallest things to tank your grade. No remorse. I'm convinced he does it for fun. Feedback on why points were taken off is obscure or not even available. Went from an A to a C in just 2 weeks. Choose. Another. Professor.

Grading is pathetic. Biostats is about data and numbers but he grades for English. He takes away points for wording and doesn't care if you get the answer right. We use Excel to calculate but he would ask you to break down the Excel formula into 15 sentences. He gave 8 assay-type questions for a quiz and only allowed 20 minutes to finish.

He's horrible. Threated to fail me if I didn't use resources from his material for my assignments and homework's. This isn't specified anywhere in the syllabus fyi. His quizzes are lengthy and time given isn't adequate for you to finish them on time.

The worst professor I've ever had. Grading scheme is arbitrary, and he will knock off points for wording when you actually had the correct answer and processes. Questions in assignments are vague, and it is never clear what is expected of you. He stresses not using any outside resources for assignments except the lectures which makes no sense.

Honestly the most confusing professor I've ever taken. Tests and assignments have points taken off for small wording choices, which is odd, since he doesn't know how to use most words correctly.
Enjoys reminding everyone how he has worked in agriculture, government, biotech, though he should scratch professor from that since he's not a good one.
Extremely tough professor. please never take this person to teach you Biostats. you will regret definitely. he cut marks for even a minute mistake.

He once stumbled into class, some 15 minutes late, with an uncomfortable expression on his face. It was clear he had pooped his pants. He sits down for quite some time, not saying a word, but gradually growing more and more uncomfortable and fidgety. Then, about 10 minutes later, he shot up from his chair and said, "Class! I have pooped my pants!".
Horrible experience. Very unfair grading with vague questions almost designed to make you lose marks.
He is awful. He is an unfair grader. His classes are assignment heavy. Exams are lengthy and questions are very vague. I would never take him again.

There are many assignments for this class like discussion posts, proposal paper, presentations, quiz, midterm and final. His exams are extremely lengthy and has lot of short answers. module content doesn't match his lectures. lectures are too basic compared to module readings. he is a tough grader

Wish I could have more than 350 characters to describe how bad my experience was. Absolutely do not take any classes with this Professor - lot of reading, lots of assignments (weekly quizzes, midterm, group presentation, group paper, discussion posts, final). Assignment questions are based on one-off comments that weren't in the reading.

The field trips were annoying because we had to miss other classes to go on them (museum visits). You are guaranteed an A if you put in the minimum effort. Lots of extra credit.

Such a funny and chill professor. The actual course has a ton of reading + attendance is mandatory. I didn't read any of the readings and just read AI summaries and was fine. Just pay attention during class discussions + write down notes based off what she writes during lectures. Exams are straightforward: she tells u exactly what u need to know

reviews.comment: I actually took EECE 5580. I thought the professor did an excellent job; his pronunciation was impeccable. He explained the material with great clarity—making complex concepts easy to grasp—and the overall difficulty level was manageable. The workload was also within a reasonable range, though the final project did feel a bit tight on time.

Professor Saha is new but I have not found a Professor who cares more. He makes a real effort to make sure that his students understand and will go over topics again if asked. He's a fair grader who gives really good feedback. It's a hard class but I would be surprised if there was a better Professor teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He explains clearly and really tries to help in office hours. He doesn't give answers outright but asks guiding questions that make you think and understand the material better. A patient and highly effective professor.

Professor Saha is an amazing lecturer, he is very approachable and super helpful. He goes in-depth with concepts during class, and explains thoroughly when asked a question. Also, he responds to emails quickly, and is transparent with how grading works. The content in the class was hard, but taking the course with him made it much more bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is the first time the professor has offered a course. Despite its even graduate students take it and assignments being entirely programming-based, the professor never teaches programming in class. You must rely solely on AI and textbooks to acquire knowledge. You won't want to be at 3 a.m.still debugging code with mounting errors.

Her lectures are long, and I struggled to pay attention in class. There are two group projects throughout the semester with the same group. I wish we had switched who we worked with because if you get stuck with an unproductive group, it's difficult to navigate.

Prof Kurt is a nice teacher who assigns light hw. Tests aren't bad and very similar to practice material & the group project can be interesting if in a good group. Participation is light as long as you try. There is also very little feedback given for literally anything turned in? Still would recommend, but not a life changing class by any means.

Too much content, flew through slides, missing information on slides / slides were vague and she spoke most of the content which was hard to keep up. Two group projects which were very annoying to complete, needed a special software, didn't provide time in class to connect which made it difficult. Tests were only multiple choice but difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing prof! If you do the readings and actually are interested in learning about consumer behavior, this class is pretty easy. Prof Kurt is super nice, but make sure to actually attend class and do the readings!
Dont take her class, cannot learn anything
No feedback for everything, everyone get same grades Give the score casually, all depends on the luck
Don't listen to the bad reviews. She is a great teacher and her class isn't that work intensive. Highliy recommend having her.

Worst professor. Grades super easily until the final project. Went into the final project with a 98, left with an 86. She doesnt give clear expectations and is simply wrong about a lot of things. Idk if it had to do with faculty politics and her realizing not everyone can get As, but she clearly doesnt care about her students. Avoid.
The best prof never met in neu. Professional, kindly and helpful for every student  only if you are concentrated.
Great prof.  I am a physical science guy and I learned a lot from his mol bio class.
I liked the class. the subject matter was hard so had to study a lot.
He knows his subject well but not his students.
he is versatile.
Very helpful professor. Really works to help students understand. Class is not easy but def doable. You will have to work hard to get a good grade.
excellent person with love for yeast...

Great professor, will tell you exactly how to do well.  But do not take that as an indication of being an easy course.  Exams still test how well you studied, and especially on the last exam, you need to study well.  Book is really helpful.  I just attended the review sessions and read the book to do well.

Good professor who likes to use the figures from the text.  He posts powerpoints but if you go to class and listen to his explinations you will do fine.  Definatly a doable class.  Great guy and a great professor.  Three exams 50 questions multiple choice he lays everything out for you to do well in biochemistry.
No Comments
No Comments
He was really passionate about his work and really cared for his students. The class itself was way easier than the other inquiries!

Lectures make no sense but he is very passionate about what he teaches. Literally had no work for that class ever and used class time to study. He tells everyone they are guaranteed an A. I HIGHLY recommended taking his course especially if you are taking other hard classes to save time and your GPA. (There was also no final exam)

This guy is so awesome. You don't learn a single thing but he is a free A and you can use this as a chill class or like a study hall. Any assignment turned in is a 100, his quizzes he give you a 100 regardless of what you write. That said, you do not learn from him, but he is good for gpa.

I used this class as a study hall. I didn't learn a single thing which is honestly fine because the project is self-driven and he wants his students to end with an A and makes it pretty easy to get there

He's definitely a sweet guy, and you can tell he's passionate, but he's not very good at teaching. He made us by his $30 book (only could pay cash to him) and I never used it all semester. I didn't learn anything all semester because he just rambles, but a good GPA booster. We basically spent the whole sem working on symposium project.

He taught the class out of his own textbook and I never really had a full grasp on the content so if that bothers you he probably isn't a great prof for you. That being said he is very sweet/ very easy to get a high grade, he wants you to succeed and learn a little about a topic he's passionate about which I really loved. It was great for my GPA.

His lectures make no sense, he makes up his own terms (can't find them on Google), he makes you buy his own textbook, etc. However, this class is an easy A. It is way easier than any of the other inquires classes. If you turn in the assignments and take the quizzes you will get a 100. You can write literally anything related on the quiz and get 100

very nice guy, but cant teach. his lectures are all over the place and impossible to follow. he makes up his own terms for things, so you can't even ask google if you're confused. no one learned anything in this class. however, he doesn't give anyone below 100 so its an easy A

O'Malley genuinely just wants you to do well in his class. His lectures can be convoluted and hard to follow, mostly because he just really loves what he teaches, but he gives you every possible opportunity to get an A. I really just used his class as a study hall. He is generally a funny and caring guy, so do your GPA a favor and take his section!

It is a great class. He is very nice as he brings candy to class to encourage participation among students. As long as you know something on the quizzes he will give you an A or allow you to make it up to get an A. The group project is really easy and he will help you with anything. 10/10 recommend taking his class! The final is a one-page paper.

Do your GPA a favor and take him! His class is very lecture-heavy there are open response quizzes which he will allow anyone who gets less than an A to redo. As long as you attend class and are somewhat knowledgeable about something he will give you an A in the class. No final exam just a paper. He's a great guy take his class!

Prof O'Malley's class was a joke. I attended class but you really done need to. Grade is based on 3 major tests and thats it. April 14th and no grades have been put in yet. The slides are wordy and he goes off on tangents a lot. Nice guy but I don't think his main interest is anatomy. Book is unnecessary, first test is hard others are prac tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don's class is the definition of lecture heavy. Longggg lectures that even I couldn't keep up with note taking just bc of how boring they were. He is sort of nice but kind of sassy and also thinks he is smarter than his own doctor (which he told us). DO THE PRACTICE TESTS!! Grade is not posted and our final is in three days...

His tests were just the practice tests. Literally same position and everything, I learned nothing in this course but just memorized the practice test the day of and got one of the best grades on the final.
So funny and wants his students to do well. Easy class, GPA booster, automatic A. He would also give out candy if you answered a question. He would ramble a lot about random things.

Real sweet guy, he rambled a lot during his lectures, but you don't really need to listen. He did ask for $30 for the textbook, but I used it as a laptop stand the entire semester, so not worth it. Tests were really easy you could pretty much talk about anything semi-related to the topic, and he would give you an A.

Genuinely nice guy, but he really needs to retire. Taught out of his own textbook that we had to pay for with $30 cash, and most of the vocab are terms he made up. Lectures are ramble-y and the slides are very confusing. Easy A (he even says he will allow you to redo assignments if you don't get an A), but I don't think I learned anything.

I honestly would've given Prof O'Malley 1 star, but had to give him credit for how nice he is and how easy his class was. If you want an easy A, take his class, but if you want to learn anything at all, go somewhere else. He is an AWFUL lecturer and is so hard to follow. I seriously didn't learn a thing in this class, attendance isn't mandatory.

He's super nice and understanding and you could tell he is very passionate about what he teaches. However, his powerpoints were very disorganized and it was hard to learn in the class. He doesn't care about your grade and always mentions how everyone will leave with an A at the end of the semester. The class is a bit of a joke, but he's nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Complete waste of time and money, his lectures were completely unorganized and I genuinely don't think I learned a thing. Also the textbook was one he wrote himself and made us pay him for and it was a complete joke. He told us we would all get A's from the start so there's that but frankly I would rather fail than have to sit through that again
He's a nice guy but horrible lecturer and presenter. He's so all over the place it's so hard to follow along. Do not take the class.

I do agree that his slides are a bit disorganized, but if u ask him to do a review of the information - he connects the dots for u pretty fast. Also, the slides certainly LOOK like a lot, but if you listen to his lecture you realize a lot of them reinforce the same idea:) Funny guy too.

Don's a bit of a rambler, but he is such an intelligent professor. He constantly updates his lectures to current research which keeps topics interesting. And yeah, it does mean he adds abstracts to his slides - if you don't like reading don't take a 4000 course! He wrote a textbook that directly correlates with his teaching(good for review).

Although Don was very caring, his lectures were super heavy! Get ready to memorize hundreds and hundreds of disorganized slides. Content was hard to follow due to the arrangement of slides and there is a clear expectation to know everything!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An absolute dumpster fire of a class. Lectures are often disorganized, un-engaging, and long. The slides are usually cluttered with grammatically erroneous statements and random facts. There is no flow to any lecture, which makes it extremely difficult to take away a clear message of the class. Take if you want an easy A and nothing gained from it.

Lecture heavy, but his slides are messy and hard to understand. His grading is based on a few quizzes and assignments, but as long as you write something somewhat correct you'll get full credit. Everyone ends with an A, so if your looking for an easy class take this. I personally got frustrated with how I wasnt learning anything - most people did.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don is such a kind professor and wants all of his students to get the best grade possible. He is very invested in his research it shows in his enthusiasm for the subject. His research on Language Evolution and the Brain is super interesting and he is always willing to answer student questions inside and outside of class.

Professor O'Malley was such a kind and caring professor. He clearly cared about the material, and really made an effort to get to know students (a rarity in the College of Science). Definitely would recommend taking a class with him, he will go above and make sure you do well, and loves answering questions.

Don is super funny in class (if you show up- which most ppl don't). However, his lectures drag on forever and its very hard to keep up with notes out of pure boredom and he is fast and skips random slides. The only grades are from his midterms (3-4 of them I think). His tests are almost identical to his practice midterms- so look at them!!!

Neurobio of cognitive decline is unfortunately a mess. Lectures are composed of slide shows with abstracts from at least 30 different papers, many times contradicting one another, and most times random facts are highlighted instead of important material. He gets sidetracked easily and makes no connections between any of the material.
