reviews.comment: 2+2 is 4 - 1 that's 3 quick maffs. he taught me that, he teach quick maffs
The greatest biology I have ever had. Such an inspirational person.
Goes off topic all the time and refers nearly everything to the text instead of adequately answering in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: this is an intro class so you have to be dead not to get an A. i skipped 50% of class and  don't miss much. he is very interested in biology and tries to encourage students to get into it as well.  he is friendly but not very intune with the students, though he tries.  show up, bring a lap top to keep occupied,he rants, you get an a.

He's always sidetracked and isn't clear at all.  Its really hard to pay attention to his lectures, which is a bummer because neurobio is super interesting, but he just makes it dreadful, long and painful.

He knows the material very well, but gets sidetracked and wanders off topic. His slides are useless until you read and understand the textbook. He knows the material very well, but isn't so great at teaching it. Tries to help, makes himself readily available for office hours. The curve really helps! Wouldn't recommend...
Computational Neuroscience. No. Just, no. The man's clueless. Epic fail.

I enjoyed the class, but you must be motivated to learn this material.  Class averages were 68-76 plus a usual 10 pt curve.  He's funny if you like punny and nerdy cultural references (esp monty python).  If you only took Psychobio you are not prepared for this class!

Had O'Malley for Neurobio.  He knows the material very well, but gets sidetracked and wanders off topic.  Loves his slides, which are useless unless he's explaining them.  He knows the material very well, but isn't so great at getting anybody else to understand it.  Tries to help, but not so great at it

He trails off after every sentence so its hard to understand him.  THe use of projectors doesn't help in the slightest.  Hes all over the place with the slide.  He is willing to help however.  Unless your a grad student i would not recommend this class to anyone, unless i didn't like them.

really great professor. really funny and goes out of his way to be very accessible. hard class though- be prepared to read the text thoroughly. exams extremely hard, but he curves so no one gets screwed. gives pop quizes (basically excuses to give you points based on attendance) so it's good to go to classes.
confusing teacher, he was all over the place.

This guy ws all over the place. His lectures were confusing and his use of the overhead projector diagrams was even more confusing.  Exams were so hard that almost every exam he scaled about 40 points.  Every once in a while he cracked a clever joke tho

He's a nice guy and is clearly passionate about innovation. However, his lectures are extremely tedious and overwhelming. He would repeat the same topic every class making it even harder to want to pay attention. The group project matters a lot and he will be brutally honest if he doesn't like it. Will make you present in front of the class a LOT.

Overall, he is a good person and truly wants his students to succeed. reviews.comment: AVOID THIS CLASS. 14 weeks of hearing the same things over and over again without actually learning anything. He gives cryptic feedback, grades so inconsistently, and even if you follow the rubric, if he doesn't like your ideas or project, you'll get a bad grade. Entire course is about the project but you will still have a final exam.

He's a nice guy. However, his feedback is extremely cryptic and not helpful. He repeats the same 3 ideas/topics over and over again. Exactly like a broken record. The entire class is a massive group project that doesn't make sense half the time. If you can, take the class but avoid this professor if you actually want to learn something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Just be a half decent student and he will love you. Literally just google the titles of the readings once and a while and then talk in class and he eats it up. It is so easy.

Very passionate about the class but grades as accurately as possible. Some may say he is a difficult grader but not hard to get an A. Very understanding/wholesome and easy to listen to. Lectures can be sometimes boring or really interesting. Homework's are readings or group project work.
harsh grader, makes us guess his expectation, teach the concept after we present, always have comments about everything but expectation not clear

I haven't taken the final yet, but I have an A which is obviously very good. However, during the group project we all worked really hard, but nothing was ever good enough for him. If he doesn't like your product that you base your final presentation on, even if the class likes it, you don't do well, and it's almost 40% of your grade. Don't take!!!

absolutely horrible. i am an extremely hard worker and my group and i follow guidelines exactly, but he was never satisfied. It wasn't just our group. extremely and unnecessarily a hard grader. all other inno classes had easy professors. i also have heard that i am one of VERY few students who had an A, my group members all had B/C…. Do. Not. Take.

half of the class is a loosely formatted final group project. Mark doesnt help all that much and he barely preps you for the final. its possible to get a good grade but he doesnt really teach you anything.

Very nice guy overall and is passionate about teaching. There's a final for this class, which doesn't make sense because the majority of the class was a group project. If you don't like your group in the beginning, get out of it because the group projects reflect heavily on your grade. Assignments and discussions are not difficult, just do the hw.

One of the best teachers I have had at northeastern. He's very knowledgable and knows what he's doing in class. Also he's always there to help. I don't know why an exam is necessery but its doable and it's a very fun course overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was torn between giving a 4 instead of 3 for difficulty. It's not that the course is hard, but he is all over the place, will teach you concepts after you write a paper on them and expectations aren't clear, but then will give you harsh feedback. This class took up a lot of my time & didn't really listen to students clearly.

yeah just don't take this class. He yaps a lot during class and lowk none of it is useful youre better for self studying at home. Attendance is 2.5% but like dont skip more than 6 times or else he fails you. Tests are online so you can cheat ig but he watches you like a hawk as he sits in the back. Final is like 4% but is lowk a 10 page analysis.

Class is easy and tests are online. The professor is clearly passionate about teaching, but lectures can be hard to follow and often feel more like him talking through ideas. The term project shows up late in the semester but is manageable and not too difficult.

Dimitrios was not an effective instructor in my experience, and often seemed more confident in his teaching than his delivery supported. The homework was easy, but the written portion of the exams was difficult and bad. Didn't understand anything from lectures, self-study but it's easy

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I've had

His lectures are impossible to follow. Handwriting is illegible, and slides are a complete mess with typos everywhere. Does not convey information clearly. All tests and exams are extremely long, and there isn't enough time to complete them.

Dimitrios doesn't cover content well and doesn't actually answer questions; he reforms the questions and answers the question he pretends you asked. More class time is spent discussing the same "life advice" every lecture than statistics. Also he says the grades on Canvas are "very misleading", so you don't know how you're doing during the course.

Dimitrios is a very nice professor and cares about his students. However, he is an awful teacher. He is all over the place when teaching and his notes make 0 sense. It is so hard to read his little scribbles and somehow his online notes are no better. Self-studying is required because he doesn't efficiently cover test materials.
Professor Fotiadis is very passionate for stats. However, he is not the best teacher. If you want an easy A take his class, but if you want to actually learn avoid his class.

PLS AVOID!!! Class was very hard/lectures made no sense. If you missed 1 class or just went to the bathroom, you would fall VERY behind. Board is just hieroglyphics and impossible to follow/read. All exams even final are very difficult and impossible since you don't learn in his class. People with knowledge of stats could not comprehend anything.

his lectures doesn't make sense because those who understand stats would find his lectures useless due to prior understanding while those who don't understand stats would find his lecture still useless as they can't comprehend his lectures. it is a poor mixture of technicality and accessibility. also attendence is mandatory and that sucks alot

Dimitrios is passionate about teaching; however, he is truly an awful professor. His lectures are just him rambling on to himself without actually teaching us the material and they're impossible to follow along with. Also, he's awful with Canvas and the quizzes are difficult to actually do good on. Plus, he refuses to curve or give extra credit.
He really cannot teach. If you want to learn stats AVOID because trust you won't learn a thing. If you want easy A and online tests, final, and projects, this is the class for you.

He's very kind and all and it's an easy class given a lot of the work is done online, however his lectures are awful. They just look like scribbles and he gets very confused with what he's talking about. Overall, extremely easy, but avoid if you're actually looking to learn.

We use webassign and there are only 2 tries. A good amount of tests but they are all online at home no camera. Final project doesn't make sense and he will only explain it 2 weeks before the due date. It is hard to understand him, but I usually do the homework while he teaches. Very unorganized and you won't learn the material. Take for Easy A.

Participation doesn't matter at all in this class, even though it's part of our grade for the semester. As long as you show up to class, you get credit for attendance. Dimitrios isn't tech savvy at all, so be ready to work out a bunch of your own technical issues by yourself because he won't be able to help you there.
He cares a lot and loves his job but his lectures were confusing and all over the place, same with his canvas, all tests were online including the final and they are worth 90% of ur grade

Great person, but the worst professor I've had. His organization is a disaster. His online notes look like a preschooler wrote them—just random scribbles—and he talks way too fast. Class was mandatory but all exams are online, even the final.

a horrible teacher in almost every respect. that being said, its not that hard to get a good grade since the exams are take home and very very very similar to the practice questions. 

also, he's difficult to understand, messy, terrible with tech, extremely unorganized, out of touch, and more. 

otherwise, he's a nice man.

DO NOT TAKE! He cares about his students and is easy to get in contact with but trying to learn in class was impossible. The canvas is the most disorganized canvas I have ever seen and the notes are not helpful. Going to class is basically the same as not going to class - you will not learn anything. Attendance was mandatory but was a waste of time

Worst professor I've had. He is a sweet guy but definitely can't teach properly. Don't take this class if you have no prior experience in stats. Goes fast on content and his notes are a mess. He made attendance mandatory to scare his students into coming to class. If I studied on my own and never attended class I would have gotten the same grade.

His handwriting and typos when communicating, seriously needs to be checked on. I wish I could attach examples because its truly atrocious. He changed his syllabus to make attendance mandatory and threatened to drop our grade a LETTER each time we were gone halfway through the course because everyone realized how low quality his lectures are.

Lectures were a waste of time since his teaching style is next to impossible to understand, frequently does not answer questions students pose, saying that they are pointless and that they should be "paying attention to the textbook" if they are confused. Exams are super lengthy and typically have numerous errors in them. Canvas is a mess.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. 90% of your grade is dependent on your tests and the class material does NOT match what he teaches in lecture. reviews.comment: Good professor. Grading is a bit annoying because you have to get over a 95 to get an A. The exams make almost all of the grade but if you go to class and pay attention you will be fine. He usually curves all exams.
worst teacher ever. does not follow curriculum.
This is the worst teacher I have ever had.

One of the best courses I've taken at Northeastern. Dimitrios clearly loves teaching stats and puts a lot of effort into teaching every day. Very clear syllabus and he is very understanding. Best professor for business stats.
The absolute man. Is very funny and also passionate about stats. Take this class if you want a good and easy class. Love this guy.

Really nice guy! Sad to hear he is retiring this year, but I thought he was great. Helps guide students in the right direction in this course and outside of it. Despite this, lectures can get a little confusing even if you watch the pre recorded lessons. But all the information he gives, helps so much. Questions from tests can be found on homework.
Went slow through easy topics and then sped up when we got to the tougher material. Very passionate about the course, maybe just not my style.

Why does Dimitrios give ridiculous curves on tests and allows you to drop one of your test grades? He is simply a bad teacher. Sure he cares about his students and is passionate about stats. But if you don't know how to engage your class and organize your notes/lectures in a good manner, it doesn't change the fact that he is a terrible teacher.

Dimitrios is easily, EASILY, the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. He has an awful, slow, boring, mindless teaching style which results in every student in the class is looking at their phone or computer, 80% of the time. The only reason he gets good ratings is his insane (20%) curves, which is just a testament to his teaching abilities.

There is too much workload for one class! Long homework assignments. Quizzes every week. Exams are impossible. Extremely irrelevant to what we learned in class and 10x more difficult. reviews.comment: Too many documents and readings on the BlackBoard. Some say read the textbook to do well on quizzes, others say look at his articles.. I say read EVERYTHING..!! Bad
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fotiadis is very passionate about statistics. The class material can be a little boring and repetitive but he wants you to learn. He encourages students to push themselves. The tests are hard, but graded on a curve.

Not helpful in office hours and no TA. Off topic often. Would not recommend unless you've taken a stats course in high school or want to just teach yourself. Ended w ok grade in the class bc the curves are huge because nobody understands what is going on (30%+) but felt like it was huge waste and learned nothing helpful. Studied a lot.

This class was tough, but there is a VERY generous curve (usually 30%). I got a 78 on a test and that curved to over 100%. He is hilarious and provides us with great life lessons. He still remembers me and was very friendly when I saw him outside of class.

Excellent professor. I would recommend him to anyone who is willing to put in a lot of work and doesn't mind getting frustrated. He cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed in life. There are a lot of quizzes based on the textbook readings, but they help you to understand the material better.

Take Dimitrios' class. Although his lectures can be a bit confusing at times, he posts very detailed notes online, and tons of practice material before each exam. Also MOST IMPORTANTLY he gives very generous curves on all exams. I got a 67 on one exam which was brought up to a 97. He truly cares about the success of each student.

His lectures are hard to follow since he moves very fast.  Nonetheless, he has extremely detailed notes and an abundance of practice problems and answers on his website which are where I learned everything I know. The tests are very reasonable and large curves are added.   Very easy to do well as a non math person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dimitrios is a great guy, and clearly loves what he teaches, which made getting to the 8 am a *little* easier. The class is pretty straightforward, but is still difficult. The tests are definitely designed to be extremely challenging, but the curves on them can be very large. Overall, it's a challenging course, but his care for students is better.

A wacky dude, but very nice. Can get off topic but incredibly knowledgable. Goes very fast during lectures but highly encourages  students to stop him when they get lost. Office hours are very helpful. Tests are difficult and study guides aren't incredibly specific, but he usually curves them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic! His tests are difficult and the course is not an easy A. He curves fairly. For example, I could get a 78 on a test and he would curve it to a 104. His tests are EXTREMELY hard. He's a professor who will really push you and recommend have a strong background in math and like a challenge. He gives you the answers to a whole project

Attendance unnecessary. Responsible and respectful professor. Always reach out to students. No need textbook, all of the materials are provided free on blackboard. Could not find a better professor.  The quizzes are actually not hard as long as you study and really understand the materials. Students who say it's hard is probably not that diligent.

Very had to understand, he means well and wants his students to succeed, however his exams are really difficult. He gives a lot of homework that you need to pass in but you are also given the answers.  good luck.
The tests are hard. The average grade on final before curve is like 58%.

His explanations are not great and he makes everything seem x10 times harder than what it actually is. Also, his final is impossible. However, he helps a lot with assignments and the project. Also, the notes he posts on blackboard are enough to get an A.

He's complex in class because he writes out every single step of a problem on the board, so it looks a lot harder than it actually is. Just read the book if he's too hard. If the book is too complicated (like in the later chapters), pay attention in class. Tests aren't particularly difficult, the entire class is just using the formulas he provides.
don't even dare....
Great person, but no such a great professor. Really hard to understand his accent.

His class is no longer easy. The structure has been changed drastically, don't expect to receive free A's like previous years. He had to drop an entire exam (lowest of 3) so students wouldn't get C's and D's. Work hard, and you'll do fine. No need to buy the textbook, he uploads all necessary readings/assignments to blackboard.

He is definitely NOT super easy. It is clear that this semester he changed his methods. He doesn't give study guides or any kind of material to prepare for the test other than his lecture notes. He is in love with stats and he is very helpful and funny but don't expect an A if you don't work hard for it.

His tests are the exact same as the practice quizzes online (different numbers), so as long as you study those you will be fine. Lectures can be confusing, but again you don't really even need them as long as you study the practice quizzes.
Best Professor in NEU

This class was so easy! All of his tests are based directly off of the review packets he gives out. Most of the test questions are exactly the same as the ones in the packet. Go to class, do your homework, and study the review packet, and there's no reason you shouldn't get an A. He is also a very nice guy, and helpful too.
All his review packets and homework questions are very helpful when reviewing for exams. The exam questions come directly from review packets so it is very difficult to not do well in this class
Best professor for this class! Honestly do not think of taking this class with anyone else.

He's a sweet man, very enthusiastic about the material he's teaching.  I found everything he taught easy to grasp, and he would always state that he loves teaching and if anyone ever had any questions feel free to ask.  I enjoyed this class more than many other's, and really appreciated his genuine interest in wanting his students to succeed.

I took Dimitrios for statistics in my freshman year. I usually do very well in school but this class was (NO EXAGGERATION) the most difficult class i have ever taken. The students with other statistics teachers said the course was a breeze. Please dont make the same mistake i did. AVOID THIS CLASS. ps the class avg on the last test was a 45
Easy A. It's an extremely watered-down form of the ENGL classes I took in hs so it's a waste of time.

Lynn is a little crazy but she means the best. There is not much homework but there are three papers and none of them are hard you just have to put in effort. She is a fun time and I always enjoyed going to her class. You can't miss more than 3 classes but she is very understanding.

Such a sweet professor, her assignments aren't very interesting but it's easy to understand what she expects from you and if you do exactly that you're fine. She's very understanding and will respond kindly if you ask any type of questions online. Not what I expected from this course but I was definitely pleasantly surprised. Go for it, she's good!
She was super nice. You will do well in this class if she likes you and you put in time with her. Would recomend though.

She is a nice professor, however, can be extremely condescending during class. You have to write the papers exactly how she wants them and provides no constructive feedback. I do not recommend this professor.
Loved her for connections and decisions. I haven't had her for english, though.

This professor is the worst. Constantly assigns first drafts to be submitted but won't ever give criticism or corrections until after the final draft has to be submitted. Harshest grader who only likes one writing style. I am not an English major for a reason and SHE made my experience that much more unenjoyable. AVOID AT ALL COST!!

Professor Dornink was really great. I did learn anything in this class but it was a good way to get a break from the stress of other classes. It is extremely easy to do well. She really cares about her students and occasionally brings in treats for special days. A very nice lady.

Lynn doesn't know how to do math, but her enthusiasm nearly makes up for it. She is sweet and means well, but feels more like "The Crazy Aunt". If you really need something, ask the TA. But in general, it is an entertaining class.
She is definitely tough. The hardest in the department but you will definitely learn a lot! She is helpful and available... Overall Great!
Attend class and you will be fine.

She is a very easy professor! But to get an A you must definitely ALL of the assignments which definitely are NOT hard and are NOT many. Her essays could be very fun if you are into creative writing and learning new writing styles. Ask her to check your essays (only 3) so that you can know what she wants and what to change to get an A!!
She is little bit challenging Don't expect an easy A AT ALL!! Always willing to help. Remember to show effort, and you'll do just fine...

Really great class.  Although she is a bit challenging its definitely doable.  ITs really rewarding when you finish that class, you really feel like you've accomplished something and feel somewhat enlightened.  Shes a really nice teacher and very accomodating to the students needs.  Freshman english sucks but if you need to get though it, go w her.

I really enjoyed her English class. She was always making us do these crazy but helpful things for class. She was very clear on what to do, and was always there for office hours if you needed help with something. One of my favorite classes this year.

I really enjoyed this class. It was challenging, but if you put in the effort and the time you will do well. I think a lot of how well you do depends on how developed your skills were to begin with. She keeps class interesting while challenging you to look for more. She is one of the best teachers I have ever had.

She is a really good teacher and one of the most helpful teachers I have ever had. She is always there for her students and will help you in any way possible. Lots of class discussions and not a lot of work. It's your standard freshmen English class so unless you're interested in English you won't love the class but it is a good class nonetheless.

Ms. Dornick is the best teacher at this school! i had her all of my first year. She is the most helpful and understanding teacher you will have if you participate, and she makes a boring class really interesting. She is so fair and motivating. I would take this class just to have her as my teacher.
although the class might not be that interesting...the assigments and papers are quiete easy to write...she is very helpful and tries her best to meet with students with problems

Took this Fall 2025. Lots of readings. You have reading logs due on Tuesday and Friday. Lectures are basically based on the readings and more in-depth explanations. For the more graded assignments, please ask her about the assignment in full detail. It will help. WARNING: This is not a Republican (Trump MAGA class), be aware! Very liberal class.

reviews.comment: This professor is amazing. She is not the most tech savvy but if she made a mistake, she would never fault us for it and would give us an extension if needed. In the middle of the semester, she had us sit down and write down what we would like her to change about the class/teachings, and she actually changed everything that we asked her to.

Profe Dominguez is passionate, knowledgeable, and very kind. She can be confusing, but is very helpful and receptive if you ask her questions (plus she's more responsive via email than most profs). She's also super understanding so if you have any issues just communicate! Also very chill grader (almost everyone got 100s) and LGBTQ friendly!
The goat, does not deserve previous bad reviews, could be more tech savvy

She did not put any resources on canvas aside from the required reading.She did not put in any grades during the semester and arbitrarily sent me an email saying I got a B with no explanation of why.She isn't hard? the reading and class lectures aren't hard? apparently grades hard but doesn't give any feedback to why you scored what you did.

reviews.comment: Shes so confusing. She makes the work given harder than it looks and gives busy work instead of meaningful assignments. Protect your mental health! Dont take it w. her

reviews.comment: I took Senior Capstone with this professor and it was horrible. She already has negative reputation in the Sociology department but I had to take this course to graduate. She took 1.8 off my grade for missing a single class and 7 off my grade for participation. She didn't give a single grade back all semester. Doesn't teach and forces students to read about 150 pages a week. Disconnected from students. Worst professor at the university.

Dominguez gives a hell of a lot of reading, and can be biased in her teaching... BUT conceptually this class is one of the most interesting i've taken at University. Despite the quantity of work given ; weekly essays and one 10 page final paper (no midterm or final) if you pay attention and participate you will manage fine. Tip; do the reading!

reviews.comment: Worst professor at this university. I wouldn't wish this professor on my worst enemy. Hard pass on ever taking a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I've ever taken at Northeastern. For an elective you have to write tons of papers, and her biases clearly show in her teaching. I would strongly recommend against taking anything with her unless you absolutely have to.

This is her first time teaching Sociology of Violence (the other professor is retiring). It isn't bad. There's only 8 people in my class so all we do is have a discussion on Tuesdays and watch a movie every Friday. There are no tests! But there is a LOT of writing (a short analysis every week, and three 10 page papers throughout the semester).

WORST TEACHER EVER!  Don't take this course. For an elective you have 8 papers, two presentations and a midterm. If you don't speak more than twice a class your grade will be negatively affected. A class that's about realizing how people are treated unfairly concerning race, she does the same thing with grades.  Save yourself now.  DON'T TAKE IT!

Unclear and vague when teaching and especially on test questions. Often defensive and thinks her students are dumb. Would not recommend the class and be skeptical of most of what she says because she is usually wrong

Do not take this class. She is way too vague in class, prints her quizzes offline and doesn't edit them to what was covered in class, argues with students whenever they go to her with a concern, doesn't practice what she teaches, is not helpful at all, and basically is just an all around terrible professor. The worst I've had at Northeastern.
doug is the GOAT he is so passionate about graphic design and i genuinely think i'll remember this man for the rest of my design career. 10/10 take him

took graphic design history online duirng covid and loved it, he's so knowledgeable and caring for his students and you can always reach him by email/office hours. the course itself is a great foundation for art history/graphic design majors.

He knows everything about design and his class is so enjoyable. The projects were really fun and he gives really good advice and critiques for them. There are quizzes but they're really easy and he isn't a harsh grader and he gives extra credit. Take his class!

this class was really interesting for me and I truly enjoyed all the lectures. doug does a lot of show and tell w/ his personal collection of stuff which is really cool. you have to watch lectures outside of class, but the class is pretty evenly split between studio projects and lecture. he is very passionate and knows literally everything

He's my FNCE 623 prof in UCW. He doesn't teach visually, only verbally, so lectures are very hard to understand. But his class is very chill and sometimes dismisses us early. Pop quizzes, but only for participation and not graded. 1 individual assignment, 1 group assignment, & 2 exams. Advice: REALLY STUDY HIS SAMPLE TESTS.

Amazing prof, amazing lectures. He is always happy to help students. There are quite a lot pop-up quizzes, but if you show up and listen carefully, quizzes are easy. He wants everyone to have good grades by giving easy quizzes and easy midterms. But for final exam, if you don't study hard for it, you won't be able to finish it.

Professor Drissi is one of the nicest professors i have had at Northeastern, take part in class and he will remember you and like you. He does pop quizzes but is very lenient in grading them. Kristen is a great professor. She inspires me as a successful woman and a disciplined professor. She gives her best to make students involve in the projects. I am more excited to be in her class which is so far the best class in my grad life.

He's a great professor - if you're pre-law.  The course is very discussion heavy, but there is only one grade for the total number of discussions.  He doesn't provide much feedback.  If you ask for ways to improve, he is unlikely to respond.

run if you can... i had a bunch of deadweights for group projects and he basically told me to deal with it. did nothing to help me. i ended up doing two projects basically on my own. also the final is ridiculous, worth 40% of your grade but it isn't even clear what's on it. he grades participation harshly too.

great class

Netty is a fun lecturer and has a good sense of humor. He's makes participating in class easy for anyone who pays attention and feels comfortable speaking in class. Netty was a great professor. He lectures, but always gets you to think in the lectures, so participation heavily matters. Netty was an extremely passionate and excellent professor, information was went over in a super clear and steady pace in class, directions for how to preform well on individual and group projects were clear and matched the grades our group received, and the midterm and final did not have any unfair questions. take this for an easy a not if u want to learn

shes the best
Pretty easy class make sure to do the homework on time, everything is through canvas and cengage, caring professor, attendance not necessarily mandatory, one duo project that isn't too difficult
A very nice lady, teaches effectively & makes learning fun. Material is relatively easy. Take her class!

Prof Dupree is super straight-forward with all of her assignments and exams which makes it easy to do well in this class. Very understanding professor and overall a chill class!

Guys at first I was like I'm so scared of economics so I went to every class, but one day the class was freezing and I kept hearing noises so I was like maybe I will stop going a little and I did some work on my own w/ A+. She is nice professor, but her classes don't really help with tests. She usually grades assignments at long intervals, which makes me confused about grades.

Easy class overall if you aren't interested in economics. Take it asynchronously if you want less work. There is a big group project which takes a lot of time each week, so make sure you have a good group and you get to choose your group in the beginning of the semester.

I don't know why this professor got such bad reviews, she's entertaining, kind, caring, responsive, and easy grader. Definitely the easiest macro theory class as it is not quantitative heavy at all. I would recomemnd this professor.

If you participate a LOT in class, he will like you. Sit in the front, and laugh at his jokes. If you actually want to learn marketing, don't take him.

Did not learn much. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: do not take this professor! his lectures are very boring, and is a harsh grader for participation. the highest participation grade was 85%. easy class in the beginning, but refuses to give full credit on the presentation/paper at the end of the semester. you have no control over your grade

Honestly he was a very lazy professor. He was funny at first, but his lectures are so boring. No one participates and instead of trying to fix the issue, he just has the kids present the slides to each other. Also he doesn't hold students accountable in group projects. I ended up doing all the work for my group but not the grade to reflect my work.
Easiest class in the business school and the best marketing professor. His grading is so light and he wants you to succeed. He is a professor you want to take for marketing no matter what.

Super easy A. Not a very interesting class because he basically just reads the chapter summary during class. To do well in this class, make sure you do well on the weekly online quizes, take the marketplace simulation seriously, and participate in class. You don't really have to ever read the actual chapter, just go to the chapter summary.

At first, I thought this class was going to be the easiest class I ever took at Northeastern and quite frankly it was. But he switched up really fast. His lectures are boring and consist solely of fluff. I didn't learn a thing in his classes. Assignments were pretty easy. But participation and attendance are mandatory.

He's great at the start... don't take him if you actually want to learn marketing. His classes are extremely mandatory, or your grade will drop to a 15%. Little homework and his lecture provided absolutely nothing, but he made the class easy to pass... unless you don't participate or show up. No midterm and the final is a joke (one page paper).

Course was very boring and repetitive.  Did not actually learn anything important and the professor was not understanding.  Put over 80% of the grades in during the last week and the highest participation grade was an 85%.  Do not take if you actually want to learn anything and have actual control over your grade.

Very easy but also very boring. Grades were put in at the end and he was kind of harsh especially with stuff like the presentation and participation. If you're a marketing concentration and looking for an informative and exciting introduction to your major -- this isn't it. If you're looking for an easy A to knock out a requirement -- this is it.
Great class, informative lectures, very passionate. Only negative is attendance is mandatory

Professor Dummit was great! Very funny guy who made lectures entertaining and fun. The homeworks were very time-consuming, but prepares you well for the tests. Exams were doable, and the review material given was representative of what was on the exams. Overall fun class!

Amazing professor. Really nice person. Lectures are great and recordings are provided. Homeworks are very long (8-10hours per week) but they are important for understanding the concepts. He did made adjustments and curves to the exams, and lots of practice exams are given. Lecture notes are very well structured.
Prof Dummit is a great person, but his homework assignments are very long and take forever to complete. He is very understanding during exams, and he has a generous curve.

Funny guy and good professor here at northeastern. Homeworks are long and hard, but I guess that's expected when you take Advanced Linear Algebra. Lectures are good and have bits of comedy in them. Responds quickly and thoroughly to all questions on piazza. Overall good stuff!
Incredible professor!

I had Dr. Dummit for MATH3543 and WOW! It was an amazing class! Dr. Dummit was funny when he taught the class and he was a great teacher too! I highly recommend you attend his classes and OHs are a good way to catch up. Overall, the class was amazing and I would take another class with Dr. Dummit again!

*MATH3543. Hands down the best math professor at NEU. The math department here is underfunded and understaffed, but there is a small batch of great professors, and he is definitely one of them. In terms of class, homework can be time-consuming, but it is well thought out and will help you understand the material. If you like math, take his course.

The actual content may be difficult, but the professor explains all concepts in a formulaic and engaging way. The lectures are accessible, but it's very easy to fall behind. The tests are much easier than the homework and the study guides, so as long as you do them well, you can get a good grade. TLDR: content is hard, tests easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a super good teacher, I will be taking his class again simply because of how good the lectures are. Tests count most of the grades, be ready to do a lot of homework, and actually learn the stuff.

Professor Dummit is talented at describing extremely complex mathematical concepts. However, if you miss even a minute, you are at risk of falling behind -- attend all classes, and unless you're ready for a LOT (and I mean a LOT) of homework, don't accelerate the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All around a great professor, and if you haven't found this before, look up ChipsChallenge fandom wiki, and search for Evan_Dummit. The man has his own damn wiki page in this random game I've never heard of. If that ain't qualifications, I don't know what is.

Couldn't have asked for a better math teacher. The kind of guy where attendance isn't mandatory but you still show up to class because he's so good at teaching. Tests are reasonable. Homework might take a few hours but is manageable especially with piazza.
Good prof

Does an excelent job explaining concepts. While his homework does take a really long time to complete, the modterms are pretty easy in comparison and he is a very generous grader -- giving lots of partial credit.
Great lectures and notes, a bit too much homework though. If you put in the work, you'll be able to get a good grade.

His lectures were amazing, as he clearly knows so much about the topic and is always willing to answer further questions. The homework is difficult and pretty much impossible to do if you start day-of, but if you start beforehand you'll be ok, and the tests are much easier than the homework. Overall difficult, but very rewarding class!

Dummit is the most talented math professor at NEU. His lectures and (detailed) notes are extremely easy to follow and interesting. He knows so much about a breadth of topics. His homeworks are extremely long but rewarding, and he is very fair when it comes to grading. I highly recommend taking any of his courses, you'll learn a lot.

This was a pilot version, so I was the lab rat. Professor Dummit knew how to explain his content thoroughly and was good at leaving notes online and was easy to review. That said, he did give intense homework and can assume you have learned a topic before. Good professor overall
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit's courses are a fabled right of passage at Northeastern. MATH 4527 was one of the most demanding classes I've taken. Incredibly heavy material is compacted into just 4 months. That being said, the course taught me a lot and was very enjoyable. Time seems to fly when you're having fun or when you're finding reduced quadratic forms.

Evan Dummit is a great professor. His lectures are always so engaging and his homework is usually straightforward. If you read his notes, it usually does not take a long time. Also, there are only 3 exams, which are generally very passable. Overall, you should take his class as it will boost your gpa without having a lot of work.

The homework can be very difficult, the midterms are usually easier. Attendance in lectures isn't mandatory but you won't get by if you try to read the posted notes because they are very dense and can be confusing.

The notes work great to review what you've learned already, but it's still useful to write your own.
Great professor for 3081. Explains in a calm and collected fashion - types out notes on canvas and supplies great review sheets for exams. Would totally take again.

It's only been two weeks but I've already found myself to be a lot more engaged and interested in Professor Dummit's class. His explanations are clear and concise, and the questions he works through are challenging but lead to a deeper understanding of the subject. One of the best teachers you could take 3081 with.
Great teacher, would def take again. Highly recommend.

Evan Dummit was an excellent professor in just about every way. It was clear that he had an enthusiasm for the material and would always provide excellent examples and feedback. He also created a ton of supplementary material that helped immensely with learning any confusing material. I would recommend any math course his name is attached to.

In one word: amazing. Evan is clear during his lectures and manages to make linear algebra intuitive and simple. I have taken another linear algebra course at NEU and the difference between the courses (the content was virtually identical) is insane. Homework is standard, once a week. For tests, he grades super fast so you always know your grade.

An excellent professor. His lectures are excellent and convey really advanced material in a digestible way, and his lecture notes are superbly written. If something comes up and impacts your ability to do well in the course, he'll accommodate. He genuinely cares his students.
I enjoyed his class immensely. Evan Dummit is a brilliant professor and his notes are amazing. I recommend taking any class he lectures at NEU.
Loved this class, expectations were very clear and he gave really good feedback.

Professor Dummit is the best! Knows everything there is to know about the material he is teaching, and gives great lectures. The material and practice problems are exactly like the exams. Has a great sense of humor, too.

Absolutely amazing professor. I guarantee you will not regret taking any course that he teaches. His brilliance and extensive knowledge on all areas of mathematics are obvious. He is a very pleasant guy. He makes every concept so simple and easy to understand and provides proofs for everything. Overall 10000000/10. Take his class fr.

Evan Dummit is a fantastic professor and a great person. He is really funny and I feel bad for him since I would be laughing during class, but my mic was on mute all the time. If you attend lectures and do the online project sets (which were immensely helpful) you will enjoy the class. Plus he writes his own notes that are better than any textbook.

Adjusted very well to COVID struggles and has very informational lectures.  The no questions asked homework extensions are amazing and the default extra time for exams has been very helpful.  Makes these calculus concepts seem effortless.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit is one of the best professors I've had at NEU. He made the hardest topics of Probability + Stats straightforward and clear, and he truly cares about his students. He added in policies throughout the semester to help students (midterm drop, final exam percentage choice), and is overall such a cool and funny guy.

I forgot to do my Trace evaluations, so I'm gonna give my brother a bit of love here. In short, Evan is incredibly fair and transparent; he doesn't make you pay for a textbook, he doesn't have pop quizzes, and if you take the time to study, you will get an A. He is also funny. Take his class if you can. Seriously.
Great professor. He's funny and his lecture notes are thorough and easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dummit is one of the best instructors I've ever had. He's an absolute genius and makes extremely hard topics and math seem intuitive and straight forward. His lectures are incredible, and his free notes are better than most math textbooks out there. His grading is super fair, and he cares that you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's great and his tests are online in class lockdown browser. I would say to go to class since he reviews before every exam and basically tells you what's going to be on the test. Make sure to take good notes during class because his slide shows kinda suck since they are basically all images/graphs LOL.
good professor knows what he is doing.

I took his current topics class and it was my favorite class I have taken at Northeastern. He was an INCREDIBLE teacher. Super enthusiastic, great at explaining complex topics, super kind and understanding when answering questions. 3 exams, challenging but very fair. He would often give points back if a lot of people got them wrong.

This class was great! You read papers, present a poster, and listen to lectures that help you become well-versed in limb regeneration. Prof. Duerr is genuinely one of the nicest professors I've had at Northeastern - his exams are fair, he's accessible outside of class, and he truly cares about student understanding! Plus, axolotls are super cool :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Duerr is incredibly passionate about regeneration, though teaching is evidently not his area of expertise, at least not yet as a postdoc. He teaches at an accelerated pace, and lectures can oftentimes be difficult to follow - owing to the specificity of his research. He is an amicable person outside of class though and is always willing to help.
Such boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is a hard class. Not hard to get a good grade just a lot of work.
Prof Dunne is definitely a challenging class but gives many opportunities to succeed. If you put in the effort, you get an A.

Professor Dunne might be knowledgeable about data visualization, but when it comes to teaching an academic class he simply seems like he doesn't know what he is doing. His lectures are just talking about random topics as he reads from slides he made years ago. Assignments have nothing to do with the lectures and you will not receive any help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Worst professor, I have taken in my life! Claims he teaches a design class but all of his hw and projects are technical. Takes multiple days to respond to emails. When you need help on the hw, well good luck with it because you will find none as the professor will only point out console messages and the TAS for the class are simply clueless.

Prof is clearly passionate  Imagine putting hundreds of hours into a disorganized class and going 2 1/2 months without having any idea about what your grade is, risking your ability to graduate or maintain a scholarship etc. or even learning and using that knowledge in the next assignments. TAs are bad,  don't take this unless you're nasty at JS.

If you can take this class with another prof, pls do. I can't stress this enough. There are no clear grading standards and he takes points off as he pleases. It's so frustrating. The TA's are horrible too. I have had such a terrible experience in this class

Terrible professor! Doesn't teach anything remotely related to the HW in lectures. Very harsh and completely unreasonable grader takes off many points for  ridiculos things such as not including name or not tagging pages on GradeScope. Class is so disorganized and the professor seems clueless about how to run an academic class. Do not take!

Grades take 2+ months to be released and homework assignments are useless. Lectures are boring and not related to the homework assignments. The professor holds everyone to a very high level while making the TAs teach class sometimes and not grading anything. However, this class ended up being very easy because you don't end up learning anything.

Professor Dunne is one of the better professors I have had at Northeastern. 
He isn't the most socially savvy, and his lecture structure could use some work. 
But he is a very genuine and caring person who is passionate about the topic of Data Vis. He is very helpful in office hours, and just wants his students to succeed if they put the effort in.
Worst professor ever. Biggest mistake I made is taking this course. Non-sense and waste of my tuition

Waste of my tuition. Don't know what I've learned in this "writing class". All kinds of inexplicable demands for HWs and Projects. Always get 0. Only spend one class teaching how to write code, assuming everyone is skilled in programming in JS, Python. Don't take the course with this daydreamer with obsessive-compulsive disorder.

Worst professor I've ever seen. Two quizzes with 6 multiple choices questions worth 10 points of the total grade. Don't know what he's doing in lecture, showing ridiculous pictures in slides. I taught myself JavaScript-d3, HTML, CSS, Python, Tableau the whole semester. Making last-minute grade change without reason. No recording during the pandemic

The worst professor I've ever taken. The syllabus is a mess. The only thing I got out of the class was all the bad habits I acquired while teaching myself javascript (d3), html, and CSS at the same time. Will give 0 on assignments. Mandatory attendance/participation during COVID, no recordings. makes last-minute grade changes. Very slow email.

I had a great time in Dr. D's class. The lectures were thought-provoking and he cares about his students. Tests are worth a lot but aren't too difficult. Absolutely take the class if transportation even remotely interests you!

Great guy, even better professor. Dr. Dulaski's lectures were incredibly engaging and useful if you're someone interested in multimodal transportation. Keep in mind he's very test-heavy (like 80% of overall grade), but if you go to class and engage with the content you'll have nothing to worry about.

I was so grateful to be in Dr. D's transportation class. I loved starting class with transportation news, keeping the class up to date with current events. Class content was engaging and if you payed attention in class exams, while worth a lot, were not very difficult. Would recommend to anyone interested in transportation!

Amazing guy, AMAZING professor. Keeps you very engaged in class and makes sure that you understand every concept you'd be expected to know. Have him for CIVE4554 and had for Statics, has been fantastic in both and has clear expectations of his students. Only complaint I have is he is very hard to reach via email.

I've taken five classes with Dr. D during my time at Northeastern. Take his classes. They're usually difficult, but you learn a ton. He deeply cares about his students and has unmatched passion for transportation. He is extremely detail-oriented, and accessible outside of class for help (book a meeting or go in-person!). Hands down my favorite prof
Dulaski is the greatest professor of all time. Love this guy
He's the best!
The GOAT. Cannot make statics any easier.

Can't recommend enough. Establishes a friendly, first-name relationship with EVERY student. Wants you to do well and will do everything he can to ensure you do well. Lectures were great, homework is helpful, and exams are very fair. Funny guy too.

Dulaski was such a great statics professor. He was so caring and kind and really wanted his students to be successful. He has been the best professor I have had at Northeastern and I could not recommend him enough. He does in fact call on you during class but it keeps you prepared. He also will not judge if you don't know the answer. Great guy.
Overall a GREAT teacher. Dulaski is a super nice and respectful person. He explains concepts well and encourages questions. I would 100% recommend and would definitely take again.

Professor Dulaski is a great Statics professor. While I took the class in summer so it was an accelerated course, he had reasonable tests and homework. His notes are very clear to follow and he always makes sure everyone understands the material. His tests don't trick you, they just ensure you are grasping the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor

Ran a bit like a high school class, short homework due almost every class, 6 exams throughout semester, calling randomly on students. Very good at communicating topics and helping students who aren't grasping at first. Respects students and commands respect in turn.
Great professor. Prepares you for the real world! More than any other professor. He expects a lot because he gives you a lot to learn.

Highway design was not an easy class, requirements for hw format were pretty strict, final project took time, especially design part in CAD. However, it's been a year since I took this course and I still have all the info left in my brain. Lots of work but it was worth it. Also by the end of the semester the class turns into almost a family.

Talk. If not, he'll call on you. Do practice problems for  midterm and final. There is also a paper due for this class. I recommend do the paper from AWD on transportation and use it again for his class. Homework take forever to do but that's just him. Remember, MEMO formats. His class gets harder each time he teaches it. Highway and Transportation
Great course covering the important background of advanced machine learning !

Really liked her machine learning class. It's a very tough class, broad and math heavy but if you are attentive you will gain a solid foundation for machine learning. She is both very knowledegable about ML and over the years has mastered the way to teach it. The HW can be a little intense but they are doable. Tough exams too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is willing to help if you ask.  Not the best explainer.  Class was pretty easy, her slides are straight forward.  Accent is not an issue, just humerous.

Digital Logic is a fairly easy class, her lectures are straight review of the homework so you can pay attention if you want or just teach yourself from the book (most of the class is easy enough to do this).  Very unclear and doesn't have the best command of the english language (though I've seen worse).
A good teacher, passionate about math, but not teaching.

He gave us quizzes that were intended for us to fail. We would ask for examples of how concepts would be applied on the quizzes, and he would scold us for asking, and refuse to give examples. One time, to spite us, he decided not to write on the board the entire class and described a 3D graph to us, using only his hands. So yeah.

Pretty good at explaining the larger concepts behind the math and connecting it to real world applications. It was Calculus 3, so it was still a fairly difficulttough class. Grading is fair. Quiz problems were usually based on text book examples, but tests were hard. Had extra study sessions before final. Generally good teacher.

Dylan is a good professor. He is a very good Mathematician and obviously loves Math. His lectures are generally clear and he is very helpful during office hours. That said, he isn't necessarily easy! Quizzes and assignments do tend to be pretty rough once in a while and he sets high standards of high grading. Overall, a great teacher!

So weird. I am in her class at another college and it's like she doesn't prepare for her lectures at all. There will be pauses that last minutes as she scrambled to find the materials she needs. Seems to me that her expertise is in subjects other than what she's teaching. so so weird.

I appreciated the class structure, with each week building off the previous material. I also enjoyed the peer-review forums. Professor Dygert provided clarity and constructive criticism, responded to my questions, and met with me via Zoom. The work in this class is what's expected from a grad-level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I never write a bad review cause I don't believe in it. As a student, you'll always have areas for improvement. But this is like she is waiting for you to fail her class. She would say that your topic has great materials and well-cited, but it's still weak. Don't give feedback to her feedback, she doesn't take well to it.

She is ridiculous because she won't tell you that your topic does not work, she let you finish it, and then give you really lower grade. If you have any questions about your project, she just tells you your project is great, you should work on it, and other lower grades are not important, you will get a good grade on your final proposal. F end.

Dylan clearly cares about the topics he teaches but his class was not challenging by any means. There were two exams, a presentation, and one paper--all were graded extremely leniently. He attempts to give feedback but it is sometimes lacking in substance. Nice guy, not the best teacher.

Took him for intro to Intl Relations last semester. He's a really tough grader and there is a lot of work for the papers. He's accessible in office hours but has very high expectations and criticism isnt always constructive or helpful. You'll learn a lot though if you can keep up with him.

I took Professor Maguire's International Relations in my freshman year and I wouldn't regret it at all. Sure, theres a lot of reading and he may be a sort of tough grader, but what I learned in his class was absolute superb. I'd never learn what I learned from one class than in any other class I took. This was my first political science class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The curriculums challenging which is rewarding once you commit and he's there to help every step of the way. Even in an online class format, he will happily zoom with you! I agree that your grade is dependent upon what you put into it. He rewards genuine engagement with analytical thought and persuasive arguments, all skills his class sharpens.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is challenging but rewarding. The simulation pushes you to think critically, and each assignment adds meaningful value. The professor is interactive and provides detailed, genuine feedback. If you stay committed and put in the effort, you'll learn a lot and enjoy the experience. Great class.I'd definitely take it again with Prof Lefevre.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tough grader compared to others, but fair. Feedback is detailed and super helpful. Responds to emails fast, which matters in a demanding capstone. The simulations are challenging but feel real-world applicable. A lot of work — wish I'd taken it earlier. Knowledgeable professor who genuinely cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic course. Prof. Lefevre is also an amazing instructor/person. Could not agree less with the review left before mine. Would take this class again if I could. Every interaction I had with him was extremely pleasant. Your grade is highly reflective of the effort you put into the class. Thank you, Prof. Lefevre!!

I believe my performance in this course was not evaluated fairly because the grading criteria were neither consistently nor transparently applied. He is the worst instructor I have had at Northeastern University. I don't recommend that he continue as an instructor at Northeastern.

The professor made class really enjoyable, and the work was pretty straightforward. If you set aside 2 hours or whatever you need for those big tests, you'll be fine. Also was not really a harsh grader and I think his grades were pretty fair.

Information through presentations gone over in class have little to no resemblance on the two exams taken (makes up 40% of your grade). Makes class engaging by bringing in guest speakers, but you need to read the textbook to do good on the exams. 2 group projects where you cannot choose your group. Attendance and participation is 15% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wonderful class changed my career trajectory. Class is engaging while not being overly taxing, and is such a good representation of why I love NU's global focus. Make sure to start projects early too. My best piece of advice is to get to know the people in your group even if you've never met, this will make you look forward to going to class!

Makes presentations engaging. Not my fav prof, he can be a little passive aggressive. Other than that answers emails fast. Participation matters a lot; there are no excuses for missing class. Group projects are important, you will get assigned a random group in the beginning of the class. If you get stuck with a bad group, just pray. harsh grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Duane is a great professor who cares about his students. Classes are very discussion-based. There are a couple long case-study analysis papers and a term group project that is very intensive, but that should be expected for a capstone course.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. it boring and i learnt nothing of value. everything is dependent on a group mark in which he doesn't mark each member separately, you will get the same grade as your laziest group member. Groups are given at the beginning of the semester and don't change. very hard marker and very unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tried to make all lectures fun with guest speakers and interactive simulations during class.

reviews.comment: Best prof, go ahead eyes closed
Lefev is one of my favorite professors that I have ever had. He is fun, kind, and is actually a really good teacher. I would 100% recommend!
Great professor that is open to communication as long as you show effort. Definitely recommend. Learned a great amount from this course.

Professor Lefevre sticks to the syllabus, the assignments are perfectly connected with canvas. The rubrics are clear for grading criteria. Discussions are also very clear in terms of what is expected. Lastly, group projects are very well planned. The organization makes it easy to learn. They are also very responsive to emails.

Professor Lefevre's Business Strategy course is challenging but rewarding. The simulation exercise was intense and team-driven, pushing you to apply what you learn throughout the semester. Be ready to invest time, but the real-world value makes it worth it. Highly recommend if you're serious about the subject.

Professor Lefevre is very hands on. If you're looking to skate through a class with minimal interaction, look for a different instructor. Professor Lefevre has incredible knowledge and experience which is shared though content and comments throughout discussion boards and rubrics for assignments. I can confidently say I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great class, professor had clear instructions on the assignments and was understanding of students questions/concerns.
Great professor, and definitely helps students who care about the class. Overall experience 10/10, I would definitely take class again with him.

Made the class engaging. This was his key strength. Most of learning is done outside of class by reading the textbook as his lectures are very general and mostly consists of reading off of the slides. Willing to curve depending on class averages. Group project contribution form responses are not reflective of the grades we receive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was very interactive, with engaging lectures. The main projects were a country debate and a market entry project, graded as a group (provide feedback if group members don't contribute fairly or if they exceed expectations), Professor Lefevre takes it into account. Study the textbook, and you'll do well!

Professor Lefevre is a great teacher. He is very personable with students and wants everyone to do well. Group assignments matter a lot as each project is based on these groups. Graded by two quizzes, a debate, a presentation, and participation. Quizzes are pretty fair, but you are definitely expected to read outside of class in order to do well.

Really fun activities during class, but doesn't really do much to prepare for the quizzes. You have to read a lot of the textbook to actually do well on the quizzes. The course is graded very heavily on the group debate and the group final presentation, so your designated group really matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class and really good speakers

Professor Lefevre makes the class engaging with discussions and activities. Though textbook-heavy, his enthusiasm makes lectures enjoyable. Doing well on group projects and studying with Unstuck AI is key to succeeding.

This is the best course I have taken in my academic journey so far, so I truly recommend Professor Lefevre. I took a version of the class with an experiential learning component that gave me a taste of what working in Marketing is like in the real world. If you are passionate about Marketing and truly want to learn, this class is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This is my second class with him.This course is challenging and requires hard work. Discussion and simulation are effective and engaging, yet quite demanding. In order to succeed in this class, you need to stay on top of assignments. His grading criteria is clear, so paying close attention to his instructions and rubric is crucial for a high grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class and professor are tough - but in talking with peers all professors are for this course. If you stay on top of assignments and participate you will be successful.

Much like the business world and most professors teaching this class, he has high expectations. The simulation is very lifelike and challenging. Duane is a wonderful professor. His class is very interesting and can learn a lot of business basic strategies. I was total into his class!
