DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!  You will hate college if you sign up for this class.  It is not worth the aggravation.  She takes forever to grade everything you hand in, and even though you might do well in the class she'll still give you a B and blame it on participation!  STAY AWAY FROM SULTAN!!!

She is absolutely terrible.  I went to the bar after almost every class.  She has unrealistic expectations and no one can stand listening to her for an hour an forty minutes.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!

Prepare to do****loads of work for this elective.  She will take you to the computer lab every other class and expect you to do a report, powerpoint, and then a presentation in the class time.  Also she will randomly pick people and ask them about the cha
Harda** so be prepared to work, but really a good teacher and just expects a lot.
Alert! She is so terrible. You can actually get an A in her midterm and final exam, but she will give a B as a final grade just because she wants to!!!

She is an effective teacher but the course load is extremely heavy for an elective. She gives you this thick ass packet but thats not all, over the semester she'll keep whipping out more requirements. She is a very nice and helpful person when you do talk to her one on one in her office!

He's a pretty chill professor, he's good at explaining problems and generally pretty amenable to partial credit if you can explain your thinking well. Super funny and down to earth, clearly cares a lot about making sure we're actually learning. Very open to feedback, the course was pretty flexible and a lot was up to what works best for us.

Farzard professor is incredibly engaging and truly cares about student learning. Lectures are clear, thoughtful, and well-structured. He creates a welcoming environment where questions are encouraged. He challenges you in the best way and provides meaningful feedback. You leave the course feeling more confident and capable.

This class was extremely difficult to follow. It is a statistics course, but very little statistics were taught but rather most of it was stated to be intuitive and that we should already know the math side. He uses a lot of AI and will answer students questions in class using AI rather than using his own degree. Very test heavy.

Honestly a joke this class used so much AI it's not even funny, the lectures were unegaging and fast paced for an introductory level course. Gave extra credit for attendance but wouldn't be my first choice, the exams were extremely difficult and be prepared to put in a lot of effort

Farzad is very nice and clearly likes the topic but he often goes on unrelated tangents. Homeworks are fine but the tests are not like what we learn in class. He uses AI to teach and spent an entire class plugging our questions into AI. He is very bad at responding to emails and hard to reach.

If you want to pass this class, then DO NOT listen to anything he tells you to study to prepare for his midterm or final exams. He told me to focus on the 2 practice exams he posted and the review questions for we over in class for the midterm and the actual exam was NOTHING like what he posted. Just focus on his slides mostly and assignments.
Good instructor, funny and informative.

If you have the option for biostats you should 100% take him. I didn't attend lectures a lot cuz he just goes through slides which I did on my own. There are weekly labs and (easy) quizzes. I recommend trying to do good on those and get help from recitation because you can get an easy B+ or A from doing well on those. Also a midterm and a final.

Professor Noubary usually did a very good job at explaining statistics concepts, but sometimes he would over-explain to the point where he bored the class and he became difficult to pay attention to. That being said, homework consisted of weekly quizzes and labs that were usually not too difficult but were annoying to do.

Don't take this class with Fabricius if you don't care to really learn the material. You cannot get away with memorizing how to do problems without fully understanding the concepts, but he does a good job of teaching in class and gives a decent amount of points for participation (I think around 30% of total).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor cares a lot about his lectures and is very intelligent. I would love to take another course with him! He cares a lot about makes sure that his students fully understand concepts and he is always trying to help students succeed in his class.

Professor Somogyi knows his material and consistently goes above and beyond. He expects attention and active participation, and his homework, lectures, and exams mirror real industry knowledge. The class is challenging but he explains concepts clearly, supports students, is understanding, and offers a fair curve, which helps everyone succeed.

Every single lecture is incredibly informative and engaging. He explains concepts in a way that's both sharp and practical. He knows his stuff and it shows. What stands out the most is how much he cares about students actually understanding the material. He's also very accessible outside of class. It's obvious he wants his students to succeed.

Mr. Somogyi is an excellent teacher who genuinely cares about his students and has a deep passion for finance. He is enthusiastic and passionate about investments and always comes prepared to teach every class! The exams are tough, so you'll need to dedicate significant time to studying. Come prepared to class and participate; it's worth it!

Favorite class I have taken at Northeastern. Professor Somogyi is clearly passionate about teaching and class is super easy to understand and he is very good with questions. He brings in guest speakers to talk about their experiences in the field, it was super interesting. Tests are fine if you pay attention in class and do the homework diligent.

Smart and knowledgeable professor. Hosts a great introductory course for concepts regarding investments if you actually want to learn. Exams can be difficult, but not impossible. Definitely the most rewarding class I've taken as a finance concentration student. Graded on: midterm and final, participation, and weekly homework

Professor Somogyi was an amazing teacher. He thoroughly cares about his students and has a real passion for finance. This was my favorite while also the most difficult class I've taken. The exams are not easy. You will have to study a lot for them. All in all while this class was very hard, Professor Somogyi made it much more enjoyable.

This class is challenging but extremely rewarding. Fab clearly knows his stuff and his course prepared me for the material on a level I have not experienced in other courses at Northeastern. If you have the privilege of taking his class you will come out of class every day having a deeper understanding of investments and the markets as a whole.

Professor Somogyi's class is challenging but highly rewarding. Pay attention and participate actively, and you'll gain financial knowledge that sets you apart. He's extremely knowledgeable, and his engaging teaching style makes complex topics easier to grasp. A must-take course if you're ready to put in the effort and learn deeply!
Professor Fabricius was a very fun teacher. He implemented his own personal style into lectures, and I believe that created an easy environment for everyone to learn in.

Best finance professor at northeastern. Tests were really hard and averages were in the 50 to 60 range, however everyone gets curved at the end. HEAVILY CURVED. Somoygyi is very approachable and there is no one that knows as much about finance than him. If you want to learn but also do well take this class because you will learn and do well.

Professor Somogyi is absolutely one of the best professors you can have for thoroughly learning the fundamentals of investments. He expects a lot from his students and can move very quickly through material, so his classes are challenging, but extremely helpful for anyone who is interested in rigorous learning.

Professor Somogyi is passionate about investments and gives excellent insight into how securities pricing works. Although the exams are super tough, you'll be golden if you do the revision slides and practice the problem sets. It is easily one of the best courses in the Finance Department if you want to learn.
Excellent Professor, knows a lot about investments and if you put the effort in you will do well.

Fabricius is one of, if not the best, professor in the finance department at Northeastern. If you are serious, take him for investments; his section is challenging but very manageable. You will learn the concepts at a very advanced level and will be well prepared for upper-level finance courses. Incredible class!

Honestly a great professor. He is very young but so intelligent and so good at what he does and teaches. His tests are really hard but he curves final grades so you will pass. Homeworks are fairly easy and if you show up to class you will get good participation. Somogyi is actually the Goat

This was the best class I took this semester. It is difficult to earn an A but the class is amazing. Somogyi is very approachable and treats students with the utmost respect. He is easily reached by email and responds promptly.

this professor has clearly never taught american students before. his grading method is outrageous, meaning that 60% of your grade rides on 2 tests. on top of this, he also can't teach. most of his lectures have nothing to do with the homework assigned online. he made an interesting subject into one of the worst weed out classes at northeastern

Nice guy. An expert in Investments, but clearly has no teaching experience. If he is the only available option when registering for Investments, find a different class to take unless you want to spend a whole semester teaching yourself the material.

Moves VERY quickly over all material, which there is A LOT of. You better be reading the slides before class, doing all of the work before class, and coming in already knowing all of the material or you will be very quickly left behind. The course is extremely difficult and he does not help. Super nice but assumes everyone knows as much as he does.

He expects everyone to know as much as he does. Rarely goes over materials. Problems done in class don't reflect the homework or exams, which is terrible because 60% of the grade is 2 exams. TA's are pretty helpful, but I constantly felt behind because there is just so much material and he skims over most of it.
He was not accessible outside of class. His lectures are boring and hard to follow. He promised extra credits, which were never given.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do the practice quizzes so you can survive from every exam
One suggestion is to participate in his class, than he will be really nice to you. If you don't really participate, he might cold call you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Multiple-choice questions are taken online, and attendance is mandatory. He provides extra credit for the portfolio, so remember to take some notes and follow his instructions for what should be included in the portfolio.

Professor Peter is a nice professor. Exams were very easy; it was all multiple-choice questions, exactly the same as those in the practice questions. As long as you can complete the practice questions, you'll do well on the exam.

Class is super boring. He just talks and writes on the board, no slides. Tests are easy if you do his practice questions since they repeat, but there are tons of them per chapter. Participation is okay if you speak up. Make sure to take notes because he grades them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There were so many group projects that he expected us to finish in the time of class. Expectations were unclear and did not reflect the syllabus. Feedback was always critical but never felt helpful. Got off topic quite often. HATES technology, he cannot stand students using technology while he is talking.
Professor Fell does not care about student success but only for himself. His instructions are often misunderstood making students really miserable. He is also not accessible outside of the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fell is widely considered a poor instructor due to their inconsistent teaching style, lack of clear expectations, and apparent disinterest in student engagement. Additionally, his grading criteria appear arbitrary, with inconsistent feedback on assignments, making it difficult for students to understand how to improve their work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Daniel Faber is an inspirational teacher. He emphasizes all topics that he will put on the test in his lectures, show up and you'll be fine. The essays are graded based on his rubric, based on the quality of content and analysis, everyone did very well on them. The exams are multiple choice and very easy to answer if you listen in lecture.

love this king, attendance isn't ever taken but pretty much everything on the exam is something he said in class so you do kinda have to show up, half the classes are films, other half are lectures, your grade is based on 2 tests and 2 essays, he is one of the smartest people i've ever talked to but he does tend to ramble on in class

Danny was a great teacher! He's super passionate about what he's teaching and every lecture was insanely eye opening. There are only two tests and two papers but he is very clear that as long as you show up and pay attention you will do well. He doesn't tell you anything about the tests before you take them but it's everything you learn in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Faber is one of the best professors at Northeastern. Although his lectures can be a little hard to follow, he is super down-to-earth and super understanding. Attendance wasn't mandatory but if you want to do well on the exams then you have to show up. Exams and papers are super chill, with most of the class getting A-/A. 10/10 professor and class.

He is a genius. Take the opportunity to learn from him because he knows a lot. He also brings speakers to teach about subject. As long as you reflect in your papers, you'll do good. It's a 4500 level course but don't be intimidated by it. Around 1-3hrs spent/ week in hw and assignments

Prof Faber is very accomplished in the ENVR field and is highly respected. HOWEVER, he often doesn't use slides during lectures and goes on tangents that make it hard to tell what we should be taking notes on. Very lecture heavy, but sometimes shows documentary. Lots of reading, but content is very interesting. Two exams and two papers (all 25%).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Faber is a great professor and I learned a lot from his class. There are only two tests and two essays. Essays aren't too bad (around 6 pages) and most of the class gets A/A-. Tests are little harder, you need to go to class and do the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely unorganized and classroom is ridiculously difficult to navigate. Simply provides topics for essays and the rest is up to you. No study guides for tests but is based on whatever he randomly claims will be on the test in class + ppt he covers + five/six hour long films with no emphasis on what is important.

Great guy. Very knowledgeable. Fascinating lectures. 2 tests and 2 essays are your entire grade but the tests are all multiple choice and if you show up to class, you will get an A. Highly suggest taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Faber was very well spoken and the lectures were very interesting. There are weekly readings (kind of optional) and two essays and two multiple choice exams. I didn't have to devote a lot of time to the essays or studying for exams and I still got good grades, but I also felt like I still learned a lot from the course.

Danny is super experienced and knowledgeable in the subject, and a really a great guy! The lectures are pretty intense, but the content is so interesting and important. You can't pass the exams if you don't come to class, as it is mostly lecture based. I highly recommend him, but this was by no means an easy class.

Professor Faber is an amazing lecturer. Attendance isn't taken but the final/midterm are easy to pass if you attend. He is a great public speaker and captivating, lectures were always pretty funny, albeit heavy. The class is 2 essays and 2 exams. He isn't strict on essay formatting. I learned a great deal from this class. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Environment and Society couldn't be taught by anyone else. Danny is highly knowledgeable and qualified. I mean, the guy wrote Bernie's climate platform in 2016! He's got the framework of the class down (rightfully so, after like 30 years of doing it), but he never phones it in- the lectures are all engaging and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Faber is no doubt an intelligent man. However, his political bias comes out quite clear. The class might as well be called Socialism 101 or Why Capitalism sucks. Granted, some problems may be accredited to it, we look at zero solutions to problems that aren't dismantling capitalism. Lectures became so frustrating I'd leave early often.

Danny Dimes is an absolute stud. This is a heavily policy based class with tons of readings, but its all super interesting, and he has tons of personal experience (wrote Bernie's Environmental plan and Boston's Green New Deal). There are few graded items, but pretty straightforward if you pay attention. Lectures are a little all over the place.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I heard others talk about how great this class was, so I decided to take it. Even though it was not part of my requirements. I went in a little skeptical about all the hype. I was immediately blown away! This is hands down the best class that I have ever taken. Faber is a fantastic lecturer, and really opened my eyes to the ways of the world.

Absolutely loved his class. I learned so much and would love to take other classes taught by him. There is a lot of reading to do and you do have to put in some good work on the midterm and final papers but the tests are pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really interesting lectures; he focuses a lot on current events and when he does go over his PowerPoint presentations he makes sure to relate them back to relevant events. 2 Tests and 2 papers are the only thing you get graded on. First test was very very easy, second one was slightly tougher but still manageable if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy A. Only two papers that constitute your grade. You get to choose the topics to write about. Professor was unorganized and didn't really have a solid curriculum. I never knew if there was a reading that I was supposed to read. He also repeated a lot of the same things every lecture. Intelligent man. Very passionate about the environment though.

Very interesting class and definitely eyeopening. However, his lectures can get quite heavy for 1hr40 and although the conversations are really interesting, I was often confused with what to write down as some if it sounds irrelevant and you don't know how to prepare for the exam. (1 midterm paper and test, 1 final and paper) A LOT OF READING!

This dude is so cool!!!  And plus his lectures are fascinating.  A couple I would even call spellbinding.  Despite it being a large class, he invites student participation.  YOu have to come to class and do the readings in order to get a good grade.  There were a few Ds and even some Fs in the class, but that is because they did not do the work.
Daniel Faber was hands down the best professor I've had. He's very effective and his classes are very compelling. Take his class if you can.

He's a chill guy and extremely knowledgable about the environmental movement. I personally agree with almost everything he says but he doesn't really allow an alternative point of view which can be frustrating for some because there isn't any debate. No final though which is clutch

He is v involved in the real world, he's not just a prof. He knows what's going on& enjoys talking about current events. He's passionate. Class is very educational& entertaining. Grade is based on 2 MC tests&a research paper only. 1st test wasn't too hard but the 2nd test was hard. I suggest that he add another test. Not an easy A but v enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor filled with so much knowledge! This class is a real wake up call regarding climate change and how change has to be done immediately.  I really enjoy this class and learn so much in 4 months than I could learn in a year in other classes. 2 exams and one research paper. I  HIGHLY reccomend this class!

Dr. Faber is AWESOME! This was probably my favorite class so far. 2 MC exams, 2 research papers, and 2 extra credit opportunities. His lectures are so interesting. Exams are based on lecture and textbook. Probably one of the nicest professors ever. I didn't believe the hype about how great this class was but now I am a believer! Plus, he is so hot!
Probably the best class I have ever taken.  I wish there were more classes like this one at NU.

Environment and society is a life-changing class. Prof. Faber treats his students as the next generation responsible for building the future. You learn a lot of important things you may not get to learn in any other setting. His lectures are incredibly informative and eye-opening; grades end up seeming like formalities.

It was a lecture-style class and he talks about politics and our environment. There is homework (just readings) but it's not bad and it's interesting. There are only three grades: midterm, final, paper. The midterm and final were easy A's if you showed up. Eye-opening class, as long as you're not closed-minded.

Faber's lectures are AWESOME. He knows so much and his class really changed the way I look at the world. The class is also comically easy, with two easy tests and a paper being the only real work assigned. You didn't really need to do the readings but I did because they were so interesting. TAKE THIS CLASS!! You'll get an A and it's fascinating

Simply the best class that I have ever taken at Northeastern University.  His lectures are amazing.  He has so much experience in the environmental movement, and he brings those insights into the classroom.  This class changed my life, and my major.  I now plan to switch to sociology.  There is a great deal of work but you can do well. Best ever.

Faber is a great great teacher. If you have a chance to take Environment and Society, you should definitely do so. Learned a ton of relevant information in the class and lectures were interesting. Tests were easy as long as you go to class, and you could go to him if you needed help on the two assigned essays.

Two ten page papers and 2 tests. Lots of reading to do outside of class. No final during finals week. Even though there were only four assignments and they each weighed heavily on the overall grade, you can totally get an A. Go talk to him personally about the papers because he is really helpful. As long as you go to lecture, you'll do fine on test

Such an awesome guy! Very very knowledgeable and definitely knows what he is talking about. the exams are not difficult as long as you study the lectures and go to class. From what I know, he's had a badass life and his book is just generally fascinating. The material is also intriguing and shows different sides of situations. take his class

His lectures run dry sometimes, but overall you do learn about the environmental movement. There is A LOT of reading that gets assigned, but realistically speaking, you don't need to read everything to do well. Study his powerpoint slides and lecture notes because those sum things up pretty well. Extra credit write-ups come in handy.

Faber is simply the man. If you're taking a class with him, it is probably because you have at least some interest in environmental problems, and he is actively involved in identifying and solving these problems. I could not imagine a more suitable professor.
Teacher is great and tests are easy!!! This class is extremely easy and guaranteed A.  I think the TA is helpful, she replies emails real quick.

Faber's a great teacher. I had him for the First Year Inquiries class on environmental politics, and it's always worth my time to go and listen to his lectures. He also shows a lot of interesting and helpful films. He's always willing to help you out if you have a question, and gives very good advice about career-seeking in this subject. Great guy!

Midterm and final were extremely easy. Essays are pretty generic. Only 4 grades per year.  Lots of movies which are kind of entertaining.  His speeches tend to be a tad disorienting as he rarely provides written accompaniment. As someone else said, the TA is useless. Her grasp on English is lacking and she somehow doesn't know how to use Google.

Class was very interesting. Only four grades: 2 ten page papers, midterm, final. Tests were really easy, class average almost a 90. lectures can get long, but pay attention to that and movies and you'll do fine.
Dude is awesome

Very interesting class, although the lecture can sometimes be very dry. Many interesting videos used. At times however, the professor's bias was very apparent. He is very socialism slanted, and seems to hate everything capitalist. Overall, very informative if you can filter out the radical marxist rhetoric. Oh, and the TA was useless.
Really great class, easy exams. A lot of supplemental films. Lectures tend to get long and boring with little class interaction, but the material is very interesting.

This is a pretty fun class. The lectures are interesting and he shows alot of movies. The readings are very dull though. Just take notes in class and you'll be fine on the 2 exams, because he usually covers whats in the book during class. Also 2 papers, which aren't too bad. Good class overall, plus he looks like Tim Robbins!!

This class is the bomb!!!!  I couldn't wait to go each day, as I would learn so much.  Environmental politics is my passion, and not all students shared this passion going into the semester, but I think Professor Faber really turned them on to the importance of global warming and environmental justice.  He is the best!!

One of the best classes that I have ever taken.  The lectures are demanding in terms of content, but his storytelling and examples are very entertaining, and make the subject come alive.  The films are wonderful!

This class is awesome! I learned so much about environmental politics in the U.S. Professor Faber's lectures are extremely compelling and inspiring.  If you do the readings and come to class lectures, you will do well. If you don't, those students are in for a surprise on the exams.  I highly recommend this class.

Assigned two papers and two tests. I didn't do any reading except a little for my papers and I got an A on the paper. I was a little worried for the midterm because I felt we hadn't learned anything yet, but it was a piece of cake. He shows a lot of movies, too... just go to class, pay attention, you'll do well. Highly recommended!
Very good teacher, very knowledgeable about subject.. BUT talks about himself a lot. Assigns his own published essays to read!
Professor Faber knows a lot about what he teaches and the subjects are really interesting, but the lectures can be kind of repetitive. All in all it's a good class
Great teacher. Take this class if you can. Very interesting stuff covered.
Awesome teacher! Take his class if you get the chance... environment and society. I learned a lot and it was really interesting.
Smart, personable, and involved. Only a few other professors that I'd ever give such overall goodmarks. I would highly reccomend him - especially if you're into that social theory bag.
good teacher if you're interested in the topic.  he lectures the whole class and is pretty monotonous.  shows movies often.  pretty good teacher...

He brings valuable experience to every class, which helps illustrate key concepts. Every class is a lecture, and I found them all really interesting. I like the class discussions that take place, it feels very engaging and easy to participate. Great experience!

Environmental Planning is a class about regulations and planning - already a dull class. Felix does his best to provide ideas and input, but it's mainly just him reading off slides. No rubrics or guidance for assignments, although he is an easyish grader so not horrible. For a required class it's boring but easy and you can do other work during it

Big assignments are vague. He refuses to give a rubric or any specific guidelines (he didn't know what a rubric even was). Lectures are dull and subjects are outdated. I learn much more from student contributions than anything he could say. Take this class if you want to pay to become unbelievably frustrated two times a week and gain nothing.

Gave weekly quizzes on like 3 different articles each week. Big on class discussions and will randomly call on you. Felix seems to not know 100% what he's talking about and oftentimes fed wrong information and argued with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class was ok due to the small class discussions but Felix was pretty dull. Has relevant professional experience but cannot relate it well outside a few specific examples. there are better classes to take in the environmental and poly sci colleges for applicable environmental policy

Despite his years in the Mass. DEP, he is not very knowledgeable, or aware of, issues outside the confines of MA. Of all the professors in the ENVR Department, a true disappointment here. He has no idea how to teach, doesn't source anything he says, and makes incorrect statements all the time. Waste of time. Felt like an intro high school class.

Really boring lectures and class exercises that felt pretty pointless, but it may also just be the material. Professor Lassk's grading criteria was often unclear. She would take points off for not including something that was never communicated to be a requirement. Very unorganized canvas page.

This teacher is terrible at explaining material and the lectures are painfully boring. Our exam was 3 hours long despite class being 1.5 hours, forcing 20+ students into her office to finish. She ignores student feedback and assigns extremely difficult SPSS work without proper guidance. She gives us homework/projects with no guidance or outline.

LOVE Felicia! She's an amazing professor who is super approachable and experienced within the field of market research. I personally wasn't ecstatic to be taking a course concerning anything with analytics, but she made me fall in love with the subject. The class is HEAVY on group projects and she's definitely a difficult grader. Would def again.

Felicia is a very nice person, however her class is taught in an interesting way. There are many printed handouts - making it feel like you're in elementary school. The Role Plays are a high percentage of your grade & they are super awkward, although I understood her reasoning for it, it just felt very staged and unnatural. Easy grader though.
great teacher...exams were easy and she is really nice...the semester project long and she was a tough grader on it...but overall i really liked her and would def take her again

This is a good class and you get to learn different research methods. Guests speakers are good too which adds practicality. Prof Lassk is kind and knows her stuff. The text book is not used a lot although it is better than other statistics books. The amount of time required for deliverables is sometimes more than necessary.
Assignments are pretty easy, but group project is a pain.  Also graded participation, which favors students who love to hear their own voice.
Decent teacher.  Very nice, but you don't learn a whole lot from her class.  She is also a tough grader when it comes to tests.

She's a good teacher who knows what she is talking about since she is still in the industry. A bit of a tough grader at times but always fair. She lets you argue for more points on tests.  I would recommend her to anyone needing this course.
She is a horrible grader, with unfair tests and no class structure.  GET OUT!
This was one of the easiest classes ever.  We spent the entire semester working on a Citi Bank project.  You didn't even have to show up to class to get a B or better!

She is nice, and she doesn't grade so hard. The exam was extreamly hard, but she curved it so it was cool, or else both of her class would average 60. Take her and I promise you will get a B- or higher
i would rather d1e than sit through another class with this ho3 i am dropping this minor because of her. DONT DO IT OML

Prof. Fitzgerald is extremely knowledgeable and knows more than just about anyone about the field of urban planning. There is a lot of reading, so be prepared for that. Weekly reading responses are important and she grades them somewhat strictly. Extremely nice, cares about students, and willing to talk a paper/ project through outside of class.

Professor Fitzgerald really knows what she's talking about on each of the topics that we covered. Definitely do most, if not all, of the reading -- it'll help you with your papers and the exam, and on your participation grade. I think her lectures were very interesting, as long as you care about the topic.
Worst professor I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: She might be a PhD but she doesn't how to teach. Her classes are just boring. She is a boring person. Grade is based on individual and group papers, plus huge final presentation, but she wont't grade on content, but only on her personal opinions on the matter! If she doesn't agree, she will question everything you write until you fail the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Knows her stuff but the class was a LOT OF WORK for an intro class. 3 exams, giant presentation (30% of grade) and massive 12-15 page paper (25% of grade). policy issues discussed in class were interesting. everyone in my class was on their way to grad school the next year so as a first year it was very intimidating. tests were somewhat difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I never in a million years would think that Law and Public Policy could be boring -- but Joan made it unbearable. The lectures are long and she drones on and on // It was not engaging or interesting at all (and I LOVE the law, so I was very disappointed)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take this class if you have a light semester. 2 part paper-15 pg and 8 pg -ask her to review in office hrs), 100 min group presentation, 3 quizzes(on EVERYTHING from class) & participation (TA writes down every time you talk) make up grade. Grades pretty easily. Tons of reading, do none of it except review Cole book and class notes before quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: lots of theory & discussion. If you're interested in law and public policy then this class is fine for you. if not definitely don't take it. Decent amount of reading, you should do most of it. some of the reading is really interesting, and some is just boring. grading criteria isn't super clear, but she lets you choose topics you are interested in

Wow. Worst professor ever. I can't even begin to tell you how awful it was. Walks right into the classroom and declares herself a Hillary supporter. So not open to discussion of different views. Don't get me started on her crazy specific quizzes, absolute abomination.

Avoid professor at all costs. This class will tank your GPA. No clear and consistent grading criteria, not clear what material will be on quizzes, semester-long essay was 40% of grade and was only mentioned once. This class was the single cause of all my stress this semester. She said she hadn't taught undergrad in a long time and it showed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This professor will prevent you from getting your PhD.  It does not matter how much you know, or can offer to vitalize your research field.  She is a PhD student sink-hole.  Avoid the LPS PhD program, unless you want to waste $36,000 and a LOT of time.

I thought she was pretty good.  I just didn't like that she took attendance every class and then wakes you up if she finds you sleeping in class.  I think the people who didn't like the teacher, must not have liked the subject matter because it is very interesting and the movies were very relevant.
357omigod she makes zero sense.  i had to take drugs to stay awake in her class.  a chimp could of taught better

This women is such a bore.  It is like 100 minutes of torture with her everytime.  Papers that use info from lectures are frowned upon, but you can't skip class due to strict attendence requirement.  Grade papers on agreement with opinion, not content!

This class is hard and if you fall behind you will have a really hard time catching up. the lectures can be an information overload and very long. He posts lectures which is nice. not much homework but a lot of material to learn

The best! Logic can be a little confusing if you're not super familiar with it, but he's very understanding. He's really nice and gives good lectures. He encourages group work and is a pretty fair grader. Take him!

Bless his soul and everything he touches. Amazing, caring, and understanding professor. If any problems ever arise, don't hesitate to contact him - the response time is usually half a millisecond. They should pay him more.

I had zero knowledge of logic prior. He explained everything so well and broke it down right from the beginning for an introductory level. I never felt left behind or too confused even though sentential logic was such a foreign topic to me. It's because he's such a great lecturer. Attendance isn't mandatory. 1/3 quizzes, 1/3 midterm, 1/3 final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite college professor I've had thus far. Caring, intelligent, and super passionate about the information he teaches. I went in with no prior knowledge of the topics in the course, and felt that I developed a comprehensive understanding by the end.

The best professor I have ever had. He is very passionate about what he teaches and that's what makes his lectures so enjoyable. Sometimes he rambles but the class is easy and laid back. Highly highly recommend.

Absolutely loved this class. Branden is a genius, and he's so obviously passionate about what he's teaching. Don't want to go to class? Fine. He doesn't care, all the lectures are recorded. If you can teach yourself the material, great, if not, his in class explanations are really interesting and he's happy to help! Bro has great music taste too

Branden is one of the smartest people I have ever met and that really does show through his teaching. While the class is difficult and sometimes hard to understand, he makes it worth it and he will always do his best to make sure everyone gets it in the end. He is also amazing to talk to outside of class if you need help or just want to catch up.

Makes Logic pretty easy to understand. Lectures and homework are more complicated than the tests. He provides sample tests for both the midterm and final which are very similar to the actual thing. Take this professor if you get the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fitelson is an absolute legend and I would definitely take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Fitelson makes logic, which is complicated, easy to understand with clear lectures. He gives many examples. Before every quiz he gives a practice quiz which is the same format as the quiz. You do have to put in work as logic isn't easy to understand. Grades are based on HW, Midterm and Final as well as Participation (commenting on Modules).
I love this class. Logic is very complicated, but Professor Fitelson makes it so interesting and you learn so much. Very engaging lectures and he's such a nice and down-to-earth person.
If you wanna learn, you will learn (to the point where your head hurts). If you don't wanna learn, you can still coast thru without much or any effort. Super smart guy and so chill!!!
Do the lectures before classes, do the homework in groups, show up to class, study before exams, and youll get an A. Hilarious, charismatic, accessible outside class, and overall joy of a professor.

This is the one class I never skipped. Easy lectures, bi-weekly homework that aren't difficult, a midterm, and a final exam. All are super simple and predictable. He even gives you a review for the two exams that are in the same format as the real deal. Also, he played music at the start of class while everyone got settled. Great vibes.

Such a great Prof, such a great class. I had Brandon for Intro to Logic and this class was such a breeze! He gives biweekly homework assignments that are graded pass or fail. He is extremely knowledgeable as well. I studied only the night before for our midterm and still got an A+! I definitely recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Branden, as he tells his students to call him, is probably the smartest guy you'll ever meet. But, he knows how to explain things to students and doesn't rub his intellectual abilities in your face. The class can be hard but he' super chill, actually grades easily, gives lots of extra credit, and is occasionally hilarious.

The love of my life and the best professor I've ever taken! He personally made his Intro to Logic class extremely fun. Was always accessible outside of class and genuinely wants his students to do well, would always chat with us before class started. I'm taking him for an advanced Logic class next semester, so hopefully he'll be the same.
Interesting subject.  Useful regardless of major.  Great Professor and crazy easy.  Recommend for all.

One of the best professors and people that I've ever met. He really wants students to succeed and will do his level best to work with you in whatever you need. 

He teaches directly from the textbook though. This can be bad for some people but it worked really well for me because I thought the textbook he chose was great.

The homeworks were well made to develop an understanding of the material we would need for our exams. Unfortunately, his lectures were more akin to a textbook reading session. He rarely drifted off the exact path of the textbook, often skipped insightful calculations while doing out tedious ones, and did not do an amazing job teaching us.

Professor Fiete is an incredible professor. I had him for Modern Physics and you can tell he's very educated/passionate about the content; he could answer virtually any question anyone asked. His lectures were very informative and even if something was confusing, the homework was catered really well to solidify the material. 10/10 guy and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'd forgotten that there existed professors who actually test you on what they teach you. More than that if you use the provided materials (textbook and lecture) and do the homework you will be prepared for the exams. I found the lectures sometime interesting and sometimes boring but that's due to personal interest. Would highly recommend this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I was honestly really scared to take this class based on her reviews but it was much better than I anticipated. Biochem is hard but she's a great teacher. if you use the resources she gives you and actually study you can succeed. also really helpful if you have to take the mcat, i feel like i got a great biochem comprehension from her course.

The class was VERY organised and VERY structured, and Professor is very knowledgeable and caring, but can come off as condescending. Exams were based very similarly to the study guides, and there is honestly not a ton of material, so it ends up being pretty easy. But attendance is VERY important, and participation matters to make her like you

Her class was structured extremely well and her expectations were clear. The lectures were interesting and this was honestly my favorite class I took this semester. She provides practice tests for exams, which helped me a ton. However, she is condescending and rude. If you participate too much, she gets snippy. Good professor, not too nice, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Attendance mandatory. Tests are so wordy and like an SAT. Would not take again with this Inquiries topic, take an easier one.

I actually enjoyed her lectures and understood concepts well, but her exams are extremely difficult. They are unnecessarily complicated and if you are a slow test-taker, they are hard to finish. I've never done so poorly in class, esp with concepts I really knew/understood. Additionally, she is very condescending and not easy to approach.

prof fertuck is not horrible, but her explanations are unclear and i learned far more from youtube and other supplemental sources. exams are formatted like the SAT where there's a bunch of meaningless jargon to trip you up and it doesn't even help with finding the answer. 35% of your grade is basically padding, and trust me, you're gonna need it.

I thought that the exams were way more difficult than they had to be, and were much more difficult than the practice done in class. The entire class is a lecture besides 10 minutes of group work every class that she uses as attendance. I think she seems to be a really nice person and is very knowledgeable about biochemistry, but it was very hard.

Feel like other reviews are being overtly harsh. Lectures could be slow but were thorough + there was ample review material from past lessons which made studying for exams extremely easy. Reasonable amount of hw & other assignments given with clear deadlines, instructions & rubrics. Prof was also very understanding & made it interesting to learn.

She tries to be nice but it comes across as very condescending and treats you like a kid. Her lecture slides are fine but the way they're explained in class is very inefficient and very slow. She is very controlling and I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eh she was a good teacher and cared about how much we learn. But it did feel a little like I was being babied and even if I did know what I was doing. Tbh it's not hard to get a decent grade but I wouldn't say I looked forward to going to class.

While the content of the class was interesting her tests and class overall was a lot more difficult than the other inquiries sections. She often treated us like we were little kids with seating arrangements and the language she used when she spoke. If you have the choice, I would choose another section.

she's alright. the class is mostly graded by the 2 midterms, the poster project, and the final. the midterms are heavily based on the lectures and like the SATs. the poster project is basically easy points if you do it by the rubric. the final is basically the same as the midterms, but cumulative.
don't take if not interested in (bio)chemistry.

Professor Fertuck comes off as a caring professor, trying to get to know everyone's names. However, she only cares for attendance purposes. She is not the best socially. Tests have way too much reading. Lectures are a waste of time. However, she has all lessons written out, the material is easy to learn, and consultations for project are helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I understand that she's trying to be upbeat, but it comes off as very annoying and condescending. She talks to you like you're a kid. I asked her a question and she cut me off and walked away. She makes topics much more complicated than needed. One of the only sections for BIOL2299 that had a final. Avoid her, to be honest.

People are not lying when they say that Prof. Fertuck has an overly dramatic tone of voice, but I don't think it's meant to be condescending. She likes to focus on teaching first semester students for this section, so she seems extra because she is trying to be extra supportive.
Overall, knoweldgable and easy to spend an hour with half of the week.

Where do I begin with this woman. She is the most BIZARRE professor I've ever had. She treats her students like children with her name tags and assigned seats (ALL YEAR). She will laugh like an evil witch and screech words throughout the entire hour- making this course painful to sit through. Take this as a warning. Get as far away as you can...

I usually do not complain about my professors. HOWEVER, this woman is truly INSUFFERABLE. Get ready to leave class every day with a pounding headache. Her voice is my least favorite sound in the world if im being kind. Her screaching volume of every other word, especially her "ANDDDDD" and "EHHHHEMMM" will haunt you in your sleep. Good luck........

Professor Fertuck seems passionate about what she was teaching but she liked to waste time and the lectures felt really long. She talked to students like children and had assigned seats and daily turn and talks. Her exams were reading comprehension and required specific answers for short responses.

I could tell that Professor Fertuck was passionate about the topics; however, she likes to waste time in class and each lecture fell long. She treats students like little children with assigned seats and turn and talks at the beginning of each class. Exams were lengthy and had paragraphs of information before questions. I would avoid her if you can

Lectures are difficult to get through. Fertuck is condescending, over-explains every detail, and generally treats students like they're dumb. Exams are blocks of text that make it difficult to get to the important information. The actual information gained from lectures is diluted by hours of waste. Avoid at all costs.

Her exams resemble the SAT questions a lot. She is very condescending and in my opinion, she lacks social cues. I would avoid her at all costs. While she is extremely knowledgeable, she is not very approachable. Exams are only 30 questions, so you cannot get like more than 5 questions wrong.

Fertuck loves to go through her lectures very slowly with oversaturated explanations that take up so much time. Can't forget about the obnoxious tone or the ways she dilates her voice to speak to you like you're a 3rd grader. Exams are blocks of text that hardly contribute to helping you answer the question. Overall, decent instructor, just boring.

Fertuck was not the most enjoyable professor. As a person, she was tough to deal with and talk to. The content of the class wasn't bad - she overexplained a lot thinking we were kindergarteners. Her exams remind me of the SAT and are more reading comprehension than understanding which was annoying. She does curve A LOT. But overall, decent class.

You can tell Prof. Fertuck is very knowledgeable about the subject but she's an incredibly boring lecturer as mentioned in other reviews. Exams are wordy and could be confusing but if you pay attention in class you will do well. Attendance, PollEv, and weekly quizzes are easy points and will bump your grade up. She will also curve the exam scores.
Literally the worst person at this university. Treats kids like 5 year olds. Avoid at all costs. Prayers up to all biochem majors forced to deal with her.

She does not care about students. She will not care about you. Is extremely uptight and is genuinely one of the most uncaring professors I've come across. Save yourself and do not take her if you want to keep your sanity intact.

I don't think I've every left this class without a headache. The sounds she makes are unbearable. Lectures are hard to get through because of the time she wastes and treats you like a child. She is condescending and talks down to you. I will never take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor treats you like you are in kindergarten through assigned seating and turn and talks. She tends to talk down to you and if she doesn't like you, you will know. The test are difficult, wordy and very specific. Her voice is excruciating so make sure you have Advil with you because you're going to need it. Also, she wastes time in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgable, but talks down to students so you feel like you're in kindergarten all over again. The gremlin voice is funny at first, but gets annoying VERY quickly. Exams are EXTREMELY nit-picky, require you to read a paragraph before you even get to the question, and were 18 pages (front and back) for 30 questions for reference. BEWARE

Professor Fertuck is one of the professors I would never take again. Her class was very difficult, and even asking for extra help felt pointless as she never explained things well to get a good grasp on them. She does not do a great job going over things that are important in depth for the exam. She wastes time during the lectures.

-talks to you like a child. Tests (30 mc questions) are not reflective of lecture AT ALL so theyre very difficult to study for. Office hours/ outside help are useless bc she simply repeats lectures rather than letting you ask questions. Luckily participation and assignment are easy 100s so thats a good 35% padding to your grade (youll need it)

Prof. Fertuck is one of the few, if not only professor that I will not take again. Although she is good at explaining concepts, she wastes a ton of time during lectures and does not go nearly in depth as what we were tested on. Furthermore, she had moments where she was a bit condescending to students who were needing help/asking questions.

Fertuck talks to the class like we are in elementary school. Has a big issue with earbuds and she pretends that she doesn't take attendance but she tracks who was in class everyday. Her lectures are boring and she wastes a ton of time going over only a few topics because its the way she is. She also micromanages the entire classroom, quite annoying

Fertuck is not a harsh grader and her exams are easy to pass. My only issue I had with this class was that it was so slow and impossible to pay attention in. She spoke to us like we were middle schoolers which made it really tough to listen. Other than that, the class is not horrible and she gives you a lot of opportunities to have an A

Very nit-picky with grading exams and will dock points for anything. The exams are very wordy, like other reviews said. The amount of homework is very reasonable. She's nice and somewhat understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class overall is pretty easy except for exams. They are wordy (paragraphs of background info for a few multiple choice) and very difficult to follow. Very broad info is taught but the exams can be kind of specific. She talks to you like your in kindergarten, but is pretty nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Paying attention in class and actually doing the work she recommends (doing hw, studying a reasonable amount for exams) can get you an A. The assignments are extremely reasonable, the lectures are well-thought-out, and her excitement is easy to pick up on if you just lean into it a little bit. You'll get Exactly what you put into this class.

I felt like I was in a kindergarten classroom. Attendance and showing enthusiasm during lessons are mandatory. Content taught in class is pretty broad, yet the tests are very specific and she will dock you points if you get the question right but don't answer with enough specificity. Some opportunity to make up easy marks with take home quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fertuck is the absolute worst professor I've ever had. Lectures mainly focus on broad stroke concepts but then the exams come around and she expects you to memorize the smallest details from her slides. The way she speaks too makes lectures hard to listen to. Also not even worth going to her for help, she just points you to tutors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She can be over enthusiastic and her lecture can be really slow sometimes. However, she almost always finishes what she planned for class and she makes things clear to understand. Her test can be tricky but her grading is fair overall. As long as you study and attend recitations, you will do fine.

Attendance is extremely mandatory. After 3 absences, you get points off of your grade. Tests make up 55/100 points. Honestly don't even know how she gets test info from her lectures. All other assignments are easy. Speaks to you like its kindergarten. Tests have really long drawn out answers which makes it confusing and wastes lots of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although she has some quirks, Fertuck is one of the best professors at Northeastern. Her best qualities are that she is a good lecturer and the class is designed in a way to motivate and help you learn. Her worst trait is she is bad at understanding and answering questions. Unlike other classes, I retained what I learned in it. Tutors are good too
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's really unfortunate that NEU won't hire more biochem professors because Fertuck is unbearable. Her exam questions are wordy and full of useless info that makes them hard to parse what she's actually asking for. Good luck to anyone taking this class, I suggest going to tutors and asking for past exams because she reuses 80%+ of past questions
Took this class in the summer - It was ROUGH. Exams are based about 70/30 on lecture material vs readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Fertuck! She makes the course material really easy to understand and is always willing to offer assistance or help to students. Her exams make you think, but they seem quite fair in their assessment of ones knowledge. I did not do as well as I would have liked in the class, but I felt the grade was deserving.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very easy class to get a good grade in, took her for toxicology biological inquiries and it was low effort but I still feel like I learned a good bit. Her personality can sometimes be grating and she sometimes talks to the class like we're her Pre-K class. But with that being my biggest complaint, I'd recommend taking the class
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel bad for everyone taking Biochemistry and have no choice but to take professor Fertuck. She is by far the worst professor I've ever had here at NU. She will trick you on exams!! But my advice to you is to study her ppt slides and read the book! You have no choice but to take her! I think it's time NU hire others Biochem professors! Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love Professor Fertuck and her passion for teaching biochemistry. It's a hard class and she makes you work for it but the exams are very fair and based completely on the lectures and slides. Attendance is absolutely mandatory and weekly quizzes and clicker participation factor into your grade. Overall, highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I honestly think Prof. Fertuck is great. Her exams are very hard but do-able if you study and go to tutoring as much as possible. Don't get me wrong, it's still hard to get even a B in exam, but hey if you do, you'll feel more proud (since its harder). Although tests are hard and questions sometimes confusing, i enjoyed biochem with prof Fertuck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you can, try to take biochem somewhere else. This professor gives impossible exams, and even if you know the material very well, it is extremely hard to have even a B as each exam is only 30 questions. She is very condescending and doesn't explain the material well. Her lectures are all over the place too. Tutoring will be your best friend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: For an intro class, her exams are far too difficult and she tries to trick you on purpose with her questions. Does "name practice" for students in her class to make you feel like she actually cares about learning who you are, but it's so she knows who's faking attendance with the lecture clicker questions. Exam grades solely determine course grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Fertuck for toxicology; it was a great choice. She comes off a little strong in the beginning of the semester, but by the end I really loved her, her teaching style, and the class overall. Quizzes every week that are easy and tests are As if you study. Highly recommend

While lectures were very dense and sometimes dry, the course was definitely doable. Professor Fertuck provides slides, highlights important readings, and is available for extra help after class. Though tests are difficult, and are only made up of 30 MC qs, putting in the work will yield good results.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Fertuck is an amazing person! She's the only prof who takes the effort to learn over 200 peoples names. she does talk alot but extremely approachable, sweet, and knowledgeable. is fair with the material and lecture ppts are amazing but lectures were long. really cared for students and wanted them to learn and love the subject. the tests hard
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: she tells you exactly what is on the exams and is always available if you have any questions. if look over the textbook before lectures and show up to class you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pr. Fertuck talks too much and doesn't really focus on the essentials of the lecture. Lectures are too long and not helpful at all.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is an unreasonable person who will not hear her students out. Exams are very difficult. Out of 150 students, only 2-3 will get perfect score on exams (exams are graded out of 30). There is no curve and only 2 exams and the final. Her lectures are unbearably boring. Spent way too much time on genetics review so must prepare yourself for MCAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a wonderful teacher who gives great feedback on the projects/papers you complete throughout the semester. The papers require a fair amount of work, but they are usually very rewarding and about a topic you enjoy learning about.

Dr Finn is so sweet! She heavily encouraged group work in class and sometimes we got to do some fun activities. She is also very kind, and will respond to emails outside the classroom. Her feedback was insightful, and helped me grow as a writer. Take her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sarah is one of the kindest, most caring humans I have ever met. If you can take any of her classes, do it!! I promise you will succeed, because thats what she wants from her students. It is an easy class, and she makes it really hard to do badly. Besides that, she really does care about her students, and their wellbeing. Amazing prof.
Professor Finn is very kind and gives good feedback on assignments. Decent amount of work, but graded fairly lightly. Would recommend this class.

Took 3307 with Professor Finn. Amazing instructor! Great class. Easy if you put in the work. It's graded by a few assignments, but easy to do well in them. The course is organized well and will be a breeze if you're participating and doing the assignments properly. Highly recommend!

I enjoy having 3315 with professor Finn. She's very helpful and encourages strong participation outside the classroom with student groups. Her activities were also fun and helpful to destress ourselves or improve on our writing.
I took ENGW3315 (Interdisciplinary Adv writing) with Prof Finn and she really helped me improve my writing skills. She is easily approachable and really wants you to do well.
She is so nice and caring. Very easy grader and clear. Does not give out a lot of work and wants all students to do well.

Prof Finn is the BEST writing professor!!!! She truly cares about her students and gave very helpful feedback on the projects. In an online setting, Professor Finn did whatever she could to keep the class engaged and organized fun community-building exercises for breakout rooms. I also liked the themes and genres that she picked for our 4 projects!
Best professor at NEU. A sweetheart.

Shes a bit boring and a 1 hour 40 min class really drags sometimes. But, shes super nice and wants to help even if the assignments seem contrived sometimes. Show up, look interested and put some effort into papers and youll get an A. A good break of a class, but dont take it looking to be inspired or really improve your writing.

The course is super easy you only have 4 projects along the semester and they're pretty easy. It tends to get kind of boring for 1 hour and 40 minutes but it's a pretty chill class that you can take as a breather in between a packed schedule. There's a lot of readings assigned but they're not really necessary. I didn't ready any and got an A.

Dr Sarah Finn is one of Northeastern's best professors for the first year writing course. Her choice of project topics along with her supportive and detailed personalized feedback really set her apart from other professors. WOULD definetly reccomend her to other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Sarah Finn is a really nice professor who cares about the work and also about the student. She really likes to teach and enjoys being with her students. She's nice about giving equal quantities of praise along with constructive input. Be prepared to have to think to get an A.
She's very helpful. The class is pretty boring but if you do your homework, it's an easy A.
She is very nice and always trying to help. Her classes can be boring but when comes to write your essay the lectures help a lot. she understands any situation you are going through.
Easy, small class. Gets to know each student personally. Crazy, but hilarious.
Great professors, makes challenging tests with fair curves and as long as you know what's going on an A is extremely feasible.

He was very accessible outside of class and willing to help you! He was also good at emphasizing concepts to remember for quizzes or tests and mistakes to not make. You can tell he really cares about students and curves exams heavily. A great teacher for accounting!

overall a challenging course but he is a good professor, but doesn't post completed slides (we fill them out in class) or handout answer keys which is annoying. homework will take you up to five hours to finish weekly. answer questions during tests, curve is greate(you need it)

I have greatly enjoyed this class, this semester and I manly owe it to Prof. Fitzgerald. You can tell he really wants you to learn. Very helpful in and outside of class. Lastly, he was able to do something I thought impossible: make accounting interesting. I highly recommend anything to take pick this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a great teacher, I would hard recommend him for ACCT1201. Also don't be afraid to ask him questions during the test, he's VERY helpful when you have a question or two.

Professor Fitzgerald is an amazing professor and person. He was always willing to help with any and all doubts, and genuinely cared about everyone in the class. Although accounting can be fairly boring, he tried his best to make it interesting by showing us real life examples.
He's a great man! I took him summer 2019 and he was really there for me when I had issues in the class. He cared about my mental health and did all he could towards my success. An amazing professor!

He's one of my favorite teachers in Northeastern. Listen in class, study the handouts, homework, and slides and you're good to go. Very caring and able to help outside office hours. You don't really need the textbook.

Always willing to help students during office hours or by appointment. He wants his students to do well and he will give you every opportunity to succeed as long as you are trying. Good lecture material and use of practice problems in class. The case study was super fun! Definitely one of my favorite teachers.

Amazing. helpful & encouraging. Sincerely wants students to succeed and is very helpful in office hours. You will have to put in effort but he will help you in every way he can. Would 110% recommend- especially if you're not naturally good at accounting or was kind of afraid of accounting like I was.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man wants everyone to get an A and is there to help you get one.  Awesome teacher, makes a boring topic interesting, and is an overall great man.

Accounting is a challenging course as a whole so I believe Brian Fitzgerald is one of the best professors for it. He is very patient with students, but you have to do your part as well to understand the topics. If you go to his lectures you do not have to read the book to understand.
This man is a legend. If you know what's good for you... take this class.

He is a very good professor, he would like to help everyone. His class is clearly and logistics, he would give many examples in the class help to understand. The exams are from the examples and hw. Only one final paper for group.

He is really hard working teacher, and really willing to help. But his class is dull, he only uses simple examples and example to teach. His homework is difficult, but definitely help. Sometimes the  test is beyond the ppt, so you kinda need to study by yourself. Take this class if you have acct base, or it will be gpa willer. BTW final is 30%.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was definitely challenging, but Prof Fitzgerald is such a genuinely good person and will do everything in his power to help you succeed. If you're struggling, definitely go to his office hours. He's clearly passionate about accounting & teaching! Tough course, but awesome professor!

Notes are very good, and his lectures are very clear. Gives a lot of quizzes, but if you do the work, you can get an A. Notes are clear and tests pretty much are from his practice examples and whatnot
He is a good professor, but tough grader  Tip : go to office hours!

He's a very nice professor. Explains everything in detail, always willing to help his students. You need to attend classes cuz he puts fragments in the slides that you should complete in class. His tests are quite long, you need to be a bit fast to complete them. Very nice person

He's great, so understanding, passionate, and knowledgeable. Has interesting hobbies and background from previous careers.The topics itself are interesting but the problem sets for homework / sometimes class lectures can feel repetitive. At the end of the day, walked away learning the key concepts. He is not a hard grader, just put in the work.

He's not THAT bad, chill class, I recommend taking him for this course instead of other profs. Unfortunately he could only be heard at the front of the room (good ASMR voice tho). Work turned in should be of quality but he is oddly nitpicky about small things like formatting and citations. Also, participate enough and go to class bc that is graded!

One small group project, one bigger group project, one research paper (counts as final), and ~4 discussion posts. Cares a lot about citations, gives randomly assigned groups for entire term, and grades group as a whole. Long lectures & open note midterm, willing to answer any questions. Def harder profs for this class, Flaherty's class wasn't bad.

Dr. Flaherty's lectures were honestly the most boring I've had in my life. The classes are 2.5hrs and spent three classes on how to cite sources down to the period (something any website can do for us). He's also so quiet you can only hear him if you sit in the front. This class shouldn't be called "healthcare system" but rather "insurance system".

I took his 1201 class at Northeastern. Looking back, I really should have appreciated his class more. It was an 8 am accounting class, so yeah it wasn't exactly the most thrilling course in the world, but he provided sufficient resources to succeed and prepared you well for exams. His class motivated me to pursue a degree in accounting.

Took this course about a year ago when it was his first semester teaching. While lectures were kind of reading off the slides, in-class activities were great. They were very practical as we used Excel. Exams aren't too hard, you just have to understand the reason rather than memorizing it. Group project was nice, and final was curved. Nice guy too

Loved this professor, great teacher, but do NOT skip class otherwise you are screwed. Getting behind = you're done. I got behind, and my A dropped to a B-. Funny guy, helps a lot if you ask for it, the final project and report are graded pretty lightly.

Flake is the best accounting professor at NEU. Attendance is mandatory for understanding and his lectures can be a little dry and long, but he gives a break during class. Grade is made up of two exams, homework, and four quizzes. Make sure to study for these using practice problems in Canvas. Great class and the final grade is curved at the end.

Despite it being his first semester teaching, Professor Flake is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. Although it is a lecture heavy class, he is available outside of class and is easy to reach via email.  The study guides for tests are very helpful, and if you show up and participate it is impossible to not do well in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best professor I have had at Northeastern. It was his first semester teaching but he was very organized, straightforward and accessible outside class. Responded to my emails within minutes. Also uses Excel which is great and very easy to understand. Overall great person and couldn't recommend him more.

For his first semester teaching, he did a really good job. While lectures can be a bit on the boring side, he does a a good job at simplifying topics and equations. He's very accessible for students in and outside of class. Overall, he was open to feedback and grew as a professor over the course of the semester.

Do not reccomend. Very apparent he lacks teaching experience, slides have typos, frequently misspeaks during lectures, overall unprepared. Class was confusing for learning accounting for first time. Seemed to dislike me reaching out for help, made me apprehensive to get feedback. Seems nice in general, but bad at teaching. Lectures are SO BORING!

Jared is the best prof I've had, it just sucks that the class was at 8 am which I feel hindered my learning. Accounting is generally a tough subject, and you need to put a lot of effort/practice in to be good. Do the extra practice, go to office hours, put the work in and you'll be fine. As long as the student puts the work in, you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring professor, he wants to see everyone succeed.  However, it is VERY evident that this is his first semester teaching, and it is quite often when is unable to answer students' questions. Very by the book so be prepared to attend class, very lecture-heavy, and the presentations are usually regurgitated information from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVE Jared Flake so much! Even though it's only his first semester of teaching, his lectures are so straightforward and pertain to what will be on his exams. He is so caring and wants to help everyone succeed and I thoroughly enjoy his class. His quizzes are all online with no lockdown browser and he provides so many resources to study

He got fired before the first semester even ended and isn't coming back next semester. If you have him as your prof you're better off not going to class and self teaching. His methods of teaching are bizarre and inefficient. I have learned nothing from taking his class but at least he didn't take attendance lol.
Professor Kacaku is just the right amount of funny and serious. You won't regret taking his class, but you might regret asking a dumb question in front of the class
