He's actually fantastic in office hours, but in class, he moves very quickly and he's not the best at communication. He doesn't take attendance or make much of an effort to interact with the students- just starts writing on the board. I took calc in high school and loved it, but this semester's been rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: great
easy grader

She doesn't give good or consistent feedback. She is extremely confusing and made it difficult to do well in an otherwise fairly simple class. As an introductory class, it is a shame, as the foundation that should have been built is underdeveloped. She is knowledgeable, but not the best teacher.
How can a level 1000 class be this hard? Prof is friendly but exams are unlike what we learned in class/ in homework. Need more practice problems with answers/ feedback/ support. class avg is a 69
the worse math teacher you will meet in college. she does not know how to teach.
Very good professor, smart, cares about students
too much beating around the bush, can't point what matters, inefficient.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is the second time I took Prof Morosan's course. I enjoyed it as much as the first time. Insurance and Risk Management is not an interesting topic by nature, but Prof. M. offered us concrete cases and explained the rationale behind the numerous insurance policies, which made things much easier for me. Besides, he is a very friendly person.

Professor Morosan's class is the best I've ever taken in Northeastern.  He has abundant working experience as an equity analyst, and he delivers financial knowledge and skills to students in a very effective way.  What impressed me more is his patience dealing with students' questions. Generally he spent at least half an hour on them after class.
He's a really cool guy and the assignments are creative enough that they don't feel like a chore.

Great professor. Has a specific sense of humor, very ironic and funny! Very "chilled" and pleasant class atmosphere. He tends to give a lot of worksheets in class and gives homework due every class, however most of the time we just go over it. Sometimes he'll decide to collect it. He is very laidback though, so I would definitely recommend him.

Flores is such a funny, light spirited, and  laid back professor. He really tries to make the class funny. The subject itself was hard for me, but he's willing to meet with you to make sure you get the material. He doesn't care about attendance. Never replies to emails. He hasn't given any grades back all semester, and only had like 2 assignments.

Sr. Flores es fantastico! I had so much fun taking Spanish with him, and only wish I could take another level with him! It was pretty casual, and he was always making jokes and although it was mostly in Spanish, there would be an occasional English explanation. Not very time consuming (BEWARE the service-learning project though-some like a 2nd job)
He is funny and all, but he failed to control the class. He has a potential to become a good professor, but when the classroom atmosphere feels like one in highschool, you are not a good instructor.
Very funny and entertaining, but gives no progress reports and is a very hard grader. Never answers emails.

I really enjoyed Professor Flores' class. He's funny and engaging, and I always looked forward to attending his class. However, there was a lot of homework and I feel like he didn't cover grammar, which is something I need to work on.

Spanish 1 was so much fun! It is one of the only classes I looked forward to going to every day.  We do a lot of talking so it is really helpful to feeling comfortable using the language, but it is always really fun.  Professor Flores is awesome!!!
Guy is great. Easy class (Spanish I), hilarious examples, easy going, and relaxed.  I actually enjoyed going to this summer class.

Fantastic professor.  Easy-going, fun to be around, overall nice guy.  I learned much, much more in this class than I expected to.  I had him for a summer semester, so things got a little bit rushed towards the end.  Other than that, my only complaint is that he doesn't teach Spanish 2.  I highly recommended.
funny yes, but i am surprised no one has mentioned his blatant sexism in class. ugh

Wonderful professor! Very approachable and engaging. Class is very fast-paced but the fun atmosphere makes it easier to learn difficult material. Not too much homework, no tests, mainly  class discussions and presentations. Take him!

Really nice guy and extremely funny but is a very tough grader. He does not have office hours and was not the most helpful. His class was fun but when it was time to take a test the class had no idea what the material was because he does not stay focused during class. Articles due every week and multiple essays throughout the course.

Awesome professor, very nice and very funny.  The material is as challenging as any other Spanish course but Prof. Flores is very good about answering any questions or helping you during office hours.  Overall, this was a very helpful and fun class.

He was the funniest foreign language teacher I've ever had. I looked forward to going to class just to see what he was going to pull out of the hat each day. He made the class easy to learn in. By far the best spanish class I've had so far! Very enjoyable.
Had him for spanish 2. Class was pretty easy. Really boring though.

The best professor ever!  He's soooooo funny and entertaining that I actually didn't dread speaking in class and making mistakes. He's very comforting. I was very flaky with the language, but I feel much more comfortable with his help.  If you can take his class, do it! He's absolutely great!  Not a day went by that I didn't laugh out loud.
Best professor at NU, by far. Made class so much fun, was actually enjoyable to go to. Tests can be a little hard, but he grades fairly easily. Preps you for them well though. Awesome guy!
One of the most engaging teachers I've ever had.  He made an 8 oclock class worthy of going to.  If you can take a class with him, DO IT!
Nice guy, but if you really want to learn something, go somewhere else. He is very entertaining, but my language skills have dissolved.
one of my favorite professors at northeastern. if you can take spanish with him, DEFINITELY do it. he's hilarious and i never dreaded going to his class.

He's very nice and the class is fairly easy but he's teaching techniques are horrible.  Spoke so much English in class...you can definitely get an A but don't think you'll really learn the language.  He's like a high school Spanish teacher...definitely a waste of my money and time.

I switched from a spanish class where the instuctor was SO intimidating that I didnt want to speak! He is by far my favorite prof, he makes you comfortable even when you make mistakes, is always joking and in a good mood, definately made this class much less painful than I thought!
Great guy.  I suck at Spanish, but he is pretty helpful.  Very funny, and makes the class feel like a small community.
Best teacher here, great guy, really funny
Nice, funny guy. I suck at foreign languages & he definitely went easy on me on my final grade. He'll keep you entertained for sure.
Great prof!! So nice and so funny, makes a fairly boring class quite enjoyable!!  If you have to take this class, def take it with him!

dude... this teacher is the coolest honduran you'll ever meet.  always cracking jokes in class.  and even though they are stupid you'll catch yourself laughin.  he's good people... northeastern is lucky to have him

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!! This guy is great. I've taken five years of Spanish and he's the first teacher who's actually taught me something. So nice and funny too, work isnt difficult at all. highly recommended!!

Great prof. and soo funny!  Not easiest for me since languages are harder than other classes for me but you will learn alot in this class.  There is a good amount of homework and stuff.  Best Spanish prof out of the 3 I had at NU.
He is an amazing teacher. I have taken soooo many years of Spanish and he was by far the best teacher I have ever had!!
Cool guy, cracks stupid jokes to try to get us to laugh, but he means well.  Ridiculously easy class.  If you have any history with spanish then god help you if you fail.

I was surprised to see such a low rating for professor Fleche. I really enjoyed class with her and found the in class discussions to be stimulating and educational. A lot of people seem to be down grading her because she's a feminist which is really quite a shame as not kind of cultural study can be taught divorced from feminism.

WORST Professor I have ever had. Ridiculously tough grader and will pick you up for things such as Split infinitives and comma splices. Unnecessary in a film class. She picks favourites and will use your opinionagainst you if it differs from hers. Unhelpful and useless comments on papers and then when asked about them, she still has nothing to say.

had her for Shakespeare, and I really enjoyed her. managed to make a 3.5 hour class on 16th cent plays fly by! she is a very nice woman, but expects a lot from her students, especially class participation. speak in her class a few times and she will like you! I never thought I would enjoy intro to shakespeare, but I really did :)
She is very helpfull! And kind! Se is very understanding!! The best professor I had here. She  should teach more classes...

Awesome..maybe not the class materials but the professor! She is great, she didn't share much of her personal life- was kind of in a distance. =( Was very helpful if we had questions regarding the class or regarding anything. Because of her, I loved the class!

Extreme liberal feminist and if she feels you do not agree with her that will reflect on your grades. Preached too much about Bush and never about what we are actually supposed to learn. Tried has an agenda that has nothing to do with english

ridicuously easy grader on papers and tests, I did almost none of the readings and I always got A's.  That aside, very boring class, and it doesn't seem like she really knows what she's doing.  She picks favorites and only allows one absence for the semester.

Awful, awful, awful. I'm a film student and I wanted to throw up coming to this class. Did not teach what Film and Text is supposed to be. Instead, it because a pro-Gay course (I'm gay, and I thought it was ridiculous and unnecessary to base any portion of this class on homosexual ideals.) I withdrew and got a "W". SHOULDNT BE TEACHING CIN. STUDIES

I thought she was nice and very understanding. She knew that we were all freshman and that her class was the LAST one that we wanted to take. She was a hard grader though. She was interesting to talk to and we had some interesting conversations in class.
Papers are graded a lot on opinion, and assignments arent alwats clear.  She brings up good points, and is helpful if you ask.  Somewhat tough grader.
Easy A if you know what you are writing and you should be talking to her about your paper 20X before you submit your final paper.

I was completely interested in this class BEFORE I had her as a teacher. I withdrew based on the fact that she did not want to hear what I had to say and thought my opinions were meaningless. She is very much a feminist and has solid views on how things should be. She picks her favorites in the beginning and detests anyone else. Horrible class.

If you blindly listen to what this woman has to say in class, you will come away thinking that all of film theory is about how women are objectified.  This is not a film theory class.  Rather, it is soley about feminism.  Get used to her preaching things like: "women are always seen as inferior to men...Blah blah blah."  BAD CLASS!

Bases class on her own personal politics. The class became a feminist theory course and she went out of her way to antagonize the male students, all three of them. Oftentimes her theories of female oppression are blatantly incorrect, more often a far stretch. Her French is execrable, also. NOT recommended.

duno if she teaches this class anymore, but mediocre at best. I'm not a writing/film/lit major so some of the stuff we did was awful. However, not a bad teacher by any means. She knows what shes talking about, but sometimes i was confused about what she wanted in a paper. She wants kids to do well. I got a good grade in the class with average work
strange teaching methods- topics of conversation were interesting but the overall structure of the class was lacking

Worst class EVER. A complete and utter waste of time and money. As an English major I have become accustomed to receiving high marks on papers, especially reflections, which are supposed to be YOUR personal interpretations of something. Apparently no one told this woman that cause she gave most of us check-minuses on everything.

I don't know what the hell is wrong with you people, she is an amazing professor. I not only learned but I actually enjoyed coming to class, I don't doubt that the reason she got a low score is people are too smallminded to listen to someone else's beliefs
if you put the effort in you'll understand the concepts.  she is a hard grader but she is nice in class.  as long as you can bring a valid point in class and back it up she will accept it.
Is nasty and tries to impose her political views on students. Is inflexible and close minded to others opinions. Learned NOTHING and would definitely NOT NOT NOT recommend.

We have a great Cinema studies department here which she shouldnt be a part of. She contradicts what I learned in other Cinema courses and pushes her own views on her students. I learned nothing and and angry for her wasting my time.

Horrid class teaches nothing. DOnt buy the book you wont ever need it. Thinks Shes interesting when shes really not. I don't care that your **** please stop telling us everyday. I dont think she has tenure which is a great thing. Hope she never gets it.
She teaches things that are not relevant to the class. She has beliefs that she tries to bring upon the class. They have nothing to do with what we are learning.

Completly irrelevant. Does not teach the material classes should cover.  Has her own elitist psuedo intellectual wannabe philospher viewpoints that have no connection to the classes she teaches.  Does not explain her expectations. I Learned NOTHING.
Fox is a pretty good professor for this class. They are really understandable and has a really lenient grading system along with the participation/attendance requirements.
Unreasonable grading. Ridiculous. Type of class if you end up having bad teammates, you cooked.

I never went to class and ended with an A+. She's super nice and everyone loves her. Her classes are either interesting lectures about games, playtesting (playing games), or making you go on a field trip to a museum! HIGHLY recommend taking her.
Awesome.

I absolutely loved Fox. They are by far one of the best professors I have ever had, and probably ever will have. Gets to know the students very well and genuinely cares. Graded mostly on effort so an easy A but they still push you to put your best into each project. All the projects were so fun and great portfolio pieces.

Fox was absolutely an amazing Professor, 100% recommend taking a class with them if the opportunity is there. Throughout the semester there were readings then lectures/discussions based on the readings. The readings were never too difficult and they were always understanding if other classes got in the way. They always gave amazing feedback too:)

Loved this class and this prof. Fox is a super dope and interesting person who grades very generously but also gives constructive and useful feedback. There was some reading early in the year but it was never mandatory to participate in class discussions. Soon you get into group projects, which can easily become valuable portfolio pieces.

He is an amazing professor! He tells real life stories and experiences in the field that we are covering. He states statistics, reads from a textbook, understanding with absences and missed homework, easy grader, engages with the class and never keeps the class for the full time. He is great and would DEFINITELY take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jamie is a great professor who is good at explaining statistics even to those of us who aren't considered "good at math." Very helpful and the workload was fair. Read the textbook, do practice questions and go to the recitation sessions and you will get a good grade.
Terrible. Just terrible experience. Northeastern should reconsider his job.
I have to agree, absolutely terrible.  His arrogance and condescension when answering students' questions prevented me from asking any questions.
Very Smart guy, terrible professor!!!
The absolute worst professor in CJ.  Arogant and vile.  If it's not his way, it's no way.

Interesting class, sometimes quite disturbing...his midterm and final are worth a lot so you can't afford to do poorly. His class seems easy but the test are hard..unless you pay attention to every little thing he says and read everything and memorize everything for the midterm then the final you should be all set.

Professor Fox was the best professor hands down I have had at Northeastern. He is well known in the world of criminal justice and every tad bit of info presented was useful and applicable in other classes I took. His test are hard but he is a tough grader who displays the phrase "college is not easyyyy". Overall a great class! Reccomend it to all!

Fox has a tendancy to be a bit self-indulgent.  Sometimes goes off on tangents either about himself or leftist political agenda's that have nothing to do w/the class, a bit annoying.  Go to the classes, every now and then he has you do summaries of his lecture, which are worth points.

Fox is an amazing professor. He's highly animated, funny, knowledgable, and well-known in the CJ world.  I LOVED this class. Every day was so interesting. I agree that his tests were hard (but fair), and each one was worth 20%. Just write everything you remember him saying about the topic. Read all of the material. Good luck!

This class was awesome.  Grading was based on 40% two exams, 40% two papers, 20% lecture summary, and forum participation.  I thought the grading was very fair, but I'm not sure how he graded other semesters.  It is true you need to be on point with your exam answers though.  Also depends on your TA, we got lucky. Material is by far though THE BEST
This class was amazing, and wicked hard.  class flew by, but the tests were impossible

Material is extrememly straight forward, but he makes tests beyond difficult. No amount of studying can get you a good grade. Also he says he scales grades and he doesn't. Unreachable, screwed up my GPA and a complete arrogant dick. Class is definitely not all that its hyped up to be
Cocky, arrogant, rude, condescending. Old Foxy is starting to believe his own press clippings.
Tough grader, in class he says it will weigh out at the end of the year to avoid the heat, it doesn't, low class averages, and very redundent... He will hurt your GPA
boring to sit through class. no break give during long lectures

the subject mater is interesting, but redundant (if you like gross stuff). very hard to get in touch with, doesn't return emails. tests are kinda vague and books are what he wrote, so it's like reading all over again...

Subject matter is easy, but professor is hard.  Exams were way off base, resulting in D averages.  Take him with caution:  class is interesting, but damaging to your GPA.  (Plus Fox is a bit of an ass)
awsoem subject..horrible cocky professor

This was one of the best CJ courses I have taken so far! Prof. Fox knows a lot about what he teaches The course was not the easiest, but every class was interesting and worth while. I wish he taught more classes!!
This class can be somewhat challenging. Prof Fox is a well known expert in this field.
The serial killers class was the highlight of my years at NU

Best class I ever took, Jamie Fox is a great professor. I waited untill my senior year to take this class and it was well worth it, if you have a good CJ background and enjoy serial killers, youll LOVE this class
Horrible teacher.  May hold a special chair in the dept, former dean of the college, and is called in to speak in Congress...but he is HORRIBLE

This class is not a fun elective nor is it easy. Only take this class if you're a music major. She gives out weekly quizzes and they don't correlate to the slides or material covered in class. Her lectures are informative but not engaging at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes + tests determine majority of your grade. The quizzes are 5 questions with written response, questions aren't covered on slides, and graded harsh. Midterm average was like a ~60 with NO CURVE. Go get your DD credit with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Jazz at NEU is no longer the easiest class in the world, but it's far more interesting now that she teaches it. has a firm grasp on the material, and handles a huge and complex topic tactfully. She's kinda weird but a good professor -- clearly gets uncomfortable talking about race, which is strange, since she has a phd in South African jazz lol

She teaches from her slides and audios from the textbook. Half the time her questions on her quizzes and exams are not even discussed from the slides. Very boring lecture and does not how to make all her students participate. AVOID if you want a fun elective. Seems to be a first-time teacher as her classes aren't very planned, which make it boring

I attended Northeastern because of their co-op program. Charles was one of my 1st professors and provided history, inspiration and support. 20 years later I still think of him. He taught me to write obituaries, that they were the most important things you'd ever write. This knowledge recently came in handy when I had to write my brother's obituary.

He's knowledgeable but others aren't lying when they say he'll host a 2-hour "discussion" where he's the only one talking. Taking him with hybrid online/offline was a godsend. 17 people went in person on the first day. 2 or 3 went regularly after the first two weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fountain will talk for the entire class with no lecture material. You almost have transcribe everything he says to begin to understand. There's no discussion. There's very little guidance with assignments and it feels like he's bothered answering my questions. Quizzes are hard and it's all from what he says in class. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's the guy kind of professor you either love or hate. To me, he's the worst college professor I've had so far. There is absolutely no discussion in his class. He just talks for an hour and a half. He's also just a pretty weird guy in general

I love Chuck!  I won't lie though, Interpreting the Days News with him was not my favorite class.  I felt like no matter how much of the news I read I was never prepared for his obscure quizzes.  History of Journalism with him was challenging but I definitely learned a lot and love his enthusiastic teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Will talk for the entire 1 hour, so do not zone out. There is a LOT of reading. Quizzes are hard, because there's a lot of material to study. To get any help from him you have to go to office hours, he doesn't respond to e-mail very quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chuck Fountain is one of the most enthusiastic and passionate professors I've ever had. He is very well-read and a great lecturer. Don't expect to get a word in during his classes though. He loves the sound of his own voice and will talk for the entire block of time with many ramblings and without taking a breath. Great professor though.

I love the professor. Enthusiastic and intelligent. The classes are discussion-based entirely, and there's no homework but 1 group project, 1 paper, a final, and A LOAD of pop quizzes on the daily news. Can't pass the class if you don't keep up with the news. Got me started on a bunch of subscriptions and gave me a good habit of reading newspapers.
One of the best classes I took at the School of Journalism!!!!!

Had him for Day's News and hist, and I love him. He expects you to be a good writer, but is willing to help any time. He is fairly Liberal, but respects all views so long as they are fully-formed and articulate, but don't be surprised if he challenges you to defend your statements in class! Don't skip class! Is a model professor and my favorite.

Amazing professor.  I had him in two courses. Day's News was a pleasure to attend.  History, his signature course, difficult because he only lectures; but is great at it; the quizes can be tough, and the final (4 take home questions/4 pages) took me 10 hours! But, he is always available, loves the material and loves teaching.  Absolutely recommend.

I had him for History of Media after our original professor had to drop out for the semester. He integrated us into his history of journalism class and did a great job working with the change. I would reccomend him in a heartbeat, and I'm planning on taking more of his classes in the future. Great guy, great professor!
Chuck is definitely my favorite prof. at this school. I've had him for three classes and he's the bomb.

I had Chuck for Day's News, easy class provided you read the Globe, TMZ, ESPN and WBZ's website for news quizzes. Papers are kinda random but fairly easy. He's very liberally biased and for a JRNL class that showed way too much. Very enthusiastic, brings energy that some professors half his age don't.

Chuck is a great professor. The class is not hard as long as you listen to him in class. You don't even have to read the books, if something is on the test and only in the book he'll tell you. But his tests consist mostly of what he says in lectures. Entertaining, extremely knowledgeable, and only wants you to do well. Best professor at NU yet.

Chuck is a nice guy, but this class is not the best. his lectures can be interesting, but his tests are horrible. only way to do well is to make flash cards of the people in lectures and in the readings and memorize everything they did. papers are not fun, but aren't horrible. the bright side is he is always in his office and is willing to help.

chuck's a smart guy and really knows what he's talking about. class is usually dull, but i've also had some of the most interesting discussions in it. random grader. attendance def mandatory. if youre not lazy and actually interested in the subject, id imagine itd be pretty easy to get an A.
Top two profs I've had at Northeastern. Take history of journalism! its so great!

one of the hardest classes i have ever taken. i studied my ass off and i still managed to do poorly on his tests. you must go to class and you must write down everything he says so you can memorize it for the tests. very cocky, interesting guy, horribly unfair and random grader.

A really fun class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you're pretty much screwed if you don't show up. In love with his subject, in love with hearing himself talk about it, but really tries to make the class interesting for those who may not find it so fascinating.

he is an awesome guy. could get very vain in lectures, he's very proud of all he's done. classes could be great or horribly boring. you have to study the newspaper daily like it's your life for the new's quizes. overall though, he really cares about journalism and his students though, so he knows what he's talking about.

He does not take attendance but if you do not go to class, you are in for a bad grade. Pay attention and TAKE NOTES. Everything he talks about in class will be on the test. He is really vague with assignments so ask a million questions or get help.

Chuck is a nice guy overall. the classes were hit or miss. Some were really boring and others were really heated discussions. News quizes get obnoxious, you HAVE to read the newspaper and watch the news to pass the class, theres no way around it. He knows a lot about the topic, so you do learn a lot.

Be carefull in this class. To pass, being in class is nearly a must. He covers almost everything in class, barely read the books. Take lots of notes and quote him. He loves to hear himself in the answers of tests. If you dont take good notes and dont have good attention, I would not take this class. Be prepared. He does talk down the students .

Professor Fountain is the reason I was excited about coming to NU. After I heard him speak at Welcome Day I couldn't wait to get here because he's so passionate about journalism and he really knows everything there is to know. He has a rep for being a tough grader but if you go to class and take detailed notes you'll be fine.

Not only does he talk down to his students, but he is threatened by intellect and would rather make you feel as though you're wrong, then correct his own mistakes. His teaching skills are under par and should consider a new career choice. I'm sure under all the condescending remarks, he's an intelligent, caring man.. But teaching is not his calling

Oh wow. Knows his stuff, but is the hardest grader I've ever had. Close to impossible to get A's on tests. Does make class interesting though, I'll give him that. But if you're looking for an easy A, or easy B for that matter, dont take this class.

An amazing teacher, and the best I've had so far at NU! He's very passionate about his subject, and really knows his stuff. He's always been available for help, and really respects his students. I'd recommend anyone- journalism major or not- to take his class.
Ohh Chuck. Very knowledgeable, easily excitable, knows his****. Very particular on tests. Dease class.

History of Journalism Teacher. Knows his stuff and makes the class very interesting, but he is a very hard grader. I have a 3.9 GPA and I am a 90's student. I got a 46 on my first test. You can answer the test questions right, but he wants what he thinks is important, not the real reason.

Chuck Fountain is more enthusiastic than any professor I've had at NU.  The passion he has for the subject and the delivery of his lecturing bring to life the topics being discussed.  He takes his work, as well as his students, very seriously.  He's extremely attentive to students' questions, in and out of the classroom, and he's always available.  Chuck has inspired me to pursue journalism in school and possibly as a career.

A great resource on the history of journalism, he's right at home teaching that class. I wish I remembered half of the things I learned in that class. In my limited experience, not the most personable guy thereafter.

Never a dull moment. Belts out what he wants to say, and I've never caught him saying things he's not an expert about. VERY, and I mean VERY!!!! knowledgable about what he talks about. Even though the class is one big lecture, he makes them the most interesting lectures one could possibly imagine.

Professor Fountain is not only a professor but an advisor for the School of Journalism, therefore he has had a lot of experience with dealing with students and helping them. His class is always interesting and his ways of teaching is amazing. He's very cle
Chuck Fountain is an awesome guy, and he has a totally sweet bow tie.

Oh man, Chuck Fountain. This guy knows his stuff, and is compelling, and is a spit-talker. Absolutely fascinating one-on-one. Sure, he likes the sound of his own voice, but at least he's got plenty of interesting stuff to say.

This man loves to hear himself talk.  Guys will get along great with him, girls not so much.  I don't want to go into print journalism anymore because of him, he killed the desire.  His ego is out of control, I counted down the days I had until no more fountain. If you are taking another journalism class at the time I would avoid him.

He is the man! I had him for HST/JRN and will in the future, but he's immediately a favorite of mine. I didn't use him much outside of class, but he was very accomodating. His HST class, he took what could have been a utterly boring class and made it very engrossing. TAKE HIM! Grades a bit tough.

Chuck is a great guy, once you get on his good side.  Come to class, stay awake and nod attentively when he looks at you.  Go to his office and talk about the 1903 Worlds Series or any deadball era baseball, this type of discussion will serve you well.  His sports writing class is incredible.
Very smart. Very very available for help, and that can't be understated. If you don't like him, it's probably cause he didn't like you.
Total ****.  Likes to hear himself talk.  Doesn't aknowledge students out of class.  Pompous jerk...and boring lectures
awsome
Great professor with a huge amount of knowledge! Is one of those prof who is willing to help you out as much as possible and makes himself available more than any prof. i have had here

You will not find a more knowlegeable, more well versed Journalism teacher at Northeastern.   He genuinly cares about the students, and will help you as much as possible.  The best overall journalism teacher at this school, no doubt about it.

He is a great speaker. He is very full of himself. He could probably spend a whole lecture talking about himself. He knows his journalism though. He knows what he wants in a student, he'll tell you. Do what he says and you'll do well.
He is a horrible teacher. Very boring and loves to talk about himself. I don't recommend taking any classes with him. He is rude and speaks down to almost all students.
Very smart; any journalism show take his history of journalism class if you want to have a clue in this business
A great speaker and he knows what he is talking about. He is haughty but he kept my intention in a class that could have been very boring.

Hated him at first. Can be very full of him self and boring. Also can be quite funny at times. Don't take History of Journalism with him but Sports Writing is good. Meet with him in his office... he likes that.
Tough but fair
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Charvet's tests and grading are tougher than average. Negative reviews probably from students not putting any effort and expecting to coast anyways. CLosed book and expects you to know most of the material. Fair teacher, knows a lot and uses real-life examples.
Worst professor ever!! Never take già class! Very hard-graded. Hates every international student
I was interested in Supply Chain before taking this class...Worst Professor I ever had! DO NOT TAKE HIM!

Worst Professor EVER! Doesn't want to give full credit (always finds some lame excuses to not give 100%), and the only way you can get a good grade is by memorizing his incredibly boring slides. Quizzes are hard and final exam is comprehensive. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!

If you expect an easy A, don't take this class. Don't expect to get 100% for particiation just by being in the class. My experience have been great with Prof. Charvet. His class actually prepared me for the real world. When you get out of school, don't expect much hand holding by your managers.
Hard hard hard class. Hard grader, boring and way too much HW. So much reading every day and crazy about participation. Got D for participation for attend every class, and speak out once per class.

Worst professor in the supply chain dept.  takes the subject of transportation and makes it even more unbearable.  assigns way too much reading for each class and online book is difficult to read.  professor simply does not know how to teach effectively.  Slides are confusing and tests are hard.  Class is much harder than it should be.
I was very interested in Supplychain management before I took this class. He should learn how to teach.

His tests are extremely difficult.  Assigned a simulation to do every week, before he taught us the principles behind it.  Does not speak clear and is very hard to understand.  Must read and try very hard to do well in the class.

I'm writing this for the capstone. This course is so difficult as a capstone, the last semester of college. He makes you write 3 FULL paragraphs for every discussion with in-text citations and a bibliography. He also gives you a lot of feedback, where he expects you to implement everything he says. The work never ends, even after the last class...

This professor is very reading-heavy. There is a lot of reading and extensive research, involving around 20-50 pages of reading per week. There are also numerous other requirements, such as discussion boards where you are expected to submit three full-length paragraphs with citations and incorporate three readings every week.

For my entire life as a student, this is THE WORST class I've ever taken in my life. The number of readings he assigns every week is ridiculous, and the video length is about an hour or more each. Discussion work each week will definitely make you go insane. If you want a life, don't take this class.

Truly the worst course I have ever taken. Endless material to read, papers to write... the workload is comical. On top of this, your assignments are graded weeks later, without a rubric, so expect arbitrary numbers like 3.72/5. You are expected to dedicate your life to this class while receiving little to no effort from the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: please dont take this class if you want to have a life
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Never ending discussions boards each of which require 5+ paragraphs of 8 sentences each PLUS constantly responding to his and other comments. That is on a "light" week. The discussion for the week never ends. Very very tough grader and does not provide feedback. Was denied documented accommodations for canvas quizzes and he did not care. AVOID!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gives feedback one or 2 months after you submitted your assignment and tells you why you have received this grade. Terrible professor and gives endless homework. I am taking this class to fulfill my electives requirements and I spend more hours on this course than my other courses (btw I am EE major)

The way the course is structured makes it so students aren't able to see various viewpoints on subjects. You're not allowed to use outside sources on assignments, only the readings he provides. Not to mention the class is almost entirely discussion boards  which are 8 paragraphs per week. He acts like the world revolves around his class schedule.

Took this history online elective as a biochemistry major to fulfill my NUPath and it is horrible to say the least. I am currently enrolled in this and I do more work in this class than all my 5 other classes combined. He grades with random decimal points (4.68/5)? He acts like everyone's life revolves around this course. Extremely time-consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very intensive reading and writing. Weekly HW requiring 6-7 paragraphs minimum, plus source. 4 sentence minimum peer response, 3 paragraph minimum response to his question comment. No rubric for grading or anything. Canvas is not very organized. Requires a lot of time for this course. Due dates are not specified on Canvas but on Syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very contradicting due dates. Syllabus has one date and Canvas has another. Hours of documentaries and loads of reading material for multiple parts to a questions. When have to spend HOURS writing discussion questions. Materials are not the most organized. No rubric for grading, all based on his mood ig. Tests are just harder DQs. Do not recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor at NU GSIR. Weekly discussions continue beyond Sun, burdening students with last-minute questions on Mon, impacting other class preparations. Grades harshly but doesn't give feedback, unlike other profs. No concrete scoring rubric either. Hypocritically, he emphasizes error-free writing, but has made typos himself almost every week.

Professor Fraunholtz is knowledgeable about the topic and provides many good resources on the topic. He assigns a heavy workload, leaving little room for balance with other courses. He didn't provide feedback until the midterm. The final had contradicting information in the rubric and it is very difficult to all of the goals he expects to see.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: You'll be lucky to receive any specific feedback from the thousands of words you'll write/week. No rubric for grading so expect arbitrary numbers. Expects countless hours of reading, video-watching, and writing every week in return for almost no effort on his end. Don't take this as an easy online elective. Be warned: 5k word/wk midterm AND final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: gives too much work and seems to not understand that a person can have a life outside of his class. not very helpful and confusing most of the time. his class seems like it is designed for you to fail and have a bad time. 0/10 would not take again. also like literally no one has said that they would take his classes again and he still sucks lol.

The amount of reading and video material assigned is absurd. Grading in unclear, he assigns grades like 3.62/4 on homework. Two decimal points? More like random objectified grading based on arbitrary factors. This class is more work than all of my other classes combined. The information is not presented in a unique way which makes it very dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took a class on campus as well as went on dialogue with him! He's very insensitive and is often inappropriate in speech. He is a tough grader and does not understand that students have a life outside HIST 2211!   Not a fair grader, let alone easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Personally I found the class boring as he seemed to talk at us a lot with disjointed stories with multiple people and dates. There is a lot of extra info so I found it very helpful to rely mainly on what the TA's specifically said was important. The readings were important but can be skimmed. He is a nice professor but needs to work on lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE THIS. He knows a lot, don't get me wrong. But knowledge is only half the heart of teaching. He cannot communicate effectively, made a joke out of most question regarding the essay he assigns. If you've already done a Cold War class, don't do this. Never mind, don't do this regardless. The TA is your friend, the teacher will confuse you.

Class isn't difficult, with 20% participation credit it is difficult to get a clear grasp of how you're doing in the class. The midterm and finals are essays, but only got the midterm back 1 week before the final prompt , so you're not given a lot of time to understand what you did wrong. His lectures seem unimportant, he rambles and presentations.

Fraunholtz is not the type of professor you want if you're looking for an easy A. I worked my butt off every single week and managed to read every single assigned reading just on time--it was very tough. He assigned four or five books in the accelerated summer course which is CRAZY! That being said, I learned a lot and enjoyed the course immensely.

Took his class online. A ton of reading and all 5(?) of the books are necessary. Weekly discussions need quotations from the books and need to be very detailed (extremely difficult to get an A on these). Multiple sets of directions for the class papers with contradicting instructions, (8 pages vs 12 pages, ect.) Not terrible but not great.

He is a great professor, very approachable and explains everything very clear. A lot of group work, a lot of work in general but he can always can explain things again also his TA's very nice. He uses PowerPoint, documentary and books so we will have a lot of information to work on. he is not a super tough grader but u should work hard

Hard class. Tons of information. Lots of reading and group projects. But in the end, you learn A LOT. You learn to look at history more analytically. Lots of essays, but he isn't a super tough grader. Take this class if you're willing to learn, put in the effort, and be a good group member. Don't take it if you want an easy A.

I really enjoyed this class and the professor that taught it. I learned more than any class I have taken at Northeastern. Lectures were engaging. All this aside, there definitely was a LOT of work. Be prepared for that when you walk in on the first day: essay tests, 12 page papers, group projects, and lots of required reading.

I thought he was fine. Tests aren't bad as long as you go to lectures and study. One 12 page paper, but there's plenty of information to write about and you get to choose from different topics. Lectures are broken up with documents and films. I would not say get out immediately... but you should buy the books and be willing to try.

Prof. Fraunhotlz is fairly rude to students and not very open to other points of view, but his class wasn't terrible.  He broke up the class with videos and documents so that it wasn't just solid lecture.  He was a fair grader and I thought the amount of reading was manageable.

He is the worst teacher I have ever had at Northeastern. He sits up in the front of class and reads off a timeline. He is rude and mean. He makes everyone do group presentations on the readings so that he doesn't have to teach. He assigns a stupid 12 page paper and tells you that you need 5 main points 5-7 sentences each main point, doesn't add up.

The WORST class I've had at Northeastern so far! MORE READING THAN YOU CAN HANDLE; from a ton of books which cost $$$! RIDICULOUS 12 page papers for only a 200 level course! His lectures are IMPOSSIBLE to take notes on, yet alone stay awake! Exams are all essays. I feel so bad for you if you get him for this class. DO NOT TAKE! REPEAT! DO NOT TAKE!

The hardest professor at Northeastern! Hundred page readings every night and weekly presentations! Handouts in class are extremely important for the midterm but the final is take home (two 5 page essays). Lectures are boring and is an extremely tough grader! DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! EVER!
DO NOT TAKE HIM. He is one of the meanest teachers you'll have. He is unnapproachable, makes students give presentations every friday and is an impossible grader. STAY AWAY

Professor Fraunholtz is rude to his students and, even when the entire class is at a loss, continues to lecture and confuse everyone. Go to class, because he passes out about 8 handouts a day that you WILL be tested on. And don't plan on leaving class when it ends - he thinks its kosher to keep lecturing 10+ min. after class has ended. HORRIBLE!!!!

A TON of reading. The 2x a week was pretty rough as the class was an hour and a half long. The material can be really interesting, but his voice definitely gets old after the first hour.  In essence, it was boring.

If you take any HST class make sure it's 3x/wk & not 2 (way too long otherwise). Very boring. Way too many reading assignments-2 semester's worth for 1. Lots of writing assignments. Changed the final last minute to several papers due at the end of the semester - major ****. Probably a nice guy, but not a great professor.

extremely boring. very monotone, claims to not lecture that often at the beginning of the semester, but that is all the class is. take good notes, pay attention to the movies (sometimes), and do all the required readings. you will not have fun in his class. thats almost a certainty.
Lectures could be a little boring but the material was pretty interesting, GO TO CLASS, tests were fair read the books and try to pay attention and you will be fine

I'll give him a break as he covered a lot of material...we had 5 books to read (!) plus an $100 textbook which was kind of annoying as this is a low level course.  Class was very boring at times, however film clips are used to augment the readings and lectures so that helps.  No matter what, GO TO CLASS.  You will be screwed if you don't.

Very boring and monotonous speaker and meticulus test grader. Lots of required reading but the tests prety much covered lecture material--show up to class or you're screwed. The only thing that kept me going in each class was knowing that we'd get to watch a movie for the last 30 min. I suggest dropping a class with him as fast as you can.
I enjoyed learning History from Prof Fraunholtz this semester and his grading of assignments has been reasonable. Thank you!

At first you think the lectures are interesting with his different views on the subject, but as the semester continues, his monotonus voices starts to make you very tired. Grade all depends on your recitation teacher. make sure to read all material, becasue tests are not really over the lecture material.
hes a very good teacher...intelligent, coherent, interesting, and knows alot about the subject matter.  Manages to incorporate movie clips well into the class.  Good teacher
A horrible teaching style. Very disorganized. Ran class around in circles not following any type of chronological order. Tests were poorly constructed with no clarity. Don't take this class.

One of the best online instructors I have had. He also did a great job of reigning in students drifting from the subject material and bantering on with personal opinions. Great at responding to questions, sticks with online syllabus and grading policy, very knowledgeable, and always great feedback.

very boring teacher, but if u do the work and study hard you will pass. he probably says 'essentially' like 100 times during a class - VERY annoying habit. and when he writes on the board, he uses up the whole thing, but u cant understand a word. boring, but u learn a lot
if u got his class, drop it rite away..u will be bored and would want to skip it all the time, therefore u will fail. he is the worst teacher...

Top 3 worst teachers i have ever had. He speaks in monotone the entire class time while you sit and take notes. You have to go to all classes or else you'll be screwed on the test because they are all essay. theres no hw, but trust me, drop this class.
The worst teacher I ever had in my life.  I strongly suggest you to drop this course. It is very boring.
No Comments

Really nice professor, grades leniently and explains concepts in class well. I came in with no knowledge of audio editors or DAWs and learned a lot about them in this class. The class is an easy A if you work a bit and have interest in what you're learning. Attendance = mandatory though, you can only miss 1 class before a % reduction in your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Everybody I know who is in music tech has taken a class with him and loves him. He is a great lecturer and I learned so much in the class. He was also willing to help me outside of class with personal projects and questions I had. Overall a great professor, can't recommend enough.

Professor Frengel is the goat. Came into this class with almost 0 knowledge of music technology and the software, and I learned so much in this class. He clearly is passionate about what he teaches, and it shows in his lectures. Do the work, and communicate with him, and you'll do well.

I have learned SO MUCH in his class, and a lot of the stuff I have learned in this class I have started implementing in my own music creation! Professor Frengel is very smart and patient, he is always enthusiastic to teach and you can tell he has a genuine passion for music technology. Make sure to pay attention closely in lectures though.
Really nice professor - Gives many feedback, and understands student's personal situation.
Very nice professor, offers a lot of help and feedback.

This professor is an Angel. I missed so much class and so many projects because of personal issues and he was so incredibly understanding. Theres NO WAY I should have passed but he let me and I will never not be grateful. Awesome guy.

Had Mike for Intro to Music Technology. I wasn't very good at the material as I was new to much of it, but he took that into account and made sure I was comfortable with what I was learning. Very respectful and knowledgeable

I had this professor for Music Theory 1 at 8am when I was a Freshman.  He's really cute! Incredibly smart!  Helpful!  I had a rough time going to an 8am 3 days a week, but he made it interesting.  He knows that some people get theory and some people don't. So he's there to help.  I've been looking to take another class with him!

Frengel is a cool guy. Not a great 8 a.m. class, I don't know how he's so energetic then. Teaches the material well and if you do the workbook stuff you'll do fine in the class. Considering his knowledge is so far beyond the class curriculum he does a good job simplifying it.
Just do the homework and the group project of coding the robot and you're good, might take a bit of work but not hard
Tells some jokes and gives homework but no tests really just group projects that count for a lot of your grade.

Freeman teaches in an interesting way. The workload was pretty average but she didn't truly prepare you to the fullest for quizzes. The group project was hit or miss depending on who you got but as long as you did your work it was an easy A

Professor Freeman wants her students to succeed. She is very clear in explaining the course material, and she posts recordings and the lecture slides from each class. She creates a very open atmosphere to ask questions, and I wish she could be my professor next semester. If you do the homework she gives, you will get an A in her class.

Professor Freeman is truly a wonderful woman. She cares about all of her students and takes the time to help everyone both personally and academically. Her class is not necessarily challenging but can be a lot of work at times but provides a great introduction to engineering for freshman students.

Prof. Freeman is a little heavy on meditation and joke-telling activities, at the expense of using class time to learn what is going to be on the homework. In addition, the textbook I spent $100 on was basically never used/only used for busy work. She is a fairly nice woman, however.

If I could take every class with Professor Freeman, I would. Take her service-learning section of cornerstone. She teaches well and isn't too anal about the details as long as it shows that you put in effort. I love seeing her around campus to this day, and she really cares about each student.
Love her, she is amazing

Prof Freeman is awesome with first year students and does a great job teaching. She's a pretty easy grader with the group project stuff as long as you put in the effort. There were A LOT of assignments but she was always willing to help. I definitely recommend her office hours. She really made a difference during my first year at NEU.
Professor Freeman is an amazing teacher. She teaches her course very clearly and makes complex topics seem easy. Cornerstone II with her is a fun class and I would take it again with her if I could.

Professor Freeman is an amazing teacher for Cornerstone of Engineering I. She is very excited about the class and teaches concepts in a very clear way. She is also very accessible outside of class and can help out on whatever you need. If you go to class and do all of the assignments on time, you'll get a very good grade.

Prof Freeman is a very nice person. As a freshman being thrown into the deep waters of first year engineering her class can be daunting but you will survive if you stay on top of the constant homework (don't forget to do the Tophat). Get reading to have a ton of paper homework to keep track of. You will pass if you pay attention and do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's a great Professor and a real gem. So much enthusiasm!

Prof. Freeman is a great teacher, she will always help when needed and her exams are extremely easy for the exception of the final exam that is a little tougher. If you go to class and do your homework you can get an A.

Awesome teacher, especially for first year engineering students. I took the cornerstones robotics class and it was really fun. She's pretty lenientunderstanding with due dates and grades, but you do have a fair amount of homework. Also, worked in a group a lot. Overall great class, would definitely take again.

Professor Freeman used to work as an Industrial Engineer and she displays the passion for engineering in her classes. She is very entertaining in class and enjoys telling stories from her life that most of the time relate to the subject matter. If you respect her and the class then she will respect you back.
She loves her students. Extremely helpful. She listens to students and constantly takes the feedback & modifies teaching methods / work load accordingly. A rare quality in a professor.
Super Enthusiastic, gives a lot of work but is a relatively easy grader. Her exams are long but if you study you will be fine. Really friendly and loves her students, wants you to succeed.

Unbelievably enthusiastic and energetic; obviously loves her job. Very nice to all the students. The class is usually interesting, and the projects are valuable. There is one "major design project" that culminates in a ~50 page report, but you spend all year working on it in parts so that it's manageable.

very funny, nice, helpful, and enthusiastic teacher. she made class fun, although notes can get boring once in awhile as with any class. She is very fair and lenient with grading, although she will take her time getting it back to you.

Enthusiastic professor, gives a lot of effort. Doesn't seem to know the material very well. Uses powerpoints every class which gets extremely boring and hard to follow. But, she's very helpful and a pretty easy grader. Take her if you get the chance.
she is so bad in teaching this class. i had to learn the stuff from the book. her exams are long. try to avid her

I LOVE Prof. Freeman! I had her for Engineering Problem Solving, and never knew anything about programming. She opened up that world and made all her students interested. She has a rare ability to make inspire genuine enthusiasm. I nominated her for Professor of the Year at Northeastern.

Excellent teacher. very engaging and hands on which helps in learning. For midterm and final just read the case studies the day before and do all of autocad and projects on time to get on her good side (which isnt hard) Very helpful and is very understanding. If you can get her for ANY class i would recommend it
Very nice and helpful

Really engaging professor.  Both knowledgeable and enthusiastic in her subject.  Her projects are pretty easy (even the final), the hardest part is dealing with some of the partners you get for group projects (she won't let you change them even if they stop attending classes).  Tests are relatively easy, just memorization and math.

Very helpful and available online or in her office on a regular basis. Quizzes can be tricky, but the programming assignments are interesting and very helpful in reinforcing the material. Had no programming experience going into this class and did fine.

This was the second class that I had Freeman and I really enjoyed it. She is a very nice person as long as you show some effort and show up to her office hours once or twice. The class is only hard if you put no effort into it otherwise she is not afraid to give out an A to those that deserve it.
Shes a great teacher for a rather difficult subject
Shes a horrible programing teacher. And fakes niceness.

Freeman was my favorite professor. She is really nice and the class is pretty interesting, although it ends up being a lot of work. She grades really fair though and her class seems to be easier than some of the others based on what I've heard from other people who had different professors.

One of the best professors I've had. She sounds patronizing at times, but she's very interactive and serious about Industrial Engineering. She gives out her AIM sn and is willing to help with everything and anything. Textbook is only used for homework, and a couple of times in class. Exams are easy but very, very long. More time would be nice. A+
Best Professor I every had.
Hands down, best professor i have ever had. Very helpful, loves her job and is good at it.
Good teacher, but would be even better if she didn't use baby talk all the time

an awesome teacher who obviously cares a lot about her students.  definitely makes the work (relatively) fun and is extremely approachable.  she is perfect for incoming freshman (and in my case transfer) students uneasy about the new major.
No Comments
I took this class winter of 2003 (Excel class). It was self explanatory but it was more so cuz she was crystal clear. Seems like a really nice person too.
She's very approachable... If you have a problem, she'll help out... She's good like that.
I was her TA for some lab. Honestly I have never seen a more motivating teacher. The students adored her.
by far one of my best teachers.

Freeman is a great professor.  She gives a decent amount of work, but is always clear on what she wants (i.e. hands out rubrics, outlines).  Her lectures are animated and well organized.  Take her if you can.
good teacher.. very animated.  she wants her students to do well.  gives a good outline of the work and when it is due and is always organized.
Shes one of the best teachers ive had. helpful, kind, personable, understanding, knows and conveys material well. has a son who goes to NU so she knows how things are. Try to get into her classes
awesome teacher, explained stuff well... as long as you do the work youre golden
awesome professor...nice to talk to, gives good advice, made 8:00 classes bearable.
All I can say is run as fast, and as soon as possible.  DANGER
she owns!
great teacher, a lot of energy, do the work and you will do well, she's really nice
Very nice woman.  Good teacher.  Fun Class
nice, upbeat, makes class fun
Good teacher, helpful also. one of the best teachers i've ever seen.
nice.  good teacher for first year students.  Just hard enough on students without being harsh
Pleasant at first, picky as hell in the end. Beware: she's not as happy as she seems. More helpful than most computer programming teachers
Best teacher ever
No Comments
No Comments

I absolutely love Dr. McSherry. Attendance is important and you need to try, but if you do, she will respect you and grade you fairly. She puts a lot of effort into making her class interesting and inclusive. If you put in the work, she is flexible and will work with you if you need help. This is my second class with her and I would take her again!

she picks and chooses what she wants and grades the most random things. will assign things she doesn't know how to do. Had us working like dogs with not even a second to breathe or to have a break. So many group projects, caused drama. She is also just kind of mean
Solid professor- organized, knowledgeable, and visibly passionate about fashion/costume. Expects good effort from her students, rightfully so. Would take another class just to have McSherry again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great class content, but absolutely nonsensical grading and absurdly strict teaching. It's impossible to get an A on any assignment, and the professor won't explain why. Prof is not understanding when it comes to any student issues, and partial credit doesn't exist. Would be an amazing class with a kinder professor.

She is a severe stickler to deadlines. If you don't show up in class with your project (even if you simply forgot to bring it in) then you automatically get a D. No negotiations. She also assigns a lot of homework/art projects. The class itself was very hands-on and abstract. Some of the projects seem completely irrelevant to theater.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: i took this class thinking it would be a piece of cake and i was wrong. There is so much memorization! and i spent the first month focusing on the book and it turns out all the answers are in the slides. She was extremely understanding and gave me extra credit after i talked to her and it brought my grade up to a C from an F in the last month!

wish i didnt have to take fashion, but i did. Thought this would be an easy A, but you actually have to study for tests. Tests are pretty straight forward, just have to know the material. Power points are always posted on line and pretty much contain the majority of her lecture's content, so skipping a class isnt the end of the world

I LOVE Professor McSherry! I took her for two classes and wish I could take another one. She gives out a good amount of extra credit and grades fairly easily. On top of that she's an incredibly nice woman! But make sure you go to class!

EXTREMELY BORING CLASS, but she explains the material well. Read a chapter or two a week (20 pages each, more or less) with a quiz after every 2-3. One presentation on a fashion designer that compares historical fashion to more modern types. Attendance mandatory. Mostly rote memorization, try to avoid this class just because it's so boring.
Great teacher! Always very positive and helpful, and is a great designer. The Best!

Wonderful person, but class not for all. She does all she can to accommodate, some concepts tough for non-theater majors, especially for engineer minded folks. Lots of art, abstract design ideas. Need to be EMOTIONAL in projects. Very good grader, second chance policy. Class requires spending $(50 - 150). Can b fun, NU productions are great!
I don't know how I passed this class with a B-. She must have felt bad for me. She's very passionate about what she does.  She's ALWAYS smiling and willing to help.
Love Frances! So sweet and an incredibly helpful teacher/person! Take her classes if you have the option!

AWESOME professor and designer.  Learned an incredible amount in all classes I took with her.  Always easygoing, fun, clear, and offers lots of help when needed.  I suggest taking as many classes as possible with her.. probably my favorite prof at NU.
One of the best theatre profs. She knows her design, IS a great practicing designer, and really strives to make sure her students are understanding everything. Take EVERYTHING you can with her.
Frances is an amazing teacher and a great person in general. She's really interested in making sure you understand what you're doing. She definately knows her stuff.
Wicked nice and super helpful. She is also an amazing designer. Recommend for any class.
Avoid this professor.

I took Prof Friar's online STRT 6220 class. Well, his name was on it, the TA's did all of the heavy lifting,  I never met the man.  Even when I emailed, the TAs were the go-between. He would briefly mention a topic, no required or recommended reading, then a major paper would be due on the subject, so be prepared for a lot of independent learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor ignores his own rubrics and assignment rules and makes up grades on the spot depending on how much he liked you. Might as well throw a dart on a dartboard. If you put in a tiny bit of work you'll probably do fine, but you won't learn anything.

Dont even try,this guy was born a **** and always has been.I submitted my assignments a few days late and he didnt check it till the end of the semester and gave partial credit for not submitting on time.On top of that attendance is mandatory and participation being 30% of the total grade.Would absolutely not recommend.

Attendance and participation can make or break your grade, and participation is based purely on how he feels about you. If he doesn't feel like he talks to you for the entire class, he will take a ton of off for participation. Other than that, grading is fair. Midterm, group project, and final paper are easy. Homework is a bit annoying at first.

Prof Friar knows his stuff, but is not good at specifying his expectations for assignments, but usually gives feedback. His lectures are dry. Participation and attendance are a huge part of your grade. He offers some extra credit too. Grading is definitely subjective, though. Some readings, assignments, a group project, midterm, and a final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Friar is a real gem. This course will help you a lot in the long run, whether you wish to become an entrepreneur or not. You do not need to have prior knowledge - everything will be taught. His grading criteria is based on the syllabus and the course (online due to covid-19) is asynchronous but there are zoom meetings held from time to time.

Prof Friar is fantastic. His lectures are very interesting and even if you don't know anything about entrepreneurship, you will learn so much in his class. My favorite class I've taken at NU by miles.

A good professor with a huge amount of real world entrepreneurship experience. Quite fair with grading, willing to help. A solid teacher/course that will introduce and make you better at entrepreneurship even if you are a complete zero, interesting to listen to the lectures.

This a  classes where you will learn alot from the lectures but not have to do any outside additional hw/busy work. He is an easy grader. He teaches really well and has a ton of real world experience and is also really chill. Greatest entrepreneurship professor I have had. Too bad ENTR1201 doesn't fullfill any business reqs

Prof. Friar is the best professor I have ever had.  It is not only because he is a great professor but also his incredible personality. He always tries to build your confidence and have a lot of patience on you. He is warm, trustful, open-minded, charming, and wise.

Incredible professor. Just the smartest, nicest guy you'll ever meet. No textbook for the class but he expects you to ask questions and engage with him. Provided you keep up with the HW he assigns and read the cases, you'll find the course simple enough. Took away so much from this class. Cannot recommend it enough!
great and essay course!

This guy is awesome! Very laid-back teaching style. He's the dean of the department and knows his stuff- really experienced. This was a fun class with minimal work. Take it, its a good class and he's a good guy.

Best class / prof. in my college career. You will learn a lot from this man. He is not only brilliant but also a great teacher who is interested in his students. Grading is tough but reasonable. He does not give out A's. His lectures are not dry. They will hold your attention.

Grading is EXTREMELY subjective and throughout the class, he never gave anything more than a 88, no matter how hard you try and how much you ask him for help. Decent enough guy, but make sure you're on a sports team or else he will ignore you. I wouldn't recommend and will avoid in the future.
classroom participation is 40% of the grade. one midterm and a series of smaller papers leading to one final paper
Hands-down best class I've ever taken. If I would have taken this in the beginning of college i probably wouldn't still be here. seriously amazing class. (im an econ major)

Professor Friar is a very easy going guy with a great sense of humor. I have the suspicion he is a rich man but does not come off that way, he is really down to earth. Knows the material very well and explains things very clearly. Not a lot of workload in this class and it is pretty interesting. I definitely recommend it Friar is awesome.
He was one of the greatest professors I've ever had.  If I hadn't transfered from NU, I would have tried to sign up for every class he taught.
I had both Meyers and Friar.  Meyers is the best teacher I've ever had.  I found Friar to be a little more dry, but he is a hillarious guy!

This class was taught by both Meyers and Friar.  Meyers was hands down the best teacher I've ever had, but Friar was good too.  He is a lot smarter than he makes himself out to be, but you can't go wrong taking him.

Nice guy but some of the lectures were boring and a little drawn out at times.  There were some interesting speakers though.  This class wont teach you how to get rich! but will teach you the different types of small business and the challenges you will face

Definitely passionate about the subject but expects too much from students. 
Very all over the place with lectures and will shame you if you don't know something when it's literally his job to teach it to you. Tough grader but was nice enough to give us the chance to makeup points we missed from past exams with repeat questions.
He's an engaging lecturer but kinda all over the place with slides and the tests are hard. He is really confrontational during class and will tell students that they aren't doing enough.

This professor will tank your gpa, avoid at all costs. For both midterms the class average was a 60, and no curve was added. He is very passionate about the industry, but is a horrible teacher. His slides are missing alot of information, and he expects students to come into this course with a fundamental understanding of energy systems.

Passionate but the lectures are all over the place, no exam prep is given, & half the things he just expects you to know. Extremely tough grader; even math errors can drop you a letter grade on a test. Repeatedly asks if we actually use our brains, publicly shames students who can't answer questions he asks, & consistently holds the class over time

Furth is passionate about the subject and teaches it well, but his tests are something else. the average was in the 60s for both midterms, there are no study guides, and many questions on the test aren't in any of the homework or class notes (he expects you to just "know" them). While he is good at lecturing, his grading and feedback are awful.
Not really very good at answering questions + bad at communicating with ta so sometimes grading was confusing btwn tests + homework
Professor Furth is very passionate about this subject, which makes class extremely enjoyable if you're a transportation nerd. If not, I wouldn't recommend this class.

I have taken CIVE4566, 4567, 5376, and GE3300 with Furth, and after my time I've come to learn so much from him over any other professors I've had in college. He is very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches, which can come across strongly at times, but he means no harm. His courses are intellectually challenging, but in a good way.

He can come off as rude, but he's just very passionate about sustainable transportation, so don't take anything he says personally. He'll rip even his favorite students to pieces. Exams aren't super tough, but there is a lot of homework. He's very animated and enthusiastic in his lectures, and seriously an expert on the field. Highly recommend.
Arrogant while grading. Expects you to know everything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I got the top scores in exams and assignments after comparing with other students. However, a girl with lower scores than me got an A. But I just got B+. I believe the grading system is not fair

The rating is unfair! After we compared all scores we got in the assignment and exams, the person who got an A grade has lower scores than the person who got top scores but got B+. This happened several times before. I and other students felt UNFAIR. However, since the grading is confidential we never knew how we got the grade.

Furth is very knowledgable about traffic and sustainable design - if you pay attention in class and critically think through the homework assignments, youll do good. HOWEVER! his character is awful. Very demeaning and he will think youre stupid. He expects you to be an expert in his field by going to class, so be ready for him to talk down on you

He is very passionate about sustainability, but sometimes can be unclear in lectures. His homework can be tough at times because it's based mainly on combining a lot of concepts briefly talked about in class. The tests were not on what we practiced because it was written by the other professor teaching the other sections, so that made it harder.

Great course, awesome experience, OK professor. A terrific guy, extremely knowledgeable about his subject-- transportation engineering, infrastructure, policy, Boston-area developments, international stuff-- but has a tough time interacting with students in class. He can be extremely critical to the point of being rude. But he's alright.

I have had Furth twice. Be prepared for a lot of hw (3 per week). Tests are easy but he takes off for the smallest things (i once got the right answer but -5 for no commas after every 3 digits). Is slightly arrogant, unorganized for cive 2221. Hes a better teacher for traffic

He can be a hard teacher to get along with and can come off as kind of a ****. If you get to know him though, he can be one of the best and most helpful teachers at northeastern. Very passionate about his subject areas
Great at explaining the topic but can be intimidating to approach for help and is not a very patient professor.
Make sure to sit in front of the class. Stay up to speed with readings and homework. Make sure you get tutor to work you through homework.
Makes student feel stupid when they ask a question. Can come across as arrogant.
He is the worst professor I ever met! very arrogant and selfish. Please do not study with him. he is good of nothing
kind outside the classroom

Very easy class. Grade is based only on 5 tests and a final. There is a test every other week, which is actually good because you can't fall behind. Gives difficult hw, but the tests are the most simplified examples. Pay attention and it is an easy a.
he's fine if you listen

very one sided discussion during class, could have been more interesting and beneficial had there been more opportunity to give opinions.  I found it frustrating that there wasn't a chance to discuss things in class, its Furth's way.  Period.
He's great. Don't say dumb things and he won't be mean.  He loves bikes too.
