Definitely wants classes to participate in discussion and be mentally present, display that they understand the material. No tests at higher level classes, few assignments but those assignments are important. Basically just do the work and share your thoughts in-class.

Easy to get an A, all of her assignments are group based with 3 exams 70% individual and then taken again with your group for the other 30%. Class is a waste of time to go to with busy work and attendance taken only at the beginning of the semester. Take home final online, but read the textbook, her lectures are useless

Genuinely so disappointed. Not only are the lectures useless, but she is grading every assignment the night before grades are submitted and making countless mistakes. Read the textbook, teach yourself, and be prepared for awfully written exam questions. Not hard to score well, just a disappointing course overall.

The lectures were not hopeful at all. Each class, she goes through a set of slides and assigns discussions that are unhelpful to learning. She is horrible at lecturing, spends a lot of time of the useless material and breezes by the useful topics. The exams were online and consisted of an individual and group portion.

I would recommend reading the textbook and teaching yourself for the exam. Professor lectures on a few diagrams during class, then gives you unrelated group work. Seems like a sweet woman, but not an effective professor at all.

Prof Godoy-Carter is a nice person but a horrible lecturer. She spends a lot of time discussing topics that aren't even on the exam but does not touch on important concepts. She also isn't helpful with questions in class. The tests were online and difficult but doable. Only way to do well is to read the textbook and learn yourself.

She does not teach, her lectures have mandatory attendance but she does not teach anything meaningful. Her exams and quizzes have awfully-worded questions where you cannot even decipher what she's asking of you. Buy the textbook and read it on your own. Not a tough class to do well in but she is god-awful.

You take all of the tests twice, once individually, and once again with your group. You are graded 70% for the individual portion and 30% for the group portion. The test questions often have typos/ are badly worded. She's not a great lecturer, but if you use all of your resources (textbook, achieve, TA lectures), it's an easy A.

The wording of some questions on exams and such were a bit difficult to understand, but other than that an easy A for Biochemistry! Exams are remote, and are weighted 70% on the individual portion you do at home and 30% retaking the exact exam in groups that are assigned.

The tests are graded 70% individually and 30% with your group. The final individual is online outside of class and the final day is with the group. Bad wording but not terrible. READ THE CHAPTERS!! The only way you will pass is by reading and attending class. If you do that you will do good!! There is a small extra credit achievement assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor is a very nice person and truly cares about student success. She is very open to feedback, so while the course was disorganized at first she listened and adapted and by the end, it was truly fun and interesting. She makes up for bad test questions, removing them from counting if people have issues with them.

DON'T take if you can avoid. She means well as a person (I think), but she's disorganized, confused, and does not teach at all. All her quiz/test questions are badly worded and open to multiple interpretations. This class is easy to fall behind in bc you never know what's going on. She tells us certain things and then does the exact opposite.

Don't take this class if you can avoid it. I wish I listened to the reviews. Super nice lady, but she does not teach, you teach yourself everything. Test questions are poorly worded. She won't take responsibility for poor wording/multiple interpretations when every single person in the class agrees. She blames the students for not studying enough

Incredibly frustrating class. We spent every single class in teams on zoom working on quizzes and discussion posts. No lectures whatsoever, no teaching us. In my group, 1/2 of the people didn't speak all year .Test questions were badly worded or not properly coded into canvas leading to mass confusion and spending lots of class time debating them.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. She doesn't teach a single thing and refuses to answer questions. The final wasn't too difficult until I found out she marked questions wrong that were word for word out of the textbook. Completely bull that exams are worth 60% when she doesn't teach.

The whole class consists of talking about the content in breakout rooms. She does come and visit breakout rooms, but seems kind of shocked when we have questions about the content... which is strange because she literally does not lecture at all. You're basically teaching yourself here, she just fills in the gaps if you ask for clarification.
Refused to lecture and gave group quizzes every class. We taught ourselves for most of the class. Had to rely on the textbook. Do not take this class if you want to learn anything.

Great class.  Loved the lectures - very engaging and informative.  Very clear in explaining topics, and was always willing to clarify points of confusion.  The tests are hard to prepare for, as she tends to ask questions about seemingly unimportant details from the text, which are not mentioned or emphasized during class.

I agree that this class was mostly molecular biology. She squished everything else about microbes in at the last minute which was exceptionally disappointing. She's a nice person, but her tests are confusing and the lack of feedback make them difficult to study for. Do not take microbio with this professor.

Dr. Godoy is clearly very interested in the topic, but most of the class is just learning about genetics and molecular NOT microbes! So If you have had biochem or molecular be prepared for a giant review.  Tests are confusing and worded weird.  She is very nice and helpful though, just hard to understand at times.
Really amazing professor. Really makes sure you fully practice all problems in class and prepare for the tests that are similar in difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a really nice guy. Policies are made by the department, and she is very easy on the routine part. She doesn't really compel you to listen to her throughout the class, as long as you understand. She is also very reachable and she is always patient. She is the kind of dream math teacher I've wished to encounter!! Math needs practice!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is very strict and fast paced. if you go separately for 1-1 she's much more caring in that. shes accomodating for taking tests later on for emergency cases. Spam her practice tests because those are essentially the tests but with different numbers.

GO TO CLASS, you'll think you can get away without going to class but it will come back to bite you at the end of the semester.
Prof. Rangoli is genuinely one of the kindest instructors I've ever had. She may come off as rude or condescending but if you get to know her she is super sweet and more than willing to offer support if you are struggling.

pick a religion and start praying.. her notes arent legible and she teaches each class like shes a drill sergeant screaming at the class for answers after giving us 30 seconds to do the problem while she yaps nonstop! tests r only easy if u memorize the hell outta the study guides bc theyre identical to the test

Rangoli teaches very well and says she cares about her students, but her class environment is subpar. She's far too intense and teaches like a coach. She expects a 3-minute problem to take us 30 secs, then harasses the class for an answer. I've heard she is warmer one-on-one, but I am too scared to go to office hours. The final is 40% of our grade.

She has a very thick accent that's hard to decipher and also speaks incredibly fast. Additionally, she somehow goes really fast while also getting behind in her units. She delayed test 2 and so we had three major tests back to back with a quiz squeezed in between. Third unit is an immediate F if you use a TI-83 due to her harsh grading.

dr goyal is goated she is very nice. many may think she is intimidating during class but it is because she is trying to encourage participation. exams are straightforward, and if you put effort into learning and fully understanding the content it's hard to not get an A. stay on top of things and don't be afraid to ask her questions.

Professor Goyal was an amazing instructor! Though she could be a tough grader, that seems to be inherent with a proofs-based class, and I really appreciated that she took the time to thoroughly explain concepts and help with homework. She was also very considerate in taking the time to check-in with students and ensure our success in the class.

This professor is very sweet as a person, especially during offic hours, but in class she makes you feel insanely unconfident. She was always yelling and I feel like class was a race - stressful 24/7. The tests were understandable,  we learned everything in class, my only downside would be the classroom environment (I never wanted to be there lol)

She's so dedicated to her students, and always devoted extra time for us. She always explained WHY she posted a certain worksheet, posted a certain homework assignment, etc. Her whole purpose was for us to learn. She taught us some life skills and university skills for our first semester as well. She's one of my top favorite professors!

I never used to enjoy working with proofs, especially after my past struggles with geometry, but this course changed my perspective. It introduced me to a new, fascinating side of math that I've grown to really appreciate. Prof. Goyal's expertise and passion for the subject truly made a difference in how I understood and connected with the content.

he taught a quite complex class very well, always available for her students and always wanted the best for us. Lectures were fast-paced but as long as you put in time outside of class in the right way it was never too hard of a course. The way she taught the material was almost immaculate. Up there with the math professor/teachers I've ever had.

This professor made such a positive impact on my academic journey! After taking the IMR course with her, I decided to pursue a math minor—something I never imagined I would do, especially considering my struggles in high school math. Her dedication to helping students truly stands out, and her encouragement helped me improve significantly.

This professor made Calculus 1 easy to understand and boosted my confidence in math, something I had struggled with before. She was always available to help, whether in class or through online materials. Her teaching style really motivated me to work harder. I highly recommend her and will miss having her as a professor when I move to Boston!
Good Professor, really cared about her students. Disregard other reviews.

I was nervous about starting a higher calc class after a 3-year math break. After our first class ended (@ 6pm), she stayed back to review the syllabus and guided me on what to brush up on. Her genuine care, high energy, and passion for math, while not for everyone, made staying engaged in a late-day course enjoyable and encouraging.

Class moves fast and she rushes sometimes, but she's very accessible and helpful during office hours in case you have any questions. Several times have I went to office hours for help on homework and even ended up having a very nice off-topic conversation. She also responds to emails very fast and sometimes has a sense of humor.

She often yells at students while they are trying to solve a problem and shows no interest in actually helping students. Lectures are extremely repetitive and provide no time for questions or participation.  I like calculus this class made me hate it. Her accent is not understandable, I just had to reteach myself everything after each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Here's some of the many things that she did: she yells a lot, especially when solving class problems. Went through 2 lessons in 1 lecture multiple times. Openly talked about one student's grade in front of another. Complained that a 91.65% test average wasn't good. Extremely rude and abrasive and much more. Stressful class and even worse professor.

She yells at the students to answer her questions in less than a minute. Professor has a heavy accent and the lecture notes provided are unclear and messy. Overall, the class is test (exams are extremely difficult) and lecture heavy.

If there is one professor out there to find your weaknesses and make you much stronger academically, she is the one to do it.

Frankly, I went into this class feeling confident, and that was torn right down immediately - And then over time, it has been built back up, and I feel much stronger and able to take on difficult concepts.

The true goat

By far the best math teacher I've had. She is very strict and adamant on her student's grasping concepts. Some might argue that she is too aggressive, but the results in her class's exams speak for themselves. She wasn't afraid to call me out for poor habits and mistakes which helped me secure an A+ in her class.

I have never felt this angry in my life. Extremely fast paced, no empathy for those that don't understand, rushes students through tests. Doesn't greet anyone, and has no interest in her student's lives or relating to them outside of the lecture. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS it was hell on earth. fav quote: "I don't know your names, and I don't want to"

Currently taking Calc 134. She has thick accident, messy handwriting, and moves quickly. In class wants us to try and do a problem and in less than a minute she yells at us to give her the answers. Very test heavy class and lecture heavy. Says she makes the test easily and mocks students about she can't wait to see the average.

Very thick Indian accent and moves EXTREMELY fast during class. Test heavy but she lets you replace a bad test grade for a better one. She's nice at times and has a sense of humor. The group project is a grade booster. Don't take this class if math is not you strong suit.

"Study smart not hard. No matter how much you push a wall it will never move". Amazing professor beyond any standards - go to lectures, go to office hours, put in those hours and you are sure to get an A. Tough class, tough love - but she will make you smart.

The course was heavily test-based, but she gave practice tests from previous years, the same format, and the same style of questions. She was also lenient on partial credit. It is mostly lectures, with her doing sample problems on the board with input from the class. She is very accessible and questions are answered fairly thoroughly.

Professor Goyal Was very caring towards her students; however, her teaching style was not designed for everyone. She was test-intensive and held grudges against students and classes in general. However, if you work hard, you will be fine.

I had Rangoli for Calculus 3 and she was amazing. She always encouraged us to ask questions or speak up if we were confused about something and answered any our class had with no judgment. The material is somewhat difficult, and there is a textbook, but she uses her own notes to teach, which are much more streamlined and easy to understand.

I found the instructor to be very caring and dedicated to her students. She provided lots of helpful
course materials and were always willing to answer any questions we had.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do 90% of the learning out of class. Pay attention to quizzes and the reasonable homework and example problems, exams are similar but by no means easy.

Loved this professor! Expectations were very clear and possible to achieve with a little hard work. He really wants you to understand the concepts, as well as be able to solve problems. Office hours were helpful and fun, he explained things very clearly and made it all feel very approachable. I would take him for all of my classes if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Every day I left class more confused than I came in. I didn't even look at his notes when I studied because it was so confusing. Midterm was fine, final was hard: Mean70 Med75 High 94. ILS quizzes were difficult. Barely offered any office hours, especially for the size of the class. Wasn't willing to be accessible outside that one weekly session.

This man is lowkey so boring. I had taken physics before but was forced to take calc based in this class, and he made everything so much more complicated than needed. In all that he said, 10% was important but that got lost in the 90% of yap. I gave up trying to follow along and just taught myself the main concepts later. Very lowkey class overall.

Took Phys 1 and 2 for engineering with him. He teaches these classes like you're going to pursue a PhD in physics. He makes everything as complicated as possible because he probably doesn't realize most (if not all) of the students he's teaching are going to take Phys 1 and 2 and not take another physics class for the rest of their degree.

Good guy, really cares about his class. If you haven't taken calc 3 the class can be a bit tricky but with the HW and Lab propping up your grade you'll do fine. Lectures are bit confusing and goes in depth on derivations that you might use once in a HW. But overall a really good professor.

He's super passionate and cares that his students understand the course. However, you definitely have to put in the work if you want to do good on the final/midterm (mostly just based off of in-class/hw problems). You'll only get the full worth out of the class if you go to office hours, do the hw, and read the textbook every now and then.

The lectures move way too fast, but he normally explains the concepts somewhat well. the lab reports every other week are HORRIBLE and ILS is meh. The homework is very difficult, even if you understand the topics.

Lectures move very fast and aren't very clear at all, especially if you haven't taken calc 3. ILS is helpful, Lab reports every other week are awful, weekly homework is very difficult but if you try to understand it is helpful.
He was helpful during office hours and over email. However, he goes very fast during lectures, which makes them hard to follow—I usually leave class more confused than when I walked in.

Professor Camille was a very good professor for Physics 2. He's very caring and helpful (especially during ILS). Read the textbook before his lectures (the readings will help you understand what's happening in class) and the group work in ILS will help you prepare for the quiz. Overall, great professor and I would take him again.

Camille was a solid professor for Physics 2. He is definitely passionate about the subject and likes to demonstrate a lot of the concepts in class. A lot of the homework that was assigned was confusing, however, and did not always reflect the material covered in class through the lectures. The quizzes were also sometimes misleading and difficult.

Lectures were rushed and many topics weren't explained clearly. Sometimes the course went way too in-depth. Be prepared to read the textbook. There is one homework per week; Camille is super helpful at office hours. 
Exams were ok, mostly based on quizzes and problems done in lecture. Camille is a great person, just not the best lecturer!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: camille was hard to talk to. in class, he always seemed rushed for time and didn't seem to like when students asked questions, since then we would be "wasting time". outside of class, such as in emails, i felt that he would put me down and make me feel worse about myself than i had going into the interaction (probably not intentional). wouldn't rec

Really decent guy. Cares about his students and how well they're doing in his class. It is challenging though and there's not a lot of grade booster opportunities if you start off struggling. Decently fast paced lectures so make sure you are paying attention or be prepared to teach yourself a lot.

Definitely a great professor if you're a physics major or if you have a higher-level class with him, but for introductory level physics, the class was very confusing. A lot of the equations used in class had lots of subscripts that were hard to understand compared to the equivalent AP Physics C - Mechanics class I took in HS.

Professor Gomez-Laberge always came into class with enthusiasm and encourages questions during the lecture. He is always available for some time after the lecture for questions and he sets clear expectations for the midterm and final.

Passionate about what he is teaching and gets excited when people ask questions, however, sometimes he uses math that goes beyond what is expected for this course. The grading criteria is extremely fair and I always felt like on the quizzes/tests a lot of partial credit was given. Lectures hard to follow at times but activities in class helped.

I want to give him a 4/5 so badly because he's clearly a great teacher and passionate about the subject, but the reality is his homeworks and lectures are far more advanced and difficult than they need to be for the class.

Super nice person and eager to answer questions, but not the best at teaching. He often goes off on tangents and more in-depth than required. Lectures can be hard to follow, so reading the textbook beforehand helps. Quiz questions come from lectures and activities, and tend to be conceptual. Go to office hours because it helps with the homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Camille is possibly the sweetest prof I've had in years. Not the best at teaching, but he answers questions in class and seems very accessible outside of class, even with a massive lecture hall. Homework is often harder than anything in class or on the tests

He is a nice guy who wants the best for his students, but I think he should be teaching more advanced classes. The homework "goes a little beyond in-class material" and is impossible to do without going to office hours/looking online. All the in-class lectures involve useless derivations and problems solved in the most complicated way possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you've never taken Physics before, this class will be terrible for you. He flies through his lessons, barely even explaining. He goes really fast and assumes you've already taken physics before. There's a quiz and homework every week but it doesn't even reflect what we do in class. If you take this class, get ready to teach yourself the lessons.

Camille is a pretty great professor overall. His course is pretty lecture heavy due to the nature of the class but he does a great job building in review and answering student questions. I also had Camille for ILS and he is helpful when it comes to answering questions and has good availability for office hours. There's 1 homework per week, ~2hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Camille simply does not teach things that are on the homework. He barely covers a concept in class, and we have to teach ourselves everything else. And the homeworks have almost no clear example to base off of from the text, meaning we have to guess if we are doing something correct. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Gomez-Laberge is easily one of the coolest professors I have ever had. His slides and super clear and he does a great job of explaining the course content. He is a really chill guy and is very approachable if you need extra help. Overall physics 2 is a challenging class but he makes it fun and enjoyable. Absolutely recommend this guy, he is awesome

He was an amazing professor. I loved his course and his lectures. You could tell he was passionate about his content and about helping students succeed. Devastated to hear of his passing. Sending love to family and friends
One of the most genuine and kind professor I ever had. He was very passionate about the field he taught, and made me like psychology. Very sad to hear about his passing.

Genuinely one of the best, most caring professors I've had at NEU. Was clearly dedicated and passionate, and one of those professors whose classes you'd undoubtedly enjoy attending. Devastated to hear about his passing and wishing the best for his family
An extremely kind, knowledgeable, and empathetic professor who I was lucky to have for bio psych. I was devastated to hear of his passing and wish him and his family peace.
Such an amazing professor and person. Extremely knowledgeable and passionate, a true light at Northeastern. Rest in peace.
Kyle was an amazing professor and inspired so many students. I am heartbroken to hear about his passing.
exams are open note and take home, awesome prof. he is very knowledgeable and caring
Such a kind and understanding human being, and very knowledgable on his subject. Take developmental psych if you like watching good movies

Professor G is one of the most inspirational professors I've had. His lectures are fun, engaging, and actually apply to real life. He's super charismatic, but more importantly, he understands you on a personal level.

Dealing with hardship in my life, Professor G, was able to level with me and understand. I'm grateful I got to take his class!

Lectures are engaging and varied. Shows a lot of interesting films in class. Assignments are creative but tedious and time-consuming, and there are a lot of them. He grades mostly to completion, so it is easy to do well. He is very approachable and encourages student participation and feedback through Slack. Highly recommend his course!

Dr. G is a really caring professor who wants students to succeed. The class itself is not very difficult and very much graded on completion. A bunch of written assignments graded to completion, 1 presentation graded the same way, and 2 take home, open note tests (midterm and final) that you have a week to complete.

Dr. G has by far been one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. All tests are online, and he devotes time for you to work on assignments in class. His use of external materials, like TedTalks, films, and interviews outside of the slide decks gives you a well-rounded learning experience. I left every day feeling like I really learned something.

Very passionate about the subject, super respectful and made class very open-ended and engaging. Super easy grader, made class more about learning. One of the teachers I'll actually miss seeing each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great, caring professor. Grades come from 2 open note, take home tests, a presentation, and a lot of homework assignments. Not difficult to get a good grade if you put in the work, but be prepared to do a lot of smaller writing assignments.

Dr. G is one of my favorite professors at Northeastern! He goes above and beyond to create an inclusive and safe space in his classrooms. He is always willing to talk and work with you more outside of class too. He made this course so engaging, and encouraged great discussions in class. Definitely recommend any course with Dr. G!!
great.
Amazing professor who cares for students and the art of learning.
Amazing, down to earth professor who cares for students and the art of learning.

Graded mostly on online discussion posts and in-class activities. All work is done in-class so there really isn't that much homework. Exams are open-note and outside of class, but it is important to pay attention to his lectures -- I found that the exams got more difficult as the semester progressed. A bio intro class should be a pre-requisite.

Dr.G is without a doubt the best professor I have taken at Northeastern. He always makes himself available to his students if they ever need help with the projects or the material. If you have the chance to take his class, I would 100% encourage you to. He is extremely lenient and understanding and you'll never want to miss class!!!

Dr. Gobrogge is one of my fav professors. I had him for 2 classes & his lectures were always engaging, he applied subjects to relevant current affairs & taught through articles, movies, speakers, etc. He's also incredibly understanding/empathetic allowing for extensions & help to ease stress. I recommend taking a class w/ him, you won't regret it.

Second time taking Dr. G. He is a fantastic teacher and is super passionate about everything he covers in class. There was a lot of pretty lengthy homework assignments, but they were all graded on completion. Midterm and final were take home, open notes. Highly recommend him and all of his courses!

the amount of work that dr. gobrogge uploads for an elective class is absolutely absurd. the amount of assignments are suffocating and makes the class unenjoyable. his assignments require so much from you.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Gobrogge is an amazing professor who is super lenient and understanding. He does give extensions as long as you ask, he grades papers on completion, there was only one capstone project, a midterm, and final which he left open for a week and was multiple choice. He is super kind and easily the best professor I have had.

Dr. G is the best professor I've had at NU. Cares a lot about his students and makes sure that we're getting a lot from the class. Uses slack: 4 posts/week for participation points, a few easy assignments based on films/documentaries etc, 2 open note, no time limit, multiple choice, open for a week exams. Can't wait to take more of his courses.

I literally created this account to write a good review about him. I loved the class and using slack for class. It is very participation heavy so I think going to class and participating is important. Doing the writing assignments are important and helpful to your grade. I wish I could take his class again; he is so sweet, kind and understanding.

Dr. Gobrogge is an incredible professor. They worked hard to develop the format of this course and consistently maintain an inclusive, safe classroom setting. Dr. G is available outside class and is so understanding of their students. Assignments are meaningful and thought-provoking, and synchronous class time is very enjoyable!

I totally recommend this professor if you're looking for a class that'll give you an easy A. We watch films in class then have essays to write afterwards, but they're based on completion. There's a few pop group projects done in class which makes attendance important.

He is amazing! He's lectures are dynamic and you'll get exposed to the content in various ways: Movies, TedTalks, Short Videos or readings. The movies we watched were amazing and the content was really interesting. Every week we submit Slack posts into the course's Slack channel and exams are online (you have one week to complete them)

Dr. G is an incredible lecturer. A lot of the class material was TedTalks and documentaries. Participation was graded by your number of weekly slack posts and most assignments were graded on completion. Easy A class but still very engaging, definitely take his class if you get the chance!

One of the best professors I've had. Exams are take home and open note which is really helpful because the material is dense. Gobrogge makes class very interactive and engaging so it's easy to pay attention. Be sure to participate and stay active with discussion posts as this will make up the rest of your grade. Overall 10/10!

Great class and a great professor! There are 2 open-note 100-question exams you have a week to take. The final is the same format you have a week to take it and it's online. You have 4 SLACK posts a week for participation which are really easy. 10/10 would recommend taking.

Dr. G is extremely caring and provides various types of assignments outside of tests. Attendance isn't mandatory, but participation is graded by posts on SLACK. There are two open note exams from information in class and in the textbook, but they aren't too difficult. Would highly recommend.

This guy rocks. The lectures are super interesting & you will learn so so much. Exams are take-home and you get to watch a bunch of movies and documentaries in class. A lot of slack posts, but they're very doable.  I highly recommend prof G and going to the class regularly (he has a photographic memory for faces, so he'll notice if your gone)

Dr. Gobrogge is the best professor that I have had at Northeastern. He is so kind and understanding. The class is very easy and overall you will do well if you do the work. He doesn't try to make things difficult everything is very straightforward.

I took Clinical Psychology / Mental Health (formally called Abnormal Psychology) with Dr. G in fall 2022, and it was probably one of the best classes I have ever taken! Dr. G uses Slack to create an in-person and virtual sense of community in the classroom. We watched films in this class which really contributed to my understanding of the content!

Dr. G made this course fun because he included interactive activities in addition to lectures. We learned through watching movies and TED talks, reading articles, and doing case studies (my favorite part), which helped us apply our knowledge to real-world situations. Plus, we rarely had HW and almost every assignment was only graded on completion

Loved Dr. G! The class was really interesting but definitely got more into the neuroscience side of psych which I didn't except. Participation was based on slack posts which I LOVED. The exams were a bit overwhelming because they were 100 multiple choice, but they were take home and open for a week which was nice. Great person, great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: best class and best professor, took it during summer session, classes were supposedly 4 hours twice a week but always ended earlier. two tests were online, only one final research was assigned. Dr.Gobrogge is so amazing I can't recommend him more enough.

Dr. G is a great professor! Class participation is based on slack posts during the semester and exams are open book and open for an entire week to take outside of class. There are two exams and one project and participation. He is very understanding and encourages class discussion. I would definitely recommend taking Dr. G!

Dr. G is an amazing professor. He wants everyone to do well in his class, and it shows. Lectures were discussion based, so he encouraged students to read the slides before and come to class with questions. His exams were take home and open notes. I hope to have him again in future courses!

Dr. G is a g. An incredibly engaging lecturer, experienced and knowledgeable in the field. He's passionate about what he does and it comes through. Also, all assessments were completely open note take home tests. Will definitely try to take more of his classes.

Prof. Gobrogge is my favorite professor at NU. He is the most passionate and caring professor, and he clearly cares about what he is teaching. I've taken all the classes he offers, and I've worked with him outside of class. He is so interesting, and he talks about all his experience in the field which really adds to his class. I 100% reccomened.

I have taken every single class Dr.G has offered at NEU. He is so intelligent and accomplished with no ego whatsoever. He respects and understands his students. You'd be making a mistake if you didn't take him as your prof.

The most amazing professor I've had at Northeastern so far. Genuinely made my entire semester because he's so passionate about teaching Abnormal Psych and cares deeply about his students. I hope to have him again!

I LOVE Dr. Gobrogge. I have taken 5 classes (all the ones he teaches) and his teaching style is very aligned to support students and enable them to succeed. He makes all exams take-home even pre covid because he believes that students perform better without stress, and he cares so much about learning and facilitates discussion, even for lectures.

Super nice and enthusiastic + exams were easy. Gives some random group assignments in class so you have to go everyday. The lectures for this class were more discussion based and you had to do the reading beforehand to learn the material. We watched five movies total which was nice especially for a 9am. Very easy A.

Dr. Gobrogge is a great professor! He's very engaging and shows a lot of interesting videos in class such as ted talks, and Netflix documentaries he participated in. Our midterm and final were both open-note, open-book, with 24 hours to complete. You can tell he genuinely wants students to succeed. If you keep up with assignments, it's an easy A.

Dr.G is easily one of the most fun and caring professors I've taken here. He made sure all of the students learn and shows a lot of interesting TED talks and netflix documentaries that he was directly involved with. Most of the grade comes from exams and assignments that are held during class so make sure to show up!

You should go to class because he does do group projects some days. The textbook is heavily used on the exams and there are some lecture points on the exams as well. Overall, Gobrogge is a very caring and interesting professor, and as long as you put in the work, you will get an A.

Professor Gobrogge was one of my favorite professors and he made abnormal psych really interesting. he shows a lot of ted talks that are related to the material and he enjoys a discussion based class rather than lectures. truly cares for his students success

Dr. Gobrogge is an amazing professor! He truly wants to see his students learn. Attendance is mandatory because he gives short open-book pop quizzes. There is a midterm and a final that are both take-home with 100 MCQs and you have a week to complete them! His class is super fun and an easy A. Take his class! He even brought pastries for the class!

The majority of the grade consisted of writing assignments, pop quizzes, midterm, and final. He will give you full credit on the writing assignments and pop quizzes if you just answer the questions he asks. Attendance is important because of the pop quizzes and the writing assignments are based on class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Love Prof. Gobrogge! He genuinely cares about his students and in most classes, you just watch TedTalks or 1-minute-Neuroscience videos on Youtube so you can always watch them again. Both the midterm and the final are take-at-home (open-book) tests that you have a week to complete: they're 100+ MCQs but all answers are in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and take prof Gobrogge. Not only is he really enthusiastic about what he's teaching but he also really wants you to succeed. HE IS THE BEST. He'll help you out with other psych related things like an internship, and you can totally go talk to him about anything. Honestly 11/10 recommend.
Dr G was incredible; personable, caring, and wicked smart! Made classes fun and engaging.
Gobrogge was great, overall. Very approachable and smart. Lectures were discussion which I enjoyed as it was a nice break from my typical science courses. Would recommend him to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr G. was solid! If you enjoy a discussion based lecture type course, youll have a fun time and learn something. Hes an easy A because he isnt lecturing for grades but rather to help apply concepts. I attended office hours regularly and learned quite a lot during our conversations.

This professor is amazing! His lecture style is about promoting interesting conversations rather than teaching to the test. Unlike other teachers, he bases his lectures of what is interesting to his students. His extremely smart, kind, and considerate. I wish he would teach every class. 10/10 recommend

Everyone studying neuroscience/psychology should take Professor Gobrogge. Northeastern is extremely lucky to have him teaching. Please do yourself a favor and enroll in one of his classes - he wont disappoint.
Prof is one of a kind. His teaching strategy is unique and effective. Go to class, listen, pay attention, and youll not only get inspired but youll also get an A.

Dr. Gobrogge is the best professor Ive ever had! Sudents who rate Kyle less than exceptional either didnt come to class and/or werent paying attention. For example, as he stated in class, his lectures come from pre-prepared textbook slides that all professors have access to and give him credit for not having TAs yet teaching over 150 students.

Kinda boring, often feel unengaged. Doesn't post grades often enough so don't know how well Im doing. Doesn't post lectures until right before exams, not helpful when have to study of quizzes and always focusing on vigorously typing. LARGE focus on history and some points we had to know didn't seem like important (ex. "XX was the least fav child"

If you have the option to take a class with this professor, don't hesitate! He is AMAZING! His classes are easy A's b/c he makes it that way for his students. If you do poorly on a graded assessment, there is a 90% chance he will let you re-take it completely. Super sweet. He likes group projects. Attendance is mandatory as he does easy pop quizzes

He's good and a fun person overall, but the class it self is very very very disorganized and stuff gets pushed back A LOT. Group project to make your business was fun, met lots of good people in the class and we all connected well i'd say. Quizzes are js case studies so like review those, and get ready to speak A LOT ALOT ALOT...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Discussion-focused class. Quizzes are solely based on case-study readings, which may not reflect true understanding. The semester-long presentation is done twice: midterm and improved for finals. Prof is helpful if asked, but communicating outside class can be tricky at times + his feedback is vague. I didn't leave this course having learned much.

You might be randomly be called on to present daily HW readings, & participation is heavily graded by tracking hand raises each class. Public speaking is unavoidable. Quizzes cover (sometimes) long case studies; lectures matter little. He's a good guy and takes end-of-semester feedback seriously, so future iterations will likely improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation is 15% of the grade while quizzes/tests are 20% the group project is 35% of the grade and is the same group you keep for the whole semester. Group-mates get randomized by the professor so if you get unlucky, well, thats it. Homework every night is just basically a reading, although very doable. Very very little actual course content.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ta is amazing, but lectures run on and make me hate my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, quiz heavy, do not take this class as an elective.
Drop the class…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: save urself while u can; participation is heavily needed, or else no A/A-/B+.

participation is a huge part of the grade. you need to speak during class as it is counted and goes toward your final grade. got a 95 on final project and 97 on final exam and still ended with a B- because of my participation. few quizzes that are not hard as long as u do the readings and pay attention during discussions. not an easy A.
very disorganized prof, never take this class for ur elective. his lectures are NOT helpful lol

Grading was incredibly unclear. Participation was 25% of grade and base off of how many times you raised your hand each class. Assignments became redundant and boring. Quizzes were really easy if you skimmed each of the readings before. Not trying to get him fired bc he cared and was nice just wish there was more organization and set expectations.
Participation is 25% of grade, grading system is incredibly unclear, super disorganized prof.

Tries his best to get ideas flowing around the class. Class is led by students for discussions. Grades very fairly and can understand who puts in effort for the group project. Easy to prepare for quizzes and exams, he gives you everything you would need. Highly recommend if you want basics for entrepreneurship. Taken as an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Was not super clear about grading and took a long time to input grades. Participation was graded weirdly
Just yaps and goes on tangents for lectures, all the info you need is in the readings. take the group project seriously

Great professor if you are looking to start a start-up. He is very knowledgeable about the subject. Tests and the final is straight forward. Make sure to go over past exams for the final. He cold calls and read the readings cause he will ask you about them. Take his feedback on your group project seriously it is crucial to getting a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Everything we learned was through random articles that were daily homework assignments, you'll be fine if you memorize those key concepts. He counted attendance for lectures but you won't miss much if you decide to skip. Big group project at the end where you create a start-up, he can grade it harshly but provides a lot of feedback!
Fine Professor, course material is repetitive and kind of BS. Not a difficult A.

Favorite professor at Northeastern ever. She is so kind, brilliant, caring, and helpful. Though her handwriting is hard to recognize, lectures never end on time, materials are tough and abstract, she is so inspiring and enthusiastic about math and every topic she delivered. She is extremely helpful if you go to office hours.
Wow, what a terrible experience. Please go far away from Number Theory. Extremely unprofessional. Class never ends on time. She is clearly intelligent, but not good at organizing at all.

Todorov is fantastic, please take her class if you can! She really cares about your learning and provides extremely helpful feedback on quizzes. If you catch a mistake she makes, you get extra credit. My only complaint is that the HW is loosely connected to the content and very long, but she let us choose whether or not it counts for the grade.

A lot of hws, she never posts the assignment due until the last day(always due on Sunday). A tough grader on hws. She was always in a rush about the lecture, but she never finished it on time. Very bad handwriting . Likes to skip solutions/proofs for examples. Her quiz is always outside the class, and takes really long time to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tons of homework
Lectures go through really fast, and they are mostly theorems and proofs. There are quizzes which are pretty important every two weeks so you want to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She was unavailable for her schedule office hours most of the time.  When I tried to schedule other meeting times, she was dodgy because of other obligations.  Also, her lecture style is very sporadic as she makes numerous mistakes and her lecture writing is messy and hard to follow with the many boxes she uses.

She is by far the most amazing teacher I've had at northeastern. So nice and explains everything clearly. Very helpful during office hours. I didn't do any homework and got an A, because her practice quizzes/tests are so helpful. Take this class! I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.
GREAT one-on-one. Very kind and helpful. She genuinely cared for all students. Group Theory was the hardest math class I have ever taken and she made the class survivable.

She is really nice and cares about the students. She also teaches really well and is very clear in her explanations. If she makes a mistake and you correct her, you can get points extra for the quizzes. GREAT PROFESSOR!!

Great professor to learn number theory from!  If your a math minor and/or not a math major, this is a good professor/class to learn how to formulate proofs.  Kinda wish I had this professor before entering another theoretical class.  Exams are easy if you do the homework, otherwise they can be a nightmare if you don't (by knowing that the hard way)

Amazingly sweet.  She gets offended if you leave class early or go to the bathroom without asking, and in that sense is like a high school teacher.  It's impossible to fail this class.  She goes over everything at least twice and will spend an entire class doing one problem.  If you get anything below an A, you probably shouldn't be in college.

Very nice professor, perhaps a little too easygoing with the students who take advantage of her passiveness. Gives plenty of help if you need it, including a 3+ hour review of everything right before the final for any students who want to attend

Her accent isn't very hard to understand, but I didn't feel that she understood the questions that I asked or cared about the concerns that I brought to her. She seemed to be irratable, not very helpful and a bit unprofessional. It's a terrible class and I would avoid it at all costs.
She's a really great woman!! Has helped me a lot in and out of class. Is willing to go the extra mile! You should get her as a professor!!
Very nice and sweet professor. ALWAYS willing to help her students out and very patient if you don't understand something. Take this professor!
she is an awsome woman, extremely nice and really helpful. If you pay attention and do the work, its a guaranteed A
Such a great woman.

Easy enough class after coming out of Calc 1 in highschool. Accent it a bit hard, but you get used to it. If you're nice, she is the best. I had a really annoying kid in my class so she was a bit irritable. Always willing to help.

Accent is not too rough to understand. She is very, very nice and is always willing to help students with the material. Rather basic material because I was a transfer and shanked the entrance 2+2=4 exam

I highly recommend this course and professor! This class was one of my favorites and was very helpful for gaining teamwork experience. There is a semester-long group project that was really fun to work on, and I was able to use that in interviews and my resume.
Incredible

I've looked through a lot of the reviews, and I think many people really enjoyed their time in his class. I agree he is enthusiastic and authentic, which allows you to take a lot from the class. However, he is also a harsh and inconsistent grader. It can also be difficult to ask him questions.

This is long overdue—Golden's Lean Design course in 2023 was the best class I took at Northeastern. I'm now a software engineer and still hear his voice when I hit roadblocks: “What would Golden do?” His clear, no-nonsense advice shaped how I work today. Take his class, listen, and learn. Thanks, Professor!

This class was online async. Extremely group project heavy. Multiple required meetings throughout the semester. The course content is straightforward and all individual assignments are essentially busywork. The canvas is fairly disorganized and assignments instructions can be unclear. Prof. Golden himself is very enthusiastic and responsive.

The strengths of Professor Golden's Innovation class are that he is very enthusiastic to teach it- He wants to make sure groups have what they need to succeed, and has identified that business classes can be boring. The class is very group-work based and has a lot of real-world preparation.

The team based environment of the course is defi nitely the strongest point. It helps build connections and teamwork skills thatcan be used a bit in the future. The weekly guest speakers were also very insightful.
Used class time eff ectively, rubrics were clear for presentations so we knew exactly what was expected of us, also let us knowwhen a certain concept came up that would appear on fi nal exam.

Best course and professor ever.  Course flows nicely, he is informative and passionate. The rc car story brings the entire course together. Tough to get in his class but if you can, do it!  PS. he is big on teams so make sure that you have a good team.

Lectures aren't boring, you really learn a lot. If you closely follow the rubrics for the case studies, presentations and discussions boards you will get 100 or close to that. 3 group presentations that are just graded on the powerpoint slides you submit to him, not the actual presentation. final exam worth 10% of final grade, no midterm. Fun class

Lectures aren't boring, you really learn a lot. If you closely follow the rubrics for the case studies, presentations and discussions boards you will get 100 or close to that. 3 group presentations that are graded on the powerpoint slides you submit to him, not the actual presentation. final exam only worth 10% of final grade, no midterm. Fun Class

He is passionate about entrepreneurship, but he is really rude sometimes. He grades EXACTLY based off of rubrics and can be really harsh. The high score for our presentations were a 9/10 with an average of 8/10. He doesn't care to learn your name and will call you out if you are even a minute late.

Absolutely amazing guy, would definitely take it again. Down to earth, he isn't fake, which is relieving. Has the life experiences to back his points/lessons, which I think every professor should have yet so many don't.
Memorable: circles exercise, making spaghetti, einstein, choosing dinner, mix-ups, and fabulous life stories. Get a good group or make a good group.  Lots of reading, tough on grading.

This was one of my favorite courses at Northeastern and he is a great professor. You can tell how knowledgeable he is in the course material by how well he can teach and explain it. The lectures were interesting, enriching, and engaging. The professor always encouraged our participation. MAybe a little too much reading, get on a good team!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Liked him a lot.  Honest and fair grader.

Solid professor. Follow his rubric, come to class, and participate. You will do fine, he is a reasonable grader.  He tends to cold call a lot, but it works once you get used to it.  He cares about students and greets you by name in each class.  Don't be late. That bothers him regardless of the cause!  
He is very approachable and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not let the ratings fool you, he is an ok guy. He did grade quickly, but I am still not sure what my grade is. The group project is good if you have a nice group of people, I did not. I recommend getting to know him, he likes that and you will get better feedback. This class is not horrible, but it also was not my best experience.

Great professor, should do fine if you follow the rubric and instructions. Cares about his students, class was very engaging. 

Would definitely recommend taking his class again.

It's the best class ever at Northeastern. Pulled everything together from all my other classes. Approachable, friendly, and funny.  Participation matters a lot, and I get to know him. Clear instructions but tough grader.  This course was much more intensive than I expected.

He does not give clear feedback or instructions and doesn't return to the emails. He is very enthusiastic with what he is teaching, but sometimes weird, and Canvas is a mess. If you want clear feedback you won't be able to get any.

Professor Golden is a gem! He has a world of knowledge about entrepreneurship, but he doesn't show off like some other professors do. Instead, he uses his experience to give honest, relevant, and engaging lectures. The group project is weighted heavily and you'll be working with the same people all semester, so get to know them well!!

Prof. Golden's class was engaging and fun. His industry experience shines through, and he makes entrepreneurship super interesting. Unstuck study was a big help for prepping. Reasonable grader if you put in the work.

Professor Golden is the epitome of a masterful instructor, someone every student should aspire to emulate. While he can be demanding and occasionally confrontational, he consistently delivers in every class. Follow his guidance, and you'll thrive. I highly recommend him for any cornerstone business course.

Wanted to take him in-person but settled for online expecting to be disappointed. Course material was amazing, readable, interesting and well structured.  Unlike other online classes I have taken, he includes several live sessions and takes appointments. Definately need the right team to make this work. "Follow the rubric"! Great course. Take him

A legend. I am glad to have had the opportunity to take this class in my final semester.  Golden has an incredible understanding of the innovation process and more importantly, he knows how to share that wisdom in a kind but encouraging method.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was very engaging and fun, and I was able to learn a lot of real-world applications, as the course kind of promises to do. Professor Golden always made this class very fun! Notably, the classbenefi tted from Professor Golden's industry experience and matter-of-fact approach to teaching. I learned a lot in this class.
Thank you, Professor Golden.  Amazing, delightful course.  Group work dominates and a fair amount of work outside of class.  But a great learning experience as my introduction to entrepreneurship.

Golden is just a good guy who cares about us. If you can, take him. He will take you on a ride that you won't want to get off. He is the best professor ever (I matriculated at Northeastern).  A fair amount of work, but his expectations are clear. And he is an extremely fair grader.  Love him.

I took this class as an elective but I was blown away by Professor Golden. Probably the most enriching class I have ever taken at Northeastern. He has loads of credible experience with what he is teaching and incorporates what he has learned along the way into the lectures. Extremely fair grader and helps with public speaking! Would 100% take again

Fair grader and outlines what he is looking for in his rubrics. Your grade is extremely dependent on having a good team. A majority will be done outside of class, as much of the actual lecture is analyzing videos  and learning to think like an innovator. Word of advice to not leave his case reports to the last minute, they really sneak up on you.

This class should be a capstone course for business.  It was more work outside of class than expected and a whirlwind, but it all came together.  I built the best relationships with my team, and the class work was incredibly applicable both to the course but also to my life goals.  Working with engineers was eye-opening for a phylosophy major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I have taken! The professor did an amazing job of guiding us through the complex journey of being an entrepreneur, giving thorough insights, project tasks, and overall advice that can translate to growth in a wide array of career paths and industries.

Must love teams and get a good one to do well. Tough but reasonable grades.  No BS, great job realting his real world experiences.  I will always remember the RC Car story.  First real professor I had at Northeastern - not a robot like the others.

Weird guy. Sometimes mean, sometimes nice. Cannot organize canvas for his life, you're gonna be scurrying tyring to find how to do your assignments. But very fair grader. Do exactly what the rubric says and you've got a guaranteed A. Last, pray you get a good team cause you're stuck together all semester.

Clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about entrepreneurship.  His excitement definitely rubs off on students. Very fair grader and clearly states what I required of students.  No surprises with grades. Used class time effectively. Usually only spend 50-60 minutes of a 1 hour and 40 minute class, gave us the balance to work on projects
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is my last semester at Northeastern and I am truly glad that I took this class as my capstone.  Crazy fast paced course and he can be brutely honest in his feedback, It was the one class that I had a professor who really cared, not a robot.  I love how he relates the material to his personal experiences.  I wish that I had taken him earlier.

He's made it more than clear that he wants to retire and is dissatisfied with his work, and it shows. You'll definitely be able to pass this class with a C or higher, but there's no easy A. He gives meaningless feedback until it's time to actually grade your work -- except accompanied by the long-awaited necessary feedback is docked points.

Grades and judges students under very unreasonable expectations. Never makes it clear what he wants us to do in assignments then gets mad at us for trying to talk to him and clarify it. Most classes he seems like he hates teaching or just doesn't teach at all and belittles students simply for asking clarifying questions.

His lectures were so exciting and thus made me more intrigued to learn. His passion for entrepreneurship shone through each session, and I am grateful to have been part of this class. I would also like to acknowledge his effort in providing us with valuable resources, thought-provoking assignments, and timely feedback.

I thought he did a great job teaching the material overall and showed a lot of enthusiasm for the course. While there was a fair amount of work for the class it is doable. He was very responsive too, and gave a lot of good feedback. Some complain that he may be a tough grader but I found that he was more than fair.

Prof. Golden was very enthusiastic and had a lot of practical knowledge to share.  He was a great teacher! It was the class I learned the most in. He makes learning easy and makes you curious by incorporating creative activities in lectures. Everything is so applicable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: "Studying" entrepreneurship is hard, but Professor Golden makes sure he makes the lessons as engaging as possible by talking about his personal experiences. There's a lot you'll learn in this class that will help you if you're applying to VCs, even if you're not involved with entrepreneurship-based organisations on campus too. Best class ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Golden was my favorite professor at Northeastern. Teaching entrepreneurship is second nature for him because of his extensive experience in the field. He has so much knowledge to share and I absolutely feel like I gained more from his lectures than most other classes. He's always happy to discuss projects, ideas, and questions.

Professor knew how to get us to achieve exceptional results. We worked with students from other colleges and learned interdisciplinary skills not taught in my other classes. I felt like I had accomplished something when I finished finals.  The final presentation was surreal.  High recommend this course

Not an easy A professor, but I'm sure you'll enjoy the lecture and really learn important values. Must say you'll need a bit of luck getting a good teammates, cuz you'll be working with your team the entire semester.

This class was one of my favorites at neu, and Professor Golden has been teaching it how I learn best by using real-world examples and activities to help us apply the principles we are learning in class rather than just reading off slides.  No question that there was a fair amount of work, but he tells you precisely what is expected

One of the best classes that I took at Northeastern.  I cannot say it was easy and at times I was overwhelmed and confused, but by the end of the semester, it all came together and I felt good.  This is project based course with reliance on your team, so make sure that the team is accountable.  The final presentation was awesome.

I took Professor Golden for innovation and then was offered a TA role for the class.  I graduated in December and I must say that he is the most genuine, caring, compassionate professionals that I have ever met or worked with.  He really cares about students success.  If you did poorly, I can tell you, you deserved it.

Professor Golden is incredibly engaging. It's evident he cares a lot about his students and subject matter. Don't take this class if you want easy grades. Stay on top of readings and assignments and you'll be fine, but be prepared to work really hard if you want to do well. Done right, you will learn and grow a lot throughout the semester.

Thank you for being a professor that genuinely cares about your students. I learned so much throughout this course through your engaging lectures and the hands-on activities we do daily. I have enjoyed participating in the innovation process with my team and have learned how to collaborate better with others. I hope to have you again.

Often ambiguous and unclear about grading/expectations. It was impossible to understand how hard to try to please him, and overall, much of the grading was confusing and subjective. Still, he was nice and his lectures were mostly engaging.

do the work and get the grade.  was by far the most inspirational, caring, and passionate professor that I have had at Northeastern.  He is a serial entrepreneur with lots of personal stories that help you assimilate the content of the material.  Fair enough there is a large number of assignments, but they are align well

Golden is hilarious.  He's entertaining and clearly a very intelligent person.  That being said, get ready to work in Innovation!  Nearly your entire grade will be determined by your group and the grading criteria is very convoluted.  This is a guy I would get a beer with, not take a class from.  If you want to learn, take something else

Amazing classes, the only 8 am class that I have ever looked forward to. There is a fair amount of work involved and your grade is heavily weighted toward team participation (you don't get to pick your team) so that can be a challenge.  Fortunately I had an amazing team and now we have come good friends.  This is the best class I have ever taken
He is a very special professor, it was a enjoying but strange experience having his class

Although this professor is great in many respects, his grading style is very, very stringent. If you put in the right amount of time, you could do well, but it seems as though the professor expects everyone to know how to write case studies. 

Also, in my whole semester, I have never met the TA.

Stephan Golden teaches this course with his heart and passion.  I heard that he was good, but he exceeded my expectations.  Blows my engineering classes away.  If you can, take him.  Best class in my three years here.  We love you Professor Golden, you smoked it.

This is my second course with Golden and I am glad that I chose to take this prototype course.  Prototyping is a 100% hands on experience class where you larn how to work with a team (real challenge) to come up with a problem and build a solution.  I liked working with Mass College of Artists students and in their makerspace. Take this course
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is hands down the best professor I have had at Northeastern so far. Take him if you want to learn.

In five years at NEU this was the first time that I regretted the end of the semester. As others have said, his lectures are inspiring and helpful.  He is not only approachable, but he actually reached out to me several times just to check in after I indicated confusion.  Best professor ever.  I only wish I could take him again.

Professor Golden clearly cares about his students and is very passionate about the material. He is very experienced in the subject matter and intertwines his lectures with his personal experiences in the industry. If you are lucky enough to have him, pay attention and ask questions as he will give thoughtful and helpful answers. Best class and prof

Professor Goldin is one of the kindest professors I have had during my time at Northeastern. On top of being extremely knowledgeable about entrepreneurship, he offers valuable advice on life during his team meetings and even outside class.  This class was the most hands on, challenging courses I have taken but he made it worthwhile and fun.

Wow.  My last year and I had to take innovation and got Goldin.  Amazing,  Professor is all about the experience both academically and practically.  His ancedotes put learning in perspective.  I cannot recommend this guy enough.  I only wish that I had taken him sooner and I probably would have changed majors. Always available to talk

Honestly, the best professor at Northeastern University. He is so good. He makes his lectures very interesting and teaches up to the point. Has only one exam that too in the middle of the semester- so the finals week is chill. If you really wanna learn and understand what innovation is, TAKE HIM.

I took this class as an undecided freshman. This class was my favorite course in the 2 semesters I've been here. It helped me choose my business major with a concentration in Entrepreneurship. Prof Golden is extremely helpful and receptive to other people's ideas and has a genuine interest in your ideation process.

Easy workload and he is a good lecturer but he has a really frustrating sense of humor. He uses a lot of group exercises which aren't the most fun and gets upset when we don't enjoy them. I guess he just forgets we are 20+ and not children. He is a good teacher but ehh as a person. Not a bad professor just not for me.

I wish all professors could template his style of teaching.  Best instructor that I have had in four years of education.  Fun, interesting, contemporary, relevant, and beyond approachable.  Seems like he is always available, at all hours.  Sometimes he is straight up with his opinions but its refreshing to have a professor be so honest and real.

Professor Golden is a great person, but sometimes his teaching mechanisms can be ineffective despite the lectures themselves being entertaining. He can be a strict/harsh grader on team presentations so make sure that you really follow the explicit rubric he gives you for them and do well on the one test (final) worth 25% of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You should know that this class is A LOT OF WORK. I think they changed the curriculum in the department cuz everyone was getting As but by just adding more things (exam, group projects, readings, etc), the class didnt get harder, but more unpleasant and less fun. Prof is great tho, even if he says that hes not an academic (he is).

This is supposed to be an intro course. This class was the best that I have taken at Northeastern in my four years here. The load might be heavy for an intro course but it all makes sense in the end. A lot to read but his lectures are so real world, it makes going to class at 8am worthwhile. Amazing energy. Lots of assignments and team project
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: professor golden really knows his material and shares real examples that are releavant and interesting. he is a tough grader but fair. my team explained a misunderstanding and he changed our grade. there is a lot of work in this class, but as a rising junior, this has to be the best class I have taken and he is the best professor ever - solid

Prof Golden is funny and intellectual, but annoying. Most assignments are 1 point. The final exam, which he never stressed, was worth 25 points. Set no expectations, vague rubrics, tough grader. This class was more stressful than it needed to be. I wouldn't take another class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Tough grader--Group projects

reviews.comment: worth taking the 8am course - always energized and funny - brings the content to life with personal stories - I was nervous at first because he calls on you a lot but is kind and engaging. Will take again.
golden is solid, what you come to northeastern for .. tough grader, but open to discuss, very helpful outside of class

Nice guy, but on day one he says, "most of you will not get As". 2301 is almost entirely weighted on the group project and as the only freshman in my group, I found it hard to be heard despite trying. Got an 89.4 final and he was quite rude when I asked if he'd consider moving it up.

Prof. Golden is a delight. ENTR2301 and ENTR3303 are both great courses. Prof. Golden pushes his students to succeed, his classes do require a good amount of effort. But all the effort is worth it. These are fantastic classes, and this is a great professor. You will learn a lot and have a great time.

One of the best professors I've taken at NEU - super engaging class, funny, and really encouraging. It's hard not to do well in this class and along the way, you learn a lot about entrepreneurship and business. Has excellent connections and brings in great guest speakers.
He always encourages students to explore our horizons, solving the problems existed in business, and creates innovations to make peoples lives better.

Prof is very knowledgeable but he does not care about his students/this class at all, and his use of peer evaluations is extremely unfair and is just a way to lower students' grades so he doesn't have to think of a way to do it himself.
Great professor that will go out of his way to help you out. Gives very useful constructive feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Definitely one of my favorite professors at Northeastern. Prof Golden is always ready to teach. He devotes a great level of energy to class and always inspires his students. The feedback he provides is solid and detailed. I had lots of takeaways and would recommend taking his class!

This professor was an absolute pleasure to have for the semester. He brings a great level of energy to the classroom which is necessary for an entrepreneurial class, a characteristic that is a rare find. He really took advantage of the online learning by bringing in fantastic professionals to guest speak to us. Great professor, highly recommended.

the whole class is based on the group project, where you come up with a product and go through the lean design process. I took Innovation! with him on-campus and it was a great experience. I can't say the same about the online Lean Design. Assignment instructions were very unclear and vague. Be prepared to go hunting for grading rubrics/guidelines.
Great Professor and one of a kind business mentor. Take his class if you want to be challenged and inspired.

Ever sat down to play blackjack at a table where the dealer silently decides that the new max number is 11 and you have to count backwards from 10 before you draw a card? If you did, you would understand what taking a class from Prof. Golden is like. Prepare yourself for a series of invented problems that you can only solve by reading minds.

He's probably the best entrepreneurship professor, but the class in general was a waste of time. The entire semester you work on a new idea and creating a business using it. Basically, every group made out of mostly business majors just thought of some idea and said they would use artificial intelligence to solve it.

You definitely have to work hard in this class, but Prof Golden is a great professor and all around person. He really inspires and motivates his students, and is available for help and feedback when your group needs it.

One of the best professors I have ever had. His dedication to teaching us the material is like no professor I have ever seen. He is willing to go the extra mile in and out of class to ensure that you understand the information and its importance to you. For anyone considering taking his class, stop thinking and just sign up now.

Professor Golden is one of the best professors I have ever taken. His dedication to teaching us the material is like no professor I have ever seen. He is willing to go the extra mile in and out of class to ensure that you understand the information and its importance to you. For anyone considering taking his class, stop thinking and sign up now.

I just took professor Golden for a 2 week dialogue that turned onine due to Coronavirus (so yeah this review is from 2020... weird times huh). He has been by far in my 2 years at Northeastern so far the most inspirational and effective teacher. He adapted amazingly to the online situation and brought very respected speakers in *linkedIn Boost* ;)
Fantastic professor! Amazing and super helpful! Definitely to take his class!! A big treasure!

Prof Golden is great! He really prepares you to use the MOSIAC organizations on campus and take your learning beyond class to start your own small business if you want. Super helpful! Super available! I took as a summer online dialogue, but lots of VERY speakers and super helpful feedback. Teaches from experience! HIGHLY RECOMMEND IF YOU CAN!
Great Prof! Really enjoyed taking innovation with him! There is no final exam for the class and the mid-term is an interview with an entrepreneur. Would definitely recommend taking this class.

This was probably one of the best classes I've taken at NEU. During the course you and your team make a LEGIT product, so it really is a lot of work. However, the grading is very fair and Golden always gives good feedback/critique. This was really a no BS class that gets you one foot in the world of product development & design.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects
