He has very good notes. If you have taken statistics before, this class is an easy A. He is pretty boring but at the same time he's trying his best to help you understand!
Great Professor - take lots of notes, and make sure to pay attention
He's not as bad as these reviews make him out. He genuinely wants his students to understand the material and is pretty lenient with grading. That said, the lectures do leave something to be desired.

I will not take his class again. Not helpful. Exams and Homework are harder than he teach in the class. Did not have any examples for the materials. He wants to prove that he knows a lot, so he gets deeper in the materials; however, it is confusing all the time. Even he gets confused by his own materials. Do not have formula sheets for Exams.

Do you plan on taking Econometrics in the future?? If yes, then don't take stats with him. It'll screw your basics and then you'll fail econometrics too. Its not just one course grade that'll suffer. Northeastern needs to recruit better professors for the econ department
He is an alright teacher but explains things in a way very unlike the textbook. If you do all the book exercises, you'll be okay. He is enthusiastic and doesn't move through the material too quickly.

Northeastern is a great school, don't get me wrong. But their Econ department sucks due to the awful professors. Gustavo is the worst of them all. I can't believe he's a professor there. What a downgrade for the school. Worst teacher I've ever had. Period
Great guy.   Come to class, take notes, and you'll do just fine.

DO NOT CHOOSE HIM!!!!!! Worst professor I have ever had. Not helpful at all. You need to learn everything by yourself. He is not good at teaching. Statistic is important for econ students, he just screwed it up.

Just don't take his class. Just don't do it. He does not teach very well and you will suffer once you move onto Econometrics which has more statistics. You need your foundation to be strong and he will screw it up for you. There's still time, turn back. I don't get why he gets to write a confuing textbook and why we can't use a legit textbook

He's just plain rude. Be ready to be embarrassed in class in front of everyone. He does not care how others feel. He will make you feel so small and miserable. He will kick you out of class and eventually fail you.

He is funny and explains things slowly and in detail. I would recommend him. He also seems really nice and I haven't noticed any rudeness to students. He does not kick people out for being 5mins late. Or maybe not anymore.

He is really annoying when it comes to discipline. It feels like I am back in high school. Like the other people said, he kicks people out if you are 5 minutes late. He wont accept assignments 5 minutes after class starts. He doesn't like when people leave to the bathroom. He teaches sort of well but the class can get really boring.

Class was not too difficult, but his teaching is drawn out and inefficient. He was often rude to students and would kick people out for being 5 minutes late. One day he was outraged someone was leaving to go to the bathroom. Would not recommend.

Gustavo is a very good professor. He is fair and cares about his students. He wants the class to participate, and for those who see college as an extension of high school I would not advise taking this course. For those who said he isn't clear, try retaking the course with Dadhka. Read the textbook, do the homeworks, you'll do well.

He was a really funny, nice guy. If you go to class, text book not really needed to get a good grade, but helpful if you want an A. He really wants everyone to not only do well, but to actually understand the subject matter. Highly recommend.

Nice guy, his real only fault is his stutter can mess with how clear he is sometimes. Class is not hard but you have to read the book a lot if you don't go. He grades with a very nice curve and you have to put in effort for an A.
He is a wonderful professor. Dr. Jones was my thesis advisor. I recommend him very highly.
Excellent. Best biology professor. Very interesting lectures.

Dr. Jones was easily the best professor I had at NU. He's not easy, you have to pay attention in class, and there will always be something from every lecture on the tests. He was also my academic adviser for my entire time at NU and he was the only person at the school who cared about getting me through college.

Goes on tangents and loves to lecture students about unrelated topics. His tests are extremely difficult and usually test on obscure concepts that he barely mentioned in one of his tangents. He doesn't scale grades and there is no extra credit. If you are taking this class for a Bio requirement, i recommend taking plant ecology instead.

He's a little odd, kinda talks down to you in class though he says he doesnt, and has a weird sense of humor. but outside of class he's fine to talk to, is very clear about what he expects out of you and is very understanding in cases such as illness during finals week as long as you let him know.

One of my favorite professors here so far.  I like his teaching style, and that he shaped the class to make it more of an intro-to-college, since it's an honors inquiry course and doesn't really have guidelines.  Sit close to the front- you'll hear his jokes and understand his sense of humor. Extremely helpful during office hours.
Loves to talk about himself, arrogant, interrupts, shapes the curriculum so that the students teach the class so he doesn't have to.  Extremely hard tests.  Very boring classes.

I really enjoyed this professor's zoology course; he really knows (and loves) the subject. He tends to go on tangents when giving lectures, and some obscure facts do end up on exams. If you listen to and write down every word that he says then you will get a good grade. The lab can be difficult but if you put the time into it then you will do fine.
Hard Tests, impossible practicals, no extra credit, no curve, and if he tells you that he won't let you fail do not believe him.
If you have the chance, take him.  One of the best professors you will ever have.  Don't worry about claims that he's too tough.  He's not.

best teacher at nu, though can come off as arrogant. If you study and actually go to class you will pass with at least a B, if you skip class and dont take notes and look down your nose at the subject and the prof, obviously you will fail; tests are not hard, they literally ask what is in lecture; dont put down a prof bc of the grade you earned.

Dr. Jones is very intelligent and knows a LOT.  He is also very proud.  Treat him with major respect (even if you're faking it) and listen up cuz the stuff he's saying is fantastic.  A good guy to be on your side.  He's tough, but welcome to college.  Try learning something.
No Comments
Going from Dr. Dan to this guy was AWFUL!!!!
He is the reason I'm not a bio major anymore.
Good teacher
very difficult but also helpful
No Comments
Pretty tough, but worse than that I thought very negative and unhelpful.  Also arrogant.
Possibly the worst prof there is. If you're failing and he sais that you'll do fine...NAHH...you wont. You'll still fail. Getting him to know your name doesn't work either.

As a freshman class it can come as a shock. He does curve as his tests seem to be considered ridiculous. He uses similiar tests every year, so if you don't cover something it still might be on a test. This class is no longer offered on semesters.

Gwil is a good guy, his lectures are a bunch of slides and there is a LOT of information.  If you study it and want to learn it though, you will be fine.  He does not curve, so don't whine if you get the grade you deserve.

I'm sure he's a capable researcher but it's so clear that he doesn't care about teaching. Every lecture he would stumble his way through some slides he didn't care to prep for. One day he delivered a lecture he already presented! I felt so disrespected that even though tuition is expensive and I'm a busy student, he didn't value my money or my time

Hari is rarely prepared for class and cannot function without his TA. His syllabus is so unclear that he accidentally gave the exact same lecture three times in a semester without realizing it. He does not listen to students and likes to answer the question he wants to answer rather than the actual question that was asked.

Hari was the worst professor I've had at Northeastern. I had genuine discussions with peers about whether he knew the Systems & Signals content. If you ask a question, he loves to give an answer to a unrelated question and fumble his way out of answering your question. He obviously didn't care about my class and put even less time into preparation.

Dishonest about uploading HWs when he promised - we had 2 short homework assignments the whole semester. Exams worth 85% of grade. Scrolls aimlessly thru handwritten notes for the whole lecture. I heard him talking demeaningly about certain students' intelligence. Unprepared, incapable of answering questions, and rarely accessible by email.
If you attend lectures, you will do fine in the class. Class is graded off of mostly homework and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only thing that gets put in the gradebook are three tests or "quizzes" worth 15% each, 5% in class participation and attendance, and a final worth 50%. While he is generous with his grading, he does NOT curve. Only 7 people passed this one quiz with 80%+, the others had 40% or lower, and he did nothing about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For ILS he mostly just talked to us about the problem during the group work which could be a bit distracting at times but you could always follow along and get the right answers. Overall the group problems helped a lot for the quizzes and he would give specific formulas or hints.

Hari's teaching style is a hit or a miss. His lectures can often be long-winded but he uploads quality slides to canvas. No final exam and I personally thought the final project was well organized. He cares about students' success and is accessible.

PHYS 1151: he doesn't just reads off his slides, so attending class is pretty important. if you miss, you also cannot make up the ICA. He does a lot of practice problems in class, exams aren't super difficult, they are exactly like the problems in class, he will never put a problem on a exam that he HASNT gone over in class. Attend his lectures!

This is for PHYS1152 - he is a nice guy, he may come off very strong in lecture and a bit aggressive, but he is really smart and helpful. His accent is hard to understand at some points and he's very blunt, but overall, a good ILS instructor.

Forced to take this class as a requirement for architecture and it's brutal. Homework is endless yet useless for his 3-question quizzes—miss 1 question, hello 67% (not all of the time, but a lot). Easy grading scale (88% = A) doesn't justify the stress. Delay or take earlier with a different professor if possible!

Generally good but virtually none of the homeworks line up with the actual tests. Its rather difficult to study for them as you have to know the entire thing backwards and forwards to do well on the tests. He never does examples in class until the date of the test, wish he did more before.

The good: Helpful outside of class, very nice prof and is excited to teach

The bad: Although he is excited to teach, his lectures are very very scattered and things are difficult to understand. The lecture notes lack fully solved examples. Additionally, the textbooks aren't so great either.

Professor Hari was a great teacher for physics. The course is fast-paced with a quiz on the previous week's chapter each week which can get a little overwhelming. The quizzes and tests are quite easy however, he is very generous with extra credit and will always find ways to boost your grade. I learned so much in one semester and I 100% recommend.

Dr. Salter is an amazing professor and subject expert regarding colonialism and imperialism. She assigns a lot of reading and homework, but they are very helpful in understanding the course material, and she isn't a tough grader. Very kind and understanding if you need an extension on an assignment. Definitely take a class with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: shes great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shes compassionate, organized and knowledgeable. Your grade is attendance (you evaluate yourself), 2 weekly assignments, 3 book quizzes, and a project. Weekly HW is like 100p. reading and 700+ word HW. You ought to read the books. You can put in the effort and get much out of it, or skim for an easy A. But she was lovely; I'd take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Colonialism & Imperialism with Professor Salter and she was beyond amazing. She was incredibly organized, kind, and understanding. I learned so much in her course, and appreciated that all her materials were free and educational. The one thing I will say is that homework was due the night before class, so you need to manage your time well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Goated Prof mehn

Professor Salter is genuinely such a kind and caring professor who wants her students to succeed! The class structure is very doable, she gives extensions to students when needed, and she always gives sufficient feedback. The class is not meant to be difficult, if you put in the work you'll get a good grade. I highly recommend her class to anyone!

Professor Salter is amazing and I couldn't recommend her history class more! She's passionate about the history of colonialism & imperialism, and her lectures are always engaging. She's also very clear about what to expect with assignments and quizzes. Even as a history major, I think anyone who keeps up with the material would find it manageable.

Professor Salter and TA Dr. Benjamin Gray, were an incredible teaching pair that made this semester informative and impactful. You use her textbook, three books, and lectures throughout the semester, which could be a lot of reading, but grading was always fair/clear and they both left great feedback. I would highly recommend taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is passionate about the Colonialism class. I took 2 HIST classes to round out my minor and many of my classmates were Int'l Affairs majors. I succeeded and enjoyed the course, especially the capstone mapping project for which I researched the migration of an indigeneous tribe in Quebec. Reading not too bad; do them => good reading quiz grades.
Very caring and helpful. Makes you want to attend classes.

Professor Salter is one of the most thoughtful professors I've ever had. She truly cares about her students and made class time engaging even on Zoom. Her field of study is not related to my major but I would take any class she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Saltzer is clearly motivated and passionate about her class. She can rush a little bit during the lectures but she gives a great overview of history and makes it interesting. You get a lot of grades which is nice, though the debate was kind of disorganized and hard to do well on. Sit near the front of the class and you'll do well

Plenty of opportunities to pick up your grade, book exams are easy if you just do the reading, final paper and debate are pretty nice too, overall great lecturer who makes class very interactive and her TA's are very helpful too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I had a Northeastern. Her class can be work heavy, but she kept me engaged in her lectures all the time!

Heather Streets-Salter is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. Her class is a lot of work each week, but not too difficult. Additionally, her lectures are engaging and insightful. She makes every student care about history and the class as a whole. I could not recommend her enough to any student in Northeastern.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: KRH loves to talk about current events, gives great feedback on written work, and is always flexible with deadlines. I would highly recommend taking advantage of tea with Prof RH, where you can chat about class with tea. She also gives students the option of attending any and all class remotely, no questions asked. Amazing professor.

This Professor is highly qualified to be teaching considering her vast experience at the United Nations. She is also caring and very good at delivering feedback and making sure you succeed. Very easy to access outside of class and even served tea at her office hours. She deserves a 5/5 because she makes sure you understand the difficult content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: so so nice!

she was the prof for the intro to polisci @ neu class. she was often late and more than once arrived and said "I have nothing for you, really". she seemed very nice but she rubbed me personally the wrong way. may be others' cup of tea, but def not mine.

KRH is the best! Highly recommend taking any class possible with her. She has an insane depth of knowledge, is the most caring and relatable individual, and is guaranteed to provide insights into life at Northeastern, political science, and life in general. One of the highlights of my Northeastern experience and someone I will miss a lot! :)
I've taken two classes with Professor Rodine-Hardy and she is the kindest and most understanding professor. I would highly recommend taking a class with her

Extremely understanding. She is very flexible provided you communicate clearly (no last minute requests). She does assign a lot of reading for class but this can be skimmed over. Class participation is needed. Allows students to express their learning in multiple forms (poster, podcast etc.) not just long papers, although some are still required.
Professor Rodine Hardy is a tad disorganized but one of the most caring, understanding people you will ever meet.

Prof. RH is the kindest and most understanding professor! Though some feel her lectures can be rambling and the readings are too much, you just need to skim them to get the main points and class discussions were interesting to me. She is not a tough grader and is very supportive if you are struggling in any way - she wants her students to succeed.

There is no reason for Dr. Hardy to have such a low score. I took her class for International Political Economy, and having been warned about her, it was probably the best class I had this semester hands down. She is funny, she looks after her students, and wants you to succeed. Exams and Quizzes don't exist unless you want them. Best Professor!

She is a very intelligent professor who genuinely knows a lot about the material and cares about the students. Always available outside of class and very responsive to feedback. If you have a problem with the class or a reading or a grade she is receptive and willing to adjust to make her students more comfortable.

She did not teach us directly. She did not impart any material to us. The entire class was presentations, so I guess we learnt from each other. Still, would have been nice to have a teacher rather than an M.C.

People are giving Dr. Rodine-Hardy negative feedback because she is a "tough professor", that is VERY wrong. She is a very caring teacher who is interested in the course she teaches, she is very helpful in office hours (you will pass ALL exams if you go). Although her lectures may get annoying or boring, read, pay attention and you get an Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Rodine Hardy can get a bad rap, but I think in general she's a fair and passionate prof. Yes sometimes she does get off track in her lectures but to me recitation always made up for any blank spots. Only not giving 5 stars because I felt rubric could have been clearer + less reading toward the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I was nervous for this class because of the review, but it turned out to be fine. There is a lot of reading and after a few chapters, you get the hang of what you need to know and focus on. Recitations and TAs are super helpful. Prof RH is very knowledgeable and accessible outside of class. I learned a lot about theories and less about countries
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Loved when she lectured but most of the time it seemed like class deteriorated halfway through as she follows some whim of a discussion assignment where all the students split into groups and talk about how none of us did the readings because she assigns so much. Expectations for assignments are unclear but she grades easily enough that it's okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Boring

Lectures are useless, Professor RH talks in circles and rarely answers questions directly. She is disorganized and cannot manage class time so we rarely get to important material. Recitations are almost useless for studying because all you do is watch other people present. Heavy readings and memorization, and we never know what is expected of us.

A lot of reading? Yes. Welcome to the world of Pols research. Class might seem boring at times, you MUST memorize all the authors and their readings but if you are planning to continue in the field of PolS you will be thanking yourself forever for taking this class and doing it then, if you are in just for the grade then this class is not for you..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Get ready to read hundreds of pages a week! The class was only hard because you are forced to skim chapters for main ideas and for our midterm and final you had to memorize around 30 authors and their theories. DO NOT GET BEHIND IN THE READINGS. The lectures are absolutely useless and your TA will be your lifeline.

The amount of reading for this class is insane. The lecture is entirely useless as all of the quizzes/exams are based on the O'Neil book and none of that is covered in the lecture. Prof RH has no control over her class, students lead the direction of the lecture and the entire hour is spent off-topic. Recitation is absolutely necessary to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pick a country you are interested in! This class is hard not because of the subject itself but because of the amount of reading you are required to do. You have to remember every authors and their theories. Proff Hardy cares about the class but her lectures are so boring. The class is based on exams and papers. Recitations r super important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is pretty interesting, but there is so much reading. Like, tons of reading. Study groups are essential. Professor Rodine Hardy doesn't lecture a whole lot, but you do a lot of group work and discussions. She is one of the most genuinely caring profs I've had. Make sure you pick a country you want to research for the entire semester.

There is a lot of reading for this class. Like, hundreds of pages a week. It forces you to learn how to skim and get the main ideas. If you like Model UN, you might be one of the few students who gets excited about all the readings and takes notes and is a huge participant in class discussions. I found it difficult to keep up.

It would have been a more interesting class if she was better organized. We never knew what was expected of us and when asking specific questions, she wouldn't give a direct answer. She is a really nice person outside of class though.

Prof Hardy is clearly very knowledgeable and very engaged with students. She loves when students participate and is very eager to work with them. However, I did not enjoy her lectures at all, and I felt that we spent way too much time covering unimportant material, and not enough time on crucial textbook stuff.  The O'Neil textbook is ESSENTIAL

While I understand that people don't like her because of her disorganization, she is one of the better professors, especially if you're willing to participate and to do a little bit of extra work like reading the news.  Otherwise, no complaints.  Do the readings because most of the class discussions revolve around articles from the Rogowski book.

She is a professor who placed a huge emphasis on reading the textbook, but would fail at explain the theories in class and how it related to what you learned. Extremely dull lectures, and fake enthusiasm for her students. For her midterms and finals make sure you specifically mention the authors, or ull do poorly

Rodine-Hardy is very nice and teaches a lot of information, but I wouldn't recommend the class unless it is a major requirement solely for the amount of reading (120-150/week).  I did learn how to skim properly though which will be useful for my college career in the long run.  Overall professor very nice and TAs even nicer (Diane anyway).
Don't take IR with her!!! The class is boring, too much assigned reading, and she and her TAs grade incredibly hard/strictly. She sort of looks down on all of her students in a weird way.
Very dull class. An unreasonable amount of reading and she treats students like children. If you enjoy useless theories that mean nothing in today's world, take her class.
She's smart and enthusiastic, but DON'T TAKE IR WITH HER. There's SOOOO much reading; it's overwhelming. The lectures are insanely boring as well.

i had her for an intro to IR and I think she over did it. reading was about 140 pages a week. for an intro it was a bit much bt you do learn alot. Midterm and final arent that hard tho pretty simple but its because she prepares you really well with the reading and lectures. I ended the class with a B. tough but if you do your work you will be happy
had her for IPE. bery knowledgabe and a very nice person. looking back i definitely learned more than i realized at the time. have no complaints other than she assigns lots of readings.

Had her for a 100-level Int'l Relations class. Readings were 130-140 pages a week. Students complain, but her excuse is "you aren't in high school anymore, grow up". I haven't seen the halls of a high school since 2006. Her lectures are entirely theory based, and boring. I have done int'l co-ops and have a strong background in the field, hated this

I took International Political Economy with Professor Hardy in 2007. The class was really tough at times, but looking back I learned a lot so it was worth it. She is really nice and very smart. The readings were important and so were class discussions. If you're interested in economics, it is a very interesting course.

This professor is useless. Te content of the class is very interesting but the teacher makes it painful. No lectures but rather group discussions on the readings, that nobody reads. She has office hours for two hours before class... that's it and does not return e-mails. Take another class if you want to learn something. She does not teach.

I would highly recommend taking International Relations with another professor. Not helpful at all. All she teaches is theory and every lecture is the same (and boring). Exams and papers are ridiculous. This could have been a very interesting class had it been taught differently.
Sometimes you'll hate the class but at the end of the day it's worth it. A lot of reading but good prof, interesting material and class discussions.  (International Political Econ)
Make sure to give lots of examples. Always give more than is asked on a test or you will be marked down. Hard teacher, but definitely knowledgable, has a ton of international experience.
Well-informed and over-all ok teacher.  Keep up with the readings and you'll be fine.
No Comments

Easy A if you try but some people, like my group, just didn't want to try. He let us switch groups in the middle but I wish we didn't have any group work at all tbh. He answers emails fast if you need help.

Honestly, Joe is the most boring professors I have taken yet. I was in his 8am section but I heard that his 5pm section has just as many students attending, if not less. He usually just sits down and reads off of slides monotonously and whenever I do go to class, I end up regretting it. Also your group is basically the same the entire sem. 0!!!!
Great interactive learning environment, respecting every answer and question and never made fun of anyone. Engagement in class kept me awake after 4pm.  Well planned course schedule

Great professor. He really takes feedback to heart and adjusts his class accordingly. You do a lot of group projects, but they're not too bad and a great way to learn. No tests and minimal quizzes. Not sure why there are so many bad reviews. I would def take again and recommend to anyone.
This is definitely the hardest corporate finance section. Harsh grading, lots of homework, and lecture-heavy. Overall, repetitive and mundane classes and constant graded assignments.
Participation really matters and u could get a lots of extra credits if u participate, case studies were pretty easy and interesting, midterm and finals are really easy if u listen to the lecture
Participation points are very fair and achievable. Office hours are very helpful. The case studies are really interesting andtaught me a lot.

Definitely a homework heavy course, which was nice if you don't test well/ have time to devote to these assignments. Prof is easy to reach outside of class and wants to answer questions so students produce their best work
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: every class is just lecture lecture lecture. he seems smart and that he knows what he's doing. he's open to discuss differing opinions. if you know finance the class is probably easy, if you don't, it's very hard. he curves a lot and is reasonable on grading. no one comes to class because it's optional. if you try, you'll get a decent grade
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was honestly really scared to take his class due to his reviews, but it's not a bad class at all. Start participating early in the semester, as it will build the courage for the rest of the class. Go to his office hours, start the group case studies a week early, attend every class, and you will seriously be fine.

Very knowledgeable and passionate professor, clearly enjoys teaching the subject. Had a no-judgement environment and was very open to questions, and considered points carefully before answering completely

Professor Henry is a very smart guy. He is nice and definitely cares for his students (nice curves). With that said, he is not the most experienced professor. I honestly wish attendance was mandatory cause I found it so easy to skip (along with most of the class) which had poor repercussions on my grade. I would recommend but read and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I believe he did a great job at teaching us the technical aspects of Corporate Finance. Building a Discounted Cash Flow Analysis, calculating Net Present Value. Also extremely helpful and beneficial office hours for me within the course. He did a great job teaching and helping those who came to him.
quizzes are too hard but good otherwise

Joe is incredibly smart, and expects a lot from students. It's possible to get an A in this class, however he expects top quality work 24/7. He is also a very boring person, so you would have to tolerate that. I recommend a different professor, however if he is your only option then good luck dedicating a minimum of 8 hours a week for an A.

Case homework overlaps with what we were learning at the time, making it easy to apply what we were learning that week. Quizzes were really hard though but he curves. Overall very good, would recommend if you want to learn a lot

very boring lectures, incredibly tough grader, unclear grading criteria
semester long group projects (if you get a bad group kiss your grade goodbye)
if you are not 100% comfortable with excel you will have a disadvantage 
TRUST ME TAKE INVESTMENTS over corporate finance
Harsh grader

I learned so much in this class and provided a lot of case assignments that can be used for interviews. Attendance isn't mandatory (just need 5/10 participation), but if you want to know what to do for the weekly case assignments GO TO CLASS & refer to his slides/excel work. Knows a lot and if you have any questions he responds quickly over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: if you want to learn some technical and real practical skills take this class

Took in fall semester, and content and material of the course were excellent, case studies were hard but I really learned a lot because it put me out of my comfort zone. Wish he was more expressive, enthusiastic, engaging in class (not be monotone)
nt perfect but pretty good

Professor Henry is very dedicated to the course and understands all the concepts of what he is teaching. He truly enjoys what he does and that is refreshing. Hard grading though and class is heavy on participation.

Honestly, the material is difficult and the assignments are challenging, but if willing to put in the time it is very rewarding. I learned more from this class than any other finance ones combined, and the case studies are very helpful in applying the lecture concepts to real world. Professor Joe is willing to guide you when you need help
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is smart in this subject but his class is extremely boring and the workload is too much. His feedback isn't the best and the quizzes and assignments he gives require too much effort and are too mundane.

He is genuine and very smart, but teaching-wise, he's HORRENDOUS. He doesn't explain his Excel or topics and barely gives any feedback for the case studies. With his teaching he assumes we already understand the material, making it difficult to translate. Maybe he'll improve in the future, but if he wants to be confused and waste time, be my guest.

HORRIBLE. He's young, so it feels like he has something to prove in the worst way. Terrible teacher—teaches like we already know the material. Made us face the back wall during tests and REPORTED BASICALLY THE ENTIRE CLASS TO ADVISORS WHEN EVERYONE FAILED instead of changing his teaching. Unless you want to be confused and stressed, AVOID HIM.

Such a shame he isn't a good teacher because he is smart. Unfortunately, knowledge of the subject does not always translate to being able to teach it to others. It is a very difficult skills. His tests are by far harder than any other finance class/teacher. He doesn't do curves AT ALL and the exams are the most difficult I have taken at this school
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unclear grading, and extremely poor feedback. Lots of homework, rubrics are rare, and partial credits do not exist at all for him. The lowest grade I ever got at Northeastern, and I don't even know why. Assignments and instructions are extremely subjective.

Only 6 students get an A. Grading extremely unclear due to this weird curve. 30% of grades is asking chatGPT about the course content (not as easy/effortless as you may think). Super non-objective, unclear and doesn't give detailed feedback. Topics covered at surface level. Would never take another class with this professor.
no slides or book at all, just monotone talking. mid term class average was 14% and then he curved grades down instead of up, SO unfair
Worst professor ever!! The average on the midterm was only 27/100 with no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: I've learned more in 2201 than any other finance class, and Prof Henry goes out of his way to help you if you put in the work he expects. Grading is tough but fair, you have to read the whole question and round correctly, but he shows you exactly how to do it in Excel. Also he curves to like an 80, no idea why others think it's lower

Terrible lectures, seems like a chill professor initially but his lectures are awful and you just look at excel for the entire class, does not explain things and gets annoyed when asked to go over questions. No practice material given for exams, was forced to curve the midterm because the average was a 52 and only brought the average up to a 58.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wouldn't take class again, tough tests, homework harshly graded and doesn't really help during office hours or seem engaged with students during lecture.Should probably make class more interesting since half of the class is asleep or doesn't show up. Is a nice guy just doesn't make lectures interesting or truly care to help students succeed, sadly.

Nothing special about his class, had bland powerpoint and goes through the information during class very basic. However, BEWARE of his tests. He won't tell you this till the morning of but he makes all students turn around in their seats and face the back wall so he can see your screens during exams. Very tough grader, curves by only 2 points max.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: took her for comps clsss and she was an angel, so down to earth and funny. class was very relaxed and clear guidelines were set up. projects/ work is a lot but not impossible and she really wants you to understand. she respects that there is a learning curve and helped through it, very hands on. lovely persona

Henry gets a lot of hate but I think it's really unwarranted, at least in genomics. She teaches the class well, provides examples, and the learning goals are exactly what's on the exam. Her exam are honestly pretty easy and surface level. The class averages were always A- or higher with one exam median being a 97.5% which is pretty crazy.

i have no idea how this woman is even still allowed to teach. do anything and everything in your power to not take her class. tutors/tas weren't able to help bc no one ever knew what she was talking about. went on random tangents and would shame students when she made mistakes. she needs her tenure taken away or smth

Arrogant! Disrespectful! Terrible at outlining explanations and offering direct instruction. TA would give assistance on assignments that later turned out to be wrong, sacrificing my grades and giving zero opportunity to cushion it. I'm finishing the course with a 92.9, and she virtually scolded me for asking for advice to end with an A +0.1 pt.

Literally a horrible teacher. DO NOT take her. Do absolutely everything you can not to have her. Doesn't teach you anything then expects you to know it all. You won't learn a thing with her. She needs to be evaluated by Northeastern.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Save yourself. Take any professor but her.

Do not take her. My GPA took such a hit. She drops your lowest exam, but I had a medical emergency last minute and she did not let me retake as it counted as my dropped. I had already done horribly on the first exam and I should've just W'd the class. Anyone else for genetics is better than Henzy.

Mrs. Henzy is disorganized and confusing as a professor, and she is disrespectful as a person. I've never heard a professor speak with such self-importance and arrogance to a student before- not even ones actually successful enough to warrant an ego. Good luck to anyone who has the displeasure of interacting with her.

I think Henzy gets a lot of undeserved hate, I think that people blame some of the difficulty of the course material on her; I enjoyed the class but it is definitely not an easy A. I think Henzy does a lot to try to help people raise their grades, and is helpful at office hours.

W'ed this class b/c my grades did not suffice to get anywhere above a B. I lost so much motivation from the prospect of having to retake this course, but glad to say I ended it with an A now. Her lectures were very disorganized/lackluster, did lectures even on exam days, and coming to class was a drag. I would TRULY never recommend her to anyone!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures were good and she taught the concepts really well. Tests were straightforward and the practice quizzes let you know what kind of questions to expect. Henzy is really nice and if you participate in class or talk to her outside of class, she'll remember you. Office hours are super helpful and lowest exam grade gets dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is based on 3 exams and a final and the lowest exam before the final will get dropped. I would suggest reading the textbooks, using any extra practice that she posts, and making sure that you understand the answers to the questions that are posted at the end of the slide. For everyone saying she isn't that bad, she is that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be on top of the textbook reading because her exams ask for details that she brushes over during lecture. I think that during the lecture she focuses on topics that matter long term (for MCAT and other advance classes) but her tests are based on whether you read the details in the textbook and lectures. It wasn't that bad if you stay on top of it.

This class was pretty difficult, but if you learn how to do her class its really not that bad. She uses the same questions in her practice exams that are on her tests, and rips test questions directly from her ppt slides. She really isn't a great teacher, but if you study her slides before tests instead of studying the textbook you'll get an easy A

She's not as bad as these reviews, but she's not great. Discombobulated lectures/says wacky things. Come to class because she says things that show up on exams (not written down). She gives some buffer questions for each exam, but there are only 3 (lowest is dropped). Also grades with peer-graded homework and short quizzes with multiple attempts.

At first I was thrown by her using chalk and not ppt slides, but I ended up liking this style. I learned a lot more than skimming through a bunch of slides. The ant wranglers and practice quizzes boosted my grade and she drops the lowest exam score. If you're interested in genetics and motivated I think you'll really like the class.

This professor is very knowledgeable when it comes to science but cannot teach. She teaches as if everyone is already an expert on the topics discussed and has learned it from other classes and our own research alone forgetting we're students still learning the material and can be very hostile when you ask questions, she doesn't care & won't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely atrocious professor. Class is graded off few exams and quizzes. Group projects should help boost your grade, but not when instructions are unclear. Asking for further clarification leads to dismissal. No rubric for projects and must attend office hours to look. Is also condescending towards students during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Henzy is a great professor, she cares about her students and is more than willing to help if you ask. She provided extra credit opportunities throughout the semester and dropped the lowest quiz, ant wrangle, and the second group project score if it boosted your grade. As long as you read the textbook and do the recommended problems, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment:
*BEWARE*
If you are reading this and are thinking about taking Henzy's class for ANYTHING, please, save yourself the pain and DO NOT. Also if you're reading these reviews and seeing the one or two 5 STAR REVIEWS and are thinking, okay, maybe people are being overly harsh, please THINK AGAIN. Those reviews were probably submitted by her mother.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Its kind of sad that a professor can take a class I was so excited to learn about and make it absolutely dreadful. lectures are so completely disorganized that you are learning unrelated information everyday. does not use slides just writes random information that pops into her head on the chalk board and rambles on about it. avoid if possible!

definitely not the most organized, but it really just takes little bit more effort to pay attention and then it makes sense. sometimes lectures go over exact questions on the exam. but if you dont put in the extra work you won't get a good grade. she does support your learning, but is kind of like a backseat driver in it

Professor Henzy gets a lot of hate on here and I dont think she deserves it. She cares about her students learning a lot and is very open to feedback. Boring lectures, but if you just do the suggested reading and questions, you'll do okay in the class. Going to lectures probably supplements 50% of work if you dont go to them

Henry is my least favorite professor I've ever had. I worked so hard in this class and. still ended up with a C (even though I got a 4 on my AP bio in high school). She is incredibly disorganized during lecture and jumps around topics. She goes way too fast in class and exams are on stuff she barely touched on in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the most bizzare class i've ever taken at this school. jamie is such a nutcase. her lectures are disorganized, she doesn't have powerpoints, and no matter how many times you do the homework problems, go to class, or read the textbook, the exams never seem to reflect the material. and don't bother emailing her because she will never respond.

Absolutely terrible. The material could have been very interesting but was not taught well at all. Lectures were all over the place and she made the simplest topics insanely confusing. I strongly advise not taking her class.
Absolutely the worst professor at Northeastern. Terrible at explaining concepts and makes the simplest things confusing.

Henzy gets a bad wrap but is a really nice person, mid professor. Her lectures are a Q+A where she asks some questions, and then maybe demonstrates how to do a problem, and then pulls up an image in canvas. The material isn't extremely diffucult, but Henzy is all over the place. However, everyone I know has a good grade bc  of HW and projects.
Possibly the worst professor at Northeastern, avoid at all costs

Prof Henzy is just not a good teacher. She has NO SLIDES and no structure to her lectures. You leave more confused and she cant even answer your questions. That being said, unlike other years we are graded on group projects, as well as the homeworks. They are definitely very time consuming but helpful to get your grades up.

No lecture slides or online resources at all; not convinced she knows how to use a computer. Relies on students to upload their own notes of her lectures; will not provide review materials. Refuses to utilize technology; she draws by hand on the whiteboard and it's impossible to see. Very disorganized. Also refuses to acknowledge student feedback.

Worst professor I have ever had. Lectures are VERY disorganized. Quizzes are impossible to study for because some topics we don't review in class, so reading the textbook is a must. What makes the class worse is she doesn't take accountability for the fact that it is her teaching style which is why half the class is failing the in person quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This woman destroyed my mental health. Go to class, take notes, do all assigned reading, study every night- you will still do bad on the exams. If you ask her a question she will only confuse you more. This class made me want to drop out of college. The material is not difficult, she just makes absolutely no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures make no sense, and everything is structured awfully. You could read the textbook and do everything she asks and still do horrible. Class is a waste of time, read the book. Won't even give answers to textbook problems unless you make one with other students and will confuse you when you ask a question because she won't answer it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Most disorganized class I've ever taken. Survive off of the textbook alone. She just kind of talks at the class the entire time and doesn't have any tangible purpose or goal for each lecture. She writes some random important information on the board but your notes won't make any sense, and if you tune out for a second you're pretty much lost.

The class material wasn't super hard, but her lectures made it so confusing. She spent an entire lecture going over one topic right before the exam, and there wasn't a single question on the exam about it. Her lectures are disorganized and not in the same order as the textbook. If you email her with a question, she might answer with a question
Honestly worst professor I've had, none of the lectures make any sense and she is all over the place. She's also weirdly obsessed with ants.
Very unclear and explains concepts poorly. This class made me depressed.

Worst professor I have ever had. Lectures make no sense and are a waste of time. Her analogies make you leave class more confused than when you walked in. So much reading and most of it isn't tested (test material is super unclear). Absolutely terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Henzy's class was disorganized. She included information for later lectures on earlier tests which caused confusion (our grade was also entirely based on 8 quizzes). There were also a lot of readings and videos to watch (as it was an online course). Her lectures were easy to follow but I felt like I learned nothing in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You'll leave her lecture more confused than when you went in. She teaches different information to different sections yet puts everything on the exams so make friends between sections if you can! Her analogies are wholly unhelpful. The textbook is very dense but you will need to read it in order to understand anything that's going on.

BIOL2301 was the most horrific class I've ever taken. The online format is a disorganized mess and a complete joke. Co-taught by visiting assistant professor, and the two obviously did not communicate teaching methods. Material for future lessons would appear on current tests.

Don't even try to email asking for help or with questions. Good luck.
Conveyed a difficult topic such as genetics in an easily digestible way. Had a fun class that effectively navigated covid through use of group work.

I am taking her class online and it is just too much going on. There are topics that just do not make sense and is not needed for her exams. You can definitely see her trying to improve her teaching style, but there are too many unorganized lectures that make you want to self-teach the topics. Overall, would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
If you are taking her class in person: make friends, read chapters & watch videos on topics she doesn't explain well, memorize outlines, & use peer tutoring. With all that, U would assume u wouldn't need to go to lecture. Yes u do.

Despite this, she let's you drop the lowest test grade and you can see she's trying to improve... So 2/5

Professor Henzy is extremely disorganized and overcomplicates every single topic. I used to like genetics but after this class, it's a hard pass. She posts worksheets with her own problems but refuses to upload an answer key for students to check. Good luck, you'll need it.

I am fascinated by genetics, but she has made me despise it. She over complicates every detail, to the point where it is extremely unnecessary. She uses analogies that do more bad than good. If you are misfortunate enough to take her class, I recommend reading the textbook before going to the lecture because she is all over the place. stay safe rip
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the worst teacher I've ever had in my life. The textbook will be your best friend in this class. No lecture slides--she writes on a small whiteboard in a giant lecture hall. Very confusing/unorganized teaching methods. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures can be disorganized at times. Switches between teaching methods (slides, whiteboard, online content). A lot of the test questions come from the assigned textbook problems, so if you do those you'll be okay. Not an awful professor, just hard to get in touch with. She also makes grading clear and exams/quizzes are open note, including final.

Henzy is well known for being super disorganized in lecture. She tells you everything you need to know, sure, but not in any discernible order. Her analogies will most likely confuse you more than help you. I recommend digital notes so you can group your information in a normal way. Tests are decently hard but study up and you'll be fine.

While Prof. Henzy isn't the most organized and her lectures are dry, I don't think that she deserves the bad reputation that she has. She drops the lowest midterm grade, offers easy online quizzes with multiple attempts, and all the exam questions come from the discussion boards. I think its pretty attainable to get an A in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: yikes is all I can say. she never responds to emails, doesn't seem to care much about helping her students at all, and is kind of rude, to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are scatter-brained, jumping from chapter 1 to chapter 3 and back to 1, etc and at the end of the day the test is on ZERO material from her lectures. the material itself is pretty easy but her tests are so poorly worded you get questions due to poor wording. Help outside of class is deferred to poorly monitored discussion boards
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found this class excruciatingly painful. I used to love biology and genetics and her style of teaching made me not. Her power points have nothing of substance and her tests are hard. She doesn't give you any warning of what specific things we are need to know. She just expects you to memorize the entire chapters, 100-150 pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Henzy doesnt deserve the bad reputation she has!! She really cares about her students and you can tell she wants everyone to do well. If you do all the work she assigns, and listen to the lectures, the class is an easy A. The ant metaphors can be difficult to decipher at first, but once you just go with it, her class can be a lot of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The class is pretty straightforward once you decipher all the ant metaphors. The exams were extremely fair: all the topics you need to know are covered by the "daily ants." She's nice if you talk to her 1 on 1 but she can be a little rude answering questions in class. Just go to class, read the TB if you don't understand something, & do the ants!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class isn't too difficult, but is a bit unorganized. The notes were always given in weird formats, making it hard to keep up with your own notes. The class is 100% exams and quizzes but she drops a whole unit. During lecture, she would spend too much time on the easy stuff and barely any time on the more confusing material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was worried when I saw so many negative reviews before taking Professor Henzy's genetics class over the summer. However, I just finished the class today with nothing bad to say about the class or her. It's obvious that she cares about the class's success, taking time to answer every question. She radiates positivity and expectations are clear.

Not hard at all... Exams and Quizzes might be daunting at first, but if you listen in class and do her daily ants, it is pretty straightforward. I did my daily ants on the day before the exam and then I did fine on the exam. You just need to focus and actually know your stuff. If the daily ants don't cut it for you, go read the textbook.

Professor Henzy is by far the worst professor I have had at Northeastern. Her lectures and notes are all over the place and hard to follow. Even if you watch all of her lectures and do her weird ant stuff, the exam is always much more difficult than the preparation. She has made me completely despise genetics and has ruined my GPA, thank u :(

It's a pretty easy class overall, just keep up with daily questions, and not too much studying is required for quizzes/exams. All exam questions are based off questions she gives you in class. Class format is confusing at first, but it's fine once you get the hang of it. She's nice, is a bit quirky, but is not great at answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Henzy's lectures are super confusing and disorganized most of the time. I never understood how all the material fit together, and I feel ill prepared for the MCAT. Make sure to study the ant hill and practice quiz questions thoroughly if you want to do well on exams. It's nice that she drops the lowest test grade, but your grade is 90% exam still.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: yikes
avoid her. she made me actually hate genetics.

Henzy releases a document of practice questions that she pulls about 90% of the test questions from so definitely fill this out throughout the semester. Her lectures are not very helpful for understanding the content, but they will help fill out the practice questions. It is very manageable to get an A in her class.

Lectures were all over the place and made studying for the exams difficult to organize. Weekly assignments (for completion) that are on material she hasn't taught yet. I would NOT recommend taking genetics with her but if you do make sure to be proactive about doing the Ant Hills concurrent with the lectures and not all before the exams.

Her ant fetish is sooooo inspirational!! As a biology major, she made me lose interest in my major and genetics. She is a sub par professor and doesn't teach well. I do not recommend taking this professor if you have the option not to. If you have a weird obsession with ants, take this class!

overwhelming/confusing at first but once you get used to it, not bad at all. class is test heavy (90%) but she gives a document that she pulls questions from + posts supplemental videos that are actually v helpful. attend class + understand the material and youll be fine. very manageable to get an A in the class, but you have to work for it.
the content of the labs aren't hard, but the INSTRUCTIONS... dear god, what???

Avoid this class, if you can. The tests are extraordinarily difficult and the material on them often blindsides you. The lecture topics feel so sporadic you'd think you were taking three different classes at once. This class also has a lab corequisite, which is very straightforward and well constructed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Henzy is a decent lecturer. I only watched the lectures and managed to do fine on tests. The lowest test grade got dropped which was nice. However, she is bad at answering questions and often switches to the next slide too fast, not giving you enough time to copy down notes. She also doesn't go back to the last slide if you ask her to.

yes, the class is easy and exams are very manageable. HOWEVER, considering is the first class you probably take to learn more in-depth about biology as a whole after foundations & inquiries, this is by far the worst introduction to concepts within genetics. biology classes after this DO GET BETTER, but don't have high hopes 4 this class.

Had Spring 2020, so half online. Idk why ppl are so hard on her! She is not a naturally gifted lecturer, sure, but the quizzes are super manageable if you read the textbook and take notes! (the slides are straight from the textbook, so no new info in the lectures) She's truly passionate about genetics & is trying her best. Grade  quizzes

Taking this class online is worse experience, she expects you to understand material s beforehand and quiz on the powerpoint that she presents in class. If you have to take this course, I would advice to do practice exam she put out before exams.

Professor Henzy is not the best professor at Northeastern. She is not very good at teaching her students during class, and she expects you to watch lectures before the lectures so that she can quiz. I would avoid this class at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's a nice lady, but a very poor professor, as she doesn't explain concepts well, and her lectures are not well geared towards tests. Your grade in this class is based off of only exams, and the labs that she designs are very confusing and the directions for them often don't work.

Despite the bad rep, she is actually a pretty good lecturer. Skimming the textbook before the lectures really helps understand what she is talking about. The lowest midterm gets dropped. She gives you a list of all possible questions which will be on the exams (many will have different wording), so no reason not to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She gets a pretty bad rap on here but from my experience she was a kind lecturer. Definitely could've organized material better (lectures were kind of all over the place). Considering this was my 2nd time taking the course she explained things better than my first professor did. Definitely need to take note of EVERYTHING though for exams.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Grade is based off of four tests including final, lowest midterm grade is dropped. Lectures are like alphabet soup, she includes awful, confusing analogies. Makes it sound easy, claims questions are based off of master list but isn't so exams are hard. Need a 92.75 for A, 89.75 for A-, etc. Tries to help but is ineffective.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Jamie is not the best lecturer - boring, monotone voice, tends to ramble, tries to slip jokes into the lecture that aren't that funny. Classes are awkward, many students don't show up. Grade consists of 3 midterms & 1 final, but she gives you a study guide of questions very similar to the test, so as long as you can do those it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst profs at NU. She is a poor lecturer - disorganized and unclear 95% of the time. Used many weird analogies that just confused you more. She rarely gave clear answers to Q's students had just overall was unhelpful. Learned mostly from the textbook. Don't take her if you don't have to. Her tests were deliberately confusing.

Probably the worst professor I've had in NEU. If you skip her lectures, you won't get a good grade. She has a very poor teaching style, and you get graded only from the midterms and nothing else. The only good thing she does is she gives questions before the exam. But the questions on the actual exam are super tricky. Her lab structure also sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She might have sufficient knowledge about genetics, but her teaching style is extremely poor. She has a very difficult time conveying information in a clear manner and 10/10 times will just confuse you more - her lecture notes/ slides are chaotic and extremely unhelpful. Her exams are very poorly worded and made to deliberately confuse you.

Henzy makes everything seem really easy in lecture and then just goes way beyond the scope of it on the tests. Her lectures are all over the place, impossible to follow, and honestly just painful to sit through. Got better grades in much harder subjects basically just because I couldn't stand this class.
Jamie Henzy is probably the worst Genetics professor in Northeastern. Don't take her if you don't have to. Your grade is purely based off of the midterms and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lecture is boring and unorganized. She will try to explain a concept with weird analogy that will confuse you even more. She makes things more difficult than it already is. Also, her test is very random. She is the worst professor I've had in NEU. I do not recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Jamie's tests are convoluted and challenging. Her lectures are scattered and do not follow the textbook. She can be funny on occasion but also can get basic problems wrong on the board. I'd recommend taking someone else if you're trying to get a good grade in Genetics or even learn it for that matter.

Jamie Henzy clearly doesn't understand genetics. She made a mistake on a punnett square and when other students pointed it out, she couldn't figure out what she did wrong. She also can't calculate expected double recombinants. Her explanations of stuff she does know usually don't make sense either. Worst professor I've encountered at Northeastern.

Not accessible outside of class whatsoever. He would be late to office hours or have his own meetings during them, making it hard to meet with him. He put in maybe five grades for the whole semester, so be ready for a very skewed grade most if not all of the time. Very nice and has a lot of industry experience, but certainly not the best professor.

I wish he was more organized. Grading and assignment criteria are not clear at all. Can be condescending when he believes he is right (which he always does) by constantly interrupting students. If you want an organized class this is not it.

Had Professor Herlihy for Artist Management and Copyright. He is an incredibly awesome person outside of class BUT as a professor he is boring, unorganized, and EXTREMELY lecture heavy. He will talk at you for 2 hours straight every class. Lots of reading (you don't necessarily have to do all of it though) and take home exams (2 midterms, 1 final).

Herlihy is very nice and approachable, but his class is very disorganized. Not super hard to do well, but lectures run long and we were behind the syllabus schedule after like one week of classes. Also hard to keep track of assignments on canvas. Good for intro to industry, but not the best

He's a super nice guy, and even though the lectures can run pretty long, they were super interesting and really got me excited to come to class. Attendance is mandatory, but he allowed online attendance as long as you submitted a one page reflection for the class. Sometimes the class is a little confusing, but the professor is pretty approachable.

Sometimes the class could feel long because the professor would go a long time lecturing, but the lectures were fairly easy to understand. The canvas and syllabus for this course was a bit disoorganized, so at times it was hard to know what was due. However, he would tell us what was due in class as well as send announcements via canvas/email.

I like this guy as a person but man oh man are his lectures long. Talks to hear himself speak- even in personal meetings. If you can get past how much he speaks in a 1950s radio announcer accent, the content of this class was super interesting and he's respected in this field. Despite the lectures, I want to do copyright law for a living now.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you appreciate any element of organization at all. Though he means well, Herlihy rarely utilized the required textbook for the course or any slides/any visual representation. Herlihy will talk at you for 50mins straight with no structure and expect you to know enough for a quiz you spend more researching by yourself.
If you want to work in the music industry this is the class you need to take! he has so much information and brings it all together for class.
very organized and current material, take this class if you can!

He has a lot of experience in the music industry and means well, but his class is unorganized and not conducive to learning. His 15 question online "quizzes" take hours to complete, he'll send emails about new assignments the night before he wants them submitted, and he gets extremely sidetracked during lectures. A nice guy, not the best professor.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: David Herlihy is a sweet man and he tries his hardest but all of his courses are the same, they are unorganized and thrown together last minute. He emails us the night before class asking for large assignments that seem to just pop into his head. The content does not flow, the classes are not engaging.

He's very knowledgeable, but he can't convey his ideas or what he wants us to take away from his lectures at all. He does not use class time efficiently whatsoever and we were tested on things that were rarely mentioned in class. He also was away on a business trip for an important part of our semester long project. He wasn't an active teacher.

Definitely a nice guy with a passion for copyright law because he really knows his stuff.  3 open book/note tests online and 1 online take home final which aren't even too hard if you pay attention in class at least 80% of the time.  No need to do the readings either, but they will help.

Dave's a nice guy hard to follow in taking notes...Knows whats hes talking about but doesn't always convey it in the most efficient method...I wish I kept count of how many time he said "in gemral" instead of general. The quizzes are a little much to do on a computer and I acutally wished they were more traditional in setting and length.

One of the most interesting classes I've taken. It could be a bland subject, but Herlihy brings real/current examples from the news and his career. The tests are pretty easy, they are online and open book. Kind of long, but there were only three plus a final. Highly recomended.
He really knows his stuff. Very interesting classes.

He's a good teacher that really knows his stuff.  Gets you to think like a lawyer almost.  Definately a lot of reading and the tests aren't easy, but it's a worthwhile class.  Especially in this day and age.  He is definately the right person to be teaching the class too.
No Comments

Loves to go on tangents - difficult to follow and extremely difficult to try to take notes. Dave is a very cool person that definately knows the material, but can't convey it well. Very poor teaching skills. And his tests are too long and insanely long final.

Professor Hertz was an amazing professor for Cornerstone. He made sure everything was clear within the lectures, his quizzes and tests were fair and clear on how he graded them, and he was very enthusiastic about what he was teaching. Overall, would definitely recommend this professor!

Honestly one of the best professors in the department. Cares so much about his students and their well being. He will go out of his way to make students feel included. Grading is also easy, if you put in the work and show up to class you will do great.
Good professor. Nothing stands out, but he teaches well, and he is kind.

Genuinely the greatest to ever do it. It's honestly almost a bad thing to have taken Cornerstone with Prof. Hertz cause my standard for a good professor has risen to such a high bar that I doubt any other professor will ever reach. Fun group projects, challenging homework, but usually fun still, and you genuinely learn in this class. HES THE GOAT

Hertz is one of the best. He is a main professor responsible for the first year engineering curriculum. His class is amazing due to the amount of learning. You learn multiple skills that are useful while learning how to work in groups. Tests are straight-forward while the homework is helpful for understanding.
Fun group projects. homeworks are graded a little harshly, but are engaging.
Good prof would take again

sigma

only d- because i didnt do the homework

I don't know about the other cornerstone profs, but I feel confident in saying that Prof. Hertz is definitely one of the best. He cultivated a relaxed classroom environment while still covering everything. He was always willing to help with any questions about assignments or projects. It would be hard not to get an A as long as you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hertz is an incredible professor, who puts in the extra work to care for students. He goes above and beyond to plan unique experiences and projects to facilitate learning. The grading can be challenging, as a 95 is required for an A and the homework can be easy to loose points on. He knew how to cultivate an engineering community.

I was initially worried about the class as I didn't know anything about coding, But Professor Hertz did an amazing job teaching the language (C++ and MatLab). What I will say is if you don't know the language, DON'T miss a class, you will be behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Taking this class with Hertz made me fall in love with engineering from the group projects to the engineering curriculum like decision making, coding, AutoCAD, etc. I absolutely loved this class. I even enjoyed doing the homework assignments. Classes are super fun and have a laid back atmosphere while still getting curriculum done.

Great dude, great class, great curriculum. Hertz was very nice and a fun guy. His class was super interesting and very chill. Weekly hw assignments, straight forward quizzes and tests, and a final project.

Super funny. Very efficient with time, easy grader. And all but gives you answers for quizzes before them. HIGHLY suggest. HW once a week takes about 2 hours and no final, just a group project. Easy to reach at office hours, and very caring.
Awesome course and a passionate instructor.
Very enthusiastic, strongly encourages group work and promotes a friendly classroom dynamic.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hertz is awesome! He is super enthusiastic about the material and the projects. Everyone I talk to absolutely loves him. I learned a ton in his course and the course-load was fast-paced but manageable. He even helped me outside of class with a side project I was working on with the skills I learned in the class.

A great professor and an even better guy. Extremely caring and organized - every single assignment is planned out to a tee. I feel like I learned a lot more in Cornerstone than a lot of my friends in this department who had other professors.

Amazing teacher who truly likes to teach and is good at it. he is very willing to help and i highly recommend going to office hours. compared to another cornerstone teacher, i think he does give a bit more homework, but i'd say the class is worth it because you learn a bunch of cool stuff

Professor Hertz is amazing. He has a warm aura about him and is always willing to give good feedback or extra help. Definitely recommend taking his Cornerstone classes as they're really fun with his lectures. He gives a weekly assignment, which is never too hard but is very relevant for future engineering co-ops/internships and other classes.

Hertz has been the best professor I've had so far at Northeastern. Admittedly, if you have previous experience with basic level engineering, this class can be a bit easy or boring at times. But his projects are fun and engaging, and he is really great at making each student feel comfortable at engineering.

Professor Hertz is amazing, he is an interesting teacher and is really good at answering questions in class. While attendance isn't graded it is really important to go to class to learn the information you will need to finish homework assignments that are a big part of your grade. Overall Hertz is a great prof. who really cares about students.

Made an account just to rate Prof. Hertz because he is just that amazing. Breaks down fundamental engineering concepts very well. The weekly homework is interesting and challenging, especially if you do the extended work options. Exams are very easy, and the projects for both semesters were a blast. Cares about all his students and is just amazing.
At the begginning of the year I was failing. LOVED HIM!

Joshua Hertz is one of the best professors Ive ever had. He somehow manages to condense course information so that it is presented in a way that is both interesting and extremely easy to understand. You only have to know whats actually important. Incredibly understanding and down to earth guy, exemplifying great care for his students. Learned ALOT
Best first year professor

Professor Hertz is one of the best professor's you'll ever have. He cares about his students and conducts the course with passion. Comes off a little quirky at first but by the end of the course he's a blast. Could not recommend him enough. His class is also project based, while focusing on fundamentals. Would take again in a heartbeat
