Dr. Hertz is just all around an awesome guy. He's always happy and enthusiastic to teach, and makes the lectures engaging and fun. The coursework revolves around multiple different topics, (usually multiple per class), and can sometimes feel overwhelming. But Hertz is around after class and active on the online discussion board for any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: My absolutely favorite professor; he teaches material in a very understandable way and he is incredibly personable and respectful. The class is fun and if you do the work/grind through the group projects you will get an A.
This guy almost has a 5.0 rating for a reason. He's AWESOME and so nice. I wish all my professors were like him. He actually makes the class fun.
I've been with Hertz for a semester and he is the best. Definitely better than all the other options.

Two years later, I still use Professor Hertz as my standard for professors at Northeastern University. He is a pioneer in education and treats you as an equal. He doesn't just teach, he gives you the confidence you need to bring your own ideas to life. Glad to see that other students are having as great an experience as I did.

Hertz is a fantastic teacher. His lectures are organized and feel relevant. As a teacher he's relaxed, funny, but provides a lot of chances for extra challenges. He takes pride in his students and the work they do and is always willing to help out.
Easily my favorite professor. He's clear, helpful, and genuinely cares about your learning. Hertz is more than just a great professor, he's a great person.

Hands down my favorite professor. He's clear, NICE, and caring. He makes this my favorite class. Probably the best Cornerstone instructor. I got lucky getting him as a professor. He also makes the class very laid-back and not stressful but we learn a lot!

By far the best professor I had my Freshman year. Not only is he an extremely adept and intelligent teacher, but also just a great, relaxed person. He really focuses on his students being challenged and learning, rather than the grades. If you have the chance, you'd be missing out by not taking a class with him!

Best professor ever! Really helped you understand what engineering is about and made you feel inspired to work hard. He focuses on learning and not grades, and that is exactly what college should be like.

Hertz is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. He not only is a very likable, fun and quirky guy, but also great at explaining difficult concepts and willing to help you out. His lectures are generally pretty fun and he adds to them with his good personality. Homework and workload isn't too bad either. Overall, great guy, great prof.
love this guy. great prof.

Hertz is a great professor but an ever greater guy. If you take his class, you'll see that he isn't teaching because its his job but because he genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He is very approachable and helpful when you need it. Very fair grader and great at teaching how to code, use AutoCAD, etc

Hertz is not only a great guy, but a great teacher as well. He teaches you everything that you'd need to know for tests, quizzes, etc, and always is happy to help you out when you struggle. He's super nice, always responds to emails, and is available to help you a lot too. He may have hard material sometimes but it's definitely manageable.

Challenging course, at least for me, but I learned a lot. Prof. Hertz is definitely one of the best professors I have had at Northeastern. I learned a lot about programming, having no prior experience. Very reasonable grader, and really willing to help you succeed. Wish I could take more classes with him.
Prof. Hertz demands quite a lot of work consistently, but it's definitely worth it because it's work that you benefit from. His classes are fun and informative.

Hertz is a really thoughtful professor who truly cares about his students and their learning.  Although his lectures can be a little boring sometimes, they are a great time to catch up on homework in his class.  His homework includes memos which aren't super fun but aren't terrible.  Overall he just wants you to succeed so he'll be there for you.

Prof. Hertz was my favorite teacher this year. Not only did I actually enjoy his class, but he really cares about his students learning and it shows. I am super pumped he is teaching my class next semester as well. I wasn't really into engineering yet and I had no experience with coding or any design software he was great teaching it!

Professor Hertz is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He, unlike most others, really cares about the students. We took frequent surveys for him, where he asked how we thought the class and his teaching was going. He challenged us, and was a very fair grader. I learned a lot about coding through his class. I definitely recommend him as a prof

Great teacher. Knows a lot about the topic, but lectures can get a bit dry. The class becomes a bit hard, so it's very up to you to teach yourself a bit of coding. Huge payoff, though - you come out knowing so much more about how to code than other GE1111 students.

She assigned so many readings (3-5) per night and an hour-long documentary on top of that, which I thought was just excessive (especially for an elective). Her lectures were so incredibly boring, it was so hard to follow, and lastly the tests, the first test, almost the whole class failed it, so she had to recheck the scantrons, so hard for what?

She gives tons of extra credit, but the tests seemed a bit excessive. Also, half the items regarding the topics in the Caribbean and Central America were just flat out wrong. I took this for my minor, it was easy but SOOO boring. And the TA was bad and would never grade things until 30 minutes before the next test (5 tests in a semester btw).

Pros: LOTS of extra credit (17 pts this semester), will learn a lot if willing, popculture & engaging clips in class, last quiz is online, enthusiastic professor, grades are rounded up if within .5 | Cons: around 4 readings and an hour long documentary due for homework before every class, must do readings before tests, lectures can drag at times
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for a general elective as a biology major w/ a english minor. I really enjoyed the class and felt like I learned, however you really have to read the required texts/ watch the documentaries in order to do well. Tests have transitioned to be in person, however you get a 1 sided "cheat sheet" for each in class exam/quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Unless this class is required for your major/other anth classes you want to take, don't take this for an "easy elective." The professor is very accomplished and passionate, but tests are dependent on memorizing details from the 25ish readings/videos you must have done that unit (videos can be up to an hour). Not a hard elective, but def takes time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: very enthusiastic but it got very boring for me personally. only annoying thing abt this class was in person paper quizzes (4 of them, 5th online) for an elective class. for quizzes you will HAVE to know the readings and films as the short responses (has multiple parts) will ask you only about readings and films. overall an okay class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is very enthusiastic, but the amount of supplemental readings/videos expected to be viewed outside of class makes it very discouraging. She also made the exams in person and closed note, so you have to remember every detail from the readings/videos due to how specific the questions are. Your grade also heavily relies on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Hersh is an extremely passionate, engaging, and accomplished anthropologist, but unfortunately her class falls short. Tests are too often and too difficult, and focus on regurgitating small details from any of the units 25-odd readings or videos instead of actually understanding concepts. Time needed to do well is absurd for a 1000-level class

This class was so so so easy. The only real downside was that there were so many readings outside of class and that the exams pulled specific examples from them, but it was still very doable since all the exams were online and open note. I would definitely recommend this class if your looking for an easy elective to take up space in your schedule.

Prof Hersh was vary enthusiastic about the subject matter which really came through in her lectures. There were definitely excessive readings assigned (3-4 per class session, along with discussion boards) but the exams were very reasonable and completed out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kind of a boring class, but it's pretty easy, and the tests are all open note. There's a ton of readings and a book you have to read too. There are also like 1-2 discussion boards every week they're easy but take a while to do. She is a good professor and likable, so I would recommend.

Prof. Hersh was nice and a great professor for the class! Three easy take-home, open-note exams make up 75% of your grade. One negative comment is that our 2nd test took 1 month to be graded (the TA does the grading). But since there's always a little extra credit, it's really not too bad. Lectures were interesting and engaging. It was a fun class!

Super easy class but super interesting. Exams are take home and open book. My attendance score was 51% and still ended with a 96% For the lectures that I went to, Dr. Hersh is an incredible prof and anthropologist. She clearly has passion for the subject & very knowledgeable. Took this class for fun and I can't recommend it enough.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I will be so fr I barely went to Prof. Hersh's class. There were a lot of readings, and your grade came from discussion posts and three tests throughout the year. The class is fine, but it could be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clearly cares about her subject and gives fantastic lectures. Lots of reading but it's all important. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her presentations are available to students and very informative. You will have to read a lot of articles and watch documentaries and films.

Good professor and would take the class again, lectures were available on Zoom and recordings were available afterward. There were 3 exams and a couple of "group" assignments, with extra credit available.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Interesting course material, the lectures are available on zoom and recorded, 3 tests throughout the year with a couple "group" assignments and extra credit options. Nice professor and would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've taken four classes with Dr. Hersh and she is amazing. Really funny, uses good examples to demonstrate concepts, available to discuss outside of class, and gives helpful feedback. Highly recommend!

Dr. Hersh's class is very interesting, but it's a bit boring due to the length of her lectures. Most of your grade is determined by 3 exams, that are open notes, but ask specific questions about what she said in class, a film or the reading. Somewhat easy class if you take good notes, write her examples, and watch the films/ read the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her tests are ridiculously specific and you are given very limited time. The tests are heavily based on the readings and films which take hours to go through. She doesn't take into consideration that, as students, we don't have the time to complete 10 multi-hour readings/films a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had at Northeastern. Lectures are very boring and lack interaction, but attendance is not mandatory. She is extremely biased with her own viewpoints and her class is nothing more than a promotion of communist agendas. Also, quizzes are extremely hard but there is not much work required apart from that.

Do not take Professor Hersh's class. She acts like this class is a student's only class and does not care. She assigns several required readings a class, which are then tested on for the exams. The questions on the exam are so specific from the readings so you really need to understand them all. Exams are online but extremely time pressured.

The kindest professor I've ever had, pushed deadlines back and removed readings when the class was struggling with other classes. Exams are a little tough but are open note and if you study all of the readings and organize your notes you'll do well. A good amount of readings but she goes over them in class so you only really need to skim.

Professor Hersh believes that her class is the only class students are taking. She assigns many required (tested on them) readings for exams that take up all your time outside of class. She is completely unaware that her students have lives outside of her class and does not respect their time.

A very kind person who clearly wants her students to succeed- provides lots of help for exams and offers many extra credit opportunities. Very knowledgable on the subject and makes class interesting. There are a decent amount of readings for each class (important for the exams), but they're usually interesting and relate to whatever topic we're on.
The exams contain so many terms with details about films or readings; need to spend lots of time on it

She helps students to succeed in the class, but you definitely have to put in a lot of work for your grade. Soooo many readings!! You need to know the readings to do well on the exams. Had about an hour time limit for the exams, but they were open note. I wouldn't recommend this course as a "chill elective" as it requires a lot of outside time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A truly boring class. She is not at all as engaging as others made her seem. Her slideshows also look like they have been made by middle schoolers.
Professor Hersh was so thoughtful and kind, I would take any class she teaches. Even on Zoom she made discussions engaging and is so approachable and easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Hersh is clearly very passionate about what she teaches. Her Peoples and Cultures is full of a lot of very interesting and engaging material. Taking this class over Zoom didn't create many difficulties in the course, at times the workload was a bit heavy, but since the information is interesting, it didn't seem like a burden. 10/10 recommend!

I took three classes with her and never regretted it every time. She gives a lot of readings but goes over it the next day. She expects you to know at least the general idea of the reading. Pretty flexible with due dates. Knows what she's talking about. Uses a lot of social media to keep the classes entertaining.

Prof Hersh is very professional and deals with difficult issues with logic and understanding. I gained a lot of new insights on topics I thought I already knew a lot about. Her readings are a little crazy but you can skim them and be fine. Class participation is encouraged and can be really fun, so don't be afraid to get involved
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Carie is awesome, she brings a sardonic wit to all of her classes and she is a pleasure to have as a teacher. She expects a lot of her students (for higher level classes more so) but she is also very understanding. I messed up submitting my final paper online and she was like, "whatever, I get it!" Listen to her Anth podcast!
Very professional, explains sensitive social issues in an effective and logical manner.

DO THE READINGS. The class I took, People's and Cultures, was a pretty straight forward class. She took attendance and it was graded and added to the final grade. She doesn't give work, its all tests and attendance. TESTS USE THE READINGS. If you want to do well, then read.

Such a sweet and caring teacher. Attendance not mandatory, but helpful. She puts all the powerpoints online before class and plays clips that really help you understand the material. Three exams, no cumulative final - read the textbooks/articles and show up once in a while, easy A.
Great professor for Gender and Sex. She's awesome. you should show up for class, because a lot of the answers to the tests are right there, but she's awesome.
content is so hard, you will put in a lot of time and effort and can still easily get a bad grade. difficult class but amazing prof

Took this class last semester and this is not an easy elective whatsoever, so be prepared to put in a lot of effort and probably still not do good. The class can be very confusing and doesn't make sense. Problem sets are really difficult and felt like it was almost impossible to keep up. Lectures are long too.
I'm not sure I learned much of anything in this semantics class, but I love the professor.
Professor Littlefield was awesome! Super easy course :)

Heather was possibly the best first semester professor a person could have. She was incredibly welcoming and kind, always available/willing to meet outside of class, and the perfect amount of passionate to keep students engaged. There are weekly-ish paper assignments and she left consistently leave helpful feedback. Definitely take her classes!!
heather is the best ever

Prof. Littlefield is amazing!! I absolutely loved her class. Content was so fun, and I looked forward to every day I had her class. Homework is graded fairly and pretty easy because all the content is covered well in class. I highly recommend this class/professor! My grade was above a 105% the whole semester because of extra credit. 10/10 recommend

This course was definitely harder than expected, but it was extremely fun in how tedious it was. Though the lecture videos are quite lengthy, Heather explains each topic very clearly- making the homework straightforward- and has extra credit for each module. She is easy to reach, incredibly kind, and understanding. Would absolutely recommend!

Heather is excellent! The class is a lot of work since there is so much to cover! Expect about 2-3 hours of videos per module, and a problem set for each module. Further, there is a summative problem set which is much longer. She was also accessible outside of class, and was happy to meet over Zoom! I definitely want to take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is awesome, kind, and her lecture videos were so interesting! However, the class was a lot more time-consuming than I was expecting. MANY hours worth of lecture videos to watch a week, and you can't get away without watching them because then you can't complete the assignments. But if you do all the work, it is pretty straightforward and easy.

Professor Littlefield is an amazing professor. I took her class Summer 1 and it was really enjoyable. Her lectures are a little long and the homework does take some time. If you are looking for an A, you just have to do the work and it's easy to. There is extra credit for every module that can add over 10% to your overall grade if you do it all.

littlefield is approachable and takes the time to care about you individually. lectures were instructional and easy to follow. no exams; grade mostly homework-based (~1-2hrs of hw/week; no readings). only downside is lecture slides are kinda bare--most explanation is done verbally; recordings aren't accessible--so prepare to pay attention in class
Heather is incredible and everyone should take a class with her if they have the chance. Super friendly and genuinely cares about the students' thoughts.

Littlefield's honors inquiries was very fun. Discussions were a huge part of what we worked on. She welcomed every question and idea, and they were my favorite part of class. It's a lot of reading but the reading is interesting, and she wants everyone to do really well. The projects are tedious, but she gives clear feedback and you'll learn a lot!

The assignments were very time-consuming and not always straightforward. However, she is very accessible for outside help as she will schedule 1:1s with you outside office hours to help on projects. Checking projects by her before I submitted really boosted my grade for the second half of the course.

Ling Analysis is a hard class but Heather did her best to make sure we all were prepared for writing our papers and doing our research. She does the best with what she has considering each intro to ling class is different meaning everyone starts with a different knowledge base. She's super understanding and is always willing to work with you.

A lot of reading, but we had really good group discussions! This was my first class in linguistics, and I really enjoyed it overall! Heather is very compassionate and genuinely wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Nice lady. Very knowledgable. Expects way too much from her students. Avoid courses with her, if you can. The linguistics department has great professors, all of whom are much more reasonable than her.

Professor Littlefield is really funny and has interesting stories. However, I do feel that she is an overly tough grader. The assignments are interesting, but it's hard to know what she expects, and you get points off seemingly at random sometimes. I also agree with one of the other commenters that she can be somewhat condescending at times.

Incredibly difficult course that requires a lot of outside work. However, it's most definitely worth it. You will leave that class a much better student. Heather is incredibly kind and offers all sorts of help and takes all of your comments and concerns seriously.

Heather is very kind and helpful most of the time. She can also be condescending. Her assignments are very difficult and she's a pretty hard grader. She's always open to answering questions though. The key is to explain yourself in the papers that you write for her class; anything is admissible with an explanation.

Extremely nice lady, always glad to discuss the material after class and very intelligent and knowledgeable - you can tell she loves linguistics! However, Linguistic Analysis was one of the most work-intensive and harshly-graded classes I've ever taken. She's a great teacher, but almost too tough to recommend.

One of the best profs I've ever had. She's very smart and really knows her stuff. She's also incredibly helpful and HILARIOUS! I looked forward to her class every time. She is the goofiest, nicest person. Answers emails within the hour. She challenges you, but it's always within reason. love her love her LOVE her! I was so sad when class ended.

Good: super nice, passionate, incredibly knowledgable, willing to help, and energetic. Bad: apparently doesn't realize students have other classes and assigned a gratuitious amount of work (and I didn't procrastinate). Reasonable final. Tips: pick the simplest language you can and take phonology, syntax, and semantics courses first. It will help.
The class was really interesting but the work was really demanding.  She's slow on grading, so don't expect to see that paper you worked all night on ever again.

Work intensive class. Thoroughly goes over concepts and brings people of all levels to the same speed. Huge language research project of your choice - best not to procrastinate. She's tough but very fair and funny as heck. Quite dedicated and passionated about linguistics and helping her students.

nice, sweet woman. horrible class. attendance is mandatory (only allowed 2 absences..excused or not) structure of class very boring, most notes i've ever taken in a class. if intro to linguistics isnt required for you, i reccommend taking a different class.

Littlefield is an awesome teacher and person. She's sooo funny and down-to-earth, which is VERY refreshing in academia. Class has a very communal feel. My time commitment for the class is low since the only assignments are a few homeworks and a final. No book is necessary-- just take good notes and you'll be fine.
Great sense of humor and quirky lectures kept me interested and regularly attending class, but the homework kicked my ass. Probably the first class I'm failing but would recommend anyway.

She is a great teacher, and I would tell anyone to take this class. You need to spend some time on the homeworks but if you do them you will do fine on the final! its an easy class if you put in some time....she has a great sense of humor and wants to be there teaching you!

Teaches well. Good sense of humor. Homework was tough. Exams were reasonable. No need for a textbook. Has a passion for what she teaches. I recommend her for any linguistics course. She could be more clearer and give the bigger picture instead of focusing on details all the time. Great teacher. Always cheerful.
Very helpful. Really bright.  Loves the fulani culture.  I loved to learn in her class.  I  still remember the samoan culture from that book.
Challenging homework--NOT busy work. Grades attendance and participation. Good sense of humor. Expects a lot from students, but grades fairly.  You will EARN your grade. Good office hours.

Heather is an amazing teacher.  She's interested in what she has to say and makes the classes fun.  She's a tough grader, but she's usually fair.  She puts in a lot of effort and expects her students to do the same.

Prof. was a very effective teacher in this basic linguistics course.  Any problems with clarity came from the course material not from her lectures.  It was a challenging class.  However, she used a great sense of humor and good teaching strategies to explain the concepts.  Enjoyed it thoroughly.

Hard but interesting class. Very smart prof, work every class, mainly lecture. homework, midterm, and final, all difficult and time consuming. EC offered on homework. tests aren't curved. highly recommend going to class otherwise material very hard to understand.
He is such a sweet professor, with a passion for the topic. He can be pretty soft-spoken. The lectures can be long, but he tries to make them more engaging.

Mal is a fantastic professor, but you'll need to meet him halfway to get the most out of his courses. He's soft-spoken and an easy grader, so it can be easy to slack off, but you'll truly learn so much if you sit closer to the front and pay attention. He rewards good ideas and doesn't care much about the details; make an effort and you can shine.

Mal is awesome! this was my intro to GIS class and I found him to be so sweet and talktative. his lectures could get a little boring sometimes but the info was all online and his slideshows were easy to engage with. the labs were interesting and i learned a lot. the final/midterm were not hard and a good way to make sure i had actually learned

Mal was genuinely so kind. The lectures did get boring at times because you are just learning a bunch of facts about data but Mal tried to keep us entertained. This was also his first time teaching this class so the grading was lenient. Overall Mal is 10/10 and definitely wants to see you succeed.

Mal is super sweet and super funny. Always willing to bump your grade up if you correct your mistakes on assignments. The class material is boring no matter who you take it with, but Mal will always try to get you out of lecture with time to spare. Would highly recommend

I took his class exactly a year ago, and he is perhaps my favorite professor at Northeastern. The subject matter didn't come easy to me, especially as an environmental studies major with very little experience in technical or computer-related areas, but Mal really gives you every resource you need to succeed, and is so kind and funny.

GIS is a slog regardless of who teaches it. Lectures are super abstract if you don't practice them in the lab. However, Mal made the lectures as painless as possible and would always share his expertise with students. The midterm and final felt a little unnecessary, but he posts all the material you need, and they're straightforward. 10/10 guy
Very entertaining prof, has lots of good stories and is quite accessible for questions. Definitely makes it easy to get a good grade if that's what you're looking for
Although the class itself is difficult, Professor Mal is an easy grader, take his class! One of the best professors in Northeastern, love him so much!

Mal is such a gem. He cares so much about all of his students and makes the effort to make all his lectures entertaining while still being a great professor. He has the most hilarious stories and makes sure to connect with all of his students. Such a great person - take his class!!

Professor Hill is an amazing professor!! Took him for his Honors Water in the Environment class and he was very clear with the grading criteria - one paper, a midterm, and final (all open-book). The workload was very manageable! - Take his class if you can - the professor is great and it's an Easy A class where you learn a lot!

Mal is a treat, a sweet and funny guy who also knows what he's talking about it. The lectures can be abstract if you don't really make use of the lab time to practice the concepts, so definitely do. He was super slow with grading things, but in the end he did do it, and he'll give feedback directly if you ask.
really nice teacher. a bit lecture heavy but manageable.

Mal Hill is such a rare gem. Hes definitely an odd ball and his teaching style might not suit everyone, but he truly cares about his students. In the end, all Mal wants to do is teach you something meaningful and useful to you and your career. He takes the time to connect with students in a way that most profs dont anymore.
The Lorax! Good teacher. Funny and super nice. Gets to know his students and cares a lot about their success. Can go on tangents occasionally but is easy going. Fairly easy A if you study.

Mal is pretty good professor, he is very professional in the fields, and the way he taught is pretty interesting(Just the handwriting is very, hum.... hard to understand) But overall, the review sheet describes everything you need and want to know. Also he is very flexible about homework, exams and final essays, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Mal is entertaining and very enthusiastic about his subject. He makes constant analogies that often go off-topic and his lectures can be hard to follow, but showing up to class isn't always necessary. He's an easy grader- just skim the chapters before the midterm & final, only tests we had. Loved this class.
He is a pushover and doesn't care about the material we learn, only that people like him.  Take his class for an easy A but don't expect to learn anything.

I have had multiple classes with Mal and also worked with him as my faculty advisor. He was so helpful to me in working out my class schedule. He loves what he does and it clearly shows. Great teacher. :)

The man loves what he does and it clearly shows. He's not a stickler for attendance but he'll make a joke about it the next time you show up and keep right on teaching. Labs are straightforward and he has the best and funniest ways of explaining difficult concepts and making them clear.  Favorite teacher, hands down.

Nice guy who knows his stuff, but the lecture is totally pointless for this class and labs are right out of the book. No real due date for labs, and no attendance in class-- as long as you get everything done by the end of the semester, this is an easy A.

Good prof, on a first name basis with most students. Loves what he teaches and it shows. sometimes a little hard to follow in lecture, so speak up if you're lost and he'll explain it more clearly. His quirks are awesome and hilarious.
Mal is one of the best professors I've had.  He teaches difficult material, but makes it as fun and interesting as possible.  All around great guy who will go above and beyhond to help you out!
Very Poor Professor and unnecessarily strict. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS if you want to have a sane experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Unclear Grading till the end of Sem

Firstly it's very difficult to keep in sync with his lectures since he keeps jumping from one topic to another. And his tests are barely related to what he teaches. I wouldn't recommend this professor to someone who really wants to learn algorithms course

Amazing Professor! One of the few Professors at Northeastern (COE) whose courses feels like a Master's level course. Very structured, amazing assignments and projects to work on. Definitely would recommend this course to anyone in COE at Northeastern.

What I like the most is all assignments and projects in his courses has clear and detailed specification. If you found something vague, you can always ask for clarification.
His courses use Slack workspace and he is online most of the time. Can easily reach out to him for any questions and he gives good feedback.
He is very nice. However all the slides we used are same as Princeton. So I would like to learn this course from Coursera because thats free.
Nice!
Nice

I took Algorithms class under Prof Hillyard. He is a very organized teacher with clear syllabus and grading criteria. He really wants us to understand the concepts. The quizzes, assignments and final project all made me learn algorithms in the right way.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Well, it might be hard for someone to take his class. As he teaches at a relatively high level. I mean it is not a kind of step-by-step class but a class which supposes you have some background. His speaking speed is a little bit slow, but meanwhile, you will have more time to follow up.

Robin is a very gentle and kind professor. In his class, you can learn about how to solve problems in an intuitive way and analyze code in aspects of time and space. Also, course content is constantly updated and keeps up to date with the latest technology, eg. functional programming, new parallel processing APIs.

This class is designed to take an engineering approach to algorithm rather than a scientific one. The class has regular assignments and weekly quizzes. The professor focuses on solving algorithm problems for real-world applications & writing production grade Java Generic code. This course is not designed for algo proof analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Robin is a very nice man and an excellent professor. Actually the other review was mean and I don't think that was fair. About style of teaching, some people like it some people don't, those words were too harsh. Also, about the Princeton slide, professor has his own works on it. I also took his scala course from Northeastern, He's nice and patient

Well, Robin is a good person, he is very kind and willing to help others. However, His teach ability is awful. I took his Algorithm class. He uses Princeton Slides and hardly changes. What is deadly is that he cannot answer you questions about algorithms and he is boring at class. He cannot control the rhythm of course neither.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the best Professors that I had ever studied under. Approachable, understanding and has got excellent teaching acumen.
Why not just learn from YouTube?
I'm sure I would have gotten a higher grade in this class with a different professor.
Lectures get boring by the mid of the semester. The assignments are extremely lengthy.
Take any other professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fun to be a part of her class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i WOULD RECOMMEND TAKING A CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The lectures are really great. The concepts taught are implemented during group projects. No assignments are given. We had weekly project report submissions and class tests.

The lecture might be a little dry to concentrate for more than 1.5 hours but asking questions and participating in the class is always appreciated by the professor.  Presentations are prepared in detail and class notes are shared after each class. Easy assignments if you understand the basics and tests are based on the sample papers released.
Assignments are easy. Gives good grades

Grading was straightforward. Lectures were heavy. She did not take much effort to make students understand what she is teaching. Students were clueless. Score marks anyhow in assignments & Tests and get good grades is all that matters.
Stay away from her.

She accused me of using AI because my work was "too good," giving me a low grade despite no such policy in the syllabus. I only used translation tools. This is disrespectful to honor students who work hard and had 3.95 GPA. After my academic complaint, she changed my grade but never apologized. Her opinions was often subjective in class too.

Easy elective class to take. She gives 100's on homework as long as something was turned something in, the quizzes are definitely a bit hard but if you create a study guide based off of what she tells you you'll be fine. Easiest professor I had all semester. She is extremely kind and funny and made showing up to class worth it.

Professor Poriss is awesome! Super engaging lectures and super relevant and fun assignments (feminist music criticism, final paper, interview). Some of the topics are not the most fun (lots of Opera and 1800s musical stuff), but she does a good job of trying to balance that with modern examples. Highly recommend!

Great class. New and designed by her, which made it very flexible. Awesome professor, and super passionate about her specific field. Big thesis paper was massive, but she was willing to help and provided ample time.

Hilldawg is great. Nice class for getting NUpaths out of the way. Dr. Poriss is funny, down-to-Earth, and easy on the grading. Lectures are nice, the class isn't that intense. Quizzes, Midterm and Final are open note, the three projects in the class are easy. Great class great prof.

I really like Prof. Poriss. The class is clearly made for NUPath, which means it's very easy, but I loved her lectures. Fair grader, you get what you put in, and you don't actually have to do the readings if you know music or have taken an ethnomusicology class. I'm taking Songs that Made History next semester. Love you Hilldawg.

You will receive what you put into any class with Hilary Poriss. She is a fair grader, clearly states what she wants you to take away from the course and will help you if you need it. She is super positive and class is actually enjoyable as long as you put in the effort. Makes sense-why should a professor care about you if you don't give a damn?
Class is fairly difficult, but if you show up and complete all the assignments, you should be fine.  Tests are pretty hard...STUDY.  Prof is nice and very funny.

I love this woman. I came into this class not caring about opera at all, and now I love it. She is so hilarious and good natured and really knows her stuff. I'm not a music major, but she had me wanting to take more music classes with her. I would recommend her to anyone. Such an awesome woman!! Do NOT make spelling/grammar errors though.

study for tests and try hard and you will do well. dont need any music background altho that really helps. if you are bad at writing papers or always make gramatical errors, STAY AWAY!!!! written papers make up 45% of your grade!!! she lets u skip 2classes w/o penalty. class participation is require but not graded. very passionate & funny prof!!
she's really fun and knowledgeable about opera

Had her for Opera and HT2.  Very easy if you come to class and pay attention.  She expects a certain level of respect from students and perhaps people aren't prepared for that.  Don't send texts in class, don't come in late, pay attention and you'll do fine.

easy A. im not a music major and just took it to meet a requirement. she is nice, funny, and as long as you come to class, you will do fine. the first quiz might be challenging, but after that it's simple. exams are short and easy and she tells you what exactly will be on them.

She is extremely intelligent and passionate about her subject (opera and classical music) but she expects her students to feel the same.  Gives lots of pop quizzes and homework and seems to enjoy catching students off-guard.  Not easy coursework but required for music majors, so be wary.

DO NOTE TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER IF YOU DONT CARE ABOUT MUSIC. It's the hardest class I've taken at NU and it's a 101. She does not realize that most people taking the class have to take it and don't want to at all, its awful. Totally useless class that takes for to much work

I though this class was going to be easier than it is, you have to do recognition of listening on quizzes which is hard. No book used, don't even bother getting the one assighned, you have to print out all the liberetto's for the opera's being studied.  Nice woman, take good notes and go to class.  Can be easy if you put in a little work. No final
No Comments

It's not hard to succeed in this class if you put in effort and do the assignments, Jesse makes it clear from the start. I am not a theater major and you don't have to be to do well. Definitely would recommend to a friend, had a lot of fun and the class was pretty laid back, the readings also were easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy this class at all. Jesse thinks he knows everything but is not open other ideas or opinions. I tried my best but he never thought my best was good enough which left me feeling sad but I had to stick it out so I could get the credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jesse is not nice. He yelled at me and my group mate because he said we weren't good enough. He embarrassed in front of the whole class. I understand that acting doesn't come naturally to everyone, but he was out of line and I tried my best. I will never want to see Jesse on campus again. It feels like I'm back in high school with my bully again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Hinson made class very fun and engaging with several games that definitely were a nice break from my other classes. He always gave good feedback on our technique and was very accommodating to students who struggled with improvisation. Homework consisted of a few readings and two papers, which were not difficult and were straightforward.

Jesse is the best! He makes class very fun and you learn a lot besides just improv. The readings are light and easy and very interesting. You get what you put in and it's the perfect elective to take that's just fun and laid-back but also requires effort. Definitely take improv with Jesse if you get the chance
Best Prof, Best Class

Higger was amazing for ML1! All his lectures we're fairly easy to follow, and he's just a really nice prof, really takes the time to help you understand each topic. The exams were very similar to the practice ones, and although they were a bit tough, if you understood everything on the practice, you would do well.

Super nice guy. Only reason I didn't get an A was because I split screen studied for the final while watching a tv show. He gives study guides that are incredibly similar to the exams, which made studying so nice. Puzzles were worth 6% of our grade and could be really confusing. Homework assignments didn't always correlate to what we were learning.

LOVE THIS GUY had him for recitation, and he was very helpful with breaking down some of the more complicated bits of discrete. Made sure we had all the prep we required before quizzes. Would come around to each table and ask if there were any questions, you can tell he cares about educating a lot.

Professor higger is honestly the best!!! This man needs a award. he makes the class fun and engaging. although 4400 is a difficult class, he tries so much to make sure everyone is on track and gives so many resources. I can confidently say I can walk away knowing I've learned so much. Please take his class at least once, you won't regret it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Such an awesome professor. Has an incredible understanding of the material and is very kind.
Super kind and helpful.  He actually wants you to do well.

Professor Higger was a very engaging lecturer, and teaches you pretty much everything you need to know for homework and exams in class. Homework and exams were similar in content, and neither were too hard. As long as you attend lecture and do the work, you should do just fine in this class.
the absolute best. Cares so much about each individual student even in 150+ person lectures and gives clear and passionate lectures. Definitely take if possible.

Literal King. One time I was nervous because people had already finished the test & I hadn't, but he told me & those still working to not worry and take a deep breath. He's so kind and gave us chocolate too. He posts recordings of his lectures so if you can't make a class you won't fall behind. Tests 2 & 3 are like practice, but test 1 wasn't.

recorded all lectures, which made it easy to catch up, and made it clear what he was looking for on the tests. your grade heavily depends on homework, which is definitely manageable. overall, CS1800 is a well-thought out class and prof. higger is super engaging and clear!

This guy was such a joy to be around. Not only is he funny and understanding, but he is down to earth and an amazing professor. The only criticism that I have, is that the first exam wasn't at all similar to the practice. Take him if you want to pass, he's awesome.

This dude is the absolute goat. He makes it as easily as he possibly can while still maintaining a level of order, Do not expect to be able to BS him there are clear rules and everything is lined out in the syllabus, but he makes understanding discrete math seem super easy.
Hes such a good teacher and gives great engaging lectures. Hes super clear on what he expects on tests and hw and gives practice tests for every exam. Rly easy class.

Professor Higger was a super nice introduction to Computer Science for me, I highly recommend taking any of the classes he teaches as he ensures that everyone understands topics and encourages people to speak up if they do not.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GOAT. He is very caring, and wants his students to do well!!! He has very engaging lectures and frequently walks around the room to answer questions while he gives us practice problems. I would 10000% recommend him for Discrete Structures, he is the best person ever!
The goat of all time.
Prof. Higger is one of the best lecturers I have ever seen. He is effortlessly engaging and an extremely kind human. He cares about you and wants you to succeed.
Higger puts so much effort into making lecture engaging and worth attending. He really cares about his students and loves what he does. Wish more professors in Khoury were like him

professor higger is one of the most caring professors i have encountered! he really really just wants you to learn and especially in a low level class like CS1800, he tries to ignite a love for math and logic. super great guy, funny, and every test was take home open note.
Seems like a genuinely good guy. Loved his class.

Amazing. He explains concepts multiple ways in case you didn't understand it the first time and tells funny analogies/stories. Very friendly and approachable. Only area that was iffy in his teaching was the counting and induction unit, but if you took MATH1365 or stats you'll prob do better. Overall feel like we got an easy version of discrete.
Excellent, need more such professors in other CS courses.

he is a fun and funny guy. he helps students a lot even during class. he makes it easy to understand the course and loves making jokes during class. he even stays after for question people have. the tests/exams are a little bit of hard and the grading is a bit harsh but you can always ask for a regrade.

By far my favourite professor this semester. Professor Higger really knows his stuff and makes lectures engaging and informative. He had a very hands-on approach and cared about his students. I really enjoyed taking this class and wholeheartedly endorse him.
Caring and funny guy, good lecturer. The TA's will nickel and dime you for everything on tests and homework.

My favorite professor so far! He always makes himself available for his students. Very understanding person who cares deeply about what he teaches. Typically it's hard to get to know your professors in lecture style classes, but not Professor Higger. Nothing but great things to say about him :)
gave all 200 in the class chocolates during a lecture! math is not my best subject but he and his TA's offered a lot of support outside of class. very caring and cool guy :)

Easiest A+ of my life. Did not go to class. Did not go to recitation. All the notes are posted and the homework will prepare you for the tests. I never recommend skipping but you definitely can in this class.

Prof. Higger was one of the best professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and makes the lectures fun. It's clear he likes what he does. The homework is a large portion of the grade but you can do it in a group, tests were online and open note, they answer quick on piazza, and recitation is super helpful, go to it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great class, great prof
Great guy and very understanding. Lectures are great and are recorded. HW makes up 50% of credit so do do all of it!

Prof. Higger is an amazing teacher! If you go to the lectures and learn the material, it's an easy A, but if you already have some experience with basic statistics and comp sci, you can manage on your own too. All in all great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a nice professor and fair class. He explained things very well. Highly reccomend.

My favorite professor of all time. His lectures are so helpful, but even if you don't go to lectures his notes and online recordings are super clear and easy to follow. The only issue I've had is the grading (TA's can be harsh and take off points for literally no reason), but Prof Higger is the best!

What could I say about Mat that someone else hasn't already? 
Even though I had a hard time in his class(mainly my own doing),
Mat created a fun learning environment for a relatively hard subject.

I wrote a poem to express my gratitude. 

Mathew, tough class strife,
Guiding light in math's tough sea.
Awesome teacher, the key to glee.

Great prof! I didn't even technically have him but watched his online lectures for discrete and they were awesome -- explains the concepts clearly and also the most responsive professor on Piazza ever! clearly cares about the subject and his students and would love to take another course with him!
He is a passionate teacher and the best for discrete math. Recitation is helpful and I didn't need tutoring but that is available if needed which i have heard is helpful.

HE GAVE US FREE CHOCOLATE DURING CLASS. WHAT PROFESSOR DO YOU KNOW WHO DOES THAT??
20/10
Give this man a raise.

This guy is a human ray of sunshine. He's so excited about everything he teaches that you can't help but be excited with him. Beware, he has a chronic addiction to spelling "equivalence" as "equivilence."
really fun classes and kind professor
One of the best professors here at Northeastern.
Professor Higger emerges as an illustrious paragon of pedagogical distinction.

Professor Higger is amazing! His lectures are very engaging, and are all live-streamed and saved for future reference. While attendance wasn't tracked, each class had a short assessment due at the end of day. Homework is graded fairly strictly, but isn't difficult if you start early and understand the concepts. No tests.

He is a very nice professor, you can tell he is passionate. It is important to listen to his lectures because his homework depends on it. Him and his TA's do critique your code a bit, but if you just stick with it it is easy to do well in his class. (Cons: no rounding grades :(()

This class can be difficult if you don't have a solid coding background (especially the homeworks), but Prof. Higger's genuine love of teaching and supporting students in their learning really shines through and makes this class worth it. I appreciated having him as my professor a lot!
Gives good lectures

Class taken during covid, writing this review 1.5 years removed. His class was amazing. Breakout rooms were required to discuss solutions to problems with others which was insanely awkward since nobody wanted to participate, but his lectures were always engaging, informative, and the homework was relatively straight forward. Love him!
Great lecture and fun project

Great professor if you go to the classes and pay attention, but it's a little hard since they're so long. No assignments or tests are dropped (and very little test prep), but he does drop your 4 lowest ICA's (in class attendance). He's great at explaining things, so if you are taking Data Models I highly recommend.

Higger is a great professor. He is considerate of his students and cares for their wellbeing. He is always willing to help students both during class and after. He also provides great lectures and in class assignments that are very helpful for exams.

Prof. Higger is a great guy. He's really intelligent and clearly has a passion for what he is teaching. However, here are some of my complaints:
- Sometimes he goes too fast through lecture content and it's hard to take notes or process what is being taught. 
- The grading system is kind of stingy. They often take too many points off of HW/tests.

Honestly one of the best teachers I've had at Northeastern. His ICA's and lectures really help with the homework, though the tests are challenging but doable. He really cares for his students, and you can tell that he wants people to succeed in the class. Always willing to spend time outside of class to help students understand the material.

A great professor! My respects to his passion of teaching. Quizzes are mostly formatted like the homework. ICAs in class are manageable and always goes over them. Also, his review sessions for quizzes are the best!!

Higger is amazing. His classes are very engaging to attend. He takes easy ICAs in class which are graded based on effort and help a lot in understanding topics. Answers any doubt a student has thoroughly. Prepares lectures and slides really well and cares about every student.

Prof. Higger is easily one of the best professors I've had at NEU. I don't think he's been around long, but if he sticks with it I'm sure students will put him up in the ranks of Gold and other legends. He puts a lot of effort into planning coherent, engaging lessons and is super passionate about math. Grab him for any math/CS/DS class if you can.

Ho and his class were incredibly challenging especially if music theory does not come naturally to you. I really struggled in this class and found the homework and grading criteria to be unclear and confusing. That said, Ho was always willing to spend time to help me understand the material and met with me outside class and to have retakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Ho is definitely a caring teacher, however, he gives too much homework and if you are not fluent in reading and writing standard notation you are cooked. He relies too much on the textbook as well.

taken as an elective, thought it would be simple and easy. no. insane amount of homework (coming from an engineering major). tons of reading, hws are twice a week but take several hours, especially if you're acclimating to new software. attendance is mandatory. Tests are unnecessarily hard, given less than a weeks notice and no in class review
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor jumps right into theory assuming everyone has been playing music for 10 years. I do not play an instrument (music tech major) and i was given no chance to review or catch up and fell behind immediately. 3 chapters of work the first weekend, spent nearly all of my time doing homework, just for him to say “practice more”. Super unhelpful.

Echo what else has been said here. Lots of homework for this class which is always due next class which can be overwhelming at times. He is a great lecturer though and seems to have a genuine care and understanding of students, I repeatedly see him giving extensions and all homework and quizzes can be revised to improve your score.

Acoustics and Psychoacoustics with Professor Ho was the most difficult class I've ever taken in my life. With that being said however, it is also my favorite class I've ever taken in my life, and Professor Ho is one of the best professors I've ever had. If you're willing to put in an ungodly amount of work, this class with Prof. Ho is a must-take.

If you can avoid this professor, please do. He gives an insane amount of homework. Also moves through topics very fast and expects you to understand everything. Not very helpful during office hours either.

Professor was decent, class was awful. Very tough grader - if you got even part of a homework question wrong he gives the assignment a grade of 10% until the question is corrected. There is also a ton of work. If you want to have free time during the summer, don't take MUSC1119.

Cannot stress enough unless you're a music major stay away. This class is impossible unless you're insanely good at math and teaching yourself material. Doesn't review material from homework or exams and is willing to tank the class average(our last exam averaged a D and didn't receive a scale). Every review says he's hilarious but it gets old FAST

I love Dr. Ho. He gives a bit too much homework but makes up for it by giving amazing lessons and being a hilarious and endearing guy. He goes above and beyond in ensuring his students are understanding the material, even going as far as typing out the plan for the daily lesson in perfect detail so we get the most out of our limited class time.

Dr. Ho is a great professor. He really wants you to learn the material and great at explaining concepts. He does give a lot of homework but I think in the end that helped because of extra practice/review before the midterm and final exam. He also lets you redo your homework for a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Homework due next class is assigned every class; this is workbook exercises and sometimes textbook chapters. I recommend reading the book; it helped me grasp concepts, but it's not required. Quizzes start after a few weeks and are short. Try not to start the homework the day before it's due or this class will be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had an excellent experience with Professor Ho. His lectures and homework are difficult, but accessible. Outside of class, he is very willing to schedule office hours and give students extra help. On his homeworks, he has a great range of "easy" problems and more in-depth problems designed to challenge your thinking. Great class, highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ho is a shining light in this University. He is exceptionally talented, passionate, and genuinely cares about his students. He is very accessible outside of class and wants to see you succeed. Although the course content is hard, you will learn a lot, and he wants to support you in your learning. If you get the chance, take his class.
Professor Ho is super talented and really wants students to learn the knowledge. A LOT of homework tough.

Professor Ho was great - super friendly and cracked jokes throughout class. In general, the classroom had a welcoming environment between both Prof. Ho and the students. There is a bit of homework, but it's definitely nothing out of the ordinary, and he makes it manageable/is flexible about deadlines as well.

Dr. Ho is great, he cares about his students and facilitates an open and comfortable learning environment. You can tell he is really passionate about the subject matter and very much an expert. You should get ready to do a good amount of homework if you're planning on taking this class, but it's not anything that won't benefit you in the long run!

Hubert is a beast. 10/10 music professor, he really makes the NU music program worth it. I did a few of his classes. He's highly skilled as a musician and he's pretty good at explaining things if you ask questions. The work is not usually very easy but it is never a lot so you get to explore things well. And he is funny and very aware.

Very fun professor, a bit silly. Tries really hard to make sure you understand the material, and he will call on every person in class so if you're shy be prepared. A reasonable amount of homework that you don't automatically get an A on but if you keep up you'll be fine. Lots of group discussion
Such an awful professor. Inconsiderate, so much work. This class literally made me break down 3 times a week. Avoid, especially if you run anxious. He has good intentions, but NOT a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: As someone who's never taken a music theory course before, I found his class to be one of the hardest things I've ever taken. He moves really, really fast in the class, so it was difficult for me to catch up. Seems like a good person, but i wouldn't take a course from him unless i was an experienced musician.

Professor Ho is really humorous, and he always made the class interesting by playing us some songs to explain the music theory. He knows everyone's names because he gets everyone engaged in class. There are a lot of quizzes but very easy as long as you understand the theory. One of my favorite class at Northeastern! Recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE FILM MUSIC! This may seem like an easy A elective, but it is anything but. Even though this class is for non-majors, he takes this class way too seriously. There are so many assignments and readings every week, and you need to watch at least one movie a week. He is disorganized and unclear and grades the essays too harshly.
Ho is an experience. He's very nice and kind of bizarre. I had a faint feeling of anxiety whenever I was in his class, but it's better than being bored. I would recommend.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! I cannot stress enough how bad it was. The professor is not bad, but the content is impossible for an 1100 class. If you are not a music major STAY AWAY. Taking this class was probably my worst mistake in Northeastern

Very charismatic professor with a corny sense of humor. He teaches at a very fast pace, but slows down if students ask and seems to be learning to ask students if he needs to slow down. Weekly quizzes, and nightly homeworks, with a final project and two exams. He's probably the most likely teacher to really get you excited about music theory.

Having Professor Ho for Film Music has been a nightmare. The timeline for assignments in class is so messed up that you never end up completing them all. He assigns group papers with a short page limit, so you cannot add enough info to get a good grade. He also expects you to write critical analyses WHILE using other sources.... Stay away.

Professor ho is a brilliant professor, very skilled in music. hes a little unclear sometimes and expects you to know dates from the syllabus without him explicitly saying so. class was pretty easy and straightforward

I've had professor Ho for 3 different classes now, and I'll be taking a 4th with him in the Fall. He is a brilliant mind, a hilarious (but corny) guy, and is always willing to help students in need. He moves very quickly but will slow down when asked. Some people won't like how upfront he is, but honestly, this man is a genius, take his classes.

Hubert Ho has changed the way I see music, arrange my furniture and talk to my friends and family. He is ridiculous. Did I mention he has perfect pitch? Honestly, Hubert is a great guy, with a sense of humor and a firm understanding of his field. Class flies by (my first time check is usually half way through class) and Hubert makes it interesting.

Great professor, really goes in depth individually correcting your capstone drafts so you know exactly what you need to do to get a 100. Keeps things light - makes a lot of jokes and plays a lot of videos but also seriously knows what he's talking about. Majored in physics/music at harvard so yeah, smart guy

Hubert is not afraid to act silly in front of the class in order to get his point across. He actually cares about students and always answered the few questions I had completely. I really enjoyed his class and learned aspects of film that I'll never forget. I think he's a great teacher overall and the class was easy.

He's a nice guy. He explains things pretty well and the mid-term and final aren't so bad if you follow his powerpoints and pay attention in class. He's not afraid to sound a little dorky when he starts humming out different tunes, and I'm glad he does because it really helps you understand exactly what he's talking about. Recommended.

great guy but definitely a little disorganized, sometimes late too. honestly once he gets in his zone he does a great job explaining concepts, but you have to follow closely. if you need a lot of structure and organized lectures probably not the professor for you

If I could go back in time and select this professor again, I'd want to know that he is consistently 5-10 minutes late to class, always unorganized, never answers emails, late on grading, never uploads grades to canvas, and doesn't show up to office hours.

Chill guy tho
Very disorganized. Doesn't read emails or post lecture notes at all. Always late in posting grades. Quizzes are mostly easy if you do the homework. Final was really difficult.

He is a very caring and approachable person. The lectures can be a bit hard to follow, but easy to understand if you skim over the textbook or attend office hours. Only wished he provided more supplementals like answer key and notes. Also, a pretty slow grader (didn't get all weekly quizzes back before the next exam).

Don't take this professor if you need an organized lecture to succeed. He is always late and in such a rush while doing his lecture. He is all over the place during lectures and the whole course in general. He gets extremely distracted and goes down a rabbit hole for half of the class. He doesn't know how to teach in a clear way. I would avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had. Very kind, but ineffective as a teacher. Disorganized, constantly late, doesn't post ANY supplemental material on Canvas (notes, practice, answer keys), slow grader, rambles during lectures, and NEVER responds to emails. Only take his class if you're ok with self-learning and don't require any communication with your prof.
He's an easy grader and very approachable. Explained concepts in an easy to understand way. The class had a great personality!

Hogancamp's lectures are sometimes hard to follow, but if you take the time to skim over the textbook and go to his office hours he clarifies everything. He's a caring teacher who grades very leniently and is passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very easy grader
Rambles a little and can sometimes be disorganized but very genuine and understanding guy.

Very kind. Genuinely very helpful, especially at office hours or if you ask questions. A bit disorganized, but not as bad as these reviews make it seem. We usually got our quizzes/grades within a couple of days.
Very nice but very unorganized

Mid Hogancamp. He was constantly disorganized in appearance and in his lectures. We would be told not to worry about certain topics and then those same topics would make up the entire weekly quiz. I would have rather taken this class with a chimpanzee teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Every single grade is late. Expect to wait for homework grades and feedback for over a month. Expect random changes in the homework and syllabus and no respect for your time. Sent a notification after class that the homework was due the next day even though he has posted it to be due in a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Pros: Kind teacher. Will talk to you about your academic path. Academic with ties to research. Knows what he's talking about and passionate about maths. Very lax with hw deadlines

Cons: VERY disorganized. Does not respond to emails. Lectures are unclear/ ramble. Very slow grader.

ONLY TAKE IF you'd trade self-study for a nice prof with lax grades
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: By far the worst teacher I've ever encountered. Spent multiple hours in study groups every week prior to every quiz teaching ourselves all of the material. Refused to give practice quizzes when our class asked numerous times. Never responds to emails. Does not organize online notes and they were the only resource we had to learn material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible.

This professor doesn't teach directly from the textbook making it hard to study from it. He only posts his hand written notes from lectures on our canvas page and gives no other material to help with the course. When he grades homework he doesn't correct our errors so we don't know the right answers for the exams.

The professor has a strong materials background. However, this course is quite intensive, covering a broad range of topics including atomic structure, electron configuration, crystalline lattice, miller index, defects, phase diagram, phase transformations, diffusion, polymers, mechanical properties, and strengthening mechanisms. Not an easy course

Her class is pretty intense. I'd recommend it if you really want to learn, but if you're not very interested in research or science, it may not be the best fit. She is a responsible and hardworking professor and sets high standards, especially in research.

I learned so much from Prof Zhu in MATL6280. The course content was vast. There were topics that were more difficult; she gave great attention to those topics for students to cement concepts. The lectures were long but definitely all necessary for a deep understanding of the content. Performing well on the final presentation is a must for an A!

I learned a lot about battery materials, how battery works, and how they're manufactured. This course truly changed my future career plans. I'm very confident I can pursue battery companies after this course.
She is very knowledgeable, and I learned a lot in the class.
I got 94 in the final. She always responds to emails promptly. I learnt a lot in this class. It inspires me to pursue a career in Materials in the future.

I took her class and scored 97 out of 100 on Midterm 1 and 91 out of 100 on Midterm 2. Her class is well organized. However, this course includes many concepts, terminologies, and calculations, so it does require additional efforts to read textbook outside of class. I personally have no difficulty understanding her lectures. Just my experiences.
It is hard to understand the professor. She will help when asked questions but the explanations are difficult to understand as well

I'm in Professor Zhu's Materials class this semester. This Thursday, when I asked her about my Midterm 1, surprisingly, she know every single number-even the exponents-at every step of the solution! Then when I saw her notes, I realized-she had worked through every single step of the exam questions herself step by step in every single number.

When I asked her questions, she always provided detailed, step by step explanations. A responsible professor. However, she seems not in industrial engineering. I'm quite surprised a professor in another field was assigned to teach this senior IE core course.

I took her class in spring 2020, during the hit of COVID 19 pandemic. While many classes faced challenges during that time, her classes always ran smoothly. She was consistently punctual and never missed a class due to COVID. Well, she had an accent. But I'm from Texas myself. I'm proud of my Texas accent. This is where I'm from. How can we blame?

I had the opportunity to work with Prof. Zhu for two semesters in IE4530-first as a student in her class and later as TA. During my time as her student in the Fall 2025, I was truly impressed by her dedication. Despite being 9 months pregnant, she stood and lectured for 100 minutes without any complain or excuses. This left lasting memory.

I'm in her ME2340 this semester. Based on my experience, Professor Zhu is approachable, smart, and passionate about the class. Her slides are well organized. She come to class with sufficient preparation. When I ask her question, she always response with patience and clarity. Meanwhile, she encourage us  to her office hour. She is responsible.
Worst college Professor EVER. Never take her class or work with her. Beware Bad Experience.

The first midterm is in a week and I still don't know what he was trying to "teach" in week one. He stands at the board and writes equations for an hour with no explanation of how to use them. The language in the textbook isn't any clearer. He continuously says we'll learn how to use it next week. Weeks have past and nothing has come together yet.

Great Professor. Not sure why he has so many bad reviews, but, for my class, he was a good lecturer, graded fairly, and cared about students. There were 2 midterms that were open book, and 1 final that was open book take home. The lab manual is horrendous, but the TA was helpful. If you put in the work to understand the material, you'll do well.

Homeworks do not prepare you AT ALL for exams. Exams arent on topics we covered, majority of class fails. Gets upset when you ask him questions outside of lecture time. Would not take again, avoid 100%
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very dry lectures that consist of him standing at a board and writing down equations. Calls exams easy and then fails the majority of the class. Skips steps as if they were obvious and then wonders why students don't understand the concept. If you take his class, prepare for A LOT of homework (that barely impacts your grade at all).
not a good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Boring, non-helpful classes. AVOID IF YOU CAN!

Avoid this professor. His lectures involve him writing on the board for hours with little class interaction. Assigns very long HW's every week that are barely worth part of your grade. Midterm and Final are impossible and teacher does nothing to prepare you except tells you to "read the book" . Makes the class think they're failing entire semester.
No Comments
His voice makes you sleepy in class. He's always immersed in his own world, you cannot not learn anything from him in class.

Very cool prof! If you want a deep understanding of the mathematical side of Machine Learning, take his class. He focuses heavily on the theoretical aspects, which is rare and valuable. Despite the rigor, he is extremely understanding and patient and is always willing to go the extra mile to explain things during office hours.
Sometimes he UNSURE of what hes trying to say. Poor communication skills.

had him for cs4100 but that wasnt an option. Freest A of my life. Midterm was takehome, attendance wasn't mandatory, and homework assignments had so much starter code I was basically just uncommenting lines and submitting. Learned absolutely nothing though.
He is a highly approachable professor with a wealth of knowledge. As long as you complete the homework and put effort into a strong final project, achieving a high grade is very manageable!

This course covers conventional machine learning materials. I have taken cs6140 under another professor, which actually covered similar topics compared to this course. But that one is more profound and interesting, I guess it's due to the teaching style. This course could be more solid and easy-to-understand for whom just got into this area
Course itself is great, I have learnt quite a lot. However, I wouldn't recommend the professor to take his session on. He is great, but not good at teaching.

I learned a lot from Professor Zhang's lectures. Each presentation/class had a well-structured flow and the content was relevant and useful. He is also very well-versed in the topic which meant that additional comments were typically insightful. He also cares about students and wants to help them in any way he can.
It's ok class. Prof knows a lot in his area, but he's not a good teacher.

Professor Zhang is clearly very knowledgeable in the field of machine learning, and did an amazing job explaining difficult theoretical concepts during lectures. His class includes a reasonable mix of machine learning theory (underlying mechanisms of machine learning algorithms/techniques) and opportunities to apply them to practical datasets.

Professor Zhang is approachable and encourages students to ask questions. Office hours are well-utilized, we often go to his office after class to ask questions, and he was always patient and happy to answer.
