Professor Zhang displayed exceptional knowledge and passion for machine learning, making complex topics understandable and engaging. Also, feedback was always constructive and insightful, significantly aiding in our learning process. Besides that, I love how the final project was laid out and presented which gave students many free discussions.

A must-take class if you want to claim that you understand why deep learning works. He comprehends and complements the difficult-to-self-learn textbooks very well so that the large topics fit within a semester. Through the project, he trains you how to read, critique, and build on the latest literature. He is very considerate and accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take other courses if you have chance. The grade is fair, but if you really wanted to learn something from the course, probably NO. You won't feel any passion from the instructor at all.

Professor Zhang taught this course very well and I have learned a lot from this course.

If you are going to do research, please this course. This course will prepare you very well for research.

Professor Zhang is a nice person and answers students' questions patiently.

The course is tough with often unclear lectures. Grading is fair, but a foundation knowledge is recommended. Prof focuses on theory, lacking practical examples. Would recommend other courses at Khoury unless you don't have any other choices.

Prof Zhang's class was a good mix of applied and theoretical ML techniques and was a fair grader. He involves the students in his teaching a lot which was engaging and conducive to learning, so would recommend this class! It helped me with foundations for my ML research and I think others would benefit too.

CS7140 is a challenging course, but you will learn a lot if you dive into it. Please take CS6140 machine learning before you pick this one, or you will feel lost for the entire semester. Professor Zhang is knowledgeable about the mathematical theory of ML. The classroom atmosphere is relaxed. Feel free to ask any questions when you confuse!

I found this class to be incredibly difficult and lectures/materials hard to follow. Homework required a lot of research on my own and slides weren't helpful. However, I thought the grading was fair and the TAs/professor tried their very best to ensure everyone performs well. As long as you show that you put in effort, you should be fine.

He is the best lecturer if you want to learn machine learning. He teaches tough topics effectively using his own words that makes us much easier to learn the topics by reading texts. He has clear instructions and offers support as needed on assignments so that each student can learn through these assignments.

If you have no experience with ML,take cs6140 or NLP,before taking this course. Prof. Zhang didn't provide any solid examples for each theory. I personally just learnt the topic from textbooks/online sources,and used the lectures for review.Northeastern should hire some professors who know how to teach and convey their knowledge to the students

Prof Zhang's 7140 class was focused mostly on mathematical deep learning theory. The materials were in-depth, and I learned a lot from the lectures and the assignments. The class is challenging and can get quite technical, so I can see why some students struggled with it. Be sure to allocate enough time for his class as it can be quite demanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang is extremely knowledgeable in the mathematical and theoretical aspects of ML and he managed to teach the core ideas very well in this course. He was very accessible outside class (also responds to emails in minutes) and provided excellent guidance throughout the course and in picking up research topics after the course as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is an amazing class. Prof. Zhang is very approachable. His brilliance and extensive knowledge of the field of machine learning are obvious. You can study a lot from this class, especially for the theoretical and mathematical parts. He is always available to help and efficiently explains every lesson!

If you want to learn deep learning, look at some free edX/MIT classes; if you're taking this for PhD, I'd recommend taking other sessions other than his. The lectures are super dry, often skipping showing how to solve actual problems. He didn't did do well explaining the concepts. We had to check lectures on the internet to fully understand them.
Excellent course. Prof Zhang is very polite, accessible and extremely knowledgeable in his area. Anyone pursing machine learning/deep learning will gain a lot from this course.

Took his course last year. He's probably good at his field but the course is poorly designed. Just read off the slides which just copy&paste from other universities' slides. He didn't organize them well and plan beforehand. Often changed the assignment's requirements at the last mins. Very little passion for teaching. Doesn't care about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doesn't release grades so you don't know how you are doing in the class. Lectures are just her reading of slides

Professor Nikolova was extremely nice and caring! She did her best to make the lectures engaging for us and brought many interesting guest speakers. There was also very little homework assignments, so your grade is mostly based off two exams and the marketing simulation. Spoke a little fast during lectures so sometimes it was hard to keep up.
Boring lectures
She mostly just reads off the slides, so lectures are boring and not engaging. Grades aren't clear until the very end. If you actually care about marketing, I wouldn't recommend her.

She is very average. Lectures were not engaging and 'in class activities', which were a large majority of what we did, were only graded for completion. She doesn't release grades until the very end of the semester which is really inconvenient. Good guest speakers though. If you're really interested in marketing, don't recommend.

She did an excellent job to make the class interactive, engaging, and fun; this was her main strength. I wish she went through the content a bit slower during lecture as she speaks quickly and typically ends class a bit earlier. Assignments apart from the two exams are extremely straight-forward and doable; however, the exams are quite difficult.

I had Prof. Nikolova for her first semester teaching at NEU and she was great! Super caring, more flexible than other profs with deadlines if you ask, and tries to keep class engaging. MKTG 2201 itself is very term heavy which is annoying, but prof did her best to make us love the material. From what I've heard, she's def nicer than other profs.

Hilarious class about humor theory and the ethics behind it. Prof is super knowledgeable. This is also a difficult class. The professor is not afraid to debate you, say you are wrong, or cold call; but he won't dock points you for flubbing a question or two. He is caring and quite fair. Bottom line: great professor, but not an easy A.

Really cool new class that dives deep into the philosophy and ethics behind humor. Highly recommend for those interested in that intersection, just don't expect this to be a super chill 1000 level class (i'd say it should be closer to a 2000 level in terms of expectations especially for COMM standards). One of my favorites of the semester!

Can be very rude/makes unnecessary comments, doesn't let you use technology for notes & doesn't use slides (hard to keep up with his accent), lots of presentations & purposely quizzes/argues with you in front of the class. SO MANY READINGS THAT DON'T MAKE SENSE. Has one midterm and it tanked everyone's grades. He is very funny & engaging tho.

Relatively difficult but extremely rewarding. Readings were often dense and time-consuming, but when debriefed in class, very interesting. The content started theoretical and then became more practical. Prof Hoppmann is likable and clearly passionate, but will also push you to meet high expectations. Prepare to get up front and present/debate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This was my hardest class but also the only class where I would be interested for the whole 2 hour lecture and never get the urge to look at my phone. It requires a lot of work and practice but Hoppmann is a very funny and engaging prof. Beware of LOTS of class participation and solving problems before the class, but it prepares you for the exam.

Michael is hilarious but also an incredible teacher! He makes the content very accesible and interesting, and I loved the introduction to logic and argumentation. A little heavy on group projects, but everything was valuable and relevant. Love the reversed lecture format of the course as well!

I've taken away lot from his class. It took me a minute to warm up to him since he's class is pretty intensive with mandatory attendance and no electronics rules but its engaging and he teaches in a dynamic way. A challenging class and the midterm is worded weirdly, but its very easy to succeed if you do like1/2+ the readings and show up to class.

This was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken, but be aware there is a lot of reading and preparation for each class. If you do the reading and prepare somewhat (just have a general idea going into it), you'll be fine. Amazing lecturer, funny, and always fun to come to class. Assessments can be difficult, but he's a pretty fair grader.

WHAT A GUY! I took his Legal Argumentation class first semester at Northeastern, and it was so interesting! The topics cover CRAZY stuff, and you really do learn a lot. The readings can be difficult, but he always makes sure to explain them more clearly in class. This man is hilarious. My roommates and I still talk about him. Wonderful professor.

He's so knowledgeable and he's great but he does expect the highest quality of work from his students. Be ready to really put your back into the work, but if you want to learn something real I definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst educational experience I've had at NEU. Least favorite class and professor. He comes across fun and jovial but the facade quickly dissolves into passive aggressive insensitivity. His pedagogy (teaching method) and course structure for the online version of PoA made me increasingly disinterested and dread attending class, the content and HW.

He is witty and caring and always has time to help outside of class. Reading the textbook is key to pass any of his quizzes, but other than that, the workload isn't heavy. He is passionate and extremely well prepared in what he teaches. I don't usually write reviews like this but he really is a gem. Take his class if you can.

Professor Hoppmann was one of the most intelligent professors I've ever had. He is so well respected in his field and is so knowledgable about what he teaches. I was very intimidated at the beginning, to the point where I considered dropping. But it ended up being one of the best classes I've ever taken. He is hilarious and caring, highly recommend

Dr. Hoppmann is one of the best professors I've had. He'll make you work hard and really engage with the material, and it's completely worth it. He gives some assignments that seem strange at first but are really valuable to understanding argumentation. He can come across as intimidating but is a great guy.

reviews.comment: He is really patient and good at explaining things clearly. One of the best professors I had so far.
Michael is absolutely amazing. He's hilarious. Amazing at what he teaches. Makes every lecture interesting. I never wanted to skip class
He's a little intimidating but he's honestly just a sweet guy. He jokes around a lot and isn't afraid to debate anything you say so don't speak without thinking.

I love Michael Hoppmann. He's brilliant, engaging, and perfectly aware of his own flaws. Principles of Argumentation was informative and truly useful, and I believe that Hoppmann is one of the most knowledgable rhetoricians I've ever met. He doesn't give the best feedback, but he does his best to explain things in multiple ways during lectures.

I hope this class is kept around for other students.

One of the best professors I've had at NEU.  Loved that he made you get up in front of the class to talk. Other people complain about this, but if you are taking a public speaking class, you shouldn't really expect anything else.

Dr. Hoppmann is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. Though he is an absolute genius at his craft, he's not a jerk about it. It is not an "easy A" but if you really put in the work and go to every class you will do fine and enjoy yourself.

Class can get a bit boring, but he is genuinely interested in his Classical Rhetoric material and teaches it well.  Easy grader and always curves exams.  Rarely homework, mostly readings you can get away with not doing, and 2 exams. Easy A.

Great public speaking class. Many speeches but they are not bad. The speeches are to help you get over your fear and to prepare you for all sets of possible speeches you will have. Very nice and only one test.

He's a nice guy but, he really doesn't teach the class very well. He makes us do group presentations (only 2 people in each group) teach the class a genre on classical rhetoric on which we have never learned before. He doesn't even go over it himself afterwards. His reading materials are really long and his tests have a weird format..it's tricky.
Hoppmann is AWESOME. He is so passionate and really makes you comfortable with getting up in front of everyone... A little nerve racking but altogether I loved the class!

Great guy, very interesting and funny. He makes Public speaking fun. I had this class at 8 am, and still found it worth my time. Pretty easy, four speeches and one test, but no final. If you try during your speeches, you should do fine.

Professor Hoppmann! What an amazing public speaking educator. I took his summer course so everything was condensed. However, he does an incredible job to help you improve your public speaking skills. We all loved him, funny accent. 4 speeches and a final exam. He's only here for a year or 2 more so if you can, DEFINITELY take his class!!!

One of the best teachers I've had so far. Extremely engaged in what he was teaching. You could tell he really loved it and that he knew his stuff. Very friendly and always willing to help. In Germany, he was a big shot comm guy. Wrote books in German. Lots of in class practice that helped with the material. 100% recommend taking a class with him!

this class is agonizing. class is boring if it isn't confusing. He introduces topics by giving layered problems and expects you to already know the material. if you've never taken calc before, RUN. he basically just takes notes on the book and then just writes them on the board with little to no explanation/teaching. if you go to office hours and display an ounce too much of misunderstanding he quickly gets condescending. just a bad teacher overall, your better off switching

How tf does he still have a job. In class he just copies worksheets onto the whiteboard and expects you to make sense of it- gives NO explanations . Lectures can be a bit boring at times but he is a really nice man who does plenty of example problems to make sure you know how to apply a certain concept. Homework isn't graded and as long as you understand the material presented in lecture you don't really need to do it.
Investments is a hard class at Northeastern. However, Da is an amazing professor, and he is so nice . He gives you the recipe to succeed, you just need to put it together and be consistent

Hands down the best teacher I've had in college. Super knowledgeable and knows what he's talking about. Always responsive even when he's traveling. I like that he uses attendance as a way to make us read the news and comment on what's happening every week. A little worried about the exam but honestly great teacher if you care about learning.

The instructor not only talked about investing, but also incorporated the current investment context to help explain the class, which was my favorite part! I enjoyed this lecture. This course is exceptionally tough, focusing mainly on exams. Midterms make up 30%, finals 40%, without a grading curve. Emphasis is on computational questions, without points for steps. Grades are base on ranking but still very challenging. Avoid this class!
