reviews.comment: legit best teacher ever. He makes accounting so interesting and fun. care for his students. if he teaches 100 classes, I would attend all of them. Legit good.
Posts a lot of material online, is very helpful when  you don't understand something and explains well. Good lectures
He's a super chill teacher, but at the same time is skilled at teaching the material to you.

He cares about the students, apologizes for hard tests, gives back extra credit. He even made helpful packets to understand information after feedback that we don't understand the material. He has great lecture videos in addition to in class lectures to further help students. He makes the content easy and has a fun personality. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!
The only reason to not skip class would be because the lectures are more efficient and helpful than the book. He makes sure to give a lot of practice examples, and actually cares about his students.
Great professor overall
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Hurley makes accounting more interesting. He way of teaching allows the students to be able to follow him in class. He is a great professor, highly recommended!

He made accounting manageable to learn while understanding that it isn't an exciting subject. His tests were hard but he always curves them to make it fair.  Overall a hilarious and great teacher! Take him!
Really great teacher, highly recommend
He is a great professor that goes through problems and examples in a lot of detail.  He is able to explain tough concepts and answer questions well.

Professor Hurley is amazing, he cares a lot for his students and really tries his best to set us up to succeed. One example is that he doesn't lecture off slides and writes the notes as he goes so that he can pace himself. There's an e-text we were required to buy for the course (not him), but I never had to open it because his lectures were great.
Hurley does a great job of teaching and he doesn't want any of his students to fail his course.

Great professor! He really goes above and beyond to make sure that his students succeed. He puts in a lot of effort to make his class more educational and fun, such as creating extra video lectures that we can watch outside of class. Additional comments: funny, engaging, fast grader, accessible if you have questions, fair grader.
He's brilliant. If you show up to class you'll pass. His lectures are the best.

Patrick Hurley is the best professor at Northeastern University. He is an amazing professor with interesting lectures and a positive attitude. He is very caring and tries to increase your grade as much as possible. Not a hard course. He is the reason I am considering a future in accounting. Definitely, take him if you can.

Hurley is a great professor. He made this subject very interesting and fun. He is very open to feedback and incorporates class suggestions. The key to doing well is being attentive, asking questions and doing the practice problems in the packets.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall a GREAT professor he really wants you to do well! Extremely fair grader, tests and quizzes are also very fair. Pat has a great note taking style (I thought), he actively writes the notes he wants us to write down under a document scanner that projects on the board. Very easy to keep up w/ and he explains all very thoroughly. TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Hurley is able to make accounting interesting, which is no easy feat. He is very responsive to emails and answers questions in class, even if you are asking him to explain something again. The exams and quizzes are tricky, but he makes up for it by dropping a couple quizzes and curving grades at the end of the semester. Take his class!

Great professor and fair amount of homework. His lectures are very clear and concise. Also he is willing to help the students who have questions from his lecture. Participate, do your homework, then you will be just fine.
He's a great professor and makes accounting understandable.

Professor Hurley is a great guy and a fantastic professor. He's hilarious and presents the material in a clear and concise way. He is very accommodating and helpful if you don't understand something or need something. He scanned class notes and prepared review packs etc to provide us with everything we needed to do well in the class. Overall, 10/10

He is a very good teacher. He really cares about the class and wants his students to do well and learn life skills. The toughness of the class varies depending on the student, but he always seems available to help when it is needed.

Professor Hurley is the best professor I've had. He is not only a good professor but also an inspirational human being. His notes are clear and easy to follow through; his quizzes and grading are fair. He is hilarious and always lightens up the mood of his students in early morning classes. I most definitely recommend taking his class!

Mr Hurley tries to understand his students as much as he can in order to be able to help them with grades and comprehension of the material. He is also very available when it is about receiving visits in his office after class or responding to some email. He posts every lecture online which is usually much more helpful than the online eBook.
Patrick Hurley is one of the best professors ever. Great lectures, very kind, also really cute
Very good teacher, always willing to help students.

He teaches well in accounting and his notes in class is really clear. The quizzes and the exams are fair and he helped students a lot. He usually replies to student's email or questions very fast. Great teacher!
He's a really chill guy. As long as you do your homeworks and pay attention in class you'll be more than fine.
One of the best professors at neu, really cares about his student.
Hurley is a great person! Material is hard sometimes, but he teaches very well. All handout and sample tests that he gave are super useful.  I would definitely recommend his class.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Very well-organized and fair. The class itself requires a good amount of work, but I think taking it with Professor Hurley helps a whole lot. I would definitely take another class with him again!
One of the most organized professors I've ever had.  Cares a lot about being fair to students, and class is not difficult at all of you pay attention and participate.
His teaching is extremely effective. Going to his lectures alone has helped me understand the material very well.

Professor Hurley is a great professor who really knows how to teach. he always tries to engage his students and makes really good Game of Thrones references. It is sometimes easy to get behind with some of the course material, but Professor Hurley gives you all the materials you need to succeed. He also genuinely cares about his students.
Best professor at Northeastern hands down.

Great Professor! He is nice to every student and you won't feel boring in his lecture. He won't test you anything beyond his class; even he does, he will drop those questions/give back those grades to stduents.
Great guy, great professor. Clear lectures and instruction, teaches by taking notes on document camera so he keeps the same pace as the class. Show up and follow along and you should be good.
Amazing Professor, I would definitely recommend taking his class.  Also go to his office hours, cool guy just to talk to.

He is a wonderful professor and I would highly recommend him. His lectures are clear and make a boring subject interesting. He is very understanding and approachable. By far one of my favorite professors are Northeastern.
Best teacher ever!!
He is the man! Best prof ever!

100% would take this class again. He makes accounting actually enjoyable and I haven't missed a lecture yet because I kind of like going. He's also really fair; if he thinks an exam/quiz/homework was too hard or unfair it'll show in the points you get back. Super funny and chill, overall great guy.
Great professor. He got me hooked and interested in a topic I had no knowledge about. Makes the lectures funny and entertaining. Would definitively recommend taking him for accounting courses.
Professor Hurley is funny and smart, but he doesn't explain the material. Tests and quizzes were hard. Wouldn't recommend him because of the way he teaches

Absolutely the best professor I've had. I haven't met one student who doesn't like Professor Hurley. He teaches thoroughly and concisely, and has the fairest class I've taken in college. Overall, he's an awesome and hilarious guy. I still keep up with him because of his invaluable information on real-world accounting, and just because he's great.

He is a really great professor, the best I have had at my time at Northeastern. He's funny, makes the class fun and really teaches the class well. Definitely choose him as your professor if you have the chance.

Even though the class is difficult he makes it as much fun as he can. Will explain any concept again if you don't understand. He also curves grades up by a lot if the class is under performing. Homework assignments are due every week get longer towards the end of the course.

I absolutely love attending his classes. He explains only what is important and that is what comes in the exam. He gives extra credit. Yippee. His classes are funny yet interesting. Online homework is due every monday. But he is understanding and sometimes pushes deadlines ahead :). Grading system is fair and I'm going to miss him :(

Pat is a great professor and person. I definitely recommend taking accounting with him. I found this class very challenging, but he was happy to help me understand the material and help boost our grades if we were struggling.

Professor Hurley invests a lot of time into his class by preparing study material for exams or working to help students during and outside of class. He has an accurate read on the student's comprehension of material and is great at creating an open class room environment.
Easy to talk to, can relate to the students. Makes accounting about as enjoyable as possible, which is saying something.

Patrick is the best accounting professor!! He always makes the lecture and notes very clear. If you understand what he mentioned in class, you will be find. The quiz and exam sometimes are a little bit harder than usual but it's good for you to think and figure it out. You can learn a lot in his class. Highly recommended!
Great teacher, lectures very clear and material easy to understand. Attendance needed to pass course. Tests difficult but fair. Easy to listen to, good guy and woud definitely take again.

Professor Hurley is a great guy! He is young, motivated and knows what he is talking about. He is a very easy-going guy and definitely is on the same wave length as the students. His lectures are full of jokes but at the same time putting in work is a priority. It truly has been a pleasure having him and I can only say - GO FOR HIM!
Great professor, helpful in class, funny without detracting from class. An absolute ledge. Make sure you really pay attention, the work is a lot of studying and cramming.
Prof. Hurley is an amazing Professor. He tries to make class really interesting and I ACTUALLY looked forward to a 4:30 accounting class. I would advise everybody to take this class.

Professor Hurley is the best professor I had at NEU so far. He makes all the materials very clear and easy to understand. He's always there for students and he's very patience when students having questions in class. He makes sure everyone is stay on top and he has a sense of humour. I would definitely recommend him! p.s. He doesn't use ppt.

Pat is very nice, youthful and a great professor. Accounting itself is a very boring subject, but Pat tries his best to make the subject interesting. He makes the problems funny and cracks some good jokes too. Very cool guy!

Easily the best professor I've had thus far at Northeastern. Somehow makes the class interesting and always is sure to incorporate humor. Clear with what he expects of students and is always looking to help in any way that he can. 10/10 would recommend.

Enjoyable class with moderate work load. Felt prepared for tests and enjoyed the sense of humor, made lecture less long. Did a lot of in class work and was able to ask questions so I left class each day confident with the material.

Professor Hurley somehow manages to make accounting interesting. I am not at all a fan of the subject but I still was engaged during lectures because he would keep the mood light through humor while also teaching the material in a way we could all understand. If you are ever confused he is always willing to stop and go over something again to help.

I really abhor accounting. Before this class I was terrified to even attempt the subject. Patrick has helped immensely with my hatred for the topic. He is hilarious and doesn't mind cracking a couple of jokes. He is always trying to help us understand accounting and is always available. If you have to take accounting definitely take it with Hurley
Amazing.
He's an awesome teacher. Makes accounting fun.

Patrick is great! He's always willing to help and does a lot to help you get a good grade, even when the material is difficult and not the most interesting . Not the easiest class, but if you work and pay attention it is possible to get an A. He's super funny too! Definitely recommend.
IF you go to class and pay attention to his lecture and do your homework, you barely need to study for quizzes and tests

A bigger Game of Thrones fan than George R.R Martin himself. Has more jokes in the quizzes than the amount of questions in it. One of the coolest professors around and a delight to be part of his class.
The professor clearly knows what he is talking about and is very knowledgable. However, the course is quite difficult!
I'm going to miss this class a lot! He makes accounting fun and teaches the material very well. Tests/quizzes are straightforward and there aren't any surprises.

Patrick Hurley is one of is not the best teacher I have ever had at Northeastern. He is extremely hilarious and very caring towards his students. He somehow manages to make this course fun. I would most definitely recommend him!
Extremely understanding and makes this boring subject so much more interesting.
Extremely clear, helpful, and all around just a rad dude. I can genuinely say I enjoy this class solely because he's a fantastic professor.

He made accounting fun, and was very thorough in his teaching. He writes everything out clearly on the board. Best professor I've had at Northeastern so far. I love going to his class. The questions on his tests are always hilarious. Not an easy A, but he gives a lot opportunities to improve your grade.
Simply put he is great. Only guy that can make a smile crack in an accounting class. AN ACCOUNTING CLASS!
LEGEND.
Patrick is a great professor who has a very good relationship with his students. He is always willing to help out and give feedback on ways to improve in his classroom. Very understanding teacher

Financial accounting is not the most exciting class. However, Proffessor Hurley made this painful class as entertaining and interesting as possible, and for a required class I would definitly suggest to try and get intoa class of his.
He brings the fun into accounting.

Need to take an accounting course?  Take it with Patrick!  He is an excellent professor-- young, relatable, articulate, and most importantly, HE SLAYS LECTURES.  You truly understand the material he covers in class if you pay attention/take notes.  Would I say the course was crazy easy?  No, but you can do well if you put in the necessary effort.
The best teacher I have had thus far. He has industry experience and has the humor to back it up. Cool guy and if given the opportunity I would choose to have him again as a professor.

Patrick is great. He's a really cool guy that cares about his students. Tests are hard but there is a massive curve usually. He taught the material very well for a relatively new professor. If you take notes and do the homework, it is very possible to get an A, but you will have to work for it.

Patrick is a very very smart guy. He knows what he's doing and he is really good at teaching it in a way that makes sense and is clearly stated what's important and what will be on the exams. He's also hilarious and makes class fun and entertaining.

Pat is a great professor who cares about his students and their understanding of accounting. He is funny, keeps a fairly dry subject interesting and light hearted, and always goes above and beyond with his fairness in grading. He explains the material well and will take the time to go over anything which is not clear as many times as necessary.
He's awesome and hilarious. Definitely would recommend taking his class.

gives lectures where she mumbles at the front of the class with no visual guides, then has the audacity to ask YOU to speak up when participating in class. biased, won't take opinions that don't align with her own, just argues til you give up. make sure your papers are skewed to what she believes or else she'll take marks off. disorganized too.

Horrible teacher. Graded based on 4 things, so unbelievably old she doesn't listen or teach. She makes her student give the lectures thru presentations. No clear guidelines and participation worth 20%. To be honest the class and content itself is so easy but talking to her is like talking to a wall and she will ruin your grade because of it

Her personal biases constantly get in the way of her lectures. She is out dated and argues with students until her opinion is accepted. She struggles to deliver clear expectations and is constantly going back on her word. I had to write what I think she'll like, not what I've learned. Also, our midterm was 30 paragraphs handwritten in class.
Class is a joke but the tests are a ton of take-home work. She's a bit stuck up.

reviews.comment: This professor is quite possibly the worst professor I have ever had. There is not structure to her class. She says one thing, and then grades you on another. I even got reprimanded for citing sources. If she doesn't agree with you then it is wrong in her eyes. I had to skew all of my papers towards her ideology. Awful teacher.

HYPOCRITE. If you don't generally agree with her then she won't let you speak and will consistently interrupt/undermine you even in group presentations and to other students when you aren't present. Tests are 20-30 handwritten paragraphs of pure memorization of vocabulary that you are given in advance, but which often hasn't been covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Beware, you have to put a lot a work in, but you don't feel the need to since classes are mostly discussions. Textbook not discussed in class, yet she expects it in the exams/papers, which is why the grading is tough. Loved her, but would recommend to people that are interested in the class and ready to commit. If you want an A pick someone else.

Illingworth is very knowledge about the topics but her lectures are lacking. For the majority of the class lectures were based off of group projects done by students. There are few grades in the class and she is an extremely tough grader. Her lectures can be confusing and you are forced to supplement the material in order to pass the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She has an average 3.1 as of right now, and I think that's 3.1 points too high. She sucks. She's really boring and dry. She doesn't teach much, just talks about anything she feels like talking about. She doesn't tell you anything about the upcoming test, so you're left studying anything from the book. Wouldn't recommend taking this class.

Prof. Illingworth is solid, but the class is HARD. You really need to read and understand the material, so you can participate in class discussion, or you won't pass. She's not available often to talk to or go to for help, but in class she speaks passionately about the material, and really knows her stuff. That said, it can be very confusing.

I really enjoyed the class, but she grades VERY hard, and provides very little feedback and support.   Almost all of this class is lecture and discussion. No powerpoint, you have to transcribe what she says as she goes on.   Illington is a great professor, but the brutal grading and lack of office hours makes her one to avoid.

She's a very confusing professor and can often times be rude. Lectures are pretty long so be prepared. She loves debatingarguing so participation is necessary. I would recommend going to class and the book is good to have as a reference. There are two tests and I just studied my class notes and skimmed the text and got a good grade.
She's kinda hard to reach. Doesn't reply emails. Doesn't have much office hour. Her lectures are okay but she simply isn't helpful at all. Also, she's sometimes condescending. Don't recommend.

Terrible teacher, if you don't see an idea her way it is wrong even if it is a completely open ended question.  Hard to talk to out of class and when you do gives you misguidance rather than help. Avoid her if you can.

Shows up late almost every time.  Rambles incoherently often.  VERY conceited.  Does not seem to have a lesson plan some days, and often relies on her students to teach portions of the class through presentations.

Do NOT take Busn Ethics as a Freshman! It's a complex Philosophy Class that won't help you in your immediate future. The class is mostly discussion, but the grades are heavily weighed on 4 essays that are graded strictly. If you go to her for help though, she's very fair and gives you advice and extra time. She's a great person, but a tough teacher

Took Business Ethics. Although teacher is a bleeding-heart liberal, the class is engaging, the discussions relevant, and the issues presented are interesting. Open-forum class format, teacher is very open to anyone's opinions. I recommend the class.
Took business ethics.Great professor and tries to engauge the whole class. Midterm and a final with a paper... Thought she was a hard grader although I knew all the terms.

Illingworth gets a bad rap on this site. Philosophy majors, like me, know that she is very good. You can learn a lot from her and she is very helpful to students who want to learn. Unfortunately, she teaches large classes to students in med and business related programs who don't get philosophy. They lack motivation, give up, slack off, blame her.
An open forum class that allows free expression and fosters creative thought among students.  The unorthodox class structure provides a break from the monotony of college lecture classes.

This is a very interesting class. It is pretty much just a class discussion/debate each week. There are 2 essays, one midterm and a take home final which is an essay. All in all a great way to fulfill the arts/humanities req. Professor Illingworth does a great job teaching the course and it is not stressful. I recommend it.
Horrible. SO BAD. DONT EVEN THINK ABOUT TAKING IT.

Dr. Illingworth is a very intelligent professor,however, she is not a great teacher.She has a set of things she wants to talk about and she proceeds with them not paying attention to the class.She assumes that everyone knows as much as she does.She doesn't spend enough time explaining the basics to students.I felt like I was in graduate school...

The topics discussed in this class are really interesting to me. I actually enjoyed going to class sometimes when we discussed interesting or controversial issues. She tends to take a side on an issue and won't be afraid to basically say you are wrong. However, she's still nice and it's not too hard of a class. Just participate a lot!

She is a great teacher.  She's perfect to take a class with because she talks about interesting things so you can participate and get into interesting discussions/debates, but you can also zone out and it doesnt matter.  She's really smart, engaging, and relaxed.  You can get along fine without ever reading the book.

She definitely knows her stuff, and does a good job of advocating multiple sides of an issue without compromising her own conclusions. The worst part of the class is listening to other students spout off personal opinions and irrelevant anecdotes, but Illingworth is great. Try to be as thorough as possible in your written work.

Talks a lot about nothing. Very boring class. I felt she was always unprepared. Her teaching style is not the greatest, you watch a lot of movies and talk to each other. TA does ALL the work. But I never read a single page of the textbook and got a C+

Class is pretty dull most of the time.  She knows her stuff and is very intelligent but can sometimes be a little outthere.  She's very nice though.  She does none of the grading herself but instead makes the TA do all of it.  As long as you do the readings and go to class you should be ok.

I am trying to figure out why everyone else thinks this woman is intelligent. She teaches ABSOLUTELY nothing, class is led simply by listening to opinions of others. She lacks professionalism, comes in late to EVERY class, has missed several classes, her phone goes off in EVERY class, she allows it to ring. Definitely THE WORST professor I have had
As long as you come pretty often and talk just about every time you are there you can probably pull off a C without really trying.

Wow! Prof. Illingworth was by far the best teacher I have ever had!! She is insanely brilliant and articulate, I hope to have a fraction of her intelligence someday!  I went to every class, even more suprising!!

very difficult grader. i worked way too hard in that class for what i earned. she is belittling and gives the sense that she knows everything because she is a LAWYER. give me a break. extremely snobby. likes to namedrop the lame books she has written. most boring class in existence.
Great teacher with interesting ideas.  Lots of movies.  :-D

She's a great teacher! She's very smart and knows what she's talking about! She made this class a lot easier then I expected. Her grading wasn't bad at all. We only had one test and 3 essays 2-3 pages each. No sweat if you go to class
she's awesome i don't know what these two are talking about.. very analytical and brilliant she knows her stuff and helps you too
she is really smart and clear. Easy teacher if you get concepts and enjoy sub.

As long as you attend his classes you will be fine. He has office hours before classes and his study guides translate very well to the exams. If you can answer all the questions on the study guide you will do well on the test, he is not a harsh grader and the course involves almost no math.

Very old fashioned - uses chalkboard to teach. He clearly cared deeply about environmental economics, so he always had a lot to say. Not a lot of hw assignments, and he's an easy enough grader. Can be hard to follow at times bc of his lecture-heavy style, but if you pay attention you will do just fine. Does often give vague instructions on purpose

Had Bakkal for a Critique of Capitalism class, and most of my concerns came from the way he organized the class.Towards the end of the sem lectures became way more disorganized. Still, he was clear about what terms /questions would be on tests, and as long as you actually listen in lectures and do all readings you will be fine.

THIS GUY SUCKS. If you can take someone else, do it. Discussion posts are SUPER unclear and not clearly marked when due. FURTHER, the graphs he draws up in class are NOWHERE to be seen in the textbook. Please save the GPA.

Good lord. Where do I begin? I hate this man. He explains things like he doesn't want you to understand them. If you pay attention in class, it is futile. All your attention should be paid to the textbook out of class. He is extremely boring, and by far the worst teacher I have ever met. Be prepared to see points taken off for no reason. Curse you.

reviews.comment: Try and take another professor, this class is just not worth it.

Honestly don't understand the bad reviews– Bakkal is an amazing professor who gives you all the tools you need to do well in his class. You need to attend and pay attention in each class to understand the concepts, but he makes an effort to consistently review topics. Follow along in the textbook and do all his review questions, you will get an A.

Bakkal gets a bad wrap with reviews. He is an intelligent and funny man that will clearly communicate topics in a non-math way and will provide help if you ask for it. In order to get a good grade, you must attend every lecture. The reviews he gives before is significantly helpful for the tests, and opportunities for extra credit exist on tests.
He used the time very will, teaching us a lot

Professor Bakkal gives great lectures and it's clear he really cares about students memorizing and understanding the material. He's a super fair professor. Attendance is part of the grade but all of the lectures are recorded on zoom.
Professor is hit or miss - lectures can be dry, but tests are manageable with the textbook. Unstuck study was a lifesaver for study prep. Overall, a decent class if you put in the work.
Professor Bakkal was one of the best professors I've had during my time at NEU. His grading is clear and straightforward. He cares about you learning rather than memorizing. 10/10 funny man.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER. No textbook, no slides, boring dry lectures, harsh grader. The only way to study was to note down and memorize everything he writes on the board, or you will fail tests. Tests are all short answer questions, which just requires you to memorize everything.
Very interesting and knowledgeable about the history of economics. He's excellent at helping you understand concepts in layman's terms.

Good professor who gets a bad wrap because he makes you learn. His course was very lecture-based. You could read along in the textbook (and he recommends it) but in my opinion that's not necessary. Go to class, take notes, ask questions, and study for exams and you'll do great. His exam grading is odd sometimes, as is he, but overall a good course.

If youre looking to take Principles of Macroeconomics, take another professor. His lectures are ok, but he doesnt write anything down, and tests are mostly based on the textbook. He is also super nitpicky with his grading on exams and is very bad with technology. Stay away from him if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No slide, No Textbook, Only note in class, the note is a lot in each course. If you don't write note, you will be terrible, so don't take his class. The grading system of him is different from other. 200 total,4 exam: 35each, discussion: 20,attendance:10, paper: 30.A plus is over 190. if you got 30(it is not bad, over Mean) in each exam, you will..
I loved his teaching in class. You will learn so much. If u actually want to learn, take him

Great professor. Takes attendance but I loved going to class because he obviously knows what he is talking about and makes it interesting. Only downside is that the tests cover a lot of material and make up a large part of your grade but as long as you have been reading the textbook, going to class etc. you will be fine.
Amazing. U will learn so much. But u need to put a decent amount of work. Nothing extraordinary. Amazing lectures. U cannot miss class cause u will fall behind

BEST ADVISOR EVER! she is so helpful and truly cares about what you want to do. She'll make sure you are taking the right classes and that you don't overload your schedule.
AWESOME ADVISOR! she is a great woman and is willing to help with anything you need. she is funny and makes everyone feel welcomed and comfortable. Definitely take her connections and decisions class

Kim Irmiter is a great advisor. Very down to Earth and ALWAYS willing to help. She is very aware of events and programs happening around campus and is the head of the Peer Mentoring program at NU. Overall, she has been a great resource to have not to mention a great reference for future employers.
Always willing to help. Is very funny and likes to have a good time.
Awesome advisor. She's so helpful with anything you need and will try to do whatever is possible.

Brilliant professor and knows what she is talking about. However, on the teaching side, she can be arrogant on some days and helpful on others pending on her mood I guess. Doesn't really "teach" well, she's one of those brilliant professors in their field but not in the classroom. HARD CLASS

Mixed feelings... she is brilliant and knows the material, but doesn't really TRY to teach. Sometimes she is really nice and sometimes she is condescending and arrogant. This class covers way too much material and she flies through it, then expects you to regurgitate every detail on the exams.

Professor presented quite the challenge almost to the point that it became miserable. She was helpful, however very arrogant. Advice: Pop Quizzes, 2 tests on 8+ Chapters, cumulative final exam, "microwiki", in-class presentation. !Uses textbook test bank - how creative.! Lab was interesting, however oriented for someone who has zero lab experience.

The exams are extremely difficult. Read the text book before each class if you expect to pass. She explains the material well but covers too much too quickly. Do well on the final and in lab and you will get a good grade. Put more effort in to this class than any other.
Horrible professor made the class extremely hard. alot of tough materials to learn. tricks you with easy quiz but extremely hard exam. only two midterms so they are very intense and hard.

She made a somewhat tough course on par with Organic 2. Crazy amount of work, exams were really tough. She's barely engaging and when she does illicit response it's normally under pressure of some sort. Lectures were drawn out and mundane. She seems really smart but smart doesn't mean you can teach, too.
This class will make you want to pull your hair out. High stress, recommend anyone else

Very high expectations of her students. Flies through material and difficult to understand at times. Exam questions are always very different from those she asks in class or quizes. Toughest class to date.

Absolutely loved him as a professor; my favorite so far! His lectures are super engaging; you can tell how passionate and knowledgeable he is in the field. There is a lot of material covered, but it's all explained clearly and all of the exams were open-note. I found the subject to be fascinating and you really learn a lot!

Had him for the honors section. Phenomenal teacher and clearly knows a lot about the material. He keeps it pretty entertaining but he doesn't have slides or anything so you kinda just have to write what he says and organize it later. Also, the grade is made up of only 2 assignments and 2 exams (+ the final)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for an honors section. You learn A LOT, so there's a lot of material on the exams. A harder psych class I've taken at NU, but he's really passionate and you learn a lot.

Only take his class if you hate yourself. The lectures were hard to follow and very unorganized. Provided almost no resources (textbook, class notes) for review outside of class. He spends the whole class proving he knows the material rather than explaining the concepts. His jokes are even worse than his teaching abilities.

The most Useful Professor in an entirely useless class. Thinnest kid in fat camp. Principals of Exp. Physics. It's the bloody CAPSTONE COURSE for a physics major...  The actual class is a poorly made conglomerate of badly designed physics experiments none of which he or any of the professors understand.   Whats it say about my about my major?

Say what you want, but I found the guy endearing, in a funny way! He was sweet, however much of your classic science-professer he may be! I actually learned a little in the class (though it was way more physics-based than I would have liked) If more people had participated I think it would have been more interesting.
You learn very little during class because the teachers notes are not easy to understand.

Was very dissapointed - the class was too science oriented for me as a business major. Professor was not very helpful. The homework assignments are much harder then the quizzes so they just stress everyone out for no reason. All in all not my favorite but it won't kill you to take it.
Prof. Israeloff is a wonderful teacher.I never imagined I could enjoy this subject so much.

I thought the class, Energy Environment and Society, would be based more on social/current issues, prof Israeloff took a very math/physics direction.  Doesn't really answer questions.  Go to class because his exams aren't nearly as hard as the homework and you can usually get him to give you most of what will be on the test.

The physics department at Northeastern is lacking in general, so the rating of a lecturer should be taken with a grain of salt. Prof. Israeloff means well but seems to be a bit scatter-brained. Perhaps it would be a better class if ILS were effective...
Crazy ****, but I found him amusing. He's extremely sarcastic most of the time I think, and fairly self-deprecating. I enjoyed it.
Nice guy, means well. Tells really lame jokes, and yes I do think he teaches while stoned.
crack?
nicest guy in the world, but a wildly inneffective teacher.  No structure to his lectures at all, generally scatterbrained.  I don't see any groundbreaking research coming from him anytime soon.
probably the worst teacher in the entire world.  talking to him is like trying to talk to a rock.
completely useless, just puts things on the board he saw once, some classmates claim he's usually high which would explain why i learnt nothing in that class despite attending regularly if not always

Nice guy, but really scatterbrained and irresponsible.  He'll lose your work and not tell you.  He'll walk away when you're in the middle of asking him a question.  His lectures are worthless.  He hasn't a clue about any of the labs that he teaches.  He'll cancel class and not tell anyone.

Great professor really professional and makes you like the class even if you had no idea about the subject before you go in. In addition, she is amazing really funny, and enjoyable to be in one of her classes. She really energizes you. Most of all you learn so many things.
had her for material science: hard class, but shes a very good professor.
No Comments

I had this woman 4 years ago and she was the best prof at NU next to Metagulchi that is. She really cares, speaks english, and has a great personality. I learned more from her than I did from almost all of my Profs. I wish NU had more teachers like her, if they did maybe students wouldn't constantly wonder what the hiring process is like for Profs

I had Jackie her first year teaching and she was fantastic, enthusiastic, helpful, informed, friendly, the list goes on...  the TA was useless (could barely speak english, kept talking about the 'gibbous face equation'), but that's not the professor's faul
Excellent teacher, if only other professors could learn from her.
Really don't like chemistry but she was easy to understand and follow. Great professor.
Really don't like chemistry but she was easy to understand and follow. Great professor.
No Comments
easy to learn from, easy to get along with.
Awesome teach who really enjoys teaching and feeds her students a plethora of knowledge
Reasonable work-load, his lectures are clear and the quizzes match the material form the lectures.
Very boring class. He is a very hard grader and test questions are unpredictable and not really related to the class. Must use textbook to teach yourself the material. I would not recommend him.
you never receive the grade you deserve. He's very tough on grading. his lectures are so monotonous that you fell asleep all the time. he goes by the book all the time.

His class is okay, but he's a really tough grader. His grades are based 75%  on a midterm and a final, so if you mess up those, you're screwed. He gives pop up quizzes and his class is graded on a curve.
Decent guy in class, TOUGH grader. Not rude or anything, just boring.
He tries to help, but it doesn't help. Either he doesn't answer your QUESTION or he helps you but then you still don't do well on exams (the midterm and final are worth a huge chunk).

For the clarity rating, it's not that he isn't clear... it's that the stuff he says in class isn't what is on exams. The exams don't match well to the quizzes. Take down everything he says because he will use things you barely talked about!

He grades very very tough and makes it near impossible to know what type of grade you're going to get until the end.  He's a smart guy but a horrible teacher. One mistake can cost you more points than you thought the problem was even worth to begin with.
class is boring, and he uses a rediculous way to calculate your grade, you never know how well you are doing before you receive your final grade.

If you make one mistake on his quizzes and it carries through to the next question, he will take points off for both. He is a tough grader and not lenient. He has a boring teaching strategy and the material is dry.

Professor Isakower is an average teacher...my biggest problem is that he sticks too closely to the text, making me feel that i'm wasting my time showing up to class...he's a smart guy and he definitely attempts to answer questions you may ask in class and is willing to respond to questions via e-mail which is nice...he's a bit dry but overall okay

He's chill and not bad at all. I've missed only some of his classes and I'm able to keep up by reading the textbook on my own. It's very important to study from his worksheet, it's way more useful than studying from the book. If you pay attention in class it will be visible in your grade.

Isakower is a chill teacher. Attendance is not mandatory, but I think his lectures are more helpful than just reading the texbook. He is very lenient on grading, and gives partial credit. He is also very clear and answers questions. Overall chill guy and not so bad class.

Ivan, as a professor, is a very understanding and easy-to-talk-to person. The course ARCH 1110 is inherently challenging to teach and only really makes sense if you are an architecture major. The course covered so many things in such a short time, and for each project, you learn something new thats completely different from the week before.

Should not be considered a professor because he legit doesn't teach. Every single class, he goes through a 100 pg slideshow, critiques everyone's mistakes on drawings, then has the poor TAs teaching everything else. When we were struggling with the software, ESPECIALLY Rhino, he would get irritated and commanded TAs to scramble around. Terrible.

Class goes like this: Ivan critiques work from the previous assignment, then he has the TAs teach how to do the next assignment. If you're good with technology, time management, and willing to put in the time this class will be a breeze. If you're stuck, it's better to look up a youtube video or ask a classmate than waiting for office hours.

Ivan is arguably the worst person you could pick to teach this course. All of the learning and almost all the grading was facilitated by TAs, since he doesn't understand half the software that he teaches. Expect homework to take at least 5 hours a week, and you will have to learn most of the techniques yourself.

Professor Halacheva was extremely caring! Her lectures were a bit hard to sit through but I mean it is math. The course is extremely test heavy but her homeworks aren't too bad. Also her office hours are extremely helpful. Overall, she is very sweet and honestly the only reason I got a bad grade was because I was not very good at it.

Proffesor Halacheva was awesome, you could tell she really cared about all of her students. Course was difficult for me but her office hours helped a lot and lectures were very informative. However, it's important to note that this course is very exam heavy and little depends on the homework.

For a math class where all you are doing is writing is proofs, you want loads of examples. Iva teaches strictly through examples which makes learning multistep proofing techniques easy to pick up because there is so much repetition. Can't go wrong with taking Iva.

Please do yourself a favor and take Dr. Halacheva! The best teacher for Math 1365 hands down. Lectures are always clear and if they're not, she will find every way to explain them even more. Great office hours as well. I wish she taught more math classes!!!!

Professor Halacheva is a godsend!! She's one of the best professors I've ever had at Northeastern. She made the content very easy to understand and provided many opportunities for help. Go to office hours to get amazing hw help and exam prep. Do EVERY practice problem bc very similar problems show up on exams.
Awesome professor who really cares! Provides lecture notes and is very understanding and helpful when you need it.
Informative lectures explained well, though can get pretty boring (probably just the actual content). Good notes and reviews posted online. Fair grader and understanding for late homeworks.

Prof. Halacheva is clearly a very dedicated and caring professor. Notes, practice exercises, and other study materials are always posted online. She has a way of simplifying math concepts into real world examples that makes the class so much more manageable. Not to mention, her grading is very fair.
Providing all notes before beginning of courses
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Ivy is experienced in her field and enjoys teaching the subject. She cold calls often, but it forces you to pay extra attention in class. She may be intimidating at the beginning, but she's actually a pretty nice and funny person. She is a tough grader, and her tests are solely based off readings, so effort must be put in. No final exam.

Prof Ivy knows what she is doing and she is very successful in her career. She cold calls alot and is a pretty tough grader but overall she made class somewhat enjoyable. I think her lectures were kind of confusing and the tests were solely based on the textbook. Overall, solid professor that care about her strudents and no drama.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ivy is good, she is very accomplished and is a good professor she definitely knows her stuff. However, she cold calls a good amount and values participation a lot. Very hard to get an A in her class, she rarely gives a 90+ on assignments. Caring person and not scary, just come to class prepared to talk a little. Not having final exam was great too.

Liked her a lot: participation matters, a lot of readings, and a heavy group project (no final tho). The lecture was fascinating, but get ready to talk. 2 Case studies you choose from, and weekly chapter notes. Hated my team in the group project, so get ready to suffer a bit. Otherwise, lovely teacher. Sent case to competition and referral letter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and cares a lot about students. Group project is a little tough and directions can be quite confusing at times. But overall great!

nope
nope nope

Weekly chapter readings plus 2 case studies to finish over the year. Final is a large group project consulting case that she does not clearly tell you what to do most of the time. First language isn't English, so she speaks with an accent but its not bad. You need participation but she doesn't give too many opportunities to participate.

flipped class meaning ng all learning is done via notes. You have to choose 2 case studies out of 5 throughout the semester, and notes are due every monday (i had a M/W/TH schedule). There is no final exam, but a project you wokr on through the semester with a group.

Does not give clear deadlines for assignments with very vague instructions. Does not grade fairly at all. Not empathetic towards the students at all. Would not recommend taking her for any of the courses.
I loved taking her class! Highly recommend others do too. The class does require participation and reading outside of lectures, but is highly beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very caring and sweet, wants everyone to succeed BUT group project was STRESSFUL. Spans across whole semester, much more extensive than other classes'. Instructions/expectations not always clear, but was usually understanding about it. LOTS of reading, tests were medium difficulty, participation matters, harsh grader (doesn't give 100s easily).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Quite literally the best professor I've ever had in my entire life. You will have to work hard in the class but she sets you up for your future like no other. She has 2 PHD's, is funny, and she is the most caring woman you will ever meet. If you try in her class she is an angel. Regardless if you care about your future PLEASE take her.
very difficult to understand what she says, talks very fast

Professor Ivy teaches a class that many find boring, but the content is very easy (just read and take notes). She values participation and at times will cold call. Her test are longer than other sections and asks the most detailed questions that are easy to miss in the textbook. HOWEVER, she does really care about her student's success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class gave me a lot of anxiety due to constant cold calling for questions sometimes no one even knew. Her directions were unclear and at times, I had no clue what was even due. Her exams are straightforward and from the textbook. The textbook will save you. The final project group makes or breaks the final grade.
Amazing

Professor Ivy is an incredibly warm and inspirational woman. This class is fairly simple if you went to a work heavy high school: read the chapter, take notes, put it into a quizlet and take the test. The tests are all multiple choice  simple memory-based questions that ask "what concept is this called" or "which strategy is described."
Overall a hard class. Ivy will cold call you and emphzsizes participation. A good lady and a good teacher who wants students to suceed but is definitely hard to get an A or A-. Tough grader

This class is harder than any other section but ppl serious about the subject need to take Julia Ivy. She is funny and makes class interesting. She will make it hard to get a C but harder to get an A. Know what you're getting into. If you have the time for this class and study far in advance you will do well and leave learning a lot.

Ivy is a good teacher but sometimes annoying. She really emphasizes spoken participation but doesnt not always give fair chances for participation. Even on days where kids cant really participates, she keeps track of how much you talk. Overall, reading the textbook & paying attention will get you a pretty good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: GROUP PROJECTS, PARTICIPATION MATTERS, VERY TEST HEAVY, GIVES VERY LESS FEEDBACK, ASKS FOR NOTES EVERY CLASS, LECTURE HEAVY, FEELS LIKE ETERNITY. THE COURSE ISNT HARD AT ALL BUT TAKING OTHER PROFESSORS WOULD BE BENEFICIAL.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You are required to take this class as a Sr business student. Ivy has bad English speaking abilities but is a sweet person. There are like 1-2 other profs I would take before her but shes a solid number 3

- Julia is perfect! She makes the class very interactive especially the group assignments when the students need to make a presentation during each class. This has developed my skills in public speaking and I have learnt to think on my feet. The case studies and quizzes were very helpful. Julia made sure we read the text and applied the concepts

The professor was enthusiastic and brought considerable knowledge and experience to her role. She had valuable insights to offer students and was an effective communicator, checking in with students and making sure everyone was on the same page. She was invested in students' learning and genuinely worked to help students' succeed in the course and

I was honestly surprised by how much I learned - the professor opened the class saying this was supposed to be an introductory level course for part timers but as one of the full timers that took this at the very end of our program, I still found it challenging and very very helpful. Very fun too! Would love a bigger class size and honestly wish it

By far my favorite professor at Northeastern thus far. She is truly interested in what she teaches and it makes you want to keep learning. Yes, the group project requires a lot of time and effort but it indefinitely pays off. Make sure to read and take notes on the assigned chapters, b/c it help with the quizzes and your own understanding.

She made the lectures very engaging and was a very friendly teacher who really tried to make sure you understood the content. The assignments included case write-ups, news updates, exams, one debate, and the final project, with some individual and group work. But keep in mind that she is strict on participation and occasionally cold-calls.

This class is difficult, as it should be for a capstone class. If you want an easy A, don't take this class. If you want to walk out of college with a real project that matters, take this class. Prof. Ivy is great and spends time on her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ivy teaches an amazing INTB 1203 course. She truly cares about the topic, has great experience and most importantly, cares for her students. Her new method that she is writing her book on made our freshman market entry project actually matter. It is a lot of work, but the work MATTERS. You walk out of freshman year with real deliverables.
I believe the Instructor was the strength of the course, very well prepared and lectured enhanced the experience.

Absolutely fantastic course. I learned so much about global international strategy. The cases were fantastic and all had similar formats, thus by the end for our final project of writing one of these cases, it was doable and eye-opening. Truly amazing how everything intertwined so well

Taken many classes at Northeastern and she is by far the weakest one I have had so far. Not a very engaging class. The grading system is based on very few items so it is hard to know where you stand in the class. Would not recommend this professor.
Very dry lectures. Expectations were not well outlined. Poor communication. I don't feel like I learned anything from this course.
Tough grader with vague grading metrics. Grades seem arbitrary and you will get little feedback.
Heartless professor. Took interesting topics and made them boring. Was rude and spiteful to students in the class. I felt personally attacked in her class. Do not take her class it will not be fun.
One of the worst professors I've had a Northeastern.

Great professor overall. Interesting lectures but classes are intense and grade might be an issue for students looking for an easy 'A' out. Nevertheless, would 10/10 recommend to take the course with Professor Ivy!

I really enjoyed this class overall! Although it is very textbook-heavy, if you do the reading the class and exams are very straight-forward and easy. I found her to be a very useful resource and helpful outside of class. She cares a lot about her students and treats everyone with respect. I definitely recommend her, she's awesome.

She's the best teacher that I have taken so far. But, this is not show up and pass class. You can definitely develop some skills in her classes. I am taking LDR6150. Her classes involve a lot of reading and a lot of homework. Also, she gives quiz before her classes,  not too difficult just to ensure that students read the material. Lots of homework
Favorite class, I've taken by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you can get into one of his classes, take it, and it will be your favorite that semester.
Goated....
Maybe the best professor I've had. Makes you feel like you're discovering the answer along with him. Effortlessly funny and charismatic. A nerd in the best way.

This guy is the man. You could literally be any major, any personality and you are going to be engaged in this course provided you have any interest in philosophy, which i'm assuming everyone taking the course is. Dude's the defintiton of eccentric but he's so engaging it works perfectly. Actually top 2 class i've taken at northeastern, take him!

The best phil professor I've ever had! It's incredible how he facilitates discussion so well, and you learn so much! Very accommodating and wants you to learn and grow.Doesn't force participation either. I felt as though I could truly come to love and do philosophy in his class, instead of stress, and be unfairly graded like in prior phil classes.
So kind and funny! I learned so much in this class and Professor Stump genuinely wants you to succeed and makes class fun! He is super supportive, 100% reccomend!
A great man in and out of the classroom. Feels more like a friend than a professor. Please take him if you get the chance. He genuinely cares about his students and is so funny!
really flexible, kind and caring, excellent lectures

Prof. Stump is really fantastic! I loved his class and looked forward to each day. Highly recommend taking a class with him if possible! Homework was quite manageable and class content was interesting and engaging. He created an amazing sense of community amongst the students. 10/10 recommend him and he's great to have conversations with as well!

Professor Stump is the greatest professor I have ever had at Northeastern. He's chill, mindful of his students, accessible outside of class, and enthusiastic to teach the course. It truly seems like he wants you to succeed and has opportunities to make up for any work that you may have missed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had and I hate philosophy. The only professor who has made me want to attend class every day. The content of the course is super interesting.
Very good.

I looked forward to these lectures everyday. On the first day of class he admitted that he didn't know the material very well (this was his first semester teaching Modern), but it was impossible to tell. He's actually a genius. Highly recommend taking any class with him if you can; assignments aren't too hard, and he's very lenient with due dates.

TAKE ANY CLASS WITH PROFESSOR STUMP! I took his philosophy of emotions class and truly looked forward to our classes and the discussions. There are some reading but it is manageable and Professor Stump makes sure everyone understands the arguments before we begin discussing. Great professor, great person, I could not recommend this class more!

Prof Stump is INCREDIBLE! So accessible out of class and clearly wants you to succeed. Loved the structure of the week-to-week assignments and the flexibility with the final project. Made me love philosophy and feel comfortable speaking up in class. Would definitely take another class with Stump if I had the opportunity.

He's genuinely passionate about what he teaches. He's very understanding and won't be on you if you don't come to class, but if it's sudden he definitely takes the time to check-in and make sure you're okay, beyond just asking you to catch up on course work! Also incredibly engaging and makes class provoking, even when it's just Ancient Phil
My thoughts have become more coherent after this class. Love Jacob stump. He's a genius. Take this class if you can.

I loved this class! I was nervous because I hadn't had prior philosophy classes, but Dr. Stump explained everything thoroughly! I enjoyed the argument analysis worksheets and the open-ended final paper; the course emphasized critical thinking instead of regurgitating material. 

Plus, Dr. Stump is hilarious. I looked forward to class!
love prof stump. this class is great and i think everyone should take it. this is a laid back class with only a handful of fairly simple assignments. highly recommend this class and professor!

Easily one of the best professors I've had. All other reviews covered it perfectly, but it felt necessary to advise anyone who reads this to enroll in his courses immediately. He's witty, caring, insightful, and facilitates conversation unlike any other. Can't say kinder things about him and recommend him more.

Professor Stump is an extremely down-to-earth and charismatic person who is very engaging during class and is truly passionate about the material. He makes each class very mentally challenging in a fun way, and always had me thinking about the material far after class. I highly recommend taking one of his classes.
Facilitates super interesting class discussions, very understanding, easy to do well in class of you follow syllabus instructions, makes things very clear and comprehensible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Stump is a rockstar of a professor. He makes class incredibly engaging. He takes time to build a real connection with his students. He inspired me and many others to become combined majors or minors in Philosophy. It is very easy to do well in his class and his assignments are very straight forward (he is a light grader). A must take!

Stump is a gem of a person and professor. He is very open and available outside of class. He grades fairly and his assignments have specific instructions when needed. He is understanding and flexible with deadlines. Stump knows his philosophy well and is very passionate. He makes hard concepts and discussions fun to have!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Stump is a gem. He is so funny and is very open about his life. He is very respectful and always helps those who ask. He reads every assignment and is a genuine person and professor. He knows his philosophy well and is passionate when he teaches. If you do the reading and lecture, the course is easy to understand and makes intro to philosophy fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Stump was very engaging! He made learning introductory philosophy fun and kept it relevant. He treated everyone with respect and was very welcoming. He is a fair grader, too! Overall he is a gem of a person and is passionate about philosophy! He is very understanding when it comes to submitting work and is very available outside the class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: As someone who was hesitant to take a class on ancient philosophy, I was pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed it. Jacob's easily accessible outside class, and provided the most useful paper feedback I ever received in undergrad. I highly recommend taking his class, regardless of your major or preconceived notions about philosophy.

Excellent prof and someone you should meet. A previous student told me to, wait and see how he makes participation so easy. Class is fun. Students voice absurd&/brilliant ideas because they trust hell do something productive with them. The work, while intellectually challenging, is simple and short. Take it before he moves on to greater things!

Professor Stump is one of the best philosophy professors I have had an Northeastern. He is kind, engaging in class, and very accessible outside of class. He assigns a lot of small assignments, which can start to stack up. He really cares about the content of the course and is truly inquiring with the class. Take his class for Ancient Phil!

The class was easy if you do the work and is a nice prof. Her prompt for the semester long project is worse compared to other profs who had more engaging or varied options. She does not check in that much with group dynamics or give specific feedback for what you can change to improve your project until after it's done. No say in group selection.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely kind and understanding professor and person overall. She made GE1501 the least stressful class overall. She's super reasonable and takes her feedback (from students) seriously. Always lets us out early and is super accessible outside of class (whether through email or in person). If you get her as your professor, consider yourself lucky.
Kind, approachable, very receptive to feedback. Best professor by a mile!

Professor Jay my beloved. Try to take her if you can, very easy assignments if you are a fairly quick learner. basic C++, Autocad, engineering design process. Just do all the work and it is pretty much a guaranteed A. Some people do bad in the class but that is because they don't know how to code or anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher! Genuinely one of the nicest people ever and so caring. She is so understanding of outside factors and will work with you. Great lectures and very good at explaining everything as well and provides great feedback on assignments!
She is the greatest of all time. That's all I gotta say

Amazing professor to take. She knows her stuff very well and is always available after class. She also prioritizes the mental health of her students and has often pushed back tests or given us time to review when she knew we all had big exams that week.
Jay is super sweet and is very understanding. She is always clear about expectations and is a fair grader!

Professor Jay is an all around amazing professor who cares a lot about her students and understands at the most basic level that everyone has sh*t going on. That makes it super easy to approach her when you don't understand material or are just having general problems with the course.
Extremely kind, super accessible and easy to understand content. Always willing to help, has fun projects, and is lenient.
