BIGGEST ADVICE: GO TO OFFICE HOURS and ask questions, no matter how "stupid", as long as it helps you. An A starts at 91.5(she rounds), + final redemption grade. Super nice lady
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are great- she writes notes with you. Everything is covered in class, but it's your responsibility to study. Exams are hard, so it's important u REALLY understand the material. Super approachable & nice, quick to respond to emails & addresses all ur concerns. Difficult course but she gives u more resources to study with than other profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very kind and so knowledgeable in chemistry. However, the textbook problems and practice do not compare to the difficulty of exams, which make up mostly all of your grade. She is a very tough grader. If you take orgo with her you will learn a lot, but do know that it is very tough

Such a kind professor. But to be honest, her test are NOTHING like the assignments and previous exams as she claims, PREVIOUS ONES R 10x EASIER! She puts EVERYTHING reviewed in class on exam, class avg is usually in the 70s or low 80s. Classes are so hard to sit through and you get exhausted and bored by the end. Ur in for a treat, a GPA bust :(

Danahy is a great lecturer and qualified, but her tests are extremely difficult and the final was worse. She recommends you do the textbook problems + her homework which may seem helpful but come no where near the difficulty of the exams. She's super sweet but her class is very difficult to pass with a good grade :( If you are pre-med save your GPA

There are many mixed reviews about her, but to be completely honest, she is an amazing professor. Chemistry has never been a strong subject for me, but her lectures and office hours show that she is such a great teacher and genuinely wants you to do well. During finals week she provides so many study guides and resources and her TAs are amazing.

Professor Danahy is very sweet and kind. I really enjoyed having her as a professor and would say that she is really great at teaching the material! My only recommendation is that you also need to practice a lot outside of lectures to really grasp the concepts which will be on the tests. I recommend attending office hours when you can.

Great professor and overall really good lectures. Exams get progressively harder (including the cumulative final). Textbook problems are OK for grasping a basic understanding of topics, but come nowhere close to the level of difficulty on exams. Tough grader and not very generous with partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Danahy is very kind and a good professor with engaging lectures, however this class is very difficult. I found the cumulative final was very tough and way harder than the practice. In addition to puzzle sets and poll everywhere there are 3 exams then the final for the overall grade. I definitely learned a lot, though.

The reviews lied...yes Danahy is a good lecturer but her exams are very difficult making it hard to pass with a good grade. Her TA's aren't helpful because they don't understand her assignments and always cancel. The textbook does not help since her questions on exams are totally different than textbook practice problems.

DO NOT TAKE THIS WACK CLASS HER EXAMS ARE SO HARD IT'S INSANE AND HER FINAL WAS A MILLION X WORSE THAN ANYONE COULD EVER IMAGINE. Now you may think I'm dumb or smth but no I did good 2/3 exams but the last killed grade and the final was EXTREMELY hard. No curves, corrections, or extra credit. Good luck if u take her :(

Genuinely might be the best professor I've ever had. I've taken organic chemistry before and love it so that was definitely an advantage but for someone who is brand new and/or scared of orgo, she is AMAZING! You definitely need to read the textbook and do ALL the extra problems. I used a lot of notecards and she was always super easy to email!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Organic chem is hard and while Danahy teaches well in class her exams are EXTREMELY difficult and she is a tough grader. Her TA's aren't helpful bc they dont even understand her weekly puzzle set assignments. I would not recommend or take her again because if you mess up one exam you're done for grade wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a very kind and approachable woman. If conceptualizing content is not easy for you, don't take her. The tests were extremely hard. We were not given much material to study from. We had 2-3 hw to study from for that exam and maybe some textbook problems that did not have much to do with what was going to be on the exam.
Sweetest lady ever.  Sometimes lectures can get confusing but going to extra help definitely helps.  She cares and wants you to do well.

I loved Prof Danahy for Orgo 1! Her lecture style makes it very easy to follow along. Utilizing her and TA's office hours was essential, though. I wish she provided more difficult practice problems/materials as her tests were pretty difficult. She is great with partial credit, though, and truly cares about your success in the class!

I absolutely love Professor Danahy. She is so amazing at what she does. Her lectures are incredible and make ochem seem easy. Her homework is based on participation, and is so helpful for studying because her tests are based on similar questions. Answers emails quickly, and has lots of office hours. Take her if u want to fall in love with chemistry
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is probably, if not the best, organic chemistry teacher! I had her for both organic chemistry 1 and 2, and I got an A in both classes! The most important things are pay attention during class, ask her questions, and review content. You really need a deep understanding of the material to do well. She really cares about her students doing well!

If you honestly want to be prepared for Orgo 2 and fully comprehend Orgo 1 you should definitely take this class with Jude Matthews. Jude may come off as aggressive but she will honestly give you all the material you will need to succeed unlike Danahy. Danahey doesn't teach to learn but to pass with low grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Danahy was one of the best professors that I have had at NU! She did a very good job of explaining the topics in a way that students could easily understand. She provided many examples in class and was very willing to answer questions and re-explain topics. Overall, she is a very kind-hearted professor who wants to see you succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I have taken Danahy for Orgo 1 and 2 and she has been the best prof I could ask for! Exams were open response and personally, that was difficult, but she gives partial credit. Find someone to study with who genuinely wants to help you (there's some stingy pre-health kids), but also utilize office hours and tutoring. Textbook also kind of helped.

As much as Matthews is hyped up, Danahy is a great option for orgo. She emails back super quick if you ask a question and I found her office hours very helpful. The tests are hard, especially the final, but if you put in the work you can absolutely get an A. Participation is taken via Poll Everywhere and you need to complete 90% of questions.

Danahy is a solid option for orgo. She's super sweet and her lectures are very easy to follow. As long as you do the recommended reading and the practice problems you'll get a decent grade. There are three exams and they are graded pretty harshly, it's all free response and she doesn't give a lot of partial credit. Definitely learned a lot though.

My favorite professor I've ever had at NEU. She is SO caring, helpful, and intelligent! I HIGHLY recommend doing the readings before classes, textbook questions after class, rewriting notes, and going to office hours once a week. Lectures are fast paced, but her tests are very predictable and manageable if you stay on top of things. Take her class!

Such a genuinely nice person. I've never had professor be so caring about her students. She wants people to do well and is interested in you as a person. That being said, her class is not easy and her final is hard if you are not the best at orgo. She is probably the smartest professor but very down to earth.
Really good at explaining things, the material on the tests are exactly like in class.

It was a privilege to have Danahy for Orgo 1 - while a bit shy, she is incredibly coherent and intelligent, and more importantly, good at teaching. Her mandatory lectures can be fast-paced at times, though she explains concepts coherently and they MUST be complemented by the textbook and her weekly puzzle sets. 

Also, DO NOT bomb the first exam.
best teacher ive ever had. really wants students do to well

explains things well
- skimming the reading before class and doing the recommended textbook problems within 24 hours of the lecture makes the A
- good review materials and review sessions
- the puzzle sets are basically practice tests, if you study them you will know everything you need to know
- a lot of helpful office hours

TAKE DANAHY. I was so scared of orgo coming into this class but she made the concepts so much easier to understand. Her tests are difficult, but she doesn't throw you any curve balls. Go to office hours! She's definitely a professor you want to form a relationship with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best professor I have at at Northeastern, she is extremely clear about what she expects you to know and she's great at explaining concepts. Tests are open ended; she is very generous with partial credit, and the content of the test is predictable. If you really study an A is within reach.

Her lectures are very important, orgo 1 is just pretty overwhelming to begin with but she made it better for me. It's just not an easy A. It depends if u like lecture heavy and open-ended exams or not

Professor Danahy is one of my favorite professors that I have taken here at Northeastern. She truly cares about how students do in her class and also gives lots of partial credit. She makes the material extremely digestible which is nice for Orgo.

I enjoyed orgo 1 but I feel like her open response tests were just overwhelming for no reason. She gives partial credit but honestly your enjoyment of the class depends on if you enjoy her style of teaching tbh.

Danahy is a very generous grader but her exams are open response and difficult. For Orgo 1 she was fine, but I wish I took Jude for Orgo 2 bc Danahy's overcomplicated and difficult exams felt like we were being set up to get low grades. She is super kind and office hours are sort of helpful. Get a tutor and study immediately after a lecture.

Organic chem is a hard class no matter the professor. Danahy does a decent job explaining the topics. Read the textbook and beware that topics build on each other. Homework is hard but for completion. Exams are very hard but you get to understand her style. Gives generous partial credit. Helpful during office hours. I am taking her again!

Same guy as the previous post. If you want to actually do well, TAKE HER, NOT JUDE. Jude requires tons of work outside of lecture, and her only redeeming quality is multiple choice tests (you can't get partial credit!!) Take Danahy, thank me later.

AWESOME. Prof. Danahy is everything you could ask for for a challenging course like orgo. Her handwritten lecture style is far better than a slideshow style, and she gives examples for every topic presented. I believe that she is the best possible orgo professor, and an A in the class is very manageable if sufficient preparation is done.

Attendance is mandatory. Teacher is very nice but has a tendency to overcomplicate topics when explaining. Exams are open response and she does not curve or give extra credit. Even peer tutors would be confused on the homework she would give. Nice person, did not enjoy the class at all. Had to learn most of the content myself outside of class

If you're someone who benefits from handwriting notes, having a relationship with your profs, and values a smaller class size Danahy is your professor. HW is in the form of puzzle sets which are challenging but so helpful for exams, office hours are accessible, and lectures are actually understandable. Orgo isn't easy but she makes it manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a nice professor, however her teaching style is definitely different. Her exams focus on the process of why something is the way it is more than the products, i.e explain why this carbonyl is more nucleophilic, or why is this compound have a certain composition? Take a different prof with multiple choice exams and not a cumulative final......

This woman is so slept on. She is wonderful! If you put in the work and aks questions you will get it. She is so willing to help and responds to questions and emails so very fast. She is always willing to help and is the cutest human I know! I love her soo much! TAKE HER! Better than Jude!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love the way she explains chemistry! Lectures are clear and easy to understand. Tests are fair and class is manageable.

Prof. Danahy teaches Orgo 2 really well. The tests are open-ended, not multiple choice, which makes studying for them trickier since you need to know the content, but there's lots of partial credit. Going to class and taking good notes is important to learn the material, the puzzle sets also give a good insight into what test questions are like.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 3 unit exams and 1 final exam, puzzle sets are very hard so I recommend the peer tutors for help. She is always available outside of class. Orgo is very difficult but she makes it bearable. Exams are mostly open ended but she gives a ton of partial credit. Definitely take her if you have the option.

Kelley is the sweetest prof ever!! She cares so much about all her students and is very passionate about what she teaches. The exams, though open-ended, were a lot easier than the homework assignments and she's a very lenient grader (she will defs give you points wherever she can)

She is thorough with her lectures and her exams are somewhat difficult but very fair. There are some open ended questions however you can get partial credit for these. There are a few homework assignments graded on completion which boost your grade a little. She also takes time to answer every question during class and in office hours.

I loved Professor Danahy. She's passionate about chemistry. She writes down examples and notes as she talks about them and focuses on concepts that may not otherwise be focused by other teachers. The homework she gives is hard, but is graded for effort/completion. She prepares you well for the free response exams - nothing comes as a shock.

Danahy was one of the few professors that I've had where she seemed like she wanted us to learn something. I found that she explained topics clearly and was happy to answer any question that we had, either during lecture, office hours, or over email. Exams are exactly what she teaches, and homework really prepares you for exam material.

Professor Danahy is one of the best professors that I have had. She is always available and super helpful in her office hours. The exams are open response, which was difficult, but she gave fair partial credit. She returns emails and grades very quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is such a nice professor! I didn't prefer her teaching style - several concepts were made very confusing and overcomplicated. I had gone to her office hours multiple times and I didn't feel like she would help explain problems and often left confused. Her homework assignments were also very tricky that it confused my peer tutors at times.
She is passionate about chem! Personally, I did not enjoy her style of teaching. I came to her when I was struggling and she did not try to help. Her example problems even confused the peer tutors.
Homework was difficult but prepared you for the free response exams. Questions were a bit confusing at times. Very accesible outside of class and really cares
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great prof that loves chemistry. She has some great lectures that you need to answer a poll to get credit for. Very information dense, but that's how organic chemistry is, and she drills the ideas into your head. She really wants her students to understand everything instead of memorizing. Very tough hw but it teaches you how she wants you to think

I had Danahy for orgo 1, great lecturer and good at explaining. She always responded to emails quickly. However the puzzle sets are very hard and prepare to study beyond the lecture material. She gives a lot of partial credit on tests. Overall I recommend her but her class is a little difficult, I thought I did a lot better than the grade I got.

I had Prof Danahy for CHEM 2311 but she was an absolutely amazing professor. Takes her time explaining tough concepts in class, is truly caring about her students, and is always accessible out of class for office hours and fit you in outside of them as well. Exams are open response but A LOT of partial credit. HW is great bc it preps for the exam.

Absolutely love her! She is always available outside of class and over email. Tests can be intimidating due to free response, but if you understand the homework and lectures you will be fine. She clearly cares for her students and hints at what may be on the test. Also gives lots of partial credit on tests.

Keivan's an engaging professor although the course is inevitably lecture heavy. He doesn't follow the same structure as other sections so comparing content with people in other classes isn't helpful, however he's clear in his specific expectations. Offers bonus points during the semester; exams are easy as long as you study (2 midterms, no final).

Took him for 3308, not 2301. He is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. He knows the material through and through, so it is super easy to get things cleared up if you are confused. Most of the time, he shows up to class with just a marker and has the whole lecture planned in his head. Lecture heavy but they are easy to follow and fun

Nicest professor at Northeastern to where I voted for best professor for DMSB. His classes fill up quickly which shows how great of a professor he is. Please take him for the intro class. I wish I could have him for the upper division courses.

Prof Sadeghzadeh is genuinely so nice and articulate with his lectures. He only tests you on material you explicitly went over in class, which was very digestible and simplified a lot of what the textbook was trying to convey. You honestly get out what you put in, it is a chill class if you want it to be but you can really learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this professor, you won't regret it.
I could not recommend him enough. Fair grader and gives great practice for exams. Take him. Lots of group work, so just hope you get a good one.
Amazing teacher, I highly recommend

Professor Sadeghzadeh was an amazing professor. He always came prepared, and his lectures were highly interesting. He offered in-class extra credit points, making participation only help, not hurt, your grade. I recommend taking Professor Sadeghzadeh.
Great professor, makes sure students understand the material well

One of the best professors I've ever had. He cares about every student, somehow manages to make lectures on a boring topic engaging. Makes it very clear what is going to be on the exam, manageable if you study for a few hours a few days before. Has a review class the day before exam so study before then and come with questions.
Love him, actually knows how to teach. He does a lot of problems on board so its important to come to class

Professor Keivan is a incredible professor. He had the magical ability to make every student of his engaged and feel like they are apart of something more than just a classroom. He is incredibly resourceful, respectful and accessible outside of class, he makes time for his students which i really appreciated.

Keivan was an amazing professor, he makes a super boring subject extremely interesting and engaging. He's funny, kind, and always available outside of class. The exams are a bit hard but very doable if you just study. Take his class!!

Excellent professor and would recommend. Real passion for the subject and has made me want to concentrate in Supply Chain. Have to do well on tests to get good grade. Module games are time-consuming and not super educational but I thought they were fun once you figure them out. Lots of assignments due at end of semester but no final.

Keivan is a super chill guy would recommend for Supply Chain There are practice modules that are tedious and a group project but it wasn't too bad. There are two tests each 13 questions based on what he teaches in class and any extra material given not in the textbook. Offers bonus points throughout the semester for answering a question correctly.

Had her for Cornerstone 1 and 2, and she is such a sweet, kind, and caring person. There are quite a lot of assignments on top of group projects, but she is understanding and if you manage your time, you'll be fine! She is very clear about what she's looking for so it's not hard to do good in her class.

I enjoyed this class. Dr. Keyvani is such a nice, caring, and charismatic person. She is very understanding and is always ready to help when u need it. She provides so many resources if you are struggling, and her lectures are long but helpful. An overall wonderful professor!

Cares about the students and is extremely helpful. Sometimes assignments were not graded very quickly, however you can just ask her anything and she provides great examples. Learned a lot from her and it is easy to talk to outside the classroom. Very understanding.
Confused teacher. Does not allow to code independently

Keyvani cares alot about the wellbeing of her students and was an amazing lecturer. Watch out for group projects because they can be brutal, but she is very understanding of any hiccups and difficulties as long as you put in effort

An amazing lecturer who was pretty accessible outside of class. There was one semester long project that got to be a lot at some points and was pretty stressful, but she understood that and helped in every way she could.
Lots

Took for full cornerstone, so there was a lot of material in little time, but she spaced out due dates and was available for office hours. The assignments will be difficult, and the grading is tough, but if you actually do them yourself you will be very prepared for exams. And the group projects are annoying but graded lightly.

Professor Keyvani is amazing. She is very helpful in answering questions and working with you if you are struggling. The only textbook requirement was a TopHat course online. There is a lot of work outside of class but it's worth it and I was able to add a lot onto my resume just from one semester.

Professor Keyvani is an excellent prof who cares about her students. I took stacked cornerstone with her and I have learned more than any other class. Definitely be prepared for a lot of assignments and group projects. The pace is very fast. The rubrics can be vague sometimes, but if you ask for help she is always willing to provide clarification.

I'm doing stacked cornerstone and Keyvani is a phenomenal professor. Be prepared for lots of homework and multiple projects. Assignments can be confusing but if you follow the rubric you will be fine. She is very kind and you learn a lot from her lectures. Very fast-paced, and grading is very strict. Lots of work, but it is so worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was a lot of work but worth it. The professor can be confusing with directions sometimes but she is really nice. She challenges you to think through possible solutions. I found the class valuable with all the material you learn and the presenting, leadership, and organizational skills you gain while taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT take Professor Keyvani for stacked cornerstone of engineering. She makes this course extremely difficult compared to other professors. She gives you no free time and her instructions for her assignments are often unclear. Be prepared for a 100+ page paper after your second final project. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: For an introductory course, this class was extremely difficult. I spent upwards of 10 hours a week working on the projects with our group. We had a semester long project, with homework divided up week by week. The instructions for each week were very vague and difficult to understand, and when asking for clarification, we were not given any.

Professor Keyvani is a nice person and will make sure to help you when you have problems. HOWEVER, if you plan on taking Stacked Cornerstone of Engineering with her be prepared to have little to no free time. There are two major projects you will have to complete alongside countless minor projects. The pace will be fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I- she just gave us a project and we had to hand in a draft from 50%-80% complete. Said it was fine to do 50%. Then gave us bag grades for only doing 50%. Most of your grading comes from peer reviews (other students) and TA's. The peer reviews are not nice. engineerings are annoying. i dont get why you would give ur classmate a bad grade. 3/10

Professor is really kind and accommodating, especially when you ask her specific questions in class. She will spend time doing her best to help you. One problem is that her instructions can be vague and confusing, especially since there are usually 2 or more assignments going on at once. You can tell she really loves teaching & engineering.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: with online learning--she doesn't teach us much in class; it is up to us to use the resources she provides to learn the material on our own time. she assigns a lot of group projects and uses peer-review grades as real grades (your peers will not usually be nice). otherwise, the TA grades many diff websites to do work/hand stuff in--confusing

Professor Keyvani is very strict with her grading, but I would say that she is pretty fair. If you get all your work done, you are likely to finish with an A. The group projects are nice, but I could do without the final. It was difficult and redundant, and it wasn't related to anything we did in class.

Professor Keyvani is one of the young professors in college of engineering. She is a fun and caring person. She gives so much homework and is strict about grading. The lectures are usually interactive and the whole class passes with group projects, which is very helpful for the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Keyvani is so sweet and puts a lot of effort into making the class educational and understandable. As long as you follow the assignment rubrics, you'll do fine.

This Prof. is crystal clear with explanations and is always willing to offer help. The class itself is pretty easy but she makes you fully understand the material. She is willing to work with you (and the class) as a whole to make sure you understand and do the best.

This professor is super enthusiastic and willing to make the class engaging and fun by her humorous tone. She definitely wants to bond with students during class. You should take her, she is amazing, and her class is super chill. Mostly based on group projects and some quizzes.

Professor Coleman is very kind, taking the time to get to know all of her students and very engaging for an 8 am class. There are pop quizzes but not too difficult, but doesn't give easy 100s on homework assignments. There is a semester long group-project that is randomly assigned and worth most of your grade. Definitely important to participate!
Yes, there are pop quizzes, but she drops the lowest. She is super kind, and she wants you to succeed. Build a relationship w her too, she is great

Professor Coleman reminds me a lot of a high school teacher in the best ways, she's super caring and very easy to get along with. The class itself is super easy all year and as long as you get along with your partners you should be fine for the group presentations.

A kind and caring professor who loves discussing business. Participation matters, and she enjoys engaged students. Expect group projects and presentations in 1101. She's a tough but fair grader and accepts late work.

Super kind and her pop quizzes are easy if you do the readings (they are short). She does have favorites so just participate. The whole class is based on a group project. Do go to class or your grade will take a hit. Very easy to reach her outside of class. Overall a fun class that is not difficult. Be prepared to present a few times!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A very enthusiastic and sweet professor. Makes it super easy to contact her, allows students to text/call her when needed. I was required to take this class, and I didn't find it super necessary.. but she's great. Kind of harsh grader so make sure you follow rubrics and feedback.
An amazing professor who is always available during office hours. Grade is determined by a few writing projects; however, Professor Kehoe gives clear feedback on the drafts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kehoe is a very kind and thoughtful lady. Your grade is primarily broken down into 4 writing projects, with multiple drafts due in each. The projects were different from other writing projects I have completed and offered a new set of skills in each. She is an EXTREMELY lenient grader; I finished with a 99.75.

She's a kind teacher; I'm relieved to have had her my first year as I've heard other profs' assignments for first-year writing classes. While there are only 3-4 projects, it seemed pretty easy. Each project became more group oriented, however make sure you do it since writing accounts for I think ~85% of the grade. Not a harsh grader and has OH.

Prof Kehoe was great to have during my first year! She has a really clear and organized Canvas with lots of resources and information needed to do her work. Really entertaining class to be a part of, not too much of a workload. Would definitely take her class again if I had to.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is boring. She talked quietly, and any fun I had in class was from myself. Four projects make up your grade, with 2-3 being essays. I wish she was more engaging or something like that. Attendance is a grade also so don't skip.

Lectures are long and can be boring if you're not interested in what she's talking about. However, she is really knowledgable and has a lot of cool stories. The class is not hard, but go to class. She lectures off the noggin, so you have to be there to get notes. She answers emails quick, but it will seem like she's mad at you. Overall chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's very intelligent but the class is based on 4 assignments and she grades incredibly hard for an introduction class. Goes on tangents that take up class time and doesn't post on Canvas, leaving many assignments unclear. I took this class for an NUPath requirement and I would only recommend taking it if it's required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall really chill course. Consists of 2 midterm papers, a final presentation and a final paper. She doesn't take attendance but it's important you go to class because there are no in class slides on canvas. Because of that classes can be a little dreadful and long cause you have to make sure to pay attention, but I would take again!

Professor Kelting was a very nice person. However, her class is only graded on 3 assignments. 2 exams and an essay which is only done outside of class time. The only lecture notes are the ones she says during class and there are no slides to follow along to, and her lectures are not recorded. Dont take this class unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof. kelting is very nice, seems like she cares about her students and the class load is generally pretty light. the final paper was graded in less than a week so the grading comments read like she only took a cursory skim of the essay. i'd reccomend taking another class if you're actually knowledgeable or passionate about the topic

Never done a review here, but Kelting definitely deserves it. Essentially, you come into class and sit down and take notes on her lecture for the hour. But she is incredibly knowledgeable, engaging, and clear, and I look forward to class every time. If you go to the classes and take notes, the tests are intuitive, and she is a very fair grader.

Professor Kelting is a very good professor overall. Lectures were very interesting and she knows her material well. There were two exams, which were free response questions. You should attend lectures to answer them well, and don't need to do any of the readings. There is also a ten-page research paper, but there is ample time to do it.

Please do yourself a favor and do NOT take her class. As an elective, this class is very hard and requires so much writing. There’s also a 10 page research paper with exams every few week. She’s a nice lady but doesn't explain stuff relevant to the exam. DO NOT TAKE IT!!!! I did the mistake of taking because it’s “online”
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Kelting is an amazing person and very easy to approach. Get ready to attend all classes and take notes because her exams are based on that. There are many readings but I didn't do them and still got an A. She isn't the most responsive person by email so it's better to ask your doubts in class. Also her grading is vague with no feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The topics in this class are super interesting and she clearly knows a lot about the subject, but she is incredibly aloof, does not reply to emails and gives very vague instructions to the assignments, which leads to low grades for things you didn't even know she wanted in the first place! Just avoid if you can, unless you love the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: while she is a very kind and positive person, kelting is not a good professor. she is all over the place when it comes to her lectures, she is inconsistent with providing information about class work and exams/homework, and she is very bad at responding to emails. i would not recommend this class as it is just so much to deal with.
Very Good Professor, smart in Eastern & Western Religions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: OMG! I would never a take class with her again. She is all over the place and dosen't know how to deliver her thoughts. I probably didn't have one complete sentence written in my notes. She also has many facts about Hinduism and Buddhism wrong, since my family is Hindu I could vouch for certain traditions. She also never gives back papers on time.

You don't have to do any readings to get an A. Show up to class and prepare to take notes. 3 grades are a take home midterm, take home final, and research paper. She's a ridiculously easy grader. Tries to be open minded nice but was surprisingly rude. I will never forget hearing her say people with skin conditions are broken and need to be cured ew
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Kelting is an amazing professor! In her class on Islam, I have learned all about that religion and beyond. You absolutely have to attend lectures as she is the main source of information and without the notes you won't be able to get a good grade in the class.

Kelting is super cool, really smart, and one of the nicest profs you'll ever have. She's super down to earth and understands what it's like to be a a student. However, she is all over the place. She has a lot going on and puts grading on the back burner. I did not get a single grade (for either of the two classes I took with her) until mid-April.

I took her class last year and she was an amazing woman. She's so fascinating. Knows a TON about religion. She assigns a couple cool projects - like she'll have you go to a religious service (of a different religion than your own) and write about it . Very cool. She uses blue books for exams.

I really enjoyed her class; I think she's a great teacher. You do a lot of reading, take a mid-term and final and write a research paper. It isn't an extraordinary amount of work. We're in college, right? She knows her stuff--speaks Farsi and has lived extensively in India. Very friendly. I took detailed notes, used those for exam and got an A.

Kelting is great. One of my favorites and I would love to take another of her classes. Seems to really know what she's talking about and makes for some truly interesting lectures. Assigns a great deal of reading but doesn't use it on the exams, which are essay format.

Loved the class and Kelting and am definately planning on taking her other course offerings. She is interesting and passionate about the class and accepts and encourages student input both in and outside of class. A great professor, my favorite so far at northeastern.  Good amount of work and fair.

Prof. Kelting offers challenging courses (I've taken two) and heaps on the work. I have no problem with that. I'm here to learn. She's taught me a lot. Her enthusiasm, availability, and helpfulness are above and-beyond. It's sick that the negative reviews of Prof. Kelting here stress how much work she requires. Stop whining and try studying!

Kelting is one of the best professors at NU.  She is funny, open, warm, engaging, and INCREDIBLY knowledgeable.  She is constantly striving to improve the classroom experience in any way possible.  She does a great job of writing notes on the board as well as giving examples most people can relate to.  Highly recommended!!!!
Awful class. Huge amounts of reading, but tests/papers are on her terrible notes. Took class as requirement, bad idea. Way too much work, and way too difficult. Take an easier class.

Very smart, personable.  Lectures are very interesting, Kelting makes room for some discussion and interaction.  Reading is decent except for when we start a new unit.  Midterm was difficult, but papers are easy if you pace yourself responsibly.  2 papers, 1 is small, 1 is a larger research paper.  In class essay midterm and final.

Obviously, there's a difference between the Islam and East. Rel. ratings. Here's my opinion: This prof is AWESOME. So funny, so enthusiastic, so clear in how she explains things. One of the best NU profs I've had. Easy tests if you read and take good notes.  HE IS SO SMART and has knowledge about practically everything in the world. Great person.

Clearly a very inteligent professor and deserves respect for it.  I took this course to satisfy a diversity credit (as most did) and there was more work involved than I anticipated. A lot of reading to do. Her tests are passable if you do the readings. If you are just trying to meet a diversity requirement however I suggest taking an easier course.

This ... is the world class I've ever taken in my whole life. I wish I would've come here to see what people had to say first. Do yourself a favor if you're thinking about taking this class ... and just run away. Anywhere. Anywhere but wherever Kelting is.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  It's awful. There is so much work, including a 10-page research paper.  It is so hard and everything about it sucks.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Worst professor I've ever had.  Erratic, unclear teaching style.  She pays attention to 1 or 2 kids in the class and then forgets anyone else is even there.  Thank god we had some books to read because what she taught us in class was utterly useless.  Do youself a favor and avoid her at all costs, that is if she still has a job!!!!

Fabulous professor - best ever! Lots of reading, lots of papers and wonderful, engaging and respectful class discussions. Not an easy class but you get back what you put in - she is very open to students and one of the most intelligent people I've ever had the pleasure of meeting.  Would highly reco

Terrible teacher, unclear, crazy in a bad way, immature.  Bad teacher = uninformed and confused students = bad grades = bad vibes.  Acts friendly to your face and stabs you in the back.  Stay away from this one, if not for your time than for your GPA.

Don't take her for this class! She's a very nice and fun person but won't teach you anything worthwhile and her grading sucks. She expects you to write quite a few papers the second half of the semester and there's lots of reading. Tends to repeat what's in the reading. Made a cool topic very boring
This class sounded great in theory but is SO much more trouble than its worth.  Her essay assignements are unclear which makes her hard to please and the expected reading every week is unreasonable
She's very funny, but that doesn't really make up for the boring class...I don't feel I've learned anything in it, pretty much a waste of time.

Very nice lady, but this class is extremely boring.  It has no modern world context whatsoever, and often focuses too heavily on the theoretical/historical aspects of Islam.  Random, boring tangents are not uncommon for her.  After the class, you feel like you've learned nothing that day.

She is extremely personable and excited about her classes.  She is very intelligent but she teaches on a level for beginners.  I agree with the statement that her tests don't always let you showcase what you know but overall I don't think she's a hard grader.

This professor is AWESOME. Very funny, has great stories. The class is easy esp her essays. she can unclear about topic. her tests are little tougher because they don't quite pertain to lectures; her readings don't at all. overall, the class is great- highly recommended

I agree with the previous comments: very friendly, excellent sense of humor and TONS of knowledge. Still, the tests are based on "pick two out of three" essays that are somewhat narrow and don't allow you to show what you really know. Definitely an interesting and rewarding class, though!

One of the best professors at NU.  She knows everything about everything, presents it with great sense of humor, and is very personable and friendly, and very flexible with grades and deadlines.  Short essay assignments, essay exams, opportunities for extra credit- easy to get a decent grade.
Sooo funny.  Lots of reading, but not too hard of a class

Professor was very nice. The lectures are detailed and clear with many practice questions and examples for better understanding. Only 3 exams in total with some very do - able homework. Allows cheat sheet for exams and some exam prep questions are also on the exam itself. Overall, great experience, very nice Professor!

Amazing teacher, really wants to help his students. I really enjoyed his class and found him to be one of the best professors I have had at this school. He makes the subject simple and breaks it down so that everyone can understand.

He's one of those professors whose enthusiasm for a subject wears off on you, and you find yourself excited about something as basic as intro stats. His class is lecture-heavy, but so engaging that time flies by. He's available to discuss anything you might be working on outside of class, and he did so happily (most of the time).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him for INSH 6500 which is Statistical Analysis as an in-person class. I did not have a good experience with him, most of the homework took me anywhere from 3 to 6 hours for a maximum of 5 questions. Also, the projects were not good either. It took me and several other people 5-10 hours per project and we'd get different answers to them.

He is one of the best-balanced professors I've taken. Assignment due dates are clearly communicated. The workload is well-structured and manageable. His video lectures are light. The assignments are clear and well-organized, and he gives detailed instructions along with a grading rubric for all writing assignments. I would take his classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Shantanu is a really good prof who cares about you and wants you to do well and will do everything he can to help you get there. His lectures are engaging and is very open to questions. Gives many practice questions for revision and midterms (2) do not contain anything out of practice. HW are usually easy-medium, shout out to TA Dayonara!

Methodology revolves around getting students to think outside the box and highly philosophical only for tests/exams to be true or false questions, which goes against this way of teaching. Participation is based on how "smart" your answers are and results in a curve for participation, which is incredibly unfair

Professor Khrapko is incredibly knowledgeable and kind. He cares a lot about genomics, and tries hard to teach very difficult concepts. There is NO busy work in this class, so you just focus on making sure you understand content. Being involved during class by asking questions is the best way to succeed. Very generous with extra credit.
Some may not see it clearly, but one of the best professors at Northeastern! 10/10 would take again, this is not a professor for taking a class, he is one to insight wonder and interest!

Dr. Khrapko is fantastic but NOT everyone's cup of tea. Super passionate about the topic, really challenges you and makes you think, but his assessment style is unique (peer grading) and his slides are not helpful without having attended lecture. If you want super organized class he might not be for you- but he is a lot of fun and genuinely cares!

While Dr. Khrapko is very intelligent, his class is organized terribly. The peer grading system is broken and run by his TA, and the assignments are a pain. The lectures are long and difficult to sit through, and I won't know my grades until the day of or before the optional final. Overall, I would advise against taking this section of the course.

The professor is brilliant but is not a great teacher. Doesn't explain a lot of terms. This class requires a lot of attention. So if you struggle with a long attention span, this class is very difficult. Class is not structured well and I learn better with organized lectures so I had a horrible time keeping up with the content.
Yes.

Even those that do not see Prof. Khrapko as a good professor will agree that he is a wonderful person. I, however, also thought his approach to BIOL5591 was both innovative and useful. Students may be initially uncomfortable in a peer-graded, lecture-based course, but the key to success is not working against the system, but to embrace it!

Professor Konstantin's style is unique and challenging, and so many students are uncomfortable in his class. But this is not a bad thing. He challenges you to think critically, and if you do then you will be rewarded not only with an A but also with more skills and knowledge than you thought you could ever get from a single class.
Very disorganized and even disrespectful at times. The homework is peer reviewed, which is awful and completely subjective with no rubric or answer key. Definitely avoid him if you can.

Makes students grade each other's HW. Couldn't respond to emails. Changed the syllabus halfway in semester to reward the inherently smart kids. Couldn't follow his own syllabus. Graded on SDs from the mean which rewards the inherently smart kids again. Couldn't communicate a lesson properly. Homework sets were ridiculously difficult.

He is super smart but horrible at teaching. Talks in circles, contradicts himself, loses his train of thought, extremely disorganized. The grading is incredibly arbitrary and you have to go above and beyond in order to get an A. Study groups to collaborate on the homework are a must. I would definitely not take a course from him again.

Really nice man and clearly loves what he is teaching - however, the lectures are extremely long and disorganized and the peer-graded homework is normalized to a curve (but we're not provided with answers keys to use while grading). If you're not required to take this class and don't have a deep interest in genomics, I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute gem of a human being. Super passionate about what he teaches and wants everyone to succeed. That being said, he is brilliant - almost too brilliant to be teaching college kids and lectures can be decently unorganized. But if you show up and pay attention you will do perfectly fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. He's clearly intelligent but has the worst presentation skills. Nothing is made clear in class and the grading criteria for peer-graded homework is so arbitrary. Definitely need a solid study group.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This man is a national treasure. I wholeheartedly recommend taking his class. All the nonsense that goes along with a lot of classes at Northeastern is stripped away and you're allowed to just be interested in a subject and to learn it. Khrapko is hilarious and really respects his students

Get a study group on day one, since the only assignments are 4, ten short answer assignments that are graded by your fellow classmates. Helps to attend his office hours to discuss the questions and anything unclear to gain understanding! Very accommodating and will schedule more office hours if you ask. Loves when you participate in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: You get peer graded on homework, no exams. No textbook, just lectures. He does Tegrity if you want him to. GET A STUDY GROUP EARLY (like day 1). Do not leave homework for the day before, you won't get it. Honestly, best class I've taken at NEU. I learned so much and it really helped on job/co-op interviews. I can explain NGS at the drop of a hat!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class was extremely boring and you WILL fall asleep but thats because the subject itself isnt very interesting. The professor himself, though, is a pretty nice guy. Going to class every day gets you an extra 5% of your total grade and there's also an extra 2.5% for doing HW. Study past exams and class slides and you will get an A.

Good thing about this professor is he provides the previous exams and everything he says is in the book. The bad thing is that he does not give answers to the previous exams and he uses highly technical language. For an introduction to immunology it's almost overwhelming especially since he doesn't organize his slides well.
Immunology is about as interesting as watching the paint peal of your walls. But he's a nice guy.  Study past exams for the midterms and pray on the final.

The class was mostly easy hes a pretty good grader and an understanding nice guy a bit boring though and the 4 hour lecture was insufferable but overall easy class to take and do well in as long as you attend regulary and keep up with the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a heavy group project, so it's important to have a good group. The professor does try to help students work through issues with difficult groups, but your group's performance can still impact your grade. Overall, he is very kind and genuinely wants students to succeed. The 4-hour class is not as bad as it seems once you get into it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took the wub for innovation. To be honest the entire class really depends on your group, so please pick a good group and topic. He was genuinely not a tough grader and graded my group higher than we lowkey deserved. However the class is pretty exhausting when the assignments are all due at once. Quizzes aren't bad if you go to class

I'm genuinely confused about a lot of these negative reviews. I think a lot of the class hinges on whether you get a good group, but generally I feel like he's a pretty engaging lecturer and an understanding Professor. Innovation! with Prof. Wubneh in 2025 was pretty easy, all of my friends have 90's or above, and the workload is super manageable.
Nice prof but this class took 10 years off my lifespan

The course itself is somewhat strange and annoying - it requires a lot of reading/participation. As he would say, "his hands are tied" and the course kinda sucks sometimes, but he's a fairly nice person who can grade harshly. He tries his best to make it interesting. Pick a good group because group work is a big part of the semester/ grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
He's not as bad as people make him out to be in all reality. You definitely have to come to class and come to class ON TIME. Be sure to pick a good group at the start of the term since this will be your group for the whole term. 

People are harsh on the Wub but he's a nice guy when you get to know him.
Harsh grader
The Wub is inevitable.

Guy is nice but still new to teaching so he isnt the most organized, clear, tech savy, or best teacher. If you put in the time you will do fine but its so draining if you do. We had case studies, group project/presentations, quizes, and tests. Lectures are boring and he just goes on and on to an unnecessary extent.

He is a nice guy dont get me wrong, but he holds students to a impossible standard. His grading was the harshest ive seen at neu, and he did not provide guidelines. His quizzes are purposefully confusing didnt prepare us for the final. Despite reaching out several times regarding issues with teammates on the group project he did not intervene.

Overall a frustrating class to attend. It was Prof. Wubneh's first semester teaching at Northeastern, so a lot of his  lessons were still a work in progress, and seemed to always have some tech or other problem. His tests did not correlate to the final exam and and not much feedback on assignments was provided. Hopefully he will improve over time!

it was his first semester ever teaching here so i give him some slack but being part of his learning process was torturous. innovation is an NU Path class, not a major specific class that should have had this much work. he barely gave feedback on assignments, graded so tough, and was just overall frustrating. hes a good person though, he cares
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Avoid the Wub with your life unless you wanna get absolutely pummeled by lots of readings, quizzes, papers, case studies, etc. and harsh grading. Most boring class I've ever taken. Avoid at all costs.
not the best teacher, the tests he gives in class are very irrelevant to the final exam format
Great professor. Awesome sense of humor. I would take every class with him if I could.

O, my. Khalil makes the topic interesting with his Afro-twist on sociology and anthropology, as his background includes Rasta and hip-hop (you'll learn the etymology of that term). His disdain for the dregs of the university system makes him relatable. You'll want to come to class just to look at him, and I enjoyed the discussion-oriented classes.

Virtually no work for the class and all you do is sit there and listen to other people babble about things.  If you have a class that's into the material, it's great, but otherwise you're just wasting your time.
No Comments

We never had a test during the entire semester.  Our grades were only based on three ethnographies, a book review, and a final.  When many of us received grades in the low 80s, he simply kept telling us how easy it was to write a good ethnography, but never gave an example.  He offers more extra credit assignments than actual work.

Either hit or miss, asleep or riveted in class. Only grades ethnography and book report at end, plus a ton of available extra credit. I wish the class was harder because it's definitely one that you COULD get a lot out of. I thought he was a bit on the weird and pretentious side though. Just love Marx as much as he does and you're golden.
Awesome class, amazing professor. If you take any class he teaches, you'll learn so much from it and have fun at the same time. And no tests, just papers and journals.
He's very into the subject which he teaches.  Open to new and different opinions and is willing to help you if you put out the effort.  Great professor!

This prof gave me a reason to go to a 9:50 during summer 2, and not just b/c he was nice to look at.  The class is seriously one of the best I've had so far at northeastern.  If you put the effort into it you get plenty out of it.

One of my favorites at NU. Extremely knowledgeable in social theory, esp. Marx, Foucault, Lacan and Freud, among many others. Can seem arrogant but is much more personable outside of class. He's all about essays though, no exams.
most people like him, but i thought he was pretentious--too good for the class, too good for northeastern, too good for teaching. the class itself was easy - if you show up you do fine.

I was really excited aboout taking this class but I ended up bored. He would be a great teacher in a group of eclectic students. My class was full of kids who'd grown up in a middle class suburbia who all seemed to think alike. This class had great potential to spark great discussions and debates, but sadly, this never happened.
he's a good teacher, but this class would be amazing no matter who taught it. just take this class period. he's also good.

He is an awsome professor!! His classes are always great and he makes everything interesting. He never gives exams but a fair amount of papers. If you prefer papers instead of exams, like I do, then I suggest you take any of his classes.

Awesome teacher, I actually looked forward to the class and the assignments.  He relates to the students on their level, and class discussions were always active and interesting.  Plus, yah, he is hot.

Great Class, i'd take it for fun! Talk with people from all over the world, people from different backgrounds bring different thing to the table,  The first class that i've taken that teaches life not just facts
Great class-for the most part lectures are interesting, though some of the reading is boring. But the professor is the best I've had at NU. Awesome class.

This guy is by far the best professor at NU.  I've never taken a class that was so interesting and fun.  Its probably the only class that I acctually look forward to going to.  I'm taking another class with him next semister.  If you can deff take a class with this guy.  He is the man.

This class is really interesting and yes, as everyone else has said, he is pretty attractive. He's also really funny and makes you think. Class discussions are never boring. Some of the readings are boring or repetitive, but a lot of them are valuable and really relate to discussions.
Best class at Northeastern.  Not too much work, but you'll learn so much.  You have to go in with an open mind...
Peoples and cultures was an alright class. A lot of focus on countries other than US and Europe.  Saucier is a very cool guy.  Laid back and easy to approach.

Love the class, pretty easy so far. the material is really interesting and there are usually good discussions. a good amount of reading though, but its not that bad. but what makes it all worthwhile is that he is sooooooooooooooo hot! i love him! do the reading and speak up and you'll be fine.
HOTTTT! Very educative and informative class. Class discussions are amazing. the guy is amazing! Def take this class.
By far one of my favorite professors at NU. He's a really great guy who knows what he's talking about and presents it in an interesting way. I highly reccomend taking a class with him.

This is one of the best classes I've take at NU and he does a great job teaching it. If you like writing papers/are good at it, this class is perfect for you otherwise I'd advise not taking it. He likes if you incorporate other new ideas into papers- different is good. yeah, he's a hottie for sure.

He is a total hottie, which makes this class awesome! Some days it is hard to pay attention! Overall though, he is a really cool guy and makes the class interesting--Just do what you are asked and you will be fine.
Very cool guy..really laid back..no tests, all papers based on short books that we read...best part of class--the fact that he's really hot...
Really interesting class.  Very laid back. SO hott.  Totally made it worth while going to class over the summer.
Great teacher, loves class discussions, interesting, not a hard class if you do what is asked. H'es kinda hot too!
He had some great lectures and although he was tough on my classmate Diego V, we all were able to finish his course.

When I told Kimani I couldn't make it to class, he checked my course schedule and basically did a background check on which other classes I had and when. It was really invasive and out of the scope of what he's supposed to do. He is very strict with his attendance policy for no reason. Would highly not recommend. Very rude attitude towards students

First non A in college and honestly it was my fault. If you do the class the way it is intended by Kimani, you will do well. You just need to on it 100% of the time. You can have a pop quiz any day, any time so you need to pay attention every minute of class. Do not take this class if you cant dedicate the time it needs. Lectures are boring
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Taught myself outside of class but thats understandable and the topics are interesting. Grading policy is fair although labs are quite heavy (my tip: work with a partner). My main complaint is the TAs which are grad students who have very harsh grading and super unhelpful, they never know whats going on. Not a bad class (even better w good ta's).

Professor is very kind, approachable and his teaching style is clear to follow along to. Even though the class can be challenging, the grading policies are very forgiving (two optional homeworks, lowest homework grade dropped, lowest exam grade dropped).

The class was easy. The lab was hard. Slides were good. Homeworks easy and quick. I attended three classes; one for the midterm, one for the second midterm, and another with my girlfriend to explain why I wasn't going to the class. Exams not bad. Optional attendance for this class is the most effective method of suicide prevention.
Very nice guy. The course was rather hard, but worth it for the teacher. He was very helpful, and the class was fun. A bit of knowledge is necessary before the class, but I had enough to pass!

Not that great, the TAs don't care and take off points from assignments & labs for no reason and the instructor never checks them. The exams are poorly written and professor assumes everyone knows what the content is. He always says you can do well in the class if "you know what is going on."
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kimani is a nice person and relatively cares about how you apply your knowledge in the industry if you ever considering pursuing EECE or EECS. However, he seems to rush through the content and lots of the course content is pretty much copied from UC Berkley (refer to RISC-V assembly lectures). Class is 80% exams and one exam can ruin your grade.
I loved him.

Not too bad of a class if you have some coding foundation. Seems passionate about what he does and a overall nice guy. Exams weren't too difficult and projects can be done with a group (of up to 3 I believe)

Kimani offers long pseudo-monotonic lectures that can put one to sleep. He is funny, kind, and generally understanding, but I found the class hard to engage in. The homework assignments aren't too bad but beware, he does not give any practice exams for the midterm or final, and they are difficult to study for without any practice to go off of.

I found Kimani to be a very effective professor. He explained complex concepts in a relatively digestible and efficient manner, and always seemed to know exactly what he was talking about. The labs and HW in this class take a ton of time, but I found that I learned a lot from doing them, and they did a good job of building upon concepts from class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very helpful in office hours.

This guy is a legend. He explains the concepts very clearly -- if quickly -- but is always happy to answer your questions. He's also hilarious if you get to know him better. If you understand the lectures, you will do well in the class. I'd take any class with him again in a heartbeat.

Expected to know how to do homework with little to no instruction. Very tough homework grading on top of that. Labs aren't bad. Easy lab reports. But again, little to no instruction in how to do things. Nice guy, tough professor.

The class was easy but a lot of work - very standard teaching and help - nothing special but I didn't have any problems. Not the most interesting teacher by far but gets the job done and will field questions in and out of class.
He gives pop quizzes with trick questions.

His lectures aren't always very clear, but he has ample office hours and is very willing to help outside of class. Labs were a lot of fun and lab reports were minimal. pop quizzes were awful, but halfway through the term he switched to announcing them. Homeworks were long and difficult, but again: ask for help.

Absolutely great teacher. Was not too sure of how I might do in the class due to such low ratings, but if you really put the effort forth, the course is one of most interesting and enjoyable classes you will ever take. Very helpful during labs and after classes.
For real though? To they guy rated him first

Possibly one of the worst professors I've ever had. He will introduce a basic topic in class, and then assign a homework requiring advanced knowledge of said topic. The lab was mostly a copypaste type of format, ensuring that I got absolutely nothing out of this class! Avoid him if you can

Stuffs classes with too much content. Never gives leeway for anything. When you ask questions on projects or assignments the response is to check the rubric. really bad handwriting considering thats all she does on the smart board. doesnt allow you to review your exams in class.

Easy class if you attend and take notes and pay attention. Her tests are exactly like her homework and in class examples. Not much review for tests, but just do the inclass examples. Grades very fairly!
Pretty chill but hard class so if you want an A take another professor

she's a nice person and classes are good. she goes through examples in class.
she has 0 tolerance for late work and homework is not labeled well on canvas. her notes in class are ok but very bare minimum and gives 0 study materials for tests so you need to use the textbook but not all the textbook material relates to the test.

Professor Moreno is not flexible or accommodating whatsoever towards student schedules, which is very disappointing for an online summer course. She is cold and rude when asked for help or assistance. I would recommend avoiding her class if you have any other options available.

Lectures are very unhelpful- she doesn't break questions down, nor is she able to teach topics thoroughly, but rather assumes you remember everything from prior courses. Policy on late work is cruel- handing out zeros rather than partial credit. Assigns a long case activity paper, with harsh expectations and rubric. Worst for online classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Moreno is a great professor and is extremely knowledgable about the subject. She always has office hours and highly encourages them to go over any tests to prepare for the final. She is happy to explain any questions and explains the material well. However, the course is 65% exam based, so be prepared to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do you like public humiliation? Take accounting with Kimberly! She is rude, and only favors the students who are naturally smart. BEWARE

I wouldn't recommend this professor, as I found her approach to be less supportive and not particularly conducive to fostering a deeper understanding of the subject. Despite reaching out for help multiple times, I didn't feel the environment was welcoming or encouraging for students seeking assistance. Take the course with another professor.

Lectures are important, so you have to attend class. However, there was a lack of resources for students who couldn't make it to class. The only things available to you are the in-class slides (that don't have the complete notes) and the in-class examples (which don't have answers, so you have no idea if you're right or wrong). Hard class.

I loved Professor Moreno's class, she was always willing to answer questions and explains material clearly and in multiple ways. Attendance is very important but if you pay attention and do the problems it is not a difficult class.

Reads notes, does practice problems. Repeats. Is upset when people aren't starting in class problems when it is evident people don't know how to do it. Doesn't care at all how people do, but not outwardly unkind. Doesn't explain changes that can occur in different scenarios, only the problem at hand. Not awful but definitely would not recommend her

She has good lectures and you must attend for grade. I thought the slides and practice problems were well balance. The practice problems were clearly gone over, which are similar to test problems. I wish there were extra practice problems for the exam. The exams were ok and no curve. I hated the group project; there was not much guidance on it.
Asked the professor numerous times for help and she did nothing and knew I was struggling. Had to drop the class. So much attitude always.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Moreno is a great prof and teaches in a very clear way, however, the exams are EXTREMELY difficult and unlike any of the practice problems you do in class. She's also a very difficult grader and will take off tons of points for minor errors. However, she's very caring and always available outside of class for help

Moreno is a very sweet professor that makes the class really fun and engaging. This, however, doesn't take away the fact that exams are extremely difficult, with very little to study on. She makes up questions so you will have to know the basics and apply them. Recommendation: If you are a good exam taker, go ahead, and if not, stay away
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had a great experience in 2301 with Moreno. While exams were pretty challenging and the semester long group project was really tedious, she cares about her students. Has students take notes in the class pack, didn't really need to read the text book.

I was having a hard time in the class and went to office hours, specifically to review after not doing well on one of the exams. Instead of taking time to re-review the problems/concepts she asked me who was in my group project and told me I'll be fine because the other two in my group are smart. Made me feel even worse and clearly not helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Moreno is a good prof and a great person. Patient and thorough in her explanations. I appreciated that she would do every problem with us. The tests were very difficult and anxiety-inducing, especially because they're a majority of your grade bc there were no HW assignments. Have to put in serious work for this class, but if you do, you'll be fine.

Professor Moreno is very helpful in explaining course contents. Sometimes I got confused by the textbooks, but her explanation during office hours are very clear and easy to understand. The exams are very closely related to homework. Anyway, if you have any questions just go ask her. She is really nice and very willing to help.

My rating is based on her class when I took it, Fall 2015. I was not a good student, but this was the first acct class I enjoyed after my co-ops because it seemed more work-oriented and I learned a lot. She also called me out for being arrogant for the first time in my life and that's why I'm writing this years later. She was right. Thank you, Kim

the class is a walk through of oversimplified problems via powerpoint and then doing in class problems. these problems are fine but it's the only thing we have to study for the test, and the test is obscure questions that are not whats done in class. her grading is also biased - points back to some people but not others for similar mistakes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very difficult tests. If you have a passion for cost accounting and you are willing to put in 5-7 hours per chapter when studying for an exam. Otherwise, avoid because it's simply stressful and too much work for little credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are way too complicated. No study guide for exams. They are worth a lot of points so it affects your overall grade a lot. The questions are really different than the ones she gives in class and does not give additional practice questions. Do NOT take this professor. You get the feeling that she wants you to fail. Also, useless office hours.

Tough grader, makes exam really complicated. Even though they were so difficult, but I spent a lot of time on this class and I got 92 for exam 1, 85 for exam 2 unfortunatly, and 98 for the final. Sounds great right? But I got a 75/100 of my group p, that's ridiculous, we spent almost 1 month for it. If I had a chance, I WILL NOT CHOOSE HER CLASS!!!

I'm blown away by these positive reviews. Moreno was one of the most ineffective teachers I've had at NU. Each class consisted of brief 20-25 min review of chapter and then practice problems. Prof did poor job explaining answers to problems. Test questions like nothing covered in class. Refused to post materials to BB. Was rude during office hours

She is a tough but very fair teacher. The book does not seem necessary, but if you want to do well it is a must to have. The practice problems at the end of the chapters are the best way to review for her tests, and some of the questions are very similar to some of them. If you show interest in the class she is willing to do a lot to help you.

She's tough but fair. Ignore the textbook, read her class pack like the bible and you will be able to do well on her tests. Great sense of humor! Made class very interesting but DO NOT fall behind or you will not survive. Overall, one of my favorite teachers from northeastern (people who didn't like her didnt put in the effort necessary to succeed)

I understand why people give her a poor rating. The tests were hard, the project was extremely difficult, and it was not easy to get a good grade. However, she was very clear in class and always challenged you to learn. Put your effort and study hard, you should be fine. Don't just complain.

If I have two words to describe this "teacher" not the class: SHE BLOWS! The wording of problems are beyond help, since you won't understand what it is trying to say.  Also, she goes out of her way to make her questions overflowing with excess information.  So, if you want your dreams as an accountant crushed, then feel free to take this teacher.

1. Moreno is a good, but not an effective teacher. She over complicates the concepts and makes the test really hard, compared to class work. Every class, she would read through the power points and do in class problems. The problems in class are pretty fair. BUT, on the test, she makes everything super complicated. Bad teaching style, period.

Entirely unhelpful, she just went through powerpoint in class.  If you were even a couple minutes late, she would humiliate you publicly. This used to be a school for commuters, she had no sympathy  for someone who is working full time in addition to attending school.  Tests were much harder than any homework or in class examples.

By far my favorite teacher so far at Northeastern. No powerpoints to sleep through. Clear examples that are gone over in class. To study for her tests I just went over the in-class packets again and aced them easily. Three tests and one project plus participation.

She is an awesome teacher. She gives out plenty of examples for each chapter so there is no way you can't understand it and if you still don't get it she is more than willing to explain it to you. She definitely keeps the class interesting. I recommend everyone take her

Like many courses, you get what you put in to it.  If you're looking for an easy A, this isn't the place.  If you want to learn a ton through application of accounting rather than staring at a book, Moreno is the professor for you
