Poor teacher overall. Lacks patience, lacks expertise.

He is not up to date on the technology needed to effectively teach. His handwriting is also very difficult to read and his lectures are rarely helpful. He is never prepared for class. Limited prep materials are provided for exams. I would avoid taking this class with him, one of the worst professors I've seen at northeastern.

Worst prof ive had at northeastern so far. If you HAVE to take his class, my best rec would be to completely ignore everything he's saying and not take in any information from the lectures. Go home learn everything on YouTube. But dont forget to go to class as he tells you what topics are going to be on the quizzes.

I do not say this lightly, Yong-Bin Kim is the worst professor I have ever had.

I had severe medical issues during his semester, his behavior towards me was so bad (he told me *in writing* my surgery wasn't necessary, and kicked me out of multiple classes) that the school gave me a full refund for the semester.

Beyond that, super awful lectures.

Terrible teacher. Can't hear him from the front row, can't read his handwriting, incredibly stubborn.  Will not post anything online, no practice tests or problems, and will not record classes. He has no idea how to teach an introductory electrical engineering class and assumes students will and should know complex topics. Don't take his class!!
Only take this professor if you are willing to learn everything by yourself.
Rushes through lectures and concepts at the speed of light. Doesn't bother explaining things from first principles. He's pretty much teaching himself.
Good Prof. But the exams are overlapped so many, which seems to be a little bit meaningless for exams and lots of us got very high grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He promptly replies with clear explanations when I send him emails asking questions. He is very knowledgeable in electronics. I hope all electronics class are taught by him. Students generally enjoy his class because he explains the concepts and usage of electronic circuits clearly. I became confident about electronics after the class.

His explanation is very clear. Before I took his class, I worried a lot because Electronics is a difficult in general. However,  he explains the concepts clearly and I could follow the class very well. I became to like the subject.

Master of electronic circuits!  Very nice professor when I asked his help outside the classroom. He is very fair and enthusiastic about teaching. His exam is actually not hard because everything is from homework and class notes. I am planning to take electronics II with the professor.

He is an excellent professor. I didn't know much about electronics before I took his special topic class because my electronics professor was horrible. However, Prof. Yong-Bin Kim was a totally different person. His explanation was so clear. I like to take all the previous courses with the professor  if I could. Strongly recommend him!

He knows what he teaches. Before I took the class, I heard that his exams arehard. But is is reasonably easy because most of the exam are from the homework and the stuffs he emphasize in the class. So if you listen to him during the class and don't skip homework, you should get A without any problem. I bet!
Nice guy.  Really enthusiastic about teaching and the well-being of his students.
nice guy.

He seems to think everything he says is crystal clear. Wrong. He only shows one example and tends to look down on those who don't get it. "Everything is common sense." Then why does no one understand your materal after the lecture?
He is fine in 1 on 1 conversation but in class is a whole different story. Tests are pretty hard but tend to get progressively easier (grades are too low.) Suggest taking ECEU524 before ECEU526
Very crazy guy. He is very hostile and causing lots of issues every semester. He doesn't hesitate to fail students at all.

While Kledia is a nice person, it did not feel at all as if she taught the class. Very minimal effort was put on her end to actually teach or communicate, making me think she almost didn't even think about the course beyond class time. Grades were never put in or discussed, so beyond feedback during classes themselves we had no idea where we stand.

ARTF1240:nice person, does not teach you how to do anything, just gives assignments and expects you to know how to work with Adobe/learn it (huge learning curve). You never work in class, the only thing you do is watch example videos and sit awkwardly, leave early. Hasn't put any grades in the entire semester. slightly judgemental, prefers abstract

I don't think Kledia is best suited for the introductory experience design course she teaches. With a young teacher complex, she focuses on aspects of teaching that don't necessarily foster curiosity and enthusiasm in students. Sweet person, but not an effective teacher. Lectures are tedious and assigned work is geared for time intensive effort.
Really unhelpful and confusing. Don't take interactive experiences with her. Most disorganized Canvas I've ever seen.

Kledia's classes are not necessarily easy, but you get what you put into them. Almost each class is a critique-but art is best learned through critique. Showing work each class motivates students to do their best, as well as see what their classmates come up with. I do think that the screening/reading assignments each week are a bit tedious

If I could put 0 I would.
Every 3-hour class is 2 hours of "critiquing" which is never useful, anxiety-inducing, & frankly a waste of time. She has screenings that are barely related to our projects, & discussions are like pulling out teeth. Heavy workload + vague HW instructions, & I've taught everything to myself so far (more than I normally do).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Won't go easy on you but her high standards are because she knows you're capable of meeting them. Will critique your work in class but still check in with you if you're having a bad day. I will admit the standards sometimes feel unfair, especially if the entire class drops the ball. Regardless though, if you work with her she'll work with you.

Do not take her class, the first day of class she literally gave a lecture about how she's "not that tough" because her grad professor would make students cry during critique...She makes us present our homework every single class/critique and it gives me so much anxiety. On top of that, she gives little to no explanation for our homework prompts.
One of the best criminal justice professors at the school
The classes was barely even related to CJ the way that she presented the course.

Didn't learn anything!  It was by far the worst class I have ever taken at Northeastern.  Gave terrible examples in class and just read off the powerpoint.  The most interesting part was when we got to watch movies, I actually learned something from them.
Lectures are really boring. He is a really nice person but I wish he tried to make the class even a little interesting. Most of the class seemed bored.
Fantastic professor! Makes things interesting and gives excellent feedback on speeches. If you show interest in the class, he'll show an interest in you. Also, he's funny.

He is a pretty average teacher. He is nice and helpful, lectures are pretty boring but that's just because of the topic. Gives good feedback on speeches. If you deliver speeches well and read the book to prepare for the final quiz you will do fine.
I learned a lot in this class about Fintech industry and innovation. The class includes test version of cryptocurrency transactions and I never tried those before.
Super boring lectures (he just reads the slides). Very very difficult to learn anything without just reading the textbook on your own.
I learned a lot in this class. Great selection of business cases related to Fintech. Team work was fun too and I transacted using cryptocurrencies for the first time!

Enjoyed this class. Mainly lecture based and had a mix of online assessments and group projects on interesting topics. Professor Koparan was very accessible and was always down to help if you had questions. Would highly recommend if looking for a chiller FINA class.

I took fintech in summer 1 and although the pace of the course felt a bit expedited due to summer scheduling, it was super fun to explore fintech landscape and Alper creates a friendly classroom environment. Assignments are helpful and I also learned a lot about cryptocurrencies.

Very enjoyable lectures and friendly classroom atmosphere. I really liked group project which is about creating a startup idea and investor pitch at the end. Alper is extremely knowledgable about Fintech and makes concepts easy to understand.

I really enjoyed this class and even at 8 am Professor Koparan made lectures engaging and interesting. Some assignments are in class and there are hands-on exercises to experience cryptocurrencies and decentralized finance. A must have class if you are interested in Fintech!

FINA4604 is a super dense finance class in nature covering Levels 1-3 of the CFA curriculum and dives into highly quantitative topics. Unless you're super passionate about fixed income I wouldn't advise taking this class unless you're ready to read through a 900 page textbook and spend 6-10 hours a week on homework

This is a very technical and difficult course. I would not take it unless you are interested in Fixed Income. It covers topics from Level 1-3 of the CFA and it takes a lot of work outside of class to do well. I spent 6-8 per week outside of class studying. Alper cares about the material and his students. I learned a ton in this class.

Hard grader, exams extremely hard, midterm 1 20%, midterm 2 20%, final 30%. assignments consist of mcq and excels very hard and complicated. if u miss class get ready to figure out how to do assignment/hw. didn't know this class was tailored for CFA. work hard or else ur grade is gonna have a big drop.

I'm in Fixed Income Securities class and it is going great so far! It is not an easy course but Professor Koparan makes it engaging and practical. Hi is always available for questions and care about student success. He is one of the best at Northeastern and highly recommended!

Do not take fixed income securities with Alper Koparan. He is extremely disorganized and doesn't have the answers for homework figured out before the test, so you can't study effectively. Tests make up a large portion of the grade, but his test questions are not specific whatsoever and he solves them differently from how he teaches them in class.

Prof. Koperan is one of my favorite profs at NEU. He is extremely kind and caring and genuinely a good person. His Fintech class is relatively easy as long as you do the readings & study. He's always available outside of class too. He breaks down complex concepts into really easy ones. Take his class!!!!

Truly one of the worst professors I've had at the school. Not even as a professor, but I honestly don't know that he has a good personality. I often feel like I have to double check what he is saying, he overcomplicates simple things. Teaches things off the textbook simply because he feels like it.

Honestly, Professor Konan is a really fun and genuine guy. Lectures are mandatory and can get boring sometimes, but the tests are online and he gives tons of opportunities to make up your grade with make-up tests and extra credit. He's super understanding, actually cares about the class, and is overall an absolute chiller.

Not the worst prof/class. Exams are online which is fire, homeworks are annoying but not too much. Martin is a weird fellow but kinda funny at the same time. If you get him off topic it's a great time
Just a chill guy

if you love and are passionate for economics take Mr Konan. He knows his stuff, explains concepts intuitively and doesn't overcomplicate simple concepts. theres a bit of work and homework but it gives you an extremely solid understanding of the coursework. very funny guy too. if you like econ or basketball youll like him

Not to glaze Prof. Konan but don't listen to the horrible reviews! It's extremely easy to do well in his class– it's basically impossible to get lower than a B+ (if you're not dumb). The tests are easy and he offers make-ups. He's a strange and funny guy who seems to enjoy teaching. The only con was that his classes are often lecture heavy.
Probably biggest waste of time ever. His lectures are mandatory and useless. You can only take certain homework if you arrived to class. Attendance is a part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Konan is my favorite professor at Northeastern. It's not that hard to be a good student in his class. As long as you show up to class, he is not only entertaining, but makes learning fun. I really loved his class.

Whoever says they don't like Professor Konan probably can't take good notes or a joke. If you are not sensitive you will laugh in most of his lectures. He has all his exams online so he can lecture during class time. He gives you multiple opportunities to improve your grade by offering a makeup exam. Do the work and you will get a good grade.

Genuinely one of the worst classes/professors I've had. Attendance is mandatory; he will fail to mention many busywork/random "In class assignments" before class ends. These assignments don't take up much time WHEN YOU KNOW ABOUT THEM. The tests aren't terrible, but if you can, AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS. Worst class I've taken.

Terrible. His lectures are the least valuable material in the course. To compensate for the fact that no one gains any value from them, he forces attendance, mandatory in-class assignments, and an ungodly amount of assignments overall. He makes you buy a 150$ textbook that no one ends up using, and one he himself tells us not to study from.

honestly didn't pay much attention in class but im sure of you put in the effort you can do well. midterm and one other exam was take home with 4 cheat sheets, but are proctored by camera and microphone recording. attendance is mandatory and you cant do some of the homeworks if you didnt go to class he checks. just take notes and youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't learn anything from his lectures and found myself teaching myself everything. The tests were extremely difficult, he gave little to no feedback on tests and homework which made it close to impossible to understand what you did wrong. He doesn't check or answer emails at all. I would absolutely not recommend taking his class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy and I think he means well but when he has to offer retakes for his exams because the class average is so low? Attendance was mandatory and he issued in class assignments to penalize people who skipped but really it ended up hurting everyone

He decided halfway through the semester that because people weren't showing up to class we should have assignments due every class on top of the already assigned textbook work, he claimed they were just like the ones we did in class but they never were and he would grade them very harshly. The tests were very very hard.

Konan's lecture style is fine. The main problems were, 1 attendance is the mandatory, counts towards final grade, no online option even if you are sick. 2 he does almost never responds to email. 3 you pretty much teach yourself everything from the textbook. 4 he started assigning in class HW, 2hr worth, completed after class due by 11:59 that day.

Martin's lectures are fun and his exams are online asynchronous which is nice, but he never releases grades until like a month later, and goes so fast. Also goes off the textbook and no lecture notes are posted so if you skip class you will fall so far behind.

Lectures are not the most engaging, course uses Cengage MindTap for HW which doesn't work half the time and he doesn't do anything about it. The exams are pretty difficult, although they're take-home over multiple days which was probably the only positive thing about this course. Would avoid if at all possible. Also, he doesn't respond to emails.
God awful. Prepare to teach everything yourself

Martin Konan is the worst teacher I ever had during my MBA. He does not care, he is in class simply for the paycheck. Runs thru materials without a single example, can't understand a word he says so get ready to help yourself by yourself. This teacher missed a few classes, he bragged about being traveling overseas during those classes.

Class is super lecture-heavy, and material can be confusing because the topics are so similar but with minute differences. If you don't take notes, it'll be easy to get distracted, but the tests are pretty difficult. All the HW is due at the end of the semester, so don't leave it to the end.
best professor evvvvvver

He grades students based on how much he likes them, lectures for hours by reading directly from the book. You would be better buying the book and doing the work on your own, Do not waste your money taking this course, or any other, with Martin Konan. He is stubborn, and autocratic.

~30% of lectures were fully online last sem and he canceled ~10%. Lots of HW and Tophat questions (required to buy). Generally curves tests, gives make up tests. Doesn't respond to email, encourages students to text/call. Style helpful for theory courses; hard to get confused if you are listening and engaged. Would NOT suggest for electives.

Graded everything on the day before grades were to close. He'd spend time topic going through content covered in the principal classes and then go deep into it which is helpful. Classes are basically copying things from the board but not really engaging. However, there is a lot of homework some of which is good practice for the final.

At one point the class starts going at an extremely fast pace and you are expected to remember the 20 pages worth of notes for every exam. Doesn't spend enough time reinforcing ideas so you will have to study and review the material almost every day. Positive thing is that lectures aren't boring and he asks engaging questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: much homework hard tests

He gives ALOT of homework, tests, and TopHat. I don't know if it would have been better to take his class in the fall or spring, but DO NOT take it as a summer class. You really have to work for it. He's really nice tho and you have to text him instead of emailing him which is weird but he's a good teacher. It's just too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class (Econ of Sports) was enjoyable. I find that Prof. Konan is a nice guy, offering helpful review sessions and makeup exams. However, he does make you buy Top Hat, he goes over time in most classes, and he is poor at responding to emails. Overall he is a decent choice if you like the class being taught. Be sure to do notes on the textbook.

Professor Konan is the worst professor I have ever had. His lecture notes are confusing and if you ask him questions he gets frustrated. He ignored both "care days" we had this semester and held class even though he was reminded of them by students. He is a harsh grader and very boring lecturer. Avoid him as a professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He started the semester with a bit of a harsh tone, but he warms up to students and enjoys participation. He is not a very fast responder to emails or when grading assignments, but he definitely is passionate about the subject, and the class can be interesting. I recommend reading the textbook before or after class so you can soak the info in well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Please please please do yourself a favor and do not take this professor. Yes he cares, and is not a bad guy. But his class interaction, his teaching style, and overall effectiveness is awful. At the start of the semester, questions were discouraged and if you do he's stubborn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He was okay, he seems like he cares but can be difficult to speak to. Which seems like it wouldn't be a huge deal, but he wouldn't speak about them in class. They were random and unrelated to the bigger picture of what we were learning. Even if you do really well on the math portion, you won't do well on exams or class b/c of weird multiple choice
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Konan's lectures are a mess. He is disorganized and gets lost and goes on tangents easily and often. He tries to teach and cover upper level econ theory in a couple weeks when the class has no prereqs. Unless you have a solid micro and macro theory background you will be lost. He grades based on how much he likes students and is way too harsh
Too hectic in short term

Great Professor, explains well about the core concepts and necessities in the subject. Highly knowledgable. Just do hardwork, show your own genuine work and that's good. Strict on academic integrity, but for our own good. Eventually, he prepares you to be a true professional engineer, not just get grades.
The grading policies in this class do not make sense. There is little incentive to try. The majority of the class will end up with a B or a B+ regardless of the effort put in.
he teaches very good and if you are joining neu for ece this is a must take course, highly recommended. if you are coming to neu and do not take this subject it is a waste.

He is the best professor I've ever meet. 
The lecture is fascinating because he will make sure everyone understands what he's saying. 
Heavy workload including homework, lab, and projects. 
The tests are not that hard but need time to prepare. 
Zero tolerance to academic integrity.
Useful lectures but a little hard. Heavy homework.

Somewhat interesting lectures, does not put in enough effort. Comes late to class, uses class time inefficiently, ended class early every lecture yet did not finish all of the material in the syllabus. Quizzes always had errors and ambiguous questions. Clearly did not care about the class or anyone's learning.
Dr. Klein is a great professor although tue material gets a bit boring when studying about the Lakota.
I love prof Klein. He lectures a lot but knows a ton, he literally wrote the book, and he has plenty of great stories to tell. Would 100% recommend taking one of his classes.

Great professor, interesting lectures but you need to pay attention to all the details of the lecture. Grade consists of 4 exams and the exam material is all information from the lectures, so if he did not discuss it during lecture, it wont be tested. Tests are difficult and sometimes he goes on tangents, but overall extremely interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: one of the sweetes, caring professors. absolutely loved him as a person. Class is super easy just show up.

He goes off on way too many tangents so you have no idea whats important for the exams and what isn't. This class is incredibly boring if you do not have to take it for your major do not take it with him

Just go to class and you can get an A. Tests are easy and you do not need to do the readings to pass. Lectures sometimes drag on, but his tangents and stories are always entertaining. Professor Klein is a nice guy and is very understanding.

Such a cool/funny person!! Really interesting to listen to all of his crazy stories. The four quizzes are based on his lectures, so it's important to limit skipping class. We have a review day in class per unit, but its solely based on people asking questions so you get what you put into it. And the quizzes are easy (coming from a bad tester).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Super super great guy, cares about his students and truly wants us all to succeed. However, the exams kind of come from nowhere and it's hard to prepare for them. It's hard to know what'll be on them. I remember for one, I did all the readings and attended every lecture but was still very uneasy about the info when I took the exam and afterwards

I truly enjoyed having class with Alan Klein. His lectures are terrific, and he is engaging and hilarious. It was like being taught by George Carlin. That being said, the final grade is mostly based on quizzes, which is unfair to those who aren't good test takers. Even so, I recommend Alan Klein for his engaging, interesting, and humorous lectures.

He shows up to class unprepared and lectures about completely random stories. There is no outline or slides, or anything to go off of when studying for his exams. Taking each test is a crapshoot. Not a super hard class but not sleep-through A either. Horrible professor that is biased toward anthropology majors or sport team members.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really easy class... The TA does a review before all 4 of the quizzes. Prof Klein gives an optional extra credit paper which boosts your final grade up one (ex B to B+) if the paper is better than a B.

Alan Klein is the professor you spend 15 minutes drafting an email with detailed questions about the upcoming term paper for, only to get a five word reply that doesn't answer a single question asked. He also has a weird obsession with Native American tribes in  South Dakota. 0/10.

Prof. Klein gives really interesting lectures, but struggles to clearly connect his lectures to the concepts that he wants you to learn. He'll tell you stories and go on tangent-esque lectures, so if you take good notes and come to class you should have all the abstract concepts you need to get a good grade. Grade is the average of four quizzes.
Professor Klein is a great guy and a great teacher. If you care about the class you will do well!
Alan is a good professor even if he tends to ramble on telling stories. Super helpful and kind. Go to review sessions and do the reading if you really want to do well, otherwise easy to get an A.

I took his introduction class this semester and his tests are quite easy. He likes to tell stories as everyone else said and I think his lectures were useful but you don't have to pay too much attention to them. Easy for me to get an A

Professor Klein is very clear, inspiring and nice. He likes to tell stories. His lectures cover almost everything you need, but make sure to read extra documents for an A. Go to review session! Those will save you
Interesting guy with some cool stories, but tends to ramble. Going to the TA run review sessions covers everything you actually need to know to pass.

professor klein is great. the class is easy but you learn a lot and his lectures are interesting. attendance isn't that important and neither is doing the reading but both are interesting. going to review sessions with the TA before exams saves you. your grade is made up of just 4 quizzes (no hw, attendance, participation, finals, etc)
Really really easy to do well, just go to class and pay attention. Readings aren't too necessary, he basically goes over them in class

One of the best professors you'll ever come across. Don't skip class and make sure you can tie readings to other examples from in and out of class. Klein gives great feedback and will work closely with anyone willing to put the effort in. You'll see your writing, critical thinking and discussion skills improve dramatically!
The class is required for IA Majors. Was easy if you went to the reviews before the exams. Professor Klein is very nice and makes class fun. I definitely suggest him!

He may have some interesting stories but they really are useless. Always attend his class because that's where he mentions the smallest things and then puts it on the quizzes. Although I got a good grade in the class, I thought the grades being based solely on the quizzes was stupid. No one pays attention in class either. Useless course.

Professor Klein is funny and class is interesting. But, you have to go to class or else you will fail the test. He includes questions on exams about minor details he mentioned one time, so pay close attention at all times and take good notes. Class is based entirely on 3 or 4 tests.
Loved him! He makes a lot of jokes and since it's an intro course he is easy. The load is not that much, but still you have to read.
horrible teacher. ABSOLUTE WORST. can't teach. tests are hard. lectures are incredibly boring

Terrible. Thinks he's a gift to the anthropology department yet inept at teaching. If you take his class, take a 101 course with a guided structure -- he has no idea how to guide a class without a day-by-day guide for both he and students to follow. You will literally learn nothing if he has control over a loosely structured classroom.

He seems to have made his tests years ago and never looked at them since. He doesn't know what's on them and can't answer many of the questions himself. I can't say that I learned much from this class, wasn't a result of anything he did as a professor.

Professor Klein is a great teacher. His lectures are really engaging, the readings are not bad at all, and the three quizzes are easy so long as you pay attention and do the readings. One of the funniest teachers I've had. Always has a great anecdote to tie into the material or even just to entertain the class.

Lectures can be interesting but can go off in tangents with pointless anecdotes. Attendance is a must as he uses notes from class in the quizzes. Silly three quiz system - if you do badly in one, will have to do very well in the other two to get a good final grade.
Absolutely my favorite professor. He doesnt do bs but his class is AMAZING!
Completely lecture based, thinks he is god. Class was useless.

In order to do well in Klein's classes, you need to put in the work. Going to class is mandatory since its where you get all your notes. Keeping on time with the reading schedule is really important too. Klein is a brilliant and interesting prof. If you're willing to put in the effort, go for it but be warned: he doesn't but up with any BS

Anth101 was a complete waste of time with him.  His 'easy' three quiz system is the biggest teaching joke ever.  He's disrespectful to just about anyone on any level and his lectures consist of him rambling without end..interesting stories sometimes, but ultimately I learned nothing.  If you're looking to actually learn, get a different 'professor'

Best professor I've had at northeastern!!! I took sports culture and society and it was the most interesting class I have ever taken. I'm an Econ major and this class made me want to change to Anthro... He has a passion for teaching this course and has a lot of history with Baseball in the D.R. Take this for your comparative cultures!!!

if you're the type of person who doesnt go to class. switch out asap. I didn't go to class all the time and it really took a toll on my grade. theres 3 quizes so if you fail one you do bad in the class. if you dont show up to class you will fail.

Nice guy, really knows a lot about anthropology and has some great stories to share. Your grade is only based on 3 tests so definitely do the reading and attend class. He makes it pretty easy to get a good grade, just put in the effort.

if you're looking for an easy grade don't take his class. he's an awesome proffesor, always has great stories to tell but there is NO structure to his class. there's only 3 quizes so if you do bad on one of them you pretty much do bad in the class. you have to go to class because everything he says is important and can be on the quiz

alan is by far the worst professor i have ever had.  he will not return your e-mails, he is very arrogant, and makes virtually no effort to help his students outside of class.  this is not an isolated event i know many people who feel the same way.  aviod alan klein by all means
Great prof, vast knowledge within the subject, which leads to tangents, but often times even the tangents help you to further understant the culture being studied

The class wasn't too bad, but I thought it was pretty stupid how your ENTIRE grade was based soley off of three tests... and the tests weren't exactly easy. I wouldn't recommend this class if you're looking for an easy A elective.
good prof., funny and very and smart. lectures are interesting but not absolutely mandatory - def. get the notes though. only 3 quizzes for the whole class and read the books
Has lots of knowledge in the field. Goes off on tangents quite often. There are only 3 quizzes, that is all that the grade is made up of, so don't screw those up.

Klein is a very smart man who will make you view the cultures and people you study in through a totally different perspective.  You must do the readings and he will take a shine to you if you come prepared to discuss the material.  So, read, comment and listen and you'll really glean a lot of Dr. Klein.
great teacher, very smart and open, strays from topic at hand a lot though - but always funny and interesting

Klein is the man.  Classes can be kind of difficult, you should def go to class even though its not mandatory.  Lectures are interesting and he has lots of anecdotes from his personal experiences that are both relevent and funny.  Take his classes, you wont regret it

imo, klein is an example of what professors SHOULD be like. doesnt hand out A's to students- you def have to earn your grade by attending lecture, taking thorough notes and keeping up with readings/material to do well on the tests. entertaining, knows his stuff.

Tells very interesting stories, very inteligent, teaches the material well.  Sometimes its hard to tell whether its just a story or test material but you learn to tell them apart with time. lectures are 100% mandatory, test is 95% lecture. Funny and very open to any opinion. Makes that class a bit interesting. Not an easy A, though, takes effort.
Really good professor.  The lectures are very important to attend.  If you show up for class and do at least some of the textbook reading, you'll be in good shape.

He's very intelligent and has great stories, but not really the nicest guy and not really all that helpful.  Kind of came off as a jerk, but definitely knows what he's talking about, but has a chip on his shoulder
Very interesting. Hard to stay focused in class sometimes but you can tell he is such a smart guy and really knows what he's talking about. Study for the tests and you will really learn something.
Interesting professor who really knows what he's talking about.  If you go to class and actually pay attention, you CAN pass, and pass well.  Even his tangents are entertaining.
Funny guy, great class. Tells amusing stories. And he's a real hippy. No one else knows what they're talking about- the tests were fine, as long as you study.

Hands-down my favorite professor. If you like anthropology, you like Alan Klein. He breaths Anthropology and knows incredible amounts of information. It takes a dedicated student to score an A, but just going to class will ensure a good grade. It's all about the notes.
Great Teacher. Great Guy. Interesting Class.

this class was harder than it should've been because he doesn't lecture well--just tells stories from his field work. which is ok until you need to take the test and realize you don't know much. i wouldn't take another class with him.

can make class interesting, has some pretty cool stories but only gives three tests and unless you were there for almost all classes and paid really close attention even a good student can have difficulty

Sport in Society: this guy is cool. tells great stories. take good notes and read books and you will suceed. hes down to earth and honest. his experience has given him lots of credibility in books, news media, and he worked out with arnold schwarzanegger.
Tons of stories but didn't really teach out of the text which all of his two test were out out and made up your grade. Would not take a class with him again.

Wasn't really a fan of this guy. The quizzes that make up your grade don't really have any formal organization to them(multiple choice, short essay, matching all randomly mixed up). Most of material can be gained from lectures, but does include some random things from extremely boring readings. Unless required, I would find another elective to take

Well, at first i though this class woud be interesting but it really wasn't.  I thought it was boring and unorganized.  He never tells u exactly whats on the tests and there are only 3 tests that makeup your whole grade.  He seems like a nice guy but the class is definately harder than he makes it sound.

Amazing Professor, classes are greatly interesting, mostly because of his storys. Tests had questions that he didnt emphasize in class but everything on tests were discussed.  He is a true hippy and has the storys to prove it. take his course if u have the opportunity or if u just like funny storys
3 essays make up your grade, grades fairly. Tells interesting stories and goes off on funny tangents. I enjoyed the class.
Likes to ramble but good stories.
i liked what he said a lot, he just tended to ramble and digress a little - but his tests weren't bad as long as you payed attention and he was interesting

He's fine. The class is very boring. Rastahs were neat before this, but now i know too much, yah know? Great stories, but stories don't get me up at 9:15, and the tests were mostly common sence. Grades on the doors suck too. Take it if you have to or can cram real well:)!

Three tests made up our grade, and they included material from lectures supplemented with a lot of reading.  He only posts grades outside his office door! Argh!  Tells a lot of really interesting stories, but doesn't seem to want to help anyone and some of the stuff on test is not really gone over.
I really didn't like this teacher as a person.  He kind of creeped me out a bit.  He did tell pretty good stories, but the tests were not based on anything he talked about.

interesting classes but sometims gets off topic with random stories (funny though)  If you take good notes you'll do ok but some things he doesnt talk about in class and puts specific questions on the tests

tests are impossible... i'm a 3.6(my GPA would be higher if i dropped his class) student and wrote detailed notes....... still did awful..... he doesn't give back tests, only posts the grades outside his office.... AVOID him
No Comments

If you could hear him, then maybe you could have a chance.  He doesn't give you study guides and his tests are specific. He is also never at his office hours and never lends any extra help. I wouldn't take him again
awesome teacher
stories are really funny, tests a little hard, but not anything you can't study for, took the class as an elective and thought it was great
****, too in love with himself for anyones good.  Gives tests based on Material he doesn't give to class
Funny stories!  Passionate about his job!  Great class.
He's a cool guy, very interesting stories and LOVES what he does.  His tests are somewhat hard...however i went to about 1/2 of his classes...and I still got a B
sit in front, always come to class.  Tests are hard, mix of names and ideas.  very nice man, interested in his students, but gets off track telling funny stories.

The people that say his tests are hard are MORONS.  His tests are not bad at all.  He is really laid back, but VERY dry and boring, and talks to friggin quietly you can't even hear him half the time.  Overall, a fairly ****ty teacher.
Sport and society class is very good...great prof.
interesting subject matter.  tests are multiple choice but still challenging.  average of 5-6 profanities/class
What a tool, i just can't stand him.
Great interesting teacher, final was impossible
No Comments
this was one of my favorite classes at NU.  best teacher.  cares about his students but doesn't take bull$.
No Comments
Very interesting guy and easy to pay attention to... Study hard for his exams, they're unbelievable hard.
Great teacher, interesting, actually talks to students
Funny teacher, interesting class, but tough exams

Every week, we were assigned an excel spreadsheet (10 hours) and powerpoint (1 hour). The instructions were unclear for many of the steps and you have to figure it out yourself. Grading was slow however this is likely due to the TAs.

Dr. Pauwels is a nice guy. Very smart. Friendly. But be warned: this was not a marketing class. This was a statistics and econometrics class. Unless you understand both econometrics and statistics, you'll be in trouble. A group project every week. 20+ hrs work/week. TAs in fall 2023 semester were bad.
Great professor! Easy grader, friendly guy, understands that you have other classes outside of his. Does his best to make his class interesting and engaging. Great professor!
Great Professor. He made the class fun, engaging, and as long as you do the work and put some effort in you'll pass.

By FAR one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. It's so clear how much he cares about his students - he really wants you to succeed. It also seems like he was pretty accomplished in his marketing career before teaching so he has tons of real world experience and knows what he's talking about. Take this professor!!!

I thoroughly enjoyed the class. Make sure you take notes during the lectures as this can make the difference. The professor is very knowledgable and his presentation skills made his lectures a real pleasure. Northeastern should have more faculty like Prof. Kontis.

I liked this class a lot and I learned quite much. Professor Kontis made sure that every one of us kept up with the material and we were all comfortable. Moreover, his examples, case studies and comments were extremely useful and provided us with a real life experience.

Professor Kontis is a citizen of the world sharing his global experience with his students quite often. I learned a lot in his class, but I feel what matters more is to see him lecturing and enjoying every moment of it! Northeastern University needs more faculty like him.

I enjoyed the class even though I am not a numbers person! Lectures were very interesting with an international
flair as per professor's global status. 
Professor Kontis was caring for his class in every way. Always available and flexible during class hours or outside. I would love taking a class such as International Business with him.
Knowledgeable, open to class discussions and a great speaker. Professor Kontis made the difference in my sophomore year!

I learned a lot and it was not just accounting or finance. He provided us quite a few business cases with respect to our particular topic. His lectures were a bit heavy at times, but he cares for his students and he can manage this very well.Good support outside class, i.e. office hours, appointment etc.
This professor thinks that we only take one class and it is his! In spite of this, I learned a lot and I gave a good evaluation as I am sure the excessive workload was to my benefit!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was quite a speaker! A great lecturer and I am sure you could make it big in politics. His public speaking ability is amazing. At the same time, he has a very high emotional intelligence and makes the students feel great. A good mentor, too.
A good course overall. It was lecture heavy and I thought he should have given us a few more assignments other than the usual homework..
I learned a lot. A knowledgable professor, tough to follow and great mentor.
Great lectures, tough grader, be ready to participate in class!
Knowledgable, demanding, fair! A great semester!

Prof. Kontis is a great communicator with in-depth knowledge of the subject matter. A cosmopolitan educator, a well versed business executive and a citizen of the world. He changed my attitude towards business and learning.
Very good teaching skills! Very demanding in class participation and homework. Overall, a good class.
The best professor I had during my Northeastern years. I will never forget his lectures as he changed my way of thinking and navigating business problems.
A good teacher with outstanding communication skills. It was a great pleasure spending time with him during his office hours. A great source of information and a mentor to respect!
Great presenter as I learnt a lot. A business leader with a cosmopolitan flair. I wish I could take more courses with him.
Very knowledgable, cosmopolitan and business savvy! Respects students and treats them in a fantastic way.
Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best professor I had in my first two years at Northeastern University. Knowledgeable, caring with an a cosmopolitan flair. An all around academic and an accomplished international executive. I wish I could take on of his courses in the future.

Kontis is the worst professor I have experienced so far at Northeastern. He doesn't dumb down accounting for an intro level class. He doesn't answer questions at all, just kind of redirects the conversation. Although he is available out of class, it is hard to really get the time with him to improve anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good luck if you have Kontis for the accounting intro course and don't have an accounting background. He explains things that are generally simple in the most convoluted way that he confuses the whole class. Contradicts himself frequently when trying to answer questions he blatantly misunderstands. Offers no review guides for quizzes/tests. BAD

He was my favorite professor this semester. Was always clear with material. Would spend hours with you outside of class at your convenience to make sure you understood material. Really cares about getting to know each of his students as individuals. Some tests are harder than others but work hard, take notes, and this professor is a pleasure.

If I were to say he had a strength it would be his propensity to screw the class over, by not explaining the information properly, then becoming frustrated with the class for not understanding his vague statements.
Please do not take this professor! He does not curve anything even though some other professors do test corrections and such. The tests are way too difficult and it is not worth going through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Knudsen's lectures are very informative and he enables us to think conceptually about abstract linear algebra concepts, which helps us understand related material beyond just this class. While tests were difficult, they're mostly fair if you do all the review worksheets, attend lecture, and watch related videos. Solid professor overall.

Ben's a good professor. He tried very hard to teach in class and asked if there's any question (yet people barely answers him). He's relatively funny compared to other math profs. This class is just generally hard and very conceptual, u need to spend some time outside of classes, especially before tests.

This is hilarious. Looking at the ratings, you can see that some of the only positive ratings are written on the same day, which is just Professor Knudsen going on to rate my professor and creating fake positive ratings. It's quite sad, honestly. 

His class was awful. All tests are theory-based, while homework and lectures are practice-based.

Great professor, the people posting 1 stars are just salty after a test they didn't prepare enough for. Lots of freshman in the course so they probably expect high school math classes. All of the 1 stars are from the exact date exam 2 was graded. One of the best math professors I have had in college. Great lectures.

He's a great professor. Linear algebra isn't a subject ur gonna get right away so u still have to watch videos or read the textbook. But he does a good job introducing it. The test are easy but if you get one wrong loss pointsHe asks us if we understand and for any questions so take advantage of that. The peolpe hating are mad they got bad grades
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a good professor I think he does good and he evens asks us if we have question and knowone answers him. If you take advantage of that then he'll be great. It's a tough class you'll still need to some YouTube lessons for deeper understanding but he's a good guy. The people who rate him lower are mad they got bad grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please do NOT take this professor. He is very moody, and does not seem enthusiastic to teach the class. His tests are very difficult and focus more on theory than practicals which is what the homeworks focus on. handwriting is difficult to understand, concepts are not explained well, and he seems mad if we ask questions. Tests are weighed too heavy

Ben is a great professor with clear lectures that are focused on understanding concepts, not just memorization. The homework is basic to help you learn the concepts, and the test isn't much harder and the review guide is very similar to the test. People complaij. cuz they don't go to class (his lectures are empty) show up and you'll do fine!

Never seen a professor actively watch his students fail and be ok with it. He gives hw that's mostly practical and then gives exams that based on theory. If you're a bad exam taker good luck with 85% of you grade being exams. Avoid at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Will be a great choice if you are one of the following:
Love cryptography and willing to decode his handwriting on notes
Get 4.0 on all other classes and want to make your transcript more diverse
Good at test taking so that can earn most credit from the 85% weight tests
A big fun on submitting homework that need to be handwriting
im gonna lie, hes a great professor
WORST TEACHER AT NORTHEASTERN! AVOID AT ALL COST!

Extremely Bi-polar. Gets pissed when he asks questions he never taught. Zero application on exam all conceptual, genuinely forced to teach this class - he does not want to. Hostile during office hours and lectures have nothing to do with the actual exam. I have never taken a worse professor in Northeastern. I went to every class and OH - BEWARE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture notes are a mess. Roasts students. Always says he doesn't understand students' questions when he should. Thinks we are crazy for asking questions he doesn't like. Makes us discuss in math class on things that weren't taught at all. Worse math teacher in Northeastern.

Ben was honestly an amazing professor. He brings humor to the class and makes the lectures interactive. I would always walk into his class very tired from my previous class, and he would never fail to keep me engaged in class. I genuinely learned a lot in his linear algebra class and would HIGHLY recommend him!!

Oh my god, she does not show up. 90% of classes are either cancelled or moved to Zoom, but deadlines stay the same. She's a lovely person and clearly knowledgeable, but also does not care for teaching. She didn't teach us any of the design suites, and most classes she did show up for were less than 20 minutes long.

ARTG 4550

Very nice professor. She obviously cares about her students and is always open to help them, provide guidance, or give extensions.

Prof McCambridge canceled class multiple times with only an hour warning. She's good person and designer but didn't know what was going on in the lecture that goes with the seminar. Her lectures were disorganized and she was unprepared for every class. She also hasn't graded anything for the entire semester and classes are now over.

i am NOT a stats person lets make that clear, he made me at least tolerate if not enjoy it. my only complaint is this class for me was 8am tuesday and friday, absolutely BRUTAL. go to lecture is my biggest advice, skip one and you will be very behind. i missed a few bc i got sick and that was rough to come back from. super sweet guy!!

Easy homework (unlimited attempts), easy quizzes (2 attempts), and lectures are very clear. He's accessible outside of class and helps anyone who needs help. You have 6 makeup attempts for assignments you did poorly on/forgot to do. Exams are also easy; he helps if you ask him. Don't cheat, doesn't make sense. Also, the final exam is take-home.

This is the most peak professor ever. He let us introduce ourselves during the first day of class and I mentioned that my favorite show was Hunter Hunter, and he actually looked it up in front of the whole class. TALK ABOUT PEAK. Deserves a raise after that one for sure.

Bradley was great for psych stats; grade is made up of TYK, homework, quizzes, tests, and a presentation. Quizzes were taken in groups, and the tests were open-note for a section every time. Tests also mirror some of the quizzes. Lectures are clear and concise (we got out early almost every day), and the course was overall not too difficult!
Good guy. Funny. Easy A if you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teaching methods! More then fair exams and great professor. 10/10 would recommend.

Love this professor so much. Gave so many opportunities to learn and internalize the information. Spent a lot of time on extra videos, spreadsheets, and practice tests that helped so much. Quizzes are open-note and mirror exams. Homework is simple with 2 attempts. Not much classwork. Easy to do well if you pay attention. God bless Kristopher!!!!!!!

I LOVE Kristopher Bradley. I cannot recommend him enough. He is so passionate and clearly cares about each and every one of his students being successful in his course. He puts in so much effort outside of class that he is so proud of, and we are proud of him too. Not too assignment heavy, pretty easy A especially if you do the quizzes. TAKE HIM!!!

No reason you should not be getting an A in this class. Group quizzes, 2 attempts on homework and TYK quizzes, and he drills the content into your brain. Also, super nice and funny guy, and very flexible about retaking quizzes and how you do the final presentation.
Good professor, class is an A if you put in the work.  Kristopher is also very caring of his students and smart.

Ok yes I got an A, but I don't think I learned a whole lot. Love Bradley as a guy but his class is basically guaranteed to pass so it kinda takes away the actual learning and more about just getting random stuff done for your grade.

If you want a zero-effort course, Bradley is your guy, which is not a recommendation in my opinion. It's frustrating that there is nothing that differentiates a hard-working student from a lazy student. He is just okay in my opinion.

Quizzes: In class taken as a group, open note open everything, he sometimes even lets you check your answers before submitting it (For formatting purposes). Tests: Take home open note untimed. Classwork: None Homework: some (very easy graded for completion). Final: Take home very easy to get an A on of you follow the lecture notes as you take it.

Very knowledgeable and caring. Was very supportive & lenient outside of class. Class was graded by weekly open-note group quizzes, HW assignments, and 4 open-note take-home tests (including the final). Easy class, easy A.

If you want an easy A or just want to happily learn about Social Psych, than take his class. He's funny and extremely nice on if you miss any assignment. He want's to see everyone do well. The final is also optional..

I feel fortunate to have taken Professor Bradley for both Statistics in Psychology and Social Psychology! He is an amazing teacher who teaches you a lot and also is very caring. His assignments and tests are very straightforward and he is understanding about possible absences. I highly recommend him if anyone is looking to take a class with him!

This class was a huge disappointment. I have never been less motivated to attend a lecture course in my entire college career, and my attendance reflected that. The slides needed much more detail, and many of our assignments were moved earlier, reflecting that this class was not well-organized.

Had Bradley for PSY31 at Tufts. GREAT MAN, EASY A (and he does it on purpose!) Tests and quizzes are open-note. Quizzes are done in groups. Easy final project. Easy final exam (open-note, online, no time limit). Easy homework only graded based on completion. Many extra credit opportunities. I am so grateful for this man. Has an adorable son.

This was one of the best professors I've ever had at Northeastern. I ended this class with a 103%. As long as you apply yourself, pay great attention in lectures, and take notes you'll be fine. He also offers extra credit so take advantage of that. I did and it helped me end with an amazing grade. Overall a nice caring guy, I recommend him a lot.

Professor Bradley is a very nice guy with a passion for psychology, and it shows in his lectures. The class was relatively easy and there were a lot of discussion posts to boost your grade. However, you have to read the textbook to know everything on the test, as some of it just isn't covered in lecture.

One of my favorite professors. Dr. Bradley is very easygoing but knows what he is talking about, so it made learning statistics enjoyable. Quizzes are in-class with groups, and tests are take-home, open-note. He allows you to re-do questions you got wrong on exams and gives you the points back. No complaints at all. Definitely take him if you can.

dr. bradley is an extremely nice and overall great guy. it's easy to get an A if you do well enough on the tests (which pull some questions directly from practice quizzes + textbook), since the rest of your grade depends on open-note group quizzes, group discussions, and one project. you should read the textbook in addition to the lectures though

One of the best professors I've had. Makes the lectures very easy to follow and understand and really wants students to succeed. Very understanding and helps all the time. Really easy to do well in this class as long as you show up to class, pay attention and follow the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, took him for summer 1. Graded by 3 tests, homework, in-class quizzes, and a final. All homework and tests were done at home and online with no time restrictions. Lectures were easy to understand and he explained how to use SPSS easily. He offers extra credit throughout and it's actually quite fun to do. He's very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy professor, does assign homework but is very understanding when it comes to grades and requesting regrades. Tests are mostly online and open book, so definitely recommend.

Super interesting class, but an easy A. Classes mostly consist of lectures and participation assignments which are often discussion questions. These you can complete with a group. The final project was a group 15-20 min presentation on a topic of your interest from the year. These get a little repetitive becuase they go on for several weeks.

Dr Bradley is a good lecturer and I learned a lot! Also, all the quizzes are with groups in class and you can ask as many questions to him as you want. The exams are take home and online which definitely reduces stress as well. He is very open to feedback and wants you to succeed. Would recommend

Great professor! He is super interested in what he teaches, and his lectures are easy to understand. Tests are SUPER similar to practice exams, and he wants you to do well. Grade based off 3 tests (optional final can replace worst score), canvas "participation" questions, and group/open note quizzes. Take this class!!

Professor Bradley was a great professor! Allowed for quizzes to be taken open notes and in groups and as a professor overall was super understanding and caring, definitely relates to students by being human.

Even though attendance was not necessarily mandatory, there were graded assignments based on in-class discussions. The tests were very straightforward and built off of the online group quizzes we took in class. There was one group project at the end of the year which was not very difficult and an optional final if you wanted to boost your grade.

Professor Bradley used one class (of the week) for a lecture and the other two for a discussion which was really interesting. I found that to be more effective in learning and reeled me to attend class. We had a quizzes, discussion questions, 2 exams, and a group project (and an optional final). He kept class very chill and questions open-ended.

was a good introduction into psychology, very lecture based- barely any material on the posted slides which makes it difficult if you're a visual learner or miss class. lots of group discussions on topics, tests and quizzes are heavy on vocabulary so as long as you learn that you should do well.

Exams are fine, the problem are the projects. Doesn't provide a grading criteria, gives low/avg grades, and gives little and extremely vague feedback. Feels like his grading is totally arbitrary and that he honestly doesn't care much. Learned very little and definitely do not recommend, even for CS/Business majors such as myself.

He truly cares about his students LEARNING and not just memorizing. He gave 2 tests the whole semester and a test for the final; homework is assigned every week and it really helps with learning. He gives ample amount of practice problems and the test is like the study guide. Lastly go to class it counts as participation and he randomly tracks it.

He makes his midterm review with ChatGPT, and doesn't give any rubrics for any of the group projects or grading of them. Basically he says "just figure it out on your own" so you make a bunch of mistakes sacrificing your grade until you find what he's looking for. (a lot of group projects btw.) Feedback is also extremely ambiguous. Don't take him.

Consider carefully before taking this class if you are a Business Major with a Fintech concentration. The workload is heavy, with expectations to fully learn DS2000 and DS2500 in the first 2 weeks, followed by extensive machine learning material. While exciting, be prepared to get a 70 on each project.

I have gotten an A in every DS course in Khoury including ML1+2, but I received a 70 on every project in this class with 1-2 comments on each. There is almost no justification for grades and he doesn't look at your code. You are graded on a slideshow presentation of your model that "shouldn't be technical" but also needs to be or you'll lose points

Likes to say his class is difficult, but he really just doesn't give a rubric for projects and then grades like an a-hole. It's almost impossible to tell why you got the grade that you did and it has been one of the most frustrating classes I've taken at Northeastern. Don't take this class especially if you've had other ML classes. Learned nothing
worst professor i've had. he expects you to do 1000 things in his projects when he only teaches you a few basic models in class. don't recommend

This class was unfortunate. You can tell he's a smart guy but he's just not a good teacher. Class had no structure, half of the classes were guest speakers since he had no material to teach us. Entire class was based around useless case studies. Also, this didn't bother me but EVERY SINGLE assignment is w/ a group, so if you hate that don't take it

Needs to go through the material slower, especially the math. The speed of the class makes this course more difficult then it may need to be. Maybe less guest speakers and take more time on the material that were tested on. Also, the course name should ONLY state Venture Capitalism, because that's all you really discuss the whole semester.
Very hard exams!!

Just took the midterm for this class, and chose this professor due to the good reviews he has received. The most impossible class ever. Pulled 2 straight all nighters to do review questions for a 50 on this midterm. He expects your finance background to much broader than what it actually is. Only recommended for very qualified students.

if u want to get a good grade, take corp finance with him! gives u review sheet, practice problems with answers. Tests are really easy and are the exact questions as in the review sheet. Lots of cases though and picks 3 out of 4 cases. lectures are boring though and u can easily get a 100 on the tests if u dont come to class. easy grader.

corp finance is the easiest class thanks to krishnan. tests are not only short but easy. all u have to do is do the problem sets and ur set to get 90's on his tests. He also gives ton of practice problems and a review tests to get u ready. Also make u do cases but he drops the lowest out of 4. IF you want a good grade, take his class!!!!

While he does know his stuff and while he is capable of explaining things very well, he is not as easy as people think. He assumes that you already know EVERYTHING about finance and wants to make this class seem nothing more than a refresher. Puts a lot of emphasis on group project (5). Online homework are a pain in the neck, exams are ok as most.

Great teacher. Makes a hardish class simple. you can definitely tell he knows his stuff. i would definitely recommend taking him for financial management.  2 graded assignments, 3 exams and a final. drop the lowest exam grade. and can use a formula sheet on exams.

Classes are all lecture/practice problems, which can get very boring after awhile. However, Krishnan is very clear and good at explaining finance. Tests are not too hard, if you pay attention in class you'll do fine. Overall a good professor, I would definitely take him again.
Very nice guy, very clear and helpful powerpoints, allows formula sheets and has very helpful test reviews. best two out of three midterms.

Took her for love hate online class very rude. gets mad when you ask a question and replies with one word answers. literally should not be teaching an online class if she can't handle people having questions. shes not clear with directions and then gets mad when someone has a question. avoid.

Syllabus said the class was PASS/FAIL, but on the last day when grades were out turned out it was a letter grade class. She did not know that faculty hadn't made the class pass/fail yet and even upon clarifying in person said it was pass/fail and never bothered to check. Had to appeal the grade from C to A; the whole class trades were altered.
love her humor!

Class is boring but it's required. Weekly conversations with professors/board members/ students/etc with a reflection due. They're annoying but take like 10 mins. Anyone who says the instructions weren't clear can't read. I got a 100% on everything and I started them half and hour before they were due. Just show up and you'll be fine.

She was fine as she didn't teach the class. She refused to give you credit for the weekly assignment if you did not attend class, no matter how much notice you gave. She never made clear what the assignment requirements were which made it nearly impossible to get a full score.

Take a different prof for light work & easy A, take Larsen to learn. I worked hard but got a 97 plus 10 points of extra credit. Her lectures are only her speaking about what we read in the textbook which wasn't for me. probably wasted my time reading. the TA grades the papers & projects and she's too harsh. PARTICIPATE AND LISTEN IN LECTURE

Excellent professor with entertaining lectures. Encourages students to answer questions, and always provides additional classifications during class. Easy to access outside of class for lingering questions.
Get Larsen if you can you won't regret it!

She is an entertaining professor to listen to, gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit and we get to go to court and witness cases in place of class lectures at times. 
I cannot complain, she's great! She also gives you one or two chances to turn in a late assignment without asking or explaining.

Prof Larsen is awesome! She's super passionate about the CJ system explains her first hand experience as a Defense attorney (super cool). The quizzes are based on her lectures - if you skip class, you won't pass! There are a few extra credit opportunities which are amazing! (court view) and the final is a video presentation. 10/10 professor.

I have had professor Larsen twice now. She is a great professor, always willing to help and has very interesting and engaging lectures! The material is easy to understand when you participate, go to class, and do the homework and take notesssss!!! You definitely won't pass if you don't show up in class. I enjoyed this class overall.

She is a great professor I would 100% recommend. The class was very simple, just based off textbook chapters and in class lectures with unit quizzes and a semester long easy reflection writing assignment. Final project was an online project, very doable.

Professor Larsen may come off as funny to some, but to me she came off condescending and rude. This class was easy because it's a seminar, but she was not understanding of absence because of sickness and treated us like we were in high school.

Professor Larsen was overall a good teacher. Her lectures can be boring, but within them she covers important information that will be on her quizzes. If you follow the textbook you will do just fine, even if you don't attend lectures. There are about 5 quizzes, a couple writing assignments, and a final project. The work load is doable.
This class is all cases! Lots of reading and doing case studies. That being said, she goes over every single one during class and has a great amount of office hours.

There are definitely complicated concepts covered in this class, so it is important to go to class and participate. Do the readings, but you don't need to buy the textbook (it's over $200 and you can find the cases online). Wording on tests can be confusing. Not an easy class, but you can succeed if you do the work. Do the extra credit.

Professor Larsen is very educated in her field, and I enjoyed her lectures. It's important to read the case studies before class because she takes note of who participates. I recommend looking through her lecture slides before class as well. She offers many extra credit opportunities that aren't too difficult, which is a helpful grade booster.

Krista Larsen is a great professor and creates a lot of chances for extra credit and general redemption in her class. She's also very funny and her lectures are engaging. I would definitely take another class with her if I could.

All the people who gave her low scores obviously don't understand her humor. She's silly but fair. I've had her for three different classes and each time I got an A. The tests are hard, but if you do the extra credit you'll be fine. Become friends with her, go to office hours if you are struggling with tests, email her and she will help you.

Prof Larsen is very charismatic and really knows what she is talking about. I learned a lot in this course and found it very interesting, despite the quizzes and exams that were somewhat difficult. As long as you pay attention in class and study the cases well, you should be fine. A lot of extra credit opportunities as well. Definitely recommend.
Amazing in lectures and keeps your attention. Everything is in the book that you can find online for a free download, very kind.

Professor Larsen is a fun and solid professor overall. She makes class very fun and engages her students well. Larsen makes criminal justice fun in light of how heavy it can sometimes be - definitely would take again. Also - grading is very reasonable

She's a great lecturer and incredibly accessible during class. The quizzes are frequent and tough, but as long as you study the cases beforehand you should be fine. While she doesn't take attendance she will probably notice if you don't show up enough and will mark you down, especially because participation matters, so ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took her Intro to Criminal Justice class asynchronously. The workload is manageable, and the course is well structured and organized. You just gotta make sure you stay on top of deadlines (which can be hard in an asynchronous class but the prof and TA issue reminders for major assignments). Plenty of extra credit options. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Larson is a good teacher, you could learn a lot from her. What I dislike about her is how unnecessarily rude she is to her students. She is an attorney and a professor so she has a lot of work, however, this doesn't excuse the multiple times she has been rude to me and other students for no reason.

I've seriously loved Prof Larsen. I really wish she taught more classes because I would take all of them. The material of this class can be a little convoluted at times but she does a really good job of explaining it. She will tell you over and over again that if she didn't say it in class, it's NOT the answer - and she means it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fantastic experience with Professor Larsen.  Wish there were more class offerings with her.  Would 100% retake her courses.
Amazing class and even better professor!

Prof. Larsen is honestly a great lecturer, but tests can be difficult if you don't know how to apply cases to the scenarios she makes up. If you pay attention in class it's doable. Her extra credit is great, four opportunities for 10 points in total added to your final grade - you can go from a B+ to an A+ if you get all the points.

Larsen's legal practice significantly interferes with class. She appears to have been completely unprepared for this class, even saying she was uncomfortable with the material. Larsen could be described as completely absent from the course for the first half of the semester. Grading & assignments are posted late; treats grad students like children.

I felt the grading of papers was extremely subjective, and unfortunately this accounts for like half of the grade. Tests are intentionally hard and questions poorly written with a lot of typos that can make the question confusing. Very inflexible with deadlines. Didnt wear a mask when in classroom w students. Overall bad experience do not rec
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The extra credit was a life saver. Cool teacher, many tests which were the only graded things, and makes up your final grade alongside extra credit. Tests are tricky but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Larsen is funny, easy to understand and relatable. She makes lectures interesting and is happy to answer questions (incl. about her own experience as a defence attorney). Lots of extra credit opportunities. The only thing I would criticise is that she references MA law a lot since she practices here - her knowledge of other states is limited.

One of my favorite professors at Northeastern. Her lectures are very helpful, and just listen and participate, and you will do well and learn a lot. She really is a funny and interesting person as well, I definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Larsen is a good and clear lecturer so pay attention, take good notes and you should be fine. I found her tests to be a little difficult because she tries to trip you up, even though she claims otherwise. Be very careful of deadlines, she is extremely inflexible and not very understanding. She does give extra credit which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best at NEU. She's straightforward and tells you what you need to know for each case, so get ready to take notes. The tests are hard and she does try and trip you up. This is why you need to read carefully and pay attention to the class discussions and lectures. This class is no easy-A, but you'll definitely learn something.
love love love her. do yourself a favor and take her. she's amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, makes you enjoy class. homework is basically just reading cases, and never very much. gives a decent amount of extra credit. If you're interested at all in law you'll love this class.

Prof. Larsen is an awesome teacher.  Take notes!!! And pay attention.  If you do both of those things you will do fine.  Test and quizzes are directly from the notes.  Reading is not really even necessary because she goes over every reading during class.  Awesome, funny and kind teacher.  Take her class!!!

Gives out tests throughout the semester; is very clear about exactly what needs to be studied in order to do well. Also gives a few brief writing assignments, but as she puts it herself, "Bozo the Clown could do it." Don't be lazy; come to class, pay attention and be a decent student and you'll learn a bunch. Krista is funny and kind and awesome.

Great professor. Is energetic, is great at teaching on the whim and answering questions. You must participate, must show up, and must have either read the textbook or know the topic from previous classes. Fair grader and more than enough extra credit to get through the class easily.

I thrive in classes where the teacher is interesting, lively, and helpful. This is that exact course! Probably gained the most knowledge in this class out of all my other ones this semester. If you read the cases, participate, and take good notes you will excel. Make sure you study for those exams though- they can be tricky and count significantly!

Professor Larsen is an amazing professor. She did a great job of constructing the course so that we could come prepared for discussion. She kept the material fresh, and never stodgy. Her tests/quizzes were fair and balanced. She gave students plenty of opportunities to improve their grade, and was available to students outside of class.
Very interesting. Doesnt take the size of cops often, since she is a defense attorney. Funny and laid back. Talks to fast and loud, but its worth it.

(due process) Interesting,and experienced in the field. Shes a practicing defense atty. theres 4 quizes, a mid term and a final. she also gives 4 opportunities for extra credit. if you study you can get an A.
