reviews.comment: i dropped this class and am retaking it with jude matthews, best decision ever. it seems like professor lopez has gotten worse since i last had him, which was already quite bad. i can't wait to take my orgo final where i now have the confidence + knowledge to ace it. i highly recommend you all to get a different professor, do not rely on the curve!

I can only say that taking his class is worse than self-study, becausestart from chapter 6 is all recored class, we watched his vedio recored  and answered questions freely in class, Our average score on exam2 was 96 /150, as you can imagine. You need to do a lot of pre-study work to keep up with his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM IF YOU WANT TO LIVE IN PEACE. The entire grade is based on quizzes and exams. The grading doesn't help the students score better as every MCQ is 6 points. The FLIPPED classroom in the latter part of the semester will eat 2 hours before every class and he would expect you to understand everything to solve questions in class.

DO NOT TAKE ORGO WITH HIM. I am currently in Orgo 2, and according to my current professor, he failed to teach us the most important chapter for Orgo 2, meaning I now have to spend extra time learning what I should already know (Chapter 11). Also, do not rely on the curve, it doesn't help anything.

One thing I really appreciated about Prof. Lopez is that he was always willing to take feedback. He changed things up (test dates, etc) based on student feedback. He started giving quizzes with partial credit when he got a TA so that the overall grade wasn't dependent on just four tests. Go to his office hours for the types of questions he asks!!

Great man, kind, cares about his students, and always willing to help clear up misconceptions. HOWEVER, the TA for this class when I took it seemed to take joy in taking off points on quizzes, so just be very careful with everything you write. Be aware this class features a flipped classroom setup later in the year (just google it)

Prof. Lopez knows what he's talking about. We fell behind schedule about halfway through the semester, so the last few units felt rushed, but overall he taught the material pretty clearly. If you pay attention in class, you'll be fine. He also gives a VERY generous curve at the end of the course, which helps a lot. Tests were all multiple choice.

Professor Lopez is a nice person, but you would want to consider other professors first before taking his course. His lectures don't really make sense and his exams are nothing like what he covers in class. Your grade is based mainly on your four exam grades. Do not bank on the curve at the end of the semester, it's not worth it.
get a different teacher for orgo !!

He tries his best but confusingly presents information. I strongly recommend you attend office hours and email him with any questions. He will work with you if you show you want to do well. Tests are worth a lot so they will take a lot of effort.

Orgo 1 is definitely a challenging class in general . He is pretty lecture heavy but is very conscientious of his students and course corrects when necessary. he always curves exams and is very accessible through email and online. adds a significant curve at the end of the year to bring class avg to a B. Overall pretty good professor.

Maybe this semester was not his semester, but it was rough. He did not keep up with the syllabus and made LOTS of changes with exams. He was extremely behind compared to other sections and would rush through lectures. Exams had about 30 questions, worth 200 points. You're better off choosing Fulton, at least there is more organization there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A good curve is given at the end of the class. Your grade is basically dependent on 4 exams so you have to make sure you study hard and attend lectures. He is always willing to help students outside of class during office hours so make sure you take advantage of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very smart, knows the material well and takes time to answer students questions, but each exam is worth 20% of your grade and are significantly harder than other orgo sections. lectures also move very fast and it is very easy to fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Disorganized and unhelpful lectures

Clear syllabus from the start, sticks to four tests and a bit of homework for grades. Fair grader and goes over the exam after testing. He's overall a really nice dude and actually cares about his students. Orgo is a hard class, but because of the homework/practice questions he gives, the tests are less scary and he offers a nice curve at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lopez is great but moves really fast in lecture. He drops your lowest test and homework score and is super helpful in office hours. Reading before class can help you stay up with lecture content.

Prof Lopez really cares about his student. He is willing to listen and compromise and he wants everybody to feel the class is fair. At the start of the semester I was unsure because his test were a little unfair. He course corrected and acknowledged how students felt. He's such a great guy and LOVES orgo will take as many questions as needed!

Sometimes professor Lopez can be a little hard to understand but he is an incredibly smart individual. His lectures are really heavy and dense but he takes a lot of time out of class to host meetings for recitation and office hours in order to help.

I would pay to have a different professor for this class. One of those teachers that says something once and never reiterates. God forbid you ask a question because he will either say "I've said this" or give some snarky, condescending comment. His tests are harder than the other ORGO classes & it almost feels like he wants you to fail...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Maulsby is an excellent professor. She gives incredible lectures, teaches interesting topics, knows exactly what she is talking about, and fosters an amazing environment within the classroom. Her teaching style is exactly what I envisioned college professors to be like. I could not recommend her any more highly

Prof. Maulsby is a true inspiration. She is thorough and kind and sort of "all seeing" She holds her students to a high standard, but also gives them the means to reach high. She is kind to all and non-judgemental. Her class is a great space to learn

Very knowledgeable, inspiring and amazing historian. Her knowledge and amazing story telling make waking up 7am worth it. She is SO nice and encourages class conversation. Has interesting media, movies, tidbits and stories to spice the class topic. But you have to WRITE everything in class.  If you have to take Arch History, take it with Maulsby.
Class taken Arch Modernity and City. Very intelligent. I'd also recommend her book "Fascism, Architecture, and the Claiming of Modern Milan, 1922-1943.
Would definitely recommend. Best professor ever.

She's very knowledgeable but I honestly question her teaching methods, and I think I really need to reflect this because she can be one of the best architecture professor. Her main problem is that she talks way too fast so you probably only get 25% of what she said in class, and her presentations are only pictures so it is quite hard.

Extremely knowledgeable, rarely need to look at her notes during lecture, shows the how much she understands her material. However she doesn't have any notes in her slides so you have to absolutely pay attention in class to know what's going on.

Probably the best instructor I have had at Northeastern so far. Interesting and captivating lectures that convey a knowledge and passion for the subject matter that is above and beyond expectation. Expects much from students but her conversational lectures prove very helpful of gaining cogent understanding of material. Definitely one of the greats.

Professor Maulsby is the Best History of Architecture professor at Northeastern.  While she is demanding, you will learn if you put in the time and effort.  She is very helpful and knows the material well. Take her classes!

Maulsby is by far the best arch history prof at Northeastern currently, i've had all of the others and Maulsby tops them all. She does demand a lot out of you but is very fair, very helpful and very intelligent.

Her lectures aren't that great...she says 'um' a lot. She is obviously a very intelligent person who is clearly interested in architecture but she wants to prove to the students (maybe a bit too much) that she is very informed on the subject.  Tests are slide id and short essay (for world architecture) which can be difficult

This professor does not know much about anything and just recycles old notes from 10 years ago. I really am disappointed in their ability. Will skirt tail any opportunity to explain something to students.

Amazing professor, gives very heavy feedback that can feel discouraging but will sit with you and go through everything to make sure you succeed. Really available for office hours and extremely knowledgeable, overall an amazing professor.

Professor Landherr is truly a great person. He cares deeply for his students and is always willing to help make your life better in any way. He does not grade using tests, and instead uses a portfolio of work due at the end of the semester, taking a lot of the stress out if the class.
Super great professor! Recommend to everyone!

Prof. Landherr is the BEST. They give so many opportunities for you to improve upon your past submitted assignments and make it really easy to actually learn class content. They provide skeleton notes so you know exactly what information you need to be getting from class, plus there were no tests. They truly want you to succeed in their class.

I highly recommend this prof for any chemE classes. He cares about his students and the topics he is teaching. He uses skeleton notes so it is easy for students to take notes. The weekly problem sets are hard, but his / the TAs office hours are a lifesaver. He offers lots of assignments so you grade is not solely based on exams.
Probably the funniest prof i've ever had! You can tell he loves what he does and he cares about you. Very accessible and his lectures are amazing.
He really cares about all of his students. Overall, a really great professor. Would definitely take one of his classes again!

The professor clearly cared about all his students. His lectures were based on doing lots of examples and he provided skeleton notes for ease of note-taking. Overall, he was a good prof, but his tests were quite difficult, especially since the test questions were not similar to the in class examples or the practise questions.

Professor Landherr is a very nice man who really cares about his students. His lectures aren't boring. His tests though are pretty hard. I would say the examples provided in class arent very equal to what you would see on tests. Problem sets are hard and I went to tutoring for all of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Landherr is the best ChemE professor I've had. Besides actually being competent, he is a genuinely nice guy that cares about his students. He always communicates his availability outside of class and is willing to help anyone struggling.
He's nice but it's a bit hard to hear him because he speaks very quietly and softly. The course itself is incredibly difficult and graded on 3 exams each worth 30%.

reviews.comment: If you can avoid Luca, do it. He is not a good teacher. His lectures are just him doing practice problems but he doesn't explain anything and just starts doing it and gets it wrong half the time. Then he gives 3 tests that are a combined 90% of ur grade and hw is the other 10%. He grades the hw so hard my hw average was lower than my exam grades

letter grade dropped by 2 whole letters just because submitted four homeworks late :((((( like im sorryyyy i had stuff to do
gpa dying
late policy is all the others after the first late assignment get zeros >:(

the professor is a very nice guy but i did not like his teaching style at all. just sort of talks at you while doing the problems. exams are each worth 30% of your grade and are three questions each, easy to get partial credit but also difficult to lose a lot of points on.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! Very smart person, but doesn't know how to teach AT ALL. The only thing he does in lectures is examples, which are wrong half the time. reviews.comment: He just does examples for the class without really explaining what he's doing.
Does not teach, all he does is example problems the entire class. Avoid him for statics at all costs. Nice and friendly guy, and grades decently, but you will end up learning better online.

Prof Caracoglia is a nice and approachable person, but his lecture is very hard to follow. Most of the students cannot follow what he is doing. Tests are not as hard as other professors and he gives generous partial credit if you try.
Prof Caracoglia is a friendly and caring person. However, his lectures are extremely unclear and most students cannot follow. His tests are easy, though. He gives generous partial credit on exams.
very kind and helpful

I had Luca for Statics. He's pretty funny and overall a nice guy. You have to really pay attention to him to learn, he is a genius but he speaks quietly and with an accent. His tests are pretty hard. He makes a lot of mistakes in lecture, but does not tolerate your mistakees on tests! Grade are typically scaled.. A lot.
He's a brilliant teacher. Always willing to help. Had a great time in his class. Highly recommended.
Overall, he is a decent professor yet fails to explain  the lesson easily. He isn't a very grader, and he isn't fair with exams but if you work hard in his class you ought to be ok

He is a brilliant guy who struggles from a language difference. I took Structural Analysis 1 which wasn't easy. He definitely knows his stuff, but has a hard time communicating concepts. However, if you don't understand something, he'll give you 110% to help you out. You just have to be patient with him. He's a great guy.

Wonderful person, not so great undergraduate professor. I'm cutting her some slack because it's clear she hasn't taught any other u.g. courses before this one. Unreachable outside of class and her grading guidelines weren't clear when it came to our reflections, but all "exams" are done asynch on canvas. Be sure to read the textbook or ur cooked.

unclear grading, no in person exams but harsh grader on take home "knowledge/skills checks" which are mcq/frq like quizzes. participation matters A LOT- i did not really learn anything, she yells a lot, doesn't post lectures, impossible to get a hold of her outside of class. no real attendance but she takes mental attendance. doable but would avoid

I took Law 3101 (law and legal reasoning), and did not enjoy it. The entire grade was made up of around 15 (FRQ&MCQ) homework assignments that were harshley graded and had unclear criteria. She also gave us red, yellow, and green cards to tell some students to stop participating as much. She is very loud and yells a lot (not at us, just speaking)

This professor is the sole reason I did well in 1800. Everything I learned was from her seminar. She's hilarious, gives a lot of time to work on the 1800 project, and is a phenomenal lecturer. It's obvious she cares a lot about her students. My friend and I are taking her for CS3100 next semester. Best professor I've had at Northeastern.

Recitation for cs1800 is extremely important to go to. Sucks that they often seem to be during lunchtime. No mandatory anything, no grading (it's a recitation for cs1800), and the topics covered are often identical to what will be on the quiz.

She's an amazing professor and she generally review regrade requests upon request. She can be a little aggressive at times, but she really does care about her students. GO TO LECTURES!!! My only regret is not going to lectures and cramming before tests. This call can be really easy but it depends all on you. Make sure you choose your partner for hw
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She explains concepts clearly and is accessible to students, responding to emails in a timely manner. The grading policies are strict, and some assignment instructions are super vague. This version of the course required a heavy workload, but it's changing next semester. She was challenging but you'll learn a lot from her for any course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor has her flaws, but does okay to explain the content. The problem is the content is quite useless when you think about it. We spend excessive time analyzing design patterns that are unlikely to show up in a real SWE role. Across my past 3 internships and 2 upcoming ones I doubt I would need any of it. I wish we focused on DS instead.

Professor Nunez is all-around a great teacher. The lectures are very helpful for understanding the content. There's a lot of homework, but you learn a lot from this class. It's not too challenging as long as you plan your time well. Definitely would take OOD with Nunez again.

The only problem with this course is that there is a LOT of material and homework. But the lectures are amazing and Lucia is very helpful. Great professor, she tries her best, is "tough but fair" lol.

I took OOD with her, and overall she truly does the best she can given how challenging the course is structured to be. She cares about her students, is very understanding, and knows how to teach the material. While the class itself is extremely difficult, she is supportive and does everything she can to help students succeed within that structure.

One of the best most engaging professors I have ever had. She is a great lecturer, extremely knowledgeable and always willing to answer any question you may have. In addition, she just always knows the answers to literally anything CS related. Highly reccomend taking this class with her if she decides to teach the new OOD.

Nunez is incredibly passionate about the class and is very committed to making sure every student (that is willing to put in the work) matures past the first year CS curriculum. Course is very hard but it is necessary for the workfield and pushes you past the learning curve of CS. VERY active on piazza and easily accessible. TOUGH but fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nunez is by far one of the best professors in the CS department. She truly cares about her students, whether it be through quick online responses or even in office hours, Nunez is already there to provide quick and efficient help. Generous with giving extra late tokens and always keeping us updated. Always responds outside of work hours as well!
CS3500 is ridiculously hard. If you can avoid it, quoted from Nike, "just do it".

CS3500 is without a doubt one of the hardest CS classes at NEU, and given this, I don't think Nunez was a bad professor per se. Lectures were quite good, and questions were quickly answered on Piazza, the class forum. However, she was not very approachable, and answers at office hours were extremely rushed/unhelpful.

Took her for one of the last sections offered for OOD. Genuinely one of the greatest professors I've ever had. Truly, truly cares about her student's and work. Is quick to respond/help according to student's neads (sometimes even at odd hours on weekends). Makes an otherwise tough and life-draining class bearable and sometimes even quite fun.

She is the most thorough, detailed, and passionate professor ever. Very quick at responding, happy to help students, and really wants us to learn. However, the course load assumes your entire life revolves around OOD and the grading is harsh and nit-picky. They are changing the course so maybe the new one doesn't make you as depressed.

Very accessible but super harsh on grading(exams), time investment into this class is too much considering you have 3-4 other courses to worry about. 
If I was only taking like 2 classes, this class would be good. Make sure you are completely ready and can program well before taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she was good for the first 2 months and fell off. bad teacher. not sympathetic about actually teaching from mistakes. will get mad if you ask a genuine question. scary. The course is already hard enough, and she is not a teacher for beginners. Their slogan, "CS/for everyone," is a lie because of this teacher.

Lucia is a great prof. She responds to emails quickly and is very active on Piazza. She is patient and respectful in situations where others wouldn't. Its evident she cares.

The homeworks take a LONG time and TAs grade harshly. The curriculum is also very boring, but that's not her fault. If you HAVE to take OOD, take it with Lucia.

Phenomenal professor, she's a really tough professor but if you put in the work, go to office hours, and don't cheat she quickly becomes one of the best experiences you can hope for. Took this class in spring and had an amazing time.
The best prof I had at Northeastern before I transferred. Hands down.

It was a pretty average experience. Exams are tough (not curved), HWs are a lot of work if you don't start early. Self-Evals are brutal at first. TAs are very helpful. She can sometimes come off very snippy/rude or quick to condemn, which is not entirely conducive to supportive learning, but her heart's in the right place.

Professor Nunez is easily the best professor Ive ever had. She makes the concepts super understandable and really wants you to succeed. My only problem was the tests are super difficult. In this year, our questions just didn't make sense to me. She is also very firm on no curving or such. Overall really good class and teacher. OOD IS ALOT OF WORK!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher, terrible curriculum.

Homeworks are very long and intensive, and the grading is super tough. Personally for me the exams weren't too bad for me, but there are no curves when the whole class does bad. If you're taking OOD or whatever replaces this in the fall, read Head First Design Patterns, as that helped me study and do well on the exams.

While she is helpful and accesible, this class is nearly impossible. You won't be successful unless you devote basically your entire life to this class. That is impossible while students balance other things. It's too complicated, tests are confusing, lectures are too fast, and on and on. Bad class and can't wait for the change.

I can't even imagine taking OOD with anyone other than Prof. Nunez. She's extremely understanding and caring that the class itself is very hard and time consuming. I showed up to office hours consistently, dedicated over 40 hours/week to this class out of SURIVIVAL, and still hope to get another class with Prof. Nunez. She's awesome!
Nice lecturer, tough class. Grading feels random—depends on TA luck. Exams nearly impossible, curves nonexistent. Good luck, brave souls!
Avoid at all cost. This is not a joke.

OOD is tough, no getting around that. The class being challenging is unavoidable, and is a fault of itself, not the professor. Lucia is phenomenal. She truly cares about her students, and she is very responsive on Piazza and emails. I'm hoping that the curriculum changes don't water OOD down, because it does teach you a lot, despite the challenge.
The exams are extremely hard.
Horrible professor, do not take, extremely disrespectful towards students, inappropriate as well
Do NOT take Professor Nuñez
Horrible professor, avoid at all costs

It is clear through many of the other reviews that the workload and grading was extremely harsh. While I do agree, I'd put it 20-80 on Lucia. Although the first homework felt like being kicked out the nest, she is super accessible outside of class, often answering Piazza as late as 3AM. Some TAs need help. Lucia is an extremely caring professor.

Let me preface, she's a great person and very easy to talk to when you need help. However, her lectures aren't helpful for the homework and her instructions are highly unclear, which was a struggle. HW takes 20+ hours in the beginning, but eases up at the end of the sem. TA grading is frustrating, seems like some of them don't fully read our hwks.

Horrible class; assignments were posted back to back. You truly cannot get a perfect score on the evaluations unless you cover every single edge case possible in your testing. Got a 50% on the extra credit only because of my tests while everything was functioning. Missed 2-3 tests out of 90 that I wrote total.

*MUST READ*

The teaching style was solid, but the class was terrible. Self-evaluations after assignments were weighted heavily (e.g., 6% for an assignment, 3% for the evaluation) and they were pointless bringing down grades harshly. Extra credit was mediocre. I lost major points for missing a few test cases, and she doesn't round up grades.

I agree with many other posts. But I personally did not enjoy the group aspect of the class and was not clear for the requirements of the class. Material given in class is often unclear and the notes or slides don't help too much.

Homework is very time-consuming, but thats an OOD thing not a Lucia thing.. I think Lucia as a professor is fine but tends to ramble.. its her personality & grading -- and grading is EXTREMELY inconsistent, it entirely depends on which TA you get or if you get Lucia herself. Exams were prob easier than the hw in this course too, just prep 4 hw tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Lucia is a good teacher. Communicates content well, available outside of class, genuinely cares about her students. The workload is insane. 15-20+ hours of homework weekly.
Grading felt arbitrary, hostile, and particular, like she wants you to get the worst grade possible. Lock in and pay attention to detail, it's you vs Lucia in OOD

I do not believe the issues with this course lies with Professor Nunez, but in the course itself. Nonetheless, lectures did not feel engaging and group projects are the worst. I hope the recreation and restructuring of the 3 fundamentals of CS classes at NEU end up fixing some of these issues

Prof Nunez is a very good professor, OOD is just a really hard class. She does her best and communicates the ideas very well, the exams are weighted more heavily than they should. The homework's are long, be sure to start early. Try to get a good lab partner, it really helps.

OOD is a hard class. Nunez's very ambiguous and 'open to interpretation' instructions were probably the worst part of the class. But, this is kind of a part of OOD, as you are supposed to interpret these problems your own way and come up with a solution. 15+ hours of homework per week. Difficult class, Lucia isn't amazing, but shes fair, and kind.

I mean, it's OOD, there's gonna be a lot of work. BUT Professor Nunez made sure that people survived the struggles of OOD by being a good support resource, exams and homeworks were curved if the class did particularly poorly and late policy is super flexible and forgiving.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nunez is an amazing prof all around, cares about her students and wants to help them succeed

Professor Nunez was an amazing professor!!! She was so understanding and had very reasonable policies. She clearly cares about her students and their success, and puts a lot of effort into supporting us in what is known to be a very difficult class. I would definitely recommend her as a professor for any class, but especially OOD.
Had for a lab class, so helpful and willing to help when you are not understanding the content.

In CS it felt like all professors were just going to be cold and irritating till I took Nunez. Turned a class I was worried about as I had a weak math background and completely aced it. She is so caring and extremely good at teaching and breaking down concepts to a basic level. only had one exam and was not bad. only one topic our of the 10 was meh

Lucia is patient, thorough, understanding, and just a fantastic professor. She made learning the concepts of object-oriented design fun. The material and projects were a challenge at times, but Lucia's class helped build my coding confidence and made me hopeful for the future. I wish I could take her class again.
Professor Nunez is a fantastic professor, she's super kind and caring. I also had her for my lab, and she uses the same examples and problems she does in the lecture, which is excellent.

Professor Nunez is a great professor. The class was pretty intimidating to begin- many people claim that its a weeder class. But Nunez and the faculty do everything they can to make sure that students understand the material presented. She is accessible, you can ask questions in lecture without embarrassment, overall pretty great. 10/10 recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: kind and helpful to students. lectures are not too bad

Nunez is such a genuine person who really cares about every student. Although the information being taught was complex, she did a great job trying to explain and giving her time into office hours and extra help.

Professor Nunez is really good about explaining concepts in a way that it's digestible, understandable, and interesting, she'd stop and ask us questions and it is evident she really cares about making sure we understand the material before moving on overall great professor.
Very nice and you can tell she cares about her students. Lectures well organized and clearly taught.

CS 3500 - OOD. Lectures were very boring. You don't really even need to go. Just look over the notes when implementing MVC in homework (which are VERY time consuming). Exams aren't really based on any design patterns taught in the class: the only thing was Inheritance vs. Composition, and then they are mixed in with some algorithmic-like problems.
Professor Nunez is great! Discrete is basically a puzzle game, but the professor explains concepts very well.
Had her for CS1800, CS2510, and CS3500. She is great :)

A QUEEN!! RMP won't let me say CS 2510 which is what I had her for (not 1800) but she is a phenomenal lecturer. She makes things fun and interesting and is always understanding and willing to help and re-explain (even when I ask dumb questions lol). Fundies 2 is a tough course but she always tries her best to make sure everyone understands. 11/10

The course itself is quite challenging. However, Professor Nunez usually responded fast on Piazza and on emails. He was very responsible and tried to explain concepts in an easy-to-understand way. He is also very caring because I remembered screwing up midterm. He suggested me not worrying about it anymore and giving myself self-care!

Prof Nunez does a really good job of breaking down concepts and explaining them well. Additionally, the homeworks he writes are fair and relate to the lectures he gives in class. With his help + the tas, I felt like I had a reasonable grasp of the material and was able to succeed.
Lectures were confusing and not helpful at all for exams. Had to reteach myself all the material before exams.

Prof is smart and passionate but the structure of comm research was absolutely miserable; felt like everything about the class was designed to punish rather than push students who aren't good at stem topics. Even if you did ok on your own, semester-long group projects hurt your grade. Strict grading and large tests are the biggest assignments.

I love her, never met a prof who actually reads our discussion posts and plans class activities revolving around the class's discussion board. Will warm call if she liked your discussion post
No textbook, have to read articles and play 2 games per week and write discussion post, can be a bit time consuming but I find the process fun

The textbook selection was good and the lessons were valuable, but reading the textbook yourself would be good enough. Professor's accent was hard to understand at times. He gave the impression that deadlines were flexible and wasn't clear about deadlines. Did not receive feedback on papers, refused to grade submissions by the time grades were due.
Teaching style is extremely p underwhelming. Learned nothing new. No different than doing your own research. Class was a waste of money.

The syllabus clearly defines expectations and course objectives. Professor Lwin's comments on discussions and proposals are opaque, and it isn't easy to understand his preferences. His grading seems to be subjective. I didn't love this course because I didn't enjoy the subject, but the professor was informative and passionate about the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Lwin is very kind and caring, especially with students who have an MH diagnosis such as anxiety. Be prepared to not get grades back though - I have received a grade on my first two weeks of work, my short answer quiz, and my group proposal.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Tun puts together a good online course that is really comprehensive. There is a lot of reading, but the instructions are very clear. He also responded to my emails quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Tun is difficult to understand, often speaks too quietly, and does not deliver material in a focused manner. He took well over a week to respond to my emails. He gave little and inconsistent feedback, and did not grade weekly assignments, thus the class was in the dark about their final grade throughout the quarter. Nice man, notsogreat educator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Tun can be difficult to understand sometimes. While the syllabus was clear, his explanation of tasks were not always clear. Moderate-heavy amounts of reading with lengthy weekly posts. 1 paper due during term, along with TermPaper Proposal. 1 final paper. Very educated & knows what he is talking about. Always is trying to make you understand deeper
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Takes FOREVER to get grades back to you so you don't actually know how you're doing in the class. Takes extra long to e-mail you back, if he does at all. With the semester nearly over he has graded about 3 assignments we've had, though so far we've taken 2 quizzes, submitted term proposals, & completed 10 discussions.

Very harsh grader and exams were difficult compared to what is presented in the textbook and slides. He did boost the classes overall grade, so I went from a B- to a B+, which I feel like was fair for the effort I put into the class. Exams take up 60% of the overall grade and if you mess up once its hard to come back from it. Take with caution.

Professor Dau is very engaging and his lectures are interesting. He is very passionate about what he teaches and great at conveying information. His exams are difficult and memorization-heavy but fair. He makes good use of class time with group activities. Definitely the most engaging professor you can have for international business.

Very tough instructor. Take it with another prof and avoid him. Seems he enjoys having a class with lower average by making exams more difficult. I prefer to watch paint dry than attend this guy lectures.

Classes are very interesting and fun, you'll feel it's worth your time because you'll read/learn things that are important and not just theory. He is very passionate about teaching and really good at it! (Very organized material) Also, I was shy in the debates and he encouraged me to participate and gave me tools to become better. 100% recommended!

Very challenging class, but you get the work that you put in. Lectures are quite long, but very entertaining and easy to follow with. He encourages participation, which makes the class a lot more engaging. Make sure you study hard and read the textbook. Definitely not an easy A, and you will have to put in the work, but overall a fun class.

Professor Dau has incredible lectures and the debates are so fun! The tests are difficult and require a lot of studying. Class participation and attendance is important. The group project was very harshly graded but a fun project to work on overall.

Dr. Dau is very kind and cares about his students' well-being over anything. He gives solid lectures but is an incredibly tough grader. The tests are tricky and the group projects are time-consuming but fun to be a part of. This class is the farthest thing from an easy A, but you will learn so much and be glad you had such a qualified professor.

I mean it's your classic "hard but good" class. Yes, the tests cover a lot of material. Yes, there's an annoying group project. Yes, you have to show up and participate. Prof. Dau is super passionate and his classes get ur brain going.If you're looking for an interesting class with fun debates that really get your brain thinking, this is the class.

Professor Dau did a great job with us graduate students. Despite the difficulties of remote learning, he handled it like a champ and really seemed to care about our learning. Interesting class, great professor!

Easily my favorite prof at NEU, his class is tough but also enlightening, he is extremely kind and respectful to students, the exams and HW are really hard but he's always available for office hours and questions, attendance is mandatory and he makes you sign in to know if you're actually in class, overall an amazing prof, take his class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dau is a great professor who truly cares about his students, and actively considers any feedback you give him. I really enjoyed his lectures as I found them informative and engaging, and would recommend his class to anyone with an interest in the subject matter. You definitely need to put in the work to succeed in his class though.

Professor Dau is a very caring professor who has a lot of experience and enthusiasm for the subject matter. There is a lot more reading than your typical high school class, however, it is doable. You will need to read a chapter of the textbook and 2-3 supplemental readings per week, due on different days. He is easily my favorite professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This was the best class I took first semester. He is passionate about what he teaches, is very friendly and willing to help, and gives very fair exams. He is clear about expectations for assignments and grading. Take this class, you will have to read but it is 100% worth it. Homeworks take anywhere from 30 mins-1 hr and are once a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Dau is very passionate about his job and truly cares about his students. His lectures are more or less engaging and his quizzes are straightforward. If you participate and enjoy the concepts that you are learning in his class, it is fairly easy to do well. Great teacher overall.

Professor asked us to do the TRACE evaluation in class and basically made sure that 100% of the class completed it before he released the grades. He is a VERY VERY tough grader when it comes to your final group paper. For participation, if you open your mouth you get points, so people who have the audacity to talk any irrelevant crap get points

Professor Dau is definitely one of the best professors I have ever met at NEU. He is always friendly, passionate and ready to help. He literally tried his best to make everyone participate in the class. If you want to learn something, choose him. He judges issues without favoritism or bias, he will give you pros and cons and let you think.

What a professor! He truly cares about each student, and one of the few professors that pushes the envelope to help you challenge your own way of thinking. He regularly invites professors from different concentrations to lead every class in a different subject. If you ever have a chance to take any of his courses you will not regret it!

This professor literally read off a script and assigned so many readings that it became difficult to study for the tests. And if you didn't do well on these tests your grade would plummet. The group project was terrible too; you and one other person will end up doing all the work. Don't take this class with this professor; your GPA will thank you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Dau is one of the most nice people and professors that I have come across, which can be seen by his devotion and dedication to his students. He is willing to do whatever it takes to help each student succeed, offering a lot of office hours, and although his class is a lot of work and definitely not an easy A, I would say it is worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Your grade is based solely off of 3 tests and 2 group presentations. Both of which are unclear on how they should be completed. The tests are based off of so much broad material it is difficult and overwhelming to figure out what to study.
Made tests harder just to bring down class average. Difficult to communicate with outside of class. Other sections of this class are way easier and less stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Dau is AMAZING. His class is fun and the debates are very rewarding if you do the work. The exams are challenging but you can get A's if you know the material (almost all from the book.) By the end of the class, I thought they were straightforward. Put in A LOT of effort for the group project because he grades those tougher. Take his class!

Very friendly professor. If you participate in class, he will like you and you will get a good participation grade. Tests require a lot of studying, but are manageable (but do the reading!). However, classes are interesting because they are interactive with lots of debates. Definitely worth taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a good lecturer who brings in enthusiasm for the course, and mixes in debates/case discussions with his lectures. Keep up with the readings and you should do fine for class participation. His tests are noncumulative and not too tough in my opinion, but he is very harsh on grading his project. Connect with him to understand his expectations.

Professor Dau makes every class enjoyable through his always-interesting lectures. He is very clear on his intentions with every assignment and project, and if you follow his lead and pay attention, you will do great. Cares a lot about students doing well and actually learning. He is DEFINITELY worth taking, especially for International Business.

Participate. Talk in class or you will not do well. He only likes the people who talk and if he likes you your class experience will be so much better. His tests are brutal but if you study you can do well. He places a lot of emphasis on presentation skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dau is my favorite professor that I have had at NU! He is a caring guy who genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. His material is always very current and practical. Case studies, lectures and discussions are all interesting. Lots of reading, but manageable. Tests are difficult but if you put in the work you can do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The exams are too hard to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Three exams each worth 20%. My strategy is to read the chapters in preparation of the exam, develop a quizlet based on the powerpoints, and memorize it. Participate in class and check up with him early in the semester to see how you can improve. When it comes time for presentations, ask what he looks for because his grading on this can be arbitrary
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite courses so far at NU. The exams aren't easy but if you read the book you can get a good grade. There's a good amount of reading in this course but the lectures are very interesting and relevant. Mr Dau is a great guy who truly cares about making the world a better place.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dau is a great professor who genuinely cares about the success of his students. However, what you put in is what you get out. Exams are very difficult, but seek help from Dau in office hours to better approach preparing for them. Attendance and participation are mandatory, and weekly homework assignments must be completed on time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice and teaching well for the course. If you work hard and participate in the class, you will get a fair grade. Never feel hesitate to reach him outside the class, he is willing to help everyone who wants to learn more from the class.

Makes the class interesting with debates, discussions and personal stories. Participation is important. The midterms are directly from the textbook and fairly straightforward. A great professor, highly recommend him!

Dau is one of the most interesting people at NEU. Every class is filled with interesting stories about himself. Attendance is a must, and keep keeps track of how many times you talk during class... which helps keep discussions going. There are great debates each week. The tests are reasonable if you really read the chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very interesting class, but the tests are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Probably my best professor this year. He came in everyday to our early 8am class with a burst of energy and made an almost two-hour class bearable. You have to read the textbook on your own, so pace yourself, cause you need it. Participation counts a lot and it is sometimes hard to get called on in a big class. Show effort and you will be rewarded.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof Dau is such a caring, genuine and kind professor, and also as a person. Tries to know each of his students individually and helps them improve for THEMSELVES. I was struggling a lot on his tests, but he helped me and spoke to me very calmly. Class content is very interesting, but A LOT to apprehend. Wants his students to do their best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best! Highly recommended
Professor Dau is a strict grader and there are many chances you can get to bring your grade up. Really difficult exams. Avoid.

Attend class, do the hw, understand the material and you will pass. There were only two tests + one semester group project. Participation is a big chunk of the grade, and attendance is mandatory. The tests cover a lot of content, so make sure to start earlier. Moderately high amount of reading. He's a great lecturer and classes were interesting!

Prof Dau is good and is passionate about Int'l Business but most of the class is just powerpoint and he conducts stupid debates that go over the same assignment that you wrote last night. Tests are mostly multiple choice and right off the chapter summary but sometimes get super specific. Constant assignments but he gives a 100% easily on those.

His tests are no longer multiple choice, so if you don't know it you'll get the question wrong. There's a lot of material and he expects you to know almost every minute detail. Doing assignments aren't that hard, but they're long. His tests are unrealistically hard. The homework contains 20+ pages from Harvard Business School.

Don't choose him because he'll expect you to master the material to his level. You won't learn much the first half of the course and his class will most likely cost your grade. This is not a core level class because he forces you to come to class and be as immersed as he is with the subject.

This is my hardest class even with concentration classes because of the amount of work he gives. The tests are ridiculously hard. The homework and class material are straightforward, but his tests are on a different level, which makes no sense. I lost my interest because he doesn't prepare you.  He expects his students to love it as much as he does

Professor is very friendly. Most of the class is taught from power points but there are frequent debates based on readings and an assignment. If you do the readings and debate assignments the class will be easy. The TA did most of the grading for my class though.
Great speaker and he is a hottie

Professor Dau is a nice guy and he really enjoys teaching Intl Bus. Dau is a really smart guy. He has a lot to offer and knows what he is talking about. ALTHOUGH, he will call on you out of the blue and you have to be on your toes the whole class. EXAMS ARE HARD, CLASSES ARE OK

He is the best professor I've had at Northeastern so far. He's amazing. If come to class and participate,do the readings and writings, u should get an A. We also had to read case studies and debate it in class,which is interesting. his exams are fair and easy. They're multiple choice. Already recommended my friends.U WANT TO RAISE UR GPA? TAKE LUIS
Great Teacher

This proffesor is one of the most interesting proffestors. He makes the course fun and enjoyable to attend class and learn. Attendance is mandatory, basically participation and attendance is half te grade. Of you do the work and attend class it's an easy A. Exams are not hard at all. The exams is based on the chapters in the book.

One of my favorite professors.  He is clearly an intelligent man who is very interested in the subject that he is teaching, which makes the subject matter in class more interesting.  Come to class and participate, and that's basically half your grade.  The book is the other half, so make sure to read the chapters if you want to do well on the exams

Very intelligent who knows what he is talking about.  He wants everyone in his class to do well. Topics in the class usually have to do with relevant topics which makes the class more interesting. He makes it very clear what he expects from his students.

Professor Dau is an amazing professor due to his desire to get his class involved an interested. Attendance and participation are mandatory but you will be rewarded for them both. His texts are always focussed on the textbook reading as well as case studies. Very interesting subject matter and overall an amazing professor!

Professor Dau makes his class very dynamic. Read the book since quizzes and exams are mostly based on this. Prof Dau is great, and if you put in the effort you will be rewarded. I enjoyed the class more than any I took this semester and Dau was my favorite professor. Got an A as well.

Professor Dau is great. If you enjoying talking about global trends and events you will love the class. Dau's trademark line is "no curveballs." Nothing but positive things to say about Luis Dau. He is enthusiastic and one of the best professors, if not the best, I have ever had. You will need to put in a bit of effort, but it is not difficult work just basic preparation for discussions and debates which are really fun. Enjoy

Prof. Dau wants us to be relevent with contemporary issues in the business world, the reading assignments help us understand them.For slow readers, the readings might be too much. Professor Dau is the man. He is super friendly and his classes are interesting. He really wants everyone to do well in his class and will go out of his way to help you. Take his class if you have the chance!

Very open prof, most of class is used on discussions, so that's easy.  Assigns readings, and some textbook stuff.  Regular but minimal busywork from readings to help out your grade. He is very strict and he is very very unclear about the test. He is inflexible with the homework assignments, and makes you believe he does not actually read the class summaries.

Professor Wermers is amazing!! I was in another section of this math course a few semesters ago and had to drop it because it was too difficult and the professor was very absent. I wish I could take more of her classes.

Having not taken a math class in a long time, I was a bit nervous. She eased those fears. She offered feedback when asking questions, was constantly involved, and was quick to respond. It was nice having a teacher who would ask us questions and listen I didn't use the textbook much, but others in the class did. Would take a class of hers again.

failed MTH1001 at NEU with Robert Perutti as an on ground instructor. Ms. Wermers helped break thing down carefully and attentively to renew my faith in learning math. Since then I have gone on to pass MTH1001 and are sure to pass MTH2002 this semester

I was extremely nervous about taking Algebra as I hadn't taken a math class in years.  Lynn was a challenging teacher, but also very supportive.  She wants her students to succeed and it shows.  Its hard to believe I'm saying this, but I'm actually looking forward to taking Algebra 2 with her!

She is an amazing professor! She really cares about studens and is always there to help. The course is difficult but as long as you do the work and ask for help you'll do fine. Love her and have taken 3 of her courses. BEST math teacher by far :)

I don't feel I learned much from this class. And I've never seen such a tough grader. I don't think she respect our work much. reviews.comment: Great professor, very easy to get an A if you do the assignments on time. One of the most engaging and lively professors I've had.

The best professor for sure. This class was really fun and definitely so much more interesting and fun work compared to other professors teaching the same course. Do participate and pay attention. GOAT English prof. So passionate and genuinely nice, always super positive and interesting. Very engaging classes where you actually want to participate. Prof McCluskey is the GOAT! Never enjoyed any english class before until his. Shares the point of class is to read and understand stories, but generalizes stories to ourself, communities, and places. Such a fun class, and very funny professor. Actually might be the best class I have ever taken!

My glorious goat Michael McCluskey. This man was so amazing he literally made me write my first review on here. It's really clear he truly loves to teach, and he leads his lessons by making room for all of his students to voice an opinion. He's witty, funny, and genuinely cares about his students. He also offers opportunities to boost your grades.

Best prof, take him if you can! Super engaging classes and let you resubmit any assignment whenever. Hard not to get an A in his class. The daily readings were sometimes unnecessary, but aside from that, no complaints.

Prof McCluskey is genuinely one of the best professors at NEU. He truly cares about creating a welcoming environment for all students and is super funny. Lectures are easy to follow & you know why you are learning something. Incredibly kind and great grading policy - rewrites and extensions if you communicate. 10/10 and hope to have him again.

This was easily my favorite class of the semester. His classes are super engaging and loves to joke around with everyone in the class. I actually ended up learning a good amount of writing skills in this class. Awesome teacher and easy and flexible grader.

Easily the best professor I have had. Consider yourself lucky to be in one of his classes because it will be the most enjoyable part of your day by far. Given any chance to take his class again, I would.

Participation heavy class, makes the class very interesting by incorporating the students, very understanding teacher, easy A if you do your work

Her tests are super easy people just don't like her because her lectures are hard. She was great her final was a little tricky but it impacted my grade slightly. She gives so much extra credit and her resources are great.

please just do yourself a favor and drop her

hard to understand and she does not explain things well but gives opportunities to boost your grade via corrections and assignments

not organized, unclear about information not found in syllabus or that had to be changed mid yr. really frustrating. constantly complains about her work and how she is busy ?? generous with extensions and makeups, though, but doesn't make up for the fact that nothing in her canvas makes sense and half of the things are in wrong order/switched names

Barely can understand what she's saying during class. Super messy when it comes to teaching and planning. Spends way too much time on some chapters and very little time on others. The one good thing is that she is open to due date changes.

Vaso's work is completely disorganized and then tries to cover six chapters in two days.

Vaso is overall a nice person, but if you decide to take her class be prepared to have to teach yourself everything and attend office hours consistently. Her lectures are disorganized and confusing, which increases the difficulty of an already hard course. Despite this, she gives a ton of free points and holds extra reviews to try and help.

She is so sweet and really knows what she is talking about, the course and subject is naturally hard but she gives really good study guides for test and a recitation booklet that is basically a roadmap for the exam. There are extra credit/ easy free point opportunities weekly and you can make up for lost points from exams on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think she's as bad as people are saying. She is very nice & wants you to do well & has a lot of availability outside of class. But. She is not very good at teaching. You will have to rely pretty heavily on teaching yourself as she can be very confusing and disorganized. If you have to take her, don't be scared by the reviews you'll be ok.

She is pretty disorganized and we were always behind. I feel like the exams aren't as hard as everyone says but they can be challenging. She gives extra credit and some assignments to boost our grade. However, she's pretty bad at teaching and makes things a lot more difficult and complicated than they actually are

AVOID TAKING A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. She is incredibly disorganized and went over 4 chapters in 2 classes, saying it will be less than 20% of the final, but it was almost half of the exam. She put things on the final she never went over. She can be passive aggressive when people ask her questions and she can be rude in emails.

Horribly disorganized, you are better off just learning the material by yourself. My class was three weeks behind, and she only started teaching the three new chapters in the last week. And a lot of the questions on the exam were those new chapters. Unless you're great at teaching yourself, avoid AT ALL COSTS.

She is a nice person, but one of the worst professors I have ever had. Very unorganized and makes me confused. The tests are harder than what she gives us to practice with, containing a small amount of questions so it is very easy to get a low grade if you make two mistakes. Final was made of the content we only had a week and a half to spend on.

Professor V. is kind and willing to help, but she is very disorganized. She spends so much time over-explaining one idea and goes through 20 slides in the last 10 minutes of class. There is extra credit, but it doesn't help when the midterms and finals are nothing like practice problems. There were topics that she did not teach on the final.

Professor is very caring and provides a lot of extra assignments to boost your grade. But, the tests are difficult and do not reflect what is taught in the course. Her canvas is messy and her lectures are not helpful at all, so at least 50% of the class does not bother to show up. You must be able to teach yourself material or be good at chem

Lectures are hard to understand. Doesn't realize most of us haven't taken chem. Tries to cram everything in the last 5min. Offered a 10min break at the beginning, which somehow got down to 2min by the end. Final included content she didn't get to in class. Work due AFTER the final, bc she keeps giving extensions noone asked for. Overall, avoid.

The class itself was not overly difficult, but she is very disorganized and does not use class time effectively, so we were constantly behind. Her lectures were really wordy but never really solidified any points or explained concepts well. A good recitation TA is a lifesaver. Prof is also passive aggressive and can be borderline rude.

Do not take her horribly disorganized! Her lectures don't cover content needed for actual exams and SW assignments don't help and the final was everything she didn't have time to cover but promised would not be on it and everyone failed. Don't take her you will regret it and if you think you're doing well just wait for the final to ruin your grade!

She cannot teach during the allotted lecture time but makes it your problem. She promised that the things she taught for two seconds would not be that many questions on the test. IT WAS LIKE A THIRD OF THE FINAL. She takes forever going over slides, getting us so far behind it's not even funny. I've never met someone so disorganized.

DON'T TAKE HER FOR THE SAKE OF YOUR GPA!
- lectures are disorganized and if she doesn't finish or get to the content you simply don't learn it and will be done for on the exams + final, she will say oh yea not on the test YES IT IS and you're cooked
- recitation lol a joke bc you don't get to all the content bc ur always a week behind thx to her

Lectures are not helpful at all. She tries to be generous by giving a few extra credit assignments, but they are to no avail because the final tanked everybody's grades. It was nothing like any midterms/practice exams given. I stopped attending class completely because I always left class more confused than when I came in. Avoid her if possible.

RUN DO NOT WALK. HER LECTURES ARE NO USE AND SLIDES ARE INCREDIBLY MESSY AND DISORGANIZED. COULD NOT UNDERSTAND HER BC OF HER ACCENT AND HAD TO LEARN THE ENTIRETY OF THIS ACCELERATED COURSE ON MY OWN. CURRENTLY CRASHING OUT BC I DONT KNOW ANYTHING AND IS GOING TO FAIL.

do NOT take this class if you can afford to - she is incredibly disorganized on canvas and in lectures, never actually teaches the full amount of what's on the quiz, and is so hard to understand 

the tests are short so each question is worth many points making it easy to lose lots of credit by getting only 2 questions wrong

Vaso is a quite caring lady. But as a professor she does not explain very well. Since it is an accelerated class she moves at a very fast pace. Everything I learned for material was from YouTube and tutors. I will say she gives plenty of homework assignments to boost your grade and often pushes due date. My  suggestion is do plenty of practice prob

She is so incredibly unorganized I'm honestly impressed she is still allowed to teach a class that has so much material to cover. She spends way too long talking about topics that don't appear/appear very little on tests and then rushes through the important material towards the end of the unit (2 chapters in one day). Yeah don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID THIS GREEK GOD. She hyperventilates within the last five minutes of class when she comes to the epiphany that she's gone over 20% of the slideshow. I have levitated in this class class out of pure boredom. You will not have the bandwidth to deal with this class. Save yourself and your future headaches from banging your head against the wall
Don't take her, its for your own safety.

If I could give Vaso a 0/5 I would. She can not teach for the life of her and spends majority of her class time ranting about how to navigate her canvas modules. YOU WILL NOT LEARN. Her practice exams are significantly easier than her actual exams (which are impossible to pass unless you fry each one of your individual braincells). DO NOT TAKE HER.

This class was so hard. High quantities of long assignments. Confusing lectures, and horrible tests that have errors and content we didn't learn. The tests are short, so you can only miss 1-2 questions to score well. There are "test corrections" but they are for a daily grade, so it takes about 2 hours for no added points to your test. Do not take.

This is one of the WORST professors I have ever had, not only is she obscenely unorganized but gives unbelievably unhelpful assignments, cannot physically teach to save her life and gives obscenely hard tests that get average class scores of 50%. Her canvas is unorganized her slide sets are messy, and her hand writing is god-awful. Save yourself.

DO NOT TAKE VASO. This is by far the hardest class I have ever taken in my entire life. She can not teach for the life of her and is even worse at explaining. I went to one of her office hours, needing help to understand a homework question, and I walked out more confused. It's honestly more useful to skip class and self learn.

Worst professor I've ever had. The only professor I think could be worse is one that never shows up. She cannot teach and does not know how to use class time effectively. For the final, I had to learn 40% of the material on my own because she was so far behind for no reason. Do not take her unless you already have a strong chemistry background.

One of the most disorganized instructors I have ever had. She is very smart, but is terrible at communicating to students. Going to lectures, taking notes, doing the homework, much of the class still fails her exams. She is very confusing and while intelligent, a terrible instructor. If you can, take ANY other professor for this class.

She seems like she cares, but the class is structured very poorly. Be ready to teach yourself all of the material and don't even bother going to class, it will only confuse you more. Her notes/slides are illegible and disorganized, so most of the time it is incredibly hard to follow her work. By all means, please avoid this class.

I have very mixed feelings. She is genuinely very kind and flexible. She will always give you an extension if you ask and really makes an effort to make herself available and give students extra support. Her teaching though is awful she overcomplicates everything and doesn't organize the material in a straight forward way. Very tough grader too.

Such a bad professor do not even bother going to class it will confuse you more. Get ready to spend hours teaching yourself all the content out of class and doing all the practice she gives and still not knowing what to do on the exams. Only a few multiple choice problems so a few wrong means you will fail the test.
Very difficult to understand, disorganized, tests are very few questions so difficult to receive an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. This woman can't teach. I try so hard every day to pay attention but it's honestly impossible. Her tests are difficult, and often don't have anything to do with what she teaches in class. Avoid if possible.

Teaching and lectures were incredibly disorganized, and she spent an entire week describing one stoichometry problem. Be prepared to teach yourself outside of class. Practice exams and study guides do not at all match what is on the actual exam, and she's incredibly unhelpful if you ask her a question. Don't even bother showing up to class.
Don't go to her lectures! Waste of time. Be prepared to teach yourself everything and still be surprised on tests

DO NOT TAKE THIS WOMAN IF YOU CAN AVOID IT. She's so rude to her students, doesn't answer questions and blames us for things that SHE DOES. Listening to her lectures makes me even more confused about chemistry so it's basically worthless. oh and her tests have nothing to do with the material she gives/ you learn in class.

Vaso is very nice, cares about her students, and wants you to get a good grade. That being said, she's not the best teacher and has very disorganized, hard to read work. She does provide a lot of resources to study from, but I would not want to have her for a more difficult topic.

I love Vaso as a person (so sweet), but as a professor, she can be quite disorganized, change/add a lot of assignments. For many of the test questions, she'd put the answer in wrong so the students would have to correct her to change the grade. Can be passive aggressive sometimes. Overall though, she makes tests only 60% of your final grade.

Very caring prof who wants her students to do well. Makes herself very available outside of class. However, she is definitely disorganized and overcomplicated some topics + unevenly distributed time on topics. Her green book for recitation is very helpful and the exams are similar to those practice questions.

Took Gen Chem 2. I didn't go to class or study very much, I felt like it didn't help going to lecture. Professor is so nice and caring but can't understand a thing she says and can't read her writing, she seems super disorganized. Make sure to make friends in class to work on things together. She has a lot of things to boost your grade to get an A.

Vaso definitely cares about her students and wants them to do well. However, she is terrible at teaching, very disorganized, and has a very heavy accent and bad handwriting. If put in the effort and study a lot on your own, you should be able to get an A. However, if you're not a self studier, would suggest a different professor.

Although well-intentioned, Lykourinou has a Greek accent that makes her already poorly structured lectures difficult to follow, which is compounded by her tendency to complicate otherwise simple concepts. Numerous opportunities are available throughout the semester for extra credit though, so be sure to take advantage of that.

- her handwriting is not the best, but it is not as bad as everyone makes it seem

- she goes the extra mile to literally hand you good grades, the rest is up to you

- her tests have been shaky sometimes, however, if you listen to her during class then you should do well (attendance is mandatory)

- takes her for Gen Chem no matter what
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really cares about her students! Wants for everyone to succeed. (course completed in 2020)
Genuinely wants to see her students succeed. If you put in the work you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think that she has changed her teaching style drastically since the previous ratings. Her lectures were organized and she truly cares about her students learning the material. There was a lot of extra credit and office hours on weekends if you needed more help. Easy A if you go to lectures and recitation.

Prof. Lykourinou is a solid choice for a professor. Her lectures may be boring, but attending lecture, doing homework, and going to office hours will get you the grade you want. In addition, she is a truly kind person who really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof really knows what she is talking about and genuinely cares that you succeed. There are lots of extra credit and tiny grade boosters. The class is pretty easy to do well in but there is an opportunity to get a good grade in the class and not learn the material too well. If that doesnt bother you, highly recommend.

Vaso's lectures are super hard to follow because her handwriting is terrible and you don't know what's going on. But, outside of class, she's so nice and she helps so much in office hours and review sessions. She also gives extra credit and is super flexible if you turn in anything late.

Prof. Lykourinou obviously knows what she's talking about, but her lectures are somewhat disorganized and roundabout. Her handwriting is also kind of hard to read, especially when online. I was able to learn the material better from friends and reading the textbook than going to class. However, doing well on the homework boosts your grade a lot.

A lot of content is packed into such a small course. I took IB Chem SL (2 years of chem) and I still had moments where I was stuck and needed help. Lectures were hard to follow at points, but they're good at clarifying in office hours. A lot of content is covered in lectures, so missing isn't an option. Overall pretty average professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Vaso's lectures can be a bit confusing and disorganized at times. Other than that, she really cares about her students and wants them to do well. There's extra credit, and she drops a lot of grades at the end of the semester. Just make sure you do tons of practice q's before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: definitely willing to help students and listen to their concerns!! she lowered the points from exams and added points from simple assignments such as reflections and watching random videos related to the chapter being discussed. super nice!!

She cares a lot, but knowing your final grade is difficult because she does not put in Pollev, smart work, recitation, or any extra credit until the end of class. Odds are your grade at least a half letter grader higher. You literally shouldnt fail this class if you put in a good amount of effort.

Vaso's lectures can get very confusing at times. If you are having trouble understanding, I suggest referring to the textbook or going to peer tutoring. I found that doing as many practice problems as possible was also helpful. There is TONS of extra credit, so do take advantage of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Everyone is being rather harsh about her teaching during COVID. I believe that although it is true that her online lectures are a struggle as she isn't technologically sound, she offers the class time to work together and truly cares about the class. Always willing to move homework, and is relatively light with homework

Vaso is not that great. Her lectures are difficult to understand and follow, they are disorganized and technologically inaccessible. She's unclear with test expectations. She doesn't teach, she just talks to (now with covid) an empty room of students. She is nice and responds quickly to emails but not worth it.

Vaso was the worst at explaining things. It's even worse when this is a class you need to just get over with. It is extremely difficult to follow along, she moves at lightning speed, and makes zero sense. She seems like a perfectly great and caring person, but her class was awful. I did not listen for like a month.

She is very caring about students, but her lecture won't help you a lot. She uses her laptop with a touch screen and writes a memo with her pen. But her handwriting is too "artistic" and barely can read. If you want to get high points on exams, I highly recommend watching youtube videos and read a textbook rather than listening to her lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Vaso definitely cares about her students learning and is always willing to answer questions and go over content. She is also big on extra credit and very fair in providing additional opportunities for success. Her lectures are a little all over the place and hard to pay attention to (she writes all over the boards in a confusing manner).

Learned to that I hate chemistry during this class! I had her for Gen Chem 1 and 2. She's a fine professor, but I think she would be better suited to a smaller class. She had a hard time controlling the 100+ person lecture, and she wasn't always great at explaining things. It was good to come to class already having read through the lecture.
The most caring and knowledgeable Professor ever!
Vaso was an alright teacher. Her lectures were boring and hard to pay attention to, but you do learn a lot, and if you enjoy chemistry, you will enjoy this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Anyone who did not receive an A in this class did not communicate with Vaso. By going to her office hours, I was able to review and better understand things. She bumped my grade in the end after my consistent effort and attempts to better understand the material. I learned a lot but only because I made the effort. It is not that hard if you care.

While some people had a hard time understanding Vaso, she was always available for extra help and always took time to answer people's questions in class. Online homework is due every week and are pretty easy. You can get by with not going to class and just reading the textbook but, Vaso often gives examples of problems in her slides.

Vaso really cares about her students. Although her lectures weren't necessarily the best, you can tell she tries her absolute hardest and she goes above and beyond getting feedback from students and how she can improve. I don't think I paid attention past the first week of lecture and I still managed to get a B+. Her tests are easy. Tutoring helps

You will never encounter another professor who genuinely cares about her students as much as she does. If you don't understand her lectures, be sure to read the textbook and go to tutoring! Go into office hours if you're still struggling; she's super understanding and will go out of her way to help you out.
