If you want to get a good grade but learn nothing take his class. Online organization is horrendous and he is a horrible lecturer. Nice guy though.
The tests are SO hard and extensive to the point where you may not finish even with studying for days.

Really nice guy, but the majority of actual learning comes from the textbooks. Group projects were interesting but I found the combo of too little guidance + grading projects on a strict rubric to be frustrating. Course materials are disorganized, deadlines updated on the fly (keep your Canvas notifications enabled or else you'll miss something).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is a very nice, funny, and lenient professor who is passionate about what he teaches. He covers a wide array of subjects, responds to emails, and gets us working together to create pitches.

Professor Muscolino gives out a year-long project at the beginning of the school year, so choose your groupmates wisely. You must buy the textbook to do Connect assignments. One midterm (20%) and final exam (20%) were both taken upon the professor's decision and the class's preference.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Muscolino is one of the sweetest and most caring professors I've had. Some of his assignments can be unclear if you miss class but he's very willing to help and is extremely accessible. You can tell that he genuinely is passionate about the subject - highly recommend him if you want a prof that gives you industry insights.
Extreme lack of structure, does very little to no explaining. The bulk of his lectures is him going on Bloomberg and talking. Also an unreasonable amount of work for this class. Didn't learn anything
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Firstly, Professor Muscolino does not deserve anything less than a 3. Only downside is that he is disorganized and can be hard to follow sometimes. However, he is not a hard grader, students will always be doing very manageable group work. Exams are online open note and questions are straight forward. Extra credit also offered frequently.

Vincent Muscolino is a very nice man but stays clear if you are not planning to teach yourself all the content outside the normal class time. I hate to say it, but one of the least teaching professors at Northeastern.

Teaches nothing in class other than Bloomberg terminal and he expects students to be prepared for exams. You will not learn anything throughout this class and I highly recommend any other option. Thinks he's the funny guy alive and has no idea how to teach.

TERRIBLE experience. Professor Muscolino was wildly disorganized and painfully dull. Absolutely 0 clarity in what was expected of us for projects and assignments, and asking him questions generated vague answers and even more confusion. I am not sure what the quality of other professors is in this department, but definitely avoid this one.

He is trying to be funny, but he's not. He likes to talk about Bloomberg and other stuff in class. Be prepared to learn all the formulas and concepts by yourself, cuz he ain't teaching in class. The homework is crazy, we never learned anything related to what's on the homework.

He is a caring man who wants his students to succeed. The class material was easy and graded easily, despite sometimes him taking off points without explaining why. Make sure you get a good group because the entire class is based on group work. He was also confusing about what is due, especially readings. Still a nice guy and VERY accessible.

Muscolino is a good guy and tries to be funny, but he is really unorganized and struggles to communicate. His rubrics are napkin scratch that has never been revised. The midterm, final, and projects (emphasis on the plural) were all so brutal. Don't take him for corporate finance if you have any other options.
ONE OF THE GREATEST FINANCE PROFESSORS EVER. Very lucky to have him here at Northeastern University!

I give him credit that he had passion and was always reachable outside of class, but he did not convey the material in an effective manner. Many of the concepts were not explained thoroughly enough to understand for the tests.

Vinnie is a great guy, he wants to be accessible and fun but my god this man is the most disorganized mess. What we should read? Doesnt explain it. Module slides are unhelpful and confusing. He doesnt lecture or teach, half the semester is spend on a stock project. This is the first class I have come out of asking did I even learn anything? Awful
Was viewing rate my professor grades for past professors and glad to see that Muscolino still doing what he does best. Never left a review for my course, but dude is a gem.

He was a great professor. I actually felt like we touched on abstract questions related to investments in class as oppose to the normal NU finance requirement classes where we just read the textbook (via PPTs) in class and work on end of chapter problems (what boring people love doing).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I like his style of teaching, but he is not for everyone. He is focused on application (building financial models) and real world scenarios instead of textbook material, making connect homework v difficult. So depends what you want to get out of the class. He is also very accessible outside of class and is all around just a very nice professor.

Avoid him if possible, I know he probably has some good feedbacks from other classes. But for FINA 3301, he doesnt teach anything, spends every class on bloomberg and other stuff, assigns tons of connect work that he never taught. If u want to truly learn something out of it, take someone elses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He was a really nice guy, but was a confusing teacher. The class consists of a final presentation and paper that ends up being 40% of your final grade. However, his grading and overall feedback is very unclear. Although he is really knowledgeable, his advice was often unhelpful and he expected you to know far more than you would as a first-year.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Financial Management with him and my overall experience was positive. He incorporates lots of practical assignments into his syllabus that would help you outside of class, such as Bloomberg Certification, valuation analysis and stock and budget simulations. With that said, his curriculum can deviate from your textbook materials
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't know why people had problems with Muscolino. Easy class. Especially if you know investments or are actually interested in the subject matter. He cares a lot about participation which some people hate. If you are not someone who likes to talk in class this might be a turnoff. For me personally, participation classes are free points.

The man. One of my friends told me to take him because he was "an industry" guy and not an academic. I'm glad I did. Gives great advice on co-ops and career paths. Class material was content that I could recycle for interviews.

He's an incredible guy--he's funny and is always willing to help. However, his teaching style is very practical and a lot of people leave his class at the end of the semester without having learned anything. It very negatively impacts you if you're a finance major and take more advanced finance classes in the future.

Very good prof if you have a basic understanding of investments already. Incredibly passionate, most of class is spent talking about recent news and he gets very excited. Awesome lecturer. Tests are tough, most material comes from the book which seems like an optional read but definitely isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Nice guy, interesting final and group project. But - disorganized, ridiculous number of Connect problems plus larger assignments. All knowledge for the Midterm, assignments, and Connect problems will come from the extensive reading because he never actually teaches anything. Frustrating lack of structure, no idea what your grade is at any point.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I received Muscolino forFINA2201 after my other prof left mid way through. I personally really enjoyed Muscolino. He was funny, engaging and very practical; which is great if you're interested in finance. However, classes lacked structure and what was on the tests was not always clear. So it really depends if you need a structured/clear prof or not
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His classes do lack structure but if you are going into investments or pursuing a career in PM or other intensive areas of finance, his dynamic approach is ideal. You leave his class with an idea of how to stay on top of the constantly evolving world of finance whereas you leave other classes with definitions and outdated theories you can google.

Establish a good relationship with him and make him know that you are serious about making a good business plan and you will be fine. He is pretty disorganized and I did not learn much from the curriculum in his class, but he is very knowledgeable about business. Most of the lessons learned were from working with and motivating my team.
don't take him if you know nothing about investments, extremely hard to keep up if you are unfamiliar with the industry

I really have no idea who are all those people who gave him these good reviews, because his class is a total joke. He might be a funny guy and he is from the industry, but he does NOT teach you anything. Like really. All the knowledge is coming from your reading (which is very extensive). He just spends time flipping through the slides and talking
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If I had to describe him, he's kind of a caricature of himself. Always has a smile and great with career advice. Shares his thoughts about the markets in class. Has a good grasp on lots of different issues. A good person to bounce ideas off of.
The greatest. Works in the investment industry and it shows (the course project is on valuing a stock). Dude is also funny if you get to know him (ends class with a joke of the day).
Awesome guy. Really enjoyed the course and learned a lot. Would definitely take a class of his again.

He's a great guy, but sometimes I felt lost in his class. He asks us to participate (20% of the grade) but the level he expects is high. Choose wisely you mates for the group project (20% too). A lot of work, 4 take home assignments, connect problems are taking forever and they are only worth 5%, midterm and final in class, but grading is very fair

Look, he's a great guy and really cares about engaging students with the subject matter. But, there's so much emphasis on "current events" and the group project that it's very easy to fall behind and try to catch up for the rest of the semester. Promotes participation but speaks  about Investments and Markets at a high level - difficult to understa
Work hard and you will love it.  Always willing to help outside of class and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: great class, always looked forward to it

Professor Muscolino has been the most insightful and explorative teacher I have ever had and has been a great mentor. He is not afraid to deviate from the prescribed course material to talk about relevant current events in order to help students advance their careers. Interactive, upbeat, and ends with a joke of day!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: - Great professor! - If you want to learn about the investments on a practical and applicable level, TAKE THIS CLASS - By no means an impossible grader or class, go to every class, do your work, study, and go to his office hours and receive an A-A.
Excellent prof that gives easy to understand examples.  Saw an old interview online of him on cnbc.  Knows his stuff.
Definitely the best prof i have taken at neu.  He is from the investment industry so he gives interesting realworld examples.  Also takes a lot of time with students. I highly recommend his class.

Prof. Muscolino is by far the best prof I have had at NEU.  He gives real world examples since he is from the investment industry.  I have learned a lot.  Also a nice guy willing to explain things and take time with you.  Definitely recommend him.
One of the best professors I had at NEU. I think people who dont like him dont understand how to compbine theory with the real world

He really doesn't teach all that well. He is a nice guy and tries to be friends with his students. He thinks he knows everything and that he teaches us everything, but he doesn't. A lot of self-studying. Welcome to college
Nice but boring

He's a real nice person for sure, but he often appears very distant and unclear. He's the type of professor that you need to see during his office hours for him to be effective. His grading is very fair and likes to joke around a lot.

Prof muscolino was just grand. His class was my favorite ever I learned a lot. His availability was the the advantage of us because he was always available. If you don't like prof muscolino then you don't like finance! Favorite teacher ever

excellent class. professor muscolino will spend lots of time answering your questions and really helps you learn financial modeling. this class is super interesting and follows the stock market closely. a great teacher who really cares that we succeed. this class is worth signing up for.

It was a challenging class, but kept my interest with real world experience of my professor. I learned so much about finance and investments.  It gave me a insight how Finance is so crtical in todays economic environment.

Classes were so boring. Very hard to stay concentrated on the course. Makes Investment finance uninteresting. Very superficial class. I havent learned a lot even though the teacher is really nice. I won't recommend him if you want to enjoy the class and are really interested in stocks, options , futures, etc.

This was a great class.  Professor Muscolino is the best Finance professor I have ever had at Northeastern.  His practical applications of financial theory really helped me learn.  I also appreciated the extra time he took outside of class room to give me insight in direction with my projects and assignments!
Very helpful.  Uses real world examples.  Take this class!

Prof Muscolino was great at relating real world examples.  What really helped me is the time he took to help me succeed in this class.  He made himself available where as other Professors handed me off to their aides!
Professor Muscolino is a great teacher.  He uses real world examples of how to apply finance and valuation methodologies.  I finally understand regression as well.

This class is so boring. No tests, just straight projects. 3 of the same projects per semester... these projects take FOREVER. First project was due after spring break. Waste of a class really... didn't learn anything we didn't learn in corporate finance.

Mya was great! I took her for online style and editing (ENGL2710), the class is low-pressure (yet packed with learning and opportunities for improvement) and she does a great job of getting back to us with feedback and developing us as writers. You can tell she cares a lot, recommend her a lot!

Professor Poe was an absolute delight. She was super understanding about the difficulties of online learning, but her class still felt like a class, even over Zoom. She seriously inspired me to think about pursuing writing studies at the graduate level. Great teacher and super caring, highly recommend!

If you want to learn how to teach well or experience how a teacher can be life-changing, take her class! A kind person who checks in with her students, doesn't overwhelm the class with her lectures, and lets students participate. Her assignments are reasonable and will help you in the long term. She wants YOU to succeed.

I've never had a more disorganized and confusing professor that had such high exceptions for students. The grading system is awful (he makes you pick the grade you will get and if you dont meet the expectations, your grade drops. EX: A -> C if expectations not met) and he makes it hard to do well due to the absence of support. Don't take. Please.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Garvey has a lot of knowledge in his field. However, with a class like MKTG 2602 where there are many different skill levels, he was not able to simplify his teachings to a beginner's level. He was unclear when grading and resulted in failing to fulfill his relative grading and giving all students a B+.

He was not able to actually assign or teach anything and used relative grading (a 90-98% could be a B- given the right conditions). He did not plan out the course at all and even had to give students an option to take a B+ and just stop doing work if they wanted to because every student had too high a grade to do relative grading correctly.
Best teacher I've had at northeastern so far. Such a funny guy and has a lot of interesting stories. Garvey cares about his students and what he teaches. 10/10 would take one of his classes again.

Late to classes, late to finish the classes, late or doesn't respond to emails at all, unclear grading criteria, not using time efficiently; you have to make up with extra videos he posts (which is also late). Had an unbelievable time in this course. Not recommended but only professor out there for DS2001 Business.

I thought of dropping this course many times in the first few weeks. The homework was very hard and the software we used was a pain. HOWEVER, give the man the credit because he gave a reasonably long time length to submit your assignments. The exams were not hard. He loved it when you engage which really helped your grades and the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures were very clear and overall useful, but if you aren't actually interested in topics you'll be bored. Homework was pain mainly because the textbooks not on chegg. Tests were really fair though and if you studied they're no problem. Graders gave partial credit which was a huge for engineering. Overall really nice guy.

Do not take this class with Andrew. He is incredibly dull in his lectures, uses his colleague's mediocre, typo-ridden textbook (which in itself is very unprofessional), and fails to effectively communicate key course ideas. On top of this he assigns extremely long and difficult homework. I would not recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: First and foremost, i regret taking this course with Andrew. His lectures are extremely dull and lengthy. Writes so  much on the board, most of which is theories and derivations that you will never return to when studying for test/exam. His homeworks are the worst, by far. The software he expects us to use is Mastan2. This software is horrendous.

Homework takes forever and is very hard and kind of useless. Lectures are too conceptual and he hardly gives any example questions. He writes a lot of notes but does not take the time to explain for students to fully understand. Erases what he writes on the board too quickly. Worst design class to take.
one of the best teachers ive had at school. His class was always interesting and his lectures were very well done. Hard homework but thats to be expected for steel design.

Professor Myers has literally changed my entire world view of engineering.  OMG!!!1!  I can't even look at a bridge anymore without thinking about him.  HE IS SO CUTE.  He likes the Red Sox.  I like the Red Sox.  He likes math. I like math.  I feel like he's sorta perfect.  Take his class.  Just don't take it with your boyfriend.
Professor Myers makes me love Structural Analysis.

He expects a lot, but he gives you all the tools you need to do well in the course. More specifically, he goes over all the types of problems that will be on quizzes and exams. Professor Trusbkyy is a fair grader, and if you go to office hours he will work with you.

I ABSOLUTELY LOVED HIM!! hands down my favorite professor ever. he's right, the class and subject of economics isn't designed for those who don't have an intuitive understanding of the material, and he implies that. But if you are have any natural ability at all he will REALLY educate u, is VERY fair, and so so funny.

Its a pretty reasonable class, As long as you keep up with the book and home work you are fine. He gives pop quizes that you can't make up but HW+quiz count for 10% of your grade so it doesn't matter. I never talked to him before and needed a letter of recommendation and he delivered 200%, Hes got your back if you need it. Really good guy.

Trubskyy implies that you are stupid if you don't understand the material. Can be helpful if you go to his office hours, but is hard to understand in class, mostly because he thinks you should automatically understand it. His analogies are hilarious and will never fail to entertain. "This class is like a bad marriage. None of us want to be here"

Have to go to every single class cause he gives pop quizzes. If you miss one you can't make it up. I learned most from the book and homework mostly because the class consisted of lectures that moved too quickly. If you get lost it is very hard to get back on track. Do not take his class if you are not a economics person because he expects you to be

Worst teacher I have had at Northeastern. He can not explain anything well and is constantly proved wrong by students in the class. Takes him forever to get quizzes and tests back. Assigns a vast amount of (graded) homework online due at the end of each week. AVOID him at all costs.

'Misha' is a difficult teacher. He warns the class that students are going to fail and drop out before the end of the semester. However, he is very willing to help students if they put in the effort. He gets frustrated when students sleep. Pay attention and ask questions if you don't get it and he will explain. He jokes around and is adorable.

this class was a living hell. he graduated as a "cinematography" major and all of the readings are about ancient films and producers from the 1700s. NONE make sense and you have to do 3 papers a week. he is willing to give extra help but I felt clueless the entire time. seriously, avoid this professor at all costs.

Although Chris assigns difficult readings, their purpose is to arouse a reaction. Very conversational and straightforward, he encourages the transition from a high school student to rise to the collegiate level through abstract reasoning. Chris brings charisma to the classroom and is well versed. Great guy overall.

This professor is extremely confusing and you have to write at least 3 essays a week. He is obsessed with Film and Cinema and the readings he assigns make absolutely no sense and are at a College Writing level. They are graduate school readings and are impossibly hard. DO NOT TAKE HIM

This class had a lot of group work. You have a material experiment project and the teacher that grades that is different and he is a very tough grader you have to follow the rubric exactly if not he will take of a lot of points. Make sure group members held accountable for work. Exams are fine as long as you do HW.

Dr. Nancy is great. She is super kind and approachable and wants you to succeed. The exams aren't cumulative which was super nice and she provided exam prep material and will review anything you want. Hw and lectures were super straightforward and she loves to tell stories and was very efficient with her lectures
She's a nice person, but I just don't get what she's teaching

Dr. Nancy is great! She is kind and understanding, for ex the whole class struggled with a hw problem, so she didn't include that stuff on the test. The tests are not cumulative, so there are 3 midterms - no final. The class is totally manageable and super interesting because she is clearly passionate about what she is teaching!

Dr. Nancy is really great at explaining concepts. She is super down to earth and easy to talk to. Go to class and take the practice exams and you will do fine in the class portion. The project portion is an added burden over the semester but is a great grade boost. I found the homework to be the hardest part of the class.
he is good
Overall good

It is hard to understand him in class and I didn't learn anything from classes. I just spend 3 full days to get ready for midterms and I did great. Participation is 5% extra on top of final grade. Midterms were easy, final gets droped. Take it if you want an easy A/A-. He was never late, loves his class, though.

Avoid this professor if you can. Worst instructor I've had. Mandatory attendance for lectures that add little to your understanding. Everything is explained better and faster online. This is the only class where showing up felt like wasted time. Choose another section if possible.

Class was moved online last-minute at least 8 times over the course of the semester, and prof showed up 20+ minutes late to many many others... on top of that, making the students' attendance mandatory halfway through the semester was very ironic. Was an easy A tho (didn't learn anything).

Do not take this professor, if you need this class take the other professor. He has no respect for your time as a student, every day he is late by 10 mins. He just rips the lecture slides off the other professor and while teaching them it's like the first time he's ever seen them. You can get more information by just skimming the textbooks.
Good Lecture

professor is not great. super boring lectures with mandatory attendance. often makes mistakes writing homework and test questions. on midterm, received an impossible question that took time away from other questions. can see he tries to teach, but fails. he doesn't convey points well, makes things more confusing than just reviewing the slides.

Horrible organization, does not answer emails, reads directly from the slides, does not explain concepts clearly. Lectures are not helpful so you have to teach yourself. Don't torture yourself by taking this professor. Only upside is the homeworks are not that bad and lab reports were graded somewhat leniently which I guess depends on your TAs.

Classes were pretty bad, the professor teaches but its the same as reading the slides and watching videos during your own time. There was attendance at the end of every class so you couldn't skip. Homework and test question difficulties were okay but graded leniently.

Incredibly boring lectures that take an hour to cover what you can learn yourself by spending 10 minutes reading the class notes provided by a different teacher. For the actual rigor, the course itself is really easy, but the labs lowkey take a lot longer b/c the TAs aren't all that helpful and the lab report is tedious to write.

Naveen is Northeastern's dark knight. He gives only 4 homeworks which is lesser than what Kimani gives. If you do good on both midterms, you don't need to give the final as the score is dropped. He gives a practice exam which is same as the actual exam. He is not a good teacher but makes the course low effort.
Do not take this professor. He does not answer questions very well. He does not respond to piazza. Every class goes for five minutes longer. There is no organisation.

This is the most poorly organized class I've taken at Northeastern. Professor does not respond to emails and piazza questions, cannot manage time in class, explains concepts poorly and very slowly, and does not release important study resources for exams.

DO NOT take this class with this professor.
Rarely responds to emails or questions on Piazza. Content is exciting but lectures tend to be boring and he is not great at answering questions or explaining concepts in class.

Constantly late to class, would end class over 5 minutes late regularly. He moved so slowly on material(despite the fact no one was asking questions) that we ended up weeks behind the other professor, and he'd hold online classes at 7pm to make up for it. He also held online classes to "make up for" the holidays. Test guidelines constantly changed.

These were some of the worst lectures I have ever sit through. Prof. Sapavath belabors simple arithmetic and glazes over the interesting content of the course. A 20 minute YouTube video teaches me more than his 70 minute lectures. He also frequently arrives to class 10+ minutes late and will make mistakes on simple math.

Not the best professor I've had so far. Her lectures are BAD; she just copies and pastes her notes onto the board with no explanation. She uploads the notes, but doesn't label them. She doesn't care about her students; even if you're in the hospital, she won't let you make up a test. Avoid this professor at all costs.
dont do it
Difficult, but doable and very informative. Go to office hours, she is generous with revisions on tests and quizzes.

Her lectures are not helpful because she has a thick accent and moves very fast. She tells us what to study for tests and quizzes, but I still did not do well on them. She lets you do test corrections to boost your grade. She gives us finals and answer keys from previous semesters, and the final is the same with changed numbers.

Don't get me wrong, Natalia is a very sweet professor. However, her class sucks and she's not very good at teaching. She makes a lot of mistakes and skips a lot of steps and information. Office hours are slightly better and she's very flexible a lot of the time if you're sick. Final and midterms are hard. Take at your own risk.

Very difficult, but good teacher. Lecture style is hard to follow for some, but not extremely difficult once you focus. You need to go to office hours, she is strict on grading but generous with revisions.
Please do not take her.

I was in the trenches the entire semester. Her accent isn't even the problem, it's the way her lectures are structured that was so chaotic and confusing. One of the worst professor's I've had at Northeastern. If she is your only option then drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Go to class, and go to office hours

Professor Ptitsyna is a very nice and caring person. However, her teaching style for Diff. Eq. was overall too difficult, very theoretically heavy and not enough application of formulas. I had prior experience with Diff Eq. and Linear Algebra and was still struggling through the class. I wish everyone the best of luck!!

She has a very thick accent which makes it hard to understand. However, this class is easy, everyone who has a bad grade in this class doesn't try. SHE GIVES U PRACTICE EXAMS that are the same as her tests. Her multiple-choice tests are hard but she has no homework. I didn't take any notes and got a good grade, it ain't hard

Her lecture style is very difficult to learn from; she goes at an extremely fast pace, and spends the entire class time going over theoretical things, only ever briefly touching on the actual formulas and their applications that will be seen on the quizzes and exams. Be prepared to teach yourself if you take this class with her.

This was my second time taking Calc 2 so I might be a bit biased but she wasn't the worst teacher I have ever had. She does truly care but it just a bit unorganized and rushes sometimes. She has an accent but you get used to it. If you can, switch professors.

Her lectures consist of copying and pasting the notes she posted online onto the white board. She is so slow at them that we did not finish all of the content by the end. The quizzes and tests were all made by her and were harder than other sections (with the exception of the final). Expect to study most of it on your own and still not understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took AP Calculus in High school so I came into this class with background knowledge, and I also know how easy Calc 1 can be. However, she made a subject that was easy to me 10x harder because she does not know how to teach, she reads off of her papers and only gives theory, and her tests and quizzes are much different than her classowork.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor P is so sweet and is extremely nice and caring, however, she is not a very good lecturer. The topics are often more confusing they need to be and difficult to understand. The weekly quizzes are not great and you have to learn a lot on your own. She is very helpful in her office hours though and gives a substantial midterm curve.

Professor P is a very nice and caring lady. She seems so genuine and really does seem so sweet. Unfortunately, she can not teach. She is extremely misleading on the test subjects and does not provide adequate practice and leaves the test very unclear. Its really confusing why someone would not explain how to properly study. Sweet Lady, Bad Prof.

Many of the other reviews you'll see here are spot on. Such a sweet lady but just a terrible educator. Hard to understand, lectures way too fast, inefficient communication, and way overcomplicates otherwise simple concepts. If you take her class you'll have a pleasant experience, just be prepared to do everything yourself.

As someone who isn't the best at math, she definitely did not make it any easier. Her lectures are fast paced and confusing, and doesn't give good answers to questions. Give quizzes/tests every week. Test content isn't always what's reflected on the practice. If you aren't a math/engineering/physics person, avoid her.

Weird class as the test were very difficult with retakes but the final is rather simple. I would not recommend if math isn't your thing as she is very theoretical. Quizzes are rather straightforward however practice test were much harder than test. Has an accent too so is hard to understand but is funny at times. Recommend going to lecture too.

Professor P is very sweet. She is passionate about the subject. Lectures give a lot of info and can get confusing at times, but office hours are very helpful. The class does have a quiz every week but half are take home. Her midterms also have test corrections or retakes. All the practices posted are almost identical to the tests quizzes.

Professor Ptitsyna is really sweet, but not the best teacher. She gives way too many notes during lecture, to the point where it just is the textbook regurgitated. I really struggled in her class and found that self-studying was more successful for me, but that doesn't help for the final; beware of her class.

She's nice and passionate about what she teaches but isn't good at teaching. Lectures aren't easy to follow as she explains the concepts in a difficult way. Office hours are helpful. Test prep barely prepared us for the tests. Class did so poorly that she did retakes/corrections. Only reason I passed was because I had to teach myself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless you're only taking this class as a refresher, switch. She has an accent that makes lectures hard to understand, notes you take will not be clear. She makes the easiest concepts difficult. Some of her tests are similar to the practice, but not always. If you don't have the discipline to constantly teach yourself, just don't take her.
lectures are hard to follow, incredibly strict grading, unapproachable. I completely relied on YouTube lectures provided in the syllabus.

Poor lecturer, spends 90% of class deriving formulas then proceeds to do half a practice problem. Online material is hard to read, basically have to self study. Gave us lots of points back on test corrections to make up for bad test scores.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The fact that everyone in the class had taken calc 1 before, yet everyone still struggled says a lot about her teaching. She is such a sweet person but is a harsh grader and doesn't adequality prepare you for tests. She does a lot of proofs which don't help your understanding and won't get to the point until the period is about to end.
Lectures do not help at all, she just talks and reads off of papers in her hand. Gives practice quizzes for tests and quizzes. Overall not a good professor but class is not hard

Professor Ptitsyna is so funny and nice. Sometimes she is hard to follow, but if you pay attention, you can definitely succeed. You are only graded on tests though, so do not take if you are bad at tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Natalia is a very caring professor. Although her lectures can be very theory heavy; a math class mostly comes down to practicing problems. She is very approachable in office hours.

Professor Ptitsyna is a lovely lady; however, she is a horrible lecturer. I have not understood anything in any of the 100-minute lectures I have attended and I have learned all the material from online resources. This being said her quizzes and tests are graded generously and aren't always as difficult as expected if you can teach yourself calc...

Dr. Ptitsyna is a great person, but a mediocre teacher. Although she is helpful after class and gives good explanations, she doesn't ask students questions. Furthermore, she rushes through lectures and doesn't get through them on time. If you go after class for explanations, she does a fine job explaining concepts. Good teacher, also a tough class.
An awesome professor who always focuses on the teaching content. Showing up at her office hour is also very helpful.

She wasn't that great with technology since it was hard to see what she wrote on the board through zoom and her lecture notes are way long and dull. Also it's hard to hear well especially with her accent which I don't blame. But the best pro is her exams aren't difficult as long as you know the basics from her lecture in which she goes overtime.

Nice and caring professor. Her teaching speed is slow with every detail explained. No attendance is required but I still recommend people who never learned calculus in high school to attend every course. Not difficult compared to other math courses. No homework and only quizzes and tests are counted in grade, which are fairly easy to get full marks
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took calc 1 with her last semester. She went a bit too fast and I often just went over her notes online instead of listening in lectures. Tests were a lot of the grade, but most of our quizzes were take home so not as bad as they could be. Seems like a very sweet prof tho, just not for me personally.
Had her for calc 1. Lectures are fast and kinda hard to understand, I ended up doing better learning on my own. Quizzes and exams are okay, sorta predictable. Homework not mandatory, but helpful.
Avoid at all costs. You will not learn anything from her and learn everything from the textbook/internet.

Although she is enthusiastic about the material, she does a terrible job of explaining things. The homeworks were terribly unorganized and it was unclear what we should do. Her lectures a dull and staying awake was very challenging. If you have never taken Calc before, she is not the professor for you. She struggles to solve the problems she gives.

Although her homework is optional it is best to get some practice down. As well as taking notes during the lectures. Although her grading is sometimes late, she will do her best to explain when asked to do so. Pretty lecture heavy so it is best to do it in the afternoon rather in than in the morning where you might be quite tired.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor is very biased when it comes to grading, she has her favourites. Does not provide any resources or materials on canvas to prep for the exam.

Professor Dave is very passionate about the topics she teaches in class and explains them well. There are three exams, which are based on the HW assignments and notes, and cheats sheets are allowed for all exams. Make sure to show up to the lectures because that is the only way you can get the notes. She also does not miss with her diet coke!

Lectures were very confusing. Not content wise, but just the way she explained it. Theres no online materials so you have to either be at all lectures or ask classmates for notes. The good thing is that she allows cheat sheets for every test AND theres no final so I found her class especially easy to get a good grade in. She also lets us out early.

She gives you a cheat sheet, and if you copy the lectures onto the test from there, then you'll get 100%. It feels wrong but that's what she wants you to do. Besides that, there are no supplemental materials outside of class, so you gotta go or you'll be lost. Very passionate and occasionally goes on side tangents that are unrelated to the material

In my opinion Professor Dave was very informative and taught the course with enthusiasm, if you went to class and paid attention it was VERY EASY to get a good grade, it was one of the easiest courses I have taken in college.

You really shouldn't skip class because theres no where else to get notes, unless your friend takes them and shares.

An amazing good econ professor. She write it all out on the board before class starts but her writing is very small. Her homework is all based on the content she writes up and are relatively easy(though all have to be physical copy). Her exams are the same structure as her HW and she allows cheatsheets which is hard to do bad.

Professor Dave's teaching method is interesting to say the least. She comes to class everyday with only a few markers and a diet coke. If you attend the lectures, this class is very easy. The tests are based only on the lectures and all hws are group assignments. She allows a note sheet for each exam and has helpful TAs outside of class.

Professor Dave was horrible all around. Her lectures are extremely boring. Notes aren't posted online yet; she writes like chicken scratch. The time limits for tests are terrible. Grading isn't clear until after you do assignments. Her TA's are useless and don't know the material. She isn't accessible outside of class. She ruined my love for econ.

You must come to class and take good notes, if you do this you will get a good grade. Her tests come straight from her lectures and she does not try to trick students. Your grade is based on 2 things: the 3 tests and a bunch of different hws which you work on with a group you choose. One more thing about Neha- she doesn't miss her diet coke!

She is very passionate and clear on what she talks about. Barely any homework, and they were all group assignments. Tests come directly from the lectures, and she lets you use a cheat sheet. Very easy course, but you actually have to come to class if you want to do good. If you don't show up, don't get mad and blame her for your bad grade...

I personally did really well in her microeconomics class (econ1116). BUT, she is a very condescending and unprofessional teacher who doesn't give clear examples and sets grades for exams depending on her mood and whether or not she likes the student. She allows cheat sheets (only pro). She will not help you one-on-one either. DO NOT TAKE.

Rude professor, doesn't care for students success, she think she is god, unfair grading, and unfriendly. I don't think she truly understands the subject herself, but she thinks she does. The course is super easy, but if you want to learn Macroeconomics, I would recommend teaching it yourself if you take Neha Dave. Her class is also very political.
Let us use a cheat sheet for tests but graded super unfairly when I had similar answers to my peers they got better grades with basically the same answers
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really like Ms. Neha Dave as she's inspirational and lectures fairly well. Quite a few people I know are doing well in her class including me. During my 1st and 2nd exams, I got an A (with my 2nd exam getting full points). I'd advise future students to pay attention & go early to take notes. She advised us to buy the textbook but I never used it!

tests are based on homework questions--so makes it easy

x2 homework per week--she really cares about showing your work BUT it has to be the way she likes it, so that can be annoying but as long as get used to it then it is fine

homework is the heaviest weighted grade in the class

Dave was just alright. She didn't assign most Homeworks and discussions from the syllabus. So, the grade was based almost entirely on 3 non-cumulative tests (no final) and an end-of-semester discussion. The tests aren't hard, especially with the cheat sheet she allows. However, she is very nitpicky with grading and doesn't provide clear feedback
Not for me: pretends to be creative but grades on a whim and seems full of herself
Acted condescending and did not have a lot of structure to the class

1200 word essay due on the third day of the semester for an asynchronous class, always takes off points, 0 leniency for late submission no matter the circumstance, overall just a horrible experience.

Seems to think you aren't taking other classes and assigns the workload accordingly. dih

There is a ton of work for this class. You essentially have 2 weeks to write a 1200-1500 word essay with 2 peer reviews. Laurie is an amazing professor and will help you through it, but you definitely have to work for an A, moreso than other ENGW1111 sections. You will work a lot, learn a lot, and enjoy her class a lot.

Laurie was one of the best college profs I've ever had. She made the class interesting when the content might not have been. Her feedback was very good, and you were able to make points back because she grades out of 105 instead of 100. Overall one of the best I've had!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Nardone puts a lot of effort into her class. She asks students about the assignments they want to do and makes sure it is interesting for them. A lot of homework but it is manageable. Always wants to help students.

I don't care for creative writing and really should not have taken the honors section, but it was way too much work. I've probably spent most of my time on this class last semester, and I'm in a STEM program! For each of the four essays, you will have to submit 2-3 discussion posts, a free write, draft, revision plan and final draft (in 3 weeks).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is the best writting professor at Northeastern. But soooo hard. Too much and hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor. Office hours were incredibly helpful and you could tell that she cares about her students. This class transformed the way that I write for the better, and it's really not hard to do well. Definitely would recommend!!
She is a really really good professor. I do not like writting at all and she is tough. But if u want to learn then she is best. To get a easy A. Not the best, not a difficult A but u need to work

Genuinely one of the best professors i've ever had.She transformed the way I write and think about writing and genuinely feel like this is the most i've learned in a class. She was tough but fair and honest. So kind and understanding and I genuinely was sad that her class ended. 100% would take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Nardone is amazing !! I really enjoyed writing papers for this class because the topics were so flexible and interesting. She grades very fairly and it's not difficult to get an A. She's also a really interesting person and her lectures are actually enjoyable

For a mandatory class with absolutely no value whatsoever to my major, she took every assignment way too seriously. Even after checking off everything on the rubric, she'll still find ways to take points off your paper, while feedback provided is vague and unhelpful. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amazing.

I LOVED Laurie's class. I had her my whole freshman year for writing. She is hilarious and picks interesting topics to write about. This isn't your average writing class with boring essays. She works with the students to build the grading rubric and helps you with all of your papers, giving feedback. Make sure to take advantage of her peer tutors

Prof. Nardone is a great educator and provides fair feedback. She's polite and usually answers emails within twenty-four hours. I would suggest taking a different section of advanced writing if you want your individual contributions to be factored into your grade equally with group work.

Laurie isn't a teacher that lets you phone in your work. You'll have to try hard to get a good class, but the payoff is totally worth it. She lets you really bring your voice out in your work, and she truly wants to see you do well.

Laurie is an amazing teacher! I had her for Advanced Writing in the Sciences online during Summer 1. Although the class is a lot of work, especially in a condensed summer semester, you can see the value in every assignment you do and she gives great and quick feedback! Take her class if you want to want to put in work and learn something.

Do yourself a favor and stay far away from Laurie Nardone, especially if it's for AWD. Worst class I have ever taken at Northeastern. Syllabus was 15 pages long, on top of 8-10 page syllabi for each assignment - not that they actually helped at all. Instead they were confusing and unclear. PChem was easier than this.
Laurie was a tough professor. I feel that she really helped me learn in an online setting, and she guided me in becoming a better writer.

Laurie doesn't make you feel like she's the professor and you're the student. Rather, she makes you feel like you can write anything! She'll never tell you what to write, but give you all the tools to come up with your own ideas and mold them into a great essay. Very happy to have had her as a professor.

Laurie is the best! She will improve your writing skills. My writing abilities have increased 10 fold...It's quite a bit of work, but you just have to try. She really cares about increasing the student's ability to think and write critically. Fun and engaging classroom setting. The most laid back professor I've ever had.

Laurie teaches advanced writing in both the classroom and online. I took her class online and it was the most organized and helpful online class ever. Laurie is a fair grader and always willing to help you. She offers in person office hours and gives great feedback and suggestions. If you have the opportunity take her class! :)
don't take her class online unless you want to spend 50% of your life writing essays. The other 50% for sleeping because your too bored and tired to do anything else.
Class is required but took up 90% of my school work, too much and the work was too hard for the level the class was supposed to be. Hated it

one of the best professors sophomore year. take her! she expects a lot out of her students so it's pretty challenging but also fulfilling. tough grader. go to office hours! great sense of humor but again, doesn't do BS. make sure you get her in both ENGL1110 and ENGL1111.

The classes are pretty demanding. You can and are encouraged to be active, but even without constant participation you will be challenged by just soaking up the classroom discussion. You have a lot of freedom when writing you essays, which makes it more fun and yet more demanding. Laurie's class taught me how to write good essays.

Laurie was a great professor and I learned a lot from this class. As long as you make the commitment to show up and put effort in, she will help you with anything you don't understand. She provides useful feedback and is very fair. Also, she has a great sense of humor and isn't too uptight.
Her class took up way too much effort and time. Not an enjoyable class at all, overall a very stressful experience.
Laurie is an amazing professor. Very fun and funny. Attendance is mandatory in her classes. Hardgrader (extremely!!), however, shes worth it. She's amazing. AMAZING.
REALLY great teacher. Intimidating at first but really funny and interesting when she warms up to you. It's a hard class but totally worth the work. Highly recommend her.
Down to earth teacher.  Fun and interesting class with plenty of open discussion but hard grader.
No Comments

NOT a college student, but she moved to teaching hs Pre-Calculus H
I know 5 people who have dropped out of this class with her
First quiz was a 2 page front and back assessment -- she said it was too long and "shortened" it in the form of a 3 page test next
Barely teaches anything, teaches too slow for hs class times (~ 1 hour only
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Neale cares deeply about her students and their success and holds frequent office hours to help with any topics, homework, and test prep! Honestly, the best professor I've had at Northeastern! If you come to classes and office hours, you will do well in the class!
She's a good lecturer but her TAs have no chill and grade the homework like MANIACS like jeez my test scores were higher than my hw grades

I think Bridget's a great teacher and makes the concepts clear! She's great especially if you struggle with math, because she explains the concepts with a lot of detail. If you do the homework, you will be fine.

I took Math1215 (it didn't let me select it). She is super kind. Office hours are helpful and she will make time to be able to meet you. Lots of homework and the tests are fairly hard. I spend a good amount of time on work outside of class but she is. great prof and helps me understand the material (I am not a math person lol).

The math department as a whole usually does optional homework but weekly quizzes, but she decided to do graded homework instead of quizzes with our section. I think it was too much work, but it helped me more than quizzes would. Personally wouldn't take the class again though as I learned most of it through the homework and not her lectures.

Bridget is one of those magical math professors who will never shame you for being out of your element. If you're taking this course as a non-stem major, highly recommend choosing Bridget as your professor because she will adequately prepare you for the final. She is so accessible outside of class and will stay for hours to help students out.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Neale was very kind and understanding. Her office hours are very helpful!
Very Good Professor, was easy to work with and was very understanding.

Professor Neale was awesome! She went over strictly practice problems in class, which was very helpful for practicing and understanding the topics. The quizzes were assigned once a week, but they were pretty easy if you just did the homework. She always posted practice quizzes and tests, which made them all a breeze.

Most concerningly, the professor would deduct pointed, or even refuse to grade assignments—for various unclear reasons.! She often questioned whether students used AI or participated in class activities without any solid evidence, unfairly lowering students' grades. Overall, this course felt unnecessarily harsh and discouraging for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Run as far as u can

Good but very very strict professor, you have to speak in every class, but the questions asked are very tricky, and if you don't want to speak, you will get a very low participation grade or even a warning. If you miss a class, it will result in a LOWER letter grade!

This class includes debates and presentation and the requirements for attendance and participation are strict. Everyone is expected to speak in every class. You might receive a "warning" if you not fully engaged. It's not easy to get high grade. The prof is serious and listens carefully but unless this course is required I wouldn't recommend it
Not accessible at all, no response to emails, no feedback on discussion boards, due dates are not consistent.
Really funny, easy class, especially if you've got experience with Photoshop.

I've taken this class course because I had Lisa before. However, she never had worksheets for the assignments, so she would argue with you that she said something and she didn't. She also didn't keep the grading up to date. She is a very tempered person and if she wasn't in the mode she wouldn't be cooperative. I am very disappointed.

Easy class, especially if you have PS/AI experience.  Due to personal obligations, Lisa wasn't in class as much as usual this past semester and it caused a lag in semester, but overall not a bad professor.

Lisa is quite the character. She is lively, hilariously sassy, almost too open, she sang happy birthday to a girl in my class nearly by herself. I love her! 2D Tools was agonizingly easy for a person who has experience with photoshop and illustrator, so take it with her to have a fun and easy time!
No Comments

Great professor.  Treat her with respect and you will get respect back.  Show up to class and put effort into the class, don't just sit there and think it is a walk in the park.  Make sure you show her that you are putting in the effort and you will get a good grade.

I passed with a C in this class even after failing all three exams. The homework assignments brought my grade up. He initially said that it would be a difficult course and it was. Make sure to do the readings in the textbook outside of the lecture notes. He talks fast but records his lectures. He also gives good feedback on your homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Though exams are hard and material can be confusing, Prof Pearlmutter takes time to really explain the material in such a way that will bring you success in his course. I never thought I'd enjoy psycholinguistics but he truly is a good professor and knows what he's doing. He's transparent about grading/curves so you'll always know where you stand.

Avoid this class if you have a disability/need accommodations. Prof Pearlmutter is very ableist, refuses to follow legally required disability accommodations, and calls out/belittles disabled students in class. He creates an unsafe learning environment, and his behavior is appalling. Why be an educator if you won't teach and respect all students?

Professor Neal has great acknowledgment for this subject, and he is the most responsible professor I have seen that always willing to help. I learn a lot from his class, although I didn't receive a high grade because I am a poor writer. Overall, I am very happy to take his class.

Grades very harshly for the 10-page reports in his Lab Cognition class. Takes off a ridiculous amount of points for everything. He doesn't even grace you with a B or C, but actually gives you an F, despite following all of the guide lines that he goes over in lecture. DON'T TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class if you haven't taken/are not interested in linguistics.  He talks so quickly. Oh, also,it has NOTHING to do with psychology. Awful to sit through. Pain exists in the mind; and this class exacerbates pain. I've seriously considered writing him a letter about learning how to teach. I posted this instead, to avoid controversy.

He wants you to understand everything he's teaching, and he will go the extra mile to make sure that you do. The information is a little bit difficult (but very interesting), and the textbook is the literary equivalent of Nyquil, but you really only need to read a few pages when you study, and he outlines them for you in his study guides.Great prof
Talks wayyyyy tooo fassst

nice guy, grades fair, gives many chances to re-write labs. very good with email and he seems to follow through when he says he will do something to help the class. nice guy who talks kind of fast, but still does a good job. he looks like egon from ghost busters.

Very helpful; sometime his lectures get a bit boring, especially if you've taken linguistics courses before (a lot of overlap). Lots of people dislike it because it's required for psych majors; interesting material; animated professor; EASY hw assignments; ok tests...generally, he's a really dedicated prof who will help you if you ask.
Aww he's the best. He is boring but he's really sweet. The subject becomes really interesting once you put in the effort. Go to every lecture and you'll do fine.

THE WORST class I have ever taken.  I can't even describe to you how boring it is, not to mention it has NOTHING to do with psychology.  The tests also have very little to do with lecture. SAVE YOURSELF AND AVOID THIS CLASS (unless you're a linguisitics major).

I agree with other's comments. He talks way too fast. The subject matter is about as compelling as watching paint dry. If he tried a different approach it might be more interesting. I didn't find it difficult though. His wife rules though - she taught my middler year writing class. I wish I could remember her name so I could rate her.
Talks too fast, boring
No Comments

great prof...really nice and easy to talk to. Very helpful with everything, but the class sucks. Real boring very hard to sit through the entire class. I think i may have only done it a handful of times

I don't know if it's the subject matter or the way it's conveyed, but class definitely drags by the end. Nevertheless, you couldn't find a more helpful teacher that doesn't leave you up in the air about homework assignments, tests, etc. That means if you miss a class you're not out of luck.
Knowledgable, professional. Speaks quickly. Tough-ish but fair.

Katharina was amazing! Her lectures were so great even when we were talking about difficult things relating to psychology and crime. The class topics could have been boring but she made them so interesting, and the class was set up to be discussion based which I liked.

In my section there were quite a few classes cancelled, but Katharina always made sure to update us on schedule changes. She is very caring and is always there to help out of class. Midterm was take-home; reflections are easy to get 100s on. Doesn't require a ton of effort, but the class is more interesting if you do the homework/know the content.

I absolutely love Katharina's classes. I've taken two with her just because I loved her first class so much. She is so understanding and kind and she obviously cares about her students. She structures her classes in a way that makes them easy to pass, but super interesting so you'll actually want to pay attention. Truly the best professor I've had!

I can't recommend Katharina enough. She is AMAZING, and one of the best professors I've ever had. Great course structure. She makes people actually WANT to participate in class. She's extremely understanding and accommodating. If she doesn't know the answer to your question (unlikely), she'll find it out and send it to you later. TAKE HER CLASS!!

The lectures are kinda boring but its like a standard algorithms lecture. Sometimes its hard to follow but you can always ask what's going on and he'll clarify it. The homeworks are meant to be harder than quizzes (online & super easy) or exams, since you can use office hours and talk with peers about concepts. A decent professor who is a kind guy.

Just super boring, I learned the entire class on YouTube. His explanations turn relatively simple concepts into complicated ones. He makes things confusing and there is no point in showing up to lecture.

Huy is seemingly competent in algorithms. I cannot say the same for his ability to teach. His explanations often focus on the most trivial parts of the material and skims past the "interesting" or difficult portions of the content. The explanations he gives are also at times unclear as he can ramble and trail off.

He gives good lectures and posts the slides. I never had a problem understanding him, but he does have an accent. The curves on the exams are very reasonable, and the homework is also manageable.  He is accessible outside of class too and is a really chill guy.
Not sure how to feel about the lecturer. (Slightly dry) lectures only provided so much, much of the learning/studying takes place outside of the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I should have gone to lecture more

homeworks were short but time consuming, exams were easier than homeworks. Reasonable curves

good published slides but not sufficient without lecture

Worst algorithm teacher. Do not take this class cause you will learn nothing. He is a very bad lecturer and does not know how to teach. Homeworks are much harder than things that are discussed in the class. No late policy so you will lose a significant grade if you miss even one of the homeworks. He is not flexible at all.

Professor Nguyen is definitely a very kind and understanding professor, and really wants to see his students succeed. That said, he does have a bit of an accent and has trouble properly conveying some mathematical concepts. Many of the tests and homework assignments had very low averages (40-60s range), but the curve made sure everyone passed.

Professor Nguyen is the best professor I had so far. She is extremely helpful and you will learn new writing techniques in a very interesting and stimulating environment. Attend class, be on time and you'll do a great job. The professor is also very helpful outside of class, take advantage of that. 100% recommended!

Professor Nguyen is very helpful and tries to help you whenever she can. She is a fair grader, a very lenient one actually. Just make sure you attend class, participate a little, and do your assigned readings (fairly short) and you'll be more than good to go.
She is the nicest professor in northeastern and u can very easy to get a good grade.
Duyen is a great teacher. She is incredibly helpful and loves what she does. She is pretty easy on grading, but also teaches very well.

Had her for advanced writing in the disciplines. Overall not a difficult class, and she is very nice. As long as you write your papers and make it to  class you will do well. Taking it in the summer was nice because there wasn't enough time to waste on pointless writing exercises.
Very understandable and nice to talk to.

Real boring class. She can hardly talk half the time. Class is a waste of time. Could be better done over the internet. Horrible teacher. Get out if you can.I've heard there is an english class that just watches movies..get that one.

Should have been an easy freshman course, but his stubborn attitude and heavy heavy accent got in the way. He writes everything he says which is helpful because you won't understand him, which begs the question, "Why even say it in the first place?" Very monotonous, and there was no TA to boost grade or help with the teachings.

Easy A, for the most part. He can be difficult to understand but he writes everything on the board. The TA is more crucial in determining your grades than anyone so make sure to go to the recitation and take part in those discussions. Class is made up of two exams, a term paper and recitation attendance/participation.

Professor Ngeow was a a very nice professor but his monotonous and sometimes hard to understand accent may deter people from the class. Its a fairly easy class, just go to class, take notes (he writes everything he says) and you should be fine. The only issue would be the TA, definitely go to the recitations, if you don't, your whole grade will be

Probably a great guy but not a college level professor.  Hard to understand what he's saying, read his handwriting, and follow his notes. If you know someone who has had the class he uses almost identical midterms/finals and doesn't change them between semesters. I was able to learn more from reading the book than listening to his lectures.

He gives you the opportunity to get a good grade in this class. As long as you go to the class and take notes you should do well on the tests. Midterm, final and 5 recitation quizzes. Multiple choice, short answer and essay tests. Presents the material well, easy to understand, unbiased.
Boring subject matter but is very clear with his teaching method even though he has a thick asian accent.
Good lecturer, boring at times but knows his stuff.  Very smart.  Also, he isn't biased...just gives you the facts.
She very strict about coming to class unprepared . She spent over 30 min talking about the protocol which take away time from labs experiment. Otherwise very easy to pass with A

I had her for my chemistry 2311 lab. She would spend 45 minutes of our long lab session explaining the protocol, which I found completely unnecessary, because she required us to rewrite them from Canvas into our notebooks before the lab. Sometimes, it took longer for her to go over the protocol than to do the lab.
Great lab instructor; might come off strict at first but is very friendly as long as you come to lab prepared. Generally answers questions clearly and gives good feedback on lab reports.

She's just a chill girl, will give you extension if asked for, she's nice, never makes you feel judged when giving speeches. Fosters a nice class enviornment. Course load is very reasonable. And attendance is 'mandatory' but it's for points that will help your grade, but not harm it if you don't have them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If your a good presenter you'll get an A, honestly one of the most down to earth and understanding professors I have had.
One of my favorite Professors at Northeastern. Would definitely recommend it. If you go to class, you will get an A. She is so nice and helpful and gives out extensions often.

Personal favourite in Northeastern. Gave really great lectures (although quite content heavy so be ready). If you do listen in, you'll find yourself learning quite a lot. Her feedback is top-of-the-line, never seen a professor so dedicated to giving well worded, well thought out feedback.
Best professor I had this semester. She explains things really well and clearly has a lot of knowledge/insights to share.
Incredibly pointless lectures that make absolutely no sense. Never received any feedback on how to better improve my writing. This class is a requirement but frustrating.

She's kind and cares about her students. She's accessible after class and is helpful when 1:1. However, the structure of this course works against her. It's a lot of heavy reading which isn't helpful, and conceptual, for the semester long paper the class prepares you for. This means there's a lot of reading, and writing that may seem useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Nikki genuinely cares that all her students understand what is expected of them/the material. She is great at explaining the concepts and makes lectures fun and interactive. She won't force you to participate & is very encouraging <3 real gem

Professor Weickum made me feel very comfortable in a class about public speaking. She gave great advice and pointers on each of our speeches. There is a little bit of reading homework for each class. If you write and present speeches that follow the rubrics and show improvement, you shouldn't have any problem doing well in the class.

Dr. Ali put social justice in front of me in a way that was so evidence and researched based that it rejuvenated my belief in higher education by way of reminding me why it is so focused on this crucial topic

I loved taking EDU 6051 (online) with Dr. Ali. She is an excellent professor. Her materials were well-suited the class. She met with each student about our final project topic and was incredibly sharp when providing feedback on ideas. Feedback is given on all work.

Wish I had more room to write here- take her class!
Overall she was nice and the class was easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly, one of the worst professors in the world. He doesn't understand that students are learning this material for the first time-so when we're confused, because there's so much to know, he mocks. He answers questions as if you're stupid for asking, and he doesn't even make an attempt to try to ensure students grasp the material. Avoid him.

Overall, the powerpoint slides were too wordy and the class lectures were not that clear.  This made pharmacology harder than it was supposed to be.  Even if you study, you will not be guaranteed an A in his portion.  Quizzes are "fairly" straight-forward.

He is very knowledgeable but sometimes has a hard time realizing that students are learning the material for the first time. He is definitely approachable and wants his students to learn and understand the material. His slides are very wordy but most likely due to the fact he wants us to know everything. Overall, nice professor. Can't complain.

Dr. Boisse started teaching the class talked very fast and seemed unapproachable but after the first few lecture i think he got feedback from us and he got MUCH BETTER! He slowed down and explained the material much better. Less words were on his slides and it was less confusing.  Gave practice questions before the test. Test still wordy & hard

Absolutely awful teacher - he is so rude to students when they ask clarifying questions, his tests and quizzes do not line up with what he is always saying in class, and he's just an overall bad teacher. ONLY perk is that he posts his lectures on Tegrity.

I was afraid to raise my hand and ask a question if I didn't understand the material because he would yell at people, which is a shame because he's a really smart man. He records his lectures though which is nice...

Very knowledgeable about his subject, but tends to present information too much too fast. Always seems confused and annoyed by questions which makes students afraid to ask. Very very intense, but only taught half of the class

He's possibly the worst professor i have encountered.  He talks a mile a minute, keeps you after class, his exam questions are out of control.  Everytime i think i'm finally finished with Norman Boisse he shows up to teach one of my pharmacy classes!

He speeds through large amounts of information and acts really annoyed if anyone asks for clarification...i was scared out of my mind to miss a class and i got picked to do the powerpoint presentation at the end of the semester and was so scared i cried afterwards
This guy is very intense, at times too intense.  He goes through a lot of information in class way too fast.  He has a hard time answering students questions.  To sum it up, a very strange man
Challenging class but really worth it. You will learn tons if you put in effort.

Wants to make students sweat for the fun of it. Cares but gives a lot of work for the fun of it. Class participation is important. Shady grader. What she tinks you deserve is what she gives you, not what you earned. I would not take her.
She's a force. Assigns work that is not important to a students college career, or their general knowledge. If you have the opportunity to NOT have her as a teacher, take it.

She's a decent teacher but the class is awful. The amount of reading assigned is impossible to complete, the final assignment is long and time consuming. Only good thing about the class is you get a cheat sheet for the mid term
She is helpful just as long as you put the effort in. If she realizes that you're not putting in any work, you will be out of luck. Basically, just do the work, and you will get at least a B.
No Comments

Worst teacher @ NU. A 20 page paper w/ field work is required for this 100-level class. Ridiculous! Classtime = watch films & students present reading summaries (the amount of reading she assigns is actually impossible to do). Extremely hard & unfair grader. Loved the class the first week. Now I regret ever signing up.
She does have an Awful accent but shes a good teacher. She really tries to help. her class is relatively easy and her quiz questions come from the practice quizes.

She is AWFUL! Very difficult to understand- spend most of the class time deciphering her "English" before we can begin to learn the math.  She'll teach the same thing as the book, but the tests do not reflect what she teaches.  Ridiculously awful grader and worst class to take if you want to maintain a good GPA.  AVOID!

Don't know if it's her or the 1980s textbook, but something is making a class that should be easy much more difficult. She tries to be friendly and helpful, even changed office hours to be more convenient for us, but she's a very tough grader. Could definitely be a lot worse, but still try to avoid her I'd say.

She turns an easy subject like Transformation Geometry into the hardest thing.  Memorizes theorems, posts them on the board, yet does get the logic behind them, which doesn't help the student either.  Makes mistakes frequently on the board, which makes figuring out the theorems really annoying.  Tests are really hard! Avoid at all costs!

horrible. speaks very poor english and has the most irritating accent because she is from turkey. barely understand the material, and can not explain things in different ways because she just memorized how to do a problem and doesnt really understand it. midterm and final are a lot harder than the weekly quizzes. avoid her if possible.

Worst. Professor. EVER. Does not understand or speak english.  Doesn't care if you do well in the class, only concerned with her lesson plan. Do not take any classes with her if you want to learn anything and come out of a class with your good GPA still in tact.

SHe is not bad. and to respond to the other comment, if your smart and know math you shouldnt be taking algebra u idiot. Her english may seem to be a problem but its not that bad u'll get use to it. She is really nice and really tries to help u understand.
