Anyone who says that she can not speak English is just being ignorant. She's speaks clearly, and will slow down when ever asked. Made Calculus very manageable
boring and annoying  dont take if youre actually smart and know math
She singles me out I swear.
it would be nice if she spoke english
Good
She is kindhearted and she explains well inspite of her accent.. just takes some getting used to but really good
it woulda been nice if she spoke english to explain somewhat complecated math stuff, just a thought
No Comments
I loved her so much she gives a good amount of work but clarifies every thing so much. If you are weak in math definitely take her class

She is absolutely wonderful and deeply cares about making sure every student understands the material.  She is always there for office hours and willing to meet and help many other times as well.  Great teacher and helped me get one of my first good grades in math

Oblas is great.  She is high spirited and eager to teach.  The class has mandatory attendance, but if you are planning to skip it often you aren't going to last.  If you miss something, go to her office hours, where she is even better at explaining the material in a very compact way.  Usually, the portfolios were redundant, but the exams are easy.

Extremely helpful. I took this class because I SUCK at Math, and at first, I was confused, but is a piece of cake. Attendance is MANDATORY, which sucks A LOT. You don't understand a thing after missing. Go to her office hours if u dont understand, she will help you out. Very nice person. Test are exactly the same as practice test.

Oblas is an awesome teacher! I have no interest in math, but Interactive Mathematics completed my math requirement and it was a good class. She explains things very clearly and is eager to help. If you have a question, ask and she'll help you understand. A little notebook provides all the homeworks and assignments, the class is very organized.

AWESOME professor!! Definitely take a class with her. She is so nice and understanding! SUPER EASY course for those who aren't math fans (like me). Had a printed book, not a text so much cheaper but required. Labs are easy - go to her office hours and she'll give you the answers. All assignments are quick and easy! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Oblas is great! She wants students to do well and the way that the class is structured makes it so easy to understand. She'll work with you until you understand the material. Tests are very similar to practice tests. HW & Problems of the Week aren't difficult if you go to class and pay attention.

Oblas is such a great prof! She's super nice and cares that her students do well. If you go to her for extra help/information she'll basically give you answers. She strives to make sure her students succeed in her class. I only took her course to fulfill my math req, and I'm so glad I did - awesome class/prof!

Absolutely a great professor. If every teacher cared about their students like her, life would be a whole lot different. Very helpful with explaining the material, great teaching method for students who arent mathematically inclined. Easy to do well if you go to class. Completely recommend this class and professor!

SO easy. Anyone who doesn't really like math but needs the requirement should take this course with her. Like an hour per week of out of class work to type up portfolios and stuff, it frees up time for other classes. She's really nice too and it seemed like she helped out the people who needed it. Great stuff all the way around.
Easy Class. Sweetest teacher ever. Do all the POWs and the portfolios and you will be fine. Easy grader. Easy work. Great teacher tho!!
One of the best math professors I ever had, so helpful and attentive.

Class is VERY easy, and its hard to handle if your moderately competant in math, and are taking it to fulfill a requirement. But Oblas never loses patience, and is always enthusiastic. It's an easy A but you must show up to class because she doesn't teach out of a book.

I can barely add without using my fingers, and I scored a B+ in this class. Oblas does anything she can to help, the assignments are really easy/pertinant to your work, just make sure you have all the homeworks right and do your portfolios. Def look for her to take this with

To the person who said they met the dumbest people at NU while in this math class, get a clue. There is such a thing as a math learning disorder. Math doesn't come easily to some people. Oblas has to be one of the kindest Profs at NU and encouraged me to get tested for Dyscalcula. She's overall just a great lady and is willing to help you
I hate math! And prof oblas made it easy to understand and fun! Great course for non-math people.  The MOST helpful professor ever! Very dedicated and such a nice person!

I placed out of College level Calculus and took this class as an elective. I met some of the dumbest people at Northeastern while in this class. I could have taken the tests blind, high, ****, and with a gun to my head and still pulled off a 100 on every one. P.S.- The Camel POTW was awesome.
Great class, and i hate math. Very easy and she is always willing to help. She is always very high spirited and in a good mood.

Very helpful, kind, fair teacher. She makes math accessible even to those who're not the biggest fan of the subject. Save your homework and ask questions, and you'll do fine. She creates a very positive class atmosphere. Easy class.
Very easy class. Take notes and save your homework.
Awesome teacher, really nice, easy to approach. Go to class and you'll do good.
very easy A. as long as you go to class! she teaches a lot of stuff in one period but is very friendly and approachable if you have questions.
she teaches interactive math... which in itself is an easy class, but she's easy to pay attention to. very helpful, and understanding. easy A.

Antonio is probably my favorite professor. He gives great feedback and is always wanting to help you improve. Highly suggest taking his class, but if you don't want to participate, then don't. It's an interactive class and the only way he can help you is if you try.

Great professor! Antonio wants his students to get out of their comfort zones, he will push you to what he believes you are capable of. Great professor in class, great person out of class. Definitely recommend any of his classes!
Antonio will push you beyond your boundaries, but not beyond what you can deal with. Insightful, intense, brilliant. He's an invaluable ally as a friend and professor.
so hot

Roberto is definitely the best teacher I've ever had. He goes above and beyond for his students with their design work as well as their knowledge of the field outside of studio. He took us on an architectural tour around the Boston area and brought us donuts a couple of times over the weekend before our final project. All around awesome guy.
The most dedicated studio professor NU's schools of architecture ever had

Very dedicated professor who really looks out for his students. Takes time outside of class to come in and help with design work. Gives insightful feedback and helps with problems. But he won't do it for you, which is helpful for learning.  ALOT of work involved, so you'll be spending almost all of your waking hours in studio. Its worth it though!

roberto is the most dedicated teacher i have ever had. he is totally committed to his students and even comes in at 11:30 at night with pizza to help. although the work load is intense, it definitely pays off in the end. expect a studio boot camp.
Great teacher all round and cool guy. Very smart - knows his stuff. He expects an awful lot of work but it is well worth it. If you keep up with the work you will do well. Sometimes he buys pizza!

His class does not have much writing and no in-class essays, which I liked. But he does not really teach writing or give feedback on the many small assignments. He also does not post on Canvas, and nothing I've done has been graded yet. As an engineering major, I think the class is okay.
Grades off vibes, AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Noonan is awesome. I enjoyed his new way of teaching the course, a way that doesn't involve strict assignment-based grading. Show up to class and do the work on time for credit. The final project was also fun and unique.
I took this class while on co-op. A much bigger time commitment than I thought. The readings were geared more towards English majors.

Honestly I really liked Prof. Noonan! He was very easy to talk to and made the classroom environment very comfortable/friendly. The grading was very holistic and it was based a lot on individual effort put in. If you try your best and you show up to class consistently then you will get a good grade. Take Noonan! He may be strange but he is fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Noonan is a very nice man, his class environment is welcoming and encouraging. This was my favorite class and I recommend everyone to take this class. The class was not that hard but taught me valuable insights and was overall very fun.

I had him for Honors First Year Writing. He was unorthodox with his loose grading and conversational class. I enjoyed it and grew as a writer. He made the course relevant by presenting the concept of audience to us in the context of AI. Some assignments were worded vague. The final project was too involved for a required FYW class.

Fine professor - relatively easy grader as long as you put in effort. However, the class is excruciatingly boring and pointless. The assignments are a complete joke and you will learn nothing useful in Adv Writing Arts/Media/Design. Put in decent effort and you will get an A, but be prepared to roll your eyes every assignment.

Doesn't seem to realize that Advanced Writing in the Disciplines isn't necessarily a class for English majors. Assigned readings (of which there will be many) are dense pieces written by and for academics that wax poetic about "genre" while teaching nothing relevant about writing for your discipline.

Professor Noonan is the worst professor Ive ever had. His assignments are extremely open-ended, not in a good way. He does not give clear answers but instead writes in circles, never telling you what he wants. He only hosts office hours for 30 minutes and is so rude and condescending if you ask questions or challenge him. Avoid at at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: So disconnected from reality. Acts as though the assignments are open ended but will then harshly grade for going somewhere off of his 6 page prompt. No changing of the class layout for COVID. Snarky short comments on pieces don't help to improve your project for the next assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach during class. Assigns 10 paged papers a week before they're due. His assignment documents are 6 pages in length; you have to dig to just find the prompt. Gives no rubrics, no information on how you'll be graded (which assignments are worth more than others), and no course calendar. The only thing I've learned is to not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's awesome!

Noonan is certainly a challenging professor. His "vagueness" is admittedly on purpose. The assignments are very broad, and his vagueness is an attempt to give the student the ability to choose how they take on the assignment. It is accurate that he tends to ramble, and feedback is sometimes lacking, but he makes it a point to ensure everyone learns
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 1 Noonsky is the man 2 He definitely makes you work for it. There are three projects that are particularly long. It takes a while to write them but if you don't procrastinate, make a plan, and churn it out the grading isn't that harsh at all. Attendance is non-mandatory but participation helps your grade. 3 I AM a better writer after this class.

Professor Noonan was by far my worst professor at NEU. His weekly letters are so condescending and rude, its like they are his own personal vanity projects. His assignments have nothing to do with writing in the disciplines and his expectations are maddeningly vague. He leaves short, pompous comments on peoples work publicly that offer no help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: No respect for his students. Rude & condescending, he attacks students if they have questions. His weekly letters have no clarity, tend to ramble, and are very difficult to understand. He's another example of the disappointing NEU English department. It is nearly impossible to succeed in his class because of the lack of direction and rude feedback.

Horrible professor. AVOID at all cost. Was not clear on our assignments and definitely pointless course. Does not apply to business knowledge / further development. Students are majoring in business not reading or english or journalism.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Noonan was great. A gifted writer and experienced teacher. Really good at getting you to think in the right ways. Tough grader but his assignments are fun if you get into it.

Noonski is the man.  At first I was apprehensive about the course as I heard he wasn't very clear, but I learned to embrace it.  He's a fun guy to have teach a class and his dry sense of humor was pretty great too.  Be sure to talk to him in class during the workshops and discuss the direction of your project and you should be fine.

Difficult professor, definitely do not recommend. Assignments are pretty vague, poorly timed (day after Super Bowl), hard grader. Places a lot of emphasis on post-paper reflections rather than paper itself. Pretty pompous guy, doesn't really teach just has class break into small groups.
Very hard and confusing, I dont recommend him at all
Excellent professor.  Made a dreaded AWD class very enjoyable.  Don't be shy about playing around with him in your work either- he's open to wit and humor.

Advanced Writing in the Disciplines. Difficult Class. Super super nice guy! He wants you to work, he wants you to think. Don't be lazy and you'll do fine. Haven't gotten my final grade yet but I worked really hard on our first three big projects and got either A or A-. Sometimes frustrating at how much work was required but no regrets on keeping it

Out of four of my classes Noonan's class is the worst. He is not clear with the projects, he asks for way too many assignments and is never satisfied. I do not recommend any one to take his class it is a nightmare

Ridiculous amounts of work.A lot of all nighters devoted to him. Very unclear when you ask for help.Honestly gave this class my all and still ended up with a C.Transferred schools and asked him to write a recommendation thinking I demonstrated hard work, his response "do you really want me to write a recommendation? You didn't really do well" PRICK

He is a strict and hard professor. I got crazy for this course at the beginning. It was hard for me to catch uo with him. And also ,like most people said, he may not usually tell you what is good and what you should do etc. H e prefer to let you think by yourself more. I can felt that he had definitely helped me improve my ways of thinking.
Had him for college writing. I hated him at first because he is a difficult grader and requires a lot of work, but he is a great teacher. I learned a ton, and I put in the work to get a good grade.

Not a class for the lazy. I hated the hard work at first, but grew to really love and commit myself to the projects. The class is a student workshop, I hate seeing people get upset that he's not doing the work for you. It's college. Grow up and put a little effort/thought into your work. Great Guy, always available for help/questions.

When he talks about the course matter, he's very ambiguous with words! Will never tell you straightforward what to do and what Not to do, juggles a lot with words and mostly bs-ing!! Attendance is "Extremely Mandatory" in this class and even though it's 10% of the grade he won't stop at failing you for that. Horrible Teacher, HIGHLY UNRECOMMENDED!!

Took the class a year back. Definitely worked for my grade. My writing improved drastically thanks to his class. Not for the lazy by any means. He genuinely wants students writing to get better. You just have to think outside the box for his assignments. Don't be afraid to experiment. I did not pay for NEU to watch monster movies in an Eng. class.
One of my favorite teachers. Noonan's class is hard, but he's always willing to help you as much as you need. And trust me, you will use the tools you learn in his class in real life.
Extraordinary amounts of work. Yes, practice makes perfect but this is way beyond the limit.
Professor Noonan is a great teacher- I took his AWD class which I was hestitant about taking, but he turned out to be a great professor, and the class was fun!

I love Noonan!!  I was so nervous about being in his class but we only have class 2 out of the 3 days we're supposed to and he usually lets us leave way early.  He's super nice and really wants to help you do well and explore your major and interests.  Awesome professor.

Amazing teacher! This classes really helped me define which area of my discipline I want to pursue. The class is a lot of work, but it's worth it in the end - TRUST ME. He's a really cool guy who's approachable and friendly. If your work ethic meets his expectations, you'll have no problem. The reviews before this are misleading, don't listen.

I had this guy a couple years back..at the time I thought life couldn't get any harder with his ridiculous papers but in all honesty I have used those papers since, for jobs and for transferring schools. Mr. Noonan is deff. a different style of teaching but I loved it.... Put in effort and he is the man and it will reflect in your grade! I miss him

Despite the class being hard as balls, he is the absolute man! and I love his bow ties and he is classy for not wearing a clip on, he ties that sh*t everytime he wears it. Keep it up Mr. Noonan, dont listen to the other D-Bags on this list.

this guys pretty much the hardest teacher I've ever worked with, and I'll tell you why: he's not teacher material. He knows his stuff, no doubt, but he's not committed to helping students, and not understanding of their occasional difficulties. He asks a lot from students in a short amount of time. And the whispering-while-talking thing. not cool

This class was so aggravating... He assigns a bunch of work that is supposed to help you but he doesn't check them or give credit. The work is tedious and he assigns huge essays. Very nice and understanding professor.

coolest guy ever.

Best professor ever. He truly cares about you and actually wants you to pass.

Amazing professor! I really enjoyed taking Critical Text Analysis with them. They make difficult reading and writing concepts easy to understand and always encourage class discussion. good guy overall

The variety of graphic novels we went through in the course is great. However, the best part is how the instructor and the teacher assistant create a free environment. It's definitely (A+)-able class. Definitely do the challenges early, I mean right when he post. Spam him stuff. you need some previous knowledge to take this class or else it'll be difficult. that's all i can say

Professor Kaan is the best Professor I've had at Northeastern. He is beyond knowledgable in his field and wants you to learn so that you are prepared to enter the industry. Great lectures, challenging but rewarding homeworks, lots of (difficult but doable) extra credit opportunities.

Kaan has made CY 3740 without a doubt the best class I've taken at Northeastern. His lectures are fun and engaging and I always looked forward to working on the challenges. The class was difficult, but fair. People rating him below 5 stars clearly did not pay attention or seek any help out from the TA's. HW always built on what was in the lecture.

Only way to explain Kaan is like an ex-girlfriend, no homo. You remember her as a genuinely nice person, and you even love her from time to time, but the relationship was tough. He is kind and approachable, but his class is definitely challenging in multiple ways. The lectures are solid and engaging, even if the material can be difficult at times.

The challenges were hard, not surprised about that at all. You just go through it, that's how life is. The slides during class instruction were good, but made me think all throughout the place. I don't know how to really fully comment this class. It's strange, but kind of normal. Yes, it's on Thursday night. Could be a con to readers of this review

Extremely knowledgeable and well spoken professor. The challenges required understanding of the material and significant thought but were still doable and allowed for hands on learning. Kaan has clearly spent ample time and energy to get the course to be what it is. Would recommend.

Great professor. Lectures were engaging and the assignment structure made the course pretty fun. He was very responsive on Piazza whenever I asked questions and provided helpful feedback. I learned a lot and found the content very valuable. Would definitely recommend both this course and Kaan as a professor.

reviews.comment: he has a weird grading system. if you don't know how to do one challenge, your grade drops.

He's a good person. Tests and quizzes seem to be more lecture heavy and theory. Challenges are hard, you need to memorize basically everything from computer systems. A lot of analysis of C code and writing Python code. No one really supports you with the challenges at all. If you don't know how to do anything, then it's wraps. That's all I can say.

Pretty hard class. Midterm and final were alright, they make you think of what was taught. More of class instruction and how to analyze it with what you were taught. You need a foundation of computer systems, C code, and Python. If you don't have that foundation, it's going to be hard. No one helps you with the challenges, TAs and Kaan don't help.

Kaan is a thoroughly engaging lecturer. On top of this, he has clearly put a lot of time and effort into designing the course (homeworks, tests, lectures), and it shows. I cannot more highly recommend this course.

I've never had a professor that made me want to attend lectures like Kaan did. The material he curated is so interested and has real modern-day implications in the cybersecurity world. The challenges and gamification of homework made me legitimately look forward to the next challenge coming out so I could  try to break it. 10/10, would recommend.

Top 3 class for CS/CY majors. Kaan is amazing and you'll walk out of the course being actually prepared for security jobs and get a solid understanding of the principles. Homework is actually enjoyable to do if you're interested.
Amazing prof

Cons: There is no fluff in this course, meaning you need to be well equipped to catch up on stuff you haven't really learned in prerequisite courses involving Systems and Databases. Pros: This course teaches you lessons you will apply in both your day to day life and your career. Khan stresses the importance of being thorough and self supporting.

Every professor should take notes from Kaan. All of his lectures are incredibly insightful, and the gamified challenge system makes you WANT to do his homework. Genuinely leagues ahead of any other professor I've had here.
Just a great guy overall. His lectures are very interesting and has a good sense of humor. Challenges are difficult but doable.

I took him in Fall 2024. Thursday night, brutal. The challenges were hard, since it was hard to even know any commands or whatnot. No notes or anything on the two quizzes and midterm, final. You basically had to memorize and understand everything and there was a lot. The bonuses were unsolvable, so don't be praising yourself with any extra credit.

I literally never use RateMyProfessor but it would be criminal not to praise Kaan.
If you are thinking about taking this course, do it. Even if you aren't pursuing a career in security.
Kaan is an expert at making you address your weaknesses in the material without making you feel bad about yourself.
You WILL learn a ton-- challenging but rewarding

The most helpful class I've taken at Northeastern. Kaan's lectures were very helpful and engaging and the topics discussed in class are very interesting and insightful. The coursework can be challenging, however the support from himself and the TAs was incredible.

Kaan's class was extremely rewarding. It is important that lectures are attended as he does give live demos of things that you just can't really get on your own, but it's not graded on whether you go. The challenges he provides are genuinely tough but definitely not impossible especially given the support you can get from him and the TAs.

The best class I've ever taken! I gained a lot from every single session. Also, the teaching style is engaging and fun, and relevant to real life. 
The assignments are definitely challenging. But, if you attend the office hours, Kaan always gives just the right amount of guidance to help you solve it.

Kaan is the kind of professor you actually want to get.  This has been the most valuable class ive taken at northeastern content wise, and kaan does it best.  Each lecture is entertaining and relates directly to assignments.  As long as you go to class you will be fine for the midterm and final.  Challenges can be difficult but very valuable.

Kaan has been the best professor I have had the pleasure listening to at Northeastern. He's incredibly personable but also a master at his craft. This is the one course I can comfortably say is worth the however many thousand dollars each class at Northeastern costs. You will be leaving lecture every week with ACTUAL practical skills. 11/10

Class can definitely be difficult at times but it is so worth it, every challenge is truly a learning opportunity. Kaan cares a lot about student success and you come out of class feeling like a 1337 hacker with all your new knowledge ;)
Probably the best professor most people will have at Northeastern, and easily the most effort any of my professors have put into a class.
Easily one of the best courses all time.

Kaan keeps challenges fresh and engaging. He's very approachable and gives you enough help where you can move past walls in the homework but still feel like you learned something. He helps you learn both technical and problem solving skills very well and rewards high performance.

Kaan is one of the best professors I've had. CY 5770 is tough but incredibly rewarding, especially for those with a good C programming and Linux background. He pushes you to apply concepts creatively and organizes the material brilliantly.

One of the best professors I've ever had. I recommend anyone who has a background in software security to take CY 5770 with Kaan. It was a difficult class, but it's a class I got the most learning out of. He pushes you to be a top-tier problem solver using the material you've learned in class, and organizes the class material extremely well.

One of the most valuable classes I've taken at Northeastern. It was definitely challenging and at times demanding, but the experience was more than worth it. Kaan is one of the best professors I have ever had.

If you have a chance to take a course under Kaan, just go for it. Keep in mind though, you need a certain level of C and Linux knowledge. If you have got the prerequisite knowledge, go for it probably gonna be the best course you have done in your program.

Kaan is the best!!! He is one of the best professors I've ever had. He explains complex cybersecurity concepts in ways that actually make sense, and his lectures are engaging and well organized. The assignments are challenging but fair and help build real-world skills. If you get a chance to take his class, do it!! you won't regret it!

He is truly one of a kind—extremely knowledgable. Classes are fun. I learned a lot about cybersecurity throughout my degree, but I truly understood concepts when Kaan taught it. Some technical challenges he designs are tough but rewarding; builds technical confidence. Kaan gives his absolute best & his dedication to teaching is inspiring.
It's tough enough to make you question choices, but interesting enough not to skip it.

reviews.comment: The most rewarding class I took at Northeastern. It was super difficult, but once you solved the challenges, it felt so satisfying. Khan put a lot of work into the structure of the class and it just shows. Kahn was a big part of how great this class was set up and I wouldn't have enjoyed the class as I strongly do if he wasn't the professor.

Kaan did a great job at keeping the class engaged, using real world examples to explain the content. He uses his work experience to give us motivation behind the content and activities in class. Kaan also did many in class demos and examples to show us how to complete our CTF's. The coursework was very rewarding, and Kaan was a fair grader.

Easily one of the best classes I have taken at Northeastern. It was definitely difficult and time consuming sometimes, but incredibly rewarding. One of the few classes where I genuinely felt like I learned a lot. Kaan is an incredible professor. He's funny, engaging, and just brings a lot of enthusiasm to class which makes it worthwhile.

I've said this too many of my friends, "Kaan is the best professor I have ever had." I don't think a second of my time taking this course was wasted, "challenges" (hw, CTF style) are super helpful in applying your learning from class (with a little learning left for outside of class). Exams were like 70% understanding hw, and going to lecture.

By far the most engaging lecturer and most fun and educational class I have ever taken at Northeastern. In no other class have I ever felt this challenged and rewarded, Kaan really pushes his students to learn in so many different ways, and I feel so much more confident in all my cybersecurity skills. Super funny guy, just wish he had his beard :(.

Kaan is an incredible professor. If you want to get into security, you have to take this class. He goes over all the fundamentals and is also a engaging professor. The homeworks are hands on CTF-style challenges, while the tests are more conceptual. Overall 10/10 class.

Kaan says he tries to teach everything about security in 4 months, and he really does. He brings years of experiences to the classroom and is passionate, knowledgeable, and invested in the topics of this class and the future of the students taking it. This is easily my favorite class, and I would've regretted not taking it before I graduated.
Kaan is fantastic, it is obvious he cares deeply about the material. The class is tough, but lots of help is available.

Best professor by far. Almost failed just to take again. 
First and only CS class I feel I have learned relevant material in.

Before this class started I really wanted to be the first one to give him a bad review on this site but I literally just cannot do that. Fair play to the guy, he's an amazing teacher and I've never learned more than I have in this class.

Amazing professor -- class is difficult but well worth the effort needed. Would recommend taking even if you are not necessarily interested in security as the course touches many core topics in CS such as networking, distributed systems, compilers, operating systems, and more. Challenges are fun and there is lots to learn from them

Had a wonderful experience taking this class as CS major, by far the most I've learned in a NEU course. Couldn't have asked for a more amazing prof - Kaan is patient, inspirational, extremely knowledgeable, caring, and approachable. Lectures (theory, research, and demos) and challenges (hands-on, DIY) complement each other perfectly.
Best course this college

Kaan does what I have not seen before in other professors: keeping a 2-3 hour long lecture engaging, fun, and meaningful. Nearly every lecture is grouped together with a live demonstration of how to apply the concepts covered on the slides. These demonstrations often give pointers on where to start on challenges, giving some starting direction. -44

This class is the best I've taken so far. Kaan is an excellent lecturer who keeps us engaged even during the late sessions that run until 9pm. The challenges are the highlight though - each one is intellectually stimulating and genuinely fun to solve. However, be prepared to spend lots of time on challenges! I can't recommend this class enough. -68

Spent by far the most hours working on his homework out of the 4 classes I took this semester. However this was by far the best and most rewarding hours spent. His challenges/homeworks are always hard but relevant and fun. This class rewards you for your effort, if you take it be ready to give it your all. 
-86
Show up to class. I loved taking this class and doing his challenges. Lots of fun and so much learned. Highly recommend.
Kaan is a very engaging professor for such a boring time slot

If you're unsure about taking this class, take it. Kaan is one of my favorite Professors. He's highly knowledgeable and has years of experience in his field. CS3740 is uniquely structured, with most of your grade based on hands-on CTFs that expose you to real-world online threats. Kaan genuinely enjoys teaching and wants the best for his students.

This class was tough and challenges could take quite a bit to complete, but it was very intellectually challenging and Kaan equipped you with all you needed to solve them, given that you put some creativity into it. Professor covers all important topics and ensures the lectures are interesting. The challenges are fun and tests the understanding of fundamentals thoroughly.

Prof. Onarlioglu's assignments are very fun and effective for learning practical skills. Lectures were well-organized and he was highly knowledgeable in all the content. He was very responsive and made sure support was always available outside of class (even answering questions at 4am). Overall, a funny and amazing professor that I highly recommend
Loved the lectures and the many challenges.

Kaan was the most prepared educator I've ever had. The challenge environment, concepts, and application of these concepts to real world scenarios tied together seamlessly. Have a question at 3am? Kaan's responding immediately. This is not an easy course, but I've gained more knowledge that I can apply to future work than from any other I've taken

I was told this before taking the class, and now I'll point out the same: It's the best class and instructor! I guarantee you will learn a lot. The assignments are challenging, but the feeling of achievement is priceless when you solve them. If you're not sure about your technical background, you better take this class alone just to fully enjoy it.

reviews.comment: Kaan is an amazing professor. I struggled but I learnt a lot and did things I didn't think I could do. 11/10 would recommend. Everyone needs to take this course under Kaan.

Kaan is a great lecturer and his homeworks are difficult but enjoyable. Also, there is office hours every week and constant support on Piazza so you are not alone at all, you will have plenty of help if you need it. If you have an interest in security at all, take this class, it's the best one I have taken at Northeastern and I have learned a ton.

Kaan is an amazing lecturer. He will keep you engaged with his enthusiasm and the occasional funny slides that pops up. He explains things very well and is very understandable. His course is also very hands-on while also balancing it with theory side. All in all, I really enjoyed this class and I learned a lot from it. Would take again!

Absolutely one of the best profs at Northeastern. Weekly lectures are fast paced and intense, but the material is presented incredibly clearly and Kaan is always willing to slow down for tricky concepts. The CTF-style homeworks are super fun and a great training ground for your technical skills, and the exams are great too! Expect to learn a ton.

Syssec will be the best cybersecurity class you take at Northeastern. Not only is Kaan an amazing lecturer--complete with anime references and top-tier memes littered throughout his slides--but his assignments are second to none. His CTF homeworks are a blast and he and the TAs are always available outside of class for assistance (even at 4am).

One of the best courses I have taken at Northeastern. I learnt so much from this class, and the 3-hour lecture per week goes like a breeze. I always look forward to what is to come next week. The content is hard for someone like me who has no prior exposure to security, but the support to successfully complete the course is impeccable.

Kaan is extremely passionate about the course material and teaching his students. Without a doubt, this was both my favorite class I've taken at Northeastern, measured by my ability to retain focus in and out of class, and most rewarding. The challenges will push your understanding of the course material to the next level, in a gamified fun way.

Interesting, fun and challenging class. As a CS major this was the first security class I enjoyed. Lectures are well planned and entertaining. Homework is time consuming but you gain experience using real world attacks.

Class was very fun and interesting. Homework is hard. Require shell bash scripting, but it is easy to learn. Exams are in person and written. Bonus points available to help with low exam scores. Office hours are extremely helpful. Only recommend this to student that wants a challenge and is confident in their CS knowledge/finesse.

Professor Kaan's lectures are amazing, he provides extra support to understand the concepts. His lectures are super intense and funny at the same time. His classes are worth your time and money :) In short he is the CoOlEsT and BeSt teacher I have ever had!! If you have a chance to take his class, without a doubt TAKE IT!!
Coolest professor you'll ever meet, if you are given the choice to take only one security class in your life, BLINDLY GO FOR THIS CLASS !
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kaan might be the best professor I've ever had. His subject matter expertise is inspiring, he gives detailed information in lectures, and he cares so much about the topic that he set up his own hacking lab for students to exploit vulnerabilities. This was the most demanding class I've taken at NU; it was well-worth the challenge. Take his class.

Hands down!! The best course I have ever taken in academia. The course structure is brilliant and you will get addicted to challenges(you get to see your number on class rankings website in real-time :) ). Great piazza and one to one support. Extra credits saved the day. The stories/memes are great too. Salute Kaan!

Professor Kaan excels in teaching, crafting real-world-aligned assignments, and fostering accessibility through Piazza. His support and mentorship leave a transformative impact on student's academic journeys. A true beacon of excellence in education. I wish I had taken his class earlier during my master's program.

For a three month course, the structure was perfect to go over a wide variety of system security topics. Anyone even remotely interested in software security should take Kaan's class. His commitment to the course, engaging lectures, availability outside of class hours are second to none. Challenges simulate real world attacks and are super fun!

Kaan is a security guru we all wish we had lol. His teaching style is spot-on, making cybersecurity a breeze. 
The challenges? Intuitively fun! His cutting-edge research and legendary stories are just the icing on the cake!

Kaan is an amazing lecturer, knows his stuff, and cares about students. The lectures teach concepts and a security mindset, while the challenges (homework) are fun and teach practical skills. Grading is straightforward and fair. Kaan made an entire Arch Linux lab environment for this class, which should say enough about how much effort he puts in.

Every student who has the chance to take syssec with Kaan should. Best class I've taken at Northeastern. Homeworks and challenges were fun and addictive. You learn a lot too. Kaan puts a lot of effort and passion into the class, and it shows.

CY3740 was an indispensable course that gave me a well-structured and fundamental understanding of system security. Kaan is funny and entertaining in class and always ready to answer questions for his students. He always finds a way to hold the student's attention. In other classes, I would be distracted, but never in kaan's class.

Kaan is extremely knowledgeable about security and is a very engaging lecturer. Lectures are very informative and the slide decks are great. Challenges are somewhat difficult but definitely a lot of fun.

Kaan is really great. He is knowledgeable, really funny, and is always trying to make himself available. He responds on Piazza fairly quickly and gets grades back usually by the next class. Kaan has no problem being real about his opinions and is always trying to educate on past security issues that we should learn from.

reviews.comment: Kaan was an admirable professor, not only is he extremely knowledgeable about this field, he wants us to succeed as long as you put in the work. This is a very challenging class in terms of the homework "challenges" that are given to us, but I promise you will have a clear understanding of certain security aspects after this course. 11/10 recommend
He's an amazing professor. He is also one of the best researchers in security, just look up his google scholar. You will learn a lot in this course.

Kaan is an absolute legend, and this course might be the best one I've taken at Northeastern so far. The challenges are somewhat difficult with no prior experience, but he's super responsive online and has office hours after class--if you get stuck somewhere, you aren't left to bang your head against a wall. 10/10, take this class if you can!

reviews.comment: This was honestly one of the most difficult classes I've taken. I spent a lot of late nights thinking about buffer overflows and cross site scripting. Nonetheless, I found that I've also learned so much from Kaan's class. He's incredibly knowledgeable, charming, and one of the most caring professors I have met. Also he's simply a security wizard.

Kaan is very likely one of the best professors at Northeastern. He's *extremely* skilled and *very* accessible after class. I'd highly recommend taking his class if you have the chance, even if it's at night (don't worry: the class almost never ran more than 2-2.5 hours). The challenges can be difficult; but it is definitely worth the experience.

Extremely effective lectures and assignments. Everything is usable in the real-world and the grading is based on whether you do the assignment or not. No scores, no partial credit. You either did the assignment or you didn't. The professor is super accessible if you need help and will generally respond quite quickly to questions.

A great course with a well-rounded syllabus and amazing lectures. Professor's delivery and explanations ensure that you understand the content from the ground up. The exams and assignments are fun and practically applicable in the real world. I feel better prepared to enter the world of security after this course. Would definitely recommend it!

reviews.comment: Incredibly interesting and challenging course.  I really enjoyed this class and I learned a lot

reviews.comment: This is a great class and you will learn a lot, but you need to do the work. There's no way to bullshit the assignments for partial credit, you need to commit to figuring them out start to finish. Lectures cover a lot of in-depth technical material useful for security career. Tons of opportunities for extra credit for those who want it.

Coming from a Game Dev background, I was shown how beautiful security is and absolutely loved every challenge and especially the fact where we having to be self disciplined as there were only 2 deadlines.

Hey Folks, 

So if you are here, That means you are in dilemma to take this course?

I am a student who took this course with the same dilemma and you know what? This is one of the greatest dilemma decisions of my life which yielded astonishing results. Go for it. You will love what you are doing. This is the real world, real challenges. GOAT!
One of the best classes I have ever taken at Northeastern, Cant find anyone better at teaching security than him!

Kaan is easily the best professor I have ever had at Northeastern. Great lectures, great challenges, and very accessible outside of class. I learned more from him and his class than every other class here combined. If you can take CY3740 for CY5770 with him, do it!
Great real-world experience, hugely accessible and helpful.

reviews.comment: If you are remotely interested in Security, take this class. Kaan is a great guy, and the challenges are by far the best part of it all.

This is probably one of the best classes I've ever taken, and Kaan is a major reason for that. If you like solving puzzles/challenges at all, you have to take this class. The homeworks in this class are pretty much "here's what you have to break, here's some hints, go", and they're incredibly fun. Plus, Kaan's always there to help if you get stuck.

CY3740 was one of the most entertaining classes I've ever taken. Kaan lectures on interesting topics and the challenges he creates are awesome. No doubt, Kaan's challenges will make you struggle and feel frustrated, but they are so well crafted that the sense of satisfaction you feel after completion is unlike anything.

Out of all professors I have had at Northeastern University, Kaan has been THE BEST professor. He is extremely knowledgeable and translates complicated topics into understandable lectures. His assignments provide practical experience in exploitation and are also fun/engaging :)
Fantastically designed the class with applicable challenges as hw. Very accessible outside of the class for hw help. 10/10 would take again.
Very interesting and fun challenges

If you have even a remote interest in cybersecurity you need to take this class with him. It's gonna be tough but you'll learn so much along the way and Kaan is a chill guy, so he'll always help you. There really isn't any book that'll teach you this stuff. You'll struggle through the challenges, but the high after solving them is worth it.

He is a great teacher and always ready to help you. The assignments will be tough if you have no previous experience in the Security field but if you ask a question he will guide you through the solutions.

i just love him. he is very smart and kind. whenever I needed him he was there to help me out with my questions. i took 3 different classes of him and each of them were extremely informative and challenging. i found myself asking questions that never bothered me before. so do take a class of him and find out how amazing and nice person he is.

I think he is a great professor. he explain things in the way that not many professors care.. when i did not get something he took his time and made sure that I got it well. he is very very kind and nice human being as well.
Lousy class based on watching movies and aimless discussion board postings.  Easy grade but you learn nothing.

Bad structure of course and tons of micro management. Murmuring all the time and could not explain even the most basic OOD concept clearly. Also, expect to use some tech stack in HW that has never been taught before.

The professor expects 100% compliance and will call people out for not paying attention, yet the content being taught has no actual value. reviews.comment: Easily the best class I have taken! Structurally the class is fair in terms of grading and forgiving if you have a rigorous schedule. The lectures are the best I've experienced from a professor. The class focuses on gaining a deep understanding of ML and how it can apply to any field whatever it is you want to do in life.

Professor Ostadabbas is extremely knowledgeable about all advanced computer vision topics. Her lectures are both engaging and concise. She also fosters a safe learning environment in which students can ask and answer questions without fear of being judged, which is key in an intellectually challenging course. 100% recommend for any AI Masters/PhD.

The course provided a great overview of the techniques for mitigating the limited data issue! I loved the walkthrough of models' evolvement history. It really helped me to understand how researchers innovate on top of prior models. The course load is not heavy but all the work is meaningful. The prof is very knowledgeable and always ready to help!
The course is good and the teacher is very easy-going. The course load is not heavy as well.

Dr. Ostadabbas was my professor for EECE4512: Healthcare technologies. The lectures were amazing with hands-on practice labs after every module. Professor provided us with the basics of data visualization and analysis of the body signals. I think this class gave me a perspective on how data analysis can be utilized and help people around us.

I thoroughly enjoyed taking this class. There was a unique focus on on new technologies and how they may be utilized in a real word scenario. I was able to conduct my own experiments to apply what I was learning. and gained a better understanding of data collection/analysis. I also became much more comfortable giving presentations.

The course is very math heavy and can take up a lot of time if you aren't familiar with signal processing and linear systems. However, getting a good grade is definitely doable so long as you pay attention to the lecture and do all homework by yourself.

reviews.comment: I have learned a lot from your class. This class has a very open classroom. Professor also have different invited speakers come to class all the time.

One of the best professors in the ECE department. Truly cares about whether her students understand the material and how its applicable in the real world. Semester long project allows you to dive deep into a topic that you are passionate about (be prepared for routine check-ins). Staying on top of assignments and moderate effort can lead to an A.

Great class, you get experience reading technical papers and presenting your work. In the group project you take data, learn to gather important features, and optionally use machine learning. You really get out so much from the class if you put in the effort. Occasional guest speakers are all really interesting to listen to. Can't recommend enough

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors so far as an engineer. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her do it. you will learn a lot, she is not overbearing and very supportive.

Professor Ostadabbas is a very caring woman and really wants you to succeed in her class. I failed the first time I took this class, and had to retake the course with Professor Ostadabbas. Professor Ostadabbas gave thorough lessons and was a fair grader. bad teacher! He does not know how to teach. He is very unorganized and never clear on hw assignments. You have to go to every class or you will miss him mutter a random hw assignment. His grading is arbitrary.It is hard to get a good grade.

All the bad ratings are for the lab which she has nothing to do with! This class is super easy the exams are right from the slides and theres plenty of ways to get participation credit (including ways outside of class). She's great, the lab is hell

Honestly she's like fine ig she's just a big pushover and everyone used chat on her exams cause they're all online and she doesn't have proctors which was annoying. Also her lectures are basically just reading off the slides w/ some small additions so don't really need to go to class tbh. Participation activities were kind of just checking a box
Lectures are decent and exams are fair, nothing really special about her teaching but I dont think its as horrible as everyone says it is.

Her low rating is unfair. She's VERY straight forward & intelligent, its clear what you need to know, very willing to clarify what will be on exams. Exams are all MCQ, you need to put in effort as A&P itself is very difficult, but people take their frustration out on her by low ratings. 100% recommend taking her class she is amazing. #queenpeacock

True honesty, I think she gets a bad rep and she's overhated. Peacock is organized and clear on how she grades, and she gives so many resources to help study: lecture videos, free textbook, weekly, short, open note take-home quizzes, etc. I understand how the course in itself can be difficult once you find a study method it'll be worth it.

Honestly think she gets a bad rep but she's not that awful. As long as you make sure to stay on top of participation that will help boost your grade. Course had 4 midterm exams throughout the semester that were each 50 MCQ. Each midterm usually covered around 5 lecture topics, so usually studying a few days in advance would help.
I think she's being unfairly rated here. The exams are based solely on the lectures, and as long as you follow along, you'd be fine for the exams. It's very lecture-heavy, so be prepared to study.

I've really enjoyed Dr. Peacock and her course! You do have to do participation activities every week, but they're easy to do. Lectures are fairly easy to follow and she truly wants people to understand. Exams are mainly application, but its MCQ and she does review sessions the class before an exam. As long as you put in effort you'll be fine!

honestly a fair professor, exams are usually straight forward. A&P is a hard class which in general requires a lot of studying so if you put the work in its fine. my only thing is that sometimes she doesnt super clearly explain things, but she keeps a poll everywhere open so you can ask questions which i like.

Overall, your going to find yourself studying to survive, not to actually learn and retain the information which sucks. Tests are made to trick you, not for you to succeed. At first, it bothered me that students would cheat in order to pass her tests, and although I still believe it's wrong and wouldn't do it myself, I understood why.

Her slides makes it really easy to understand and is much better than the other professor, she makes the slides simple while the other professor copies off the online textbook and doesn't explain as clear as Professor Peacock. Take her class instead of the other professor

I loved this class and I loved having her as a professor. I don't know if she changed her style or the course but after having her for both 1 and 2 I think she's a great professor. Exams are straight forward and she gives you practice before each one including the final. If you actually study and put in the effort it's actually pretty easy

Idk why everyone hates her but she's great. I had her for both a&p 1+2. Her lectures are clear and straightforward and the exam was exactly her lectures. She provided a practice exam for every one on topics that students have the most trouble on. If you actually study it's really easy. I loved her class and truly didn't think it was bad at all

i don't think professor peacock's low rating is fair. as long as you pay attention to lectures, it is easy to do well. i never saw an exam Q that i had no clue how to answer. she gives a lot of options to do well (exams, participation, quizzes, etc). she was accommodating when i had to reschedule an exam for an emergency. highly recommend her.

While Professor Peacock is not the best professor I've ever had, she is certainly not the worst, and I think her rating on here is completely unfair. The course is hard, but I don't think her exams are unfair - all of the material you need to know is in her slides.

I dont think Dr. Peacock deserves the hate she gets. Class participation is required 2x per week. Exams are pretty difficult and more complex than the slides, but if you study its fine. People rating her badly are freshmen who have never taken a college class before. It's as difficult as any other STEM class. Don't be scared by her reviews.

Professor Peacock is a great professor! It is very doable to get an A in this class. Everyone who gave her a 1 or 2, did not try enough. In class she said PEOPLE SHOULD PUT IN EXTRA TIME FOR THIS CLASS. If you studied each lecture, meaning you did not just memorize, then you should be able to get an A in this class. I would take this class again!

The slides, which she reads straight off of, are too simple to make a student gain the complex knowledge required for her tests. I recommend skipping class and going through the slides slowly and chatgpt concepts that are unclear (which is most of it). Lectures feel like watching a teenager that prepared for the presentation the night before.

Dr. Peacock really just is too nervous to teach in a college setting. She seems to be very timid when she is teaching, causing her to just read from the slides in a monotone voice while never explaining any definitions. A free online textbook is provided but doesn't provide any help at all and isn't used.

Overall, Dr. Peacock is a good professor. Her tests were hard but doable & it helped to rewatch lectures and note-take on each lecture. Exams are weighted heavily but there is an opportunity for corrections and she factors in participation. FYI Lab is a different animal & somehow harder than the lecture course! I spent more time studying for lab...

lectures aren't the best; they provide the material but exams sometimes don't correlate and it seems like questions are purposely trying to trick you rather than test your understanding. reads straight off the slides even when answering questions. explains concepts in a very convoluted way. i think she is a good person, but not a good professor.

Peacock is the worst professor I've ever had. She doesn't communicate with students and either takes days to reply or doesn't respond at all. What we study in class is never reflected on the exams, making it difficult to prepare and succeed.

Dr. Peacock is a great professor and I think she explains the content really well and is super organized with the way she structures her class. It's anatomy so it's supposed to be hard but if you put in the time to memorizing you will do well. I think a lot of the complaints here come from the lab (which another professor runs...).

The real problem with A and P is the lab. This lab is the worst thing conjured from the depths of hell. The class so far is much easier. In the first month, you will have to memorize every part of every bone and muscle for humans AND rats. It's like learning a new language and the expectation is you become fluent within a month.

As a third year bio student, I think that these reviews are because this is a class that mostly first year nursing students take. Adjusting to college is HARD and I mean no hate at all- class felt impossible at first. But if you take time to figure out what study methods work for you, doing well in this class won't be a problem.

Overall, Dr. Peacock is a good professor. Her rating is unfounded on here. Taking A&P 2 with her over the summer wasn't really a challenge, as the material on the tests aligned well with the content taught in class. Engagement is key to performing well, and she makes expectations clear for content on the exams. Would take another class with her!

This class is definitely manageable. There are 4 non-cumulative tests, all multiple choice and you have plenty of time to answer the questions. My advice is too make sure you focus on the content on the slides. Be familiar with definitions and make sure that you really understand more complicated topics by searching supplemental content on youtube.

Took over summer 1, very easy class. Look over slides, exams all multiple choice, final is non cumulative. No homework besides weekly multiple choice quizzes with 3 attempts. Gives very few extra credit points. Memorize as much from the slides, not textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. P doesnt deserve the hate she gets! Had her for A&P 1+2 & loved her class. She does a great job at breaking down difficult topics. Her tests can be tricky but they test your knowledge & I aced them by studying slides+lecture content (focus on what she says when notetaking!). She cares & offers opps to boost ur grade (participation, team tests).

Ms. Peacock is an overall lazy teacher that explain complex concepts poorly. If you ask her to further explain something she will just read exactly what it says on the slide. Tests were entirely multiple choice and online, but she would hide the grades and not release them until a week after we took them which was very frustrating.

reviews.comment: Reads directly off of slides and rushes through content. Records all lectures but requires participation which wastes class time since this is a large lecture. I honestly pray for any one who takes this class. This class is extremely hard to pass unless you study extremely hard. I do not recommend her. reviews.comment: Utilize the textbook honestly cause all this professor does is read off of slides and not explain content in simple manner.

The class itself wasn't super hard but her exams made absolutely no sense at all. They were loosely based on our lectures but it goes way beyond them. (The question will touch on a topic but the answers make little to no sense). Her communication wasn't great and she didn't answer questions properly; she would direct you back to the slides.

Never seems to know what she's talking about and repeats the same concept like 3 times but in different ways making it hard to understand -she sometimes contradicts herself too. Lectures are lengthy but she speaks quickly. Exams are mostly based on what she says so make sure to take notes on that. She does record her lectures though. don't take her

Would basically just read from the slides, and if you asked her a curiosity question she probably wouldn't be able to answer it. The exams weren't too difficult though, and she made sure to provide practice exams before each one.

Lectures are garbage. If you have a question about a section you didn't understand, she will read off the slide again in the exact way she did the first time. reviews.comment: This is the only A&P teacher but my advice is to not slack on participation it can be the saving grace for your grade at the end of the sem. Weekly quizzes also act as grade savers in my opinion. She's not horrible but like you have to teach yourself everything so... Good luck!

Peacock does not know what she's teaching...you will have to teach yourself the topics because she overcomplicates them in lectures. Lectures are very excruciatingly heavy & the tests are nothing short of a nightmare. They are excessively difficult and fail to assess our understanding of the course material accurately. Teaching methods, grading practices, and test structures are simply atrocious. AVOID IF POSSIBLE!!!!

If you can, don't take this professor. She does not care about her students at all and only cares about her agenda and course content being "taught". I'd say avoid this professor but there's really no other choice. Grades were dictated by weekly quizzes & three assessments + an anatomy lab taught by a TA but much more immersing and enjoyable. All assessments MC which sounds easy but was actually difficult considering questions asked are often NOT covered by lectures and go beyond what is taught

I thought knew what I was getting myself into, but somehow it's so much worse. She has three tests throughout the semester and then the final, accounts for 90% of your grade. She talks (well more like reads off the slide) way too fast. She records all her lectures so you can stop showing up to lectures. If you can avoid it, don't take her.

Terrible professor. She reads directly off a powerpoint so most people don't go to class and she doesn't seem to care at all. Grade is based almost entirely on exams that are all multiple choice but the questions make no sense. This class is such an important concept but I have learned nothing because of her.

Dr. Peacock was an excellent professor.  Her lectures were well-paced and informative.  She was always willing to answer questions, and would even write down the question if she didn't know the answer to find the answer for you.  Her tests were somewhat difficult, but definitely doable if you show up to lecture (where she had practice questions).

reviews.comment: Professor Peacock is the most horrible and unprofessional teacher I've ever had. Each exam can make or break your entire grade so doing poorly on one tanks your grade. Professor Peacock is knowledge in Human Anatomy, but her class is structured in a way where students are not well benefited and a single bad grade on a test can make or break your grade. Sarah Peacock's lectures are oftentimes her reading off the slideshow, so showing up to class makes no difference in learning.

reviews.comment: This class was all lecture and she talked very fast. She would move on to the next slide when the whole class was still writing. This made it hard to learn any information. However that this class is very content heavy so I understand why she has to move quickly. But she was not confident in her speaking and just made lectures more confusing.

Class is basically only lectures and exams. Graded on three exams and one final that is partially cumulative. Exams are almost all application questions, and based on concepts that aren't on the slides but instead things she says aloud in class, so they're really hard if you aren't prepared. Just come to class and take notes on what she says.

Prof. Peacock seemed to be very knowledgeable but she mainly reads off the slides in addition to adding a ton of information quickly. I would advise writing every word because they tend to be asked in test questions. You are mainly graded on four exams, and weekly quizzes that are 10% of your grade. To do well, you need to dedicate a lot of time.

I honestly hated her class, her style of teaching is so difficult to learn, I literally get a seizure reading her exam questions--some straight up do not make sense. She only reads off lectures and talks way too fast to even understand. If you don't need to take her class for credit, please do yourself a favor and DON'T. #itwasbadformymentalhealth

reviews.comment: Prof. Peacock seems knowledgeable but the lectures are content-heavy with the occasional poll everywhere questions. The grade for the class is made up of 3 exams, the final, and weekly quizzes that do not get graded.

This class was hard as hell, and Professor Peacock did not seem confident when teaching. Lectures went super fast, and many things that were not on the slides but were said, were on the tests. No scale, and lack of empathy.

Prof Peacock speaks fast. She sounds like she is nervous when she is speaking to the class and it is hard to pay attention. Grade is determined by three exams+final. The final is 1/3 cumulative. The class/subject is not easy, but all material you need to succeed is given, so be diligent and you will do well (grade based mostly on four large exams, so be careful).

Seems like a nice lady just not a good professor. Unprofessional. When asked questions in class she says "ill write that down and get back to u" then NEVER does. majority of grade is 3 exams + final exam which is TOUGH. Exams are mostly applications based questions that are often tricky and way too difficult for an already tough class. dont take

reviews.comment: HOF professor. One of the kindest and most caring teachers I've had in high school or college. No midterms/finals in 2308 but still learned a lot through lectures, online quizzes, and group projects which were a lot of fun. 10/10 would take again.

Great person, not so great as a teacher. Often got confused on her own practice problems and spent the whole class trying to understand. Grade was based on problem sets, take home quizzes, and a project, no exams. Problem sets were very different from class, but she was very accessible by email. Easy A but need to put in effort to actually learn.

Professor Pfluger is a chemical engineer first, professor second. She is knowledgeable in her discipline, especially sustainability. The course had no exams, rather had group projects to apply knowledge in real-world scenarios. She was frequently unclear during lectures, but this improved significantly by the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She's very vague with directions and after 1st semester when we all did "too well" she started to grade us 10x tougher 2nd semester. She also warned my group that our final project might not work days before the semester ended and expects us to do months worth of work in less than two weeks. She also "teaches" intro coding, but can't do it herself.

I liked the class a lot because it was the easiest A ever. She is caring tbh. And a really easy grader. I was disappointed we did not do robots, but she still gave me good grades. She gave me a great start for engineering  here at NEU.

*sigh*. Pfluger is a very nice lady, but you don't want to be in her class. She has very little programming knowledge, and lectures like she's talking to a group of pre-schoolers. Ended up learning most everything on my own.
Take this class if you're okay with teaching yourself everything.

She is a very nice lady. I personally never needed her help with the programming part but her lectures were not very in depth and I'm sure I would have been confused without previous experience. She is a very easy grader, particularly if you get on her good side.  Easiest A of college so far.

Fun lady, can't teach. Class descrip. said no programming knowledge necessary, but she didn't give any lectures before throwing students into group projects (assigned groups; put people with no experience together intentionally- NOT HELPFUL). Errors in EVERY assignment resulted in HOURS of extra work. Incredibly disorganized, unclear expectations.

terrible teacher. awful turnaround time (1 month), arbitrary grading system (based on how much she likes you, didn't read reports fully), highly unprofessional (actually called a student's work "retarded" in front of the entire class), offers little to no clarification or help on assignments. doesn't understand the lab assignments she gives.

I really like Professor Pfluger, she's a lovely lady and she is always very helpful. However her group projects are a lot. But her classes are really engaging. I dislike evening classes but having it with her was quite nice.  I will recommend you take her!

Great person, not so great a teacher. She is very enthusiastic and and helpful. But it's very difficult to get a clear idea of what she wants. Easy grader for the most part and I would recommend her to future students.

Professor Pfluger is a great person and knows her stuff. Sadly, her stuff does not include knowing how to teach or give instructions that are helpful. She expects you to know what she wants without her telling you and has typos on 4 year old slides she still hasn't fixed, however if you make a typo its the end of the world.
Doesn't know a lot about computer programs. But many projects that sound hard do end up being fairly easy.
Very bad. Not interesting. And the attitude really made me upset. Never choose her again.

Professor Pfluger really doesn't know much when it comes to programming. I ask her what's wrong with my program and she doesn't know how to fix it.. to make things worse she is a really tough grader. Don't recommend taking her.
She is just a terrible grader! I am pretty sure if I had someone else I would get an A for that class.

SHE IS VERY UNPROFESSIONAL. I FEEL LIKE SHE IS JUDGING BASED ON HER FEELINGS. ALTHOUGH MATERIALS ARE VERY EASY, YOU HAVE TO DEAL WITH HER NONSENSE ATTITUDES. EASY MATERIAL, TOUGH LADY, NEVER CHOOSE HER.
Enthusiastic and nice. Not exactly easy, but pretty lenient. A is very possible if you put in effort.

Professor Thai is a really nice lecturer. But his class is so note-based. You need to be in class to take notes, or you don't know what he wanna present on his slides with pictures only. Since this is a history class, the exam is kinda subjective. Attendance is mandatory, one midterm and one final.

Professor Thai is a good, well-prepared professor. In order to follow along in the lectures, make sure to do the readings. The exams are 60% of your grade (midterm and final, 30% each), weekly quizzes are 20% of your grade (12 in total), and class participation matters.

reviews.comment: Professor Thai is a kind and smart teacher, but his class setup is not for me. Attendance is better than other classes, but still somewhat mandatory. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is just lovely. Class is straight forward and easy, and I did fine without reading the weekly readings. If u want to, you can skim them. He tries to get to know his students and memorizes everyone's name. He really is the best, if you have the chance to take this class take it. Tests are easy to study for and all the material is organized well.
Run!!! His quizzes are playing with languages!

Professor Thai is a good professor who always comes well prepared. The class isn't hard, but you do have to write a good amount of essays which are graded (way too harshly lol) by the TA's. But he gives lots of extra credit opportunities so your overall grade won't really suffer.

Professor Thai is just a really nice and caring person and pretty funny but in a weird way that only came out like once a week. 12 Weekly quizzes are fine and he dropped the 4 lowest. The TAs graded the essays but he reviewed them all and his final grade adjustments at the end were very nice. He was also always available after class and by email.

I 've learned a lot in his lectures on modern Chinese history. The classes are graded through four essays and a lot of weekly canvas quizzes. The essays are easy to get B+ or A- but very difficult to get an A on, so prepared to work hard in order to get an A. But overall, it was a very enjoyable class but do be prepared to work a lot.

reviews.comment: Professor Philip is a good man in person. He is very passionate about the subject and sometimes sounds 'sarcastic' too - mostly funny. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very engaging solid professor. Makes the material of the class very interesting. Beware of him calling on your if he sees you not paying attention in class, but doesn't do this often. Overall, clear grading criteria. Reading quizzes are relatively simple. Essays are fairly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor is nice. If you are not confident for your essay, you can go to his office hour and discuss the essay with him. He will provide about 1% extra credit. Quizzes are easyas long as you read, you can get 5/5 or 4/5.

He's knowledgable in the subject and open to questions & critique. Lecture and reading heavy. Weekly quiz with paper every 3 or so weeks (4 total). No final. Attendance is taken. I wouldn't suggest buying the textbook and you can get the books from the library. Decent, easy class to take and fill NUPath reqs.

Took Philip Thai for Law, Justice and Society in Modern China. He assigned a LOT of reading, and there were four 4-to-5-page papers due throughout the semester. Also had a couple short presentations, and you were expected to have done the long readings even in the weeks when you weren't writing a paper on them
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Best Professor Ever.  Gives great lectures, kind grader and extremely nice and funny.

His lectures are really engaging and you can really learn a lot by showing up to class, listening, and doing the readings! That being said you could definitely pass this class without touching a textbook by listening to his lectures , OR reading the textbook and not paying attention in class. He's funny and an easy grader. 10/10 would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have taken 2 courses with Professor Thai and he is one of my favorites. Getting an A is not easy but if you read, pay attention to what he asks for, and do the work it will pay off. He expects participation, you don't always have to talk but if you show up and he knows ur face and name that counts. Read the books because they are useful for tests

Really great professor. Goes out of his way to help students and makes lectures interesting. Also super hot. He gives out take-home practice exams and holds review sessions before tests. The only issue I had was that it can be a little hard to recognize places and names that are in Chinese, since they're often not pronounced the way they're spelled
So. Hot. But married (can't catch a break) A little impersonal, but a respectable and fair professor

Great lecturer who can make a dry subject interesting. Exams were all in-class, but he gave us the possible prompts ahead of time. His TA helped grade the exams and was fairly lenient. Some of the readings can be dense and boring, but I did not need to read all of them to do well in the class.

Professor Thai is a wonderful lecturer! Exams are all short answeressay questions, and he gives us the possible questions ahead of time. Lots of readings, but I rarely ever read them (sometimes skimmed) and went to review sessions (which filled me in on the readings). Going to lectures alone is enough to do well. Generous grader.
Felt like he really cared about the learning, really unstructured in a good way. allowed everyone to get what tehy wanted out of teh class.

Hanser has had an extremely accomplished and experienced career in Energy economics. The class itself was a bit useless, as he makes students present the topics. But, anytime he speaks to correct an issue or add an anecdotal example, it was simply brilliant. Grading was based on two things, your presentation and a 10 page long research paper.
