Very caring professor, will always answer your questions and help. GO TO ALL THE LABS. Its literally just attendance credit, class however is not mandatory I went to like 2 maybe the whole semester. But make sure you learn on your own if you do not go, you need to know stuff for the periodic skill tests. No real exams tho.
Rush is the best!!! He is so caring and it's clear that he loves computer science.

Picked him because of good reviews and he seemed nice at first, but he's extremely passive aggressive. Power-trippy too (told me “say thank you” after helping). Arbitrarily accuses students of cheating and reports them to OSCCR. I think he enjoys doing it. Genuinely think he had it out for me. Class is easy, but take it with literally anyone else.
Amazing lecturer, amazing professor, always willing to help students during class, responds to emails and is just a really funny guy in general. You will love any class if you take it with him!
hes so sweet like so uwu but he dont play about his class its not hard at all if u pay attention in lecture and understand the material

Terrible professor. Unclear lectures, unhelpful guidance, and an friendly classroom vibe. The content wasn't the problem it was his nature and structure.If you can I highly recommend going with any other professor so you can be in an uplifting learning environment where you feel encouraged to learn.

Seemed like a nice and helpful professor at first but don't be fooled by the facade. Truly in my 3 years at college he is one of the worst professor I have had he's super passive aggressive and genuinely doesn't care about anything other than his tangents on the class code. I genuinely believe I could have 100% done a better job teaching myself.

he seemed super nice at first but later on it became abundantly clear that he is a terrible lecturer, and doesn't give any actual practice. he also arbitrarily accuses MULTIPLE students of cheating during skills. wished the T would hit me every time i went to his class it was genuinely so boring and i could have learned the entire thing on my own.

Two tests and ~7 homework assignments. Your lowest homework grade will get dropped but homework is worth like 80% of your grade so make sure you perfect your code. He really cares about his students and is willing to help you if you go to office hours or talk to him after class. Cool dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rush is very caring and so passionate about the topic. I feel like things could have been explained in a simpler way at times, but that being said, data science is not my strength. Be prepared for challenging homeworks - getting a Knack tutor will change your life. Thought I was going to fail this class and ended up with a 100.8. I recommend!
5 % extra credit if u attend class. Hes great at explaining and is very understanding

Best professor I could have asked for DS2000. You get up to 5% extra credit just for going to class, and overall teaches concepts extremely well, albeit lectures not being very needed since he posts code after class. Extremely caring as well; it felt like you could tell him anything. You can't go wrong with taking his class!
By far the best professor I've had here. Very caring and accommodating, and his lectures are genuinely interesting.

I wish we had spent less time recapping DS2000 and more time on the new, more complex/difficult material. I wish this were 65 minutes instead of 100 - really hard to absorb everything you learn in one sitting of the longer classes. A kind professor who is passionate about the material. Clearly cares very deeply about his students - take his class!
Really awesome and kind professor. Made learning how to code so fun and manageable. Made us feel empowered to code and learn. Lectures were great.

I liked Rush and the lectures were solid. This course is surprisingly graded by few things as we only had 4 homework assignments in addition to a couple PPP and Lab assignments. Overall this was good and besides getting marked off for a couple silly things (imo) I had a good time and learned stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truth be told I am not the smartest student but rush was the most amazing and supportive professor. Always available to help and I ended the class with an A which was shocking to me
Such a great professor, really cares about the subject and tries to make lectures interesting. Assignments are not easy but not too difficult, you really learn a lot through this course.

Rush is really kind and tries his best to explain certain concepts. The courseload is managed by someone who creates the curriculum for all sections, so you'll have a lot of work no matter what professor you take. You only have one assignment per week, but it takes a while. There are textbooks, but you'll be fine if you don't read them

A really good teacher and a even better person. Grades are based off homework and weekly online open note quizzes. Homework gets difficult very fast (5th week in). If you're lucky the TA grading your homework won't be too harsh. Class consist of intro to a new topic and shows how to use it for homework. Homework on avg took me 8 hours to finish.
He is great - very outgoing and easy to understand his lectures. He is easily accessible outside of class and is a wonderful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tony is a great professor. The his exams are often challenging. The final was extremely hard, nearly impossible and I felt unprepared, even with weeks of studying. You don't practice as much in terms of solving problems in class as I wished and was more lecture focused. He does often go off script and talk about himself for long periods of time.

Tony is a funny and decent guy, but he seems tired of teaching and just wants to talk to his students about his life. The material wasn't too hard for me to learn on my own, so that is what I would suggest. Would take again if I had to. Go to class if you want to hear funny anecdotes mixed with an outdated slideshow.
Exams were challenging but if you do the textbook problems (and I mean DO ALL of them) you can get an A. Go up to the board because you will need a good participation grade to get a good grade.

Great guy. He goes over exactly what is on each exam beforehand, question by question. Offers lots of office hours. Go to them he's very helpful. Accessible over text + email
Exams seemed like people either did really well, or did poorly, not much in between. When he asks people to write problems on the board, make sure u study that for the exams

Love this guy. Honestly one of the most fair professors I've ever had. If you do the work that's required you'll definitely succeed in the class. Taking his class again next semester and I can't wait!

I loved Tony's class so so much, you can tell he cares about his students and is funny and witty when giving his lectures, he even went out of his way to do extra study sessions when we needed it. I highly recommend his lectures if you get to! I haven't gotten the final back yet but I really think he was great!
He can't really explain concepts properly and it was a lot of self study required. He usually just reads off the textbook during his lectures.

Tony was the best. 

I really appreciated how he would have us work through problems together, and help prepare for exams. 

I found him really funny, even if some people think he comes off a bit abrasive, but it's always with the best intentions and a good heart. 

He cares about his students and wants them to succeed (and show up to class).

Tony is one of the coolest teachers I've ever had. The lectures are very laid back and he talks about his experiences in Accounting which is very interesting. He prepares you very well for the quizzes and tests

He just read off of slides & made us complete problems in class, so I had to teach myself most of the course, but this seems to be the case across ACCT1201 courses and he seems to be one of the better profs. 25% of the grade is the midterm and 30% is the final, which both had a ~70 average. Barely got an A. He's funny though and accessible for help

Tony is a great guy but his teaching style was something I personally wasn't a fan of. Attendance isn't mandatory which was nice but if you miss class then you will definately be lost. He reads off the slides which I am not a fan of and it forced me to teach myself most of the course. But he is really easy to reach and helps students out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gets side tracked a lot and most of his classes were of him yapping. However, he is nice guy and average professor. In my opinion, If you actually want to learn accounting I would go for someone else tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HE IS SO FUNNY AND KIND AND CARING. Literally, even though I didn't participate much in class, he still knew and asked if I understood the lecture or had any problems. He cares about his students and being in his class is truly the best thing ever because I can't stop smiling at whatever he is talking about. Please participate, dont make him sad!!!

Tony the goat, he's super funny. All the bad reviews are from liberals who hate the fact that he's republican. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you should show up so you don't fall behind, his lectures are funny and essentially 2/3 of the classes are just practice review problems. GOATTTTT
Tony was a great professor. Class was very relaxed, and he was a fairly lenient grader.

in the beginning I didnt like him as most of the lectures consisted of him reading off the slides but overtime he started to grow on me. Reading the chapters before class is needed to not be behind. OFFICE HOURS, will help him get to know you and he teaches way better one on one.

best professor i've ever had, super likable, funny, knowledgeable, and caring, the material can be overwhelming but he is very accessible and can help you with anything you need, easy A as long you put in the effort
Working in accounting knows his stuff! If you are nice to him he reciprocates, go to office hours. Great Italian/American guy who makes accounting fun with stories.

Tony was a good professor who made the lectures engaging with funny stories mixed in the lessons. The quizzes were tough, but the homework so far has been very doable along with the readings. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but it helped a lot with understanding the concepts.

Tony is an amazing professor who somehow found a way to make financial accounting bearable at 8 in the morning. One thing about him is that he will NOT hesitate to cold call you, but you do get to opt out of his calling if you really want to. Attendance isn't mandatory but I HIGHLY recommend you go since his lectures are the funniest in the world.

He's a solid professor with an excellent background in accounting. He knows managerial can be tedious, but he made the class enjoyable with his fun accounting and off-topic stories. He's super reliable and has so many opportunities for office hours, and if you're scared about what's on the tests, just ask him. He's super transparent about it.

He's a classic old school italian who has a lot of experience in the field, doesn't take crap, and will make the most boring stuff tolerable and even entertaining. I couldn't have taken managerial accounting with another professor.
Decent teacher and really funny guy. Let him teach tax!
Tony is a great professor. Managerial is a boring class; he understands that, and he manages to make it tolerable with his stories and humour. He is a fair grader and wants everyone to do well.

Tony is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern and is very knowledgable from his industry experience. He makes a dull class tolerable with his funny commentary and off topic discussions. Tony is always available outside of class and is very transparent about what will be on tests.

Tony is a cool dude, If you want to pass the class go to the office hours and do the homework.If you want to know what to expect on the midterm and the final literally just ask him, and he will tell you about each question. Read and go to lecture. He push due dates, attendance is not needed but he likes people who come.If you have questions ask him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tony is a good professor who makes class interesting with funny remarks and real-life examples of accounting. He does tend to get sidetracked which can feel like a waste of time, but overall a great professor with clear and manageable expectations who will help students succeed.

He's got amazing accounting skills but no teaching skills whatsoever. Half of class is taken up by his random thoughts which are sometimes offensive and inconsiderate. The other half of class is used for going over slides or textbook problems, which is helpful if you pay attention. Exams are normally just questions straight from the book.

Makes extremely inappropriate comments in class. Doesn't know what's going on with the class in terms of projects or Homework (class would have been impossible without the TAs so shoutout to them). Quizzes are super hard. Don't take a class with him.

Tony is a nice guy, but his class is not good. I didn't put enough effort into this class until it was too late, however it is a tough class regardless and the exams are super difficult unless you're a god at accounting. He also assigns way more HW than other accounting profs. I would recommend someone else. Also his sense of humor is outdated.

everyone who's saying that he's funny is 100% white. he makes so many inappropriate racist, sexist, and homophobic jokes. he confused me for another asian girl in the class who i look nothing like and called her "jasmine" as a joke. i stopped attending class bc i couldnt stand his jokes anymore but the textbook should be enough to pass.

So many people praise him for his humor, sure he's funny but he's an awful prof, TA office hours were filled with just his students, the Final average was a 69% in his class WITH the curve, he randomly calls on students to come up to the board to do problems on stuff we just learned, dozens of people, including myself, were in office hours daily
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Such a hard class but nobody better to teach it. I would suggest taking notes on the connect homework since having the option to pick random answers and check if they're correct made me not learn a lot from the connect but it's still a good tool. Also take notes in class and on the slides, Tony explains it better than the textbook.

Tony is a great Professor. Be ready to answer questions in class. His office hours are very helpful and he explains topics well if you need help. Make sure to read the book and do well on all your homework. Mid term and Final are worth a lot of your grade so these are good for a buffer. He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed.
I have never met a teacher who cares as much as Tony. He is hilarious and wants all students to succeed. He likes to move fast so I would recommend seeing a TA once a week.

Tony is easily the best professor I've ever had at Northeastern. He's super funny and his class is really engaging. He also knows a lot about accounting but explains it in a way that makes sense to those who don't. He really takes the time to make a personal connection with his students and it shows. Please, do yourself a favor and take this class.
Tony is such a good professor! Explains the material very well and supplements it with real world stories and a great personality! Pay attention in class and read the textbook and you will get an A.

Tony's a great guy, he cares a lot about his students. He cracks a lot of jokes that some find insensitive, but if you get past it, he's a genuine guy who loves accounting and has a great understanding of the subject. If you pay attention and just do the homework, you'll get an A.

Tony is my favorite Professor at Northeastern. He is very helpful and will make sure you know the material if you show interest in wanting to do well. It is important to participate in class. Still love to chat with him outside class to this day!

He is extremely demeaning and very vocal if you mess up a problem in front of the class. Considering that the class is for students taking a minor in business, I think he is too harsh and the lectures are not cohesive or helpful. CRAZY difficult exams. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS if you expect someone helpful and understanding.

You dont actually have to buy the textbook because the powerpoint slides of each chapter explain everything really well and draw from the book. Prof Russo is a really cool guy and makes you not dread going to an 8am class. I thought I wouldnt like accounting but Tony made it seem fun. 2 exams, 2 online quizzes, 10 required hw, cumulative final.

Absolutely phenomenal professor. He knows absolutely everything about accounting, explains it very well, and is always open to questions. Class is completely chill, just get your work done and youre fine. Tests are only an issue if youre a slacker because Russo will give you everything you need.
Brilliant guy. Just show up to class and study the material.
Just attend class, understand the material and do the homework. You will be guaranteed an A in the class.

I really enjoyed this class. His grading is very fair. He does expect you to work, but is extremely approachable and with help with any questions. He adds humor and real life experiences to his class. Northeastern needs to hire more professors like him.

He doesn't really teach but expects people to know every detail in the textbook for quizzes and exams. Offers extra help, but homework problems have little to do with what's on the tests, since they're only MC and T&F. Choose a better prof if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Guy is a great actual accountant, but a terrible professor. He told me he hasn't given an "A" in 3 years. I was consistently the top student in the class and that was because I spent a ridiculous amount of time reading the book. He doesn't teach well and just expects you to know the material.
Definition of a goofy guy. Michael know how to balance the line of work and play. Ma boy also gender neautral af luh you Prof Ruff, would love to light one up w you foo

Took him summer 1 and he's very nice and understanding. If you need extra time for an assignment and email him beforehand, he will give it to you. His lectures are good and he's just a nice dude in general. The material itself is hard but he is very helpful.
One of the nicest human beings on the planet. Seriously. He cares so much about his students. He's a terrific professor. I would highly recommend going to office hours.

His class is half lecture on the slides he posts to canvas and half exercises from the packet he hands outs. He's got chicken stratch handwriting and his lectures can be boring but he's a nice guy. I found connect homework to be helpful. Connect quizzes (online)(10%). Connect homework (15%), midterm (20%), Final exam (30%).

Took this class online and everything was extremely organized. You knew exactly what you needed to do and all the assignments given were incredibly useful in terms of preparing for an exam and learning the material.

My class was full with 35 students and after 3 classes it dropped down to 8, then after that it was me and two other students. I am only taking the class because it fulfills a requirement, but given the chance I would have dropped too. Very disorganized class, disrespectful professor, unrealistic expectations. AVOID IF YOU CAN.

My class started with 35 students and is down to 3 after the add/drop deadline. He gives homework like the class is a full-time job, his Canvas is so confusing, and he's overly particular over every assignment detail. He's kind of sexist, snide and not very professional. Good luck to the remaining three in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I didn't even make it through 3 sessions before dropping. He is very all over the place and the canvas is super disorganized. I would warn you to not take a class with him, it will not be a pleasant experience. We started with a class of 35 students, and after 2 sessions it was down to 8 students because everyone had dropped the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor is so passive aggressive. Will personally call you if you don't show up to class. Jumps from topic to topic and expects you to read up to 400 pages per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had. Rude, unprofessional, and makes inappropriate remarks. Comes across as sexist and demeaning to girls while much more respectful to boys in the class. Doesn't lecture so much as rambles for class period. Class trajectory confusing, and assignments lack clear outlines or instructions. Tests confusing.

Worst professor I've ever had. Although he is very knowledgable in his field, he does not know how to teach. Very rambly/unorganized lectures and encourages class participation but interrupts/laughs at students when they speak. Often gave sassy/unprofessional remarks towards students. Assigns homework as if this is the only course you're taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Requires a lot of in-class participation (definitely not a class for introverts). Doesn't give clear expectation on grading criteria for any assignments. Unorganized lectures, but you can tell that he is knowledgable. Can't teach. There are a lot of readings in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You will immediately get the impression that he is very knowledgeable in his field. That is the only good thing about him. He is very poor at lectures, he jumps from idea to idea with little clarity with no slides or visuals. On assignments, he micromanages the littlest detail, while providing no real rubric or expectation of the final product.

Knowledgable but lectures were incredibly disorganized. Midterm debate and final Foreign Market Entry project. Interrupted constantly during both. FME was interesting, you can choose your country and firm. Most of the knowledge I gained form this class was just from reading the textbook and personal research during projects, not from the lectures.

Disorganized and rambling lectures. Final project is a presentation/paper, both of which have little to no firm guidance and were micromanaged the whole second half of the semester. Will interrupt during presentations and while students speak. Despite obvious knowledge of the subjects, is unable to convey anything clearly without overcomplicating.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely pretentious and full of himself. Always interrupts students and all of his lectures are extremely unorganized. His assignments are never clear and then he gets upset when they are not to his standard. He goes off on random tangents during lectures, assigns so many readings and never talks about any of them in class. Don't take his course.

No homework, no projects, take home tests and quizzes. The final is also take home but we were not given a lot of time to complete it so it hurt my grade. She's done research in what she teaches and the topics you learn and cool.

This is actually for EXSC1120 but it wasn't an option to select. Has an accent so kinda hard to understand and talks quick. Slides are messy, Canvas is a hot mess, and some of the quiz question wording was absolute nonsense. All exams/quizzes were online, but if it was in person the class average would probably tank. Recommend use outside sources.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Li is great.  She is talented and funny when delivering the lectures.  She is fair for grading, always offering  bonus credits in tests.  If you study, you'll get good grades.  I'll take her courses again.

Has an accent that makes it sometimes hard to understand what she is saying, she talks super fast so just record her lecture and try to catch up at home. Her exams are not fair tbh she ask questions about things that are mentioned once and not in slides. you wont get an A unless you use other stuff for exams. She is not that great with tech.
Dont ask him for extra help all he's gonna do is call you r$tarded and threaten to kick you out of the MSA program if you are struggling. Just stay quiet and take your B

Tim subtly called some students in the class stupid.
Regarding his four final exam "review" sessions: held at strange times, therefore difficult to attend all. He taught new information that appeared on the final, but made the attending students promise to refuse to share any details about the new topics taught with classmates who could not attend.

Please take his class, you'll learn a lot and he's one of the best professors out there (he's funny too)! It's fast-paced with a lot of content but Tim holds your hand the entire way and makes sure you understand the content. You don't really need a textbook, if you do all his modules and practice problems, but it's helpful for assignment 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I asked for help on an assignment and he pretty told me to figure it out. Not very considerate of student needs especially when it is a busy time for us.
He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is caring, passionate and brilliant!
Excellent professor!  Absolutely one of the best!
Just Amazing!
Prof. Rupert was our sub-prof in the undergraduate tax class for a couple of weeks and he was excellent. Great review sessions & easy to understand. Made Taxes fun to learn. Excellent professor!
one of the best professors ever. make sure you study what he gives you and you're all set!
No Comments
Excelent teach. Makes a boring topic interesting and devotes a lot of time to his students. He wants everyone to learn and is one of the best professors i've ever had

Tim is by far the most helpful, clever, & fun Prof.I have had in my 6 years of schooling.  Tim finds time on the weekend to help his students and plays no favs. His students leave his class with knowledge in a subject that most prof. will put you to sleep

He is a very chill professor, but his lectures were not always helpful, as he just writes stuff on the chalkboard without really explaining the reasoning behind it, and his handwriting is extremely messy. The exams are not too bad as long as you prepare effectively, and he is very lenient with partial credit on the short-answer questions.

Great professor. The material is difficult, you have to pay attention in class and take your time on the homework. Prof Mike is really sweet, cares about his students, if you participate once in a while he will really like you. His handwriting is really bad, but besides that the class is awesome! Highly recommend.

Prof Mike is incredibly sweet, yet unfortunately he's unable to stay on topic during classes and is the stereotypical "chalkboard professor" to a fault. He gives no study guides or practice exams, and the tests are nothing like the homework and almost always like the work done in class, so if you actively participate, you'll be golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a chiller, kind and sweet guy.

He is Very nice person, he is doing well in preparing all the materials in the class, but he does NOT know how to teach you the train of thought.He will just write down the answer on the assignment and barely explain it at all. There is a gap between teaching and homework

I took the Summer 1 asynchronous online course for ACCT 1201. I have attended his online office hours. He tries his best to help the students, despite the challenges of the online course. He supports the students through constant reminders and office hours. If you make an effort to try in the course, he will reciprocate.

Prof Mike is great! The way the class is structured you only need to do homework once a week pretty much. The content can be confusing, but he does a decent job at explaining each topic well, as well as talking through problems. Make sure you participate!! He is a fair grader, and if you stay decently on top of your work you will do really well

A genuinely sweet, caring, kind professor. He loves when you participate, even when you aren't correct. Sit near the front/participate often and he will know your name. Sometimes a bit monotone/boring, but I'd take him again. Try and read textbook before class and following lecture will be easy. Lots of practice problems done in class to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice but does NOT know how to teach. Really boring lectures and does not offer support to students. Really tedious in class work and he will cold call you. Attendance is mandatory and do not sit in the front row he spits

Prof Ruff is a great person and for his age taught the class well, however if you don't pay attention for a little bit you can fall behind easy. His handwriting is unreadable at times which is inconvenient because he spends most of the lecture writing on the chalkboard. Even with all that said, I would still say take his class. Great guy!

Professor Ruff is a great guy and cares about his students. The quizzes are online, multiple choice, and open note. He does not curve individual assignments, but is a generous grader and curves final course grades. He is not the best lecturer, but appreciates you going into office hours which helps.

Not the best at lecturing or explaining the actual concepts, but very caring and understanding. He gives a lot of extra credit if you participate and practice resources, but most of the actual learning has to be done but the student. Really nice guy but he should probably retire.

Very kind and funny professor, made class very entertaining and manageable. Only two major tests the entire semester so you truly have to study hard on those because they make up 50% of the final grade. Overall very good professor and very generous grader. My advice would be to do the optional hw assignments, extra credit, and use his office hours.

Overall, Michael Ruff is a very kind person who will work with you. He is very knowledgeable in accounting but is not great at teaching concepts. He tends to speak over his students and doesn't answer specific questions. If you are not great with conceptual learning I would recommend a different teacher.

Ruff is very caring and teaches the material well. Gives a lot of chances for extra credit. Only issue is the group project (10% of grade), but he also is very receptive with issues with groups. The course is very test heavy, with about 50% of your grading riding on 2 tests (20% midterm 30% final). Grading is pretty favorable too.
Stay away, there are better ACCT profs. than him
he is so funny and teaches so good
Fair grader. Enough extra credit opportunities. Submit hw and quizzes on time.

I absolutely love this professor. I really struggled with the course, but he was always available whenever I wanted to meet to discuss my quizzes/homework support. He also offered extra assignments that definitely helped me understand the material on top of the lectures/problems in class. There is a group project that will require excel knowledge!

Mike is the best! He is the sweetest professor and truly cares about all of his students, even the ones that don't participate. His lectures are very basic and easy to follow so you don't ever feel lost, and he's always willing to meet outside of class, even just to chat! He's easily my favorite professor at Northeastern, highly recommend.

Had this guy for asynchronous classes and can confidently say after seeing about 4 videos of him, I already love him. He is the sweetest, kindest guy, the kind of guy you could never be mad at. Already love him. He talks slowly, but I can put the video in 2x speed so it's easier to get through.10/10 Would rate again.

Prof Ruff tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed. If you do the homework, study for quizzes and exams, and ask questions when necessary, you'll do fine. If you put in some extra work, you'll do great. He is nice, and is understanding if you have any problems. I find his lectures to be very helpful. Do the optional assignments!

As many have said, Accounting in itself is not an easy one. But Prof Ruff helps you understand the material. Do your homework, LearnSmart, etc and you will pass. Going through end of chapter exercises will really help in quizzes/exams. Engage as much as you can during class! Prof Ruff is someone who genuinely cares for those who are keen to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His class was by far my favorite and he goes out of his way to make it more interesting. He also wants you to do well and if youve put in the work hell try his best to get you a high grade.

Professor Ruff was funny and easy to understand which made Accounting a lot more interesting than I thought it could be. He says that students are expected to read the textbook and spend many hours outside of class. I didn't do this and ended up doing fine. The final is very hard so get ready for that.

Professor Ruff is very caring to his students and has a lot of experience in his field. During class he does practice problems but its up to the student to teach yourself the material. The homework takes a long time to complete, and exams and quizzes are quite difficult, but Professor Ruff is pretty flexible.

This was the hardest class I took last semester, and the exams are difficult. The online class heavily relied on the textbook which was confusing at some points if you have not taken a previous accounting class. However, Professor Ruff is extremely caring, does a great job answering any questions you may have, and is flexible.

This class was SO HARD, but Professor Ruff is truly the most caring Professor ever. Hell do anything to help you understand concepts-he even stayed on an office hour zoom call with my friend for 2 hours to make sure she understood the concept. He replies to emails super fast, and is super understanding about the pandemic and your other classes.

I took this course during the pandemic online. Professor Mike is a really nice professor, though his course is extremely tough! You need to read every chapter carefully, so you are able to do homework and quizzes. There are few assignments that are optional, but they are good practice for exams. Exams are tough, so better prepare for it!
Ruff makes the intro classes very fun and I would recommend him for any accounting classes. He acknowledges the comical nuance with a lot of the material and manages to make it interesting

Most students in my class did ok. However, I usually studied acct1201 with angry tears in my eyes. The midterm and final were SO hard. I realized that I wouldn't receive an A grade right after the midterm. The quizzes were 10 MCs so be prepared. Email him, talk to him, he's very inspirational and thoughtful. Put in some work and you will be fine.

One of the most caring professors I've ever had. He sees the best in every student, and seriously wants us all to understand the material & do well. Accounting will never be the easiest or most fun class to attend, and he teaches the tough classes which I don't think he gets enough credit for. He will go to the ends of the earth for u to succeed.

Professor Ruff is a solid choice. His class can be difficult at times, but his lectures are very easy to follow and you can tell he really wants everyone to learn. He always mentions when he is accessible outside of class and gives clear expectations about what is due. The homework assignments are an easy 100 and he gives lots of time to do them.

Prof. Ruff really cares. He is super responsive to emails and is available when you need him. He curves with the attendance/participation grade, so be sure to participate and ask questions. He wants you to do well & visit the TAs too! Weekly homework, 4 quizzes each 5MCQ, 1 test &the final, and the project are grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Respectfully, Professor Ruff is one of my least favorite professors I've had at NU. He isn't very kind, doesn't do a good job of helping students understand the material, and the tests are extremely difficult. Overall not a nice guy. Can be rude to students.

Professor Ruff is a great guy and a fair teacher. He has a lot of experience in accounting and gives good lecture; however, the majority of your learning will need to be done outside of class through the very long homework assignments or TAs. The quizzes and exams are tough and require a lot of studying and the online textbook is not the best.

One of the nicest professors I've had. Gives a lot of practice problems which are super helpful in understanding the material. 4 quizzes, each are 10 mc's, which can pull down your grade. Always holds office hours and makes sure he can reach students if needed. I wasn't the best at accounting but still loved him as a professor

Literally the nicest professor I've had here at NEU. Definitely cares a lot about his students and how well they're doing in class. All this being said, he isn't the BEST at explaining content, but the class is primarily reading the chapters so mostly independent studying. Participate in class and he'll help you out on your final grade!

Prof Ruff is a super nice teacher and really cares about his students. He is very reasonable and listens to his students. The homework can sometimes take a few hours and make you want to tear your hair out. His tests are pretty tricky and his lectures are very boring. My best advice is to practice the problems he gives you in class over and over!

Prof Ruff is definitely one of the kindest and most caring professors I've ever had. His lectures aren't the most engaging and can sometimes be confusing, but when asked questions he takes time to make sure you fully understand the material. The class itself is difficult but he's a fair grader and tries to give you as many points as possible

Ruff is your typical dad accountant making stupid jokes that he himself laughs at for a good minute. He teaches by doing many examples on the board (sometimes theyre hard to keep up with) and giving powerpoints. Tests are reasonable, doesn't curve though. Also, homework is long and tedious on an online textbook but is great practice for tests/quiz.
Prof. Ruff is a very kind person and really cares about his students,  attendance is mandatory. He is willing to explain any of your confusion... about the course. Highly recommend.

Accounting is not easy in itself. Ruff's class seems engaging and requires a lot of attention. Professor tries to be as clear as possible while explaining the material. However, his quizzes and exams are hard! He is a tough grader. You will need to participate as much as you can and attend his office hours to get some extra points in order to pass!

As has been said Ruff is a cool guy, but that doesn't excuse what was/wasn't taught in his class. His lectures are clearly stock from McGraw Hill and he does a poor job of conveying the messages and, by extension, he does a poor job teaching the material. I learned 99% of my accounting this semester from Youtube despite paying to learn in class...

This is accounting and it's not easy. Ruff is a great guy like everyone says, but his exams and quizzes hard. The book is useless for learning and connect can only help you so much. He gives projects and hw (unlimited tries) to balance grades. The final exam is extremely hard, be prepared to study a lot. You can survive the class, wont be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor ruff, is overall a great guy. However, he is a really tuff grader. His exams, while mainly multiple choice are extremely hard. I attended every class, went to office hours and saw the TA and still struggled.  He over complicates the subjects and is heavily power point based.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's one of the nicest professors I've had, but he's very strict when it comes to participation and attendance. He cares about his students and wants you to do well. Accounting is a tough class but he makes it bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof Ruff is a great dude, not the best teacher by any means, but a great guy. If you haven't taken accounting beforehand or you don't learn by reading the textbook outside of class, this class - despite Ruff being a good guy - is a hard pass. He's a tough grader for how little he actually conveys in class and the homeworks aren't even relevant.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is funny and caring to his students. You can tell that he tries hard to make people love accounting. This class requires you to read the book before class as he tends to go through stuffs quickly. He cares about his students a lot so he will try really hard to help you to understand the knowledge so make sure you reach out to him via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: While Ruff is hilarious and a good guy on the whole, if you haven't taken accounting prior to this class, then this class isn't worth your time. He's a tough grader, he gives no partial credit (on multiple choice questions that require a ton of work), and on the whole he's just not the best at conveying the material to the class.  Great guy though.

Prof Ellis was a very engaging lecturer who values student participation (prepare for him to cold call on people!). He's relatable, funny, and approachable if you have questions. There were several short-term group projects that you'd complete mostly in class over 1-2 days and then present.
I loved him. He cares about content and students and manages to be fun and educational at the same time. Great class (Comm 2501)

Wonderful professor. Very dad-like, makes jokes that nobody gets sometimes. Hard grader tho, definitely not an easy A class. Lots of readings, and it gets awkward when the whole class doesn't read and he asks people questions. WOULD TAKE AGAIN 100% THO.

The class is fine apart from one thing, the professor thinks it is ok to assign students a major group project on a Thursday and expect a full fledged 15-minute presentation on Monday. Our group spent many hours on a Sunday (the only day we were all free from work, sports, extracurriculars, etc.) to finish this. This occurs three times a semester.

Ellis is simply just the best prof I have had at NU. He really cares about students, offers to meet outside class time, and just wants the best for us. The course content is unbelievably relevant to today's world which makes it that much more interesting. Cannot recommend this class enough. Tests are hard and lots of reading, but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His class was just great. I can't recommend it enough -- I learned a lot and Ellis is just a good guy.

Dr. Ellis taught remotely this semester. He managed to teach a great course despite only having synchronous meetings once a week. There was a decent to high amount of reading, but the lectures tied in all outside reading very well. He showed himself to be a generous professor and understood that his students have lives outside of his class. 10/10.

A semester-long research paper. He provides benchmark due dates to keep you on track and meets with you one on one after each section. He works with you to write the best paper, considering your interests and give extensions if needed so you can write your best Lectures are great as the content is interesting and he is funny and a wonderful speaker
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Ellis is very nice, however, his class is almost entirely lecture-based and he randomly calls on people all class, every class. Don't come to class and not expect to participate, he makes sure everyone speaks at least once each class. There's a lot of reading but the content is interesting. Tests are almost entirely writing-based.

Excellent teacher, really engaging and makes you want to learn. What he expected work-wise was very fair, and is conscious of how busy we are during finals. Make sure to do the readings he assigns: they're not too time-intensive, are mostly interesting, and are important for active class participation. Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: Good Professor, lots of class discussion

ok disclaimer: i DID take this class five entire yrs ago so this review is probably a little rusty the class has presumably evolved since then, however with that being said!! literally the best class of my life. genuinely the closest i have ever come to feeling true joy in an academic setting. prof cordell if youre reading this id take a bullet 4 u
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super incredibly liberal one sided assignments and articles. I myself am a liberal and think the class is not only ridiculously liberal, but unfairly one sided. Nice guy though
Maness' lectures were so boring, I would not take another one of his classes.

Ryan Maness is lazy. He missed more classes than assigned, and was boring when there. He offers plenty of office hours, but does not help throughout them, advising us to "look at the book," typically. You only get graded on the midterm, final, and a paper, but given how poorly he teaches, don't expect too much ease (though he is an easy grader).
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a fine professor, bit confusing and his lectures are boring. but it's stats so its not really his fault. He really appreciates you coming to office hours, gives extra credit for it. tests are straight forward, homework isn't graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are weekly reading analyses and the readings are usually long, but he's a pretty easier grader. Because this is his area of expertise, this is a much better class than the others he teaches and you learn a LOT. Exams are take home papers so it's not too hard a class if you are willing to put in the time.

Really nice guy, extremely approachable. Classes are absolutely a joke/unnecessary. Read the book and go to his office hours where he is incredibly helpful. Other than that, tests are pretty straightforward memorization. Not too bad, would recommend for Quantitative Techniques.

He knows what he's talking about, but the class is pretty boring and it's hard to pass the tests when you're not really learning anything. He would be there if I asked for help but the class is so drawn out and monotonous that I don't really know what to ask.

Professor Woodside was a great professor. The negotiation was great, and the group project was not too bad. Her tests were very weird (heavy on the multiple choice and just not a lot of points up for grabs). Additionally, the tests were not a good representation of the learning from the class. Very interesting class to take, but don't expect an A.

The professor is organized, but the teaching style can feel rigid, with emphasis on constant participation and frequently asking students to close their laptops. The 2 exams were super difficult and did not always align well with the material. In-class negotiation exercises felt repetitive, group projects were annoying, did not add much new value.

Negotiation with Prof. Woodside has been one of my favorite classes at Northeastern! Not only is the course content interesting and relevant to the real world, but Professor Woodside is an extremely talented instructor. We got to roleplay negotiations which was my favorite part because it was both fun and informative. Take this class if you can!!
Amazing prof. Respects her students, very fun lectures and activities, make sure to be present for classes and participate. Definitely learned a lot and had lots of fun.

Loved this professor! She is such a great speaker, every lecture was insightful and interesting. You don't have to read the book at all. All the activities and projects we did were timely and she was very accessible. Great professor, take her!!

The class itself is fine if lecture heavy. You are responsible for a lot of content and you need to be very specific or you won't get credit. What brings this score down is the semester-long project which requires you to interview people from a former job. Its a massive hassle to try and get three people to interview and is worth 30% of the grade

Prof Woodside is definitely one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. She is very knowledgeable and her class is super engaging, which also leads you to learn organically. This class also teaches very valuable topics which are applicable to every aspect of one's life. 100% take this class if you can!!

Prof Woodside does a great job of incorporating relevant, fun activities and balancing lectures with projects/exercises. Really interesting class and she's clearly knowledgeable and respected. Would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor. Really cares about her students and making sure they do well

I really enjoyed ORGB with Prof. Woodside. She was extremely fun in lectures, got to know everyone's name, and was easy to get in touch with. Orgb is a harder class and you do need to know a few concepts, but Dr Woodside was as flexible and helpful as possible. 100% would take again.

Definitely recommend Professor Ryan. She is super nice and accommodating and the course load is manageable if you stay on top of it. There is a weekly hw, quiz, and simulation deadline which is not too bad (some weeks are harder than others). Make sure you put a lot of effort into the simulation bc thats what your final paper is on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I enjoyed her as a teacher. She is very monotone and her lectures can be boring, however it is very easy to do well in the class. Respect her by just paying attention and not being on your laptop, she will appreciate that greatly. Study for the exam. Spend a lot early in the simulation (whatever you think to spend,triple it). And you'll get an A/A-
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She succeeds in availability outside of class once you contact her, and tries to be accomodating. She is nice and nonchalant as a professor, but her lectures are very monotone. The class environment is disengaged, and I think she could teach better by better commanding the class's attention. READ the textbook & ask her questions to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: make sure to bring cup of coffee to your class, she will definitely make you fall asleep. Never listened to her class just read text book and PowerPoint, and I got 90 for my exams. she helps me make the decision to change major from marketing to others

She's a very bad Lecture Giver, the examples are repetitive and she pauses every 10 seconds. But she is very knowledgeable and the class is pretty straight forward if you know literally anything about Marketing. The Simulation she uses is basically "outspend the competition". Don't bother with the textbook, she pretty much reads it to you in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a nice teacher. Read the textbook and listen in class to her examples and you'll be fine for the midterms.. The simulations is very fun and she's very helpful if you meet her during her office hours. However, her voice is monotone so it can get boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: you have to know how to use SPSS. exams require reading and good understanding of material. group work required many meetings
She is mellow and not very engaging in class. But her lectures are great and she gives notes that are the best!

Class feels like I'm staring at a wall, though in reality it's my computer that I have to look at bc my psyche can't handle another 20-second pause bw each sentence. Only if classes were 20 minutes long would this have been a good use of my time. Should be 2 credits. Could have learned it all in a few hours. What a waste of everyone's tuition.

She was a pretty good teacher. The class was boring at times, but the tests are super easy if you just memorize the powerpoint slides. I took this in the summer so I think we had a little less work but we had just the midterm, the final, and this marketing simulation thing. She's an easy grader.

Class is okay, really dull at points though. Sometimes she goes off on tangents and its hard to stay focused. The class goes until the very last minute, and she takes attendance each class. Exams are fair, but sometimes essay prompts don't ask you for what she is looking for. Easy grader.

Paula is great.  She's super nice and friendly, and the tests are clear.  Pay attention in class and study the slides and you'll do fine.  The project is very easy.  Homework assignments are few and quick.  This class made marketing really interesting, you watch a lot of interesting commercials, and if you have an A you don't take the final.

Attendance is mandatory.  Participation is not even though it is part of your grade.  Project and rare assignments are pretty easy.  Read the book and do the practice questions that you can access via blackboard to help you study and ace the exams.  If you do well enough for the two exams, you do not have to take the final.

Oh Paula, how you love Diet Coke. I love this woman, even though I thought she was a huge weirdo at first. For the most part, this class is easy. The second test is tricky but homework is simple. Project is easy too except for having to use SPSS. She will help you though, and encourages students to call her. I'll miss you!

Professor Ryan is great.  She passes around a sign in sheet every class.  She encourages participation, but I do not think she requires it.  Her tests are not that hard as long as you read the book/ look at her powerpoints.  There is one group project and she grades this leniently.

Very good teacher. The book was useless unless you skip the class. If you attend every class, you'll do great. The HW's were easy and helped a lot for the exams. The grade is based on a project and 3 exams. Great class. definitely better than other professors ive heard of. Highly recommended

Shes definitely a nice teacher but too much useless work. 9 Page review sheet on just the vocab words for the midterm is a little bit too much and seems a little bit reminiscent of ineffective old school teach methods.

Great professor. A little bit of work, but it pays off. She is veryyyy clear in what you have to do, and its not too hard. She helps enormously if you ask and don't hesitate- she doesnt mind at all. Awesome professor

She was the most helpful teacher I've ever had. DO NOT hesitate to ask questions, she will answer anything and help you out completely. If you study her reviews, tests are a breeze-- and the project isn't that hard if you pay attention and ask questions!

VERYYYYY Easy! My favorite professor at NU. Knows what she's talking about (she has her own market research business) and loves to help out when you don't understand something. Is veryyyy clear in her lessons, uses all powerpoint slides. Will email you back in 5 minutes if you need help. Great teacher!!!
Easy, breezy.
No Comments

Professor Ryan is a great professor. She makes everything easy to understand by providing real life examples and all the notes on power point slides. If you study the slides and pay attention in class you will ACE the tests. The team project is pretty open ended, just pick something and tell how the product or service is marketed.
Very nice lady, helpful when you need it, reasonable and no reason not to do well in this class!

Really clear, easy grade.  Relies a lot on powerpoints, so if you just print them out and understand them, her lectures are pointless.  Final group project was a huge percent of the grade, but it wasnt very hard

Great class. Sometimes can be slow. Very easy going. Likes class participation. Not to much work. Nail the project and you should be fine. Very helpful and will guide you through computer work. If you have the option take this class.

The negative reviews here are cope. Shane was undoubtedly one of the best professors I've ever had. He taught the course in an engaging manner (with projects/activities) and was always very prepared. Highly recommend
Very tough grader. Don't take this class

Three 1 page reflection reports, and 2 group projects + 2 exams. Assignments are chill but exams are case style open-ended questions. If you want an easy A don't take his class. Tests are hard and he takes significant points off if you don't use the specific concept he wants. He tries to make class engaging and is a nice guy but I don't recommend.

He grades like his life depends on it. Cuts points for no reason and never gives any clarity. Takes tests full of questions that are open-ended, but expects only one type of answer. He does not understand the subject; I don't even know who made him a professor. The class average on the midterm was a 32/40. DO NOT TAKE HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When i say this is the chillest dude i mean it. The only class i used to look forward to going. Makes every single lecture engaging with games, podcasts, and discussions. The material is engaging and the midterm is online in person. Take him and dont think twice.

Loved Shane! Absolutely amazing professor and teaches the class in a much more engaging way than other professors. Pretty easy grader on the writing assignments. Tough (but fairish) grader on the midterm and final. If you have a 92.9, he will not round and give you an A just a heads up. But other than that, I highly recommend him for Org B.

Tests are insanely difficult. Good luck. The material he covered did NOT reflect well on the exams, and  they were incredibly subjective answers. Only 4 exams and no other grades. Boring class, just powerpoints every class which waste time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is AMAZING. As long as you follow exactly what was on the study guide then you would be fine. A lot of materials to memorize. Not a very harsh grader. It's not a difficult course but it is very material densed. Also he is so fine, such a silver fox, I had a crush on him.

Classes are very boring, he just goes through powerpoints. Tests are extremely difficult, multiple choice. Your grade is based on 4 tests which are insanely difficult. He also posts review guides and then puts different topics on the exam, it feels like a trick. Would not take again, it's not worth it. On the outside, he's nice, but it's difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I knew going in that this class was difficult and it really was. You are graded on 3 tests and a final exam. I may not have done well in this class but I REALLY enjoyed his lectures and the content. There is a lot of content which is why it is harder, but he wants to help you succeed, he will answer your questions no matter how dumb they are.

This professor is amazing i wish i could take more of his classes, the class is SO HARD. Don't take this class if you aren't a good test taker and don't have a lot of knowledge in sex relations. But amazing professor.

Super interesting class but I would not take it if I had fully understood how difficult the exams are. The questions on the exams are challenging/not straight forward. Even with lots of studying, it's still very challenging!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very challenging, especially if you're not confident when it comes to tests. Your whole grade is based on 4 exams, and they're tough. The questions are scenario-based, with answer choices that reflect different topics covered in class, which can make it hard to pinpoint the right answer. Attendance is through a code you have to enter during class.

This class can be pretty tough, especially if you're not a strong test taker. Your entire grade is based on 4 exams, and they're challenging. The test questions are scenario-based, and the answer choices are usually different topics from the class—so it can be tricky to figure out which topic best applies to each situation. No homework or projects.

Great class, super interesting and the Professor is very nice and easily accessible. Grade is based of 4 pretty difficult tests. DO NOT TAKE IF YOU ARE NOT A GOOD TEST TAKER! But it is still super, super interesting, and I would definitely recommend it to people interested in the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A nice guy but he moved very fast through his presentations and it was hard to keep up, even with studying and going to exam reviews the tests were still hard. This class is only based on 3 tests and the final and the test are multiple choice with wordy answers that are similar. Take at your own risk but to me, it just was not worth the hassle
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a good professor who clearly cares about the topic. Online summer class, and the recorded lectures were super easy to follow and enjoyable. The class is graded off of few assignments (including some tests). If you take notes and understand the general topics of the course, you should do fine. Not a good class for a bad test taker.

My favorite professor. Clear guidelines and expectations for the class. Yes, you need to put time into studying, but a lot of the studying will be review because his lectures really stick. Gives hints like "write this down." Always covered material with time to spare. Super nice and funny too!

This class was really interesting, but definitely hard to do well unless you are a really good test taker. Also, attendance is mandatory, if you miss more than 2 classes, your grade moves down a whole letter. He's a great lecturer and includes fun clips from tv/movies, but don't take it if you don't like pure lecture classes.

Dr. Schwartz's sex and relationships communications class is not easy. Take it if you are a good test taker, but do not take it if you aren't. You are only graded on 4 exams, and they are so hard. Make sure you put time into studying. No homework, though, or projects. He's a good guy; just moves really quickly through his lengthy presentations.

I can't rave about this class enough. The class is lecture based and the grades for the sem are just three tests and a final, but if you take notes (listen carefully when he says "write this down") you should do well. He is passionate about the content and is very engaging. If you are a good test taker and are into comm I'd 10/10 recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: comm3201 health communication was the toughest course I have ever take. He was too trenchant with word choice and format, and gave very low grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Schwartz' guidelines and expectations for the class are so perfect. He gives you everything you need, really, but also makes his lectures interesting, fun, and interactive. Loved this class so much, I'm taking another one taught by him.

Only tests for the grade, which was nice b/c you didn't have to worry about homework or group projects (unless standardized testing isn't your thing). Lectures were generally pretty interesting, and he always had fun example clips to demonstrate class content.

This class was a great class to take on learning the importance and the contextualities behind Sex, Relationships & Communication. Even though I went to Office Hours before every exam and built a relationship with this professor, I would personally not take this class again. 

Take during the summer with diff professor. He made it hard to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Lectures/content is super interesting and engaging fun to listen to. Lots of lectures and tests in my opinion were not super good at measuring how much you know - some questions are vague/unfair, hard to do super well even if you know everything. Still very fun and interesting class, not super easy but would recommend.

Avoid at all cost!
The materials in lectures are simple and straightforward, but the questions in tests are hard, some of which never appeared in his lectures. There are a lot of readings and you have to read them all if you want to do well in tests. Tough grader on essay. Do NOT take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was very interesting and he makes it easy to follow in class. the 3 exams + final all require a lot of studying but very manageable - never used the textbook and his lectures were concise. all and all loved this class and even though its a fair amount of work, it is not bad :) would recommend. only downside is there only 4 exams + paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love Joe! thoughtful and funny. Likes to cement research and concepts with videos and pop-culture references. You'll have four tests and a 7 page research paper all out of 200 points

He will not give you any extra credits or curves. There's a lot of reading to do in class, and if you don't, you're going to get a terrible grade on the test. His lectures are straightforward, but the exams are extremely difficult! There are six exams in one semester, and they are killing me. Runaway when you see his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is very engaging and a good speaker. The lectures were entertaining as I had him for Sex and Relationships. It's not a SuPeR easy class though, and you'll have to study a little bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a great professor who teaches the material in a way that is both clear and concise. He also breaks up the lecture with video clips so that it doesn't get too monotonous. The tests are not easy, and you do need to study, but they're fair. You don't need the textbook. I always looked forward to this class and definitely recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is big - lectures are all material (no discussions). Either go to class or get notes, exams contain a lot of material. Do study, I crammed in one day and did well, but its helpful to start earlier. Schwartz does a great job of applying concepts to relationships, adds pop culture ex. in class, and the topics are interesting and relevant!
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Love Prof Schwartz! His lectures are so entertaining, he has a good sense of humor, and he always finds the best/coolest video clips for examples in lectures! However, tests are harder than one would expect- typically 30 multiple choice, but definitely study! Don't buy the textbook. Lectures are powerpoint with fill in the blank, so don't miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Your grade depends entirely on 4 tests, and he makes them harder than they have to be; you have to memorize a lot of information and you're tested on small details that aren't relevant. By mid-semester a lot of the students are struggling, and he doesn't offer any extra credit or other opportunities to raise your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He displays fun examples during his presentations, however, tests are much harder than you think, by the middle of the semester most students are struggling. He is very pedant and arrogant. The material is not that complicated but he makes it so. Avoid at all costs if you want to be on a very pretentious and useless lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Schwartz is my favorite professor at Northeastern. He is incredibly clear, helpful, and understanding. He pushes and motivates you to produce your best work, and works hard to understand each student as an individual and what they care about/how they learn. He's also hilarious.

I really enjoyed the class but the exams are a lot harder than you would expect mainly because you have to memorize so much information and so many little details.  My biggest complaint is that he does not reply to emails and seems to not give grades according to what's on the syllabus.

Class was all lectures, with four total exams (final exam cumulative). It's not as easy as a 1000 level COMM class normally tends to be, but it's manageable. Study a lot and don't skip any lectures! You don't need the book, but you do learn everything you need for exams in the lectures. Seriously, study! You won't pass with an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is adorable and sassy. He's talking about statistics so you'd expect to fall asleep but you don't. He's a pretty easy grader and he is very helpful when you ask questions. He made stats fun and keeps you entertained.

Great professor. All exam information is base on class powerpoints. All you need to do in class is to copy down things from his powerpoints. He post powerepoints with only titles for students to take notes. If you don't go to class, he won't give out complete version of powerpoints. Final grade base on just four exams' average grade.

I took this class online with him because I enjoyed him so much for COMM1131. He is a little bit less clear online compare to in-person, but he was always available to help with clarifications. I didn't do amazing in the class but I wouldn't put that on him. The class kind of sucks but he's such a good guy it made it tolerable.

He uses poignant examples that help you to remember new terms and concepts and has a sharp sense of humor. I've heard some say he comes across as tough, but every time I spoke with him he was understanding and flexible. There are 4 tests all equally weighted (i.e. no final) and all are MC 30 questions. Easy as pie. Plus crystal clear study guides.

Probably the most applicable class for the real world you will take. Professor is also really funny. Just make sure you study at least 3-5 days before a test as there is a lot of information. If you study really hard you will get an A, easy.
Very interesting but A LOT to memorize and even though it's interesting I can't tell if the content is really useful for my major or life.

Dr. Schwartz is an amazing Professor and I really enjoyed  his class. I took him for COMM 1131 and the class is not difficult, however,  you really need to study using both the text book and his lecture notes.  If  you miss his class you will not pass the course and relying  solely on the lecture notes will not get you an A in the class.

I really am enjoying this class. It is my biggest class, but I don't feel too much like a little fish in a big pond. The only thing is that during his lectures he is always slapping his thighs. When I caught on it was very distracting. He doesn't give homework which tells you that you need to study or you will not pass. And don't get the text book.
His lectures are entertaining and if you go to class then you really don't need the textbook. Tests are simple, but a bit tricky. Other than that, I really enjoyed him as a Professor.
Joe Shcwartz is possibly the worst teacher. Have taken 4 classes and he's very irritating!!!!!!!!DO NOT take a class with him.

Joe Schwartz is super entertaining and totally hot. He makes research methods fun with his examples and persona. If you are paying attention in class and show respect, you will like him. Try to make him smile.
Definitely a hottie if you swing that way... really great professor though. Cares a lot about his students and can really help students improve on the dreaded task that is public speaking.

If teacher does not like you forget it! He makes you feel extremely uncomfortable even when you try to reach out to. Does not give second chances to hand it or rewrite a paper. Classes were pretty dull-responds to email late and is harsh. Do not recommend.
He was awesome, so passionate and fun. All of the quiz and test questions came from slideshow notes, so as long as you copy that down or study from those you should be fine.

I had this professor twice. He is extremely nice and a great guy. He makes class interesting and fun. All the questions on his tests are straight from his notes, you don't have to so the readings. I would definitely recommend a class with him.
Great professor. I wish I could take him a few more times because he is so helpful with everything. If you have him as a choice when signing up for classes, take him.

He's a good guy. I had public speaking with him this past semester and although the material for that class is repetitive and boring, he found ways to make it interesting. His quizzes were right from the notes, as were his tests. This is mainly because his lectures come directly from the book, so honestly I didn't do much of the reading.

KSG is caring and does help you a lot. The course is a lot of work but it's definitely worth it. Just hope you get good team members and speak up soon if you have bad ones. I know there are other professors that give less work and grade easier but the work in this class is rewarding. Be prepared to work 10-15 hours per week tho.

Be prepared to work hard, but the work is very rewarding and clearly connected to engineering. Ask good questions, go to office hours, and work hard and she will like you, which makes the class more fun. If you get stuck in a bad group, speak up early or this class will become incredibly difficult. Work collaboratively, and FYELIC is your friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: KSG was great! She is incredibly passionate about what she teaches. We got to go on a few optional field trips in the class which was really fun. The actual content on energy systems is super interesting, and very applicable to modern day politics. I really recommend this class and this teacher. There's readings, but you can skim them.

KSG is by far the best professor/teacher I've had in my entire life. She is super understanding and cares for all her students. As long as you try in the class, you will have an amazing experience. The class IS difficult, but extremely rewarding if you want to really learn about engineering. Stacked cornerstone with KSG is worth it.

the class was interesting and the prof was great. there was a lot of homework and reading, but her expectations were clear and she is a fair grader. she also gives a few points of extra credit on the exams. she sets up interesting guest speakers and optional trips for the class as well, would recommend taking a class of hers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved this class and KSG's teaching! I enjoyed the mix of hard science and calculation with policy and what's happening in the world, the field trips and guest speakers, and I got to learn so much about so many different niches of energy. This class had a great balance of work load, I learned a ton but it never felt unmanageable.

KSG was funny, intriguing, and clearly cares about us students. She made class fun and interesting with her lectures. Also I liked having interactive classes with lecturers, activities, and projects throughout the summer semester.
KSG is amazing!

KSG is one of the best professors I've had at Northeastern! I was super excited to take this class with her because I had heard such good things from friends who had her for Cornerstone. She's funny, engaging and breaks down difficult topics really well. She is also very friendly and approachable and great to talk to in office hours!

Stacked Cornerstone is a tough course where you learn a lot in one semester, but KSG was able to break down each concept so we understood. KSG is one of the most caring professor I had at Northeastern and she prepares you well for the rest of college. I would highly recommend her class to anyone that wants to be a disciplined engineer.

KSG is GOAT. She loves teaching and cares about her students. Taking a summer class with her after having her for cornerstone. Guest speakers, field trips, and a lot of reading - but I low key like the books, especially since they were all  free. Summer semester pace is fast but work is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: KSG just wrote my recommendation for med school and I'm speechless. She has been my biggest cheerleader and supported me through figuring out what I want to do. Her class was tough but I get what she's doing. I want to help  others in my work and I learned that in her class. Work hard and you'll reap the benefits later. Don't be lazy, take KSG!

Assigned groups of 4 have a 150+ page report due by the end of the semester on top of 12 page memos 2-4 times a week. You have to learn AutoCAD, Solid Works, MATLAB, C++, and Arduino independently, and the assignments feel like busy work. Really really time consuming busywork. The grading feels unfair at times. She teaches grit and determination.
