The essays covered everything from analytical writing to personal narratives and it was a great experience to do these and My writing improved.
Her lectures and requirements for assignments were confusing. So much work.
It is nice to take her class! She loves to help students. She will answer all questions that you have.
Great class

Although she ramble senselessly and the only improvement you find in your writing is from just having to write over and over again, this course is incredibly easy. As long as you show up, show you put in effort, participate in class, and organize your portfolio you will get an A.
SHE IS AN AWESOME PROFESSOR AS LONG AS YOU GO TO CLASS KEEP UP WITH WORK AND SHOW THAT YOU ARE PUTTING THE EFFORT IN....CLASS TAUGHT ME A LOT ABOUT WRITING AND PREPARED ME FOR MY SOPHOMORE YEAR!

She can be really lenient, you can submit stuff several days later and most of the time she wont care. Much course work but if you do a decent job and put effort into the organization of the folio you should get a good grade.  Dont buy the book, it's isnt useful you can find stories on the internet

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!! It is a waste of time. If you do take it do all assignments and try to word things nicely and to give the impression you understand the reading. If you follow those advices you should get an A.

She is very unclear when giving out assigning. It's hard to understand what is she asking for her assignments. Make your essays sound good and you will do well on her class. That's what i found out while taking her class, its how you say it and not what you're saying.

Very easy but PAINFULLY boring and EXTREMELY useless class. She is a nice person, but she rambles and is oblivious to the fact that nobody is paying attention. There is a lot of pointless work. The content is boring and the curriculum is weak. Unprofound and basic concepts are overanalyzed. The textbook is barely used so don't buy it.
She would be a better teacher is she would not go on talking about senseless things.
Had her in 1993, bad teacher if you get her drop the class. You pay enough at NU and it is not worth the money.

Prof. Anton was my instructor for EAI6980 Capstone at Northeastern University,focused on Agentic AI in Biotechnology.He explains complex research concepts with clarity,encourages critical thinking, and guided us in producing high quality, publishable research.I enjoyed his classes and highly recommend him to future students considering his course.

Excellent instructor who explains ML/AI concepts clearly with strong intuition, not just formulas. Built a real crisis detection chatbot for my project, learned the entire ML pipeline hands-on. Lectures are well-structured, assignments challenging but fair. Very responsive and supportive. Highly recommend!
So professor was very good, it was little bit tough but very good experience. The class was very good and I learned a lot lots of new things.

Professor Anton is an excellent professor who knows how to combine theoretical knowledge with practical application. I learned a lot from his course. The professor is also very energetic and dedicated to teaching and his work. The course are also well-organized. If you are fortunate enough to see a course taught by him, don't hesitate to choose it.

The professor demonstrates professionalism and keeps the course material consistently updated. He is also very approachable, if you have questions or concerns, don't hesitate to ask. You get to know how techniques used in biology connect with machine learning and artificial intelligence, even if you don't have a strong background in biology.

Dr. Sinitskiy is a great lecturer, and taught one of the most enjoyable classes I've taken at NU. Besides the engaging lectures, he commonly is able to help apply the course material to the real world where his experience helps highlight many ways the material is used in relation to AI and ML. Additionally, he gives good feedback when asked.

Professor Anton is very good at making the lectures interesting and really cares about introducing his students to real-life situations which is great for understanding the reality of biotech. The exams are easy if you pay attention during class and revise the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Anton captivated our attention with his profound knowledge and dynamic teaching style. He seamlessly navigated complex concepts, breaking them into fragments that resonated with students of varied backgrounds.
Class sessions were not mere lectures but vibrant discussions where every student felt empowered to participate actively.

Most amazing Professor I have ever taken class of. I like the way he teaches. His teaching style is very unique, he integrates these intelligent jokes/fun trivia into the lectures which I like the most.The explanation of the topics are on-point. Grading is very good. If you're doing the work on time, you don't have to worry about the grades.

The professor is truly exceptional. His expertise extends beyond the realm of biotechnology into the intricate world of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) in biotech. He is one of those professors who are always more than willing to teach and want you to get the most out of his class. The lectures were really helpful and worthy.

DO NOT take this if you want an easy class. material is interesting, but SO much work. Every other week, theres a test and assignment(which requires background knowledge of products) on lockdown browsers. Other weeks, there is a discussion post which is fine. They give an 85 for assignments that are "satasfactory" so it is hard to get a good grade.

Non tech savvy, incompetent teacher, teaches horribly extremely simple and uninteresting concepts, but the quizzes are hyper specific and it is absolutely not clear how to prepare for this class. The material is extremely simple, yet the grading is unforgiving. NEVER TAKE THIS ONLINE CLASS.

I actually like marketing a lot, she ruined this course with unclear and strict grading standards. I've met bad professors, but trust me she is the WORST. Anyway it's a lesson I learned from blood and tears, make sure you get far away from her.
no. just no.. heavy workload for a such useless subject
She's not helpful at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It's a shame that she is retiring, because she has been the best marketing professor I've had at Northeastern so far. It was a heavy workload, but she set high expectations for her students and forced us to look at case studies in a unique and challenging way.
Professor Sieloff's class if tough, but very rewarding. She's intelligent and passionate about the material, and if you try, you will learn a lot.

Susan is a good teacher and uses real life examples to explain concepts, however her tests are pretty difficult. Shes also a tough grader but if you read the chapters and the power points you should be okay. Also class participation really matters.

All I will say is, I changed my concentration AWAY from marketing because of her. Awful, disrespectful, barks at students. I had an interview once and emailed her in advance letting her know I wont be able to make it but I can come at the end for the evaluations (they are graded) she told me not too and took points off which dropped my grade.

First review ever because this one is worth noting. By far the WORST professor I have encountered in Northeastern. She is quite rude, does not care about her students, and genuinely does not care about your performance. She dropped me a whole letter grade down because I didnt participate as much as she wanted avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Sieloff is awesome! Definitely one of my favorites at Northeastern. Her class is mainly based on long cases you dissect on your own and then go over in class. It is hard work, but if you're interested in real world cases of how marketing can make or break a company, you will love this class.

Unpleasant professor with the most ridiculous workload i have ever encountered in 4 years of university. Expect two case study's that take about 5 hours to write each per week. You often have only one day between them. You can also expect to get C's for them. Her workload is incredibly detrimental to the rest of your classes. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Susan is a great at teaching, but she won't just give you a grade. The group project lasts all the semester and it's super hard. She probably won't like it and will give you a C. There are weekly cases that are super hard too
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Group/team work is a waste of time, since sometimes others in the class are useless. Instructor is helpful at understanding the cases, great diagrams on board to help with cases. Case reading and classes are a great way to get real world understanding.

Professor Sieloff is passionate about the subject she is teaching. The class is very case heavy so be prepared to write! The lectures can be mundane considering you spent time analyzing these cases at home and then that is all you do in class. The final project is worth a huge percent of your grade and the groups are assigned randomly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not one of my easier classes, but I learned A LOT. The class is case-based, so there are about 2 one-page cases every week. It's a fair amount of work, but definitely doable. Professor Sieloff is a tough grader, but she always tells you what she expects and is realistic about your workload. One of my favorite professors so far.

I did not enjoy being in Professor's Sieloff course. It was an online class, and the homework was never very clear and she was very bad with emails. I would ask questions via email and her response were never helpful.  It being an online class, I was at least expecting some more feedback through email and more support, but there was none.

Professor Sieloff is tough in general. She expects you to participate (your grade depends on it) and she gives four exams, all of which were essay format. Although her assessments were tough, she did a great job of explaining the material clearly and concisely. She's an expert in the field and I would definitely take her class again.

I would take her class again if that was even possible. She is the most entertaining person I have ever seen in my Northeastern life. You HAVE to go to classes though. I really enjoyed her class because she taught us the concepts in a very entertaining way. Loved her class even though I passed with a C+. I must warn you; the exams are really hard!

Strikingly unpleasant Professor. Shows little respect for students (often sarcastic and even confrontational). Engages class yet shoots down opinions that don't align with her own. Tests memorization rather than understanding of concepts, e.g. the 5 P's of research (Purpose, Plan, Performance, Processing, Preparation). Class exercises r unhelpful.

She is the greatest. Her class is challenging, but also not impossible to get an A. She is helpful and she genuinely cares. She incorporates fun demos into her lectures. I think many people are intimidated by her because she is a strong woman, but really she should be seen as an inspiration - to men and women both! Would take her again if I could!
Some people found her abrasive, I think Siel Team 6 is just misunderstood. Really passionate, definitely strict though. Certainly far from an easy A, but getting a good grade is not impossible.

She is the most condescending and spiteful professor I've ever had. She words her exam questions extremely vaguely and is a tough grader. She gives no wiggle room in homework or exams. She loves herself. a lot. and is very unwilling to answer any questions. She gives students dirty looks and is just a very rude person in general. Avoid her!

Very difficult to work with and ask questions to.  Always gets defensive even when the whole class bombs the exam, she blames us instead of the fact that she was misleading about what would be on it.   She also words the questions so she will trick you. Also, she will tell you it's fine to hand write the assignment, then take off points afterwards.
She is a good teacher, she has some flaws though.

She is an awesome professor.  Her class was really enjoyable and she helped us out as much as possible.  When the whole group did badly on a test, she threw the test out or made it count less.  She was very fair.  But GO TO CLASS.  She knows all.  She will notice if you are not there.  But honestly, I loved this class because of her.

GO TO CLASS!!!! she will notice if you don't. do the assignments, ask questions, be involved. If you do this, she will love you and you're good to go. If you don't care about the class, she won't care about you. She plays favorites a little, but overall she's a good teacher who knows her stuff.

Ok teacher. Pretty easy class, likes when you show up, really likes it when everybody is there.  Notices a lot if you stroll in late.  Agian pretty easy however she is very vague about any work.  She does not really explain what needs to be done.

If she likes you, she likes you and you're fine, otherwise, watch out. Overall, she is a good professor and explains the material well. The way she words her exam questions is not good and though you may know the material that she is asking for solid, the question will confuse you and you will not understand what she is looking for. Overall, decent

Awful person! Skipped 2 of her classes in a row and never forgave me. Went to her office hours to ler her know I still had interest in the class and she was rude and unhelpful. Kiss her ass and you'll be fine.
Nice lady.  4 Exams and one project.  Final is not cumulative. Very straight forward on exams.
This class will become like a plague if you let it. Just get everything done in a timely fashion and it wont pile up at the end of the semester.
She was a really fair teacher.  If you go to class and pay attention and participate you can get an A.  The tests are very reasonable.  I would take another one of her classes!
Average class right down the line, not to hard, not easy. She is pretty good but dont get on her bad side
No Comments

unless you plan on kissing ass and regurgitating knowledge all semester.. dont take this class. If you bring up an opposing view on a subject she feels strongly about be ready to be chastised for it the rest of the semester. Sieloff is incredibly **** and biased, she also manages to teach as if shes talking to a bunch of sophomores in high school
She made the class very interesting. Good insight. Easy project. An overall easy professor.

Nice teacher..Our class failed all the quizzes so she threw them away. However, not very helpful with the TJX project. We were left on our own to do everything. project was ugh but we got through it with a good grade. Enough said
i thought her teaching style for this higher level class was inadequate.  she seems to lecture quite a bit and doesn't relate topics to real world enough.  overall, mediocre

Knows a lot but sometimes her lectures compared to the book are a bit confusing but deff study her slides for tests and you'll ace them.  Do your interesting hws, go to class, and show up on time...you'll get an a!
full of s**t...but decent teacher... project sucked
really great and knowledgable professor.  makes marketing fun.
She was a pretty good teacher. Midterm was kinda hard, like everyone bombed it. TJX project sucked.

We called her bull **** so that tells you something about her, you def have to get on her good side, just ask pamps. Russle he was def on her good side if you know what i mean. She married a guy thats 6 10 and she is 6 3, big kids going on. SHe was  good
No Comments
GET ON HER GOOD SIDE!!!

an effective teacher who understands the material. always finding ways to add some fun into the class to bring life to the subject. the exams are all essays questions so good luck to those who doesn't like writing.

you MUST show up to class. I got through this course without looking at the textbook, only doing the homework and going to lecture. She is incredibly sweet and objective when it comes to grading. Homework is very helpful in learning material. Tells exactly what is going to be on exams/quizzes.

Weekly homework assignments are manageable and not too difficult. If you attend lectures and actually pay attention, you'll be fine in this class. She is a nice professor, but it's important to lock in during lectures or you can fall behind quickly.

She is better than people give credit for. She's a little difficult to hear sometimes, but she just had brain cancer and came back to teach, so she's a little dedicated. If you lock in and ask for feedback and actually pay attention in class it's fine. She gives a lot of practice questions and teaches clearly. JUST PAY ATTENTION. You'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: decent, but not outstanding. she was pretty nice, i would definetley recommend going to class if you can, lectures really give everything you need. homework isn't too bad, and textbook is optional if you pay attention in class. there are group projects which were fine, and then at least for my section, she curved grades at the end.
great professor

I do not know how she has so many bad reviews here. She was great, taught very well, and was extremely organized. The reviews were very similar to exams which was helpful. She was always willing to answer questions and clearly cares about students.
Exams are particularly numerous, with bi-weekly exams and only three attempts at assignments

I usually never write negative about professors but this one was necessary. She has literally made me cry and given me immense stress and anxiety. She gave me an F on my recent test because I reached 10 minutes late and I begged and pleaded but she couldn't care less. I am an A student with a 3.89 GPA and I am shaking as I am typing this.

I can't believe that there are reviews here saying that she is caring and she's not that bad. She is honestly the meanest professor I have ever had, she is a terrible teacher and will do anything in her power to make sure that you suffer through the course and have the worst experience. Don't take her even if she is your last choice.
She is the worst. I am taking her this semester and she is the most uncaring woman ever, I have never hated a professor as much I hate her and she has made my life miserable.
Very caring professor but that's where the positive ends. She is unreasonably tough and has made the course EXTREMELY EXAM HEAVY ESPECIALLY THE FINAL.

I really enjoyed taking Professor Wang's class! Her teaching style is effective and easy to follow along (frequently worked through problems in class, started with simpler problems and worked up, etc), and exams are similar to homework which made it easy to prep. She gave credit back on our group project and the final was curved generously.

Class wasn't bad. 4 quizzes with the lowest grade being dropped, 2 exams, and 1 final. You will need to pay attention and study to do well in this class. Overall, Professor Wang is caring and not as bad as the reviews seem. Class wasn't boring, and as long as you put in work, you will be fine. Make sure to do the homework, as they help you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Every review on here is so negative but I promise, she is not bad, at all. She has TONS of resources like slides and notes for every chapter and gives reviews all the time for exams and quizzes. The only reason why people don't like her is that the exams are hard. If you put In the effort though you will get results!
Hard grader like she never will give people 100% for any assignments

Don't take her!! Doesn't explain stuff, tests are very tough, and to make it worse she grades it so harshly. There is one project that makes up 14% of your grade but be prepared to get a low grade on that and the final accounts for 30% of your grade. NO EXTRA CREDIT WHATSOEVER! She is a nice person but a terrible teacher.

Professor wang reads of slides. Also, the class is not a safe space for people to ask questions, as she often laughs, smirks, and dismisses answers or questions that do not fit her agenda. She is incredibly rigid and does not create a super nice environment to be in. Also, her tests are hard, the grading is hard, prepare to study to do well.

This class is fine. She reads off the slides but she's a nice person and is generous grading. Take this class and it may be a little annoying but won't be problematic if you study. Homework assignments take a little long (1.5-2 hrs each) and there's one for each chapter. Exams are fair and she grades leniently.
Great insights and point of view; good historical example, witty, expert.

Hates CJ majors so keep that under the radar, extremely liberal but does not grade unfairly. Does make an attempt to make everything you read and write about his own views rather than challenging ideas. Did not fail me but I got B's on everything which seems a little extreme seeing as I got over 50 grades over two classes all being in B range.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor although thought provoking, was not responsive to numerous attempts for individual emails. I sent him emails for clarification on things that I was not graded well on, and never received a response. Also seemed too biased andnto me it seemed that it would reflect in the way he graded you. (Can't confirm since he didn't respond!)
american gov. and politics. one of the most thought provoking classes i've ever taken
Dr. Slaner is a brilliant professor, I enjoyed his class very much. He made me love the complexities of American government and the politics behind it. Definately take a class with him!

An excellent professor, definately one of the best in the department. His class discussions are some of the best I have ever been involved with. He succsessfully incorporates current events into the intricacies of our American Govt. The class was very  well taught and I hope to have him again for another class.
Very chill guy, but boring class. 2 big tests, case studies, and online hw. The tests are online and he doesn't use a lockdown browser. Attendance is mandatory. Grading isn't bad at all.

He is so nice and imo lectures are great and he covers the material thoroughly in class. There are two exams, no actual final, a few case studies and ch quizzes for hw. I learned a lot from him and he's rly funny. If you acc show up the written response parts of the exam are easy. Tests are weighed a lot though.

Prof. Slusser is too old to be teaching MISM. He doesn't email formally or on time, lacks technological skills, and begins 30 minutes late. He failed to cancel classes during poor weather, cancelled classes AFTER class ended without his arrival, and adjusted the schedule without communication. He may be easier than others, but don't expect quality.

He is extremely old. He takes almost half an hour to get class started because he struggles to share his screen to the board. He seems like a nice person, but on exams, the written portion is harshly graded. You could get an correct answer and explain it but you will most likely lose points due to not writing in excessive detail.
Not a hard class. But not a very good teacher either.
Terrible class. You don't learn much even if you do well. Prof too isn't great.

Professor Slusser wants everyone to do well, that is very clear. The class is not hard, some homework and 2 exams, which is not too difficult. Show up and pay attention and you will do well. He is also very flexible!
Lectures are fairly dry, but memorizing the content of the class translates fully to the exams.

Professor Slusser cares about the course content and was a joy to see in class. However, his lectures are not engaging and don't hold students accountable to participate or complete homework on their own. It would be an easy class to cheat in each assignment and fly under the radar. He lacks applicable knowledge of technology, which is ironic.

Very sweet professor, and made boring content worthwhile and engaging. Unfortunately, the tests were very heavy weighted, and he was very bland when giving directions for the case studies. More than likely, what you get on the tests is what you end the class with. He wants a lot of participation. Offers zoom if you are sick/woke up late.

Great professor, super nice and caring guy, and made the class interesting. Cases and exams were perfectly manageable. Would 100% recommend this course and the professor. Probably one of the best MISM2301 professors at Neu!!!
Lectures got boring extremely quick, but the content was easy. Case studies and quizzes aren't hard, but tests lower your grade by a bit, even if you ace the homework.
His lectures are long and boring. Ask obvious questions that do not help you learn the material. He re-explains things and almost never finishes class PPT
He is so kind and he is always available to respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The subject itself was easy but stillsuper hard to get an A. I got 90s for all the exams but they don't really help. He wants specific things for those case studies but never tells what he wants and gives no feedback. He indeed is entertaining but lectures are long and not really helpful. No finals but three exams throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Treats his students with respect, is honest, funny and very informative. Can be a tough grader but a fair one.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Better choice out of the other professors. No final exam, just a final project.

I enjoyed the class with Prof. Slusser. He is engaging and wants you to be engaged. There are several (long) case studies (needs to be purchased online) to read and case analyses to write for most of them. But I found him to be an easy grader as long as you follow his clear directions on the syllabus. Get ready to participate a lot in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not a bad class. I would recommend taking it as he's the only one who does not have a final exam out of all the other teaches in MISM 2301. Nice person. Likes to joke around and wants you to perform well in the semester and has a very clear outline of your grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wants particular things but is not completely specific on what those are. Very little feedback. Unwilling to admit when he made mistakes in assigning the wrong grades to the wrong people. You will spend forever writing the final case study. Clearly had not read his own syllabus. Quizzes okay. Tests were based on things we never discussed.
The quizzes are extremely easy. He also gives out a study guide for test. Compared to the other teachers for an intro level MISM class, he is the best.

Northeastern decided to take away the book out of the course, that was mistake number one. Now his class is based off timed BB quizzes 10Qs in 10min which are taken from these condensed readings that someone wrote up for the department. The readings aren't particularly clear in any way and the questions on BB are vague and subjective. Poor Overall.

Provides insightful thoughts and makes decent jokes. Interesting cases. Always let us go early which was great. The workload is decent except the quizzes can be hard unless you have read the cases thoroughly

I'm not sure what he's like now, but I took him for the required MBA class as part for 1.5 credits.  Nice guy, but makes you write what seems to be many unnecessary cases that could've really just been read for homework.  For a 1.5 credit class, he makes the workload like a 4.5 credit class.  I took him 3 years ago and things may have changed since

Great teacher. Hilarious guy. Quizzes are easy as long as you study and there is no final. Homework makes up half the grade and as long as you do the work you'll be fine. Made an otherwise dull subject pretty interesting.
Very nice professor, writing intensive a lot of memo's but no tests and exams. It's quite easy just be ready to write.

Excellent professor! Fun and easy class. She helps a lot when you have questions. Do the practice final, it is so helpful!  The labs and tests are sometimes tricky, but beatable. DO TAKE HER class, no regrets!!
Excellent teacher. She's very thorough, fun, and seems to enjoy teaching what she's teaching. Very helpful and straightforward, I have no complaints!
Avoid her if you can
Professor Skinnari is a phenomenal teacher! Lectures were laid out, willing to explain fundamental concepts (even math), always accessible, kind, and truly very inspirational.

She explains the concepts well and makes them easy to understand but she rarely lectures. A lot of class time she gives you to complete practice problems but it is just wasted time spent waiting around for her to explain concepts. Homework doesn't relate to what you're doing in class. She just needs to change how she spends class time.

A truly horrible professor. Goes through material fast and does not give through responses if you ask her a question. Terrible at teaching the material. Also there was no partial credit given for exams at all. If the answer entered does not match EXACTLY what she inputted on canvas (even if it is a rounding error), no credit will be given.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's does her best to explain everything but be distracted on your device once and you'll be behind. Goes fast with the examples but some are well connected to the quiz and homework. You only get one midterm and a final exam so study well cause you won't get a second chance until a year. Also be prepared to use Achieve if you're taking 1161.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Even with background knowledge in physics, this course was kinda hard. Although she knows what she is talking about, I found the lectures to be boring and unproductive. Needs more examples and conceptual explanations. Homework due every week, weekly quiz, midterm, and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very clear of how she runs the course and does not give many resources for studying for exams. Also, the textbook is not very clear. I found overall her lectures left me confused, but I don't have much prior physics background. Also, the quizzes are very challenging and even if small mistakes are made there is no partial credit given.

She is a all-around solid professor. Sometimes, her lectures can get very slow and feel like they are dragging, especially on problems which you are able to figure out quickly but she wastes times going through slowly. The entire class is just weekly tests and homework, so if you already know physics, you really don't even need to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is an easy class to get an A in. With that being said, it is hard to understand any of the points he is trying to make and most of his lectures fall flat. Most of the time he seems very uninterested and bored at his own words. Graded very easy on some things and extremely harsh on others. A new professor who has some things to work out.

Getting an A was easy, there were online quizzes that were open note and one final paper as well as lots of extra credit. However, the readings felt completely unnecessary as he went over the chapters in class and overall I don't really feel like I learned anything. While the class was easy, it wasn't worth the time.

I liked Professor Skobic's class, you could tell he is very knowledgable about sociology. There's not too much work, just quizzes, reading, discussion posts for extra credit, and research paper+anno bib. No one likes doing research papers but he provides so many resources for you and is very helpful during the process. There are presentations!

Professor Skacel is the best professor I've had at Northeastern. He makes sure everyone understands lectures and slows down when people are confused. He is always available outside of class, and if his office hours do not line up with your schedule, he will make himself available for you. He cares about his students and is clearly very knowledge.

Prof Skacel was literally amazing. his lectures were so informative and he actually went into detail about small things rather than assuming we already knew. Whenever he saw we were stuck on a question on a test he would explain the question and give us hints. He was super gracious with partial credit and there was no graded homework

Professor Skacel was always available outside the classroom for help. He really cares about his students. His quizzes are very similar to homework and as long as you do the homework and go to his office during hours if confused you will have no problem getting an A. As long as you don't forget stuff during quizzes you won't get a B+ lol.

Professor Skacel's lectures are detailed and organized and he cares about his students. He would explain the problems in class clearly step by step. He tells us exactly what topics will be on the test and quizzes and how we should study them. The class was not difficult as long as you attend lectures and take notes.

Skacel is the best professor I've had so far at northeastern. I never understood calc in high school but this course was taught at a really good pace, and Skacel gave so many opportunities to reach out. His office hours are extremely helpful if you're feeling overwhelmed and he's really good about answering emails. Get the textbook for the homework

Danielle is probably the nicest professor/teacher I have ever had the privilege of having. She is helpful and very informative. The class is easy and you get to read comics. She is extremely understanding and allows you to decide the rubric for each essay. I would definitely choose to take her for College Writing!
She's the sweetest, nicest, and most chill professor. Very helpful with discussions and essay feedback. Easy to get an A in the class. I would recommend her over any other College Writing professor.
Pretty cool teacher, what we did in our class was much more interesting than what other classes were doing. The class is really easy and can sometimes be interesting and fun

Professor's Smead gives really entertaining and engaging lectures. He obviously is very passionate about what he's teaching and it shows in his lectures. I will say that going to class is super important, most of the content is taught in-person and not on lecture slides. He also lets you re-do any homeworks until you get a 100% so easy to get an A.

Super fun lectures! He does not take attendance but wants you to complete participation exercises (~80%) that you hand in at the end of class. Homework is optional but super helpful. Extra credit is a possibility at the end of the semester. Always available for office hours and outside of them by appointment. Would 100% recommend his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Warning: if you're taking intro to philosophy know that he changed the course this year. Previous years didn't even have tests and now the tests are so hard he awards you 5 points just for taking it. Nice guy and if you put the work in it's a fun class. But know that this is no longer an easy A. Also, better suited for a smaller class size.

Smead is an incredible lecturer and an overall very nice guy. If you are struggling with the homework, go to his office hours and he will literally walk you through the entire thing. I definitely recommend taking his class (especially since there are no midterms and 50% of your grade is determined by the homework.)

I've heard a lot of great things about Smead, and I'm sure he's great for low level intro philosophy classes, but he really goes ham in more difficult classes. I took him for Ethics and Evolutionary Games and he neglected to explain anything at any point during the year. Very nice man, but unhelpful and an extremely picky grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took his introduction to logic class. He is the best professor I have had so far at Northeastern. He is very approachable  to students when asking questions. I went to his office hours when I didn't understand the homework and he guided me through it, but didn't just tell me the answers. He really helped me understand the concepts. Take Him!

Second class I took with Professor Smead. He's great! No textbook, but lots of readings posted online. The readings can be dense, but they are always clarified in class. He's a fantastic lecturer. His classes are especially good for students who like to debate, as there are always in class discussions.

Easily the best professor I've had at Northeastern. Smead's enthusiasm and passion is infectious; his lectures are interesting and engaging. He's approachable and really cares about his students' success.
A very intellectual professor with great leadership, I will definitely take his class again. Text book is nothing comparing with his lecture, so don't skip class!
Amazing teacher! Very clear and straight to the point. Very willing to explain a concept when the class is confused. Very funny guy. You won't fall asleep in this class.
He's an awesome dude. Definitely recommend this class.

Awesome teacher! His explanations are very clear. He's approachable and will answer all questions - doesn't mind explaining things in a different way if you didn't understand the first time. His class was very interesting and I really enjoyed going. The homework was just enough- not too much or too little.

Professor Smead is the man. I am a neuro major and I found Intro to Logic to not only be extremely relevant but possibly one of the best classes that I've taken at NEU. If you pay attention in class and participate then you will do well. He is very patient and able to explain things in several different ways. I would recommend this class to anyone.

I took Intro To Logic. He was very helpful. He explains things in a way so they're easy to understand. He's very open to answering questions in class, and willing to go over concepts multiple times, for people who need help. I found him easy to learn from. I like his teaching attitude and his assignments are not overly difficult.
Awesome teacher. Very easy tests. Easy A.

I took Intro to Logic which was one of my harder classes. He is very willing to answer questions during class and is extremely helpful during office hours. Going to every class is necessary because if you miss a class, you can easily feel lost. He's not intimidating at all and very friendly, so it makes the class feel easier.

(He's at Tufts) Really passive aggressive, not fun to have as the conductor. Often contradicts what he says and can be very much in your face if you mess up an important rhythm, but then explains the rhythms and melodies poorly. Directions and changes to score are often unclear. That said, he's nice outside of class and invites cool guest artists.
MUSC2208 - definitely NOT recommended for students who have not learned Jazz Theory/Jazz Music
This class was really interesting but 9am so really hard to get there on time. Sometimes he gets mad if you dont do the reading. Overall easy class
Dude's got this one dred that hangs kinda like a leach that suctioned to his forehead.... Distracting when conducting otherwise, well he's the Bill Lumberg of jazz.

I really enjoyed Professor Smith's class. Sometimes he seemed a bit like he was showing off with the piano playing, but in general it was a good class, and he was a good teacher. Of course, I had music experience going in, but if you didn't, it might be hard...
Ehhhh. Doesn't come across as very genuinue. Asks ridiculous "life" questions. Unclear to those new to the subject. Not recommended.

No clear instructions for the midterm exam (worth 15% of grade). Attendance is basically mandatory. There are no announcements on Canvas and doesn't reply to his emails. Decent lectures but gets sidetracked easily. A lot of reading...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This rating pertains to PHIL 4535 (Philosophy of Mind). Professor Smith is the most dynamic lecturer and best professor I have had at Northeastern. The subject matter is extraordinarily interesting and challenging. This course is Smith's bread and butter. If you are looking for a course that will intellectually challenge you, look no further.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor basically loses it if you challenge him. The material is very shallow and he has attention deficit issues. There really seemed to be no point to this course or him being a professor...
very intense lecturer (in the best way), never a dull moment! near perfect syllabus

Great lecturer, but sometimes gets off topic. We don't always go over all the material due to lack of time. It's easy to fall behind since you can get away not doing the reading. It's hard to follow every class because of heavy reading. A lot the grade is participation based, so it's not all too difficult until you have a paper or a presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Smith is a funny guy and explains broad philosophical concepts in a way that is digestible as well as entertaining. However, when you challenge him he will challenge you right back so that isn't always comfortable but his intent is to help you learn. He's a tough essay grader, but eager to help. Overall attendance isn't really important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very nice. Give you credit at long as you tried.

Honestly, Smith can seem a bit scary because of the style he uses when he lectures but he knows how to keep the class engaged and entertained. Phil 1160 is VERY VERY reading heavy, at least, 5-10 hours of reading a week. His system of assignments and grading is a bit odd and can be easy to procrastinate since he doesn't grade much until finals week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Smith. He's great at engaging the class with concepts that are foreign to us. He makes sure that all students comprehend what he is saying since it's easy to get lost. The only thing about the class is that it demands long readings and the professor really can pinpoint if you did the reading or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class all you have to do is show up and do the work and you'll get an A- or A. Subject of the class can be challenging but not the most interesting. Smith is a great dude and will be willing to help.

Smith puts a lot of energy into the class and tries his best to keep students involved. He doesnt require much of the students except weekly discussion posts based on readings. Nothing is really academically challenging until the final paper. Had an experience where he basically yelled at me for not understanding what was saying but its ok

Matthew Smith is very energetic and makes class much more interesting. If it wasn't for his personality, then there was no way I could survive the almost 2 hour class. He grades thing based on attempt (except for the final project/essay). There is a discussion post and a weekly question due each week, but it is not hard. Overall, great professor.

Prof Smith is too good. If you show up to class, he makes the lectures interesting and holds your interest in things you wouldn't think are interesting. If you do the work, then you'll get a good grade easily. The only thing he grades with some difficulty is the final essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He knows what he's talking about but doesn't always know how to tell you about it. Super nice personality and I managed to do well in his class. Might have been better in-person.

Professor Smith is one of my favorite professors. His lectures are engaging and he is really knowledgeable about the subjects. He does a great job of not putting his own opinions into discussions. There is a good amount of reading but it is doable if you stay on top of it.

Prof. Smith is a great professor who is clearly very interested in the material. He is a genuinely nice guy and his lectures though long, are not boring. There is a decent amount of written work but the key is to read everything thoroughly and participate in class. If you do that the other assignments should be a breeze.

took Ethics and Politics of work. He is an energetic and entertaining lecturer. He also did a great job of assigning a reasonable amount of reading and writing. Sometimes I got a bit lost since he understands philosophy so well and I do not, but I really liked the class.

Mr. Smith is really high energy (too much for some people I talked to, but I enjoyed it) and class time is entirely devoted to group discussion about the reading. There were only like 5 things in the grade book for me at the end of the semester, but he was really generous with my grade on the midterm and final papers imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: amazing teacher. passionate. compassionate. understanding. good teacher if you work hard and show up to class. if not, you'll have a hard time. :)

Smith is the dude! Very funny and keeps a really open and engaging class discussion. Attendance not mandatory but he does NOT like it when people dont show up. Readings are gone over in the lecture, papers are kinda weird but just go to office hours hes super helpful 1on1. Scatterbrained is a good word but hes super excitable and passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really funny, easy A if you read and talk in class. Takes attendance sometimes. Uses discussion board posts, participation, 2 papers, and 3 assignments for grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Matthew Smith is a funny guy and a decent professor. The class is conversation based instead of lecture based which is a good way to approach philosophy. He's a little scatter brained but he was good at making you think. The readings were also interesting for the most part and very diverse, so you get exposed to lots of different ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Smith's lectures and assignments were unorganized at times, and he was a little conceited. He clearly answered questions, and tried to be objective, but we studied only leftist theories without exploring counter arguments. Very tough grader, but fair. Definitely go to office hours before a paper is due, he is much more approachable one on one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment:
He's a good professor overall but if you are an international  student I wouldn't recommend taking classes with him.
His instruction papers made no sense and he has a poorly English so he wouldn't be able to explain you the assignments in another context

I truly loved Daryl so much. He inspired me so much when designing outside of class. The assignments he gives all build up and really help you to become a better designer. Daryl is the most positive and uplifting professor I've ever had. He is very helpful with critiques and overall was super fun to have.

Daryl is a caring and easy-going professor. He knows a lot about design/type and is always excited to teach. Do some great work, put the time in, and he will praise you. Sometimes I felt like he didn't give enough critique or constructive criticism for designs, he will tend to focus on what is working rather than what isn't.

Daryl is an awesome professor. He gives very helpful feedback and really helps you grow as a designer, no matter how much experience you have. He assigns unique but helpful projects and you never have to worry about busywork. I would highly suggest taking a class with him.

My favorite professor at Northeastern University. He developed my curiosity for SEO and NLP. I love the subject. The tests were challenging! But overall the professor is amazing. You should take the course.

Smith is an good lecturer, who's knowledge of philosophy makes the course even more engaging. He's clearly passionate and knows his stuff. He perhaps spends too much time drilling the same concepts over and over which can be boring, but that results in knowing most of the stuff really well.
I have worked on assignments for this course and it has really developed my programming practices for the good.

Had him for ILS for physics 1. He definitely seems passionate about physics but isn't the best at explaining most things. It's an ILS course though so you shouldn't really be learning that much in it and just ask the TAs for help if he's not explaining well. Surprisingly tech literate for his age.

Prof. Smith is certainly very nice, but he just can't explain a lot. He mumbles a lot and it is often clear he's not sure what he's talking about. He also drones on during lectures and is not very good at explaining things.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: unclear explanations and mumbles. Just goes over basic equations, but doesn't add anything onto them to increase your understanding. Lecture was a waste of time. He was a pretty lenient grader

Prof. Smith is easily the best physics prof I've had at NEU. He explained complex principles in multiple different ways until it stuck, and encouraged discussion and class feedback as he taught. He is kind, thoughtful, and makes the material moderately interesting. I would play double tuition for Henry Smith to teach every physics class here.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Regurgitates the very little info you'll learn in lecture.  Does not elaborate further on it.  The  group questions have been either way too easy or WAY too hard.  The quizzes assume you have done and understand the homework that is due the next Tuesday after you've had ILS, which makes no sense.

I never had him as a professor, but he is amazingly helpful for my ILS for physics too. He's really nice and so willing to help, and he goes over all of the equations right before the quizzes, which is nice.

useless. way too caught up in formulas. class doesn't match up with online hw or lab. cant answer questions clearly. doesnt understand real applications. real nice guy if that counts for anything. nu physics dept is a joke
class is useless.  nice guy but he doesn't explain anything and the lectures are useless.  could figure it out in physics 1, but am currently screwed in physics 2.

The professor is a pretty nice guy, though he cannot explain material in a way that will make you understand. he will throw out equations that he derives on the board without much explanation of the variables he is using. Don't take this teacher if you can help it. Otherwise finish the homework and learn the material before going to lectures.

Like everybody has said, very nice guy, kinda boring teacher.  He rambles a lot and gets off track.  He doesn't explain things very well, and he is poor at giving examples.  The online ebook is helpful though.  All the homework and weekly quizzes are online.  If you are good at physics, you don't need to go to the class, just use the online book.
nice person but not a very good teacher.

Not the most interesting class. He's nice, but you should sit in the front to hear him speak. He goes a little fast on the problems, but he takes them right out of the book. If you plan to not go to class, study the problems and DO THEM.
No Comments
He is not the quickest of teachers.
one of the most sedating classes ever zzzzz. very round figure and sloooow voice. book was terrible as was he. nice guy but very lazy. his teaching is bad but he has nice hair.

Prof. Smith is one of the laziest people I've ever met. If it wasn't for our lab TA, we (a class of 20) would never have gotten anything graded or returned. That said, he's too lazy to make up difficult assignments or tests, so if you can remain sane through 2 lectures weekly, you'll be fine.

The class is a joke.  If you have a Natural World core to fill, get him for Astronomy.  You only need to ace 2 of the 3 exams to get an A for the course and skip the final.  You only really need to go to class the week before an exam and you'll do fine.
he's such an easy teacher.  i never went to class and i still knew what was going on.  tests are just like practice tests...somewhat difficult final, brought be from an A to a B but he curves
he's a really nice guy, he'll do anything for you.  nobody goes to class, if you do, you'll get an A...but you'll be bored out of your mind.  Take this class to be done with science requirement.
Not a bad teacher. I had him for astronomy class. Talk to him and suck up, you will def. do well.
Very mediocre teacher. Not the best nor the worst. He is pretty old though so is class is very slow and soooooooooooooo boring!
Soheil spends a lot of time on his lectures. Very helpful.

I took CS3000 with Soheil. I made it to most of his lectures, and they were pretty clear and helpful. For the ones I missed, I just watched the recordings. The homework assignments were a bit tough, but manageable. The exams were curved, which was nice.

The logistics were the same for all 4 profs in algo. Soheil is great. He is hella fine so that helps with the long lecture (he records them all). Homework are weird but not impossible to get a good score. All exams have curves but that final was way outta pocket. Algo is already a hard subject but Soheil did the best job in his ability to teach it.
Barely curves. Doesn't care enough to guide his students to succeed in his class.

She is a nice professor and clearly cares about writing as an art form; however, the class is needlessly difficult. She grades tough; she hasn't given an A on any of the 5/6 assignments. Mainly, I don't feel like I learned much after taking this class. Class is boring, and the assignments are time-consuming. Only take it if you really want to work.

Took this class in Spring 2022. This professor's workload was very hard to manage considering it's a first-year writing course. The worst part is that while reading MLK's Letter From Birmingham Jail aloud to the class, she read the n-word (hard R)...out loud. She didn't repeat it after that but once was enough. Do not take this professor's class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Realistically first-year writing should not be a very difficult class, but she gives us an essay due every week, and she's a tough grader. If you are taking a first-year writing course I highly recommend not taking it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I initially found her intimidating, as the first few weeks we were bombarded with papers due every week. Got easier as the semester progressed and her teaching style grew on me. Holds workshop sessions before the final paper is due, so make sure you have a complete draft ready so that you get her feedback before submitting the final version.

She is an amazing professor and is hilarious too. You need to put in effort to get an A but she cares a lot about her students and improving their writing skills. There's always a workshop before a writing assignment is due so make sure to have it done before the workshop so she can give you feedback before you turn in the final draft

Be ready to have a 1250-1500 word essay due every week. The guidelines are ridiculous, the class is corny and boring, and discusses topics nonimportant to real-world issues. Every time a paper was submitted there was something new wrong with it, be prepared to spend 6+ hours a week on her assignment and writing combined. Overall bad experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice professor, often let us out of class early. Definitely helps you grow your writing skills and the essays are fun to write because she gives good prompts.

Prof Spilecki was a great advanced writing professor. She assigned lots of reading, but was very fair on grading. At times expectations were confusing, and I was not sure what we were supposed to be doing. Take advantage of the peer review time and be prepared for the due dates to creep up on you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you are only taking writing to get the credit DO NOT TAKE HER IT WILL BE YOUR BIGGEST REGRET. The papers are due every week and end up being 15-20 pages. She is also the most unorganized teacher I have ever had it's awful. She redid the syllabus so many times because the due dates were wrong. Plus its so much work to get an A.

There is a reading due every class and a paper due almost every week which were interesting. She wants to see her students succeed and is passionate about writing but you have to work for your grade but she is easily accessible outside of class. She is also pretty lenient with deadlines but canvas does not match what she assigns in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Run away. I had to take her because I had no other option. Tough grader and the classes are really boring. Canvas is completely messed up and no clear instructions on due dates.

Compared to other first year writing classes it is much more difficult and you have to really work for your grade. Most of the time spent in class is spent "workshopping" where we come to class and sit in silence while we are supposed to work on our papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Spilecki was nice and great at keeping the class engaged. The class itself was not a breeze as there was a paper due almost every week, but the prompts keep the class interesting. Also super flexible with deadlines.

Had her for First-Year Writing and I loved her class. You write a lot, but the essay prompts are super interesting and allow for a lot of creative freedom. She's also a lenient grader and really just cares that you try your best to become a better writer. Another bonus: if she gets through her lesson plan early, she lets you out early, no busywork
This is the god professor

Professor Spilecki is a very nice person. She will grant you an extension for pretty much anything and is very understanding. You end up writing a paper every couple weeks, and they are usually a bit lengthy. Her grading gets easier as the semester progresses, even if you do not improve. Not super hard, but also not a super easy A.
Had her for first year writing, she made it very interesting and enjoyable. Grading and workload is fair but not super easy. Would take again.

Really cool and passionate. Her essay topics are more interesting than a lot of other professors and I really enjoyed listening to her talk. She gets to know her students and there isn't a lot of reading. She even nominated one of my essays to be published in a journal.
Difficult to understand what is required from class. Nice lady and means well however i don't believe that she conveys information clearly.

Prof Spilecki is the best! My interest in writing increased immensely over the semester because of the interesting writing topics and essays. My own writing definitely improved. Not too much work and pretty easy class

Professor Spilecki made College Writing an interesting experience. She's very acoomodating, and doesn't every really get upset with the class. The workload is very light for a college writing class, and the workshops are very helpful. As long as you show up and write all the papers on the day they're do, you'll do fine in this class.

Best one out of the three. Was the only one who communicated out of all of them. Great guy, super caring, and very eager to help in and outside of class. Everything about the class sucked but he made it bearable. Started every class with three deep breaths, offered lots of extra credit/easy points on weekly quizzes. Truly a chiller

Was the best out of the three professors in my opinion but still not amazing. Your grade is made up of mainly the midterm and final. Basically had to teach myself everything since class time was spent doing group work while you had to watch videos at home to learn concepts. I would avoid.

The class is reverse-classroom style, meaning you watch the lecture videos for hw and do practice problems in class. His lectures are alright, but he is the least approachable guy ever. He acts like it's a burden to answer your question and is not particularly helpful. Overall extremely mid

Great guy. Lectures are short, but he is willing to walk you through any points of confusion if you ask. He makes you take 3 deep breaths before every class, which I lowkey liked. Just watch the lectures and take notes before class, otherwise you'll be a little lost.
Incredibly mid professor. You learn on your own and lectures arent the most helpful thing, but he is really informative and answers questions well when you ask.

you basically have to be prepared to teach yourself because there are only 10min lectures outside of class and during class time your only working on practice problems. midterms and finals are nothing like practice problems. They do drop your two lowest quiz grades and have extra credit so as long as u put in effort u should get atleast a C.

Class was alight. Half the semster the students barely came to class ,  you have to teach yourself basically, 
had three professors. The teachers  cared  but office hours wasn't helpful either so just make sure you do homework ande do well on the quiz and midterm which wasn't to hard
Terrible. Do not take. Does not teach the class, uses a bad reverse classroom methods.

his teaching is good *when* he teaches. there are no lectures, just pre-recorded videos. you just do problems in-class and can ask questions. this is not how a physics course should be ran. there is an incredible lack of connection between professor and student. half of the class stops showing up about a few weeks in.
very respectful teacher and nice all around.
Bryan was great, a little soft spoken but really knows his stuff and wants the students to succeed. Makes problems that are easier to understand and really works with the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I loved abnormal psych with Dr Snyder! The flipped classroom structure allowed for alot of group discussions. However, there were times when the discussion could have been more structured for this format to work, rather than just generally leaving it open to student questions and going over specific one on one questions.

I love Dr. Snyder! Her classes are a bit hard, but if you pay attention and do the reading you're set. She's so interesting and funny, and she has a lot of experience in Psychology. I love hearing the stories she tells and she's clearly passionate about what she does.

I do not recommend taking Intro with her. Lectures are boring, she's disorganized, tells random stories that don't help reinforce the material, and is generally rude. Study the outlines before the exams and you're all set.

She is a great teacher, but a little out of practice in the field of psych. She is kind and passionate, but often has brain blips and mixes up words in her lectures that creates difficulty if you aren't familiar with the material. Tests are easy, she provides study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoy taking this class. As long as you show up to Prof Snyders lecture & take lots of notes, you should be fine for her exams. There are 4 noncumulative exams, which is good cuz then u have less to study. Make sure you look at outlines before an exam cuz it helps to know exactly what to study: read specific parts in textbook if necessary
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I found her to be tedious. The class is all lecture which is understandable, but she is just boring and very unapproachable. It just seems like she's been teaching for way too long and is set in her old school ways. Basically, I had trouble getting interesting in a subject that seems very interesting otherwise.

Dr. Snyder is awesome. She really tries to make her lectures interesting (even the dry topics) and uses her experiences to help give examples of topics. Your grade is basically 4 exams, a paper, and group project. The exams are not hard if you go to her lectures and use the outline to study. Take a class with her!

I loved this Professor. Her teaching is very lecture-based, but she uses a lot of side stories to help you understand the material. I was rarely bored in her class and found that she was very helpful and supportive when you ask for help. There are very few assignments in the class, so make sure you study hard and do your best on the projects!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: disorganized mess, tests are impossible if you don't read textbook, frankly rude to her students, extra help is recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever. Rude and boring. Will never take a class with her again, had her as an advisor but ended up switching programs so I wouldn't have to work with her.
Exams are really hard, classes are boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nancy is the worst professor I have ever  had! Her classes are dreadful & boring. she is extremely disrespectful towards students,  & rude when you ask her questions. She is very demeaning and not friendly! Her lectures are all over the place and not clear at all. Her quizzes are tricky, and difficult, plus includes a lot of memorization.
She is very helpful and explains everything well. Her tests can be a little tricky if you do not study. Also her lecture outlines help a lot.
Going to class and taking notes will make you get an A in this class.

Her class is sometimes confusing but if you go to office hours she'll make you understand. Quizzes aren't difficult if you study from your notes and textbook. My notes were really bad so I used only the textbook to study and for me that was enough.

This class was confusing to me. Granted, it was my first college semester but I felt that whenever I asked for an explanation, I was more confused afterward. And her TA was NOT helpful. The class was not as enriching as other Psych 101 and If I knew any better, I would've chosen a better psych 101 professor or read a psych book instead.
Her lecture are unorganized and all over the place. She does not know how to teach or explain any topic.
Study her slides & read the book. She likes to ask questions about prevalence and concordance rates.

Her classes are long and boring. She's a very knowledgeable  woman but because of this she expects everyone to just understand anything she gives to us. She's quite condescending! What is the worst, is her quizzes. No matter whether I spend days  of study or whether I don't study at all, I always receive the a score in the same range!

If you are good at memorization you will be fine. She gives out outlines but many questions on the exams are not consistent with her lecture. You can easily miss the class and just use your textbook and the outlines but it's a lot of reading and memorization. Not friendly at all if you ask for help.

Very easy! Gives printed outlines, just fill in as she lectures (so don't miss class). Outlines are easy to follow and informative. I didn't buy or use a textbook once. Exams are easy multiple choice taken right from the outlines.

She spoke fast and went through her slides too quickly. She said a lot of personal stories, supposedly to help understand concepts but it's debatable if they were actually helpful. Of course though this is my biased opinion. I was miserable but at least it helped me decide to change my major lol.

Nancy is by far the worst professor I have had at NU. She does not care about her students what so ever, she is rude and she lives in the past. She expected a class of 25 people to go to the psych office to fight over 5 copies of an article she refused to put online. And then yelled in my face when I emailed her that I couldn't get them. She sucks.

Nancy is AMAZING! She is probably one of the best teachers I have EVER had. She makes the material interesting, the class is NEVER boring. If you go to class, pay attention, and study the outline it is IMPOSSIBLE to get a bad grade. Take every class possible with this professor. She makes you realized why you LOVE psychology! AWESOME!!!

Snyder is one of my favorite professors. Her classes are big, so if you want extra help you have to seek her out after class. But chances are, you won't need the extra help. Snyder makes her lectures clear and very interesting. You'll never be bored in her class and you'll learn so much! I definitely recommend her!

If you get this Prof, you will have the best Psychological experience of your LIFE.  She promptly brings the class into the field of Psychology as a science, sharing with you the latest in the way of Psychological findings!  Take as many courses with her as you can!  She's GREAT!

I loved this class. It was so easy if you went to class. Everything on the exam is from class and the minimal reading. If you have common sense and an understanding of the disorders, you will do great. She loves the class and it really shows through. A great class!

You need to go to class to do well on tests. There are only 4 tests in the semester, each worth 25% of your grade.  They are all multiple choice.  If you're not such a great multiple choice test-taker, do not take this class.  You also need to go to class to do well.  She does not take attendance which is nice, but you pretty much need to go.

I had her for Foundations of Psychology and I thought she was awesome.  She is very clear and makes sure you understand the material.  Good discussion in class - PARTICIPATE!  Go to the discussion sessions - it's where you take your quizes and they really help
Good professor. She really enjoys the topics and it shows. She is very clear and her lectures are not boring.

Dr. Snyder is a great professor. She is VERY clear on what you need to do. Outlines are provided and only what is on the outlines will be on the quizes and tests, so as long as you pay attention in her class than you will be fine. Attendance is not mandatory, except in discussions, but it is recommended. Great professor overall!
An awesome teacher. You can tell she loves it!
She knows how to make the classes interesting. She also knows that students sometimes work better in smaller groups and therefore does discussion sections.
She's a great professor that loves teaching.  This class was very interesting and very fair.  Crazy people are so interesting!  Just study and you'll do fine.

She wont put you to sleep, but she's nothing amazing either.  If your interested in Psych than it's nearly impossible to do poorly.  You'll do fine as long as you don't let the "ider's" get in the way.
Very good teacher. explains things clearly. if you study for the quizzes you will do well.

She likes to talk. A lot. If she could she would keep you there for hours just talking. Discussion sections are a must. Tests are a breeze if you pay attention. Not much work involved. As good as a teacher as she is, she is very rude in person, so be careful when approaching her. The TA is much more easy to talk to...and much funner to look at.

I had her for abnormal, and she was an ok teacher but was very rude to me as an individual when I asked her for help.  I was not doing extremely well in her class, and tried talking to her twice about it, and both times left the meeting crying.  When going over a test I got a C on, she asked if I "even ever bought the book".  Unnecessarily rude.

I heard mixed reviews before I took her class but she really is a good professor. She teaches you what you need to know. Lectures aren't mandatory but the stuff she emphasizes are usually in the quizzes, but if you do the reading, you'll be fine. Discussion. Her anecdotes help you learn better.

She is good because she only teaches what you have to know and what will be on the quizzes. The discussion sessions are really useful and the guy who teaches them probably explains it better than Snyder.

My favorite teacher in the psych dept! She is a very effective and straightfoward teacher. You can really tell she loves teaching and cares about her students. (Make sure you turn you cell phone off before class, she really hates when it goes off!)

I learned a lot in this class and it was very interesting. Reading the book and the case studies is basically mandatory if you want to pass the tests, which are very challenging but you can do well if you study. Her lectures are long-winded and it's hard to write down everything she says, but if you pay attention you will do well.

She knows her stuff, and she will never mince words, which is nice. Tests are tough, but I'm told if you listen AND read you can do well. Personally, I couldn't deal with the book, it's rather tedious, so I just did ok. DO NOT COME LATE TO CLASS.  She has no sympathy for lateness, unless you email her beforehand. Overall she's great, but tough.

Kind of boring and i find it hard to get myself to go to the class but mostly likely that more because i learned most of this info my senior year in high school. But she is definitely a good teacher and her teaching style is very straight forward and as long as you go to class and pay attention, you'll be fine. reading the textbook does help, tho

I have taken 2 classes with Prof Snyder and enjoyed both. She is straight-forward and teaches the material very well.  Do the reading, go to class, and you will learn a lot. I highly recommend this teacher.
No Comments
She is a great teacher. If you don't understand something, she will absolutely make you understand if you ask. Fairly easy. Take notes and read the books.
she's great
great professor. she's very clear and has a lot of experience in the field, so she has a few good stories... highly recommended!
I learned a great deal from this professor.  She gave really interesting lectures, and was very helpful to students who asked questions.
You learn a lot from her. Also, if you know the material on the outline then you'll do great on her tests
totally awesome she's very accomodating and respectful, as long as YOU are -- follow her simple requests (don't come in late, turn of your phone, don't talk in class) and she's cool with you
Go to class, take notes, if she knows your face she'll help you out. Go and talk to her just to meet her in person (seeing as though she teaches many auditorium classes).
No Comments

Provides useful course outlines. Remember to do the reading from BOTH books. All tests are multiple choice, and there's only 4 (no midterm or final). Very friendly and approachable. Don't be late to her class. Don't let your cell phone ring. Other than that, she's fairly lenient and a good prof.

She's not a super hard teacher.  This is the second class I've has with her, and she gives out outlines for everything that she teaches.  Her test are all multiple choice, they're not super easy, but if you go to class and study, you should have no problem. She's good professor, I recommend her.
great teacher, presents material clearly. tests are easy if you pay attention and study. she speaks from experience, which helps the class move along.

She is great and her hand-outs help you take great notes so you can study for the tests and quizes. Tests and quizes are all MC and very straight-forward. I would take another class with her anytime. She is great and very understanding and helpful.

Snyder's awesome. I had her my first semester here and she's really clear and fair so I took a second class with her. She provides a good mix of real-life stories and factual information. If you show up for class and stay awake you should do really well and really enjoy her class.
Pretty easy if you read the material.  The lectures are often optional.

she was a good professor.  but you have to make sure that you study because there are quizzes every week and if you do bad that could really lower your grade.  but other than that, she's a really nice professor and takes the time to teach things clearly in lecture.
If you follow the outlines, come to class, and take good notes, you've got this one in the bag.  Snyder's very clear in class, and her honors adjunct just requires some reading and group discussion.

Amazing Teacher. She keeps the class so interetsing and gives examples for everything. She also gives out outlines that prepare you for the tests and quizes. She gives quizes almost every week that help your grade and one midterm and final. I loved this class and recommend the Professor!!

great great teacher. gives outlines of every lecture that she gives. if you go to class and take notes,  you should do great in the class. always very helpful and very clear and concise. i recommend taking her class.

Prof. Snyder is very clare and organized in her lectures. As long as students keep up with the reading, there should be no reason to fail her course. I signed up to take Abnormal Psych with her because I enjoyed Foundations of Psych so much.

Pretty good teacher.  She gives outlines of the material and quizzes every week or two to make sure you keep up. Don't fall behind, go to lectures and stay on top of the material, and you will do fine.
Awesome abnormal teacher. Gives outlines, so easy to follow. Most material on exams based on outline, but also good to read the cases studies. Overall, great teacher!
Intro is an easy class and she makes outlines which help
She covers alot of material so you really need to stay on top of getting the notes and understanding the material
Nancy....good lady
