Professor Sylvanus is a great professor that truly cares for her students. The course is a bit reading-heavy but her lectures / discussions are very engaging. As long as you participate in class and put effort into group projects and discussion boards, you'll do great.
She was trying out new course material in our section, so it was a bit rough. She moves quickly and sometimes assumes everyone knows what she means. Really caring and cool person though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Nina is a great professor who clearly cares a lot for student's well-being and genuinely wants everyone to be engaging with the material. She will treat you like an adult, which is good.

I took Dr. Sylvanus's class in my last semester as an elective. The material wasn't particularly new to me, but she taught me to look at it as an anthropologist. She genuinely cares for her students' mental health, and is very responsive to what her students need, educationally and emotionally.

Shes such a nice lady and has an aura through the screen (because i had her online this semester) that is really inviting and makes you feel comfortable and want to participate in her class. She did say the class wasn't heavy on reading.. I would say that there was quite a bit of reading. Shes easy to meet with and cares about her students.

I've had her as a professor twice now. Very open ended class with lots of discussion, and she really cares about teaching what the students are most interested in. There is a quite a bit of reading, and they tend to be hard and theoretical, but really interesting.

Make sure you study the book well and take the practice quizzes online from the book. She picks obscure facts from the books and puts them on the tests. The class appears to be easy but the tests are unproportionately difficult when compared with the subject matter and the class.

taught right out of the book, assigned tedious take home quizzes and make up assignments that ended up taking students a minimum of 4 hours to complete. for such an intelligent woman with great career experience and stories to share, i was very disappointed.
Teaching right out of the book, not answering email, making up BS assignments, and missing tons of classes?  I really think a student could have taught this class better.

Do not take any of her classes. She doesn't get grades back to you nor do your grades reflect your actual knowledge. Tests are ridiculous and require the memorization of random statistics, she also gives no type of study guide. She seems like a nice person but that doesn't really make you feel better as you see your gpa plummeting before your eyes.

The most irksome attribute of her is the arbitrary way in which she treats her class. She cancels class frequently and with little warning, does not effectively convey assignments and their importance in the overall scheme of the class, and does not regard her syllabus in the slightest. She made the class as bad of an experience as it could be.

Entered Abnormal Psych with enthusiasm. Most ineffective professor Ive ever had. Class time is a waste. Puts little thought into assignments. What is required for quizzes is inconsistent with syllabus. Assigns lots of busy work but doesnt adequately cover what is on tests. Material on test is from reading, not class, which makes no sense to me.

terrible class. do not take it because she never gets her tests back quickly enough and her lectures are very lengthy. heavy reading involved. talked to her outside of class and she seemed sympathetic but in class she is a hard grader. her tests are not designed well. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless you want your GPA to drop

This class is seriously damaging my GPA. Amy does not report the grades in time for you to know how well or how poorly you are doing. She is a really lazy professor.  Her tests are not designed for her students to succeed. Do not take any of her classes unless you want a semester long headache.
Agreed. Lazy professor, more interested in wanting herself to do well/look well to her students.

I'm gonna have to disagree with the whole "wants her students to do well" thing. The 1st test was straight from the online quiz, the 2nd changed just enough to confuse or trick people. Definitiely gonna damage my GPA.

Do not take her class. She IS NOT AT ALL HELPFULL. She knows her stuff, but good luck if you dont get something in class. I actually ended up having to go get help from my other psych professor. A lot of reading. I feel like I basically teached myself. She lied bout the final and told us some things WERNT goin2b on it and they were.

Last day of class is tomorrow and I'm missing grades she hasn't submitted to blackboard so I don't even know where I stand in the class. Don't bother e-mailing her because its as good as banging your head on the wall aka you get nowhere but older. Good luck taking the class.

She does want her students to do well, but she can't balance her private life and professional life. Which unfortunately means she will just make notes of EVERYTHING in the book and give them to you and then quiz you on them. My advice is good luck to anyone who takes her class. Or try and take the class with another (better) prof.

WORST TEACHER IVE EVER HAD IN LIFE. and I got a B+ in the class. I don't care if shes easy or a nice person. I pay $40,000 for good education...and I taught myself in this class. On the last day of class she said that if she was a student, she would have withdrew...REALLY? regardless of personal problems, you need to be a professional and step it u

Teacher tought straight out of the book.  The only reason to attend was for in-class assignments.  She eventualy makeher lecture useless by not going over the power points she made but by brainstorming useless information with the class.  Don't take her class unless you can't avoid it.

Disregard the statement below this one. She had a tough semester this past fall and it was due to a loss of a close friend. People need to chill out and be human. She didn't cause anybody their future and if this class was the difference between a good one and and a bad one then you might want to think about changing your major.

Had her for Dev and Social Psychology.  She's very nice and enthusiastic; one of my favorite professors.  She's still writing the curriculum so it's not perfect yet.  She asks you to critically analyze research and topics, so she's not as easy as other professors.  I thoroughly enjoyed her classes.

I don't know why people have a problem with her-if they do its probably b/c they don't pay attention in class. If you're there then its really not that hard. No one should be complaining about the lit review-she gave the rubric ahead of time&offered to read a rough draft. She's very knowledgeable & enthusiastic about the material. Loved the class.

reminds me of a 3rd grade girl at summer camp. cute little girl in a womens body. very nice lady, and wants everyone to do well. doesnt try to trick you but wants you to know your material. not an easy class but if you do the work you can do well. i never really tried that hard outside of class but some things in class i found interesting

She definitely means well and wants her students to do well. Class time is not very useful. Tests are hard but when you put in effort there is potential to do well. Does not grade quickly and takes a long time to get back to you.

Great professor, really cares about his students learning the material. The class average on one of the tests was a 63% and he let everyone retake the exact same test for a new grade. Besides that one test, I got A's on the other 3, just study and you will be perfectly fine!

Professor Syed is a great guy. He loves teaching and interacting with students, hes the sweetest professor I've ever had. But he can be very difficult to understand at times, and can get things wrong as well.

cons: not a great teacher & not clear at all b/c he is unfamiliar with the subject, which is why he was replaced. pros: he "accidentally" gave us the previous term's exams as practice which were almost identical to the ones we were about to take... haha nice guy but will prob never teach this class again

Apparently Calc1 students like Syed. If you're taking an intermediate math class and actually expect to learn from your professor, look elsewhere. Syed was of little help; he was often wrong, knew little about linear algebra, and couldn't answer a simple question. He was replaced by a much more helpful grad student halfway through the semester.

Awesome guy. He is serious about his math but enjoys teaching and is an expert. Old man, but quick in the mind. He has a great sense of humour and is extremely helpful, tends to go out of class during quizes, he wants you to do well in everything! Does not take attendance, but "you will feel the effects" of not coming to class.
Can be mean at times, but easy.

one word...AWESOME!  He'll re-explain anything to you until you get it.  He'll let you re-take quizzes and actually grades homework for credit.  GREAT professor.  I wish i could get him for Calc 2..........

Bottom line is that Syeds Business Calc Class is a guaranteed 'A' unless youre either an **** or a moron or both. If you want to be treated like youre in kindergarden and not do any thinking on your own, then Syed is your man. I have a feeling mostly the idoits at NU are the ones who like him jmo

This teacher really wants you to do well. He explains everything thouroughly and if you go to him for extra help if you still do not understand the information her will GLADLY help. Very nice man. WANTS YOU TO SUCCEED. Best teacher I have had this year!
HE IS THE MAN! TAKE THIS CLASS! BE NICE TO HIM!
Great teacher, always available for help and if he likes you, hell help you on tests... easy class
He is the man, if u wanna do well on quizes just go up to him and ask him for help.  Its an easy A class...get this guy
ishy is the best teacher alive, i dont care wat any kids say, dont listen to them, he is hilarius, so chill, always teaching and laughing, only positive things about him.
Ishy is the man i swear he is the funniest teacher alive, so cool, and jokes about not knowing things which is real funny- everyone should experience the world of syed- my boy
Funny because i dont understand what hes tryin to say half of the time.  Good teacher, explains things well.  Class is farley easy
Ishy's my boy...He's the funniest teacher I have ever had..and he gets you prepared for the final
He is one of the best professor I had this year. He is very helpful if you try in his class. I would suggest him as a teacher.
he yells at you when you ask for help; the worst teacher i have had here!

Super nice and unconventional when it comes to grading. The class has busy work, but as long as you do the work and show up to class you get at least a B. You have to advocate for your grade to have it go higher but the attendance and work is super easy so it's not difficult. However, I think a lot of the assignments did not help my writing grow.

Complete all your assignments correctly, on time, and participate in class --> you get a B, not an A. She assigns a lot of busy work readings, and attendance is mandatory. She also provides vague details on what she actually wants to see from you in your writing. She is very flexible and obviously cares a lot, but I would not take her class again.

Dr V. is a great professor. She doesn't believe in typical grading, and the entire course is effort-based. If you go to every lecture, you WILL get an A. The class is also interesting and changes your perspective on writing.

I thought this professor wasn't gonna be bad, but ended up getting tanked with reading and work. Would recommend taking any other professor, my friends took the same class and had half the work as I did. Also, grades very harsh and that says something because I put in upwards of 5-10 hours a week on this course

Talia Vestri is one of the kindest and most supportive professors I've ever had. I highly recommend her. If you just attend class on time and complete all the assignments, you're definitely going to earn an A.

If you do attend every class and complete the papers on time, you are likely to get a good grade. All the papers are graded by effort and completion. The class itself can be a bit boring and non-helpful, but it is a good intro to writing class to take.

All you have to do is show up on time and submit the work.  There isn't much work at all and when there was work you didn't need to spend more than an hour on it.  She seemed to be against university as a system of learning which is strange as a yk... university professor?  If you can write a high school level essay, you'll get an A.

reviews.comment: Easy class, she grades based on completion so as long as you show up and submit assignments on time, you're good. Some of her assignments were a bit annoying and discussions were repetitive. If you speak in discussion she will ask you a ton of follow-up questions, which can get annoying. But she's a good person and tries to make class interesting.

Dr. V definitely cares for her students wants us to learn, and has a nice grading policy (as long as you do the work - you'll get an A). She also gave us plenty of flex time to use on assignments. It was not an unreasonable amount of work at all, and she always gave us thorough feedback.
Class is graded on completion. Complete your work and you get an A. 2 projects, every week you build on it. Should take around 2 hours a week to complete all assignments

reviews.comment: We had homework/reading due for every class but never received any kind of credit so I just stopped doing them. The class was an easy A but we are only graded on the 3 papers. A lot of class is busy work or just working on your paper/peer editing it.

Dr. V is a pretty good English teacher. She does give a ton of feedback, and we have a ton of time in class to work on our papers. While the class is only graded off of three papers, we do spend a lot of time working on them, so it isn't too terrible. She is very reasonable, and she does want to see her students do well.

Dr.V clearly organized every week's schedule and provided ample feedback. We were graded only one a few papers so each one held a lot of wait, but she very much wanted to see every student succeed and was always available to meet outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: We got over HALFWAY through the semester without a single grade. She never put grades in Canvas so you have no idea what your grade is. Instead, she just sent us an email 3/4 of the way through the semester giving us a rough range of what our grade is. The class is graded based on only 3 papers. She gives us homework but we don't get credit for it.

Very knowledgeable scholar and ready to talk about any topic. First professor I've seen who genuinely cares about each and every student. Class has a LOT of readings but as long as you participate you will receive a good grade. She does tend to go on tangents but discussions are engaging.

What ruined it for me was how this class was fully online, even though I registered it to be in person. She goes overtime while I told her multiple times that I have another class after hers, so she gives me only 3-5 minutes to get to my next class. No modules page, no slideshows, and boring discussions.

The class was switched fully online after registration, which really ruined it for me. Two-hour Zoom classes with little structure or slides were unproductive and boring. Grading was mostly completion-based with minimal feedback, and emails often took days to get a response. This course would've been much better in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Anjanette is so sweet and genuine. I didn't love the amount of readings and presentations, but she makes the class such an interesting and comforting space. The class is fascinating, and if you participate often, you will do very well. Loved her!

Best professor I had at Northeastern. Highly recommend taking afro-asian relations in the americas. Chan Tack is a brilliant scholar, extremely personable, and genuinely cares about making connections with her students and making sure they learn.

Chan Tack was, without a doubt, the best professor I have ever had. She is smart and cares for every student. Her lectures are amazing. She assigns a lot of reading, but none of it feels like busy work. She is a fair grader and prioritizes the learning of students over cramming the Syllabus. I cannot recommend this course enough!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tareq provides high-quality instruction. The course difficulty is well balanced, and he pays close attention to important details in his teaching.

Prof Nasralah is a great teacher who cares about his students. The class might be a bit more difficult than other business courses, however his generous grading compensates for that. Definitely recommend him for business stats, one of the best professors.
easy A if your group members are reliable.

reviews.comment: Professor Nasralah was so nice and understanding. His lectures were a bit dry but you can tell he really cares and wants everyone to succeed.

reviews.comment: A kind professor who is always accessible outside of class. We had 4 quizzes, 4 individual homeworks, 4 group homeworks, a group project (which wasn't bad at all), a midterm, and a final. Not too hard to do well in the class- beware he does spend class going over the lectures which can get boring. He is not a tough grader and you can tell he cares!

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but what he doesnt realize is that he doesnt teach us anything by simply doing it in front of us. We had to teach ourselves everything which is very hard to do when youre learning to code for the first time.

I really enjoyed having him as a professor! He was very enthusiastic, kind, and was always happy to answer questions. The group project given was very logical and was not random like some other classes. One note: I wouldn't recommend getting the first textbook, it was rather confusing. 100% recommend taking this class with him.
Great professor! Very understanding and kind and always ready to help you.

reviews.comment: Overall great professor. He really knows his stuff. Class was interesting and assignments and exams were not too difficult. 10/10 would take this class again.
She is great, super helpful homework. If you don't use AI, you will learn a lot from her homework

The format of the class is very clear with well defined lectures, labs, homework, and other assignments. There is a huge availability of resources and a lot of help available including Piazza and office hours. The professor is extremely reasonable and accessible, and if you do the work assigned without the use of ChatGPT, you will do well.
do not take her class
I thought this was a great class. Will thoroughly prepare you to improve your coding design skills.

Professor Bonaci's ability to fluently explain why she is doing something in the code speaks volumes to her knowledge in computer science and object oriented design. You can also tell she genuinely cares deeply about your learning experience and will help you if you're struggling. I recommend taking any of Professor Bonaci's courses if you can!

Professor Bonaci is well versed in the topic of OOD and makes each and every lecture interesting and full of helpful information to help students also become knowledgeable about OOD principles. She makes sure that every student is prepared to succeed, given that they put in the work and shows a respectable amount of effort on each assignment.

Professor Bonaci is the best professor, she cares about her students and would love to address problems for students. She gives us a clear explanation of the conceptual ideas and gives us examples to demonstrate the concepts. Her homework is well-designed for practicing the conceptions we learned in class.

Professor Bonaci goes above and beyond to produce a great learning experience. She organizes her lectures in a way that allows for review of the material as well as introducing new content. Professor also takes time to ask for feedback and designs her assignments in a very thoughtful way. Highly recommend taking this course with Professor Bonaci!

Tamara inspired the class to think about issues associated with Data Science, AI, and ML. We read a lot of papers and were also asked to find papers relevant to the domain on our own. As an MS student who was taking an advanced-level course, this was the course that gave me a clear-cut idea of what I should be pursuing in the future.

This professor's professional abilities are sorely lacking. Teaching style is confusing, material remains unclear. Availability is virtually nonexistent, feedback is a rare sighting, and rudeness seems to be their forte. To top it off, even emails go unanswered. Overall, not a stellar educational experience.
Not a great professor at all.

The professor doesn't understand OOD concepts and is a terrible teacher. She barely uploads course materials on time, and she seldom walks codes but just reads the slides during lecture time. She made the course unnecessarily confusing. You might ask a simple question, and she will give you an answer as if you're doing brain surgery. DO NOT TAKE!
Nobody knows what his grading criteria is

Very kind and understanding, if you have anything he is always willing to listen and accommodate. Like the previous review said, just work hard on the review sheets because the questions will be on the exams themselves. Quite an easy grader as long as you put in the right ideas. Overall a great professor that makes class fun to go to.

Fantastic Professor who does very well in giving in-depth lectures on the curriculum. Good balance of assignments and makes tests easy to study for. His practice tests will often have questions that are present in the official test.

This is my favorite professor at Northeastern, although I didn't do too well in the class it was completely my fault. He gives practice tests that are very similar to the test. There was one group assignment, but it was pretty quick and nice grade booster. He truly cares about you doing well and will give you all the help you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super passionate about economics, wants to see all students succeed. Tests are very straightforward and easy if you do the practice beforehand. I would suggest reading the textbook chapters before the lectures to make them a little easier. Lectures can feel long at times but he gives ten minute breaks which is great. Overall a great teacher!

He's pretty nice and you can tell that he cares about the class. All the homeworks are pretty easy and for all the tests he posts a practice test that tends to be pretty similar. Sometimes he's hard to understand but if you follow the slides you'll be good. Join if you want a good grade and don't care too much about the details of macroeconomics.

Probably one of the kindest professors I have ever had. He really cares about his students and their progress . Get ready to be organized to excel in his class. Overall great person and teacher. Sometimes lectures are a little mundane but what do you expect its macro...
hes great, just do the practice tests and take time on the few homeworks there are assigned

I've taken macroeconomic theory with this professor, and returned this semester for microeconomic theory. His lectures are clear, he is very well-versed in the material, and he is very available for clarifications. I thoroughly enjoy learning with him and he is also very understanding about certain situations.

I think this professor is a very responsible professor. He will patiently answer my question when I don't understand something. I promise, if you pay attention in class, there shouldn't be too much problem in the exam. More importantly, through the course taught by this professor, I have a clear understanding of the framework of macroeconomics.

Very by the book prof. His lectures are pretty much him regurgitating the textbook back to you and his homework and tests are almost exactly taken from the textbook as well. Happy to answer questions and a very considerate prof, but you will need to pretty much teach yourself most of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The man is just so old, absolutely impossible to learn anything from this class. He just mumbles information from his terribly written slides for an hour and a half while not a single person in the classroom is paying attention. If you value your sanity, take econometrics with another professor.

He's super nice chill, especially for Applied Econ, which is supposed to be an intensive writing requirement. Zooms every lecture, only grades are problem sets & final project that he assigned around Halloween. He isn't as tech savvy but that was fine. Make an effort to get to know him & for him to get to know you he really enjoys it!!

Guys he's chill. His grading is amazing. He's not a tough grader. If you want a chill class this is it. Idk what the other reviews are talking abt. I recommend him. Attendance isn't mandatory. The final is a project. Your gonna be graded on the final project and problems sets.

Mr. Tardiff is a nice guy but not suited for teaching. Struggles with technology. Teaching style is boring and bland. He just reads off of prewritten slides and I have learned nothing from this class. Assignments are extremely easy, no quizzes, no tests, and the final is just a project that he assigns basically a month before its due.

Professor Tardiff is a little too old to be teaching and this "introductory" statistics class is impossible to understand if you haven't taken AP Stats. Problem Sets are incredibly confusing and half of the class time is spent correcting something he wrongly put onto them. I would highly recommend taking this class with anyone else if possible.

I took her Art History class in University of Delaware. She is a really caring teacher who is passionate and presents good presentations. She gives clear feedback and grades fair. The class was easy, however she does have an attendance policy, and personally I found it boring. I could've gotten an A and never showed up if it weren't for attendance.
Very friendly professor, unparalleled, meticulous guidance and care for students.

really loved this professor and the content of the class! she was super passionate about the topic which inspired me and was very accommodating and not too demanding with papers and homework. she would ask the class what kind of projects or homework we wanted to do at times which was so appreciated.

Prof is so bad, his class lectures and assignments were poles apart. he is crazy - he started shouting and banging a students table and told him to get out of the class for speaking in the class during a presentation. never take his class. 
he was suspended by the end of the semester. 
he refused to go by the university rules & said he doesnt care

I was never able to finish labs during class - he didn't explain what we had to do and they were very hard (didn't align with what we had learned in class at all). Very unfair grading on our final project - he did not listen to my concerns about my group members (who literally did not contribute at all) and gave a poor grade without explaining why.
Professor is very bad with his skills and end of the semster university suspended him. very poor skills and knowledge .

Very kind and inspirational prof! Can tell he loves what he does. Clear about grading (not very harsh either), available via email, and tries to guide you to problem solve. Weekly in-class code was challenging, I'd spend a while after class to finish it. Having it due the same day at 12am was a little stressful but doable. Highly recommend!

He makes the in-class coding exercises way more difficult than they need to be and we almost never finished it during class (which we were supposed to). Despite that, he is very enthusiastic about the course and grades every assignment besides the project on completion so it's a pretty easy class. Some of the applications in class are interesting.

Prof. Matherly is fine. I took him for DS2000 Lab (DS2001) and he did his best to accommodate all students. The coding problems were difficult but he seems to try and compensate for the difficulty. Nice guy.

Not only is the workload crazy, but every single assignment's requirement is filled with ambiguous languages, last minute changes, yet was accompanied with extremely difficult grading sessions. The only way to make sense is to ask dozens of extra follow-up questions to the professor and hoping to get some decent replies, if not self-contradictory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Tough but a fair grader. I started off as a beginner but learned a lot during the course. Ensure that you are prepared for the quizzes, and start your assignments early. 

I would definitely retake the course and also plan on being a part of his advanced cloud computing course!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One quiz per lecture, attendance only, each assignment needs over 20 hours or more, and it needs to pay for the tool you use every month, no curve and low policy. He doesnt give you any chance to make up.

Mr. Parikh's class was stressful due to his rigid grading. He doesn't reconsider grades or offer extra chances, intensifying pressure. Despite attempts to discuss, he remained inflexible. A more understanding approach is needed for a healthier learning environment. He also refuses to give assignment extensions unless you die.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever met! Don't response to students' questions. Never show for scheduled appointment. Too much unrelated talking on class. Don't give guidelines for assignment until the last minute! In a word, I had the worst experience taking this course!

Although there's a lot of reading involved in the class I think the course material itself and the way Professor Thornton teaches the course makes it a lot more easier and interesting to digest. If you're looking for an easy A this probably isn't your class.. this class requires genuine effort but if you dedicate time and effort you'll be fine.
I had this prof for HIST1150. He is really chill and warm. Super understanding, class was really easy. He hates ChatGPT, and will call you out for it, would recommend!
This is genuinely the best professor I have ever had. He is hilarious and cares about what he is teaching. Would absolutely take his class again.

a lot of readings but hes super fair with his grading! u can tell hes super passionate about ea studies and your effort in the class definitely dictates the grade u end with! u can tell he cares about the students and theres no penalty for late assignments except u wont receive feedback comments. u can also rewrite papers for a better grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Thornton actually seems to know a lot about the subject and clearly cares somewhat about what he's teaching. The readings for each class are important, but other than that, the grading is pretty straightforward.

Really funny and nice guy, had a no technology rule but it was fine since all of the assignments could be completed without any of the lectures. A basic understanding of the readings are necessary to do well in the class, but he was a really chill grader and fine with late stuff. Lowkey was attracted to him too tbh...

Professor Thornton has honestly been one of the best professors I've ever had. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches and if you're willing to engage, it'll make the class a lot more fun. He genuinely cares about his students. Just a heads up, there's a lot of reading, but that much should be expected from a history class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you wanna a good grades, plz don't

Very passionate about the subjects he teaches. If you are even mildly interested in East Asian history, he's a great professor to have. The class isn't too challenging, and his expectations are fair. There are extra credit opportunities so do them if you want a grade boost. Lotta reading but no tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: mean guy，just run
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: As a rising senior in college, Prof Thornton is easily the best professor I have ever had. He is always available outside class, gives exceptional lectures, provides a welcoming class environment making it easy to participate and make friends, and is overall extremely knowledgeable in his field. I highly recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is really a good guy! Allows computer use during the exam. And if your grade is an A, you don't need to take the final.

James is the goat. He let us use computers and a formula sheet on the tests and he even let me leave during the test for course registration. He also didn't make us take the final. easist A ever, james is an inspiration.

Tests were very easy often using questions straight from the reviews and homework. Does not post alot on canvas in terms of course materials and class slides so you should come to class. Gave out 100's on final projects just for presenting. Drops you're lowest of 3 exam grades. Really is the GOAT. HW is posted weeks in advance and is very little.

prof. thelusma is the guy. he is funny as hell but if you haven't taken stats before it's not gonna be a walk in the park. the material is pretty easy and you can teach it to yourself without a lot of trouble. one hw assignment a week and three tests, open note. he tells mad funny stories in class too, highly entertaining.
Very nice professor, wants students to do well, but very disorganized.
Took business stats over the summer. Great guy and easy course but didn't learn much

I discovered early I already had credit for MGSC2301; but from my time in the class, I learned Prof. Thelusma is a caring and kind person, but a mid-tier educator. Expect long tangents about unuseful life experiences and unclear demonstrations, even though he genuinely cares and tries. A nice professor, but not ideal if you actually need to learn.

Professor Thelusma is a beast. He's super funny and only tracks attendance on some days. There are 3 exams plus a final exam but they are easy. He is a pretty easy grader and gives out a lot of extra credit. If you struggle with math, take this class!

Professor Thelusma is nice & makes lots of jokes. He takes attendance sometimes but most kids don't show up anyway.  He's always willing to explain things/answer q's. Cheat sheets/computers are allowed during exams and we had 5 homeworks that were simple. One group project at the end that my group did in one sitting & if you present you get 100
He is very disorganized and boring but is a very understanding and very easy grader. This class was a breeze (coming from someone who isn't great at math). Take him!

One of the easiest classes I've taken. He's very good at explaining everything and is willing to answer any and all questions asked. He would make jokes in class, which made it enjoyable. The tests and quizzes are easy, he allows us to use our reference sheet. He gives us a lot of time on homework assignments. Lastly, he ends class early a lot.

Thelusma is really chill and nice, but he is also pretty disorganized. The tests aren't hard whatsoever and there is a tiny bit of homework, but he always sets it due really far in advance. Sometimes he gets onto tangents that aren't relevant to the coursework, but other than that, he's a great teacher who goes over a lot of examples.
Really good professor. Has really good lectures. If you go to his classes and take good notes you will pass. He is really understanding and cares if you understand the material.
HE IS VERY ORGANIZED!!!! LOTS OF TEST BUT HE GAVE SO MANY RESOURCES!!! LOVE HIM SO MUCH

Great professor, Thelusma is a character for sure. He's new here so he's still figuring some things out, but the class was overall pretty easy despite a little disorganization. He'll tell you exactly what to review for the tests so there are no curveballs, and he is very understanding with his students. Homeworks aren't hard either.

This guy is so disorganized but he is easy. His class is not boring. He grades so easily and tells you what is going to be on the test beforehand. You will enjoy this class if you are laid back and just deal with his bs and end up with a good grade. Goes back on a lot of his statements he makes like extra credit opportunities etc.

I took his course years ago and worked very hard, but he was easily irritated and often deducted points without clear explanation. My final project lost many points despite careful preparation. I later asked for another professor to review my work. He appeared to have favorites, and students outside that group were treated unfairly.
Great teacher as long as he likes you. Definitely not afraid to speak his mind but for me that honestly made the class better.
he definitely writes his own reviews. avoid at all costs worst, rudest, professor ive ever met. if he doesn't like you don't expect any basic respect

Ted was fantastic. If you were respectful of his rules and didn't cause trouble in class he liked you. He was a more than fair grader and probably gave me better grades than I deserved. Really nice guy if you play to what he likes. Although, if he doesn't like you, he really doesn't like you.

10/10 professor! He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His feedback is very helpful and he's super efficient in grading. He broke up the assignments so you aren't scrambling to finish all the papers at once. While it might be more work on a daily basis, I was never stressed getting the work done and not knowing where to start

These other reviews are harsh. I think Ted is an decent guy who really cares. Yes, it's kinda a lot of work for FYW, yes he takes it a little more serious than necessary, but he provides genuinely good feedback and wants students to succeed. He's funny and a kind person. You need to put in a lot of time to get a good grade. Some projects were fun.

Ted is hit or miss. He's snarky, for sure, but his class is fun. Three major projects, a basic research paper, a group project, and a final op-ed. Some assignments in between those, so be prepared to put some effort in. Def expect to get out of the class what you put into it. If you don't like his attitude, look for a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was briefly sick and missed classes. Despite my absence, he never offered me a chance to make up for it. Instead, he was "very offended" and lowered my assignments by one point below D- to ensure I failed. They were at worst B level compared to other students. He did everything he could, even going to my counselor to force me to drop, awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: guys this is the worst most unnecessary class for FYW. pick anyone else and you'll have hours less of work for better grades. he claims a C is a good grade and is bascially impossible to raise. AVOID

Rude to students, negative attitude, rolled his eyes at someone for asking if they were in the right class. I expressed personal concerns to him and he dismissed me/ gave me the rudest response ever.  He is condescending, no clear grading criteria, he claims a good, passing grade is a C. idk why he is still at NU. Dropped it so fast.
Did three projects in the class that were fairly easy. You will do well in the class if you put in the effort and listen to his feedback. Overall really nice teacher and not a difficult class.
Great professor, sometimes has strong feelings towards student work but overall is a great professor. He asks students for their input on the rubric and projects are super fun to work.

Ted is very helpful and cares about his students. Attendance is mandatory, but you'll be fine if you email him ahead of class. The class has 3 projects but he changes them semesterly depending on how they go and what the students think of them. The rubrics are made with/by the class before the end of the assignment.

I have never hated a professor more in my entire life. The guy didn't like the company we chose for the final project and gave us a 0 to do the work again. He gave terrible grades for the smallest of mistakes, and he also made my life during co-op a living hell (basically no time for myself after work). DO NOT TAKE HIM.
Ted moss was possibly the worst professor I've ever had at Northeastern. He was continuously rude and picked out favorites in his class. if u want him to like you then participate and also be a POC.

Ted is AMAZING! I was unsure going into the class after reading reviews, but after taking his class I would def take him again! He truly does care about his students and the work that they put in. It's clear that all of the feedback he gives is thoughtful and truly helps you to revise. He lets you make your own rubric on how to grade you as well.

DO NOT TAKE FOR FYW!! Assigns way too much work for a First Year Writing class. The class consisted of three projects. The first is your standard paper based on two books, the second is a poster and the third is a op-ed. There are also extensive and unnecessary reflections for each project. He also takes attendance so you have to go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Idk what these negative comments are about. Professor Moss is a caring teacher who is very fair to his students. He is really funny and super understanding. His grading is reasonable and he takes the time to understand his students. Plenty of time to work on assignments in and out of class. If you put in the work, you can easily get an A!

Best professor ever. He gives great feedback after each assignment, and whenever he does, he validates the amount of work you have given. He also gives out great energy in the class. However, he does give out a lot of work, and even though the assignments aren't hard, they are time-consuming. Recommendation: stay on top of your work.

Ted Moss accused me of faking my physical disability when my health was deteriorating freshman year. I was registered with the disability center and had previously made him aware of my disability. He told me it was convenient my condition was flaring up when things were getting more demanding in class. I am traumatized by his actions.

Gives good feedback and made me a better writer. He made a class I really didn't want to take a lot better. He also gives a lot of time in class to work on your paper, and you get the sense he cares about his students. He was remote Fall 2020, but that didn't impede his class.

Wanted to see what people said since I had him. Any positive review is undoubtedly Ted Moss writing about himself. Spiteful, nasty. Makes it his mission to make you feel inferior. Followed his instructions exactly as assigned and he failed me bc he didnt like my co-op. Jokes on him, my co-op got me my dream job. Only masochists would take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Ted Moss is highly undeserving of these hateful comments. He is an amazing Professor who maintains the perfect balance between being authoritative and relatable. Every lecture was an absolute pleasure and I would 100% recommend taking this class. If you go to Northeastern you should be used to working hard. This is no space for slackers!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible, if you are in his course - SWITCH NOW.

Seems nice; definitely isn't. Gives A's to a very low percentage of class and is disrespectful to students who try to figure out his grading system to avoid being failed. Very disapointing for NEU to count him in their teacher body.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: All of the assignments revolve around the co-op you are on or career you want to pursue. He failed me on assignments because he wouldn't accept my career. Not about to quit my co-op or change my career path because of his delusions. provides no input and "will not answer questions until the assignment is submitted." avoid like the plague.

There's definitely an easier version of this class if you're looking for it. However, you will absolutely learn something from Ted. You really have to work for an A, but it's possible. He can be a tough grader, but this class definitely made me a better writer.  Expects you to be in class and on time, but is understanding of other conflicts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: avoid at all cost. the writing is very intense, instruction is vague, and he expects you to know everything. Grading based on how he likes you. if he doesn't like what you do in the class, no matter how hard you try, and how much effort you put in, you will still receive bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed AWD with Ted. Yes he's a tough grader, but he gives credit where credit is due. You need to work hard for a good grade in this class -- or at least try -- which is fair & self-explanatory. He's also SUPER helpful if you reach out. This isn't a class for the lazy, but I promise it's rewarding if you work hard.

Worst professor for advanced writing!!!DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He will grade you whatever he feels like and give no clarification. You can spend hours and hours on an assignment and end up with a C just because he feel like giving you a C. He give a lot of busy work so you won't even have time to work on your draft. Avoid him at all cost!

Zero clarity. He will grade you based on whatever he is feeling that day. What differentiates an A from an A-  or a B could be as stupid as your choice of font. If he decides he dislikes your writing style, he will grade you down. Most of the other advanced writing professors will give you an A so don't take Moss's class.

I don't know how he graded things but it seems like he picked things out of a hat. I spent hours in the writing center and then would end up with a C. I turned in everything on time and he gave me a B participation and never specified how he graded that at any point along the course.

Ted is a terrific teacher. If you put in even the smallest effort in your papers, then he will give you a good grade. Just follow the guidelines for papers and put some effort into them. He is very helpful, always funny, and made research writing at 8 a.m. more enjoyable than it would've been with another teacher. And he brought us donuts one time!

I had Ted for Intro to College Writing at Emerson, and he was a pretty good instructor. He was clear, and usually fast to get back with emails and such. His personality is very "love-or-hate" and while he didn't bother me at first, his snark and passive aggressive comments about class members really annoyed me by the end of the semester.

Honestly I had a problem with his enthusiasm at first, but after getting through my first essay I truly found him to be a caring teacher who will give you constructive criticism with plenty of comments to fully understand how to better yourself.  His syllabus is actually captivating and there is never a dull moment.  Just be punctual.

Professor Moss is a wonderful teacher. This class definitely was not easy, but I really learned to love reading and writing. I grew so much and I have him to thank. Don't take this class if you are looking for an easy A, but if you want a fun class that challenges you, then I absolutely suggest this one!

Had Ted for my college writing class. He can seem intimidating at first, but it's just his sense of humor. He's a really good professor, and you'll learn a lot. His classes are always interesting and thought provoking. It's just really hard to get an A. Like nearly impossible. If you want to have a good experience, take his class. For aneasy A dont

I honestly loved my college writing class with Ted back in the day. Super helpful, really smart, nice guy. Really funny too, if you get sarcasm and wit. The peer reviews were helpful too; he made us actually interact with each other. I'm still good friends with a lot of people from the class because of it.

He is tough, comes across as arrogant, but truly cares about your success. He expects the best of you, and wants you to expect the best of yourself. I put more time, energy, effort into this class than any other, but it was definitely worth it. I'm a much better writer thanks to this class! If you want an easy A, switch to another AWD professor.
The arrogance and condescension of a 50 year old Pulitzer winner with the face of a pudgy 16 year old.

I'm a finance major here and I never thought I would learn as much as I did in this class. Professor Moss is literally the best teacher I have had my entire life. Hands down. It is not an easy class but it is not "hard" either. Take this class and try, and you will succeed in and out of the class.
Great professor.  If you sincerely try and put the effort into what he's looking for, it will be a good class.  I hate writing and english classes, but I actually enjoyed this class.

He is an awesome teacher who sincerely cares about your improvement. His class is extremely hard, but his sincerity and humor makes up for it. The class is definitely not an easy A. However, if you go to consultation hours, he will help you as much as he can. Make sure you go to class! Overall, two thumbs up!

He is a good teacher who sincerely cares about our grades and our improvement as writers. There is a fair amount of reading and writing, but if you do all the work you will do well. A lot of peer reviews, but they help out. Overall good teacher, I would recommend him to anyone.
This class is difficult but rewarding.  You rely on peer reviews but your writing will really improve by the end.  Overall really nice guy and very smart

Definitely not an easy A, but if you work hard it can be a very rewarding class. Moss creates a good classroom atmosphere and really challenges you to do your best writing.  If he knows you can do better, he won't hesitate to give you a grade that leaves much to be desired.
He isn't a bad teacher or guy but sometimes he comes off as being overly cocky and pretentious. The class wasn't bad but grading was tough..

not a bad guy or teacher.  definitely one of the more difficult U111 professors in terms of grading, and sometimes seems pretentious and overconfident, but overall i have no problems with him (other than my low grade).
Grades difficultly, especially compared to the other college writing 111 profs, but overall an enjoyable class and good teacher
Good guy. helpful. sarcasm is great.
Moss is terrible. He's young and cocky, and he gives his students low grades to make himself feel like a tough, smart professor. Do not take his class! You'll regret it...

Super chill dude, teaches everything about VR from the beginning, all the work is projects. Just make sure to attend class, you will miss quite a bit if you don't show up, but Jamal is really understanding and gives extensions. Super manageable class and interesting, easy A!
A total G, 1000/10
fun class, but assignments dont correlate with what's going on in class sometimes, but good professor and good TA, fun to listen. Very interesting conversations, not boring.

Jamal's awesome. He def knows his stuff & is passionate about teaching it. You'll learn a lot in this class and from him. He has great energy and his feedback is really helpful. Not much busy-work, everything relates to the projects. You also don't need to know anything about VR, he starts from the beginning

The class was super easy and informative--perfect for new design students. The assignments were busy work, but all were graded easily. Thorne is very caring and passionate about supporting his students! I recommend asking him for advice because he understands design and NEU's program very well.

i had jamal for ARTF1220, and he was overall a great professor. he has such a great energy and cares about all his students. the projects we did were interesting and he provides useful feedback. i really enjoyed his class and i recommend you take his class.

Jamal is a great professor. I had him for ARTF1000 and ARTF1220. He's very understanding and gives good feedback on art pieces. I look forward to his class every week and while his ARTF1000 assignments were just a lot of busy work, his ARTF1220 assignments were very intriguing and engaging. 10/10 recommend having him at some point while at NEU!
Jamal is a great guy with a passion for art. He loves to talk about random things but somehow connects it all back to the topic. Would absolutely recommend a class with him.

Jamal is amazing!! Very comfortable environment and puts in effort to get to know his students. Within a day or two of classes he already knew all of us by name & would specifically ask us questions. He also gives incredible feedback and explains why a creative decision is either good or bad. Absolutely hoping to take more classes with him!

This prof is extremely racist. If youre a white or black student, then like the other students said, he teaches not bad. However, if your are an asian, he gives extremely unfair grades. Me and other four asians, including boys and girls, have all put the most efforts in the class and received the worst grades.

Jamal is the best professor ever. He gives good feedback, and ample time to rework and resubmit assignments. He is very understanding, and grades based on your personal progress in the class. Hilarious, and makes class so enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Jamal is not only a professor, but an art mentor to the students who enter his class. His skill doesn't only translate into results on canvas for his students, but merely allows him to understand each student's strengths and weaknesses in order to aid each student in the way they individually need to be. Highly engaging and charismatic as well.

Jamal makes class so much fun and introduces a huge variety of projects that test you're capabilities and make you think outside of the box. He challenges you, but evaluates each student on an individual level and pushes them to improve, not to meet a certain standard. He's a highly entertaining teacher and will keep you engaged.

Jamal (yes he's a first name basis professor) is the perfect combination of mentor and bro. He's a genius himself, and his paintings are incredible, but he also helps all of his students learn how to create. It was an honor to be in his class and watch him work. Note on grading: he lets you resubmit work for a new grade. 11/10 would take again.

Jamal is the man. Amazing teacher, always willing to help. Tough on attendance, but when it comes to feedback and helping you improve as an artist he is incredible. Gives you a lot of freedom in playing with the project the way you want, always there for you to give an advice. He was more of a mentor than a teacher, best art teacher I've ever had.

I've had Jamal for a few classes, and he's one of my favorite teachers. He gives you a lot of creative freedom and will help you if you have any questions. He grades fairly (easily?) and gives great feedback. If you're taking a class with him, don't skip, and don't be late- he's really tough on attendance.

First, he's absolutely hilarious. Smart guy and always dresses really sharp; makes him kinda sexy. Always willing to help, but he's serious about coming to class. Don't mistake him for an easy teacher. He assigned a decent amount of work but not enough to make me cry.

Extremely frustrating course. Weekly assignments were excessively long and felt like busywork rather than teaching concepts. Instructions from TAs and the professor contradicted each other, issues were brushed off, grading was delayed for weeks, and problems took months to resolve. Unacceptable for a $7k+ course and led me to transfer out.
