I'm a junior but I can honestly say this man is one of the best teachers I've had at this school. Thanks Brad

If you have the opportunity to take him, please do! One of the best professors I've had at Northeastern. A bit awkward but his jokes make class a lot more lighthearted and fun. Very understanding and class isn't too hard as long as you use your resources and pay attention. He is more than willing to help. Easy A as long as you do your work.

An amazing professor, take him if you can! Makes calculus so fun because he loves math. He cares a lot about his students and wants everyone to succeed, very accessible outside of class time. You don't gave to show up to class but you should because he often brings treats for his students. Overall a really nice guy and my favorite professor at NEU.

By far my favorite teacher in my entire educational career. I thought I was horrible at math until my senior year of high school, which is why I was scared of taking this calculus class. He proved me wrong! His teaching is easy to understand, and he always clarifies or re-explains if you do not understand. Also, his many jokes lighten up the class!
Brad is an amazing math prof! He is SO PASSIONATE! Love his jokes and energy in class. I would recommend him 100%. His worksheets are easy to follow!

Prof. Turow is lovely. He creates a great classroom atmosphere for his students. He's a young professor and is passionate about math. He explained Calculus to business and econ majors in a way that was simple and easy for us to understand. His class is well organized and straight forward. I feel like I learned a lot. 11/10 rating for this Prof!

This course was supposed to "develop a knowledge of particular cities" but Prof Turam unfortunately did not achieve this. Seminar-based, there was little feedback/input from Prof Turam except a starting point. She appears helpful, but then you get a shocking reaction if you disagree with her in discussions. Wish I'd listened to other students.

Very little content of substance and material that was discussed had very little to do with the course description. I understand that its a seminar, but there was virtually no instruction and discussions frequently went off topic. No assignments were graded until release of final grade. If you're taking this to fulfill a requirement look elsewhere.

This module was an interesting module by Professor Turam. She appears helpful, and answers questions during class, but if you ask outside, she's moody and doesn't give an answer/seems annoyed, despite me being an A grade student, so I'd hope I'm asking smart Qs ! Her exams are ok but you'll need to read outside resources, and avoid annoying her !

Berna Turam makes class fun! She had us all sit in a circle and engage in class discussion. It is not a hard class  and is interesting. We got to choose a semester long project to collect field notes on. She is always eager to help students and loves to get to know people and hear about their life experiences.

Class was good and there was a lot of reading. like a lot. but it was still a very interesting class and she is very knowledgable and makes the class interesting. There was no final, only a presentation.
She gives a lot of feedback so although you have a lot of work, students can manage
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very tough grader, sometimes feels like you are in highschool with strict guidelines. Absolutely inflexible, very finicky, too many breakdown in assignments. It's a graduate school course, so I think we are serious enough and wish the professor understands that and gives some room!

She wants students to work on projects, powerpoint and discussion board. You can't write brief, she send students to college writing center, even if your first language is English. She's a tough grader, takes points off for minimal thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Was he teaching Bostonography or Criminology? Hard to tell from the daily 90 minute lectures on crime in Boston instead of learning Pandas. Feedback wildly inconsistent with grades (1 bad comment  drop letter grade). Expects students to be pro data scientists when grading them. Isn't aware that grades are numbers not ranges. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

Prof Tucker has a very specific grading criteria and does not make it clear, which can be very frustrating. It's possible to do well in his class, but you have to know exactly what he's looking for. He also seems to be unqualified to be teaching the class. Overall, the lectures and readings were quite boring. Take crim with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Tucker is not as knowledgable or experienced as other professors in the field and may be less qualified. Lots of reading for the class that is unnecessary. Projects and tests make up most of your grade and they need to be executed in a specific way if you want to do well. Would not recommend if you want a serious and professional course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Tucker tries really hard to be a good professor but fails. The readings are long, confusing, and its impossible to digest all the information. He grades harshly on random things and it does not seem like he is qualified to teach undergrad students.I recommend taking crim with a different professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've never dreaded a class more than this one. He is incredibly boring and makes jokes about serious topics which make me feel like he's not qualified to be teaching the class. Lots of boring readings for homework and weekly quizzes. Sometimes he graded really tough and sometimes easily so it was hard to tell how you were doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nat (usually) boils his lectures down to the very core: if you listen, you will learn exactly what you need to succeed at the homeworks. The challenges are tough because he doesn't give you the step-by-step like he does for the HW, but they are also completely reasonable given the info you learn from the lectures. Just don't make bad jokes in chat
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tuck is completely unwilling to explain concepts from scratch, often rambling for an hour and a half about a concept he never even defined. No room for questions, is super unhelpful and just tells people to look at the notes if they're confused, and expects everyone to be on the same page as him. He does not care, do not take it with him if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not the absolute worst experience I've had in a class at Northeastern, but that's about the kindest thing I have to say. I took computer systems with him and it was extremely difficult, as if the course is made to give you no help at all.

Homeworks take well over 20 hours (sometimes 30-40) and range in topics from orbital mechanics to computer vision. I definitely learned a ton, but the cost was lots of sleepless nights and a near constant stress. Fwiw, I've heard that he's usually much better prepared, but this class was awful. Don't take robotics with him.

I took CS5335 under Professor Nat Tuck. Although the course for a rough ride because of the ongoing pandemic, but Professor Nat tuck handled in an awesome way. Learning robotics in an online environment is always difficult, but the assignment were amazing and helped learn orbital mechanics which is something new and mostly skipped in basic robotics
Gonna be a tough class but he knows what he's talking about and he's a good teacher

I was looking forward to this class... We didn't cover any robotics concepts systematically just completed arbitrary assignments. Not clear what was the progression of topics from week to week or the goal of each assignment, unclear grading, starter code filled with bugs, no additional resources provided. By far the worst class I have taken at NE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you want to learn and improve, choose Nat Tuck. No exams, just assignments. His assignments are really good. You will become a good C programmer and have your OS concepts clear if you diligently take efforts. Nat is not "academic", he is from industry and keeps only relevant things in the course. Paper reading and theory are off the list.

I've always heard that Nat Tuck was notorious for making his classes hard. This class, however, is a total train wreck with no support at all from himself or the TA's, and the projects are given with little to no guidance from lectures. The starter code we get are often riddled with bugs, are super difficult, and this class is not enjoyable at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid Choice!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Does not teach in-depth. Unless you question him at every step he won't explain how things are working underneath. Huge load work and assignments are given before the related topics are taught in class. If you take CS5600 Systems under him be prepared to forget about internship/full-time search because the assignment will take the entire week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: really hard assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Heavy homework without good explaining. The project just let someone who is not able to code be your teammate but he will not listen to the situation and give a fair score based on distribution.

Your grade is completely determined by the projects with Tuck, and be ready to spend 20 hours / week on them. Tuck tries to be funny but I didn't always find it amusing, only immature. He is very good at responding to emails and questions on piazza and helpful at office hours. I recommend taking him for systems only because he doesn't give exams.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. Uses sarcasm effectively to convey that we should start our homework and/or read the online reading material. Reading is not necessary but is recommended. Don't need to buy a book. Goes over what we need for homework in class and gives good feedback on Piazza to guide us. Project-based, no quizzes. Also, he's a spicy chili pepper.

Good lecturer with a sense of humor that you will either love or hate.  Personally I found him to be amusing and thought he presented the topics clearly with plenty of examples.  No matter who you take this course with you'll have a lot of homework, so be ready for that.  I would recommend Nat Tuck to a friend.

Moves at a daunting pace. If you look away for a split second you feel as if you miss six lines of code. He answers questions and asks for participation but sometimes it seems as if he doesn't take it as seriously as he should.
nat is love. nat is life
Take a sip of his mountain dew and you're guaranteed an A 10/10

I took Bonnie’s multicultural lit courses at Bowling Green SU in 1993-94. Class discussions were often loud and personal. She and my classmates challenged my prejudices in lit and life. I became a better person in her classes. BG’s loss was Northeastern’s gain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. TuSmith's short story class is great. The readings are not too long, and are a great selection. She's really passionate about literature, and it comes through in her discussions. Most of the work is Blackboard posts, which isn't too hard. She's a really caring and funny person, and she even brought us snacks sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: TuSmith is engaging and really gets the class involved in discussions! Reading is required. Blackboard posts, and the occasional essay. She brings up your posts and validates all opinions. Gives out snacks, is genuinely nice and enthusiastic and is one of my favorite professors-absolutely adorable. Easy essay grader. SmallSeminar with 11 students.

Prof. TuSmith is an enthusiastic and energetic instructor. I would just say that she could do a better job of engaging students in discussion rather than imposing her own ideas about the text onto her class through long tangents. She is forgiving, even though I missed a lot of classes due to personal issues, she gave me a second chance to pass.

The most adorable professor in existence. I took her Modern Short Story class and it was easily my favorite class. The reading is short and to the point -- she doesn't waste your time or give you busy work. 3 papers a semester and she grades pretty easily. She often brings snacks for the class like cookies & is just generally friendly.

Whoever said Professor TuSmith can't speak English is just being rude and ra cist. She's a professor in the ENGLISH DEPARTMENT; she's extremely well versed in both the English language and American literature. She's very smart although she does go off-topic quite a bit. The class is interesting; she is very conversationally engaging. Easy grader.

I highly enjoyed her Asian American literature course. Though in part I think it was fun because of the people who were in the class, together it was a great atmosphere to be in. People who badmouth her...they probably did it because they couldn't deal with having to face racial or ethnic issues and this is a major part of her courses.

Classic teacher! Bonnie is easily one of my favorites. I can't quite say why, though. She likes me, I suppose thats why. Just be sure to get her off topic and ask her about her karate skills. I challenged her to a fight several times but she wouldn't engage me. Weak.

Bonnie is actually one of the most intelligent professors at NU, and those who say otherwise are too dumb too recognize that. She doesn't coddle you, but she does give you credit where it's due. She is fluent in like, 6 languages, and she is extremely well versed in many different kinds of ethnic lit., not just Asian. She is legit, worth taking.

The 1 positive thing about this class was that the book selection was impecable. I read magazines during class every day or did puzzles. Lectures are completely useless and your forced to read bc of blackboard postings, and then she just tells you wat you read the whole class time. Never helpful, always chnges the subject, doesnt seem to know much.
I did not mind TuSmith. She does tend to get off topic sometimes and relates to her asian-american culture, but so what! She is an easy grader.

Easy class, easy grader.  She is better with a smaller class and yes she does go off topic a lot and talks a lot about culture and heritage which I don't think is necessarily all that bad.  Just read, do your essays and you'll be fine.

She tries to turn every subject to herself and her asian-american heritage.  assigns books for class regarding ethnicity regardless of legitimacy to topic.  No offense, but she is not all that bright.  I've asked several questions and she says "oh, that's an intersting thought" and then changes the subject and does not answer them.

Professor TuSmith is perhaps better with smaller groups of students. I had her for a seminar and she was great, much more of a conversational instuctor than a lecturing instructor needed for a larger class. She does go off topic. The smaller classes are better, big classes don't bother going to class sometimes.

you could work really hard and get A's for your papers but still end up with a C. grading scheme isridiculous+illogical. no common sense not understanding only talks abt herself.also forces her opinions down your throat evn if it has nothing to do w/theclass. she needs to get ovr herself.

She can go on and on and on and go off on tangents about things. Very nice woman though, grades really easy although the final paper is ROUGH. The class is a bore, but if you need it to fulfill a requirement, take it. Zone out during class, your'll be fine.

i agree, she's extremely self-centered. 1 time i went to talk to her after class & she went on & on about other stuff instead of answering my question! i think i was there for 30 or 40 min. before she finally answered my question. the class itself isn't hard but she keeps repeating her resume to us.
Can't speak english and makes her own students correct essays........... no clue where she's coming from.
doesnt teach the material, but very easy grader. going to class is a huge nap time.

This teacher was awful, I would have enjoyed the class if it had'nt been for her. Honestly, she is so self centered it's hard to learn, and I ended up taking my own notes from the book because she couldn't teach me anything. Ugh.
Words can't describe how bad she is. Nice woman, but should not be allowed to teach.
It's sad when a great class can be ruined by a horrible professor. Never before have I felt dumber after leaving a class.
got to be one of the worst teachers ive ever had, if you are thinking of taking her american indian lit class dont, i wanted to take my life multiple timed during class
No Comments
Unbelievably unhelpful teacher.  Concerned only with her own agendas.  Simply unable to communicate effectively.

Only final answers count and even harder because no multiple choice. Does not explain how to get to correct answers for homework/quiz/test even after submission. Buying the textbook was a waste since no math in textbook but all math for assignments.

Excellent Professor in every sense of the word. Regardless of your major or interest for finance, her clear passion for the material (and teaching) coupled with the fluidity in her presenations will have you drawn in. Group projects are involved, so just pick your groupmates wisely and you'll be fine. She also grades very quickly. 12/10 overall.

Kovacs give lot of home work. Very particular about steps but don't look at final solution to award grades. Hard to understand and follow. She looks at fine details in excel, column title missing, color missing etc. rather than the content. Her group project is task oriented and very hard to work on, with mid-term exam around the corner. Skip!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Kovacs was the best teacher I have ever had! She explained really well, gave amazing examples with detailed steps and enough homework to make you practice and remember all the concepts. Her project was great and really helped to grasp on the concepts, and give real world experience with investing and use of excel. Always available for questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The course is difficult, but Professor briefly explains the lecture slide and gives examples to ensure her students understand the materials. Pay more attention in the class, and review the homework exercises, you sure pass the exams.

One of my favorite at UML. Nicest lady you will ever meet. Class is tough but Tunde does a good job at explaining the material. You'll get the grade you earn.  Stock trak is worth a large part of your grade so get a good group. Would definitely recommend her
This professor has no patience and very emotional.
Great teacher, however is soft-spoken. She makes the class very interesting and is always willing to help.
Makes the class enjoyable and fun to learn. Helps you with everything, no matter how many times you want to go over the material. Highly recommend her.
Average professor at best. Material can be hard but she is always willing to help. Exams were tough but assignments and homework were easy.

LOVE her. She's really helpful and you can tell she really wants you to learn. The material is not bad if you pay attention in class. Refer to her lectures, slides, HW assignments and practice questiosn and you'll be fine. And best of all, she gives out chocolates during exams!! :)
Softspoken, but explains the material very well. A really nice professor, very reasonable in terms of grading and homework.
softspoken, but very helpful. go to her office hours. genuinely wants students to learn. she's got a phD, very intelligent.
investments - great teacher, material is easy, approachable
no commets

Do not take this class.  It won't be fun.  Just avoid it.  If you're a crim major and you're required to take her change your major.  You watch films and write vague papers on them.  If you don't believe me I hope you like Star Wars.  Also: Tobacco and Heroin use is the same thing I guess.  Have fun.
No Comments

"Fair" grading but very inflexible. Tests were 4 questions, each worth 25% of grade. Points were full or 0 credit - no in between. On one question, there was a circular shape that was not specified as a cylinder or sphere. Asked proctor (Narusawa wasn't present), he said to state assumptions. Solved for sphere perfectly, 0 credit - he wanted a cyl.

He doesn't really talk much in class. However, his notes on the board are great; never had to read the book, just for homework problems assigned from the it. He's also very helpful in his office, willing to help you almost anytime of the day as long as you make an appointment with him beforehand.

Narusawa is one of the most fair professors I've had date. He helps you prepare for his exams by doing examples out on the board and there are never any surprises as long as you attend lecture, pay attention, and take notes. He speaks very softly does have an accent, but his lectures are very beautiful and organized. He is a very fine gentleman.
One of the most universally fair professors at NEU. His exams are straightforward and based on his lecture notes (which are exemplary). Speaks softly but is perfectly intelligible if you listen.

Had this "professor" for thermo.  he never turned more than 15 degrees from the chalk board, was impossible to understand (even if his volume should ever reach a legible volume...which it didnt), and very unclear.  Goodluck.

had him for thermo.  Great prof.  Very straightforward.  Just go to class, give the homework an honest try, and take good notes.  He doesn't throw any curveballs, and is one of the most fair professors ive had at NU.  A little hard to understand but you get used to it and his exemplary notes make up for it.  Just attend class and youll be fine!

Had him for Thermo and Fluids. He seemed kind of like a jerk in Thermo. But when I had him for fluids his demeanor had completely changed. Gives good study guides for tests that accuratley show what he will be testing on. Pay attention to his examples in class, and stay on top of the homework and his classes wont be that bad.
He helps those who are willing to help themselves.  He is one of the better engineering professors at NU.  Everything is straight-forward with this guy.  If he speaks up, he would be outstanding.

Cannot hear him as he talks to the board..Does not really care if you have a question or don't understand something. Neat handwriting, but you have no idea what he is writing down! Very frustrating class.

A good professsor, it's hard to hear him as he speaks to the board and he's tough if you don't want to show up to class but if you're willing to show up and put in the work he's very straightforward with his exams and what material will be on them.

What a bunch of babies the other raters are.  His English is exemplary for a second language.  His notes are clear and complete and he tests to his notes (but not to the book, so pay attention).  It's a shame so many students feel a lecture professor ought to baby them and give them individual help.
Hard to hear, hard exams, but very nice guy.  He won't fail anyone as long as you show up to exams.  but keep in mind a failing grade in engineering is less than a D-
No Comments

This was the absolute worst professor I ever had at Northeastern! He is way to old to be teaching and doesn't care about his students one bit! His english is also lackluster at best. And, his exams have material on them that he never covered!!! If you get him I recommend switching to another section.
Had him for 3 classes.  Tests are impossible (you need to extrapolate too much), notes are good, and he is brilliant.  I've learned a lot from him, but my GPA sucks because of him

In a class of 60, 6 students can hear him. Somebody get him a microphone! All I learned was we ruined a weekend of his cuz he had to grade our terrible tests. I can't believe we have him again for Heat Transfer. NEU is cruel.

VERY hard teacher, but very clear lectures. Useless during office hours (Cannot tear himself away from writing to buddies in Japan, and just throws a copy of the HW solution at you). Exams are impossible, and he will blame students for being stupid.

Was nice enough, not always sure where she was coming from though.  Uses case studies to teach and tends to not allow for a lot of creative thinking in your review of the studies.  Tends to rely on text too much for tests and doesn't review the material enough in advance.  Does she like teaching?  Hmmm...
unprofessional, condenscending, reads off books. repeat the text. no standarised grading system.plays favoritism. basically waste your time.

Possibly the worst teacher I have ever had. She puts words in your mouth, grades you unfairly and just treats you like a complete idiot because you didn't go to Harvard. Don't take her. She is the hardest prof for intro to marketing, and she just seems angry at the world. She isn't nearly as smart as she thinks she is...

Worst teacher I've ever had. She went to Harvard and thinks she's better than everyone else. She cant teach or even grade her own papers she has people do it for her. The only reason why I think she still teaches is because Northeastern can say they have one more prof from Harvard. Aweful class avoid at all costs.
Great teacher, only have to take one test if you can get above an 85 and she gives chances for extra credit.  two easy case studies and a short group project. very nice lady

Horrible, can't teach and her grading system is bad, no clarity, you never know what she wants, and her test don't even test what you learn and it based solely off the book which she doesn't talk about in class.

Participating is 35% of your grade which is ridiculous given how large the class size is.  She seems nice in the beginning but she's a tough grader and kind of passive aggressive.  She also misinterprets the comments you make, which can get annoying.  Long winded.  I wouldn't recommend her.

Professor Urman is super smart and funny. Very lecture heavy class and theres a lot of outside reading. Theres no rubric for any of the assignments so you have no clue what grade youre gonna get. He also gives very little feedback and can be a little unfriendly when you ask for clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Urman's humor often falls flat and he makes jokes about his students that made me not want to speak up and risk being wrong-- but it's required. Rules are strict, and there's a lot of reading and assignments. Tests are fair. Not a fan of his attempt at dry humor. Class was stressful and uninteresting due to his teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Urman is a very funny guy who makes the lectures pass by quickly and keeps the conversation interesting. If you are respectful and take class seriously, he's a great teacher and a fair grader. His class(Intro to Law) wasn't very hard but it did require a fair amount of reading to be able to participate in the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Had Fall 2019. Only graded by quizzes. Very impersonal but she's good-hearted and really wants you to understand. No powerpoints, all board work (but that's typical for math). I think she did post her own notes though. Provides a lot of practice problems. Do the homework, ask questions when confused. If u did well at math in high school u'll be ok.
Not an effective lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unhelpful lectures and TAs grade too harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best math teachers I've ever had. Super accessible outside of class, and cares more about you actually understanding the material than always getting it on the first try. The only complaint is the reliance on students watching textbook videos. But you just need to skim the videos and she ends up going over it again in class.
Don't even bother coming to class after the first two weeks. Her teaching style is garbage and ineffective. Just read the textbook and watch youtube videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst teacher at Northeastern. Confusing lectures and inconsistently uploads materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't know what's causing the sudden uptick in positive reviews. Calculus 2 at Northeastern is generally considered a weed-out class, and having Leopold only makes the problem even worse. Even though her lectures are extremely useless due to the fact that she glosses over important concepts, she still passes around a sign in sheet. Very unhelpful
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Leopold is not for everyone. If you learn the material on your own and use the lecture to check your understanding, this class will go well. If you try to learn from just the lectures and then try to do the homework, you'll likely struggle. Not the best in lecture, but is generous with quizzes, posts accurate practice versions and reviews
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She gets a bad rep but she's actually a really good teacher. She is very thorough in her lectures and as long as you pay attention in class this tests and quizzes are not bad.
Is terrible at explaining concepts n a way her students will understand. People who have taken calc 2 and have learned the concepts already are even confused.
I completely appreciate the extra credit questions on her quizzes. I do also appreciate her help at office hours. I did however find a little bit hard to catch on to her teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is not a very good lecturer at all. She doesn't engage the class at all, so it is difficult to know if you actually understand the material. The tests are hard and are graded even harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She handed out granola bars during the exam and her class isnt bad if you do the homework before quizzes
She brought her child to class once, not sure why she has so many bad ratings. her class is not hard if you put in the work, she gives extra credit on all the quizzes. great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great teacher very informative and goes into detail upon request. Will work with you outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had her for Calculus 2. After the first few weeks, I was constantly lost during class. She rarely addresses questions and just talks to the board. Her idea of helping is to just have you do a problem you don't understand. Get familiar with your textbook, because it will be teaching you the course. Switch out if you can. Would not recommend. :(

Took Calculus 1 with her, and had a horrible time. She doesn't explain her work clearly, just shows up to class, copies a problem down off the board, and that's it. She isn't mean or unorganized, but she shows now effort towards her students. Office hours not helpful, she just asked you to solve a problem and doesn't provide help. Switch if you can

Worst teacher I have had yet. Talks into the board without addressing students questions, often ignores raised hands. Failed to teach us all the material required for the final, and was unkind at times. If you have her, switch classes immediately.

By far the worst teacher I have ever encountered.  Makes way too many mistakes in-lecture for students to absorb anything, not that there is anything to absorb: she blindly starts reading off her notes and writing on the board without any context whatsoever.  Only way to pass is copying everything and doing more than all the problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Poor communicator, failed to understand most of the concepts presented and would often get halfway through an idea before realizing it was completely incorrect due to her errors. Not concerned helping students, extremely disappointing. Office hours are a joke, she is just not an effective communicator in the slightest.

Easily the worst professor NU has ever hired. Language barrier presented issues. She was terrible at teaching. Wasted my time going to her for help after class.  Did not seem to care about helping her students. A majority of the  class did very poorly. Stay away

Honestly the worst teacher I've had at this school. She was rude, not helpful, and gave you a dirty look when you asked any questions. The language barrier was horrible, you couldn't understand her, and she didn't even get the class herself. Switch out if you have this teacher unless you want to fail the easiest math class at Northeastern.

Had her for game theory and she is a decent teacher. I am naturally a poor math student, so I found I had to go in for extra help regularly in order to do well on quizzes. She is German, but her accent is barely noticeable.
Very enthusiastic, passionate and knowledgeable. Class wasn't too difficult, and I learned a good amount. A genuinely cool guy.
funny and smart

he brings the real world into the classroom in a unique way.  I like that he pushes people to think beyound the technical information in the text and try and treat all of their school projects as real projects that matter.  he constantly asks students for feedback and changes the assignments based on student input.

He is very smart and super nice. However - he does not use Blackboard, his syllabus sucks as you can never prepare for what's coming due. Although I appreciated 20 minute long classes in my busy schedule,I learned nothing from the class,but everything from the textbook. Spent time on his cell phone in class + watched BBC movies.Projects were unclea
Ben is the sexiest teacher I've ever had.
smart, funny, and charming
He is the most positive and optimistic architecture profs I have ever had.  He is really encouraging and supportive.

He teaches completely differently than any teacher you have ever had before.  He has accomplished so much already and hes very young.  A good role model.  Very easy teacher.  I didn't learn what I was supposed to learn that semester but I did learn a lot about the profession.
She is a good lecturer. Paper is kind of subjective, definitely speak to her before handing in assignment. Quizzes have out of the ordinary current events

I love Alison Uzdella!! She's very knowledgeable and very clear in her teaching. She's by far the most approachable and helpful professor I've had thus far at Northeastern. She expects a lot of you, but understands the pressures that can come with being an undergrad. I too plan on taking every class I can with her!! highly recommended!!

Alison was my TA for POLU160, but she is now going to teach courses on her own. As a TA she showed genuine interest in the class and its content and was often more knowledgable than the prof. She grades fairly, I did well on her exams because I payed attention in lecture. I plan to take every class I can with her before she leaves (Phd student).

Unfair grading. Participate multiple times every single class and you still get a 60%, tanking your grade and he refuses to ever change his grading. Tries to cold call students who already regularly participate. Grades horribly on regular essays and exams. Repeats posted slides in his lectures. Don't waste your time.

Probably the harshest grader in existence. Median for his essays is like a 70. You can go to class every single day and participate and he will still give you a 60 on participation (which is 15% of the grade btw). His tests are also ridiculously hard, lockdown browser in person. His actual lectures are fine but its not worth it at all.

Professor Vaulont is a great professor. He is extremely knowledgable of what he is talking about. He expects a good amount of participation, usually in group activities, but they are interesting. He grades pretty tough on essays, but if you stick to each point of the rubric, you'll do better as the semester goes on. Tests are alright if you study.

Professor Vaulont is a very caring, passionate professor, but his rubric for his essays are very difficult. He gives you feedback, but it seems very open-ended on a lot of things, and it's very frustrating. The group activities are fun, the tests can be a bit hard, but if you study, you will do fine. Very strict attendance policy as well.

While I just started in Professor Vaulont's class, I can confidently say that he is an incredible professor. I believe he recently started at NU, so I thought I should leave one of his first reviews. He is incredibly passionate about the material, has an amazing energy, and I look forward to going to his class. For ORGB, I easily recommend him.

Manuel makes a boring class as fun as possible with in-class activities and a fun and easy group project. Papers are a bit difficult, and he grades them tough but gives good feedback so you can improve on the following ones. Exams are easy and a lot of elements go into your grade which is nice. Overall, very manageable to get an A, highly recommend
Absolute chiller of a guy. The midterm and the final were easier versions of in-class quizzes and homework.

I have had far worse physics teachers. Vivek is honestly good. Like the lectures being before class is one of the only ways to productively learn physics. The bonus problems on the exams boost your grade so much and most of the exams are the same exact problems from the quizzes/homework but different numbers. Just do problems and u will be fine

reviews.comment: Your grade is made up of mainly the midterm and final. Basically had to teach myself everything since class time was spent doing group work while you had to watch videos at home to learn concepts. I would avoid.

I think he was the best out of the three professors. Then again, it's not a very high bar. He lectures a bit more than the other two and runs review sessions. reviews.comment: Makes things so much more complicated than they need to be. Insanely condescending and 0 empathy. Does not reply to emails and is very little help. Avoid.

Vivek is the worst of the three professors in this class for fall 2025. He was TERRIBLE at explaining concepts and made everything more confusing than it should be. Avoid taking his class if possible.
Terrible professor. Rude about questions and doesn't actually teach. Between the three of them one brain cell is shared.

Structure of this class is very annoying. No in class lectures, all online and when you ask for help he's super condescending.  Literally made fun of a student once in the middle of lecture. Be prepared to teach yourself everything. Not amazing for people that haven't taken a physics class before.

The flipped classroom setup works as long as you do the preview work before class. Of the three professors, he seems the most talented at teaching these concepts. I was never great at physics but still did decently. The midterm is very simmilar to the quiz problems.

Class is terrible. The flipped learning setup doesn't work at all. You teach yourself everything. The professors barely explains anything in class and expects you to already know the material. It's completely unhelpful, confusing, and honestly a waste of time. If you actually want to learn, this is not the class or professor for you

reviews.comment: so basically its three professors and they switch out every couple of weeks. quite literally the worst 3 professors ive ever had, there extremely lazy with grading and you basically have to be prepared to teach yourself because there are only 10min lectures outside of class. midterms and finals are nothing like practice problems.

I took AP Physics in high school and hated it but Professor Venkatachalam was pretty good at these explaining concepts, and happy to explain further after class or in office hours; the structure of this physics class, which balanced homework and exam grades to make up a final grade, was really great.

reviews.comment: Professor Venkatachalam is very passionate about physics, but it was hard to learn anything in his class. A typical day consists of 20 min of lecture and 45 min of practice problems. reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:

Paul teaches the course in the 2nd half of the sem. He's way better. Go to him for OH

Take anyone else. Lectures last no longer than 20 minutes most days, then you work on homework on your own. Most of the time this homework is past the level of the material lectured. Excellent conveyor of the physics curriculum. Engaged in class and helpful during office hours. Always willing to assist students with academic concerns.

reviews.comment: If you took any AP Physics, this class is super easy, I almost felt that paying attention to Vivek confused me. Most of the time though he made the concepts simple. His tests were really easy too.

reviews.comment: Real great teacher. Our class had three different professor and Vivek was by far the best. He was able to explain physics in a much simpler way that was easier to grasp. Really wants his students to succeed and will do his best to explain things to you if you are confused.
Hands down the worst professor I've seen. Not effective in any category of teaching — I'm sure she understands the material but she shows no capacity to transmit it to students

worst professor ever and they can't fire her cuz she's tenured. i stopped going to class because her mumbling was distracting me from reading the textbook. she does give out nice packets but the class would be much improved if she just gave out the packets and cancelled class.

Poor instructor. She faces the whiteboard while talking quietly in a strong accent. It was hard to understand her in a tiny room just 6 feet from the board. Completely illegible handwriting to top it off. I only showed up for the weekly quizzes on Thursdays. The textbook+assigned problems are good enough.

She talks so quietly it is very hard to hear her. When there's construction in the next room it's impossible. Her handwriting is not only tiny but also illegible. And that's when she's not standing in front of it. Her lectures are unorganized and make no sense. She seems nice enough, but think hard about taking a class with this professor.

Oh god why. Why have I don't this to myself. This was the worst, least interactive teaching style I've ever seen. Sit close because she writes in size 4 font, and practically whispers her lecture to the board. The book was my savior here. Awful at her job and would recommend waiting a semester rather than taking a course with her.

Quite literally useless. She is the worst professor I have ever had. Avoid by all means neccesary.  Talks quietly, spends entire class facing the board, her lectures consist of her writing out her notes on the board (and they aren't even good). Did fine in the class but taught myself everything.
Avoid if possible, her lectures are a copy of the online videos that come with the book. Worst professor i had so far at NU
great professor! elucidates what she's talking about through examples and has a wonderful step-by-step approach for every topic that makes studying a whole lot easier.

General ineffectiveness as a professor, leaving student to rely solely on the textbook to learn anything unfamiliar. Multiple section class required very difficult final which she did not prepare students for at all.
If I hadn't taken AP calculus in HS i would've failed this class.    Thick accent, but she sucks at teaching anyway.  I tried to follow her work without listening to her and still couldnt get it.

Avoid if possible. Not as bad some some I guess. She is hard to understand between an indecipherable accent and talking very quietly. When she finally notices you raising your hand, she doesn't understand your question and acts like your crazy. Her quizes suck because she says one thing will be on the quiz and then gives a quiz on the next section.

possibly the worst professor i've come across thusfar. her accent is very thick, but i can deal with that. she just doesn't teach. all she does is write examples from the book on the board. we had a TA for one day when she was out and i learned more that day than i have all semester. any knowledge i have of this class comes from taking AP calc inHS

she is the goddess of math! she explains in detail the theory and the procedure. her notes are organised and crystal clear. she will tell you what you need to work on to improve. i loved working hard for her. final was tough, but her quizzes and exam were easy if you did the hw.

She's a solid professor and knows what she's doing. Attendance codes, VERY lecture heavy and hard to maintain attention span. Homeworks can be really tedious but quizzes were fine, drops lowest quiz, very accessible outside class. Not too hard to get decent grade. Group project is probs hardest part - shes picky with grading so pick ur group wisely

Prof. Vittori was great!! She was very knowledgeable as she had worked at one of the big four firms. Homework's were long but they prepared very well for exams and quizzes. There was a group project to complete through the semester which wasn't bad as long as you had a good group. Overall, she is an amazing professor!! Definitely take her class!!

Very accessible, sweet teacher, and breaks down accounting in a good way. Lectures are a bit monotonous, but she gives a lot of practice and curves very genuinely (2-4 above average was an A). I hated McGraw-Hill, but tests were always easier than homework. Could choose people for the project, so it was not bad. Lucky if you get her.

Professor Vittori was a great professor. Her lectures were great, and she did a good job of explaining and answering questions in class. Lectures could get boring at some points. Everything is curved. Assignments like homework were straightforward, but took some time to complete. I would recommend Professor Vittori.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Vittori is AMAZING. Provides lots of online resources (lecture videos, handouts, test practice packets). She is such a great professor and if you pay attention in class you will do well.

Has video lectures available and many other online resources that are extremely helpful. Easy grader. Homework is relatively easy and doesn't take too long. Amazing person, amazing professor. Ratings are correct.
Loved how organized and reliable this course was. She gives so many materials to study with and is a great professor.

I have learned so much from her class. Professor Vittori really prepares you well for the final, and she makes sure that you understand everything. Her quizzes and exams aren't the easiest compared to other professors' but she prepares you well with practice problems that reflect what will be on the assessments.

best professor at NU, she made me love accounting! Prof Vittori is a great teacher, amazing at answering questions and she obviously loves connecting with her students and getting to know them. The class is hard but she made it so easy with all the resources she provides in and out of class. Do the practice tests and study the HW you'll do great!

I loved Professor Vittori as a teacher, she's very knowledgeable in Accounting, and she ensures that her students understand the material because she's well organized and provides lots of study materials. She's always willing to meet outside of class and really helpful. If you take advantage of the study guides and handouts you'll pass.

Honestly, she's not a bad person just not the right teacher for me. I'm a person who expects to learn material in the lecture and only study like an hour outside of class.I have to spend a minimum of 5 hours a week to catch up on the course material because I learn nothing in her lectures. She just explains it in just a confusing way.

best accounting 1201 professor!! its a difficult class, but she makes it easier. there are four quizzes (lowest gets dropped), connect hw for each chapter (lowest gets dropped), two exams, a final, and a group project. take the practice exams, and you will pass. also a very generous curve at the end

Professor Vittori is amazing! Financial Accounting is a tough subject, but she really tries to make it easier. You don't need to read the textbook, unless you are having trouble in an area, as she provides notes and practice problems for every chapter. You have a group project, 4 quizzes, 2 exams, Connect hw and a final. TAKE HER

Professor Vittori is the best! There are four quizzes (lowest dropped), two exams, and a final exam. As long as you do the practice handouts, and read the notes you will do extremely well on all assessments. Provided are notes, slides, and tons of practice leading to most students doing very well. Lastly, she makes everyone enjoy accounting!

best teacher ever. favorite teacher. homeworks off connect (easy free A with 10 checks and 3 redos). Drops 1 quiz, Quizzes are the easiest. Just do her practice quizzes and exams to get an A on both the quizzes and exams. Final is just a final... and final project (start it early).

Best teacher I've ever had. Literally no negatives. Provides every resource you could ever need. Participation is required but answering "what's 20+40?" is enough for the day. Gives partial credit on projects and exams at every opportunity. Always smiling and somehow memorizes everyones name immediately. Love her. I wish she taught more classes.

As a professor, she is extremely organized, teaches brilliantly, has clear grading criterias, and gives the student all the resources to succeed. She is extremely kind, and caring.

The only thing is that the student needs to put in consistent effort from the first class to do well. At least one to two hours a week outside class.

Probably the best intro to accounting professor. The material can be difficult at times but she gives you all the resources you need to succeed you just need to do the work. About 1-2 hours of work a week outside of class. Do the practice for tests because they are often so similar to the test. Her chapter outlines give you all the info you need.

Professor Vittori is great as you can see by other reviews. However in comparison to other accounting professors she is one of the harder ones. The homeworks are extremely time-consuming, and not always helpful. However her lectures are great, and she provides a lot of material for practice. Overall a great teacher, you just have to put the work in
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Vittori was great. Expectations were set early but were never too high to reach. Many opportunities to improve grade with four two-chapter quizzes, drop the lowest. Her online lecture videos were absolute life savers when I found myself falling behind due to other classes, allowing me to get up to speed. Best ACCT1201 professor there is.

Great professor. Gives practice handouts for each chapter and each exam. The exam questions are like carbon copies from these practice problems. As long as you do them and study the exams are easy. She also gives an extremely generous curve for each quiz/exam making it an easy A.
She is amazing! Tons of handouts and notes, each chapter has its own review video, multiple drops allowed on attendance and homework. Two big exams and a large final.

Pros: Great lectures, amazing planning, accessible outside of class, good curve, understanding, enthusiastic

Cons: Hard class (difficult content), group project instructions not completely straightforward

Prof Vittori is an amazing teacher and made me actually like accounting. The material is difficult, but she gives you everything you need to succeed. There is a lot of extra practice and you can do well if you want to. There is a generous curve at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great accounting professor. Gives lots of extra study materials to make sure you are well-prepared for the exams. You really just have to put some work in and pay attention.

Incredible professor. Honestly accounting is pretty hard not matter which professor you have but she's awesome. Lectures are engaging and she really cares. Great at explaining whatever you don't understand. She give you notes and practice handouts for every chapter and records online lectures, which are super helpful when studying. Highly recommend

She is a very good teacher. Gives out great notes and handouts that prepare you for the exams and quizzes. She is very kind and wants to see everyone succeed. Huge curve which is great. If you are taking accounting, take her. She prepares you very well to get a good grade in the class. You don't really need to read the textbook, just do graded hw.
I love Professor Vittori! Definitely recommend her. Everything that was said below truly reflect my experiences in her class!

Professor Hetrick is the best! I was a bit concerned about how challenging Financial Accounting would be, but she made it seem so simple. 4 quizzes (one dropped) and 2 tests. All of her lectures and handouts clearly resembled exams/quizzes and she is an amazing teacher. Take her!!!! You will learn to LOVE accounting!
ACCT1201 with Hetrick was great! She very clearly explained the course material, and was very clear in how her grading and assignments worked. I'd recommend anyone take this class with her

She is amazing. If you like to memorize stuff and treat math like a little fun puzzle, you'll love the way she teaches. She gives hella handouts to prepare you for 4 quizzes and 3 exams over the course of the semester. She has lecture videos in case you miss class and they were lifesavers when I was sick and didn't go to class. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor is super caring and explains accounting concepts in great detail. She has worksheets for every chapter that looks exactly like the exams/quizzes and gives students many opportunities to redeem their grades and explains grading criteria in detail. (Drops lowest quiz, curves grade, had projects, etc.) I would recommend her to anyone.

Professor Hetrick is a good professor. She knows her stuff and her lectures, while potentially boring, are super helpful. The readings are not completely necessary if you pay attention in class. There is usually a big curve, given the difficult material. The tests are not impossible and her lectures are amazingly easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm currently in the middle of my semester with Professor Hetrick for ACCT 1201. She is literally the best professor I have ever had! She provides so many resources and genuinely cares about her students and will act based on feedback. ACCT 1201 is a hard course no matter who you have, but she makes it enjoyable and creates a good environment!

The best decision I have ever made in my life is taking Prof. Hetricks class. If she taught all the subjects I needed for my degree I would take them all in a heartbeat. She will make accounting a piece of cake and your favorite pastime will be doing accounting homework. Shes extremely polite and organized and is the best professor ever!
She is sooooo nice!

Great professor, explains material very well, and the structure of lectures was great. Provides practice exams or practice sheets before exams which are similar to actual exams. Curves exams. Offered some extra credit but not too much. Provides textbook notes for each unit which are basically study guides. Great choice!
She's really nice and her lectures/slides are very clear and easy to understand. Lectures could be boring at times but they are really helpful I rarely had to read the textbook. She curves tests too.

She is incredibly friendly and articulate. She was always willing to further elaborate on topics and could make a student understand after visiting her office hours. She is really nice and easy to talk to if you need questions answered. The tests get progressively harder so definitely keep studying from in-class handouts and study guides. She curves a lot, which really helps.

I found her exams were pretty easy; as long as you come to class, participate, and practice problems. You will get an A. Her lectures are very boring though but all the exam review materials are very helpful. She curves as well :)

im not a masochist but this class be turning me into one

Accelerated Section. Difficult class and content, requires attending lectures and OH. Honest and chill professor, does not care much about deadlines and attendance as long as the work is completed. Not a tough grader but the class requires time and effort.

reviews.comment: He's a very inspirational and motivating lecturer. reviews.comment: A very hard prof., but a very good one as well. He gives great lectures and is more than willing to work with students to help you succeed, despite being a very challenging course.
Fantastic professor. Extremely intelligent and passionate about math. Very helpful during office hours and lecture. Asks a lot out of students but very worth it.

Taken for accelerated Discrete (HIGHLY recommend!). Best professor so far at Northeastern. Very friendly, and easy to access during office hours. I ended up going because they were fun to attend, but also helped with anything in the homework. Hard work, but he ended almost everyone with an A.

reviews.comment: Best professor ever. Classes are difficult, but he spends a lot of time and effort on his students.
The best professor at NEU. He is tough, but the outcome of the course is worth the struggle.

I'm here to comment just because of his "some Russians live forever" joke. 

Best professor at Northeastern anyway.

Very smart guy, but covering the content of the lecture is prioritized over people actually understanding what he has to say. Professor Pavlu is extremely bright but his lectures are difficult to follow and he is very condescending. He often talks about how easy many concepts should be, which discouraged many students struggling with the material. Most stopped attending by the end of the semester.

Professor Virgil is amazing, and it is very evident he cares about his students. The final grade was essentially determined by an 8-hr midterm and 6-hr final that have a high level of difficulty. Great teaching

Prof.Pavlu explains things very well so if you follow him during the lectures you can understand the concepts pretty well. Assignments are hard but they really helped me understand the lectures better. I learned so much from him this semester and would love to take another course with him again.

reviews.comment: There are many topics that the professor could explain better, and provide more straightforward demos. But overall, Prof. Pavlu does a decent job and this course(CS5800) covers the essential materials. I cannot complain about that.

One of the best and most productive classes I ever took! Professor cares about his students, the thing is you have to figure out whether you are up for this challenge or not. Smart guy, realistic, and upfront about the difficulty of this class, but that doesn't really help when this class is a core req for several programs. reviews.comment: PLEASE DONT TAKE THIS CLASS! YOU CAN attend his lecture and he teaches pretty well. But IF YOU ARE CONCERNED ABOUT GRADES, DONT TAKE IT!!!

Honestly one of the most condescending people I have ever met. He is a very smart man, and he makes sure you know that, but his teaching leaves a lot to be desired. Also, the turnaround times for homework and exam grades are horrible.

Awwfull ! cannot explain some questions and topics well.

Best professor I met so far. His lecture is interesting and inspiring. He can very flexible about the homework as long as he knows you're really working on it and just need more time. Hes the best professor in Northeastern. I extremely enjoyed the experience of taking algorithms course under him. He teaches very well and conducts office hours for 3-4 hours atleast 2 days/week. The office hours are more or less like a class where he explains every single question of each student. But his midterm is very tough and 8-9 hours long
One of the best decisions of my life is to take a class under him. He keeps the lectures very interesting and he will come to TA hours to help the students. He is the best.

Teaches really well. One of the finest professor who can chunk down complex concepts in Machine Learning and Algorithms to a simple understanding. Provide exposure to Professional knowledge and Industry practice besides academic boundary.

He's always ridiculously hyped about what he's teaching and has infallible faith in his students' abilities. He made every class super fun, and that's coming from someone who doesn't usually like math.
Always engaged and enthusiastic to the point where it's infectious.

One of the smartest people I've met. It can be hard to follow his lectures because he goes off on tangents and is somewhat disorganized in how he goes through proofs. reviews.comment: He teaches well but assumes that you already have knowledge on the topic. So he is not so good for beginners. His assignments are difficult but really good. He is very passionate about whatever he teaches but doesn't have a proper course structure.

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best professor ever!! He is genuinely interested in teaching, knows what he is doing and loves to answer questions during or after class. You can take any of his but beware there is gonna be lots of homework. His classes are worth it.
Virgil is both really good at explaining stuff and is a really nice guy in general. He likes to see students get excited about the material and encourages us to pursue it on our own as well.

A great professor. He will make sure you don't get messed up in the mathematics of the subjects. Gives a great start to every topic. If you attend the lectures, you will learn a lot. He will make sure he comes down to your level and explains the concept. Make good notes and you are good to go!

By far, one of the best professors at NEU. Has a great grip over the subject he teaches. He has been instrumental in making me think about a problem in the right way. Also, it wouldn't be fair to not mention about the exams. Don't include straightforward out-of-texbook questions and the exam duration is not definite. An inspiring professor!!
I still remember the lines he told us in first lecture: Grades wont matter. What matter is how we think at the end of the semester. #CS5800
Great classes
